Food lovers have been flocking here for over thirty years, lured by the unbeatable value for money and the text-book perfect Italian nosh. Farfalle al dente with fresh shrimp, preserved lemons and a knockout tomato sauce – authenticity is the goal! Order the chef’s daily special with your eyes closed and don’t forget the enticing wine list.

Name: Le Moulin
Address: rue de la Lesse 61, Daverdisse, 6929, Belgium
Description: This former watermill is a charming place to experience the beauty of the Ardennes, starting with the view of the babbling river and the typical façade. Inside, cosiness is the order of the day. This is a family-run business, with a mother-and-son team providing friendly service front-of-house. In the kitchen, chef Ludovic puts a subtle modern spin on his father Jean-Pierre's classic cuisine – savour a rich game consommé with venison shank, or scallop ceviche. Foodies will be delighted by the extensive à la carte selection and set menus. Quiet guestrooms available for a pleasant overnight stay.

Name: Durbuy Ô
Description: This friendly restaurant (which also offers accommodation) is idyllically located to explore the picturesque small town of Durbuy. You will feel right at home here thanks to the family-run vibe and attentive care lavished by chef Timmerman on his guests. The pedigree French repertory is enhanced by local produce, such as scallops and venison. The chef treats all his ingredients with the utmost respect, further enhancing the experience with fascinating sauces and side dishes.

Name: Le Confessionnal
Description: Opposite Leffe Abbey, this nostalgic neighbourhood bolthole provides a showcase for the owner’s passion for flea markets. Red and white checked tablecloths, decorative soup tureens and silverware set the friendly scene. The traditional fare oozes with the charm of yesteryear and the regularly changing menu offers an array of hearty, traditional dishes, such as duck leg à la bourguignonne or roast shoulder of lamb with garlic confit. Hunger obliterating food free of fussy frills and a treasure trove of French wines at prices that make sense.

Name: Osteria Bolognese
Address: rue de la Paix 49, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: Giacomo’s mission is to correct the hackneyed image of ‘spag bol’ and his mouth - watering tagliatelle al ragù does just that! All his ingredients are sourced direct from Emilia Romagna, ensuring an explosion of flavour in the mouth. A delightful Osteria that will introduce you to the real taste of Bologna.

Name: Cadre Culinaire
Description: In addition to hailing from Alsace, Grégory Baruthio avows a passion for pastries, as you will soon realise, and his Gugelhupf is truly second to none! Ever enthusiastic, the chef dons his apron to enhance ingredients that suit the modern palate without losing sight of high-precision cooking and traditional generosity. A welcoming establishment with eater friendly prices.

Name: L'Espièglerie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Since 1988, gourmets have been making a beeline for this romantic hideaway, whose old vaults and bare brick walls lend it masses of cachet. Choose from the daily special or the menu to sample rich authentic food that has earned the establishment its well-deserved reputation as a fine dining venue. Succulent pheasant pie with crisp veal sweetbread or an unusual cannelloni of confit pear with fresh fruit. Sensibly priced. Splendid selection of beers and Bordeaux wines.

Name: Le Tournant
Description: The lively, vibrant Matongé district is home to an equally buzzy neighbourhood eatery: Le Tournant. People drop in to sample a glass of “natural” wine (trust the sommelier – he knows his job!) and dig into unfussy, nostalgic dishes reminiscent of grandma’s cooking, together with a few more modern bistro recipes. Examples include gutsy beef cheeks braised in Orval beer or lamb in dried figs. Every dish is an authentic festival of flavour!

Name: Le Saint Boniface
Cuisine: Cuisine from South West France, Country cooking
Description: Picture tightly packed tables, red and white chequered tablecloths, a collection of biscuit tins and French songs and jazz playing in the background: the scene is set in this friendly welcoming bistro. The locals flock here to sample its specialities from the Basque Country, Lyon and Southwest France. Calf’s brain and tartare sauce, confit of duck leg, veal sweetbread and kidneys rich in regional flavours. Heart-warming authentic nosh steeped in traditional Gallic generosity!

Name: Les Potes en Toque
Description: This renovated farm cottage in the heart of a residential neighbourhood is depicted by a characteristic Belgian blend of rural chic. The menu majors in flawlessly prepared brasserie favourites, served generously.

Name: Cul de Poule
Description: A colourful, cartoon-inspired chicken adorns this small bistro, but the real draw is Arnaud Molle. This seasoned chef lets his creativity run riot in regularly changing menus with a Gallic slant. His food is flavoursome, original and ideally suited to make the most of fresh produce. His flawlessly cooked pheasant served with a creamy Fine Champagne cognac sauce is to die for! The meat, from his parent’s butchery, is first class and the prices are truly eater friendly – what more can we say?

Name: De Vous à Nous
Address: rue de Grand Bry 42, Montigny-le-Tilleul, 6110, Belgium
Description: De Vous à Nous (From You to Us) sports a stylish interior, a peaceful, lush green landscape and eater-friendly prices. The know-how and generosity of chef François Duvivier are outstanding and he doesn’t hesitate to add a personal flourish to traditional recipes, such as croquettes of pheasant, pigeon with a gutsy sauce or Belle Hélène pear jus that will knock your socks off! A safe bet every time!

Name: Au Petit Château
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This endearing villa has, quite rightly, been a firm culinary fixture of Mouscron for eons and its infectiously friendly vibe is nurtured by the cheerful lady of the house. The traditional menu, which features the occasional modern tribute, always hits the spot. Carpaccio of sea bream, frog’s legs, Rossini tournedos… 100% French recipes that pay tribute to the finest traditions of culinary know-how and generosity.

Name: Villa Singha
Address: rue des Trois Ponts 22, Auderghem, 1160, Belgium
Description: Villa Singha is a proud ambassador of Thai traditions. A characteristic Thai decor and references to the mythological lion, Singha, set the exotic scene, further enhanced by an extensive mouth-watering menu. Crispy Po Pia Tod fried spring rolls and Thai dumplings stuffed with ground pork are a few of the generously crafted and perfectly seasoned and spiced dishes. A word of advice – don’t forget to book.

Name: Maza'j
Description: Maza'j serves dishes bursting with bold colours and exciting flavours. The tables here are decked with authentic Lebanese specialities that delight diners with their distinctive spiciness and generosity. Velvety hummus with pine nuts, barbecued minced lamb with a delicately sweet bell pepper confit, an array of vegetables elevated by a blend of aromatic herbs… You and your dining companions can look forward to sharing a real feast in a convivial atmosphere. Experience the richness of Lebanese culinary tradition!

Name: Le Grand Maur
Description: An air of romantic nostalgia reigns throughout this charming small Ardennes castle. Ideally located for a spot of sight-seeing in Spa, the castle also serves a bang-up meal. The attractive range of dishes demonstrates the chef’s passion for first-class produce, which he prepares generously, flanked by polished side dishes and subtle sauces.

Name: Vilain
Description: Vilain offers a choice of 10 to 15 dishes to share, which often change weekly in line with the seasons and the suppliers and sports an irresistible vintage vibe, overflowing in good cheer and boasting a lovely garden for alfresco dining. The occasional international twist jazzes up the traditional pageant: butternut ravioles with ricotta, jus of bacon and walnuts. Sharing such delicacies can pose quite a dilemma!

Name: Onslow
Description: Onslow, a buzzy landmark in the peaceful Sint Anna district, offers casual dining and a terrace bathed in Mediterranean charm. Its international menu with a host of tasty dishes to share is extremely popular with the locals. Lieven Vynck whisks us off to Nice with a pissaladière that is a perfect balance between caramelised onions, anchovies, olives, thyme and lemon peel, unless you would rather sample the fresh, spicy, acidic tang of a mouthwatering ceviche. A feast of flavour awaits you at Onslow: “Food with Drinks, Drinks with Food” is their baseline!

Name: Au Phil des Saveurs
Description: A quick look at the pool and garden overlooking the countryside confirms the holiday vibe as soon as you set foot inside Phil Garcia’s HQ. The food features an intelligent blend of classical cooking techniques with Mediterranean influences. He offers a new spin on vitello tonnato with cod cooked on the skin, flanked by a velvety mousseline of mashed potato and leek oil. Enticing set menus and the cheerful relaxed service of the lady of the house add the final flourish to this fine dining portrait.

Name: Les 4 Saisons
Description: The charm of this Ardennes house is encapsulated by the landscaped garden, providing the perfect foil to the warm, inviting interior. Ingredients take the star role in gutsy nostalgic recipes, albeit with a scattering of refreshing creative twists. For example, the chef’s perfectly cooked veal in truffles with Asian flavours. The menu with options is a model of full-bodied generosity. Deliciously eater friendly prices!

Name: il était une fois toi et moi
Description: Looking for the perfect romantic spot? Look no further: this restaurant ticks all the boxes, starting with the name! A smart lounge interior serves as the backdrop to an exciting culinary story. The extensive menu, which offers made-to-measure options, combines traditional Gallic recipes and more contemporary offerings. The food is both inspired and suave, whilst remaining reassuringly familiar.

Name: Ferment
Description: A drop-dead wine list, a knock-out collection of authentic local beers and updated family favourites to share: this bustling restaurant on Lennik market square attracts foodies like bees to honey! They swarm here for shrimp fritters, melt-in-the-mouth asparagus (served with melted butter, finely chopped hard-boiled eggs and parsley), grilled sea bass and a host of other delectable morsels. Generous home-made cooking that shines the spotlight on local produce and know-how.

Name: L'épicerie Nomad
Description: Cosmopolitan par excellence, Brussels’ international character is emblematic of this bustling eatery which features tightly packed tables and a slate menu that makes no distinction between starters and main courses. How about a fresh, bitter ceviche of seabass with mango and passion fruit, a Spanish zarzuela of seafood, or shakshuka - a vegetarian one-pan savoury dish? The chef’s creativity, which knows no bounds, is further enhanced by his superlative knack for marrying flavours. Pair this culinary journey with one of the carefully curated tipples to make the most of this fascinating experience.

Name: Le Sixième
Description: There is something for everyone in this modern bistro. Chef Clément draws his inspiration from top-notch ingredients, to which he adds a subtle personal spin. Asian influences, the authentic flavour of marinated beetroot, a velvety beurre blanc and the subtle smoky hints of the wood-fired Josper oven… Splendid harmonies and great value for money. A word of advice: if you would prefer a more romantic vibe, ask for a table in the second room.

Name: Magnific
Description: Lounge music in the background, trendy urban wall graffiti and the warm hospitality of Limburg: a meal at Magnific is always a treat. All the more so, as the chef cleverly juggles with French and Italian recipes, throwing in the odd Asian theme. Whether you start with cannelloni or continue with a venison steak and a cranberry sauce, you can rely on the stellar craftsmanship and full-bodied flavours to come up trumps every time! The set menu with choices is highly recommended.

Name: Bienvenue
Description: John van Leerzem is a fan of tradition and of the ingredient before all else. This institution on the main square of Maaseik does far more than showcase time-honoured classics. The chef happily subverts traditional recipes, particularly thanks to carefully devised side dishes, such as a terrine of veal cheek and tongue that he subtly contrasts with sweet-sour chutney. His stamp can also be tasted in the tournedos and stroganoff sauce that strikes a perfect balance of flavours. A feast for foodies!

Name: Au Dos de la Cuillère
Description: The establishment has been treated to a (forced) makeover after the flooding of 2021 but has lost none of its charm. The chef specialises in Gallic cuisine with a fondness for local ingredients, such as Herve cheese and pork from the Tabreux farm. Everything is generous and homemade, even the praline of the decadent Paris-Brest pastry. Don’t forget to book!

Name: La Table du Boucher
Description: Luc Broutard avows a passion for top quality produce, red meat in particular, as you will immediately realise when you cross the threshold of this buzzy brasserie. Seared foie gras, tartare of Salers beef, marinated pork cheeks or grilled tenderloin: carnivores will be in seventh heaven as they drool over the extensive menu. Rich, spot-on cooking, happily free of gimmicks and there are even a few fish dishes. Everyone feels at home at the Table du Boucher, to such an extent that many return in their droves.

Name: Comptoir de l'Eau Vive
Address: place des Jardins de Baseilles 14, Erpent, 5101, Belgium
Description: Trendy and buzzy, this small eatery is the epitome of a Bib Gourmand. Whether you go for one of the classics on the à la carte menu (like meatballs in tomato sauce or rib of beef with fries) or for the more modern set menu (featuring Mediterranean ingredients such as mullet), all the food is depicted by wholesome, instantly recognisable flavours. The wine list and the sommelier’s suggestions are greatly appreciated, as is the possibility of purchasing cheese and wine, in particular, from the shop. One final word of advice: take a seat at the counter if available, you’re in for a treat!

Name: Arti'Choc
Description: The welcoming interior and Katja’s warm personality provide the perfect foil to this friendly modern stube. Chef Daniel is a fan of fine produce, such as trout and sweetbreads, that he pampers and enhances in traditional recipes. Expect rich flavours and authentic sauces rather than prissy details. You can even take a few preserves and liqueurs home.

Name: l'Amitié
Description: When you arrive in this fully renovated bistro, it won’t be friendship, but something more akin to love that you will feel. Fish takes pride of place and the first class ingredients are prepared according to modern techniques and served in small dishes. Scrumptious!

Name: Strofilia
Address: rue du Marché aux Porcs 11, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This always-bustling establishment near the fish market is a hub of authentic Greek hospitality and generosity. Whether you come as a couple or a large group, everyone gets the attention they deserve. The menu features a whole host of delicious mezze to choose from. Tamara with sourdough bread, tender octopus with fava beans, a salad of green lentils with smoked herring, orange and sultanas… This authentic food is packed with vibrant, honest flavours that hit the spot every time. The wine list features an impressive range of Greek options that won't break the bank.

Name: L'Echappée Belle
Description: The quintessence of a Bib Gourmand, this eatery is embodied by Grégory and Camille’s warm friendly welcome. The couple has created strong ties with local producers, such as Ferme d’Artagnan and Ferme Fourchette, who have become part of the family. The chef crafts their excellent ingredients generously and creatively, underscoring the distinctive flavour of Belgian endive with braised beef cheeks, crunchy celeriac and marinated onion. Authentic Liège recipes and a fine view of the cottage garden from the terrace.

Name: Cœur de Bœuf
Address: avenue du Général Gracia 23, Profondeville, 5170, Belgium
Description: The barbecue gets ample use in this Bib Gourmand establishment, a family-run brasserie where you can feast on traditional meat specialities in a laid-back setting. Beef from all corners of the globe is the main feature of the extensive à la carte selection and set menu. Think succulent Rouge de Famenne rump steak tagliata served with fresh fries. Generosity and à la minute cooking are the norm here. Feel free to take the menu home afterwards; it's full of fun facts!

Name: French Kiss
Description: A pleasant restaurant renowned for its excellent grilled dishes and impressive wine list. Dining area with a low ceiling and bright paintings adding colour to the brick walls.

Name: dis-moi où ?
Description: Tell me where? Well, here! If you are looking for food that combines tradition and generosity, this upbeat eatery is the place for you (don’t forget to book). Chef Nicolas Michiels not only knows how to concoct good sauces and grill meat to perfection, he is also a dab hand at whipping up more elaborate recipes of great delicacy. He might mix a subtle quenelle of scallops and langoustine with a seafood jus, creating an exquisitely delicate balance. Choosing from the extensive menu may pose something of a conundrum. Why not try one of the excellent whiskeys suggested by the chef at the end of your meal?

Name: l'Apropos
Description: After a facelift, L’Apropos now sports a warm, bright interior with colourful artwork. Chef Fournier shares his love of world, Mediterranean, Asian and North - African food, which he skilfully mixes and prepares, demonstrating a flawless sense of balance.

Name: Tou.Gou
Description: A single glance at the wholesome country menu, featuring rustic staples such as grilled tripe and snails, pork pie and partridge with endives, will set your tastebuds tingling. The veteran chef, a true disciple of text-book Gallic fare, enjoys adding the odd international twist. Gutsy flavours, hearty helpings, culinary proficiency. A take-out delicatessen service is also available.

Name: Sel et Poivre
Address: rue de la Fontaine 3, Hollain, 7620, Belgium
Description: Welcome to Nathalie and Alexis’ lovely little restaurant. Their enthusiasm is as communicative as their traditional cuisine. This is made from excellent produce and is enticing without forgetting the occasional dash of humour. A salt - and - pepper combination to which we will happily return.

Name: Borse van Amsterdam
Description: Borse is a landmark of Amsterdam, as much for its colossal architecture and historic Flemish décor as for its restaurant. With its huge terrace overlooking the Grand-Place, it has been a blue-chip value for donkey’s years. The menu focuses on generous helpings of time-honoured family favourites and you will instantly be able to taste the deft hand of a seasoned chef who knows how to enhance authentic flavours.

Name: Michel
Description: Time seems to have stood still at Michel’s. From the classical interior to the traditional, no - frills food, everything is authentic. Walloon produce and young cockerel take pride of place on the table. A treat for your taste buds.

Name: L'Ôthentique
Description: All that remains of the former farmstead are the old stone vaults, yet the land and its produce are at the centre of this establishment. Chef Collignon hunts out top-notch ingredients that he deftly crafts into appetising, primarily French classics. Don’t miss the house foie gras and its pageant of fresh, unctuous garnishes. The trout, straight from the aquarium on the terrace, is another house speciality. Authentic generosity.

Name: L'Entre D'Eux
Description: Caroline Druine combines delicacy and generosity in dishes that demonstrate her commitment to local, organic ingredients. For example, she pairs wild boar from the next-door forest with “grandma’s” red cabbage and a gutsy dark brown cocoa sauce that is so good you will be licking your fingers after mopping it up with bread! The casual vibe is further amplified by Alexandre’s natural, friendly service. A small patio in the garden planted with pear trees is ideal for alfresco summer dining.

Name: De Farmasie
Description: A good meal is just what the doctor ordered! So, book a table quickly in this fashionable establishment, quirkily adorned with a 17C pharmacy cabinet. The chef, a keen “farm to table” adept who is equally at home with rib steak and Thai curry, demonstrates an innate flair for flavours and tastes. The owner adores sharing his love of fine (Italian) wine with diners.

Name: L'Embellie
Address: rue de la Station 115, Soignies, 7060, Belgium
Description: Make your day that little bit better with a visit to this restaurant run by charming maître d' Géraldine and seasoned chef Pol. Grab a table at the front of the cosy dining space, or head to the back, where light pours in from the lovely garden – either way, you're in for a treat! When it comes to the quality of his ingredients, the chef refuses to compromise, a pursuit of excellence that is matched by his culinary expertise. This cuisine is incredibly generous, and it shows in every dish, from the rich foie gras terrine served with succulent pheasant to the rich miso jus that lends a subtle spiciness to the sea bream. Pure passion is at play here!

Name: De Gebrande Winning
Description: This characterful farmstead with a cafe at the entrance has lost none of its authentic charm. The focus is on beer and premium produce before all else. Indeed, an annual beer festival, an awe-inspiring beer menu and knockout beer associations demonstrate the star role of brewed beverages here. Chef Sainte pairs this ethos with no-nonsense food that shines the spotlight on nostalgic Flemish recipes, albeit with subtle modern touches. Rare beef is served with fresh green peas, asparagus and a gutsy gravy: rugged, generous cooking that hits the spot every time and which never fails to bring a smile to the face of satisfied diners.

Name: Boris & Maurice
Description: It is crystal clear that Boris and Maurice have worked together before (at Bodo). Their friendly neighbourhood eatery with a long counter offers tasty bistro fare with a twist. For example, you may start with deep-fried bites of sole and tartare sauce, followed by a juicy breast of chicken and a masterful Archiduc sauce (mushrooms and cream), finishing with a chocolate mousse. The French wine list adds the final flourish to this appetising banquet.

Name: Ni Shifu
Description: Sichuan cuisine is renowned for its hot spices, pungent herbs, rich oils and wok hei preparations and the chef here deftly mixes all these components. Traditional fish soup is prepared with a rich stock and marinated Chinese cabbage, while pork belly and pork neck are braised and cooked in chili and fermented black beans: comfort food so good we warrant you will be wiping your plate squeaky clean. Close your eyes and the bustling ambience of this down-to-earth eatery may well transport you straight to Chengdu. The endless menu is truly mind-blowing. The quintessence of a Bib Gourmand!

Name: Magma
Address: Rue Porte aux Oies 43, Liège, 4020, Belgium
Description: It is heaven to spend time in this hip, upbeat eatery. Tom Foguenne has creatively sourced a lineup of local organic produce out of which he crafts mind-blowing flavours. He might mix smoked trout and tomato with subtly spicy oils, or serve fried chickpeas with cream of yoghurt. Each dish is steeped in unusual tastes and savours, further enhanced by the knockout organic, natural wine list. Instinctive cuisine and a frequently changing menu.

Name: Furbetto
Description: Gust and Jasper have established their friendly eatery a stone’s throw from Heverlee railway station in a smart if somewhat low-key town house. Their love of cooking and devotion to simplicity shine through as you watch them wield their magic in the open-plan kitchen. Homemade is the name of the game here, underscored by a constant quest for superlative local produce. After nibbling on a delicious focaccia appetiser, dig into homemade pasta and subtle dishes, such as blue cheese pie paired with fermented raspberries. Furbetto hits the spot every time, all the more so due to its bargain prices!

Name: Bizie Lizie
Description: At Bizie Lizie you can choose from a modern brasserie dotted with vintage details or a swish, bordering on Baroque interior. However, those who find it difficult to make up their mind, may well find the amazing choice on the menu somewhat daunting! The menu that will find favour with lovers of nostalgic nosh features heart-warming brasserie fare, such as shrimp fritters, calf’s tongue in Madeira sauce or eels in sorrel.

Name: Glou Glou
Description: The distinctive sound of fine natural wine “glug glugging” into a glass is the hallmark of this friendly eatery. Let yourself be guided by the expert insights of the sommelier. The chef, for his part, showcases his personal take on contemporary tapas, mingling French, Asian and Italian influences with enthusiasm and generosity. Full-bodied soy flanks aubergine, while fresh, spicy kimchi jazzes up beef hanger steak without forgetting the irresistible lost bread. Everything is impossibly tempting –don’t forget to book!

Name: K restaurant
Description: The imposing K gives you a choice of a modern setting, a more elegant, classical room and a terrace. The fantastic range of dishes is further proof that everyone will find something to suit their palate. From classical dishes and brasserie fare to more elaborate recipes, all prepared generously and, wherever possible, at the last minute. Go on! Treat your taste buds!

Name: Bonifas
Description: Bonifas is steeped in the charm of a country inn. Welcoming staff and a warm contemporary interior. Chef Grégory enriches his French culinary score with international influences and modern techniques. The lunchtime and suggestion menus are very popular.

Name: St Kilda
Description: St Kilda is emblematic of Belgium’s capital, whose restaurants strive to please. Established on a lively street corner and depicted by a casual vintage vibe, don’t expect fussy frills. The menu is stuffed with unusual recipes such as terrine of leeks and nori with egg mimosa or a mandarin, honey and speculoos dessert, all packed with depth. Intelligent combinations, loving care and attention lavished on the veggies and bold punchy flavours set the culinary scene, explaining its success. Now add eater-friendly prices and you will quickly understand just why this eatery is so popular!

Name: Yoka Tomo
Description: A friendly restaurant in a residential neighbourhood with limited seating and a chef who crafts dishes from Southern Japan in his open-plan kitchen. Rather than decadent ingredients, you can expect authentic craftsmanship and seasonings that stimulate the tastebuds. Crispy chicken with a sweet-sour sauce is paired with crunchy vegetables and a rémoulade sauce in a tasty, almost addictive dish. Tomoyuki Ohara has no qualms about surprising us, whilst religiously respecting Japanese culinary traditions. Truly irresistible!

Name: Gaston Vouzote
Description: If you feel like a slap-up meal with all the trimmings, make a beeline for this authentic brasserie whose vintage interior is paired with a Parisian vibe. Family favourites that warm the soul, such as traditional terrine (depending on the season), steak tartare and soufflé, set the scene on the menu. Homemade, hearty cooking and a festival of flavours. Gaston Vouzoute knows how to satisfy our appetites and our senses!

Name: Mamy Louise
Description: This multipurpose new building is made entirely out of wood, glass and steel. It is home to a restaurant, cocktail bar with terrace, lounges and meeting rooms. The equally varied menu features a fine choice of brasserie fare, including tempting salads and confit of duck, all of which are at reasonable prices.

Name: Origines
Address: Rue de la Coupe 25, Mons, 7000, Belgium
Description: A narrow lane near the main square of Mons leads to the endearing restaurant of Céline, the charming and ever cheerful lady of the house. The sunny rear patio features an olive tree in its centre. Chef Watteyne crafts a menu dictated by market availability, the seasons and his innovative ideas. Examples include his personal take on vitello tonnato or a fascinating tomato-strawberry-burrata dessert. Bold, distinctive cuisine crafted by a chef who takes pride in ensuring that each flavour is spot on and punchy.

Name: abCd
Description: The abCd of French cuisine has no secrets for Borg Da Silva. Pairing goose liver or suckling lamb with just the right sauce and just the right crunchy vegetables is second nature to this artisan chef, whose technical prowess can also be sampled in drop dead desserts. Generosity is the watchword in this tastefully appointed restaurant.

Name: CCnomie
Description: David Coisman seeks to add his signature originality and generosity to regional produce. Rather than gimmicky combinations, he woos us with consummate skill and familiar flavours, adding a fresh twist to pheasant or steak with shallots thanks to inventive side dishes. One thing is certain: a visit to this restaurant, established in a restored 1800 barn on the family farm is synonymous with a festival of flavour.

Name: Brasserie N4
Description: This friendly family brasserie abuts the busy N4 highway, but as soon as you see the rolling Ardennes countryside to the rear, your peace of mind is restored (don’t hesitate to book a room here if you would like to explore the region). Frédéric Bolis finds his inspiration in purebred French classics, to which he is not averse to adding a personal spin. Terrine of foie gras with savoury sides, entrecote steak in a Josper charcoal oven, fresh pasta with truffles: the enticing dishes on the set menu and the à la carte offering of this seasoned chef will win over the most discerning foodies!

Name: JB
Address: rue du Grand Cerf 24, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: This stylish, family-run establishment, which is located in a quiet street just a stone’s throw from Avenue Louise and the courthouse, has acquired a loyal crowd of regulars since it opened in 1979. The onus is on authentic classics that hit the spot every time. Asparagus à la flamande with a velvety hollandaise sauce, juicy lamb served with heapings of gratin dauphinois, and a sweet crêpe normande. Know-how, generosity and eater-friendly prices: the epitome of a Bib Gourmand.

Name: De Maurice à Olivier
Description: Amusingly, you have to walk past Maurice’s newsagents before reaching the Parisian-style bistro of his son, Olivier. Gallic tradition permeates both the service and the food. Dishes range from a delicious white pudding of poultry, served with chunks of lobster, truffles and a frothy sabayon for a masterful finishing touch. The chef may add the occasional original note, but he remains a steadfast champion of classical French fare. A well-stocked wine cellar and a splendid choice of cigars and whiskeys round off this enticing portrait.

Name: La Fermette
Description: Sarah Bohet and Michaël Vancraeynest are at the helm of this authentic farmhouse in the Ardennes. The chef consummately grills entrecôte steaks on an open log fire, which are then served with a velvety béarnaise sauce. He may also mix scallops with smoked game, flanked by an onion sauce, a compote of plums and a frothy espuma of pumpkin. This exuberant culinary lineup is further enhanced by the wine list painstakingly selected by Sarah. A hit since 2003!

Name: Selecto
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This bistro is thriving in the casual vibe of the buzzy, alternative Saint Catherine neighbourhood. Selecto never fails to deliver thanks to its knockout set menu. Bistronomic fare that hits the spot every time, with a dash of Mediterranean flair, such as creamy risotto with shrimps or a sun-drenched tartlet of aubergine, coppa and burratina, throbbing in no-frills, down-to-earth flavours.

Name: Les Coudes sur la Table
Description: Baudouin Galler has mastered the art of sobriety. He not only shines the spotlight on fresh ingredients from local producers, crafting intelligent recipes that focus on powerful flavours, he also enjoys tossing in the odd Mediterranean or Asian touch to jazz up the culinary regional festival. The handwritten wine list offers a fine selection of organic tipples to accompany your meal.

Name: Tero
Description: Tero pays tribute to the land and demonstrates great respect for produce like the veggies and pork from its own farm (Rabanisse farm). Each ingredient is assembled in intelligently curated, light dishes that favour a natural approach. A 63° egg with a personal version of shakshouka and croutons. Playful, flavoursome and bang on target. The former workshop of artist Fernand Khnopff provides the backdrop to this sparkling foodie parenthesis so in tune with the zeitgeist.

Name: La Cuisine de Yannick
Description: Red and white tablecloths set the warm bistro scene, reinforced by a soundtrack starring the likes of Jacques Brel and Georges Brassens and, above all, the personality of exuberant, fun-loving Joelle in the front of house. It is the perfect spot to (re)discover the importance of home-made cooking and the sheer strength of traditional flavours. The regularly renewed menu shines the spotlight on a line-up of classics ranging from beef tongue in Madeira sauce to a consummately crafted, oozing with taste kidney stew. The reasonably priced wine list is equally awesome.

Name: La Broche
Description: This cosy restaurant has been a firm fixture in town since 1998. The secret of its success resides in Eric Fieuw’s generous cooking. Traditional dishes, jazzed up with the occasional modern touch. Save room for pudding - the chef is a trained pastry cook!

Name: Ciro's
Description: The nostalgic interior, working class atmosphere and traditional Belgian fare will provide the opportunity to turn a meal at Ciro’s into a taste of Antwerp’s past. Steak and chips with six sauces and vol-au-vent deluxe are the stars of the show. Book ahead – you won’t be disappointed!

Name: La Chapellerie
Address: chaussée de la Seigneurie 13, Petit-Rechain, 4800, Belgium
Description: Sophie’s grandparents were hatmakers (hence the name), but Sophie’s love was cooking. In a tastefully refurbished brick townhouse, she turns out comfortingly familiar dishes, oozing with elegance. Spot-on cooking, a sprinkling of creativity and punchy, powerful sauces are combined in well-balanced dishes.

Name: Nulle Part Ailleurs
Address: rue de la Gare 10, Couvin, 5660, Belgium
Description: Hospitality is the Corman family’s raison d’être. Spend a night in a pretty room, hunt out a few excellent bottles in the shop (or the restaurant) and sample fine cooking, enhanced by modern techniques. The result is remarkable and fully worthy of a Bib Gourmand!

Name: Le Clos des Récollets
Address: rue de la Prévôté 9, Durbuy, 6940, Belgium
Description: The picturesque charm of Durby is fully echoed in this delightful restaurant with a superb terrace. The cuisine, firmly anchored in classical techniques, occasionally delves into a more modern repertory. Each dish is a skilful association of flavours. Stay overnight to finish your meal in style.

Name: Ko'uzi
Description: This sleek minimalist interior draws sushi fans like bees to honey. Whether it is a classic salmon maki wrapped in a soy crepe or a more inventive sushi of smoked eel and red beetroot, Junko Kawada effortlessly combines purity of flavour with cutting-edge Japanese precision. The offer is varied and also features sashimi and salads, without forgetting a knockout range of teas to take home and sushi lessons.

Name: Schnitzel
Description: Good simple food is the ethos of this vintage-inspired bolthole which offers 5-, 6- and 7-course menus. Gert Weyn hits the nail on the head with intuitive personal inventions crafted with just a few ingredients. He has a knack for pairing the gutsy flavours of black pudding with slices of radish, sorrel leaves and herby fromage blanc, for example. Food that is refreshingly hearty, wholesome and oozing with flavour: such is the hallmark of Schnitzel.

Name: Ferme des 4 saisons
Description: A menu rich in exemplary classical dishes and first - class brasserie fare will set your taste buds tingling, an inspired, innovative chef and an authentic, jazzed up interior combining contemporary and rustic details. Franck and Cathy have breathed new life and vitality into their parents’ brasserie!

Name: Le Barathym
Description: Barathym is synonymous with good food in a casual, warm vibe, whether on the terrace or in the updated rustic village cafe interior. The tasty seasonal fare is traditional, although sprinkled with modernity, often in the form of Asian or Mediterranean accents. Don’t expect fussy plating, but rather the simple joy of a tender juicy cut of meat served with a crisp salad dressed in a spicy sauce. Good country cooking that our grandmothers would have been proud to serve adapted to today’s tastebuds and ethos. All of which at unbeatable eater-friendly prices!

Name: Les Fines Gueules
Description: This bright, airy restaurant is surrounded by the gently undulating green landscapes of the Herve region. Home to an inventive chef, it offers a tempting à la carte selection, as well as a simpler set menu. The chef puts a great deal of effort into his dishes, playing with techniques and combinations without compromising on flavour and generosity.

Name: La Fermette des Pins
Description: A picturesque farmstead in the heart of the countryside whose terrace makes the most of this idyllic rural setting – ideal to sample top-notch brasserie fare. You won’t regret booking a table here! The seasoned chef’s veal kidneys served with a velvety béarnaise sauce are out of this world. In short: the quintessence of wholesome country cooking.

Name: Faraya
Description: The Harika family has morphed the Faraya into an elegant restaurant, whilst retaining its home from home vibe (songbirds included!). True to Lebanese tradition, the authentic dishes are piled high in the middle of the table to be shared by all the guests. Smooth hummus, labneh, mixed grills rich in spices and baklava dripping in honey… Don’t miss the buffet (Saturday evening and Sunday lunchtime).

Name: Terminus
Description: Don't hesitate to pull into this establishment, just before the French border. You will see the Verheyde family’s farm and the meat comes from their own cattle. The traditional, generous food uplifts the hearts of travellers. Ask the owner Pieter, an excellent sommelier, for his advice about wine.

Name: Biestro H-eat
Description: A hip bistro that never fails to appeal. Trendy lighting, a vintage wood-burning stove and a full view of the chefs consummately rustling up flavoursome fare in the open kitchen. Their boundless inspiration features Flemish classics, Asian nuances and Mediterranean flair in a scrumptious menu. The epitome of a friendly bistro – from the décor to the plate!

Name: Amu
Description: The elegant, intimate decor of Amu sports a marriage of romantic and sexy. In her open kitchen, Marjanne Moonen rustles up genuine delicacies with just a few ingredients that are free of fancy frills, but always spot on. Her distinctive culinary signature is a patchwork of Mediterranean influences, spices and fermentation techniques. The wine list is sourced from all over the world.

Name: Le Baan Thaï
Description: A whiff of exoticism subtly contrasts with the historic character of the Patershol district in this grand old abode. The welcoming interior sports high ceilings and works of art, without forgetting the walled courtyard - exquisite in fine weather. The dishes are visually appetising and generously presented, revealing the wide range of flavours of traditional Thai cuisine. The ingredients are fresh, steeped in rich perfumes and aromas with just the right balance of spices. A blue-chip value since 1989!

Name: Appel Thaï
Description: Appel Thaï, which is a firm favourite with fans of Asian fare, makes the most of its lush green oasis in Anderlecht. Choose between the peaceful terrace or the buzzier, casual vibe indoors. Fresh, spicy, intense flavours crafted by a veteran chef. Home-made nems served with a tingling sauce, rich massaman curry or a Pad Thai all cooked to textbook perfection: high-flying Thai cuisine in an unstuffy, relaxed setting. Wide variety of choice and dependable first-rate quality.

Name: De Garage
Description: You will probably have guessed from the name and the industrial look that this space to be a garage. Now reimagined as a bistro, the blend of untreated materials and vintage design elements creates a unique atmosphere. The menu puts the emphasis squarely on authentic and familiar flavours, eschewing any unnecessary frills. Think braised pork cheek in a robust sauce, sole meunière with pommes frites or even vegan green curry. Sommelier Fitzgerald Rigole's recommendations are always spot on – and his enthusiasm is infectious!

Name: ANJU
Address: Rue de la Source 73, Saint-Gilles, 1060, Belgium
Description: Sang Hoon Degeimbre reveals his Korean roots in Saint Gilles. In a hip, minimalist interior, he has recruited a kitchen team that crafts an extensive range of dishes to share, ranging from gutsy stocks and hot pots to kimchi. Dig into the decadently addictive Korean-style fried chicken with a sweet, spicy sauce. The antithesis of fussy, but with lashings of traditional generosity.

Name: Pluriel
Address: Rue de la Colline 58, Transinne, 6890, Belgium
Description: A slightly smoky aroma tickles your nostrils as soon as you reach the carpark of this former farmstead, which tastefully sports untreated materials to create a warm vibe. Loélia Gachadoat and Vadim Poncelet, steadfast champions of barbecue cooking, demonstrate their combined talents, mingling rustic flavours with a creative festival of occasionally surprising nuances. The symbiosis between these two chefs signs the characterful cuisine.

Name: la cantinetta
Description: La cantinetta possesses a distinctly casual and convivial feel that is very appealing. Thomas is the host and sommelier, and his brother Matthias, the chef, showcases the skills his mother taught him, cooking up a bold take on authentic Italian cuisine. For instance, he spices up raw salmon with a zingy tomato broth and various beans that have been imbued with subtle bitterness. A wasabi granita provides an extra kick. Expect generous flavours and original ideas. Great value for money!

Name: Quatre Vins
Description: Put on your rose-tinted spectacles and bask in the warm, cosy interior of Quatre Vins, without forgetting the walled terrace, which is bliss come summertime. The menu features a line-up of international dishes to be shared in a friendly, buzzy vibe. How about steamed pork belly with crunchy hispi (pointed) cabbage in a rich BBQ sauce and a bread roll on the side, or steamed haddock on a bed of leeks and a light, herb-flavoured sauce? In addition to a fine range of biodynamic and natural wines, Maxinne and Olivier bend over backwards to ensure guests feel at home in their fun-loving establishment.

Name: ANAM
Description: At this humble diner situated in Bukchon Village, Seoul, the pork and rice soup comes in two sizes: medium and extra-meat. In the soup, a special oil made with Cheongyang chili pepper and kale is drizzled on top of the agreeably clean broth, with their culinary harmony creating a unique visual appearance and rich flavors. Plus, the Spanish Duroc baby pork ribs and thin slices of pork butt that complement the dish are exceedingly tender and boast subtle flavors, raising the gastronomic experience to a new crescendo. Visit Anam and enjoy a warm hearty bowl of its trademark soup. One last thing: Feel free to add cilantro to taste.

Name: Cor Pasta bar
Address: 2F, 13 Dongseong-ro 25 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47305, South Korea
Description: Walk into a hip alley in Jeonpo-dong, and there is a thick steel door on the second floor of a glass-walled building, behind which is an elegant ten-seater diner. As the name Pasta Bar suggests, this eatery offers a wide selection of its namesake dishes made with fresh housemade pasta. Visit Cor Pasta Bar and treat yourself to its shrimp spaghetti with rich bisque sauce; bottarga pasta with sea urchin and fish roe; or roman-style Korean beef honeycomb tripe in tomato sauce – with its house-baked focaccia or your favorite wine.

Name: Tokyo Babsang
Description: The familiar vibrant vibe of Gwangalli Beach, a landmark attraction in Busan, will have given way to that of calm and peace by the time one arrives at the door of Tokyo Babsang, which specializes in unaju (grilled eel over rice) and hitsumabushi (Nagoya-style grilled eel), the two representative Japanese eel dishes. The fare at this diner mirrors Chef Kim Tae-woo’s dedication to authenticity. Each bite of the thick and chewy eel, which stands out with its inherent flavor, goes perfectly with the accompanying sauce brimming with umami. But above all, its harmony with the glossy steamed rice, normally made from newly polished rice, heightens the appetite. The chef’s respect for authentic recipes, coupled with his sensitive culinary creativity, is what keeps the joint’s fare trustworthy.

Name: Anmok
Address: 3 Gwangnam-ro 22 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48307, South Korea
Description: Anmok’s unique take on dwaeji-gukbap, or pork and rice soup, may surprise customers with novel flavors and charm that defy their memories of the dish. The soup is not merely unconventional. It’ll make you nod in appreciation. The dish also has a distinct flavor that evokes those of many other Korean soups. Indeed, the diner has successfully differentiated itself from countless other famed restaurants in Busan, the capital of dwaeji-gukbap, giving the impression that it continues to change and evolve while exploring diverse culinary directions. Though everyone has different preferences, we recommend you savor Amok’s soup offerings as they are prepared without adding chili sauce or salted shrimp.

Name: ARP
Address: 35 Taejong-ro 99 beon-gil, Yeongdo-gu, Busan, 49035, South Korea
Description: ARP offers a 100 percent vegan menu. An acronym formed from the phrase “Around Plants,” the eatery’s name symbolizes the positive, ethical kitchen table of the round Earth and the unlimited possibilities inherent in veggie cuisine. Here, customers can enjoy a diverse range of non-meat dishes paired with housemade wine made of rice. And these offerings immediately debunk the common misconception that vegan food is not delicious. For instance, the signature bracken pasta features dried bracken and mushrooms for a maximally chewy texture and pleasant nutty flavors. The vegan cheese, though made from coconut oil, tastes exactly like cheddar cheese. Come and relish the gastronomic charm of ARP’s delectable non-animal-based fare in this elegantly designed space.

Name: Egg & Flour
Description: As implied by its name, Egg & Flour is an Italian restaurant specializing in fresh, handmade pasta composed only with egg and flour. Even the entrance to the establishment greets us with sacks of flour and pasta rolling machines. The space is located along a winding alley in Haebangchon, yet the Itaewon skyline seen from the terrace and through the glass wall evokes majesty. The establishment’s signature offering is freshly made Italian pasta with a Korean twist – be it Jeju black pork ragù featuring red chili paste and fish sauce, burrata cheese, or roasted Ecklonia cava.

Name: Ggupdang
Description: Situated right near Sinsa station, this restaurant specializes in grilled pork butt cured for 15 days before being quickly grilled on a specially made aluminum grate over Binchotan charcoal. Thanks to this method of cooking, the meat is fatty, tender, and juicy. As in the case of sushi, when it is eaten with rice (prepared with a recipe conceived by a Japanese consultant chef) and Korean horseradish, the meat juice is absorbed by the rice, making it even softer. The side orders are not to be missed.

Name: Haemok
Address: 8 Gunam-ro 24 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48094, South Korea
Description: Popular among both tourists and local regulars, Haemok offers accessible Japanese fare. Its blue fence and inexplicably exotic edifice create a vibe that makes this spot stand out in the neighborhood. Its wood-based décor and tatami floor also add to the exotic ambiance. Haemok’s menu includes a few selections of Japanese rice bowls, sashimi, tempura, and tataki dishes. But its signature item is unarguably hitsumabushi (Nagoya-style grilled eel). Coated with umami-rich sauce, the eel features bottomless flavor and is a perfect accompaniment to the rice cooked to perfection. And just so you know, Haemok also has outposts in Seoul.

Name: Nagahama Mangetsu
Description: Tucked deep within the Haeridan-gil area, this establishment stands out with a long line of diners waiting to be seated. This ramen joint in Busan is the first Korean outpost of a restaurant that started during the 1960s in the Nagahama area in Fukuoka, Japan. The ramen is prepared by simmering pig bones for hours until the broth becomes milky and smooth. Combined with a secret homemade soy sauce, the broth tastes rich, but never heavy. You may request your noodles be cooked to your liking, or add raw garlic or a spicy sauce. If you find your new broth a little too salty, feel free to ask for additional broth to savor your dish to the fullest.

Name: FAGP
Description: In a city where a plate of pasta is as ubiquitous as a bowl of kalguksu, it takes a good dose of creativity and knowledge of the genre to be recognized for one’s craft. Chef Lee Jong-hyuk is armed with both. FAGP is a casual restaurant that offers a simple yet inventive menu with a focus on the relatively humble pasta. There is a genuine sense of conviviality here, which comes as no surprise, as the chef says he revels in engaging with his customers while cooking in the open kitchen.

Name: A Flower Blossom on the Rice
Description: Located in a quiet alley away from the touristy bustle of Insa-dong, A Flower Blossom on the Rice is a restaurant that caters to the health-conscious diner, serving wholesome home-cooked fare using only certified organic ingredients sourced straight from the farm. The signature dish at this restaurant is the Bojagi Bibimbap — a log of cooked rice topped with five different sautéed vegetables in their multi-colored glory, encased in a crépe-thin egg omelet resembling a gift, tied with a seaweed ribbon and presented with a single flower on top.

Name: Soi Mao
Description: Thai cuisine meets natural wine at this new location of Soi Mao. The word mao is Thai for inebriated, a nod to the restaurant's focus on natural wine. The first floor offers a simplified menu, while the second floor offers a more extensive list of dishes, intended to be enjoyed with wine. Bestsellers include the sweet and spicy grilled pork shoulder, crispy Thai spring rolls and tom yum noodles. The supremely aromatic and pungent nature of Thai cuisine and the flavor carnival of natural wines prove to be surprisingly complementary.

Name: Hadongkwan
Description: This beloved family-owned culinary landmark, located on a busy side street in Myeong-dong, has been serving rustic bowls of beef bone soup since 1939. The version here is served in traditional brass bowls with rice already submerged in the hot soup. The broth is pure and rich with an unmistakable sweetness that can only result from boiling large amounts of beef for a long period of time. This old-fashioned, no-fuss eatery opens early in the morning and closes when its soup vats run dry.

Name: Woo Lae Oak
Description: Lauded as one of the best Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodle restaurants in the city, Woo Lae Oak has been serving consistently stellar food since 1946. The family-operated establishment is tucked away in the back alleys of Euljiro 4-ga, a bustling business hub. The restaurant interior is spacious and spotlessly clean. Indulge in their legendary Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles, served in broth or in a spicy sauce, and their bulgogi, grilled tableside.

Name: Goobok Mandu
Description: Run by a Korean husband and Chinese wife, Goobok Mandu is a no-frills establishment that specializes in Chinese-style dumplings. The couple prepare the dumplings from scratch based on an old family recipe passed down to them by her grandmother. The dumplings are freshly made to order each time. Try the restaurant’s signature pot stickers with their glorious wafer-thin web of crispy golden crust as well as the steamed xiao long bao.

Name: Pildong Myeonok
Description: Located near Namsangol Hanok Village by Chungmuro subway station, this restaurant is a Pil-dong landmark that has been serving Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles for decades. The restaurant’s chilled broth has a delicate beef flavor, its subtlety both loved and disputed among cold buckwheat noodle aficionados. Another highlight of the restaurant is the buttery and tender boiled pork slices, served in thick slices with a dipping sauce. Homemade dumplings are also popular.

Name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
Description: Located along a main road in Sindang-dong, Geumdwaeji Sikdang can be easily spotted by its gold-on-white-tile signage and the queue outside the door long after peak dining hours. The establishment serves up fine cuts of YBD pig, a cross breed between Yorkshire, Berkshire and Duroc. The texture of the pork is firm and meaty, with a good balance of flavorful fat that renders the meat supremely juicy. Items are is cooked on a cast-iron grill over coal briquettes that help keep the temperature constant. The restaurant does not accept reservations.

Name: Yonggeumok
Description: Since 1932, Yonggeumok has been offering piping hot bowls of loach soup, a popular local dish believed to boost energy, especially during the summer months. This restaurant serves two different versions of the hearty and comforting soup: the chunkier Seoul style with whole loach, and the smoother Jeolla province style with ground loach. Everything on the menu as well as the complimentary side dishes are prepared daily by the longtime owner and chef Han Jeong-ja.

Name: Gebangsikdang
Description: Soy sauce-marinated crab and stylish décor don’t always go hand in hand, but at Gebangsikdang, they do. A collaboration between fashion marketer Bang Geon-hyuk and his parents, veterans of the soy sauce marinated crab restaurant business, Gebangsikdang caters to a trend-conscious crowd with its polished interior and its wide selection of raw crab dishes. For those who find it bothersome to eat crab on the shell, there are options that come with just the crab flesh and crab roe on a mound of hot rice.

Name: Buchon Yukhoe
Description: Occupying a corner of the well-established raw beef alley of Gwangjang Market, Buchon Yukhoe has been in business since 1965, originally started as Buchon Sikdang selling short rib soup. The founding matriarch’s original Jeollado Province-style raw beef, seasoned with red chili paste, gave way to the more popular Seoul-style in the 1980s, seasoned with sesame oil and eaten with matchstick pears. Try the raw beef bibimbap for a more substantial meal. Locally sourced beef is delivered to the restaurant each morning.

Name: Okdongsik
Description: With his take on dwaeji-gukbap, Chef Ok Dong-sik has managed to singlehandedly change any preconceptions the local diners previously had about the hearty pork and rice soup dish Koreans hold near and dear to their hearts. Think bacon-thin slices of silky tender pork meat piled on a bed of rice, all submerged in his trademark consommé-like clear broth. The 'extra large' portion comes with double the amount of meat. The space is limited and only 100 bowls of gukbap are sold daily so get here early.

Name: Yukjeon Hoekwan
Description: Three generations spanning five decades have kept this restaurant in business since its opening in 1962. At the time, their iconic crispy thin-sliced bulgogi, grilled over open flames, was all that was offered on the menu. The dish became so popular that the name bassak bulgogi was patented. Today, the restaurant stands four stories high, still serving the same dish that has fed generations. Their coagulated beef blood soup with a clear broth is another stunner.

Name: Jinmi Pyeongyang Naengmyeon
Description: According to owner and chef Yim Se-kwon, long time experience in the kitchens of one of the most iconic Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodle restaurants is the secret to the success of this place. The menu here is what you would expect to see in a typical cold buckwheat noodle restaurant. Other than the noodles, it offers staples such as boiled pork and beef slices, bulgogi, dumplings and Pyeongyang-style beef hot pot.

Name: Yangyang Memil Makguksu
Description: The not-so-secret secret to the longevity and success of Yangyang Memil Makguksu is that its noodles are made with 100% buckwheat and that they are made to order every time. The proprietor of the restaurant began his business many years ago for one reason only - buckwheat noodles were his favorite food. Although the restaurant specializes in the Gangwon-do Province-style cold buckwheat noodles, it also makes a fine bowl of spicy noodles composed with homemade kimchi. The basic spread is simple, but it’s rustic food at its best, made with love.

Name: Sarukame
Description: Sarukame is currently run by its second-generation owner-chef Hiroto Honma. Going beyond merely retaining the title of the restaurant, the current chef is carrying on its culinary legacy by staying in contact with its founder and preserving its original recipes. Such effort, coupled with Chef Honma’s vast experience in the restaurant business and gastronomic sensibility, garnered and developed over the years working in cities around the world, are adding new narrative layers to this establishment. Sarukame continues to create exclusive menus that combine the flavors of trendy ramen in Japan, classic flavors and new original flavors, thereby shaping its brand identity and serving the ever-changing needs of Seoul’s ramen aficionados.

Name: Damtaek
Address: 34 World Cup-ro 8-gil, Mapo-gu, Seoul, 04035, South Korea
Description: Damtaek is a cozy little ramen haven nestled in a quiet alley near Hapjeong Station. Chef Jo Won-hyeon has purposefully adorned this quaint space with vintage artifacts. The restaurant’s shio ramen, and associated variations that use the same soup base, are in stark contrast to its homey, down-to-earth vibe. The refined and clean flavors of the soups are singular and inspire lingering addiction. With a passion for creating tastes unbound by culinary convention, the chef has persistently dedicated his craft toward perfecting the art of shio ramen, creating ramen that can delight any palate.

Name: Loveurth
Address: 32-1 Gwangan-ro 49 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48296, South Korea
Description: Tucked away in a back alley near Gwangan Elementary School, Loveurth is a vegan restaurant that serves vegan versions of familiar foods. From casual dishes to filling, hearty meals, this innovative diner continues to embark on diverse experiments that transcend culinary boundaries. Building upon their experience and insight into vegan food, Co-CEOs Kim Han-sol and Jung Myeong-won transform familiar classics, such as rice bowls, pastas, udon dishes, and soups, into vegan equivalents with a fun and playful twist. Since offering an extensive vegan menu is no easy feat, Loveurth instead tweaks its menu every once in a while so that it can better provide customers with gastronomic pleasure derived from a diverse compendium of vegan cuisine.

Name: Mattdol
Description: Mattdol is a Mexican restaurant run by Chef Lee Chang-yun, who has been steadfastly honing his culinary skills with an exceptional adventurous spirit. He has a particular passion for tortilla. At Mattdol, customers can often see the chef kneading masa to make tortilla, just as he learned in Mexico. Anyone who tries its tostada and taco dishes, featuring his housemade tortilla, will instinctively realize that, compared with common tortilla-based dishes with run-of-the-mill flavors and textures, his creations are on a whole other level. Mattdol is where the chef’s training in diverse culinary styles meets Korean seasonal ingredients. And the result is a unique Mexican cuisine with intuitive flavors that can captivate the palates of gourmets.

Name: PILI PILI
Address: 54 Muhak-ro 33 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48268, South Korea
Description: Take a stroll around Gwangan-dong, and you’ll come across a restaurant whose exterior and interior design will make you ask yourself whether you are in Busan or Thailand. Piri Piri is a Thai-style dining bar that serves Thai cuisine and exotic cocktails. Its hip vibes, music resonating from a turntable, and generous servings of authentic Thai dishes evoke a magical feeling of traveling in that exotic country. So why not come and indulge in the visual feast of the spectacular Poo Pad Phong Curry (stir-fried crab in curry powder) while imbibing a Thai highball?

Name: Yurimmyeon
Description: For over 50 years, this family-run eatery has been serving bowls of noodles to those seeking comforting nourishment. The fresh buckwheat noodles, one of its bestsellers, are made from scratch, daily, using premium salt from Bigeumdo Island in Sinan County, and buckwheat flour from Bongpyeong. Topped with seasoned vegetables, thin strips of egg garnish, and a dollop of sweet and spicy sauce, a bowl of these noodles makes for a satisfying meal. Garak-guksu, wheat noodles in piping hot broth, comes with a generous serving of fishcake.

Name: Mijin
Address: #116-2 le Meilleur Jongno town, 19 Jong-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul, 03157, South Korea
Description: Located in the heart of Gwanghwamun, Mijin has been serving Korean-style cold buckwheat noodles since 1952. The restaurant operates a factory in the basement where the dipping sauce and buckwheat noodles are prepared fresh daily. One portion comes with two stacked tray baskets of noodles, a large kettle of chilled sauce and basic side dishes. Dress your dipping sauce to your desire with grated daikon, light wasabi, crispy seasoned laver and chopped green onions that have already been laid out on the table for you.

Name: Tim Ho Wan
Description: Tim Ho Wan has played a major role in making Hong Kong-style dim sum popular in many countries worldwide. The main force behind such growing popularity has been its policy of maintaining the traditional form of Hong Kong dim sum dishes and making them available at affordable prices. This management philosophy has been upheld in its branches in Seoul, making them as authentic as the original. The franchise’s capacious Samseong outpost, which is also the main location in Seoul, can serve up to 110 customers at one time and offers ample parking spaces. It is the perfect place to indulge in a wide variety of traditional dim sum.

Name: Jin Jin
Address: 60 World Cup buk-ro 1-gil, Mapo-gu, Seoul, 04031, South Korea
Description: For over 40 years, Chef Wang Yuk-sung has been committed to popularizing Chinese cuisine in Korea. Unlike most generic Korean-style Chinese restaurants ubiquitous to Seoul, Chef Wang offers a limited menu of just ten dishes to ensure that the quality of the food he serves is consistently high. Some of the most requested dishes include shrimp toast, stir-fried crab meat with egg white, mapo tofu and stir-fried beef with gai lan.

Name: Menten
Description: Menten is a one-chef ramen restaurant that serves only two dishes: shoyu ramen and tantanmen. Solely responsible for the entire cooking process, the chef has streamlined the menu to concentrate his efforts on quality. Based on their clear broth, the two ramen dishes offer an appealing balance between mild and strong flavors. Each ingredient is precisely prepared and cooked, but the shoyu ramen in particular, delivers a mixture of complexity and umami. As the chef puts it, his ramen dishes are “simple and uncomplicated but aim for perfection." The chef is almost always quietly absorbed in his work, thereby reflecting a sense of responsibility and confidence.

Name: Hapjeongok
Description: Hapjeongok is a restaurant born of nostalgia. As they were reminiscing one day on the father-in-law’s beef bone soup and boiled beef slices, the latter suggested to his daughter-in-law that they should open a beef bone soup restaurant. The establishment stays true to the inspiration — deeply flavorful beef broth, rice rendered soft and sweet in the piping hot soup, tender slices of beef, and a generous serving of boiled offal. The restaurant’s cabbage soybean paste soup is also a must try. Only around 100 portions of soup are served daily, so go early.

Name: Base is nice
Description: Base is Nice is a vegetarian-friendly restaurant. Chef/owner Jang Jin-a had a fairly long career overseas as a restaurant consultant, food stylist, and food & beverage planner. The diner’s natural ambience and well-balanced, vegetable-centered dishes are proud manifestations of her lifelong culinary endeavors. Creations of rice and vegetables, accompanied by soup and side dishes, are refined and tasty. As Jang puts it, the restaurant’s menu is a way to experience everyday food through a natural, veggie-centered diet, and not thanks to a conscious approach to vegetarianism. Reservation required.

Name: Oreno Ramen
Description: Foreign foods are not always embraced by local diners. In fact, authenticity is often shunned by many due to its sheer “foreignness. ” But for chef Shin Dong-woo, years of experience in the ramen business has led him to success, and he did it by introducing the authentic flavors of Japanese ramen to local consumers. The restaurant’s tori paitan ramen, with its rich, velvety-smooth chicken stock, and the shoyu ramen, clean yet deeply flavorful, are good examples of Shin’s ramen know-how. The fresh noodles and stocks are prepared in the kitchen, daily.

Name: Bongsanok
Description: Mandutguk, or Korean dumpling soup, is a dish that is deeply rooted in the day-to-day lives of Koreans. Owner Yoon Young-sook became acquainted with Hwanghaedo-style dumpling soup through her mother-in-law, a native of Sariwon, which is north of the border. To emulate the pure taste of the original dumpling filling, Yoon says she follows her recipe to the tee and feels very proud when she hears customers say her dumplings remind them of their own grandmother's.

Name: Mapo Ok
Description: In the realm of Korean comfort food, there is little else more quintessential than seolleongtang — a hearty bowl of soup made by boiling ox bones and beef for hours until the broth turns almost milky white. Mapo Ok, which opened its doors in 1949, makes its signature dish by boiling brisket and ox bones until slightly opaque. The ox bone soup is served with thick slices of tender brisket and rice already mixed into the piping hot broth. Ask for a side of kimchi juice to season your soup for that extra dimension of flavor.

Name: Hwanggeum Kongbat
Description: Tucked away in Ahyeon-dong, this hidden gem specializes in rustic homemade bean curd. The unctuously creamy bean curd is made from scratch, daily, at the crack of dawn. The secret to the elevated nuttiness of local soybeans that shine through in Hwanggeum Kongbat’s bean curd is the extra thick soymilk and reduced levels of the coagulant. With a desire to share healthy food with other people, the proprietor also makes and sells homemade rich soybean paste stew and unrefined rice wine.

Name: Kyoyang Siksa
Description: Sapporo-style lamb barbecue is the name of the game at Kyoyang Siksa, which specializes in tender young lamb less than 10 months old. Flown in from Australia, this meat is juicy and tender and the menu offers three cuts: French rack, ribs, and loin steak. These may be grilled tableside by the staff. Other solid dishes include soup curry with grilled vegetables and aromatic garlic rice served with small sheets of laver to wrap it in. Seating is limited, so be sure to book ahead.

Name: Nampo Myeonok
Description: Tucked away in a small alley among densely populated office buildings that sees a constant stream of foot traffic, the main building of this long-standing institution recently underwent a major facelift. A longtime favorite among patrons of all ages for its authentic Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles and beef hot pot, Nampo Myeonok continues to charm with its consistently good food and friendly service. Chair seating and floor seating are both available.

Name: Manjok Ohyang Jokbal
Description: At Manjok Oyhang Jokbal, the beloved Korean braised pig's feet dish is impeccably crafted with the utmost dedication and care to hygiene and quality. The restaurant, armed with a systematic central distribution system, offers consistent quality at all of its franchised locations. Here, the popular pork dish can be enjoyed warm until the very last piece, thanks to the specially designed hotplates installed into the tables.

Name: Daesungjip
Description: For a soul-satisfying bowl of ox knee soup, look no further than Daesungjip. Its reputation for quality and consistency has seen generations of loyal patrons come for the rich, hearty signature so thick with ox knee cartilage that you can stand a spoon up in it. Take a bite of the slow-cooked cartilage doused in the special soy dipping sauce and all is right in the world. A long queue is the norm here but, thankfully, takeaways are also possible.

Name: Gaeseong Mandu Koong
Description: Established in 1970 by an elderly Gaeseong native, this restaurant has been serving Gaeseong-style dumplings for three generations. The dumplings here are large, plump and filled with a generous amount of shredded napa cabbage and mung bean sprouts. The soup broth is made with beef brisket, and the owners prepare the dumplings by hand daily with the freshest ingredients. The traditional Korean hanok setting is both charming and elegant.

Name: Subaru
Description: Chef Kang Yeong-cheol has for long studied and developed the soba-making craft, with the sole aspiration to serve the same outstanding soba as can be tasted in the birthplace of the dish, The chef spent many years in Japan, where he became enamored with the pure taste of soba; and it is this love that propelled him on his culinary journey. In Subaru, soba for the day’s meals are freshly made in the traditional way. He sticks to the classic ni-hachi-style version, which consists of two parts wheat and eight parts buckwheat. The signature dishes include zaru soba, which boasts a clean and pure taste; soba with umami-rich duck meat and green onion; as well as soba with perilla oil.

Name: Myeongdong Kyoja
Description: Myeongdong Kyoja is a family-owned place in operation since 1966. The restaurant, which offers only four items on the menu, specializes in dumplings and noodle soup. An impressive number of patrons flock here daily, largely because all the dishes, including its signature garlic-laden kimchi, are made in-house. Simple décor and service come with hefty portions at affordable prices. It has a sister operation in the same area of Myeong-dong.

Name: Mandujip
Description: Located in a trendsetting part of the city dominated by state-of-the-art fashion, this restaurant has stood its ground for 30 years with a humble dish that has wooed the palates of countless people — dumpling soup. Mandujip specializes in Pyeongando-style dumplings, filled with minced beef, bean curd, mung bean sprouts, green onions and sesame oil. Each order comes with six large dumplings in a clear, flavorful beef broth made with chunks of brisket.

Name: Hwangsaengga Kalguksu
Description: No matter what time of day, always expect to see a line outside this beloved establishment, known for their humble noodle soup and dumplings. Originally called Bukchon Kalguksu when it opened in 2001, it changed its name in 2014, but that hasn’t stopped the regulars from coming time and again for its freshly made dumplings and silky-soft noodles served in a rich ox bone broth. Boiled beef slices and noodles in cold soybean soup are also popular.

Name: Samcheongdong Sujebi
Description: This local haunt has been an integral part of Samcheong-dong’s history since 1982. The signature dish here is sujebi — rustic hand-pulled dough soup served in a savory anchovy broth. The restaurant is also known for its potato pancakes, made with grated potatoes that are pan-fried until crispy on the outside and pleasantly chewy on the inside. Avoid the lunch rush if you don’t want to stand in line, but be warned — the restaurant is always busy.

Name: Halmaejip
Description: The original matriarch who opened this restaurant is still the heart and soul of the kitchen which has been dishing up legendary pork backbone stew and boiled pig’s feet since 1975. Chili powder is the only spicy agent used to add the pleasant kick to the taste. It’s a common sight to see Mrs. Mun, walking around showing her patrons how to eat her food “the right way. ”

Name: Bao Haus
Address: 2F, 62-9 Seojeon-ro 38 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47294, South Korea
Description: When Chef Choi Haeng-rak opened Bao Haus here in his hometown of Busan, his extensive overseas training at last found a place to flourish. His restaurant offers simple and casual Taiwanese-style dishes. By lowering the threshold for fine cuisine, the chef ushers diners into the familiar yet exotic world of the different variations of Chinese cuisine. The menu features dishes loaded with inherent flavors and executed with Chef Choi’s novel twists, including bao (Taiwanese steamed buns), lu rou fan (Taiwanese braised pork rice bowl), mapo tofu, and deep-fried eggplant. Since the eatery is housed in a compact space, the wait can be long without a reservation.

Name: Hapcheon Gukbapjip
Description: Dwaeji-gukbap (pork and rice soup), the representative culinary delight of Busan, has continued to evolve with changing times and dietary trends. Amid this evolution, the variant served at Hapcheon Gukbapjip has long adhered to the original recipe, delighting customers with its time-tested flavors. Here, pork is repeatedly covered with broth and drained right before it is included in the soup and served. This technique eliminates unpleasant zests while enhancing the meat’s rich flavor. The clear broth, on the other hand, is brimming with umami and clean flavors; they will be etched in your memory and reverberate every now and then. Another signature item, boiled pork slices, is often unavailable due to limited daily portions, so arrive early. Solo diners are advised to avoid peak lunch hours from 11 am to 1 pm.

Name: Jungin Myeonok
Description: When a restaurant continues to attract large crowds of hungry diners, then it is doing something right. The proprietor of Jungin Myeonok has had just one goal since day one — to continue the legacy of his parents for as long as he can, using only the best ingredients. The establishment’s legendary Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles are based on a tightly guarded family recipe handed down to him by his parents, who both hail from North Korea. The room gets packed quickly during lunch service, especially during the warmer months.

Name: Shunsai Kubo
Address: 17 Yangdal-ro 4 beon-gil, Buk-gu, Busan, 46517, South Korea
Description: Shunsai Kubo is a hitsumabushi (Nagoya-style grilled eel) restaurant helmed by Chef Lee Jae-wook. Trained in Japan, the chef is continually striving to raise the bar on the flavor and quality of his signature dish made only with live Japanese eels (Anguilla japonica). The rich aroma of the eels, rubbed with a special sauce and carefully grilled, creates a delightful gastronomic harmony with the rice cooked to just the right texture. The restaurant serves a hitsumabushi menu for children, a considerate gesture that caters to families. Shunsai Kubo also offers authentic light bar snacks for long-time regulars with fond memories of its former Japanese kappo cuisine.

Name: Buda Myeonoak
Description: For those familiar with Buda Milmyeon in Banyeo-dong, the name Buda Myeonoak may ring a bell. Relocated to the present location near Haeundae Beach in 2021, this noodle haven offers Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles made out of 100% buckwheat flour. Unexpectedly resilient, the pure noodles reveal additional nutty flavor with each bite. The broth, made from Korean beef and mixed with vegetable broth, is earthy and mild yet full of umami. When topped with your choice of garnishes that are served separately, such as sweet and sour radish, winter cabbage, and cucumber, the noodles are sensationally addictive.

Name: Tasty Cube
Description: A combination of Chinese characters for heart, meat, noodles and restaurant make up the four-syllable name Jeongyukmyeonche. The cozy space, which only offers bar seating facing the open kitchen, is the brainchild of a group of friends who wanted to launch an eatery that focuses on a wide array of noodle dishes. Although Chinese and Southeast Asian flavors dominate the menu at present, the owners say the plan is to eventually introduce noodle dishes from other cultures as well. Signature dishes include beef noodle soup and noodles dressed with zhi ma jiang, a savory paste made with crushed sesame seeds.

Name: Kyewol Gomtang
Description: Kyewol Gomtang in Seongsu-dong specializes in Korean chicken soup or gomtang, as the name of the eatery plainly suggests, with the menu consisting of a mere three chicken-based offerings. Warm rice, chicken breast slices tenderly cooked at low temperatures, winter cabbage blanched to crunchy perfection, and clear broth skimmed of fat – all culminate in clean yet rich flavors in the soup. For lunch, spicy seasoned chicken with laver chips; and boiled chicken, which is then marinated with soybean paste and torch-grilled, are available as wallet-friendly side orders. The joint’s cold noodle soup, a summer special, is another not-to-be-missed treat.

Name: Niroumianguan
Description: Niroumianguan features a memorable juxtaposition of clean white and vibrant rust colors in its décor. Chinese beef noodle soup, a popular delicacy across the Greater China region, is commonly known to have originated from Taiwan, but its real origin is Lanzhou in mainland China. As the chef learned the recipe from a noodle joint in China’s Shandong Province, his restaurant serves up fare that is slightly different from the classic Taiwanese style. Add plenty of cilantro to the mildly sweet broth, complete with a clean yet rich taste; or a dab of chili sauce to give your dish deeper flavor.

Name: One Degree North
Description: As suggested by its name, which denotes Singapore’s geographical coordinate (one degree north in latitude), this establishment is dedicated to popular Singaporean dishes and Asian barbeque specialties.
