Description: Singaporean chef, Ah Ho, cooks locally raised chickens using his family’s recipes. The chicken has a succulent meat, thin skin, light soya and sesame sauce, chicken broth and aromatic rice. The chicken offal sells out early every day. Don’t be surprised if the queue takes 1-2 hours.

Name: Ton Mayom
Address: 23/1 Mu 6, Thep Krasattri Road, Ratsada, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: The Mayom (star gooseberry) is a local tree located at the front of this outlet that offers a shady setting. They serve fried local fish with an aromatic curry and Southern Thai sour curry soup with seabass and young coconut shoots. The signatures are delicious and a must-try.

Name: Jun Hom
Address: 8/3 Mu 5, Mae Nam, Ko Samui, 84330, Thailand
Description: This unpretentious, open-air eatery is a local gem on the island, offering an affordable opportunity to taste simple, local dishes in a knockout beach location. The portions are hearty, modestly priced and lip-smacking, as the salty, crispy appetiser of deep-fried local silver sillago illustrates. The stir-fried squid is tender and beautifully cooked in a sweet, flavourful sauce and steeped in a lemongrass aroma. Alfresco dining on a blissful beach location.

Name: Charmgang
Address: 14, Soi Charoenkrung 35 (Nakhon Kasem 5), Talat Noi, Samphanthawong, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: A young crowd sips on cocktails in this trendy hangout, where the décor and lighting render a ruddy hue. The smart menu uses local ingredients to create interesting new textures while preserving Thai authenticity. The barbeque smoked pork with young mango salad is a tasty creation; the crunchy, sour fruit hitting it off with crispy shallots and cha-muang leaves. The seared scallop on crispy coconut milk cupcake has a moist texture with crisp snow peas.

Name: Sum Gradang Nga
Address: 31/57-59 Soi Donnok 8/1, Donnok Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Set in a charming house surrounded by ylang-ylang plants, Sum Gradang Nga is a hit with the locals for its Southern Thai cuisine bursting with gutsy flavours. Take the spicy pork cartilage with piquant seasoning, for example. Alternatively, the crab curry, which exudes umami, is served with vermicelli, fresh vegetables and a sweet-sour cucumber salad. Two dining areas: an alfresco space shaded by trees and a cool interior with a pastel pink décor.

Name: Kin Kub Koi
Address: 83/3 Phuttha Monthon Sai 2 Road, Sala Thammasop, Thawi Watthana, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: The chef-owner here knows seafood. Not only does her family run a wholesale seafood business, but she also ran the previous incarnation of this place in Samut Sakhon for years before moving it here. The results are skilfully cooked dishes made from choice seafood, like standouts grilled river prawns and stir-fried crab with bitter beans and shrimp paste. Two dining zones (with and without AC) are available; both face a leafy courtyard.

Name: Magnolia Café
Address: 131/70, 131/82 Rattanakosin Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 503200, Thailand
Description: With just four large communal tables, Magnolia is a simple, cosy spot enlivened by bold colours, vintage décor, and chandeliers. Their à la carte menu offers tasty, well presented fare from across Thailand. Dishes are distinguished by vivid, gutsy flavours; fried sun-dried squid with peanut sauce and fresh watermelon with desiccated salmon are exemplars. In lieu of a dessert menu, they serve lovely complimentary pandan pudding. Do visit their wine shop next door.

Name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
Address: 116 Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road, Bang Si Thong, Bang Kruai, Nonthaburi, 11130, Thailand
Description: Every day, in a small alley in Nonthaburi, a long queue forms for the deep-fried battered banana with its crispy golden-brown texture. A special machine removes the excess oil to ensure the crispy finish. Other treats include taro and potato, and a deep-fried potato dough ball.

Name: Hong Khao Tom Pla
Address: 5 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Named after its signature fish porridge, this feels like something between a snack bar and restaurant. The owner is the only chef. The delectable wok-fried crab uses a curry powder that absorbs nicely into the fresh, sweet meat. They use local ingredients and produce well-balanced flavours.

Name: Somsak Pu Ob (Charoen Rat)
Address: Soi Charoen Rat 1, Khlong San, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
Description: This cart serves some of the best steamed crabs or prawns on glass noodles at wallet-friendly prices. Make sure you stir the noodles to soak up the tasty juices. It has a few branches, but this is where it all started. Come early or the wait will be long.

Name: Choy (Phuttha Monthon Sai 2)
Address: 9/19 Phuttha Monthon Sai 2 Road, Bang Khae Nuea, Bang Khae, Bangkok, 10160, Thailand
Description: A little out of the way but this is one of the best kept secrets for roast duck with egg noodles. Try the signature duck noodles with shrimp wonton in Tom Yam soup. Choy is named after the owner; the duck recipe came from his father.

Name: Por. Pochaya
Address: 654-656 Wisut Kasat Road, Ban Phan Thom, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: For over half a century, unwavering quality and rare dishes have kept loyal fans visiting this traditional Thai-Chinese spot, which is now run by the third generation of the same family. Among the top-sellers are crab omelette and stir-fried beef with cumin leaves. Crowds are to be expected, so make sure you book to avoid disappointment. It’s closed on weekends and holidays.

Name: Takola
Address: Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas, 79 Mu 3, Khuekkhak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82220, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in lush gardens by Khuekkhak beach, Takola is named after the Takua Pa city’s former title when it was a major spice trading port. Their ancient and original cooking methods produce intense traditional and southern Thai flavours. The fried fish fillet is a large seabass topped with a tamarind-based, sweet and sour sauce that works wonderfully with the freshness of the fish and the basil’s fragrance. The Thai crab dip with crab meat also gets the nod.

Name: Burapa
Address: 26 Soi Sukhumvit 11, Khlong Toei Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: This Orient Express-themed restaurant aims to take diners on a journey from east to north-east Thailand via flavoursome cooking that joins culinary elements from Isan and the province of Trat. The ground floor is designed to look like a luxury train bar – perfect for enjoying one of their many signature cocktails –  then the 1st and 2nd floors resemble the business and first-class carriages respectively. The well-priced dishes use recipes from the owner’s mother. Booking is essential.

Name: 100 Mahaseth
Address: 100 Mahaseth Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: This nose-to-tail inspired offal restaurant serves elevated Isan fare made from quality ingredients sourced from local Thai farmers. The chef puts great care into balancing flavours and presenting attractive plates – and this is evident with dishes like the aged beef tongue and the fried offal chips. Guests are served in a dining room that matches the rustic with the industrial; a dry-aging meat cabinet adds a modern touch. Don’t forget to check the blackboard for aged steak specials.

Name: Jao Nai Fish Ball (Bang Khae Road)
Address: 103/14 Bang Khae Road, Bang Khae, Bangkok, 10160, Thailand
Description: Nestled in a vintage townhouse, this popular street food joint serves up savory fish ball noodle soup. Expect fresh, made-to-order meals that might require a wait due to the frequent bustle. However, the wait pays off with homemade seafood like fish balls, fish dumplings, and fish cakes, all enhancing the soup's umami taste.

Name: Baan Landai
Address: 252/13-14 Phra Pok Klao Road, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Don’t let the slightly unkempt exterior keep you from visiting Chef Landai’s eponymous restaurant, where he practises the craft he learned from his mother. The interior exudes charm with its eclectic adornments and window to the kitchen where chefs whip up pan-Thai dishes like flavourful pork ribs with red wine sauce (plus several veggie offerings). Pair with flower tea, mocktails, or cocktails, and finish with mung bean marzipan and egg yolk in coconut milk.

Name: Aunt Aoy Kitchen
Address: 377 2 Chiang Rai Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: The décor is simple, with a display of photos and messages on post-it notes from customers gone by. Aunt Aoy spent much of her career cooking in hotel kitchens. Her expertise is realised in the fluffy yet crispy Chef Omelette with stir-fried minced pork, salted egg and pork crackling.

Name: Praprai
Address: 345/1-2 Airport Road, Ban Pet, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Arrivals and departures are better with a stopover at this simple restaurant in front of Khon Kaen Airport. For more than two decades, Prapai’s friendly owners have been serving authentic Isan dishes made with fresh local ingredients that change with the season. To experience traditional Isan cooking, try deep-fried sour fish or the off-menu Somtum in fermented fish sauce with salted crab.

Name: Jok Guay Jab Tom Sen Bat Queue
Address: 123/20 Namueang Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: This eatery has been serving rice porridge, Vietnamese noodles with pork rib soup, and glass noodles with chicken feet for 30 years. Try adding chả lụa ham and soft-boiled egg for extra indulgence. Eat in to avoid the takeaway queue.

Name: So Jeng
Address: 599/3-4 Mu 2 Chaeng Sanit Road, Nai Mueang, Ban Phai, Khon Kaen, 40110, Thailand
Description: After starting several unsuccessful businesses, the owners of this Isan-style beef place gave it one last shot and named it So Jeng, or “surrender to failing” – it was a surprise hit and 40 years later, locals still frequent it for delicious budget-friendly meals and cheerful service. The no-frills shophouse setting naturally puts the spotlight on the food here, with the grilled beef sausage and the spicy clear soup with beef and beef offal shining brightest.

Name: Kaeng Pa (Loong Sa-Nga)
Address: 285/162-3 Soi Ngam Wong Wan 23 Lane 11, Bang Khen,  Mueang Nonthaburi, Nonthaburi, 11000, Thailand
Description: Run by the same family for over 20 years, this restaurant is something of a hidden gem for spice-lovers. Their signature dish, jungle curry soup with hand-minced fish, provides suitably lip-smacking flavours using ingredients like red chilli, fingerroot and turkey berry. An outdoor area embraces nature, with curved tree trunk tables and an arboretum. Herbs and spices from the forest are used as seasoning, often with game meats – the succulent stir-fried deer with cumin leaves is a must.

Name: Elvis Suki (Soi Yotse)
Address: 200/37 Soi Yotse, Phlapphla Chai Road, Wat Thep Sirin, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: The king reigns supreme. Elvis Suki rules over local competition having dished up the same delicious recipes for 30 years. Seafood, beef or pork sukiyaki come in a secret eggy sauce with a smoky aroma. The grilled scallops, squid and cockles with spicy sauce are also delectable.

Name: Salaloy
Address: 52/2 Wiset Road, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: The focus of this casual Rawai Beach eatery is on fresh, expertly cooked seafood. Among the highlights are shrimp paste dip served with vegetables, and soft-boiled wing shells and deep-fried Sillago fish with turmeric powder – dishes to inspire diners to return and explore the rest of the menu. The outdoor eating area, opposite the main dining room, is a well-shaded and relaxing spot to enjoy a meal. Be early or some seafood ingredients may run out.

Name: Khanom Bueang Wan Phueng Noi (Chok Chai 4)
Address: 134 Chok Chai 4, Soi 54 Yaek 5, Lat Phrao, Bangkok, 10230, Thailand
Description: This shop is entirely devoted to the delicious dessert known as Khanom Bueang. These crepes are crispy and topped with just the right ratio of aromatic coconut cream, sweet egg floss, and young coconut slices. Be sure to arrive near opening time to avoid a wait.

Name: Bunloet
Address: 360 Soi Nakhon Sawan 8, Nakhon Sawan Road, Wat Sommanat, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: This enduring street food stall is renowned for its egg noodles with grilled pork, prepared using an unchanged recipe for over 40 years. The secret lies in marinating pork rump slices for four hours in a mix of soy sauce, sugar, salt, and pepper before grilling over charcoal. The well-cooked noodles have a soft, sticky texture, served in a flavourful pork bone broth.

Name: Pa Lek Boat Noodles
Address: Bang Lan Road (opposite to Maha That temple), Tha Wasukri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This third-generation family-run street food joint has been offering tasty boat noodles for over five decades. Their experience shines through in the delicious broth, well-balanced in flavours. Try their pork or beef boat noodles for great value, or consider the recommended dry tom yum-style egg noodles with pork. The friendly owners' hospitality attracts a bustling lunch crowd.

Name: Krua Apsorn (Sam Sen)
Address: 503 Sam Sen Road, Wachira Payaban, Dusit, Bangkok, 10300, Thailand
Description: This family-run stall is inevitably a hit with anyone who eats here, including patrons such as the Thai royal family. The simplicity of the exterior belies the gem of a Thai kitchen hidden inside. Some dishes are unique and feature the family's secret recipes. The stir-fried pork with bird's-eye chilli is tender and bursting with herbal aromas. The signature yellow curry with large prawns and crispy lotus root strikes the perfect blend of sour, spicy and sweet.

Name: Jidori Cuisine Ken
Address: 10/12 Soi Sukhumvit 26, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Jidori roughly translates as ‘premium chicken’. In a friendly, welcoming atmosphere, the signature chicken skewer menu is available in 5, 8 or 10 courses. The chef masterfully uses a range of chicken parts to conjure up different flavours and textures and adds salt throughout the process which enhances the underlying smoky complexity. Save room for the homemade Japanese Ken custard – a decadent caramel dessert that manages to avoid the cloyingly sweet trap.

Name: A Pong Mae Sunee
Address: 99 Soi Soon Uthit, Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: For over five years, Sunee’s street food stall has been renowned for its Khanom A Pong—delicious coconut crepes. Cooked in mini woks over charcoal, the crepes are unique for their light, crispy shell and soft centre—a perfect balance of sweetness and creamy coconut. Be sure to arrive early at this beloved stall to experience these irresistible snacks.

Name: Pa Pu Boat Noodles
Address: 1/36 Mu 5 Chao Chet, Sena, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13110, Thailand
Description: Octogenarian Pa Pu is the talent behind the recipes in this simple shop next to the local rice field. The signature boat noodles with shredded chicken or pork and soft eggs are a delicacy. There’s no need to add any condiments; Pa Pu produces the perfect blend of flavours every time.

Name: Som Tum Jinda
Address: 63/1 Phichitrangsan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Chef-owner Jinda is a specialist in somtum dishes. She first plied her trade back in 1974 in the local university before moving downtown. The Isan-style spicy fish maw with bamboo shoot salad has a nice balance of herbs and its powerful aroma is punctuated by the intensity of the Tiliacora juice. The signature, somtum with crispy catfish, dispenses an impressive tang. Somtum Jinda is also famous over the border in Lao where they have another branch.

Name: Dan Chicken Rice (San Sai)
Address: 45 Mu 3, Old San Sai Road, San Sai Noi, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
Description: For over 20 years this local favourite has been serving tasty, wallet-friendly chicken rice, first in Sam-Yaek Market in San Sai and now at this larger branch on Old San Sai Road. Show up early, both to beat the crowds and because the food invariably runs out before closing time.

Name: Here Joi Beef Noodle
Address: 127 Mu 20,  Kasikon Thung Sang Road, Sila, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Open for almost 4 decades, the shop is named after the owner's father, Joi, who created the menu. The beef noodle soup has juicy slices, tender beef balls and offal. The aromatic soup broth is slow-cooked daily with beef bones. The smoky beef satay skewers are chargrilled and juicy.

Name: Krua Boonlert Bangpu
Address: 251 Sukhumvit Road, Thai Ban Mai, Mueang Samut Prakan, Samut Prakan, 10280, Thailand
Description: This canal-side restaurant offers various dining spaces, including a wedding-ready dining room, high-ceilinged pavilion, and a large terrace. It predominantly serves central Thai cuisine, complemented by Thai-Chinese and Isan dishes. Quality ingredients are showcased in dishes like fried shrimp with tamarind sauce and Chinese-banquet favourites such as stewed duck with brown gravy. Live music adds to the evening ambiance.

Name: Nina's Cafe & Restaurant
Address: 59/1 Mu 6, Thanaratch Road, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30450, Thailand
Description: Nina’s homely restaurant, surrounded by greenery, has two dining areas. The inside is decorated with vintage furniture, chandeliers, standing lamps and a classic clock, while diners in the garden can enjoy nature’s shade. The dishes are well seasoned and many of the vegetables and herbs Nina uses, such as betel leaves, coriander and basil, are grown on-site. The fried pumpkin coated with salted egg sauce and the deep-fried sea bass with chilli and salt are both divine.

Name: Pae Araya
Address: Rim Khong Road, Khong Chiam, Ubon Ratchathani, 34220, Thailand
Description: Where the Mekong and Mun Rivers meet, this floating restaurant, whose name means ‘noble raft,’ serves central Thai and Isan fare featuring fish from both rivers. The Tom Yum redtail catfish and local roe served with herbs are both flavourful and recommended. They and everything else on the menu come with cooling river breezes and gentle undulations from passing boats. Arrive early for dinner to catch sunset views over the river and the Laotian landscape beyond.

Name: Watsana Khao Man Gai
Address: 9/275 Phuttha Bucha Road, Bang Mot, Chom Thong, Bangkok, 10150, Thailand
Description: Despite several moves from its original location, this shophouse has kept its customers so expect queues for its famous chicken rice and the recent addition of noodles. Quality ingredients and consistent cooking are the secret of its success.

Name: Ta Tuay
Address: 57/10 Mu 5,  Soi Ruam Chai 1, Mai Khao, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Sarasin Bridge is the link between Phuket and the mainland. Set in a friendly community at the foot of the bridge, Ta Tuay has a tropical garden with water features. The menu is popular for their seafood and southern Thai expertise. When the deep-sea cockles and sand worms are the catch of the day, put them at the top of your wanted list . The signature spicy grape seaweed salad offers lots of umami and crunchy textures enriched by a tangy dressing.

Name: Baan Yai Phad Thai
Address: 108 Soi Inthamara 47, Din Daeng, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
Description: This is one of the best places for Phad Thai – piping hot noodles cooked to perfection, boldly flavoured and with a distinctive smokiness from the charcoal stove. Expect to wait in line. Come with a local since you have to write in Thai to make an order.

Name: Somtum Khun Kan
Address: 6 Soi Wachira Thammasatit 23, Sukhumvit 101/1, Bang Chak, Phra Khanong, Bangkok, 10260, Thailand
Description: Starting from a small shop in Mueang Thong Thani, and then winning a Som Tam (spicy papaya salad) competition in 1999, Khun Kan has earned his reputation through high quality dishes and great flavours. As well as the famous Som Tam, the menu offers a wide variety of mostly Isan dishes along with a few from other areas of Thailand. Try the juicy grilled pork shoulder with honey and herbs, followed by their signature sweet sticky rice with mango for dessert. Live music adds to the atmosphere on Friday-Sunday evenings.

Name: Chakki
Address: 1/35 Soi Watthana Yothin, Rang Nam Road, Thung Phaya Thai, Ratchathewi, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
Description: This family-run Cantonese shop has been on Rang Nam Road for 30 years. Chakki’s owner doesn’t believe in menus – everyone is here for their famous deep-fried wontons or deep-fried rice noodles and beef topped with gravy. Once these dishes sell out, the shop closes for the day.

Name: Naam Yoi
Address: 63/250 Ruam Phattana Road, Ratsada, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Going from steam-table hole-in-the-wall to a small cook-to-order eatery to a casual, tree-lined, open-air restaurant, Naam Yoi has cemented its identity as a solid family restaurant with a canon of tried-and-true dishes. Ingredients are obtained daily from local markets by the auntie of the family who is the head chef. Homestyle classics like river snail curry, spicy stir-fry of split gill mushrooms, and braised pork rule the roost here.

Name: Rung Rueang Pork Noodle
Address: 10/3 Soi Sukhumvit 26, Khlong Tan, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Depending on your appetite, choose between a small or large portion of clear minced pork soup and perfectly flavoured tom yum broth. Each steaming bowl is topped with homemade fish balls and, if you so fancy, crispy fish skin. The minced pork balls are also a highlight.

Name: Pathongko Mae Pranee
Address: 57 Wirat Hong Yok 3 Road, Wichit, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Customers with a sweet tooth and fans of deep-fried goodness line up here from 6am to get their daily fix. The deep-fried Patongko (dough sticks) and salapao are freshly prepared; the crunchy fries are golden-brown. It’s all very tasty; even without the dipping sauces.

Name: Flourish
Address: GF,  Sindhorn Kempinski Hotel Bangkok, 80 Soi Tonson, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: The spacious yet homely Flourish is the elegantly decorated sister restaurant of Saneh Jaan, located inside the Sindhorn Kempinski hotel. The open kitchen runs the length of one wall so guests can watch a hearty menu being lovingly prepared as if by their own grandmother. Quality ingredients power traditional dishes, with the ‘Nuea Aroi’ Wagyu beef curry a highlight. The rich, thick sauce is well-balanced, while the meat is tender and the addition of bergamot brings a lovely aroma.

Name: Krua Praya Phuket
Address: 216/19 Mu 3, Soi Hua Tha, Si Sunthon, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Krua Praya showcases Southern Thai, especially Phuket, cuisine. Its traditional décor and captivating rooftop charm visitors. The menu features skilfully prepared dishes with bold flavours and enticing aromas. The standout pork belly dishes include the signature fried pork belly with curry paste and young coconut shoots, delivering a crispy, spicy delight. Alternatively, the Phuket-style stew offers a rich non-spicy option, served in a satisfying gravy.

Name: Sam Chong Seafood
Address: 39/1 Mu 9, Phet Kasem Road, Kalai, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82130, Thailand
Description: The restaurant is located on two large rafts near the mouth of Bang Lam river. Most of the customers are locals who appreciate the laid-back atmosphere and panoramic views of the estuary, mangrove forest and fishing villages. The seafood menu is composed from the fresh daily catch. We strongly recommend the signature fried sea bass with two sauces; its crispy, golden-brown exterior beautifully melts in the mouth with the tender and juicy meat of the fish.

Name: VT Namnueng (Posri Road)
Address: 345/1-3 Posri Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: This well-known Vietnamese restaurant is particularly favoured among families who relish the owners’ renditions of long-time favourites within its spacious and inviting two-storey dining area. Their signature grilled pork sausage is available in three sizes and accompanied by various condiments. Additionally, the pork sausage wraps—consisting of sausage and omelette bites wrapped in fresh greens with sweet and sour sauce—are highly recommended.

Name: Samuay & Sons
Address: 103/8 Si Chomchuen Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: After studying and working in San Francisco, brothers Num and Joe returned to Thailand to open a fine dining restaurant not in Bangkok, but in Udon Thani. Samuay & Sons serves a contemporary Isan tasting menu and great value à la carte dishes in a loft-style space. For the full experience, try the excellent seasonal tasting menu, which not only balances flavours but is also nutritionally balanced.

Name: Pranom Shredded Chicken Noodles (Wat Phanom Yong)
Address: 47/9 Commercial building in front of Wat Phanom Yong, Mu 4, Tha Wasukri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayuthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: On Ayutthaya-Ang Thong Road, near Wat Phanom Yong, the shredded chicken noodle soup needs no extra seasoning. The tom yum broth is perfectly balanced; chicken is tender, while slow-cooked chicken feet are an option. Available for breakfast and lunch only.

Name: Krua Kao Kuk
Address: 47/4 Phatthana Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Somboon Saesor, lecturer at Phuket’s Peranakan Association and a first-generation Peranakan, turned her small roadside food stall into a restaurant in 1995. Nowadays, the matriarch’s granddaughter, Ratanavalee Saeton, is at the helm to continue the family’s legacy. Notable dishes among the homely offerings include lemongrass soup with sweet clams, dry stir-fried minced pork with holy basil, and fried kingfish with soy sauce.

Name: Baan Pee Lek
Address: 39 Chaloem Phrakiat Ratchakan Thi 9 Soi 9, Nong Bon, Prawet, Bangkok, 10250, Thailand
Description: Step inside this Northern and Central Thai restaurant hidden on a side street in Prawet District and you enter a charming dining room adorned with an old-fashioned wooden European decor. Opening the menu reveals dishes, many of which are unavailable elsewhere, that honour the owners’ birthplaces, Chiang Mai and Bangkok. Highlights include stir-fried beef with Massaman curry, yum Luang Prabang and fried minced pork with salted mackerel.

Name: Tang Jai Yang (Bang Kho Laem)
Address: 171 Chan Road, Wat Phraya Krai, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Tang Jai Yang’s chef started cooking char siu, or Cantonese-style barbecue pork, for family and friends before selling it online. There, it went viral, so he opened this understated place. Since almost every dish on the menu contains the succulent pork, you can’t really go wrong.

Name: Kai Yang Saeng Thai
Address: 126 Ratchadamnoen Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: At this rotisserie stall, they have spent over 50 years perfecting their signature dish of chicken (farmed or domestic) marinated in a secret peppery, herbal blend before it hits the spit. Juicy and tender, with a thin skin, the meat comes served with a sweet chilli dipping sauce.

Name: Baan Pang Hom
Address: 185 Mittraphap Road, Ban Mai, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: Named after the owner's mother, Ban Pang Hom has served Thai dishes with intense flavours for two decades. The open-air structure, wooden interior and greenery give it a rustic feel. Choose the snakehead or seabass and they’ll cook your fish in two halves. We recommend the deep-fried seabass with crunchy roasted peanuts. With half spicy sauce and half miang kam sauce, enjoy fiery Thai sensations before cooling off with a refreshing herbal Isan taste.

Name: Mok
Address: 115 Phrommarat Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Stepping into this two-storey house feels like visiting a friend's welcoming home, with a snug dining room and a plant-filled terrace. Adapted from grandma's Thai and Isan recipes, they offer a variety of menus suited for modern tastes. Don't miss the herb-infused seabass with fermented fish sauce and the unique fermented fish paired with pineapple relish and fresh veggies.

Name: Joong Borikan
Address: 85 Prasoet Som Road, Sena, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13110, Thailand
Description: There’s a reason why this unpretentious-looking restaurant has been highly regarded among Thailand’s food connoisseurs for over eight decades: it serves appetising local river prawns and fish cooked using old-school techniques. Among their best dishes are fried river prawns with salt and spicy grilled river prawn salad, thanks to the impressive flavours, textures and aromas. A history-filled conversation with the owner is equally delightful.

Name: Madam Pahtehh (Tumruat Road)
Address: 34/1-3 Tumruat Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: Madame Patehh, a fusion of 'Madame' and 'Pâté', features a signature homemade sandwich with Pâté. Chef-owner Madame Mui, with her food knowledge drawn from her life in Thailand and Laos, established this unique eatery in 2005. The menu, merging Vietnamese, Thai, Laos, French, and Chinese cuisines, showcases delicious and well-balanced dishes. The spot is a local favorite for breakfast and lunch. Dishes like Pho with beef and Mae Khong steak are also notable.

Name: Roti Sai Mai Mae Pom (Mother's Branch)
Address: 51/1 Mu 2, U Thong Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Opened in 1985, this wooden street food venue near Preedee Thamrong Bridge specialises in traditional roti with candy floss. The plain and sesame rotis are freshly made, soft, and thin—perfectly complemented by the sweetness of cotton candy. With its popularity, make sure to pre-order, as they announce dates on Facebook.

Name: Roti Chaofa
Address: 44 Chaofa Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: For over 35 years, the locals have flocked to Roti Chaofa for Thai-Muslim breakfasts, curries and Thai-style chicken biryani. The crisp, golden-brown rotis with a fluffy inner, are nicely salted and enjoyed with sweets or savouries. The tangy, juicy Beef Massaman curry is delightful.

Name: Rasik Local Kitchen
Address: 44/3 Sridonchai Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: This chef's table experience showcases seasonal flavours and beloved Thai classics. The talented chef interacts with guests from the open kitchen and uses traditional cooking methods, such as a charcoal stove, to add depth to the dishes. The mild red curry with grilled pork and damask rose looks simple but the authentic taste of homemade Thai curry paste hides inside. The sliced pork is tender and the curry texture is smooth with a rich but balanced flavour.

Name: U-Khao
Address: 99 Mu 2, Khanon Luang, Bang Pa-in, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: U-Khao, or ‘land of plenty’, has 2 dining areas smartly decorated in white and blue. The menu serves up the nostalgic flavours of the owner’s childhood, as it’s based on her mother’s Thai recipes. They use traditional cooking methods presented with a modern aesthetic. The old-school style egg stew with pork belly is a flavoursome, intense stew with juicy meat. The grilled shrimp relish with vegetables is also highly recommended for its spicy relish and smoky aroma.

Name: Plaew (Nakhon Pathom)
Address: Soi 5, Mu 1, Nakhon Pathom, Mueang Nakhon Pathom, Nakhon Pathom, 73000, Thailand
Description: This no-frills outlet is popular with locals for its tom yum noodles and homemade pork balls. They use premium ingredients and jumbo-size seafood. Also check out the homemade fish cakes, with a curry-flavoured spice, served with deep-fried crispy basil and a sweet and sour sauce.

Name: Kapi Sator
Address: 25/236 Mu 6, Tawirat Phakdi Road, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
Description: The restaurant upholds authentic Southern Thai food thanks to a culinary repertory that is hard to find elsewhere. One example is the delectable local squid in sweet coconut milk soup with a hint of lemongrass. The daily fish menu changes according to the catch of the day. If available, the deep-fried whole pomfret topped with spicy Southern Thai curry is highly recommended. They offer indoor and outdoor dining with plenty of parking.

Name: Yok Kheng
Address: 5/2 Tonpo Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Consummately crafted regional specialties are the highlight here, particularly long tong, a Surat Thani delicacy. It features succulent dry noodles in a pink sweet and sour sauce with tender portions of pig’s blood, skin and meat. Leave room for the delectable mango with sticky rice.

Name: Han Thueng Chiang Mai
Address: 63/9 Soi Suthep 4, Suthep Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Occupying gable-roofed houses near Chiang Mai University, this place may lack a sign but locals have been flocking here for its delicious, competitively priced Northern Thai fare for over a decade. The rustic décor echoes the no-frills food with delicate flavours and textures. Their steamed beef slices with galangal dip are recommended; and for a delicious off-menu dish, order the seasonal special made from ingredients like wild mushrooms. Service is friendly.

Name: Lucky
Address: 1 Thathong Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Lucky is a 2-storey restaurant with a simple, vintage vibe. The chef-owner has upheld the legacy of previous generations in this family-run eatery. She visits the market every day to select the freshest ingredients and oversees every dish that leaves the kitchen – a selection of Thai-Chinese, southern Thai and seafood cuisine. Don't miss the allure of wok-fried shrimp with chilli and salt, where the enticing blend of salt, chilli, garlic, and pepper creates an aromatic delight.

Name: Rote Yiam Beef Noodle (Saeng Tawan)
Address: 164/48 Chang Khlan Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: For over 30 years, this renowned shop has been famous for its beef noodles — tender beef and flavourful broth with Chinese herbs. Each component, including beef balls and offal, is prepared fresh daily. There's creamy beef curry for non-noodle lovers, and don't miss the coconut ice cream!

Name: Sanae
Address: 64/1 Wangsingkham Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: This halal kitchen next to the Ping River is one for beef fans. With indoor and outdoor dining, the big outdoor kitchen cooks a creative à la carte menu with balanced flavours. The beef fat rice topped with egg yolk has a smoky flavour. The spicy Thai soup with beef shank is packed with spice aroma.

Name: Ekachan
Address: 95 Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: This new restaurant in the heart of old Chiang Mai is run by a local chef who embraces the slow food concept, using ingredients from around the country. The fried rice with sweet shrimp is nicely cooked with sweet shrimp paste and tasty condiments, including fresh chilli, shallots and mango. The spicy beef turmeric curry is a standout, with an intense mix of herbs and spices. If you’re looking for the spice bomb, they can add fresh Thai chillies.

Name: Na Chantra
Address: Chantra Khiri Hotel, 49 Mu 3, Ban Pong, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai, 50230, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Set up in the hills inside the Chantra Khiri Hotel, Na Chantra offers gorgeous views of the national park and a menu that features central and northern Thai dishes. Vegetables and herbs come from their next-door farm and everything else – like the savoury northern sausage with chilli paste – is made from scratch. Don’t miss their signature minced pork with fresh veg and spicy sauce, or the piquant yellow curry soup with sea bass. Start your evening outside, with a seat by the infinity pool.

Name: Mu Krop Chi Hong (Vichitsongkhram Road)
Address: 66/6 Vichitsongkhram Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Rice with roast pork belly is the best among an array of offerings at this shop. The pork comes in generous slices – its skin impossibly crisp and its meat lean and seasoned just right thanks to an old family recipe. An abundance of fresh side vegetables and a bowl of sipping broth come with it gratis.

Name: Khao Soi Mae Manee
Address: 18 Soi Chotana 24, Chotana Road, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Khao Soi is one of the best-known dishes of northern Thai cuisine, and the version they serve at this long-standing, family-run shop is a real winner. Like the other options on the menu, the Khao Soi features quality ingredients and house-made noodles. There are multiple toppings available – with the beef version proving particularly flavoursome – and it’s accompanied by generous sides.

Name: Pa Ting
Address: 1/8 Mu 5, Don Sak, Surat Thani, 84220, Thailand
Description: Established in 1967, Pa Ting is run by the founder’s daughter. The restaurant is a basic, open-air building overlooking Don Sak River, serving seafood cooked according to local recipes. The spicy salad with salted Kulao fish bursts with flavoursome Thai herbs. The crab curry with seablite leaves enjoys the natural umami of freshly caught seafood, enhanced with spicy in-house curry paste. Plenty of parking at the front.

Name: Khon Kaen Grilled Pork Neck
Address: 77/4 Klang Mueang Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: This grilled pork spot is among the most popular street places in Khon Kaen, and its grilled pork neck with rice is the reason why. The tender, sweet and salty marinated meat perfectly matches the accompanying spicy tamarind sauce. Also recommended are the spicy salad and soup.

Name: Huan Soontaree
Address: 208 Pa Tan Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Soontaree Vechanont doesn’t just own “Soontaree’s House” – the singer also performs here nightly. Set on the Ping River in an open-air, Lanna-style building with more tables outside, this charming restaurant can accommodate up to 350 guests. Among the Northern Thai cooking they serve is their signature boneless murrel fish stuffed with pork. It’s a creative dish, with the well-seasoned sausage proving suitably fragrant and spicy.

Name: Leng Yentafo
Address: Klang Mueang Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: When Mr. Leng left Bangkok’s Chinatown for Khon Kaen in 1984, he brought a secret recipe for Yentafo, or pink noodle soup, and set up shop. His signature dish, which features toothsome noodles, fresh fishballs, shrimp balls and fish wontons, and a tasty broth, continues to delight.

Name: Beer Hima (Prachachuen)
Address: 12/21, 99/231 Thetsaban Songkhro Road, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, Bangkok, 10900, Thailand
Description: Despite its quirky name and simple interior, Beer Hima offers so much more. The family’s seafood recipes from Nakhon Si Thammarat province are loaded with flavour. The southern Thai sour curry with grouper is packed with turmeric and chilli and delivers the perfect harmony of sour and spicy, while the rich, aromatic shrimp paste in the stir-fried prawns with bitter beans awakens the senses. There’s ample parking and a private room large enough for 30 guests.

Name: The Charm Dining Gallery
Address: 93 Dibuk Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Having grown up working in his family's food business, Chef Buriphat always wanted to do something special with their recipes. Over the last few years, he has realised that vision, impressing diners with his honest interpretation of traditional Southern Thai-Peranakan cuisine. Check out the delicious stir-fried pork belly with herbs and sweet dark soy sauce, and be sure to try the pork rib soup with tofu and salted fish.

Name: Tu Kab Khao
Address: 8 Phang Nga Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Set in a grand Chino-Portuguese building, Tu Kab Khao is an elegant, atmospheric restaurant. Portraits of the Royal Family grace its walls, along with one of the owner’s mother, Khun Linchii, whose recipes inform the menu. The cuisine is distinguished by high-quality ingredients – don’t miss the subtly spiced crab curry with rice vermicelli. The front area has a homely feel while the Portuguese-tiled rear room offers more privacy. Live music adds to the mood.

Name: Guay Tiew Khua Gai Suanmali
Address: Khlang Hospital Intersection, 266/1 Soi Thewi Worayat, Luang Road, Wat Thep Sirin, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: Family-owned and managed, this small stall’s hallmark dish is roasted chicken noodles. The noodles have a crispy, non-oily texture and are rich in seasoning aromas. Khao Lao Haeng, the dry option, is served with a crispy omelette, chicken and squid: highly recommended.

Name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
Address: 29/1 Ratchaphruek Road, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Believed by many to be the world’s favourite curry, this affordable street stall serves the famous khao soi. Their signature dish hits the spot with intense herbs, rich curry paste and tender braised beef. Also, don’t miss the vermicelli rice with northern Thai pork curry and tomato.

Name: Polo Fried Chicken (Soi Polo)
Address: 137/1-3 Soi Sanamkhli, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Run by the same family for three generations, this restaurant (actually two outlets in the same alley – one with air conditioning, one without) has been serving up affordable, delicious food for over 50 years. The draw is the deservedly famous fried chicken topped with deep-fried garlic, made from a secret southern-style recipe created by the first-generation owner. The generous som tam with seafood is also highly recommended, with a good balance between sweet and sour flavours.

Name: K. Panich
Address: 431-433 Tanao Road, Sao Chingcha, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: This iconic family-run eatery serves delectable mango sticky rice made to a recipe that has been handed down the generations for 80 years. Their preparation is masterful: the flavour of the steamed sweetened sticky rice is enhanced by the richness of coconut milk.

Name: Huen Muan Jai
Address: 24 Ratchaphruek Road, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Headed up by former TV chef Charan Thipeung, this restaurant – whose name means ‘happy home’ – has been serving authentic Northern Thai food since 2011. Set in a Lanna house with a tree-lined garden, it’s a popular, wallet-friendly destination that offers hard-to-find traditional dishes alongside classic favourites. The uniquely flavoured spicy minced fish salad is highly recommended and if you’re unfamiliar with the cuisine, start with the excellent Northern appetiser sampler.

Name: Tumkratoei Sagate
Address: 88-89 Mu 20, Maliwan Road, Ban Pet, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The owner is from Roi Et Province (formerly Sagate Province). The place offers flavourful food, warm service and wallet-friendly prices in a relaxed setting. The signature spicy seafood salad with fermented fish sauce is recommended, and beyond the Som Tum dishes, standouts include fried sour fish and spicy chicken soup with glass noodles. Indoors and outdoor seating are available. Nightly live music adds to the experience.

Name: Baan Heng
Address: 54/2 Klang Mueang Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Baan Heng was born out of a souvenir and grocery shop the owners’ grandparents started in 1957 called Heng Nguan Hiang. It sold products like homemade Chinese sausage, pork floss and pork jerky. Now, the restaurant serves Thai-Chinese breakfast fare, like their signature Baan Heng sandwich and baked rice with sweet pork sausage in a remodelled wood-themed design that exudes old-school vibes. Add a classic hot Thai black coffee or milk tea for the full effect.

Name: Maadae
Address: 86-88 Thapae Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Meaning ‘come’ in the Southern language, ‘Maadae’ invites you to enjoy delightful seafood in a welcoming atmosphere. Supporting local Chumphon fishermen and sourcing seasonal organic produce, their menu rotates with fresh ingredients. The evening selection offers diverse options, including superb freshly grilled seafood paired with a spicy sauce.

Name: One Chun
Address: 48/1 Thep Krasatti Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Merging the owner's fashion design flair and passion for fine fare, One Chun offers a vintage-toned dining experience in a 19C building. Diners still enjoy the family recipes, which have been passed down the generations. Among the specialties is a spicy yet refreshing dish with boiled shrimp and shrimp paste, perfectly balancing the salty and sour notes. Be sure to try "Mu Hong" for its bold flavours and soft, tender pork belly.

Name: Chom Chan
Address: 242/2 Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Chom Chan has flourished with its own charming character and refreshing ambiance. Situated in a small white house with a leafy façade, the interior is a blend of modern Sino-Portuguese with antique decoration. Some dishes are shared with the other restaurants but do try the fried crab’s spawn with chilli, pepper and garlic; steamed minced pork with salty egg; and deep-fried pork belly with salt.

Name: Sanyod (Sathon-Bang Rak)
Address: 89 Soi Charat Wiang, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: For over 50 years, a small alley stall has been serving up Thai-Cantonese noodles to regulars. Its modern dining room, across from the initial take-out spot, offers specialties like secret-sauce chargrilled duck and crispy shrimp balls with mustard greens in sticky sauce. The menu also features tender clay pot-braised beef.

Name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Dinsor Road)
Address: 115/5 Dinso Road, Bowon Niwet, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: The tempting scent of sizzling pork greets you at this vibrant restaurant by chef Andy Yang. Their signature dish features nicely char-grilled pork loin slices atop savoury Pad Thai. Another recommendation is the Pad Thai with fresh prawns, stir-fried in their shell for sweet, delicious meat. For top-notch Pad Thai and skilled wok-based cooking at a fair price, this is your spot.

Name: Khok Kloi Bami Tom Yam Khai
Address: 6/10 Phet Kasem Road, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
Description: Their fresh tom yum noodles are accompanied by piquant spicy and sour flavours; dry or in an intense broth. They’re known for impressively sized portions at reasonable prices. The soft minced pork and healthy liver have a beautiful scent of fresh lime juice and chilli in a sweet broth.

Name: Baan Ta Ko Rai
Address: 112/941 Mu 3, Khlong Suanplu, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Here at this blue-roofed local favourite they prove there’s more to Ayutthaya than grilled river prawns. Ingredients are carefully selected from produce grown within the community and it uses fish from nearby rivers as the catch of the day. The herb-scented fish cakes are delectable, while stir-fried Chinese kale with deep fried salted fish is equally impressive. Portion sizes are generous, so check before ordering.

Name: Khaotom Chedi
Address: 254/14 Rochana Road, Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This well-known street food seller is an ideal spot for locals looking for a late-night bite. Check with the owner for the special ingredients on the day’s menu; the seafood is especially good, as the owner visits the market himself. Stir-fried dishes are a real highlight – try the shrimps with salt and pepper, or the seasonal clams with roasted chilli.

Name: Majchapasuk
Address: 166 Mu 8, Udon-Nong Khai Road, Mu Mon, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: A serene pond encircled by wooden pavilions is Majchapasuk's tranquil setting. Each spot in the expansive seating area has a soothing atmosphere, ideal for savouring local seafood steeped in over 40 years of Isan culinary heritage. Standout mains showcase Isan tradition with seabass and snakehead fish. Don't miss the crispy deep-fried spring rolls stuffed with minced pork and pork skin. Evening promises optimum weather conditions and idyllic pond views.

Name: Lab Nua
Address: 24 Phachauthit Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: ‘Lab Nua’ means delicious Isan-style spicy salad and that’s certainly the focus here. Often featuring homemade fermented fish sauce, dishes like spicy seafood salad with Dong Daeng noodles and Isan soup with rice field snails attest to the chef’s skills. The lively open-air restaurant also sports pink wooden tables and chairs and is popular with friends and family groups who appreciate the friendly service, reasonable prices and late closing time.

Name: Tek Heng Mee Krob Jeen Lee
Address: 326-330 Soi Thoet Thai 18, Talat Phlu, Thon Buri, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
Description: History is on the menu at this legendary Thai-Chinese restaurant. Starting out as a floating shop on Klong Bangkok Yai before moving onshore in 1907, it’s now run by 4th generation descendants of the Thai-Teochew founders. It fills three shophouses adorned with articles, awards, and photos, including some of King Rama V. He is said to have enjoyed the Mee Krob, or crispy vermicelli – one of this place’s many classics based on 130-year-old family recipes.

Name: Laab Somphit
Address: 169 Chan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: For over 50 years, Granny Somphit has been crafting flavourful Isan cuisine daily, balancing local spices with Thai herbs. Fresh offal cuts and the signature Isan spicy calf beef salad, seasoned with smoky rice powder for crispness, stand out. The homemade beef sausage and fermented meats are also notable.

Name: Thai Niyom
Address: Mahatun Plaza, 888/28-29 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Hidden in the shadow of skyscrapers is this gem of a restaurant, which got its start serving family recipes, but now offers an array of Thai cuisine from Chiang Mai to Hat Yai. It is a great place to sample delicious Thai cooking from every region on the same table. Quality ingredients are sourced locally and turned into dishes like the recommended Phuket stir-fried pork belly with shrimp paste and the Chiang Mai Combo, a Northern Thai-style appetiser plate.

Name: Bokkia Tha Din Daeng
Address: 323 Tha Din Daeng Road, Somdet Chao Phraya, Khlong San, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
Description: Tucked away in a small market stall, this family-run dessert shop is famous for its sweet Bokkia. It's a unique treat: egg noodles, topped with crushed ice and syrup, which is amazingly refreshing and not too sweet. The condimental options are also good quality.

Name: Go Neng (Wichayanon)
Address: 77 Praisani Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Go Neng has been serving deep-fried dough sticks for almost four decades. No matter what shape they take – crocodile, dinosaur, dragon or elephant – each one boasts the same puffy perfection and crispy texture. Other bites, such as the deep-fried bun and fried whole-wheat dough are also great.

Name: Khanom Chin Pa Son
Address: 3 Borirak Bamrung Road, Thai Chang, Mueang Phang-nga, Phang-Nga, 82000, Thailand
Description: Across from a Chinese shrine, this self-service buffet has been drawing devotees for over 30 years with its tasty khanom chin and four curry options to mix and match. Pick from a wide range of condiments, fresh vegetables, boiled egg and crispy anchovies. Lunchtime is always busy, so arrive early.

Name: Gop Phochana
Address: 58/2 Mu 7, Phet Kasem Road, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82120, Thailand
Description: Now in its second generation, this popular destination attracts locals and tourists seeking comforting favourites with intense seasoning and spices. The stir-fried shrimp with coconut curry is the delicious signature; it’s creamy, the shrimps are plump, and it boasts natural umami.

Name: Thien Duong
Address: Baan Dusit Thani, 116 Saladaeng Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Thien Duong is a showcase of Vietnamese classical design; the antique artworks, mustard-coloured walls, rose-pink granite tables, shiny black floor tiles and exposed ceiling are an interior design lover’s paradise. The menu of Vietnamese dishes includes plenty of clean and fresh-tasting vegetables, with one eye often on health and wellness. The grilled lamb rack with mint-tamarind sauce is worth ordering, delivering a great balance of flavours.

Name: Penlaos (Pak Chong)
Address: 56 Mu 17, Thanaratch Road, Mu Si, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30450, Thailand
Description: Penlaos started over a decade ago as a street stall. Today, it’s an altogether different operation offering a quality menu in a building with high ceilings surrounded by lush gardens and views of the mountains. They serve Isan food using homemade condiments – the spicy catfish salad is a must. The Laosian style spicy mushroom soup is made with Tiliacora juice, seasonal mushrooms and gourd which adds a natural sweetness. The Thai coconut milk custard rounds off your meal nicely.

Name: Tonfon Bistro
Address: Krabi 1002 Rural Road, Bo Saen, Thap Put, Phang-Nga, 82180, Thailand
Description: Since opening its doors in 1995, the chef-owner has consistently cooked flavoursome, well presented southern fare with an emphasis on locally sourced ingredients and authentic recipes. Daily deliveries of fresh seafood and organic produce come from nearby farms. Savour dishes like stir-fried pork with shrimp paste and bitter bean or curry with crab legs and betel leaves. While the menu may be concise, each dish reflects the chef's passion. Indoor and outdoor seating is available.

Name: Phed Phed Bistro
Address: The Circle Ratchapruk, 39 Ratchaphruek Road, Bang Ramat, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: Phed Phed has many branches, but this one stands out for its minimalist wire mesh theme décor. The menu offers comforting Isan favourites steeped in flavour. Don’t miss the herbal pork soup with its tender, crispy cartilage and sweet pumpkin, while the green apple som tum and salty fish sauce with dried shrimp perfectly blends sweet with sour. Large groups of locals pack the place at lunch and dinner. As they don't accept bookings, arrive early to avoid a wait.

Name: Lung Khajohn Wat Ket
Address: Opposite to Wat Ketkaram, Charoenrajd Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: For decades, this place has been serving distinctive Khao Kriab Pak Moh, or steamed rice skin dumplings, opposite Wat Ket Karam. These contain a tasty salty-sweet filling wrapped in a coconut-infused rice flour sheet and a side of coconut cream. Tapioca balls with sweet pork are also offered.

Name: Tue Ka Ko Na Prince
Address: Kaeonawarat Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: This Tue Ka Ko – or taro fritter – place has been open for over 20 years opposite The Prince Royal's College, hence the name “Tue Ka Ko Na Prince." Savoury and sweet, their version of the Chiang Mai snack is perfected textured and served with peanut sauce. Deep-fried tofu is also sold.

Name: Toh Daeng
Address: GF, Baan Ar-jor, 102 Thep Kasattri Road, Mai Khao, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: ‘Toh-daeng’ translates as ‘red dining table’ – and you will find one here, running the length of the kitchen wing at this renovated manor house which serves as a window into Phuket’s past. The restaurant is surrounded by farmland, where they grow ingredients including mulberry and coconut. Well-balanced dishes allow the natural flavours of the produce to shine; rambutan red curry with grilled pork neck is a highlight, with the rambutan adding a natural sweetness.

Name: Hong Seng
Address: 280 Mu 2, Chaeng Watthana Road, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
Description: On the Chao Praya by the Rama IV Bridge, this renowned Thai-Chinese spot has been known for reasonably priced flavoursome fare since 1957. Its open-air dining room and wooden terrace set the stage for relaxed meals featuring highlights like grilled giant river prawns with spicy sauce and mini deep-fried crab meat wrapped in tofu skin. Open for lunch, the place extends its hours on weekends. Reach it by boat, or if driving, park in the public space under the bridge.

Name: Kua Kampan Khao Yai
Address: 94-94/1 Rural Road NMA.3052, Mu 6, Mu Si, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30130, Thailand
Description: The kampan (Thai for sailing ship) is an antique boat at the heart of the restaurant that has been transferred from Ayutthaya. The menu, designed by the owner, uses classic Thai recipes packed with intense flavours. The minced pork spare ribs with betel leaf is a signature dish; every meaty mouthful contains crispy cartilage in a spicy curry. Meanwhile, the red curry rice field snail with coconut milk is brought to life by the enlivening aroma of the betel leaf.

Name: Krua Suwimol
Address: 1229 9 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This simple, open-air restaurant serves Thai-Chinese fare. The food is distinctive for its simply cooking techniques yet quality dishes with extra-fresh ingredients and intense flavours. They offer a fantastic range, including several seafood and made-to-order options. Deep-fried chicken thigh with fish sauce and stir-fried spicy seafood are recommended.

Name: Indochine
Address: 170 Sappasit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: The name Indochine is derived from the connection between two countries - Vietnamese family recipes have been served here for over 50 years. And family is the key to this popular business where everyone pitches in. The restaurant boasts vintage décor, using old wooden furniture and tables made from defunct sewing machines. The Vietnamese rice cake with grille pork is highly recommended, while the signature namnueng comes in a big basket with a mix of fresh local vegetables.

Name: Mook Manee
Address: 1120 Wiset Road, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83100, Thailand
Description: Located near Rawai beach, Mook Manee stands out for its array of live seafood for diners to choose from, from squid and tiger prawns to a variety of crabs and 3kg Phuket rainbow lobster. The restaurant holds up to 300, but the best seats have views of the vibrant seafood market trading outside. The menu highlights include Tom Yum soup, Phuket lobster with spicy dip and stir-fried mantis shrimps with garlic and chilli. A wooden terrace on the beach is also available.

Name: Nong Rim Klong
Address: 51 Soi Ekkamai 23, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: This former canal-side food stall found new life as a simply decorated shophouse spread across two floors. A semi-open kitchen lets you glimpse the chefs as they work on intensely flavoured, great value dishes based on prime quality ingredients. The sea bass tom yum soup has a wonderful herby flavour and a generous portion of fish, while the rather unique crab omelette offers fresh flavours and a natural sweetness.

Name: Kin Lookdeaw
Address: 35 Mu 9, Tha Chao Sanuk, Tha Ruea, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13130, Thailand
Description: The name of the restaurant asks guests to ‘focus on eating’ (Kin Lookdeaw) at this quaint house with an open-air pavilion above a serene pond. The chefs, veterans in the kitchen, cook simple Thai dishes and make their own chilli paste from scratch. The regular pounding of pestle in mortar reverberates through nature’s own soundtrack. Try the deep-fried boneless red tilapia with garlic and stir-fried green curry with clown featherback fish balls.

Name: Roe Dang
Address: 55/15 Mu 1, Phet Kasem Road, Lam Kaen, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82210, Thailand
Description: Basic furnishings and modest dish presentations belie the skill behind their precisely cooked recipes, which are made to order. Specialising in authentic Southern Thai seafood, they source the day's catch for dishes such as red grouper with bitter melon, and simple stir-fried melinjo leaves with fresh prawns. Their home-made curries use local Phang-nga ingredients. The wall of celebrity photos attests to its popularity.

Name: Samlor
Address: 1076 Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Samlor means ‘tricycle’ in Thai and a traditional one hangs outside this cosy restaurant. Inside the loft-style space, chef Napol creates flavoursome, well-presented elevated Thai cuisine inspired by local street food with specially selected ingredients. They also have an à la carte menu, which includes a cut and catch of the day. Guests need to check with the chef what is available.

Name: Tune In Garden
Address: 139 Mu 3, Pong Yaeng, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is owned by the late National Artist of Thailand and his wife. She cooks delicious homestyle fare drawn from a cookbook she wrote based on her mother-in-law’s recipes. First-timers are served a fixed-price menu; returners can order from the cookbook. Roasted pork ribs with cabbage and fermented pork with fermented bean curd relish stand out. Booking is required.

Name: Maan Muang
Address: 165/7 Soi Ramkhamhaeng 112 Ramkhamhaeng Road, Saphan Sung, Bangkok, 10240, Thailand
Description: This lovely wooden Lanna house with rustic charm will magically whisk you off to Chiang Mai. The dining area under the raised house is decorated with traditional Thai wooden furniture and earthenware. The staff too are dressed in Northern Thai fashions and speak in a regional dialect. But it’s the dizzying array of dishes and beautiful blend of northern ingredients that tops it off. The Thai curry soup with pork ribs and jackfruit hits the spot.

Name: Roti Sai Mai Abeedeen-Pranom Sangaroon
Address: 32/1 Mu 4, U Thong Road, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Over 70 years have passed, but this renowned spot opposite Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Hospital still serves the same perfect rotis with candy floss, made by the same family. Their specialty, the green pandan roti, is known for its delightful gooeyness. As popular as ever, be prepared to queue.

Name: Here Klae Pork Satay
Address: Pamaprao Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Now run by the third-generation grill master, this humble shophouse boasts a history spanning over nine decades and remains one of Ayutthaya’s most cherished spots for charcoal-grilled pork satay. The skewered meat is meticulously marinated, offering an aromatic blend of nine spices. Don't miss the pork offal – it pairs perfectly with the accompanying peanut sauce. Please note: takeaways only, and cash is the accepted payment method.

Name: Hok Kee Lao
Address: 19 Senarat Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: For over 40 years, this heritage restaurant has been serving up delicious Thai, Chinese, and Southern flavours. It's an ideal spot for family gatherings, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere. The menu includes Chinese favourites such as nicely moist chicken pae sa flavoured with seasoned soy sauce and paired with morning glory. If you are lucky, try the fried tofu with minced pork and shrimp.

Name: Krua Khun Nid
Address: 64 Soi Nonnivet 1, Udon Dussadi Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: For over four decades this restaurant has been a mainstay for locals. Focusing on freshwater fish and meat, it serves large sharing portions. Seasonal options and occasional fish specials accompany enduring classics, such as the flavourful deep-fried Pla Som, or snakehead fish in flavoursome tom yum soup. The friendly staff are happy to share their recommendations.

Name: Nai Ngieb (Phutthamonthon Sai 4)
Address: 125/21 Mu 6, Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road, Salaya, Phutthamonthon, Nakhon Pathom, 73170, Thailand
Description: One of the best eateries in the area for noodle soup lovers, where the bouncy, MSG-free fish balls are made the traditional way from mackerel, yellowtail amberjack and wolf herring. The tom yum soup stands out; and the fish noodles are perfect for low-carb dieters as they go well with any soup.

Name: Lian Tai
Address: 70 Chonkasem Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Lian Tai specialises in deep-fried doughnuts. The family uses the original fermented dough recipe concocted by their father more than 5 decades ago. Cooked to a crisp, outer golden-brown with a soft, puffy inside, the Patongo is irresistible when dipped in rich sweet pandan custard.

Name: Prik-Yuak
Address: 108 Pradiphat Road, Phaya Thai, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Prik-Yuak has flourished for 30 years, starting in the bustling Chatuchak markets and now stationed in a spacious, inviting location. The restaurant maintains its beloved approach to home-style Thai cooking. Signature dishes like the Southern Thai pork belly and egg stew showcase tender meat, boiled eggs, and tofu. The venue charms with light, earth-toned decor, a serene garden, and includes a café and boutique shop to enhance the dining experience.

Name: Mor Mu Dong
Address: 9/4 Mu 3 Soi Pa Lai, Chao Fa Road, Chalong, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83130, Thailand
Description: Mor Mu Dong takes its name from its owner, Mor, and the Mu Dong Canal, where it is located. Nestled in a mangrove forest, it is housed in a set of rustic pavilions where diners can enjoy seafood and take in the views that change with the tide. In the open kitchen, tanks of live seafood affirm the freshness of the food. The signature dish – Pla Tu Yat Sai, or spicy stuffed fish – and the stir-fried squid with lime are both highly recommended.

Name: Meena
Address: 13/5 Mu 2, San Klang, San Kamphaeng, Chiang Mai, 50130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Don’t be alarmed when you pass through a rice field driving here, as this hidden gem is worth it. As its name suggests, this alfresco restaurant specialises in rice, alongside new spins on Thai classics. Most are garnished with fruits and edible flowers, giving them bursts of colour. Along with the five-colour rice balls, northern-style spicy minced fish salad is a delight. Vegans will enjoy their many options, including the spicy stir-fried eryngii mushrooms.

Name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song Lao Ohw
Address: 22 2 Witeetad Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: With a legacy spanning 6 decades, locals flock here for the exquisite satay pork and renowned phra ram long song, an ancient Siamese delicacy. It features tender sliced pork in a curry sauce that masterfully balances rich gutsy paste with creamy coconut milk.

Name: Krua Chao Baan Samui
Description: Krua Chao Baan means local kitchen, which aptly describes the vibe of this eatery specialised in Southern Thai food. The signature omelette is simple: crispy, not oily, with mixed seafood and well-seasoned minced pork. The stir-fried squid with pineapple, a local recipe only found on the island, is depicted by joyful sweet, sour and peppery notes.

Name: Keo Pla
Address: 560/4 Na Mueang Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This locally renowned noodle shop first opened in 1959. The homemade fish dumplings with celery and fish balls packed with umami invariably attract long queues. The soup strikes just the right balance of sweet and savoury with a herbal aroma. Hearty, generous portions.

Name: Phunisa
Address: 11/1 Mu 1, Khao Hua Khwai, Phunphin, Surat Thani, 84130, Thailand
Description: Standing atop a picturesque hill, the restaurant commands splendid views of the Tapi River winding through a green landscape of palm tree plantations and mountains. They serve tasty Southern Thai fare, including salted duck egg and local river prawns. A spicy seafood sauce and chargrill aroma add depth and complexity to the natural umami of prawns, while a spicy Southern Thai curry soup with pork cartilage features intense peppery and spicy flavours.

Name: Saiyut and Doctor Sai Kitchen
Address: 32 Chotana Road Soi 12, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Since 2004, Doctor Sai has been serving pan-Thai dishes, including royal fare, following recipes from her mother, Saiyud, a former cooking instructor, in a setting reminiscent of dining at home. Start with an elegant appetiser like fried prawns and peanuts in an egg net, flower dumplings, or deep-fried pork wrapped in egg noodles. By dessert – try the sweet potato in syrup – you’ll guess this home, with its warm service, belongs to a royal from a bygone era.

Name: Roti Thaew Nam
Address: 6 Thep Krasattri Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Soft, crispy, non-oily roti emerge from a huge charcoal pan. At this 70-year-old Halal breakfast spot, they're shaped, fried and served in the blink of an eye and served with tender beef or chicken curry. The sweeter roti with banana and egg has no added sugar.

Name: Kha Mu Boran (Kathu)
Address: 17/11 Mu 6, Praphuketkeaw Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
Description: This long-time favourite serves a standout Kamu, with slow-braised, spiced pork shanks. It's a classic dish, but they do it better than most. Their shanks are top-notch and cooked until they're incredibly tender. You can get them with a tasty broth, complete with bones for extra flavour. Both locals and travelers make a point to stop here for this meal.

Name: Here Hai
Address: 112/1 Soi Sukhumvit 63, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Good value, high quality seafood sent directly from Surat Thani is the draw here. Its prices may be considered high for street food, but portions are large and ingredients superb. Go for the fried rice with crabmeat and fried mantis with crispy garlic, both cooked with traditional technique and offer pleasant smoky aroma.

Name: Kai Yang Rabeab (Khao Suan Kwang)
Address: 99 Mittraphap Road, Kham Muang, Khao Suan Kwang, Khon Kaen, 40280, Thailand
Description: Throw a stick in Khon Kaen and you’ll likely hit a street food place serving grilled chicken and Isan dishes. You’d be lucky if you landed on this one. Its secret is tender, juicy chicken from three local breeds. A second downtown branch offers the same menu minus grilled offal.

Name: Ruean Panya
Address: 1300/600 Soi Ekkachai 13, Norarat Uthit Road, Maha Chai, Mueang Samut Sakhon, Samut Sakhon, 74000, Thailand
Description: Open since 1995, this family-run restaurant – which blends food and art – is a hidden gem. Spread across four houses, it has a relaxed vibe that gives the impression of dining at a friend's, while painting-filled interiors add a gallery feel. Owner Prunhnee does all the cooking herself; her attention to detail and the complexity of flavours make her dishes memorable. Local seafood is a feature, and their signature mud crab coconut dip or ‘Lhon Pu’ is a must-have.

Name: Chuan Chim
Address: 37/3 Montri Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: At one of the oldest food shops in Phuket, now run by the second generation, all the seafood is fresh and everything is prepared à la minute. The results, including the stir-fried noodles and the stir-fried seafood with curry powder, are impressive and worth the wait.

Name: S.B.L.
Address: 710-714 Maha Chai Road, Wang Burapha Phirom, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Open since 1954, this Chinese restaurant is currently run by a second-generation family member who is keen to make every aspect of the dining experience pleasurable. The menu features mostly traditional Chinese fare with a few creations that show novel twists. The X.O. scallops are a must-try, as is the expertly-steamed snow fish with soya sauce. Quality ingredients handled with skill and experience is the formula that guarantees a good meal here.

Name: Sawang Noodles (Si Phraya)
Address: 264 Si Phraya Road, Maha Phruettharam, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: This is the place to enjoy crab noodles in Bangkok. The sweet, giant crab claw meat pairs well with sticky egg noodles and shrimp dumplings. Be sure to try their signature noodles with extra soup and barbecued pork on the side.

Name: Sae Phun
Address: 112 Mahannop Road, Sao Chingcha, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Opened since 1926, it has been relocated. This small shop is now run by the third generation. The owner has been cooking with her grandfather's recipes for many years. The signature dish chicken stew is juicy with chicken and rich in sauce. It can be paired with rice or deep fried egg noodles.

Name: Baan Benjarong Pai (Bang Kruai)
Address: 2F, The Crystal SB Ratchaphruek, 555/9 Mu 1, Ratchapruek Road, Maha Sawat, Bang Kruai, Nonthaburi, 11130, Thailand
Description: The original Baan Benjarong, in northern town Pai, was set up to champion the region’s cuisine. This Nonthaburi branch opened in 2017. The typically friendly staff all hail from the north and deliver the best of Pai as well as central Thailand dishes. Served in a quintessentially northern sweet and sour soup, the snake head fish is fried to a crispy golden-brown; the caramelised sauce on the baked pork spareribs melds dreamily with salted fish and herbs.

Name: Surf & Turf by Soul Kitchen
Address: 115 Phangnga Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The menu changes every month in this intriguing restaurant. Regular options range from home-made pastas to a signature seafood dish, plus specials that are cleverly curated to showcase Chef Tom's latest culinary creations. The chef artfully prepares his dishes, blending quality ingredients to tantalise the taste buds. And thanks to the ever-changing selection of handpicked wines, there's always something different to sip with your meal.

Name: Grim Nguan Noodle
Address: 75/70 Soi Chom Thong 16, Chom Thong Road, Bang Kho, Chom Thong, Bangkok, 10150, Thailand
Description: This hidden gem, tucked away in a Bangkok alley since 1999, excels in fish ball noodle soup. They offer fresh, umami-rich fish balls, al dente noodles, and a savoury, aromatic broth. Optional toppings like cheese and poached egg, along with large servings and ample condiments, provide great taste and value.

Name: Roti Pa Day
Address: In front of Wat Mahawan, Thapae Road Soi 4, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: First-timers should order the plain crispy roti with condensed milk to start. The roti dough here is uniquely made without eggs. Instead, Thai-Pakistani owner Pa Day (Auntie Day) adds salt to the dough that’s cooked to a crispy-chewy perfection in coconut oil. Choose from 20 toppings.

Name: Nai Muang
Address: 33/4 Mu 6, Soi Loma, Khuekkhak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82190, Thailand
Description: The nostalgic bric-a-brac, old tin mining memorabilia, record players and sewing machines exude a quaint retro charm. It’s all about the seafood here, guaranteed to be fresh, vibrant and big on flavour. Order the crab curry with rice noodles, or stir-fried shrimps with stink beans and shrimp paste. Another popular southern Thai dish is the signature spicy salad, served with crispy prawns, squid and taro, with diced lime and fried chilli for extra pep.

Name: Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla
Address: 816 Chan Road, Thung Wat Don, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Entirely focused on top-drawer seafood, this eatery offers a wide range of dishes. The soft-boiled rice with silver pomfret comes with a juicy fillet and fresh, clear soup. The baked mung bean noodles with prawns feature sticky mung bean noodles, underscored by a spicy-sour Thai seafood sauce.

Name: Somchai Go Tae (Bang Len)
Address: 18/13 Mu 1, Bang Phasi, Bang Len, Nakhon Pathom, 73130, Thailand
Description: Go Tae, the owner of this Thai-Chinese restaurant, got his start almost 80 years ago selling stewed duck noodle soup on a boat, before heading to dry land to open this place. Inside the three-storey building (topped with a giant rooftop duck statue), the simple dining room has high ceilings and a roasting and stewing station. The menu features old-school Thai-Chinese fare, including the recommended stewed duck and spicy climbing perch with Chu Chee curry.

Name: Sanpakoi Kanomjeen
Address: Thongkam Market, Soi Thasatoi, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: Established in 1977 and a local favourite at Thongkam Market, this spot offers tasty and affordable Kanomjeen (fresh rice vermicelli) with various curries. Try the Nam-Lo, a mix of spicy pork and chicken curry sauces. If noodles aren’t your thing, swap them for rice. Not only are the street food dishes here delicious, but they’re great value too – especially when you consider that side vegetables are unlimited.

Name: Plu
Address: 3 Soi Phra Phinit, Suan Phlu Road, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: The Water Library’s Plu offers outstanding food, a cosy ambience, and great service in an Art Deco-adorned colonial house. Among the beautifully presented authentic pan-Thailand dishes is the signature braised pork belly and soft-boiled eggs in five-spiced soup; the pork belly is tender and juicy, the deep-fried tofu absorbs the aromatic broth, and the soft-boiled eggs only enhance the flavour and texture. Start with one of the restaurant’s signature cocktails.

Name: Guay Jub Chang Moi Tat Mai
Address: 99/11-12 Chang Moi Tat Mai Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: This place specialises in Guay Jub with Sai Ua sausage, served in a unique peppery broth, featuring with crispy pork and pork liver. They also offer another delightful dish: fresh spring rolls, topped with sliced omelette and aromatic sauce.

Name: Prasit
Address: 44/4 Ammart Road, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
