Name: LEV Foodbar
Description: The relaxed atmosphere at LEV perfectly matches the concept behind this food bar: sharing dishes and enjoying good food together. The dishes (in snack-sized portions) are not overcomplicated; a couple of ingredients suffice to create amazing taste sensations. Steak tartare, pork tenderloin, cauliflower tempura, truffle risotto... At LEV, the table quickly fills with irresistible delicacies, often prepared using produce from the Achterhoek region. The perfect accompaniment to one of the many beers!

Name: Serre
Description: A bright space with a gorgeous canalside terrace, Serre has a Japanese minimalist feel. Reflecting the international atmosphere of the luxury Hotel Okura, this restaurant serves fusion cuisine with a slight penchant for Far Eastern influences. Start with a platter of super-fresh oysters and then pick one of the sharing dishes. Alternatively, there is a set menu with mouth-watering options for each course, such as smoked salmon with a refreshing Thai twist. And those who prefer to avoid meat and fish are sure to find something to their liking.

Name: Uit de Kunst
Description: Hikers and cyclists who test themselves to their limits on the Vijlenberg are rewarded by this modern restaurant situated right at the top. The superb view from the terrace is a feast for the eyes, while the traditional dishes served here are a treat for the taste buds. Simple yet refined and delicious cuisine.

Name: Basaal
Address: Dunne Bierkade 3, The Hague, 2512 BC, Netherlands
Description: A cosy neighbourhood restaurant, Scandinavian and vintage vibes included, nice terrace on the water: what a nice place Basaal is! The full à la carte offer and the attractive wine list complete the picture. The modern market cuisine is based on intense sauces, generous flavours and creative, tantalising ideas. A deliciously unconstrained feast of flavour!

Name: De Aubergerie
Description: The sweets that used to be sold in this establishment dating back to the 1700s have given way to delicacies such as lobster and Venus clams. This new direction is reflected in the artistic photographs hanging on the walls of this cosy, intimate-feeling restaurant. Chef Han showcases his ingredients in cutting-edge dishes drawing on solid French foundations and with the odd creative flourish. Take, for instance, his succulent marbré of goose breast and rillette, with the sweet earthiness of textures of beetroot, combined with vibrant pickled mustard seeds and punchy creamed rocket. The friendly atmosphere of De Aubergerie also comes down to the personal service of your hostess Ingrid.

Name: HAVN
Description: Two views, one of the historical harbour and the other of the open kitchen, grab your attention as soon as you enter this restaurant with a buzzing atmosphere. The same playful energy is even more apparent in the creations of chef Robin Blaauw. He is, for instance, as happy to dabble in the rich flavours of South American cuisine as he is to dive into the Asian culinary world. Drawing inspiration from his travels, he works with the finest Dutch produce to conjure up his dishes. Thanks to his eye for detail, this young chef has already made an impressive career for himself.

Name: De Schans by Mike & Wes
Description: When they took over De Schans, Mike and Wes, respectively sommelier and chef, added a trendier, more relaxed vibe, whilst retaining the establishment’s commitment to fine food and wine. The chef crafts dishes in tune with the zeitgeist using cutting-edge culinary techniques to create a subtle blend of textures and unexpected flavours. The set menu is definitely worth sampling!

Name: Bergpaviljoen
Description: Choose your fish from the counter, treat yourself to one of the classics such as steak tartare or just opt for some tasty bar food accompanied by a good glass of wine. In this light-filled pavilion, with its Art Deco design features and spacious terrace by the beehives, you are spoilt for choice. But rest assured that, thanks to the quality of the produce that the chef has to work with, you simply cannot go wrong here.

Name: Fa. Pekelhaaring
Description: Welcome to the urban canteen of a number of Amsterdam’s local residents – a relaxed eatery without unnecessary sophistication, but one which is both authentic and welcoming. The cuisine is influenced (but not exclusively) by Italy and the chef enjoys adding his own variations and personal touches (such as crunchy textures and local influences) to his cooking. The varied à la carte is impressive indeed!

Name: Lazuur
Description: This charming neighbourhood restaurant proposes a refined fusion of French and Portuguese cuisine. The appealing set menu offers a choice of dishes including, for example, kale, bouchot mussels and molho de coentro. The chef cooks his ingredients to perfection and adds a dash of Mediterranean flair, as demonstrated in his soft-cooked pulpo, creamy riso venere and espuma of paprika. Be sure to check out the impressive port collection, which contains plenty of surprises.

Name: Bij Erik
Description: Wood, metal and leather create an intimate feel, although a table on the terrace is also a good choice: the view of the lock and windmill is magnificent. Erik Tas will have diners' mouths watering with fresh combinations in which stocks and sauces lead to wonderful harmonies.

Name: Marie
Description: Marie possesses that charm typical of the South of France. The brasserie decor exudes luxury, but the terrace overlooking the boats and bridges is where everyone wants a table. This tranquil oasis in the heart of the city is enhanced by the Mediterranean finesse of the cuisine. The lamb fillet and cheeks with a perfectly balanced hollandaise sauce, the salt-baked sea bass, the generous beef tartare: these are down-to-earth dishes that pack a punch, and they are simply irresistible. This is what Bib Gourmand is all about!

Name: Café Caron
Description: This cosy bistro is run by Alain Caron (a well-known TV personality and chef) and his family. The ambience here is typically French, as is the menu which features traditional, generous bistro-style dishes which are a work of art in their own right. Trying out the à la carte here is a real joy.

Name: Le Nord
Description: This authentic farmhouse dating from 1885 combines rural charm and modern design – the ideal setting in which to experience Grégory Nicole's cuisine. The finesse with which this French chef pays tribute to his homeland is a testament to his expertise. More modern inspirations add a dash of excitement without overcomplicating things. He surprises diners with, for instance, his own take on Poire Williams, or a beautiful cod fillet infused with zesty notes. Be sure to try the tuna pizza, a tribute to master chef Joop Braakhekke. A great Bib Gourmand restaurant that is also a sure bet at lunchtime!

Name: Rijsel
Description: The interior of this lively establishment resembles a classroom, and indeed this building was once a home economics school. Today you can see the 'master' at work preparing his lesson in French gastronomy thanks to the open kitchen. He has a sound knowledge of his ingredients and incorporates a nod to Flemish cuisine into his no-nonsense dishes. Whether you order the intensely flavoured typical Southern French fish soup or côte de bœuf served with a house-made béarnaise sauce and fried potatoes: at Rijsel, every dish is a feast!

Name: Alma Bodega
Description: The more down-to-earth little brother of MICHELIN-starred Alma has its own personality. Chic marble and stylish design give this laid-back restaurant flair. You can drop in any time of day to indulge in a fresh take on familiar flavours. The menu features a variety of dishes that will tempt your taste buds, including gyoza, köfte, pâté en croûte, perfectly done entrecôte with a delicious veal jus, rum baba and more. The skilfully prepared and generously flavoured dishes never fail to impress. Curated by Malou Hagenaars, the wine list always includes some exciting finds. Be sure to make your reservation in good time to avoid disappointment!

Name: Bistro TWO
Description: If you're craving comfort food and a glass of fine wine, Dux hotel's vibrant bistro, with its lovely terrace on Roerkade promenade, is the place for you. With an extensive à la carte selection and a more playful set menu created by Lambert Walter, there's something to suit every taste. A duck liver terrine to start? Then perhaps Livar pork belly with an exquisite shallot sauce, freshly cut fries and a salad with a zingy vinaigrette? Or would you prefer their Mediterranean aubergine dish, before finally tucking into your tarte Tatin? Here, familiar flavours are given a subtle modern twist, without skimping on the portions – and its fantastic value for money!

Name: Witlof
Description: With the view of the River Waal, the jovial hostess and the chef who you see cooking as you make your way to use the facilities, at the Witlof, you will immediately feel at home. Jurgen Eikholt lovingly prepares classic cuisine with his trademark sophisticated, often oriental touches. Each dish on the menu can be ordered as a large or small portion.

Name: Brasserij Kok Verhoeven
Description: Take the left-hand door to a fashionable, cosmopolitan restaurant offering delicious fish and shellfish. Or, the right-hand door to the more relaxed brasserie with an extensive menu (again largely fish), which will win guests over with its quality and powerful flavours.

Name: Bistrobar Berlin
Description: This vibrant bistro-bar shares its avant-garde spirit with Berlin. Choose a spot in which to enjoy the restaurant’s home-grown creativity: the music is louder downstairs, while upstairs you’ll find more comfort. The cooking is modern and daring and the menu is international and eclectic – don’t miss the Kreuzberg dumplings with frankfurter sausage!

Name: Rotonde
Description: They pick up their vegetables in a van which runs on biogas obtained by composting their waste. The aim is to utilise every part of their produce, which is grown with respect for nature and the seasons. Only biodynamic and natural wines are on offer. Sustainability is at the heart of the ethos of Rotonde, which is constantly seeking to improve itself. This vision translates into creative, intriguing taste sensations which are sophisticated and full of surprises. A spot by the open kitchen is a must if you want to watch the chefs tame the flames of their wood-fired barbecue!

Name: La Vie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The 'living room' of the Hotel Valuas is a cosy luxury brasserie that is open all day long. Generous breakfasts, pastries or afternoon snacks, an enticing à la carte menu and a three-course set menu... there's something for everyone. The chef takes his inspiration from classic French cuisine and selects high-quality (often local) ingredients – and it's outstanding value for money. A seat on the terrace, overlooking the River Meuse, is a must!

Name: Bistro Aragosta
Description: The Aragosta has the warm, intimate feel of a bistro, where your welcoming host will introduce you to cuisine that is mainly French in feel with the occasional Italian influence, ranging from seafood risotto to duck terrine. Overall, the cooking here is classical, highly subtle and very tasty!

Name: Arles
Description: Arles brings Provence to Amsterdam. The prints on the walls of this bustling little bistro hark back to the hometown of the chef, who also shares his love of jazz music here (get a table in the dining room at the front if you prefer a quieter space). His culinary style is neo-bistro – a fresh take on the familiar flavours of French cuisine. Think the earthy flavour of beef cheeks cooked in red wine with buttery carrots or a new take on rice pudding. The set menu changes monthly and offers unbeatable value for money!

Name: Bistrot Regent
Description: Why travel all the way to France when you can dine at this timeless bistro, where the best of what the country has to offer is showcased in both the excellent wine list and traditional dishes? Think aromatic fish soup with rouille and croutons, or butter-soft duck leg confit with a zesty caper sauce, followed by crisp tarte Tatin for dessert. You can tell that Robbert and Heleen put their heart and soul into running Bistrot Regent.

Name: Restaurant ñ
Description: The yellow façade of this relaxed restaurant gives it a southern feel, which is further enhanced by the aromas of typical, authentic Spanish and Mediterranean dishes that greet you as you step through the door. The delicious options on the menu include fresh seafood, spicy chilli peppers, and dishes served with fresh, sophisticated sauces, as well as an excellent selection of cheese and charcuterie.

Name: 't Nieuwe Diekhuus
Description: This old thatch-roofed farm on the banks of the Yssel provides a charming setting (including a terrace with a stunning view of the river) in which you’ll feel immediately at ease. To this splendid backdrop, enjoy international delicacies (often with an Asian influence) prepared with top-quality ingredients and well-crafted garnishes that provide the perfect accompaniment. Generous cuisine that is well thought out yet gentle on the pocket!

Name: Bistrôt Chapeau
Description: Experience the charm of its colourful bistro decor, the peace and quiet of the terrace and a soothing ambience in this restaurant straight out of quintessential Burgundy! Here, Nicky Quarz revives often forgotten French classics without any unnecessary frivolity yet teeming with authentic flavours. Through his sauces, intensity etc, enjoy a welcome return to the very roots of French cuisine.

Name: Huson
Description: Huson is a trendy establishment where a lively industriousness always prevails. Here guests' mouths will water at the marvellous pairing of creativity with international ingredients in small dishes which are as subtle as they are exuberant. The chef is a dab hand at beautifully balancing fullness of flavour with freshness, as his signature dishes show.

Name: De Watermolen
Description: The watermill dating back to 1391 is the main attraction of this rustic restaurant, although of course the warmth of the place and lively terrace are also a draw. The chef sometimes opts for more modern techniques, but mainly serves honest, traditional dishes. Vegetarians always have good options here, including the set menu.

Name: Restaurant élevé
Description: A superlative view from the top of the WTC Hotel over Leeuwarden is underscored by a hip, casually welcoming ambience. The restaurant is both affordable and yet exclusive. Chef Kalkman’s cooking is modern, subtle and free of unnecessary frills. You can expect premium local produce, jazzed up with the occasional modern twist and generous flavours.

Name: Bistro LOF
Description: The essence of nature permeates the ambience in this former farmhouse in Parc Broekhuizen, which is now a restaurant with a splendid timber framework. This is a laid-back restaurant with a modern yet rustic feel, where the experienced chef draws inspiration from Dutch produce, including from the surrounding kitchen garden. He showcases premium vegetables in a vibrant appetiser, for example, or elevates farmhouse chicken with a celeriac cream infused with curry and a rich jus. Despite their unassuming descriptions, the dishes – underpinned by modern ideas – pack a punch with their deep flavours. Cleverly devised, sophisticated and indulgent.

Name: Waers
Description: Waers is the incarnation of anti-conformity, which sums up Dennis Vermeulen to a T! In his restaurant showcasing a strong sense of Scandinavian purity, he brings out the very best of market-fresh ingredients and the seasons. There’s no fuss here, just original, well-balanced dishes with a contemporary feel that are well worth discovering and offer excellent value for money.

Name: Gym & Gin
Description: The name Gym & Gin is a reference to the balance we all have to find between pleasure and healthy living. After a workout in the gym upstairs, unwind in this lounge-like establishment with its vintage colour scheme and designer furniture. The cocktail/gin list as well as Kevin Valkhoff's set menu and à la carte options are all as impressive as each other. Inspired by exotic subtleties, he brings flavours to life with original flashes of inspiration, such as adding red pepper to cucumber and mango in order to give salmon some extra pep. If you fancy an afternoon aperitif and a light bite, the good news is that Gym & Gin is always open.

Name: Oriole
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Oriole is a haven of calm in the bustling city centre. The upscale bistro decor is alluring – the bar is terrific – though a spot on the verdant terrace is really the place to be. This is quite the hidden gem! The contemporary take on Mediterranean flavours, with a particular emphasis on vegetables, suits the setting perfectly. The "Oriole Express" set menu, with different options for each course, showcases the cuisine and produce of a given country every month. Whether you're tucking into grilled pimientos de Padrón, pâté en croûte or frango estufado with chicken, this Mediterranean-style feast is authentic, exquisite and inspired.

Name: Poortman
Description: Having been around for more than a century, Poortman has evolved from a café-style eatery into a proper restaurant where authentic memories add to the friendly atmosphere. Dutch classics such as veal tongue with pointed cabbage and hazenpeper (hare stew) with red cabbage are prepared with just as much skill as international specialities including ceviche or the celeriac-based dish. The dishes on the menu are certainly hearty but in no way lacking in finesse – the game jus, for example, is testament to this. At Poortman, flavour reigns supreme!

Name: Gaar
Description: The world is Joachim Müller's culinary playground. Generous dishes such as Limburg pork terrine or crispy tortilla with Asian-style marinated tuna and wasabi give expression to the chef's sense of fun. The extensive and varied menu never disappoints, and diners will enjoy the interesting wine pairings. Chef Joachim and front-of-house manager Myrthe make it their mission to show guests a good time. The pops of turquoise in the decor are in keeping with the convivial spirit of this place.

Name: Specht
Description: This restaurant in a little side street in the city centre is a wonderfully cosy setting for a pleasant tête-à-tête or meal among friends. Diners can expect delicious traditional Viennese cuisine prepared using local ingredients. The pretty interior combining modern design, wooden floors, dark green wall panelling and partially vaulted ceilings creates a warm atmosphere. There is a U-Bahn station conveniently located close by.

Name: Mochi
Description: A lively, informal restaurant serving authentic Japanese cuisine with some more modern twists, at very moderate prices. You can watch the chefs at work, preparing sushi rolls, yakitori or gyu don. At lunchtime, the food is served in bowls; in the evening the presentation is a bit more elaborate. Tables are much sought after, so book early!

Name: Meierei im Stadtpark
Description: One floor below the Reitbauer’s gourmet restaurant, you’ll find another upmarket eatery. Alongside some 150 wonderfully matured cheeses, it boasts delicious classics like Wiener schnitzel of suckling calf. Or perhaps you’d prefer a whole Arctic char or some venison goulash? Attractive terrace facing the Stadtpark.

Name: Vestibül
Description: With a penchant for seasonal and regional produce, this restaurant serves flavoursome culinary delights such as freshwater fish dishes or classics like Wiener schnitzel. The imposing historical building, which also houses the famous Burgtheater, makes for a unique location with a stylish interior that has a typically Viennese feel with its striking columns and gorgeous stuccowork.

Name: Gasthof Auerhahn
Description: Run with great dedication, this friendly, family-owned restaurant is located at a slight remove from the city centre, close to the train station, but it's well worth making the detour for the excellent food. The cuisine is regional, seasonal and pleasingly down-to-earth. Their appealing range of dishes includes venison ragout with bread dumplings and chanterelles, as well as delicious desserts such as Topfenknödel (curd dumplings). Order à la carte or opt for the set menu, which comprises three to five courses – a vegetarian version is also available. Dine in the inviting interior or out on the charming terrace to the rear of the building. The adjoining hotel has well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: MAST Weinbistro
Description: Set in a historical town house, this trendy place is a winning combination of modern wine bar and upscale bistro. It is very popular for its great food, is made with seasonal ingredients sourced from local producers – and at fantastic value for money. Organic and biodynamic wines are recommended to accompany your choice of dishes. There is an appealing outdoor dining area, too.

Name: Carnozet
Description: Tastefully done out in a modern take on Alpine style, this restaurant provides both excellent food and friendly service. The menu features an appealing selection of seasonal dishes, mostly made from locally sourced produce. We highly recommend the grey cattle goulash with Walser Knöpfle (similar to spaetzle).

Name: ONYX
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The location is fantastic! On the sixth floor of DO & CO Hotel in the avant-garde Haas building, a trendy restaurant with a lounge feel awaits. It boasts a breathtaking view of St Stephen's Cathedral – a table by the large floor-to-ceiling windows is practically a must! The menu features exciting Asian dishes designed for sharing, along with sushi, sashimi and specialities from the Robata grill.

Name: Woracziczky
Description: Diners are given a warm welcome In this pleasingly informal inn (pronounced "Vorashitsky"). Both its laid-back atmosphere and Viennese cuisine are a hit, with house specialities such as beef tartare with avocado, or Tafelspitz (boiled veal) served with a creamy chanterelle sauce. The reasonably priced lunchtime set menu, which changes daily, is especially popular.

Name: Divinis
Description: You’ll find this intimate, homely restaurant tucked away on a side street; it’s run with great passion and has a friendly feel. Rustic, seasonal Italian dishes have original touches and are cooked with flair. The perfect accompaniment comes in the form of a large collection of wines from Italian growers.

Name: Dejvická 34 by Tomáš Černý
Description: Chef-owner Tomaš Černy worked in the best Italian restaurants in the city for many years before opening his own charming neighbourhood restaurant north of the river. The menu mixes Czech and Italian dishes and showcases some top quality imported ingredients. Dishes are robust and packed with flavour.

Name: The Eatery
Description: This highly regarded restaurant in the suburbs delivers much more than its name and industrial styling first imply. The menu evolves from day to day, in line with the latest seasonal produce, and is accompanied by a superb wine list. Ask for a seat at the counter to witness the efficiency of the kitchen team.

Name: Na Kopci
Description: Leave the city behind and escape to this buzzy bistro, whose name means ‘on the hill’. The wallpaper is a montage of pictures of the owner’s family and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. Classic Czech and French dishes are packed with flavour and the local beers make a great accompaniment.

Name: Eska
Description: A café, bakery and restaurant in a converted fabric factory. The dining room has a stark, industrial feel with exposed bricks, pipework and girders, and the open kitchen adds to the buzz. Old family favourites are given modern makeovers; much use is made of traditional techniques like marinating and fermenting.

Name: Skof
Address: 3 Federation Street, Manchester, M4 4BF, United Kingdom
Description: Located in an old textile warehouse, this restaurant from former L’Enclume Executive Chef Tom Barnes gives a nod to Manchester’s industrial heritage with its exposed brickwork and girders. The cooking skilfully blends measured Japanese influences with those from the restaurant’s doorstep; for dessert, you’re just as likely to get amakase sorbet as you are Manchester honey ice cream. The meal ends with a scoop of “Barney’s Tiramisu”, touchingly inspired by Tom’s late father. A relaxed atmosphere is encouraged, with the chef’s hand-picked playlist and the chattering diners combining for a brilliant buzz.

Name: Albatross Death Cult
Address: Newhall Square, Jewellery Quarter, Birmingham, B3 1RU, United Kingdom
Description: It is key, when structuring your restaurant around a kitchen counter, that you provide an engaging, relaxing experience for your guests. This is something that is perfectly understood by the team at this eye-catchingly named restaurant, inspired by the albatross in Coleridge's 'The Rime of the Ancient Mariner'. Everyone, from the chefs to the sommelier, is full of enthusiasm and confidently chats away with diners throughout the experience. The food itself carries a heavy Japanese influence, with the tasting menu consisting almost entirely of pared-back preparations spotlighting top-notch seafood, with plenty of raw and cured dishes among them.

Name: Julie's
Address: 135 Portland Road, North Kensington, London, W11 4LW, United Kingdom
Description: Judging by the amount of diners flooding through its doors, the residents of Notting Hill are glad to have this bright bistro de-luxe among their roster of neighbourhood haunts. Inside, it’s an eye-catching place with rich, warming colours and booths that are perfect for date night. The menu offers an appealing range of dishes, from the light (chopped salad of the day) to the luxurious (lobster soufflé). The extensive wine list and cocktails from the trolley will ensure you’re well-refreshed, while the service team are friendly and engaging.

Name: The Coach House
Address: Main Street, Roundwood, A98 P635, Ireland
Description: A complete top-to-toe refurbishment has left this former Victorian coaching inn looking fabulous, with an aesthetic that could be best described as shabby-chic meets Irish country house. The front bar has been retained, making this still feel very much like a pub, while the large, airy dining room provides a great setting for dishes that come free of gimmicks or over-elaboration, instead showing off the natural flavours of the produce, such as quality cod from the Irish Sea. There is a welcome originality too, as when offering beef cheeks in a bun instead of the classic pub burger.

Name: Volta Do Mar
Address: 100 Draycott Avenue, Chelsea, London, SW3 3AD, United Kingdom
Description: Volta Do Mar may have relocated to a new premises, but as the team here will tell you, its soul is very much unchanged. The cooking remains a tribute to the cuisine not just of Portugal, but of the countries it established trade routes with centuries ago, hence the restaurant's name meaning 'to return from the sea'. So expect to find Goan curry sitting alongside piri piri chicken from Mozambique, as well as dishes from Brazil and Macau. The intimate room is decorated with colourful modern artwork, mirroring the vibrancy of the cooking.

Name: Roe
Address: 5 Park Drive, Tower Hamlets, London, W14 9GG, United Kingdom
Description: Launched by the team behind Fallow, this vast restaurant can house up to 500 diners in the heart of Canary Wharf, all while being run with impressive slickness. Guests are spread across several dining rooms, some with counter seating, plus a lovely wrap-around terrace that boasts commanding views of South Dock. The wide-ranging menu offers something for everyone, including playful takes on British classics like maitake Cornish pasty or market fish served with parsley liquor, that's reminiscent of an East End pie and mash.

Name: Camille
Address: 2-3 Stoney Street, Southwark, London, SE1 9AA, United Kingdom
Description: Situated at the entrance to the foodie wonderland that is Borough Market, this intimate French bistro is rooted in an ethos of unpretentious, pared-back cooking that perfectly suits its rustic interior design. The blackboard-written menu is regularly changing, and you can expect straightforward yet eminently satisfying dishes like pâté-en-croûte or whole mackerel with café de Paris butter. A friendly welcome and cheery service ensure you’ll be dining with a smile on your face.

Name: daróg
Address: 56 Lower Dominick Street, Galway, H91 K225, Ireland
Description: There’s a huge amount of passion channelled into this welcoming little wine bar. Hungarian-born Zsolt Lukács has an infectious enthusiasm for wine, which comes across in his carefully curated list that gravitates towards small artisan producers using organic and biodynamic methods. Accompanying the wine is a selection of sharing plates – like kingfish crudo – that are exactingly executed, deliver on flavour and provide brilliant value for money. The regularly changing artwork from local artists is on sale and is curated by co-owner Edel.

Name: Bistro Air du Temps
Address: Rue de la Croix Monet 2, Liernu, 5310, Belgium
Description: The square farmstead, in which chef Sang Hoon Degeimbre works his magic in the kitchen of the high-flying L’Air du Temps (evenings only), is also home to a country chic bistro (open for lunch only). Meals are served beneath a canopy of greenery or alfresco in fine weather. Chef Denis has adapted the house DNA into bistro recipes. The result is a cornucopia of bold associations and an abundance of veggies, Asian influences and innovative techniques. For example, the chef may pair pork belly with a frothy espuma of potatoes and coffee, salty caviar and spinach leaves with a subtle olive vinaigrette. Ideal for a bistro lunch with a difference!

Name: Cella
Description: One half of the restaurant commands a view of the kitchen team crafting all sorts delicacies, while the other overlooks the Antwerp docks and skyline. There is never a dull moment at Cella, starting with the industrial cachet of this stylishly repurposed warehouse by the team that used to run Het Pomphuis. The menu features a tempting lineup of pedigree Belgian fare with matured meat grilled over charcoal embers, fresh fries and a last-minute sauce, together with a smattering of ubiquitous international dishes of the likes of ceviche and sushi. Flawless technique and aromatic sauces are the hallmark of the gifted chef.

Name: 't Gasthuis by InstroomArt
Description: Seppe Nobels, Charuwan Pauwels and Nico Dockx make no bones about the fact that they source the majority of their produce from sustainable farms in the Mechelen region, in line with an ethos that naturally encompasses their HR policy. The result is international cuisine by a youthful generation of Europeans, keen to tell their story at your table. Examples of dishes you may sample include a Ukrainian borscht of red beetroot or al dente asparagus with Palestinian moussaka made with mushrooms and sumac with a lemon thyme mousse and parsley root fries. The stories are fascinating, as is the artwork that adorns the different areas of this former inn. This restaurant demonstrates that there is more to a sustainable future than just ingredients.

Name: Compagnique
Description: Ideal for a romantic date night, this charming farmstead is the quintessence of poised and intimate and only offers tables for two (but there is a private room that caters to groups). Working hand in hand, Angélique manages the front-of-house while Tim runs the kitchen, in a bid to provide a personalised experience. Luxury ingredients enjoy the leading role on the menu and the chef might sign a high-flying combination of oysters and seaweed, caviar and a distinctive beurre blanc made out of curds. He has a soft spot for fresh, tangy notes, illustrated by the subtle sauce vierge that contrasts so wonderfully with the mild yet sweet flesh of turbot. A mouthwatering prospect…

Name: Jean-Philippe
Description: Jean-Philippe and Sara-Sofia have crafted a cosy cocoon in this townhouse. Artwork by Isidoor Goddeeris underscores the restaurant’s classy interior and reflects the chef’s love of seafood. The couple’s experience shines through in every detail. Sara-Sofia seamlessly manages the front of house, while presenting her latest cocktails. Jean-Philippe draws on his flawless technical background as he works with outstanding ingredients. Examples include wild seabass, grilled to keep the skin crispy and flanked by different textures of fennel, a baby artichoke and characterful crab bisque. This consummate chef, a master of delicacy, has a way with flavour and gutsy sauces that is second to none.

Name: Sardis
Description: Tiziano Cappai welcomes diners warmly into this stylish red-brick terraced house, which boasts a cosy interior, sensual artwork on the walls and a blissfully peaceful patio at the rear. Chef Eveline Cappai deftly updates a pure-bred lineup of Italian classics. For example, she might pair bigoli pasta with a subtle stock, to which she adds white wine, parsley, savoury vongole and a hint of umami thanks to kombu. The tiramisu manages to underscore authentic flavours with an amusing new spin thanks to a play on textures. Attention to detail is the watchword here.

Name: Qin
Description: Emperor Qin provided the inspiration for the team at the helm of the restaurant of Hotel Keiser, hence the dark wood furnishings, soft red fabrics and oriental details like Chinese lanterns and paintings. The Cantonese culinary lineup is the quintessence of authentic, albeit subtly updated to suit today’s palates. The varied range of home-made dim sum dishes are characteristic of this ethos. Stuffed with chopped wagyu beef and a black pepper Chinese sauce, or with ginger and taro - piping hot delicacies that embody the generous character of this aromatic cuisine.

Name: Flamme
Description: Flames and fire are central to this buzzy gourmet bistro. Entirely open, the kitchen provides a fascinating insight into how the food is smoked, roasted and grilled. The menu may be concise, but making your choice remains a challenge. Veggies take the star role in big-boned recipes. Slices of celeriac are roasted like shawarma, rubbed with pitta spices and flanked by a garlic sauce. Or would you prefer pleurote mushrooms cooked over the open fire with a tempura of enoki mushrooms and marinated vegetables? You can trust the wine tips of the smiling, spontaneous lady of the house with your eyes closed.

Name: Nova
Description: Tineke and Guy have left their stamp on this stylish townhouse steeped in serenity and tucked away in a working-class district near the Grand Place. We warrant that Tineke’s natural charm and Guy’s creative way with seasonal produce will win you over. Take a seat at the counter or at a table with a view of the chef and get ready to be bowled over by the surprise (or à la carte) menu, depending on availability. The chef works closely with local producers and rolls out an ethical zero waste farm-to-table concept. While barbecue flavours take the limelight in his culinary score, he might also make a ‘loaf’ out of old bread and a bisque of shrimp heads, jazzed up with fennel and a cream of veggies, or just with brown shrimp and wild fennel. Most definitely a restaurant with a soul.

Name: De la terre à l'assiette
Address: Rue de la Poste 13, Arlon, 6700, Belgium
Description: Magali and Guillaume Lempens’ colourful venue is the quintessence of comfortable and steeped in feelgood vibes, a large proportion of which are courtesy of their bistronomic cuisine. The latter includes fried cod flanked by a subtle bouillabaisse, white asparagus, homemade gnocchi and a knockout aioli mayonnaise. Big-boned, punchy sauces and impeccable technique bear witness to the experience of seasoned chef Guillaume. Rather than fussy frills, you can expect wholehearted authenticity and no-nonsense rustic fare.

Name: Bakea
Description: This minimalist-style restaurant, with its dominant dark colour scheme, pays homage to the local terroir, iron, fire, arts and crafts, and to those meals with family and friends that are forever engraved on our memory. The large central table recalls the spirit of traditional Basque dining societies known as “txokos”, given that the idea here is for guests to share different dishes and experiences. From the unique wood-fired grill, designed by the chef himself, and the space used for hot smoking, the team creates a single, highly personal tasting menu with strong roots in the Basque Country that is always constructed around just a few well-balanced ingredients, all of which are sourced locally and are fully respectful of the seasons.

Name: Sushi Bar Hannah
Description: Behind the discreet façade of the Sushi Bar Hannah, located in a narrow street next to the luxurious Rosewood Villa Magna hotel, you’ll find a Japanese restaurant home to the full mystique of the Orient. Its soups, pickles, sashimis, nigiris, makis, tempuras, as well as its steamed and charcoal-grilled dishes, are part of the varied culinary repertoire of London chef Janek Flemyng, who creates technically adept cuisine that is fully respectful of tradition. This is complemented by two highly interesting tasting menus (both of which need to be booked a minimum of 24hr ahead): the Kaiseki menu, with its strong focus on meticulous detail; and the Omakase, which places more emphasis on seasonal fish and seafood. We recommend sitting at the bar counter, where you’ll be able to best appreciate the chef’s skills.

Name: Rocacho Plaza
Address: Plaza del Marqués de Salamanca 9, Madrid, 28006, Spain
Description: Located in the heart of the city’s Salamanca district, Rocacho Plaza boasts a pleasant terrace and a menu that focuses on grilled dishes. Among its choice of meats, the selection from El Capricho, the famous farm in Jiménez de Jamuz in the province of León, are a real draw, including its premium “Selección José Gordón” ox chop and its beef chop aged for 90 days. It also offers market-inspired dishes, recipes featuring seasonal vegetables, superb grilled fish, and rice and fideuá options. It also occasionally hosts full-day food events such as those dedicated to the delicious oxtail.

Name: Varra
Description: This restaurant in the elegant Salamanca district of the city is run by two young chefs, Jorge Velasco and Joaquín Serrano, and is usually full every day. It offers two highly distinct dining concepts: the informal Varra Fina on the ground floor (with a bar and bare tables), focusing on tapas such as Joselito ham croquettes, crispy bull’s ears, Russian salad etc), and the gourmet restaurant called Varra, upstairs. In the latter, somewhat confined in space but with a more refined decor and an exclusive menu completely different to Varra Fina the floor below, the level of cuisine rises several notches thanks to options such as snow peas with green asparagus and ham, and the chicken cannelloni with a truffled bechamel sauce and game jus. Make sure you book ahead and specify where you want to eat.

Name: Shibui
Address: Paseo Milicias de Garachico 1, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, 38002, Spain
Description: This Japanese restaurant occupies the space that was formerly the Kazan and can be viewed as a reinvention of the latter. And although chef Gerardo Cruz is at the helm, the award-winning David Arauz (Zuara Sushi, Madrid) still oversees the cuisine here. The word “shibui” refers to the Japanese aesthetic of beauty and minimalism, and as such the aim here is to see beauty in everything around us, including its imperfections, from a respectful and mature standpoint. The à la carte is complemented by the excellent Shibui menu as well as an Omakase-style option that takes guests on a journey of gastronomic discovery. Whatever you choose, as you take a seat at the bar you will develop an even greater appreciation of the Japanese mystique of each dish. The team mainly works with the freshest quality fish caught daily off the island’s coastline. We can also highly recommend the traditional nigiris, created by hand one by one.

Name: LUR
Description: Taking its name from the Basque word for “earth”, this unpretentious yet welcoming restaurant boasts a contemporary decor that includes earthenware jars adorned with large tree-like olive branches. The young chef in charge here, Lucía Gutiérrez, is keen that the land and its soil are brought to life, hence their concise, attractive and modern-inspired menu that is based around seasonal ingredients from small-scale producers. Interesting dishes include the rice with aged partridge cooked on the barbecue and served with blood orange, Requesón cheese and Oloroso sherry, and the Tierra de Campos pigeon stew.

Name: Sa Taula
Address: Segundo Ispizua 27, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20001, Spain
Description: Eating at this diminutive restaurant, in the heart of the Gros district, is like being welcomed to the home of a good friend, such is the warm welcome and the glass of Cava almost imperceptibly placed in your hand on arrival. The two owner-chefs, Carlos and Manel, cook, chat, serve and wash the dishes, seemingly at the same time, and in a highly relaxed atmosphere given that they only attend to a maximum ten guests per sitting, all eating together. They work with a single surprise menu, usually based around ingredients sourced from small-scale local producers. Drinks are included in the price.

Name: Prebe by Bret
Cuisine: Farm to table, Meats and Grills
Description: Bret Fernández, the chef at the helm of this restaurant named after the Galician word for “sauce”, defines his culinary concept by the mantra “celebration, abundance and satisfaction". At this tapas bar-style eatery located along a pedestrianised street in Lugo’s old quarter, you’ll find quotes by leading Galician writers plus a meticulous dining room with a rustic feel on the first floor, the latter also boasting an ageing cabinet. The extensive à la carte features hints of fusion, and showcases an impressive array of beef (Friesian, Rubia Gallega etc) and fish (both whole and different cuts, all cooked on the grill). An array of daily specials is also available here.

Name: Mambo
Description: This highly original eatery, with its attractive and informal bistro-style ambience, is the fiefdom of Brazilian-born chef Gabriel Conti. He arrived in Palma having spent many years working in Barcelona, which enabled him to acquire a rucksack full of different culinary experiences and expertise, which he now highlights, in particular, in dishes prepared on the grill. If you decide to eat at one of the four seats at the bar counter, the chef will be happy to share the secrets of his dishes with you step by step.

Name: Local de Ensayo
Description: Located just a few steps from the cathedral, with a completely revamped concept that comes as a pleasant surprise in a setting occupying the former home of the equally successful Ajo y Agua restaurant. The contemporary and elegant interior features an initial dining room with a large table for groups, and then a second dining space from where the kitchen is partially visible to guests. Here, chef David López conjures up cuisine that is high on presentation and showcases a strong creative flair that he describes as “experimentation", with an extensive à la carte and no fewer than three tasting menus (Tradición, Endocardio and Desfibrilador).

Name: Bacaro
Description: This restaurant, steeped in the essence of Italy but which the team describes as a “Venetian taberna”, is located just a few steps from the emblematic Boquería market, and is one of those places you look forward to visiting given the caring and kindness in evidence as soon as you walk through the door. Bistro in style, and split between two floors, it boasts an eclectic yet simple decor, the idea being not to interfere too much with what is really important, namely the food! The latter is clearly rooted in Italian tradition, with a continual emphasis on flavour. You’ll find pasta here, of course, but don’t miss the typical sardines “in saor”, the Venetian-style veal liver, or the marvellous tiramisù. As you would expect, the wine list includes some classic Italian labels.

Name: Yakitori Kiyu
Description: The chefs’ busy hands deftly grill the chicken as the enticing aroma of Korean tojongdak chicken yakitori fills the entire space. The experienced chefs who grill each cut of tojongdak to perfection add extra charm to each dish. The restaurant uses chickens that are naturally raised on various medicinal herbs so diners can experience healthy, quality cuts of chicken. The menu features unlaid chicken eggs, or chochin, (which means lantern in Japanese), that can only be obtained when an egg-laying hen is slaughtered, highlighting the freshness of the ingredients. Kiyu's goal is to study the attributes of tojongdak to take the flavors of yakitori to the next level, is the place to enjoy delicious yakitori.

Name: ALT.a
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This is a Korean-Chinese restaurant that uses all plant-based ingredients including plant-based alternative meats. That’s right. It’s a vegan Chinese restaurant. Chinese food made without any meat piqued my curiosity. They create incredible flavors that are sure to entice even diners who aren’t familiar with vegan food. The food is also low-fat so it’s easy on the stomach. They serve vegan jjamppong and fried dishes like tangsuyuk and yurinyuk that are so delightfully bouncy and chewy that no one will notice that they aren’t made from real meat. It is both a great vegan and a great Chinese restaurant.

Name: Okdol Heyonok
Description: Taste the deeply savory broth and the nutty flavor of the noodles made from 100% buckwheat that intensifies the more you chew at Okdol Hyeonok. The restaurant is fairly new, but it has gained a solid following among Pyongyang naengmyeon connoisseurs. Some of their most popular dishes are mandu with a nuttiness that comes from plenty of tofu in the filling, eobok jaengban, and gajami shikhye. You can also have your favorite wine with your meal for a corkage fee. Enjoy the mild flavors with incredible depth.

Name: RMW Carne
Description: RMW Carne, which is located on the second floor of a renovated old house, isn’t particularly spacious, but you can enjoy your food in a comfortably petite, cozy venue. The restaurant which is named after the first letters of steak doneness - rare, medium, and well-done - dry ages various cuts of beef of a variety of different cattle breeds. Salami, chorizo, pastrami, sausages and other charcuterie, all cured in-house, are available for purchase at the store inside the restaurant. They also serve simpler dishes like grilled vegetables and pasta that can be enjoyed as a light meal or refreshment.

Name: Neungdong Minari
Description: The gomtang at Neungdong Minari is topped with a pile of minari so tall that at a glance, it doesn’t look like a tang at all. The clear, clean broth is made from fresh hanwoo beef that was slaughtered on the day, which is topped with piquant minari that was grown in clear freshwater for added freshness. You should expect a wait, but you will think it is well worth it once you take your first bite.

Name: Manao
Description: Enter Manao, and you will be greeted with exotic vibes bolstered by seek décor and an array of art objects brought directly from Thailand. Its prix-fixe menus consist of multiple dishes in small portions, allowing guests to enjoy a variety of plates in one meal. The kitchen does an excellent job of presenting authentic Thai cuisine with its characteristic spiciness. Another appeal of this spot is that the meat and seafood are grilled to order over charcoal. Manao means “lime” in Thai, and its fare is as refreshing as its name.

Name: Kirameki
Description: Kirameki is a Japanese restaurant that serves a tasting menu centered on rice. I expected rice to be the primary focus of the meal, but after experiencing the meal, but it consisted as a wide array of dishes. The menu is designed around the Japanese washoku, and showcases kaiseki cuisine prepared with seasonal ingredients. Once the ceramic pot rice is served, small morsels of food were served over scoops of aromatic white rice. Each savory bite lingered pleasantly on the palate.

Name: Gomtang Lab
Description: True to its name, Gomtang Lab is dedicated to studying gomtang (beef bone soup) and developing diverse new recipes. Chef Yim Jung-sik has relentlessly pursued this culinary journey since the days when he helmed Pyeonghwaok. His signature dish is collagen beef bone soup, made by simmering beef leg bones, tendons, feet and oxtail for more than 10 hours until thick. Once you finish the bowl brimming with chewy, tender meat and savory broth that make a perfect meal, you’ll find your lips sticky with gelatinous collagen. To cater to different tastes, the menu offers several variations of gomtang, including a clear, meat-only version and a spicy version with added beef tripe. One last note: The signature soup is limited to only 20 bowls per day, so be sure to visit when the eatery opens.

Name: ÎNT
Address: Rooftop F, Best Western Sukhumvit 20, 17 Soi Sukhumvit 20, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Ascend to this rooftop restaurant to soak up an ambiance of elegant earthy tones blended with a subtle blue hue, all set against the warmth of an open kitchen. The tasting menu reflects Chef Patin 'Knock' Promsawadi and his team's unique, artistic approach to simplicity. Using French culinary techniques, he strikes a masterful balance between Thai and French ingredients to produce contemporary dishes that capture the essence of Thai cuisine. Advance booking necessary!

Name: Bisou
Address: 68 Soi Langsuan 9, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Chef Antoine Darquin and sommelier Théo Lavergne bring a fresh, fashionable Parisian flair to Bangkok's dining scene. Bisou delivers sexy simplicity through modern French cuisine, prioritising premium ingredients. The stylish yet relaxed space features enchanting lights, a spiral staircase and wall art. The dishes and rare wines contribute to a unique local experience influenced by the latest trends from Paris.

Name: Morakot Kitchen
Address: 28 Mu 4, Rangsit - Nakhon Nayok Road, Rangsit, Thanyaburi, Pathum Thani, 12110, Thailand
Description: For over 120 years, this no-frills kitchen in a wooden house on a main road has been dishing up intensely flavourful, comforting Thai fare. Don't miss the fish cake, made from authentic spotted featherback fish and heavenly spiced, served with the sweet house-special dipping sauce.

Name: Khao Mun Gai Nha Jone
Address: 119/239 Soi 17 Chumchon Ruansuk 1, Lam Phak Kut, Thanyaburi, Pathum Thani, 12110, Thailand
Description: There's a real buzz about this perpetually busy shop that is worth the drive from Bangkok. The delicious chicken is tender and juicy, served simply with sauces that add a real kick. Opening times are limited as they often sell out within a few hours – a testament to the quality.

Name: Shrimp Noodles Ao Kae
Address: 76 Phoonphol Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: It has been crafting meticulous shrimp noodle bowls for over a decade. Tom yum and original shrimp flavour noodles, available as wet and dry options, come with the perfect number of condiments. Pork wontons are the standout! For intense flavour, try the dry tom yum noodles.

Name: Pa Pleung Mhee Kratok
Address: 1 Mu 8, Chok Chai, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30190, Thailand
Description: Locals flock to Auntie Pleung's for Korat's quintessential noodle dish, Pad Mhee Kratok, served in its purest form – with a soft yet chewy noodle texture that requires no additional seasoning. Her tiny district shop also whips up award-winning spins on Pad Thai and papaya salad.

Name: UNA-VERSE
Address: 268, Section 2, Wuquan West Road, Nantun District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Una, formerly the pastry chef of some distinguished restaurants in town, opened her own venture to serve a multicourse dessert tasting menu, complete with wine and non-alcoholic beverage pairings. Done out in beige and light wood tones, the space feels elegant; counter seats allow diners and the chefs to interact. The menu focuses on modern, sophisticated interpretations of Taiwanese sweets with a French twist and the occasional savoury undertone.

Name: Aleisha
Address: 16, Alley 4, Lane 217, Section 3, Zhongxiao East Road, Da’an District, Taipei, 106080, Taiwan
Description: The Argentinian-Irish owner-chef Nico Gellon crafts a new take on pan-Mediterranean cuisine with eclectic influences. The tasting menu, cooked in purebred Italian or French style and seasoned with Middle Eastern spices, alongside Greek staples such as olives and eggplant. The dishes satisfy both the eye and the tastebud. Choose the counter seats to stay close to the action or book a room for more privacy.

Name: Kohaku
Address: 15, Lane 32, Yixian Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The serene Japanese garden is matched by the minimalist wood-clad room and exquisite tableware. Celebrating a career that spans over 20 years, the Japanese chef serves a single season-driven tasting menu dominated by the freshest catch from Kyushu, Japan. Seasoning is intentionally light-handed and nuanced for diners to appreciate the natural flavours. The soy-free seared sesame tofu appetiser is heavenly. The sake list is short but sweet.

Name: Xiantaosu
Address: 496 Minglun Road, Gushan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: After a long stint in a Taipei vegetarian restaurant, the chef returned to his hometown, piquing curiosity with his refined plant-based cuisine. He serves three set menus with artfully plated courses that layer rich flavours. Varied techniques, such as fermenting, pickling, grilling, braising and searing, are deftly used to great effect. The vegan braised pork rice uses diced monkey head mushrooms instead of pork, creating light, briny umami.

Name: Hsin Hsin
Address: 245, Section 2, Minzu Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: He may be in his 70s, but founder Chef Ah Tu is still hands-on in the kitchen and his restaurant is a veritable institution of vintage Taiwanese cooking. Symbols of joy and good fortune are deeply ingrained in the décor – from the red shop sign to the red tablecloths. There are only 18 items on the menu, including specialities such as fried shrimp with egg, and traditional fried pork liver. Some dishes require pre-ordering.

Name: Da-Wan
Address: 5F, 199 Jingye 2nd Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Da-Wan moved to the shopping streets of Dazhi in late 2021. The dining room adopts a hip, faux-industrial style, with dramatic lighting while at night, the full-height windows let in the electric glow of the department stores nearby. As always, the signature remains Wagyu beef, mostly from Miyazaki prefecture – oyster blade, chuck eye roll, flat iron… grilled to perfection by skilful servers. Thick-cut ox tongue is divinely springy and beefy.

Name: Crab's House
Address: 93 Minsheng 1st Road, Sinsing District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Founded in 1976, this household name was the first restaurant in town specialising in live seafood shipped daily from the island county of Penghu. As you can tell from its name and the giant crab sign, crab is the signature dish, especially the spiced salt and pepper variety. Besides the eponymous crustacean, ask the friendly servers about the catch of the day. Try also the shrimp rolls wrapped in pork caul fat before being deep-fried.

Name: A Ming Zhu Xing (Baoan Road)
Address: 72 Baoan Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: Don’t be surprised if you see a queue even before this shop’s opening at 5pm – after all, its cellophane noodle soup with pork offal is one of the must-try Tainan delicacies for many travellers. Chef A Ming still cooks the offal like his father did almost 70 years ago – in a bain-marie to prevent overcooking. As well as the signature pork heart soup, try pork ribs or duck feet and wings braised in a garlicky herbal stock.

Name: Moment in Beijing
Address: 57 Wuquan 7th Street, West District, Taichung, 403, Taiwan
Description: Named after Lin Yutang's novel and channelling the style of northern China's grand mansions with its gable roof and grey tiles, this well-known restaurant has been building a loyal following since 2002. The menu revolves around northern Chinese classics such as stir-fried shredded pork and vegetables in an omelette "hat" or sautéed lamb loin with a sweet soybean glaze that marries well with rice. There are also Jiangzhe and Taiwanese choices.

Name: Iron Chef Teppanyaki
Address: 2F, 215 Zhifu Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
Description: Along with impressive skills, founder Chef Hsieh with almost 50 years of experience on the griddle is also passionate about Chinese medicine. That’s why the food here is lightly seasoned and cooked in tea seed oil instead of butter. The prix-fixe menus emphasize dietary needs according to the time of the year, without sacrificing gastronomic pleasure. Signatures include U.S. beef sirloin roll, popcorn and soufflé made on the spot.

Name: Fresh & Aged
Address: 2F, 128 Minshan Street, Neihu District, Taipei, 114, Taiwan
Description: Owned by the largest meat importer in Taiwan, Fresh & Aged specialises in premium beef cuts from Nebraska, U.S.A, typically dry-aged for 28 days in a custom-made chamber. Diners can even pre-order steaks dry-aged up to 128 days. Non-beef choices are also ample and include Cherry Valley duck breast and SRF Kurobuta pork dry-aged for 21 days. The annexed supermarket selling a smorgasbord of raw meats is worth checking out. Pre-ordering is recommended.

Name: Papillon
Address: 26F, TAi Urban Resort, 189 Linsen 4th Road, Qianzhen District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Named after the French word for butterfly, the French chef strives to transform quality ingredients into radically different culinary gems. The spacious room, in muted wood tones, is dotted by butterfly motifs with a tree-like centrepiece being the focal point. Only one tasting menu is served and it’s inspired by the chef’s travel across three continents. Exotic elements come through subtly in his refined French cooking.

Name: Yu Yue Lou
Address: 783, Section 2, Gongyi Road, Nantun District, Taichung, 408, Taiwan
Description: The high-ceilinged dining room imparts an imposing sense of space while the gold-and-black colours and dew-like strings of pendant lamps exude drama. The kitchen team from Hong Kong reinvents Cantonese cooking with creativity. Grouper fillet poached in lobster bisque over crisp rice uses live seafood from Penghu. Cherry Valley duck is roasted in a longan wood oven and needs pre-ordering. Dim sum is served at lunch and private rooms are available.

Name: FReNCHIE FReNCHIE
Address: 1F, Fulwon Hotel, 636, Section 2, Wenxin Road, Xitun District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Inspired by mid-century modern aesthetics, this moodily lit space in a longstanding hotel seduces with its curvy lines, dark wood furniture and muted green leather banquettes. The Shanghainese head chef curates the menu according to the season; the set menus offer good value. His must-try French toast, caramelised on the outside, gooey on the inside, transcends your average brekkie fare. Ask the sommelier about wine or tea pairing options.

Name: Yuan Huan Pien Oyster Egg Omelette
Address: Ningxia Night Market, 46 Ningxia Road, Datong District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Has been making its tasty omelettes, with oysters from Tainan drizzled in homemade sweet hot sauce, since 1965.

Name: Gi Yuan
Address: 324, Section 1, Dunhua South Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: Regulars come for the signature chicken soup casserole – it takes 10 hours to make the milky rich chicken stock before free-range chicken, ham, dried scallops and pork trotters are added and cooked for two more hours. Other famed Sichuan dishes are also on the menu, such as dry-fried French beans and Kungpao chicken. Some dishes can be customised with condiments of your choice. It’s always busy so early reservations are recommended.

Name: Paul's Canteen
Address: 162 Sihwei 3rd Road, Linya District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Cash only
Description: The Macanese owner-chef, who has been cooking professionally for over 30 years, opened this bustling spot in 2022. The menu is based on Taiwanese fare, with occasional Cantonese twists, and he seasons his food lightly allowing the natural flavours to shout their name. His deft hand is best sampled in simple dishes like scrambled egg with spinach and tomato – the mild peppery heat, bright colours and light seasonings work together seamlessly. BYOB.

Name: huist
Address: 3, Lane 22, Shengping Street, West District, Taichung, 403, Taiwan
Description: After graduating from culinary school, the owner-chef honed his skills in different places before opening huist (Dutch for "home") in 2023. His prix-fixe menu is inspired by Taiwanese cooking, finessed by Western techniques and has lots of home-style touches: appetising raw scallops marinated in chilli garlic kombu soy; smoked marlin in sugar rub with sliced chicken comb sandwiched between the silky fish for contrasting textures.

Name: Xiang Se
Address: 1-2 Hukou Street, Zhongzheng District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: That the owner is also an antique dealer explains the abundance of exquisite pieces dotting the room. The terrazzo and reclaimed wood flooring also echo with the overall vintage feel. The young chef creates only one fixed price menu based on European traditions, but heavily influenced by South Asian and Tibetian cultures. The intimate ambiance makes it perfect for date nights or casual get-togethers.

Name: Ukai-tei
Address: 3F, Silks Club, 199 Zhongshan 2nd Road, Cianjhen District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The first overseas venture of Japan’s Ukai group greets diners with a circular staircase and a warm-hued interior that exudes understated elegance. On top of witnessing quality ingredients being cooked skilfully on the iron plate right before your eyes, the experience is completed by attentive service. The signature Wagyu menu includes a rump cut for optimal marbling, while Kaohsiung Ukai-tei course predominantly features local seafood.

Name: Shan Shin (West)
Address: 21 Cunzhong Street, West District, Taichung, 403, Taiwan
Description: Health-conscious diners come to this well-lit eatery with views of a manicured garden for creative Taiwanese food made with reduced oil and sodium and, for the most part, traceably sourced ingredients. Some dishes are amusingly named, e.g. "When Huadiao Meets Cherry Valley Duck" (duck sliced and cooked in the famous liquor). The seasonal offerings are worth trying; set menus are great for big parties. The trilingual menu makes tourists feel welcome.

Name: Plum Chang
Description: The owner’s family used to run a plum farm in the neighbourhood. In the 1990s, they opened this restaurant, incorporating the tangy stone fruit into their recipes. Diners’ favourites include plum-scented pork, egg tofu in plum sauce, and stir-fried pork intestines with sour plums. There is a shop selling plums next door and the Meiling Scenic Area nearby is a famous viewing spot for plum blossom in winter. It’s best to book at the weekend.

Name: Principe
Address: 34 Xihua Street, North District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: The wood-rich interior is homely and understated, matching the elegant food with its meticulous attention to detail. The chef honed his skills in Japan and his prix-fixe menu recounts Tainan’s culinary stories with classic French techniques, Japanese influences and ethereal touches. The amuse-bouche is always inspired by a Tainanese snack, while produce from small local farms, such as local beef, takes centre stage in many courses.

Name: Zan
Address: B1, 192-1, Section 4, Chengde Road, Shilin District, Taipei, 111, Taiwan
Description: A mishmash of different styles seems to work miraculously here – Italian stained glass window and a marble counter are juxtaposed with Chinese wooden furniture and silver cutlery. The chef was trained in one of most prestigious teppanyaki restaurants in Japan and has over 40 years of experience under his belt. Signatures include U. S. SRF Wagyu, braised abalone in kombu salt, and prawn with French sauce. Hida beef is also available for pre-ordering.

Name: Shan Nay Chicken
Address: Nanjichang Night Market, Stall 3, 20-3, Lane 307, Section 2, Zhonghua Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Good-value steamed chicken is feted for its springy skin and juicy flesh. Come before 8 pm for chicken legs.

Name: Shing-Peng-Lai (Zhongshan North Road)
Address: 55, Section 7, Zhongshan North Road, Shilin District, Taipei, 111, Taiwan
Description: Since 1987, this joint has been popular for get-togethers among family and friends on account of its remarkable traditional Taiwanese fare. With an array of both home-style dishes and banquet classics, the menu features sharing plates and comforting staples that deliver big flavours. Try signatures such as boiled free-range chicken, and Buddha Jumps Over The Wall. Taiwan-style ice lollies at the end of the meal are the icing on the cake.

Name: Set.
Address: 110, Section 2, Chengde Road, Datong District, Taipei, 103, Taiwan
Description: Far from being stuffy or overly formal, this fine dining spot boasts a friendly, laid-back vibe. Inspired by personal experiences, nature and the seasons, the dishes are underpinned by solid Western technique and packed with Asian flavours. The chef couple gives kitchen scraps a new lease of life as house-made condiments, such as mushroom chilli paste with pumpkin skin, in a bid for zero waste. The wine list comprises natural choices only.

Name: AKIN
Address: 8, Lane 92, Section 1, Jianguo North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan
Description: Chef Ah-kin hails from Hong Kong and Akin is a love letter to his homeland. The single tasting menu changes with the seasons, but the distinctive Hong Kong influence remains. His deep-fried sea urchin and purple shiso puff pastry is a nod to Hong Kong’s dim sum radish puff. Next to the Yitong Park, the understated elegant interior exudes natural earthy tones around an open kitchen. Concise wine list - ask the sommelier for pairing tips.

Name: 44 SV
Address: 10, Alley 33, Lane 216, Section 4, Zhongxiao East Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The founder used to live in Forty-Four South Village, one of Taiwan's many juan-cun – post-war villages for military families. At this cosy bistro, he cooks spruced-up, refined juan-cun classics using quality ingredients. His signature red braised pork belly is made with caramelised sugar and honey instead of soy sauce for exceptional depth. All items need to be pre-ordered two days ahead; small à la carte menu for add-ons only.

Name: Capstone Steakhouse
Address: 1F, H2O Hotel, 366 Minghua Road, Gushan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: The first outpost of Danny’s Steakhouse outside of Taipei shares the same design motifs with its flagship – a high-ceilinged, spacious dining room with a mezzanine glass cellar and a show kitchen behind a glass wall. The set menu follows suit and is also the same as its Taipei sister, offering multiple choices for each course. The dry- or wet-aged U.S. beef steaks remain the culinary highlight. Private rooms are available.

Name: Tainan Wang
Address: 187 Liouhe 2nd Road, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: The Tainanese founder started selling fried noodles with eel over 60 years ago. The second-generation owner is a passionate foodie and has been adding new items to the menu. That said, the speciality is still the eel, either fried with scallion or braised in sesame oil, boasting tasty, springy flesh. House-made meat balls, cuttlefish balls and taro balls are also addictive. Those interested in trying virgin crabs should pre-order when booking.

Name: Marc L³
Address: 231 Renyi Street, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, 80145, Taiwan
Description: After living abroad for 10-plus years, the chef opened a pop-up kitchen at Yancheng Market to much acclaim. In memory of his childhood friends, he opened Marc L³ in 2021 to serve fine dining food in a relaxed atmosphere. His 9-course menu comprises modern, Western dishes made with local seasonable produce, weaving layered flavours with his witty descriptions. The soundtrack of English and Taiwanese oldies adds to the experience. The cocktail designed in-house is worth trying.

Name: KR Prime Steak
Address: 52 Shizheng North 2nd Road, Xitun District, Taichung, 407, Taiwan
Description: This restaurant set amid luxurious apartment towers is famous for its precisely cooked wet-aged US steaks, especially the Certified Angus Beef USDA prime rib eye cap, prized for its tenderness, flavour and succulence. Consider ordering the set menu that includes an appetiser, side and sweet; opt for the umami-laden bottarga sauce to go with your steak. The house-made desserts – such as silky crème brûlée with fresh berries – are also a must.

Name: Cheng Jia
Address: 6, Lane 92, Section 2, Minquan East Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: After honing his skills in an establishment of classic Taiwanese cooking for over 20 years, the head chef opened his own restaurant with only three tables in an alleyway hectic with street food stalls. Taiwanese all-time favourites are given a new spin here and his chicken soups are hugely popular. Try also sautéed shrimps with scrambled eggs in lettuce wraps. Book a table on social media and discuss the menu with the owner in advance.

Name: Mochi Baby
Address: 111 Raohe Street, Songshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The transparent case houses gooey mochi – they’re freshly made every day and have a strong sticky rice fragrance.

Name: Muji Beef Noodles
Address: 239 Wuxing Street, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
Description: The three sisters who run the place are very specific about their cooking. The flavoursome broth is made with beef bones and meat, Chinese herbs, scallion, garlic and a secret fruit that lends a subtle sweetness. The signature beef noodle soup uses only local beef for its unrivalled meaty flavour. Equally addictive is their jinbing – a fluffy pancake made to order with beef or pork wrapped inside. Don’t miss their marinated food either.

Name: FIRNS
Address: 19, Lane 50, Jingcheng Road, Xitun District, Taichung, Taiwan
Description: Chef Ricky from Hong Kong honed his skills in some prestigious kitchens in Europe and his home city. From his unique vantage point, he champions a modern French-Asian cuisine featuring locally sourced produce. His love for Taiwan also manifests itself in the papier mâché lamp, cutlery and tableware crafted by local artisans. The incredibly fresh catch of the day and the beautifully plated seasonal dessert are the highlights on the menu.

Name: Baho (Da'an)
Address: 4, Lane 102, Section 1, Anhe Road, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: This Japanese barbecue restaurant buys whole Omi Sawai hime cows, offering over 30 Shimofuri and Akami wagyu cuts to be enjoyed in eight different ways, including tartare, sushi, soup, and seared steak. Rare cuts like top round and inside skirt tend to run out but you can pre-order them. The very flavoursome beef lard rice in lotus leaf is not to be missed. The dimly-lit room is cosy, service impeccable and presentation dramatic.

Name: Duck Zhen (Wufu 4th Road)
Address: 258 Wufu 4th Road, Yancheng District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: After opening its doors over 60 years ago, Duck Zhen now takes up two retail space, but still has barely enough room to seat the hordes of diners lining up for its duck dishes day and night. Its smoked duck platter is the must-try item, with juicy, flavourful meat to be dipped into the house-made garlic sauce, and best enjoyed with a bowl of braised pork rice. Portion sizes of assorted duck offal or duck soup can be tailored to your party size.

Name: The Ukai
Address: 46F, Breeze Nan Shan, 17 Songzhi Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the second Taiwanese outpost of its namesake in Japan, famous for its Western-style table experience delivered with teppanyaki techniques. There is no à la carte and the two set menus change with the seasons. Signatures include steamed abalone with rock salt, garlic fried rice, and Wagyu steak or tenderloin from Tamura farm. Finish in style with a choice of dessert made with seasonal fruit and served in the cosy lounge.

Name: A-Yu Beef Shabu Shabu (Kunlun Road)
Address: 733-1 Kunlun Road, Rende District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: It took the founder’s wife and son three years to build A-Yu’s second outlet that spans over 3,000 square metres. Just like the original branch, this restaurant uses only the freshest beef from Shanhua district and serves it in beef stock hotpot to let its natural flavours shine. Order different bovine cuts on a form, but help yourself to the sides, veggies, drinks or the famous braised beef rice. Reservations aren’t accepted so expect long queues.

Name: Yuan
Address: 35 Dadun 12th Street, West District, Taichung, 408, Taiwan
Description: After stints at some top restaurants in Japan, chef-owner Yuan opened this dining concept in 2013. In 2024, it moved to this spot with a compact dining room gracefully decorated with floral arrangements. The single menu with three main course options is inspired by Taiwan's culinary history. Banquet classics such as eel rolls with salted egg yolk and ham are given a fresh spin. House-grown herbs and edible flowers add colour to the attractive plating.

Name: Sushi Nanami
Address: 6, Lane 452, Section 4, Ren'ai Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
Description: This place feels like a secluded Japanese home – the kimono-clad hostess walks you through the garden to the dining room with 12 seats at a cypress counter. The Japanese chef serves an omakase menu that draws on both tradition and innovation with dishes such as octopus with house-made ricotta. The sashimi shows intricate knife skills and the sushi rice is dressed in a special vinegar blend. The panna cotta with honey rounds off the meal nicely.

Name: L'herbe
Address: 950, Section 2, Yonghua Road, Anping District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: The head chef trained in France and worked in some top-tier establishments in Taipei. She opened L’herbe in 2019, recruiting an all-women kitchen team to imbue traditional Gallic cuisine with distinctive local flavours. Expect to see angled loofah, basella, pork offal and the like on the table. Her tasting menu changes every season, with a choice of several main courses – Lumina lamb chop from New Zealand is especially worth trying.

Name: Mao Su
Address: 43 Fudong Street, East District, Tainan, Taiwan
Description: Light wood furnishings, arched windows and a crackle effect wall combine to create a relaxed, modern space. Run by a Tainanese catering group, this restaurant is aimed at omnivorous diners who wish to reduce their carbon footprint by forgoing meat once in a while. The lacto-ovo-vegetarian dishes are loaded with Asian spices and condiments, such as satay, Sichuan pepper and kimchi. Try the classic stir-fried king oyster mushroom with basil.

Name: Komboi
Address: 28, Lane 270, Section 1, Dunhua South Road, Da’an District, Taipei, 10685, Taiwan
Description: Komboi is the homophone of the Taiwanese phrase for ‘empty plates’, as the chef hopes his guests enjoy their meals down to the last bite. Modern dishes embody his novel ideas, finessed by techniques acquired when travelling in France. While a shorter set menu is offered at lunch, we recommend the unabridged ‘experience’ menu to best appreciate his vision. The minimalist room boasts warm hues, dark wood furniture and ribbed glass pendant lamps.

Name: Ça marche
Address: 14 Jhengci Street, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Ça marche opened in a quiet alley in 2021, with a modern classic room dotted by retro knickknacks. Honing his skills in Japan and France, the Taiwanese chef offers a 10-course prix-fixe menu that changes seasonally. French-Italian inspired dishes are tweaked slightly to cater to local palates, such as using Chinese-style dumpling skin in ravioli and Taiwanese basil instead of the sweet variety. Open only for dinner at 7 pm; cash only.

Name: Fu Yuan
Address: 9F, Grand Hi-Lai Hotel, 266 Chenggong 1st Road, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: This restaurant in a luxury hotel is the group’s only F&B outlet serving Taiwanese cooking. With crystal chandeliers and oil paintings, the classically furnished room can feel a bit dated, but the friendly service, homely dishes and seafood sourced daily from neighbouring ports more than compensate. Deep-fried chicken nuggets offer a hint of camellia oil aroma that works well with the crispy sliced ginger.

Name: Thomas Chien
Address: 11 Chenggong 2nd Road, Cianjhen District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Not only has Chef Chien got culinary acumen and all the classic French techniques, but he also cares for his carbon footprint and sustainability of food sources. By eating here, you’ll be supporting small local farms and fishing communities. His set menus use mostly local, seasonal ingredients and his lunch menus change monthly to keep them fresh. From time to time, top guest chefs are invited from overseas to broaden diners’ gastronomic horizons.

Name: Chope Chope Eatery
Address: 4F, Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Xinyi Place A4, 19 Songgao Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, 110, Taiwan
Description: While ‘chope’ means to reserve a seat by putting a tissue pack on it in ‘Singlish’, you can call to book a table here. The Singaporean chef helming JL Studio in Taichung opened this Kopitiam concept to celebrate casual Singaporean dining. Try har cheong gai (fried wings in fermented shrimp sauce), kopi pai kut (coffee ribs) and house-made murtabak bread. Asian-inspired cocktails such as Tan herbal tea in a plastic bag are both fun and delicious.

Name: The Tavernist
Address: 12F, Kimpton Da An Hotel, 25, Lane 27, Section 4, Ren'ai Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: With globe light fixtures connected like an oversized pearl bracelet, the bamboo-clad room has a whimsical feel. In addition to European classics such as fish and chips, thyme-roasted chicken and beef Wellington, the Taiwanese chef also caters to the local palate by using Western techniques to cook local produce. Try his dried radish chicken soup with squid, and kelp popcorn chicken. It's also a pet-friendly space, so book ahead for your furry friend.
