The menu focuses on beef steaks, including some top notch imported choices such as Japanese Hitachi A5 Wagyu, Aussie Sanchoku MB5 and Black Angus, and USDA Prime. Chargrilled to perfection and flawlessly seasoned, the steaks are tender, juicy and flavourful. Round off your meal with New York style cheesecake.

Name: Bà Diệu (Tran Tong Street)
Address: 17 Tran Tong Street, Thac Gian Ward, Thanh Khe District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: This simple shop specialises in bún bò, or rice noodle soup with assorted cuts of beef – thinly sliced, shin, tongue, tendon... Alternatively, the noodles can be paired with pork balls or pork trotters. The broth boasts a robust meaty flavour with natural sweetness and mild heat; the meat is cooked to perfection and the seasoning is spot on. Their signature thập cẩm noodle dish allows diners to sample the beef and the pork at the same time.

Name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân
Address: 16 Hoe Nhai Street, Nguyen Trung Truc Ward, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: The chef crafts delectable bánh cuốn, Vietnamese steamed rolls with minced pork and black fungus. She also serves an option with a soft poached egg. Order the pork meatloaf and sausage, and season with fresh herbs, chilli, lime or garlic at will for a great breakfast or snack.

Name: Ốc Oanh
Address: 534 Vinh Khanh Street, Ward 8, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: This joint on a busy street serves a range of seafood cooked in countless ways. Whelks, tiger prawns, lobster, octopus, crab… the choice is yours. The authentic outdoor vibe more than makes up for the lack of air conditioning.

Name: Highway4 (Hang Tre Street)
Address: 5 Hang Tre Street, Ly Thai To Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: This Vietnamese tửu quán (tavern) has always been popular with the locals and tourists alike. Most diners take their time, enjoying the food and drink in good company. The inn serves Northern Vietnamese fare and we recommend the subtly flavoured appetisers, such as salads or spring rolls. The catfish spring roll is the tasty signature dish. The heart-warming main courses come in earthen pots. The deliciously tender oxtail stew with herbs is to die for!

Name: Nu Đồ Kitchen
Address: 11/1 Luu Quang Thuan Street, My An Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: The owner’s parents used to sell mì quảng, noodle soup from Central Vietnam. The shop is named ‘Nu Đồ’, a transliteration of the word ‘noodle’. The menu boasts four versions of mì quảng served in traditional bamboo baskets like in the old days, each with a special broth to highlight the key ingredient. The snakehead fish variety with pronounced turmeric aromas is not to be missed. Tables are laid in the covered patio, surrounded by greenery.

Name: Bánh Xèo Bà Dưỡng
Address: 280/23 Hoang Dieu Street, Nam Duong Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: This 30+-year-old no-frills shop at the very end of an alley serves a concise menu of crispy pancakes known as bánh xèo, alongside skewered pork, grilled meat and noodles. Everything comes with fresh herbs, pickled papaya, cucumber and strips of eggplant. Feel free to customise your own rice paper pancake with meat to order and condiments on the table. The minced pork peanut sauce dip is a must.

Name: The Temptation
Address: 125 Ho Nghinh Street, Phuoc My Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: This modern villa with a beautiful courtyard and an opulent dining room is home to an upmarket eatery helmed by Vietnamese chef La Thua An. Brought up in France, he opened The Temptation in 2019, wowing diners with ingenious creations, layers of flavours and often whimsical plating. His signature dessert The Sweet Egg Nest of Han River, for instance, features numerous ingredients encased in a spun-sugar egg-shaped shell in a bamboo cage.

Name: MaSa French Eatery by Hervé
Address: 204/20 Nguyen Van Huong Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Abutting the swanky upmarket Hervé Dining Room, MaSa (Manipulator of Savours) is the same chef’s more accessible sibling eatery. As opposed to a multi-course experience, the menu focuses on French tapas to share. The food shows a hint of Asian accents, paired with a well curated wine list. Try Black Angus hanger steak from Korea, and the signature snickers dessert. Al fresco dining with a pond and a charcoal grill dripping in unique charm.

Name: Bún Thịt Nướng Hoàng Văn
Address: 137 Chan Hung Street, Ward 6, Tan Binh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: There is only one item on the menu – rice noodles in a tangy sweet dressing with a spring roll, grilled pork, lettuce, bean sprouts, cucumber, carrot, peanuts and scallion. The contrasting textures and flavours are magical.

Name: Oryz
Address: 51 Tran Nhat Duat Street, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Rice is the staple ingredient that links all Asian culinary cultures, so the chef named the restaurant after the Latin word for rice. Naturally, he endeavours to present the grain in various forms, from puffed rice and deep-fried rice noodles to koji and sparkling sake. Familiar Asian recipes are reimagined with a flourish. Try his version of cơm lam, or glutinous rice in a bamboo tube with shrimp and 18-day home-cured pork and sausage.

Name: Olivia
Address: 31A Le Van Mien Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Named after Chef David Green’s daughter, Olivia is another highlight of his glorious culinary career. The serene oasis amid the hustle and bustle of Thao Dien ward features a white colour scheme, pale wood and European-style furnishings. The kitchen behind a glazed wall showcases the chefs working their magic. Food-wise, Asian ingredients are precisely prepared with sensuous flavours and underpinned by modern European techniques.

Name: Chapter
Address: 12C Chan Cam Street, Hang Trong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Chapter’s façade of Corten steel slats leads into an open kitchen that produces unique flavours and textures over a charcoal grill. The single tasting menu features 10+ courses anchored in Vietnamese heritage, all artfully plated. A small clay house is set on each table and each course comes with a postcard in which the chef shares his memories. Globally sourced produce is combined with Vietnamese culinary heritage to great effect.

Name: Bún Bò Huế Cô Như
Address: 274/29 Vo Van Tan Street, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
Description: This family-run shop is tucked away in a narrow alley. It takes a little effort to find, but you’ll well be rewarded by tasty beef noodle soups. First-timers may go for bún bò thập cẩm (mixed beef noodle soup), a great way to sample all four toppings of beef and pork, boasting robust meaty flavours. The sweet broth with great depth is made from beef meat and bones alongside herbs like lemongrass. Add a dollop of chilli sauce for added whoomph.

Name: Lai
Address: 28F, Sedona Suites, 92-94 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Bringing 30 years' experience to the table, the Malaysian-born chef has worked in six major cities across Asia. The interior is done out in traditional Chinese décor featuring modern paintings and flowers. The menu combines classical Cantonese with contemporary elements and a twist of southern Asian in a creative presentation. Be sure to try the há cảo thủy tinh (crystal shrimp dumpling) and the xá xíu ướp thao được quay kieu 'truyền thống' (traditional roasted pork belly with herbs).

Name: Duong's
Address: 27 Ngo Huyen Street, Hang Trong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Doung's is low profile yet easy to find. Over two storeys, the setting is cosy with comfortable wooden furniture and intimate, soft lighting. The set menu is suitable for smaller parties, while the à la carte presents a selection of more substantial signature dishes from Hanoi. The traditional grilled La Vong-style fish is a treat for the eye, while the consommé of beef soup has a clear broth with layers of spices. The chef also offers cooking classes.

Name: Hoa Túc (District 1)
Address: 74/7 Hai Ba Trung Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Remodelled from an old opium refinery, Hoa Túc boasts an al fresco dining area steeped in an early 1900s circa Parisian vibe, while the Colonial-style interior pays homage to Vietnam’s history. On the menu, traditional Vietnamese dishes are updated thanks to fancy presentations. Start with refreshing pink pomelo salad with crabmeat and shrimps, followed by bò lá lốt bánh hỏi (grilled beef wrapped in betel leaves on a rice noodle nest).

Name: Bánh Canh Yến
Address: 253 Nguyen Hoang Street, Binh Hien Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Come here for bánh canh – thick, chewy noodles made with tapioca starch and rice flour in a snakehead fish and pork broth. Choose toppings like fishcake, quail egg or crabcake. Order fried dough sticks for added crunch.

Name: An's Saigon
Address: 5A Tong Huu Dinh Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Nestling in a stately 20C villa, An's Saigon is fairly out of the way, so you’ll need a cab to get there. The restaurant is divided into three zones: the garden and the lounge serve breakfast, lunch and a dinner tasting menu, while the L-shaped eight-seat Chef’s Table offers an intimate experience and a more personalised menu inspired by Vietnamese culture and nature. Artful plating and creative twists add a new spin to familiar flavours.

Name: Fashionista Café
Address: 22B Phung Khac Khoan Street, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Food and fashion are the passions of many tastemakers. This café annexed to a two-storey clothing store seamlessly melds the two under one roof. With only two tables indoors, most seating is al fresco. The food is essentially Gallic with Vietnamese twists. Local tropical fruits and nuts are generously used in the sauces and seasoning, while soigné plating pays tribute to fine French dining. Lunch set menus offer great value.

Name: Stoker (District 1)
Address: 44 Mac Thi Buoi Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: The three-storey restaurant has a bar and counter seats around an open kitchen on the ground floor, while upstairs, heavy leather chairs, dark wood wainscoting and antler chandeliers evoke classic steakhouse vibes. Grass-fed and grain-fed beef steaks are the house specialities, especially those dry-aged for over 21 days. The creamy mashed potato cooked over a wood fire is rich in smoky flavour. Round it off with your favourite whisky.

Name: Nén Light
Address: 122/2 Tran Dinh Xu Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: After walking down a narrow street, diners are invariably enchanted by the pretty lights that set the scene in the tranquil bamboo garden. The interior is equally atmospheric. Championing a cuisine without boundaries, the young chef curates a tasting menu of 7 or 9 courses that tells a story. She uses mostly local ingredients in her ingenious creations and changes the menu every four months to keep it fresh. Ask about the wine pairing option.

Name: Phở Hùng (District 1)
Address: 241-243 Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: This venue may not offer much in terms of ambience, but can’t be beaten for tasty beef noodles at affordable prices. Besides the usual raw beef, or medium-rare brisket, their springy and flavoursome beef balls are also a must. If you can’t make up your mind, order the house special with everything in the bowl. Basil, bean sprouts, onion and lime wedges are served on the side. Feel free to customise your phở according to your whim.

Name: Square One
Address: 2 Lam Son Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: With stints all over Europe, including prestigious establishments in France, chef Arnaud delivers a unique dining experience by seamlessly switching between Vietnamese and French recipes. Dishes boast balanced flavours and artful plating, befitting the stylish dining room clad in wood and brick. Generous portion sizes are intended to share and ideal for get-togethers. The dramatically visible kitchens make a meal here entertaining and engaging.

Name: Vietnam House
Address: 93-97 Dong Khoi Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: This elegant French Colonial-style building stands in the middle of a well-heeled district in the vibrant city centre. The menu is devised by Vietnamese-Australian celebrity chef Luke Nguyen. The team elevate traditional Vietnamese cooking with modern twists, in tasty dishes such as duck noodle soup, juicy chicken breast, and truly delicious silken bean curd dessert. A glass of local flavour infused cocktail adds to the experience.

Name: Bếp Prime
Address: 12 Hang Dieu Street, Cua Dong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Tucked away in a quaint historic edifice, c. 1932, Bếp Prime specialises in traditional delicacies from Hanoi and the rest of Vietnam. For a Hanoian classic, order pigeon and mushroom hot pot – veggies, pigeon meat and offal are served in a bird cage to be blanched in a herbal broth or glutinous rice porridge. The crispy rice dish with the chef’s dip, made from pork jus, dried shrimps, chilli and pepper that packs umami and a spicy kick, is also recommended.

Name: Bún Chả Đắc Kim (Hang Manh Street)
Address: 1 Hang Manh Street, Hang Gai Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Nước chấm – sweet chilli fish sauce with finely sliced pickled green mango – is the perfect condiment for the vermicelli noodles which come with shredded smoky pork and plump pork patties. It’s a win-win combination of meat with sweetness and refreshing acidity.

Name: Lüne
Address: 17/14 Le Thanh Ton Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: With offerings such as duck pâté parfait, escargot and pithiviers, the menu seems traditionally French… But the French chef (from Lyon) aims to re-interpret the classics in line with modern forms and aesthetics. The à la carte menu may not be long, but it covers all bases. For those wanting to experience the chef's vision in all its glory, opt for the tasting menu. Again, the wine list isn't overwhelming, being well curated with some solid choices.

Name: Maison 1929
Address: 2 Cua Dong Street, Cua Dong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: The restaurant, which is established in a historic circa 1929 edifice, is a sister establishment of Chào Bạn. The dining room, spread over two floors and a balcony, features a vibrant colour scheme. The menu is 80% identical to that of Chào Bạn, emphasising a modern approach to Vietnamese cooking. One of the highlights is their array of spring rolls, served hot or cold. Minced beef in lolot leaves boasts a unique aroma and juicy, tender meat.

Name: My Hanh Seafood
Address: 3-5 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Phuoc My Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: The terrace with panoramic ocean views is one of the biggest draws of this beach-front restaurant. But the well-crafted seafood is more than equal to the setting. The live fish tank heralds a feast of fresh shellfish and fish, to be cooked in various ways. But the stellar attraction is definitely mantis shrimp, boasting firm, flavoursome flesh and rich, buttery roe. Mud crab from Hoi An is another exclusive speciality not found elsewhere in Da Nang.

Name: Béo Ơi
Address: 15/20 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Off from the main drag, this simple shop is run by the owner-chef, affectionately known as béo ơi or "fat boy" by regulars, who come in droves during lunch hours. The menu features generous portions of Hanoian home-style cooking, including bún riêu cua, a flavoursome tomato crab soup topped with crispy deep-fried tofu. Order a couple of sides for a complete meal. Or go with friends and opt for a hot pot dinner with the tasty soup as a base.

Name: Miên Saigon
Address: 50A Dang Dung Street, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Soft lighting and buckets of atmosphere set the scene in the ground-floor dining room which sports an open kitchen with counter seats for those who want to stay close to the action. The 18-seat private room upstairs is perfect for parties. European dishes are spruced up and given local twists – the beef soup pot au pho melds classic pot au feu with Vietnamese noodles. To sample all the highlights, opt for the tasting menu, but à la carte options abound.

Name: Senté (Nguyen Quang Bich Street)
Address: 20 Nguyen Quang Bich Street, Cua Dong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Step away from the bustling streets of the Old Quarter, down a discreet alley and into this cosy dining venue, which is strewn with green plants and champions healthy food. The artistically presented, modern Vietnamese dishes use flowers, leaves, seeds, stems and roots of the humble lotus plant to create unique, flavourful inventions. As a starter, the shrimp, pomelo and lotus root salad is refreshing and appetising. Advance reservations recommended.

Name: Tanh Tách
Address: 3 Yet Kieu Street, Nguyen Du Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, 112605, Vietnam
Description: Nestled in a historic French colonial villa, the restaurant occupies two storeys. The chef team exhibits a knack for seafood dishes based on textbook European techniques, thus explaining their prominence on the à la carte menu. Before trying the deftly crafted fish or shellfish, kick off your meal with nori or kimchi rice crackers and tom yum mayo dip. Black chicken consommé is another smash hit.

Name: Ốc Đào (District 1)
Address: 212B/D48 Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: In addition to regular fish and crustaceans dishes, this legendary restaurant is especially famous for bivalves and sea snails – a plethora of different species are on the menu, many of which are rarely seen elsewhere. The live critters are cooked in traditional Vietnamese condiments with enough seasoning to complement the natural umami without being overpowering. The bustling vibe makes it great for casual gatherings.

Name: Esta
Address: 27 Tran Quy Khoach Street, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: The menu is depicted by spot-on fusion Asian cuisine, influenced by trips to Japan, Korea and China and the chef’s Vietnamese roots. The theatrically visible kitchen showcases his culinary wizardry, founded on high-quality ingredients. Esta believes in sourcing vegetables from independent farmers and fish caught by small boats.

Name: Hanoi Garden
Address: 36 Hang Manh Street, Hang Gai Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: The Indochine-style villa with an elegant courtyard has been home to this establishment since 1998. Expect to find all the greatest hits of Vietnamese cooking on the menu, from appetisers like spring rolls to meat and seafood dishes. Hot pot choices also abound. With over 20 years' experience, the Vietnamese chef reinvents his home country's classics with a modern twist. The food is meticulously prepared and astutely seasoned.

Name: La Fontaine
Address: 2F, Trade Center, River Garden, 170 Nguyen Van Huong Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: This bistro with a vintage Parisian vibe is a spin-off of La Villa, operated by the same French owner-chef. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner, it serves classic, no-frills Gallic fare ranging from pastries and baguette sandwiches to pork terrine and pâté en croûte. Inspired by the chef’s childhood souvenirs, the rustic Provence-style lamb ragout is unbelievably rich and flavoursome. Also check out the wine list leaning towards French labels.

Name: Bếp Người Hội An
Address: 22 Tran Quoc Toan Street, Ward 8, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: The decor is unmistakably Hội An in style – yellow walls, lanterns and wooden furniture. The menu is easy to navigate, with mì quảng noodles and cơm gà chicken rice being the main events. Trouble choosing? Try the mì quảng đặc biệt topped with shrimp, pork, quail egg, ham, fermented pork roll and peanut spring roll. Cơm gà xé comprises silky shredded chicken, onion and laksa leaves on a bed of chicken fat rice, with chicken offal sauce on the side.

Name: Izakaya by Koki
Address: Basement 2, Capella, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Trang Tien Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Tucked away in the basement of Capella hotel, Izakaya is a modern and chic setting, with various seating areas, including more intimate sofa areas. Guests are welcomed with a complimentary sake with aromatic notes of tropical fruit. Sourcing 70% of its ingredients from Japan, this restaurant has an extensive menu including a specialty of grilled dishes: the grilled black cod with Saikyo sauce is particularly impressive. Be sure to save room for the signature dessert: housemade yame matcha or black truffle ice cream.

Name: Hervé Dining Room
Address: 204/20 Nguyen Van Huong Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Set in a residential building, Hervé Rodriguez's restaurant has an open kitchen, and an intimate atmosphere that makes it just the place for a romantic dinner or low-key social gathering. The tasting menu, which changes every three weeks, sees various cooking techniques (e.g. molecular, dry aging and preserving) applied to the best of Vietnamese produce. To cleanse the palette between dishes, diners are served a series of small bites that range from acidic to fruity and icy.

Name: French Grill
Address: Lobby Level, JW Marriott, 8 Do Duc Duc Road, Me Tri Ward, South Tu Liem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: This elegant hotel restaurant boasts a sleek, spacious dining room oozing with special occasion indulgence. Counter seats offer a view of the huge open kitchen and create a connection between the chefs at work and the diners. The contemporary French culinary score is consummately executed with subtle Asian twists, flanked by equally immaculate, spot-on, courteous service. Private dining rooms are available for everything from date nights to business dinners.

Name: El Gaucho (Hoan Kiem)
Address: 11 Trang Tien Street, Trang Tien Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: This is an outpost of a global chain that specialises in steakhouse classics, specifically premium beef steaks. Certified organic, corn-fed beef from the U.S. and grass-fed cattle from Australia are grilled to perfection Argentinian style – sparingly seasoned and free of sauce to further highlight their natural flavours. Visit the adjoining butcher’s shop to take some quality meat home. Start or end your evening with cocktails at the bar. Reservations recommended.

Name: Le Comptoir
Address: 16 Che Lan Vien Street, My An Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: Run by a chef from Lyon, France, this restaurant is the epitome of Gallic authenticity. The á la carte and set menus roll out bistro classics made with premium local and globally sourced ingredients, cherry-picked by the chef. Expect items like roasted beef bone marrow and hand-chopped Wagyu tartare with Melba toast and smoked aioli. The interesting wine list offers a wide range of boutique wineries. Pop into the deli after your meal.

Name: Nén Danang
Address: 16 My Da Tay 2 Street, Khue My Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: Reopened in 2022, the first venture of owner-chef Summer Le is tucked away from the main road. The interior is modern and minimalistic, with theatrical lighting to set the mood. To keep it fresh and exciting, the single set menu is tweaked every few months and revamped entirely every 6 months. Each creative Vietnamese dish comes with a hand-drawn card explaining the inspiration and ingredients. Check out the wine- and sake-food pairing.

Name: Bếp Hên
Address: 47 Le Hong Phong Street, Phuoc Ninh Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: Step back in time and immerse yourself in the room’s vintage circa 1990s decor and memorabilia. The family business has been in operation since 2015 and the kitchen is helmed by mum. The extensive menu, which covers all of Vietnam, might seem overwhelming, but rest assured that all the sharing plates are authentic, hearty and comforting. When unsure, check out the section known as ‘mum’s favourites’, for items like fried garlic prawn, or stir-fried morning glory with garlic.

Name: Tre Dining
Address: 2F, 35 Xuan Thuy Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Down a path lined in bamboo trees, diners are led into a bamboo-clad room. The chef team cook up a storm over the charcoal grills in the open kitchen and complement the grilled food with east-meets-west condiments and artful plating. Think octopus tentacles in a spicy, buttery tom yum sauce, or Hokkaido scallops in a brown butter hollandise. Choose counter seats to stay close to the action, or the al fresco dining area for the city’s skyline.

Name: La Villa
Address: 14 Ngo Quang Huy Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: The culinary Gallic line-up whisks you back to the 1960s with duck foie gras, pâté en croûte, lobster à l'américaine and Grand Marnier soufflé. Decorated with artwork, red velvet curtains and a stunning chandelier, La Villa also offers al fresco dining in the garden. Attentive, suitably formal service, a fine wine list and cheese selection. The starched classical vibe of this restaurant will appeal to those who appreciate vintage charm and nostalgia.

Name: Phở Gà Châm (Yen Ninh Street)
Address: 64-68 Yen Ninh Street, Truc Bach Ward, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: The phở gà at this small stall might be more expensive than the average, but the chicken is premium quality and the natural chicken flavour of the soup base is impeccably seasoned. Choose from white or dark meat, or a mixture of both, and add chilli sauce, garlic, lime and chilli to taste. Arrive early to ensure the best selection of chicken cuts. This stall, perfect for an authentic breakfast experience in Hanoi, is open until 1:30pm.

Name: Etēsia
Address: 14B Lo Su Street, Ly Thai To Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: An 18-seat kitchen counter is the focal point of this snug buzzy wine bar. Shelves of empty wine bottles adorn the walls, and the wine list showcases over 350 vintages from the Old World. They offer a vast array of wines by the glass and from a Coravin. The neatly presented, modern dishes are Mediterranean at heart with an Asian twist and deliver accurate, well-judged flavours. Don't miss the homemade pasta: the pride and joy of Etēsia.

Name: T.U.N.G dining
Address: 2C Quang Trung Street, Hang Trong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: The TUNG-in-cheek acronym – twisted, unique, natural, gastronomic – encapsulates the philosophy of Chef Hoang Tung's culinary style. His tasting menu, which keeps pace with the seasons and uses local produce, boasts colourful, minimalist dishes, each of which features just 3 or 4 ingredients, whose complexity explodes with every bite. The flavours are balanced and well-judged, with contrasts of texture and temperature, and acidity often playing a key role.

Name: Azabu
Address: 2F, Hôtel du Parc, 84 Tran Nhan Tong Street, Nguyen Du Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the 2nd floor of Hôtel du Parc, bask in the elegant main dining room or watch the sushi chefs at work from the blonde wooden counter. The menu covers all the bases and is great value for money at lunchtime. The extensive à la carte menu offers a fine range of Kaiseki options. Don't overlook the house specialities, including the knockout sushi and sashimi. A smooth, professional operation run by a smart, friendly team.

Name: Bún Chả Cá Bà Hoa
Address: 27 Le Hong Phong Street, Phuoc Ninh Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: Since 2009, this simple shop has attracted a loyal fan base with only one item on the menu – bún chả cá – rice noodles in a tangy tomato and pumpkin broth with fresh fishcakes, made in house daily using a variety of fish. Almost 300 bowls are sold every day and customised to order with fishcake only or a combo of fishcake and a chunk of mackerel or tuna. Try it with pickles or a dab of shrimp paste for extra flavour.

Name: Bé Mặn
Address: Lot 8, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Man Thai Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: One of the most famous seafood restaurants on My Khe Beach, Bé Mặn knows how to bring out the best in every ingredient. Start by picking your own live seafood from the rows of tanks and then specify how you want it cooked. From crabs and lobsters to geoduck and snails, whether deep-fried, stir-fried or steamed, everything tastes as good as it looks. Try the steamed squid with ginger and onion, dipping it in the spicy sour sauce for an extra zing.

Name: Rice Field
Address: 2F, 75-77 Ho Tung Mau Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Spread over three storeys, this delightful venue with an open-air rooftop boasts a rustic décor inspired by local villages and rice fields and serves Vietnamese dishes from the north to the south. The stuffed snails with meat cooked with lemongrass and paired with ginger fish sauce, are succulent, while La Vong fishcakes strike the perfect balance combining vermicelli, marinated fish, fresh Vietnamese vegetables and herbs, shrimp paste sauce and rice paper sheets.

Name: Labri
Address: 2F, 113 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: A neon sign in the upstairs window is the clue to finding this modern-day bistro, tucked away on the 2nd floor of a nondescript building. Abri is French for shelter and the restaurant imbues a sense of cosy luxury. The open kitchen takes centre stage and four huge crystal chandeliers hang from the ceiling. The chef delivers virtuoso cuisine using French techniques and Vietnamese ingredients. For the full experience, opt for the 7-course menu.

Name: Vị An
Address: 145 Hoang Cau Street, Trung Liet Ward, Dong Da District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: The owner couple strives to replicate the authentic taste of Northern Vietnam for their Hanoian audience. Unlike the sweet flavours cherished in other parts of Vietnam, here they emphasise umami and saltiness. Chả ốc is one of the most popular dishes. The pork sausage with periwinkle snails is perfumed with herbs and fried until crispy. The pork is juicy and bouncy in texture. Gà xáo gừng is chicken cooked in turmeric and ginger. Simply irresistible.

Name: Mía Dining
Address: 12G2 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: The soft lighting, minimalist interior and romantic soundtrack make this venue the perfect spot for date nights. The most prized seats are at the counter offering intimate views of the kitchen. Three set menus star modern European recipes jazzed up by a scattering of local produce and seasonings. The must-try duck breast is velvety and juicy, clad in crackling skin as crisp as peanut brittle. Expect sound wine tips from the sommelier.

Name: Năm Đảnh
Address: 139/59/38 Tran Quang Khai Street, Tho Quang Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Tucked away in a residential neighbourhood, Năm Đảnh provides a golf cart shuttle service from Phan Vinh Street. Seafood is the strong suit of this sprawling restaurant, which boasts a huge number of tables. There is even a hut clad in live fish tanks from which diners can make their pick. Lobster, whether steamed, tossed in cheese sauce, or fried with garlic and chilli, is always tasty. Sea whelks in garlic butter exude spellbinding aromas. Early birds get the most choice...

Name: Du Yên
Address: 26B Street 10, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, 71000, Vietnam
Description: Nestled in a quiet neighbourhood in town, this place occupies two levels with its room exuding rustic chic. The eclectic menu presents Vietnamese dishes plus Western and Thai options. Gỏi cuốn hoa bướm are the photogenic rice paper rolls adorned with edible pansies. The sweet peanut dip works well with the crisp vegetables. Męt bánh Huế is the vegetarian version of the famous steamed rice cake wrapped in banana leaves with fish sauce on the side.

Name: Luk Lak
Address: 28 Bach Dang Street, Thach Thang Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Perched on the banks of the Han River, this outpost of its Hanoian namesake boasts a dining room dripping in lush greenery. This branch shares the same culinary ethos as its flagship – creative Vietnamese fare packed with bold flavours. Grilled ground beef skewer with herbs and lemongrass seduces with aromas. Wrap in rice paper with veg and fruit for a hunger-quenching kick or pair with sticky rice and cassava root in a claypot.

Name: Cồ Đàm
Address: 68 Tran Hung Dao Street, Tran Hung Dao Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Named after the Buddha, Cồ Đàm’s eye-catching architecture boasts an ornate exterior inspired by Buddhist and Champa culture and a striking arched entrance of terracotta bricks. Four floors are open for dining, but the ground floor stands out for its tranquil pond and terracotta Buddha. The vegetarian tasting menu comprises creative, modern twists on exquisitely presented Vietnamese classics, rich in flavour combinations.

Name: Elgin
Address: 27 Mac Dinh Chi Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Orange banquettes and soft lighting enhance and offset the dark green wall tiles. Run by an energetic and passionate young team, Elgin can be relied upon to pamper its patrons. The menu, which changes regularly, showcases deftly prepared European dishes made mostly with local produce. Try the pork belly with fried brussels sprouts or gnocchi with lamb sugo, both of which are rich in flavours.

Name: Quince Eatery
Address: 37 Bis Ky Con Street, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Set in a refurbished colonial-style house with a vibrant décor, bistro-style furniture and soft lighting, this culinary hotspot adds a modern twist to Mediterranean fare. A copper counter with 6 seats faces the open kitchen. Guests can pick from a wide range of charcoal-grilled, wood-fired and oven-baked delights. Our favourites: hummus and merguez, and tasty golden berry with burnt sourdough mousse dessert. The 2nd floor bar is ideal for drinks before or after your meal.

Name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Hoành
Address: 66 To Hien Thanh Street, Bui Thi Xuan Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: This is among the busiest shops in the area because of its steamed rice rolls known as bánh cuốn. Rice noodle sheets are steamed to order and then wrapped around minced shiitake and pork. They also sell bún chả, or grilled pork noodles.

Name: Cơm Gà Lan
Address: 520 Trung Nu Vuong Street, Hoa Thuan Tay Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: As the name suggests, there's only one thing on the menu – cơm gà, or chicken rice, but you can opt for the poultry roasted, steamed or shredded. Served with soup and pickles, the cơm gà xé bóp (shredded version), is especially popular. The lemongrass, coriander and onion lend the juicy chicken extra zing. Given the quality of the food and bargain prices, it's no surprise that this place is always jam-packed. Avoid peak hours.

Name: Backstage
Address: Capella, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Trang Tien Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Your inner celebrity will revel in this opera-themed restaurant, whose open kitchen takes front stage. Signature dishes like Capella Pho and Bun Cha Hanoi respect their northern heritage, whilst featuring modern techniques with European touches that will leave your tastebuds singing an aria of delight. The impressive cocktail list offers some intriguing mixes. The theatrical setting showcases stunning costumes from the world’s greatest operas.

Name: The Monkey Gallery Dining
Address: 3F, 91 Mac Thi Buoi Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Three wise founders, all born in the year of the monkey, have thoughtfully designed this relaxed "gallery" with a minimalist, Japanese-influenced decor, in which the food takes centre stage. The result is a lovely ambience that is perfect for social gatherings. A concrete dining counter faces the open kitchen where the young kitchen team uses modern European cooking techniques. Pick from a selection of dishes for each of the four courses, then choose your drink pairing from the creative list of cocktails and mocktails.

Name: Madame Lam
Address: 10 Tran Ngoc Dien Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Indochine-Art Deco design fosters a laid-back ambience in this restaurant where the chef showcases modern Vietnamese cuisine from the central region of the country, where he grew up. The traditional dishes are presented with a refined yet creative touch. Be sure to try the delicious bao ngư nướng mỡ hành (grilled abalone with spring onion oil and fish sauce). The kem chuối nước cốt dừa (banana ice cream with coconut rice and crushed peanuts) is a satisfying and traditional dessert to round off your meal.

Name: Ngon Garden
Address: 70 Nguyen Du Street, Nguyen Du Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: On the banks of Thien Quang Lake, this restaurant, reminiscent of an Indochinese-style villa, boasts a patio surrounded by lush greenery. The menu features specialities from all over Vietnam, alongside Asian delicacies of Chinese and Thai origins. From the century-old Bat Dan phở recipe from Hanoi and bún bò huế grilled beef from Nha Trang to fresh veggies from Dalat and live seafood from all over the world, every dish is deftly crafted and delicately seasoned.

Name: Si Dining
Address: 1 Giang Chau 2 Street, Khue My Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: The Italian owner-chef opened this al fresco dining spot to showcase authentic Italian fare, adding a subtle local spin. The menu changes daily to keep it fresh and hyper-seasonal, but beef carpaccio is a firm fixture – thinly sliced raw Aussie beef dressed in anchovy sauce and olive oil, topped with croutons and shaved parmesan. Fish remains his passion and the catch of the day always hits the spot. House-made limoncello is perfect to sip after dinner.

Name: Cô Liêng
Address: 321 Vo Van Tan Street, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Established in 1995, Cô Liêng serves up a modest take on Southern Vietnamese cuisine. The main draw is the charcoal-grilled bò lá lốt (minced beef wrapped in betel leaves) that features perfect savoury-sweet flavour. They also serve rice vermicelli bundles (bánh hỏi with grilled meat).

Name: Bún Chả Hương Liên (Hai Ba Trung)
Address: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Phan Chu Trinh Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Playing on their claim to fame, this joint displays photos of its celebrity guests and offers a Combo Obama, which includes a fried seafood roll, a bowl of the special bún chả and a bia hà nội. The bún chả itself delivers a satisfying blend of rustic flavours, with smoky pork, meat patties, fragrant herbs and fresh salad leaves. They also serve a tasty pork skewer.

Name: Thúy 94 Cũ
Address: 84 Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
Description: This popular restaurant specialises in crab, with a menu that shines the spotlight on the crustacean – crab spring rolls, fried rice, salt-baked crab, steamed crab… the list goes on. Crab vermicelli soup brims with umami-loaded crabmeat and roe. The broth features deep, slightly sweet flavours. Soft-shelled crab is fried to order, boasting a crispy crust and firm flesh. What’s more, crab can be replaced by shrimp in most dishes.

Name: Ốc Di Tú
Address: 144C Quan Thanh Street, Quan Thanh Ward, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: Vietnamese for snail, Ốc is the focus of this simple eatery with pila polita, tiger moon, shark eye and canarium snails on the menu. The large melo melo, the tastiest, is grilled until soft and served with scallions and fried garlic; the price depends on its size. The rich variety of seafood options includes prawns, Halong squid, Venus clams and blood cockles. The steamed Venus clams with lemongrass, chilli and pineapple exude a deep umami flavour.

Name: Chả Cá Anh Vũ (Dong Da)
Address: 120-K1 Giang Vo Street, O Cho Dua Ward, Dong Da District, Hanoi, Vietnam
Description: One of four branches in the city, this bouncy family-run operation offers slick service. The homely vibe is depicted by chequered tablecloths, patterned wallpaper and brightly painted murals. Chả cá, grilled catfish seasoned with turmeric, is the name of the game here, although you can add nem cá, fish spring rolls, canh cá, fish soup, and lòng cá, fish stomach, as extras. The fresh, tasty food delivers an explosion of flavours and textures.

Name: Madame Lân
Address: 4 Bach Dang Street, Thach Thang Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, Vietnam
Description: Named after the owner’s late mother, Madame Lân exudes Hoi An flair with its decor and lanterns. The sprawling yellow house is surrounded by water features, boasting both indoor and outdoor seating. The chef rolls out an extensive culinary lineup that covers every facet of Vietnamese cuisine, including the signature dish of Da Nang: fried fish summer roll. Sautéed beef with pepper elder is also a popular salad dish to tickle your tastebuds.

Name: Đông Phố
Address: 57 Ho Xuan Huong Street, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: Popular among the locals and tourists alike, this unpretentious eatery shares a bungalow with an ice cream parlour and specialises in traditional Vietnamese dishes and French snacks. If you find the vast menu a bit daunting, the tasting menu is a great way to sample all the signature dishes. The five-salad assortment includes banana blossom salad, pomelo salad, and baby clams sautéed in angel hair – all of which are refreshing and appetising.

Name: Octo
Address: 2F, 75 Ho Tung Mau Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Description: With bare brick walls, a wood-clad high ceiling and black metal accents, the interior is the epitome of faux-industrial. Drenched in sunlight during the day, it is moodily lit at night. Either way, it has a real buzz that makes for a fun visit. Octo, which bills itself as a tapas restobar, is ideal for Spanish tapas, like their famous traditional croquettes, gazpacho and 48-month Iberico ham, washed down with a round of drinks.

Name: Truffle
Address: 73F, Landmark 81, Vinhomes Central Park, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Towering more than 300 metres above Saigon in Landmark 81, Truffle offers knockout views. As you’d expect, this French restaurant specialises in truffles and offers several tasting menus, all of which feature the seasonally sourced fungi from different countries. The large dining area is surrounded by floor-to-ceiling windows that frame exceptional views of the city below – truly breath taking!

Name: Å by T.U.N.G
Address: 31-33 Dang Dung Street, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: With a ceiling mural of the Northern Lights, the airy dining space is a nod to chef Tung’s stint in Finland. On entering, diners first catch sight of the open kitchen before they are greeted by the chefs. Only one multi-course tasting menu is offered, and it changes every three months in line with the seasons. Chef Tung’s small plates are creative and original, paying tribute to Vietnamese food culture in terms of ingredients, flavours and techniques.

Name: Otok
Description: Located just a minute's walk away from the pretty harbour on the picturesque island of Brač, this lovely modern restaurant sits on the ground floor of the Osam hotel. The terrace is covered with mature olive trees and makes a great spot from which to enjoy the rustic Croatian cooking. Dishes have an honest island feel, with the fish soup particularly delicious. Fresh Adriatic seafood is a feature, accompanied by Croatian wines - and all at a sensible price. Comfortable bedrooms are attached, and the ferry terminal is just two minutes away.

Name: Luciano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Situated just outside the typical medieval village of Buje, this beautiful hotel complex with typical Istrian architecture provides a peaceful oasis for its guests. The Luciano restaurant (named after its main supplier of fresh vegetables) has a welcoming ambience with fine views of the surrounding countryside from its outdoor terrace. Prepared using carefully chosen, top-quality ingredients, the dishes served here are available via an à la carte or on tasting menus of varying lengths. Contemporary meat and fish options with a regional focus take centre stage, accompanied by an extensive selection of local wines.

Name: Matsunoki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the luxurious Hotel Bellevue, this Japanese restaurant boasts a terrace and an elegant dining room with an open-view kitchen and sushi bar. The cuisine here includes excellent sashimi in traditionally prepared and more imaginative recipes, plus ramen dishes, Kobe beef and sea bass carpaccio. The wine list includes options by the glass, as well as the proverbial sake and Japanese whisky.

Name: Dvor
Description: The shaded garden with its open grill and fine views is the main attraction at this beautiful restaurant on the coast overlooking the sea. The catch of the day takes pride of place on the buffet, where guests can also choose their cut of meat. An excellent selection of wine, including by the glass, completes the picture.

Name: Nav
Description: You ring the doorbell to gain access to this restaurant, where just five tables and an open-view kitchen create an intimate and welcoming ambience that deliberately gives the impression of dining in chef Tvrtko Šakota’s own home. The seasonal ingredients in the dishes here are sourced from the restaurant’s own farm, situated 40km from Zagreb. The chef chooses the dishes and Croatian wines served on his surprise tasting menu, where the focus is on small-scale producers who farm in accordance with traditional biodynamic methods. The cuisine takes guests on a creative and personalised journey through Croatia, with an emphasis on dishes cooked in the oven, from the carefully prepared bread to the traditional Salenjaci dessert. Booking ahead and prior payment required.

Name: Theatrium by Filho
Description: Situated in a small courtyard belonging to Zagreb’s youth theatre (ZKM), this young, lively restaurant boasts a bold colour scheme and retro furnishings, with an open-view kitchen and a veranda (the best seats are here). The extensive menu features classic French and Italian dishes alongside more creative options that pay tribute to local cuisine. Starters include fresh fish from the Adriatic, while the Beef Wellington is considered to be one of the chef’s specialities. The excellent wine list includes labels from all over Croatia – make sure you ask for recommendations. Don’t miss the charming outdoor space in summer.

Name: Le Bistro Esplanade
Description: Housed in one of the best hotels in the city, this elegant yet informal all-day bistro has become one of Zagreb’s most popular meeting places and is ideal for a simple snack and aperitif, as well as a full meal. The menu features meat, fish and plenty of vegetables, with a focus on local ingredients and the occasional French influence. Make sure you try the iconic Esplanade Štrukli, pasta filled with cheese and cooked au gratin, a house speciality since 1951. An excellent selection of wines by the glass completes the picture.

Name: Takenoko
Description: This restaurant’s modern appearance provides a striking contrast with its surrounding buildings. Although the menu is described as Nikkei, the Japanese influence is more noticeable here than the Peruvian. Meals start with ceviche and continue with sushi, the latter ranging from classic Japanese to the restaurant’s more creative “American” style. A well-stocked bar and attractive cocktails add to the appeal, while the restaurant’s location makes it convenient for the National Theatre (HNK).

Name: Mon Ami
Address: Trg Kralja Tomislava, 26, Velika Gorica, 10410, Croatia
Description: The many regular guests at this often-crowded restaurant seem to have no doubts about the quality of the meat and fish dishes served here and with good reason! Fish, served in simple, traditional recipes that allow the full flavour to shine through, is the real star of the show. Among the desserts, make sure you try the Skradinska cake, a chocolate speciality with chopped walnuts and orange, in which the three different flavours are balanced to perfection.

Name: Nicolo Polo
Description: You’ll find the small, intimate and privately owned Marco Polo hotel set right on the waterfront of the Makarska Rivijera. Its restaurant, Nicolo Polo, is a light, airy spot and the service is incredibly warm and welcoming. The food is a mix of classical and modern Mediterranean: start with ‘DIY prawns’, before moving on to bold main courses and contrastingly delicate desserts – the rožata is a must-try. There’s also a terrace over the road where they serve simpler dishes during the day.

Name: Boban
Description: Situated in the heart of the pedestrianised area of the historic centre, Boban is a delightful, recently renovated restaurant which serves Mediterranean-style Italian cuisine. The starters are particularly delicious, while the main courses include fish, seafood and meat dishes. There’s also a good wine selection, with an emphasis on champagnes.

Name: Bistro Apetit by Marin Rendić
Description: This restaurant is situated in an elegant and verdant residential district north of the historic centre, in an unexpected location well off the beaten tourist track. Here, the modern dining rooms are full of natural light, providing an attractive setting for imaginative meat and fish dishes, as well as a few Italian-influenced options.

Name: Bugenvila
Address: Put dr. Ante Starčevića 9, Cavtat, 20210, Croatia
Description: This long-established restaurant situated in the charming village of Cavtat stands on the seafront promenade facing the harbour. Its delightful terrace adorned with sweetly scented bougainvillea, geraniums and jasmine has a truly romantic feel, while the cuisine served here focuses on authentic, unfussy Mediterranean dishes made from high-quality meat and fish. Booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Marco Polo
Description: A cute and well-located intimate bistro which is shoehorned into the center of the old town-sited in a narrow privately owned passage. Honest and true - the menu is light, colorful and seasonal - all the dishes reflect the Mediterranean so well. The specialties change frequently; maybe a fresh tempura of mussels and fish will tempt you! The desserts will as they are a highlight - lovely creamy pannacotta - if you are really lucky, they will get a taste of the delicious house made cherry brandy. It really is the perfect place for lunch.

Name: Gallo
Description: Located in the basement of the “Castellum Centar”, this elegantly decorated restaurant serves cuisine based around Mediterranean- and Italian-inspired fish dishes, alongside homemade pasta and highly enticing desserts. Very friendly service, an impressive wine selection and outdoor dining in summer add to its appeal.

Name: Johnson
Description: Just a stone’s throw from one of the most beautiful beaches in the region, this restaurant serves fresh fish, scampi and shellfish caught that very day and prepared in simple, traditional dishes that allow the full flavour of the fish and seafood to shine through (dishes are announced at your table). In summer, don’t miss the relaxing and sunny panoramic terrace. The Jurdan family have been running this restaurant since 1996 – almost thirty years of enthusiastic and reliable service.

Name: Foša
Description: Fish and seafood specialities take pride of place at this restaurant situated just behind the town’s 16C walls overlooking the port at Foša. The Dalmatian-inspired cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary in style, while in summer, the delightful terrace overlooking the sea is an absolute must.

Name: Mediterraneo
Description: A family run eatery for over 70 years, which is snuggled away close to the picturesque harbour in the very heart of Hvar old town. You will be warmly greeted with the menus and a glass of house made honey grappa! The fish dishes are popular; do choose the delightful Grdobina - monkfish, parmesan and tomato - with immense flavour, a glass of Zlatan Pošip completes the picture. A pretty large terrace is at the heart of the restaurant, floral arrangements fringe the walls. A lovely small private room is lined with some fine wines, many from the island and Croatia. Do make a reservation at they are always fully booked in season.

Name: BÒME
Description: The exterior of this surprising “socialist-style” Modernist building decorated in bright colours is in sharp contrast with the more contemporary interior. Warmly run by owner-chef Mario himself (who has returned to the area where he grew up) and by his fiancée Franciska, the restaurant has just seven tables arranged in front of an L-shaped kitchen. Specialities here follow a modern Mediterranean approach in dishes where flavours are highly balanced and textures play an important role. The bread and pasta are made on the premises with ingredients purchased by the chef himself in the local market.

Name: Tekka by Lone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you take a seat in its delightful summer garden or beautiful minimalist-style dining room, the Japanese restaurant at the extremely modern Lone hotel provides an interesting blend of Istrian and Japanese cuisine. The techniques and recipes are Japanese, while the ingredients and personalised reinterpretations are from the region. We particularly enjoyed the duck breast with chicory, which was cooked to perfection with crispy skin and accompanied by a creamy umeboshi plum and pomegranate sauce – the perfect balance of sweet and savoury flavours.

Name: Vapor
Address: Hotel Bellevue, Pera Čingrije 7, Dubrovnik, 20000, Croatia
Description: One of the main attractions of this restaurant in the luxurious Bellevue Hotel is the superb sea view that can be enjoyed from its terrace and through the large windows in its dining room. Another is the fresh Mediterranean cuisine on offer here, which includes a delicious sea bream ceviche served with marinated citrus fruit, salmon roe and crispy quinoa chips.

Name: Mala Hiza
Description: Occupying a late-19C house surrounded by a beautiful garden with a fountain and small stream, this friendly restaurant run by its owner-chef and his family boasts a romantic ambience. The cuisine is regional in style, with a focus on local ingredients and dishes accompanied by local wines. Appetisers include stuffed pasta, while meat options (especially beef and lamb) dominate the main courses. To finish your meal in style, why not try the gibanica, a popular local dessert made with layers of shortcrust pastry, fresh cheese, eggs and pumpkin.

Name: Nautika
Description: One of the busiest restaurants in the city (so booking well in advance is recommended), Nautika serves carefully prepared, traditional cuisine that is full of flavour. The dishes here are rooted in a respect for local traditions and enhanced with French and Italian influences, while avoiding the latest culinary trends and exotic twists. The service is impeccable and the wine list highly impressive. Make sure you try the prawns with semolina gnocchi, beurre blanc, parsley cream and toasted almonds, a dish full of delicious and enticing flavours. There’s a magnificent view of the two fortresses lit up at night from the front terrace.

Name: Morgan
Description: Situated in the green heart of Istria, this long-established, family-run hotel-restaurant boasts a welcoming dining room plus an attractive summer terrace looking out at the countryside. The regional cuisine served here closely follows the seasons, with game, mushrooms and truffles making an appearance in autumn, and vegetables and fresh cheeses in spring. Throughout the year, you can enjoy delicious Istrian hams and homemade pasta, including the tasty asparagus-filled ravioli served with grilled asparagus.

Name: San Rocco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This romantic hotel-restaurant occupies an elegant stone building in a typical small Istrian village just a few kilometres from the sea. Take a seat in what was once the wine cellar or outdoors on the summer terrace, where you’ll enjoy well-crafted, creative dishes that are full of flavour and made from top-quality local, seasonal ingredients, with a choice of meat and fish dishes, as well as a 5-course vegetarian menu. In autumn, the menu is enhanced by delicacies such as truffles, mushrooms and game. Guided tastings of the restaurant’s own extra-virgin olive oil can be enjoyed in the oil boutique.

Name: Bistro Tavulin
Description: Although this restaurant is admittedly aimed at tourists given its central location in the heart of Dubrovnik, the cuisine here is prepared using fresh, local ingredients which result in pleasing, elegantly presented dishes that are full of flavour. The superb agnolotti pasta stuffed with Adriatic prawns, accompanied by a beurre blanc and parsley-flavoured oil, is delicious and beautifully prepared.

Name: Balon
Description: In a verdant setting not far from the banks of the River Sava, this charmingly elegant bistro-style restaurant, which has stood on the same square for many years but has been recently refurbished, is surrounded by glass on three sides and boasts a spacious terrace for summer dining. The classic cuisine served here is inspired by the Mediterranean and features some original touches by the chef.

Name: The Restaurant at Maslina Resort
Description: Housed in the luxurious Maslina Resort directly facing the sea, this elegant, minimalist-style restaurant is in perfect harmony with its surroundings. The cuisine combines French techniques with local and Mediterranean ingredients, such as the herbs and vegetables grown in the property’s own kitchen garden. The à la carte menu features meat and fish dishes which are served in the dining room or on the terrace alongside the pool.

Name: Restaurant Mare
Description: Situated on the island of Čiovo, just a 5-minute walk from the historic centre of Trogir, this restaurant is part of the Hotel Bifora Heritage, a 14C building that was restored in 2016. Here, chef Robert Predag Zmire uses modern techniques to create delicious cuisine from fine ingredients. Although fish takes centre stage, there’s also a choice of meat dishes and a few vegan options. The dishes are carefully prepared and full of flavour, including options such as cuttlefish tagliatelle with a wild herb pesto, sea asparagus, lemon pearls and prawn chips, and the extremely fresh sea bass ikejime served with celery and a parsley sauce. Although the wine list is not particularly extensive, it offers good value for money and includes many Croatian wines available by the glass. A welcoming restaurant a little off the tourist track, with a charming, intimate stone patio that is perfect for summer dining.

Name: Zinfandel Food & Wine bar
Description: Situated in a narrow street in the old town, this busy, welcoming restaurant is open from breakfast to dinner, when live music adds to the atmosphere. The young Croatian chef serves eclectic cuisine which includes Dalmatian recipes alongside more internationally influenced fare. Some of the dishes are designed for sharing, such as the platters of local hams and cheeses, while the homemade tonnarelli pasta with a Prošek wine sauce, onions, garlic and prawns is excellent. The well-curated wine list covers the whole of Croatia, with around 15 wines also available by the glass.

Name: El Toro
Address: Ul. fra Filipa Grabovca 1, Zagreb, 10000, Croatia
Description: A new option among the capital’s cosmopolitan restaurants, El Toro offers a Taco menu (we recommend the langoustine), as well as sushi and sashimi, with an excellent tuna hamachi served with Oscietra caviar proving one of the most popular choices at the sushi bar. The main dishes have a South American influence and are cooked over the grill, with large Rib Eye and T-bone steaks available for two or more people to share. Arranged over two floors, the restaurant is modern and trendy in style despite its location at the base of an old-fashioned building. The wine list includes top-quality labels from Croatia and further afield, many available by the glass – ask the young staff for pairing recommendations.

Name: Waldinger
Description: The name of this restaurant situated in the Art Nouveau-style hotel of the same name pays tribute to the painter Adolf Waldinger, who was born in Osijek in 1843. In bright, modern dining rooms adorned with contemporary paintings, enjoy a selection of traditional dishes, with something for all tastes on the menu. If you like strong flavours, try the Slavonian black pork cheeks, while guests with a sweet tooth will be tempted by delicious desserts from the Gold pastry shop on the other side of the street, including Krempite tart (a puff pastry speciality with custard cream). The wine list includes labels from local, small-scale wineries. Comfortable, well-appointed guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Ribarska Koliba
Description: This century-old restaurant in the modern resort of Ribarska Koliba (the name translates as Fisherman’s Hut) stands near the Marina Veruda, which can be admired through its large picture windows or from its attractive summer terrace. Delicious Mediterranean cuisine takes pride of place on the menu, ranging from pasta-based starters to fish and seafood dishes made from the freshest ingredients (the bouillabaisse is superb), although a few meat specialities also feature. Vintage car enthusiasts can also admire the Triumph Spitfire convertible that is “parked” inside the restaurant.

Name: Konoba TRS
Description: Situated in an alleyway in the busy historic centre, this restaurant boasts an elegant dining room with exposed stonework and an attractive outdoor patio. The traditional Mediterranean cuisine with a modern touch is showcased on an à la carte and a tasting menu. The house specialities include a delicious brodetto with langoustine, monkfish and octopus, which is served with creamy mashed potatoes.

Name: Konoba Tri Piruna
Description: Mature, large and aged steaks are at the heart of the business here-carved in the room with skill (the steaks are all Croatian and of upmost quality) they are modern in presentation and accompanied by a good choice of wines. The simple dining room has a rustic and relaxed feel, while the cool, shaded outdoor terrace comes into its own in summer.

Name: Konoba Fetivi
Description: A very popular restaurant in the city, which is well worth a visit for its traditional cuisine served in a simple yet beautifully kept dining room. The menu features unpretentious Mediterranean fish dishes and traditional meat specialities, with ingredients purchased fresh from the local market every day. Don’t miss the delicious apple strudel, which is made from an old family recipe. The friendly welcome from all the staff is an added attraction!

Name: Tekka
Description: A small Japanese restaurant with a modern feel and an open-view kitchen that allows guests to watch the chefs at work. Traditional Japanese specialities such as nigiri, uramaki, hosomaki and sashimi are to the fore, as well as tempura and teppanyaki and other Asian options including stir-fries.

Name: Pod Zidom
Description: A modern-style bistro with a wine bar and small attractive outdoor space in the city centre, just behind the main square with fine views of the cathedral. The chef, who describes his cuisine as “market-fresh”, makes daily visits to the nearby Dolac market for his ingredients, which include seasonal vegetables, Dalmatian charcuterie, and meat reared on local farms. The owner is passionate about wine, and includes several Croatian wines made from native grape varieties on the wine list, which also pays close attention to organic labels.

Name: Villa Ariston
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Housed in a beautiful 19C residence with a garden offering stunning sea views, Villa Ariston is one of the region’s unmissable gastronomic experiences. The cuisine maintains a subtle balance between tradition, classic flavours and the creativity which has given the restaurant its fine reputation. The menu features numerous fish dishes (the scampi-filled ravioli served with a scampi and mussel bisque are delicious), as well as local specialities such as lamb from nearby Cres island.

Name: Zlatne Gorice
Description: Situated in a picturesque and relaxing setting of rolling hills, vineyards and charming villas, this restaurant is part of a wine estate. The cuisine focuses on regional specialities with an emphasis on meat, including a wide array of grilled dishes.

Name: Konoba Buščina
Description: This beautiful rustic-style inn occupying a country house just outside Umag has been in business for 30 years. Here, traditional meat and fish ingredients such as scallops, langoustine, Boscarin beef, Istrian ham and truffles inspire simple, generous dishes which showcase the best of the region. Friendly service and pleasantly informal atmosphere.

Name: ZOI
Address: Obala Hrvatskog Narodnog Preporoda 23, Split, 21000, Croatia
Description: This restaurant boasts what is arguably the best location in the centre of Split, with a long panoramic terrace that runs alongside the southern section of the Palace of Diocletian and offers fine views of the port. The young chef reinterprets traditional Dalmatian cuisine inspired by old recipes and offer three menus: Obala (focuses on fish and seafood), Zagora (ingredients from inland areas), and a long menu that combines the two. The delicious carrot cake with cashew nuts and orange juice offers a snapshot of Split’s commercial history, combining the port’s exports (carrots and oranges) with other ingredients that were imported (cashews). We recommend booking a table on the top floor to make the most of the beautiful view.

Name: Šug
Description: Šug is the Croatian word for sauce, an important feature of this chef’s cuisine. Situated away from the busy tourist centre of Split, this informal, attractive and relaxing restaurant serves generous portions of traditional meat and fish dishes from Dalmatia, with the occasional influence from nearby Italy. In summer, the small outdoor space in an inner courtyard adds to the appeal.

Name: Spinnaker
Description: It was at Heinz Beck’s La Pergola that chef Goran Hrastovčak learned how to make an ingredient the centrepiece of a dish. In his two tasting menus, “Istrian Fables” and “Modern Tales” (as the names suggest, the first is more traditional and the second more innovative), the cuisine showcases the region and its iconic ingredients, such as scampi, squid, sea bass and Istrian beef. The ravioli filled with lobster and served with Jerusalem artichoke and a scampi bisque is highly recommended. The view of Poreč harbour plus a wine list that features excellent Istrian labels as well as an extensive selection of Croatian wines and renowned bottles from elsewhere in Europe add to the appeal. Among the local wines, we suggest the Primo Fakin, an Istrian Teran-based red with spicy aromas and a pleasant roundness.

Name: Konoba Boba
Description: A gastronomic landmark on the island of Murter, the gateway to the Kornati archipelago, which is linked to the mainland by a small bridge. Although the restaurant is a “konoba” (tavern) in name, it is decidedly elegant in feel, with an intimate dining room and outdoor space for the summer months. The cuisine has a Mediterranean focus with just a few meat dishes, while raw fish options (especially tuna) are the house speciality. The property’s kitchen garden provides the fruit and vegetables used in the dishes here, as well as herbs such as marjoram, oregano, basil, rosemary, mint and parsley. There’s also a good choice of wine with an emphasis on Dalmatia and elsewhere in Croatia. The young, dynamic staff add to the appeal.

Name: Meneghetti
Description: This rustic yet elegant hotel restaurant occupies a charming stone building idyllically situated among vineyards and olive trees in tranquil countryside. The cuisine, which is traditionally Mediterranean with personalised touches, is accompanied by the property’s own excellent wines and olive oils, with a wide selection of the latter that includes whites, reds and classic sparkling options.

Name: Marina
Description: This tiny yet elegant restaurant with a terrace overlooking the port is situated just above street level. At the helm in the kitchen (visible through a large window from the dining room), the female owner serves modern, Mediterranean fish and seafood dishes on tasting menus which vary according to market availability.

Name: Stara Loza
Address: Prijeko Palace Hotel, Prijeko 22, Dubrovnik, 20000, Croatia
Description: Housed in the Old Town of this UNESCO World Heritage city is the intimate and luxurious Prijeko Palace Hotel. Its restaurant, Stara Loza, is almost three in one – there’s a street level terrace, a formal restaurant on the third floor and a delightful open terrace right at the top which affords great views. Cooking is Mediterranean in heart, with plenty of depth and flavour. The veal risotto is a must-try and be sure to save room for dessert, which is always a highlight.

Name: ManO2
Description: Situated just outside the old town, this elegant restaurant with contemporary furnishings also boasts an attractive outdoor space near the entrance. The meat and fish dishes served here combine creative touches with a solid foundation in traditional Croatian cuisine, as well as a focus on top-quality grilled meats. There are two tasting menus (five or eight courses), plus a fairly extensive à la carte. Among the appetisers, try the prawn and crab salad with miso and toasted almond cream, salicornia, seaweed and buckwheat “pops”.

Name: Cap Aureo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the elegant and stylish Grand Park Hotel Rovinj by Maistra Collection, this restaurant offers spectacular views of Rovinj’s old town and marina from its glass-enclosed terrace. Chef Jeffrey Vella’s seasonal tasting menu showcases modern, Mediterranean cuisine made from local ingredients, with a particular focus on Istrian flavours and traditions. In addition to meat and fish dishes, careful attention is paid to vegetarian options.

Name: Kadena
Description: The main attraction of this restaurant, one of the most elegant addresses in the city, is its stunning location overlooking the sea and the delightful views from its outdoor terrace. On the menu, the undisputed star of the show is the fresh fish displayed in a chilled cabinet, although a few meat dishes are also available. Highlights include the saffron ravioli with blue crabmeat and leeks, and the sea bass fillet with baby beets, pine nuts, a white wine reduction and caper sauce. The wine list features an interesting choice of wines, champagnes and sparkling wines from Croatia and further afield, as well as top-quality gins and whiskies.

Name: Damir & Ornella
Description: The welcoming ambience and the quality of the ingredients used are the trump cards of this family-run restaurant, which serves delicious fish and seafood. Raw marinated fish is the house speciality, including scampi, prawns, squid, cuttlefish, marinated sole and a few pasta dishes. The concise menu is announced at your table, a sure guarantee of fresh ingredients.

Name: Zinfandel's
Description: Situated in the Hotel Esplanade, which dates back to 1925 and is one of the most luxurious hotels in Zagreb, Zifandel's cuisine has been overseen by chef Ana Grgić for the past ten years. She reinterprets Mediterranean traditions in a creative and personalised style, with a focus on local, seasonal ingredients.

Name: Il Ponte
Description: Located just a stone’s throw from the centre, this elegant restaurant named after Trogir’s iconic wooden bridge boasts a beautiful dining room with a veranda and stylish furnishings with a blue-and-yellow colour scheme. The cuisine is inspired by the flavours and traditions of the Mediterranean and prepared using modern techniques and creative twists – in summer, there’s a barbecue grill where the chef can be observed at work. Guests with a sweet tooth will enjoy the delicious desserts.

Name: Dunav
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Situated on the banks of the Danube (known as Dunav in Croatian), this restaurant boasts an excellent location which can be enjoyed from its outdoor terrace in summer. The menu features fish from the river, including grilled zander and catfish fillets in white wine. Guests with a sweet tooth will enjoy rounding off their meal with a taške (a kind of jam-filled pastry) or a šnenokle, the Croatian version of the French île flottante.

Name: Bedem
Description: “Bedem” is the Croatian word for “bastion” – a highly appropriate name for this restaurant which overlooks Varaždin’s historic castle and surrounding park. The cuisine here is classically French in style, with a contemporary touch and the use of local, seasonal ingredients such as vegetables from nearby Vidovce, pumpkin oil, turkey from Zagorie and local trout. The strukli (dumplings) stuffed with fresh cheese and served as an appetiser are delicious and the local wines offer excellent value for money. In winter, take a seat near the fireplace, while in summer the outdoor terrace is a must.

Name: Jeny
Address: D512, 2 località Gornje Tučepi, Tucepi, 21325, Croatia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: The first thing you’ll notice when you get here is the spectacular view: the restaurant is actually perched over the coastal village. Jeny is the tangible manifestation of a real family business whose key players are two brothers: Milenko in the dining room and Vladomir in the kitchen. In high season (1 July - 15 August) there are three tasting menus of 7, 5 and 3 courses: modern and sometimes articulated dishes, with an indisputable aesthetic appeal. The table on the patio is a great plus!

Name: Zrno Soli
Description: Enjoy views of boats and yachts, as well as of the sea and the centre of Split from the terrace of this restaurant located on the first floor of the ACI Marina. The classic, renowned cuisine focuses on fish and seafood, which diners can choose directly from the display cabinet. Large seasonal menu represents the area and the season; have the seafood tasting menu, if you are lucky the monkfish soup and the cuttlefish with bulgur wheat will be on it. Last, but not least, the desserts are not to be ignored.

Name: Konoba Zijavica
Description: The sea takes centre stage at this welcoming restaurant in a delightful fishing village, both on the plate and in its location just a stone’s throw from the water. In the dining room, guests can admire the chef at work in the tiny open-view kitchen, while the restaurant’s veranda overlooking the sea with the waves lapping the shore is a real gem. The focus here is personalised fish cuisine, where the main ingredient is the star of the show. Be patient if something is missing from the menu – the fish on offer here depends very much on the season and local fishermen’s catch of the day. Simple yet delicious recipes are to the fore, including raw fish dishes, pasta, and fish and shellfish priced by weight – a real paradise for fresh fish enthusiasts. As for Mošćenička Draga itself, this is the perfect location for lazing on the beach or cycling in the surrounding hills.

Name: PiNKU fish & wine
Description: This small restaurant, once a butcher’s shop, is located next to the Peškarija fish market, where the chef chooses the best local fish for his creative cuisine. Dishes, showcased on an à la carte (lunchtime only) and a 6-course tasting menu, can be enjoyed in the dining room or outdoors on the terrace, and are often prepared using modern techniques such as sous-vide cooking. Try delicious recipes such as poached hake with cuttlefish noodles accompanied by poached egg, a beetroot coulis and citrus fruit foam.

Name: Konoba Kala
Description: Hidden away close to the main harbour lies this intimate and beautifully designed restaurant. Take a seat on the delightful terrace with large wooden benches if you fancy enjoying the quality cooking al fresco. Two menus are available, which both reflect the island well, with seasonally influenced cooking including Adriatic fish and some lovely lamb. Some dishes are cooked over the wood-burning fire for a natural smoky flavour. Desserts are a real highlight, with those featuring figs particularly worth choosing. Top off your visit by trying one of the local island wines - a glass or two of Senjković Bosso is called for.

Name: Filippi
Description: This restaurant along the seafront promenade in the old town boasts an outdoor space overlooking the sea, the Pelješac channel and the islands of the Korčula archipelago. The cuisine here is classic, unpretentious and decidedly Mediterranean, with a focus on fish on 3-or 4-course set menus, as well as on a tasting menu.
