The concise wine list showcases wines from Korčula, Hvar and Pelješac, with particular attention paid to lesser-known producers. The sea bass served with green peas, courgettes and gregada, a typical Croatian seafood soup, is delicious.

Name: Dubrovnik
Description: In this elegant, stylish restaurant in the heart of the historic centre, the chef uses local ingredients to create fresh, delicious dishes such as scallops with soft polenta, goat’s cheese, hazelnuts and porcini mushrooms, and a mouthwatering puff pastry dessert filled with figs cooked in the local sweet Prošek wine and served with vanilla cream, cinnamon and almonds. Don’t miss the enchanting outdoor terrace in summer.

Name: Zuzori
Description: This small restaurant within the city’s medieval walls has a welcoming and informal atmosphere. The menu is imaginative and includes fresh seafood from the Adriatic, pasta dishes, light salads and vegetarian options with a pleasing contemporary touch. The attractive outdoor dining area in an alleyway in the historic centre allows guests to experience all the magic of Dubrovnik.

Name: Proto Fish
Description: Choose between the terrace out on the street, the dining room and (easily the best option) the first-floor terrace at this restaurant in the heart of the old town. The restaurant’s name hints at the menu, which focuses on fresh local fish served in tempting dishes such as the superb fresh sea bass, king prawns and delicious barbecue-grilled octopus. Make sure you leave space for dessert: the rožata (crème caramel) is the perfect conclusion to your meal.

Name: Wine Vault Restaurant - Levante Edition
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the luxurious “adult only” Monte Mulini hotel, this restaurant with a beautiful terrace serves local cuisine prepared using regional produce alongside a few Asian ingredients – guests choose the number of courses they want from the menu. Careful attention is paid to wine pairing, with an impressive selection of local labels, including sparkling wines and a good choice of champagnes.

Name: Badi
Description: Although a few meat dishes feature on the menu, it is fish and seafood that has cemented this restaurant’s reputation. Its dishes are traditionally prepared with an emphasis on simplicity in order to allow the quality of the fish to shine through. Scampi features widely, while the “Badi” soup, breaded sea bass and various “na buzaru” dishes (stewed in white wine with parsley, garlic and breadcrumbs) are among the house specialities.

Name: Kaštel
Description: This restaurant is housed within the luxurious Hotel Bastion, which occupies the remains of a corner tower of the town walls. In this intimate and elegant setting, enjoy Mediterranean cuisine with its roots in Dalmatian traditions yet with an intriguing Italian influence. In summer, booking a table on the terrace with its fine panoramic views is highly recommended.

Name: Torero
Description: Situated in the oldest, most visited part of Zagreb, this quiet, well-run restaurant welcomes guests with an entire wall covered with plants and flowers that symbolise the Medvednica, the mountain chain to the north of the capital that inspires the cuisine served here. With a focus on local, mostly organic ingredients, dishes are colourful and creative, aiming to awaken the senses by introducing a range of different flavours (sweet, acidic, bitter etc). The sommelier will happily recommend Croatian wines to accompany your meal, while the service is enthusiastic, friendly and attentive. Make sure you taste the risotto made with Acquerello rice, as well as the Torero’s own delicious cheesecake.

Name: Pjerin
Address: Villa Dubrovnik, Vlaha Bukovca 6, Dubrovnik, 20000, Croatia
Description: Situated outside the city centre, the Villa Dubrovnik hotel provides a tranquil and relaxing setting. Enjoy an aperitif at the roof-top bar and admire stunning views of the coast, which are also visible from the Pjerin restaurant terrace. The excellent cuisine here is regional and seasonal, with fish and seafood from the Adriatic taking centre stage. The home-made appetisers are truly delicious, with the lobster spaghetti now justly considered to be a house speciality. The discreet and elegant service includes recommendations on the best Croatian wine pairings.

Name: Zigante
Description: Istria is famous for its excellent truffles and this restaurant is considered by foodies to be one of the best places to enjoy this delicious speciality. Zigante’s mostly meat-based dishes are enhanced with either white or black truffles, depending on the variety and the season, and the theme even continues with the desserts which feature a black truffle ice cream. There are two tasting menus in addition to the à la carte, plus a shop next door which sells various truffle-based specialities.

Name: Ouzeria
Description: Maria Karpathiotaki and her partner Nikos Kasotakis have taken over her parents' Greek restaurant in the Belgian Quarter and turned it into a trendy, vibrant fine dining spot. While she cordially welcomes guests front of house in the well-kept rustic-style bistro space, the chef is to be found at work in the kitchen, cooking up modern, creative dishes with Mediterranean and Asian influences. The menu includes a lovely selection of starters, plated in slightly smaller portions that are good for sharing and for trying out several – examples include "baby calamari, red pepper, pine nut pesto" and "half a corn-fed poulard breast, fermented celery, baby pak choi, ponzu, miso-samos-nectar espuma". Naturally, the menu also features ouzo. There is a small terrace laid out on the pavement.

Name: TAO Restaurant
Description: Here at "TAO POP-UP – THE WAY TO ATAMA", Martin Stopp (previously of LOUIS in Saarlouis) set up shop while planning the opening of his ATAMA restaurant in nearby Sankt Ingbert. His entirely ingredient-led cuisine draws on solid classical foundations, with well-judged Japanese influences delivering interesting accents and a variety of flavours. For instance, his personal take on a fabulously fresh and succulent pikeperch – he marinates the fish in koji then combines it with a really fruity and tangy rhubarb vinaigrette and a beurre blanc that has all the subtle sweetness of roasted yeast, before finishing the dish off with petits pois and a silky, aromatic parsnip purée. Diners can expect very friendly, attentive and efficient service courtesy of the front-of-house team, with the chef himself occasionally getting in on the action.

Name: Berghotel Wiedener Eck
Description: Marie and Lorenz Wissler represent the fourth generation of their family to run Berghotel Wiedener Eck, which enjoys an idyllic location at over 1 000m above sea level – the view of the valley is stunning! For overnight stays, there are attractive, cosy guestrooms, and the restaurant is brimming with traditional Black Forest charm, interspersed with modern touches. In the restaurant, you can look forward to friendly and courteous service, as well as regional cuisine and dishes that draw on the culinary traditions of France and the Mediterranean, all made from fresh high-quality ingredients – the chef even hunts his own game. In the evenings, there is a set menu that changes every day, plus the seasonal "Wiedener Eck Menü". You can also order the individual courses of both à la carte. Tip: The surrounding forests and meadows make this hotel a perfect starting point for hikes!

Name: TAWA YAMA EASY
Description: This is a cool alternative to FINE, the fine dining restaurant also located on the first floor of the modern building and accessible by lift. Asian cuisine takes centre stage here, with dishes ranging from shumai prawn dumplings to Iberian pork katsu, white cabbage and carrot salad, ponzu and honey jus; they also lend themselves to sharing. What is more, the bill for these delicious but reasonably priced dishes won't break the bank. The atmosphere is nice and lively and the team provides highly attentive and professional service. Tip: Try one of the tasty cocktails. There is also a simple "Easy Lunch" deal.

Name: Frau Specht
Description: "Dinner is ready" is the slogan here. You ring the doorbell before being escorted into this somewhat hidden little restaurant with a modern, minimalist decor. You are shown to your table in a pleasantly intimate living room-style interior – with a small open kitchen and just a handful of tables, it makes for a private atmosphere. The service comes with a personal touch: your cordial hostess, Yvonne Specht, after whom the restaurant is named, will also recommend just the right wines from the extensive list of top-draw international labels. In the kitchen, head chef Dirk Brendel cooks up an ambitious seven-course surprise menu in the evening, further embellishing it with a variety of additional small dishes. The menu is devised based on the season and the availability of the ingredients. The cuisine is classic and Mediterranean, but also includes international flavours.

Name: Imprevisto
Description: The four young owners of this unpretentious restaurant, two of whom work in the kitchen and two in in the dining room, were keen that the name of their business was not something banal or vacuous, but rather a name that expressed their philosophy and offered the promise of a relaxed dining experience based around continual new discoveries. The end result is a contemporary style of cooking that is high on detail and focuses on seasonal ingredients, as witnessed by the short à la carte (weekday lunches) and two tasting menus (7 and 10 courses, respectively). The beef tartare with horseradish, blackberries, pickled mustard seeds and demi-glace is teeming with nuanced flavours and textures.

Name: Taberna 5 Mares
Address: Parque Monte San Pedro, A Coruña, 15011, Spain
Description: The cooking at this taberna is fun as well as delicious! And with this in mind, the duo of owner-chefs Iria Espinosa and Luis Veira have strived for what they describe as the offbeat face of gourmet cuisine. This bright space occupying the former café adjoining the Arbore da Veira restaurant reflects the more informal and casual dining option of this award-winning name, which features an à la carte of appetisers and main dishes suitable for all budgets (it also includes a section entitled “landscapes for sharing”), in addition to an affordable tasting menu that showcases several signature dishes (spherical olives, carpaccio of scallops “al ajillo” with black garlic, etc). The impressive views over A Coruña add further appeal!

Name: Mare
Address: Plaza de la Candelaria 12, Cadiz, 11005, Spain
Description: Chef Juan Viu, who defines himself as a “stewmaker”, views his cuisine as “a tribute to time-honoured cooking, to that of mothers, and to the sea”. The Pureza (Purity) menu, which changes almost daily depending on the availability of seasonal ingredients and those purchased from the nearby fish auctions in Conil, Vejer de la Frontera, Chiclana etc, reinterprets classic Cádiz recipes from a more contemporary perspective, with prominence shown to flavours from his childhood as well as maritime-inspired stews. Iconic dishes available year round include the highly original squid-based “calamar guisado en frío” and “grandmother Trini’s sofrito”.

Name: Pabú
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant that is definitely in vogue and one which continues to gain new fans – even the royal family celebrated a birthday here! Located close to the legendary Santiago Bernabéu football stadium, Pabú reflects the gourmet vision of Coco Montes, a Cordon Bleu chef who has worked in prestigious restaurants such as Arpège in Paris, under the baton of famous chef Alain Passard. His cooking is based around the purity of ingredients, hence his championing of micro-seasonal cuisine that changes daily in line with provisions from his suppliers and is highly focused on vegetables, with little protein, delicate textures and plenty of personality. It also highlights an extensive knowledge of classic French techniques and is centred around two surprise tasting menus (Pate and Bubú), although dishes on these can also be ordered individually à la carte style. The bread here is made with natural sourdough, while the selection of international cheeses is particularly impressive.

Name: Leartá
Description: Located in the heart of the city’s old quarter, just a few metres from the Plaza de la Gavidia, this restaurant exudes a passion for food, for craftsmanship and for what they describe here as “food for thought” and takes its from a word that refers to a meeting place for different Andalucian trades and skills. The focus of the young team at the helm is on a single tasting menu that showcases the flavours of Southern Spain as well as locally sourced ingredients and products (Iberian ham from Cumbres Mayores, white prawns from Isla Cristina, honey from Aznalcóllar etc). At the same time it respects the essence of tradition albeit from a more contemporary perspective, and always with an interesting play of textures and highly delicate sauces and broths.

Name: La Suculenta
Description: Based around the mantra “Taste the unexpected”, this modern, centrally located restaurant run by chef Jorge Lengua (one of the promising new names on the Valencia food scene), offers contemporary-inspired cuisine that is showcased via well-presented dishes that make full use of modern techniques, such as the Iberian ham croquettes with “torrezno” (fried bacon) powder, and the Andalucian-style glass shrimp with fried egg and kimchi mayonnaise. The à la carte, which features lots of small plates, is complemented by an impressive array of rice dishes and several set menus.

Name: Indómito
Address: Rúa Do Doutor Teixeiro 28, Santiago de Compostela, 15701, Spain
Description: Just a few minutes from the city’s stunning old quarter you’ll find the latest venture of chef Martín Vázquez (ex head chef at Casa Marcelo), who is following his own path with this relaxed restaurant that showcases his indomitable (“indómito” in Spanish) spirit. In this meticulously arranged setting, where the open kitchen behind the counter tales centre stage, the à la carte features some 20 options that constantly rotate in line with the availability of seasonal ingredients (clam soup, hake from Celeiro, semifreddo of avocado and sea bream with a jalapeño sauce). The chef continually interacts with guests, suggesting dishes so that they can create their own menu, including options for sharing.

Name: Cova Sacra
Address: Real Sitio de Covadonga, Covadonga, 33589, Spain
Description: If you’re looking for a good restaurant around Covadonga, this option in the Gran Hotel Pelayo won’t disappoint as the cooking comes courtesy of renowned chef Jaime Uz. The à la carte, with its strong roots in Asturian cuisine, is impressively supported by an extensive tasting menu called “La Santina”. The dining room enjoys relaxing views of its spectacular natural surroundings as well as the basilica.

Name: Morchella
Address: 84-86 Rosebery Avenue, Islington, London, EC1R 4QY, United Kingdom
Description: Set in a converted former bank, Morchella sports a small but well-stocked wine bar to one side, offering largely natural and biodynamic options that the wine list describes as either ‘Classic’, ‘Coastal’ or ‘Funky’. On the food side of things, the menu has a Mediterranean slant and is designed for sharing – although if the spaghetti alle vongole is available, you’ll be loath to give any up. Service is bright and breezy, while the great value lunch menu means you can dine without breaking the bank, so to speak.

Address: Cottage in the Wood Hotel,  Holywell Road, Malvern Wells, WR14 4LG, United Kingdom
Description: In finer weather, you must aim for a table on the terrace at this restaurant set within the famous The Cottage in the Wood hotel. Built – funnily enough – in 1919, it boasts one of the best panoramic views of the English countryside that you will find. The restaurant itself is a bright, stylish place serving both a tasting menu and an à la carte. A proudly British spirit shines through in the cooking, from the use of Exmoor caviar and Evesham asparagus to a butter sauce flavoured with English sparkling wine. The service is well-paced and the whole experience comes at a sensible price tag.

Name: Hansom
Address: 7-9 North End, Bedale, DL8 1AF, United Kingdom
Description: A stone-faced 16th-century house in the pretty market town of Bedale provides a fine home for this friendly restaurant. A drinks terrace sits on the cobbled street out front, while small plates are served in the interior wine bar. The main dining room, where the tasting menu is the focus, stylishly contrasts rustic beams and an old fireplace with modern décor. Eponymous Chef-Owner Ruth Hansom is a local and it shows in her cooking, which skilfully spotlights wonderful produce from the surrounding area – be it Swaledale lamb or the famous Yorkshire rhubarb.

Name: The Shed
Address: Unit 1&2 J-Shed, Kings Road, Swansea, SA1 8PL, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced Chef-Owner Jonathan Woolway worked in London for many years before returning home to his beloved Wales to open this industrial-style restaurant by the former docks. His patriotic side comes out in the use of terrific local produce, along with a none-more-Welsh lamb, leek and laverbread pie to share. The other dishes too, from Mangatlisa brawn to a Welsh rarebit on the side, are hearty, traditional and decidedly unfussy.

Name: Josephine
Address: 315 Fulham Road, Chelsea, London, SW10 9QH, United Kingdom
Description: Chef Claude Bosi returns to his Lyonnaise roots with this buzzy ‘bouchon’, where the tables are tightly packed and the walls are adorned with colourful posters. The menu could scarcely be more French if it was emblazoned with the tricolore: vol-au-vent, andouillete, frog’s legs… take your pick. It’s all executed with great skill and packs in plenty of flavour, while the service is delivered with a certain ‘bonne humeur’. The set menu is remarkably good value and the well-chosen wine list contains some notable French producers.

Name: Ballyfin
Address: Ballyfin Demesne, Ballyfin, R32 X5X8, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: It takes some doing for a restaurant to stand out when it’s in a hotel as beautiful as this. Ballyfin Demesne is a spectacular, lovingly restored Regency-era manor house that screams luxury at every turn. The opulence continues into the dining room, where the chefs serve fittingly impressive dishes. Broths, purées and sauces are a real highlight and underline the technical skill of the kitchen team, be it a rich, glossy reduction or a roasted onion consommé with bags of flavour. Charming and attentive service completes the rather special picture.

Name: Sète
Address: 238 Northdown Road,  Cliftonville, Margate, CT9 2QD, United Kingdom
Description: A characterful, bow-windowed former sweet shop is the home for this lovingly run restaurant located on the road between Margate and Broadstairs. In a fairly small space, the passionate team have managed to combine a restaurant, a wine bar and a bottle shop. The kitchen fuses some classical French techniques with a distinctly British, produce-driven approach, where nothing is overworked and the natural flavours of a few key ingredients are the driving force. The blackboard-written menu is ever-changing, but expect the likes of curried lamb mince or braised squid and peas.

Name: The Owl
Address: Hill Top, Hawnby, YO62 5QS, United Kingdom
Description: The team from the former Bantam in Helmsley are behind this characterful rural pub, which benefits from an enviable location perched above a pretty valley in the North York Moors National Park. A former drover’s inn dating back to the 19th century, there’s a vintage style to the décor and a lovely, welcoming vibe thanks to the friendly team. Hearty, unfussy and downright tasty dishes are the order of the day, with old favourites like devilled kidneys and toad in the hole sure to satisfy. Bedrooms are available for those looking to explore the surroundings in more detail.

Name: River Bar
Description: The maritime decor inside this striking oval pavilion is indeed enchanting, yet one of its main draws is the view of the Nieuwe Maas River. As you soak up the vibrant atmosphere and watch the cruise ships dock, you can choose from a fine selection of wines by the glass and the European-inspired menu. Eschewing any unnecessary frills, the chef comes up with some truly original dishes. His repertoire includes perfectly cooked Mediterranean-style turbot, foie gras as rich as anywhere in France – and even beef Wellington! The wide selection promises a delightful culinary journey along Europe's rivers.

Name: Café Visscher
Description: You could definitely call Arie Visscher's "café" a luxury brasserie. An abundance of red velvet, marble and copper give the place a remarkably warm and welcoming feel. Open all day from 11am, it's a great option for lunch, dinner or a quick bite at the bar. Chef Visschers specialises in French classics such as steak tartare elevated with smoked eel, or sea bass with a delightfully buttery potato mousseline and artichoke. He also showcases his creativity with a modern dish based on hispi cabbage. This Rotterdam native sticks to a single set menu, crafting beautifully balanced no-nonsense cuisine.

Name: Lilou
Description: This restaurant set in a row of townhouses in the centre of Goes evokes the spirit of Paris. Round marble-topped tables, high ceilings, tiled floors, French chansons – this bistro has it all. Both the tempting menu and the wines also draw on French tradition. Well-seasoned hand-cut steak tartare; pan-fried sea bream accompanied by a rich beurre blanc with fresh, zesty notes; a shellfish platter, or profiteroles with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce: diners are spoilt for choice! If in need of recommendations, ask the amiable hostess, who will be happy to help.

Name: MOUT & HOUT
Description: Beer and fire are at the heart of this establishment, whose name translates as "Malt & Wood". Next to the Beerze family brewery, which is steeped in history, there is an American-style bar with a stone pizza oven at the front. The back of the restaurant has a raw industrial feel. The chefs like to work with the Josper charcoal oven, parrilla grill and Oklahoma smoker to infuse their dishes with smoky flavours. For example, they put a unique twist on vitello tonnato by searing the veal on charcoal. Of course, meat takes centre stage in these generous and ingredient-led dishes, but there are also vegetarian and fish options on the menu to whet your appetite.

Name: Rosie
Description: Rosie is a bustling yet cosy establishment where foodies can indulge uninterrupted from noon. A love of wine pervades the place and music fills the air – the record player spins nostalgic tunes regularly. From shrimp croquettes to Jerusalem artichoke with labneh or a no-nonsense meat or fish dish: the international menu has something for everyone. This straightforward cuisine makes the most of the versatility of vegetables. Reservations are recommended!

Name: Restaurant Renilde
Description: Renilde Hammacher-van den Brande served as a curator at the Museum Boijmans van Beuningen for many years and would no doubt have been proud of the restaurant that bears her name. Located in a creatively landscaped rooftop garden on the sixth floor of what is now Depot Boijmans, this place affords stunning views over the city. In the afternoon, the restaurant is reserved for museum visitors; in the evening, it opens its doors to everyone who wishes to discover chef De Jong's surprise menu. This creative chef has a penchant for vegetables and bold combinations. His culinary audacity shines through in his sublime combination of elderflower ice cream, the subtle bitterness of Belgian endive caramel and rhubarb root. Prepare to be blown away!

Name: De Wilg
Description: The low-mounted coat hooks and ballet bar serve as reminders that the location was once a primary school and ballet hall. But there are no more strict rules here – the building has been transformed into a warm and welcoming restaurant. Boy van Gerwen steers clear of over-complicating matters, winning diners over with, for example, the fresh earthy notes of a beetroot tartare, the vibrant flavours of confit duck leg accompanied by a robust veal jus with morels, but also the spiciness of a lentil dahl. De Wilg represents generous cooking and great value for money.

Name: Reblochon
Description: Elise and Jurgen have transformed a charming cottage into a cosy living room-style restaurant, welcoming diners with genuine hospitality. The chef only serves a surprise menu, which he executes masterfully. Expect no gimmicks, but rather carefully crafted dishes with occasional influences from far-flung places. For instance, he combines pickled salmon with the earthy sweetness of beetroot and the umami of miso. Be sure to try the cheese board – a delicious way to discover the inspiration behind the restaurant's name.

Name: Resumé by 6&24
Description: A glass of crisp rosé with a fine selection of cured meats in the wine bar or on the canal-side terrace, a few small plates to share, or a complete meal in the restaurant, with its floral, slightly tropical-looking decor… You have plenty of options here. The tempting menu includes an intensely flavoursome ceviche, a vegetarian dish based on dry-aged beetroot, and a rich tarte Tatin. The chefs are just as happy to play with exotic seasonings as they are to turn out distinctly Dutch dishes. In short: delicious, inspired and generous!

Name: Bleue Bar Bistro
Description: Rather inconspicuously located on Grote Markt, there is a distinctly Parisian feel to this bistro with a predominantly green colour scheme. The long bar with ceramic tiles and open kitchen with green panelling make for an inviting setting. As you might expect, the menu features French bistro fare with the odd fresh twist – for instance, the chef incorporates kumquat into the rich duck jus that accompanies pan-fried duck breast and orange compote, without compromising the dish's signature flavours. The house-made pâté en croûte is certainly tempting. Full flavours guaranteed!

Name: Alba
Description: With its funky background music and striking colour scheme, Alba has an arty feel indoors, and boasts a spacious terrace outside. The posters adorning the walls make it clear that they are big on natural wines here. The cuisine is on trend yet down to earth. Imagine a Greek-Dutch fusion dish starring juicy smoked trout gravlax, pops of briny trout roe, and a creamy horseradish sauce that adds a kick to the crème crue. The set menu is a journey of bold flavours and clever combinations. Alba offers a relaxed setting in which to savour delicious food.

Name: Primitif
Description: Augustin Massinon and Darius Van Hoef have returned to their roots as they roll out their nature-inspired gourmet concept. First of all, they tastefully refurbished this Ardennes edifice whilst maintaining its authentic character. We recommend booking a table downstairs to make the most of the view of the open kitchen. The chefs, who are committed to using locally sourced produce as much as possible, pool their creative talents to craft beautifully plated dishes. Impeccable handiwork underscored by local ingredients, exotic seasonings and fermented flavours, examples of which include a tartare of langoustine with fermented radish, green apples, poached and foamy oyster and a hint of blackcurrant. The menu, which changes every five weeks, both surprises and enchants.

Name: Paulette
Description: True, the pretty square is picturesque, but the cute interior is something else again and often love at first sight! Timber rafters, a fireplace, floral-patterned ceiling lights and a lovely sheltered alfresco patio – simply glorious! The chef shines the spotlight on local, seasonal produce with the odd international twist. He might underscore lamb from the Vande Walle butchers with cooking juices and asparagus, while his moist, fudgy chocolate cake, which borders on perfection, is paired with vanilla ice cream in a match made in heaven. Generosity is the byword here.

Name: Vicomté
Description: Vicomté castle, part of the Arrondeau Estate, is the epitome of date-night romanticism. The wrought-iron conservatory, stylish fixtures and fittings and view over the pond are fully worthy of an Impressionist work of art. This unique setting provides the perfect foil for Quentin Gallopyn’s ode to top-drawer produce. Knife-edged precision and rich, fruity flavours set the culinary stage. He might coat delicately crispy scallops in balsamic vinegar, before adding a subtly sweet red apple and soy sauce jelly. Don’t forget to take the time to peruse the wine list of mainly French vintages, before finally heading upstairs to spend a restful night in one of the swish guestrooms.

Name: Sébastian
Address: Rue de la Cathédrale 25, Liège, 400, Belgium
Description: Sébastien Cassart is forging his own path. He works alone in his open kitchen, sometimes even serving the food himself as he embarks you on a culinary adventure. The untreated interior, adorned with art photos, is emblematic of the buzzy venue’s ethos. The chef crafts intuitive dishes that bear witness to his passion for outstanding, mainly local ingredients. Breast and leg of Malines poultry are served with a crispy skin and underscored by a mind-blowing blend of a gutsy gravy, truffles, sherry vinegar and the distinctive flavours of satay and peanut. Wholehearted, playful cuisine presented in a concise menu.

Name: LOF
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Ghent Pillows Hotel sports a regal Louis XIV vibe, whose plush opulence also extends to the LOF restaurant, albeit in a less extravagant vein. A mouthwatering range of outstanding produce sets the sophisticated culinary scene with the odd Asian twist. The chef might cook monkfish on the bone to preserve the taste and juicy flesh, while a delicately sweet cream of carrots, a stock of lapsang souchong tea and a velvety emulsion of olives and carrot juice further underscore this subtle fish. Heaven for lovers of spot-on, up-to-the-minute French fare.

Name: Bar Raket
Description: Convivial and buzzing Bar Raket provides a chic industrial-style setting in which to share a variety of delectable dishes. Flavours from all over the globe are represented here in cuisine that is all about enjoying the simple things: from Catalan bread to the umami of tonkatsu with North Sea crab to super-fresh clams with fried diced guanciale and a delectable hot sauce. The bread is simply divine! With a selection of smaller dishes and three main courses, the menu shows that good food can also be a delightfully laid-back affair.

Name: Blanc by Aytems
Description: Ayt Ems and family invite you to sample the distinctive ambiance of their terraced house in Antwerp’s hip Zuid district. Before admiring one of the Quartier Sud suites, sip a knockout cocktail and nibble an appetiser or two in the Bar Bleu. Next make your way into the snug dining area whose buzzy vibe and baroque curves provide the perfect backdrop to the talented chef’s subtle culinary score which rolls out Ottoman and French influences. Home-made spice blends and delicacies such as Baharat and chermoula enhance and underscore the food. The halibut is rubbed in spices (cumin and curcuma) and cooked in a fermented lime mousse that imparts refreshing acidity. The little buns that the lady of the house prepares in front of you are simply divine!

Name: 545 Whampoa Prawn Noodles
Description: The stall dates back to 1920s. Dry noodles dressed in sambal sauce are topped with bean sprouts, prawns and pork, and served with umami-laden prawn soup. Or opt for the noodle soup version. Add fried shallots and lard on top.

Name: Olivia
Description: Come to this lively Catalan spot for tapas and small plates packed with flavour, made with finesse and plated with modern aesthetics. Don’t miss the iconic creamy cheesecake and “spherical olives,” a tribute to the legendary el Bulli. The chic interior by Barcelona-based designer Rosa-Violán embodies the Mediterranean soul and takes diners to Spain instantly. Service is very friendly and attentive, and the maître d is always up for a chat.

Name: Shi Le Yuan
Description: Richly-flavoured braised pork and organs are a good match with the kway chap, which is served separately.

Name: Podi & Poriyal
Description: The name says it all – this vegetarian joint prides itself on the spicy ground lentil condiment known as podi, and sautéed vegetables, or poriyal. Replicating South Indian grandmas' cooking, the menu covers all plant-based dietary desires, with gluten-free, allium-free and vegan options. "Which Podi? Idli" – steamed rice cake tossed in podi – is served with a cashew and coconut chutney. Their podi dosai with poriyal filling is also excellent.

Name: Vue
Address: OUE Bayfront, Level 19, 50 Collyer Quay, 049321, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Aptly named after the French word for ‘view’, this romantic restaurant boasts one of the most stunning vistas of Marina Bay. Even the ceiling is designed to emanate light without casting reflections on the glass panes. The menu shows the culinary vision of the young head chef, with the four-course chef’s tasting menu being the most popular choice where diners may choose from a number of interesting options. Steaks and risotto are great for sharing. Executive set lunch is popular.

Name: Toa Payoh 93 Soon Kueh
Address: Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre, #01-68, 69 Geylang Bahru, 330069, Singapore
Description: The stall carries three kinds of dumplings – soon kueh stuffed with bamboo shoot, rice kueh and kuchai kueh with chives. All varieties boast elastic skin and generous filling. Try also the limited offer Hakka yam abacus seeds.

Name: Maison Boulud
Address: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, #B1-15 & L1-83, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: With executive chef Rémy Carmignani on board, Maison Boulud is located in the shopping mall at Marina Bay Sands. The patio on the upper level boasts stunning views – perfect for al fresco dining. The elegant main dining room (lower level) has an oversize wine cellar displaying impressive vintages. The menu is defined by classic French cuisine, with more sophisticated plating, as opposed to bistro-style fare. There is also their signature seafood platter.

Name: The 1950's Coffee
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-048, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Come here for the quintessential Singaporean teatime classics – kaya toast with kopi kosong (black coffee). This popular stall opened its doors in the 1950s and locals have been lining up to get their caffeine fix ever since.

Name: Feng Zhen Lor Mee
Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #03-146, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: This popular stall offers lor mee with generous toppings like meatballs and fish flakes. The noodles are springy and the broth is tasty and flavoursome. Also, try their deep-fried prawn rolls with a crispy skin and juicy filling.

Name: Lao Jie Fang
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-15, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: Cantonese-style noodles topped with beef brisket, pork ribs, pork knuckles or beef tendon are the name of the game here. The noodles are springy, and the pork knuckles are braised until gelatinous in a secret soy sauce.

Name: Roia
Address: Singapore Botanic Gardens (Nassim Gate entrance), E.J.H Corner House, 1 Cluny Road, 259569, Singapore
Description: Not only can you feast your eyes on the lush greenery, you can also taste the herbs and edible flowers grown in the garden and picked minutes before serving. In a refurbished historic edifice, chef-owner Priyam Chatterjee serves two tasting menus that are updated quarterly and feature modern French fare rooted in tradition and exquisitely plated. The top-notch produce comes from around the world and each course tells a story about its source.

Name: Khiri
Description: Formerly known as Chedi, this Thai restaurant rechristened itself Khiri in 2023. Other than that, nothing has changed – the food still strikes a balance of sweet, sour, spicy and salty flavours. The 8-course tasting menu is inspired by Northern, Northeastern, Southern and Central Thai recipes, creatively melding traditions and modern techniques. Khao pad kid terng, the signature fried rice packed with smoky aromas, is still a firm fixture on the menu.

Name: Food Street Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-173, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Loaded with wok hei, their kway teow mee is ribbon rice noodles, egg noodles, bean sprouts and scrambled egg tossed in a secret sauce. For toppings, choose clams only, or a mix of seafood with fish, squid, shrimps and clams.

Name: Guan Kee Fried Carrot Cake
Description: Kind of a misnomer, fried carrot cake is made with radish and not a dessert. It comes in two varieties – black and white. The black one has a caramel-like sweetness while the white one is eggy and salty. Order a mix of both.

Name: Fiz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Malaysian owner-chef Hafizzul Hashim opened Fiz in 2023 in a bid to showcase his native food culture. His experience menus are an ode to his childhood memories and family recipes, emphasising bold flavours and Malaysian produce. Each course is intricately crafted and composed of numerous ingredients. Expect to spend up to 3 hours over your meal. Speciality cocktails and wine pairings complete the experience.

Name: Imbue
Description: In this heritage shophouse updated with an open kitchen, the dishes are essentially European – but Asian ingredients and taste profiles lend a unique twist. The five- or eight-course dinner menu features Shaoxing-infused abalone from Jeju island, wrapped in kelp and ginger and steamed, served with ginkgo chawanmushi and accompanied by a shiitake reduction and ham jus. The sticky-sweet Malai bread with ginseng honey butter also delivers layers of flavours.

Name: Shunsui
Description: Formerly Kappo Shunsui, this atmospheric restaurant now serves three multicourse omakase menus, typically consisting of appetisers, sashimi, sushi, hot dish, main course and dessert. The interior is theatrically lit to showcase the food; the wooden counter seats 20 diners who can chat and interact with the chefs. It goes without saying that all the ingredients are top notch; the knife work is razor sharp and the sushi perfectly hand-pressed.

Name: Mag's Wine Kitchen
Address: Kesa House, #01-06, ​55 Keong Saik Road, 089158, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace
Description: Two things catch your attention when you set foot in this long-standing household name – the small walk-in cellar and the bustling open kitchen, where chef-owner Mag can be seen working with her team. Octopus with tomato and chorizo coulis is a decadent start to the meal, followed by classics such as risotto with Boston lobster: for years a staple on the menu, it keeps regulars coming back. The perfect wine-and-dine spot for a Friday night out.

Name: Hong Wen Mutton Soup
Address: Beauty World Food Centre #04-20, 144 Upper Bukit Timah Road, 588177, Singapore
Description: In operation for over half a century, this stall is now run by the second-generation owner and his wife. Their signature soup comprises mutton, tripe or tendon in a garlicky and peppery broth with strong herbal accents.

Name: Hup Hong Chicken Rice
Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-51, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: The queue to get your roasted or boiled chicken rice may be long, but the wait is worthwhile for the silky-fleshed meat and the heady aromas of rice cooked in chicken stock and fat. Enjoy with char siew or roast pork.

Name: Garibaldi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Ossobuco, costoletta alla Milanese and tiramisu are some of the signature dishes here, at one of the city’s best known Italian restaurants. The affable owner, though, wants everyone to be able to find their favourite dish which is why he offers such a large, all-encompassing menu. The impressive wine list, featuring around 7000 labels, is another feature for which this cosy and contemporary-styled restaurant is celebrated.

Name: Da Po
Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #B1-53, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: This stall serves only curry chicken noodles and Hainanese chicken rice. The latter comes in three portion sizes. Choose between roast or steamed chicken. The steamed one boasts meaty flavour, springy skin and silky flesh.

Name: Ann Chin Handmade Popiah
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-112, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Popiah packed with ingredients including eggs, shrimp, carrot, peanuts etc. provide a rich and varied taste.

Name: Fatty Ox HK Kitchen
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-84, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Offers a wide array of noodles, including pork trotter and barbecue meats. The fresh yam noodles are handmade and available for take away only.

Name: Rojak‧Popiah & Cockle
Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-56, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: This clean, tidy stall is named after the three items on its menu. The rojak features pineapple, yam bean, cucumber and fried dough stick dressed in a sweet, tangy and spicy sauce. Try their made-to-order popiah, too.

Name: Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Hakkanese Lui Cha is a soupy rice dish in which chicken, cabbage and pickles meet the nuttiness of sesame and peanuts plus a hint of herbs. Order the fish cake, stuffed tofu or fried egg toppings.

Name: Zi Jing Cheng Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-15, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: There is only one thing on the menu – Hainanese boneless chicken rice. Set menus are available for one to three guests, all served with steamed chicken, rice and soup. The bird is tender and flavoursome. Expect to queue any time.

Name: New World Mutton Soup
Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-23, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The speciality here – mutton soup – is briny-sweet with plenty of umami, and finely shredded ginger to add zing. Other lamb specialities such as rib soup, kway teow, meatballs, lamb tendon and offal are also worth trying.

Name: Ah Ter Authentic Teochew Fish Ball Noodles
Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #01-14, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: Now run by the third generation, this family-run stall is famous for its fish ball noodle soup topped with ground pork, pork liver, seaweed and pork rinds. Pork ribs are simmered for hours resulting in a broth rich in gutsy flavours.

Name: C.M.Y. Satay
Address: Chinatown Complex Market & Food Centre, #02-168, 335 Smith Street, 050335, Singapore
Description: Two shops share the same venue, so be sure you order from the right one. The grilled-to-order satay comes in pork, chicken and lamb varieties (or an assortment). The nutty, tangy sauce is tasty and you can order rice on top.

Name: People's Park Hainanese Chicken Rice
Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1098, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: Cantonese barbecue like roast pork and duck aside, the main draws are Hainanese chicken rice and double-boiled soups. The rice is richly perfumed with garlic and the flavourful chicken with a gelatinous skin is not to be missed.

Name: Loong Kee Yong Tau Fu
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Serve yourself with the stuffed tofu or vegetables. You may also add soup, chee cheong fun, laksa, mee or rice.

Name: Hua Xing Bak Kut Teh
Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-171, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
Description: (The hawker center it locates is temporarily closed.) Bak kut teh with a strong, peppery flavour and aromatic pork ribs. Add rice, pork organs, pork trotter, or vegetable soup for a complete meal.

Name: Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken Noodle
Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-58, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The curry broth may be only mildly hot, but its flavours are deep. The chicken is tender; potato and tofu puffs soak up the sauces. Besides curry, there is satay chicken served on your choice from three varieties of noodles.

Name: Ah Hock Fried Hokkien Noodles
Address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-27, 20 Kensington Park Road, 557269, Singapore
Description: Serves fried Hokkien noodles with shrimp and squid.

Name: Heng Gi Goose and Duck Rice
Description: The soya sauce duck is very popular.

Name: Singapore Famous Rojak
Description: Here, the second generation of the family sells local-style salad with pineapple, cucumber and deep-fried dough stick, tossed in a special home-made sauce and sprinkled with ground peanuts. Chilli is optional.

Name: Chomp Chomp Satay
Address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-34, 20 Kensington Park Road, 557269, Singapore
Description: Opt for pork, chicken, mutton or ketupat served with pineapple sauce.

Name: Gordon Grill
Address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, 228221, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A feature of Goodwood Park hotel since 1963, the restaurant is famed for its meat trolley service which is wheeled over to each table. Along with the meat and plentiful supplies of seafood from the grill, you can expect French-inspired classic dishes like lobster bisque, braised beef cheek, or Crêpes Suzette flambéed tableside. It’s a good choice for a quiet business lunch, a romantic dinner or weekend family outings.

Name: Jade Palace
Address: Forum The Shopping Mall, #B1-13, 583 Orchard Road, 238884, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Both the décor and the menu show strong Hong Kong influences, all the more so as super-fresh seafood and veggies are shipped from the city twice a week. The must-tries (sautéed white eel with chives in black bean sauce and braised lobster with ginger and scallion in a claypot) boast exceptional wok hei and craftsmanship. You can also specify how you want your live seafood cooked – ask the friendly front-of-house staff for advice.

Name: Ji Ji Noodle House
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-48/49, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: Local wonton and noodle dishes like chicken feet noodle and Ipoh sar hor fun.

Name: Ibid
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: After winning a popular TV cooking contest, lawyer-turned-chef Woo opened Ibid in a remodelled shophouse. The passionate chef gets hands-on in every part of his venture, overlooking the kitchen, greeting guests warmly and serving dishes himself. French techniques and Asian twists are manifested in every course of the varied and exciting set menu. Prized counter seats are the best spots to interact with the chefs and watch the alchemy unfold.

Name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang
Address: Yishun Park Hawker Centre, #01-33, 51 Yishun Avenue 11, 768867, Singapore
Description: Traditional coconut milk rice with Indonesian spicy chicken and sambal sauce.

Name: 91 Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #01-91, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: Their fried kway teow boasts exceptional wok hei and is pork free. Topped with leafy greens, cockles, egg, bean sprouts, deep-fried anchovies and a prawn, the noodles are perfectly seasoned. It closes when sold out.

Name: Bam!
Description: Gone are the days when European dishes had to be paired with wine. Sake can complement any food when chosen wisely. Bam! champions a revolutionary way of appreciating the Japanese rice wine with exquisite modern culinary creations. The sommelier can also help you pick a wine. Though it proclaims itself as an omakase restaurant, you can also order à la carte. Ask for a counter seat to stay close to the action in the kitchen.

Name: Foc (Clarke Quay)
Description: You can’t miss the huge papier mâché caricatures of the owner and chef hanging from the ceiling. The food is equally fun as the chef melds Catalonian flavours with modern techniques to create original and exciting tapas-style dishes such as smoked Cantabrian anchovies on charcoal brioche, and patatas bravas FOC style. Always busy and buzzing with a cheerful vibe. Ask for a seat at the counter to enjoy the experience to the full.

Name: Ivy's Hainanese Herbal Mutton Soup
Address: Pasir Panjang Food Centre, #14, 121 Pasir Panjang Road, 118543, Singapore
Description: Herbal mutton soup, herbal tendon soup and herbal tulang soup are delicious.

Name: Tien Lai Rice Stall
Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #02-66, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: Roast duck, roast meat and char siew are available at reasonable prices. Come early before the meat is sold out.

Name: Open Farm Community
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Adjacent to the Botanic Garden, this verdantly set glasshouse combines an urban farm and dining concept. The founder-chef advocates an eco-friendly philosophy and therefore designed a mostly plant-based menu. Produce may be sourced from local artisan farms as well as Malaysia, but the food shows eclectic technique and flavours from around the world. The menu offers vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free options to cater to different dietary needs.

Name: Sin Hoi Sai (Tiong Bahru)
Description: Located in a residential area, this well-known seafood restaurant has over 30 years of history to its name. They serve live seafood only, from fish to shellfish – make your selection from the tank. Don't miss the famous local choices of chilli crab and black pepper crab, which boast firm and briny sweet flesh; the local cze char dishes are also good. You can sit inside or outside – the latter area is particularly atmospheric and relaxing.

Name: National Kitchen
Address: National Gallery Singapore, #02-01, (Coleman Street entrance), 1 St. Andrew's Road, 178957, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Art and sculptures aren’t the only treasures found in the National Gallery – on the 2nd floor is this restaurant from Violet Oon, Singapore’s own national treasure and one of its greatest ambassadors. The handsome, panelled 1920s-style dining room is an ideal backdrop to the cooking which, through its spicing, contrasting textures and enticing aromas, showcases Singapore’s unique culinary heritage. This is a restaurant with genuine charm.

Name: Luke's (Gemmill Lane)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A favourite with local office workers, this steakhouse and oyster bar, run by a U.S. national, bustles with patrons all day long and is ideal for power lunches or after-work cocktails. It has acquired a faithful crowd of regulars thanks to high-quality food and friendly, slick service. Expect to see U.S. classics on the menu, such as New England clam chowder and Maryland crab cake. The generous portions make it a great venue for get-togethers.

Name: Mustard
Description: This halal restaurant specialising in Bengali and Punjabi cuisines is christened Mustard because the spice is used extensively in both cuisines. For instance, mustard oil is often used in place of coconut oil in Bengali cooking. Try their maacher cutlet – deep-fried fish croquettes served with a house-made fermented mustard sauce called Kashundi, which tastes strong and spicy. All food is made to order, but is so worth the wait.

Name: Path
Address: Marina Bay Financial Centre, Tower 3, #01–05/06, 12 Marina Boulevard, 018982, Singapore
Description: The place is popular with a business lunch clientele craving creative Asian fare underpinned by classic French techniques. Come evening, it turns into a romantic spot, serving a six- or eight-course dinner menu. The mildly hot crabmeat and tofu spread is the perfect accompaniment for the bread baked in the charcoal oven. The pork trotter wrapped in caul fat is doused in a sauce inspired by the Chinese classic of braised pork with pickled mustard greens.

Name: Huat Heng Fried Oyster
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-26, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 90, 320091, Singapore
Description: The oyster omelette is fried to order until the crust is nicely browned, while the oysters remain plump and juicy. The house-made chilli sauce elevates the dish considerably. Various portion sizes are available.

Name: Lor 9 Beef Kway Teow
Description: Cantonese and Fujian dishes prepared with local ingredients are tweaked to cater to local tastes. The beef kway teow is the main event. Comfort-food classics such as coffee pork ribs and sambal sweet potato leaves are also excellent.

Name: Osteria Mozza
Address: Hilton Orchard, Level 5, 333 Orchard Road, 238867, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: After a hiatus, the first Asian outpost of celebrity chef Nancy Silverton’s famed establishment Osteria Mozza reopened, now in a modern, rustic setting with a lively and inviting vibe. The small lunch menu features antipasti, salads, pizza and house-made pasta. The dinner menu steps up a gear to include her signature mozzarella dishes and other Italian specialties. The impressive wine list covers 280 labels from different regions of Italy.

Name: Putien (Kitchener Road)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: This first branch of the chain known for its friendly service opened in 2000. The menu showcases Fujian classics, with small plates and noodles being the highlights. Try the bian rou (Fujian wonton soup) – the translucent skin is made with pork pounded over 10,000 times into a paste. The lor mee, topped with an impressive array of seafood, is also popular. Don't miss the seasonal offerings, some using rare ingredients from the city of Putian.

Name: Birds Of Paradise (Katong)
Description: A mesmerising array of top-quality gelato and sorbet is served in house-made thyme-scented waffle cones. Sea salt hojicha, white chrysanthemum, and raspberry lychee are some of its outstanding offerings.

Name: San Shu Gong
Description: The owner named the restaurant after her late father and serves Cantonese and Teochew cuisines – her father's favourites. The two chefs, each with over 30 years of professional experience, excel at seafood dishes that accentuate the natural umami of seasonal produce. Some specialities have to be pre-ordered, such as the steamed and chilled fourfinger threadfin with tender flesh and generous fish oil.

Name: Hock Lye Noodles House & Fishii Tales
Address: 20 Ghim Moh Road Market & Food Centre, #01-35, Blk 20, Ghim Moh Road, 270020, Singapore
Description: Popular dishes include Hock Lye's noodle soup and "dry" noodles with meatballs, fish balls, prawns or pork ribs. The hand-made fish balls and fish cakes are springy and flavoursome. Come early, as the meatballs tend to sell out.

Name: Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-56, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: Besides xiao long bao, this busy stall offers an array of Shanghainese food, such as pan fried dumplings, sour and spicy soup. Their pork and chives potstickers are filled to the brim and nicely browned on the bottom.

Name: Sushi Katori
Description: Chef Katori has years of experience working in kaiseki and sushi restaurants in Japan and Singapore. His first venture focuses on Edomae sushi and features the freshest catch from Toyosu Market on sushi rice from Miyagi prefecture dressed in either of the two vinegar blends according to the variety of the fish. The signature abalone is cooked in liver sauce in a sizzling stone bowl which imparts appealing aroma. Nothing ends the meal better than well-made tamagoyaki.

Name: Fiamma
Address: Capella Hotel, 1 The Knolls, Sentosa Island, 098297, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Eagerly anticipated by gourmets, this dining concept by the celebrated chef Mauro Colagreco opened in the ultra-luxury beach resort. The rustic chic room comes complete with an open kitchen, wood-fired oven and a terrace overlooking the pool and garden. The menu sees a good range of Italian classics, especially those from the South of the country. Start your meal with seabream carpaccio, followed by house-made pasta, and tiramisu for two to share.

Name: Yong Xiang Xing Tou Fu
Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1084, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: There is only one thing on the menu – assorted tofu stew. Fish balls, tofu skin rolls, silken tofu and deep-fried tofu stuffed with minced fish are ladled into your bowl alongside a clear broth seasoned by scallion. Simply delicious.

Name: Sushi Sato
Description: The duo of chefs chose to open this sushi-ya in serene surroundings away from the busy CBD. In the same vein, the wood-rich interior is minimal and Zen-inspired. All the ingredients are shipped from Japan four times a week for peak freshness. Three seasonal menus are available and attention to detail is visible at every level – Yamagata rice is dressed in a blend of three red vinegars for the perfect tartness that complements oily fish.

Name: Início
Address: Thye Hong Centre, #01-06, 2 Leng Kee Road, 159086, Singapore
Description: "Início" is Portuguese for "a new start", as the young chefs aspire to write a new chapter in culinary history. The food is modern European, but the Asian influences are indisputable. The à la carte menu is short but sweet; the seven-course tasting menu changes every month to keep things fresh. Try the mackerel pickled in-house with nori pistachio butter, or ravioli with escargot and water chestnut filling in a black truffle broth.

Name: Gemma
Address: National Gallery, #05-03, 1 St. Andrew's Road, 178957, Singapore
Description: The bold decor with a bright red couch, marble wall panels and gold columns doesn't outshine the smoky aromas from the charcoal grill. The kitchen is helmed by an Italian chef, so while most of the beef is imported from Australia, Italian influences abound in every course – the house-made pasta in particular is worth trying. The steaks and accompaniments are cooked to perfection. Have a nightcap on the rooftop patio commanding gorgeous views.

Name: Redhill Pork Porridge
Description: The porridge may not look exciting but the creamy base is loaded with meaty flavour. Pad it out with sliced pork, pork meatballs, pork liver or deep-fried dough sticks. Crack in a raw egg and stir it into wispy ribbons. Open from 6am while stocks lasts.

Name: Ye Tang
Address: Beauty World Food Centre #04-26, 144 Upper Bukit Timah Road, 588177, Singapore
Description: The owner learned to make cendol in Malacca, and his rice flour jelly worms – made on the spot – are softer than most. On top of the classic cendol shaved ice, add red kidney beans, palm seeds, corn kernels or durian.

Name: Yong Kee Claypot Bak Kut Teh
Address: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, #02-78, 3 Yung Sheng Road, Jurong West, 618499, Singapore
Description: Pork rib soup is served in a claypot alongside other condiments, such as peppercorns. The Chinese herbal version strikes a fine balance, with distinctive yet not overpowering herbal flavours. Other claypot soups are also available.

Name: Sushi Yuki
Description: After helming a renowned sushiya in Singapore for 10 years, Chef Yukinori Kawakami brings the experience to this new venture in 2023. Three omakase menus are offered at lunch and dinner, featuring fish flown in from Japan four times a week. Sushi rice from Yamagata Prefecture is dressed in a blend of two vinegars for a delicate taste that accentuates the fish’s natural flavours. With only 13 counter seats and two private rooms, reservations are recommended.

Name: Ron Sheng Fish Head Bee Hoon
Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-44, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: Crispy fried fish head and fish meat with bee hoon. The broth infused with milk is smooth and sweet.

Name: Lor Mee 178
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-23, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Lor mee in robust stock offers a rich taste with garlic and chillies. You should also try the fish nuggets.

Name: Jiang-Nan Chun
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, Level 2, 190 Orchard Boulevard, 248646, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This exquisite space, reached via a marble staircase, is warm and welcoming, with heavy leather chairs that are especially comfortable. The kitchen team excels in barbecue meats, double-boiled soups and seafood dishes that use the freshest ingredients of the best quality. Try wok-fried Australian beef tenderloin with portobello mushrooms. Set menus are a great way to sample the popular hits all at once.

Name: Bedok Chwee Kueh
Address: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre, #01-19, 208 New Upper Changi Road, 460208, Singapore
Description: The freshly steamed chwee kueh rice cakes are soft and velvety and the sauce on top made with preserved radish, scallion, dried shrimps and chilli is simply irresistible. May be closed without prior notice.

Name: Hoe Kee Kitchen
Address: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 505, Jurong West Street 52, 640505, Singapore
Description: Steamed chicken rice with tender meat and flavourful rice is popular. Other options include reasonably priced char siew and roasted pork rice.

Name: Xing Yun Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
Address: Yuhua Market & Hawker Centre, #01-202, Blk 347, Jurong East Avenue 1, Jurong East, 600347, Singapore
Description: (The hawker center it locates is temporarily closed.) Its signature Hainanese boneless chicken rice is garnished with pineapple, tomato and cucumber. Dip the juicy, silky chicken in the briny-sweet chilli and ginger sauce before savouring it with the aromatic rice.

Name: Pondok Makan Indonesia
Description: Among the array of Indonesian food on offer, their grilled-to-order satay stands out in particular. Chicken satay is marinated in turmeric, imparting a mild sweetness; juicy, tender mutton satay is immaculately cooked.

Name: Yuan Chun Famous Lor Mee
Address: Amoy Street Food Centre, #02-80, 7 Maxwell Road, 069111, Singapore
Description: Lor mee here can be topped with fried fish cake, fried chicken, sliced fish or braised pork belly. The dark gravy boasts depth thanks to spices and prolonged simmering. Jazz it up further with chilli and cilantro.

Name: Sheng Seng Fried Prawn Noodle
Address: Pek Kio Market & Food Centre, #01-40, 41 Cambridge Road, 210041, Singapore
Description: It's all about rice vermicelli and egg noodles stir-fried with eggs and seafood. Homemade chili sauce enriches the flavour.

Name: Allauddin's Briyani
Description: The family has been selling its famous biryani since the 1950s. The set comes with yellow basmati rice enhanced by a spice mix; mutton, chicken or fish curry; and papadums. The mutton sambal is tender and tasty.

Name: Crystal Jade Golden Palace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Opened in 2002, this is the most comfortable branch of this restaurant group and the only one which specialises in Teochew dishes, like cold crab and sugar-coated yam. Look out too for the Cantonese barbecue meat and assorted seafood dishes; more contemporary offerings include chilled foie gras with sake and roasted suckling pig with black truffle. Their wine cellar includes a good international selection.

Name: Gaig
Description: After renovation, this relaxed and friendly restaurant run by the same family as its namesake in Barcelona has doubled in size. Catalan classics like the cannelloni are prepared the same way as they were back in the 19th century, and their tapas portion sizes allow diners to sample a wider variety. Recommendations include lamb shoulder with trinxat and mint pesto. The wine list has a great Spanish selection that’s available at a reasonable price.

Name: Claudine
Description: From chef Julien Royer of Odette fame comes a classic French brasserie, which he named after his mother. It’s housed in a lovely 1930s converted chapel, with an open kitchen at one end and a bar at the other. Those with a fondness for comforting French classics will find the rollcall of favourites very appealing, from onion soup to vol-au-vents and baba au rhum. If you’re willing to share, then go for the bouillabaisse or the pepper steak flambéed at your table.

Name: Min Jiang at Dempsey
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Amidst lush greenery, the one-storey colonial structure houses an airy dining room done up in a yellow, gold and green palette, boasting floor-to-ceiling windows, wood details and rattan furniture. The menu is Cantonese and Sichuanese with a touch of finesse and subtlety. Must-try items include turbot fish two ways, Beijing duck grilled in a wood-fire oven and various dim sum. There are also many good choices for vegetarians.

Name: Bar-Roque Grill
Description: The Alsace-born chef takes diners on a culinary journey to his homeland with authentic regional specialties such as choucroute garnie and tarte flambée aux escargots. International dishes are also popular, like Malaysian rotisserie free-range chicken and a selection of beefsteaks dry aged in-house and chargrilled to perfection. Service is attentive and helpful. Start or end the night with a drink on the terrace or at the bar.

Name: Imperial Treasure Super Peking Duck (Paragon)
Address: Paragon Shopping Centre, #05-42/45, 290 Orchard Road, 238859, Singapore
Description: Considered the crown jewel of the group, this place stocks over 3 000 Peking ducks a month, yet still tends to sell out, so be sure to pre-order yours when booking your table. The restaurant is divided into three rooms and the roasted duck – a must-try with crispy skin and succulent meat – is carved tableside. Another signature dish is the velvety poached fish in shrimp stock on crispy rice; the roast pork and slow-boiled soups are also worth trying.

Name: Cure
Description: Inspired by bistro culture, chef-owner Walsh has devised a Nua Irish tasting menu that riffs on his Celtic roots and draws on local influences. The menu ranges from absolutely purist takes on the classics to small plates with playful touches. To a soundtrack of Irish rock, learn about exceptional homegrown ingredients from the map on the table, as you indulge in dishes informed by the history and wisdom of the Emerald Isle.

Name: Esquina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The dining room is upstairs at this shophouse just off Keong Saik Road, but the best place to sit is at the counter on the ground floor, in front of the open kitchen, watching the young chef and his team. The dishes are as flavoursome as they are colourful and not without some creativity; order some anchovy sticks with bottarga aioli while you scour the sections marked ‘snacks’, ‘soil’, ‘sea’ and ’land’. The octopus and the suckling pig are two specialities.

Name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-10, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: The teochew dumplings are stuffed with jicama for a lovely crunch, while chopped dried shrimps lend briny umami. Try them with the home-made chilli sauce. Dumplings with red bean or taro paste filling are available after 1pm.

Name: Chung Cheng
Address: Golden Mile Food Centre, #01-59, 505 Beach Road, 199583, Singapore
Description: Three options feature on the menu of this stall – chilli mee, prawn mee and laksa. Go for chilli mee: yellow egg noodles topped with tangy chilli sauce, pork ribs, prawns, hard-boiled egg, fish cake and tofu puffs.

Name: Hokkien Street Bak Kut Teh
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #01-66, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The dark amber coloured bak kut teh from this stall is loaded in herbal goodness. Pair with pork knuckle, pork intestines, steamed fish, pork tail, pork kidney or pork liver on the side, as you prefer.

Name: Boon Tong Kee Kway Chap‧Braised Duck
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #024, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Boon Tong Kee prides itself on its spiced soy marinade made with aromatic Chinese herbs. With its springy skin and tasty meat, the signature braised duck is a hit. The braised pork trotter and taro rice are also popular.

Name: Ushidoki Wagyu Kaiseki
Description: This chef puts a new spin on classic kaiseki with two Wagyu set menus that honour a head-to-tail concept. He chooses Ozaki beef from Miyazaki, otherwise unavailable in Singapore, for its gutsy flavour. Various cuts from 32- to 36-month-old cattle are prepared in a myriad of ways to highlight their textures and umami. Most of the other ingredients are flown in from Japan to ensure authenticity. There is also an á la carte menu for add-on courses.

Name: Leon Kee Claypot Pork Rib Soup
Address: Alexandra Village Food Centre, #01-18, Blk 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1, 150120, Singapore
Description: The pork rib soup cooked with Chinese herbs is the signature dish; it also offers pig's tail soup, sesame oil chicken and claypot pork liver.

Name: Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee
Address: Pasar 16@Bedok (Bedok South Food Centre), #01-50, 16 Bedok South Road, 460016, Singapore
Description: Fish balls are tender and rich. The al dente noodles marry well with the fresh broth.

Name: Gunther's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This owner-chef worked in some famous restaurants in his native Belgium and France before coming to Singapore. He describes his cooking as "simple, honest and down-to-earth", though a number of sumptuous dishes are to be had. Try his cold angel hair with a 6g quenelle of Oscietra caviar – one of his proudest creations, served since 2005. In addition to the timeless classics, check out seasonal offerings such as white asparagus.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: In this stylish eatery with a bar and an open kitchen, you’ll find the eponymous artisanal French salt on each table – but you won’t need it thanks to the owner-chef’s spot-on sense of seasoning. At this ‘bistro de luxe’ he delivers classical French cuisine with a light, modern spin – making it easy to save room for his signature Baba. Two set menus - we recommend the tasting menu for a global experience.

Name: Fu He Turtle Soup
Address: Berseh Food Centre, #02-40, 166 Jalan Besar, 208877, Singapore
Description: There is an array of Cantonese soups to choose from here. The eponymous soft-shelled turtle soup emits rich herbal aromas, served with plain steamed rice or taro rice.

Name: Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
Address: 127 Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127, Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, 310127, Singapore
Description: The signature Hokkien prawn mee is made with yellow egg noodles, rice vermicelli and squid, topped with fried crispy lard that adds an extra layer of texture and flavours.

Name: Nyonya Chendol
Address: Chong Pang Market and Food Centre, #01-162, 105 Yishun Ring Road, 760105, Singapore
Description: The stall specialises in the classic iced dessert chendol. Pandan-flavoured flour jelly, coconut milk and palm sugar syrup impart the right level of sweetness. Extra toppings like red beans or durian are available.

Name: Jiao Cai Seafood
Address: Yishun Park Hawker Centre, #01-39, 51 Yishun Avenue 11, 768867, Singapore
Description: Cooked-to-order seafood dishes. Signature sambal stingray is spicy and delicious.

Name: Zheng Zhi Wen Ji Pig's Organ Soup
Address: Clementi 448 Food Centre, #01-26, 448 Clementi Ave 3, 120448, Singapore
Description: As well as pork offal, the menu features marinated pork trotter, kway chap and bak kut teh. But the noodle soup with pork liver and kidney stands out – the offal is cooked perfectly and the broth loaded with herbal aromas.

Name: Shang Palace
Address: Shangri-La Hotel, Lobby Level, 22 Orange Grove Road, 258350, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: With a graceful dining room reminiscent of a Chinese garden, Shang Palace serves an extensive menu dominated by old-time Cantonese classics that are hard to find elsewhere, such as grilled chicken liver and pork fat skewers, and deep-fried pork fat medallions stuffed with crabmeat. Order the deep-fried whole boneless chicken stuffed with glutinous rice one day ahead and ask the servers about the slow-boiled soups that exude rich deep flavours.

Name: Ce Soir
Description: Ce Soir wins kudos not only for its impossibly romantic floral theme and everything botanical, but also because of its deftly crafted French fare with strong Asian notes. Every course of both the lunch set and dinner tasting menus is visually stunning: like a garden on a plate, even the flowers are edible. The seafood stands out in particular. Everything down to the bread and the mignardises are made from scratch in-house.

Name: Heng Long BBQ Chicken Rice
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-42, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: The BBQ chicken rice is an absolute must, but the honey-glazed char siew and roast pork are also popular. Or opt for their brine-poached chicken – succulent, perfectly seasoned and with a wonderful velvety texture.

Name: Rempapa
Address: Park Place Residences at PLQ, #01-01/02/03, 2 Paya Lebar Road, 409053, Singapore
Description: In a smart, casual room with tan banquettes, powder blue chairs and terrazzo tiled floor, Damian D’Silva, a respected judge from the Singaporean edition of a popular cooking show, champions a novel cuisine that crosses boundaries among Chinese, Peranakan, Eurasian, Indian and Malay cooking. Hearty dishes sit comfortably next to century-old recipes, all prepared with shrewd judgment, and the right amount of oomph. Baca Assam (beef cheek) is unmissable.

Name: R&B Express
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-76, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: Chicken wings grilled with charcoal are crispy and juicy while the spicy sauce adds to the flavour. Also try satay, traditional popiah and kueh pie tee.

Name: Cheng Heng Kway Chap and Braised Duck Rice
Address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-05, 44 Holland Drive, 270044, Singapore
Description: The name reveals the two signature dishes – the braised duck is tender, has robust flavours and is accompanied by a perfectly seasoned, spiced soy marinade. The kway (rice noodles) are silky smooth and the soup is moreish.

Name: Tambuah Mas (Orchard)
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Since 1981, the Indonesian chefs at Tambuah Mas have been making authentic home-style dishes from Padang, Sulawesi and Java. Family recipes with delicate blends of spices and precise preparations are closely guarded secrets, passed down over generations. The signature tahu telor (deep-fried egg-coated tofu cubes in a dark sweet sauce) boasts crispy skin and perfect briny-sweetness. Always round off a meal here with a cendol.

Name: Hokkien Man Hokkien Mee
Address: Blk 19, Toa Payoh 7, #01-264, Kim Keat Palm, 310019, Singapore
Description: As its name suggests, this stall specialises in Hokkien fried noodles in a garlicky broth made with prawn heads. Besides the typical toppings of prawns and squid, you may order others, like egg or abalone, at an additional cost.

Name: Unforgettable Carrot Cake
Address: 115 Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre, #01-30, Blk 115 Bukit Merah View, 151115, Singapore
Description: Not to be confused with the western sweet of the same name, carrot cake here is savoury, made with radish and stir-fried in seasoning. Opt for the dark version coated in egg, and tossed in sticky, caramelised dark soy sauce.

Name: La D'Oro
Description: Rebranded in 2023, La D’oro now offers a single season-driven omakase menu that changes every two months. Hailing from Tokyo, Japan, the owner-chef Sasaki honed his skills in Italy. His ambitious, kappo-style cooking effortlessly blends Italian traditions with Japanese influences, delivering complex, original creations underpinned by modern techniques. Fresh ingredients flown in from Japan and Italy impart distinctive flavours.

Name: Wakuda
Address: Marina Bay Sands Hotel, Tower 2, Lobby, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018972, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This more accessible spinoff of its upscale sister Waku Ghin is the brainchild of the eponymous chef Tetsuya Wakuda. All rooms feature the traditional Japanese craft of wood joinery prominently, alongside soft lighting, tan leather chairs and banquettes. The menu offers an array of modern Japanese classics made with quality ingredients sourced globally. Adding original cocktails and a buzzy vibe to the equation, Wakuda guarantees a fun night out.

Name: Lolla
Description: The turquoise tiled façade sets nicely against the faux-industrial interior. Seasonal Mediterranean dishes in generous portions for sharing are served by the chefs themselves.
