Flavours are bold and hearty, with occasional Asian touches. Ask for counter seats to see the chefs in action, or sit at the communal table in the basement which can be reserved for private parties. Only seven- or nine-course tasting menus are served on Friday and Saturday nights.

Name: Springleaf Prata Place (Spring Leaf Garden)
Description: The birthplace of Singapore’s popular prata chain serves 20 different variations with sweet or savoury fillings. But even the basic egg prata tastes great with a crisp crust and fluffy centre - perfect for any curry in any meal.

Name: Spago Dining Room
Address: Marina Bay Sands Hotel, Tower 2, Sands SkyPark, Level 57, 10 Bayfront Avenue, 018956, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Wolfgang Puck’s fresh, revitalising cuisine may have been born in Beverly Hills, but its second home atop Marina Bay Sands has proven an equally good fit. The menu is an appealing blend of American, Asian and European influences, with dishes ranging from honey miso broiled black cod to a falafel burger with roasted capsicum. The poolside terrace may provide great views, but the elegant dining room comes with a cooling serenity.

Name: Jian Bo Shui Kueh
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-05, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Shui kueh is quintessential local street food: white rice cake with salted diced radish and a secret tung tsai sauce, packed with oomph. The house-made sambal, oozing in dried shrimp flavour, is perfect with the rice cake.

Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Address: People's Park Complex Food Centre, #01-1064, 32 New Market Road, 050032, Singapore
Description: Offers xiao long bao, dumplings and hand-pulled noodles.

Name: Yan Ting
Address: The St. Regis Hotel, Level 1U, 29 Tanglin Road, 247911, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Since the name translates as ‘Banquet Court’, it's no surprise to find a very comfortable space, ideal for impressing visitors and friends. The head chef has extensive experience when it comes to traditional dishes, especially Cantonese barbecue and double-boiled soups. Try his crispy roast pork belly for the ultimate indulgence. He's also an expert at preparing live fish – choose from 11 cooking styles. At lunch, don't miss his Hong Kong-style dim sum.

Name: Mustard Seed
Description: Before you can experience the head chef’s unique take on Singaporean-Japanese fusion cooking, you have to book a table online months ahead. Punctuality is key as the food is only served after all the guests are seated at 7.30pm sharp. The 8-course omakase-style menu changes every two months, reinventing national dishes like rojak and laksa with clever Japanese twists. Counter seats overlooking the open kitchen let diners see the magic first hand.

Name: Buko Nero
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Diners flock to this small neighbourhood joint and it’s easy to understand why: the bubbly, charming hostess works seamlessly with her husband chef from Veneto, who in turn delivers simple, delicious Italian fare with subtle Asian twists. Try his tau kwa tower – an appetising mix of sautéed Italian-style greens and Singaporean dried tofu salad in a tangy Asian dressing. Hand-made pasta is another highlight, as are the weekly specials.

Name: Chilli Padi (Joo Chiat)
Description: A stroll around Joo Chiat is made all the more enjoyable by making a pitstop here, as it’s a great place to share a host of authentic Peranakan dishes. The Nonya specialities include popiah, kueh pai ti, creamy and delicious curry chicken, and chap chye. Many of the dishes come in three sizes but prices are so good that over-ordering is easy and excusable. The batik fabric covering the tables adds some colour to this simple restaurant.

Name: Yì By Jereme Leung
Address: Raffles Arcade, #03-02, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: The chef honed his remarkable skills while working in China for many years. He returned to Singapore and opened Yi – the Chinese word for art and craftsmanship, hence the fancy dining room adorned in exquisite paper art and the food that reflects eclectic influences from all over China. Steamed free range chicken in herbal broth impresses by its umami and mild herbal aftertaste. Also check out the seasonal menu bursting with creative twists.

Name: Tippling Club
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: If you thought fine dining had to be formal, think again. Ryan Clift's discreetly signed flagship restaurant has a casual clubbing vibe. A spot at the counter is best for watching the chefs in action; a table in the dimly lit dining area offers more privacy. The tasting menu features well-crafted, nicely plated dishes made exclusively with ingredients from Japan. The delicious cocktails inspired by songs from different decades are a fun touch.

Name: Tunglok Heen
Address: Hotel Michael, #02-142/143, Resorts World Sentosa, 26 Sentosa Gateway, 098138, Singapore
Description: Clever lighting, dark wood and shades of red lend this modern Chinese restaurant a slick, stylish feel. Amidst traditional recipes, novel dishes also feature on the menu. Either way, the food is always meticulously plated. Don’t miss the fish bone and fish maw soup, double-boiled with chicken and pork for six hours. Chilli crab served in a casserole boasts firm, flavoursome meat. Order deep-fried buns to mop up the knockout sauce.

Name: Straits Chinese (Cecil Street)
Address: Keck Seng Tower, #B1-01, 133 Cecil Street, 069535, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The owner’s family opened Singapore’s first Peranakan restaurant in 1953 – this branch has been in the CBD since 2011. Ornaments and wooden furniture lend a Chinese aesthetic. The versatile menu features dishes made with local produce and lots of spices and herbs, all prepared using traditional Chinese cooking methods. Dishes to try include ayam buah keluak (chicken with local nuts) and ikan assam nanas pedas (sweet and sour fish).

Name: Wah Lok
Address: Carlton Hotel, Level 2, 76 Bras Basah Road, 189558, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A loyal clientele has made this comfortable, classically decorated Cantonese restaurant their own. The chef was born in Guangzhou but really developed his culinary skills and honed his craft in Hong Kong. His Cantonese dishes range from banquet delicacies like abalone and bird’s nest soup to seafood dishes such as steamed fish. There are also Cantonese roast meats, claypot dishes and home-style items like steamed minced pork with salted fish.

Name: Ghim Moh Chwee Kueh
Address: 20 Ghim Moh Road Market & Food Centre, #01-54, Blk 20, Ghim Moh Road, 270020, Singapore
Description: This stall founded in 1959 is a household name! Its lovingly hand-made chwee kueh – toothsome rice cakes topped with dried radish and mildly spicy sambal – are hugely popular among locals. Minimum order of four pieces.

Name: Koka Wanton Noodles
Address: North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre, #01-99, 861 North Bridge Road, 198783, Singapore
Description: Barbecue pork with wonton noodles is the signature. Deep-fried pork skin and chillies enrich the flavour.

Name: Ah Heng Duck Rice
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-64, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: The taste of duck meat blends with the spice marinade, each boasting a rich flavour. Snacks like duck liver and dried tofu are also offered.

Name: Mellben Seafood (Ang Mo Kio)
Address: Block 232, #01-1222, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, 560232, Singapore
Description: It may not be in the most convenient location but that doesn’t deter the crowds from descending on this open-air space. Nearly everyone is here for one thing: crab. The chef has 15 different ways to cook them, from black pepper crab to creamy butter crab and that, of course, includes the classic chilli crab. There’s also live seafood available, along with cze char dishes – and the claypot bee hoon soup is delicious.

Name: Maxwell Fuzhou Oyster Cake
Address: Maxwell Food Centre, #01-05, 1 Kadayanallur Street, 069184, Singapore
Description: The second-generation owner still fries oyster cakes à la minute as her mother did in the 1960s. They may be darker than usual, but the minced pork, oysters, prawns and coriander are still soft and juicy under the crispy crust.

Name: Hill Street Fried Kway Teow
Address: Pasar 16@Bedok (Bedok South Food Centre), #01-41, 16 Bedok South Road, 460016, Singapore
Description: This stall serves a single dish that is drop-dead perfect every time. Full-bodied wok hei, irresistible aromas and generous toppings like cockles, Chinese sausage, chives and bean sprouts justify the often hour-long wait.

Name: Keng Eng Kee (Bukit Merah)
Description: This popular cze char restaurant may not be the most conveniently placed, but it does some great dishes, like fried salted egg crab, coffee pork ribs and claypot duck with sea cucumber. The setting and environment are not unlike a hawker centre, although there is a smaller inside area that’s air-conditioned. It provides mostly Hainanese cuisine, along with some Cantonese dishes – the stir-fries are particularly delicious.

Name: Boon Tong Kee (Balestier Road)
Description: You won’t have any trouble finding this enduringly popular restaurant – its colourful neon sign will guide you in from afar. The group may have expanded over the years but this is the original branch, opened in 1983. Their signature boiled chicken is still the biggest draw and can be ordered in three different sizes, but those looking for a full zi char feast won’t be disappointed. Avoid peak times if you’re not prepared to queue.

Name: Nicolas
Description: The eponymous French chef has been quietly going about his business in this comfy and intimate little gem for some years now. Choose the Tasting menu to best experience his cooking, underpinned by classical French techniques and made with top-quality ingredients, like langoustines from New Zealand and pigeon from Brittany. Diners can watch the chefs at work in the kitchen through the glass wall. Don’t forget to check out the wine collection in the small walk-in cellar.

Name: Tambi
Description: Tambi is a collaborative effort by chef-owners Sun Kim, of Meta fame, and Mano Thevar, who helms Thevar, an innovative restaurant featuring the rare mix of Korean and Indian food. The menu is short but sweet, with creative combinations such as oxtail bone marrow murtabak with kimchi, and a fusion take on Korean cold spicy noodles known as "Tambi's Bibimmyeon". The young kitchen team melds Indian spices and Korean produce to great effect.

Name: Torno Subito
Description: A nod to the heyday of Italian cinema, the interior takes you back to the Adriatic Riviera circa 1960s. The red-yellow-blue colour scheme is carried through from the walls to the tableware. The concept by celebrity chef Massimo Bottura involves whimsically and creatively harnessing Italian produce in signature dishes like artisan tortellini in a silky sauce made with parmigiano reggiano aged for 36 months. Stone-baked pizzas are delicious.

Name: Béni
Description: The small, elegant restaurant boasts a minimalist décor, so as to keep the spotlight on its exquisite French cooking with a Japanese twist. Top-quality ingredients from France and Japan are transformed here, thanks to well-honed skills and meticulous attention to detail. The set menus change according to the availability of ingredients, such as seafood dishes are adapted to the catch of the day. Check with the sommelier for unusual choices not shown on the wine list.

Name: Shanyuan Teochew Kway Teow Mian
Address: North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre, #01-95, 861 North Bridge Road, 198783, Singapore
Description: Get your noodle fix 24/7 at this popular stall. With myriad made-to-order options on the menu – from fish dumplings and minced pork noodles to mee tai mak and kway teow noodle soup – you're spoiled for choice.

Name: Butcher's Block
Address: Raffles Arcade, #02-02, 328 North Bridge Road, 188719, Singapore
Description: Wood-fire cooking is the speciality of this dark and handsome restaurant within Raffles hotel. Head straight to the tasting menu if you want to experience a variety of top-quality fish and meat dishes, all expertly prepared using American wood and supplemented with Asian flavours. The moodily lit room ensures your gaze never wanders too far from the open kitchen. A restaurant to appeal to the hunter-gatherer in all of us.

Name: Sushi Masaaki
Address: South Beach Avenue, #B1-17, 26 Beach Road, 189768, Singapore
Description: This omakase sushiya with only 12 seats boasts a counter crafted from a 250-year-old hinoki tree. In stark contrast, the lively lounge for tea and dessert is clad in wallpaper with dancing cranes on a pink background. The freshest fish is creatively combined with other ingredients to great effects while the well thought-out, sometimes unorthodox, seasoning on the sushi makes the experience unique. Friendly chefs are happy to interact with diners.

Name: Majestic
Address: Marina One, The Heart (East Tower) #04-01, 5 Straits View, 018935, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Laid out beneath a glass roof, the airy dining area overlooks a garden. The food, which draws on modern techniques and time-honoured traditions, is exquisite in both taste and appearance. The claypot chicken with glutinous rice wine, ginger and wood ear fungus boasts silky, free-range meat and spellbinding aromas. The business clientele can opt for items in individual servings. Booking a week ahead recommended.

Name: Revolver
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Its name is a pun on how cooking revolves around the charcoal grill, brazier and tandoor. Whether you sit at the counter or in a booth, the chefs put on a show that is visible from all seats. Three tasting menus and a vegetarian menu are offered.  Dishes are rooted in different regions of India, but are reimagined and reborn over coals and fire. The distinctive smoky flavour  and layering of spices works magic, resulting in a delicate balance.

Name: Hup Kee Teochew Fishball Mee
Address: Mei Ling Market & Food Centre, #02-38, 159 Mei Chin Road, 140159, Singapore
Description: This popular stall is always busy, even at off-peak times. There are different noodles to choose from, and these are topped with tasty fish balls, pork balls and fried fish cakes. A little of the hot sauce goes a long way!

Name: Kang's Wanton Noodle
Address: Zion Riverside Food Centre, #06, 70 Zion Road, 247792, Singapore
Description: Alongside wanton or dumpling noodle soup, this stall serves deep-fried wanton and char siew. The springy noodles are best enjoyed with a dollop of chilli sauce, while the wantons encase a tasty filling in their paper-thin skin.

Name: Whampoa Soya Bean & Grass Jelly Drinks
Address: Whampoa Makan Place, #01-52, 90/91 Whampoa Drive 91, 320091, Singapore
Description: Tofu pudding is freshly made on the spot – just add toppings such as grass jelly, red beans or lotus seeds. Or try their drinkable versions, in which the soybean flavour is complemented by the velvety texture of a smoothie.

Name: Tow Kwar Pop
Address: Tiong Bahru Market, #02-06, 30 Seng Poh Road, 168898, Singapore
Description: Here, the rojak is made with sliced cucumber, apple and bean sprouts, topped with either crispy tofu puffs or fried dough sticks. The syrupy dressing is rich and tangy, and the ground peanuts give the salad a lovely crunch.

Name: Brasserie Astoria
Address: Victoria Concert Hall, #01-01, 11 Empress Place, 179558, Singapore
Description: An outpost of its namesake in Stockholm, this is the brainchild of the Swedish owner-chef Björn Frantzén. Nestled in the historical Victoria Concert Hall (1800s), its retro glamour complements the chef's new spin on brasserie classics, some with trolley or tableside service. Try the råraka, a Swedish potato cake topped with vendace roe, crème fraîche, chives and red onion. Toast Astoria with prawn, king crab and wasabi aioli is also unmissable.

Name: Copernicus
Description: On Krakow’s oldest street lies this intimate restaurant that sits within the Hotel Copernicus, a former palace with 15th Century origins and an impressive Gothic façade; wood-panelling and a stone fireplace lend the dining room a historic feel. Dishes are modern, adventurous and well-crafted takes on traditional recipes – like the excellent pierogi filled with fontina cheese. The Italian wines are the pick of the bunch and the lunch menu offers great value.

Name: Hana Sushi
Description: Thanks to its quality produce prepared with precision, this simple Japanese-inspired restaurant has made a real impact in Krakow. It's a professionally run place, offering colourful dishes that are fragrant and full of flavour. The lunch menu revolves largely around set bento box options that include sushi, salad and gyoza. Korean cuisine is also represented on the menu with dishes like bibimbap and kimchi jjigae.

Name: Kropka.
Description: Cool, casual and a little grungy, there is a rustic, welcoming vibe to this neighbourhood spot that’s very much in the bistro mould. The simply furnished dining room is enlivened by modern art on the walls and a corner bar that’s well-stocked with natural wines. The cooking mixes a Polish base with influences from over the world, such as the Korean-style chilli sauce that smothers the pierogi. The generous portions are indicative of the restaurant’s spirit.

Name: Filipa 18
Description: This intimate, modern restaurant blends a small open kitchen with powder blue banquettes and walls decorated with bright artwork from The Polish Poster School. The modernised versions of classic Polish dishes deliver an appealing blend of textures, alongside a careful balancing of complementary flavours. Breads are baked in-house and local ingredients are sourced from the nearby Stary Kleparz market.

Name: Papavero
Description: This long-established little restaurant serves a mixture of Polish and Mediterranean-inspired cooking in a stylish setting. The generous and well-executed dishes include their signature roast duck with red cabbage, alongside homemade pastas and classic desserts like tiramisu and crème brûlée. Sit overlooking the street or in the smaller, more intimate room to the rear.

Name: Mazi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Close to the city’s famous cathedral, you’ll find this charming neighbourhood restaurant with a distinctly Mediterranean vibe. From the bright, airy décor to cooking that is fresh, pared-back and abundant in olive oil, the pleasant warmth of the Greek and Italian coasts feel within touching distance. The great value dishes range from delicious, just-baked pitta with salt and herbs to tuna steak with a classic salmoriglio sauce. Chatty, welcoming service adds to the positive atmosphere.

Name: Fiorentina
Description: The beautiful vaulted, red-brick ceiling is a key attraction at this well-run and deservedly busy restaurant. An experienced chef takes traditional dishes and gives them a modern update, while using the best of the local larder and delivering plenty of flavour. Their house specialities include Siberian sturgeon caviar, Dover sole cooked over a wood-fired grill and, as the name would suggest, Fiorentina steak, which is dry-aged for 30 days before being chargrilled.

Name: Albertina
Description: This sophisticated modern restaurant features a basement wine bar and boasts 32 wines available by the glass thanks to the Enomatic wine system. The cooking showcases the chef’s passion for hunting and fishing, with ingredients like venison and wild boar likely to make an appearance. The restaurant has its own lobster tank too, resulting in a range of lobster dishes on offer. Across the menu, the eye-catching cooking captures the ingredients’ true flavours.

Name: elixir by Dom Wódki
Description: It’s all about vodka at this fashionable bistro that forms part of the ‘Vodka House’, which also includes a museum and cocktail bar. There are over 750 versions of the spirit to choose from, accompanied by well-cooked dishes prepared with care. The menu prioritises classic flavours in dishes like beef tartare, chicken broth and dumplings. Friendly service enhances the experience and there is, of course, always a vodka recommendation at the ready.

Name: A nóż widelec
Description: Located some way out of the city, ‘Knife and Fork’ is a modern, understated restaurant that’s run well by an engaging team. The small space has a relaxed atmosphere, while the menu is underpinned by modern interpretations of traditional Polish recipes. Seasonal produce informs the cooking too, with a tasting menu available at dinner. 'Podążaj za tym co Cię uszczęśliwia' written across the wall means ‘follow what makes you happy’ – and here you will be!

Name: Szara
Description: In the city's Grand Square, you’ll find this family-run, brasserie-style restaurant which boasts a hand-painted Gothic ceiling and a lovely terrace. The charming, vaulted dining room plays host to traditional cooking that draws on classic dishes from Polish, French and Swedish cuisine – accompanied by a largely French wine list. The well-executed, hearty dishes are brought to the table by an efficient service team.

Name: Bez Gwiazdek
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Located just minutes from The Royal Castle in Warsaw, this cosy restaurant has a real neighbourhood feel. The menu changes monthly, with each version focusing on cooking inspired by one of Poland's 16 regions. The chefs take traditional recipes and modernise them using contemporary techniques and sometimes a creative edge. Service comes from a wonderfully enthusiastic team who show considerable pride in their work. The great wine recommendations favour biodynamic choices from smaller producers.

Name: Nolita
Description: A glass-fronted kitchen is the focal point of this smart monochrome restaurant that takes on a multitude of influences. The cooking exhibits flavours from a range of global cuisines, be that Polish, Mediterranean or Southeast Asian. Check the daily specials too, for luxurious produce like whole Alaskan king crab to share. Dishes have assured flavours, often accompanied by vibrant colours, and the excellent bread is a real highlight. Friendly service and spot-on wine recommendations complete the picture.

Name: Oberża 86
Description: Tucked away amongst some more utilitarian buildings, sits this pretty red-brick cottage with a cobbled terrace out front. With a long history that includes stints as a shop, a shoemaker’s and a museum, it now feels like a perfect fit for this cosy, welcoming restaurant. Seasonal Polish produce is the bedrock of the cooking, which is allowed to shine with a lightness of touch and a French flourish, showcased in technically adept elements like a piquant butter sauce accompanying the sea trout.

Name: L’Entre Villes
Description: This beautifully elegant villa dates back to the turn of the 20th Century and sports interior décor that mixes the traditional with the contemporary, chandeliers with modern art – while its bright orangery is the most in-demand dining area come the summer. The neatly laid tables hint at the formality of the place, with dishes arriving under cloches and the smartly aproned team occasionally donning white gloves to serve. The French-inflected cooking demonstrates sound classical skill from the kitchen.

Name: Fino
Description: The city’s old town plays host to this understated restaurant surrounded by attractive period buildings. The elegant interior benefits from modern art for sale on the walls and floral arrangements adding a pop of colour. An overtly seasonal menu means you might be treated to superb, full-flavoured deer when the time is right; but there’s a luxury edge to the offering all year round, with ingredients like Oscietra caviar and top-notch beef utilised with great skill by the chefs. Go for the tasting menu, which flows together wonderfully.

Name: Muzealna
Address: The National Museum, al. Jerozolimskie 3, Warsaw, 00 495, Poland
Description: Within the impressive main building of the National Museum of Poland sits this younger sibling to alewino, which serves unfussy bistro-style food. A broad menu includes both hot and cold starters, with hearty dishes like trout paprikash a feature. There is a refined finish to the cooking, but it’s the punchy flavours that really stand out. The friendly team make everyone feel welcome and always serve with a smile.

Name: Eliksir
Description: An ideal spot for cocktail lovers, Eliksir reputedly has the longest bar in the region and holds over 400 bottles ready and waiting to be used in a mixture of classic and bespoke drinks. A cocktail pairing is also offered with the tasting menu, as an alternative to the usual wine flight. Both the tasting option and the à la carte showcase quality local produce like Masurian beef, which is given the platform to shine in an excellent tartare. Smooth, friendly service adds to the appeal.

Name: Mercato
Address: Hilton Gdańsk, Targ Rybny 1, Gdansk, 80-838, Poland
Description: Offering tasting menus named after nearby streets, this restaurant on the ground floor of the Hilton takes its inspiration from the markets of Gdańsk. Its history as a port city means this could include global influences alongside local produce such as fine Pomeranian lamb. The technical skill of the kitchen comes through in elements like sous vide and blow-torched salmon. An à la carte is available too, and the charming staff explain the dishes with pride.

Name: Café Xander
Description: Housed inside a hotel but with a separate entrance and a feel all its own, this elegant restaurant is worth the short walk out from the city centre. Start with a cocktail while you study the concise à la carte, where the Polish cooking comes with a Mediterranean influence that's noticeable in the occasional pasta or risotto. Top produce is clearly a priority, with super ingredients from black tiger prawns to glistening cod on offer. Attractive presentation and a touch of formality in the service enhance the experience.

Name: ZaKładka
Description: Just a few steps from a footbridge over the Vistula, you'll find this riverside restaurant with a striking orange façade. With their chequered floors and red banquettes, the characterful rooms have a classic bistro feel – and the French cooking also offers a traditional edge. Dishes are hearty and founded on high quality ingredients, and warm, professional service completes the picture.

Name: Europejski Grill
Description: Set in the lovingly restored Raffles Europejski Hotel, this sophisticated restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the historic Pilsudski square and is the place to be in the summer. A charcoal grill is used to good effect on prime produce ranging from Dover sole to fillet of beef; on Sundays, the menu changes to include brunch dishes, pasta and salads. To drink, try their own specially distilled vodka or pay a visit to the Long Bar, a version of the Raffles Singapore original that birthed the Singapore Sling.

Name: NOOKS
Description: There’s an appealing feel to this neighbourhood restaurant nestling in a corner basement; head straight for the hidden terrace to the rear when the sun is shining. Fresh homemade pasta is a highlight of a menu that also features Asian dishes like Jiaozi dumplings and ramen. Cooked in a semi-open kitchen, the dishes are hearty and packed with flavour. Friendly, enthusiastic service completes the picture.

Name: Noriko Omakase
Description: An engaging husband-and-wife team bring their natural charm to this intimate Japanese restaurant that relocated from Wrocław towards the end of 2022. The L-shaped counter seats just eight guests, who are encouraged to interact as the omakase menu unfolds. Largely imported produce is utilised in familiar dishes such as tuna temaki, chawanmushi and an array of nigiri. Japanese whiskies and a choice of sakes complete the memorable experience.

Name: Port Sołacz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The gorgeous Sołacki Park provides a wonderful setting for this restaurant housed inside a fine lakeside building that’s over 110 years old. The recently refurbished interior is suitably bright, but it’s the lovely terrace that steals the show. The extensive menu caters for a range of appetites, featuring soup, salads and pizzas alongside more substantial dishes like confit duck leg – which shows off the technical skill of the kitchen. Their bedrooms provide the perfect base for exploring the park.

Name: NOTA_RESTO by Tomasz Leśniak
Description: The chef to the Polish national football team is behind this brightly decorated restaurant, and also owns the more informal bistro next door. The wide-ranging menu includes both a variety of steaks – served with a choice of sides and sauces – and a 'flour and water' section that includes homemade pasta alongside classic pierogi. Everything comes in generous portions and delivers bold, gutsy flavours. The professional service team run the place well.

Name: Cucina
Description: Housed inside a historic building that was once a military barracks, the ever-developing Cucina now forms part of the City Park Hotel. The Mediterranean-influenced menu caters to a range of tastes, from pizzas and pastas to beef tartare and fine roast duck. A large, on-view wine wall is an indicator of the serious list, which features some excellent vintages and is enhanced by charming, knowledgeable service. A covered terrace comes into its own in the summer.

Name: Nami Beef and Reef
Description: In an area of the city filled with restaurants, seek out this atmospheric spot where the menu reads like a ‘greatest hits’ of Japanese cuisine. Gyozas, nigiri, yakitori… all will be provided by the skilled kitchen team; and while the place lives up to its name with a wide sushi selection and multiple cuts of beef cooked on the robata grill, it’s worth diverting your attention to the terrific vegetable tempura. It’s all perfect for sharing, so bring some friends and sample as much as possible.

Name: Amarylis
Description: Global and Polish influences are effectively integrated at this basement restaurant inside the Queen Hotel, close to Krakow Old Town. Choose to sit in either a traditional brick-built room or a more modern space furnished in black and white, then sit back and enjoy the attractively presented modern dishes. There’s a good degree of detail in the cooking, which showcases precision and effective flavour contrasts throughout.

Name: Butchery & Wine
Description: The name of this busy modern bistro says it all; the emphasis is on steaks, which are dry-aged for a minimum of 28 days in their glass-fronted ageing fridges. The cuts are then skilfully cooked in the Bertha oven, where temperatures can reach up to 500°C. Try a Polish cut or one imported from further afield, accompanied by a glass of red wine. Non-steak dishes might include homemade black pudding and Kashubian style fish soup.

Name: Farina
Description: A pretty little restaurant in the heart of the Old Town, the dining area here is divided across three cosy rooms, each with their own character and blending original features with more modern furnishings. The simple cooking eschews fussiness in favour of reliably enjoyable dishes that allow the core flavours to shine. Seafood is the speciality, with fish arriving from France several times a week and then cooked whole over salt and herbs. Dishes to share are a feature.

Name: Fisherman
Description: Just 300m from the beach and with a name like Fisherman, it’s no surprise that seafood is the focus of this cosy, candlelit restaurant, which also boasts an attractive terrace if you prefer to dine alfresco. Produce from trout to catfish is used in unfussy, flavoursome dishes – including a knockout paprikash – that are often adorned with sea herbs and hedgerow flowers foraged by the team. It sits within Villa Sentoza, so there’s rooms available if you want to stay the night.

Name: True
Description: Quality primary ingredients and skilled treatment of them form the basis of the cooking at this stylishly understated restaurant. Although multiple cuts of beef form a chunk of the menu, this is far more than a steakhouse. Seafood plays a big role too, with surf and turf platters catching the eye, while the quality of the kitchen shines through even in the smaller details – like a terrific side dish of girolles. The wine list contains some hidden gems and the service team will be happy to recommend a glass or two.

Name: Pod Nosem
Description: The bright ground floor of this characterful medieval-style restaurant is hung with tapestries and the white wooden banquettes have tapestry seat cushions to match; downstairs, amongst the brick and stone, it’s more dimly lit. Classic Polish recipes are given appealing modern updates. Above the restaurant are three richly furnished suites – with prices to match.

Name: Dyletanci
Description: Tucked away in a quiet city centre mews since its relocation towards the end of 2023, this smart restaurant is the brainchild of an experienced chef and wine importer. This background shines through in an impressive wine list with over 1,500 choices, and a particular focus on biodynamic and organic options. The cooking is pared-back and vibrant, utilising ingredients from their own farm and local producers. The friendly team enhance your visit with relaxed yet professional service.

Name: The Time
Description: This smart monochrome restaurant sits within a refurbished city centre mansion, which also houses its sister restaurants and an office space; it's somewhat hidden away within the complex, but well worth seeking out. Formerly a grill-centric eatery, the Mibrasa charcoal oven remains in use for produce like Dover sole, but these days the menu is more expansive and could include their stand-out marinated herring, which delivers all the expected zing and vibrancy. There are some seriously good wines on offer too.

Name: Ritz
Description: Chef-Owner Basia Ritz was the first winner of MasterChef Poland and used this as a springboard to fulfil her ambition of running her own restaurant. Her dream has been realised at this quayside spot nestled amongst numerous other eateries. Locally sourced produce provides many of the menu’s highlights, with the likes of in-season chanterelles laying a strong foundation for the unfussy modern cooking. The personable team provide keen and friendly service.

Name: Artesse
Description: In four 16th Century tenement houses in the city’s Old Town lies the luxury H15 Palace Hotel; within it sits this smart, contemporary restaurant with a glass roof, tropical plants and bright modern artwork. Choose from two tersely worded tasting menus that use seasonal produce in reinventions of historical Polish recipes. Precise presentation, bold flavours and creativity help to make each dish a success. Engaging service and a hint of theatre add to the overall enjoyment.

Name: Butchery & Wine
Description: Sister to the long-standing Warsaw operation and following the same tried-and-tested mantra, this well-run restaurant does what it says on the tin. Order a bottle from the wine list and take your pick of the local meats, from terrific homemade black pudding to a range of steaks cooked on the grill; the fish cookery is equally adept, meaning there’s plenty of choice. If you’re on a budget, the lunch menu offers brilliant value for money.

Name: Epoka
Description: Spread across two stylish, colourful rooms conceived by a Polish theatre designer – one bright blue, one in warmer hues – this restaurant inside the Raffles Europejski hotel takes its inspiration from the Polish cookbooks of yesteryear. Classic recipes like roasted goose are listed on the menu next to their dates of origin, but given a modern spin in their execution. Local produce plays a big role too, with the ingredients presented to diners at the start of the meal.

Name: PASODOBRE
Address: Poznań Congress Centre, Śniadeckich 25, Poznan, 60-773, Poland
Description: Just to the side of the Poznan Congress Centre, you’ll find this spacious Spanish restaurant serving up the usual tapas suspects. You’ll find Padrón peppers and patatas bravas all present and correct, alongside more filling main dishes and a selection of pintxos. Strong, satisfying flavours run throughout, while the flan is a terrific incarnation of a classic dessert. A small fridge is filled with Spanish goodies to buy and take home, including olive oil and almonds.

Name: Zazie
Description: In the city's historic Jewish quarter of Kazimierz, you’ll find this busy little bistro with a bustling atmosphere that belies its residential location. Ask for a table in the characterful cellar, which mixes French memorabilia with brick and stone walls. The Gallic influence continues into the cooking, with dishes like beef Bourguignon and classic onion soup with Gruyère cheese among the gutsy and generously sized options on the menu.

Name: Kogel Mogel
Description: There’s a chic, retro quality to this lively brasserie in Krakow’s Old Town, which sports several dining rooms – including one with a vaulted brick ceiling – plus an enclosed garden terrace. It's a smart place, with the menu bringing modern updates to classic Krakovian dishes, as well as those from wider Poland. This is simple, satisfying cooking with a generous touch that no doubt pleases their regulars. For dessert, the hot apple pie made with Polish Szara Reneta apples is not to be missed.

Name: Karakter
Description: There's a lively atmosphere when eating at Karakter thanks to its loud music, cocktails and pared-back décor. The charming young team serve an extensive menu with a focus on offal, so be prepared for sweetbreads, brains and horse meat tartare, the last of which is one of their signature dishes. The cooking of these less-common ingredients is original and refined, blending many different flavours together. The set lunch menu is a steal.

Name: Piwna47
Description: An unpretentious, friendly vibe is key to the charms of this modern café-brasserie found down a cobbled street in the shadow of the impressive St. Mary's Church. With a bright conservatory extension on the ground floor and a more rustic feel upstairs, it offers a pleasant environment for breakfast, a light lunch or something more substantial. The menu takes local produce and applies influences from other areas of Europe, often promoting the unfussy cooking style of the Mediterranean.

Name: Tygle
Description: Located on one of the city’s busiest waterside boulevards, Tygle is made all the more appealing by its enthusiastic service team and enclosed terrace that’s ideal for alfresco dining. Inside, you'll find a minimalist-meets-industrial style, with exposed pipes and Edison bulbs. The satisfying and well-executed dishes come in hearty portions – exemplified by the pork schnitzel – and there’s a sense of fun about options like the honey cheesecake dessert. They also offer a popular breakfast menu.

Name: Niesztuka
Description: There’s a mysterious, secretive feel to this restaurant tucked away inside a historic house, which sits surrounded by amber jewellers in the heart of the Old Town. Its ground floor has long high-topped tables that lend themselves to communal dining, while the first floor offers a bit more privacy. A concise menu uses excellent daily produce, with a distinct South American influence running through the dishes – from classic ceviche to delicious corn husk ice cream and meringue for dessert.

Name: The Farm
Description: A farm in Masuria, around 190km north of this appropriately named restaurant, provides produce for the chefs’ wholesome dishes that showcase big, gutsy flavours. Not all of the ingredients are local however, with the speciality in-house butchered steaks coming from Japan, Australia and beyond – the delicious beef dripping chips are the ideal accompaniment. The wine list is concise yet varied, while the bottles are stored on copper racks that suit the simple, rustic aesthetic of the room.

Name: Delicja
Description: Dine in the shade of one of the oldest trees in the Wielkopolska region in the small enclosed garden of this romantic restaurant. The elegant dining room is filled with antiques and polished silver, bringing an old-fashioned feel to proceedings. The formal and personable service is a good match for the surroundings, as is the roster of classic yet ambitious dishes.

Name: Pod Różą
Description: In the centre of the 300 year old hotel of the same name, within a glass-covered atrium, you'll find this spacious restaurant boasting a lounge bar and a dining area overlooking the kitchen. Quality Polish ingredients power modern dishes underpinned by a strong classical base, with confident and assured presentation, bold flavours and an Italian influence. The well-chosen wine list features over 300 Italian wines.

Name: Marino Bistrot
Description: Hidden away in a residential area, this basement restaurant sports rustic exposed brickwork and simple bistro furnishings. It’s named after Chef-Owner Livio Marino, who has a passion for authentic Italian dishes that manifests itself here in an extensive menu that includes a selection of homemade pastas. Look out for the gnocchi, which could come with the delicious combination of gorgonzola, pear and walnuts. For dessert, it’s very hard to resist tiramisu in a place like this.

Name: hub.praga
Description: On the eastern side of the Vistula River lies this small, modern restaurant. Dishes offer distinct, recognisably Polish flavours and have a refined touch, with each one appearing as a work of art on the plate. The menu is made up of 14 courses: enjoy them all as the full tasting menu, choose 10 for the shorter version or simply pick four or five per person to share. A chef’s table is on offer inside the kitchen if you really want to get in on the action.

Name: Tuna
Description: Wearing its fishy heart on its sleeve, this restaurant sports hundreds of tiny metal scales on its walls and a counter near the entrance displaying a bounty of seafood produce. These ingredients, ranging from skrei cod to scallops, are treated in a variety of ways, including raw preparations like tiraditos, tartares and ceviches. The titular ‘king of the sea’ does of course make an appearance too. The same team is behind Ceviche Bar on the other side of the city.

Name: Zen On
Description: It’s easy to see why this restaurant styled on Japanese izakaya is one of the city’s hotspots. Simple, fresh and fun, it boasts bright décor and a buzzing atmosphere that reverberates around the split-level dining room. The menu offers all manner of delights, from dim sum and bao buns to daily made udon noodles and stand-out ramen crafted using flour delivered direct from Japan. The 2 course lunch menu is a steal and the sake list is worth checking out.

Name: Dvor Jezeršek
Address: Zgornji Brnik 63, Cerklje na Gorenjskem, 4207, Slovenia
Description: Situated in the quiet, bucolic village of Cerklje na Gorenjskem in the heart of the Kamnik and Savinja Alps around 40km from the Austrian border, these traditional old buildings have been converted by the Jezeršek family into a hotel with large rooms and a gourmet restaurant. The outdoor tables are particularly attractive, while the dining room has small windows allowing guests to observe the chefs at work in the kitchen. Among the desserts, don’t miss the Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake), which is served in a traditional steel pan. The restaurant also organises cookery courses and workshops on themes such as bread-making and finger food.

Name: B-Restaurant
Description: This rooftop restaurant at the InterContinental hotel boasts stunning 180° views of the historic centre and castle through its floor-to-ceiling windows, especially at night when the illuminated castle is surrounded by the lights of the city. Inside the restaurant, the contemporary design and open-view kitchen provide the setting for a choice of dishes which is as extensive as the views. As a result, the restaurant has built a well-deserved reputation for its international cuisine, alongside Slovenian specialities. We particularly enjoyed the fresh red prawn ceviche served with a mango sorbet that enhanced the freshness of the prawns, and an excellent tapioca quail with green asparagus and a delicate jus. Before dinner, we recommend a cocktail in the adjacent bar to admire the views of the other half of the city!

Name: Otočec Castle
Address: Grajska cesta 2, Otočec na Krki, 8222, Slovenia
Description: This luxury hotel and restaurant in a spectacular and tranquil location in the middle of the Krka river occupies a charming 13C castle that was demolished and then rebuilt for the purpose. Antiques, a delightful bar with a fireplace and soft comfortable sofas all combine to create the feel of bygone days in the attractive dining room. The cuisine is regional and traditional, featuring carefully prepared dishes (the chicken with fregola pasta is delicious) and fresh vegetables sourced from the restaurant’s organic kitchen garden. Both the à la carte and the tasting menus follow the seasons. To round off your visit in truly aristocratic style, stay in one of the hotel’s luxurious guestrooms.

Name: Kendov Dvorec
Description: The history of this magnificent country mansion overlooking the Idrijca river valley dates back to the 14C. Today, the building houses a warm and elegant restaurant, with stylish rooms for winter dining and a beautiful terrace for the summer. The cuisine is traditional and full of authentic flavours, featuring two tasting menus – Katarina (fish) and Jakob (meat). We recommend the latter, especially if it includes the delicious “bati and bakalca” (steamed bread dough and lamb goulash). The entire wine list is dedicated to Slovenia, with all wines available by the glass – the Štemberger Malvazija is particularly good. Charming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: A3
Address: Grad Rajhenburg, Cesta izgnancev 3, Brestanica, 8280, Slovenia
Description: This restaurant, housed in the superbly restored 12C Rajhenburg castle overlooking the Sava river, takes its name from the huge inner courtyard that provides the perfect setting for an aperitif chosen from the many Slovenian sparkling wines served here. In the elegant and stylishly furnished dining room, enjoy a surprise tasting menu (4, 5, 6 or 7 courses) of modern dishes that are full of flavour – the zander with celeriac and the beef with Jerusalem artichoke are particularly delicious. The friendly staff are happy to offer tours of the castle, while the views from the outdoor terrace are truly delightful.

Name: City Terasa
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re exploring Maribor, this restaurant is a great place to stop and take a break and has a real holiday feel with its spacious terrace boasting views of the town, the Drava river and the Pohorje mountains in the distance. The menu focuses on fish from the Adriatic (including shellfish and plenty of grilled options), as well as meat recipes that include grass-fed Slovenian beef. There’s a more concise menu at lunchtime, plus a café and the sky lounge, both of which are perfect settings in which to relax.

Name: Julijana
Description: Housed in the Grand Hotel Toplice which stands amid some of the most popular landscapes in Slovenia, this restaurant boasts truly breathtaking views of Lake Bled from its dining room and its outdoor terrace. Here, the chef offers tasting menus of various lengths featuring meat and fish specialities with the occasional international influence, as well as a 4-course option (the Gorenjska selection menu) with a stronger regional focus. On the latter, the array of local ingredients is showcased via a delicious hazelnut crème brûlée served with ice-cream made from cherries soaked in Terrano liqueur.

Name: Etna
Description: On its website, this modern restaurant describes itself as “the home of different flavours from the Karst region”. Its cuisine is generous and exciting, with a focus on top-quality ingredients that the chef skilfully transforms into delicious dishes. The pizzas are excellent, as are the highly recommended desserts.

Name: Špacapanova Hiša
Description: For more than 50 years, Špacapanova Hiša has been a bastion of Karst cuisine. The restaurant has been run by the Špacapan family since 1973, while its current success is largely due to son and brilliant manager Ago, who has taken the quality of the cuisine to a new level. The regional cuisine is prepared from local ingredients – staff are happy to provide information on the provenance of the ingredients and the human stories involved in their production. Depending on the time of year, don’t miss the lamb and kid, both of which are raised in the Karst and cooked in the oven, then served with cow’s milk curd ravioli. The traditions of the Karst are also alive and well in the wine cellar (the venue for tastings of wine, ham and cheese matured on site). If you’d like to prolong your stay here, the restaurant also offers a few guestrooms, some of which have been recently renovated with period furnishings.

Name: Sushimama
Description: Situated not far from the castle and the riverside, in the city lively and pedestrianised tourist district, Sushimama serves elegant and precisely prepared Japanese dishes: sushi and sashimi, of course, in different combinations, but also soups (miso and others), tempura dishes, and cooked meat and fish options. In a simple furnished setting, the service is attentive and courteous.

Name: PEN KLUB Restavracija
Description: Head up to the first floor to this retro-style restaurant, where you pass a welcoming lounge bar before moving into the main dining room adorned with an attractive fresco. The current managers and chef have brought the restaurant back into vogue thanks to a menu which includes some of the restaurant’s historic dishes (such as foie gras) alongside new meat and fish (both salt- and freshwater) dishes, such as the excellent trout marinated with oil and lemon and served with a dried egg yolk and green tea gel. The tiny summer terrace has just a few tables (book in advance), while the wine list features a selection of mainly regional labels.

Name: Miza za štiri
Description: The name of this restaurant (Table for 4) says it all. The business began a few years ago as a type of “table d’hôte” for just four guests, then in 2020, Jure and Mia Brložnik followed their dreams and moved from the city to the countryside. Their restaurant is divided into three rooms, each with just one table – the perfect setting for an intimate dinner! The chef offers a fixed menu of 5, 7 or 9 courses (to be ordered ahead of time) which showcases modern cuisine with its roots in the region and a focus on vegetables and features dishes such as beetroot with horseradish, trout with mushrooms and delicious desserts. For a unique bespoke experience, we recommend the pairing with local wines.

Name: MAK
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Maribor, this restaurant with a slightly eccentric and very individual feel is home to owner-chef David Vračko. The two dining rooms here are decorated with a curious mix of furnishings and tables with attractively simple settings. There’s no à la carte, but instead a long tasting menu created by the chef that features colourful, playful dishes with unusual and occasionally contrasting textures. The theme here is creative, interesting cuisine, including a carefully prepared selection of appetisers, delicious salmon tartare with exotic fruit, superb prawns with cauliflower, and mouth-watering duck. Everything is served with a cheerful smile and a real sense of performance.

Name: Peti 181
Description: Although this restaurant’s excellent location is best appreciated in summer, with tables overlooking the river and charming views of the castle lit up at night, the attractive dining room also has an elegant and welcoming ambience influenced by the chef’s interior design skills. The cuisine is Mediterranean in style, with a focus on fish and seafood – the shellfish is excellent, as is the delicious grilled sea bass with buttered mashed potatoes, and the mouthwatering scampi soup with fried scampi tempura. The wines available by the glass are mainly Slovenian, although there’s also an interesting Riesling Gruss from Alsace that makes an excellent pairing with fish and seafood.

Name: Altrokè
Description: Inspired by Istria and the Mediterranean, the meat and fish dishes served at Altrokè are enhanced by the use of ingredients such as fruit, aromatic herbs and olive oil which are grown or produced on the restaurant’s own property in Plavje near Koper. The ambience here is pleasantly rustic, with exposed stonework and a brick-vaulted ceiling which blend in well with this old district of the city.

Name: Restavracija Hotela Marina
Description: Although its immediate setting may lack charm, the position of this restaurant facing the marina is delightful, with its superb sea views through its picture windows. The delicious, authentic and carefully prepared cuisine focuses on fish and seafood “straight from the sea to your plate”. Although there is an à la carte, ingredients are often subject to availability. Seafood, rock fish and pasta served with an array of original sauces are just some of the delicious classic dishes on the menu.

Name: Gostilna Krištof
Description: The Bolka family continues with their long-established tradition of hospitality in this authentic and welcoming restaurant that immediately warms the heart. The skilfully updated cuisine combines local recipes with a contemporary twist, as demonstrated by dishes such as trout tartare served with sweet and sour ginger, trout roe and a Bernese foam sauce. The menu changes with the seasons and showcases local ingredients such as Krškopolje pork, Carnolian sausage and locally farmed trout. The wine list has the same regional focus, with almost every Slovenian wine available by the glass.

Name: Landerik
Description: This small restaurant on one of Ljubljana’s typical pedestrianised streets boasts a modern, minimalist-style dining room, as well as an attractive outdoor terrace from which to enjoy the views of this picturesque district in the heart of the city. To appreciate the cuisine to the full, we recommend choosing one of the tasting menus. The desserts include a lighter version of the traditional Kaiserschmarrn, featuring small portions of pancake, apricots and a truly mouthwatering vanilla cream.

Name: Hiša Krasna
Description: Run by owners Dajana and Boris Škibin and situated just a few kilometres from the Italian border, Casa Krasna is a pleasant boutique hotel where the traditions and character of Istria and the Karst meet (she is from Istria, while he is from the Karst). The ambience and cuisine at the restaurant combine to provide one of the most interesting dining experiences in the area, with a menu that features a careful selection of the region’s gastronomic specialities, as well as home-made bread and pasta. Tasting evenings organised in conjunction with local wineries are held in the old wine cellar carved out of the rock.

Name: Stara Gostilna
Description: Situated just off the seafront in lovely Piran, this elegant, stylish restaurant greets guests with the aromas of fresh herbs planted in large vases. The pleasant, intimate dining room serves as a backdrop for two tasting menus and a concise à la carte, all of which feature local, Mediterranean cuisine with a modern touch. Try the lobster ravioli or local sea bass cooked to perfection, followed by a selection of delicious desserts. The wine list offers over 400 labels, all chosen for their excellent pairing potential, plus a fine selection of rums and brandies.

Name: Rizibizi
Description: Situated in an attractive location on the seafront promenade in Portorož, this restaurant boasts a classic-style interior and a pleasant summer terrace facing the beach and the sea. Most of the fish on the menu is local, and is served in simple, unfussy dishes that are full of flavour. Truffles make an appearance on the menu in season, adding their unique flavour to various dishes – don’t miss the delicious sea bass options (carpaccio and pan-fried). An impressive wine list completes the picture.

Name: Restavracija Calypso
Description: Housed within the Perla Resort and Entertainment Centre on the Slovenian side of Gorizia, this renowned restaurant has an excellent reputation in the region for its fish and seafood cuisine. The classically prepared dishes are announced at your table, with options such as raw and baked fish taking pride of place here and a particular focus on fresh fish from the Adriatic.

Name: Gostilna AS
Description: At this restaurant located in the centre of Ljubljana, choose between a dining room with a typical vaulted ceiling and, in summer, a delightful outdoor area surrounded by greenery with views of the castle. The traditional menu here features Slovenian meat dishes, with a particular focus on grilled options (such as the Cowboy steak of local beef which we particularly enjoyed), fish from the Adriatic, and home-made pasta.

Name: JB Restavracija
Description: This restaurant, named after owner-chef Janez Bratovž, the father of modern Slovenian cuisine, occupies a Secessionist building dating from the 1920s and designed by architect Jože Plečnik. The building provides an intriguing setting for Bratovž’s cuisine, where the chef, assisted by his son Tomaž in the kitchen and the rest of his family front of house, combines regional ingredients and flavours with classic influences. Don’t miss the iconic JB ravioli (a permanent feature on the menu), which are stuffed with cheese and pistachio and served with goose liver and a veal jus. Bratovž has also published a book detailing his philosophy, his ingredients and forty of his most popular recipes.

Name: Restavracija Sedem
Description: In Slovenian, the word for “seven” (Sedem) also means sitting down at the table. An interesting option for either lunch or dinner, this restaurant is where students from a local tourism and catering college are trained under the watchful eye of their mentors and teachers. The original dishes on offer here are full of flavour and reflect the region and changing seasons and are presented on various tasting menus (including a vegan option) and an à la carte. You can also take a peek at the open kitchen, where a future culinary star may well be cooking your meal for you!

Name: Gostilna Vovko
Description: Comprising a bar, wine bar, restaurant and hotel, the Gostilna Vovko is a family-run business with more than 50 years of history behind it, where the traditionally furnished dining room includes a charming wood-fired stove. The cuisine is just as you would expect – authentic and regional, including dishes such as delicious local trout tartare served with horseradish and herbs, and thick, meaty pork chops which are perfect accompanied by a glass of velvety and intensely flavoured 2019 Modra Frankinja wine. The wine list pays tribute to regional labels.

Name: Sophia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Open in the evening, the gourmet restaurant at the exclusive Kempinski hotel offers an elegant tribute to the famous Italian actress Sophia Loren, whose unique beauty was as Mediterranean in style as the flavours that inspire the cuisine served here. Influences from Istria, Italy and even France combine harmoniously on a menu that focuses mainly on fish and seafood from the Adriatic (don’t miss the shellfish), although a few carefully selected, top-quality meat dishes and truffle specialities also feature. The turbot steak with prawns, leek and chive-flavoured extra-virgin olive oil is superb.

Name: Gredič
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: To get to this imposing 17C castle, home to an elegant boutique hotel as well as this restaurant, you make your way through the delightful rolling hills of the Collio wine-producing region. The cuisine here reflects the multicultural character of the country, combining Mediterranean traditions and ingredients such as sea bass, cuttlefish and crayfish with other ingredients from Central Europe such as trout, carp and venison in imaginative dishes with a personalised touch. As this is one of Slovenia’s most important wine-producing regions, make sure you visit the vinotheque here.

Name: Danilo
Description: Now run by the third generation of the Čarman family (opened by grandfather Danilo), this restaurant continues to offer cuisine that is much appreciated by its guests, with Nina at the helm in the kitchen and her brother Gašper front of house. The menu includes traditional dishes such as Loška smojka, Loška medla and Loška mešta (old peasant recipes from Škofja Loka – hence the adjective Loška – which are based on semolina and served with turnips, pork or potatoes), as well as a few more creative options that also have a regional flavour. Although meat takes centre stage, a few fish specialities from the Adriatic also feature on the menu.

Name: AFTR
Description: Situated in the heart of the city, AFTR is a trendy bistro with colourful, modern dining rooms and a charming outdoor space which is perfect for a slightly cooler dining experience away from the busy riverside promenade. The cuisine here, which includes Mediterranean dishes such as taramasalata and Central European options such as suckling pig with kiwi and fennel, is fresh and tasty, skilfully combining delicate ingredients with more intense flavours. Instead of the usual division of courses, the menu has sections dedicated to cold dishes, hot dishes and desserts. The small wine selection includes a number of wines also available by the glass. Our inspector recommends the Vitvoska di Kukanja, an organic white from the Karst which both fresh and mineral.

Name: Ošterija Debeluh
Description: Situated in inland Slovenia just a few miles from the border with Croatia, this is one of the most interesting restaurants in the region. Here, highly experienced owner-chef Jure Tomič has created an excellent network of suppliers from all over Slovenia. His meat and fish dishes are prepared with a modern, precise and technical touch that is unfussy and focuses on bringing out the full flavour of his ingredients. Traditional recipes and ingredients are reinterpreted with a personal twist: examples are the plum extract served with duck and the sweet “butter, honey and milk” dish that takes the ingredients of a typical local dessert and creates something new and original. You’ll have no problem finding the right wine to accompany your meal from the extensive wine list.

Name: Kogo
Description: Situated away from the busy tourist centre yet easily accessible by car, this restaurant is home to an elegant wine bar (on the right when you enter the building) and a modern dining room with a few designer-style features (on the left). Despite the contemporary ambience, the food at Kogo (the name is the Slovenian word for “cook”) is traditional and includes a huge selection of cheese and charcuterie (from Slovenia and further afield), followed by main courses that focus on meat (although fish dishes also feature). There’s also an impressive wine list with detailed descriptions on a tablet.

Name: Restavracija 1906
Address: Hotel Triglav, Kolodvorska cesta 33, Bled, 4260, Slovenia
Description: Housed in the Triglav hotel in a superb location in the foothills around beautiful Lake Bled, this restaurant offers fine views from its brightly lit dining room and delightful summer terrace. The hotel opened in 1906 and the restaurant reflects over a century of culinary tradition, serving reinterpretations of typical Slovenian specialities, often adding typical French sauces and jus to its dishes. A small vegan menu is also available.

Name: Gostilna Repovž
Description: The Repovž family who run this restaurant are continuing a long family tradition that dates back centuries – it’s thought that the property has been in their hands for over 500 years, while there’s been a restaurant here for 300 years! Although it’s impossible to list the different generations that have worked here, one thing’s for sure – the current management has really made its mark. Both the dining room and kitchen staff work hard to ensure that guests enjoy the best regional ingredients and dishes (for example, there’s no fish on the menu), which feature on tasting menus of various lengths, with a careful balance of traditional recipes and more contemporary-style fare. The choice of delicious appetisers showcases an array of local traditional specialities, including locally bred trout, vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, rabbit with plum cream, and diced pork with a horseradish mousse. The impressive wine list focuses on Slovenian labels – make sure you try the Laški Riesling from Slovenian Styria, a natural wine, or perhaps the Frelih St. Rupert, a lightly macerated and elegant Sylvaner produced nearby.

Name: Vila Planinka
Description: Although it takes a while to get to this restaurant, following the magical Jezersko valley to a setting just a few kilometres from the Austrian border, once you’ve reached your destination you realise that the journey was well worth it! Surrounded by splendid mountain peaks, this boutique Alpine hotel and its excellent gourmet restaurant of the same name provide a warm, welcoming haven for guests. The chefs here create elegant, refined dishes that showcase the best Slovenian ingredients, paying careful attention to local recipes. Specialities include bear prosciutto served with bread crackers, hazelnut cream and pear, and smoked trout with camomile-flavoured frothed milk, carrot reduction and pickled celery. The menu always features a few vegetarian options, such as fried celeriac with pinenut butter, poached egg and hollandaise sauce.

Name: Gostilna Francl
Description: Situated at the entrance to a tranquil valley, this restaurant dating back centuries now has young new managers at the helm with a focus on cuisine that has its roots in local traditions yet with a slightly modern twist. The portions are decidedly generous, with real attention paid to presentation and colour as well as substance and quality. Meat takes centre stage here, although fish dishes also feature on the menu. In summer, dine outdoors under the trees or the delightful pergola.

Name: Hiša Torkla
Description: The view of the surrounding hills is one of the main attractions of this restaurant, along with the traditional open grill in the dining room. Although grilled meat dishes (Tomahawk and picanha steak, chops, fillets etc) naturally take centre stage, the menu also features first courses such as fuzi (a type of Istrian pasta) with various sauces, as well as some good raw fish options. An excellent setting in which to enjoy gourmet dining surrounded by unspoilt natural scenery.

Name: Breg
Description: Overlooking Ljubljana’s riverfront, this restaurant boasts one of the most famous and picturesque views of the city from its terrace in the summer months, while in the winter the historic building’s indoor dining rooms are equally attractive. The cuisine brings a breath of international creativity to the city, with influences from Italy, France and the Middle East in its dishes. A perfect example is the hummus served with lamb ragu, pita bread, pesto and pine nuts – a real culinary voyage around the Mediterranean!

Name: Vila Podvin
Description: Nestled in the countryside around Radovljica, Vila Podvin is both a restaurant and a hotel. The beautiful garden is one of its attractions, along with its fresh, strongly flavoured cuisine which showcases local, seasonal ingredients from the Upper Carniola, a region influenced by Italian, Slavic and Germanic traditions – good examples are the open ravioli with Kosec cheese and sweet chestnuts, and the turbot with mussels and apples. The dining room is classic in style, plus there’s a niche with a few tables which is perfect for a romantic dinner. A good selection of Slovenian and international wines, including some excellent vintages, completes the picture.

Name: Restavracija CUBO
Description: Situated on the edge of the city in a district little visited by tourists, this modern restaurant dominated by a dark colour scheme serves Mediterranean-influenced yet eclectic cuisine with the occasional international flavour. The maize-crusted tuna fillet with fine vegetables and avocado is cooked to perfection – the tuna is pink and succulent and a green curry sauce adds an extra touch of character to the dish. An extensive wine list (with wines also available by the glass) adds to the appeal.

Name: Georgie Bistro
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the heart of the historic centre, this relaxed, informal restaurant serves beautifully prepared contemporary-style dishes. Although there’s a focus on Slovenian ingredients here, the chef’s imagination is also inspired by influences from outside the country. Choose between an à la carte and tasting menus of varying lengths (three to nine courses). The pairing options include organic wines, as well as craft beers and home-made syrups. Popular for work lunches, and so very busy at lunchtime.

Name: Galerija okusov
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This excellent restaurant, whose name translates as a “gallery of flavours”, boasts an attractive setting surrounded by a park with an 18C Baroque palace (formerly Novo Celje castle) at its centre. The welcoming dining room is decidedly more contemporary in style than its surroundings, as is the cuisine served here, which is prepared from local ingredients using imaginative techniques and presented on a single tasting menu (usually 10 courses) from which guests can choose individual dishes as they please. Careful attention is paid to reducing food waste: the trout served with asparagus is also accompanied by chips made from fish skin, while the jus uses butter and other leftovers. Most of the wines on the impressive wine list are also available by the glass.

Name: Restavracija Shambala
Description: A “hidden oasis of peace, tranquillity and joy” right in the centre of Ljubljana, just a stone’s throw from the city’s bustling riverside promenade, Shambala serves Asian cuisine amid an Asian-influenced decor that is attractive without being overly decorative. The dishes on the menu (meat, fish and seafood, and vegetarian) are inspired by countries all over Asia, from Japan to Thailand and Vietnam. The desserts feature more European options such as panna cotta, which is served with a mango and date sauce that gives it a more exotic flavour.

Name: Protėviai
Description: The name Protėviai translates as ‘ancestor’ and their tagline is “The legend of fire and steaks, inspired by the ancestors of the world”. As you may have guessed, this restaurant is all about the primeval method of cooking steaks over fire and smoke. The striking interior takes in huge wooden sculptures and a fire-effect central counter hewn out of a huge piece of wood. The steaks – some dry-aged for 60 days – are a mix of Lithuanian, USDA Prime rib-eye, Koji tenderloin and Wagyu from Japan and Australia, and are served by weight, cooked over glowing embers and rested with care.

Name: Augustin
Description: Sister to Momo Grill and monai, this informal restaurant has a sleek modern style. Parquet floors sit below two striking circular faux-candle chandeliers hanging from a concrete ceiling, while shelves of wine fill vintage sideboards. Punchy, colourful dishes blend Mediterranean and Middle Eastern flavours and are offered in two different formats. The majority of the menu comprises modern plant-led small plates – three per person plus a dessert is about right – but there are also three main courses on offer which are based around fish or meat. Service is warm and friendly, and the courtyard terrace is a real boon in warmer months.

Name: HeJi
Description: Having been five years in the making, this impressively opulent restaurant seems like it might be more at home in Dubai or Macau than Vilnius! The cavernous glass-roofed main dining room is overlooked by two ‘caged’ balconies and a champagne bar – and there’s an intimate, dimly lit cocktail bar serving innovative Asian creations. A wood-framed open kitchen takes centre stage, and captivating and intriguing design details abound. The original menu fuses East and West, with the dim sum a hit and the signature beef dishes cooked over charcoal a real highlight. The wine list features some fine growers and the whole place makes for a glamorous night out.

Name: Apvalaus Stalo Klubo
Description: On the shores of Lake Galve, in the heart of a national park, you’ll find this intimate, modern restaurant, which affords incredible views over the water to the 14th Century Trakai Island Castle from its floor-to-ceiling windows. When the sun's shining, the lovely terrace is the place to be. Complex modern cooking is a reflection of the locale, exemplified by the likes of beetroot with goat’s cheese and flavour-packed lamb cutlets. Desserts are a highlight, with the ‘raspberries with raspberries’ always a surefire winner. Cheery service brings a smile to everyone’s face, and cosy bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: DIA
Description: You’ll be surprised how busy this formally laid restaurant in a residential spot can get, but the experienced team cope well with the numbers – among which there are many returning guests. It sits within a tardis-like building, which also houses meeting rooms, and is smartly decked out with fine glassware and crockery. The menu is one of the most eclectic around and offers everything from a burger to fine steaks, with the popular daily specials including the likes of freshly caught fish. There really is something for everyone here.

Name: elven
Description: Sister to Nüman in Kaunas, the name of this restaurant means ‘river’ in Norwegian, with the language being a clue both to the design of the room and the style of the food here. The traditional creamwashed façade of the heritage building is certainly in complete contrast to the sleek interior, which is an elegant space with a design-led style. The menu delivers a good range of creative, pared-back dishes with bold flavours, a blend of textures and eye-catching presentation, with sharing dishes for two also a feature. In summer, head for the rear terrace.

Name: Gastronomika
Description: Head through the leafy inner courtyard and down the stairs and you’ll find yourself in this chic, elegant restaurant with full-length windows. Sculptures and unique design touches catch the eye, before the kitchen finally steals your full attention. French cuisine leads the way, but you’ll also find international influences – with everything presented in a creative, modern manner. Dishes such A5 Wagyu with green curry, enoki mushrooms and eggplant impress with their precise craftsmanship and rich, powerful tastes. Champagne features highly on the wine list and there are also ‘Prestige’ and ‘Big Bottle’ sections for those celebrating.

Name: Arrivée
Description: This special occasion restaurant sits in the heart of the city, in a unique setting in a 17th Century former Dominican monastery. Modern art decorates the garden, and a good-sized terrace really comes into its own in the summer months, while inside it’s intimate and relaxed, with lovely original fittings and just nine tables. The cooking is unashamedly French, with modern overtones and flavour to the fore. Desserts are a highlight, and at weekends they sell homemade bread and delicious croissants. The evening lasts for around 4 hours, so settle in and make the most of the experience.

Name: Stikliai
Description: For a comfortingly classical experience in the city, head to Stikliai, set within a hotel in the heart of the Old Town. Here, photos of famous faces who have visited over the years line the walls – including celebrities and Heads of State – and the glass-roofed room filled with greenery has an elegant feel. Matching the atmosphere, the food has a classical French base, with the sauces in particular being a strength. You might find lamb shoulder confit with bulgur wheat, tomato concasse and aubergine caviar or haddock fillet served with sweet potatoes, fennel, pak choi and beurre blanc.

Name: Stebuklai
Description: Set in a hotel beside the Cathedral Square, you can expect an idyllic ambience here, complete with twinkling water fountains. When the weather’s good, the terrace is the place to be, as it faces the Square and the Cathedral, but the restaurant itself is also a beautiful place with a chic, modern ambience. The ambitious kitchen produce cosmopolitan dishes such as hamachi ceviche with strawberries, hibiscus, avocado and shiso or duck breast with carrot gratin, cherries, pickled onions and Pedro Ximenez sauce, which all arrive in attractive arrangements.

Name: Ertlio Namas
Description: Set over three floors of a historic townhouse in the city centre, this is a charming restaurant with wonderful wooden floors, fine period art on the walls and a historical menu to match. Choose either a 4 or 6 course set menu to experience interesting dishes from a bygone era – dating as far back as the 16th Century – which could include sorrel soup, salted and cured veal pekenfleišas or beef tart with beef broth sauce. Following each dish comes an explanation of its origins, providing sustenance for your brain as well as your body.

Name: Red Brick
Address: Farmers Circle, Žirgyno Gatvė 1, Radiškis, 20364, Lithuania
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: The Farmers Circle is a wonderfully remote 1,730 acre working farm situated an hour’s drive outside the capital. At its centre sits this beautifully restored period barn, now home to the Red Brick restaurant. Naturally, the majority of the produce comes from their farm, with the rest sourced nearby. Chef Arnór’s tasting menu is modern and hyper-seasonal, fully embracing the sustainable approach; you’ll find elegant snacks followed by the likes of skrei with chicken sauce, then maybe mint, sea buckthorn and carrots – all of which will tantalise your tastebuds. The dishes are explained by the genial team and there are cosy bedrooms for a complete overnight experience.

Name: Farmer & The Ocean
Description: Located in a busy spot amongst many other eateries, it’s worth seeking out this basement restaurant.
