The cooking is classical with a southern French influence, so expect to find the likes of salade Niçoise and ratatouille on the menu. The chefs prepare their good quality ingredients with care, resulting in authentic and flavoursome dishes.

Name: Eero
Description: Perched on the top floor of the former American Embassy and named after its architect Eero Saarinen, this restaurant and cocktail bar features a wrap-around terrace with views of the Oslofjord on one side and The Royal Palace gardens on the other. A wood-fired oven is at the heart of the cooking, which is fish-centric and takes a ‘fin to gill’ approach. So you might get cod tongue as a snack, then later its belly on the bone, enhanced by the richness of its liver and roe. Everyone is served at once from a tasting menu, and some of the dishes are presented ‘family style’.

Name: Black Milk Gastro Bar
Description: A younger sibling of Aloë, this intimate restaurant offers more great cooking with a fun and lively night out thrown into the bargain. Influenced by South America, Asia and Europe, the creative dishes deliver vibrant flavours and well-judged spicing, whilst using plenty of modern techniques. Expect to see some luxury ingredients, like Oscietra caviar and Périgord truffles, alongside an enjoyable dose of theatricality.

Name: Ego
Description: Simplicity runs through the team’s ethos at this relaxed neighbourhood spot, from the minimalist Nordic décor to the straightforward cooking that eschews overcomplication. On the ground floor you’ll find the brighter of the two dining rooms, which also has plants dotted around, whilst the cellar offers moodier lighting and exposed brickwork. There are Finnish elements to the menu, along with some seasonal French ingredients and classic dishes like steak tartare.

Name: Västergatan
Description: An unpretentious modern bistro on a city centre street; owned and run by a young couple (he cooks, while she looks after the service). The regularly changing set menu offers fresh seasonal dishes with a classic Swedish heart. Vegetarians are well looked after and juice and wine flights are available.

Name: Symbios
Description: There’s a wonderfully unpretentious feel to this relaxed, friendly restaurant perfectly suited to the trendy suburb of Södermalm. Watch the world go by as you relax with an aperitif on the pavement terrace, before enjoying classic Swedish and southern European dishes that are simple, fresh and full of flavour. The midweek lunch menu represents great value for money, and the place is informally yet professionally run by a friendly team.

Name: Frank
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at this relaxed, contemporary restaurant, with its soft lighting, flickering candles, comfy sofas and designer wooden furnishings. Choose between an à la carte and a tasting menu – both of which offer flavour-packed, original and understated modern dishes.

Name: Sushi Anaba
Description: A Japanese staple through a Nordic lens is what you can expect at this compact quayside sushi restaurant that seats just eight diners round its counter. The Danish Chef-Owner trained in Tokyo and brings a passionate approach to the cooking, which is underpinned by superb produce from Nordic waters, be it Norwegian scallop or lobster from Jutland. An excellent sake selection highlights some lesser-known choices.

Name: Brasserie Hansken
Description: A delightfully traditional brasserie, centrally located by the City Hall, with various charming dining areas and a fantastic terrace. Classical cooking follows the seasons and mixes French and Scandic influences; seafood is a speciality.

Name: Theo
Description: Located in the heart of Copenhagen, this is the sort of restaurant we’d all love to have in our neighbourhood. The team here have dedicated themselves to serving uncomplicated, appealing dishes that offer good value for money. Charming service and an unpretentious approach to both the décor and food strengthens their mission, as does the simple yet consistently high quality cooking.

Name: BORD
Description: You’re guaranteed a warm welcome at this sweetly run bohemian bistro. A communal table is at the heart of things, with a few smaller tables and counter seats available too. Starters merge into mains on the Mediterranean-inspired daily menu of unfussy, pared-back dishes. Skilful cooking keeps the focus on the top quality ingredients; don't miss the turbot from the wood-fired oven if you get the chance.

Name: BELLIES
Description: Vegetable lovers will find paradise at this plant-powered restaurant that celebrates fabulous, yet often overlooked, ingredients. Whether it's beetroot, pumpkin or Jerusalem artichoke, quality vegetables are given a starring role that they are rarely afforded. A range of Asian elements, from Sichuan pepper to ssamjang, are used to embellish the natural flavours of the produce, as are fermented and preserved components made in-house. There’s a lovely atmosphere and all dishes are served with a smile.

Name: Boulevard
Description: The welcome is warm, the room elegant, and the food heartening and eminently satisfying. The passion and experience of the two chef-owners is evident in all areas of this likeable restaurant. The quality of the fish and shellfish really comes through, thanks to the classic techniques used by the kitchen.

Name: Bulot
Description: There’s a real buzz about this neighbourhood wine-bar-cum-bistro, which makes it so appealing as soon as you set foot through the door. The personable team keep things relaxed as they serve a seasonal tasting menu which comes with a subtle French slant and plenty of seafood – the restaurant’s name is French for whelk, so expect to find one somewhere on the menu. The simple, well-cooked dishes are also available from the à la carte as small plates.

Name: freyja.
Description: Head straight for the roof terrace to kick off your visit with a cocktail and 360° views of Stockholm and, once inside, opt for a seat by the curved window to capitalise on the 13th floor location. The menu includes modernised yet comforting Swedish classics like Kroppkaka, executed with care and confidence, yielding well-balanced flavours. This is a place where you'll feel equally at home dining in a couple or as a group, as it delivers something for everyone.

Name: Oxenstiernan
Description: You can’t miss this stylish, orange-painted bistro which stands out against the greenery of a city park; in summer, dine on the terrace, under the trees. A sustainable ethos runs throughout, from the interior design to the ethically sourced produce used in the unfussy, boldly flavoured Swedish dishes.

Name: Pull
Description: Within the rejuvenated, pre-war industrial area of the ‘Rotermann Factories’ sits an impressive 19C grain elevator and, inside that, this fittingly rustic restaurant with exposed stone walls and concrete pillars. Generously proportioned Estonian dishes focus on meats and charcoal-grilled steaks.

Name: Wicca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Angelica Udeküll is not only a TV chef but a torchbearer for Estonian food. Her elegant restaurant at the LaSpa hotel sits in a beautifully tranquil spot overlooking the pine trees and the sea – and is the perfect location to showcase her ethical cooking. Dishes are creative, with some Nordic touches.

Name: Hõlm
Description: The restaurant is named ‘Hõlm’ and the hotel within which it sits, ‘Lydia’ – after Lydia Grünmann Hõlm, on whose recipes the dishes here are based. Full-length windows flood the elegant dining room with light and the attractively presented dishes exhibit appealing combinations of both texture and flavour.

Name: Art Priori
Description: Set in the heart of the Old Town, this is a wonderfully elegant, romantic spot, where two striking rooms ooze period charm and an eclectic mix of artwork fills the walls. In contrast, the food is modern and understated. Well-formed dishes give each core ingredient the space to shine, with unadulterated flavours fitting together seamlessly. You might find earthy yellow beetroot paired with soft goat’s cheese or wonderfully mature venison with a silky celeriac purée. Friendly service and a great choice of cocktails and wines by the glass finishes things off perfectly.

This pop-up turned permanent is sister to Mere 38 in Võsu. It exudes a cool, fashionable vibe, courtesy of a modern interior with striking murals which contrast with its historic exterior and quaint Old Town setting. Well-judged, creative dishes have subtle Asian influences and are attractively presented.

Name: Tchaikovsky
Description: Set within the well-known Hotel Telegraaf, in the heart of the Old Town, this glass-roofed, restaurant has something of a celebratory feel, courtesy of a beautiful chandelier and battleship-grey walls hung with gilt-framed pictures. Cooking has a classical French base with Russian influences and modern overtones.

Name: Lee
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A ‘Lee’ is the ancient communal fireplace around which families would sit together to prepare a meal – and this powder blue restaurant with ornate columns and a charming courtyard setting certainly has a historic feel. The cooking ranges in style from the traditional to the modern, with the chef’s background showing through in dishes with distinct Asian influences, like Liivimaa dry-aged beef short rib with cauliflower cream and wasabi or cherry mille-feuille with green tea and tofu cream.

Name: Rado
Description: It might be located in the delightfully historic Old Town but Rado is contrastingly smart and modern. It has a buzzy vibe on the ground floor and a more intimate feel in the basement. The chatty team will guide you through the menu of seasonal modern dishes; don’t miss the venison carpaccio.

Name: Fotografiska
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Above the Fotografiska photo gallery sits an equally striking restaurant offering picture-perfect views out across the Old Town; be sure to start or end your night with cocktails in the rooftop bar. A concept of ‘Sustainable Pleasure’ leads the way here, with a ‘leaf to root, nose to tail’ ethos and a zero-waste approach. Organic, sustainably farmed ingredients are showcased in a highly original selection of assured, understated dishes which reflect the chef’s French and Swedish training; go for the daily changing 360° surprise menu and the interesting wine pairings.

Name: Joyce
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A modern shopping centre in the heart of the city plays host to this large, split-level brasserie with bold décor, a popular cocktail bar and a buzzy vibe. Attractively presented dishes mix local and Baltic influences: the kitchen adds creative twists and flavours pack a punch.

Name: ÂME
Description: Housed within a small boutique hotel on the edge of the Old Town is this elegant restaurant where the old and the new combine: part of the Medieval city wall runs down one side of the room, yet it also has a contemporary, design-led style. Âme is French for ‘soul’ and, while the appealingly understated dishes certainly have a French heart, flavours are also drawn from around the globe and, as such, are described as ‘dishes that feed the soul’. Opt for one of the two tasting menus to sample a range of these dishes, such as goose breast à l'orange or roasted cauliflower à la Marrakech.

Name: Gianni
Description: Pop into the café for coffee and cake, or dine in a more cossetted environment in the modern restaurant. The charming team are eager to please and will even skilfully fillet your fish at the table for you. The comprehensive menu offers all the Italian dishes you know and love; the saltimbocca is a highlight.

Name: RADIO
Description: Part wine shop, part café-cum-bistro, this neighbourhood establishment is all things to all people. You enter via a shop packed full of interesting wines, before heading through the restaurant where a glass wine cave takes centre stage. The room has a bistro feel – there are even a few sofas available for those who like it super laid-back – and dishes come in the form of medium-sized plates that are designed for sharing. From sausage soup to cured trout or onion pie, each dish comes with the perfect wine recommendation.

Name: Kolm Sõsarat
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Three Sisters run this small, remotely set restaurant and each has their role to play: Kerti does the cooking, Triin looks after the service and Kadri tends to the kitchen garden. The playful set menu is a showcase of the area, featuring top quality produce from their garden and farm – such as in the country-style mushroom, potato and sauerkraut – while superb honey from their father’s long-established hives is celebrated in desserts such as honey, apple and milk with sea buckthorn. This is a truly special place where the passion of the team is palpable, as they go above and beyond to care for every guest.

Name: Lahepere Villa
Description: Built by the owner himself, this homely restaurant sits in a wooded spot behind the beach. Inside are chunky wood tables and cushion-strewn sofas; outside, a blazing firepit, fleece-covered chairs and a ‘Big Green Egg’. The fortnightly set menu is inspired by the area and warm service is from a family team.

Name: Alexander
Address: Pädaste Manor, Muhu Island, Pädaste, 94716, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Valet parking
Description: A visit to Alexander starts with a ferry ride from the mainland to Muhu Island. Named after the last noble owner of the beautiful Pädaste Manor – within which it sits – this elegant restaurant welcomes you in with its tranquil atmosphere and sweeping parkland views. Foraged and seasonal island produce guides the ambitious new Nordic cooking. Choose between the 4 course daily menu or the 7 course Degustation menu; the latter must be booked 24hrs in advance.

Name: SOO
Description: Visionary owner Ragnar Sass purchased the Maidla Estate and manor house back in 2019, then added some rather smart eco-lodges in the woods and wetlands – as well as this intimate 5-table restaurant. Sustainability and ecological considerations are key, and the set dinner menu looks to the seasons and the region for its inspiration. Dishes are rich in flavour but come with a welcome lightness, and foraging, pickling and preserving all play their part. Wines are organic and natural.

Name: Horisont
Description: Arrive early for an aperitif in the bar, which affords stunning panoramic views towards the harbour from the 30th floor of the smart Swissotel Tallinn hotel. There’s a formal feel to the room, with modern European menus to match; to see the full talents of the kitchen, go for the tasting menu.

Name: Mon Repos
Description: This former imperial summer residence comes with a charming interior which blends original stained glass windows and panelled ceilings with sleek, modern furnishings. The modern menu reflects the locale and extends across to the Mediterranean, with colourfully presented dishes exhibiting flavours and textures which have been well thought through. The gravlax with beets, horseradish and blinis is a must to start, and to finish the tiramisu is a winner. The lovely terrace looking out over Kadriorg Park is a popular spot.

Name: Nok Nok
Description: Nok means ‘bird’ in Thai, which makes sense when you spot the two stone owls set into the stonework. With its central location and two spacious, colourfully decorated dining rooms, this is a popular place to eat both amongst locals and visitors. Authentic Thai flavours are sure to warm you up on colder days and you’ll find all your Thai favourites, from a wonderful chicken satay with sweet and sour pickles to rich curries, such as a Massaman made using braised short ribs. Be sure to save room for dessert though, as the sticky rice with mango is superb.

Name: Moon
Description: The word ‘Moon’ refers to the poppy seed, which is an apt name, as it’s hard not to eat too much of the delicious poppy seed bread here! Split into three rooms, this intimate bistro comes with bright décor, a lovely teacup chandelier and a seasonally changing menu comprising flavoursome Slavic dishes. The sweet team greet both locals and visitors as if they are regulars.

Name: R14
Description: The impressive 19C stone-built powerplant of the Rotermann factories is now a wine-shop-cum-wine-bar with a rustic, laid-back vibe, where a glass-walled wine cellar takes centre stage. Good value, unfussy Mediterranean dishes have a leaning towards Italy; come on a Sunday if you’re a fan of brunch.

Name: Barbarea
Description: A former rubber boot factory in an up-and-coming area plays host to this city hotspot, which starts the day as a bakery and then morphs into a stylish, laid-back bistro in the evening. Vibrant sharing plates follow the seasons and are packed full of flavour, with the pizzas cooked over a wood fire. The wine list comprises a good selection of natural, organic and biodynamic wines.

Name: Puri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the marina development northwest of the city centre is this striking modernist building with an equally impressive split-level interior boasting floor-to-ceiling windows and contemporary blonde wood furnishings. Creative modern cooking sees seafood dishes taking the starring role; maybe start with a wine ‘baba’ topped with succulent langoustines before moving on to gratinated crab with creamy risotto. To accompany are a great selection of wines by the glass, with everything brought to the table by a cheery team.

Name: Rado
Description: Sister to the restaurant of the same name in Tallinn – and also with their signature bicycle parked outside – is this bright, modern bistro run by a sweet, friendly team. The small menu is chalked up on the blackboard and the fresh, unfussy cooking represents great value. In summer, head for the terrace at the back.

Name: Mere 38
Description: Set in a quiet village, this green-painted wooden house boasts both a fashionable New England style restaurant and smart apartments. It has a cosy dining room with fleece-covered chairs, as well as a lovely summer terrace. Dishes are largely Mediterranean influenced and are vibrant and full of flavour.

Name: Paju Villa
Description: The suburb of Nõmme is home to this elegant art nouveau villa named after Karoline Paju, who built the house in 1931. Dining takes place over two floors, with several small, interconnecting rooms creating a stylish, intimate space. Instead of being listed as Starters, Mains and Desserts, the appealing dishes are listed under the tempting-sounding headings of 'Can’t Resist', 'For a Real Gourmand' and 'Cherry on Top'; modern twists bring an extra element to classically based recipes.

Name: Casa Rios
Description: Chef Rodrigo Aguiar, originally from Rio de Janeiro, combined his skills with owner Giovanna Perrone to realise her dream here. This charming restaurant features an open kitchen where guests can view the wood oven and churrasco grill, both of which exude the smoky flavours for which Casa Rios is famous. If you sit at the bar counter, you can watch the preparation process in full flow as well as appreciate the aromas emanating from the kitchen. The cuisine here is based around typical Brazilian cooking with a focus on the south-east of the country, using ingredients from small-scale producers and a constant nod to seasonality. Whether you opt for the tasting menu or à la carte, make sure you try the wood oven-baked pizzeta of merguez sausage made with cornbread – an absolute must!

Name: Borgo Mooca
Address: Rua Barão De Tatuí, 302, São Paulo, 01226-030, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Valet parking
Description: Fried gnocchi, egg pasta, langoustine, octopus and black rice with squid ink are just some of the dishes and ingredients you’ll find here, a list enhanced by the slow-fermented and Maraschino cherry babá with a smooth crème anglaise. This gastronomic refuge is located in the Santa Cecília district and features a modern-retro style and uncluttered atmosphere. It includes a bar counter overlooking the kitchen, decoration that is teeming with details on the walls and ceiling, plus a basement bar called Bargo offering an array of superb cocktails. Chef Matheus Zanchini conjures up creative cuisine with Italian nuances, including homemade pasta, all of which is prepared with top-quality ingredients. The menu is updated weekly in line with the availability of ingredients sourced by the chef.

Name: Bicol Korean Cuisine
Address: Rua José Getúlio 422, São Paulo, 01509-000, Brazil
Description: Bicol is a must if you’re keen to try Korean barbecue-style cuisine. This classic address in the Liberdade district of the city has been run by a South Korean family for three generations. In this spacious restaurant, the tables have their own grills so that guests can cook meat (usually cut super-fine) to their individual taste. Dishes for sharing are the mainstay here, including the Burgogui, Garbi and Samguiopsar combos, always accompanied by Banchan (small side dishes of the day). The Bibimbap (a typical rice dish) and the soups are other interesting options on the menu, not forgetting the delicious kimchi, of course. Why not pair your food with the traditional soju, a typical Korean beverage with differing strengths of alcohol?

Name: Corrientes 348 - Marina da Glória
Address: Avenida Infante Dom Henrique, Rio de Janeiro, 20021-140, Brazil
Description: The name of this restaurant is a reference to the famous Argentinian tango “A Media Luz”, while the number 348 corresponds to the number of the street where the first of the brand’s ventures opened in Greater São Paulo. It overlooks the Marina da Glória, hence the spectacular views from tables on the terrace, and features several spacious dining rooms and an extensive glass-fronted wine cellar. The culinary focus is of course on Argentina and choice cuts of meats cooked on the grill, including specialities such as ribeye, centre cut ribeye, filet mignon with garlic, chorizo sausage and top sirloin, all accompanied by sides designed for sharing. To finish, the “dulce de leche” pancake served with sorbet is an authentic Argentinian dessert that is truly irresistible.

Name: Mäska
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 159, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: It's worth braving the frenetic traffic along Ipanema’s narrow streets to eat at this modern but relaxed restaurant with a contemporary bistro feel and a kitchen that opens on to the dining room in which you can savour chef Danilo Parah’s “innovative and emotional” cuisine. Here, the chef showcases Asian ingredients in contemporary dishes that are generous, colourful and pleasing on the palate. The impressively varied menu is complemented by dishes inspired by ingredients available in the market, such as the highly popular spaghetti with beurre blanc and braised prawns. The dining experience and atmosphere are enhanced by Mäska’s array of refreshing cocktails.

Name: NOTIÊ
Description: Although only recently opened, this restaurant is already being talked about by the city’s foodie community. Located on the sixth floor of the Shopping Light building, its design comes as a pleasant surprise as soon as you walk through the door thanks to its decor of yellow tones, glass-fronted kitchen enabling guests to watch the chefs hard at work and, first and foremost, the 18m panel on the ceiling depicting images of nature. At the helm in the kitchen is Paraíba-born chef Onildo Rocha who impresses with his use of typical Brazilian ingredients and combinations that result in intense and striking dishes. His recipes are based around his journeys to different Brazilian regions every season, and are showcased on 4-, 7- and 11-course tasting menus. The name of the restaurant is a fusion between one of the country’s most colourful birds, the tanager (tiê in Portuguese) and the Portuguese word for night (noite).

Name: Tiara
Address: Rua Ataulfo De Paiva, 270 loja 111, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-900, Brazil
Description: The name Tiara refers to the district (Itacoatiara) in which chef Rafa Gomes was born. Nowadays, he owns two restaurants called Itacoa and, to complete the full name, Tiara. This famous chef is known for his appearance on reality cooking shows and his impressive career thus far, including stints in leading restaurants in New York. Housed in the Rio Design Leblon complex, the restaurant boasts an elegant backdrop of soothing tones for innovative cuisine that relies on modern techniques and the use of seasonal ingredients where possible. Here, the chef elevates duck meat (a key ingredient in his story) to another level. An example of this is the aged duck lacquered with honey and spices served with pumpkin, miso and a “gastrique” sauce – a quite surreal combination!

Name: Chez Claude São Paulo
Address: Rua Professor Tamandaré Toledo 25, São Paulo, 04532-020, Brazil
Description: Part of the Le Quartier food complex, this space is divided between the Chez Claude restaurant, the Bar du Quartier and the refined Bistrot du Quartier. At the helm, famous chef Claude Troisgros follow the same concept as in Rio de Janeiro. The kitchen, which is completely open in the middle of the room, enables guests to really feel and be part of the lively and vibrant ambience here. The menu is based around French techniques and influences from Brazil and elsewhere in Latin America, resulting in colourful recipes full of flavour and texture. Standout dishes include the superb combination of scallops served with caviar, chuchu and Jataí honey; the duck magret accompanied by pear in wine and blueberry; and for dessert the light and creamy “doce de leite” cheesecake with a Canastra cheese sauce.

Name: Naga
Address: Rua Bandeira Paulista 385, São Paulo, 04532-011, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: A legendary Japanese restaurant in the city that has for a long time been a favourite address for aficionados of the country’s cuisine. It’s no surprise that the Nagayama group does not just have a single restaurant – in fact, in this area they own almost an entire block that includes the Bar do Naga, the Café do Naga etc. It is split between two floors, with access to the floor above via an attractive steep staircase. In the latter you’ll find two rooms: a waiting area with just a few tables, and a second more spacious room with a direct view of the pleasantly and subtly illuminated sushi bar. The extensive menu features a wide array of carpaccios, sushi, sashimi, uramaki, temaki, tartares and teppanyaki, and if there are several of you, you may want to try combination options such as the popular Naga Case 2 or the enticing Omakase-style tasting menu.

Name: Kosushi
Description: The name of the restaurant has a direct link with Japanese philosophy as the word “ko” (which translates as “turtle”) is associated with long life and the symbolism of the number 1. Opened in 1988 by chef George Yuji Koshoji, it is now located at a different address (in the Itaim Bibi district), where it has become a popular meeting place for locals. It boasts a welcoming, contemporary ambience, soft lighting and a decor of bright colours, plus an impressive large balcony from where guests can watch their dishes being prepared. The extensive menu offers a variety of options such as gyosas, tartares, ussuzukuri, uramaki, sushi and sashimi, as well as hot dishes that include yakisoba, octopus yaki and Wagyu medallions. It also features a superb selection of sakis and innovative cocktails.

Name: Loup
Address: Dr. Mário Ferraz 528, São Paulo, 01453-011, Brazil
Description: Loup’s unique decor and atmosphere, featuring several dining spaces, designer details, lofty glass ceilings and an impressive vertical garden, have been very carefully curated, and provide the backdrop for an enticing fusion of cuisine from different parts of the world, prepared with top-quality ingredients and enhanced by a Raw Bar section serving an array of tartares, carpaccios, ceviches etc. If you prefer to be seated at a more traditional table, the menu includes delicious mini palm heart pastries with prawns, appetising dishes such as arroz de pato (rice with duck) that take you back to Portugal, and for dessert, the irresistible cannoli with a light yet crunchy dulce de leche and red berries, which transports you to the shores of Italy. It’s also worth taking time out to enjoy a cocktail in the lounge.

Name: Charco
Address: Rua Peixoto Gomide 1492, São Paulo, 01409-002, Brazil
Description: In this restaurant inspired by the typical cuisine of the Rio Grande do Sul region, chef Tuca Mezzomo leads his team alongside Nathalia Gonçalves – masters in the art of preparing grilled and flame-cooked dishes with a continual focus on the best and freshest ingredients. Dishes that you won’t want to miss include the toasted mushrooms with smoked pumpkin and parmesan, and the succulent grilled Wagyu short rib, served with a wild tomato salad and a Bordelaise sauce. In addition, the restaurant also produces its own delicious sausages, butter and fresh goat’s cheese. The backdrop to the dining experience is a rustic, welcoming mix of exposed brickwork, wooden tables and subdued lighting that adds to the pleasant ambience.

Name: Pobre Juan
Address: Rua Comendador Miguel Calfat 525, São Paulo, 04537-082, Brazil
Description: The first Pobre Juan outlet opened in the Vila Olímpia in 2004 and nowadays you’ll find the brand all across the country. Inspired by traditional Argentinian steakhouses, Pobre Juan serves top-quality grilled meats in an informal and rustic setting. Each of its restaurants features a wide array of carefully selected meats, a process that extends from their provenance to the maturing process. Whether you order classic options such as short ribs, ribeye or flank, or the more exclusive centre cut ribeye, porterhouse or Wagyu, every dish here is perfectly cooked. If you’re eating out with friends, you may want to order the Gran Tabla, which serves three people and comes with delicious sides. Fish, seafood and chicken, all cooked on the open grill, are also available, as well as sublime desserts such as the exquisite churros with dulce de leche.

Name: Cepa
Address: Praça Dos Omaguás, 110, São Paulo, 05419-020, Brazil
Description: Cepa is one of those restaurants that always features in food-related conversations in the city, and now it has a new home in the Pinheiros neighborhood! Here, chef Lucas Dante presents creative, seasonal cuisine that prioritises the freshness of ingredients and champions small-scale producers. By his side is sommelier and front-of-house manager Gabrielli Fleming, who is in charge of sourcing biodynamic and organic wines for the cellar that are always the perfect pairing for your choice of dish. We can highly recommend the simply incredible starter of Wagyu tongue with chicken broth, okra and mint.

Name: Lilia
Address: Rua do Senado 45, Rio de Janeiro, 20231-005, Brazil
Description: This unique restaurant, with an unremarkable façade that could easily pass unnoticed among the historic colonial-style houses in the Lapa district, is located just a few metres from the conical São Sebastião cathedral. As you walk up a long, narrow staircase, you come to this two-storey restaurant featuring brick walls and corrugated iron panelling which endow it with a spacious, uncluttered and industrial feel. Here, chef Lucio Vieira heads up a kitchen characterised by its creativity, where the cuisine is updated daily in line with the availability of ingredients. A three-course set menu is available at lunchtime, while at dinner you can choose between options on the à la carte or an eleven-course tasting menu. And make sure you save space for the “queijo de coalho” cheesecake, which it is an absolute must!

Name: Mesa do Lado
Address: Rua Conde Bernadotte 26, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
Description: A recent innovation from the Troisgros Group and one with a completely different concept that ensures a unique dining experience. Here, inside the renowned Chez Claude restaurant in Leblon, chef Claude Troisgros offers a sensory gastronomic experience that aims to awaken all five senses. The small dining room, with seating for just 12 guests per sitting, provides the setting for a tasting menu that evolves in line with lighting effects and the projection of images that varies according to the background music. The contemporary cuisine has a strong French influence and somewhat nostalgic feel thanks to family recipes handed down through the generations. Timings are strict here so you’ll need to arrive and depart at your appointed times!

Name: L'Etoile
Address: Avenida Niemeyer 121, Rio de Janeiro, 22450-220, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: L'Etoile is the perfect option if you’re planning a romantic dinner with breathtaking views. Located on the 26th floor of the imposing Sheraton Grand Rio Hotel & Resort on Leblon Beach, the restaurant boasts a sophisticated and romantic atmosphere and a menu that bears the signature of renowned chef Jean-Paul Bondoux, who reinterprets classic French techniques and combines these with Brazilian ingredients. The kitchen is under the daily charge of Chilean chef Matias Cifuentes, who brings his own Latin touch to dishes, which are available on an à la carte and a seven-course tasting menu. The creative desserts are the domain of pastry chef Elena Yepes, who conjures up delicate dishes with sublime flavours!

Name: Térèze
Address: Rua Felicio dos Santos 15, Rio de Janeiro, 20241-260, Brazil
Description: Térèze is the perfect choice if you’re on the lookout for a quiet setting for a romantic supper. It is part of the Santa Teresa Mgalley hotel, a delightful historic property built in 1850 with a sophisticated atmosphere and breathtaking views. The menu is based around a contemporary theme that uses seasonal ingredients, plus a mix of Brazilian and international recipes. Chefs Jérôme Dardillac and Luanna Malheiros conjure up surprising combinations such as the perfectly grilled octopus with a chickpea purée, ratatouille and a delicious rougail sauce. After lunch or dinner, why not prolong the enjoyment with a drink in the delightful surroundings of the charming bar?

Name: Mr. Lam
Address: Rua Maria Angélica 21, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-201, Brazil
Description: Mr. Lam gained renowned for his culinary prowess in restaurants in New York and London, however he has run this modern, sophisticated eatery on the edge of the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon for almost two decades. In contrast with other gastronomic restaurants these days, the majority of dishes on the menu have been mainstays since it first opened, in so doing keeping with the tradition of offering the best Chinese cuisine. Featuring a hint of cutting-edge innovation as well as a focus on top-quality ingredients, the menu boasts memorable dishes such as the lightly battered and crispy Senhor Batista prawns, with a delicious sweet and sour sauce. The restaurant is laid out on three floors, with an attractive dining room and welcoming bar on the top floor that includes picture windows and a glass roof that provide lots of natural light and stunning views.

Name: Sud, O Pássaro Verde
Address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí 35, Rio de Janeiro, 22460-020, Brazil
Description: Walking into this restaurant is like entering the home of a friend, as you’ll need to knock on the door or announce your presence in order to be let in. Occupying a house in the quiet Jardim Botânico district, this is the domain of chef Roberta Sudbrack who describes it as a space in which to “tell and eat stories”. Inside, the decor is modest yet welcoming, with an impressive wood-fired oven next to the main dining room, plus a charming open kitchen, from which comforting home-style dishes emerge prepared with ingredients from small-scale local producers. As a result, the menu changes daily in line with market availability and freshness. However, one mainstay that is always on the menu is the superbly textured and irresistibly flavoured chocolate cake (“bolo de chocolate molhadinho”).

Name: Giuseppe Grill Leblon
Address: Avenida Bartolomeu Mitre 370, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-001, Brazil
Description: As the name clearly states, all the dishes (fish and meat) at this restaurant are cooked on the charcoal grill. The menu here includes dry-aged meat options (T-bone, prime rib, bone-in tenderloin etc). Other standout dishes include the Maminha (sirloin trip-tip), the Picanha supra sumo (supra sumo rump cap), the brand’s registered trademark, as well as the slow-cooked Uruguayan lamb shoulder served with its own jus. A number of fish and seafood options are also on display, which vary according to availability on the day. The decor here features exposed stone walls, wooden chairs and leather sofas, all of which combine to add a rustic-elegant touch. Not forgetting the extensive wine cellar in the basement, featuring over 400 labels from different countries.

Name: Fasano
Address: Rua Vitório Fasano 88, São Paulo, 01414-020, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The grand piano at the entrance and the lounge with its high ceiling and skylight take us right back to the New York of the 1940s. A symbol of quality, glamour and fine dining, the Fasano is renowned across Brazil for its classic Italian cuisine, albeit with a modern touch. The menu, designed by chef Luca Gozzani, showcases an extensive array of copious and surprising dishes on which pasta plays a starring role. We can recommend starting with the creamy burrata with Parma ham, followed by a succulent lamb fillet with gnocchi, with a delicious panna cotta as a final flourish – a combination of dishes that will take you on a gastronomic adventure back to Italy. The exceptional service from the front-of-house team makes the experience even more special!

Name: Casa Santo Antônio
Address: Avenida João Carlos da Silva Borges 764, São Paulo, 04726-001, Brazil
Description: This extraordinary partnership is the result of a bond of friendship, the fruits of which are clearly visible in this superb gastronomic restaurant. Located somewhat off the beaten track in the southern section of São Paulo, it occupies a property built in the 1960s. It features a charming and elegant space with various dining rooms, a stunning bar and an outdoor terrace when the weather allows (a section of the glass-fronted kitchen is also visible to guests). The menu showcases an Italian influence with fresh homemade pastas, generous portions and moderate prices. An “executive” menu is also available during the week. Standout dishes here include the authentic and extremely delicious spaghetti alla carbonara, and the classic tiramisu, with its perfect creamy texture.

Name: A Presto Ristorante
Address: Rua Pedroso Alvarenga 677, São Paulo, 04531-011, Brazil
Description: This restaurant has become one of the most sophisticated outposts of Italian cuisine in the district of Itaim Bibi, in so doing winning over the most demanding of palates. Taking its inspiration from the cuisine of the stunning Piedmont region, it serves several versions of its star dish, tajarin pasta (with tomato, summer truffle, rabbit ragu etc), as well as other options such as beer and rosemary risotto and the enticing “cruda all'albese”, consisting of filet mignon sliced into small pieces, and served with truffle and a Grana Padano foam. Enjoy your dining experience at the counter, where you can watch dishes being prepared in front of you, or at one of the small number of tables in the dining room.

Name: Aprazível
Address: Rua Aprazível 62, Rio de Janeiro, 20241-270, Brazil
Description: Aprazível is a must for those who love delicious food inspired by nature. This family-run restaurant, located inside an exuberant tropical garden and furnished in rustic style, boasts a superb view of the city. Here, chef Ana Castilho conjures up typical Brazilian dishes teeming with flavour and created using organic and biodynamic ingredients, yet without neglecting either elegance or delicacy. One of her signature dishes is the free-range “galinhada caipira”, served with a delicious free-range chicken-flavoured rice, plantains, sausage from Minas Gerais, braised cabbage, and a tasty pepper jelly and beans. Enjoy Aprazível’s pleasant atmosphere and charming setting in the company of a relaxing drink!

Name: Aconchego Carioca
Address: Rua Barão de Iguatemi 245, Rio de Janeiro, 20270-060, Brazil
Description: A whole host of traditional dishes such as the rice-based “arroz de rabada”, “baião de dois” (black-eyed peas with rice) and the unmissable Bolinho de feijoada (fried feijoada dumplings) are just some of the dishes served in this restaurant, which has become a popular culinary focal point in the northern part of Rio de Janeiro. Here, well-known chef Kátia Barbosa creates cooking with a focus on typical Brazilian dishes with influences from the north-east of the country, all of which are prepared with meticulous detail and lots of flavour. In this completely relaxed and informal setting, decorated with hammocks hanging from the ceilings, the pleasant garden and friendly staff make you feel very much at home. Make sure you also try the innovative and amazing cocktails!

Name: Aiô
Description: If you’re keen to enjoy a different type of dining experience, make sure you book a table at Aiô, where the menu is based around Taiwanese cooking with an international touch that will take you on a journey to some surprising flavours. Located in the same street as its sister restaurant Mapu, Aiô features a distinctive glass façade, behind which you’ll find a bar by the entrance offering an array of delightful and inventive cocktails. The menu is uncomplicated and does not differentiate between starters and mains, enabling guests to share and order individual tasting menus. Standout options include the pork char siu, consisting of mini pancakes served as tacos, accompanied by a delicious dish of meat, red rice and honey, and featuring an explosion of mouthwatering and stunning flavours.

Name: Chez Claude
Address: Rua Conde de Bernadotte 26, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
Description: Run by the famous French chef Claude Troisgros, this dining space has plenty of detail to pique your interest. Firstly, the completely open kitchen in the centre of the room, enabling diners to watch dishes being prepared at close quarters, which are based around French cuisine with the addition of some Brazilian elements. And secondly, the fact that food is served in bowls for sharing, to add to the sense of home-style cooking. The staff here recommend four dishes for two people including delicacies such as the fillet steak au poivre with a sauce that will make your mouth water, accompanied by cassava puff pastry and broccoli with Grana Padano cheese. To finish your meal, don’t miss the impressively textured melted chocolate Carola cake.

Name: Bottega Bernacca
Description: A small restaurant with a bistro-style ambience where the cuisine and decor are as meticulous as each other, the latter featuring a plethora of wood, impressive wine display cabinets and unusual details such as chairs hanging from the ceiling, a detail that is also found in its sister restaurants. The cooking here is authentic and delicious, and includes pasta cooked al dente in traditional Italian style and served straight from the pan to the table as if you were eating at home. Musts on the menu include the legendary Cipriani carpaccio, prepared with wafer-thin strips of filet mignon, served with a special house sauce and crunchy toast; and the pesto lasagne that is suitable for sharing. For dessert, the classic tiramisù, made with mascarpone, is balanced by the flavour of bitter chocolate.

Name: Maza
Address: Rua Manuel Guedes, 243, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: As well as a highly enjoyable dining experience, Maza boasts a relaxing and welcoming setting, where the combination of wood and soft tones is clearly evident as soon as you walk through the door – a decor embellished by the beautiful cherry tree. The cuisine here is based around classic Japanese fare with a modern and personalised touch, including some Korean dishes. The different types of menus on offer include a seven-course option called Shinrai (served exclusively at table), the Omakase (only available at the bar counter), an à la carte. Exquisite dishes include karasumi, ussuzukuri, Wagyu tataki, “shake butter”, as well as sushi, sashimi, temaki. An impressive choice of sakes and cocktails completes the picture.

Name: Paparoto Cucina
Address: Av. Pres. Juscelino Kubitschek, 2041 - Térreo, São Paulo, 04543-011, Brazil
Description: Part of the luxury JK Iguatemi complex, this restaurant has a spacious and modern setting with a decor that includes plants and subdued lighting that accentuates the illuminated Italian phrase “Se non ora quando?” (“If not now, when”). Famous chef Dayse Paparoto, who won the first edition of Brazil’s Professional Masterchef, showcases his Italian-inspired menu with an authentic and innovative touch that is based around fresh, top-quality ingredients. The menu features an array of options, such as the excellent egg yolk ravioli with ricotta and spinach, served with a soft egg yolk. Other options include fresh pastas and risottos, although the desserts steal the show here, highlighting the extreme creativity of the chef in dishes such as tiramisu, served with a candy floss tree, which comes as a complete surprise.

Name: Metzi
Address: Rua João Moura, 861, São Paulo, 05412-002, Brazil
Description: Although the fusion of Brazilian and Mexican cuisine is not an immediately obvious one, the end result at Metzi is really impressive, thanks to the skill of chefs Luana Sabino and Eduardo Nava Ortiz, who met while working in a restaurant in New York and decided to combine their respective culinary talents for the benefit of their guests. Their cooking is a combination of Mexican techniques and traditions and Brazilian ingredients, with careful attention always paid to seasonality. Start, perhaps, with an exquisite tostada (crab, fish or Campechana), followed by barbecued lamb cooked according to pre-Hispanic techniques, then round things off with a refined Buñuelo doughnut served with camomile ice cream and drizzled with Jataí honey. Several vegan options are also available.

Name: Rudä
Address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 118, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
Description: One of the most talked about restaurants in Ipanema. Here, chef Danilo Parah champions what he calls “emotional and creative cuisine” in a contemporary bistro-style setting featuring different ambiences and a private room on the first floor. Brazilian cuisine is very much to the fore and is showcased on a varied à la carte (plus an ”executive” menu) with a focus on local ingredients and in colourful, generous and highly flavourful dishes with little fear when it comes to combining lots of ingredients. It’s hard to forget the octopus with jambu fruit (a dish with a profusion of colours and textures that includes pasta cooked in a moqueca sauce) or the delicious cheesecake that takes on its own personality! The hospitality is on a par with the food here!

Name: Jiquitaia
Address: Rua Coronel Oscar Porto 808, São Paulo, 04003-004, Brazil
Description: If you're looking for typical homemade Brazilian cuisine prepared with quality ingredients, then this is the perfect place! Jiquitaia occupies a charming 1950s house surrounded by greenery, with a large, elegantly decorated dining room, where a plethora of wood and beautiful photos on the walls provide the decorative backdrop. Here, chef Marcelo Corrêa Bastos conjures up comforting traditional cuisine that feeds body and soul. During the working week, the playful “executive” menu is complemented by a concise menu featuring delicacies such as “coxinhas de frango caipira” (deep-fried dough filled with chicken), fish “moqueca” with shrimp, and grilled fish of the day served with a tasty pirão porridge. It's also worth noting that Jiquitaia also has a superb array of cachaças from across Brazil which have been carefully selected by the owner.

Name: Ama.zo - Cozinha Peruana
Description: This restaurant occupies the charming garden of an old property known as the Casa da Don'Anna, a 20C house with a strong coffee legacy. The ambience here is delightful, protected by the vagaries of the weather by an almost invisible roof, and features large jabuticabeira trees, tables laid out in the garden, and a semi-open kitchen to the rear. Here, Peruvian chef Enrique Paredes conjures up Andean cuisine that is reinterpreted through the use of local ingredients, strong flavours, pleasant textures and subtle nuances from the Amazon region. Among the starters, the fresh oysters with a Japanese ponzu sauce, physalis and black massago stands out, followed, perhaps, by a main of ossobuco cooked at low temperature with an Arequipeño sauce, and accompanied by a cassava millefeuille. Lovers of cacao will adore the intense and absolutely delicious chocolate x 4!

Name: Nosso
Address: Rua Maria Quitéria 91, Rio de Janeiro, 22410-040, Brazil
Description: An exclusive restaurant with three completely different floors: on the first, a bar; on the second, a dining space with an intimate ambience for a pleasant supper; and on the third, an outdoor terrace. Here, the relaxed cuisine, which is described by chef Bruno Katz as “contemporary”, features dishes that combine different food cultures from around the world in a creative and harmonious way. One example is the glazed octopus served with fried rice, kewpie mayonnaise, moyashi and nira, which is simply divine and cooked to perfection. Bartender Daniel Estevan elevates his concoctions to another level, combining classic drinks with his experience of the Amazon to create cocktails such as the surprising Tacacá Sour, with its mix of jambu, tucupi, cupuaçu and lemon. An extraordinary experience!

Name: Clan BBQ
Address: Rua Dias Ferreira, 233 Loja B, Rio de Janeiro, 22431 050, Brazil
Description: To the backdrop of a neon sign “Não apague o meu fogo” (“Don’t put out my fire”) clearly visible above the door, chefs Pepo Figueiredo and Newton Rique showcase cuisine in which fire plays a key role here, enabling them to prepare fresh ingredients imbued with a special flavour. In this industrial-style ambience with a predominance of raw concrete, a sturdy tree takes centre stage in the middle of the dining room. There’s also the option of sitting at the counter by the grill to watch dishes and cocktails being prepared at close quarters. The menu is of course heavily focused on barbecued meats, although you’ll also find other options such as vegetables, fish and burgers. Dishes you won’t want to miss include the creamy oxtail croquettes and cubes of smoked tongue with aioli. The succulent French rack of lamb, served with chimichurri, is cooked to perfection.

Name: Henriqueta
Address: Rua Aristides Espínola, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
Description: This “tasca” style restaurant in the southern part of Rio de Janeiro showcases the best of Portuguese cuisine in a bright environment with a glass façade, open kitchen and Portuguese ceramic decoration. The cuisine on offer dispenses with unnecessary frills, focusing on the quality of the ingredients and dishes designed for sharing, among which the “biff-anas açorianas”, a crispy bread sandwich filled with pork escalope marinated in wine and garlic, stands out. As a main course, we recommend the tender octopus “a lagareiro” roasted in oil, served with onion confit and mashed potatoes, followed by the “toucinho do céu” made with egg yolks, almonds and cinnamon, an authentic Portuguese dish if ever there was one!

Name: Izär
Address: Rua Barão Da Torre, 538, Rio de Janeiro, 22411-002, Brazil
Description: Located in the heart of Ipanema, a district teeming with dining options, this Spanish-inspired restaurant stands out from the crowd. Here, is presented a menu on which paella is the undoubted star of the show and is available via a range of options. The variety of fish- and seafood-based dishes is also impressive, enhanced by the freshness and quality of the ingredients he uses. The menu spans traditional tapas to generous portions of paella perfect for sharing. The main distinction that sets Izär apart is the completely open kitchen with a bar counter enabling guests to watch as many as seven paellas being prepared at the same time. Alternatively, take a seat at one of the wood tables in the charming dining room crowned by a vaulted ceiling and lighting that recreates the feel of a starlit sky.

Name: Les Présidents
Address: Rua Da Consolação 3527, São Paulo, 01416-001, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: Under the helm of a famous chef who needs no introduction and who is widely known as a result of his participation in Masterchef, this bistro-style eatery offers refined cuisine inspired by Érick Jacquin’s French roots. Occupying a striking building with a completely black façade and red doors, the interior is no less impressive with its red walls and myriad paintings and embellishments that add to the typically French ambience. To enjoy the experience to the full, we recommend the flavoursome, traditional and hearty rabbit cassoulet and duck foie gras. A seven-course surprise tasting menu created by the chef is also available, alongside the à la carte and a midweek “executive” menu.

Name: Spicy Fish
Address: Rua Maria Quitéria, 99, Rio de Janeiro, 22410-040, Brazil
Description: A restaurant that is the talk of the town when it comes to Asian cuisine, a reputation enhanced by the magnificent building in which it is situated – a four-storey property featuring a decor of neutral tones, soft lighting and lots of plants which add a touch of freshness to the space. The cuisine created by chef Emerson Kim is a fusion of Japanese and Korean cooking, showcased via well-presented dishes with a unique flavour. The menu is extensive and for those unsure what to order, the chef’s selection includes two portions of nigiri, sashimi and the “house special”. Hot dishes include the reinterpretation of the Bibimbap, the finishing touches to which are always added at the table, and the delicious Kagoshima wagyu beef, known as Hot Stone.

Name: Piselli
Address: Rua Padre João Manuel 1253, São Paulo, 01411-001, Brazil
Description: Piselli is the Italian word for “pea” and this vegetable is highly significant for the owner Juscelino Pereira who still maintains his custom of decorating every plate with three peas. Nowadays, the brand has three restaurants in São Paulo and one in Brasilia, and the cuisine is the same in each of them: namely, high-quality Italian cooking inspired by the Piedmont region. Dishes here are well prepared and full of flavour. Among them, we recommend the incredible “burrata calda al tartufo”, baked in delicious focaccia. Follow this, perhaps, with the homemade tortelloni filled with mozzarella di bufala and served with a fresh tomato and basil sauce, and the classic ossobuco alla milanese with saffron rice. In summary, a simply wonderful culinary experience.

Name: Jamile
Address: Rua Treze de Maio 647, São Paulo, 01327-000, Brazil
Description: The nostalgic Bixiga district of the city was the place chosen by famous chef Henrique Fogaça, a judge on Masterchef Brazil, to open this restaurant almost a decade ago. Now completely remodelled with exposed brick walls and a rustic-contemporary decor, Jamile features a large dining room, an open kitchen plus a bar counter for guests keen to watch the culinary action unfold, as well as an inner terrace. Traditional Brazilian cuisine is the mainstay here, showcased via a harmonious combination of ingredients and flavours from different regions. Options on the menu include crispy cupim dumplings with a pepper jelly, “cupim do sal” with yellow cassava and plantain farofa, as well as a delicious “moqueca baiana” of white fish with prawns and cassava farofa.

Name: Marine Restô
Address: Avenida Atlântica 4240, Rio de Janeiro, 22070-900, Brazil
Description: Enjoy one of the most breathtaking views of Copacabana beach at this restaurant on the sixth floor of the luxurious Fairmont Rio de Janeiro Copacabana hotel, where the panoramic terrace and swimming pool come as a highly scenic surprise! In this large, contemporary space with an open-view kitchen, choose from a mix of Brazilian and international cuisine which showcases top-quality ingredients and has a strong focus on quality and grilled dishes. As a result, some of the standout dishes on the menu are cooked on the Josper grill, such as the tender Carioca-roasted chicken, the mouthwatering Angus skirt steak with a guaraná demi-glace, and vegetarian options that include grilled heart of palm with smoked “bottled butter”.

Name: Rubaiyat Rio
Address: Rua Jardim Botânico 971, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-051, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Jockey Club Brasileiro within the boundaries of the city’s botanical gardens, this restaurant boasts breathtaking views where you can enjoy a meal on the terrace to a picture-postcard backdrop that features the horse-racing track as well as the statue of Christ the Redeemer. Inside, there is a large dining room with a counter that is home to the kitchen, where a large glass window provides views of the churrasco grill. Renowned for its array of premium meats and for managing its own production, the restaurant offers more than ten different cuts, although fish, seafood, rice and a variety of sides also feature on the menu. On Saturdays, don't miss the chance to try the traditional feijoada stew, made with prime cuts of meat, along with milkshakes and an incredible dessert buffet!

Name: Oia Cozinha - Mediterrânea
Address: Rua Barão da Torre 340, Rio de Janeiro, 22411-002, Brazil
Description: If the prospect of a voyage to explore the flavours and charming ambience of the Aegean islands sounds appealing, this restaurant will fit the bill with its fresh and bright decor typical of a restaurant on the delightful island of Santorini, thanks to its attractive plants and relaxed blue and white colour scheme. The menu includes classic Greek dishes, the personality of which are enhanced by flavours from other Mediterranean countries. Start, perhaps with the truffle egg with a potato foam, mushroom ragu and Grana Padano tuile, followed by a choice of dishes from the land or sea, such as the traditional moussaka or the tender octopus served with a fantastic roast cauliflower cream, macadamia vinaigrette and broccoli.

Name: Huto Campo Belo
Address: Rua Dr. Jesuíno Maciel 682, São Paulo, 04615-001, Brazil
Description: The star of the show here is the charcoal grill, providing a different emphasis to other restaurants in the Huto group. Taking a step back from the usual nigiri and sashimi, the menu includes a variety of seafood, fish, meat and vegetables, all of which are imbued with the smoky flavours of charcoal, alongside signature dishes from the renowned flagship eatery in Moema. The most attractive option is the Omakase, a tasting menu chosen by the chef, although you’ll also find a sushi bar serving fresh fish, roes and an array of top-quality seafood. The wood decor and soft lighting are the key features of the sophisticated yet welcoming ambience. If you have the chance, take a seat at the bar counter to feed off the energy from the kitchen as part of a unique dining experience.

Name: Cantaloup
Address: Rua Manuel Guedes 474, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
Description: A real oasis of elegance that is immediately evident the moment you step through the door. Occupying a former bread factory, Cantaloup features high ceilings and a spacious and stylish dining room complemented by a classic-style bar in the corner. Next to it is an attractive waiting area protected by a retractable roof that provides plenty of light, which combines pleasantly with a charming green space and a fountain that adds a hint of freshness to the overall feel. Chef Valdir Oliveira offers an attractive menu based around international recipes that he creates via strong technique and well-defined combinations. Starters include delicious options such as foie gras, burrata and carpaccio, followed by mains such as duck magret, veal shank and “bobó de lagostim” (a type of crayfish stew). The wine list, which includes a selection of wines from 13 different countries, is the most comprehensive in the city.

Name: Vista
Address: Avenida Pedro Álvares Cabral 1301, São Paulo, 04094-050, Brazil
Description: Occupying the top floor of the MAC USP (Museu de Arte Contemporânea da Universidade de São Paulo), this restaurant boasts spectacular views of Ibirapuera and a 360° panorama of the city. The kitchen is run by chef Pedro Oliveira, who offers guests a traditional Brazilian dining experience featuring typical ingredients from the country’s five regions, which he prepares in a harmonious and balanced way and is showcased on an “executive”-style format at lunchtime. On Saturdays, pumpkin shrimp with rice and sweet potato chips is the highlight, with crispy pururuca pork making an appearance on Sundays. The star of the show on the dessert menu is Vista’s own irresistible version of the traditional Portuguese dish “toucinho do Céu”, made with pumpkin, egg yolk and almonds. A special menu of starters and appetisers, plus an impressive selection of cocktails, is available on the terrace.

Name: Dinho's
Description: Dinho's was opened by Fuad Zegaib (the creator of the strip steak) six decades ago. Nowadays, the restaurant is run by chef Paulo Zegaib, the founder’s son. Occupying a new home on the ground floor of the Hotel Qoya, in the Paraíso section of the city (there’s also a Dinho’s in the Jardins district), it features a spacious, classically furnished main dining room, which is entirely glass-fronted and enclosed by a beautiful vertical garden plus a colourful open kitchen to one side. Renowned for its longevity in this bustling capital city, the restaurant offers superb cuts of beef, as well as feijoada on Thursdays and Saturdays, a buffet of salads and desserts, plus a copious seafood buffet on Fridays.

Name: Tanit
Description: This charming restaurant has become a reference for excellent Spanish cuisine in the city. In this bright, modern setting with high ceilings, polished cement floors and wood-clad walls, chef Oscar Bosch, who arrived in Brazil in 2009 having worked in leading restaurants in his native Spain such as El Bulli and El Celler de Can Roca, offers Mediterranean cuisine which he adapts to Brazilian tastes via refined technique and elaborate presentation. While tapas and a variety of rice dishes are an integral part of his identity, you can also enjoy other delicious options such as croquetas, patatas bravas and, as a main course, the classic roast suckling pig, cooked at low temperature and served with a velvety roasted carrot purée.

Name: Chef Rouge
Address: Rua Bela Cintra 2238, São Paulo, 01415-002, Brazil
Description: An authentic French bistro, both in terms of its black façade and red awning and its elegant, welcoming interior. The main dining space is complemented by a charming terrace at the entrance, adorned with two impressive trees and with candlelight in the evening. Some of the tables are also occupied by adorable, large red teddy bears that add to the delightful atmosphere. Understandably, the culinary focus and star of the show is classic French cooking with a contemporary touch that is showcased by top-quality ingredients and delicately prepared dishes. These include the grilled foie gras with figs, served with bitter chocolate, and the classic roast duck breast with orange sauce accompanied by gaufrettes potatoes. The incredible Eclair XXL provides the perfect finale!

Name: Fasano Trattoria
Address: Rua Iguatemi s/n, São Paulo, 01451-010, Brazil
Description: This unique section of the city is home to the super-modern Pátio Malzoni alongside the Casa Bandeirista, an example of 17C Brazilian colonial architecture. Amid these contrasts, you’ll also find this exquisite trattoria paying homage to Southern Italy with its decor combining wood, leather and the flags of Italian football teams, plus a pleasant outdoor terrace. Here, the chef has created a menu featuring traditional recipes and dishes inspired by the region around Naples, including the island of Capri. The extensive choice includes the memorable linguine alle vongole with cherry tomatoes, the classic spaghetti alla carbonara, and the polpettone al forno (baked meatloaf), another excellent choice. Service is also a strong point here, so don’t hesitate to ask for a personal recommendation or choose one of the daily specials.

Name: Fogo de Chão
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Fogo de Chão restaurant is much more than just a place to eat as it represents Brazil’s churrasco tradition that has won admirers in different parts of the world. The origins of this method for cooking meat date back to the gauchos who discovered that skewering pieces of meat on wooden sticks and placing them around a fire transformed a simple cut of meat into a true delicacy. Served as part of “rodizio” all-you-can-eat format, the extensive selection includes beef, lamb and pork, as well as the famous prime rib and dry-aged meats (only available on the à la carte). To accompany the superb choice of meat, there’s also an extensive buffet of salads, rice dishes, carpaccios, cheeses and sausages. In total, there are five Fogo de Chão restaurants in São Paulo, all of which boast a comprehensive wine list. The new addition at the Jardins restaurant is a space dedicated to cigar-lovers.

Name: A Figueira Rubaiyat
Address: Rua Haddock Lobo 1738, São Paulo, 01414-002, Brazil
Description: The backdrop here is definitely a surprise, thanks to the majestic Bengal fig, a century-old tree that attracts admiring glances inside this restaurant. The glass roof adds a special touch, enabling guests to admire the immensity of its crown and branches to the full. In keeping with its sister property in the famous Faria Lima, the cuisine is based around the "fork to plate” concept. Both the beef and pork are produced at the group’s own farms and distributed throughout its franchises. Dishes include baby beef, Denver steak, filet mignon, master beef and “tirita de picanha”, all of which are cooked to perfection, although the menu also features a variety of fish, rice and pasta options. Enhance your dining experience with the superb array of labels available on the wine list.

Name: Toto
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 155, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: This is the first venture run exclusively by Thomas Troisgros, who has created a totally unique concept unlike anything we are used to. At Toto, he creates dishes that reflect his food-inspired memories and combine French techniques, Asian influences and top-quality Brazilian ingredients. Don’t expect sophisticated and complex dishes; instead, the concept is much less complicated, with a focus on affordably priced comfort food. Standout features here are the industrial decor featuring neutral tones, the relaxed and informal ambience, and an open kitchen with a dining counter for guests. One particular dish you won’t want to miss is the popular and quite irresistible roasted rib gyoza with a ponzu sauce and watercress.

Name: Aya Japanese Cuisine
Address: Avenida Pedroso de Morais 141, São Paulo, 05419-000, Brazil
Description: This attractive property with a contemporary ambience and minimalist decor has a good location in a busy part of the city, just a few metres from the famous Avenida Rebouças. It is under the baton of sushi chef Juraci Pereira (better known as “Jura”) who, after working as Jun Sakamoto’s right-hand man for 11 years, decided to open his own venture in collaboration with his business partner Beto Ganme. Downstairs, where guests can sit at the counter to watch the expert hands of the chefs in action, the atmosphere is more intimate, while the upstairs is more modern and cosy. The cuisine includes a special Aya omakase menu, various types of sashimi, sushi (à la carte and combos), makimonos and hot dish options.

Name: Amadeus
Address: Rua Haddock Lobo 807, São Paulo, 01414-001, Brazil
Description: No description of Amadeus can be made without mentioning the Masano family, along with their passion, enthusiasm and dreams. Thanks to rave reviews of their cooking from friends, they decided to open a restaurant known as “fish corner” in São Paulo. Today, the kitchen is overseen by chef Bella Masano, the owners’ daughter, who embellishes the menu with her innovative culinary creations alongside classic dishes which have been given a contemporary makeover. Her cooking is showcased on an à la carte and tasting menu which includes options such as fresh oysters from the family’s own beds in Florianópolis. Amadeus’ signature dishes include the shrimp “à paulista”, prepared with olive oil and garlic, which is full of flavour and perfect for sharing, and the “moqueca Amadeus”, a stew with fish and shrimp, served with plantain and onion farofa – an exquisite combination!

Name: Cais
Description: A relaxed restaurant with a lively atmosphere and good food, so it’s not surprising that it’s always full. Occupying a charming small house in the Vila Madalena neighbourhood of the city, Cais features tables outdoors next to the window, seats at the counter by the kitchen, as well more traditional tables. Run by Adriano de Laurentiis in the kitchen and his business partner Guilherme Giraldi, sommelier and front of house manager, its cuisine is centred around fresh fish and seafood. The concise menu is constantly updated in line with the availability and freshness of seasonal ingredients. Having savoured the delicious appetisers on offer here, we particularly recommend the week’s selection of fish and seafood, followed by the creamy and delicate cheesecake served with a milk sorbet.

Name: De Segunda
Address: Rua Prof. Tamandaré Toledo, 160, São Paulo, 04532-020, Brazil
Description: Young chefs Júlia Tricate and Gabriel Coelho already have impressive CVs, having won TV food competitions and worked in Michelin-starred restaurants such as Noma (Copenhagen) and Oro (Rio de Janeiro). Following on from these incredible experiences, they decided to open their own restaurant, with an open kitchen and simple decor that helps to channel the complete focus onto their cuisine. Their modern culinary vision is showcased on a creative menu that champions fresh, seasonal ingredients. Start with the “katsu sando”, consisting of breaded pork belly in toasted milk bread and a sweet and sour Asian-inspired sauce. As a main, we recommend the “arroz caldoso” rice dish with cod served with a delicate beurre blanc, followed by the strawberry with yoghurt and jabuticaba, accompanied by an irresistible white chocolate ganache.

Name: Nôa
Address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 135, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
Description: Occupying a house from the 1930s with a well-preserved façade in one of the most renowned parts of Ipanema. The decor here has been meticulously designed, from the unusual fabrics hanging from the ceiling to the Hebrew-inspired paintings on the walls. The cuisine is inspired by the coasts of the Mediterranean, and includes fish, seafood and fresh pasta with a Brazilian and international flavour. The extensive menu features options such as burrata di bufala with beetroot pesto and Grana Padano. Mains range from the vegan “moqueca” stew to the excellent fresh pasta served with shrimp and an oyster foam. The charming veranda is perfect for one of Nôa’s refreshing cocktails.

Name: Nelita
Address: Rua Ferreira De Araújo, 330, São Paulo, 05428-000, Brazil
Description: A recently opened restaurant that has already made a name for itself in the city’s Baixo Pinheiros district. Under the baton of chef Tássia Magalhães, an exclusively female team is in charge of the kitchen, conjuring up innovative dishes with an Italian influence. The wine list, which includes natural and organic wines, has been carefully curated by Danyel Steinle. To a modern decorative backdrop of exposed brick walls and different ambiences, guests can choose between tables at the entrance, the marble counter in front of the kitchen, or a private room which can be reserved for groups. The menu includes delicious fresh pastas such as spaghetti with squid and bottarga alongside the appetising lamb with lentils, tucupi and pear. Absolutely perfect!

Name: Animus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The kitchen here is under the baton of young chef Giovanna Grossi, who has had an impressive career thus far. Having worked in renowned restaurants in France and Spain, she decided to open his own business where she offers creative cuisine that champions local and seasonal ingredients. Occupying a corner location in the charming Pinheiros district, Animus features a decor of warm tones combined with wood, and features an open kitchen where guests can observe the chefs in action. The menu comprises dishes designed for sharing, an à la carte and the option of a pre-prepared tray of several different dishes. An “executive” menu is also available during the week.

Name: OCYÁ Leblon
Address: Rua Aristides Espínola, 88, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
Description: Fisherman, diver and chef Gerônimo Athuel is a font of knowledge when it comes to seafood, and is keen to highlight the importance of conscious, selective and artisanal fishing. He is also strongly committed to research into preserving and maturing techniques, as well as the use of all fish and seafood species, prioritising those that are often discarded. With one restaurant in Ilha Primeira already behind him, he has now brought his cuisine to this exclusive space in the Zona Sul. Here, the decor is modern with plenty of natural light and a glass-fronted fish maturing cabinet that highlights his culinary concept. Fabulous options on the menu range from seafood charcuterie to grilled, fried and raw fish dishes which will delight guests’ tastebuds with their surprising flavours and skilful technique and presentation.

Name: Blaise
Description: Occupying the historic Maternidade Filomena Matarazzo building, this restaurant takes its inspiration from the Franco-Swiss writer Braise Cendrars. The interior is similar to a wood cabin (similar to where he is said to have lived) and includes Brazilian volcanic stone crystals between the woodwork, rustic decor and subtle lighting provided by the lampshades that illuminate the room. Here, chef Felipe Rodrigues, who has experience working in leading restaurants behind him, conjures up French cuisine with a Brazilian touch. Our suggestions include the succulent and incredibly tender braised beef tongue, served with potato salad and a refined red wine sauce. The jabuticaba sorbet with jam, jelly and jabuticaba pearls in a delicate “crème diplomate” is an absolute must!

Name: Haru Sushi
Address: Rua Raimuindo Corrêa, 10, Rio de Janeiro, 22040-042, Brazil
Description: Owner-chef Menandro Rodrigues’ passion for Japanese cuisine provides the impetus for everything that goes on at this welcoming restaurant in Copacabana. On the ground floor, enjoy relaxed serviced at the pavement tables, while on the first floor you’ll find a dining room decorated in Japanese style with an impressive bar counter overlooking the kitchen, as well as tables and chairs laid out in different sections. The chef follows the Japanese “Kaisen” philosophy (which translates as “continuous improvement”) and devotes special attention to its techniques as well as to ingredients sourced directly from local fishermen. His cuisine is served as part of an Omakase menu, and includes options such as sushi, sashimi, and special and traditional “combos”. These are complemented by an extensive array of sakis that can be enjoyed in “tasting” measures.

Name: Osso
Address: Rua Bandeira Paulista, 520, São Paulo, 04532-001, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: An address that is much prized by meat-lovers in the Greater São Paulo area. Here, chef Renzo Garibaldi, who is known as the “Master Butcher” in his native Peru, has opened his first culinary venture in Brazil. His cuisine is based around meat sourced from sustainable producers, with the option of dry aged and different maturing times covering an array of different cuts. Beef is the star of the show here, available as ribeye, fillet mignon, picanha and short ribs, alongside special dry-aged pure Wagyu, Vaca Velha and Angus. Dishes such as ceviche, salad, Josper-grilled fish and the rice-based “arroz de costela” also feature on the menu in a modern, elegant space with an extensive and superb wine list.

Name: TARAZ
Description: Part of the historic and former Condessa Filomena Matarazzo Maternity hospital complex, now converted into the luxury Rosewood São Paulo hotel, where the menu bears the signature of famous chef Felipe Bronze. In this charming space, the cooking is based around that of South America as a whole, with the open grill featuring prominently in a variety of harmonious dishes prepared with ingredients of the highest quality. Why not start with an authentic South American dish such as the excellent combination of tuna ceviche with caramelised peanuts, shiso, sesame, peanut milk and crispy tapioca? Follow this with a Brazilian classic – duck with tucupi (fermented manioc juice), sheep curd and toasted pineapple. For those who prefer to eat alfresco, the terrace is simply charming!

Name: Escama
Address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí, 5, Rio de Janeiro, 22460 020, Brazil
Description: After visiting a French restaurant with a similar outlook, inspiration struck to open this restaurant serving the best fish and seafood in a relaxed ambience. The focus at Escama is one that showcases the best maritime ingredients, which he always sources fresh from local fishermen. For your main, you can choose how you want to have your fish prepared (grilled, baked or poached), such as the sea bass, which is accompanied by a delicious champagne sauce and roasted onions. The menu also features options such as squid, shrimp, scallops and oysters, plus a splendid seafood feijoada on Fridays. The restaurant is located close to the city’s botanical garden, in a charming two-floor property with an extremely relaxed ambience enhanced by a decor of muted colours.

Name: Kubo Zushi
Address: Rua Das Tabocas 158, São Paulo, 05445-020, Brazil
