The spirit of frugality espoused at Oryori Matsumura decrees that each ingredient should be used completely. For example, the bony parts of fish left over are used up making sea-bream miso and dashi. By bringing together the aesthetic senses of disparate locations, Oryori Matsumura has created a cuisine that is refreshingly original.

Name: PONTE VECCHIO
Description: Daisuke Yamane insists on originality in everything about his restaurant. Leather seating, show plates of Venetian glass and silverware are all designed by the chef. One intriguing offering, inspired by Yamane’s days in Italy, is ‘the world’s most luxurious pauper food’, a dish made with potatoes and caviar. Each ingredient complements the other, converging in a harmonious whole.

Name: tamanegi
Description: Onion-shaped lamps hang from the ceiling. In this couple-run restaurant, the wife has studied Italian cuisine and the husband was a sommelier at a French restaurant. They chose the name (‘tamanegi’ is Japanese for ‘onion’) because of the bulb’s familiarity in both Italian and French cooking. Taking her culinary cues from her experience in Italy’s Piemonte region, the dishes are bold yet delicate in flavour. Pasta is made by hand the way she learnt in Piemonte; completely free-range beef is paired with organic wines.

Name: Washun Taiki
Description: The name ‘Washun’ means ‘complementing the seasons’. The purport here is to bring together ingredients that draw out each other’s goodness, using proper techniques but with splashes of creativity. Noting bread’s affinity with fats and oils, Washun Taiki created baguette sandwiches, breaking new ground with fillings such as grilled seafood and deep-fried items. With orthodox techniques as the baseline and smiling guests as the goal, Washun Taiki is not afraid to break a few rules.

Name: TOKI
Address: 1F, Hotel The Mitsui Kyoto, 284 Nijo Aburanokojicho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto, 604-0051, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Food born of experience with French cuisine and the famous waters of Kyoto. The chef has always prized soup stock and makes it a centrepiece of his work. As if to symbolise Kyoto, the ‘city of waters’, the prix fixe starts with hot water drawn from a spring. Even the amuse-bouche follows the soup-stock theme. Foie gras with Tango sake lees fuses Japanese and French culture; local ingredients are served on Kyoyaki vessels. Feel the mood of the seasons in the ancient capital through the cuisine of TOKI.

Name: Tempura Urakami
Description: In his tempura creations, Dai Urakami prizes lightness above all. Frying in light safflower oil brings the flavour of each piece to the fore. The meal begins with two tiger prawns. To ensure that the sweetness of the flesh makes an impression, fragrant prawn legs are served afterward. Tempura items such as abalone and milt are imaginatively paired with vinegared rice stuffed with sea urchin. The painting of Mount Fuji on the wall reminds Urakami always to seek greater heights.

Name: Matakichi
Description: A sister to Gion Matayoshi, here guests can enjoy cuisine in a casual manner. At lunch, an ochazuke (green tea poured over rice) set menu is available, served with several dishes of obanzai, or Kyoto cuisine side-dishes. Evening fare is an omakase; techniques passed on from the flagship establishment lends brilliance to both soup and grilled dishes. Hassun appetisers loaded with treats such as hijiki seaweed, croquettes and nanbanzuke are served simply. Shaved-ice treats served year-round are a popular sweet – especially loved is the matcha-flavoured shaved ice sweetened with wasanbon syrup.

Name: Sosakukappo Otani
Description: The blending of Japanese and Western styles is the appeal of creative kappo cuisine here. With its pivot foot firmly in Japanese gastronomy, the restaurant moves imaginatively to incorporate Western elements. For example, the dashi is based on kombu and katsuo but, influenced by French chefs, mixes in fish fumet, the stock from the bones of white fish. To broaden its culinary range, the restaurant added an oven. Roasts and gratins now widen the scope of Otani’s Japanese cooking.

Name: Unkaku
Description: ‘Unkaku’ is a traditional pattern depicting cranes dancing in the clouds. Masaharu Shimamura sees himself as a crane; the image expresses his wish to fly high in the culinary world. In the thrifty spirit of Osaka cooking, he uses every part of his ingredients. His signature dish, ‘Nozaki-style grilled small sea bream’, is testament to that conviction. Recalling that the area around Nozaki Kannon Temple (Jigen-ji) was once famed for its canola, Shimamura simmers the fish in rapeseed oil so that even the bones of this fish served whole can be eaten.

Name: Yoshitaka
Description: The owner-chef approaches oden as one would kaiseki dishes served in bowls. For example, in spring his oden features new cabbage and rape blossoms; in summer, anago served with slivered new burdock root, boiled salty-sweet, and topped with an egg, in what is called the Yanagawa style; then mushrooms in autumn and longtooth grouper in winter. The green spring onion and oil cake is an inspiration from the kasu-udon originating in Minamikawachi.

Name: xiang hua
Description: True to its name, which means ‘serving the cuisine of every region of China’, the menu features a rich variety of regional dishes. The background to the recipes is a tale worth telling. As the chef used to teach at a cooking school, he is well-versed in his craft. He follows Confucius’s teaching of ‘Bù shí bù shí’, that people should eat foods in season. Tour the regional cuisines of China and taste its many fascinating flavours.

Name: Sui Okazaki
Description: When he took over the restaurant, the chef inherited its teachings, preserving the forms of traditional multi-course meals while expressing his own imagination. Experience in Kyoto cuisine shines in soup stock of ma-kombu and Rishiri kombu. Pickled mackerel is paired with fruit, highlighting the tartness in both. His inspiration for pursuing the gastronomic life came, he says, from the way appetiser platters express the shifting seasons. To celebrate those seasons, dishes are cheerfully garnished.

Name: LACERBA
Address: 2F, Shin Daibiru, 1-2-1 Dojimahama, Kita-ku, Osaka, 530-0004, Japan
Description: Masaaki Fujita reaches deep into the character and history of Japan and Italy to conjure his cuisine. Eel, Chinese yam and red rice on a single plate fuse the gustatory senses of the two countries, both rooted deeply in cultures of river fish and rice. Zest of Japanese pepper married with the bittersweet of red wine sauce is somehow nostalgic. Fujita’s motto is ‘to be master of one is to be master of all’. His long study of hometown cooking followed by his own innovations proves the point.

Name: Sushidokoro Hirokawa
Description: When you order sake, the chef presents a box of paulownia wood containing Satsuma and Tenma kiriko cut-glass drinking cups. These craft traditions of Kagoshima and Osaka tell of where the chef was born, and where he apprenticed. Fish is selected at Tsuruhashi Market. The meal starts with snacks before proceeding to more creative preparations, attesting to his experience. Nigiri are formed small, in the hope you will sample as many different items as possible. The chef’s ready smile is another factor that keeps diners coming back.

Name: Miyagawacho Hotta
Description: The look and feel of Old Kyoto permeates Miyagawacho. The owner-chef, who refined his skills in Gion, is also a qualified sommelier and holds a sake diploma, so he is an expert at pairings. While the set meal respects the basics of Japanese cuisine, the owner-chef adds playful details such as Worcestershire sauce in beef cutlet sandwiches. Shaved ice is served in summer; cocktails made from fruit benefit from the owner-chef’s bartending experience.

Name: Matsu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Always take on challenges – that was the teaching of Toshio Matsuno’s tempura chef father – which is why Matsuno travelled to the USA to broaden his perspective. The experience prompted his recent changing of the family restaurant from tempura only to a general Japanese restaurant. Tilefish fried with its scales still on and served with egg yolk vinaigrette sauce and shaved black truffle on top testifies to his broad-minded approach. The one dish Matsuno never omits is his tempura, in respect for his father. ‘Matsuno cuisine’ is an evergreen that never fades.

Name: The Golden Fork
Description: Situated along one of Rabat’s typical narrow alleyways, this elegant restaurant’s new venue boasts a courtyard setting in a historic building dating from the 16C. The chef Letizia Vella here creates surprisingly creative and technically skilful cuisine full of distinctive Mediterranean flavours. Careful attention is paid to using seasonal and locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Terroir
Description: Situated in a charming square with an old fountain, this 16C building boasts original brick walls and a rustic, romantic ambience – the intimate dining room is on the first floor, where there is even a small table on the balcony (make sure you book this in advance). The cuisine focuses on local and Mediterranean ingredients and includes highlights such as ricotta gnocchi with a Maltese sausage ragù, while the wine list also features a few international labels.

Name: Rebekah's
Description: This former farmstead is over 200 years old and boasts thick walls of golden Maltese rock. Prime local produce and luxury imported ingredients are used to create modern, hearty dishes with bold Mediterranean flavours. Service is overseen by the proud chef-owner; ask for a table in the central courtyard.

Name: The Harbour Club
Address: 4/5 Barrierra Wharf, Liesse Hill, Valletta, VLT 1941, Malta
Description: Take in impressive views over the Grand Harbour from the sunny terrace or head down to the appealing restaurant below; the building was constructed in the 18C as an ice house and provides a unique and intimate setting. Well-presented, creative dishes showcase some top island ingredients.

Name: Zest
Address: 25 St. George's Road, St Julian's, STJ 3208, Malta
Description: Zest is a stylish, laid-back spot, set within a chic hotel in the bustling St Julian’s district. The menu mixes influences from many Asian countries, so you can choose anything from tempura of local red prawns to sushi or spicy Thai curry; whatever you pick, freshness and quality are assured.

Name: One80 St.Christopher Street
Address: 45A St. Christopher's Street, Il-Belt, Valletta, VLT 1464, Malta
Description: From the various options on the menu, we recommend starting with one of the excellent snacks such as crab croquette, Joselito chorizo and black garlic and then continuing with pistachio carbonara, a delicious pasta made with traditional guanciale and roasted pistachios. Main courses include excellent meat options, such as chateaubriand for two served with gravy. The restaurant has a chic, bistro-style decor and a lively atmosphere typical of the restaurants in La Valletta’s historic centre.

Name: The Fork and Cork
Description: Behind the stone walls of a historic building sits this charming restaurant. Chef-owner Carl Zahra seems to be everywhere at once: you’ll find him not only in the kitchen but also out front recommending regional wines to go with the tasty pastas and other Mediterranean-inspired dishes.

Name: Kaiseki
Description: If you find yourself on one of the most beautiful islands in the Mediterranean Sea and hungering for Mediterranean-Asian fusion cuisine, then head for Noel Azzopardi's Kaiseki. There's a cosy vibe to this basement restaurant and the Chef-Owner's kitchen produces interesting creations like soy-marinated tuna belly carpaccio, goat's cheese and grapefruit crostino, BBQ pork dumplings with teriyaki, sesame seeds and spicy mayo or roasted duck breast with pickled beetroot, pak choi and crispy duck & mozzarella roll. The different cooking styles are combined well, and the informal, casual atmosphere makes the experience all the more enjoyable.

Name: Aaron´s Kitchen
Description: This bistro in the town centre with a welcoming ambience and an attractive, colourful decor is the setting for Mediterranean fish dishes and typical island fare. Very popular with locals and tourists alike, the restaurant also offers a few outdoor tables which need to be booked well in advance.

Name: Giuseppi's
Description: Situated within the attractive Salini Resort hotel overlooking the bay of the same name, this exquisite restaurant uses top-quality ingredients to create Mediterranean-style dishes, although modern trends are starting to make a fleeting appearance in some recipes. Lunchtime options are slightly simpler than those served in the evening.

Name: Root 81
Description: This pleasant restaurant serves Mediterranean-style cuisine skilfully prepared by the talented chef with a focus on local ingredients. The outdoor space has an attractive and relaxing vibe, plus there’s an excellent selection of wines and cocktails.

Name: Tmun
Address: Martino Garces Street, Mġarr Harbour, Gozo, Għajnsielem, GSM 2413, Malta
Description: This restaurant decorated in maritime colours serves delicious Mediterranean cuisine which is often inspired by the fresh fish caught that day. The atmosphere here is informal, with friendly, welcoming staff, plus there’s an attractive sunny terrace for summer dining.

Name: Tartarun
Description: This elegant restaurant on the harbourside of a small fishing village has been run by the Schiavone family for over 10 years. Son James treats diners to a daily changing selection of simply cooked whole fish and other, more modern, imaginative seafood dishes. Apart from fishermen they support the local baker that provides daily bread for the village and a hydroponic farmer which is a few kilometers from the restaurant. Their 150+ bin wine list is renowned locally.

Name: Grotto Tavern
Address: 9/10/12 St Pauls Square, Rabat, RBT 1232, Malta
Description: Boasting an excellent location in the historic centre of Rabat, this restaurant full of character boasts a bar, a garden room and a “cave room”, the latter a grotto which has been excavated out of the limestone rock and is available for private dining (book in advance). The Mediterranean cuisine bears the signature of the new chef Mark Cauchi, who still uses local ingredients such as snails, rabbit, beef and other delicacies. Professional service completes the picture.

Name: LOA
Address: Saint Geraldu, St Paul's Bay, SPB 3310, Malta
Description: Facing the sea on Malta’s Sirens coast, this modern restaurant named after the ancient Loa river (the longest river in Chile) serves South American fusion cuisine which is both varied and delicious. The atmosphere here is relaxed and inviting with a contemporary vibe. A good choice of pre-dinner cocktails is also available.

Name: AKI
Address: Corner of Strait Street and Santa Lucia Street, Valletta, VLT 1455, Malta
Description: Look for the entrance to this sleek, stylish basement restaurant next to the Embassy Hotel, and once inside, grab a cocktail from the bar running along one side of the room. Every table has a view of the open kitchen; watch the chefs as they carefully prepare Asian-inspired – mostly Japanese – dishes. Salmon tiradito and scallop roll are the favourite choices from our inspectors.

Name: Briju
Description: The chef at Briju has a passion for all things local and sustainable. 90% of his ingredients are sourced from nearby farms and he even uses regional salt and olive oil. Cooking blends Maltese and Mediterranean flavours and the place has a pleasingly relaxed, neighbourhood feel.

Name: The Medina
Address: 7 Holy Cross Street, Mdina, MDN 1231, Malta
Description: Hidden away in the enchantingly narrow streets of Mdina is this equally characterful 500 year old restaurant. Dine beneath a vaulted stone ceiling or in the internal courtyard beside an ancient vine. Local ingredients underpin well-executed dishes which exhibit subtle modern twists.

Name: Level Nine by Oliver Glowig
Address: 58 Triq Sant Antnin, Mgarr, GSM 9026, Malta
Description: The menu at this restaurant has been designed by German chef Oliver Glowig, now an ambassador for the type of Italian cuisine showcased here. We highly recommend the tasting menu, which will give you a delicious overview of the chef’s different dishes, but if you do decide to order from the à la carte, the tournedos Rossini with foie gras and spinach is an excellent choice. Various local labels stand out on the wine list, including a remarkable Marsovin Antonin 2021 which is full and round yet retains a fruity character. From the charming terrace, the stunning views of the small harbour at Mgarr add to the appeal in summer.

Name: Al Sale
Description: In the middle of Xaghra lies this outwardly inconspicuous restaurant that extends over two floors and boasts a small terrace out front. The Chef-Owner hails from Toronto and forged his independent business here in the middle of the pandemic, showing just how much heart and soul is behind his cooking! If you love simple cuisine based on fresh produce – especially when it comes to meat and seafood – try the prawn & scallop-filled ravioli with prawn bisque, or the delicious veal rack with salsa verde. Everything is uncomplicated, ingredient-led and freshly prepared. An international wine list and the friendly, attentive yet unstuffy service round off the overall experience.

Name: KuYa
Address: 20 St. George's Road, St Julian's, STJ 3209, Malta
Description: Head up the spiral staircase and past the kitchen to this modern, light-filled room, where they offer an appealing blackboard menu of Asian classics. Cooking is fresh and authentic, with bold, vibrant flavours. Choose one of the craft beers from their wide-ranging list.

Name: Guzé
Address: 22 Old Bakery Street, Valletta, VLT 1454, Malta
Description: A striking 17C palazzo houses this cosy cellar bistro. Glance into the kitchens from street level, then head down the narrow staircase at the side to reach the two rustic, romantic dining rooms adorned with knick-knacks. Traditional Maltese dishes are generously proportioned.

Name: Chophouse
Address: Censu Xerri, Tigné Point, Sliema, SLM 3190, Malta
Description: Its superb location on Tigné Point means that The Chophouse affords wonderful views across the harbour to Valletta, both from its modern dining room and heated terrace. The cuisine served here is influenced by culinary trends from across the globe and includes top-quality cuts of meat such as Scottona, Angus and Wagyu. These are hung and matured in an ageing cabinet in the dining room, and then grilled on one of the largest barbecue grills in Malta!

Name: Legligin
Address: Triq Santa Lucia 116/119, Valletta, VLT 1183, Malta
Description: This small, rustic restaurant in the historic centre has limited space and a vaguely bohemian feel thanks to its informal tables, ceramics and candles. Delicious, simple, home-made cuisine full of Mediterranean and Maltese flavours takes pride of place here, with just one tasting menu that changes almost every day. There’s a shorter menu at lunchtime, while dessert can be chosen separately from a mini dessert menu. Excellent bread baked in a wood-fired oven, olives, extra-virgin olive oil from Gozo, pasta, and slow-cooked meat are just some of the attractions here. Booking in advance is recommended.

Name: Caviar & Bull
Address: St George's Bay, St Julian's, STJ 3301, Malta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The name says it all, as the menu at this restaurant is based on a selection of different caviars and aged beef, the latter on display in a glass cabinet near the entrance. Although fish also makes an appearance on the menu, we recommend the excellent beef tartare or Argentine ribs, grilled and served with roast potatoes and sautéed onions. The location is delightful and includes a cocktail bar, where chef Gauci’s recipes are listed in a personalised book, alongside a selection of Cuban cigars. The service is elegant and attentive, akin to dining in a private club.

Name: 59 Republic
Address: St George's Square, Valletta, VLT 1190, Malta
Description: This basement restaurant is cosy and characterful but, if it’s sunny, the terrace overlooking the Grandmaster's Palace is the place to be. Generously sized dishes blend classical French techniques with Mediterranean flavours. The 'bites to share' are imaginative, and Beef Wellington is the house speciality.

Name: Ta´ Frenc
Address: Daħla Ta' Għajn Damma Street, Xagħra, XRA 9010, Malta
Description: The reputation of this beautifully restored farmhouse goes before it. It’s been run by the same team for many years and the traditional Mediterranean cooking makes use of the island’s best ingredients. Many of the tasty dishes have a modern touch; some, like the Crêpes Ta’ Frenc, are prepared at your table.

Name: Marea
Address: Marina street, Kalkara waterfront, Kalkara, KKR 1521, Malta
Description: This chic, contemporary-style lounge bar-cum-restaurant near the Grand Harbour boasts fine views of the marina. The menu features Mediterranean cuisine alongside more Asian-influenced options, while the excellent wine list includes sparkling wines and a good choice of cocktails. Perfect for a relaxing meal, with an extensive outdoor space that adds to its appeal.

Name: AceroRosso
Address: Via Rovignan 1, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description: This secluded mountain chalet immersed in verdant woodland boasts a welcoming dining room with a decidedly Alpine feel thanks to the profusion of wood and a warming open fire. The cuisine is also regional in style, featuring local recipes and ingredients albeit with a contemporary touch. Popular dishes include the rack of lamb cooked at low temperature and served with creamed sweetcorn, leek fondant and its own jus.

Name: Iris Ristorante
Description: Not far from the 12C Basilica di San Fermo, this restaurant is housed in the Palazzo Soave (formerly Palazzo Malaspina Bottagisio). This historic address boasts highly elegant rooms with the “fishbone”-style stonework typical of Roman buildings and vaulted ceilings that provide a pleasant contrast to the restaurant’s contemporary furnishings. Your meal begins a journey back through the city’s history, as appetisers are served in their own special setting in the palazzo’s 14C wine cellar which has Roman origins, after which you return to the dining room to enjoy the rest of your meal. The talented chef here creates regionally influenced, balanced and imaginative dishes with a “green” focus. The menu also features fish, especially from the Adriatic, while the wine list boasts over 800 labels with a particular emphasis on France and the Veneto.

Name: Umami
Address: Via Ugo Secondo Partigiano 1, Badalucco, 18010, Italy
Description: A young chef with experience in renowned restaurants has taken over the old kindergarten in this village and transformed it into a delightful restaurant. Here, he serves contemporary cuisine, often influenced by local traditions and showcased on tasting menus from which individual dishes can be ordered à la carte style. In summer, there’s an attractive outdoor space practically on the banks of the Argentina river, which gives its name to the valley in which this village is situated.

Name: Almondo Trattoria
Address: piazza Gran Madre di Dio 2/l, Turin, 10131, Italy
Description: This simple yet charming restaurant located just a few metres from the Gran Madre church serves a fine array of regional Italian dishes. Although specialities from Piedmont understandably take pride of place, the menu takes guests on a culinary journey throughout Italy and the changing seasons, featuring dishes such as scialatielli pasta with seafood, Puglian stuffed meat rolls, and zabaglione with traditional hazelnut cake from the Langhe. There’s also a good selection of gluten-free options.

Name: Opificio
Description: A modern restaurant in the province of Padova which, over the past ten years, has grown and evolved from a gastro pub to the top-quality eatery that it is today. The cuisine is fairly eclectic, featuring meat and fish dishes alike, with the option of a lighter menu at lunchtime. The best dishes are showcased on the à la carte and are often made using luxury ingredients such as foie gras, scampi and Wagyu beef. The impressive wine list demonstrates a passion for international sparkling wines, while the excellent selection of wines by the glass is further enhanced by a choice of cocktails (also available at midday).

Name: Osteria Bakaré
Address: Via Venezia 30, Peschiera del Garda, 37019, Italy
Description: This small but beautifully kept restaurant set back from the lakeside serves contemporary-style cuisine that includes a good balance of meat and fish recipes, all made from top-quality, seasonal ingredients. Dishes are creative and full of individual character, with the occasional nod to Asia. Attractive enclosed veranda.

Name: Amo Bistrot
Description: Traditional features such as exposed stone walls and wooden ceilings provide a pleasant contrast to the contemporary-style furnishings at this restaurant housed in the charming Palazzo Forti, while the attractive cloister with its old walls and soft lighting is highly recommended in the hot summer months. The cuisine combines traditional meat and fish dishes with Asian fare, including the option of sharing small dishes such as tapas or bao (steamed buns). There’s also an excellent brunch on Sundays.

Name: Agriturismo Ferdy
Address: Località Fienili, fraz. Scalvino, Lenna, 24010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Once you’ve left your car in the car park and crossed the Brembo river, you enter a fairytale setting of meadows and horses surrounded by the Orobic peaks. Here, the cuisine is a declaration of love for the mountains – although occasionally technical and complex, it is always rounded and full of flavour, with meat and dairy produce taking centre stage. Guestrooms and a shop selling typical local produce complete the picture at what is an extraordinary, high-end agriturismo.

Name: Fratelli Bruzzone
Description: The Bruzzone brothers deserve a round of applause for this restaurant and its extraordinary traditional Piedmontese cuisine. In just two small dining rooms (booking is recommended), guests can choose from an unforgettable array of dishes including anchovies in green sauce, baked onions with bagna cauda (an anchovy-based dip), superb agnolotti (stuffed pasta), tripe, chicken, bonet (a type of dessert) and hazelnut tart with zabaglione. With so much choice, it’s difficult to stop eating – and once you’ve left, you’ll want to return as soon as possible!

Name: Dogma
Description: This restaurant may be small (booking is recommended) but it has a big personality. The focus here is on fish and seafood, with nearly all the dishes cooked (at least partially) over the barbecue grill, including desserts! The talented, original young chef creates dishes full of intense and convincing flavours.

Name: Innesti
Address: via San Pietro 8, Pergine Valsugana, 38057, Italy
Description: Daniele and Elisa are a couple of young restaurateurs who are familiar to us from their time at Blumenstube in Sant'Orsola. Having moved on, they have now opened their own restaurant in Pergine, where both the decor and the cuisine are contemporary-Alpine in style. As in currently in vogue, their dishes are showcased on three tasting menus (short, medium and long) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. All the recipes have a creative feel, demonstrating the chef’s playful approach to his contemporary ingredients.

Name: Lo Scalco Grasso
Description: A small, intimate restaurant with a welcoming ambience and simple yet lively feel, where the owner-chef at the helm in the kitchen also makes an appearance front of house. Mantuan traditions are evident in the generous portion sizes as well as in dishes such as the legendary pumpkin tortelli (served with butter or a tomato and sausage sauce), while other options are more creative in style – the Emilian lamb tartare delicately flavoured with its own cooking juices, and served with sautéed chard, savoury sbrisolona cake and black truffles from the lower Mantova region in season is particularly delicious.

Name: Oblige
Description: This new address with a cocktail bar and bistro (Noblesse) in the centre of historic Vignola is also home to a gourmet restaurant (Oblige), where chef Angelo serves easily identifiable yet technically skilful dishes. We recommend the game dishes cooked over the barbecue grill, such as the delicious local guinea fowl served with mustard mashed potato and sautéed radicchio. The wine list features labels from Italy and further afield with something suitable for every dish, including a few bottles that will appeal to wine connoisseurs.

Name: Anto e Robi
Description: Situated in the heart of a small town surrounded by rice fields, this restaurant has a charming and personalised feel. The cuisine is often (but not always) based around fish, which is showcased in dishes inspired by regional traditions. While Robi oversees the front of house with skill and expertise, offering recommendations on wine (over 300 labels, including many by the glass) and rum (his particular passion), Anto prepares a host of delicious recipes in the kitchen.

Name: Sa Domu Sarda
Description: Despite being an island, Sardinia’s traditional cuisine tends to focus on meat dishes, and you’ll find some of its best-known specialities served at this restaurant, with its simple dining rooms and typical local décor. Enjoy evocatively named dishes such as “sitzigorrus cun bagna” (snails in a tomato sauce), Bue Rosso “bombas” (meat balls), delicious Sardinian pastas such as “malloreddus”, “culurgiones” and “fregula”, stews, casseroles and meat fillets, as well as the famous “sebadas” and “su pappai biancu” (a type of blancmange) desserts.

Name: Simpar
Address: Rúa Do Vilar 47, Santiago de Compostela, 15705, Spain
Description: In this restaurant, fronting one of the city’s emblematic cobbled streets leading to its famous Praza das Praterías and cathedral, they are proud to say that Simpar’s daily menus are always built around ingredients sourced the same day from trusted suppliers, whose names they are also happy to share with guests. In the contemporary-style interior, featuring a spacious bar at the entrance, young local chef Áxel Smyth showcases his fresh and creative Galician-inspired cuisine with a touch of elegance on two menus (Conocer and Simpar), plus a limited à la carte featuring dishes taken from the former. Strong technique adds immensely to the dining experience, and every menu has the option of adding an extra dish (an updated version of the traditional tripe with chickpea stew) to it. One of his signature dishes is Galician-style fish of the day, which changes with the seasons and is accompanied by crushed potatoes and a three-textured “ajada” sauce.

Name: Taberna de Libreros
Description: Located in the very heart of Salamanca’s historic quarter, just a few steps from the monumental Plateresque façade of the university featuring the famous sculpture of a frog (or is it a toad?) popular with tourists, this restaurant boasts a stylish setting with a classic-cum-contemporary feel. Based around seasonal ingredients sourced from around the province, the à la carte includes interesting international influences – the result of experience acquired by owner-chef Alberto Hernández in countries as diverse as China, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand, Mexico etc. Attractive set daily menu.

Name: Anhelo
Address: Maestro Ripollés 6, Castelló de la Plana, 12003, Spain
Description: The heart and soul of this small restaurant in the centre of town is owner-chef Cristian Granero, who began his career as a baker and pastry chef, both of which served as a good apprenticeship before he headed to the kitchen stoves. His cuisine, the aim of which, in his own words, is to “wake up the senses and connect with the emotions”, is based around three menus: the “Route of Flavours”; “Past, Present and Future”; and, lastly, the eponymous “Anhelo” (the latter, a tasting menu, requires prior booking at least 24hr in advance).

Name: Shinkai Tastem
Description: This restaurant, one of the trailblazers for Japanese cuisine in the city, has embarked on a new path by reinventing both its dining space and its cuisine, with the latter continuing to showcase the essence of Japanese cooking but from a more contemporary perspective. Shinkai, which means “deep sea” in Japanese, highlights a plethora of flavours though its varied and extensive array of maki, temaki, sashimi, tempura and Wagyu beef sourced directly from Japan. It also offers a tasting menu that needs to be booked a minimum of 24hr ahead.

Name: Olivos
Description: This discreet and intimate restaurant close to Sants railway station is one of those that is easy to miss but continues to gain new admirers. Through its name, Argentinian-born chef Ezequiel Devoto pays a mini-homage to the country of his birth –Olivos is the district of Buenos Aires in which he grew up. His Mediterranean and globally inspired cuisine (a fusion of flavours from Argentina, Spain, Italy and elsewhere) is not short on creativity and is showcased on several tasting menus. Given its small size, Olivos only has a capacity for eight guests, so it advisable to book a table in advance.

Name: Miga
Address: Arco de la Estrella, Cáceres, 10001, Spain
Description: Located on the main square (Plaza Mayor), right next to the legendary Arco de la Estrella which provides access to the medieval walled city, this restaurant occupies an old two-storey house that now brandishes a contemporary interior. The à la carte, featuring dishes with a hint of tradition such as “pringá” gyozas, “migas del maestro” (a speciality made with breadcrumbs) with pork belly and free-range egg, and the grilled Retinta beef tenderloin with apple, is complemented by a tasting menu entitled Las Niñas (The Girls), in honour of the owner-daughters’ father, renowned chef Eustaquio Blanco.

Name: Espacio Amunt
Description: In this bistro, occupying the first floor of the award-winning L'Antic Molí but with its own separate entrance, chef Vicent Guimerà has diversified the food options available through cuisine which still reflects the essence of his cooking but in a more informal way. Based around tradition but with a few contemporary touches, his two menus (Bistró and Gran Bistró) continue to extol the virtues of seasonal ingredients from the Terres de l'Ebre, Terres del Sénia and the Parc Natural dels Ports. Dishes you’ll find on these menus includes chicken ravioli in broth, rice with cod and romesco sauce, and veal with quince and cauliflower.

Name: Kabuki Madrid
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Kabuki Group’s latest culinary venture, in the heart of the city’s Salamanca district, remains faithful to its roots, inviting guests to explore dishes with their essence in Japanese cuisine but with an Iberian touch – a concept which has been synonymous with the Kabuki brand over the years and its desire to transport guests back to Japan. In this spacious setting, with its restrained lighting and meticulous decor, the cuisine is centred on a tasting menu complemented by an extensive cocktail menu.

Name: Borona Bistró
Description: A small, centrally located restaurant that takes its name from the famous corn bread traditionally eaten in the north of Spain, particularly in Galicia and Asturias. The couple in charge (Víctor in the kitchen and Rocío front of house) create cuisine that is high on detail and pays dutiful respect to the culinary traditions and flavours of Extremadura, while adding a contemporary touch through modern technique and presentation. The cooking here is based around three tasting menus entitled Jariza, Jaramago and Mercado (the latter, shorter and more affordably priced, is only available on weekdays). One dish that particularly stood out was the suckling pig’s ear with white prawn tartare, which is always on the menu but with a garnish that changes with the seasons.

Name: Alberte
Description: Here, owner-chef Alberte Gutiérrez’s aim is to offer high-quality, non-gimmicky cuisine based around the very best Galician meat and vegetables but with a special focus on the incredible fish and seafood from the Rías Baixas region (spider crab, lobster, langoustine, shrimp from local estuaries, wild bream etc), almost all of which are sourced from the fish auction in A Guarda. The seasonal à la carte shows a penchant for dishes cooked on the open grill, alongside interesting daily specials and two tasting menus (Esencia and Alberte).

Name: Il Gattopardo
Description: Il Gattopardo is a charismatic Italian restaurant that possesses a certain je-ne-sais-quoi. The chef personally comes to your table to present his signature Sicilian dishes, which he continuously revamps with exciting new takes – for instance, crème brûlée made with butter-soft octopus alongside an exquisite potato cream enhanced with seaweed. He is meticulous both when crafting intricate sauces and filling home-made ravioli with gorgonzola. Be sure to peruse the wine list, which features a tempting array of fine Italian wines.

Name: Gitane
Address: Jan Pieter Heijestraat 146, Amsterdam, 1054 MK, Netherlands
Description: This restaurant's pavement terrace, where you can soak up the atmosphere of the trendy Oud-West neighbourhood, and its round windows certainly draw the eye. The Zen-style interior with its distinctive 1970s feel is equally impressive. This is a casual dining establishment, which opens its doors at 10am, every day of the week. The Mediterranean dishes served here have a lot in common with the recipes of Yotam Ottolenghi. Take, for example, the braised pork cheeks with creamy orzo, crunchy oyster mushroom, Petroto cheese and a fresh yoghurt and celeriac purée – what a beautiful plate of food! The chef makes sure that there are plenty of vegetarian and vegan options on the menu, and he keeps his prices affordable. One of Amsterdam's gems!

Name: CouCou
Description: With the mixologist doing their thing behind the imposing bar, the hip CouCou is reminiscent of a London cocktail bar. Whether you prefer to watch the chefs work their magic or enjoy a more intimate meal, this chic establishment has the perfect table for you. The wide range of sharing options on the menu is equally appealing and on trend. These are inspired by French and Mediterranean cuisines and given an original twist. Take the beautifully crispy fried lobster and prawn roulade finished with a lobster bisque gel and velvety pine nut cream. Délicieux !

Name: Le Jardin
Description: Behind the dark blue façade on the Mariaplaats, plants and cacti dominate the floral decor at Le Jardin. The front of the restaurant is more intimate; the back is brighter and airier, but it is cosy and inviting throughout. This is a lively place, both in terms of the atmosphere and the cuisine. "Groentenomie" is the name of Tamara de Borst's culinary concept, which builds on vegetables and herbs; meat or fish can be added, if you wish. Rooted in French tradition, her cuisine incorporates innovative twists and occasional Asian seasonings. Think fleshy pumpkin with a herby crunch, a fruity jus with mandarin and a succulent pollock fillet. Garden produce at its best!

Name: Sabero
Description: The names Sonja and Nico Boreas have been synonymous with excellence on the Dutch fine dining scene for many years. They have decided to work on a smaller scale in this cosy living room-style restaurant, but without compromising on quality. Hostess Sonja provides service with a personal touch while chef Nico wows diners with his culinary artistry and bold flavours. He knows the secret to creating sauces with real depth, and likes to make his mark with seasonings from far-flung places. The unusual addition of koji to his beurre blanc elevates briefly seared scallop and briny oyster. A wonderful dining experience is guaranteed!

Name: Niemeijer
Description: Janick and Leonie Niemeijer's light and airy restaurant has a distinctly natural and serene feel to it. The couple have put together an extensive à la carte menu and take great pride in their garden, from which they source vegetables and honey, among other produce. These are showcased in creative dishes that often incorporate a nod to Dutch culinary tradition. The way the chef cooks quince from the garden in a cassis syrup with hibiscus and combines it with full-fat vanilla yoghurt, almonds and fresh lemon sorbet is testament to his eye for presentation and his talent for marrying flavours. Unbeatable value for money!

Name: Restaurant Markant
Description: This cosy little establishment outside Breda city centre bears its name well. The fact that the staff take great pleasure in spoiling their diners is palpable. Decorative features such as wine crates show that Markant is driven by a passion for wine as well as food. Be sure to take a look at the wine list, which features all sorts of great finds, before perusing the extensive à la carte menu. The young chef's repertoire includes classics such as œuf en gelée, as well as vegetarian options and the occasional Asian-influenced creation. His attention to quality is evident in the generosity of flavours and depth of the sauces. Some dishes are prepared right at your table, which is a nice touch.

Name: Sea Palace
Description: With statues of Chinese warlords Guan Yu, Liu Bei and Zhang Fei, pagoda motifs and wooden chinoiserie everywhere you turn, the level of detail in the decor of this floating restaurant is extraordinary. You may be just a stone's throw from Centraal Station, but you feel like you are in a Ming dynasty palace. The wide-ranging menu is an ode to authentic Cantonese cuisine. Think steamed dim sum with prawns, stir-fried noodles with beef and soy sauce. The Peking duck (for two) is certainly a tempting option. A memorable culinary adventure that won't break the bank!

Name: Novaela
Description: Novaela encapsulates the magic of the Bagijnhof, a historical beguinage. The blend of upscale contemporary design and old architectural features is unique – as, for example, in the oval stone counter and the wooden beams. Daniel Duijster Gomero's cuisine is all about creativity, excitement and beautiful presentation. His surprise menu features some daring ideas such as the unexpectedly harmonious combination of razor clams and beetroot, but also familiar dishes like succulent quail fillet with an exquisite jus. You only have the choice of a six-course set menu and lunch, but you are definitely in safe hands with this chef.

Name: Garlic
Address: 44 Soi Chotiwat, Bang Sue, Bangkok, 10800, Thailand
Description: Head to this unassuming yet charming restaurant for Thai home-style cooking in Bang Sue district. For over 40 years, diners have been relishing the cosy ambience and a Thai menu that favours seafood over meat. The crispy pork pairs up with a distinctive apple sauce; the tom yum coconut soup is enriched by the flesh of young coconut for a flavour that is a delightful deviation from the norm. Call ahead to nab a table at this neighbourhood gem.

Name: Janhom
Address: 273/4 Soi Ramkhamhaeng 21, Ramkhamhaeng Road, Wang Thonglang, Bangkok, 10310, Thailand
Description: Aunty Paew has been serving intense southern Thai cuisine for over 20 years, using daily fresh ingredients to inform a changing menu. The chef makes her own curry paste, and signature dishes include Kaeng Tai Pla fish curry and stir-fried sataw beans with shrimp and aromatic shrimp paste. The deep-fried frog with turmeric is another standout. Chilled watermelon refreshes the palate after this fiery feast.

Name: Khaan
Address: 14/3 Soi Som Khit, Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: The new restaurant of Chef Sujira 'Aom' Pongmorn, Khaan – meaning both "tiger" and "proclaim" in Thai, roars with impressive Thai flavours, while shining a spotlight on ingredients and the provinces from which they're sourced. The chef's use of modern techniques means her culinary creations, served in an elegant space decked out in deep red hues, retain all their characteristic depth. Opt for the tasting menu, paired with wine or tea, to elevate the experience.

Name: Sriruen Pad Thai (Ruenchit Road)
Address: 48 Ruenchit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen,, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Chef Sriruen handcrafts exceptional Pad Thai, just as she has done for over 30 years. Originally from Phitsanulok, she serves noodles notable for their bold flavour, imparted by duck eggs. Savour this tasty dish with either thin rice or glass noodles.

Name: Ponyhof Stammhaus by Tobias Wussler
Description: The sort of restaurant you would love to have in your own neighbourhood, thanks to its excellent cuisine. The next generation has now taken over the management of this long-standing family business. The kitchen serves modern dishes, but also classics such as cordon bleu and “dry aged” beef from the charcoal grill.

Name: Joseph Naus Stub'n
Description: This comfortable rustic-style restaurant (named after the first climber to reach the top of the Zugspitze) is not just an attractive place where you are looked after by very friendly staff; the food is also really good and fairly priced. For overnight stays the Hotel Zugspitze has well-kept guestrooms done out in a country-house style.

Name: Hirschen
Address: Breisgauer Straße 47, Freiburg im Breisgau, 79110, Germany
Description: Hirschen boasts two restaurants. One is in the traditional Baden-style with lots of wood and small alcoves, and the other is light, bright and friendly with a small winter garden. The food is fresh and uncomplicated and includes dishes such as Wiener Schnitzel with spring vegetables, and pork loin medallions with spinach. The roast duck is also a speciality.

Name: Goldener Karpfen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this historical house, seasonal international cuisine with classic regional roots is prepared from select fresh produce. Tip: the classic beef tartare. To be accompanied by a choice of international wines. The interior is elegant and cosy at the same time; in summer you can sit outside. For overnight stays there are comfortable guestrooms ranging from stylishly refined to modern chic.

Name: Traube
Description: Run with great dedication in the heart of the old Rohrbach district, this lovely traditional restaurant has a cosy interior featuring a blend of traditional and modern elements. Chef Ole Hake's ambitious dishes are made with carefully selected regional ingredients, for example excellent game. His commitment to sustainability is palpable. The seasonal seven-course set menu comes in an omnivore or vegan version. There is also a well-curated wine list with an emphasis on German labels. These can also be enjoyed in the wine bar with snacks or a light meal. Tip for motorists: the public car park at the nearby Thorax Clinic is convenient.

Name: Weisser Bock
Description: Pretty details such as wood panelling and historical photos contribute to the cosy atmosphere in this traditional establishment. The kitchen serves up a fine selection of dishes made from regional and international ingredients, from which you can choose a three- to six-course menu. The à la carte menu includes appetising dishes such as "beef tartare, anchovies, brioche, caviar" and "turbot, wild cauliflower, capers". The hotel of the same name has comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms. The central location is another trump card.

Name: Hofgut Hohenkarpfen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant enjoys a wonderful location in the middle Baden-Württemberg's oldest nature reserve and boasts stunning views – it's well worth booking a table on the terrace. In what was once the dairy of the over 300-year-old farmstead, diners are pampered with delicious food and attentive service. The modern cuisine incorporates classic and regional influences, as well as international, sometimes Asian touches. The former barn of the heritage-protected estate has been transformed into a hotel with attractive and cosy minimalist-style guestrooms. Tip: Take the time to look around the art museum.

Name: Bachmaier
Description: Ulrike and Otto Bachmaier have been running their restaurant for many years. In addition to a modern interior done out in a palette of warm colours, they propose friendly and competent service under the direction of Mrs Bachmaier, as well as her husband's seasonal cuisine. There are different set menus to choose from, also vegetarian by arrangement. Good wine pairings.

Name: Das Ballenberger
Description: A friendly, modern restaurant in the centre of the old town close to the historic Krämerbrücke bridge, Das Ballenberger serves seasonal, international cuisine including scallops with two kinds of asparagus and orange. You’ll also find some mouthwatering home-made cakes and a delicious breakfast from 9 am after a stay in one of the five charming overnight apartments.

Name: Zenzakan
Address: Taunusanlage 15, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description: Somewhat hidden away, this elegant and stylish restaurant is accessible via a rear courtyard. The interior is done out in dark tones with dimmed lighting, and it smacks of the Far East (the terracotta warriors are eye-catching). The atmosphere is lively, and contemporary beats provide the acoustic backdrop. The menu includes a wide selection of pan-Asian dishes ranging from sushi and sashimi to classic curries and robata grill specialities – the braised beef short ribs are a real classic.

Name: Il Cortile
Description: You get to this restaurant, which is located in Erfurt's old town in a pretty little courtyard, via Johannesstraße. In a cosy atmosphere, diners tuck into fresh, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine – either in the form of the set menu or à la carte. The dishes adhere to the seasons, and there is a new menu every three weeks.

Name: Hebelstube
Description: This establishment has been a familiar and beloved landmark for decades. The long-established Hotel Alte Post offers contemporary-style guestrooms, and the restaurant serves a modern take on classic and regional dishes, such as salmon trout ceviche or dry-aged saddle of back, prepared by new chef duo Nicolas Volk and Christoph Dees and team. The wine list predominantly features labels from the region. Diners can also look forward to a friendly and charming atmosphere, as well as attentive service. The terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: HIO
Description: "HIO" is the nickname of the small village that is home to this restaurant. In the seven-course tasting menu proposed here, vegetables take centre stage. Much of the produce comes from the restaurant's own garden or from local farmers. The chic and modern interior incorporates a smattering of rustic touches, with the open kitchen being a focal point. With just 16 seats, the dining space has an intimate feel. The service is friendly and attentive, without being stuffy or overly formal. In addition to HIO, the HILZHOF also houses the MEIER restaurant and has a number of guestrooms available.

Name: Hohenhaus Grill
Description: This is the second restaurant of the idyllically situated Hohenhaus hotel, a magnificent property laden with history. The eatery has a classic-meets-rustic-style interior and a warm atmosphere – plus a lovely 18C tiled stove. The cuisine is seasonal and based on premium ingredients, which are for the most part sourced from the region. It is a treat to sit on the terrace and take in the view of the surrounding countryside.

Name: Hirschen
Description: This restaurant and hotel of the same name are among the stand-out addresses in this valley, with a friendly team taking care of guests in the rustic yet elegant dining rooms. The chef prepares dishes based on Baden cuisine, with the occasional French touch. The menu includes a range of tasty dishes from local game to sea bass, chanterelle risotto and saffron sauce.

Name: Bastian's Restaurant
Description: This country inn with a tasteful bright interior and beautiful partly covered terrace focuses on culinary classics that evolve with the seasons. You can choose from the à la carte menu or try a surprise menu. Dishes served include, for example, pigeon with savoy cabbage, parsnip and truffle. The service is very friendly and charming.

Name: Lemabri
Description: Sarah Henke and Christian Eckhardt were both working in Andernach until recently (she at YOSO, he at PURS). Now they have set up shop in Boppard to delight diners with their exciting culinary concept, which revolves around dishes to share. The menu features a broad selection of their personal favourites, from sashimi and beef tartare to spicy prawns. Other options are regional specialities, Asian and Korean-influenced fare, Italian pasta dishes, and pizza from the large Morello Forni brick oven that stands in the centre of the chic, modern dining space.

Name: Kupferpfanne
Description: Erwin Weidenhiller's restaurant, in a central location opposite the town hall, has been a classic on Fürth's food scene for decades. In the comfortable and elegant interior, they serve classic cuisine with seasonal and international-Mediterranean influences, made with good-quality produce. Tip: the reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: [maki:'dan] im Ritter
Description: Housed in the historical part of the Hotel Ritter, this exceedingly cosy and tastefully decorated restaurant serves modern cuisine in the evenings. The "Signature Menu" comprises four or five courses, and wine pairings are available on request. Alternatively, you can choose à la carte. Tip: the delicious sourdough bread from the Müller Bäckerei in Durbach! If you are wondering about the name, makidan comes from the Persian and encompasses the notion of delicacies, conviviality and hospitality. Consider the option of staying overnight – it's worth it!

Name: Landgasthaus Schuster
Description: An elegant atmosphere in this well-run restaurant serving good regional and international cuisine.

Name: Stüble
Description: Stüble is the tasteful, rustic-style à la carte restaurant of the chic wellness Hotel Lauterbad! In this wood-panelled parlour, you can soak up the cosy atmosphere while the friendly staff take care of you, serving fresh traditional, but also more modern, dishes. The hanging spit is a speciality here.

Name: Margaretenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This former farmhouse boasts a truly idyllic location. Inside, there are lovingly decorated rooms; outside, a wonderful garden terrace. Then there are your dedicated hosts and the excellent cuisine that ranges from regional to Asian, including sushi. Late Oct-Mar: "Wine & Dine" set menu on Friday evenings by reservation only. Try the afternoon tea (Sun and public holidays, 2-4.30pm).

Name: Weinstube Sibylla
Description: A good place to come for unpretentious cuisine. The menu ranges from classics such as Wiener schnitzel or Berlin-style calf's liver to a "Gourmet Tradition" section featuring dishes such as saddle and shoulder of venison in pasta sheets, with tenderstem broccoli and an elderberry jus. There is also a selection of vegetarian dishes and a range of delicious desserts. Lovely old wooden floors, wood-panelled walls and pretty decorations make for a charming atmosphere. The verdant terrace is also inviting. Guestrooms are available in the adjoining Erbprinz hotel.

Name: Lohninger
Address: Schweizer Straße 1, Frankfurt on the Main, 60594, Germany
Description: Set on the banks of the River Main in Frankfurt, this restaurant tastefully blends the classic flair of the old building in which it is housed – beautiful high stuccoed ceilings, herringbone floors – with modern minimalist design. The cuisine draws on the Lohninger family's Austrian roots as well as international influences, and the menu has been divided into two sections accordingly: "Die Heimat" (homeland) and "Die Welt" (the world). The dishes stand out for the quality of their ingredients, their finesse and intense flavours; the kitchen team led by chef-patron Mario Lohninger deliberately avoids gimmickry and places the emphasis on flavour. Their Austrian classics such as Wiener schnitzel also go down a treat. The front-of-house team is friendly, attentive and pleasantly relaxed – anything but stuffy.

Name: Bistro Fatal
Description: It would be a shame to not to get to know Alexandre and Sarah Bourgeuil's pleasantly unpretentious bistro, because the food is excellent. Why not start with a pastis as an aperitif, accompanied by some house-baked baguette with butter? You could follow that with skate à la grenobloise served with mashed potatoes and mesclun salad, and then finish off with crêpes Suzette for dessert. Delightful terrace in front of the building. NB: Finding a parking space nearby is not easy.

Name: Kronenschlösschen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant has a stylish painted ceiling and pretty terrace with adjoining garden. A set menu is served, from which you can also choose à la carte, and the wine list is also one of the best in Germany. Alternatively, try the bistro. Guests can also stay overnight in the hotel of the same name in charming, well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: Villa Feer
Description: Owner Kathrin Bucher has been running this restaurant in an attractive old villa near Lörrach exhibition centre since 2012. Dine in the cosy, bright interior or, in summer, out on the wonderful terrace. They serve lunch only: until 3pm you can order the set menu or from a small menu compiled from favourite dishes of the last decade. After that, there are desserts and ice creams/sorbets until 5pm.

Name: schuberts
Description: Located in the centre of town, right by the Lauter River, this popular restaurant has a casual brasserie feel and serves flavoursome regional and seasonal cuisine that draws on Mediterranean influences. The daily special, "Schuberts Schneller Teller" ("Schubert's Quick Plate"), is a hit at lunchtime. Entennest is a cosy and charming wine tavern that makes for a more rustic alternative – the menu is the same here in the evening. If you would like to stay overnight, the hotel of the same name has attractive individually furnished guestrooms.

Name: Gasthaus Stappen
Description: This restaurant run by a dedicated team has a cosy and modern feel, with clean lines, warm tones and decorative details. Outside, the garden terrace is also inviting. The cuisine is regional and replete with international influences. Ask about the wine tastings in the wine shop. Tip: There are chic, modern guestrooms should you wish to stay overnight. Note: card payment only.

Name: VIDA
Description: This place has it all: stylish decor, creative international cuisine and friendly service – and it's good value for money. Diners are offered a choice between the "Vida" set menu - also vegetarian - and à la carte dishes. Tip: order caviar with your steak tartare! If you prefer something a little more casual, sit at one of the high tables or at the bar and try some of the ambitious bar food.

Name: SCALA - Das Turm Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Take in the fantastic view of the city and surrounding area from the striking JenTower from 128m above street level! The cuisine is modern and international: dinner takes the form of a sharing menu (vegetarian also possible), and there is a good-value lunch. Tip: from the Neue Mitte multi-storey car park, take the lifts up to the restaurant (there is a sign). Hotel on the floors below the restaurant.

Name: TISK
Description: Situated in a quiet side street of Neukölln, TISK (old German for table) calls itself a Speisekneipe (food pub) – and the description works well. It offers a young, urban ambience and modern German cuisine with pepped-up flavours. Options include set menus (e. g. with meatballs or knuckle of lamb) and roast chicken for two people.

Name: Zur Mühle
Description: In their well-established restaurant – it’s been in the same family since 1895 – Hermann and Kerstin Berger prepare internationally inspired cuisine such as sliced salmon in a rocket and pesto crust with teriyaki beans, mashed potato and sweet mustard. The interior is cosy with a modern note.

Name: Sonne
Description: The comfortable Wellness Hotel Sonnenhof welcomes you to its cosy restaurant with fine dining standards. The inviting upscale space is perfect for enjoying Baden cuisine infused with Alsace influences. Look down through the window in the floor and you'll see some excellent wines stored below – the selection is extensive. On days when the restaurant is closed, Sonnenstüble stands in as a somewhat simpler alternative.

Name: Locanda Grappolo d'Oro
Description: It really is a joy to dine at this restaurant, which has been run by the same family with great dedication for years. The decor is bright and cheerful, and warm hospitality and service come courtesy of the lady of the house. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is fresh and delicious. The pasta, the gnocchi, the bread… It's all house-made. No wonder this place draws so many regulars from the region.

Name: Gasthaus
Description: Like the gourmet restaurant, Gasthaus also combines modernity and tradition, from the decor down to the menu. While things are a bit more casual here, the cooking is also really good – the quality of the sauces alone will convince you of that! You can put together your own menu – and even make it vegetarian. Friendly service.

Name: ZEN Japanese Restaurant
Description: Located in a residential area, this restaurant is a firm favourite with fans of Japanese cuisine. In a pared-back Far Eastern-style setting, diners can look forward to a pleasantly lively atmosphere, as well as friendly and professional service with an authentic Japanese touch. It is clear that a well-coordinated team is at work here. Your options include gyoza, tempura, grilled and pan-fried dishes, udon, sushi and sashimi, plus a large omakase set menu.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: A big name on the fine dining scene, Tim Raue has created a pleasantly down-to-earth brasserie of the sort you might be more inclined to expect to find in Paris. This place has a modern feel tempered by a slight touch of nostalgia. The food is excellent, and the intriguing menu changes every three months. Along with the à la carte selection, there are always three set menus to choose from: "Colette Classics", the "Tim Raue Menü" and a vegan one.

Name: Nagels Kranz
Description: This restaurant sets great store by the first-class ingredients it uses to create dishes such as confit Arctic char with sautéed asparagus, peas & hollandaise. The good food is more than matched by the friendly atmosphere, whether you eat in the cosy dining room or on the secluded terrace in the courtyard.

Name: Cornelia Poletto
Description: A really appealing restaurant in a great location! The upscale, modern and elegant interior is a delightful setting in which to enjoy the fresh Mediterranean cuisine. With clear Italian influences, an interesting three-course set menu is served at lunchtime; in the evening, a larger set menu is proposed, along with a selection of delicious à la carte options. Be sure to try the antipasti! The service is friendly and professional. Tip: In summer, there are also a few tables on the pavement in front of the building. Between the restaurant and the cookery school, Paola's is a bar-cum-deli – ideal for an aperitif or cocktails.

Name: Gasthof zum Kranz
Description: Built in 1769 and run by the same family for seven generations, the interior at Zum Kranz is modern and elegant in the minimalist style. The kitchens produce flavoursome, classic, international fare. If you come in the autumn, make sure you try the game!

Name: Hirsch Genusshandwerk
Description: This lovely village inn serves dishes with classical foundations and modern inspirations. The seasons call the shots, and there is a preference for quality produce sourced locally or even grown in the restaurant's own garden. The friendly and dedicated front-of-house team helps create the welcoming atmosphere. Delightful terrace.

Name: VEN
Description: This place sets itself apart with its loft vibe and a streamlined urban chic design. International cuisine inspired by the region and the seasons. Then there is the extremely friendly service. The sheltered terrace in the inner courtyard also beckons. VEN is located in the Innside by Meliá hotel, which proposes stylish guestrooms.

Name: Zum Krug
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This place has a long history that stretches back to 1720, and the Laufer family has now been at the helm for three generations. Behind the gorgeous historical façade, the cosy dining spaces exude traditional charm. Theregional and international cuisine takes its cue from the seasons, and the menu includes dishes such as a Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) of organic pasture-fed beef with potato dumplings and cranberries. The friendly and professional waitstaff will be happy to recommend fine Rheingau wines from the estate to accompany your meal. Delightful courtyard terrace. Smart guestrooms – some are especially modern.

Name: Planerts
Description: Casual fine dining near the church (Nikolaikirche) and opera house (Leipzig Oper). The high ceilings, exposed ventilation shafts, urban design and open kitchen create an on-trend industrial-style interior in which to savour cuisine with Asian influences. The dishes can be combined to compose a set menu or chosen à la carte. Friendly service and good wine recommendations. Thu-Sat, lunch takes the form of a dish of the day or a three-course set menu.

Name: Grüne Gans
Description: Housed in a former locksmith's shop in a building dating from 1825, this restaurant has been a culinary favourite since opening in 2007. Here in the heart of the old town, diners can look forward to French-international cuisine with seasonal influences and a cosy, modern feel. Lovers of Flammkuchen are also in for a treat. Tip for fine summer days: Head to the secluded terrace in the courtyard.

Name: Rebstock
Description: Rebstock offers comfortable, country-style dining rooms, attentive service and good regional fare including snail soup, pike dumplings and venison ragout. In summer the idyllic terrace offers views of the surrounding parkland and the Black Forest, while another attraction is the large selection of home-made cakes and pastries.

Name: handicap.
Description: As its name suggests, this tasteful restaurant employs people with disabilities, and the success of the venture is clear to see in the great team! Diners choose between two set menus: "Einerseits" (vegetarian) and "Andererseits" (with meat and fish). The sleek and stylish decor sets off the artwork to perfection, with a painting of the sky by Markus Schmidgall adorning the ceiling. On fine summer days, head for the very pleasant terrace.

Name: Hinterding
Description: For many years the stately former doctors' villa has been known for offering good food in a stylish setting. Dine in the comfortable and elegant high-ceilinged space or out on the lovely terrace. The service under the direction of the owner is charming; the food cooked by her husband using select produce is classical in style.

Name: Caro's
Description: Once a student pub, Caro's is just a stone's throw from the beautiful Marktplatz and Rathaus. The restaurant is laid out over two floors and boasts a cosy interior featuring wood panelling and furnishings. In summer, tables are set up outside on the pavement. The menu comprises fresh contemporary cuisine, from ceviche to Iberico pork chop and sea bream, but there are also vegetarian options. Across the street, Speisekammer is a delicatessen under the same management, which sells high-quality foods and spirits.

Name: Weingärtnerhaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not only does this place promise good food, but the setting is also inviting: the restaurant is located in a lovely winegrower's house (named after the vineyards below). Built in 1542, it stands directly on the historical estate of Schloss Leitheim. Season-driven cuisine is served in a lovely, cosy interior. On Sundays and Mondays there is a more limited offering in the form of the Azubi-Menü devised by the trainee chefs. Tip: The wine list includes a number of South African vintages. Should you wish to stay overnight, the Schloss Leitheim hotel has inviting guestrooms.

Name: Alfredo
Description: If you are looking for authentic Italian cuisine in Cologne, Roberto Carturan is your man. His father, Alfredo, laid the foundations for upscale Italian cuisine in 1973, and the second generation of the Carturan family has cultivated a straightforward and minimalist style of cooking. The chef himself is responsible for the friendly, informal and elegant atmosphere: he likes to spend time with his guests and talk them through the dishes. Besides cooking, Roberto Carturan has another talent: he is a trained singer – on Friday evenings there's the "musical culinary soirée": a five-course menu with a bout of singing as the finale! One practical tip: Parking is available in the Opern Passagen shopping centre located behind the restaurant. You might also take the opportunity to see the original 4711 store with its famous carillon.

Name: Alte Mühle Thomas Höreth
Description: With this individual and thoroughly charming establishment the Höreth family have created a wonderful retreat. The guest lounges are lovingly decorated and the inner courtyard is idyllic. This is a real gem of a place, which also has its own wine estate. Slightly higher up, charming rooms are available for guests to stay the night.

Name: Ambiente Italiano - Alte Oberförsterei - Ristorante & Trattoria
Description: Dating from 1902, this inviting villa entices guests with its scenic location and excellent cuisine that caters to all tastes. In the trattoria, the menu features Italian classics, pasta made in-house or freshly caught fish, as well as a selection of pizzas. Ristorante Ambiente Italiano, meanwhile, serves more sophisticated dishes that draw on Italian influences. The terrace with its stunning views of the Main River is a summer highlight! The service is friendly and attentive. Good to know: There is a car park directly in front of the building.

Name: Gruber's Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Austrian cuisine is served in this charming restaurant with its various tastefully decorated rooms and pretty terrace. Whether traditional (such as the excellent schnitzels and memorable Kaiserschmarrn – shredded pancakes) or modern (Carinthian cheese noodles, pointed cabbage and blueberries), the dishes are always made from carefully chosen ingredients. More limited options, plus a schnitzel menu at lunchtime.

Name: Landgrafen
Description: The restaurant close to the observation tower, also known as the Balcony of Jena, serves regional cuisine and offers a fantastic view over the city. Three individual rooms are available: country, Art Deco or honeymoon.

Name: Chambao
Description: Sharing is the focus of this appealing restaurant. Good-quality ingredients go into imaginative dishes that you can combine as you see fit to create your own set menu. Some tables afford a view into the glass-fronted kitchen. The staff are friendly and professional, and you can confidently follow the wine recommendations. Chambino bar and bistro is located diagonally opposite. Gorgeous lively terrace overlooking the Alte Brücke (Old Bridge).

Name: Die Kurfürstenstube
Description: A classic in the city! The mighty coffered ceiling and wall panelling with beautiful inlays preserve a piece of history. The cooking is classic with modern influences. Summer restaurant in season.

Name: Heritage
Description: Heritage offers a fantastic view of the River Alster and appetising cuisine to boot. Menu options include international dishes such as the North Sea turbot with black beluga lentils and lime Hollandaise sauce, as well some delicious smelling (thanks to the 800° US Southbend Broiler) prime mature steaks.

Name: NIKKEI NINE
Description: You should not hesitate to make a reservation at this culinary hotspot in Hamburg. Located in the luxurious Fairmont Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, the restaurant has a stylish and elegant ambience, courtesy of an interior done out in dark wood, cream and gold tones. On the menu: Japanese-international fusion cuisine. The service is very friendly and attentive. They also have a cool bar.

Name: CARALEON
Description: This tastefully designed restaurant is housed in the small boutique hotel of the same name, which enjoys a fabulous location in the Wasserburger Bucht and boasts stunning lake views. À la carte options include classics such as beef tartare, Caesar salad and braised veal cheeks. There is also the seasonal fine dining set menu. Friendly and professional service. Tip: Head to their Sunset Lounge for a nightcap by the lake.

Name: Zum Adler
Description: Bearing its name of old, this modern restaurant carries on the tradition of the original 19C Zum Adler inn. Today it is lovely and light inside, with a smart and minimalist decor. The focus lies squarely on high-quality meat, such as its dry-aged Angus beef steak. Fish and vegan options also available.

Name: Brechtmanns Bistro
Description: Brechtmanns is an extremely popular, friendly minimalist-style modern bistro serving Asian-inspired dishes as well as regional cuisine. We recommend trying the dishes prepared from the Oldenburg duck. In summer, meals are also served outside.

Name: Eiden Restaurant
Description: The location of this hunting lodge, set amid almost 25 acres of parkland, is superb. The lovely restaurant includes a conservatory and a wonderful garden terrace.

Name: Kamino
Description: The Zumkeller family (who also run the Adler restaurant) have transformed what was once Chämi-Hüsli into the cosy Kamino. It serves fresh Mediterranean cuisine incuding tapas and dishes such as pan-fried octopus and prawns with a mojo sauce and Moroccan couscous. These stand alongside classics such as suckling calf sweetbreads with a Merlot jus, tagliatelle and snow peas. For an overnight stay there are two pretty, comfortable rooms.

Name: Puricelli
Description: Here you can enjoy seasonal, regional and Mediterranean cuisine in a wonderful location. On the menu, for instance, supreme of Eifeler Prachthahn (cockerel), tagliatelle, basil sauce, sautéed green vegetables. Inside, a friendly, pared-down ambience, modern with rustic touches, from the terrace you have a view of the Rhine. The wine list showcases the surrounding region.

Name: Weinbistro "George"
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This bistro is definitely worth a visit. The second dining option in the Weinhaus Uhle hotel is a wine shop and appealing restaurant that is open all day in one. Seated at bare wooden tables in an attractive space, you are served tasty dishes made from regional produce, such as "Der Pilzgarten" (The Mushroom Garden) – mushrooms from the Helvesiek mushroom garden in cream with bread dumplings. And of course, Müritz zander is also on the menu. Decent wine list. In summer, there are tables laid out front on the street.

Name: Wolfs Junge
Description: The accent here is on sustainable, regional cuisine, the very epitome of “nose to tail” eating. The ingredients are sourced from selected producers with some of the vegetables and herbs grown by the restaurant itself. Serves simple midday fare such as home-made bratwurst and an ambitious, creative set menu including Angeln Saddleback, kimchi and fermented onion in the evenings.

Name: east
Description: This restaurant, housed in the stylish hotel of the same name, is quite striking on account of the fantastic industrial architecture of the former iron foundry and the slick, chic interior. The centrepiece here in what was once the factory hall is the sushi counter. The menu features modern international dishes. A tip for meat lovers: fine steaks from the Southbend Grill.

Name: Zipang
Description: The minimalist interior at Zipang has clean lines, muted colours and a smart silver sheen. This makes a perfect match for chef Toshiharu Minami’s mix of traditional and modern Japanese cooking styles. The restaurant is popular with Japanese diners – always a good sign.

Name: Meet & Eat by Sandro
Description: Hotel Stadt Tuttlingen is located on the Rathaussteg across the Danube, and on the ground floor you will find this pared-back, modern restaurant. The star of the ambitious cuisine is dry-aged beef. But on the menu you will also find dishes such as roast turbot and potato, kohlrabi, red wine butter. To the front of the house is the covered terrace facing the pedestrian area.

Name: Gänsweid
Description: In this carefully restored former garage, it is a case of ‘olive oil not engine oil’! Enjoy your meal in a relaxed atmosphere where you can watch the cooks preparing their fresh mixture of Swabian and Mediterranean dishes in the kitchen. Simple, good value menu only at lunchtimes.

Name: Zum Storchen
Description: This establishment is run by the Trienen family in a beautifully renovated old townhouse. The food here is exceptional; the cuisine is seasonal and regional, drawing on modern and international influences. Tip: Try the daily specials as a set menu. There are two pleasant terraces: one out on the pavement, and one in the courtyard to the rear of the building, which is quieter. Comfortable modern guestrooms.

Name: Lammershof Stuben
Description: To start with, the location on a 45ha estate is terrific. The cosy space with a tiled stove that draws the eye exudes rustic charm and a certain chic. Specialities include various dishes featuring meat from bison they have reared on their own farm. Note: On Mondays only bison burgers, or veggie burgers, are served. Tip: the marvellous terrace with a view of the countryside! The small Lammershof hotel, the main building of which dates from 1709, has cosy guestrooms.

Name: Jagdhaus Waldfrieden
Description: Choose whether to dine in the cosy dining room with its open fireplace, in the airy conservatory or on the lovely terrace shaded by trees – this restaurant is a charming location in which to enjoy good regional food. The menu includes, for example, veal shoulder cooked sous vide. Tip: The lunch menu is very reasonably priced. Should you wish to stay overnight, the pretty guestrooms are very inviting and all individually decorated.

Name: Alois-Anton Kaminrestaurant
Description: A good alternative to the fine dining restaurant of the Park-Hotel Egerner Höfe.
