The choice is yours: dine in the cosy Bavarian-style dining rooms dubbed "Alois" and "Anton" or in the more upmarket Kaminrestaurant. Just as charming is the terrace, which is sheltered from the wind and has a view of the pastures and mountains. Either way, you can enjoy cordial service and regional and seasonal dishes in a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Pierburg - Erika Bergheim
Description: Located in the rural outskirts of Essen, Pierburg has been welcoming diners since 1901. With many years of experience in the top league of gastronomy under her belt, Erika Bergheim is now at the helm, cooking up internationally and seasonally inspired dishes. You can choose from the à la carte selection, named "Pierburg Karte", or opt for the "Selection E.B." set menu – the individual courses can be ordered à la carte, too. There is also an extensive, well-curated wine list. Friendly service and a tasteful contemporary setting, with certain tables affording a glimpse into the kitchen. Gorgeous terrace.

Name: Redüttchen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: What was once the gardener's cottage at the 18C La Redoute ballroom and concert hall now promises not only a charming atmosphere but also ambitious cuisine. Modern dishes such as medium-rare roasted saddle of venison with cranberries, quinoa and beetroot are served with savvy wine pairings.

Name: CARLS Brasserie an der Elbphilharmonie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As you take in the view of the Elbe River and the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, you can soak up the lively and casual yet elegant brasserie atmosphere and enjoy sophisticated North German cuisine such as fish stew or whole sole. The unique location means that window seats are in demand. And in summer, diners make a beeline for the terrace. The bistro next door serves bowls and tartines. A wine bar is also part of the premises.

Name: Schneider
Description: This restaurant has been run by the same family ever since it first opened in 1884. Stefan Püngeler now represents the youngest generation at the helm, putting the emphasis on good seasonal produce. Mediterranean and French-classic inspired dishes are served, as well as a gourmet set menu. There are also a few classics on the menu. The wine list focuses on labels from the region. Accommodation is available in the small Sonnenhof hotel in the neighbouring village. For hikers, Dernbacher Haus on the edge of the forest is perfect for a pit stop.

Name: Caroussel Nouvelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the attractive Hotel Bülow Palais in Dresden's Baroque quarter, the bistro and winter garden have been combined in the Caroussel Nouvelle, with a stylish interior by star designer Carlo Rampazzi. The "Classics" menu is available for lunch and dinner, along with two "Gourmet" set menus (one is vegetarian) in the evening – also with à la carte options. Palais Bar and Cigar Lounge for aperitif or digestif.

Name: Puricelli
Description: In keeping with the historical setting of the lavishly renovated 19C Schloss Lieser (the striking faÇade of which is quite something), Puricelli has a high cross-vaulted ceiling, lovely old wooden flooring, crystal chandeliers and stylish furniture. The view through the picture windows takes in the garden and the Moselle. Contemporary classic cuisine is offered. The wine list includes bottles from the hotel's own vineyard. Pretty guestrooms.

Name: 20zwanzig
Description: Nestled in a quiet location on the outskirts of town, Hotel Freiwerk's core building is a spruce half-timbered villa dating from 1894. Its restaurant, 20zwanzig, is housed in the modern extension, built in 2020. The chic, trendy interior has a large window front that affords a splendid view of the surrounding greenery. You can order the contemporary seasonal cuisine à la carte or opt for a surprise menu comprising a variable number of courses. Friendly and well-trained waitstaff.

Name: Chang Bistro
Description: This smart and trendy bistro version of the main restaurant, Chang, in Grünwald features mostly Thai cuisine and dishes with influences from Japan and China. Here, too, the emphasis is on high-quality ingredients. The Thai curries as well as the sushi can be highly recommended. Additional lunch specials. Lovely terrace, as well as covered winter garden-style dining space.

Name: Hartmaier's Villa
Description: This modern restaurant is housed in a pretty villa dating back to 1816. The Hartmaier family and their team have been serving up good food here for many years. The menu is wide-ranging, characterised by seasonal, regional and international influences – from Zwiebelrostbraten (steak with onion rings), beans with bacon and roast potatoes to wild-caught Icelandic redfish fillet with pak choi and spinach and ricotta ravioli. At lunchtime, people flock here for the bargain set menu with a choice of starters and mains. The feel of the place is both elegant and more casual, with a lovely leafy terrace in front of the building. Tip: You can buy wines to take home at their Vinothek.

Name: zeit|geist
Description: The centuries-old Walk'sche Haus in the heart of Weingarten abounds with charm. Outside it's the pretty half-timbered façade that catches the eye; inside, the combination of sleek modern design and a touch of rusticity makes for a particularly pleasing ambience. Sebastian Syrbe cooks up modern dishes based on classical foundations, such as "onsen egg, soy, spinach, nut butter" or "suckling pig, beetroot, horseradish, chives". You can choose à la carte or opt for a surprise menu comprising four, six or eight courses. Tip: In summer, be sure to get a spot on the gorgeous terrace overlooking the Walzbach stream! For a more wallet-friendly alternative, head to stil|bruch. There are also pleasant guestrooms, should you wish to stay the night here.

Name: new josch
Description: Located in a residential area on the Killesberg, this restaurant boasts an inviting rear courtyard terrace and an impressive interior; sleek design, soothing tones and warm wood finishings make for an upscale and tastefully modern setting. Competent service comes courtesy of a charming front-of-house team. Opt for "Lacher's Fine Dining Menu" (to be ordered in advance) or choose from the appealing à la carte selection. Astute wine recommendations are also provided. There are two attractive lounges on the first floor.

Name: Adler
Address: Obere Dorfstraße 4, Wangen im Allgäu, 88239, Germany
Description: Ambitious, fresh and unfussy are the terms that best describe the mixture of regional and international cuisine offered by Uwe Zöller at this slightly out-of-town restaurant. Front of house, friendly Anne-Kathrin Zöller serves a range of dishes including scallops with Thai curry, and duo of lamb on a bed of wild garlic pesto with Barolo jus.

Name: Alte Feuerwache
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Linear design, a relaxed atmosphere, as well as competent service and good food make this restaurant so popular. See into the kitchen and watch the tasty seasonal, regional and international dishes being prepared.

Name: Grenzhof
Description: At Grenzhof, chef Sebastian Andrée and his team serve up modern cuisine that has a sharp focus on the seasons and their produce. In nice weather, the Kastanienhof is an absolutely idyllic place; on less clement days and in winter, the Gutsstube with its rural-style decor is a welcoming setting. At lunchtime only a lunch buffet and short set menu. For overnight stays, there are pretty, cosy country house-style and themed guestrooms.

Name: Strandhaus
Description: A "beach house" in the middle of Bonn? The charming decor has maritime flair and is the perfect fit to the pleasantly informal atmosphere. Not forgetting the cosy secluded terrace. The cuisine is built on classical foundations, drawing on seasonal produce and scattered with modern touches.

Name: PIER 6
Description: In this stylish restaurant located in the Havenwelten quarter, a friendly front-of-house team serves modern international cuisine. This is made with produce from the region and the menu is determined by the seasons. In addition, there is an inexpensive lunch menu. The window seats and terrace are especially coveted – the view of the New Harbour is beautiful. Given the popularity of this place, it's definitely best to book in advance.

Name: Pfälzer Stube
Description: Pfälzer Stube is as important for the gorgeous Krone hotel as the hotel is for the town of Herxheim-Hayna. Centrally located, this is a traditional, family-run business. The space has ample charm, with diners comfortably seated at attractively set tables inside, or, in summer, out on the leafy terrace. On the menu: regional and seasonal food with Italian influences – in keeping with the chef's roots, although he also puts a distinctly modern spin on proceedings. Dishes such as "roasted Venetian calf's liver, tagliolini, Blutwurst, apple, shallot" can be selected à la carte or you can combine three or four courses to create your own set menu.

Name: Landhaus Halferschenke
Description: In this beautiful quarry-stone building dating from 1832, the Schmah family serve ambitious cuisine that revolves around top-notch ingredients and the seasons – from sole meunière and Aubrac beef to oysters and turbot from Brittany. You can opt to dine à la carte or go for a set menu. In addition to the food, diners can look forward to attentive service in a tasteful setting with a country-house feel. In summer, the gorgeous terrace beckons. In addition, MA PETITE CHAMBRE is a small gourmet haven serving a set menu. They have four well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Sawito
Description: In this pleasant restaurant done out in a timeless, refined style, chef Marco Wahl injects quality, flavour and personality into seasonal dishes – this is where the Palatinate-born chef's experience in some prestigious establishments comes into play. You can dine à la carte or opt for the set menu. Tuesday to Thursday (except public holidays) they also offer a surprise menu with three to four courses. The fact that you feel in good hands here is also down to the very friendly service team under the management of Patrik Schwabe.

Name: Kantiners
Description: Steeped in tradition, this family-run business is now in its fourth generation. Kantiners is a tastefully designed restaurant that specialises in seasonal and regional cuisine. Pretty terraces front and back. The cosy bar is also nice. The Hotel Waldkrug proposes lovely guestrooms should you wish to extend your stay.

Name: Das Alte Haus
Description: In this attractive, cosy yet modern restaurant, the cooking is ambitious and creative with international influences. You can put together dishes from the menu to create a set meal with the number of courses of your choice, to be accompanied by an extensive selection of fine German wines. There is also a pairing menu. Delightful terrace.

Name: bistronauten
Description: A word to the wise: make sure you book, as this really appealing restaurant is always busy! Housed in an old railway station dating from 1903, the atmosphere is laid-back, the decor modern with industrial charm and the food excellent. On the blackboard there is a seasonal set menu – choose between meat, fish and vegetarian for the main course. They also have a selection of German wines. Dine at the counter to watch the chefs at work in the open kitchen.

Name: Gasthof Kreuz
Description: This traditional hotel and restaurant located at the edge of the pedestrian area has a gorgeous terrace overlooking the Gut Betha Fountain. On the menu: regional and seasonal cuisine, including locally hunted game. In addition to à la carte dishes, there is an inexpensive three-course set menu ("Regiomenü"), to be relished in a pleasant atmosphere. The wine list has some surprising rarities in store, and the service is cordial and attentive. They offer several immaculate guestrooms in the building itself, plus holiday apartments within walking distance. You can park free of charge just a few minutes' walk away (Parkplatz Bleiche).

This restaurant is located in the Elberfeld district in a narrow street full of eateries, bars and small shops. With its unpretentious, trendy decor, the friendly and laid-back service, as well as its ambitious cuisine, this place is a hit! The dishes are modern and seasonal, drawing on Mediterranean and classical influences, from pickled Arctic char, elderflower tomato stock and tarragon oil to wild mushrooms, mashed potatoes, chives and nut butter foam. You have the option to create your own set menu – conventional or vegetarian. Lovely courtyard.

Name: Taverna & Trattoria Palio
Description: Palio offers fresh Italian fare from the open kitchen in a relaxed trattoria-style atmosphere – you simply have to try one of the pasta dishes! The seasonal set menus are also interesting. There’s also a lovely terrace in the shade of some old chestnut trees.

Name: Gasthaus Lege
Description: This spruce inn blends seamlessly into the landscape of the sleepy village of Thönse. A comfortable dining experience is guaranteed at this warm and welcoming restaurant run with great dedication by Claudia and Hinrich Schulze. And that's to say nothing of the terrific cuisine, which comes in the form of two set menus: "Gaumenfreude" and (vegetarian) "Gartenliebe" – available in three to seven courses. The classic dishes – such as courgette flower, salmon soufflé, lemon thyme – bowl diners over with their excellent ingredients and meticulous craftsmanship. Under the tutelage of Claudia Schulz, the waitstaff are friendly, competent and well drilled; they also provide astute recommendations when it comes to drinks.

Name: Adler
Description: Here, traditional Swabian meets cosmopolitan, regional meets international. Enjoy cordial service in the comfort of either the main dining room steeped in history or the charming inner courtyard. The kitchen serves up seasonally influenced dishes. There are chic rooms for overnight guests. On Tuesday evenings, the restaurant is open to hotel guests.

Name: Al Pappagallo
Description: You will feel at ease in this elegant restaurant with a lovely bright winter garden and also wonderful outdoor garden. The kitchen serves classic Italian dishes, prepared with very good produce – a particular highlight is the pasta. Friendly service.

Name: VOLT
Description: This restaurant not only has an interesting industrial elegance due to its location in the former transformer station on the Landwehr Canal, it also offers distinctively modern cuisine. The menu features dishes such as sturgeon, onion and pointed cabbage and braised shoulder, black salsify and hazelnut, as well as a few vegan options.

Name: Asam Schlössl
Description: Shane McMahon is no stranger to Munich's gastronomy scene. In his charming restaurant just outside the city centre, the Irish-born chef serves tasty Bavarian cuisine into which he skilfully weaves his personal touch. Here you will find pub classics, but also modern dishes, as well as steaks barbecued in the Big Green Egg.

Name: Johann Grill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Overlooking Berchtesgaden, surrounded by stunning natural beauty and with a magnificent mountain backdrop, the location is to die for! At the restaurant of the luxurious Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden, you can enjoy delicious seasonal cuisine made with fresh, local ingredients. For dessert, we highly recommend the Eckerbichl-Haustorte! The sleek, modern interior design is a draw in itself. Incidentally, the restaurant is named after the first person to climb the east face of the Watzmann and Germany's first official mountain guide. Hotel guests can even take in the panoramic view here at breakfast.

Name: Genussschmiede
Description: This blacksmith's shop dating back to 1682 is now devoted to modern cuisine that follows the seasons and draws on fresh ingredients. The interior is pleasingly trendy and minimalist, with a dining area laid out beneath a high steel ceiling. Diners choose between a set menu and à la carte dishes. Vegetarians are also well catered for on the menu.

Name: Staudi's
Description: Once a butcher's, now a pretty little restaurant with a bistro feel. Decorative relics of the past such as tiled floors and stained glass in the ceiling make for a charming interior. Diners also enjoy cordial service and seasonal dishes with a modern twist – order à la carte or opt for the five-course set menu complete with wine pairings. A vegetarian alternative is available, too. From earlyNovember to early December, only the goose set menu is served on Wednesdays. "Fondue Chinoise" in winter has to be booked one day in advance. Tip: Stube can be booked as a separate room for private events (Nov-Mar).

Name: Schloss Hohenstein
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This stunning castle, which is mentioned in written records as early as the 14C, boasts an idyllic location in beautiful grounds. In addition to their tastefully decorated hotel, Alexandra and Andreas Rehberger run this appealing restaurant with a winter garden overlooking the castle courtyard. The chef-patron – no stranger to the restaurant scene – turns his hand to cooking contemporary seasonal cuisine with ingredients from the region; the proprietress delivers Austrian charm and good wine recommendations.

Name: Café GUPI
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Set up in what was the gardener's house on a historical country estate, this is the trendy restaurant-bar concept of the Düster and Schneider restaurateur and winemaking families. Their tasty modern dishes made with seasonal ingredients are served à la carte or as a set menu. In summer, the terrace shaded by the large trees of the lovely Läublin Park is highly inviting. The name of the restaurant is derived from the regional "GuPi" wines (Gutedel and Pinot Noir). Tip: Booking advisable.

Name: riva
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Hippo boasts a stylish, minimalist interior in bright, warm, natural tones, as well as pleasantly relaxed service and international/Mediterranean cuisine. The dishes emerging from the open kitchen include pan-fried monkfish with escabeche of vegetables and potato and olive mash. The pizzas area also delicious.

Name: Landhaus Rössle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Here the ambitious cuisine is classically French in nature with regional and seasonal influences – à la carte or as a set menu (vegetarian version also available). Charming service comes courtesy of the lady of the house. The interior is modern and elegant – the tables by the fireplace are popular in winter – and there is a lovely leafy terrace. Attractive guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Tomatissimo
Description: This popular restaurant with a friendly atmosphere lies slightly outside the city, in a small village. In summer you can make the most of the wonderful terrace by the village fountain, in the shade of the chestnut trees. Bernhard Grubmüller and his kitchen team serve up various set menus and à la carte dishes, including dry-aged beef from their own maturing cabinet, plus delicious offerings such as braised veal cheek, morels & peas, potato waffle & wild garlic. Tip: Bernhard's Küchentisch, the chef's table, for smaller groups (on prior reservation).

Name: Bocca di Bacco
Description: On the outside, a smart historical façade, on the inside an attractively modern and elegant restaurant complete with bar and lounge. Visible through its glass panes, the kitchen turns out Italian cooking. Needless to say, the pasta is home-made. To be paired with one of their great Tuscan wines.

The name of the game here is a culinary fusion of Peru and Italy. Drawing on his Peruvian heritage and inspired by life in Italy, head chef Matias Diaz weaves together produce from both countries in his "136 Experience Menü", a set menu that changes every two months. The restaurant's trendy vintage decor brims with charm. In summer, there are also tables outside.

Name: Restaurant 1463
Description: This half-timbered house dating from 1463 used to be a small wine tavern. Today it is a more upscale place with a cosy, rustic-style ambience. The menu lists classics, such as sea bass with artichoke and vegetable ragout. The inner courtyard is really secluded! There are six lovely comfortable apartments for overnight stays.

Name: Villa Rothschild Grill & Health
Address: Im Rothschildpark 1, Königstein im Taunus, 61462, Germany
Description: Located in a park, this smart bankers' villa dating from 1894 is home to a stylish boutique hotel as well as this chic, modern and elegant restaurant. Patrick Bittner, who previously made a name for himself at Frankfurt's Français, where he was head chef for many years, is now at the helm here. The cuisine is classic with international influences. Appealing dishes such as Breton sea bass with pickled king oyster mushroom, seaweed salad, dashi and bonito broth or Irish Hereford Prime beef "prime centre cut" with confit aubergine, pickled onion and chimichurri can be ordered à la carte.

Name: Die Reichsstadt
Description: This is the restaurant of the chic hotel of the same name, which provides the historical backdrop for your meal. The tasteful dining area is done out with high-end furnishings and a modern touch. Staff are friendly and professional as they set about serving you with fine Baden classics, modernised French dishes and various set menus, including a vegetarian one. In summer, the garden is magical!

Name: The Wild Duck
Description: This young and fresh addition to Hanover's fine dining scene is proving to be a hit – and with good reason. Part of the appeal is the upscale and tastefully trendy decor. Diners are also drawn by the modern and pleasingly pared-down dishes (eg cucumber and cherry or duck and parsnip), from which you can create your own three- to five-course dinner menu. Vegetarian and vegan options are available, too. The friendly waitstaff will gladly recommend the perfect wine accompaniment.

Name: Mühlenhof
Description: This family-run restaurant in the hotel of the same name is justly popular, for the food is well priced and the service fast and friendly. The seasonal, regional fare on offer includes dishes such as Baden pike dumplings in Riesling sauce. The good-value lunch menu is also a big draw. Don’t miss the delicious home-baked cakes.

Name: Phaedra
Description: Are you in the mood for Mediterranean cuisine with Greek influences? Then try, for example, the fried halibut with a chive beurre blanc and trout caviar or the house-made mezze – to share or as a starter. Good produce is used, including meat from Franz Keller and wild-caught prawns. The place has an appealingly trendy bistro look and a pleasantly relaxed atmosphere. Diners take their seats at regular tables or high tables – the latter offer partial views into the open kitchen. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park opposite.

Name: Medici
Address: Weißadlergasse 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: Two brothers are your hosts in this city centre restaurant. International dishes with a Mediterranean influence are served in a modern atmosphere.

Name: SonneStuben
Description: The regional and seasonal cuisine served here wins diners over with the flavours it exudes and technical prowess it evinces. The menu features mouthwatering options such as saddle of venison with a chestnut and parmesan crust or fillet of sea bass with seafood risotto. The pretty, cosy dining area affords views of the old town's historical half-timbered façades; having your meal out on the terrace that overlooks Marktplatz is a pleasant option. They are also open for lunch. Tip: It is worthwhile taking a stroll through the town. You can spend the night at Die Sonne Frankenberg hotel.

Name: Bistro Villa Merton
Address: Am Leonhardsbrunn 12, Frankfurt on the Main, 60487, Germany
Description: Villa Merton's bistro is a good alternative to the fine dining restaurant. Expect a refined culinary haven that serves tasty regional and international cuisine with seasonal influences in an attractive space with elegant touches. In addition, lunchtime during the week there is the option of a set menu. It is also pleasant to dine out on the terrace.

Name: Brasserie
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you don’t fancy the gourmet cuisine on offer at Meierei, you can enjoy fresh, international fare or just a slice of home-made cake in the less formal atmosphere of the Brasserie.

Name: Schlossberg
Description: The location on the Schlossberg (castle hill) is fantastic in its own right: located right beside the Vauban fortress, the business hotel that houses this restaurant overlooks the city and affords a one-of-a-kind view – best enjoyed from the terrace. However, the interior is also delightful with its sleek contemporary design, coupled with panoramic vistas through the expansive windows. The seasonal cuisine can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte.

Name: Frankfurter Botschaft
Address: Westhafenplatz 6, Frankfurt on the Main, 60327, Germany
Description: A really cool location - the spot directly on the Westhafen makes the terrace a real highlight! But it's also pleasant to sit in the smartly decorated interior; windows on all sides mean you also have a view of the water from here. The food is international. Furthermore, they also offer valet parking - it's best to put in your request when you make your reservation.

Name: Die Pfarrwirtschaft
Description: This is not merely Thomas Merkle's second restaurant, but a hotspot in its own right. The tasty food is wonderfully unpretentious and based on very good ingredients. Tip: Try one of the Black Forest beef dishes. The culinary experience is enhanced by friendly and attentive service, a pleasingly informal vibe and a really modern style with a rustic touch. In summer, needless to say, guests find themselves drawn to the beautiful garden. In short, a place that fosters a feeling of wellbeing!

Name: Haus Bosen
Description: This cosy half-timbered house, a restaurant for more than 120 years, now offers Mediterranean, regional and classic fare including squid Mallorcan style, vintage sardines with sourdough bread, Königsberger Klopse (meatballs in white sauce with capers) and braised pigs’ cheeks.

Name: Mon Amie Maxi
Address: Bockenheimer Landstraße 31, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description: Housed in a villa dating from 1925, this restaurant is chic, almost opulent – the wonderfully lively atmosphere is complemented by friendly, attentive and adept service. To the side is Raw Bar, and there is an open kitchen. The menu features French cuisine, including oysters, lobster cocktail, offal dishes and high-quality barbecued steak. Good, exclusive wine selection.

Name: XO Seafoodbar
Description: As well as haebel, just across the street, Fabio Haebel runs this trendy, laid-back establishment in the heart of St Pauli. Spread over two floors, the restaurant has an agreeably lively atmosphere. Upstairs there are also a few seats at a counter facing the open kitchen. The cuisine is modern with seafood specialties and vegetarian dishes. Options include daily specials and classics such as tinned sardines in oil with new potatoes, quark and dill. Alternatively, you could opt for "Chef's Choice" – a selection of items to be shared, picked from the menu by the kitchen team. There is also a small cocktail bar and a lovely terrace where you can enjoy the hustle and bustle.

Name: Landhaus am See
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasant dining experience: a lovely country-style interior, great terrace and views of the garden and lake. The food is seasonal and regional. You can also get hold of your own copy of their recipe book. For overnight guests, there are really pretty, individually decorated rooms available.

Name: Zum Goldenen Engel
Description: This traditional 16C inn right next to the church has been rebuilt in a way that is absolutely true to the original. You will feel completely at home in the lovingly decorated restaurant, thanks not only to the atmosphere and the competent, charming front-of-house team, but also of course to the high-quality food. Many ingredients come from the region. Plus they have cosy guestrooms.

Name: Gasthaus Landbrecht
Description: A typical Bavarian country house, home to this rustic restaurant serving tasty, locally grown produce.

Name: Eiflers Zeiten
Description: The pleasant, rustic-style alternative to Bembergs Häuschen has a distinctly cosy feel. The menu features mouthwatering regional classics such as roast Eifel beef with roast potatoes, as well as internationally influenced dishes such as cod with a lemon crunch topping and Chinese cabbage. There are also daily changing specials. The two chandeliers fashioned from bottles are sure to draw the eye! The view through the windowed façade onto the pond is also lovely.

Name: Weinstube Bach-Mayer
Description: In this historical wine tavern (the beautiful 18C portal harks back to its time as a royal hunting lodge), chef-patron Carsten di Lorenzi serves up seasonal regional cuisine that draws on international influences. The interior is cosy and rustic, with bare wooden tables and a pretty green tiled stove. Outside, there is the charming leafy terrace, aptly named the Gartenlaube (gazebo).

Name: Weinhaus Tante Anna
Description: This traditional family business is now in its seventh generation. Here you dine in the impressive historical setting of a 16C former chapel – the 1 000-year-old granite column by the counter is well worth seeing! The menu features sophisticated regional dishes, which can be accompanied by your choice from a large selection of German wines.

Name: Rôtisserie Jagdhof Stuben
Description: The cosiness and rustic charm of the Rôtisserie at the upscale Jagdhof Glashütte hotel are almost unparalleled – a wealth of wood panelling and beams, a roaring fireplace and the decorative remnants of what was perhaps the original kitchen all play their part. Factor in the amiable owner, Edmund Dornhöfer, and the attentive front-of-house team, too. Chef Petar Popovic delivers a wide range of classics. Excellent recommendations include "Petar's bouillabaisse" and the char-grilled veal chop with fresh chanterelles.

Name: Schwanen
Description: This family business has been going for three generations. The dishes served in this chic, modern restaurant are made with preference for regional produce and sing with freshness and flavour. For a bistro alternative, Karl Benz Stube has a short menu featuring traditional Swabian fare. There are also suitable spaces for special occasions available and practical guestrooms with contemporary decor. Tip: the "Kultur & Genuss" events.

Name: MIZU Sushi-Bar
Description: Located in the Spa & Resort Bachmair Weissach, not far from Lake Tegernsee, this restaurant boasts an understated Far-Eastern design. It serves a combination of classic and modern Japanese cuisine. Traditional sashimi and nigiri or tempura dishes feature on the menu alongside Nikkei-style dishes that are a fusion of South American and Japanese elements.

Name: Zehntkeller
Description: Located in the middle of the village, this traditional establishment serves good regional and seasonal cuisine. The menu features mouth-watering dishes such as braised beef cheek in a Pinot noir sauce. Opt for a four-course set menu or order à la carte. The house proposes its own organic wines. Very friendly and well-drilled service, a cosy interior, and a lovely terrace laid out under the wisteria. The hotel of the same name has stylish, classic guestrooms.

Name: Danzer's
Description: The contemporary ambience in a sleek and at the same time homely style makes for an appealing start – not to mention the terrace with a view of the dike. The food is international and regional, such as fillet of sea bass in bacon butter with wok-fried savoy cabbage. Short lunch menu.

Name: Zur Iphöfer Kammer
Description: This small historic restaurant is located on the market square at Iphofen, a pretty wine-growing town. The delicious fare, which includes dishes such as red mullet with ratatouille and breast of guinea fowl with risotto and girolles, can be sampled in the cosy dining room or outside on the lovely terrace. Excellent wines from the Wirsching vineyard.

Name: Brasserie Stadthaus
Description: This attractive brasserie with its striking high coffered ceiling and pretty interior courtyard promises a genuine French dining experience. Try the tourte de queue de boeuf (oxtail pie) or the seafood platter followed by the tarte au citron. All the wines are French.

Name: The Duchy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: On the first floor of the luxurious Breidenbacher Hof, overlooking Heinrich-Heine-Allee, this is an elegant brasserie. The cuisine is a broad mix, from sashimi and ceviche to beef tartare or ravioli, not to mention the steaks. They set great store by the origin of their ingredients, working with regional producers – and they keep their own chickens and cows. Decent wine selection.

Name: Setzkasten
Description: A fine dining restaurant in a supermarket? You can experience this novel culinary concept in the basement of The Crown, one of the largest food markets in Europe. It is not only the location that is worth mentioning: in addition to the smart decor and the partially open kitchen, the dedicated kitchen team turns out creative, modern and pleasingly pared-down dishes made using select produce. Chef Egor Hopp also successfully brings in influences from his Kazakhstan homeland, such as Smetana sauce or raschenka cream. There is a set menu comprising six courses in the evening and four at lunchtime. For a corkage fee, you can also consume wine brought from Zurheide Feine Kost. Top tip: If you really want to see what the kitchen can do, make a reservation at the chef's table. Those who arrive by car can make use of The Crown's multi-storey car park.

Name: Schweizer Wirt
Description: This place has been synonymous with tasty cuisine for years. The fresh, regional dishes are made with excellent ingredients. Stripped back to the essentials, they eschew any frills. The atmosphere in the restaurant is charming and the waitstaff are friendly. This beautifully situated traditional inn also has a fabulous terrace. You can park directly in front of the building.

Name: Saittavini
Description: Combining a bistro, wine bar and delicatessen, this friendly restaurant serves Italian food (including a lovely small antipasto counter). They also sell over a 1 000 different wines in the wine shop and a range of Italian specialities in the delicatessen.

Name: Adler Wirtschaft
Description: Established in 1993, Franz Keller's family-run Adler Wirtschaft is an institution in the region. Inside this charming little half-timbered house, the atmosphere is cosy and down-to-earth – traditional tavern culture is still alive and well here. The concept: you choose dishes to make up your own fixed-price menu. There are also mouthwatering steak options. They use pork from Bentheim Black Pied pigs and beef from Charolais and Limousin cows, sourced from their own farm in the Taunus region (Falkenhof). NB: The whole table will be billed together; credit cards not accepted.

Name: RIVA
Description: The fantastic location on the lake is a draw in itself – a spot on the lovely terrace with a view of the water is of course particularly sought after! But the interior of this bright, elegant restaurant inside the hotel of the same name is also appealing – the floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the lake can be opened up. The cuisine is based on classical and international influences, here and there with an Asian touch, and often on regional products. Chic bar and relaxed outdoor lounge.

Name: Michaelis
Description: Tasty and fresh food is served in this refined restaurant in a restored building from the Wilhelminian period, which also houses the comfortable hotel of the same name. The menu is seasonal – there are various set menus (one of which is vegetarian) and a sophisticated à la carte selection. Friendly and attentive service. In summer, the terrace behind the house is very appealing.

Name: Schuppen 13
Description: The Pusceddu family’s restaurant is located right on the marina and from the outside looks a little like a boathouse. The food within is classic Italian cuisine meticulously prepared using fresh produce. Try the delicious baby squid braised in tomato stock with pan-fried polenta.

Name: Wettsteins Restaurant
Description: This beautiful property is a little out of the way – on summer days, diners can enjoy sitting out on the terrace. The restaurant has been around for many years. In addition to cordial hosts and friendly service, the programme here includes regionally influenced cuisine, which you can choose to sample as a set menu or à la carte. The menu also features barbecued meat, such as rump steak, and classics like schnitzel and roast joint.

Name: Tafelhaus
Description: The tastefully modern restaurant of Neckartal business hotel is run with dedication. The regional cuisine draws on international influences and is made using top-quality seasonal produce. In summer, the attractive terrace is the place to be. In winter, Tafelhütte serves as an event location. Reservations for lunch and on Sundays and Mondays are possible by arrangement.

Name: Restaurant 1687
Description: This stylish, tastefully designed restaurant is tucked away in a narrow side street just off Unter den Linden. The cuisine is predominantly Mediterranean with hints of a few other international influences. Friendly and attentive service. Breakfast is also served here. In summer, you can make the most of the delightful terrace.

Name: Christoph Pauls Restaurant
Description: No stranger to the Rhineland's restaurant scene, Christoph Paul runs this trendy modern restaurant with his wife Juliane. The striking religious imagery on the wall is a reminder of the site's former vocation as a chapel. A seasonal three- or four-course set menu with a choice of dishes is served. The terrace laid out beneath venerable old trees is delightful. A parking space can be reserved upon request.

Name: Neidharts Küche
Description: Somewhat hidden away in an industrial area is the restaurant of Dagmar and Reiner Neidhart. Choose between the slightly more casual bistro area and the more elegant and classically done out restaurant complete with conservatory. Lovely terrace to the rear of the building. The cooking is seasonal and regional; charming service courtesy of the proprietoress.

Name: AL FORNO
Description: For fans of authentic Italian food, this ristorante makes for a pleasing alternative to JUWEL and WEBERSTUBE, the other two restaurants to be found here in the Hotel BEI SCHUMANN. Soak up the atmosphere in the wonderfully cosy dining area, in which Italian background music brings that feel-good factor, while the team in the open kitchen conjure up delicious fish and meat dishes, as well as classics such as antipasti, pasta and pizza cooked in the brick oven – the pizzas are available in smaller sizes, too. Desserts such as the zabaione di Marsala are also delicious. Speciality in winter: spaghetti from the parmesan cheese wheel. In summer, head for the pleasant terrace overlooking the SEEWUNDERBAR.

Name: Landgasthof Hirschen
Description: The dedication of chef Verena Martin and her team is palpable. In a charming setting diners enjoy cordial service and good food that is made primarily with produce from the region and draws inspiration from the seasons. The kitchen staff put their heart and soul into their work – the motto here is ä weng eppis Feins, or "a little something fine" in the local dialect. Tip: "Unser badisches Menü" or "Unser großes Menü" (for two or more people).

Name: Wieland-Stuben
Description: This restaurant serves classic, seasonal cuisine with dishes such as supreme of quail, balsamic lentils, apple and potato, and haunch of salt meadow lamb, bean ragout and carrot cream featuring on the menu. Although each delightful dish is different, each one is elegant and harmonious in flavour. Charming terrace for alfresco dining.

Name: Henriks
Description: Some ambitious cooking goes on in this elegantly designed restaurant, where the menu includes Asian, Mediterranean and regional cuisine with dishes ranging from Wiener Schnitzel to lobster. There’s a good selection of wines to accompany the food, plus a popular spacious terrace and lounge.

Name: Scala
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This modern restaurant boasts beautiful views across the lake and a delightful terrace. It also serves seasonal dishes with an emphasis on regional ingredients, and the vegetable and animal produce are used in their entirety. A smaller selection of dishes is served at lunchtime. Friendly service and fine wines.

Name: Schmidt's
Description: This restaurant is housed in the unlikely surroundings of the Hellerau Craft Workshops, originally founded by Karl Schmidt in 1909. Today the food on offer is fresh, flavoursome and regional, as well as creative. Try the pink roast leg of lamb with pointed cabbage and Saxony potato cakes.

Name: Baron.ess
Description: This trendy and stylish restaurant occupies an old bridge structure on the premises of the Brückenbaron event venue. When you enter, you can take a peek into the glass-walled kitchen before being seated in the airy dining space. The large windows look out onto the landscaped grounds, complete with a watercourse and fountain. Gorgeous terrace. A creative seasonal set menu is proposed, with an emphasis on sustainability. The chefs come to your table personally to talk you through the dishes. Franconian wine list with organic, ecological and natural wineries.

Name: C'est la vie
Description: This restaurant is dedicated to the French way of life. As you sit comfortably at your table in the stylish modern interior, looking out through the floor-to-ceiling windows, the dedicated team can be seen in the open kitchen, cooking up modern interpretations of really ambitious dishes, such as "Crevette – prawn, courgette, bergamot" or "Bœuf – beef two ways, chanterelles, potato". The creations are organised into two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, and accompanied by exclusively French wines; these are charmingly and skilfully presented at your table with the aid of a map. The wines can also be purchased in the shop. Tip: There is parking in the garage right next door.

Name: La Mer
Description: Having earned his spurs at some award-winning restaurants, most recently at Seesteg, owner and head chef Hilko Uphoffis, together with his partner Giulia Casto, is now at the helm of this smart restaurant located right next to the Michels Thalasso Hotel Nordseehaus, on the edge of the pedestrian/shopping zone. His classically French cuisine also demonstrates the odd modern flourish, as in the flambéed Chilean sea bass marinated in miso and cider. The restaurant itself is also inviting, with its beautifully bright, pared-down and modern interior, as well as its appealing terrace laid out in front of the large window façade.

Name: La Cantina by Catalana
Description: Located in the city centre, in an old townhouse accessible via a small courtyard, this restaurant is owned by Jan-Hendrik Feldner, who also runs the nearby ESTIMA by Catalana. As a connoisseur of Spanish cuisine, the chef proposes a down-to-earth tapas concept in his convivial, simple little establishment. The menu features authentically prepared small dishes mainly inspired by Catalan cuisine – it's best to order four or five. The chef also serves and talks you through the dishes.

Name: Dröppelminna
Description: The atmosphere in this pretty half-timbered house is rustic and cosy. The decoration is charming, with its antique pieces and all manner of ornaments, including the eponymous three-legged pewter coffee pots. The open kitchen sends out a varying array of classic dishes. Accompanied by fine wines, including a good selection from Alsace – the owner is a sommelier. Snug terrace.

Name: Ressmann's Residence
Description: The modern decor, with its sleek design and light, warm tones, is a hit with diners, as are the ambitious, international, seasonal cuisine and fine wines. Tip: At lunchtime, you can put together your own inexpensive three-course menu or simply order à la carte. For those hot summer days, one of the dining rooms is air-conditioned, but if you would rather sit outside, there is a lovely garden terrace tucked away behind the building. Overnight accommodation is also available.

Name: Vinothek im Weingut am Nil
Description: Set in a lovely period building, this combination of restaurant and wine shop works beautifully well. The upscale, chic interior is characterised by a blend of rustic and modern design features. In summer, make a beeline for the enchanting courtyard. The cuisine draws on global influences and is served alongside a selection of excellent wines from their own production. Tip: there are tastefully furnished guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Restaurant am Steinplatz
Description: A smart restaurant with open kitchen and adjoining bar, located in the lovely boutique hotel of the same name in the heart of Charlottenburg. In summer you can sit in the pleasant inner courtyard. À la carte and set menu options on the modern local cuisine menu in the evening. At lunchtime there is a small set menu. Be sure to check out the sparkling wine list!

Name: Wappen-Saal
Description: This imposing castle estate provides a truly unique setting for dining. Before taking a seat in the stately Wappensaal in the Schlosshotel at Burg Schlitz, take a leisurely stroll along the Goetheweg. Experience the historical ambiance of this restaurant as you savour a four- to six-course menu of ambitious classic cuisine beneath an impressive high ceiling. The charming and experienced staff will be happy to help you choose the perfect accompaniment to your meal from the well-curated wine list.

Name: Hubertushof
Address: Arzheimer Straße 5, Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, 76831, Germany
Location: Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, Germany
Description: Remaining true to the Südliche Weinstraße, Sandra Bernhard and Jochen Sitter moved from Birkweiler to this 300 year-old former coaching house, which they run with great dedication and charm. The chef cooks traditional and modern, but above all, flavoursome fare. Dishes include classics such as pan-friend black pudding and Saumagen (stuffed pig’s stomach). The interior courtyard is gorgeous.

Name: Westphalenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This stylish and sophisticated restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a residential area. Here, the Westphal brothers – one is the chef, the other the sommelier – delight diners with delicious food and excellent wine recommendations. The menu features international dishes that take their cue from the seasons, such as confit halibut fillet in nut butter, potato scales, cauliflower cream, dried tomatoes and Sardinian pasta. The walk-in wine cellar accommodates 120 different labels. The restaurant is also open for lunch on Saturdays and Sundays.

Name: Dorfkrug
Description: This historical building in the open-air village museum with its old farm implements, wooden beams and open fireplace is genuinely charming. The menu includes classics from the owner’s southern German homeland (calves’ cheeks with potato mash), as well as regional specialities such as pan-fried beef steak with onions and spätzle.

Name: Fischereihafen Restaurant
Description: This is and remains an institution – something of a home from home for Hamburg's fish lovers, young and old! A constant stream of international customers comes and goes from lunchtime to evening. In an elegant setting boasting traditional Hanseatic decor and a view of the harbour, quality fish from the fish market is served at the height of freshness. Classic dishes include turbot or lobster in different variations, but the menu also includes Asian and Mediterranean-influenced options.

Name: Alter Wirt
Description: This sizeable restaurant is in the centre of Grünwald. It serves Bavarian and international cuisine based exclusively on organic produce. Try the malt beer glazed roast pork.

Name: Cox
Description: Pleasant and laid-back – a bistro in the best sense of the word. A diverse cohort of diners enjoys dishes such as lamb fillets with pesto fried in brik pastry with ratatouille and fried capers. The service is friendly and attentive. Popular and inexpensive lunch offer.

Name: Villa Busch
Description: This beautiful, lavishly refurbished villa in an elevated location not only boasts a lovely terrace for summer, but the interior of the restaurant is also tasteful with its stuccoed ceilings, wooden floorboards and modern designer chairs. The chef-patron's kitchen team creates dishes with Mediterranean and Asian influences, including many fish specialities. Plus, you are waited on by a warm and charming front-of-house team.

Name: Kinfelts Kitchen & Wine
Description: Kirill Kinfelt, who made his reputation at TrüffelSchwein, has this restaurant close to the Elbphilharmonie concert hall. In a chic, modern interior, he serves regional and seasonal cuisine that is at once ambitious and down-to-earth. The excellent wine list has clearly been curated by a knowledgeable sommelier. Two time slots are available for evening reservations.

Name: EssensArt
Description: A bright, friendly restaurant fronted by a leafy secluded terrace with a lovely pergola. The cuisine is international with a few truly classic dishes. Great value for money.

Name: Butcher's american steakhouse
Description: At Butcher's american steakhouse you can enjoy fine Nebraska beef that the chef presents to the table personally. The cosy restaurant is dominated by dark wood and warm colours.

Name: Heimatjuwel
Description: Marcel Görke, no stranger to Hamburg's culinary scene, runs this minimalist, rustic-style and pleasingly informal little restaurant. Creative seasonal cuisine made from regional produce is served in the form of a vegetarian set menu comprising four or six courses – there is also an alternative main course of fish or meat. You have the option of dining at one of the tables on the small terrace lining the pavement.

Name: Witwenball
Description: This former dancing bar is now a trendy, modern deluxe bistro with pale green chairs and azure blue bench seats, shining marble tables, a striking white marble counter and decorative wine shelving. The themed menu changes every few weeks. There are over 300 wines to choose from as pairings to the delicious dishes – the emphasis here is on organic viticulture. The desserts are highly recommended.

Name: Brook
Description: International, German and classical influences are at play here, e.g. loin of lamb with string beans and Parmesan potatoes or venison with Brussels sprouts and chestnuts. In the evening, the beautifully illuminated Speicherstadt opposite is a sight to behold!

Name: Tschebull
Description: On the first floor of this exclusive shopping arcade the nods to Austria are everywhere: in the decoration -cowbells and edelweiss motifs on the ceiling, mountain panorama mural - and in the dishes, in the guise of classics such as Carinthian Kasnudeln, Wiener Schnitzel and apricot strudel. Beisl, serving Austrian tapas is more casual. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: LENZ
Description: Here you can enjoy regional cuisine in a friendly and modern atmosphere. Try the labskaus (a traditional northern German meat dish), braised veal cheeks, or red berry compote. There is also a simpler, more moderately priced lunch menu. The food is complemented by an appealing wine list, service is attentive, and the bright conservatory can be opened up in summer!

Name: Farmerhaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: African produce enriches the cuisine, which is international in character. Wood carvings and trophies from the country where the dishes originated are interesting to look at.

Name: Bahnhöfle
Description: The friendly host cooks French and international dishes. Prettily decorated by his wife, the restaurant radiates country charm. Lovely terrace at the front.

Name: Bistro oma & enkel
Description: oma & enkel ("grandma and grandchild") is the culinary concept at this pleasingly laid-back bistro in the long-established Posthotel. The name symbolises a bridging of the gap between the traditional and the modern. Recipes of yesteryear are given a contemporary twist. Choose between the "Franconian tapas" menu and the tasting menu. Both have optional add-ons and vegetarian versions.

Name: martino KITCHEN
Description: A charming bistro where friendly and attentive staff serve Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made using regional and seasonal ingredients. A choice of two set menus is available in the evening: one vegetarian and one omnivore. The restaurant is located in the Citta Trüffel hotel, which boasts chic guestrooms, as well as a delicatessen.

Name: Thuns Dorfkrug
Description: This restaurant offers beautifully laid tables, attentive service and good cuisine offering a mix of regional and international elements. The simple and elegant style of the decor features attractive contemporary pictures and parquet flooring. The guestrooms are in a clean-lined, modern style.

Name: Köllner's Landhaus
Description: Set in grounds covering 11 000m² this charming half-timbered house dating from 1589 is a picture-book property with a country house-style interior that certainly does it justice. Then there is the excellent regional and international cuisine. You might also choose to spend the night in one of the comfortable and modern guestrooms.

Name: WILD X BERG
Description: This chic little fine dining restaurant on the first floor of the tasteful Lammershof hotel serves modern cuisine that is ambitious and extremely technically precise. It takes the form of a set menu comprising a variable number of courses – a vegetarian version is also available if you order in advance. Select ingredients, including meat from bison reared on site. A few tables offer a view into the kitchen. Tip: Bison Bar in the rustic-style cellar.

Name: Reussenstein
Description: It doesn't get much more Swabian than this: not only is the menu exclusively regional, with dishes including Flädlesubb and Roschdbrooda, it is also written in the dialect. The glass-paned wall into the kitchen provides interesting glimpses behind the scenes, plus the service is really friendly. There is a cookery school in the vaults. Their rather novel "Spätzle Drive-in" is open throughout the day. This long-standing family business also offers cosy modern guestrooms.

Name: St. Urban
Description: Along with the fine dining restaurant Schwarzer Hahn, St. Urban is part of the appealing culinary microcosm of the lovely Deidesheimer Hof hotel, which is located right on the historical market square. The cosy interior exudes the traditional charm of a Palatinate inn. Good regional and seasonal cuisine is served, à la carte or as a set menu. The menu also includes the classic "Palatinate Favourite – Saumagen (stuffed pig's stomach), Bratwurst and liver dumplings with sauerkraut and mashed potatoes".

Name: Zucker
Description: The pretty modern brasserie with attractive exposed brickwork is located in a former sugar factory – as the name suggests. Aromatic seasonally inspired dishes are offered à la carte, supplemented by a set menu. The service is pleasantly uncomplicated, very friendly and well organised.

Name: Atable im Amtshaus
Description: Surrounded by the town wall, the Amtshaus boasts a lovely location in Freinsheim's old town, which is well worth a visit. The courtyard with its idyllic terrace leads to this chic restaurant, where you will notice a white cross vault supported by columns. Chef Swen Bultmann cooks classic French dishes that are made from fine ingredients and inspired by the seasons. The food is accompanied by an appealing and extensive selection of wines. There is also accommodation – in the tasteful guestrooms, as in the restaurant itself, the decor harmoniously incorporates modern design into the historical setting.

Name: Kö59 masterminded by Björn Freitag
Description: Björn Freitag, familiar from Goldener Anker in Dorsten, set up this interesting restaurant right on Königsallee, the shopping street known as the "Kö". The chic brasserie in Hotel Kö59 serves up seasonally inspired Rhenish cuisine, but international influences can also be detected on the menu. The menu ranges from Königsberger Klopse (meatballs in a white sauce with capers) to tartare of Simmental beef fillet with a mustard seed jus vinaigrette to fried king prawns with wild herbs and garlic.

Name: esszimmer das Restaurant
Description: Old floorboards, beautiful bare wooden tables and eclectic decoration make for a really comfortable atmosphere, almost as if you were in your own dining room. The cuisine is creative and made with high-quality and carefully sourced ingredients, many from the region - top for example Hamachi from Völklingen. There is a set menu comprising four to seven courses – including appetisers, a breadboard and salad, plus a petit four to finish.

Name: Trattoria
Description: It's no wonder that this place has more than its fair share of regulars – indeed, the food served here in the Scarpati family's somewhat more laid-back version of their restaurant is something to be savoured. Think tasty, fresh Italian dishes, including well-loved classics such as vitello tonnato. You can dine à la carte or opt for the set menu. The friendly service is also appreciable.

Name: Bootshaus
Description: The beachside location is simply idyllic – you can't get much closer to the Baltic Sea! In this restaurant at the Weissenhaus Private Nature Luxury Resort, diners are shown to their tables in a modern interior with a glazed façade that affords fantastic views. But it is of course the terrace that is the top attraction! The food is a fresh blend of Mediterranean fare – somewhat simpler at lunchtime, more sophisticated in the evening, from classic dishes to elegant culinary compositions. Service runs from 1pm-4.30pm, reservation times in the evening are 6pm and 8.30pm.

Name: Ratsstube
Description: In the former town hall, you can now dine in a stylish and inviting space that combines contemporary design with the warmth of wood and natural tones. The cuisine is ambitious, creative and modern, but at the same time pleasantly down-to-earth. The names of the dishes are original, such as "H2O" (cold watermelon and cucumber soup, trout ceviche) or "Haarscharf" ("Razor-sharp") (medium-rare wild boar, spring onion and beetroot ragout, garden herbs, horseradish pasta). The presentation is colourful and very visually appealing. In summer, there is pleasant terrace seating in the shade of lime trees. Good overnight accommodation available.

Name: Schapers
Description: A family-run place where you will be treated to friendly and cordial service. As for the food, you can look forward to ambitious classic cuisine brimming with regional influences. Choose from the à la carte offering or the set menus drawn from it, which include a vegetarian set menu. The terrace is lovely. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are comfortable and convenient guestrooms available, distributed over two buildings.

Name: der allerKrug
Description: Here at der allerKrug with its friendly hosts Sven Hütten and Petra Tiecke-Hütten, you can look forward to carefully and skilfully prepared dishes. The dishes are based on country cuisine with international influences, plus there’s an attractive terrace to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Leopold
Description: This lavishly converted stable of the Von Winning winery (part of the Bassermann-Jordan empire) is an impressively modern and extremely popular restaurant that serves excellent food. The menu includes a selection of international and Palatinate dishes. Lovely terrace. It can also be booked as a fantastic location for events. The restaurant was named after Leopold von Winning, founder of the winery.

Name: Hanse Stube
Description: The exclusive Excelsior Hotel Ernst, right opposite the cathedral, is home to the dignified and extremely elegant Hanse Stube. With its dark wood panelling, it is an absolute classic and you might say the "second home" of Cologne society. It serves ambitious classic cuisine with modern influences, as a menu or à la carte. At lunchtime there is an additional small menu. Excellent wines and friendly, trained service accompany your meal, and the terrace is beautiful.

Name: Restaurant 1718
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A beautiful setting awaits you in the restaurant of the Ketschauer Hof hotel. Stylish period features meet upmarket design here in the White Room and Black Room. In summer, you can dine in the quiet leafy inner courtyard. On the menu, French and international cuisine are the order of the day, accompanied by a superb selection of wines from the Palatinate and beyond.

Name: Nose & Belly
Description: This small restaurant in the centre of Augsburg is worth a visit, primarily on account of the cleverly thought-out seasonal cuisine. Hendrik Ketter and his team use regional produce wherever possible. There is a set menu with four to seven courses - also as a vegetarian option. In addition, service is provided by experienced and friendly staff in a pleasantly pared-back modern interior.

Name: Behl's Restaurant
Description: The dedication of the Behl family is palpable whether you're staying in their Genusshotel with its cheerful and cosy guestrooms or dining in the restaurant, complete with charming shaded courtyard terrace. You can look forward to a welcoming atmosphere and delicious dishes made with locally sourced produce such as Blankenbach brook trout or Spessart pasture-raised beef. They also host regular Brennabende ("spirit evenings") in the distillery, including a set menu with spirit pairings and a demonstration.

Name: Kucher's Weinwirtschaft
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The mismatched antique tables and chairs, the pretty decoration and the almost familial atmosphere lend this place a charming feel. The Swabian-style sour kidneys with sautéed potatoes have been on the menu here forever – a classic with its own loyal following. In addition, the menu includes contemporary dishes such as braised Ellscheid lemon chicken with Mediterranean vegetables. Most of the meat used by Florian Kucher and his team to create their seasonal regional fare comes from the Eifel area. Be sure to peruse the wine list – wine is a passion of senior chef Martin Kucher and he will be happy to advise you.

Name: KOI
Description: Head here for modern Japanese cuisine. The trendy decor and lively ambience extend over two floors, with diners able to choose from a wide range of sushi options, as well as meat dishes and light bites. Some dishes are cooked on the open charcoal grill.

Name: Remi
Description: This urban-cool restaurant in the building of Suhrkam-Verlag publishing house is run by the team behind Lode & Stijn, another restaurant in Berlin. The sleek design, the floor-to-ceiling windows and the open kitchen in the middle are the defining features of the space. The cuisine is modern and international with seasonal and regional leanings.

Name: GRACE
Description: "The place to be" in Berlin! A really appealing and stylish restaurant that oozes glamour and counts Hollywood stars among its patrons. Dishes with Asian-Californian and European flavours are served. A must: after the meal, a cocktail in the rooftop bar lounge! The restaurant is located in the tasteful, high-quality designed "Hotel Zoo" in a great location directly on Kurfürstendamm.

Name: Der Schwarze Adler
Description: Even from the outside, this beautifully restored, centuries-old building will grab your attention, while inside you can expect a cosy and comfortable decor with a touch of romance to it. Quality is of major importance for owner and chef Christian Brieske: he creates modern and ambitious dishes built on classical foundations. Very attentive and friendly service.

Name: Chang
Description: This restaurant serves a wide range of Asian cuisine – sushi, curries and wok dishes are the highlights, with the focus squarely on the quality of the ingredients. Inside, there is a minimalist decor and open kitchen; outside, a lovely covered terrace. The trip to Grünwald is definitely worthwhile. Tip: Park free of charge in the multi-storey car park on Marktplatz, a few metres away.

Name: Otto
Description: This is a small restaurant with an open kitchen and a pleasantly lively atmosphere. The modern, pared-down cuisine has a Nordic touch and is made using locally sourced ingredients. The dishes served are seasonal and ideal for sharing. Vegetarians are also catered for. There is a compact terrace in front of the building and, thanks to the canopy, you can even sit here in winter.

Name: Daniels
Description: Located in Kusel's old town centre, right on the market square, this renovated townhouse is certainly charming. Out front, there are a few trees and a fountain – the terrace seating here is delightful in summer. The place has a modern feel and a laid-back, friendly atmosphere. Wooden ceiling beams and exposed old sandstone masonry hark back to a bygone era. Ulrike und Daniel Bößhar delight diners with attentive service and ambitious cuisine in the form of a modern inspired set menu with three to seven courses.

Name: Husar
Description: The attractive, painted façade of this historic, established restaurant will draw you into the equally inviting interior with its comfortable yet elegant dining rooms. The service is excellent, while the good food – seasonal and international – includes dishes such as grilled zander fillet with Dijon mustard sauce.

Name: Gasthaus Adler
Description: Savour classic Baden fare with French and international influences in these cosy, quintessentially "Black Forest" dining rooms. In winter, for example, the game and goose dishes are popular. In summer, there is outside seating in the Adler Gärtle. The service is friendly and there are comfortable guestrooms, some simpler than others.

Name: Wirtshaus zur Sonne
Description: This restaurant has been in the same family for over 300 years. Diners can sit inside in the wonderful, wood-panelled dining room or outside on the pretty garden terrace to enjoy the flavoursome fare. This includes tafelspitz (boiled topside of beef) galantine with radish carpaccio or pan-fried skrei cod with tomatoes and herbs.

Name: Moosleitner
Description: The tradition of this restaurant has been cultivated for centuries. With their rural charm, the attractive dining rooms are cosy and inviting, and make an ideal setting in which to enjoy the Bavarian cuisine that is served here – fresh, seasonal and with a penchant for locally sourced produce. This is also a nice place to spend the night: There are well-kept guestrooms, plus a small sauna and gym facilities.

Name: Posthörnle
Description: This casual, minimalist-style little restaurant is housed in one of the oldest taverns in the town. It serves fresh, seasonal cuisine with dishes ranging from venison rissoles with black mustard to pan-fried zander with oranges and chicory.

Name: LUISE
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The beautiful landscape here is perfectly complemented by the elliptical form of Luisenhöhe hotel, which gracefully blends into its surroundings. Inside, too, modern design and high-quality natural materials make for an attractive decor that pays homage to the region – both in the guestrooms and the restaurant. The latter has a pleasantly laid-back feel, and a large glass façade looks out onto the terrace and beyond to the Black Forest including the Schauinsland mountain. A four-course vegetarian set menu is prepared in the open kitchen – fish or meat can be added to the intermediate and main courses. The excellent wine list features a good selection of German and international labels. The futuristic design of the passage that leads from the multi-storey car park to the hotel is also impressive.

Name: Jennerwein
Address: Münchner Straße 127, Gmund am Tegernsee, 83703, Germany
Description: A truly delightful establishment with a charmingly rustic inn atmosphere – it's genuinely cosy here. The menu includes freshly prepared seasonal Bavarian cuisine such as braised shoulder of lamb with root vegetables, or beef tenderloin on a bed of fried mushrooms and potatoes, as well as parmesan risotto with king prawns. More limited options at lunchtime.

Name: Schillingshof
Description: This elegant restaurant is set in a timber-framed house built in 1648. It serves ambitious, classically based international cuisine with creative elements made using high-quality produce. Overnight guests will appreciate the attractive modern rooms and the quiet location.

Name: Alte Mühle
Description: This friendly restaurant with its appealingly pared-back decor adjoins the historical building of a grain mill, which has been converted into guest accommodation. The cuisine is Mediterranean, regional and seasonal, and there will be something on the menu for those looking for vegetarian/vegan options. Lunch is also served Thu-Sat.

Name: heyligenstaedt
Description: The high ceilings, steel girders, large mullioned windows and sections of exposed brick wall show a conscious effort to retain some of the industrial charm of this old factory building: these features have been merged into the chic, modern design. The tasty cuisine has international and seasonal roots; smaller menu at lunchtime. Friendly service, and the adjoining boutique hotel has trendy guestrooms and rooftop sauna area.

Name: Wirtshaus zum Herrmannsdorfer Schweinsbräu
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: "Dishes that can't be pigeonholed" – such is the name of the game for chef Olimpia Cario. In her surprise set menu, she gives free rein to her creativity, cooking up unusual combinations such as chicken, trout, egg, cucumber, corn and redcurrants. She uses seasonal produce and high-quality ingredients, often grown on her own farm. The interior itself has an eye-catching design, with a large, high-ceilinged space reminiscent of a modern rustic barn on account of the beam construction climbing up into the roof.

Name: Zur Krone
Description: The Isele family has been cultivating the art of hospitality in this traditional building since 1854. The interior boasts a pleasant atmosphere in which to enjoy classic German cuisine that is seasonal, carefully prepared and based on a range of regional ingredients. The home-made terrines and desserts are definitely worth trying – the diet will have to wait! The wine list also has a very regional slant. In addition, there are comfortable, tastefully decorated guestrooms in which you will be tempted to stay for more than one night!

Name: Les Deux Dienstbach
Description: "Les Deux Dienstbach" refers to the two siblings who founded this restaurant at the renowned Weingut Künstler winery and whose French roots define the cuisine. Maitre d' Jennifer Dienstbach heads up the very friendly and adept waitstaff. Her sister, who is now based in her native Normandy, supports the kitchen team by providing culinary ideas. They propose a set menu comprising three to six courses made with select ingredients. Diners choose from a selection of wines from both France and Weingut Künstler. The setting is also appealing with its colour palette of muted tones, and smart, modern interior design features make for a tasteful interior in the heart of this historical building. Once a month you can dine à la carte on Sunday lunchtime.

Name: Basho-An
Description: Located near the pedestrian zone, this restaurant is a popular spot for authentic Japanese cuisine. If you want to avoid disappointment, be sure to make your reservations in good time! The decor is characteristically minimalist; there are also a few seats at the sushi counter. Tip: the reasonably priced lunchtime set menu. The options for dinner are wider ranging. At both lunchtime and in the evening, an additional vegetarian set menu is available. The wine list also includes sake, of course, and some regional wines.

Name: Kölbl
Description: Plenty of regulars come here to enjoy the regional and international cuisine served à la carte or in the form of a four-course set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. Diners can sit in one of the cosy dining rooms or on the courtyard terrace to enjoy the seasonal dishes. The guestrooms are ideal for overnight stays.

Name: Hopmanns Olive
Description: With great dedication, the Hopmanns have been running this friendly, sleek, modern restaurant for over 20 years – Ingo heads up the kitchen; Petra is in charge front of house. Based on classical foundations, the cuisine is seasonal and draws on Mediterranean inspirations. One of the classics is, for example, gently braised lamb shank. In summer, you can also take advantage of the gorgeous terrace. Tip: The adjoining historical engine shed is an ideal location to book for events.

Name: Der Löwe
Description: For years, the Sauters' well-kept establishment has been lauded for its delicious cuisine. Game from the region is one popular choice here, but their dishes with an international spin have also garnered favour with customers. Friendly, attentive service; tasteful setting. Tip: On Wednesday evenings, they serve a four-course surprise menu at an affordable price.

Name: Parlin
Description: Right in the old town, this lovely restaurant is pleasantly down to earth and lively – the impressive stuccoed ceiling really draws the eye! The name Parlin is a portmanteau word – the aim is to offer "the best of Paris and Berlin". This is reflected in the mouthwatering menu, which includes flavoursome seasonal dishes and classics such as fish soup or Wiener schnitzel.

Name: Sette Feinbistro
Description: This pleasant place is somewhat tucked away in the pedestrian precinct. Behind the name "Feinbistro", it comprises both a delicatessen and a restaurant. They are open in the morning to serve breakfast, and at lunchtime there is a small Mediterranean-influenced menu. Don't forget to purchase delicacies such as jam, cheese and wine etc from the shop to enjoy at home.

Name: Spessarttor
Address: Wombacher Straße 140, Lohr am Main, 97816, Germany
Description: This long-established family business is a well-run affair, with diners settling into the cosy dining rooms to enjoy regional fare. On the menu, tasty dishes such as roast venison with red cabbage and dumplings will whet your appetite. You can stay overnight in the inn or in the guesthouse located 300m away.

Name: Grüner Baum
Description: The terrace to the rear of this inn dating back over 300 years has a large chestnut tree, making it a particularly pleasant place to sit. The cosy interior is also appealing, and you will be well looked after by the enthusiastic waitstaff. Seasonal dishes such as saddle of veal with vegetables and gnocchi are served.

Name: La Cuisine Mario Kalweit
Description: A nicely restored building from the late 19th century houses this stylish, modern, elegant restaurant serving creative cuisine. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Piccolo
Description: You may not see the cathedral here in Porz-Langel, but you do pretty much have front row seats onto the Rhine! This restaurant serves classic cuisine with seasonal and Mediterranean influences, prepared using decent ingredients, most of which are sourced from the region. You can choose à la carte or put together your own three-course menu for a set price. The friendly staff also have plenty of good wine recommendations up their sleeve, drawing on the decent selection with a focus on Austria and Germany.

Name: Hardthaus
Description: The charming ambience of a former colonial shop surrounds you in this listed property, which boasts an inviting cosy vaulted wine cellar and a beautiful terrace opening onto the Marktplatz. The cuisine is both international and creative. Modern, high-quality guestrooms are available in the building opposite.

Name: Im Gütchen
Description: This elegant modern restaurant is accommodated in a charming Baroque mansion within the historical Schlosspark. In an airy, high-ceilinged space, diners are served classic cuisine with regional and Mediterranean sides, for you to pick à la carte or as a set menu. The proprietor himself runs the kitchen, using good-quality ingredients to cook up tasty dishes, while the lady of the house takes care of diners in a cordial manner. On hot summer days, make a beeline for the marvellous terrace.

Name: ACHT
Description: A trendy, urban establishment in the Spichern Höfe complex on the edge of the Belgian Quarter. Diners sit at wooden tables in a pleasantly unpretentious atmosphere; attentive service provided by charming waitstaff. Flavoursome, down-to-earth dishes based on regional and international ingredients are cooked up in the open kitchen. In summer, the gorgeous courtyard is much sought after.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description: Regulars flock to this 300-year-old inn, which preserves tradition while managing to keep up with the times. The Swabian cuisine follows the seasons and draws on international influences. The emphasis is on regional ingredients, including meat and sausage products made on site in the butcher's shop.

Name: Die Scheuer
Description: Once known as the Hammelsche Scheune, this 17C barn converted into a pretty half-timbered building has bags of charm. This family business a stone's throw from the market square is run with great dedication, and attracts many regulars. In summer, there is a lovely terrace out front. The interior makes for a cosy setting in which to savour delicious food such as locally hunted game. The restaurant endeavours to source ingredients locally and knows its suppliers personally.

Name: Bootshaus Bar & Grill
Description: The Bootshaus is situated right in the heart of Hamburg’s HafenCity district. Sit in the comfortable “Boot” (boat) dining room with a view of the open-plan kitchen or, if you prefer, look out over the Grasbrookhafen marina from the light and airy bar area.
