The Josper meat grill is the focus here, serving “New York Strip” and “Rib Eye” just how you like it! Good choice of side-orders and delicious sauces.

Name: Daniel
Description: In this pleasingly bright, convivial and refined restaurant, you can look forward to sampling rather classical, seasonally influenced cuisine. There are set menus to choose from, as well as à la carte dishes drawn from these. Or perhaps you will plump for the surprise menu. The front-of-house team are attentive. In summer, diners can enjoy sitting out on the pretty terrace. Tip: Browse the "Genusskalender" for themed evenings based on different produce.

Name: L'arte in cucina
Description: This attractive restaurant opposite the Basilika St. Margareta is a rare example of an authentic Italian ristorante, where the cuisine of Tuscany is served with love and culinary flair. Specialities from the chef's Tuscan homeland such as gnudi (a kind of gnocchi) or "Il Coniglio" (rabbit). The pasta is house-made.

Name: Waldgasthof am Letten
Address: Letten 13, Lauf an der Pegnitz, 91207, Germany
Description: This restaurant has various dining spaces with a charming rustic feel – including lovely cosy alcoves – where diners tuck into seasonal cuisine that is regional but also draws on international influences. Served by friendly and attentive waitstaff, the food is prepared with fresh, good-quality ingredients. Affording views of the verdant surroundings, the terraces in front and to the rear of the building are delightful in summer. This family-run establishment is also ideal for an overnight stay – on the edge of the forest, yet with good transport connections.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: This is MICHELIN-starred chef Tim Raue's take on a French brasserie.As at the Colette brasseries in Berlin and Munich, there is a small à la carte selection, as well as three set menus: one comprising Colette classics, one devised by Tim Raue himself and a vegan menu. The highlight here is the first-floor terrace overlooking the pedestrian area – but seating is limited, so you'd be well advised to book!

Name: Golden Phoenix
Description: This restaurant belonging to The Duc Ngo, owner of multiple restaurants, is located in the stylish Provocateur hotel. Expect a personable welcome and an informal atmosphere in this chic space with a visible kitchen. The French-influenced Chinese cuisine includes everything from interesting dim sum to sea bass, spinach, beurre blanc. Alternatively, you can eat in the adjoining bar. There are also outdoor tables: on the hotel terrace or on the pavement out front.

Name: EigenArt
Description: This restaurant is set in a spruce townhouse centrally located close to Marktplatz. It is hardly surprising that there are so many regulars, given the very pleasant atmosphere and friendly service. The cuisine is seasonal and can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. By prior arrangement, you can also make reservations for lunch and at weekends.

Name: Nigrum
Description: An impressive cross vault, elegant dark tones, designer elements, works of art – these former stables overlooking the city and a stone's throw from the New Castle have been stylishly converted. Drawing on modern influences, a three- to eight-course set menu is served – Beef tartare (classically prepared at the table) is available as an optional extra course. There is also a chic bar for an aperitif or digestif. Tip: You can reach the restaurant from the pedestrian area via the Burgstaffeln steps. There are several car parking spaces in front of the restaurant.

Name: Diergardts Kühler Grund
Description: This excellent family business is now run by the fourth generation. Since taking over the reins, Philipp Diergardt has upped the ante – not least thanks to his first-class training –, at a restaurant which was already operating at a high level. He pours passion into his upscale bourgeois dishes, e.g. the pan-fried young piglet blood sausage. Then there is the tasteful country house ambience and attentive service.

Name: Portomarin
Description: Red-painted walls and light wooden flooring sets the mood for dishes from the Iberian peninsula. From tapas to dessert, the menu is Spanish.

Name: esskunst
Description: The former hall of a bank is now a smart and sophisticated restaurant serving ambitious cuisine. Here, culinary tradition is tastefully combined with modern trends. On the menu, for example: char fillet, strudel dough, celery, turnips, kohlrabi. Tip: try the home-made pralines with your coffee. Charming, attentive and experienced service.

Name: Stüffel
Description: The riverside location here is every bit as appealing as the seasonal cuisine with Mediterranean and regional influences in which top-quality produce combines to create dishes such as fillet of spined loach with tomato, bread and basil salad. You can eat in the stylish modern bistro or outside on the waterfront. The wine list is well chosen and if you’re lucky the owner himself will advise you on your choice.

Name: GRILL
Description: In this restaurant housed in Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten by Hamburg's Inner Alster lake, Caucasian walnut wood, warm colours such as olive green and pigeon blue, along with a log fire create an elegant yet cosy setting that harmoniously blends traditional and modern elements. On the menu: seafood specialities such as oysters and lobster, along with classics such as steak tartare and special cuts of meat cooked in the Southbend infrared broiler.

Name: ESSLIBRIS
Description: ESSLIBRIS offers a relaxed, elegant atmosphere with a fine view of the garden. The food on offer is a mix of Mediterranean and regional. Try the suckling calf fillet and ravioli with carrots, parsley root and shallots. The kitchen is pleased to meet personal requests.

Name: Porte Neuf
Description: A good tip if you are looking for a place to eat in Detmold is this restaurant on the edge of the old town. Chef-patron Daniel C. Fischer awaits you in his compact, smartly designed establishment with a modern, feel-good atmosphere. In this setting, he serves up predominantly French-inspired classic cuisine with a modern twist. You can dine à la carte or opt for the set menu.

Name: Torschänke
Description: Right next to the Obertor (the historical city gate), Torschänke is a really inviting restaurant. The atmosphere inside is cosy and pleasingly down to earth, and outside there is a lovely, leafy terrace. Dishes with French and Mediterranean influences are prepared using top-notch fresh produce and served by a friendly, attentive and proficient front-of-house team.

Name: Backmulde
Description: This is just the sort of restaurant you would like to have at home. Great food and select wines with good recommendations. All are served in the friendly surroundings of a charming, centuries-old, half-timbered building. Wine shop just over the road.

Name: Elefanten
Description: In the heart of this charming town is this welcoming inn, which is run with great dedication by the Glässing family – now in its fourth generation at the helm. The classic, regional cuisine makes full use of what each season has to offer, often drawing on regional produce to conjure up flavoursome dishes. You might choose to pair your food with one of the locally produced wines on offer.

Name: Schaarschmidt's
Description: This building on a corner plot with a gorgeous leafy façade is home to a cosy restaurant that is run with great dedication. Its many regulars come in droves to enjoy specialities of Saxon cuisine – the beef roulade is a firm favourite! The friendly waitstaff will gladly talk you through the options on the menu. Head for the lovely small terrace planted with trees.

Name: Münsters
Description: This is an extremely popular place, with a cosy bistro feel and a rustic touch created by tables without tablecloths, wooden floorboards and partly exposed brick walls, as well as appealing wine-themed decorative details. The service is laid-back, friendly and attentive. The food is fresh, tasty and seasonal… and there's a great beer garden!

Name: alto
Description: This restaurant in the Atlantic Grand Hotel has a tastefully sleek interior, with dark wood panelling, large modern fixtures, as well as designer upholstered chairs in red and brown. The conservatory extension is also a lovely spot, as is the courtyard garden in fine weather – an Alpine-style hut is erected here every winter. The menu features classic dishes with a modern twist, plus classics such as schnitzel and burgers. Incidentally, the crockery is custom-made in Bremen. The location in the old town is ideal, with all the main attractions – the Weser River, Schnoor, Rathaus, Kunsthalle – just a short walk away.

Name: Crackers
Description: You’ll find this trendy eatery one floor below Cookies Cream. Ring the bell and the staff will lead you through the kitchen into a large and lively restaurant with a high ceiling and dim lights. The menu offers a range of ambitious meat and fish dishes.

Name: WEBERSTUBE
Description: Wood panelling, a tiled stove, pretty decor... The cosy, rustic-style restaurant in the Hotel BEI SCHUMANN has bags of regional charm. The same goes for the selection of ingredients used in the seasonal cuisine. The menu includes dishes such as spicy beef consommé, fried skrei with asparagus ragout and Saxony pancakes with apple sauce. Then of course there is the speciality: "Schuhmann's Currywurst", which comes in various degrees of spiciness. The cordial and professional service doesn't go unappreciated. Tip: Why not book yourself in for a fondue evening? Next door is the BEI CHURCHILL smoking lounge. There is a terrace at the front of the establishment.

Name: Schlegelhof
Description: The ambience is friendly, the service cordial (the chefs, too, are always present) and the food really good. In addition to regional dishes such as the Rostbraten Schlegelhof Art, there are ambitious dishes exuding finesse, such as the Arctic char with chanterelles and black mountain lentils. Interesting wine selection. It is a pleasure to sit on the terrace or in the spacious meadow to the rear.

Name: Zum Riesen
Description: The Wenz family put their heart and soul into running this place, and quality is also a top priority in the kitchen. Good-quality regional and seasonal ingredients are used to rustle up modern-inspired dishes, which are also served in the form of a set menu. Choose a regional wine to go with your food. In summer, the terrace in the courtyard is a secluded spot. There are lovely individually decorated guestrooms too.

Name: Schloss Loersfeld
Description: The centuries-old castle set in extensive grounds really is a magnificent property. Behind the massive stone walls, stylish rooms and lounges with period details await. This stately backdrop makes for a fabulous setting in which to relish the modern cuisine with classic foundations, served à la carte or as a menu comprising three to six courses. Caviar or oysters are also popular appetisers. Friendly and attentive service. An adjacent building accommodates overnight guests in three pretty apartments.

Name: Inzlinger Wasserschloss
Description: With over 500 years of history to its name, plus a stylish interior, this moated castle near the Swiss border has for years been synonymous with classic French cuisine made from top-notch produce. You can dine à la carte or choose the set menu – there is also a vegetarian or vegan option. Accompany your food with one of the great wine recommendations. Our tip: The guesthouse 150m away has terrific rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Henrich HÖER's Speisezimmer
Description: This 400-year-old half-timbered building, which houses Hotel Höerhof and its charming restaurant, is a place where you feel at home. The combination of the historical setting and modern touches makes for a special atmosphere – in summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in the secluded courtyard! Morish dishes from the region are served here, as well as a gourmet set menu (Wed-Sat).

Name: Clouds - Heaven's Bar & Kitchen
Description: Just 50 seconds in the lift and you are up on the 23rd floor, from which the view is simply magnificent. Modern cuisine is served in an urban-style interior: enquire about the extensive selection of meats; vegetarians are also catered for. In addition, there's a good bar serving a snack menu from 5pm. In summer, weather permitting, head to the 24th-floor Heaven's Nest for drinks and light bites.

Name: philipps restaurant
Description: A really appealing restaurant in the Schanzenviertel neighbourhood. A few steps lead down to this lively, modern establishment on the lower ground floor, where friendly and dedicated waitstaff serve fresh international cuisine. Tip: Be sure to make a reservation – this place is small and extremely popular!

Name: STRAUCHS FALCO
Description: This smart and stylish restaurant is next to the Maritime Museum. Situated in the Elbarkaden in the middle of HafenCity, it also boasts an appealing terrace. The menu features a variety of cuisines from around the globe, including specialities from the barbecue, Mediterranean dishes, such as fish and shellfish soup, German classics like Labskaus (meat stew) and Wiener schnitzel, as well as pasta. Additionally, there is the Bar & Deli.

Name: RIVE
Description: Sitting right on the port, this bistro is run by the same team as Tschebull. It serves good quality, flavoursome seafood and grilled meats alongside classic dishes such as Hamburger Pannfisch and Wiener Schnitzel. In summer the wonderful terrace is a must! Hot food served throughout the day.

Name: Kaltwassers Wohnzimmer
Description: Wohnzimmer offers a cosy "living room" feel with some charming nostalgic touches inside and a designer atrium with view of the glazed kitchens in the interior courtyard. The modern regional cuisine uses fresh quality produce and includes dishes such as Wels catfish served with mashed potatoes and apples, kohlrabi and Ahle Worscht sausage.

Name: James Farmhouse
Description: Fresh and tasty cuisine is served here, and the menu is strongly influenced by the restaurant's own farm – for example, they have their own Husum red pied pigs, chickens and German Angus cattle. The decor is a mix of industrial chic and a charming retro style. Very friendly service. Smaller menu at lunchtime. Tip: afternoon tea with scones, tartlets etc (reserve the day before).

Name: Ente-Bistro
Description: This little offshoot of the famous Ente restaurant is also firmly established in the city. The ambience is typical of a bistro: narrow, cosy, lots of photos on the walls testifying to well-known patrons. Floor to ceiling windows make the premises nice and light. The cuisine is classically French and imbued with seasonal and Mediterranean influences.

Name: Schimmel's
Description: This restaurant's striking red façade draws the eye. The smart interior is modern and stylish, and the atmosphere is welcoming – the wooden tables are a nice touch. In the open kitchen, regional dishes are prepared, occasionally incorporating influences from around the globe. Diners can choose between the two set menus or order à la carte. The soups, for example, are delicious, but so is the fresh fish! The proprietress ensures cordial and attentive service. They also offer pretty guestrooms and holiday flats.

Name: Atlantik
Description: Located in the Dreimühlenviertel, this charming old brick building was a fish market back when it was set amid an abattoir and wholesale butchers. Now it has evolved into this attractive restaurant, which has been designed with an individual touch. Although seafood dominates the menu, it is far from being the only option. Those who prefer meat can indulge in a fillet of beef, to name but one example. Highly recommended for groups: a whole fish to share, eg. turbot, char or Atlantic lobster. Be sure to leave room for dessert – the chocolate cake is a tempting proposition! To accompany your meal, there is an extensive selection of fine wines to choose from.

Name: Oktopussy
Description: At the restaurant of the New Wave hotel, the food is down-to-earth and delicious, with a regional focus and an international twist. The menu features dishes such as braised ox cheek and Japanese-style halibut. Characterised by sleek, modern interior design with a maritime touch, the setting is appealing. There is also an open kitchen and a custom-built table for larger groups. The friendly, laid-back service is another draw. In summer, make a beeline for the secluded courtyard terrace. From May, the rooftop bar is open for delicious cocktails in a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: MAXIME de Guy Graessel
Description: An appealing modern restaurant with an intimate atmosphere. Chef-patron Guy Graessel, who hails from Alsace, specialises in classic fare from Alsace and Baden. Diner choose between the five-course surprise menu (for two or more people) and à la carte dishes. For al fresco dining, there are tables in the charming verdant garden courtyard. Drinks are also served on the terrace in the pedestrian precinct Tip: Located in the entrance area, Café Hesselbacher has house-made cakes, tarts and pastries for sale at the weekend, over the counter or pre-ordered. For motorists, there is a car park – Parkhaus Löwenhof – not far from the restaurant.

Name: Zum Goldenen Pflug
Description: In one of the oldest inns in the region, tradition is celebrated, but not at the expense of progress. There are a number of charming dining areas in which to enjoy dishes such as Rindertafelspitz aus dem Kupferpfandl (boiled beef fillet from the copper pot), apple horseradish, chive sauce, creamed spinach and sautéed potatoes and, for dessert, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with plum compote and whipped cream. Order à la carte or opt for the "Signature Menu" for two or more diners.

Name: ESSperiment
Description: This relaxed modern restaurant with its lovely terrace offers a bistro menu at lunchtimes and fine dining in the evenings. The food is fresh and flavoursome. Try the saddle of venison with muesli, black salsify, pear and layered potato cake.

Name: Kochu Karu
Description: The fusion of Spanish and Korean cuisine may be unusual, but the combination of flavours really works. You can order à la carte or opt for a five- to six-course tasting menu (for two people or more), which also comes in a vegan version. Beverage pairings are also available. At this truly charming, minimalist-style little restaurant, you are guaranteed an enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Orania.Berlin
Description: The restaurant belonging to the lovely hotel that shares its name has a stylish, warm and relaxed ambience. The lobby and bar (with its interesting cocktail menu) are directly adjacent. Modern, creative dishes are sent out of the large open kitchen that draws the eye. Attentive and accomplished service. Try the four-course "Xberg Duck" set menu (min. two people).

Name: Kitchen Library
Description: A great team of two, Daniela and Udo Knörlein run this place together - she looks after the guests cordially, while he cooks up the international "Kleine Dinger" set menu. Available with either four or five courses, an eight-course version for sharing is also possible. The characterful decor is reminiscent of a library: rustic-style charm and over 600 collector's items related to cookery.

Name: Wilde Klosterküche
Description: This restaurant is located near the 13C Cistercian monastery with its Baroque church. The ambience is chic and modern, the kitchen partly visible. The food is carefully cooked and replete with flavour, and dishes reflect seasonal produce and ingredients that are mainly sourced from the region. A vegan option is also available by prior booking. Tip: They serve gin that they produce themselves. Guestrooms for an overnight stay in the separately run Klosterhotel.

Name: Julius
Description: This restaurant is in a sense the younger sibling of ernst, Dylan Watson-Brawn and Spencer Christenson's restaurant. Its interior is minimalist and sleek, the atmosphere youthful and laid-back. The kitchen, which is visible behind the counter, sends out creative dishes, which are also available in the form of a tasting menu in the evening, if booked in advance. A shorter lunch menu is served at weekends. You can also come for breakfast and brunch, as well as coffee, pastries and snacks during the day.

Name: Lucente
Description: If you are on the lookout for good Italian cuisine in Rüttenscheid then this ristorante is the place for you. The menu includes classics such as vitello tonnato and house-made ravioli. The daily specials on the blackboard and recommendations announced by waitstaff are also interesting. The atmosphere is young, fresh, friendly - Italian joie de vivre is in the air here!

Name: Terra
Description: In this restaurant in the attractive Ritz-Carlton hotel, a bright, modern and elegant interior awaits you. Take in the fascinating view of the VW works and the harbour basin, revealed by the large window front. They serve seasonal cuisine, which you can choose à la carte or as a set menu. Vegetarians will also be catered for here.

Name: Saxlers Restaurant
Description: This restaurant is housed in the inviting Weinhotel St. Stephanus on the riverside promenade and not far from the old market square. In a refined setting, the friendly and committed hosts serve delicious food made with top-notch ingredients, vegetarian options included. The menu features classic dishes and regional specialities. Tip: Leave room for the delicious desserts! In the basement, the Braukeller serves Kloster Machern beer.

Name: Zur Schlupp
Description: The Ehrhardt family are passionate about their charming little restaurant, in a building dating back to 1608. The atmosphere is cosy, the cuisine fresh and in tune with the seasons – why not sample one of the fine wines from the region? Just don't forget to reserve. Our tip: the interior courtyard is a romantic spot in summer.

Name: Zur Linde
Description: The fifth generation is now in charge of this family-run establishment. Sandra and Marco Linden are committed to creating a charming atmosphere and serving good food here. She courteously and competently oversees the service; he cooks up tasty regional and seasonal dishes, which are always modern in inspiration – served as a set menu or À la carte.

Name: Henssler Henssler
Description: Set in a typical Hamburg location between the Holzhafen and Altona fish market, the restaurant of well-known TV chef Steffen Henssler stands amid a plethora of seafood and fishmongers. The interior is slick and smart, with a nice and lively laid-back atmosphere. The 20m-wide kitchen serves modern interpretations of sushi in many variations, as well as dishes such as teriyaki-style Faroe salmon or rump steak from the lava grill. Senior chef Werner Henssler also gets involved in the service. It is advisable to make a reservation, whether for lunch or dinner.

Name: Die Alte Schule
Description: Torben Tönsing, scion of a well-known family of restaurateurs in Herford, took over this restaurant from his parents in 2017. He focuses on contemporary cuisine that draws on both regional and international influences. The 17C half-timbered building has a charming atmosphere – food is served on different levels, and in summer the secluded terrace comes into its own. Excellent wine selection – they even have their own wine shop.

Name: Rebstock-Stube
Description: This inn run by the Frey family is full of traditional character. Tuck into ambitious classic cuisine ranging from gourmet set menus to home-style dishes such as veal fricassee. The service comes courtesy of a friendly, attentive and well-trained front-of-house team. In summer, make a beeline for the beautiful garden terrace.

Name: Oliveto
Description: In the tastefully elegant restaurant on the ground floor of Ameron Bonn Hotel Königshof, the tables by the window or on the Rhine terrace come highly recommended. The attentive front-of-house team serves fresh, flavoursome Italian/Mediterranean cuisine. Decent selection of wines. Popular with business people at lunchtime. Some of the comfortable contemporary-style guestrooms boast a view of the Rhine.

Name: Warias Am Markt
Description: Diners can expect regional and seasonal cuisine that makes use of excellent produce – the daily specials are always a good option. The restaurant has a convivial atmosphere, or you can make the most of the terrace outside. On a practical note, there are well-kept, light and airy guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Salon 1900
Description: This inviting thatched-roof cottage, somewhat off the beaten track in Keitum, is just as pretty inside. Low ceilings and decorative details such as pictures, old sewing machines, coffee grinders and various other features create a cosy and charming ambience with a nostalgic feel. The friendly team serves up classic regional cuisine with a modern twist.

Name: Brasserie Lamazère
Description: Ready for a dose of French savoir-vivre in Berlin? You almost feel like you are in France here in the heart of Charlottenburg at Brasserie Lamazère thanks to its charming, down-to-earth and lively atmosphere. The regularly changing seasonal dishes are chalked up on the blackboard. You can put together your menu (starter, main, dessert) from a fine selection. They will be happy to recommend a good French wine pairing to accompany your food – the appealing and reasonably priced wine list is proprietor Régis Lamazère's passion.

Name: Oh Panama
Description: The way into this trendy, vibrant restaurant on two floors is through a courtyard. The service is friendly and relaxed; the food is seasonal German cuisine, with a menu featuring appetising dishes such as glazed beef cheeks with mashed potatoes. The "Chef's Choice" three-course set menu is available in both a meat and a vegetarian version. There is a delightful courtyard terrace, and Tiger Bar is also part of the same address. Just across the road is the Wintergarten variety theatre.

Name: Landgasthaus zum Kreuz
Description: Everything about this place is an appealing mix of regional and modern influences – from the cosy dining area to the food and the attractive, comfortable rooms in the Speicher guesthouse next door. The menu features classics and seasonal dishes – the "Mini-Versucherle", for instance, are intriguing. In summer, make the most of this delightful countryside location by dining on the fabulous terrace.

Name: AnnA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant inside the luxury Hotel Elephant is flooded with beautiful light thanks to its enormous windows. Seated beneath the high ceiling, diners can take in the exclusive ambience – the pictures in the entrance area are particularly decorative. The regional cuisine is modern and creative. Be sure to take a stroll through the pretty old town.

Name: KINK Bar & Restaurant
Description: Head to Pfefferberg – former brewery compound, now cultural venue – for this trendy and urban restaurant. The modern and creative dishes showcase a certain flair and sense of individuality. Perhaps you'll go for one of the interesting concoctions on offer at the adjoining bar? The pleasantly relaxed service makes for a friendly, down-to-earth atmosphere. Beautiful terrace.

Name: Rutz - Zollhaus
Description: This restaurant's location on the Landwehrkanal truly lends it something special. In summer you can make the most of the covered terrace but the interior of this former customs house is also appealing, with its tasteful furnishings and relaxed atmosphere. The menu puts a modern spin on classic German fare. Note the selection of high-grade cold meats, to be ordered as a starter or side dish.

Name: ITO
Description: In this trendy Japanese restaurant in the Belgian quarter, Kengo Nishimi combines traditional Japanese cuisine with modern European influences, drawing on top-notch produce and a clear structure. In the front part of the restaurant, you can watch the chef at work at the sushi counter. In the evening, à la carte menu and omakase menu; at lunchtime good-value set menus.

Name: Marktwirtschaft Besigheim
Description: This charmingly laid-back restaurant serves dishes made with regional and seasonal ingredients, drawing on influences from the Mediterranean and beyond. The best way to experience the culinary artistry is through the six-course set menu. There is also a popular lunch deal that changes weekly. In the summer, the terrace on the charming little market square beckons, whether for a meal, a glass of wine or a coffee. The service is friendly and attentive. Across the street is the Marktkeller brasserie and wine bar. They also put on regular themed evenings. Tip: Take a stroll through the enchanting little half-timbered town!

Name: REISERS Zehnthof
Description: The listed 400 year-old Zehnthof is located in the middle of the picturesque wine village. Inside, you eat in cosy, rustic-style dining rooms replete with historic charm; outside the pleasant terrace tables are set up in the wonderful courtyard with two shady plane trees. Both the food and wine list have a regional bent.

Name: Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller
Description: You can dine either out on the lovely terrace overlooking the city or inside – in a tastefully decorated dining area blending old-time elegance and more modern details. The ambitious seasonal menu proposes Mediterranean as well as regional dishes. The Chef's Table is an interesting affair: counter seating with a view into the kitchen, and a surprise menu. Good wine list. Be aware that the restaurant is accessed via a narrow private road.

Name: Fleher Hof
Description: A little out of the way, this traditional restaurant has a cosy interior, with all the charm of wood-panelled walls, old floorboards and wooden tables. Then there is the tasty cuisine, which includes flavoursome classics with a modern touch. Choose from the à la carte selection, or opt for one of the set menus ("Hof Menü", "Bistro Menü" or vegetarian). This pleasant restaurant is popular, so be sure to book in good time! N.B. Although finding a parking space may not be easy, it's definitely worth coming.

Name: Hofgut Albführen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This farmhouse set against a verdant backdrop of paddocks, woods and fields makes for a wonderful location. On top of that, you will eat well: seated in a tasteful interior, enjoy classical cuisine that draws on different international culinary traditions and makes full use of regional produce. Pretty and comfortable guestrooms, should you wish to stay the night.

Name: alexxanders
Description: The restaurant here offers not just an attractive interior but also great food. The food is seasonal, regional and international, with dishes such as lobster ravioli and fillet of beef as well as roast venison and Wiener Schnitzel featuring on the menu.

Name: Bob & Thoms
Description: Bob & Thoms is run by your charming host Oliver Körber (aka Bob), who treats diners to authentic Berlin-style hospitality, and head chef Felix Thoms, who has a wealth of experience at Michelin-starred restaurants under his belt. This friendly two-man operation is located in a rather quiet side street, between the small Viktoria-Luise-Platz, which was laid out in 1899, and the KaDeWe department store. Here, ambitious modern cuisine that takes its cue from the changing seasons is served in the form of a five-course set menu with options to supplement or swap out dishes. The restaurant's minimalist interior is complemented by decorative photographs of Berlin and New York taken by Oliver Körber's daughter. There are only a handful of spots each evening, so be sure to book in good time! In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous little terrace!

Name: Poisson
Description: Top quality products are deliciously prepared at this modern bistro with a fish orientated menu. The chef allows Asian, as well as Mediterranean and classic components to influence his food.

Name: Kuro Mori
Description: "The Black Forest meets Asia" is the motto of this cool, stylish restaurant located in Freiburg's beautiful old town. Kuro mori is Japanese for "black forest". Here, modern dishes are conjured up from high-quality ingredients in an open kitchen. As well as an à la carte selection, a small set menu is proposed at lunchtime and a more sophisticated one in the evening. There are also two special offers available on Tue to Thu evenings: "Dinner for two" and "Twenü" (for foodies under the age of 30). Tip: Owner Steffen Disch, who some will know from Gasthaus zum Raben in Horben, also offers cookery courses.

Name: GUI
Description: It's best to book here because this lively bistro in the middle of Bielefeld has plenty of regulars. There is an appealing atmosphere, which is down in no small part to the open kitchen, where the chefs prepare Mediterranean-inspired dishes, but also with nods to regional culinary tradition. In the summer, the terrace in the pedestrian zone beckons. Incidentally, ĝui means "enjoy" in Esperanto.

Name: ESTIMA by Catalana
Description: Set in the heart of the old town, not far from the cathedral, this compact restaurant with an open kitchen serves flavoursome Catalan-inspired dishes. At the helm in the kitchen is Jürgen Birth, who skilfully weaves both Spanish and French elements into his modern set menu. His penchant for patisserie is also evident. The set menu (also available in a vegetarian or pescetarian version) can be accompanied by select Spanish wines, enthusiastically presented by owner Jan-Hendrik Feldner – his personalised style of service is highly attentive. They also run a tapas restaurant about 100m away.

Name: Intuu
Description: Ensconced in the Freigeist hotel is this appealingly modern and lively restaurant. Diners have the option of sitting at the counter with views of the action in the open kitchen, as the team prepares a broad offering of Japanese and South American cuisine: dishes range from sushi and sashimi, tempura and yakitori to meats grilled in the Josper oven. These are also perfect plates for sharing.

Name: Rubens
Description: This pretty restaurant owned by friendly hosts Cornelia Stolzer and Ruben Baumgart – she is Austrian and he is German-Austrian – is something of an Alpine hot spot. Accordingly, classics such as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), Alt-Wiener Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake), as well as modern dishes feature on the menu. Charming, well-trained waitstaff and a decent selection of Austrian wines. Incidentally, the pumpkin seed oil comes from the proprietress's village.

Name: Goldmund
Address: Schöne Aussicht 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: The restaurant in the Literaturhaus, set on the banks of the Main, has an extremely stylish and upscale interior. The large bar area and the striking portraits of international figures from the arts draw the eye as you savour food that tends towards the classical. The adjoining Kaminzimmer ("fireplace room") is also very pleasant. Plenty of places to park behind the restaurant. This address is also ideal as an event location.

Name: Salt & Silver -  Lateinamerika
Description: A slice of Latin America in St. Pauli. With a view of the Elbe, you can enjoy a set menu (with fish and meat or vegetarian) that is inspired by the travels of the two owners. The cuisines of Mexico and Peru in particular are reflected in the piquancy and interplay of spiciness and acidity. Far Eastern touches also feature. Flavours from far-flung places are combined with local ingredients, with an emphasis on sustainability. The charming front-of-house team is professional and caters to diners' needs with a confidence that contributes to the enjoyably lively ambience.

Name: Freisinger Hof
Description: It is easy to see why this charming inn dating from 1875 is always busy. It boasts a stylish interior, a lively atmosphere and delicious food. There are classics from Bavaria and Austria – the focus is on beef but there is also Backhendl (breaded fried chicken). If you're lucky, you'll be able to try the fabulous creamy veal goulash at lunchtime. Quick and helpful service. You can have a comfortable stay in one of the well-maintained guestrooms.

Name: BEES Restaurant
Address: Am Rottland 6, Rüdesheim am Rhein, 65385, Germany
Description: This attractive restaurant serving appealing seasonal cuisine is housed in the premises of a former Asbach Uralt brandy distillery. The set menu includes a minimum of four courses, but you can also order à la carte. Sit back to savour your meal and enjoy friendly service in this chic setting with a partially visible kitchen. Tables are set up to create a pleasant terrace in summer. Tip for motorists: there is also a public car park near the train station and the Rhine.

Name: Lindenhof-Kasteel
Description: Volker and Susanne Kasteel have been playing host to their guests with great dedication for many years. In a tasteful interior (featuring ceiling beams from the original building, which dates back to 1682), tuck into ingredient-focused, seasonally inspired cuisine that draws on both classic and modern influences. Should you wish to spend the night, the hotel of the same name has well-kept guestrooms.

Name: [w]einklang
Description: In the northwest of Nuremberg, this chic little restaurant boasts a wonderfully cosy atmosphere. Here, owner and chef de cuisine Tomas Spanu, who has Sardinian-French heritage, serves a set menu comprising four or five courses – pleasingly streamlined and ingredient focused. Also available as a vegetarian menu option. The friendly and attentive service is the icing on the cake. You will want to keep coming back for more!

Name: Springbrunnen SKLENAR
Description: After almost 30 years in Mallorca, Czech-born Martin Sklenar and his wife Lucie swapped the Balearic island for the vineyards of Oberkirch. Here, they propose an interesting blend of regional (Baden), Mallorcan and Bohemian-inspired cuisine. This is served in a cosy interior with a slightly rustic feel, or out on the wonderful terrace known as the Weinberggarten. The ingredient-led dishes can be accompanied by your choice of wine from a predominantly regional selection.

Name: Wibbelings Hof
Description: Sandra and Jörn Haumann have turned the family-owned estate, which dates back to 1899, into a charming restaurant. While he takes care of the service, she prepares an ambitious set menu that takes its cue from the seasons; some of the ingredients are home-grown. Food is served in a lovely high-ceilinged room, whose modern interior design incorporates decorative features such as a wine rack, a workbench and large pictures. This space also makes an ideal venue for events and weddings. Tip: the farm shop (open on Wed and Thu afternoons).

Name: High Kitchen
Description: This culinary hotspot is perched on the eighth floor of an office building right in Magdeburg's city centre. In summer, the terrace is idyllic, commanding a magnificent view of the city and the over 500-year-old Gothic cathedral. The highly creative cuisine is served in the form of a set menu – including various appetisers. Pleasant service courtesy of a friendly and laid-back team, who always have just the right wine recommendations up their sleeve.

Name: STUBN in der Frasdorfer Hütte
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: This exclusive mountain-top location, surrounded by woods and meadows, really is the stuff of dreams. What was once a hiking lodge is now a cosy restaurant serving modern Alpine cuisine that can only be reached on foot (50 minutes from the Lederstube car park) or by booking a shuttle bus. Diners seated at the front can see the chefs at work in the open kitchen, grilling top-quality produce over an open fire. A shining example is the super-fresh Chiemsee pike-perch with bold roasted aromas, accompanied by an intensely flavoursome Jerusalem artichoke puree and crunchy rapini – a delightfully accessible combination. You can choose à la carte from a short list of options or have a surprise menu put together for you. The evening menu is also available at lunchtime, if requested in advance. The wine list is very well curated and the waitstaff are highly adept. The terrace is wonderful in summer! Simple guestrooms can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: Lovis
Description: An impressive architectural feat – a former prison has been transformed into an attractive restaurant. High ceilings and exposed brick walls, sleek interior design and soft lighting make for a special atmosphere. Diners take their seats in the former lock yard, now covered and fitted with large windows – the "Aquarium" room is truly original. The modern vegetable-oriented cuisine is available as a set menu or à la carte – regular, vegetarian or also vegan upon request. Food intolerances can be accommodated too. A selection of wines from around the globe. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif in the lovely bar, which also boasts a terrace. You can enjoy a night in Wilmina, the adjacent hotel.

Name: PULS
Description: With this culinary hotspot located in the chic boutique hotel Legend, Daniel Gottschlich (known from Ox & Klee) has another restaurant concept to his name in the cathedral city. The vibe here is lively, modern and urban. You can dine at the bar, at one of the high tables or at a regular table. In summer, there is the gorgeous terrace. Johannes Langenstück's kitchen team serves up bar food as well as dishes for sharing – also available in individual portions. Or would you prefer the surprise menu "Chefs Choice"? Decent wine list and an appealing cocktail selection including their "Signature" drinks.

Name: Zum Wendl
Description: This restaurant dating back to 1889 has a long history to its name. Today, Bavarian-style cuisine is the name of the game, presented in both traditional and modern guises. Fine examples include Bavarian Forest venison roulade stuffed with smoked meat, cranberries and pickled vegetables, mashed parsnip and potato, and a red cabbage roll, or pan-fried Breitenberg char with wild broccoli, spicy curry carrot puree, aniseed crust and lime foam. Alternatively, "Signature Dishes" such as Wiener schnitzel, cordon bleu and roast onion are available. We also recommend the two three- to four-course menus. The restaurant is housed in the hotel of the same name, which has a small spa area. This a great place to spend the night – then you can take full advantage of the excellent wine list. It features a good 180 items and is mostly devoted to German wines, especially Riesling.

Name: Esszimmer
Description: This restaurant housed in a leisure centre a little out of town is inviting, thanks to its sleek, modern interior done out in warm tones, and the friendly, well-trained waitstaff. The regional and seasonal cuisine is prepared with sustainability in mind. It's all about sharing here; small tapas-style dishes are placed in the middle of the table for everyone to dig in. So, you can mix and match vegetarian, meat and fish options as you see fit. In keeping with the dining concept, dessert comes in the form of sweet pastry tapas.

Name: vierzehn 85
Description: The former tithe farm from 1485 - still with a beautiful half-timbered façade - offers homely, modern guest rooms and a very nice, tasteful and casual restaurant on two floors with smaller and larger rooms and charming niches. The kitchen serves really good contemporary dishes from many regional and always seasonal products. Wines from the own vineyard. In summer, the terrace is inviting.

Name: VITA
Description: In his restaurant on the edge of the pretty town centre, Fabio Galizia (previously junior sous-chef at the restaurant of Schloss Schauenstein in Fürstenau) serves up a winning combination of Italian and French cuisine with a combination of seasonal influences. Order à la carte or opt for a set menu comprising four or five courses. The waitstaff are attentive and adept; excellent wine recommendations are provided by sommelier Anja Körber. The modern yet cosy interior is appealing. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace in front of the building or the courtyard.

Name: Oukan
Description: It's worth seeking out this restaurant, which is tucked away in a side street. The Japanese-inspired cuisine is completely vegan, with fermented food playing a major role – hence the "Fermentation Lab" having been built in the cellar. There is a creative menu with six to eight courses. The dishes are pleasantly stripped back, but no less complex for it. A shining example is the delicately cooked, finely sliced and grilled king oyster mushrooms seasoned with a squeeze of lime, sprinkled with a yeast/brioche crumble and served with a mushroom broth with thyme and apple cider, which adds a subtle spiciness. The intriguing tea pairing is a must! The icing on the cake is the decor. Drawing on Far Eastern influences, the aptly clean-lined, minimalist-style interior is done out in soothing dark tones. Extremely friendly service is the final flourish.

Name: Brasserie Cocotte
Description: Not only does this place have a really charming brasserie vibe (decorative pictures of cooking legends such as Paul Bocuse and Marco Pierre White), but they also serve good food. French cuisine is the order of the day. Be sure to check out the inviting terrace laid out beneath shady trees.

Name: Ursprung
Description: This smart restaurant is set in the family-run Hotel Aquarium, which is located in the heart of the beautiful city centre. With Jan Boddenberg, the third generation is now at the helm. As head chef, he curates a modern set menu and delivers classic, regional dishes, attaching importance to good produce and seasonality. Friendly service.

Name: Restaurant zum Bären
Description: The Buggle family has been running this traditional restaurant in the idyllic Lahn Valley since 1827. With chef Joachim Buggle, the eighth generation is now at the helm and his concept is impressive. He has dedicated himself to culinary classics, serving flavour-intensive, pleasantly pared-back dishes prepared without fuss or frills. Examples from the menu include dishes such as braised veal shank with root vegetables, leek, and potato and cheese purée, or fillet of line-caught sea bass with stuffed courgette, wild garlic risotto and a crustacean foam. The restaurant, with its delightful country-house style interior, has a pleasant and cosy atmosphere, while the Weinstube exudes a slightly more rustic feel. And then they have another ace up their sleeve in the form of a wonderful terrace in the shade of the lime trees! The front-of-house team provides charming and friendly service. The Landhotel zum Bären is also an excellent option, should you wish to spend the night here.

Name: Kaminstube
Description: The stylish and elegant dining area boasts the fireplace after which this restaurant is named. Classic and traditional cuisine with international influences is served – small portions are also possible. The terrace with a view of the Ellbachtal is popular in summer.

Name: Heiligenstein
Description: Come here to enjoy classic seasonal cuisine in a tasteful, modern setting. High-quality, fresh ingredients are prepared in an agreeably straightforward way that brings out their flavour. Then there's the excellent wine list featuring over 400 different bottles. Pretty terrace. The hotel boasts a peaceful location and lovely, cosy guestrooms.

Name: moriki
Description: Situated very close to the Festspielhaus (opera and concert house), the restaurant of Roomers hotel serves pan-Asian cuisine and a wide range of sushi. The menu reads, for example, "sake teriyaki – Scottish salmon, teriyaki glaze, sweet cucumber, rice". In a setting that is upscale and very much on trend, a young and enthusiastic front-of-house team provides competent service while maintaining a laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Penz Am Dom
Description: History meets modernity in this pretty old townhouse opposite the cathedral, creating a lovely, harmonious setting for the fresh, tasty and reasonably priced food. Head for the After-Work Dinner event on Monday night to enjoy a three-course set menu for €25. At lunchtime during the week only the "Business Lunch" set menu is served. Great terrace!

Name: plaisir by Hamid Heidarzadeh
Description: The minimalist, elegant look immediately catches the eye, with its gorgeous terrazzo flooring, clean-lined, pared-back design in black and white, and high ceilings with stunning mouldings. Chef Hamid Heidarzadeh blends classic foundations and modern elements to interesting effect, incorporating subtle Asian and Mediterranean influences. Two set menus are available in a four-, six- or seven-course format – one vegetarian ("Pflanzenfresser/-innen"), one with meat ("Fleischfresser/-innen"). The names belie finely tuned and precisely crafted dishes with full-bodied taste profiles, such as the boldly seasoned tartare of Balfego tuna with hints of spiciness courtesy of jalapeno cream, and beautiful layers of acidity thanks to the vinegar mayonnaise, as well as the freshness of subtly sweet grapefruit ice cream, plated on an aromatic salad of finely diced tomatoes. The laid-back yet discreet service is pleasant, and the chefs also join in with the service.

Name: FREA
Description: "Full Taste. Zero Waste" is the motto of founders David Johannes Suchy and Jasmin Suchy. Based on this idea of sustainability, their cuisine is modern, creative and entirely vegan. Choose from the refined seasonal dishes that the dedicated kitchen team concocts with plenty of finesse to put together your own three- to five-course menu – further courses are available if you would like to try more. Diners will enjoy the lively atmosphere in this trendy restaurant housed in a building on a corner plot; if you sit at the counter, you can look over the pass and see the action in the kitchen. It is also pleasant to sit on the terrace out front. The service is friendly and congenial.

Name: Hasenpfeffer
Description: This elegant restaurant in the idyllically situated Golf Resort Semlin is something of a culinary beacon in the region. They serve contemporary creations that are in touch with the seasons and draw on regional influences. Prepared from very good ingredients, these dishes can be sampled as a set menu or à la carte. The beautiful view of the golf course – through the floor-to-ceiling windows – also deserves a mention.

Name: Eulenstein
Description: Taking its cue from the seasons and made with select ingredients, the food here is meticulously prepared, flavoursome and fresh – it is clear that chef Steve Eulenstein has worked at some top-flight establishments in his time. He proposes two set menus as well as classics such as rump steak. The dining space is attractive and minimalist in style, and the service is friendly and professional. The location in a residential area just a few minutes' drive from the BAB 3 motorway is also convenient.

Name: Fachwerk
Description: Semi Hassine and Patrizia Weidemann-Hassine run this restaurant in the old town, where exposed timber beams lend the space a charming rustic feel. The lovely terrace commands a view of the old half-timbered façades all around. On the menu: Westphalian cuisine with Asian and subtle Eastern influences. Hot food is served from 4pm; on Saturdays from noon, all day.

Name: Rocus
Description: Housed in an attractively converted railway building dating from 1904, this restaurant proposes ambitious cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons – available à la carte or as a set menu. Dine al fresco in the courtyard or on the terrace facing the railway line. A table in the wine cellar, surrounded by Spanish red wines, comes highly recommended.

Name: Landhaus Hadrys
Address: An der Halberstädter Chaussee 1, Magdeburg, 39116, Germany
Description: Since 2003, Sebastian Hadrys has been synonymous with sophisticated cuisine! The food is seasonal and has an international edge. There is a set menu that you can put together yourself by choosing three to seven courses. The prices are very reasonable and the wine list is also very good. As for the setting, the pleasantly bright, modern space has a casual feel, plus a large terrace. Experienced staff provide friendly service. Tip: Cookery courses are also organised here.

Name: Engelwirts-Stube
Description: This lovely restaurant with its delightful terrace overlooking the garden serves regional and seasonal cuisine with the odd nod to international culinary traditions. A friendly and well-drilled front-of-house team help to create an inviting atmosphere. Tip: If you want to be close to the action, book the Chef's Table in the kitchen ( minimum 6 people). And if you wish to spend a little longer here, Hotel Engel Obertal offers comfortable, stylish guestrooms and fantastic facilities to help make your stay a relaxing one.

Name: Menge
Description: Christoph Menge cooks ambitious, flavoursome food that is both contemporary and classic. Dishes include sweet and sour schnitzel and Bavarian cream dessert with a duo of rhubarb, which is bound to set your taste buds tingling. Depending on the season, the menu also includes local Galloway beef, game and lamb.

Name: PURS
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Peter Fridén, of YOSO fame, has brought his "New Nordic Japanese Cuisine" to the 17C Alte Kanzlei, the interior of which has been tastefully designed by Axel Vervoordt. In a small side street adjacent to the boutique hotel PURS, this beautiful building houses a chic restaurant decorated in muted tones. Inside, the eye is drawn to the artwork on the walls and the open kitchen, visible through a glass sliding door, where Fridén brings together three different cuisines. Born in South Korea, he grew up in Sweden, and is schooled in the French culinary arts. His six-course tasting menu (vegetarian version also available) reflects his personality with an intriguing fusion of Asian-Japanese, Scandinavian and French elements. An appealing case in point is his combination of dashi chawanmushi, delicately smoked Oscietra caviar, Mangalitza bacon broth with a subtle smoky flavour and a hint of lemon salt. Accompanied by a carefully curated selection of wines by the glass (over 1 000 labels). The sake and kombucha selections are also impressive.

Name: Rössle
Description: This family-run business is now in its fourth generation. Behind a smart half-timbered façade, diners can choose from seasonal cuisine with some international influences and classics with a connection to the region. There are guestrooms done out in a modern Black Forest style. If you fancy a little excursion, the monastery complex and brewery are both within easy walking distance.

Name: Wintergarten
Description: The tastefully designed conservatory restaurant of the long-established Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa is a light and airy space with floor-to-ceiling glazing that affords a splendid view of the leafy gardens – and the terrace is, of course, especially inviting. In the evening, the classic and seasonal dishes can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. Vegetarian options are also available. A three-course set menu is served at lunchtime from Monday to Friday.

Name: Müllers auf der Burg
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: With his chic brasserie in the glass-paned pavilion at Schwarzenstein Castle, Nelson Müller has brought his gastronomical philosophy to the Rheingau. Enjoy the magnificent view as you sample fresh and classical Mediterranean cuisine with a touch of down-to-earthness: in addition to Breton bouillabaisse and Dombes duck breast, there is also veal bratwurst in curry sauce, for example.

Name: Bar Mural
Description: This hip bar is loud, lively and trendy – and therein lies its charm! The short menu features various cold cut platters, as well as a selection of tasty and carefully thought-out dishes, which are also served as a set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. A few options can also be ordered to share. For advice on what to drink, just ask the laid-back, well-drilled service team. The wine list is moderately priced and includes a decent selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Sonne
Description: In this historic inn with a lovely half-timbered façade and a cosy rural-style feel inside, the young owner serves up dishes such as braised knuckle of pasture-raised lamb with Madeira, or pike-perch fillet with chanterelles. The terrace lies under a big old chestnut tree. There are also guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Weinhaus Anker
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant that is steeped in tradition and run with great commitment. The lovely interior exudes a historical charm in which to enjoy French and regional dishes, and the service is friendly – hostess Elisabeth Deppisch is also a sommelière. In the winter, on Thu-Sat evenings, a short Franconian menu is served in the rustic vaulted Schöpple. You can also stay overnight in well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Oberländer Weinstube
Description: This townhouse, built in 1826, is full of charm: inside you sit in a cosy, traditional wood-panelled decor, while the charming courtyard beckons outside. And in addition they take really friendly care of you. The kitchen turns out dishes that are adapted to the seasons and really tasty. At lunchtime you choose from a smaller menu.

Name: Renoir
Description: This restaurant has been building on a solid reputation for over 30 years, serving classic cuisine and a sophisticated yet pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere. Delicious dishes are served as a seasonal menu comprising three to five courses or à la carte. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d', who happens to be a trained sommelier. Tip: The small gallery in the building is definitely worth a visit.

Name: Y Wine & Kitchen
Address: Rheingauer Straße 22, Eltville am Rhein, 65343, Germany
Description: Clear lines, funky colours, a striking flamingo design on the wall... this listed building in the old town of Eltville has an unexpected and stylish interior design. Modern, international cuisine is served in a friendly, lively atmosphere. In keeping with the colourful ambience, they offer a "Tasting Colours Menu" in which each course has its own colour motif. The "Y" in the name refers to owner and sommelier Ahmet Yildirim's own wines.

Name: Landgasthof zum Adler
Description: This is a charming family-run establishment. The cosy restaurant is housed in an old half-timbered building, and there are attractive and comfortable cottage-style guestrooms in both the main building and the guesthouse. The menu is dominated by home-style regional dishes, but there are also more sophisticated options. Apart from traditional fare (eg Zwiebelrostbraten – fried beef with onions), a well-devised set menu of the day is proposed, including dishes such as Arctic char, Riesling, julienne vegetables and pasta.

Name: Überland
Description: In less than a minute, the lift takes you up to the 18th floor of the BraWoPark building near Hauptbahnhof. People come here to enjoy modern cuisine in a trendy, chic setting – not to mention the view. Try the choice cuts of the excellent beef aged in-house. Incidentally, the concept is the brainchild of TV chef and food professional Tim Mälzer. NB: two sittings per evening. On the floor above, rooftop bar and terrace.

Name: Brasserie Ehrlich
Description: A French-style brasserie par excellence. Stephan Fröhlich and his wife Nadine run their small restaurant with a personal touch – he is the head chef and she is the sommelier. In this cosy setting, diners can look forward to friendly service and good seasonal cuisine in the form of two set menus. Given the popularity of the place, it is advisable to book in advance. In summer the gorgeous terrace beckons. Tip: Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: am kai
Description: Trendy, hip and relaxed is how you might describe this pleasant restaurant right on the waterfront. Great view of the container port – especially from the terrace in summer. The kitchen serves modern seafood - some dishes are also ideal for sharing. Vegetarian and vegan dishes are also available. In addition to the a la carte selection, the restaurant offers a tasting menu with six or seven courses.

Name: Museum
Description: A hip address in the Bavarian National Museum. The best thing is to sit outside on the cosy terrace, otherwise beneath the cross vaults and high ceilings in the chic modern brasserie ambience. Shorter, simpler menu at lunchtime, more ambitious seasonal Mediterranean cuisine in the evening. Wine list with specialities, but also wines for any time.

Name: erasmus
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a listed building dating from 1928, Andrea and Marcello Gallotti provide charming service and excellent recommendations from the well-stocked wine list to accompany their ambitious Italian-Mediterranean cuisine. This is served in form of the four- to six-course set menus "Terra e Mare" (meat and fish) and "Flora e Prato" (vegetarian), from which you can also choose à la carte. Or would you prefer the purely plant-based ‘Plantae’ menu? They also have a short oyster menu and organic Riofrío caviar. The terrace overlooking the garden with its old trees is marvellous! Thu. to Sat. wine bar on the roof terrace. They run a delicatessen next door. A commitment to sustainability underpins their work, and the restaurant is certified organic.

Name: 893 Ryotei
Description: The mirrored, graffiti-covered façade gives no hint of the restaurant that lies behind it. But despite appearances, this restaurant is a hit, drawing in diners in their droves. The trendy interior is done out in black and furnished with small tables. Guests bask in a lively atmosphere that centres around the open kitchen. Here, The Duc Ngu serves up a wide range of Japanese cuisine, infused with other Asian, South American and European influences, incorporating a wealth of spices. The menu includes traditional favourites such as sushi, sashimi, tempura and tataki, as well as more creative options like "sashimi taquitos", "tai yuzu truffle" and "unagi royal".

Name: Kräutergarten
Description: The friendly and dedicated hosts have been running this restaurant with an appealing elegant interior since 1983. It is with good reason that they have won over their many regulars: their classically oriented cuisine is seasonal and focuses on the quality and freshness of the ingredients. The service comes courtesy of attentive waitstaff. You'll certainly want to come back again!

Name: Forsthaus Ilkahöhe
Description: The idyllic hilltop location with its fantastic view across Tutzing to the lake is a huge draw of this restaurant – the terrace is fabulous! This converted forester's lodge has an attractive, upscale interior that combines modern style and regional touches. The menu features seasonal dishes made with select ingredients. Mediterranean and international influences are as prominent as the regional classics. While only a small selection of simpler dishes is served at lunchtime, things take a more ambitious turn in the evening. There is also a self-service beer garden.

Name: Königshafen
Description: The journey up to the north of the island is well worth it! Here, family tradition dates back to 1881, with the fifth generation currently looking after this spruce house with a white-brick façade, serving good regional and seasonal cuisine. Nice garden terrace behind the house. Closed Mon-Tue in winter.

Name: Christophorus
Description: For car enthusiasts who are fans of quality cuisine: here you can take in views of the Porsche Museum or Porscheplatz as you tuck into Mediterranean and international fare such as confit turbot fillet, pancetta foam, black trumpets, pumpkin quiche and Amalfi lemon or barbecued US prime beef. The open kitchen offers some fascinating insights. Impressive wine list comprising over 500 items. Located on the third floor, the restaurant can be accessed directly from the car park via a lift.

Name: Krone
Description: Modernity meets tradition in both the decor and the cuisine here at Krone. Try the delicious braised wild boar with mushrooms in elderberry and cream sauce or the scallops with Jerusalem artichoke puree. Alternatively, Krönle offers a simpler selection. There are also a number of attractive guestrooms available.

Name: Cube
Description: The absolutely fabulous location is as much of a draw as the glass architecture, the design and the ambitious international cuisine. There is a simpler lunch menu, too. The o.T. Bar serves breakfast, cake and after-work drinks. The lovely terrace is positioned on Schlossplatz, a square in front of the art museum. Tip for theatre- and concert-goers: Ask about their "late-night" dining slot.

Name: Habbel's
Description: Habbel’s offers a fine-dining experience beyond compare. International dishes such as tuna carpaccio coated in wasabi-sesame seeds and saddle of lamb in thyme foam with grilled vegetables feature on the menu, while the wine list offers around 1, 000 wines and spirits from the Habbel in-house distillery, including a 1977-vintage whisky!

Name: Schweizers Restaurant
Description: Originally opened in 1903 as Schweizer Hof, this restaurant is housed in a painstakingly restored listed building. In the aesthetically pleasing Jugendstil setting of this neighbourhood restaurant, the atmosphere is welcoming, which is in no small part down to the charming service team. Savour the five- to seven-course set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. The kitchen serves up ambitious, flavoursome dishes, showcasing precise technique and high-quality ingredients. There is a well-curated wine list, as well as pairings by the glass. The quiet shady courtyard terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Zur Sonne
Description: Hanspeter Rombach attaches great importance to organic ingredients in his inviting, friendly restaurant. The cuisine is regional and classical: on the menu, for example, local venison ragout in Spätburgunder sauce or filet of organic salmon and wild gambas in pumpkin juice sauce. There are also cosy guestrooms and a pretty sauna area.

Name: Bistro
Description: The bistro at the exclusive Gut Lärchenhof golf club on the outskirts of Cologne offers a somewhat simpler alternative to the eponymous fine dining restaurant, but you are just as assured of flavour and freshness – at both lunch and dinner. They serve dishes ranging from Currywurst to Königsberger Klopse (meatballs) and caviar. Needless to say, the terrace overlooking the green is delightful!

Name: Ganter Restaurant Mohren
Description: Whether you opt for a cosy-rustic or a chic-modern interior, the food on offer here is fresh and regional with international influences. Try the char with pearl barley, herbs, almonds and madras curry spices.

Name: Heim's Restaurant
Address: Moselstraße 27, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The food served in this 300-year-old restaurant is honest, fresh and full of flavour. Classic and regional cuisine is served throughout the day (kitchen opening hours: 12-8.30pm), taking the form of dishes such as cod à la grenobloise with spinach and mashed potatoes or "Original Wiener Schnitzel" with fried potatoes, salad and cranberries. You will be able to find just the right Moselle wine to accompany your meal. Service comes courtesy of a friendly and proficient team, the atmosphere is pleasant, and in summer, the wonderful terrace with a view of the vineyards and Moselle beckons. The Reiler Hof hotel has lovely guestrooms.

Name: Wilde Triebe
Description: Set in refurbished former railway buildings dating back over 150 years, Wilde Triebe offers a minimalist, imaginative and fashionable mix of art and food. The flavoursome, seasonal, regional fare is served in an upmarket brick, concrete, steel and wood interior on the restaurant’s own tableware. Great garden.

Name: Schloss Restaurant Venus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Set in the "Versailles of Westphalia", this classic, distinguished restaurant has vaulted ceilings and numerous paintings by the owner, Franz L. Lauter, an avid painter! Choose from the range of classic dishes or opt for the ambitious 12-course set menu with Westphalian tapas. The bistro with its large terrace is a nice casual alternative.

Name: ZweiSinn Meiers | Bistro
Description: If you are looking for a really nice bistro in Nuremberg, this is the place! A pleasant, cultivated atmosphere, friendly service and good food await you here. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced daily special is always in demand. The fine dining restaurant located to the rear is very popular.

Name: Imperial by Alexander Herrmann
Description: This restaurant is of interest to diners on account of its interior alone, which brings together the architectural details of the old building and a modern, chic-meets-urban look, including a visible kitchen in the middle of the space. In an unpretentious and laid-back atmosphere, they serve international cuisine with Franconian influences. There is a choice of different set menus.

Name: Atelier Gourmet
Description: Small, intimate, lively and popular, Atelier Gourmet is quite simply a great little restaurant. The food is fresh, delicious and good value for money thanks to chef Bousquet. It is served in a casual, friendly atmosphere with efficient service and good wine recommendations from the female owner. Try the capon and duck crépinette.

Name: Waldrestaurant Maxlmühle
Description: If you like trout, you can eat them home-smoked here at Maxlmühle alongside home-made brawn and pastry bakes or perhaps a delicious dish of breaded veal sweetbread sausage or braised shoulder of venison. The restaurant lies in a secluded location at the end of a street on the water, so the beer garden is also a particular favourite.

Name: Rindenmühle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Take a seat in the elegant yet cosy, country-style interior – or, in summer, out on the beautiful garden terrace – and choose from a seasonal menu. Vegetarians are also catered for. For overnight guests there are cosy contemporary guestrooms.

Name: Käpt'n Selmer Stube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Attention to detail is apparent everywhere: original blue and white tiles, antiques, Nordic style, and a wonderful terrace… The restaurant in the lovely Fährhaus hotel serves ambitious classic French cuisine with regional and international influences. At lunchtime the menu is smaller; in the afternoon there is an array of home-made cake specialities to tempt you.

Name: Die Traube
Description: This gorgeous half-timbered house dating back to 1647 boasts a cosy interior with banquette seats and ambitious seasonal Mediterranean cuisine made from excellent ingredients. The terrace in front of the old barn with its glockenspiel clock is also very appealing. Tip: There is a public car park just around the corner.

Name: Landgasthof Backers
Description: The Backers family business has a long tradition to its name, stretching back to 1843. Today, the sixth and seventh generations are running the show with great dedication. The fresh and flavoursome food draws on the region and the seasons, and ingredients are sourced locally wherever possible, including the venison and Diepholz geese. The restaurant is a long-standing member of the Slow Food community. There are also a few comfortable guestrooms. Try the "Backers zum Kennenlernen" deal: four-course regional set menu with drinks, plus overnight accommodation.

Name: Gasthof Hirsch
Description: Set in the centre of this Black Forest village, this attractive restaurant dating back to 1748 is popular for its robust cuisine with classic foundations and plenty of flavour – the sauces are also fantastic! This is all testament to the skill of owner Thomas Zimmermann, who uses select ingredients in his dishes. The atmosphere, too, is just right, thanks to the lovely decor and the exceedingly friendly, attentive hostess. Tip: There are also some individually designed, upscale guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthaus Cervus
Description: Centrally located, just a stone's throw from the train station, this lovely inn has also proved to be a hit with locals. A simple and fuss-free setting in which to enjoy the decidedly fresh and tasty food prepared in the open kitchen. In addition to more ambitious fare, classics such as schnitzel or roast beef also go down well with diners. Simpler and shorter lunchtime menu. Charming inner courtyard.

Name: Domschenke
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run restaurant is now in its third generation. Whether you sit in the rustic-style dining area with its regulars' table or in the pleasant conservatory, you are assured of friendly service. The menu features home-style, regional and more sophisticated dishes. Order à la carte or opt for one of the daily specials on the blackboard. In summer, make a beeline for the outdoor seating area, which is shaded by old trees.

Name: Landhaus Drei Raben
Description: The Koep family has been synonymous with excellent cuisine since 1995… and you can expect just that when you come to eat here on this property on the 18C Landgut Jaquetrois. This former agricultural estate is planted with beautiful old trees. The restaurant has a cosy dining area (warming fireplace in winter) and a fabulous terrace with views over the Mahnensee – especially charming at sunset! The food is international, regional and seasonal. Tip: Coffee and cake are served on Sundays.

Name: Pades Restaurant
Description: Wolfgang Pade offers a constantly changing menu, which is based on the availability of produce and relies on regional producers. Please note that there are only two service times: 5.45pm and 8.15pm – so make your reservation in good time! The garden terrace behind the pretty patrician house is magnificent.

Name: Die Achkarrer Krone
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The culinary tradition at Zur Krone dates back to 1561. Today you can look forward to a plate of calf’s kidney, tripe or oxtail stew, and in summer, a delicious sausage salad. The Baden cuisine and wines can be enjoyed in the cosy dining room or on the terrace. Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: BECKER'S Weinhaus
Description: The original building, which houses the wine bar, stands in contrast to the modern new hotel building. The abundance of pale wood makes it nice and cosy. Choose between a set menu, classic favourites and seasonal à la carte dishes. Pretty terrace.

Name: La Maison Eric
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: This absolute gem of an old half-timbered house is somewhat tucked away in a side street. The interior is tastefully decorated, while outside a gorgeous terrace gives onto the wonderful garden. A set menu of classic dishes is served at lunchtime from Thursday to Sunday.

Name: Nannina
Description: In her tiny restaurant host Giovanna Di Tommaso (known as Nannina) devotes herself tirelessly to her passion: Italian cuisine. Highlights of the fresh, ambitious menu include pan-fried zander in its skin with seaweed. Terrace behind the restaurant.

Name: Hugenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Inside Hugenhof is every bit as attractive as its exterior suggests with its lovely high ceilings, cosy old beams and a roaring open fire in winter. Every evening brings a different 4-course menu, which chef Klaus Ditz will announce at your table. This is accompanied by expert wine selections from his fellow chef and sommelier. The rooms are simple but smart.

Name: Genießer Wirtshaus
Description: This historical half-timbered house in the middle of the town is an idyllic address. Regional dishes are served in its cosy ambience. Pretty, individually styled rooms are available. There is a garden with fruit trees behind the house.

Name: mundart Restaurant
Description: Swabian-born Markus Hebestreit’s restaurant has an attractive, modern, country-style decor and charming interior courtyard. It is located in a pretty, old village house in this little wine-growing town. The fresh and tasty food includes dishes such as braised ox cheeks and tuna fish carpaccio.

Name: Hofgut Ruppertsberg
Description: This estate on the outskirts of town is steeped in history. One of the cornerstones of the Bürklin-Wolf winery, it is now also a charming restaurant with a wonderful courtyard. The cuisine is French, regional and seasonal, with a penchant for organic produce. The teahouse can be booked for exclusive celebrations. The farm shop sells delicious food to take home.

Name: Zum Hirschen & Gasthaus beim Stöckeler
Description: This family-run restaurant is firmly established in the village and surrounding area. The cosy, rustic dining rooms and pretty terrace in the shadow of the church making an ideal setting for its seasonal, regional cuisine. Overnight guests can look forward to pretty, modern Alpine rooms and a good breakfast – taken on the balcony terrace perhaps?

Name: Ballebäuschen
Description: The Allmann family has been running this friendly restaurant for over 30 years, staying true to tradition without standing still. The cuisine is flavoursome, fresh and authentic and ranges from regional to classic, including locally caught game in season. Small lunchtime menu. Pretty terrace to the rear.

Name: Kirschner Stuben
Description: This warm and welcoming place exudes a charming liveliness. The terrace overlooking the lake is an absolute delight. Complementing the inviting ambiance is a delectable selection of regional cuisine. An appealing array of fresh, flavoursome dishes awaits, ranging from braised veal cheeks to game and fish from Tegernsee. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally. At lunchtime there is a speciality menu. Maier zum Kirschner Hotel proposes pretty guestrooms imbued with Alpine charm.

Name: Juliette
Description: Are you looking for a slice of the French way of life in the middle of Potsdam? In the Holländisches Viertel (Dutch Quarter), you will find this beautifully designed restaurant, which is housed in a charming 17C half-timbered house. The dining space comprises three different levels, where you can enjoy ambitious classic cuisine accompanied by just the right wine, as a discreet soundtrack plays in the background. In addition to the menu, you can also choose a few dishes à la carte. If the weather is nice, would you like an aperitif at one of the small tables on the pavement before your meal?

Name: MINNECI
Description: The historical character of this town house dating back to 1560 makes it the perfect setting for an Italian restaurant.
