Here, diners can either opt for a four- to six-course set menu or order à la carte – think flavoursome Mediterranean dishes such as ravioli with wild mushrooms, sage and balsamic vinegar. At lunchtime, there is a smaller, more budget-friendly set menu. Friendly service comes courtesy of charming waitstaff. Delightful terrace in front of the building. For those coming by car: there is a public car park next door.

Name: Acetaia
Description: Serving Italian cuisine in a comfortable Art Nouveau setting, Acetaia takes its name from the aged balsamic vinegar you will find on sale here. Walkers will enjoy a stroll along the Nymphenburger Canal to the palace with its lovely grounds.

Name: Historisches Gasthaus Sanct Peter Restaurant Weinkirche
Description: Having been renovated following the disastrous floods of 2021, this restaurant gives off an impression of classical elegance. A 13C church with a gallery forms the core of the establishment. There are also two other attractive dining spaces (called Alte Lay and Walporzheimer Himmelchen). The delightful terrace to the rear of the building offers a view of the greenery. The menu features dishes with regional, seasonal and international influences. Classics include braised ox cheeks in Ahr valley Burgundy sauce, and turbot in Ahr valley blanc de noir sauce. The selection of Broggsitter wines is impressive, and there is a well-stocked wine shop on site, too. From 2-6pm, you can order from the smaller menu, with options such as the platter of cold meats and cheeses. They also run Hotel Sanct Peter in the town.

Name: Spielweg
Description: First mentioned in records in 1705, the original Spielweg building, managed by the Fuchs family, makes for a wonderfully cosy setting. The charming dining rooms are done out in traditional Black Forest style and the service is extremely friendly and attentive. Diners can expect classic regional cuisine that is ambitious and full of flavour, as in the warm smoked char from the Wutach in a cold potato and leek broth. It also draws on Asian influences, cf. their wild boar dim sum with soy sauce – Asian cuisine is one of the young chef's passions. The lunchtime menu proposes somewhat simpler fare, making this place an ideal stop-off for a light meal during a hike. You can stay overnight in well-kept, individually furnished guestrooms.

Name: Weinhaus Neuner
Description: With its cross-vaulted ceiling, herringbone parquet and wood panelling, this old restaurant has lost nothing of its traditional charm. The food is just what you would expect from an upmarket Munich restaurant – try the flaky pastry crust chicken fricassee pie.

Name: Huber
Description: Sandra and Michael Huber run their sleek, minimalist-style restaurant In an attractive residential area of Bogenhausen. Here, they serve flavoursome and ambitious contemporary cuisine that makes a pleasingly down-to-earth impression. There is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising four or six courses, with dishes such as spinach with organic egg and Perigord truffle or skrei, beans and 'nduja. The wine list has a few gems in store, with plenty of appealing options for every budget.

Name: IU & ON
Description: This family business in the heart of Nuremberg has been around since 1972! Many regulars keep coming back, having been won over by the aromatic dishes, which include classics like laab and tom yum. Add to that a clean-lined, minimalist-style interior and friendly service. By the way, the restaurant takes its name from the sisters Iu and On who cook here.

Name: Schloss Niederweis
Description: This tasteful restaurant is housed in the converted corn barn of a magnificent Baroque castle dating from 1751. The decor is a fascinating blend of rustic cachet and modern design – the open truss roof is striking and the two historical carriages on the wall are certainly eye-catching! Sample the flavoursome dishes à la carte or as a set menu, washed down by your choice from the terrific wine list that includes rare finds, including by the glass. Charming garden, a banquet hall and a registry office. On a practical note: easy parking.

Name: Christians Restaurant
Description: Run by Sandy and Christian Heß, this is an appealing restaurant – and that goes for the atmosphere as well as the cuisine. The interior is sleek, bright and welcoming, with beautiful arched windows affording a view of the Neckar River. And then there's the terrace overlooking the water – a truly idyllic spot in which to dine in fine weather! The cuisine is contemporary with a Mediterranean touch – opt for a set menu or order à la carte. This lovely space can also be used for private functions.

Name: HerR
Address: Herrngasse 20, Rothenburg ob der Tauber, 91541, Germany
Description: The spruce herrnschlösschen hotel, located in the old town, is home to a delightful little restaurant whose stylish modern interior design seamlessly incorporates the building's historical architectural features – the huge wooden beam dates back to 1526! There is a set menu bearing the name "INNOVATIVE KLASSIK By Sascha Bungeroth", which comprises five courses and includes a few added extras. Following stints at several top-flight establishments, here the chef takes his cue from the seasons, with dishes such as pickled Canadian scallops with sesame, horseradish and tonburi, or Franconian veal fillet tartare, burrata, olives and pine nuts. The charming waitstaff will recommend the perfect wine accompaniment. Fabulous terrace in the baroque garden!

Name: Turmstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the friendly atmosphere of this elegant space, diners are served delicious and seasonally inspired cuisine that is based on select produce. Rest assured, Wiener schnitzel is also a mainstay of the menu. Tip: Take in the view from the terrace. For those who would like to stay a little longer, Der Birkenhof hotel promises patrons a comfortable stay complete with spa facilities.

Name: Steinheuers Landgasthof Poststuben
Description: By no means a lesser version of Steinheuer, this is a restaurant in its own right where everything is cooked fresh. Taking its cue from the seasons, the menu features regional classics and international dishes. The same well-stocked wine list is presented here as in the fine dining restaurant. Dine in the cosy interior, or head out to the delightful leafy terrace. For overnight stays, there are double rooms available in the main building, as well as a comfortable guesthouse.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: Tim Raue has his finger on the pulse with the concept behind this place: you could almost imagine you are in a French brasserie, what with the stylish, cosy and pleasantly informal atmosphere, and the flavoursome food made with good-quality ingredients. The menu changes every three months and along with the à la carte selection, there are always three set menus to choose from: "Colette Classics", the "Tim Raue Menü" and a vegan one.

Name: Ontra's Gourmetstube
Description: Peter Grasmeier, the owner and head chef of Ontra in the Tech Square technology centre, has set up this modern little restaurant right next door. In the evening, he serves up a tasting menu, in which he skilfully marries classic and Mediterranean influences with Asian ingredients. Taking their cue from the changing seasons, the dishes are creatively prepared and pared down to the essentials, allowing the wonderful flavours of the select produce to come into their own. The service is friendly and competent; astute wine recommendations.

Name: ESSENCE
Description: This is a stylish modern restaurant complete with a splendid terrace. Diners are assured of a delightful dining experience not only thanks to the excellent service provided by owner Daniela Roch and her team: Phillip Schnabel brings great culinary skill and years of experience at top-flight establishments to the table. In the evening, he serves up dishes such as Allgäu venison with celeriac, hazelnut, cherry and purple curry. His cuisine is packed with flavour, intricate and sophisticated – but in no way contrived; it relies on high-quality fresh ingredients and a healthy dose of creativity. A vegetarian set menu is also available. At lunchtime, this place becomes more of a bistro with a somewhat simpler menu. Tip for motorists: There is an underground car park right next to the building.

Name: Alemannenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This historical Black Forest establishment in an idyllic location is thoroughly inviting. Inside, an attractive upscale dining space exuding bags of regional charm awaits. Affording magnificent views of the lake, the terrace beckons in summer. The menu takes its cue from the seasons and includes dishes such as Black Forest trout fillets with pickled cherry tomatoes, courgettes and parsley mashed potatoes or French corn-fed poularde breast, tender young beans and thyme pasta. There is also a "Gourmetmenü" comprising five or eight courses with wine pairings. Options are more limited at lunchtime. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel of the same name has guestrooms that seamlessly blend modern and traditional elements.

Name: Johanna Berger
Description: Tucked away in a fine 19C building in the centre of Lübeck, this restaurant has a charming interior with wooden flooring, chandeliers and an elegant feel, plus a wonderful terrace outside. On the menu are fresh and Mediterranean-influenced dishes, available as a surprise menu or à la carte. Nice selection of German and international wines, also available by the glass.

Name: Gasthaus Spieker
Description: Gasthaus Spieker serves regional cuisine with a Mediterranean touch including "Spieker’s Tasty Tapas" and ragout of lamb with bulgur wheat, green asparagus and crème fraîche served in its tasteful, beautifully decorated dining rooms. For those who fancy an extra glass of wine there are also a number of well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Helbigs Gasthaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Helbigs promises "casual fine dining" in a pleasantly relaxed atmosphere with attentive, friendly and professional service. In the kitchen, top-quality produce and skill are the order of the day with offerings ranging from traditional inn-style dishes to a set gourmet menu, the latter available in the evenings and at Saturday lunchtime only.

Name: Bayerischer Hof
Description: In this well-kept restaurant run by the Leykauf family, you can expect a relaxed atmosphere and flavoursome, fresh cuisine prepared by the chef-patron, as well as friendly and attentive service overseen by the lady of the house – this is hospitality as it should be! The wine list predominantly features local produce. There are also reasonably priced guestrooms, varying in style from simple to modern.

Name: Stilbruch
Description: This smart restaurant proposes a surprise menu comprising four to seven courses, in which good use is made not only of regional but also international ingredients. Diners are treated to dishes such as Atlantic cod with spinach cream, wild broccoli, king oyster mushrooms, walnuts and a Parmesan beurre blanc. A vegan set menu is also available. The friendly and courteous front-of-house team will also be able to help you choose the perfect bottle of wine. In summer, secure yourself a spot on the cosy terrace.

Name: Schupps
Description: Regina and Markus Schupp, after whom this restaurant is named, are both professionally trained chefs. Here they rustle up seasonal dishes inspired by the cuisines of France and Germany. Delicious examples include scallops au gratin with green asparagus, Jerusalem artichoke and almond, or venison ragout with cranberries, Brussels sprout leaves and sour cream. Those who wish to savour a more extensive meal can put together their own set menu comprising three to five courses for a fixed price. At lunchtime, the inexpensive daily specials are ideal for a quick meal. This friendly little restaurant also has a terrace for sunny days. Tip: free parking available along the street.

Name: VINOTHEK by Geisel
Description: Housed in the luxurious EXCELSIOR by Geisel hotel in the centre of Munich, not far from Stachus, Vinothek is a relaxed establishment done out in a cosy rustic style. The high cross-vaulted ceiling certainly has the wow factor, as does the array of decorative wine bottles. As you might expect from the name of this restaurant, delicious dishes that are inspired by the region and the Mediterranean, eg golden trout from the Birnbaum fish farm, parsley risotto, beurre blanc, are accompanied by a terrific selection of wines with a focus on Germany, France and Austria. Tip: Check out their reasonably priced lunchtime set menu including coffee and water. Cookery courses and "kitchen parties" are also organised.

Name: Bogenhauser Hof
Description: Built in 1825, this picture-perfect building in the smart Bogenhausen district has a long tradition in the culinary arts and is pretty much a must for any visitor to Munich! The tasteful, elegant interior and delightful terrace have been designed with a keen eye for detail. In a pleasingly unpretentious atmosphere, the experienced team led by host Stephan Fobo serves "Alpine cuisine with an Asian twist". Chef Hannes Reckziegel cooks up dishes such as Gutshof Polting char with grilled lettuce, parsley root and yuzu-spinach velouté. In the evening, you can opt for the five-course "Chef's Choice Menu" or order à la carte; the à la carte lunch offering (Mon-Fri) is complemented by a reasonably priced set menu that changes daily. Tip: the Wednesday night special "Schnitzel & Schmarrn" (for two people).

Name: Limbourg
Description: A wonderful addition to the Belgian Quarter's fine dining scene. The atmosphere is pleasantly laid-back and the vibe tasteful, whether you dine in the ground-floor space or at BelEtage. Chef-patron Alen Radic showcases his cosmopolitan cuisine, which draws on French influences and is made with fresh, good-quality ingredients. The sheltered tables on the inner courtyard terrace are particularly inviting in summer.

Name: Magnifico da Umberto
Description: Umberto Scuccia is a well-known figure in Heilbronn. Here on the 12th floor of the WTZ Tower he runs an upmarket, minimalist-style restaurant offering both pleasantly pared-down Italian cuisine with the accent on top-quality produce and a wonderful view of the city.

Name: Tischlein Deck Dich by Lilly
Description: Having worked at Lilly in Neupotz, Stefan Echle (service) and Matthis Nowak (kitchen) have found their new vocation – in the vaulted cellar of the separately run Villa Königsgarten hotel (formerly Diehl winery). A few steps lead down from the courtyard, home to a leafy terrace in summer, to the restaurant. As you make your way to the dining area, you can take a peek into the glass-fronted kitchen to see the chefs creating their modern seasonal set menu, which offers a choice of options for each course. Named after a fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm (The Lying Goat), the restaurant has a modern, elegant interior with a historical touch. Great service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-trained front-of-house team. The idyllic location in a village surrounded by vineyards, at the foothills of the Palatinate Forest, offers endless possibilities for excursions.

Name: möbius - das restaurant
Description: What used to be möbius lebensmittel.punkt, the delicatessen and bistro, has now been reimagined as a chic little restaurant by Tommy R. Möbius and his wife, Elli. In this modern and tastefully designed space, she runs the service with warmth and professionalism. In the evenings, her husband serves up bold and ambitious cuisine based on classical foundations. Simpler menu at lunchtime Tue-Sat (also available to take away). Delicatessen goods can still be bought here to enjoy at home. In addition, there are regular themed dinner menus and cookery courses.

Name: Tante Fichte
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Walk across the small terrace and down a few steps to reach this friendly and pleasingly down-to-earth neighbourhood restaurant. The decor embodies a winning combination of rusticity, elegance and modern design. The cuisine marries classic techniques with regional produce and influences from Croatia (where the chef's family has its roots). The set menu is also available in a vegetarian version. Featuring around 650 labels, the wine list is definitely worth a look. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Jacobs Restaurant
Description: The restaurant in Hotel Louis C. Jacob, which boasts a prime location, serves modern cuisine with classical elements. In the stylish interior, dishes can be chosen à la carte or as a set menu; they include French classics such as "steak frites" and rum baba. There is also a comprehensive wine list. The highlight in summer has to be the Lindenterrasse with its view of the Elbe.

Name: 1804 Hirschau
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: "Sustainable - seasonal - regional" is the motto of chef Lukas Adebahr and his team. The restaurant is housed in a historical building that enjoys an idyllic location in Munich's Englischer Garten – be sure to factor in a walk before or after dinner. He and his team adhere to the farm-to-table principle, using the finest ingredients sourced from regional producers or grown on site for dishes such as "rooster, green asparagus & morels". The cuisine often draws on imaginatively integrated Bavarian influences. Desserts such as "baba, rhubarb & sour cream" are tempting, too. There are two tasting menus: the omnivore "Vom Hof" and vegetarian "Vom Garten". The stylish interior has an Alpine feel, tastefully incorporating sleek design, wood, glass and attractive decorative details.

Name: 20° RESTOBAR
Description: This modern, unpretentious restaurant with a terrace, bar and lovely inner courtyard is located in the centre of town. In a pleasantly lively atmosphere, you can enjoy Spanish-Mediterranean cuisine: in addition to fish, meat, rice and potato dishes, you will of course also find tapas, croquetas and the like. In keeping with the Mediterranean concept, the name refers to the average water temperature around the island of Mallorca.

Name: Oechsle
Description: Serving flavoursome dishes made from fresh, high-quality ingredients in a pleasant contemporary atmosphere, this restaurant on the corner is a real gem. Its short menu draws on both Mediterranean and classical influences. This place also doubles as a wine bar, so you can look forward to a well-curated wine list. Experienced and charming waitstaff provide great service with a personal touch. In summer, the tables out front, facing the street, are in high demand.

Name: Schwane 1404
Description: In this centuries-old inn in the beautiful old town, this is a truly charming alternative to the fine dining restaurant. Both the inviting, rustic-style restaurant room and fantastic inner courtyard – the 7m-long oak table is quite a unique feature – are appealing places to eat. In the evening, you can order classic dishes à la carte or opt for the "Romantik" set menu. Many of the ingredients are locally sourced; some of the vegetables are from their own garden, and they have their own wines. Light meals are served at lunchtime.

Name: Roku - Japanese Dining & Wine
Description: This is the third restaurant to be opened by Yoshizumi Nagaya in the state capital. The atmosphere is trendy, modern and relaxed and dishes range from sushi and sashimi to tempura and Japanese fish and meat dishes. There is a good, predominantly German wine selection to go with the food.

Name: KOSTBAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Separated from the adjoining gourmet restaurant MARKOS only by optical room dividers, KOSTBAR with its plush interior of warm wood and clear design is both chic and cosy at the same time. If you can't make up your mind when faced with the great selection of modern dishes, let yourself be surprised by the "Probiererle Menu".

Name: Adler Stuben
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The traditional Parkhotel Adler, which has been a family-run business for over 500 years, is home to this historical Black Forest establishment whose origins date back to 1639. It has five really pleasant dining areas, from the charming "Stube" with its old wood panelling and a low ceiling, to the chic "Bergkristall", and of course the terrace. The cuisine comprises Baden and international dishes; vegetarian options are also available. The wine list features a good selection of wines from the region. For an overnight stay, there are cosy, elegant guestrooms.

Name: Ristorante Engel
Description: With almost 200 years of gastronomic history to its name, this place has been in Italian hands for over 40 years. Following in his parents' footsteps, Franco Iaia now runs this ristorante with his wife Yvonne. With a tiled stove and warm wood, the inviting dining space is vibrant and charming. "La Piazza" is their lovely terrace shaded by mulberry trees. Highlights of the "cucina italiana strettamente classica" include homemade pasta, brasato and osso buco.

Name: Inspektorenhaus
Description: In the city centre, opposite the brick-built Gothic town hall, is the Inspektorenhaus, from which the inspector used to keep an eye on the market and the activity it harboured. Nowadays it is a restaurant with a cosy ambience and distinct charm, thanks to old wooden beams and pretty decorations. In summer, you can sit outside in the courtyard garden. Two seasonal set menus are served, one with fish, one with meat. Friendly service.

Name: Diekmann
Description: In the mood for the charm of a typical bistro setting? At the front, amid decorative wine racks from an old colonial goods shop, is a casual dining area with high tables positioned around a free-standing oyster bar. Alternatively, nab one of the small tables in the charming minimalist-style space at the back of the premises. In the evening, ambitious French and German dishes are served à la carte or as a tasting menu. Lunchtime options are more limited but moderately priced – water, bread and espresso are included. The impressive oyster menu is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Sorriso
Address: Oppenheimer Landstr. 49, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description: In a smart building occupying a corner plot in the Sachsenhausen district, this tastefully designed restaurant serves modern Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made with top-notch ingredients. There are two set menus, one of which is 100% vegan. The owner has some great wine recommendations up his sleeve. Pleasant terrace for summer.

Name: Portun Restaurant
Description: Former co-chef at Les Deux, Gregor Goncharov, is now at the helm of this restaurant in Schwabing's Leopoldstraße. His surprising cuisine is rooted in Alpine-Adriatic culinary tradition, drawing on influences from Istria, Slovenia, Italy and Austria. On the menu, there are intriguing options such as Adriatic lobster served with peas, sweetcorn, tomato consommé and almonds, or Mangalica pork for two. The interior design is modern and stylish, with outdoor seating available in fine weather.

Name: INDIA CLUB
Description: Truly authentic Indian cuisine is to be found in Berlin! The self-styled "rustic cuisine" from the north of India includes delicious curries as well as original tandoori dishes. Many ingredients are sourced from the restaurant's own organic farm (Gut Vorder Bollhagen) on the Baltic Sea. The elegant restaurant with an interior of dark wood and typical Indian colours and patterns is located not far from the Brandenburg Gate, at the back of the exclusive Hotel Adlon.

Name: Park-Restaurant Vogelherd
Description: Quality restaurant in a former manor house famous for its good seasonal cuisine. You can also dine on the attractive terrace alongside a small pond.

Name: MANUELIS
Description: Very centrally located, this restaurant is really charming with its cosy atmosphere and cordial service. Championing regional and seasonal produce with a deep respect for the ingredients, the chef adheres to the nose-to-tail and leaf-to-root principles. The six- or eight-course set menu culminates in a delightful finale named Eine kleine Schweinerei (house-made Alpine pork specialities). Alternatively, there is a small à la carte selection. The beverage pairings are also intriguing, showcasing a selection of German wines alongside house-made kombuchas, sparkling wines, and beers. Tip: You can also book themed menus on certain dates.

Name: Kevin Gideon
Description: Kevin Gideon and his restaurant have moved to a location outside the city centre, into premises that previously housed VINEO. Diners will be pleased to hear that the concept remains the same in the new space. The team is unchanged and the pared-back, modern style of the interior and of the food is also still present and correct. Kevin Gideon and his small team serve up two creative set menus – one omnivore, one vegetarian. Comprising up to eight courses, the menu is updated on a regular basis. There are also à la carte dishes served Tue-Thu.

Name: sansaro
Description: The minimalist Japanese-style interior of the restaurant is inviting, as is the lovely verdant inner courtyard terrace. On the menu, the focus is on sushi and sashimi, supplemented by a few other dishes. The short explanations on the menu are a nice idea. Good selection of sake and Japanese whiskies, too.

Name: nagare
Description: Don't be fooled by the inconspicuous exterior of this corner-plot house! Inside, you can expect an appealing Far Eastern-style minimalist decor, and Japanese cuisine with creative, modern French influences. Choose from set menus and à la carte dishes – sushi and vegetarian dishes are also present and correct. The service is friendly, polite and professional.

Name: Zur Schwane
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Here, the Swabian Jura theme is writ large. The menu changes with the seasons and puts the emphasis on top-quality ingredients, most of which are sourced from the surrounding area. A huge panorama of the Swabian Jura landscape is the most striking feature of the modern yet cosy dining area – it couldn't be more apt. Tip: Given the restaurant's proximity to OUTLETCITY, keen shoppers might consider an overnight stay in one of the hotel's stylish guestrooms.

Name: Pizarro Fine Dining
Description: This laid-back little restaurant has tasteful decorative details like an old chest of drawers and a classic standard lamp that lend the place something akin to a living room atmosphere. It also has a snazzy open kitchen that draws the eye. Julio Pizarro calls the shots here; his creative cooking skilfully incorporates his Peruvian roots and many years' experience in international hospitality. This interesting fusion goes into a set menu that focuses on fish and seafood. Fabulous terrace with a view of the historical half-timbered town hall.

Name: AIMY
Description: Fans of Thai cuisine are in good hands at this restaurant with an attractive decor, where diners can enjoy flavoursome dishes made from high-quality produce – authentic Thai flavours are guaranteed here. Tip: The cocktail menu is also worth a look. There is also a delightful bar at the back of the restaurant. In summer, the seats in the inner courtyard are especially inviting.

Name: Landhotel Donner
Description: Here you can enjoy classic regional cuisine – for example the menu features braised wild boar in a juniper jus. The decor is warm and welcoming, the pretty country-style dining rooms boast classy soft furnishings and warm wood. Don't miss the home-made cakes served in the afternoons on the pretty garden terrace. You can also stay overnight in well-kept accommodation.

Name: Oma Wilma Heimatküche
Description: This charming old thatched-roof house in the heart of Keitum offers a modern take on Frisian interior decor, as well as a gorgeous garden terrace and friendly and professional service. Last but not least, the food is an ambitious alliance of traditional and modern. Shorter menu at lunchtime. Closed Mon-Tue from Oct to Easter, otherwise only on Tue.

Name: Bernhardhof
Description: At the foot of the hill on which Andechs's famous abbey stands, you will find this charming, chic, modern restaurant. The Holzinger family used to run a farm here, but nowadays they welcome diners with warmth and dedication. It is the son who is at the helm, serving up excellent, fresh cuisine that draws on regional and international influences. Incidentally, you can also enjoy a really comfortable overnight stay here, in one of the spacious maisonettes or suites.

Name: Restaurant Max'es
Description: A chic bistro vibe, friendly service and good food are the hallmarks of the restaurant of the Hotel Wegner, a family-run business since 1957. The cuisine is modern and takes its cue from the changing seasons. The menu includes dishes such as beef tartare with black garlic, anchovies and caper berries, or cod, beetroot done in two different ways and black salsify. At lunchtime, there is a selection from the evening menu. Tip: Head for the quiet leafy terrace! You can also come for breakfast.

Name: Salt & Silver am Meer
Address: Zum Böhler Strand, Sankt Peter-Ording, 25826, Germany
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is housed in an 8m-high building on stilts right by the beach, within spitting distance of the sea – an impressive location in which to enjoy fresh cuisine featuring produce from the region. The tempting menu includes grilled fish and meat, and their must-try signature dish: ceviche. The atmosphere is nice and lively both inside and out on the fabulous terrace. A welcome addition to the two other Salt & Silver restaurants in Hamburg.

Name: von Euch
Description: Located in the city centre, Hotel von Euch not only offers modern guestrooms, it has now also made a name for itself as a destination for foodies! In the elegant restaurant – or on the gorgeous terrace in summer – owner and head chef Johannes Schute delights diners with delicious cuisine that won't break the bank. Consisting of Livar cloister pork with potato, apple, onion and a wonderful jus, the dish "Himmel & Erde" ("Heaven & Earth") is a perfect example of how to combine superior and more down-to-earth elements to create something that is both refined and intensely flavoursome.

Name: Atelier Tian
Description: The location in Veitsburg castle is indeed something special. Once you reach the top, not only does a magnificent view of Ravensburg await you, but also Christian Ott's ambitious, flavoursome cuisine. You can put together your own set menu from the dishes on offer – flexibility is the name of the game! You can also look forward to professional and friendly service. Tip: Make your reservation in good time – this location is not only popular with locals.

Name: Momo Ramen
Description: Fancy some Japanese ramen? Then look no further! This hip and laid-back spot serves fresh house-made noodles. The aromatic dishes draw on regional ingredients and dispense with any additives. Reduced menu at lunchtime. An amusing detail: the toilets are wallpapered with Japanese newspapers.

Name: Gasthaus zum Adler
Description: In the centre of this village right on the German Wine Route, this traditional inn at the foot of Landeck Castle is now run by the fifth generation of the same family, with two sisters at the helm. Christine Baumann presides in the kitchen, putting a Latin-American spin on Palatinate cuisine; Franziska Baumann provides friendly service front of house. Regional wines are served with the seasonal cuisine. The appealingly modern, minimalist design successfully incorporates exposed old sandstone walls and wooden ceiling beams.

Name: Löwengrube
Description: This former wine tavern in the heart of the old town has been given a new lease of life. The traditional character of this historic building has been successfully mixed with modern elements. The food offering takes the form of internationally inspired cuisine made with regional produce. It is a real treat to sit on the sheltered terrace.

Name: Lindenhof 1887
Description: This North German family-run establishment is pretty as a picture! After being welcomed into the attractive inn built in 1887 with a lively local greeting ("moin"), you can expect good, attentive service in a modern and thoroughly chic ambience. Chef Tjark-Peter Maaß cooks tasty dishes of a regional bent. For example, the fried North Sea plaice, fried potatoes, cucumber salad, Tönning shrimps is a tasty and fresh option – one of the classics. There are also some appealing and cosy guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Il Teatro²
Description: In this long-standing family business near the state theatre from which it takes its name, you can look forward to fresh and flavoursome Italian cuisine with influences from France and Germany. Dishes on the menu such as the spaghetti carbonara, the turbot served with champagne sauce or the "Cioccolata Esotica" are shining examples. In summer, the terrace seating out on the wide pavement is especially appealing.

Name: Meilenstein
Description: A listed building steeped in history is the attractive location that houses this chic restaurant with its bar and lovely terrace. Here, they propose a set menu that you can put together yourself and that draws on modern influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and accomplished. There is also an appealing selection of cocktails at this stylish venue with a variety of spaces you can hire for private events.

Name: bellasLOKAL
Address: Langstraße 15, Bad Soden am Taunus, 65812, Germany
Description: Located in a narrow village lane in Altenhain, Isabelle Pering's restaurant has a pleasantly bright interior done out in a tasteful, minimalist style. With her menu, which you can also choose vegetarian, the chef shows her knack for creating harmonious flavour combinations – this is where her experience gained at top-flight establishments shines through. Most of the ingredients and wines are from the region and certified organic. Delightful terrace.

Name: Krone
Description: This long-standing family business is run with real dedication. No compromises are made when it comes to the quality of the produce, and the dishes taste great! No wonder the restaurant is widely known and popular – this also means it is better to make a reservation. Tip: the very reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: Forellenhof
Description: The diversity of the Bareiss culinary empire knows no bounds! The historic and idyllically located Forellenhof has been transformed into a charming restaurant open to all-comers from 11. 30am-5. 30pm. The emphasis here is on freshwater fish – from their own fish farm – but they also serve snacks. Tip: you can buy fresh fish in the Forellenlädle (9am-noon).

Name: Zauberberg
Description: "Zauberberg" translates as magic mountain, and the name is fitting for a number of reasons. For one, dedicated host Claudia Kimbacher, who adds a pleasantly personal touch to the service with her remarkably warm manner and is also happy to assist you in choosing your wines. Then there is Sven Gerlach's cuisine, which comes in the form of a surprise menu comprising five to six modern and creative courses. For example, he combines crispy pork neck with a Korean spicy glaze and kale kimchi or fresh, aromatic mushrooms with a creamy sauce seasoned with Shoyu soy sauce as well as Taleggio cheese dumplings. Vegetarian options are available on request. This friendly restaurant with elegant decor also has a terrace.

Name: Madame Ngo - Une Brasserie Hanoi
Description: It is definitely worth waiting for one of the coveted tables here! This charmingly informal restaurant is very popular due to its simple but excellent Vietnamese cuisine, which is also inexpensive. There is an enticing aroma from the bubbling pots in the open kitchen – a large bowl of authentic “pho” (noodle soup) is practically a must!

Name: Danza
Description: On the first floor of the culture and congress centre, Forum am Schlosspark, an interesting restaurant and wine bar concept awaits you. The cuisine is modern, seasonal and international, but also has classical influences; dishes can be ordered as a set menu or à la carte. Good wines, friendly, attentive service and a chic, light and airy space. The terrace with a view over Kastanienallee is delightful. If you are coming by car, you can park on the Bärenwiese opposite.

Name: Stubersheimer Hof
Description: The tasteful decor of this lovingly restored old farmhouse exudes rural charm. In the pleasant dining area with its attractive wooden flooring, diners are treated to a friendly welcome and delicious regional fare prepared by the junior chef. In summer, there's no better place to dine than in the charming courtyard. And if you're looking for a place to stay overnight, the family-run business also has lovely guestrooms available.

Name: BRIKZ
Description: At this restaurant – which used to be a jazz café – Arne Anker and his team serve up cuisine that takes inspiration from the seasons. The regular and vegan (or vegetarian) set menus both include water; there is also a small selection of à la carte dishes. Diners with food intolerances are happily catered for – be sure to specify your requirements in advance. Look out for the non-alcoholic beverage selection including house-made kombucha, kefir, cordials, teas etc. The interior is notable for its striking exposed brick walls and decorative artworks. The service is friendly and well organised – the chefs are also involved in serving. Pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: Johanniter-Kreuz
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This former farmhouse, which is over 350 years old, has been turned into the lovely Johanniter-Kreuz Romantik Hotel, complete with a tasteful, rustic-style restaurant in what was once the stable. Old beams and a central fireplace lend the space a cosy atmosphere. The food is rooted in classical culinary tradition, with regional influences and close ties to the seasons. Vegetarians are also catered for, and there is a decent wine selection.

The Stadtgarten Pavilion (1936) has been given a new lease of life with a trendy-chic feel, plus a good dose of glamour! Food is served throughout the day: a modern, ingredient-led take on classic cuisine à la carte at both lunch and dinnertime (somewhat reduced menu at lunchtime). There are also classics such as Wiener schnitzel and beef goulash, plus a small selection of pizzas. In addition, in the evening, a set menu made up of dishes from the à la carte selection is available. Short snack menu served 3-5pm. Lovely terrace overlooking a small park. Very good, wide-ranging wine list. Pino's Bar has a classic vibe and an outdoor lounge.

Name: Dae Mon
Description: This chic and rather stylish restaurant is an interesting option. The food is dubbed "open-minded cuisine": modern dishes that combine the techniques and flavours of Japanese and Korean cuisine in a variety of ways – for example, street food influences make their presence felt. There is also a creative vegetarian version of the set menu. Tip: As an alternative to wine, they propose a beautifully curated cold Asian tea pairing – a real treat for all those who like to go alcohol-free.

Name: Scarpati
Description: The Scarpati family have been running this inviting restaurant since 1982. In this beautifully kept Art Nouveau villa, you take a seat at your table in the classically elegant interior and let the attentive waitstaff serve you Italian cuisine. The garden terrace is also really lovely (and sheltered by an awning). Tip: On Wednesdays, come and try the reasonably priced set menu – the "Amuse Bouche Menü".

Name: Freilinger Wirt
Description: This traditional Bavarian inn has been around since 1870 and today it boasts a lovely blend of clean, modern design and warm wood. The patron and chef is a master butcher and his experience working at renowned restaurants can be seen in his good seasonal dishes. The large terrace is popular.

Name: Küppersmühle Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A fantastic location with an old industrial atmosphere, view of the inner harbour, and terrace right next to the water. This urban-style interior is the backdrop for modern cuisine with classic and international influences, served as fresh and precisely cooked dishes. Slightly simpler menu at lunchtime. Küppersmühle Museum of Modern Art next door is worth a visit.

Name: Broeding
Description: This lively restaurant is an institution in Neuhausen. In an outwardly unassuming building on a residential street, diners can look forward to a five- or six-course set menu comprising flavourful pared-down dishes such as lake trout with oxheart tomato and porcini mushrooms. The top-quality ingredients (mostly organic or Demeter produce) are sourced in the Alpine and pre-Alpine regions. The pleasingly laid- back atmosphere is in no small part down to the friendly, attentive and unpretentious service, which also includes expert advice when it comes to the fabulous wine list (with a focus on Austrian wine-growing regions). In summer, the secluded inner courtyard terrace beckons. Tip: Try out the shorter three-course early evening menu (until 7.30pm).

Name: Landhaus Mönchenwerth
Description: Good products form the basis of the ambitious contemporary cuisine of Guy de Vries, who also includes elements of molecular gastronomy. Wonderful Rhine terrace and beer garden.

Name: Zur Waage M.E.B.
Description: This long-established restaurant enjoys a charming location in the town centre, directly on the Leda River – in summer, the lovely terrace with a view of the museum harbour beckons! Inside, you can expect all the trappings of a traditional inn with the odd rustic maritime touch. Mario E. Brüggemann (who completed his apprenticeship as a chef here) proposes high-quality cuisine at reasonable prices with a strong focus on sustainability. Regional produce goes into dishes such as young herring tartare, plum, tomato – tasty, fresh and pleasingly straightforward! The simpler lunch menu includes a few of the evening options.

Name: Berchtesgadener Esszimmer
Description: This long-established inn run by Maximilian and Roxana Kühbeck with great dedication and a commitment to sustainability has bags of charm and atmosphere. Made with select ingredients sourced from the local area, the food is flavoursome and ambitious. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, plus an à la carte selection. In addition to the cosy little dining space with its vaulted ceiling, there are two very popular "kitchen tables" for those who wish to see the chefs at work.

Name: Le comptoir 17
Description: The addition of "Bistrot Parisien" to the name tells diners exactly what to expect. If you like a friendly, down-to-earth bistro atmosphere and classic French cuisine, then this is the place for you! Here, the emphasis is on the excellent ingredients that are used to make their house specialities such as blood sausage, beef tartare, mussels or fish soup. As well as the regular menu, there are specials written up on the blackboard.

Name: Gräfinthaler Hof
Description: In this somewhat more remote part of the Bliesgau region, you will feel most welcome in this gorgeous location that was once home to a monastery complex dating back to the 13C. Inside, an elegant atmosphere prevails; outside, there is a charming terrace shaded by trees. Ambitious dishes are created with terrific ingredients – the roast dry-aged pork chop (matured on the bone for 21 days), with sage, Serrano ham, market vegetables and potato fritters, for example, is a wonderful meat option. There are two set menus – one meat, one vegetarian – or you can dine à la carte.

Name: Weinstube Baldreit
Description: This lovely wine bar may be somewhat hidden away but is well worth seeking out – especially in summer, when the charming secluded courtyard terrace comes into its own. In addition to a relaxed atmosphere and friendly service, you can also look forward to seasonally influenced cuisine. They have plenty of regular customers and are always busy, so it's advisable to make a reservation!

Name: Ebanat
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Surrounded by vineyards, this modern restaurant boasts a beautiful location on the premises of Weingut Kopp, a Demeter winery complete with its own wine shop. As you savour classic seasonal cuisine that draws on international influences, you can take in the view of the vines and the plain, to which the name makes reference (the village of Ebenung used to be called "Ebanat", a derivation of the Old High German word for "plain"). Made with locally sourced ingredients wherever possible, the excellent food can be accompanied by the restaurant's own wines. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Goldene Sonne
Description: Heiner Bohnet and Constanza Piccolo have breathed new life into Goldene Sonne, which is housed in this attractive historical half-timbered building. The couple draw on their experience at prestigious restaurants in France, including a stint working with top chef Sébastien Bras. They serve ambitious, creative cuisine in the cosy space. The focus is on regional produce and close cooperation with local producers.

Name: FLYGGE
Description: An interesting location! The restaurant of chef-patron Mathias Apelt and his partner Britta Künzl is housed in the canoe club; it has a cool, pared-back design with an urban boathouse feel. There is also a wonderful view of the fjord – needless to say, a spot on the terrace is a tempting prospect. The open kitchen serves Nordic-inspired and regionally based soul food, eg bouillabaisse made with Baltic fish and rouille, which, although different to the original from the South of France, is just as delicious!

Name: Kurpfalz Weinstuben
Description: A typical Palatinate wine tavern in the middle of Berlin? At Adenauerplatz near Ku'damm, you will find this traditional bar tucked away in a courtyard. In cosy, rustic rooms you can enjoy home-style cooking and regional classics, along with 50 wines served by the glass and 800 on the wine list. Short menu of the day at lunchtime.

Name: Landgang
Description: The modern restaurant on the first floor of the Hotel Fährhaus is already a magnet for diners on account of its wonderful location. Take in the view of the Moselle as you tuck into French-Mediterranean cuisine with regional influences. There is also a vinotheque boasting very good wines.

Name: Franziska
Address: Hainer Weg 72, Frankfurt on the Main, 60599, Germany
Description: It takes 40 seconds in the lift up to the top of the Henninger Turm. As well as its magnificent views over the Frankfurt skyline, this restaurant proposes "Progressive German Vintage Cuisine". The name is a tribute to the great-aunt of the Mook Group founder. Cocktails in the Barrel Bar. Terrace one floor down. Online bookings only.

Name: Krone
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: You will feel at home here for a number of reasons. Not only can you enjoy the modern, classic and seasonal cuisine showcasing local produce, but there is also the friendly, attentive service that comes courtesy of the owner and her team, who also know their way around the wine list. The elegantly pared-down interior is equally inviting, not to mention the beautiful garden with shaded seating that draws diners in summer. Well-kept guestrooms are available should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Genießer Stube - Daniel Raub
Description: Daniel Raub represents the third generation at the helm of this family-run business. At Genießer Stube, one of the restaurants of the Landhaus Biewald hotel, he serves up classic French-based cuisine with a seasonal focus, eschewing any frills and putting his ingredients centre stage. In the evening there is the set menu ("Genießer Menü") which you can choose with four, six or eight courses. The wine list is also worth a look. In winter, food is served in the cosy parlour with its old wooden beamed ceiling. In summer, the conservatory and terrace are available. Professional service is provided by a charming front-of-house team. The second restaurant, Zur Tränke, is housed in the newly constructed modern hotel building.

Name: Drexlers
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Since 2007, this bright, modern restaurant right next to Colombipark has been something of an institution in Freiburg. Service is friendly and adept and the atmosphere warm and welcoming. Showcasing regional produce and sustainable practices, the ambitious seasonally inspired cuisine draws on French and Italian influences. The four- to six-course set menu comes in a "classic" or vegetarian version. On Mondays and Thursdays you can also order individual courses à la carte. Great selection of reasonably priced wines – courtesy of their own wine shop. Tip for motorists: Rotteck underground car park is within walking distance.

Name: Rittersturz
Description: This place has no shortage of charm: a lovely, cosy interior, friendly and attentive service and an idyllic location in the countryside! It's especially pleasant to take your meal on the terrace, from where you can enjoy the view of the castle ruins and the rocky Rittersturz Felsen. The classic seasonal cuisine – in set menu form or à la carte – is made with wild herbs, fruit, vegetables etc sourced from the surrounding area.

Name: Steinbuck Stube
Description: In the centre of town is this pretty, lavishly restored 400-year-old house. You can sit in the cosy, tastefully decorated restaurant, in the modern wine bar or on the terrace that adjoins the two. There, you will be served seasonal and Mediterranean-influenced classic dishes, accompanied exclusively by regional wines. There are also guestrooms for a pleasant overnight stay.

Name: Uwe & Uli - Zuhause bei uns
Description: A listed building standing directly on the market square, the 17C Liefrink House has an appealing exterior. Behind the pretty half-timbered façade is a charming, modern restaurant (formerly “essWebers - Küche am Markt” but now with a new name) which serves seasonal, international cuisine. The chef's set menu is complemented by a number of à-la-carte options.

Name: Seehalde
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Run by the Gruler brothers, this restaurant boasts a stunning lakeside location – tables on the terrace are much coveted in summer! The fresh and ambitious cuisine is also a major draw. The menu takes its cue from the region and the seasons with a classic bent. Fish from Lake Constance is also served and is even the focus of a three- or four-course set menu for two people. There is also a set menu based on regional classics. Alternatively, take your pick from the appealing à la carte selection. The well-curated wine list includes some gems, too. Well-drilled front-of house team. Tip: Take some homemade bouillabaisse in a jar with you to enjoy at home. There are well-kept guestrooms as well - most of them look out to the lake.

Name: Zur Tanne
Description: Housed in a charming old farmhouse, this restaurant is inviting from the outside, and the interior is rustic-looking and cosy. In this setting, top-notch ingredients that take their cue from the region and the seasons go into flavoursome dishes. For overnight stays, there are well-kept guestrooms – with no TV, but you'd rather enjoy the peace and quiet here anyway!

Name: Meister Lampe
Description: It's a real pleasure to eat here, and there's a good reason for that: chef-patron Daniel Stübler clearly puts his heart and soul into running his cosy little restaurant. He cooks up excellent regional and international dishes, and also does the serving himself – not only is he highly accomplished at what he does, he is also an extremely cordial host and single-handedly creates a fantastic atmosphere! The carefully curated wine list is also remarkable, featuring wines from Baden-Württemberg, Baden and the Palatinate only.

Name: La Bouche et El Pato
Description: This bistro with a friendly, cosy atmosphere is located in the middle of the city – the cathedral is just a stone's throw away. La Bouche is on the ground floor and El Pato is on the first floor, but diners enjoy the same international and Mediterranean dishes and friendly service on both levels. Lovely terrace in the pedestrian zone.

Name: Kugelmühle
Description: Max Matreux has been at the helm of this minimalist-style restaurant in the side wing of a factory since 2001. He is a strong advocate for sustainability, as is apparent in his classic cuisine, which features seasonal and regional ingredients. A three- to five-course set menu is proposed, as well as an à la carte selection. Tip: Ask about the "Bib Gourmand" set menu. Friendly and well-trained waitstaff.

Name: Die Alte Brauerei
Description: Florian Dauphin, son of friendly owners Eric and Isabelle Dauphin, is now at the helm of this restaurant, where you can look forward to cordial service. Diners are seated in a cosy setting to enjoy seasonal dishes that draw on French tradition . You can order à la carte or opt for a set menu. During the week, they propose a reasonably priced "Business Menü" at lunchtime. Access to the restaurant in the former brewery is via the inner courtyard. You also have the option of staying overnight: the six guestrooms have been individually designed by artist Margret Lafontaine.

Name: Krietsch
Description: This place used to be called Fuggerei – its name may have changed but it continues to be a great restaurant. At Krietsch, the cuisine is seasonal with a connection to the region, but it also draws on international influences. At lunchtime there are daily specials. Diners can sit inside, beneath the period vaulted ceiling, or out on the gorgeous terrace. Great location for a visit to the cathedral, which is just to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Gourmetfabrik
Description: This restaurant enjoys a gorgeous location at Lake Schwerin. Inside, the atmosphere is pleasantly laid back; the decor is modern and there is an open kitchen. Out on the terrace, you can enjoy a view of the small harbour. The reasonably priced daily set menu, served at lunchtime, is a hit. In the evening, you can choose from a variety of dishes, including Königsberger Klopse (meatballs), steaks, and burgers. Only the finest regional and seasonal ingredients are used.

Name: Heldmann & Herzhaft
Description: Originally the home of an industrialist, this smart 19C villa now houses this splendid restaurant, with its high ceilings, fine parquet flooring and elegant table settings – the perfect setting to enjoy Ulrich Heldmann's ambitious cuisine. Whether you opt for the seasonal set menu or order à la carte, you will be served meticulously prepared, flavoursome dishes made with fresh ingredients. The terrace is of course the place to go in summer. Wednesdays and Thursdays also open at lunchtime.

Name: Adler
Description: The atmosphere in this historical inn is cosy and rustic. The cordial and welcoming service staff is led by the charming Styrian manager, who herself is a fantastic host! In the kitchen, a father-and-son team prepares flavoursome dishes using high-quality ingredients. The menu is divided into two sections: classic Swabian dishes such as Kutteln in Lemberger (a tripe speciality) or house-made maultaschen, and sophisticated dishes like Japanese ramen soup or Breton monkfish with cauliflower and almond puree. An old jukebox provides the background music. Tip: The restaurant produces its own range of schnapps.

Name: Kraftwerk
Description: This converted power station is not only a chic location – it is also a place for extremely good food. The cuisine combines classic and Mediterranean influences, in the form of modern set menus, including "Around the World", "Pescetarian" or – if ordered 48hr in advance – the "Grand Classique" (for the whole table, minimum two people). Alternatively there is the large "Culinary Experience" set menu. They can recommend just the right wine pairing, should you wish. The high-ceilinged space channels industrial charm. Friendly service.

Name: Villa Medici
Description: This lovely villa is beautifully situated in a quiet residential area just outside the city centre. Once seated in the stylish interior, diners are regaled with Mediterranean cuisine and Italian wines. A charming terrace is laid out to the side. And for those who want to stay the night, there are also five attractive guestrooms.

Name: Gastraum
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This modern extension of the attractive Villa Hügel (1914) has a sleek and elegant feel. The ceiling-to-floor windows afford an impressive view of Trier, and the terrace is a particularly sought-after spot in this regard! Savour fresh, contemporary dishes made from good-quality ingredients and washed down with regional wines. The young team in charge of serving you are charming and professional. Cosy guestrooms and a lovely relaxation suite await overnight guests.

Name: Brunnenstuben
Description: Don’t be put off by the somewhat unprepossessing exterior at Brunnenstuben because the food is excellent! Petra and Thorsten Beyer – she running the kitchen, he managing the friendly and professional front-of-house team – serve flavoursome Swabian fare including an excellent Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions).

Name: Fässle le Restaurant
Description: Patrick Giboin prepares his own particular take on classic French cuisine in this cosy restaurant, where the mouthwatering menu includes dishes such as braised veal cheeks with king oyster mushrooms, risotto and wild broccoli. Vegetarian options and children’s menus also available.

Name: Ambiente
Description: Mathias and Melanie Luiz’s restaurant is in a small industrial area. He cooks with a Mediterranean note, which is also reflected in the bright, warm colours of the interior.

Name: Dorfstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It's no wonder people that love to eat here! In addition to its fine dining restaurant, Hotel Hirsch has its Dorfstube, which is a great option for fans of Swabian cuisine. In the cosy old dining space, completely done out in wood, you can tuck into specialities such as tripe, maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions). Vegetarian options are also on the menu. The delicious dishes are all made using regional produce. Friendly service. We highly recommend staying overnight. The guestrooms are really lovely and inviting.

Name: Zum Hirsch
Description: This charming half-timbered inn dates back to 1688. In winter you can sit in the pretty room dominated by the fireplace, in summer on the attractive terrace. On the menu, for example, roasted & braised venison from local hunting in venison pepper jus with celery, mole & apricot. At lunchtime there is reasonably priced three-course "Eat & Talk" set menu. Guestrooms for a pleasant overnight stay.

Name: Gasthof zum Maurerwirt
Description: Georg Grimm represents the fourth generation of the family to run this tastefully designed, rustic-style inn. It serves carefully prepared contemporary dishes based on fresh produce.

Name: Hermannshof
Description: This is the second restaurant of the tasteful BollAnts Spa im Park hotel. Like the first, it has a fine vaulted ceiling and an exceptionally beautiful interior done out in an attractive vintage look. The terrace in the courtyard is also inviting. Mediterranean cuisine with regional influences is served in two set menus that change daily and with courses that can be mixed and matched.

Name: Der Engel
Description: The perfect example of a traditional Baden inn! This family-run establishment has been welcoming guests since 1764, offering a consistently enjoyable experience. Behind its old half-timbered walls, there are charming dining areas – some more traditional, others more modern. In a warm and welcoming atmosphere, diners tuck into delicious regional fare. Options include classic dishes, daily specials and set menus. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of digestifs. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Kings and Queens
Description: This small restaurant has plenty of regulars, who are drawn by the modern and elegant decor, the friendly and professional service and the seasonal international cuisine. A choice of three menus, one of which is vegetarian, is proposed. You can also swap out courses or order à la carte. The wine list is sure to please, with an especially well-curated selection of labels from the region.

Name: Weinstube am Brühl
Description: These former stables have been converted into a delightful restaurant, in which terracotta tiles, warm colours and an old brick ceiling lend a real country feel. The international cuisine on offer follows the seasons closely. Diners are well looked after by a friendly and professional front of house team. Charming and elegant guestrooms are available in the Hotel Am Brühl.

Name: Berghotel Schlossanger Alp
Description: Set against the backdrop of the Allgäu Alps, this beautiful building houses both a hotel with tasteful and comfortable guestrooms, and a cosy and stylishly furnished restaurant. Affording stunning views, the terrace is naturally a wonderful spot in summer! The food is excellent and made with ingredients that are sourced exclusively from the region. Dishes such as Arctic char confit served with morels and peas are complemented by your choice from the excellent wine list.

Name: Fährhütte 14
Description: This restaurant, an offshoot of Überfahrt, enjoys an idyllic lakeside location. The modern decor has a touch of rustic maritime flair while the service is friendly and accomplished. International and seasonal dishes. You will also have the opportunity to rent a deckchair on the beach! N.B. the restaurant is not accessible by car – getting there involves a 300m walk.

Name: Gastwirtschaft Ferdinand Reuter
Description: This traditional family-run establishment serves good-quality regional cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons. Classic fare and more sophisticated dishes both feature on the menu. The atmosphere is friendly and cosy – in the more modern section, diners take their seats at long wooden tables. Hotel Reuter, which houses this restaurant, has comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Hoppe's
Description: The atmosphere is welcoming and lively, and the food is great – it's no wonder that people come back again and again. The menu features dishes from Alsace and Baden, with mouthwatering options such as "coq au vin à la chef", beef sirloin served with roasted onions and spaetzle, or Baden-style pike dumplings. They also do Flammkuchen. There is outdoor seating to the front of the building.

Name: Weingut
Description: After a stroll through the city, how about dinner at a chic restaurant with a trendy modern decor? There are plenty of options to choose from here at Weingut, including house specialities, steaks, plus a selection of dishes that changes every week (see the "Wochenkarte"). Alternatively, you could simply opt for tapas or a glass of wine – you can also buy bottles to take home. The service is very friendly and attentive. Decorative wine racks and high tables contribute to the pleasant wine bar atmosphere of the place. There are two reservation times: 17:30 - 20:00 and from 20:15.

Name: Ondersch Genusswirtschaft
Description: Going by the name "Ondersch" (a dialect word meaning different), this establishment located in the multipurpose "LOFT" building offers a cinema, a street-food bar and a gourmet restaurant. On the upper floor, a lively, urban atmosphere provides the setting for tasty modern cuisine made from seasonal and regional produce.

Name: Alpenkönig - Esslust
Description: Tables are set out ready to receive you in a lovely, upscale dining space comprising areas that range in style from traditional charm to modern chic. Cordial and professional service, fresh regional cuisine and an appealing wine selection. The restaurant is located in the attractive Alpenkönig hotel, which has inviting guestrooms and modern wellness facilities, all surrounded by the gorgeous Allgäu landscape.

Name: Löwen Genuss Wirtschaft
Description: The "Alpine lifestyle hotel" Löwen & Strauss proposes this really appealing eatery as an alternative to its fine dining restaurant. The rustic yet modern decor (complete with lovely little touches like old skis, cow bells etc) goes down just as well as the friendly service and the mouth-watering cuisine, which takes its cue from the region and the seasons. Top tip: Have a drink at Berggold, the adjacent bar.

Name: Würzhaus
Description: This really is an appealing restaurant. At lunchtime, things are toned down a little, with reasonably priced options (à la carte or a small set menu). In the evening, there is an ambitious set menu that comes in four to six flavourful courses. Head chef Diana Burkel is committed to using locally sourced ingredients. The dedication to sustainability extends to the wine selection – the list is dominated by organic, biodynamic and natural wines. The service is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is welcoming.

Name: Zum Rössl
Description: This long-standing family-run place is in a former post station dating from 1642. It is a pretty, traditional-style restaurant that offers a choice of regional classics as well as Mediterranean and seasonally influenced daily specials. A surprise menu is also available on reservation. Tip: the idyllic terrace!

Name: Il Borgo
Description: This Italian restaurant has been a mainstay of Schwabing's culinary scene since 1989. The interior is modern and elegant yet cosy, with the current decor successfully incorporating the old wall tiles and original bar. The menu sticks close to the seasons. In addition to the five-course tasting menu, there is an à la carte selection – from delicious pasta dishes to branzino al sale (salt-baked sea bass) for two.

Name: Villa Hammerschmiede
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether seated in one of the comfortable dining areas or the light and airy pavilion, you can look forward to cuisine that is ambitious, classic and regional, ranging from the intriguing "Villa Lunch" set menu to the "Feinschmecker-Menü" in the evenings. Options include turbot fillet fried in olive oil accompanied by Hokkaido pumpkin and dried apricot relish with walnut. Delightful terrace.

Name: Stephans Stuben by Marco Langer
Description: Marco Langer, well known in the region, took over the management here in the summer. The cuisine is ambitious and made using top-notch ingredients. Diners are offered a choice of two seasonal set menus, one of which is vegetarian. The restaurant's tastefully simple interior design is also inviting, and the waitstaff are friendly and well trained – the chef even comes to your table to talk you through the dishes.

Name: Little London
Description: This lively steakhouse not far from the Isartor is fronted by a classic bar of impressive dimensions – there are over 320 types of gin to choose from here! The attractive interior design successfully brings together a certain rusticity and a touch of English elegance. Meat eaters can look forward to high-quality cuts cooked on the Montague grill – tantalising examples include US Black Angus Prime Beef and Wagyu Kagoshima A5. There are over 250 wines on the wine list. Tip: Why not sign up for one of their beef-tasting sessions? With its various lounges, the restaurant also caters to private parties.

Name: Chalet am Kiental
Description: Set in an old farmhouse, this lovely modern restaurant embodies a charming blend of old and new, which makes for a cosy atmosphere. There is also an attractive terrace. The cuisine is creatively inspired with a regional touch, but also with international influences. For overnight stays, individually designed guestrooms are available – all done out tastefully and with great attention to detail.

Name: Galleria
Description: A cosy little restaurant in the city centre. It uses fresh, top quality produce in its ambitious Italian cuisine. The brightly coloured pictures on the walls change frequently.

Name: Johannas
Description: With its pleasant, upscale decor, gorgeous courtyard terrace and excellent food, the restaurant in the family-run Hotel Neumayr is certainly inviting. Ambitious cuisine is served as a set menu or à la carte comprising sophisticated, meticulously crafted dishes made from the finest ingredients. Take, for example, the saddle of chamois with juneberry, purple curry, wild mushroom, red cabbage and celeriac. Game and offal specialities are a firm fixture on the menu. The owner's œnophilia is given away by the impressive wine list, which comprises over 2 000 labels. The selection is international, but Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from Burgundy take pride of place. Such a range of small bottles is also something one does not often see. The waitstaff are highly professional yet friendly and approachable.

Name: Hippocampus
Description: In the city's well-heeled Bogenhausen area, Hippocampus is no run-of-the-mill Italian restaurant; it is a ristorante with real character, and the dedication of the proprietors is palpable! Diners can look forward to extremely attentive service with typical Italian charm, as well as home-made classic Italian cuisine, which can be ordered à la carte or in the form of a surprise menu. The wine list is impressive, featuring around 160 labels from Italy. Add to this an attractive interior with stylish details such as half-wall panelling in walnut wood, marble floors and Art Nouveau lamps. The terrace is equally inviting.

Name: Blauer Bock
Description: A cornerstone of the fine dining scene for years, this restaurant is housed in the spruce hotel of the same name, nestled in the centre of Munich – a stone's throw from the Viktualienmarkt and the city museum. The decor is tasteful, sleek and contemporary in style, with striking pictures adorning the walls. The cuisine is classic with a modern twist, and the menu includes mouthwatering options such as braised veal shoulder or sole for two. Outside, the tables overlooking the pedestrian area are in high demand.

Name: Sängerheim - Das Restaurant
Description: This pleasant restaurant in an attractive neighbourly village environment offers flavoursome seasonal cuisine at a reasonable price. Regional produce often features in the dishes and the service is warm and welcoming. There is a beautiful terrace behind the restaurant.

Name: fine.wine.dine.
Description: Located in the pedestrian area, not far from the Rhine River, this modern yet cosy little restaurant serves ambitious seasonal cuisine in the evening. You can either order the set menu or choose à la carte; on Wednesday and Thursday evenings there is also an appealing sharing menu for two. Vegetarian options are also available if ordered in advance. For lunch, there are simpler, more moderately priced daily specials. Delicatessen goods and wine can be purchased to enjoy at home.

Name: Hirschkönig
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Here, rural charm combines with elegant and contemporary interior design to create a welcoming setting – that goes for both the Hirschen hotel and its small fine dining restaurant with its upscale, sleek and stylish dining space. The modern and seasonal set menu, "Feld & Flur" ("Field & Fell"), is composed of six or seven courses imbued with a hint of the Mediterranean, such as wild garlic ravioli with tomato. Wine pairings are available upon request. Head to the delicatessen for house-made specialities such as chutneys, pickles and cured meats.

Name: Höfli
Description: The charming Höfli blends seamlessly into the picturesque old town setting. The enchanting cobblestone courtyard invites you to dine under the summer sky, surrounded by historical walls and half-timbered buildings. The interior is just as pleasant with its sleek, contemporary feel. While maître d' Alexandra Killy ensures a warm welcome, her husband, Marco, prepares delicious and neatly crafted dishes. His classical training shines through in dishes such as the Breton skate wing with buckwheat and saffron risotto, capers and shellfish stock.

Name: von Rhemen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The restaurant of the stylish Schloss Wilkinghege hotel is set in an elegant, high-ceilinged room with fine mouldings and bags of historical charm. The classical cuisine makes the most of seasonal ingredients, with diners able to choose between à la carte dishes, the "Schlossmenü" and vegetarian set menu.

Name: Jin
Description: Highlights at Jin include the upscale, minimalist-style interior inspired by the Far East and the flavoursome pan-Asian cuisine with a distinct Chinese edge, as well as Japanese and European influences. Tip: In addition to the à la carte selection, there are the set menus "Jin's Flavours" and "Jin's Degustation", which provide the best impression of the chef's skills.

Name: Pungshaus
Description: This pretty little half-timbered house serves good food in a cosy setting. The market-fresh cuisine includes dishes such as veal tenderloin with purple potato mash and pan-fried green asparagus.

Name: AUVIGU
Description: Nestled in the old town, a stone's throw from the renowned saltworks, this restaurant is a haven of pure comfort run by Gianluca Fleer, who has set up shop with his wife Inga. "High Dining" is what they call their concept of modern, creative yet down-to-earth cuisine – served as a set menu or à la carte. In dishes such as creamy risotto with Aquerello rice, nashi pear, scallop, lardo, saffron, yuzu and parsnip, the chef-patron draws on his Sardinian roots as well as French and international accents – simple yet captivating. The setting is also inviting: well-appointed, modern and with a touch of elegance.

Name: Matsuhisa Munich
Description: The high quality evident throughout the luxury Mandarin Oriental is also reflected in the minimalist-style restaurant run by Nobu Matsuhisa, who runs restaurants around the world. The cuisine is modern Japanese and interesting, refined with Peruvian flavours and techniques – an exciting mix. Don’t miss the sushi and sashimi or the classic Black Cod Miso dish!

Name: KIKU Restaurant by Jan Fribus
Description: Kiku means chrysanthemum – the Japanese national flower – and, indeed, the cuisine here is strongly marked by Japanese elements. Influences from other Asian countries, as well as the odd subtle touch of classic French cookery, can also be detected. Dishes such as tuna tartare, steamed dumplings and seaweed or salmon steak feature on the menu. The restaurant is located in a small street lined with half-timbered houses not far from the centre. Inside, the atmosphere is laid back and elegant; the service is friendly and informal, with the chefs coming to your table armed with delightful explanations about the tasty dishes. The best way to get acquainted with the food is to opt for the ten-course set menu, but there is also an appealing à la carte menu. The bill is very reasonable considering what you get for your money.

Name: IL Sommelier
Description: Behind the unassuming façade of a modern building in the Trudering district, this is a real gem of a restaurant. In the chic, contemporary space, diners are served authentic, flavoursome, down-to-earth cucina italiana. The dishes on the menu are sophisticated but not pretentious, and include tortelli with a cheese and aubergine filling or beef cheek braised with sweet potato mash. The wine list features Italian wines exclusively. In summer, the quiet terrace to the rear of the property beckons.

Name: Kulinarium
Address: Friedrichsplatz 4, Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, 90552, Germany
Description: This delightful restaurant is nestled in a spruce half-timbered building in the heart of Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, just outside Nuremberg. Modern interior design incorporating a rustic wooden beam ceiling creates a cosy atmosphere. You can feel commitment and passion here. Gerald Hoffmann, a well-known chef in the region and most recently head chef at Koch und Kellner, is in charge in the kitchen. His wife presides over the service, adding a soupçon of heartfelt charm to every interaction. There is a seasonally orientated set menu that is prepared using mainly regional ingredients. In summer you can sit on the terrace in the front garden. There is also a small hotel in the building.

Name: Knipsers Halbstück - Brasserie
Description: The Knipsers, a well-known family of winemakers from Laumersheim, opened Halbstück as a wine tavern back in 2014. Christian Rubert, who is also known for his work at the restaurant Karlbacher in Großkarlbach, has now taken over as head chef here. His roots in Alsace are evident in his dishes, which pair beautifully with the finest wines from the Knisper winegrowing estate. Laura Rubert provides warm hospitality in a cosy setting. Delightful courtyard. They also offer guided wine tastings (for 10 people or more) and accept bookings for weddings and conferences. A holiday flat is available to rent out, too.

Name: Koseler Hof
Description: At Koseler Hof, you can savour authentic North German cuisine. This pretty restaurant serves flavoursome dishes with a modern twist, and which are made with fresh, local ingredients. Opt for the tasting menu or order à la carte. In the summer, you can sit in the inviting verdant garden to the rear of the building. In addition to the restaurant, there is a boutique selling house-made goods (eg honey, pickled vegetables etc). Visitors to the region should take the opportunity to go hiking along the Sly Firth.

Name: Schreiberei
Description: In the heart of the city, just a stone's throw from Marienplatz, this restaurant is on the ground floor of Munich's heritage-protected chancery, where the city's history was first recorded in 1552. The attractive interior has a brasserie feel and, in good weather, the quiet sheltered courtyard terrace is especially inviting. The dishes on the menu are bursting with flavour and made with select ingredients, such as the veal cheeks with truffle polenta.

Name: Waldhorn
Description: This restaurant in Stuttgart's Rohr neighbourhood serves an intriguing take on classic French cuisine that draws on Spanish and Swabian influences. This concept wasn't simply plucked out of thin air: the two chefs – José María González Sampedro, who hails from Mallorca, and Caroline Autenrieth from Swabia – met while working in a restaurant in Marseille.
