The six courses on their surprise menu include deliciously aromatic lamb and braised shallot with a filling of blood sausage ragout with Mediterranean spices. In the attractive seating area, old wood panelling and modern furnishings add to the charm.

Name: Joseph's Fine Dining
Description: In the restaurant of Hotel Romantischer Winkel, imaginative cosmopolitan dishes are served in the form of a fixed menu. Dishes such as Wagyu roast beef with teriyaki, maple syrup, white cabbage and root vegetables are conjured up from predominantly regional ingredients in combination with international spices and seasonings. The decor is pleasingly modern: a small booth with an open kitchen corner makes for an intimate feel, and the floor-to-ceiling windows next door afford a view of Lake Schmelzteich. The set menu is served at the same time for all diners, with the chef and sous-chef guiding you through the evening. To finish off, coffee is brewed at your table.

Name: Lou im Cavalierhaus
Description: The estate is worth a visit in its own right. Along with the palace, there is the 620ha Branitz Park, landscaped by Prince Hermann von Pückler in the 19C. Lou (a nickname given to Prince Pückler) is an elegant restaurant housed in the smart Kavaliersbau (squire's lodge). Here, chef-patron Tim Sillack serves up a modern and seasonal take on classic cuisine, drawing on international influences, cf. his saddle of venison with chanterelles, Lieblingsbrot and wild berries. The chef also refers to the prince's own recipes, creating a link between past and present. The Pücklereis (Neapolitan ice cream) – something of a signature dessert – is a permanent feature of the menu. There are also three tastefully furnished guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Chicha
Description: Bustling, loud, rustic, and just a touch “shabby”... Chicha has succeeded in creating an informal authentically South American atmosphere to complement its modern Peruvian cooking. Quality fresh products are ambitiously blended to mouthwatering effect, with dishes such as ceviche of meagre fish and Thüringer Duroc belly of pork with smoked banana featuring on the menu.

Name: Konrad's
Address: Platz der Vereinten Nationen 4, Bonn, 53113, Germany
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant on the 17th floor of the Marriott Hotel has the "wow" factor of a great view over Bonn through its floor-to-ceiling windows. In the open kitchens they cook up modern dishes with Mediterranean influences. Pre- or after-dinner drinks are served in the bar right next door. Parking is available in the underground garage, and the lift leads directly to the restaurant.

Name: mural farmhouse - À LA CARTE
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The second part of mural farmhouse is a modern, casual bistro that places just as much emphasis on sustainability and regionality as FINE DINE. Ingredients are sourced locally and harvested from the restaurant's own raised garden beds on the roof of its affiliated hotel, WunderLocke. Delicious dishes such as einkorn risotto with mountain cheese, herbs (from the rooftop garden), piment d'Espelette and cabbage crisps are served à la carte. You can also have lunch here – the range is slightly smaller and includes some options from the evening menu, as well as a reasonably priced bento box. The selection of organic and biodynamic wines is the same as in the fine dining restaurant.

Name: Marie
Description: Marie is located in the Oststadt district of the city, surrounded by historical buildings. The modern yet warm and inviting atmosphere sets the scene for French cuisine with creative and Far Eastern influences. Chef-patron Sven Holthaus serves two set menus (one vegetarian) with up to five courses, plus oysters as an optional course. Choose your accompaniment from the wine list, which may be short but covers all bases when it comes to German and French labels – there are also wines by the glass. Attentive service. The pleasant terrace in front of the house opens in summer. Be sure to reserve.

Name: Green Beetle
Description: Environmental awareness and sustainability have always been key in every aspect of this restaurant certified as organic – from the tasteful interior design to the staff uniform and not least the food. The food is vegetarian and vegan – diners can choose between the set menu ("Your Choice") and surprise menu ("Our Choice"). During the week, a lunch deal with different options for each of the three courses is available. The exceptionally friendly and attentive front-of-house team will happily recommend wines from their almost exclusively organic or biodynamic selection. Lovely covered terrace.

Name: Alte Schule
Description: In this former school building done out with a cosy modern decor, enjoy the friendly attentive service. Here, they serve seasonal dishes prepared using regional ingredients, such as Wittgenstein venison goulash with Serviettenknödel (sliced bread dumpling cooked in a napkin) and apple compote.

Name: Clinton's
Description: Near the outskirts of Berlin, this restaurant is housed on the first floor of the European headquarters of the fashion company Clinton. The decor is up to the minute, as is the seasonally influenced cuisine – choose between a four- or six-course set menu and their à la carte "Signature" dishes, from "Berlin Blutwurst, sauerkraut, green back bacon, cassis, mustard" to "300g beef – roast beef, fillet, 16hr-cooked ox shoulder, truffle purée, teriyaki, vegetables from the farm". Fans of dry-aged steaks are also in for a treat. The service is attentive and the waitstaff professional. From some tables you can sneak a peek into the Clinton outlet.

Name: Kuhlemann
Address: Freyung 39, Neustadt an der Waldnaab, 92660, Germany
Description: You can tell from the food that the chef has worked in some top establishments. Here in the restaurant of the family-run Grader hotel, his interesting cooking style translates into a creative set menu. This is accompanied by an appealing and concise wine list. The attractive setting blends rustic and modern features.

Name: Belvedere
Description: The culinary flagship of the Travel Charme Strandidyll hotel. From your table in the fourth-floor dining area, which with its glass dome has an elegant modern feel , you can take in the wonderful view over the hotel grounds all the way to the Baltic Sea. The cuisine is classic in its foundations and partly based on regional produce. You are free to put together your own set menu. Friendly and well-drilled waitstaff. Tip: Your aperitif is best enjoyed on the gorgeous terrace.

Name: POTS
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Relaxed, chic and stylish! The eye-catching features of the Ritz-Carlton's restaurant are its striking decor and large open kitchen. Here they put a modern spin on German dishes, such as meatballs with Bavarian prawn and Riesling sauce – also suitable for sharing. Or perhaps you'd prefer the surprise menu? Run by none other than Dieter Müller.

Name: Restaurant Mühle
Description: The kitchen crew from Krone in Weil am Rhein has joined forces with the local team behind the stove here. Their cuisine – based on a contemporary blend of regional, seasonal and Mediterranean influences – is made with good, fresh produce. The elegant, rustic-style interior is inviting, plus there is a lovely terrace. Cosy, comfortable guestrooms await you in the hotel. On the practical side: it is only about 15 minutes by car to Basel, the airport and the trade fair.

Name: Die Ratsstuben
Description: One draw of this restaurant is its beautiful location in the centre of the pretty old town on the Alb River; another is its chic modern interior. The cuisine is international and seasonal – you can opt for a set menu or order à la carte. The waitstaff are friendly and professional. In summer, the terrace facing the square is a pleasant spot to sit and eat.

Name: Berta
Description: Berta would be very proud of her grandson, chef Assaf Granit, who has named this appealing restaurant after her. The energy of the chefs in the open kitchen, nestled behind the counter, is infectious, as they fill the colourful dining space with a vibrant and convivial atmosphere. A lively scenario, for which the menu is a perfect match: it is a veritable celebration of family recipes from Jerusalem infused with the modern spirit of Berlin. The "Frenavon" bread with tahini and tomatoes served beforehand is downright addictive. It is practically impossible to resist the charm of this restaurant!

Name: KOS fine dining
Description: This restaurant is a little off the tourist trail, but it's well worth the journey. Expect chic and trendy interior design, attentive service and, last but not least, culinary finesse built on exceptional ingredients, showcased in flavoursome and dishes that are nuanced without being overly complicated. Every evening there is a choice of two six-course set menus – one vegetarian, the other omnivore. Tip for those who have a smaller appetite: On Wednesdays and Thursdays, there is also a surprise menu comprising just four courses.

Name: Restaurant 1831
Description: Even the route to the magnificent moated castle, a 17C architectural gem, is an experience – you get to this stunning estate through a wooded area, then a bridge over the moat leads into the beautiful inner courtyard. The restaurant allies the character of this site steeped in history with modern comfort and winter garden-style. The view through the large glazed front is fabulous, not to mention the terrace! They serve two set menus of modern inspiration – one with meat and its vegetarian counterpart.

Name: Fritz's Frau Franzi
Description: This restaurant is located in stylish boutique hotel The Fritz, and you can have an aperitif at the bar in the lobby . The upscale interior is tasteful, and has a cool and trendy feel. Tobias Rocholl refers to his cosmopolitan, modern and creative culinary concept as "Gourmet in Action". Instead of butter, he uses high-quality oils, any dairy products are lactose-free, and he avoids industrial sugar altogether. Dishes such as Ijsselmeer pike-perch, lemon pointed cabbage, sauerkraut, leek vinaigrette can be ordered à la carte or as part of a set menu that you put together yourself. Vegetarian and vegan options are also available. Tip: From some tables you get a good view of the kitchen.

Name: Ontra
Description: This restaurant with a tastefully designed modern interior is located in TechSquare, the new centre for digitalisation south of the city centre. A friendly and professional team serves up seasonal cuisine that also includes vegetarian dishes. The shorter lunchtime menu proposes some cheaper options. The neighbouring Ontra's Gourmetstube serves a fixed set menu made up of seven courses in the evening.

Name: l'Ecume
Address: Friedberger Landstraße 62, Frankfurt on the Main, 60316, Germany
Description: L'Ecume means "foam" and makes reference to the lightness of the cuisine here as well as to French chef Alexandre Sadowczyk's native region of Champagne and its famous sparkling wine. In a friendly, casual atmosphere, diners tuck into modern French dishes that incorporate regional accents. The length of the set menu is variable.

Name: Margaux
Address: Kornmarkt 7, Limburg an der Lahn, 65549, Germany
Description: Fabian Sollbach has struck out on his own and opened this tastefully modern restaurant housed in a fully renovated 14C building in the heart of the old town. In this setting, he serves up a modern take on French cuisine, in which select ingredients take centre stage. The menu includes ambitious dishes such as beef carpaccio with onion, truffle and oxtail praline. At lunchtime, the options are somewhat more limited and simpler. There are a handful of places to be had on the small gallery level and, in summer, tables are set up on a lovely terrace on the Kornmarkt.

Name: Feinschliff
Description: This town-centre restaurant has a trendy, chic interior and a window through which you can see the chefs at work in the centrally positioned kitchen. The large floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto the church square of Pfarrkirche St Peter. In the evening, there is a modern set menu which incorporates subtle Asian influences and service starts for everyone at 6.30pm (by reservation only). Decent, reasonably priced wine pairings. At lunchtime, only a dish of the day is served.

Name: Hof Grothues-Potthoff - Hasenklee
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A charming modern restaurant serving seasonal cuisine that often incorporates home-grown fruit and vegetables. Choose from two set menus of either four or five courses (with a three-course version on Wednesdays), one of which is vegetarian. Two additional dishes are available as optional extras. The service is friendly and the chef offers helpful wine recommendations. This beautiful farm also boasts a bakery, farm shop and hotel. Alternatively, Hasenpfeffer is open in the evenings – it serves traditional cuisine and dishes drawing on modern influences.

Name: Ivy
Description: The restaurant on the ground floor of the very centrally located 133 Boutique Hotel Karlsruhe provides a stylish bistro-style setting in which to enjoy modern, trendy cuisine either à la carte or in the form of a sharing menu for upwards of two people. You can also order various steak cuts served with a side dish and sauce of your choice – you even get to choose your own knife! The appetisers for sharing beforehand are fun, too. Why not finish off with a cocktail in the adjoining bar?

Name: Ahlmanns
Description: Lasse Knickrehm is now head chef at the fine dining restaurant of the Hotel Kieler Kaufmann, which enjoys a quiet location in a smart residential neighbourhood. He and his kitchen team conjure up creative cuisine that is also grounded in tradition – an interesting example is his dish of turbot, marrow, sauerkraut, grapes. In keeping with the modern thinking behind the four- to eight-course set menu, intriguing alcohol-free drink pairings are also offered as an alternative to wine. The historical space, a former banker's mansion, has been tastefully enhanced by a contemporary minimalist design and warm tones. Tip: On summer evenings, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace overlooking the park. Kaufmannsladen is a laid-back alternative.

Name: Fangfrisch
Description: A friendly, laid-back restaurant located on the edge of the city centre, only five minutes from the Holstentor. Trendy industrial-style design, very friendly and relaxed young service team and, last but not least, tasty modern cuisine. The emphasis is on regional ingredients – for example, organically farmed catfish from Brandenburg. Hot meals are served all day, but there are also sandwiches and fish rolls to go.

Name: Zwo20
Description: The name of this restaurant refers to the year 2020, in which Andrea von Csiszer (head chef) and Sophie Herzog (the cordial and highly adept maître d') set up shop. Diners are drawn here not only by the somewhat unusual setting in a historical chapel with striking features such as vaults and ceiling paintings, but also the trendy and laid-back atmosphere, as well as the intriguing culinary concept: Asian sharing cuisine with a European twist. You can put together an assortment of several small, cleverly devised dishes to share, such as "Peking pork 24hr sous vide" with fried onion, soya and honey, or cauliflower wings with red cabbage, sweet chilli, fennel and potato. The location in the centre of the old town, caught between the Danube and the Inn, near the Dreiflüsseeck (three-river confluence), is also delightful. Tip: Römerplatz multi-storey car park just a few minutes' walk away.

Name: JAPATAPA TOSHIBAR
Description: Japatapa Toshibar is tucked away in a side street near Münchner Freiheit in the Schwabing district. Having formerly run the restaurant Toshi for a long time, owners Toshio and Tamiko Kobatake are no strangers to Munich's gastronomy scene. The small space, in which you sit at the counter or a small table, is done out in a minimalist style. Kobatake's cuisine is authentically Japanese: you should definitely try the tasty sushi, but dishes such as onsen egg with caviar and dashi broth or black cod grilled with saikyo miso are also tempting. The proprietress provides discreet and friendly service, and there is a good selection of wines as well as an impressive number of sakes.

Name: Eatrenalin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An almost futuristic spin on the fine dining experience! Using the online ticket system, you choose one of the set menus – "Red Dimensions" or "Green Dimensions" (vegan) – and your drink accompaniments in advance. Those who want extras can choose both menus in the variants "Exclusive Dinner", "Champagne Dinner" or "Sommelier Dinner". During the 2hr "Eatrenalin Experience", you are guided through different themed worlds and rooms on ultra-modern "floating chairs" and treated to corresponding appetisers and dishes. This is an ambitious take on modern and creative cuisine that draws on international as well as classical influences. The experience starts in the lounge and ends in the bar with music from a DJ, champagne and cocktails.

Name: Landgasthof Adler
Description: This centuries-old inn has long been known in the region for serving good food. Since February 2022, chef Michael Vogel has been perpetuating this tradition: he worked at the Adler years before and took over the reins after a stint working under top chef Andreas Caminada. The style of the decor is charming with its mix of tradition and modernity. Tip: The shop (Lädle) selling regional produce. Pretty guestrooms.

Name: Von Korff
Description: This patrician house, successfully remodelled and extended, has an appealing feel of modernity with its clean, simple forms and abundant light. Good selection of Bordeaux wines.

Name: In Vino Veritas
Address: Steinacher Straße 9, Haslach im Kinzigtal, 77716, Germany
Description: Inga and Ralf Müller have made a name for themselves with this friendly restaurant. This is due in no small part to the international and regional cuisine, which is made with very good, often local ingredients. The service is attentive and charming. In summer, you can dine on simpler fare in the charming courtyard with its vine arbour. There are chic, modern guestrooms and apartments for overnight stays.

Name: Rodesand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In an idyllic lakeside location by the Kellersee, this estate was made famous by the Immenhof cult film series. Today, in the stylishly elegant space within the pretty white walls of the manor house, ambitious classic cuisine with a modern twist is served. Dishes can be ordered as a set menu or à la carte. Delightful terrace with a view of the surrounding countryside; hotel, riding facilities and farm shop also on site.

Name: Ratsstube
Description: Antje and Ronny Pester's lovely restaurant is located in the town centre, in the wing of the town hall. In the cosy, tastefully decorated interior, they serve ambitious modern cuisine aligned with the seasons – the tuna tartare, for example, is delicious. There is a set menu on Fridays and Saturdays – a vegetarian version can be pre-ordered. The service is attentive and friendly - the owner's wine suggestions are spot on. Lovely terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Tupac
Description: This special restaurant in a residential area is the sort that everyone would love as their local! Named after revolutionary leader Tupac Amaru, it serves "cocina libre", in which the traditional cuisine of Latin America is freely and creatively transformed into interesting dishes packed with flavours and aromas. The open kitchen, rustic style and authentic decor make for a great atmosphere, and there is a lovely terrace for alfresco dining. Tip: Start off with a cocktail.

Name: Gutsschenke
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant's tasteful modern interior design has been beautifully integrated into the historical setting of the 150-year-old Monrepos estate. Outside, there is a delightful terrace under the shade of chestnut trees. The seasonally influenced cuisine is served in the form of a set menu (vegetarian version available) and à la carte. Options include classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with champagne sauerkraut, as well as modern dishes such as wild garlic risotto with red prawns marinated in rosemary and burrata. Tip: Take a walk through the beautiful park and take in the view of the lake and golf course.

Name: WEINrestaurant Ayler Kupp
Description: While you tuck into the fresh seasonal dishes, which the chefs here like to cook up with produce from the region, you can take in the vineyards and the lovely garden. The wine list includes Riesling from the neighbouring wine estate. They also offer accommodation for overnight guests: the hotel has inviting, well-kept guestrooms ready for you.

Name: Berghofstüble
Description: This restaurant enjoys a stunning location up above the town. The interior has a pleasing design and there is an attractive conservatory with a pretty terrace outside offering impressive views. The cuisine is based on good, fresh produce with appetising dishes such as Skrei cod on leaf spinach in beurre blanc.

Name: Schwarzmatt
Description: Served à la carte or as a set menu, classic cuisine made with seasonal produce is the order of the day here. The upscale interior is very comfortable, with harmonious, lovingly arranged decorative objects – it certainly does full justice to the luxurious setting of the traditional holiday hotel of the same name in which this restaurant is housed. For overnight stays, there are elegant country-house-style guestrooms – this is after all the sister hotel of Baiersbronn's Hotel Bareiss. Make a beeline for the gorgeous garden terrace in summer. A must in the afternoon: cakes made to Hermine Bareiss's old recipes!

Name: mondi
Description: Owner Pelle Kossmann and his young team are committed to implementing their own culinary ideas here. The set menu changes every fortnight and is made with select seasonal ingredients sourced from regional producers; some of the livestock and vegetables are raised or grown exclusively for this restaurant. The chefs also adhere to the principle of nose-to-tail eating. The decor is sleek and modern, with a partially visible kitchen and friendly, laid-back service. Fixed charge for table water.

Name: Heiderand
Description: Located close to the Dresdner Heide woodland, after which the restaurant is named, Heiderand now has Martin Walther at the helm – representing the fourth generation of the family to run the place (his parents are still involved). In this grand building dating back to 1905, diners can enjoy modern cuisine with an international slant. There are two set menus: wasser & weide ("water & pasture") and the vegetarian acker & beet ("field and beet"), each with three or five courses on offer. Wine pairings are available upon request. Tip: Tramline 11 stops just in front.

Name: Villa's Wine & Dine
Address: Moselstraße 5, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
Description: In the fine dining restaurant of Villa Melsheimer, you can look forward to imaginative and creative modern dishes that are made from very good fresh ingredients. In summer, the gorgeous terrace overlooking the Moselle beckons! Should the weather not cooperate, you can also enjoy the view from the bright winter garden. The boutique hotel has comfortable guest rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Vinophil
Description: The name is a clue to the fact that wine plays a major role here. The restaurant with its pleasantly informal atmosphere also has a Vinothek. You can look forward to sound wine advice to help you find the right pairing for the delicious modern dishes with a regional touch. Interesting cocktails are also available.

Name: Genusswerkstatt Lodner
Description: You'll find this chic restaurant in the Hotel Lodner, a building that is a good 500 years old. Beneath the fine cross vault, they offer ambitious cuisine in the evening in set menu form or à la carte. At lunchtime, there is a simpler menu. Produce from their own spice manufactory is seamlessly incorporated. Friendly and well trained service. Specialities to take away in the adjoining delicatessen.

Name: PUR
Description: This pleasant, minimalist-style little bistro near the town centre serves seasonal cuisine with a penchant for regional produce – every effort is made to ensure that the ingredients are of the highest quality. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace in the garden at the rear of the building. They also sell their own house-made sauces, fruit spreads, ready meals in jars and the like.

Name: Brauereigasthof Aying
Description: The restaurant of the picture-perfect Brauereigasthof Hotel Aying is a traditional family business. In this harmonious, upscale yet cosy setting, a friendly and welcoming front-of-house team serve excellent regional cuisine made with top-quality seasonal produce. In addition to the selection of fine wines, there are of course Ayinger beer specialities. Comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthof Widmann
Description: You can clearly taste the enthusiasm that goes into preparing the food here. Seasonal and international dishes are served alongside regional fare, in a six-course set menu. A friendly front-of-house team presides over the two cosy dining rooms.

Name: Dorf-Chronik
Description: This fine winegrower's house dating back to 1747 stands in the centre of the town. Sandstone and half-timbering create a cosy atmosphere, and decorative pictures add a touch of modern flair. Charming courtyard terrace. The cuisine is seasonal with a creative twist. There are various set menus, including a vegetarian one. Friendly service comes courtesy of your hostess Marion Schwaab and team. Head to the wine shop to sample wines from the property.

Name: Die Klosterschänke
Description: Idyllically set a few kilometres from the city centre, this warm and welcoming family-run restaurant boasts a magnificent terrace affording splendid views of the Rhine plain. The chef cooks up regional and seasonal cuisine along with a selection of Italian dishes. The mouthwatering options include a classic cordon bleu with Black Forest ham and Alpine cheese, and saltimbocca alla romana from the chef's homeland.

Name: Mine
Description: Very close to Ku'damm, this chic and laid-back establishment is run by a family that already has restaurants in St Petersburg and Moscow. The premises actually used to be home to Berlin's smallest bar. A charming pavement terrace beckons in front of the restaurant. Their Italian cuisine (including classics such as vitello tonnato or pasta) also draws on international and seasonal influences. Opt for the "Greatest Hits" set menu (two or more people) for a tempting selection of dishes. Nicely curated wine list. The wine cellar can also be booked for private dinners or chef's table events.

Name: Appare
Description: Here, traditional Japanese food – washoku – is skilfully combined with modern influences, blending Far Eastern spices and cooking methods with European food. There is a short lunch menu and a more elaborate dinner menu. In Japanese "appare" is an exclamation of enthusiasm.

Name: Schlosskeller
Description: The lovingly decorated vaulted cellar is really cosy, while the terrace next to the castle pond is simply magical. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, from classic Wiener Schnitzel to roasted pike-perch fillet with creamed sauerkraut, potatoes with chives, and Riesling sauce.

Name: Le Comptoir
Description: Located in the Nauwieser Viertel, this restaurant is housed in an old sandstone and brick building, incidentally the birthplace of director Max Ophüls. An attractive modern interior and a friendly atmosphere await you here. The seats at the counter ("le comptoir" in French – hence the name of this establishment) are very popular. In the evenings, a modern seasonal set menu comprising four or five courses is served.

Name: DAS GOLDSTEIN BY GOLLNER'S
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The former Schützenhaus is really stylish, the sleek and chic design is of high quality – lots of wood preserves the relationship to nature. The ambitious cuisine encompasses traditional classics as well as modern and international dishes, from local saddle of venison with potted spaetzle to teriyaki-style wild salmon. Great walk-in wine cellar and wine list with 500 references.

Name: The Sakai
Address: Hedderichstraße 69, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description: With Hiroshi Sakai at the helm here, you're in the hands of a real sushi master. This basement restaurant is done out in authentic Japanese style: sleek and minimalist. From the seats at the counter, you can watch the food being prepared. They serve an omakase menu, which also comes in a vegan version. The service comes courtesy of a very friendly and professional front-of-house team. Great sake selection.

Name: Fine Dining by Phillip Probst
Description: Located in The Liberty hotel, this is a tastefully modern fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows affording a view of the small harbour. There is also a gorgeous terrace. Four evenings a week, chef Phillip Probst and his team use excellent ingredients to create an interesting set menu comprising four to eight courses. The dishes are modern, yet classical in their foundations – the wonderfully intense sauces deserve a mention. The fjord trout served lukewarm with cauliflower, caviar and a brown butter sauce, for example, is a highlight. The well-drilled front-of-house team are friendly and attentive – they really pull out all the stops!

Name: Regional
Description: After being refurbished and rejuvenated, Regional has moved into the former Herrehus of Schloss Reinach. The name says it all: to create their tasty, punchy dishes, almost exclusively Baden and Black Forest produce is used, and the majority of it is also organic. It's a joy to sit on the patio terrace!

Name: Das Bootshaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The restaurant of the Papa Rhein lifestyle hotel combines a tasteful maritime vintage look with good, fresh cuisine, offering dishes such as cod in a potato crust with balsamic mixed vegetables and lentils and pesto. There is a wonderful view of the Rhine and the surrounding vineyards – in summer guests can enjoy sitting out on the delightful terrace!

Name: Das Esszimmer
Description: A small, neat house on the outskirts of the city centre houses this pretty restaurant with its modern and minimalist design. The cuisine is also modern; one of the menus is vegetarian. The choice of accompanying beverages includes not only wines but also an alcohol-free alternative. Pleasantly relaxed, friendly and professional service.

Name: Der Dantler
Description: A tip to start with: reserve well in advance! Given the great value for money and the relaxed atmosphere, it's no surprise that they tend to get booked up. They call themselves the "Bavarian Deli". In the interior done out in a slick Alpine/country-style style, the service is personable and relaxed. At lunchtime you can order pasta, a pastrami sandwich, ramen or the fish dish of the day à la carte, or the three-course "business lunch". In the evening, creative modern cuisine is served in the form of a set menu – a vegetarian or pescetarian version is also available (request this when you book). On Thursdays and Fridays, the wine bar next door serves as a pop-up location.

Name: Lamm
Description: The impeccable façade is inviting for a start. Cross the threshold and an exceedingly friendly welcome awaits you. Take a seat in the charming dining area, where you will eat extremely well! The chef's cooking is classic, pared back and made with select seasonal ingredients. There is a choice of à la carte dishes and a set menu, which is also available in a vegetarian version.

Name: Lockstein 1
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This really is a special place: you enter the charming kitchen through the 500-year-old farmhouse, which is run by an established mother-and-daughter team. They inject love and skill into their cooking, which takes the form of a vegetarian set menu comprising fresh dishes made using regional produce. The two pretty holiday flats are also popular.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: This restaurant in a residential area in Maintal-Dörnigheim brings a slice of France to the Rhine-Main area. You can look forward to experiencing French-Mediterranean flair, both in terms of the feel of the place and Patrick Theumer's seasonally influenced cuisine. The three set menus, one of which is vegetarian, are particularly appealing. Friendly service. It is also pleasant to dine on the beautifully verdant terrace.

Name: Schwitzer's PUR
Description: There have been some developments at Schwitzer's. In the newly refurbished rooms of the former fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows affording views of the park grounds, diners are invited to embark on a culinary adventure that takes its cue from the seasons. Depending on the time of year, varying styles of cuisine are proposed – à la carte or as a three-course surprise set menu. Schwitzer's Hotel am Park has upscale guestrooms.

Name: Gasthaus Assenmacher
Description: It's clear that Christian and Christa Storch put their heart and soul into running this place. The chef-patron wins over diners with his modern take on classic cuisine. Eschewing any gimmickry, he lays the focus squarely on quality produce and flavour. The lady of the house manages the friendly and attentive waitstaff. Pleasant little terrace to the rear of the building. Decent accommodation options at the hotel.

Name: KRasserie im verve⁵
Description: A former textile factory has been transformed into a modern brasserie and event space, creating an attractive new destination. The exposed concrete and ventilation pipes give the space an industrial feel; minimalist design and decorative art create a modern and stylish look. The floor-to-ceiling windows can be opened up in the warmer months – there's a small terrace out front. Fresh and flavoursome dishes drawing on regional and international influences are served à la carte or as a set menu named "Herzstück". The rooftop bar is great in summer (Thu-Sat).

Name: Abt- und Schäferstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is housed in a centuries-old monastery manor set in lovely, peaceful countryside. The food is classical with seasonal influences – the house speciality is lamb – and can be enjoyed in the historical, rustic-style interior or on the pleasant terrace overlooking the Odenwald. The very well-stocked vaulted wine cellar dating from 1524 is also worth seeing. Well-kept guestrooms in Der Schafhof hotel.

Name: Papageno zur Schweizer Grenze
Description: A stone's throw away from the small border crossing at Tägerwilen, Patrick Stier (previously of Papageno at the old location) serves up classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences. Cosy interior with wood panelling and modern details. The vine-clad terrace beneath the pergola is delightful.

Name: Trichards
Description: This chic and modern restaurant-cum-wine bar is located in the Lehel neighbourhood. The owner comes from France, and French influences can be detected in the cuisine. The seasonal dishes can be accompanied by your choice from the comprehensive wine list. Ideal for those who like to eat al fresco – the terrace and garden are covered and as such protected from the elements.

Name: Wildfrisch Gutsküche
Description: Situated in the former gatehouse of the Schulenburg family manor house just outside Wolfsburg, this modern restaurant is simple yet elegant, with a completely open kitchen acting as the focal point in the dining room. The cuisine here is uncomplicated and seasonal, with an emphasis on regional products.

Name: Carte blanche
Address: Egenolffstraße 39, Frankfurt on the Main, 60316, Germany
Description: As the name "Carte Blanche" suggests, there is no fixed menu here; instead a single surprise menu is proposed. Wine pairings for the individual courses are available upon request. The cuisine is modern and seasonal and made using regional produce wherever possible. The emphasis is on artisanal craftsmanship; even the bread is made in-house. The restaurant boasts a lovely location in an attractive historical building on a corner plot, with high ceilings and stuccowork.

Name: Luis Dias - Das Restaurant
Description: Luis Dias, who gave the restaurant his name, cooks flavoursome Mediterranean dishes, and quality ingredients are par for the course in his kitchen. In the pleasant and exceedingly elegant space, he serves dishes such as "sea bass, gnocchi fritto, spinach, lobster foam". The three-course lunch set menu is reasonably priced. There is also a small shop where you can buy spices – the menu tells you which spice is used in which dish. Tip for motorists: parking available at Parkhaus Maternusplatz.

Name: Valentin
Description: In a small side street in the island's old town, you will find this restaurant in a lovely vaulted cellar. In a stylish and modern setting, you can enjoy seasonal cuisine made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Opt for a set menu comprising four or seven courses, or choose from the small à la carte selection. At lunchtime, the options are more limited. Friendly front-of-house team. The secluded terrace in the courtyard is a pleasant spot. There is also a wine bar.

Name: Gut Steinbach
Description: Restaurant HEIMAT, Auerhahn Stuben, Bayern Stuben and Tiroler Stuben – the elegant hotel of the same name, which also has a spa, offers diners a variety of restaurant option, all of which are elegant and inviting. The terrace, in particular, with its panoramic mountain view is quite an event – it's a great place to soak up the idyllic surroundings! The cuisine is seasonal, with an emphasis on sustainability; the majority of the ingredients come from within an 80km radius. The menu also features classics such as Wiener schnitzel or chateaubriand for two.

Name: Schranners Waldhorn
Description: Maximilian and Marie-Luise Schranner's establishment is a haven of comfort and calm. They have lovingly transformed this traditional inn with a tasteful interior design concept. At the helm, Maximilian Schranner specialises in classic cuisine and proposes three set menus: the "Menü Gourmet", the "Menü vegetarisch" and the "Wirthaus-Menü" – but you can also order dishes from these à la carte. There is also a very reasonably priced set menu at lunchtime. On warm days, the gorgeous terrace on the Seebach with its views of the castle is a particular highlight.

Name: Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The brasserie in the Parkhotel Quellenhof, flagship of the Aachen hotel industry, is stylish and elegant. Ambitious French and Mediterranean cuisine is served here – examples from the menu include heirloom tomatoes with burrata from Apulia and braised veal cheek with a lemon cream. Lovely terrace area.

Name: Gocklwirt
Description: What is it that draws regulars and day trippers here in equal numbers? The richly decorated rooms are wonderfully rustic and the remarkable collection of farm machinery is well worth seeing. Classic international as well as regional cuisine, from spicy salmon tartare to "Böfflamott" (beef in red wine) to the four-course set menu. Double guestroom in the house next door, should you wish to stay over.

Name: CLYNe - Das Restaurant
Description: On the edge of the old town and just a stone's throw from the pedestrian area is this cosy restaurant run with a personal touch. The name "CLYNe" (a play on the German word "klein") refers to the small number of seats – it is advisable to book. The seasonal cuisine draws on regional produce to create dishes bursting with flavour. There are three set menus: "Menü vom Land" (meat), "Menü aus dem Wasser" (fish) and "Menü nich' Fisch, nich' Fleisch" (vegetarian).

Name: Lazarus Stube im Oberschwäbischen Hof
Description: Good, fresh ingredients go into making this really tasty seasonal regional cuisine, including classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) or homemade Maultaschen (German ravioli). For more ambitious cooking, look to the "gourmet menu" of the second restaurant, Esszimmer. Modern and functional guestrooms available at Oberschwäbischer Hof.

Name: Pure Wine & Food
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The atmosphere here is pleasingly laid-back and trendy – in summer, the lovely terrace in front of the building gives you that holiday feeling. Using the freshest ingredients, the kitchen team serves up pared-back, modern Mediterranean cuisine. Diners choose between the "Chef's Choice" set menu, a vegetarian set menu and à la carte dishes. Given the restaurant's name, it is no surprise that wine plays an important role. The friendly and adept waitstaff will gladly recommend a suitable pairing for any dish. The terrific wine list comprises over 250 (organic) labels – also available to take away. Tip: Book a wine tasting.

Name: Gutshaus Kubbelkow
Description: With its smart façade and stylish dining rooms, this listed manor house set in wonderfully peaceful grounds has lost nothing of its 1908 charm. It serves fresh, ambitious cuisine including lagoon-fished zander with jellied bouillabaisse broth and pan-fried asparagus. The idyllic location makes the tasteful upmarket guestrooms dotted with antique furniture all the more inviting, as does the excellent breakfast.

Name: Rolin
Description: Elegant ambience, friendly service, tasty and ambitious international, classic and seasonal cuisine – on the menu e. g. fillet of North Sea cod with a horseradish, honey and rosemary crust. Incidentally, "Rolin" is the name of a ship's captain. Hotel Cap Polonio has well-kept rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Hackbarth's Restaurant
Description: Behind its red front door, this restaurant has a trendy, chic interior. A welcoming and attentive service team also awaits you. The modern cuisine combines local and international elements, Mediterranean and Far Eastern influences, and an emphasis on seasonal produce. Options are slightly more limited at lunchtime, but in the evening there is an additional six-course set menu. Nicely curated wine list. Lovely terrace. Tip: It is advisable to make a reservation for the weekend (Fri and Sat).

Name: Bernhard's
Description: The very centrally located Bernhard family restaurant is inviting in its country-traditional style and attracts many regulars as well as tourists. Tip: Try the Swiss-inspired dishes – the owner is a native of the Grisons canton. The menu also includes delicious classics such as Café de Paris rump steak. It is exceptionally pleasant to dine on the terrace. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are well-kept guestrooms available here or at Seebacher Haus, the hotel under the same management.

Name: Zirbelstube
Description: Set in a smart sandstone building dating back to 1860 with an equally attractive interior, the charming Zirbelstube offers a menu including spring chicken with mushroom sauce and celery champ. There is also a lovely terrace and some pretty guestrooms ideal for an overnight stay.

Name: Hermannshöhle
Description: This former ferry house from 1517 has a loyal following of regulars. Owner Wigbert Weck prepares delicious dishes from fresh produce. Tip: the surprise menu (only for the whole table). Inside, a modern wine bar ambience with a walk-in glazed wine refrigerator (focus on regional wines); outside, a pleasant terrace – separated from the Nahe by nothing but the street. There are two holiday apartments that can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: Am Kamin
Description: The atmosphere in this lovingly decorated restaurant is charming and welcoming. Over the service counter you can take a look into the partly open kitchen and watch chef-patron Karl Ress at work. He is a master of his craft and works meticulously to bring out the full flavour of his ingredients. The dishes on the menu are classical and seasonal – you can opt for the surprise menu or order à la carte.

Name: H'manns
Description: The Hegmanns run this genuinely charming restaurant that is a hit with diners. Only the best produce makes its way into the dishes, which are meticulously prepared to bring out the full flavour of the ingredients. You can opt for a set menu or order à la carte. On Thursdays, only tapas are served. Excellent wine list. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Tip: the chef's table is very close to the kitchen, but sheltered from the thick of the action.

Name: Jagstmühle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: With its cosy yet elegant interior and charming terrace, the restaurant blends wonderfully into the picture-perfect scene of the estate, which stands against the romantic backdrop of the River Jagst. The light hues of the wood panelling, the tiled stove and pretty fabrics all contribute to the inviting atmosphere. The food draws on international influences, with subtle Asian touches here and there. Dine à la carte or opt for the set menu (omnivore or vegetarian). Alternatively, the pleasant Mühlenscheune serves regional cuisine. There are also lovely guestrooms.

Name: Rüssel's Hasenpfeffer
Description: This excellent alternative to Rüssel'schen fine dining restaurant is very popular with guests! Here in the left-hand side of this attractive country house, the buzzy atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back; the tasty food is made using good-quality ingredients. Classic cuisine with regional influences can be enjoyed as a set menu or à la carte – game and braised meat are among the favourites.

Name: Gaststube Zum Klosterbräu
Address: Kirchplatz 1, Neuburg an der Donau, 86633, Germany
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This is how you imagine a historical Bavarian restaurant: wooden beams on the ceiling, floorboards, tiled stove – rustic, inviting and wonderfully cosy (or "zünftig" as they say in these parts). There is also a wonderful terrace. The cuisine is classic, regional and seasonal – served à la carte or in three set menus, one of which is vegetarian. There is a good selection of wines to choose from. Tip: well-priced lunch menu with two or three courses (Tues. to Fri., except public holidays). You can also visit the Baroque Münster Heilig Kreuz in Bergen.

Name: Bavarie
Description: Regionality and sustainability are two principles that underpin Bavarie, here at BMW Welt. This translates into combining elements of Bavarian and French cuisine with a focus on high-quality produce. You can dine à la carte or take the set menu – there is also a vegan option, plus a three-course business lunch deal. The atmosphere in the spacious, airy, high-ceilinged room is pleasant. Nice terrace with a view of the Olympic Park and Tower.

Name: Garden-Restaurant
Description: Belgian designer Axel Vervoordt has given this restaurant a very particular look. The industrial-style conservatory design creates a setting reminiscent of an artist’s studio.

Name: Novalis
Description: Diners here can eat inside, in the stylish, elegant restaurant, or outside with a view of the historical castle grounds. The seasonal food is brimming with flavours and aromas; it is made with top-notch, preferably regional produce, such as game that they have hunted themselves or smoked fish from Leinetal. A vegetarian menu is also offered. The service is attentive and cordial. Tip: wine list with a large selection of French red wines. Tasteful guestrooms in the Hardenberg BurgHotel.

Name: Kaisers Eck
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Situated by Ahlbeck's main church, this cosy restaurant with its pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere is run by a husband-and-wife team – she manages the waitstaff in her friendly and relaxed manner while he does the cooking. The cuisine is predominantly regional, and the "Lieblingsmenü" is a hit. However, there are plenty of other options that whet the appetite – the decision won't be easy.

Name: Klebers
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you are seated in the pleasantly bright interior or on the delightful terrace in summer, you can look forward to friendly and charming service as well as international and regional cuisine made from excellent produce. There are various set menus (including a vegetarian one) to choose from, plus a selection of dishes à la carte. The restaurant is housed in the tasteful Kleber Post hotel.

Name: Gengs Linde
Description: Christian Geng offers fresh and flavoursome cuisine that is traditional with international influences. His fashionable restaurant combines clean, modern lines with warm wood. Try the veal cordon bleu or the rack of lamb baked in a herb crust with peperonata and homemade gnocchi.

Name: Gasthof Schütte
Description: This region, which is a popular destination for hiking and cycling enthusiasts, is home to this traditional family-run country hotel with its own spa facilities and lovely restaurant. There are regional, classic and international dishes on the menu, which is somewhat more limited at lunchtime. In winter, an open fireplace adds to the charming atmosphere.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description: The atmosphere is really cosy in this restaurant, which is charmingly done out in the traditional style typical of the region. The kitchen serves up flavoursome, ambitious dishes with a regional and seasonal focus, as well as the occasional international twist. For overnight guests, this long-standing family-run establishment offers comfortable guestrooms and a spa with a range of facilities and treatments and a swimming pool.

Name: Gourmetrestaurant 1751
Description: Located in the heart of the city, in a wine merchant's house that is over 250 years old, this restaurant is considered one of the finest in the region. A delightful historical setting, it boasts a beautifully restored barrel-vaulted ceiling. They serve a five- or seven-course set menu comprising dishes that are meticulously prepared using predominantly regional produce. The wine list includes a few rare finds! Tastefully designed guestrooms are available in the Weinhaus Uhle hotel.

Name: Beesten
Description: Since 1906, over four generations, the Beesten family has put its heart and soul into running this traditional inn in the heart of Rheine. The owner himself is at the helm in the kitchen, preparing classic French and German cuisine peppered with seasonal influences. The interior is elegant and tasteful, while the service is charming. Take a seat on the terrace under the lovely old chestnut trees.

Name: Kreutzer's
Description: Though the location on business premises in the Westhafen port is a little out of the way, this smart, modern restaurant is fashionable and popular. It serves business lunches in the middle of the day and delicious meat and fish from the charcoal grill in the evenings.

Name: Lumperhof
Description: At this idyllically situated country inn, now run by the third generation of the same family, Jochen Fischer cooks tasty seasonal, regional fare. Try the breast of guinea fowl with asparagus and potatoes – which you can enjoy in summer on the delightful terrace.

Name: Sansibar
Description: A restaurant with cult status! This smart beach cabin is a much sought-after place to eat. It takes five minutes to reach it on foot through the dunes – or you can use the shuttle service. Fancy a Sansibar classic such as rice pudding with red fruit jelly? Or perhaps you'd prefer something more sophisticated? Superb wine list. No reservations taken at lunchtime.

Name: Schloss Monaise
Description: With Hubert Scheid's cuisine, this place is nothing short of a culinary institution in the region. His signature style comprises pleasantly straightforward dishes made from excellent ingredients – served à la carte or as a set menu. The restaurant occupies stylish, high-ceilinged rooms that channel the stately flair of these premises dating back to 1783 – once a summer residence. Or you can dine on the wonderful terrace with a view of the surrounding nature and the Moselle. It's also worth taking a look at the wine list, which features many a big name.

Name: freistil.
Description: In addition to an appealing modern decor featuring sleek design and warm wooden fittings, diners can look forward to a selection of regional and seasonal dishes (including vegetarian and vegan options) that can be put together to create a set menu or ordered à la carte. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel has attractive, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Forsthaus Hessenstein
Description: Once a forester's lodge, this restaurant in a stunning location is very popular on account of the cosy and charming dining area, friendly service and, last but not least, the good cuisine, in the form of classics such as Wiener schnitzel, Zwiebelrostbraten or crème brûlée. Tip: It is worth taking the time to climb the lookout tower. In addition, the many tracks all around are conducive to walks in the surrounding countryside.

Name: Postschänke
Description: With its cosy and lively atmosphere, Postschänke is a fantastic alternative to Zur Post, the fine-dining restaurant. Here, the delicious seasonal cuisine made with select, fresh ingredients goes down a treat. They serve a daily set menu with options, as well as daily specials. The service is exceedingly friendly and attentive.

Name: Sülbecker Krug
Description: If you fancy prime beef cooked in an oven heated to 800°C, then this restaurant renowned for its meat is a good choice. The menu includes classics such as rib-eye, rump or flank steak served on a wooden board with superb sauces. They also have a wine bar. Various promotions are also offered throughout the year – don't hesitate to enquire!

Name: Kaiserblick
Description: This eatery is a good alternative to the Brockel Schlimbach restaurant at Nideggen's centuries-old castle, Burg Nideggen. They serve market-based cuisine in the form of regional dishes, prepared from fresh seasonal ingredients mainly sourced from suppliers and producers in the region. The interior decor is modern and the front-of-house team is very friendly and obliging. Weather permitting, you can dine on the pretty terrace in the castle courtyard.

Name: Spinne
Address: Eichkehle 58, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, 67433, Germany
Description: This restaurant situated on the forest's edge sticks to a simple winning formula, with a focus on regional and seasonal cuisine prepared using the finest ingredients. Perhaps you'd like to try the surprise menu? Take a seat out on the lovely terrace. Welcoming and modern guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Das Esszimmer
Address: Hintergasse 38, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, 67433, Germany
Description: A lovely restaurant in the Old Town: the welcoming, sleek and modern setting is bound to appeal, and the atmosphere is pleasantly intimate, the service is attentive and well trained. You can watch Italian/Mediterranean dishes being prepared in the open kitchen. Look out for the "speciality days". On Thursdays: tasting menu only. The terrace in front of the house is also a pleasant place to sit.

Name: Spitzweg
Description: This place has been serving up consistently good food for years – there's a reason why it attracts so many regulars. On the menu: seasonal, regional and international dishes. The sleek, modern decor boasting a bold red colour scheme and paintings on the walls is stylish. Friendly and professional service. The lively terrace set up on the pavement is a lovely place to sit. There is also an annexe for private events.

Name: Ostaria da Gino
Description: This delightful family-run restaurant's enduring popularity among regulars is a testament to the unwavering dedication and passion that have been poured into its operations for the past 40 years. Authentic Italian cuisine is served in a laid-back setting with bags of charm! Staff will be happy to guide you through the options written up on the board and recommend the right wine. Tip: the moderately priced lunch deal. Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home.

Name: Gute Stube im Parkhotel
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant modern restaurant complete with roof terrace is housed in an imposing building by the Stadtgarten. The cuisine is ambitious and contemporary; as well as an à la carte selection, there are seasonal set menus, including vegetarian options. The chefs try to use regional produce as much as possible. Friendly service. For a simpler alternative in the evening, head to Das Stübchen or the beer garden. Parkhotel offers cosy guestrooms.

Name: Vinaiolo
Description: Even after more than 25 years since its opening, Vinaiolo continues to bring a delightful taste of la dolce vita to Haidhausen. Attentive service comes courtesy of a charming, well-drilled team, embodying a spirit that is tipicamente italiano. Although the Italian cuisine served here is not focused on any particular region, it is unfailingly authentic. Mouthwatering options such as the Sardinian fregola with lamb ragout and the Nebrodi pork chop are testament to this. Excellent selection of Italian wines. The cosy, authentic atmosphere is accentuated by furnishings salvaged from a Trieste grocer's shop dating back to 1904!

Name: Käfer-Schänke
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The name "Käfer" has become synonymous with Munich's gastronomy scene. The ace up the sleeve of this Munich institution: the restaurant and delicatessen being under one roof means you can be sure that you are dealing with top-drawer ingredients. These are used in classics such as beef tartare, lobster stew or roast duck for two, served in two courses. The atmosphere is cosy, the service professional and friendly. An additional feature is that they have a number of individually designed function rooms available for special occasions.

Name: Nymphenburger Hof
Description: The Austrian inspired cuisine tastes just as good on the lovely terrace as it does in the friendly restaurant. Live piano music is also played on some evenings.

Name: Culinarium
Description: This chic, pared-back restaurant with a lovely terrace area is located in the Weingut Matthias Dostert, a winery that also offers cosy guestrooms. Chef Walter Curman draws on his considerable craftsmanship to meticulously create flavoursome dishes. The classics on the menu hint at his Austrian origins – try the appetising Kaspressknödel (pressed cheese dumplings) orAlt Wiener Kaiserschmarrn (Viennese pancake)!

Name: Brasserie Nodhausen
Description: The brasserie at this charming historical property serves international, regional and seasonal cuisine. On the menu, you'll find mouth-watering options such as mascarpone ravioli with truffle and parmesan or saddle of venison with wild broccoli, pearl barley and celeriac cream. This appealing restaurant has the feel of a conservatory – large windows look out onto the beautiful grounds planted with old trees. Tip: Edible oils are available for purchase at the restaurant's own delicatessen – ideal for the home or as a little gift.

Name: Herzog von Burgund
Description: First you admire the attractive exterior of this stylish townhouse. Then, inside, the impressive, heritage-protected staircase. The two dining spaces (Erftzimmer and Gartenzimmer) form a classically elegant setting – the paintings by Düsseldorf artist Markus Tollmann draw the eye. The menu has a seasonal focus, and Wiener schnitzel is a house speciality. Friendly and experienced waitstaff. Delightful outdoor seating: The terrace is a verdant oasis in the heart of the city!

Name: Martinelli
Description: If you’re looking for Italian hospitality and the food that goes with it, Martinelli offers seasonal, modern cuisine including dishes such as pecorino ravioli with walnut and balsamic vinegar or saddle of venison with quince. And to whet your appetite, there’s always a plate of air-dried ham and some delicious bread.

Name: Torkel
Description: The Stoppel family serve not only cuisine underpinned by Mediterranean and classic influences, but also plenty of regional dishes. If you are having trouble choosing, a failsafe option is the short "Fine Dining Menü". It's also well worth perusing the wine list. Sit back and enjoy your meal in the inviting dining space or out on the pretty terrace. The hotel of the same name has lovely cosy guestrooms.

Name: Rocca Riviera
Description: Rocca Riviera is a relaxed and stylish restaurant with a pleasant atmosphere not far from the Odeonsplatz. It serves Mediterranean-French fusion cuisine on a sharing plate basis, as well as meat and fish from the charcoal grill.

Name: Schwarzreiter Restaurant
Description: This fine dining restaurant boasts an exclusive location in the famous Maximilianstraße, more precisely within the legendary Munich luxury hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, complete with its own entrance from the street. The atmosphere is elegant without being stuffy; indeed, the sophisticated, modern and chic interior makes for a pleasingly urban ambience. The approachable and well-trained front-of-house team, who are always attentive and courteous but by no means intrusive, is the perfect fit. Then there is the cosmopolitan cuisine of Franz-Josef Unterlechner, who uses top-notch ingredients from the region and beyond. The Balfego tuna cheek, aubergine, salt lemon, chorizo, for example, showed us how successfully he brings to life his own ideas. A good all-day alternative, should you need one, is the pleasant Tagesbar, where the food is cooked by the same team.

Name: Gasthof Ochsen
Description: This welcoming inn that is run with great dedication has been in the family since it was founded in 1763. This place is really inviting with its charming dining areas, gorgeous terrace and courtyard. Taking its cue from the changing seasons and Baden culinary tradition, the menu includes specialities of the house such as saddle of veal and offal. Comfortable overnight accommodation available.

Name: Pfistermühle
Description: Once a ducal mill dating from 1573, Pfistermühle delights diners with its stylish Bavarian setting (including a lovely vaulted ceiling). The "Pfistermühlen Brettl" lunchtime set menu (Mon-Fri) with its four small courses (including vegetarian options) is great value. Good location only a stone's throw from the famous Platzl.

Name: Kurlbaum
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Michael Kurlbaum has run his restaurant with great dedication for 35 years. Spread over two floors, this place exudes a timeless elegance – in summer, a few additional tables are set up out front in the pedestrian zone. There are plenty of regulars who come for the classic cuisine. Lunch in the bistro area on the ground floor is popular too – they serve a moderately priced two-course set menu that changes weekly. This includes a bottle of water, and dessert is available as an optional extra. If you order in advance, you can also choose from the evening menu at lunchtime. Convenient for motorists: Kastell car park in Haagstraße close by.

Name: Stern's Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in the long-established Zum Stern hotel, this restaurant has a charming rustic feel with its wood panelling and lovely white tiled stove. The cuisine is regional but draws on international influences. There are two set menus to choose from (one of which is vegetarian), as well as an à la carte selection including barbecued steaks. The options are a little more limited at lunchtime.

Name: La Bohème
Description: A pleasingly convivial and relaxed place to eat. If you appreciate high-quality steak cuts, then this restaurant with a trendy urban atmosphere is just the ticket. But the menu also whets your appetite with a host of other dishes and delicious desserts. The sharing options (vegetarian versions available) will give you a good impression of the cuisine here. Popular brunch on Saturdays and Sundays. Tip for car drivers: Public car park ‘Schwabinger Tor’.

Name: Brasserie Les Deux
Description: If you like a lively, modern bistro, you’ll enjoy the seasonal, international dishes (such as gnocchi with asparagus and black tiger prawns) served here on the ground floor of Les Deux. Alternatively, try one of the “old” or “new” classics such as mini burgers or beef tartare with imperial caviar.

Name: Le Stollberg
Description: This charming little restaurant is run with a very personal touch by chef-patron Anette Huber. She serves up good-quality, fresh cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and draws on French and Mediterranean influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and well drilled, providing astute wine recommendations. Tip: The appealing lunch menu is great value for money! Plus light bites are served in the daytime bistro Le Petit Stollberg opposite.

Name: Altes Brauhaus
Description: The date 1779 is marked above the entrance to Altes Brauhaus, a brewery where beer was never in fact brewed. Now it serves up a tasty mix of regional and classic dishes (including vegetarian options) prepared by chef Ute Weishaupt who runs this lovely old restaurant with her sister Elke. The elegant, traditional style dining rooms alone with their sumptuous wood panelling and ornate carving are worth a visit. Charming interior courtyard terrace.

Name: Altes Rathaus by What the Food
Description: A truly delightful example of casual, down-to-earth gastronomy that brings pleasure and joy! This restaurant is housed in a picturesque half-timbered house in the pedestrian zone. The interior is modern and minimalist, and outside there is a charming terrace overlooking the forecourt. Chef-patron Patrick Schubert serves up dishes that are creative and full of flavour in the form of a tasting menu or à la carte. Friendly and competent service comes courtesy of maître d' Anne Henrichs. Good to know: they have a food truck that can be booked for special occasions.

Name: sushi Lounge
Description: The latest culinary hotspot at FAVORITE Parkhotel is a restaurant within a restaurant! Sushi lounge is located inside the hotel's Weinbar. Only sushi and sashimi are on the menu in this compact space, and everything is made with the finest produce – something for which FAVORITE Restaurant also has a reputation. Must-try nigiri: otoro for melt-in-your-mouth richness, scallops for pristine freshness or unagi for bold umami.

Name: Müllers auf Norderney
Description: Affording unobstructed views of the sea, 1884's exclusive location alone is a major draw. The charming little boutique hotel is a spa-style building complex composed of Villa Mathilde and the adjoining Villa Olga. It is also home to a chic restaurant with modern and minimalist interior design and a fabulous terrace. In the kitchen, Nelson Müller's team prepares flavoursome and pleasingly uncomplicated dishes from fresh, good-quality ingredients. Soul food would be an apt label for this cuisine.

Name: Pageou
Description: Located in the CityQuartier Fünf Höfe shopping centre, the chic restaurant of renowned TV chef Ali Güngörmüs is named after his hometown in the Turkish province of Tunceli. Here, his team serves Middle Eastern cuisine that draws on classic French influences and is available as a four-course vegetarian "Levante Menu" and as a five- or six-course "Chef Menu". A starter dubbed "Meze", for example, is a great option comprising various small dishes. A number of noteworthy Turkish labels are included in the extensive wine list. The lovely sheltered terrace is delightful on summer days.

Name: Schorn
Description: With Franz-Josef Schorn as maitre d' and Lukas Schild as chef, this restaurant in the Bilk neighbourhood boasts two big names in the Düsseldorf fine dining scene. Ambitious and flavourful dishes such as braised tri-tip of Wagyu beef from the Eifel region, with a balsamic jus, mashed potatoes, Brussels sprouts and watercress are served as part of the set menu and à la carte. The appealing wine list comprises mostly German and French labels. Friendly service. The dining space has a charming, intimate feel, with decorative features including an old stove, a wine barrel serving as a digestif table and modern paintings.

Name: Müllers auf der Rü
Description: Nelson Müller's second restaurant at Rüttenscheider Stern U-Bahn station is a popular spot for foodies, and makes for an appealing alternative to his fine dining restaurant, Schote. This is a market hall-style brasserie integrated into the shopping arcade. Sitting at high tables, diners tuck into delicious dishes ranging from currywurst to turbot, prepared in the centrally positioned open kitchen. You are also welcome to eat in Schote's dining area. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park around the corner.

Name: Hirsch
Description: This upscale restaurant serves classic cuisine that draws on Baden's culinary tradition and is made predominantly with regional ingredients. Options such as braised veal cheeks or a tasty fish medley in beurre blanc are sure to whet the appetite. Abundant wood and decorative features provide a cosy backdrop. In summer, head for the lovely verdant terrace. Very friendly service. Given the proximity to Strasbourg, the Black Forest and Europa-Park, it is also worth considering staying in one of Hirsch's well-kept guestrooms or apartments.

Name: Der Kaiserhof
Description: Run by the same family for four generations, Kaiserhof hides a surprisingly chic and fresh interior behind its deceptively traditional façade. The tastefully designed dining space is accessed via the open kitchen – diners can also watch the chefs at work. A seasonal menu comprising seven courses is proposed. The chefs are involved in serving and talk you through the dishes. In summer, head for the terrace in the small courtyard. There are well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Benders
Description: This remarkably chic and modern restaurant is housed in the pretty half-timbered building of the long-established Birkenfelder Hof. It is an ideal setting for casual dining, which is the name of the game here. The atmosphere is also suitably relaxed, and the waitstaff are experienced and friendly. The ambitious modern cuisine draws on French, Mediterranean and regional influences, and incorporates the odd Asian touch. The menu includes dishes such as Kikok rooster breast with a Madeira jus, pumpkin curry cream and pak choi, plus classics such as roast beef or burgers (only on certain days). Smart guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: DAS MAXI - GENUSSREICH
Description: Das Maxi has proven to be a successful addition to Das Freiberg hotel and is an appealing dining option – and not only for hotel guests. The kitchen specialises in contemporary, mostly Mediterranean dishes with seasonal influences. In addition to the set menu, which changes daily, there is also a small à la carte selection. Food is served in tastefully designed dining areas, and there is additional garden seating available for the summer months. The wine list, featuring international labels, is second to none. The gorgeous guestrooms have magnificent views of the mountains.

Name: La Citadelle
Address: 9 place de la Motte, Châteaubriant, 44110, France
Description: The restaurant occupies a prime position in the heart of this medieval town packed with old stone buildings and half-timbered houses. Chef Maxime, a local, and his wife Patricia, who hails from Lima, have created a delightful space in which you can sit back and lap up their hospitality. The dishes are made with fresh ingredients treated respectfully so as to bring out their intrinsic flavours, and are sometimes spiced up with a few South American touches (ceviche with tigre de leche, coconut milk etc) and dishes to share (platters of cold meats or cheeses), in a nod to Patricia's Peruvian origins.

Name: La Table - Maison Lobies
Description: In the middle of the village, with the church on one side and fields on the other, this beautiful 18C manor house with a courtyard to the front has a refined, classical decor. The premises are both home and place of work for an enthusiastic, smiling couple with experience in some of the world's top restaurants. Sun Young, a pastry chef who hails from South Korea, and chef Jérémie work together to devise an appealing, delicious and rather traditional menu: super-soft poultry with crispy skin and an excellent, generous fricassee of chanterelle mushrooms, and a buttery potato purée; beef chuck confit in its jelly sprinkled with hazelnut and boosted by a real mustard and shallot sauce! As for the desserts (floating island, Tahitian vanilla crème anglaise or raspberry cheesecake), it's as simple as this: they're all mouth-wateringly good.

Name: Au Marquis de Terme
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Surrounded by the Médoc vineyards, this contemporary restaurant is nestled in an outbuilding of the Château Marquis de Terme (a Grand Cru classified in 1855). It boasts a terrace that opens out onto the estate's pretty garden courtyard. Under the stewardship of Grégory Coutanceau, who devised the menu, chef Thibaud Guena welcomes his guests with fresh, modern cuisine that is very much of its time and shuns unnecessary frills. The appealing wine list features almost 600 labels, including a selection of Bordeaux reds and prestige wines available by the glass.

Name: Partage
Description: Julie and Hugo first met at Lameloise, later setting up shop in the house where Alexis Kreyder (1839-1912) – renowned for his still-life paintings of flowers and fruit – was born. The location, a traditional half-timbered inn painted pomegranate red on the outside and done out in contemporary style inside, wins diners over. As for the food, the talented chef creates nicely fragrant and balanced dishes that taste as good as they look, for example marinated and subtly smoked sea bream, bibalakas-style cream with herbs and beetroot shavings.

Name: Penati al Baretto
Address: 94 boulevard de la Tour-Maubourg, Paris, 75007, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It is no secret that Italians have great taste. Milanese chef Alberico Penati has set up shop in this chic bistro with honey-coloured wood panelling, and bay windows overlooking the garden of the Invalides – a highly prized location indeed! Tradition is the chef's passion. With no concessions to passing fashions, his menu features a selection of Italian classics made out of carefully selected ingredients. Home-made pasta remains the forte of this place, eg ravioli del plin piemontesi with a very good roast beef jus. The 100% Italian wine list highlights Piedmontese wines, particularly Barolo and Barbaresco.

Name: Akabeko
Description: This restaurant, which is home to Japanese chef Yasuo Nanaumi, who trained in star establishments, sports a ground-floor space with just a counter and a more upmarket, romantic dining room upstairs. At lunch and dinner, the chef crafts a surprise omakase (which literally means “I leave it up to you”) menu, reflecting his Japanese culture and his passion for French gastronomy, depicted by dishes such as foie gras with teriyaki sauce or sole goujonnettes with dashi. The entire team bends over backwards to ensure the wellbeing of their diners.

Name: La Grange de Pépé
Address: Domaine de Suzel, 267 route de Suzel, Vignieu, 38890, France
Description: In the peaceful northern Isère countryside, a family has revived the farming estate of its forebears and turned it into a hotel resort. In a picturesque, revamped stone barn, guests are invited to sample dishes overflowing in flavour rustled up by Argentinian chef Agustín Mercado Murua and inspired by the seasons and the region (Dombes duckling, farm-reared veal and locally bred trout), as well as herbs and veggies from the kitchen garden. Lovely alfresco patio in fine weather.

Name: Menna
Description: It's a family affair here: the father cooks, his daughter makes the desserts, bread and appetisers; her partner Jonathan is your host, presiding over the restaurant floor in tandem with his mother-in-law. All the food is home-made and in keeping with traditional Mediterranean style: courgette flowers and sea cicada broth; rabbit ballotine with herbs; Provençal stuffing; quasi of Aveyron veal and a vin jaune jus; rice pudding with rhubarb. From the pigeon to the Camargue rice, the olive oil and the meat from the butcher and beef farmer at the covered market, the ingredients don't have to travel far. This bistro is located in the centre of town, in a pedestrianised street near the Roman amphitheatre. The terrace overlooks a small square.

Name: L'Atelier du Nord
Description: Res nostra mare (or "the sea is our law") is the motto featured on chef Romain Paillet's website and, indeed, his modern, Japanese-inspired cuisine relies solely on what the sea has to offer. The ingredients, such as tuna belly, are impeccably fresh. Thanks to well-balanced condiments and preparations, each plate has plenty of pep… as does the chef, who, passionate about what he does, spends a lot of time in the dining area mingling with his customers. In line with the chef's cooking, the decor has blue walls and more than the odd nod to Japan. The kitchen, literally in the centre of the space, is the beating heart of the restaurant.

Name: Flaveurs - Domaine Mont-Riant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: In the Jurançon hillsides, this handsome 19C white mansion with a slate roof and set in wooded grounds is enjoying a new lease of life in the hands of a locally-born couple, Basque chef Patxi and his Béarn wife, Marilyn. The couple has tastefully revamped the bourgeois interior, whose windows command knockout views of Pau below. The decor provides the perfect foil for the veteran chef’s talented craftsmanship which slaloms between tradition and modernity. All of which is anchored in a commitment to sustainable fishing and local producers, illustrated by cèpe ravioles served with a mouthwatering slab of premium foie gras.

Name: Aïnata
Address: Le K2 Altitude, 356 route de l'Altiport, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
