Description: Zaatar, freekeh, sumac, grenade, bourghul, humus, tahini, mograbieh: the Franco-Lebanese chef, Alan Geaam, made sure he packed his rucksack full of goodies from his homeland before hiking up to Courchevel. This oriental score is played by chefs Guillaume Duchemin and Sébastien Wauxion. The former adds his light, delicate touch to ethereal desserts, in particular baklava, or the ghazel el banat (angel hair pastry) and orange-flavoured clotted cream ashta ice cream extravaganza. Warm, welcoming chalet vibe decked in wood and swish attentive service.

Name: L'Attanum
Address: 64 place de la Nation, Saint-Yrieix-la-Perche, 87500, France
Description: The ground floor of this 19C sous-préfecture is now home to a restaurant that welcomes you with contemporary interior design and smiling service. At the helm is a seasoned chef with stints at some prestigious establishments to his name. A fan of local seasonal produce, his cooking demonstrates his stellar technique (illustrated by his venison terrine), spot-on cooking and reductions (see his duck fillet served with spelt and beetroot) and delicately balanced flavours. The attentive staff and excellent wine cellar add the final flourishes to this gourmet experience.

Name: Le Canon
Description: An appealing restaurant proposing food that is simple yet exacting: gazpacho of tomato, white peach and sheep's-milk Tomme cheese; mullet caught locally, ratatouille of vegetables from the surrounding hills and black rice; fontainebleau made with sheep's-milk yoghurt, wild blackberries and greengages. Hand-picked local suppliers, the occasional nod to the Mediterranean, good 100% natural wines, with recommendations from the owner, an attractive "vintage bistro" interior: this place has everything going for it.

Name: Jupi
Description: At the helm of this modern bistro (polished concrete floor, trendy light fittings, wooden tables), with electronic music playing in the background, young chef Alice Roger shows she has experience (three years in London) and good taste (she worked with Michelin-starred chef Ryuji Teshima at Pages). Her cuisine is full of pep (thanks to elements such as the Noilly Prat sabayon, the gribiche sauce with violet mustard and the horseradish sauce) and decidedly exciting. The lunch menu is a steal. In the evening, plates for sharing are the name of the game.

Name: Maison Pavlov
Address: 199 avenue de la Libération-Charles-de-Gaulle, Le Bouscat, 33110, France
Description: Nowadays, this 17C Carthusian monastery is home to a small boutique hotel and its restaurant. Opt for a table on the terrace overlooking the swimming pool, or in the cosy dining room with an atmosphere reminiscent of an elegant boudoir (velvet banquettes, cane chairs and salvaged objects). In keeping with this setting, the chef dares to express herself in personal dishes with comforting subtle flavours: porcini, hazelnut praline and sweet wine espuma; paella with cuttlefish and farmhouse chorizo.

Name: L'Intangible
Address: Château de la Bousquétarié, Lempaut, 81700, France
Description: This 1850 family château was tastefully restored in 2022 by a young couple raised in the world of Alain Ducasse and used to high-flying establishments (Palais de l’Élysée and Plaza Athénée for her, Meurice for him). Their single set menu aims to showcase vegetables from the local terroir and their own kitchen garden, albeit scattered with globetrotting touches. Grilled white asparagus accompanied by a garlic sabayon, shiitake and oyster mushroom ravioli with egg confit, pigeon breast and leg wrapped in chard leaves. For dessert, the pastry chef steps in with fruity delights, such as a strawberry and Espelette pepper pavlova. Five exquisitely appointed guestrooms are available should you wish to prolong your stay in style.

Name: La Mangeoire
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In this picturesque Lot village, the traveller cannot fail but notice the handsome limestone edifice with a slate roof, flanked by a terrace and Belle Époque conservatory. The globe-trotting chef demonstrates a weakness for exotic combinations: velvety, humus-like aubergines, burnt rye bread, fried Camus artichoke and pork fillet dried in the hearthplace; lightly seared secreto pata negro pork with peanuts and ginger, roast fennel and whole wheat noodles. Bistronomic in style, internationally sourced and strewn with tributes to Asia and North African spices.

Name: Rond de Carotte
Address: 50 rue de la Vignette, Saint-Gervais-les-Bains, 74170, France
Description: In the heart of the resort, this eatery shines the spotlight on seasonal, sometimes local ingredients, such as Magland snails. The chef conjures up well-crafted dishes, like free-range poached egg flanked by sweet chestnuts and creamy squash, or melt-in-the-mouth chuck beef stew that is eaten with a spoon. The chalet-inspired dining room, divided in two by a small open-plan kitchen, is the quintessence of alpine charm, in particular due to the shelves loaded in bottles (the establishment is also a wine merchant). Daily brunch from 9am-2pm.

Name: Sao
Description: On the quayside of the River Odet in Quimper city centre, this restaurant is the brainchild of Kevin Gourret, who was previously chef at Le Goyen restaurant in Audierne. In an inviting contemporary setting, he serves original recipes inspired by local ingredients (langoustine, local fish, seaweed, buckwheat, buttermilk) and Asian influences (such as yuzu, ponzu, gomasio, sesame and ginger).

Name: Cheri Bibi
Description: In the city centre of this surfing mecca, this restaurant set back from the sea front is one of a crop of cool, trendy spots on the Biarritz culinary scene. Born and raised in Brittany, chef Adrien Witte was formerly a financier, but his passion for food led him to this career change. He goes to great lengths to make his guests feel good: there is an array of sharing plates (e.g. deviled eggs, aubergine confit, tuna sashimi, Lincolnshire sausage and polenta); dishes such as beef tartar with verbena and burnt lemon anchovy and white tuna with peach and kimchi jus have (already) attained the status of classics. The best local ingredients are prepared in an uninhibited and tasty way, with nods to the chef's international career. His partner welcomes you with efficiency and a smile. You can choose your own bottle in the wine shop. Inviting bistro decor with a bar and open kitchen.

Name: Mieux
Description: Three long-standing partners have opened this friendly address, the archetype of unapologetic bistronomie that satisfies the taste buds without breaking the bank. The food pays tribute to the market and quality produce, with dishes always in tune with the season. Friendly, unpretentious vibe and great value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Vacarme
Description: Chef Sarah Mainguy, who won French TV's Top Chef, has set up shop with her partner in this Nantes bistro with a cool, laid-back atmosphere and where everyone seems to be in a good mood. Renewed on a weekly basis, the bistronomy menu alone is enough to bring a smile to the face of any foodie: leek ravioli, anchovy cream; home-made sausage, rutabaga purée, citrus jus; cabbage stuffed with octopus and pork. Good list of natural, organic and biodynamic wines.

Name: Zéphirine
Description: This urban inn, sporting a bistro vibe and fronted by a delicatessen, is blessed with a quaint, old-fashioned name! It is also a family story that unites three veterans who’ve knocked around a bit. Each dish bears the chef’s distinctive hallmark (special mention for the side dishes and the starters, to share). The accent is on classic Gallic nosh with a modern twist in terms of presentation; the menu is more elaborate in the evening.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: Hôtel Bulgari, 30 avenue George-V, Paris, 75008, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Niko Romito, a chef from Abruzzo with three Michelin stars to his name, updates the classics of Italian cooking in a menu that really homes in on the produce and dares to go light (easy on the fat, limited sauces, steamed ingredients, rice starch for the breadcrumb coating etc). The saffron risotto with parmesan is subtle and does not weigh on the stomach, as is the magnificent veal cutlet alla Milanese, to be savoured in this elegantly sleek dining area that opens onto the interior garden.

Name: Terra
Description: A short walk from the city centre, in the suburbs of Chartres, the husband-and-wife team behind Terra (he is an Italian chef and she is a South African pastry chef) extend an invitation to join them on a culinary journey. The excellent and quintessentially Italian cuisine is served in a friendly atmosphere – the fiorentina-style cannelloni stuffed with veal and spinach and the house parmesan sauce is delicious!

Name: Parcelles
Description: The quintessence of retro Paris! In a side street between Arts et Métiers and the Centre Pompidou, this 1936 bistro would not have been out of place on the set of Woody Allen's Midnight in Paris: authentic bistro furniture, bare or beige walls, vintage tiled flooring, gilded ceiling, and a copper and wooden counter. The food is all that you'd expect: pressed pork shank, line-caught sea bass with spelt risotto and smoked eel sauce, and, of course, the dark chocolate and caramelised pecan tart. Ten out of ten for this restaurant that fully deserves its success. (Book if you can.)

Name: Le Sens 7367
Address: 141 boulevard de la Côte-de-Beauté, Vaux-sur-Mer, 17640, France
Description: It is a pleasure to catch up with chef Frédéric Loivel, with whom we are familiar from his Annecy days, now at home in the small village of Vaux-sur-Mer near Royan. This restaurant has almost the same name: the number 7367 still spells out "sens" on a telephone keypad. This creatively inclined chef conjures up modern dishes that enhance seasonal produce thanks to carefully thought-out marriages of flavours and a host of references to Japan (eg panko, yuzu, matcha, Kagoshima beef). The cosy contemporary space tastefully blends disparate decorative elements picked up here and there. There are also a few guestrooms.

Name: Le Comptoir Kokagué
Description: Set in the unlikely location of a tiny village in the Jura, this restaurant serving French-Japanese cuisine based on regional produce has a local following among the people of Mouchard and from the surrounding areas! In an interior that is largely unadorned but for a few plants, diners first make the acquaintance of this French-Japanese couple (she cooks, he manages the restaurant floor). Then the food is served: ingredients from the local terroir are woven into Japanese dishes, as in the celeriac purée with a wasabi kick, the trout marinated with kombu seaweed (on the kawamatsu kobujimè), or the Bresse chicken fillet worked into a tofu and shiitake patty flavoured with ginger (tori daikon). There is a good selection of wines organised by grape variety, mainly showcasing natural wines.

Name: Les Capucines
Description: The Demoget family has been perfecting the art of hospitality in this Rouen institution for three generations. In a stylish, classical interior, the focus is on generous French staples (thick juicy steaks served with Anna potatoes or salmon gravlax with a beetroot emulsion).

Name: L'Inattendu
Address: 18 avenue de la Plage, Saint-Gilles-Croix-de-Vie, 85800, France
Description: Tucked away amid the villas and holiday homes, L'Inattendu is as unexpected as its name suggests. The pleasant surprises keep on coming: from the amuse-bouches to the dessert, diners enjoy cuisine that is based on fresh local produce (including the odd herb plucked from the owner's kitchen garden), and skilfully prepared (eg hibiscus, saffron and lemon gels, ice creams and mousses). Sturgeon, endives and kombucha; a succulent 48hr-cooked pork belly, sweet potato and hibiscus; chocolate, caramel and saffron. You can also expect a warm welcome and palpable enthusiasm from the front-of-house team. A culinary hotspot that is a hit with locals and tourists alike.

Name: Maison Grandclaude
Description: Set in a handsome bourgeois house, fashionably done up in a contemporary vibe with untreated materials such as oak, this inviting venue, a ten-minute drive from Epinal, is the brainchild of Nicolas Grandclaude and his wife. The modern, soul-warming culinary slant, backed up by exquisite plating, is illustrated in the likes of butterflied and seared wild prawns with coconut milk, ginger and lemongrass, or pan-fried whiting filets with courgettes, almonds and basil. Delightful.

Name: La Table du Marché
Description: The petrol-blue frontage of this restaurant between the River Jaudy and Cathédrale Saint-Tugdual draws the eyes of passers-by. Inside the small rustic-style space, with white roughcast walls, exposed beams and old stonework, an appetising market-fresh menu is served: foie gras marbled with red wine; roast cod with Coco de Paimpol haricot beans; financier with pan-fried apricots. The chef, who boasts a great CV, draws on both tradition and bistronomy to concoct dishes that are inspired by regional produce. Wide choice of wines by the glass. The bill won't break the bank.

Name: La Traboule
Description: Just a few hundred metres from the Élysée Palace, this establishment sports a fashionable bistro interior and a buzzy vibe. The food errs towards well-crafted bistronomic courtesy of simple recipes that focus on big-boned, legible flavours.

Name: L'Hippi'curien
Description: At this small restaurant in an old building with exposed brick and pebble interior walls, diners have two options: excellent value for money at lunchtime or more elaborate cuisine in the evening with the single set menu. The new chef, who has a particular fondness for France's South-West, makes the best seasonal ingredients the focus of his set menus: grilled green asparagus, roast fillet of duckling, bluefin tuna from Saint-Jean-de-Luz etc. Attentive service.

Name: Martin - Domaine de Primard
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The bistro of this superb hotel, a subtle blend of country chic, is the lair of a new chef, Géraud Dupuis (formerly of the Domaine de Fontenille at Lauris). He crafts a traditional score in the zeitgeist, sourcing most of his vegetables from the estate's kitchen garden. Examples include green asparagus and a sage-flavoured sabayon; catch of the day, broccoli and a vin jaune-flavoured beurre blanc. Peaceful al fresco dining in the castle orchard in fine weather.

Name: Le Patte Noire
Description: Everyone is welcome in this warm, colourful establishment, located in a magnificent country home set in extensive grounds. Classical French cuisine has no secrets for chef Adrien Roux, who rustles up enticing dishes in tune with the times, such as brill, Colonnata bacon and mushrooms.

Name: La Diligence
Address: 13 rue du Bourg, La Ferté-Saint-Cyr, 41220, France
Description: This nicely restored former coaching inn offers tasty dishes showcasing produce of the local terroir; it also has comfortable guestrooms and a popular summer swimming pool. The welcome is particularly charming. A restaurant that is as friendly as it is stylish.

Name: Mets Mots
Description: What is this restaurant's recipe for success? A venue steeped in history (a former printworks), a trio of chefs who worked for Pierre Gagnaire and elegantly crafted market cuisine. Day after day, the regulars flock here, which is always a good sign. Full-bodied flavours and a friendly vibe set the scene at lunchtime for a slap-up meal; in the evening, wine bar and a range of dishes to share.

Name: Aux Crieurs de Vin
Description: The decor is trendy with bare bricks, polished concrete floors and bistro furniture, as is the concept... Choose a bottle of wine from the cellar, before pairing it with a good, simple dish with a focus on ingredients (artisan produced charcuterie, free - range meat, cheeses from Bordier etc). A tasty and friendly place.

Name: Le Réverbère
Description: Come and bask in the light of the very pleasant Réverbère, whose entirely redesigned interior is modern and light. Enjoy the chef’s creations, which rely heavily on local produce. He works with several local farmers to serve up generous and tasty dishes that are full of flavour.

Name: La Mercerie
Description: An avalanche of quality local ingredients, undeniable know-how and gourmet delicacies... You can count on the young team to take care of your appetite in the best possible way. As for wine, the menu is lovingly put together with an emphasis on natural wines, with a promising turnover: all the ingredients are in place for you to have a great time.

Name: Hortùs
Description: Hortus is Latin for "garden" and indeed plants are at the heart of the cuisine of chef Clément Lessoud (former second-in-command to Ludovic Turac at the restaurant Une Table au Sud in Marseille). This creative, healthy and eco-minded cooking (ie made using organic produce and limited meat) is an ode to the South of France, from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic. His signature style is a predilection for herbaceous notes and bitterness, as found in green asparagus, bottarga, tangy pickled red onions, creamy carrot purée with bitter orange and bergamot cream, or roast turbot with artichoke.

Name: Bistro S
Description: S like secret, savoury, sapid or Spinoza, not the philosopher but the owner who lovingly watches over this discreet Parisian establishment, and who is also a numismatist specialising in antique Greek coins and a genuine wine connoisseur. The talented Japanese chef Shimpei Oié crafts a fresh, healthy, balanced set menu backed up by his flawless culinary technique. Don’t miss the gilthead seabream: expertly fire-roasted and accompanied by white grapes and a kiwi juice. S like Super!

Name: L'Ouvrière
Description: L'Ouvrière was conceived as a community based on a beehive model. Ludovic and Kelly Dumont hope to create osmosis between customers, vegetable and meat producers and artisans. And they pull it off, with unpretentious, well-executed cooking (e.g. poultry with tarragon or raspberry pie) made from great ingredients. Located on the small village square, this intimate restaurant is good news for the town. Short menu of dishes at fair prices.

Name: Caffé César L'initial
Description: A large patio and a spacious, modern interior with an open-plan kitchen set the scene for spot-on, bistronomic cuisine, steeped in the aromas and flavours of Provence and the Mediterranean. Delicious chard-flavoured gnocchi (“Merda de Can” - a delicacy of Nice), caponata-style fillet of dentex in red wine and rose-scented rum baba… A cheerful, friendly vibe with wines by the glass from a magnum bottle…

Name: Le Braque
Address: 45 rue de la Monnaie, Lille, 59000, France
Description: Sous-chef to Florent Ladeyn and a TV cooking show contestant, Damien Laforce and dog, Marcel (a pointer or ‘braque’), have opened this eatery, depicted by brick and light wood. He crafts tasty regional fare, scattered with bold touches. Concise organic wine list, smiling service and 20 or so wall counter seats for customers without a booking.

Name: Omnivore
Description: Two minutes from Pau Château, on the picturesque Place Gramont, imagine a nostalgic bistro with a zinc-topped counter, wood panelling and upholstered seating. Pau's foodies flock here, sharing good vibes as they tuck into fish fresh from the fish auction or 24hr shoulder of pork. The slate menu features traditional nosh served generously and sometimes enhanced by touches of citrus fruit or well-balanced smoky notes. The jovial front-of-house staff are an added bonus.

Name: Là DN
Description: Don't be put off by this restaurant's location in a commercial zone. Go ahead and book your table in the company of this couple who are professionals through and through! Deftly crafted, gourmet recipes inspired by the market (including yummy home-made sourdough bread). The menu, which revolves around seasonal, local produce, changes every week.

Name: Et Toque !
Description: In the heart of Suresnes, chef Maxime Salvi creates modern, well-crafted, bistronomic fare (gloriously reasonably priced lunchtime menu). The flawless dishes highlight seasonal and top-drawer produce – tarragon and pistachio pork and poultry pâté en croûte with pickles; Bourbonnais pork belly, Jerusalem artichokes, carrots and red wine jus. In the evening, a more ambitious culinary score and a carte blanche menu that depends entirely on the chef’s mood await the diner.

Name: Le Clos d'Émile
Description: This farmhouse is home to a charming restaurant, where Madame takes care of the cooking and Monsieur provides attentive and high-quality service. They propose straightforward and healthy cuisine, with a strong emphasis on produce from farms located within a 30km radius – as well as their own beef and pork. A welcoming place.

Name: La Cuisine de la Fontaignotte
Address: 4 rue de la Fontaignotte, Semur-en-Auxois, 21140, France
Description: This exquisite 17C mansion, whose conservatory and large terrace command a matchless view over the town’s ramparts and the River Armançon, enjoys a premium location in this picture postcard medieval town. The town and its walls may be rich in heritage, but the incisive, fresh cuisine of chef Martin is light years from old school, as the brook trout smoked over vine shoots and beetroot in a salt crust demonstrates. The chef faithfully keeps pace with the seasons, working with farmers from Auxois and Burgundy.

Name: Ferme de la Besse
Description: The poultry, calves and ewes that are reared on the family farm are the starting point for this pleasant, hard-working young chef, who has energy to spare. Fresh and appetising dishes served in an informal and friendly ambience. Quite delightful!

Name: L'Informel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The gourmet annexe of the Michelin - starred restaurant Les Trois Soleils de Montal. The chef proposes generous and tasty traditional cuisine, made with fresh seasonal ingredients, such as the top - notch leg of lamb roasted with thyme. Friendly and informal.

Name: La Table d'Élise
Description: This swish, fashionable brasserie, located a stone's throw from Monaco’s Japanese Garden and the Grimaldi Forum, welcomes diners in a modern, spacious interior with pop music playing in the background. The Provençal cuisine, prepared with fine seasonal ingredients, is spot on, unfussy, generous and tasty. It is always a pleasure to watch the action in the open-plan kitchen. Excellent lunch deal.

Name: Les Caudalies
Description: Les Caudalies in Vichy has it all: a stylishly elegant dining room strewn with contemporary details, an appealing wine list with over 900 labels selected by Lucie, chef Emmanuel Basset’s wife, and a culinary line-up of tasty and generous dishes that tread a fine line between tradition and modernity. NB: check out the “cadole” dining area, between the wine cellar and the kitchen, which sports a vintner's lodge vibe.

Name: Hôtel des Deux Rocs
Description: This beautiful 12C bastide overlooks a charming medieval village… Here, Julien Beaudoire, a chef with a fine CV, works side by side with his brother – a pastry chef. He serves up Provençal cuisine that navigates between classic dishes, such as snails, and more contemporary preparations, eg octopus with tandoori curry. The food coupled with the authentic, rural setting make for an enjoyable interlude, which can be extended by booking one of the guestrooms.

Name: Auberge de Sainte-Maure
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The young owner, Victor Martin, and his chef Julien Drapier are now a well-established duo. The dishes tend towards an undeniable finesse, such as the roasted langoustine, fennel confit and shell jus. Add to that smiling service, good value for money, and a pleasant terrace by the water.

Name: L'Alchimiste
Description: Despite the name you won’t find any molecular cuisine here. Instead, enjoy good, no - nonsense dishes such as courgette and goat’s cheese flan, and poached pears. It is often full so it is best to book.

Name: Le Cèdre
Description: The food shows off the undeniable richness of the Catalan terroir, and varies freely with the passing seasons, so it is impossible to tire of it! As for the setting, it is an invitation to daydream. The picture window gives onto the fine terrace and, beyond, the port and the sea. Le Cèdre has it all.

Name: La Badiane
Description: Just a stone's throw from the covered market, this space with a pared-back decor has charm to spare, with wood and stone in perfect harmony above the nicely dressed untreated wood tables. Chef Geoffrey Poësson (trained under Roger Vergé at Le Moulin de Mougins) is quietly coming into his own, as he creates a fine modern cuisine in which vegetables and fish predominate (even if pigeon is his signature dish and lamb and beef are also served): fresh tomatoes with anchovies, marjoram velouté; roast sea bream loin, saffron-steamed belly, a bouillabaisse-style stock with the fish head and seasonal vegetables. A simpler set lunchtime menu, except in summer.

Name: La Petite Plage
Description: In this restaurant in the village port, Eric Frechon devises the menu, and the sea does the rest. Enjoy a new take on flavoursome Mediterranean cuisine, as you bury your feet in the sand overlooking the yachts, ever a subject of conversation. On summer evenings, a DJ provides the soundtrack, as is the norm in Saint-Tropez! Attentive service despite the bustle.

Name: Nobuki
Description: A zen and minimalist interior all done out in pale wood sets the scene for traditional, seasonal Japanese cuisine that stands out for its fresh, unusual flavours: assortment of cold starters and tempura of the day, chirashi (traditional dish of raw fish), a hot dish of the day and miso soup. Booking essential.

Name: Bistrot des Hauts de Loire
Description: In the outbuildings of the estate, a picturesque Sologne building with exposed timber beams and oak floorboards sets the scene. On the terrace, facing the kitchen garden, you can tuck into simple bistro dishes (matured meat, spit-roasts) or the chef’s more imaginative creations. Scrumptious!

Name: Mamma - Les Roches Brunes
Description: Clinging to a rocky outcrop, Les Roches Brunes is a feast for the eyes: the hotel overlooks the sea and offers a breathtaking view of the Château royal de Collioure opposite. In the restaurant, chef Antoine Cormoretto rustles up a mouth-watering menu that brilliantly combines Italian and local produce. A bohemian-chic atmosphere set to jazzy music. A truly relaxing interlude!

Name: Instincts
Description: "This newly established place is run by a dynamic couple who are setting about putting a spin on good bistro cuisine, all in a contemporary setting – exposed brickwork, wood, and open kitchen. Tuna tartar, gooseberries, fennel; mature beef, courgette, black olive: a treat! Already a favourite. "

Name: Domaine de Baulieu
Description: In an elegant and modern interior with large bay windows overlooking the terrace and the surrounding nature, you can enjoy food cooked up by Maxime Deschamps. Their dishes are well crafted and make the most of local produce. A super dining experience.

Name: Hostellerie Saint-Clément
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This small family-run restaurant is the epitome of friendly and the father and son team crafts a traditional, gourmet score, underscored by beautiful plating: breast of free-range guinea fowl and morel mushroom sauce; cassolette of Brittany monkfish… We recommend the homemade quail terrine.

Name: Polypode
Description: At chef Quentin Burnet's restaurant, the creativity starts right off the bat, with amuse-bouches such as a tartlet with Comté cream, wasabi and Amarena cherry. This modern cuisine, in which plants play a prominent role, demonstrates his ability to use (a limited number of) ingredients, condiments, plants and aromatic herbs (including polypodium, an edible fern!) in just the right proportions, and serve them with beautifully contrasting sauces. The pollack with peas, asparagus and grapefruit, and the guinea fowl with gnocchi and mushrooms are shining examples of his eye for freshness and precision when it comes to harmonising flavours.

Name: Le Temps de Vivre
Description: This stone-built house, dating back to the 18C but with a contemporary decor, invites you to slow down and enjoy life, especially on its shaded terrace. The chef and his wife have the laws of hospitality down to a T. On the menu: the generosity of Provence, with vegetables grown by the father-in-law, in season; aioli on Friday lunchtime in summer, and a set menu dedicated to truffles in winter.

Name: La Cassolette
Description: In the heart of the exquisite historic town, facing the town hall, this institution continues to remain a landmark of Vence’s culinary scene. It is a pleasure to take a seat indoors or on the terrace to tuck into flavoursome, market fresh dishes of Mediterranean inspiration.

Name: Le Diamant Noir
Description: At this chic restaurant perched at the top of the resort (altitude 2 400m), chef Eric Samson pays tribute to the food of his three favourite regions: his native Brittany, his adopted Savoie and his beloved Périgord. As well as spotlighting truffles – the "black diamond" after which this place is named, Samson's cleverly devised menu-carte draws on all three terroirs with finesse: scrambled organic egg with black truffle; matured abalone and ribot milk emulsion; Roscoff onion cooked in hay, summer Beaufort cheese royale.

Name: La Tour
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Nestling at the foot of a 14C tower in the heart of the famous wine-growing village, this traditional townhouse boasts an elegant, contemporary-style dining room that has retained a handful of period touches (beams, ceiling and mouldings). Simplicity, authenticity and bags of character are the hallmarks of dishes elevated by high-quality ingredients, such as cep and onion ravioli served with kale, or chuck of veal with cauliflower. Delicious, well-balanced flavours and judicious use of condiments: pared-back cuisine that makes for a delicious culinary interlude.

Name: La Table de Catusseau
Description: Kendji Wongsodikromo, owner - chef of New Caledonian extraction, fell in love with southwest France and his wife, Nadège, whom you will meet in the dining room. The enthusiastic, young couple does not lack experience as the first taste of their market - fresh, carefully crafted dishes made with tasty, regional ingredients will confirm.

Name: La Dune du Château de Sable
Description: In his open kitchen, chef Philippe Brun creates set menus inspired by the best of Brittany's terroir and what grows in the kitchen garden: purple artichokes barigoule, artisanal bottarga; John Dory from small boat fishing roasted in hazelnut butter and served with razor clams in parsley sauce, and Roscoff onions cooked on the barbecue. These fine ingredients are prepared in line with the establishment's eco-responsible ethos. Enjoy your meal in the light-filled dining area laid out beneath exposed wooden rafters, with a view of the coast. Bistronomy fare at Le Rivage, under the same roof.

Name: Le Sens Unique
Description: This friendly bistronomy restaurant is part of a small hotel in the upper reaches of the town centre. Behind a façade still reminiscent of Aix-les-Bains's heyday as a spa resort, this stylish eatery, complete with a wine bar, has lost none of its period cachet. It is run by a vital chef who often puts in an appearance on the restaurant floor. His down-to-earth bistro-style cuisine with a twist uses seasonal and sometimes premium produce (Angus beef, Corsican meagre etc). Attentive service. The enclosed tree-lined terrace to the rear is charming.

Name: Haut-Linage
Description: Not far from Eckmühl Lighthouse, this restaurant boasts a contemporary interior in shades of white, grey and gold. It is a charming place run by a couple of Breton locals: chef Corentin Ogor and the ebullient Klervi Tanniou, who manages the restaurant floor, armed with a broad smile. When it comes to the modern cuisine, each dish focuses on a fresh ingredient, cooked to perfection and served with a tip-top sauce or jus, eg mackerel confit, carrot, snow peas; haddock, einkorn, coconut milk sauce and red curry; pork filet mignon, pink onions, full-bodied gravy. The lunch deal is a steal.

Name: L'Arborescence
Description: Somewhere in the countryside north of Annecy, this restaurant boasts a view of the Jura mountains in the distance. Trained by great chefs (including Lionel Giraud, Christian Constant and Laurent Petit), this couple prepares fresh and often local ingredients to form a short menu: slow-cooked fario trout, green leek and walnuts; roast veal filet mignon, straw potatoes and condiments; soft and moist lemon cake made with rosemary from the garden, whipped cream and candied zest. Contemporary dining space, lounge area at the entrance with a library of cookery books and photos of mentor chefs. Charming service courtesy of the lady of the house.

Name: Leptine
Description: The sound system is an integral part of this place with its long corridor bathed in red light, its open kitchen behind a counter and its tables lining the wall. The name ("leptin" in English) refers to the hormone that signals to your brain when you are satiated – no question of leaving here on an empty stomach! The chef deftly draws on the culinary traditions of France, Asia and beyond, treating diners to siu mai, an array of fermented foods and Japanese seasonings. It's brilliantly done, and the seasoned team is more than happy to tell you how. Two to three savoury dishes plus one sweet should do the trick. Natural wine list, an interesting selection of wines by the glass and savvy recommendations.

Name: Odorico
Description: Isidore Odorico is the name of the Italian mosaic artist who decorated the dining room of this restaurant in 1928. The blue and gold tiles of his Art Deco fresco unfurl majestically over the walls, arches and columns. In this setting, chef Kevin Bougard, who has built up an impressive international CV, serves modern cuisine imbued with Italian influences – his way of paying tribute to the Italian artist. He does so by using the finest local ingredients (free-range beef and butter, asparagus from Maine-et-Loire etc) in creations such as tasty house-made pappardelle with lamb ragout and langoustine crudo with fruity vermouth flavours.

Name: Charbonnel
Description: This emblematic inn stands in the heart of the picturesque village of Brantôme. Inventive seasonal cuisine served in a contemporary dining room, which leads onto an enchanting terrace overlooking the River Dronne.

Name: L'Aube
Description: A new dawn for chef Thibault Nizard and his solo career (after stints at Drouant, as well as Chiberta, Taillevent and Guy Savoy). He has set up shop here, between the Louvre and Palais Royal, in a lavish space, where the service team don the full regalia. This technically proficient chef's classic cuisine is underpinned by top-quality produce, which he presents with his own twist. Arriving at your table, the dishes exude influences ranging from Brittany to the Mediterranean – for example, Breton poivrade artichokes glazed in a delicious reduction with Cévennes onion. Three set menus, each with several courses.

Name: Les Belles Canailles
Address: Les Roches Blanches, 9 avenue des Calanques, Cassis, 13260, France
Description: The view from the terrace of this luxury hotel restaurant (popular with celebrities), which looks out over Cap Canaille, is quite simply sublime. Chef Nicolas Sintes, who grew up in Cannes, serves his guests Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that has a focus on fish, but also features, for example, local lamb and seasonal vegetables. However, you may prefer to opt for the chef's down-to-earth speciality of bouillabaisse borgne, followed by a wild bass and its broth of pistou soup… All accompanied by a Cassis or Bandol wine, as you would expect. Open seven days a week for lunch and dinner.

Name: Taggat
Description: In this contemporary-style bistro with an industrial vibe, the chef showcases his culinary skills. These tend towards the creative, and he is not afraid to lace his dishes with bold flavours: burrata and cucumber, mojo verde, bread crisps, garlic confit and black olive powder… or John Dory, caponata, olive oil puff pastry and a red pepper jus. Set menu at lunchtime and à la carte in the evening in a similar vein, but with more upmarket ingredients.

Name: Restaurant Côté Marais
Description: A starter of ceviche of white mullet (a fish rarely found on restaurant menus) with rhubarb for a hint of tartness, followed by a savoury/sweet main course of pollack fished by small boats, French peas al dente and a smattering of sweet cherry condiment. The young chef applies his own personal culinary style to local ingredients, while his partner works the restaurant floor in this outlying establishment surrounded by marshland (and with a lovely terrace).

Name: Origine
Description: At this beautifully renovated farmhouse (formerly the village café), built with red bricks from the Artois region, the ingredients are of certified origin, and chef Maëllie Poynard has plenty of original ideas about how to use them! Judge for yourself: chocolate sauce on the beef accompanied by peach and chard; gherkin on the rhubarb dessert, carrot on the pavlova... Her pairings – sometimes daring – are pitch perfect. As for the decor, it is 100% contemporary. The traditional brasserie, on the same premises, is run by the chef's partner (who works front of house).

Name: Le Serghi
Description: On the old port, this restaurant (with its pleasant terrace at the front) belongs to the island's select club of restaurants that are open all year round. In the kitchen, a great chef, Philippe Tredgeu (previously at Entredgeu and Les Cocottes in Paris), crafts cuisine that calls to mind Parisian bistronomy. Fine ingredients, seasonal produce and indulgent dishes are the order of the day: green asparagus, egg mimosa, sauce parisienne or grilled and glazed confit pork belly with market-fresh vegetables. A joy from start to finish.

Name: Le Mezquité
Address: 70 rue de Paris, Le Touquet-Paris-Plage, 62520, France
Description: Courgettes, samphire and salsa macha; avocado and chocolate parfait – this restaurant in Le Touquet successfully showcases its take on fusion cuisine, with a penchant for smoking certain food items. Chef Julien Szyndler prepares regional ingredients using Mexican methods, sauces and spices, for instance cochinita pibil (with pork marinated and cooked over mezquita wood) or mole poblano with duck. The food mirrors the couple's roots: he hails from nearby Valenciennes, while Laura Flores, his wife, is from Mexico: Puebla, to be precise (southeast of Mexico City).

Name: Acacia
Address: 230 boulevard de la Plage, Arcachon, 33120, France
Description: Make a beeline for this little place in the heart of Arcachon, just a stone's throw from the beach. Behind the black and white storefront, there is a restaurant with a modern decor and a retro touch. The chef knows his stuff, astutely revising bistronomy and traditional dishes: eg a wonderful terrine of black Bigorre pork/poultry, updated with a red onion and pear compote; veal in a herb crust, sweet potato gnocchi.

Name: La Taula
Description: At La Taula (which means "table" in Occitan), Christine Maurence concocts no-nonsense family-style cuisine. Among her specialities, the veal kidney cooked whole with mustard seeds, the home-made stuffed duck's neck, and the semi-cooked foie gras are the signature dishes. An authentic restaurant just next to the cathedral, where traditions are not something to be trifled with!

Name: La Maison des Toqués
Address: 26 rue de la Prée-aux-Ducs, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île, 85330, France
Description: Aurore and Sébastien Duchenne left their small restaurant in Herbaudière to settle in Noirmoutier-en-l'Île. A new challenge, a new cosy decor, but still the same passion for quality regional ingredients, enhanced by lovely recipes that capture the zeitgeist and use market-fresh ingredients. It is always wise to book to secure a table.

Name: Le Comptoir Boutary
Description: The third restaurant of the famous caviar-producing family is all about simplicity and conviviality, with its chic bistro atmosphere and open kitchen. Chef Nicolas Arnould makes a convincing case with his contemporary cuisine and, as you would expect, the house's flagship ingredient features in some of his well-crafted dishes: smoked potato with bergamot, Bordier seaweed butter, Isigny PDO crème fraîche and caviar; caviar and cocoa tart – the scoop of sturgeon roe lends a pleasant salty note to the chocolate flavours. The set lunch menu is a real bargain.

Name: Armada
Description: A sure-fire hit! Two intrepid friends who earned their spurs working for Christian Têtedoie have opened a restaurant that ticks all the boxes: trendy and inviting bistro decor with exposed beams and stonework, Japanese-style burnt wood tables, some at bar height. As for the food, our two chefs cook up clever, creative cuisine, with dishes such as a starter combining potatoes, mushrooms and eel with a kimchi powder twist, a marriage of roast duck and beetroot with a Scandinavian-style fermented jus, or an indulgent trio of flavours in the apple/bread/yeast dessert.

Name: Céna
Description: Chef Clément Briand-Seurat has left the Pic Saint-Loup restaurant to open his own establishment (Cena means supper or dinner in Latin) beneath the ribbed vaults of a medieval edifice in the heart of historic Montpellier. A snug, romantic vibe, enhanced by centuries-old stonework and candle-lit rough oak tables, sets the scene. The chef signs a creative single set menu in which he endeavours to enhance the produce of local growers and breeders thanks to flawless craftsmanship (chutneys, oils, crumbles, crackers and whipped siphon concoctions). His knockout mushroom consommé and ‘stroll in the woods’ embodies this ethos.

Name: Tempo
Address: 5 place de la République, Rouen, 76000, France
Description: Between the River Seine and the cathedral, this restaurant has a black and red interior with a geometrical design. The son of a market gardener with a passion for vegetables, the chef infuses his cuisine with contemporary flavours and aromas. He gives free rein to his imagination and creativity in his carte blanche menu: scallops, fennel and blackcurrants; Black Angus beef, mushrooms, celery and vin jaune.

Name: Alquimia
Address: 6 rue de la Table-Ronde, Vienne, 38200, France
Description: Not far from the banks of the Rhône, this old building (parts of which date back to the 18C) has everything going for it: high ceilings, exposed stone and brick walls and, at the helm, a young French-Paraguayan couple with bags of personality. Chef Horacio Zàrate Franco composes creative cuisine with South American influences and a real feel for presentation: medley of egg, Jerusalem artichokes and truffles; scallops, coconut cream, cardoons and squid fricassee with tomato. A lively atmosphere reigns, thanks to the people skills of the hostess.

Name: Mano
Description: A quiet street in a residential area, the discreet façade of a contemporary bistro, and a compact, convivial space with tables arranged close together: this is the restaurant of former Plantxa chef, Maximilien Kuzniar. The menu features simple and tasty seasonal dishes, such as carrots with cumin and citrus fruit; fish, quinoa and curry sauce; roast apple and mint espuma. The lunch set menus are excellent value for money, while the evening dining options are more ambitious.

Name: La Cantine Urbaine - Artchives
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Previously an annexe of the local archives, this completely renovated space now houses a venue dedicated to art – and food. On the top floor, bathed in natural light courtesy of an atrium, this designer setting is home to a highly recommended restaurant. Fine ingredients, spot-on cooking and interplays of flavours are on the agenda, in dishes such as octopus with green asparagus and spiced honey, or fillet of beef with peas, a full-bodied gravy and vin jaune sauce. "Basic" set menu at lunchtime; more ambitious tasting menus in the evening.

Name: Pérégrinations
Description: At an age where some might be hanging up their apron, chef Franck Gatefin is as enthusiastic as ever in his establishment a few kilometres outside Châteauroux. Extremely particular about the source of his ingredients, he prepares the freshwater fish himself in line with the ikejime method, the organic veg comes from his ‘official’ gardener and, a keen botanist too, he grows over 150 aromatic herbs in his courtyard-terrace. Fish and veggies obviously take the limelight in the exquisitely presented dishes in line with this ethos: egg soufflé with parsley pesto; poultry with orange-flavoured caramelised endive. Charming, attentive welcome and service in a contemporary interior.

Name: La R'mize
Address: 160 rue du Vieux-Village, Les Gets, 74260, France
Description: Located in the historic village, near the church, this eatery serves traditional toothsome nosh. A veteran chef regales diners with well-crafted dishes like cream of pumpkin soup served with shavings of Abondance cheese and whipped cream lightly flavoured with passion fruit or a carpaccio of scallops with a jus of lobster shells. His gourmet repertoire also includes timeless Savoyard specialities ranging from gratinée gourmande to fondue Savoyard made with champagne!

Name: Le Jas
Address: 10 bis rue de l'Église, La Roque-d'Anthéron, 13640, France
Description: La Roque-d'Anthéron's church is home to one of the world's best-known piano festivals. Hailing from the village, chef Émeric Corbon, who worked for Michel Kayser and Édouard Loubet, came up with the idea of opening this restaurant just a few metres from the church, in a converted dry-stone sheepfold (a jas in the Provençal dialect). Beneath the centuries-old vaulted ceilings or on the terrace, you can enjoy carefully prepared dishes with a clear Provençal influence: delicious aubergine papeton and tomato concassé with fresh herbs, basil coulis; tasty squab roasted whole, with the legs, gizzards and heart in a samosa, and a creamy pea sauce.

Name: Chez Mosse
Description: The boss here is Mattéo Mosse, a youthful chef from Haute Savoie who decided to settle in this village to be as close as possible to the countryside and to small local producers. Fish and meat from sustainable breeders, as local as possible and a vegetarian score depict the ethos of this eco-responsible eatery. The chef’s modern repertory unsurprisingly revolves around seasonal produce, with a distinct weakness for organic veggies. A simple, no-fuss bistro interior in a colourful village house that is flanked by a refreshingly shady terrace.

Name: Léonor
Address: 11 rue de la Nuée-Bleue, Strasbourg, 67000, France
Description: Behind a 19C façade and within 18C walls, this contemporary hotel designed by Jean-Philippe Nuel has its own lounge-style restaurant adjoining the bar. The menu is in keeping with the culinary zeitgeist: for example, tuna sashimi, mango, avocado, with soy and sesame sauce, or saddle of lamb with herbs, crispy potatoes and courgette coulis. For tables of friends, there are large dishes designed to share (whole fish, rib steak etc). For those with a sweet tooth, cast an eye over the display cabinet, where some desserts are plated up and there are pretty pastries to choose from.

Name: Peixes Bonaparte
Description: Between Place Garibaldi and the Old Town of Nice, this restaurant is run by the team behind Peixes Opéra. Here, too, they deploy their winning formula, starting with a large terrace that is a very popular spot on sunny days, followed by a range of seafood dishes (fish, tataki, sashimi, accras, oysters) and ceviche specialities. The contemporary blue and white "marine bistro" setting calls to mind Portugal or Greece. Behind the bar, a mixologist creates your cocktails. The lunch menu is really good value. This place is open all day, with a reduced menu until 7pm.

Name: Le Bistrot de Madeleine
Description: This village inn is a real boon for lovers of the finer (and healthier) things in life. It would not be out of place to talk about programmatic cuisine in this bistro with a slightly rustic feel: whole carcass approach, local market gardening, fish sourced directly from the fish markets, a menu that changes every week… The end result? Tasty, generous and delicious cuisine.

Name: Origines Restaurant
Description: In this contemporary restaurant, Aveyron-born chef Julien Boscus serves up tasty, masterfully prepared dishes using the finest seasonal ingredients. Two shining examples are the delicious crispy tartlet filled with morel mushrooms creamed with sous-voile wine, or the sautéed sweetbreads with green asparagus from Provence (Vaucluse) steamed in citron. The wine list features an impressive selection from a vast array of France's vineyards, and the wine service, provided by the sommelier team, is second to none! A friendly and engaging place.

Name: La Table Cachée par Michel Roth
Address: BHV, 33 rue de la Verrerie, Paris, 75004, France
Description: On the 5th floor of the BHV department store, this “hidden table” lies behind a mysterious green curtain - at the rear of the lingerie department! The cosy setting (all the “props” are sold in the store) is the lair of Michel Roth who crafts an enticing seasonal score (tartlet of haddock, magret of Gers duck with bigarade sauce, millefeuille pastry with Corsican clementines) and a reasonably priced first-class market-fresh menu at lunchtime. The panoramic terrace commands a fantastic view of the townhall of Paris.

Name: Le Cœur
Description: Part of the Cœur de Megève hotel, this restaurant is synonymous with Alpine elegance, enhanced by means of a contemporary twist. The chef creates modern cuisine using terrific, carefully selected seasonal ingredients. The combinations of local produce, either with citrus fruits (Magland snails, grapefruit, sesame), premium ingredients (parmentier broth and black truffle) or Asian touches work perfectly. The chef is also very much at ease when cooking more traditional dishes, such as saddle of roe deer with pumpkin and redcurrants.

Name: CoDa
Address: 15 rue de la Tour-des-Dames, Paris, 75009, France
Description: Set back from the boisterous Rue Blanche, this pocket-handkerchief bolthole is the epitome of an authentic Parisian café. The tables are so tightly packed, it may feel like you are dining with rather than next to your neighbours. Irrepressibly cheerful, Pauline and Vincent Da Costa (former second chef of Bruno Doucet’s Régalade) pamper their guests with nosh that hits the spot every time: field to fork market-fresh seasonal ingredients. Fine food without the fuss. The lunchtime menu is a steal.

Name: Ambos
Description: Overlooking the grandiose Sénat (upper house of the French parliament) and the Luxembourg gardens, this friendly contemporary bistro sports untreated materials (exposed stone, brickwork and timberwork), an open kitchen and a small counter. ‘Ambos’ (‘both’ in Spanish) refers to Pierre Chomet and his Venezuelan wife, Cristina. Their culinary adventures have taken them from Bangkok to London and Paris, and a Top Chef TV season for Pierre. Together they concoct a light-hearted, personal, vibrant tapestry of flavours which aims to please as it draws on a variety of influences – European and Thai (pad thai-style langoustine tartar,) as well as South American (farm-reared suckling lamb and iodized chimichurri; stuffed arepa cornbread).

Name: Baud
Description: Chef Michel Verdu loves herbs (which he often collects himself), plants and vegetables (some of which he picks from the establishment's kitchen garden) – and his natural and creative cuisine, which is predominantly plant-based, makes no bones about this, with starters such as gazpacho with cucumber, tomato and mozzarella (made with raw Savoie milk), or indeed his mayonnaise flavoured with wild herbs, which goes down a treat with arctic char. The interior design is contemporary, with black and white striped carpet and crimson walls and ceiling, and the terrace nestles beneath a pergola by the river. Multi-course mystery set menu. Pleasant contemporary guestrooms.

Name: La Cour des Sens
Description: This restaurant installed in an old farmhouse boasts an intimate atmosphere and a decor in which wooden floors meet exposed stonework. Head chef Benjamin Royer creates dishes that show off an undeniable savoir-faire: scallops cooked on stones, flambéed with saffron gin, smoked aubergine caviar and beurre blanc, and pan-roasted turbot, poached heirloom turnip with parmesan and a truffle sauce.

Name: Le Sauvage
Description: At the foot of the Vauban Citadel, this smart hotel occupies the former convent of the Poor Clares. The restaurant provides a cosy setting, with old parquet floors and tablecloths, and – a major asset – its terrace overlooking the park! Chef Hugo Mathieu (trained in Lyon's top restaurants) is no novice, judging by his polished dishes: glazed pea velouté, cod loin fillet cooked at 50C, crispy pistachio tartlet.

Name: Cave et Cuisine
Description: A town house with blue shutters next to the church, a wine cellar with over 1 000 labels, a chef who is following in her parents' footsteps. An undeniable talent in the kitchen, she combines classics (eggs in a red wine sauce, ham terrine with parsley etc), contemporary dishes (salmon gravlax) and specialities such as roast pigeon and sweetbreads. To be savoured in a refined bistro decor, where smiling service is the order of the day and the wine recommendations are on point.

Name: Ombelle
Description: Having worked for a number of top establishments, chef Alexandre Frin and his partner Ludivine La Rosa, who manages the restaurant floor, have set up shop in this attractive early-20C building, with red brick walls and picture windows with small panes and white frames. The chef composes a modern, open-minded and 100% seasonal menu that keeps things simple: just good ingredients (preferably with short supply chains) and herbs and aromatic flowers from their grandfather's vegetable garden. Seared melt-in-the-mouth hake; the subtle perfume of sage and pineapple in the panna cotta: a delicious interlude.

Name: Passionné
Description: Set back from Grands Boulevards, this restaurant plays the minimalist card: a bar with midnight blue mosaics, dark walls and floor and refined lighting. A very Japanese brand of elegance, designed for this location officiated by chef Satoshi Horiuchi, originally from Hokkaido island, a few kilometres from Sapporo, a prefecture with a high concentration of small-scale producers, especially market gardeners. Horiuchi is as passionate as ever about creating a modern French cuisine characterised by his quest to find quality ingredients and cook them perfectly.

Name: Le Grand Café
Description: In the shade of the century-old plane trees on the terrace, or beneath the high exposed timber ceiling of this stunning 18C manor house, chef Mathias Dandine serves cuisine that is both traditional and generous, in keeping with the bistro decor. The short, appetising menu features dishes beautifully made with fresh produce, leaving diners with some difficult decisions! Pâté en croûte with shallot condiment; Iberian loin of pork with fregola sarda risotto; apple tarte fine with vanilla ice cream. A flawless and truly delicious culinary offering and relaxed but professional service.

Name: Lafayette
Description: Abutting his first restaurant, chef Xavier Pincemin has opened this trendy bistro that sports a series of adjoining Art deco rooms. He is enjoying himself and, in the process, delights us with a menu of varied influences (tacos, ceviche, tiger beef) and a selection of outstanding matured beef displayed in an ageing cabinet, such as the knockout black Baltic rib steak. Casual vibe.

Name: Les Quatre Saisons
Address: 3 route du Frenz, Le Frenz, 68820, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This cosy chalet is set in a landscape of forests and mountains. Christelle proposes her own personal brand of cuisine (savoury éclair filled with porcini mousse, chanterelles in vinegar and cured ham, duck pot au feu with autumn vegetables cooked in broth), while Frédéric carefully selects the wines.

Name: Frenchie Pigalle
Description: Grégory Marchand has brought a tongue-in-cheek vibe to the ground-floor restaurant of this hotel in Paris’ sleazy yet romantic Pigalle. Dishes to share in a joyful canteen ambience that err between regional comfort food, bang-on Gallic classics and world food, including a splendid cheeseboard and a wine list with natural inclinations…

Name: Sens
Description: Off the bustling tourist track of Bordeaux, this cosy, modern bistro is run by Alexandre Bru, the chef, and his wife, Loren, pastry chef. Their bistronomic cuisine is precise and deftly crafted, and particularly eater-friendly priced at lunchtime. In the evenings, the single set menu is more ambitious and changes monthly.

Name: Félicie
Description: In a rather industrial-style decor (waxed concrete, bricks, square tables made of frosted iron and wood), a young and dynamic team runs this address in the suburbs of Lille. The prices are simply fantastic for market-based cuisine of this quality – Félicie's is an absolute treat, make no mistake!

Name: Oiseau - Oiseau
Description: Sven Chartier (formerly of the Saturne) and his wife Marianne have built their new nest in this tiny Perche village, opposite a church several centuries old. Free from the frenetic pace of Paris, the chef is flourishing in this country chic décor, pampering diners with wholesome fare of classical inspiration: porkpie, young farm-reared chicken and fresh vegetables, crunchy squash and quince pie. Culinary precision and traditional flavours.

Name: Impressions
Description: After 18 years at Le Saison near Rennes, David Etcheverry has moved to this restaurant in the centre of La Rochelle. It is a small place with a sleek modern loft design, where they serve refined, unfailingly delicious dishes. A real treat for the taste buds.

Name: Domaine de Rymska
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set in the countryside between Beaune and Chalon-sur-Saône, this charming restaurant and hotel sits in the middle of a vast estate with lakes, a stud farm, and a farm that supplies some high-quality produce, including Charolais and Wagyu beef, eggs, poultry, fruit and vegetables. The chef's cuisine also draws on the finest ingredients, and sometimes finds inspiration further afield: sea bream ceviche with lime and coconut milk; scallops, mushroom gyoza and Noilly Prat sauce; mandarin, orange and Timut pepper. The beautiful space boasts exposed stone walls, a beamed ceiling and a fire crackling in the imposing hearth. Extraordinary wine list.

Name: O&A
Description: At this pleasant 21C bistro opposite the Halles de Tours (the city's covered market), good food and relaxation reign supreme. Foodies, take note: there's no fuss or frills, just sincere, precise and generous cuisine (with butter!) that celebrates quality ingredients and authentic flavours. Examples include foie gras ravioli, truffle broth; seared scallops, watercress cream, a delicious hazelnut butter, lemon-flavoured potatoes; warm chocolate mousse, fleur de sel cookie chips. The food reflects the personality of chef-patron Olivier Arlot, a real people person who comes to every table to serve a dish or two, spreading good humour and smiles. The extensive wine list makes for rich pickings (including Loire and Burgundy labels).

Name: Disciples
Description: Chef Jean-Pierre Vigato has lost nothing of his passion for passing on his knowledge. Indeed, in this bright, contemporary dining space that is in keeping with the chic neighbourhood, he has dubbed Romain Dubuisson his "disciple". On the agenda, a short menu of generous and tasty cuisine, specials and fine pieces of meat for sharing (e.g. veal chop, farmhouse pork loin).

Name: La P’tite Patte
Description: This bistro, an offshoot of its gastronomic sibling (La Patte Noire), is located in the same handsome edifice. Two small vintage-style dining rooms with the occasional modern touch and a peaceful terrace. The food ranges from eclectic (ceviche, carpaccio, Iberico pluma) to more mainstream (steak with béarnaise sauce, savarin dessert and chocolate pie).

Name: Chardon
Description: At Chardon, Julia Mitton, Laura Vidal and Harry Cummins, the trio behind "The Paris Pop Up" concept, host different chefs-in-residence, who temporarily take the reins in the kitchen. The one thing they all have in common: they use locally sourced ingredients. The result is fresh, delicious food served in a lovely bistro setting along with a fine selection of living wines. Spot on!

Name: Le Bateleur
Description: A stone's throw from the Roman bridge, at the foot of the medieval town, the chef cooks up market-fresh cuisine. In tune with the seasons, it is often Provençal, and occasionally peppered with Italian or Mexican influences. To be enjoyed on the terrace when the weather is mild. A lovely place to sample dishes that are rich in flavours!

Name: La Sérafine
Description: The Vietnamese-born chef produces modern and instinctive cuisine, together with a handful of traditional dishes. Elegant and refined interior, savvy wine list (the wine cellar is visible as you enter) and the conservatory extends onto a pleasant terrace.

Name: Un Petit Cabanon Bouillon
Description: In this minimalist neo-bistro just a stone's throw from Joliette metro station, the emphasis is on local produce, with a touch of creativity for good measure. The menu taps into the zeitgeist and highlights what's in season: confit pork belly; pasta, squid ink, dill and sea almonds.

Name: Croque Saison
Address: sous Les Sangles, Les Fins, 25500, France
Description: "The Le Mans - born chef has created his wood and glass house from scratch. Superb view from the terrace over the Morteau valley. The beautifully presented dishes showcase excellent produce (fish in particular); professional service. An ode to the seasons! "

Name: La Canopée
Description: In this vaulted Renaissance former weapons room (5m high! ), diners sample cuisine that fetes the Cévennes and Camargue regions. It is accompanied by a nice selection of minor wines from the region.

Name: La Table des Échevins
Address: Maison Prévost, 10 rue de la Massue, Douai, 59500, France
Description: Chef Jérôme Prévost (a local man and formerly sous-chef at Le Cerisier in Laventie) has brought panache to these premises – once an antique dealers' – in the heart of Douai. The elegant vestiges of the past (marble fireplace etc) blend in seamlessly with the restaurant's modern decor (with designer features such as circular banquettes, light fittings, swivel chairs). The chef makes the most of fish from the Côte d'Opale and vegetables from local producers; in season, he dedicates a menu to lobster. Boterzing, part of the same group, serves simpler bistronomy cuisine.

Name: Sain
Description: This restaurant is a café, canteen and grocery shop all in one, combining a relaxed atmosphere with a philosophy of serving food that respects produce and the planet: a stall for organic vegetables from the family farm in Guérande, a shelf of natural wines (to take away) and laid-back service provided by Samuel Huitric. His brother Josselin cooks tasty market cuisine that is on point without too much fuss: œuf parfait, cream of courgette, mint, pistachio, ham crisps; pork polpette, tomato, cumin, puréed potato.

Name: Café Compagnon
Description: After Richer and 52 Faubourg, Charles Compagnon, restaurant owner, sommelier and coffee roaster, strikes again! This cafe offers an extensive menu ranging from nibbles to share to home-made ices. The original, deftly crafted recipes feature a modern bistro slant, depicted by market-fresh starters and succulent loin of pork. Heart-warming, authentic comfort food.

Name: Le Repère
Address: Port de la Rague, Mandelieu-La Napoule, 06210, France
Description: This well-established hideaway enjoys a knock-out location, boasting a terrace right on the beach and a panoramic view over the Bay of Cannes and the Lérins Islands. It is a delight to meet up with Nicolas Decherchi, a gifted chef who trained with the best (from Bruno Oger to Alain Ducasse), once again. He has been given carte blanche to devise a Mediterranean-focused menu with a special mention for dishes to share. Flawlessly fresh fish take front stage, although juicy cuts of meat also vie for pride of place. Open all day long, you can expect a pleasure-loving, casual vibe.

Name: Le Grill Alpin
Address: Cheval Blanc, Le Jardin Alpin, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: Under the leadership of Yannick Alléno, the chic Alpine brasserie of the upscale Cheval Blanc hotel has brilliantly reinvented high-altitude dining, serving up a contemporary and uninhibited fine dining offering. Your taste buds won't know what hit them! A sublime list of top-of-the-range wines.

Name: Imperial Treasure
Description: If you are in the market for some authentic Chinese cuisine served in a luxurious and elegant setting close to the Champs Elysées, then this is the place for you. Dishes such as imperial shrimp carabinero with sticky rice, Peking duck, and smoked eel with green tea are all prepared according to time-honoured tradition by an outstanding chef from Shanghai. Fine ingredients, subtle flavours and flawless service. Don't miss the dim sum at lunch.

Name: Tracé
Description: In his zen-feeling contemporary premises close to the Comédie Française, Clément Vergeat continues to give expression to his inspiration in a carte blanche menu, which for all its deft creative touches does not neglect flavour: mushroom and coriander tart; suckling lamb with cockles, cauliflower and black garlic; medley of rhubarb with fennel. We should also mention what he accomplishes when it comes to sauces and fermentations. The restaurant's commitment to sustainability, its organic and natural wine list, and its friendly service make for an engaging and sincere dining experience.

Name: Maison de Bacon
Description: Le Bâcon, an Antibes institution since 1948, has been transformed into the Maison de Bâcon. In the kitchens, Nicolas Davouze, formerly of Bocuse and Le Bristol, celebrates the house's signature dishes (such as rockfish soup, bouillabaisse, millefeuille), alongside a fine selection of fish grilled over a wood fire. Splendid view of the sea.

Name: Les Mérovingiens
Description: Jacky Ribault (L'Ours in Vincennes, Qui Plume la Lune in the 11th arrondissement in Paris) opened this brasserie on the ground floor of a residential building in the centre of Noisy-le-Grand. It pays homage to the history of the town, which was built on a Merovingian and Carolingian necropolis. The menu proposes good classic dishes – slightly revamped – made from impeccable produce. All the desserts are by Hugo Correia, pastry chef at L'Ours. Pleasant contemporary setting. Sunday brunch, open seven days a week, including all afternoon.

Name: Les Pieds Dans l'Eau
Address: 26 chemin de la Folle-Entreprise, Saint-Langis-lès-Mortagne, 61400, France
Description: Built at the far end of the village and surrounded by fields, this old mill is also close to a lake: it is hard to imagine a more bucolic sight! A hard-working chef serves up modern bistro cuisine comprising generous mains (eg beef confit with turnips and lentils) and mouth-watering desserts (coffee panna cotta, ladyfinger sponges and mascarpone). Soak up the warm, laid-back atmosphere as you gaze out over the meadows from the pleasant terrace.

Name: L'Escoubille
Description: The name of this contemporary restaurant with a terrace and rooftop area pays tribute to a traditional stew, a speciality of Gignac in the Hérault département, which the chef fondly remembers being made in the family home. He prepares good seasonal cuisine at prices that won't break the bank: seared red mullet, fennel, capers and olives; saddle of rabbit, garlic cream and mushroom tart; strawberry cheesecake.

Name: Len'K - La Maison Bonnet
Description: Len'K is the bistronomic wing of the Bonnet establishment. Seated on the terrace shaded by plane trees or in the contemporary dining room, diners are in for a treat as they tuck into guinea fowl and olive terrine, or stuffed red mullet paired with a velvety shellfish emulsion. Laid-back service.

Name: L'Aparté
Description: When Arthur Buisson, formerly second of the previous chef, took over the helm here, the transition was naturally smooth and seamless. While the interior remains unchanged, the culinary score is now more modern in spirit thanks to an abundant use of aromatic herbs and spices of all sorts. The chef’s globetrotting past can be tasted in the manifold flavours of his fresh, distinctive craftsmanship. Even better, he also turns out to be a dab pastry chef!

Name: ICI
Description: Chef Xavier Rambaud, a real globetrotter, travelled quite a bit before dropping anchor here. The dining area is done out in an "industrial bistro" style (parquet flooring, wooden tables, exposed stonework and cast-iron pipes). The chef concocts multi-layered creative cuisine, such as stingray wing, rice and black garlic; scallops, asparagus and rhubarb; or pork belly, carrot and apple: well-rounded dishes replete with winning flavour combinations.

Name: Racines
Description: In this cobbled street of Toulon's old town, where the terrace is smoke-free from May to October, you can tuck into delicious "cuisine de producteurs" (as the chef calls his cooking). A champion of local produce and the terroir, he concocts good seasonal dishes with a fondness for vegetables – to wash down with natural and organic tipples: ravioli, burratina and a poultry jus with chanterelles; thin slices of Aveyron pork, potato gratin with Le Beausset saffron and organic vegetables from Provence; roast Solliès figs and arlette biscuit.

Name: Le Comptoir des Alpes
Description: Set in a modern hotel, this restaurant reflects the Franco-Italian roots of its chef, Daniele Raimondi. His “Ascension” menu rolls out crisp, legible flavours that refuse to compromise on quality: Carnaroli risotto with gorgonzola; agnolotti of smoked ricotta, pistachio and lemon confit; lamb cooked over embers, broccoli orecchiette and Taggiasche olives. One terrace backs onto the street, while another, quieter, overlooks a peaceful square.

Name: Caffè Cosi - La trattoria de Bruno Caironi
Description: Of Italian and Mediterranean inspiration, this colourful contemporary trattoria, housed in a former art gallery, overlooks a cobbled courtyard. We fell in love with the risotto with French green peas and different textures of guanciale – to die for! Before leaving, pop into the gourmet grocery store and stock up on first-rate Italian goodies.

Name: Chez Mon Jules
Description: The dining room is adorned with assorted paraphernalia and wooden tables and chairs. You will be treated to scrumptious regional fare, such as homemade rennet with foie gras or lacquered pork belly from Dieulefit with regional veggies. In fine weather, take a seat on the shaded terrace and sample the splendid view.

Name: La Grangée
Description: Chef Jean-Baptiste Girard, a local lad and enthusiastic champion of his region, and his Japanese born wife, Maiko, have turned this village inn around. Local produce (Bourbonnais Charolais beef, organic veg from Rouy, Vandenesse poultry) and what the chef picks at the weekends take centre stage on the menu. The bread with wild garlic is out of this world. Attentive service, lovely tableware by a local artisan. Heavenly!

Name: La Table du Château Gratien
Description: In the landscaped grounds of the Gratien and Meyer wine estate, this adorable late 19C château oozes character and cachet – herringbone parquet, glittering chandeliers and a fireplace. The cuisine deftly showcases the region's fine produce – white asparagus, black truffle and Val de Loire potatoes. Herbs from the garden, excellent home-made bread, warm madeleines served with coffee. A taste of the good life.

Name: Monsieur P
Description: On Place des Célestins, Monsieur P is the stomping ground of good food lovers. In the kitchen, Florent Poulard, who trained at the Paul Bocuse Institute and honed his skills in top houses, deftly prepares tasty modern cuisine. He loves to work with vegetables (after a stint with Alain Passard) and whole fish and cuts of meat. Love at first bite!

Name: La Petite École
Description: This restaurant moved into the premises of the former village school a few years ago. The delicate, flavoursome cuisine is definitely worth an A. Ten out of ten, too, for the chef, a lover of fine produce, who concocts precise, succulent recipes. Even better, it is excellent value for money - if only our school canteen had been like this!

Name: Loiseau du Morvan
Address: Hostellerie de la Tour d’Auxois, 5 avenue Bernard Loiseau, Saulieu, 21210, France
Description: Opposite the Relais Bernard Loiseau, housed in a 17C building, this bistro offers an alternative to the fine dining restaurant. Here, local and regional recipes take pride of place, such as the eggs in a red wine sauce or the chicken Gaston Gérard. Comfortable guestrooms done out in unadulterated Burgundy style.

Name: La Côte des Monts Damnés
Description: Developed entirely around the wines of this family-owned estate, the bistronomic menu is flanked by some of the house signature dishes: tagliatelle with Chavignol goat's cheese, hot soufflé… Damnably delicious! Comfortable rooms for longer stays.

Name: L'Orangerie des Trois Roys
Description: L'Orangerie is a gorgeous setting with sculptures and verdant plants beneath the glass roof, club armchairs in the dining area and a charming shaded terrace. Here you will be received like a king. Fish and seafood are given pride of place: monkfish with green curry and coconut milk, perfectly cooked sole meunière. Pastries from Chez Francis (a well-known local artisan).

Name: La Bourdasso
Description: This lovely traditional building tucked away in Les Corbières has been infused with the energy of an Italian family who fell in love with the region. Authentic Italian cuisine: divine homemade mozzarella (with milk from their own buffaloes, brought over from Italy!), pasta and bread made with ancient wheat, also home grown. The spacious terrace is ideal to appreciate the lovely countryside.

Name: Olhabidea
Description: In this 16C Basque farmhouse you can enjoy simple and unpretentious dishes prepared using ingredients fresh from the vegetable garden. Opt to eat in the hushed atmosphere of either the salon or the library. The guestrooms are overflowing with interesting objects and keepsakes. Outside, you can wander around 4ha of parkland planted with maples, conifers and camellias. Quite charming!

Name: Nature
Description: This appealing restaurant opposite the church in Armentières showcases some lovely seasonal and regional produce: fish from Boulogne and Dunkirk, pigeon from Flanders and Black Angus beef from Picardy, for example, go into dishes that form surprise set menus comprising several courses… Pleasant space decorated with plants.

Name: Le Chai
Description: Divinely located on Sainte-Marie-de-Ré market square, this bistro demonstrates a fine bistronomy spirit, sprinkled with more contemporary influences, showing a distinct preference for local vegetables from mainly organic small market gardeners. Fresh, tasty, well executed and good value for money, illustrated by a pearlescent slab of cod cooked to perfection.

Name: Le Président
Description: "This Lyon institution, taken over by Christophe Marguin, judiciously offers modern cuisine without ever disregarding the great classics; frogs' legs with cream, Bresse chicken with Etrez cream. The ""Président"" Edouard Herriot, then mayor of Lyon, used to come and have his coffee here. "

Name: Les Lilas
Description: In the village at the foot of the Vosges, this large salmon - pink building by the roadside is impossible to miss! Diners are warmly welcomed by Armelle, in the handsome Art deco conservatory, while Lionel, in the kitchens, turns out tasty, contemporary dishes with a sprinkling of creative touches. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Soces
Address: 32 rue de la Villette, Paris, 75019, France
Description: A gem of a Parisian brasserie, where the former chef at Clamato, Marius de Ponfilly, has teamed up with Kevin Deulio. Previously at Bar Vendôme in The Ritz, the latter has taken to the restaurant floor like a duck to water. The pair have found a formula that is as irreverent as it is on point: choice cuts of meat (cooked over binchotan charcoal, as is the fish) and plates to be shared between friends (or soces in Parisian slang), with original and clever combinations of flavours (lightly breaded scallops in pil pil sauce on warmed soft flatbread; cuttlefish just seared and served in an aromatic consommé with leek oil and "Grenoble-style" vegetables).

Name: La Table du 2
Address: 2 rue de la République, Nîmes, 30000, France
Description: This contemporary brasserie – part of the Musée de la Romanité – is perfectly in tune with the architecture of the building. It offers an unobstructed view of the Arènes de Nîmes (or amphitheatre), as well as a seasonal menu overseen by Michelin-starred chef Franck Putelat. Tuck into true traditional French cuisine: egg meurette (in a red wine sauce); calf sweetbreads and mashed potatoes with Maury jus; trout meunière; and even the iconic crêpes Suzette...

Name: AGA
Description: Alexandre Goniak and Gerie Jenner met in Australia but opened their first venture in a small country town on the banks of the Garonne just two minutes from a medieval gateway. There is no menu, as the chef only works with whatever fresh produce takes his fancy from one day to the next. The resulting contemporary bistro fare reveals his spot-on craftsmanship and flair for devising intelligent recipes, illustrated by loin of pork with Paimpol cranberry beans, bacon cream, fluffy mashed potato and roast cauliflower. Casual, smiling welcome and a genuine desire to share and inform, in particular regarding the wines.

Name: L'Alto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this pretty pink-brick château tucked away in the countryside, the kitchen uses only high-quality ingredients with a renewed look at local produce. Highly contrasted flavours, like this fillet of wild seabass with shellfish and a rhubarb emulsion… L’Alto orchestrates a fine-tuned culinary score and an equally musical interior, with a sculpture of a saxophone and a swimming pool in the shape of a violin!

Name: Mer & Coquillage
