Description: In the street of the same name, this bistro adds a joyful, even delicate spin to French country cooking, with special mention for the house speciality: cassoulet with duck confit and sausages, served on ceramic plates. Flawless preparations and high-flying seasoning; good value for money.

Name: La Ruche
Description: In the wine country where Marsanne and Roussanne grapes are grown (the two varieties used to make white Saint-Péray), a modern bistro done right! On the menu: tasty, carefully prepared neo-bistro cuisine in tune with the seasons, and an excellent list of wines from the northern Côtes du Rhône region. Reservation required.

Name: Tabi - Ippei Uemura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Tabi, which means journey in Japanese, says it all! Born in Kyoto, the chef has adopted the city of Marseilles as his own. He incorporates locally caught fish into traditional Japanese recipes, prepared in front of customers. Food-saké pairings for aficionados. One of a kind!

Name: Parapluie
Description: This lilliputian restaurant serves globetrotting food in the zeitgeist, with a sprinkling of spices and based on seasonal, mostly local, ingredients. The culinary offer is rolled out in a single set "mystery" menu comprised of several courses at dinner, and a reasonably priced lunchtime menu with options. Fine selection of wine, beer and spirits (whiskies, eaux de vie etc).

Name: Le Bélouga
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant commands a breath-taking panoramic view over the coast and the bay of the Sept-Îles archipelago. The subtle and meticulous cuisine oscillates between classicism and creativity, with some dishes displaying exotic touches, such as the pearly langoustine with yuzu ponzu combined with Breton artichoke, or the bone-in veal rubbed with Breton curry and nori jam.

Name: Mantesino
Description: The Naples-born chef, who used to be an engineer, has enthusiastically donned an apron (mantesino in Italian) and opened this small bistro in a street near the Église Saint-Aubin. He gives pride of place to his roots by tapping into the culinary traditions of Southern Italy, from Campania to Puglia. A far cry from stereotypical Italian fare, his no-nonsense bistro cuisine wins diners over by drawing solely on flavoursome, meticulously selected ingredients: mortadella from Bologna, hazelnuts from Piedmont, Ibaïama pork, as well as meat from Aveyron and vegetables from local growers. Uplifting!

Name: Auberge de la Roche
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Mercantour National Park, between the valleys of the Tinée River and Vésubie River, a duo with a longing for nature set their sights on this traditional stone-built inn. The calm beauty of the surrounding countryside won them over, as it will you, too. Our hosts serve a single set menu of natural, creative cuisine with a strong vegetable component, as well as local produce (including from their kitchen garden). There is a good selection of natural beers and wines.

Name: Bohème
Address: 47 avenue du Moulin de la Croix, Mougins, 06250, France
Description: In this smart, trendy establishment with a decor of premium and untreated materials, the food is an ode to the very best breeds of beef cattle, aged and prepared by the famous butcher Alexandre Polmard in his unique way. Peruvian chef Manuel Rondan is in a class of his own when it comes to cooking over hot coals and wild-fish ceviche, as well as some lovely Mediterranean dishes. There is a drop-dead view from the terrace.

Name: La Bulle d'Air
Description: From his open kitchen, the chef consummately crafts dishes such as low-temperature arctic char, flanked with a velvety gribiche sauce and a crunchy salad of fennel. The single set lunchtime menu is a steal – all the better when leisurely sampled on the delightful, cobbled patio in summertime.

Name: Au G'Retz des Saisons
Description: Well-travelled young chef Samuel Duchêne aligns his cooking with the seasons. His short menu, which changes every month, showcases first and foremost local Pays de Retz farmers and artisans – fish, free-range eggs, sea salt. Beetroot marinated in cider, confit egg yolk, watercress coulis or fillet of sea bass, carrot, coconut emulsion, turmeric: hard work, audacity and flavour. The house-made bread is very good, too. Limited capacity, so it's best to book in advance.

Name: Le Clos de la Prairie
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in the countryside, this charming restaurant is peaceful and bucolic. Behind his stove, the chef masterfully prepares dishes in tune with the zeitgeist and the seasons. In summer, enjoy the quiet terrace overlooking the meadow. Accessible only by reservation.

Name: Peron
Description: On the coast road, this building clinging to the rocks offers a breathtaking view of the bay of Marseille and its islands and the château d’If. A brisk sea breeze has shaken up the menu which features dishes such as local and wild fish of the day, stuffed vegetables, duck breast and beef fillet, without forgetting the ubiquitous bouillabaisse, all of which served on the splendid terrace. A genuine institution since 1855!

Name: Chez Fonfon
Description: This family restaurant (1952) is pleasing in terms both of its contemporary interior and its seafood, freshly fished in the wooden pointu boats that can be seen bobbing about in the little port.

Name: Epiro
Description: After a stint in Rome, where they ran a highly sought-after bistro, Alessandra and Marco are giving it another go near the port in Nice. Appetising Roman delicacies, heart-warming home-made pasta, lashings of generosity and tingling tastebuds, without forgetting the splendid Italian wine list – bang on every time!

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye
Address: 2 rue de la Libération, Beaumont-en-Auge, 14950, France
Description: This inn with bags of character keeps all of its promises. Nicely prepared local produce, meticulous presentation, a sense of generosity and a taste for fresh herbs, all in tune with the seasons. And not forgetting the distinctive rustic - style interior. A real pleasure.

Name: Emotions
Description: In the heart of the village, this former winegrower's house has been turned into a restaurant (previously La Vigne d'Adam) with a pared-back interior design that blends wood, fabrics and natural materials. The cuisine follows the seasons to create marriages of premium ingredients: hare à la royale in autumn, truffle menu in winter, asparagus in spring and lobster in summer! Over 400 wines.

Name: Lazare
Address: Parvis de la gare Saint-Lazare, rue Intérieure, Paris, 75008, France
Description: In the heart of the famous Gare St - Lazare is this elegant railway brasserie, version 2013. It is the brainchild of Éric Frechon, who respects the canons of the genre: French - style devilled eggs, pike quenelles or mackerel in a white wine sauce. Fine French tradition is right on track! Pleasant and very lively.

Name: Le Relais de Saulx
Description: This characterful establishment (1673) in the town centre, not far from the Hospices de Beaune, is in the capable hands of Charles Danet (previously at the helm of Le Timbre in Paris). He has had no trouble quickly making himself at home in Burgundy! His signature style is unmistakable in the wholesome market-fresh cuisine, which he describes as "artisanal seasonal" cooking.

Name: L'Agastache
Address: 1 rue de la Cave, Volnay, 21190, France
Description: This restaurant, whose reputation has grown by word of mouth, is fully deserving of its success. The chef is very attentive to the quality of his ingredients and his creative cuisine, in which vegetables and plants play a pivotal role, is as tasty as it is balanced. Examples include houmous of winter veggies with curcuma and egg parfait or a purée of celery with finely diced Granny Smith apples. Bargain priced menu at lunchtime.

Name: Autrement
Description: At a slight remove from the town centre, this quiet little restaurant lays out its own fresh vision. The chef perfectly masters cooking times and seasonings, and works with quality ingredients. His original and colourful cuisine is meticulous and tasty; for instance, his half-cooked veal carpaccio, beetroot, carrots and citrus fruit is a showstopper. Not forgetting his signature dessert: the Paris-Brest. What are you waiting for?

Name: Eclipses
Description: This restaurant, by a chef who has carved out a career in Michelin-starred kitchens (Ledoyen, Apicius, Le Grand Véfour), serves contemporary cuisine that is heedful of ingredients and the seasons. Enjoy your meal in the tastefully decorated neo-Classical setting. Lovely vaulted cellar.

Name: Le Pré de la Cure
Address: 1 place de la Mairie, Yvoire, 74140, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fancy diving into Lake Geneva! The view is as stunning as the food is mouth - watering. Fish and produce from the lake take pride of place in the menu, as do succulent local specialties. Depending on availability, you will taste pike, perch or trout. A treat for the taste buds!

Name: Le Bout du Quai
Address: Route de la Corniche, Cancale, 35260, France
Description: Aptly located at the end of the quayside (hence the name), the fashionable slate grey glazed front of this restaurant overlooks the Atlantic and Mont St Michel. Chef Romain Roland, after a stint at a star restaurant in Corsica, crafts ambitious, creative cuisine, dotted with subtle Mediterranean notes.

Name: Les Ronins
Description: In Japanese culture, ronins are samurai without a master, which is Anthony and Émilie’s metaphor for their unfettered approach to cooking and, of course, their exquisitely presented Franco-Asian cuisine, such as Angus beef hanger steak served with crying tiger sauce and a hearty gratin dauphinois. Trendy Alpine-inspired decor, friendly service and good vibes!

Name: Le Goût du Large
Description: Sheltered from the bustling port, take a seat in this cosy, modern eatery and dig into the contemporary, generous nosh of youthful Jonathan Selliez (assisted by his mum for pastries) who plays on textures and flavours. The fish is from sustainable fishing boats, such as the superb fillet of mackerel, flanked with a maki of leeks rolled in nori seaweed leaves and a medley of carrots, jelly and pickled. All the more reason not to set sail straight away…

Name: Cucina Byblos
Description: With Cucina having replaced Rivea, the restaurant at Hotel Byblos continues to reinvent itself under Alain Ducasse. Building on his success in Paris, he has adapted Cucina for Saint-Tropez. A chic and convivial place with a large glass-walled kitchen, green walls and a terrace under the plane trees. On the menu: generous Italian cuisine prepared using premium-quality ingredients.

Name: L'Atelier
Description: Chef Fabrice Rodot is a food lover, and he proves it with his dishes, which feature local and seasonal ingredients. He has a perfect grasp of the classics, and this cosy restaurant with rustic touches is a lovely setting in which to eat: cauliflower in a brioche crust, mousseline cream; organic veal, peas and carrots, sauce Périgueux-style jus; crêpes Suzette flambéed on a pedestal table. Not forgetting the excellent house-made bread! In fine weather, head for a table by the fountain on the terrace.

Name: Côté Toqués
Description: Chef Julien Chabozy's aromatic, tasty food showcases the best of local produce, with lashings of personality to boot. Friendly and endearing depict the front of house vibe, supervised by his wife Marie. The establishment also boasts a delicatessen and a wine shop, La Cave des Toqués, next door… It was love at first bite.

Name: La Table du Chef
Description: Only open in the evenings, this small bistro just two minutes from Rue d’Antibes never disappoints. In an open kitchen, a youthful chef works with local, seasonal produce, crafting subtle, tasty dishes, such as his knockout velvety carrot soup with star anise and lightly seared shrimp. Market availability dictates the contents of the “Surprise” menu which is great value for money… Booking recommended.

Name: La Table de Marie-Ange
Description: The terrace overlooking the Aravis range is so mesmerising, it is difficult to tear oneself away. Marie-Ange aims to serve fine regional dishes oozing with authentic flavour: pan-seared cèpes, fillets of wild perch from Lake Geneva, fillet of beef simmered in mushrooms and grandma’s potato gratin, without forgetting the wickedly lavish dessert trolley. The interior sports old wood and farming tools – charming welcome.

Name: LiLi
Description: Opened by the Hong Kong luxury hotel group of the same name, the already famous Peninsula Hotel is a fitting home for this Asian restaurant. In a strikingly theatrical decor, the long menu, prepared by the Chinese chef, unveils a wide range of the country's specialities (some adapted to European tastes). A culinary ambassador for China.

Name: Capitaine
Description: After working in the kitchens of some restaurants with a great pedigree (L'Ambroisie, L'Arpège, L'Astrance), Baptiste Day decided to open this pleasant bistro. Diners are treated to lovely market-fresh dishes that are inspired by his Breton origins and enhanced by exotic flavours. The popular starter of pork croquettes (ginger, garlic and chilli mayonnaise) will certainly whet your appetite! Selection of organic and natural wines.

Name: Restaurant des Grands Boulevards
Description: Beneath the hotel's central glass roof, modern and trendy decoration, a warm welcome and French-Italian flavours, under the direction of chef Giovanni Passerini. The short menu is a lesson in simplicity and deliciousness – cf. the paccheri with monkfish and bottarga or the rack of lamb grilled on the Josper, Roscoff onions, soft-boiled egg, cockles and a lamb jus. The extensive wine list features a cutting-edge selection.

Name: Auberge Nicolas Flamel
Description: As well as being a wealthy bourgeois and one-time owner of this house, the oldest in Paris (1407), was Nicolas Flamel also an alchemist? Historians still disagree, but food connoisseurs are in no doubt that the chef transforms every ingredient he touches into culinary gold. Langoustine, Belgian endive and a clementine-flavoured consommé of claws; pithivier of mallard, foie gras and truffle; confit of quince with kalamansi and ginger: dishes that are perfectly balanced, delicately flavoured, intelligently composed and free of superfluous frills.

Name: Rooster
Description: After training in prestigious houses (from Passedat to Darroze), Frédéric Duca has set up shop in the more working-class part of the 17th arrondissement. In a former street corner cafe, the Marseille-born chef signs dishes which pay numerous tributes to his Mediterranean and Provençal roots. The lunchtime menu is at delicious eater-friendly prices. More ambitious in the evenings.

Name: Tadam
Description: This delightful little eatery proposes a brief, seasonal and mouth-watering menu, underscored by a commitment to sustainable development. The food hits the spot every time thanks to tip-top ingredients stripped of unnecessary frills, illustrated by the scrumptious hot mushroom pie. A casual vibe and brunch on Sundays. A welcome addition to the Gobelins culinary scene.

Name: Auberge du Cheval Blanc
Description: This 18C coaching inn has been run by the same family since 1959. Chef Jean-Claude Tellechea adds a new spin to the traditional regional line-up: crispy hake, black pudding, Ibaïama ham, Bayonne chocolate. The interior is patriotically decked in red and white Basque Country colours. The range of menus is such that there is something for every budget.

Name: Marso & Co
Description: Tomy Gousset (Tomy & Co, near Les Invalides) runs this restaurant that sets out to take diners on a culinary journey: the food tours the entire Mediterranean basin from Greece to Portugal via Italy and Lebanon (but also Latin America). Examples of the Colombian born chef’s handiwork include an aguachile of seabream and shrimp, pink grapefruit, cucumber and coriander. The octopus-themed artwork on the walls is by street artist Kraken. Soul-warming recipes, spot-on flavours, fantastically fresh ingredients – a felicitous feast awaits you!

Name: Poulpette
Description: Now, this is a place that has it in the bag. The deliberately short menu offers tasty market-based cooking, with flights of fancy far and wide; it is made with fine ingredients prepared with care and originality. Amandine, once a dance teacher, now head of service and partner, and Antoine, alumnus of the elite Paris Institute of Political Studies but passionate about food (stints at Lucas Carton and Jadis) have joined forces to offer a delightful culinary experience.

Name: Kodawari Ramen - Yokochō
Description: The bustling vibe and cramped dimensions of this eatery instantly conjure up pictures of historic Tokyo. The ramen, made on site and served in delicious broths of Loiret poultry, attract gourmets from every horizon. The house speciality is kurugoma ramen made with a secret black sesame seed sauce and pata negra pork. Avoid peak times, as the place is very popular. Fully deserving of its success.

Name: Rhapsody
Description: This spruce eatery in the Parisian suburbs works with first-class produce to rustle up appetising, well-curated bistronomic recipes. Examples include lamb confit served with marinated aubergine and a sumac-flavoured yoghurt sauce or pollock paired with roast carrots and an emulsion of carrot and samphire, finishing with a wickedly decadent creamy chestnut and Corsican clementine dessert… Ask for a table on the lovely rear patio with a view of the kitchen.

Name: Les Trois Forts
Description: From the seventh floor, the panoramic view over the port is simply sublime! The contemporary dishes with a delicious Southern flavour make for a wonderful gourmet interlude.

Name: L'inaTTendu
Description: "This former nurse has had a career change, after winning French TV's Masterchef. He creates modern and generous food, such as the ""inaTTendue"" (""unexpected"") starter – now a signature dish: tuna tataki and cervelle de canut. In the restaurant room, his wife, a former nursing auxiliary, now takes care of diners' wellbeing. A decidedly pleasant address. "

Name: Le Comptoir de la Mère Germaine
Description: This offshoot of the star establishment doesn’t do things by halves: predominantly wooden contemporary interior, an imposing counter, an open kitchen with a gleaming spit-roast oven and a shaded terrace. Wide range of spit-roast delicacies such as young Lubéron cockerel and Mont Ventoux pork, washed down of course with a glass of Châteauneuf-du-pape.

Name: L'Escargot
Description: A pleasant contemporary setting for traditional cuisine and emblematic dishes, such as snails in butter, garlic and parsley. Chef-owner Dominique Dubert jazzes up a traditional repertory with the odd dash of modernity (combava, ginger, curry, etc). It is a pleasure to linger over a meal on the terrace of this Snail in summer.

Name: L'Ouillette
Description: An enthusiastic young couple is at the helm of this family - run inn on the village square. In the kitchen, Simon hops between traditional (eggs in red wine sauce, marbled, seasoned ham, coq au vin) and more modern creations; Maude ensures that her guests’ every need is met in the dining room. Definitely to be recommended.

Name: Les Épicuriens
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant set in a period castle concocts delicate, up-to-date food whose exquisite plating will find favour with even the most discerning connoisseurs, illustrated by carpaccio of langoustines in citrus fruit, fennel and caviar. The enticing wine list naturally showcases champagnes and the stylish terrace overlooks the estate’s gardens. Pleasant rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Le Terroir
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This spruce and welcoming establishment in the centre of the village serves appetising regional cuisine: Burgundy snails with butter, garlic, parsley and almonds; coq au vin with red wine; crème brûlée with pain d'épices. Fine choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Le Panoramique
Address: 1 village de l'Église, La Pernelle, 50630, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant, run by the same family since 1966, stands next to the village church on a hill overlooking the sea and the island of Tatihou. Initially a bar, then a crêperie, it is now an upmarket eatery that seeks to showcase produce from Normandy.

Name: Racines des Prés
Description: This restaurant in Saint-Germain-des-Prés is always bustling! Open kitchen counter, laid-back but chic "vintage" atmosphere, and delicate cuisine that is beautifully presented on the plate. The menu features refined dishes such as cod cooked with ash, burnt leek and smoked grenaille potatoes, plus delicious desserts, eg Manjari chocolate soufflé tart and cocoa ice cream… You'll be coming back for more!

Name: Les Botanistes
Description: Not far from Le Bon Marché, this pleasant bistro is in the hands of a chef who does not cut corners when it comes to ingredients or taste! Take a seat on the characteristic bistro benches and dig into mouth-watering beef and shallots or a decadent rum baba smothered in whipped cream. The well-stocked wine cellar offers ample choice to pair with your meal. Friendly, tasty and casual – a winning formula!

Name: Sinabro
Description: In the mood for bibimbap and authentic Korean cuisine? Then this bistro is the right place for you! On the programme: a concise menu, splendid meat, meticulously sourced by a MOF, slick, smiling service, and, of course, healthy, flavoursome food – right down to the desserts and all made from scratch.

Name: Le Castellane - Château Le Prieuré
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Le Castellane, part of the Château du Prieuré, serves modern fare that keeps tabs on the seasons and is predominantly local. You can choose between the Empire-inspired dining room or the terrace overlooking the Loire. Each of the guestrooms is individually appointed and fully in keeping with the historic character of the valley of kings.

Name: Le Florimond
Address: 19 avenue de La Motte-Picquet, Paris, 75007, France
Description: Florimond – named after Monet's gardener at Giverny – has a convivial bistro atmosphere. The chef makes sure to use plenty of vegetables in his traditional local cooking, featuring many ingredients from his native Corrèze. And like his father before him, who was a pork butcher, he makes all his sausages, black pudding and conserves himself!

Name: La Roche Le Roy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This pretty little manor house on the outskirts of town has recently been refurbished and modernised, all the way from the decoration to the kitchens, the domain of chef Maximilien Bridier. Taking an enthusiastic approach to high-quality ingredients, he presents elegant, precise dishes with no frills. Without fail, the menu features a vegetarian option. There is a fine selection of wines by the glass, and the service is attentive. Sit out on the terrace on warm days.

Name: Le Bougainvillier
Address: 1792 route de la Corniche, Saint-Raphaël, 83700, France
Description: Set in an enchanting location, La Villa Mauresque boasts a terrace that overlooks an exotic garden and affords perfect sea views – an ideal spot in which to sample Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. Abounding with flavour, it is cooked to perfection and focuses on local produce, in particular fish and vegetables. Drawing on a menu devised by Meilleur Ouvrier de France David Boyer, Hyères-born chef Nathan Helo puts together a range of technically sophisticated multi-course set menus, including a visually appealing vegetarian tasting menu. One to watch!

Name: Folie Cuisine d'Émotions
Description: In a heritage edifice in the heart of historic Chambéry, not far from the Château des Ducs de Savoie, indulge yourself(ves) in this establishment, set in the former courtyard of what is now a luxury hotel. In a suitably classy yet cosy setting, the chef crafts a “carte blanche” menu inspired by the seasons and travel.

Name: Belvédère
Description: Japanese chef Kohei Ohata skilfully harnesses the flavours of the Mediterranean fare that abounds in the surrounding markets to produce really appealing dishes. His talented wife brings her skills to bear on the pastry section. It is all fresh, fragrant and charged at a fair price. This excellent establishment is a little hidden away in the Hotel Belesso – reserved for those in the know, and all the better for it.

Name: L'Écluse
Description: A step away from the royal castle of Amboise and the Clos Lucé, chef Mélanie Popineau can be relied upon for joyful bistronomic cuisine, rich in flavour, in the form of brief seasonal menus. Diners are simply and warmly welcomed by her partner. In fine weather, the leafy terrace shaded by willows is heaven-sent.

Name: Les Planeurs
Description: A Japanese chef and his partner have opened this unusual establishment in a deliberately bohemian and offbeat setting. The French cuisine is precise, original, balanced and flavoursome, illustrated by a risotto of poultry and shellfish, rich in seafaring aromas or roast apricots in rosemary served with homemade yoghurt ice cream. Good value for money.

Name: Auberge du Forgeron
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A family-run establishment abounding with charm. In the fine dining restaurant, the modern menu keeps pace with the seasons, and the creative chef's dishes go down a treat every time (the "Mosaic of Artois Trout" is a feast for the eyes). Guests staying the night enjoy comfortable, well-kept guestrooms. For more traditional cuisine, head to the Bistro du Forgeron to enjoy the regional specialities of northern France.

Name: Au Bon Pichet
Description: It is a delight to eat at this restaurant that has been run by the same family for four generations! Like his forefathers before him, the chef concocts good traditional recipes: smoked pork shank with potato sauerkraut, pike perch quenelles and matelote sauce... The convivial service and winstub decor confirm that the rules of good living never go out of fashion!

Name: Le Vivarais
Address: Hôtel Helvie, 5 avenue Claude-Expilly, Vals-les-Bains, 07600, France
Description: Located in the heart of the city, right next to the casino, this Belle Époque grand hotel stands out from its surroundings. Its classic and elegant restaurant serves seasonal French cuisine made with good fresh produce, often locally sourced. Impeccable, friendly service. Spacious terrace shaded by plane trees at the side of the hotel.

Name: Le Relais des Maures
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This large inn cultivates the taste of the South. The chef creates cuisine steeped in tradition, based on the market and beautifully prepared, for excellent value. A few guestrooms with sea view, on the second floor, to extend your stay beyond your meal. A pleasant place.

Name: La Pomme d'Or
Address: 1 rue de la Panneterie, Sancerre, 18300, France
Description: A slice of The Golden Apple (La Pomme d'Or) is always delicious. A young couple from Brittany has taken over this restaurant, a former coaching inn with a slightly revamped dining area. The modern cuisine draws on the Sancerre terroir and Breton roots: vegetables from the garden, tomato water broth; pork tenderloin fillet, seasonal vegetables. You can see straight away that the chef is a pro (cf. the presentation of the dishes) who never forgets the sine qua non: how it tastes! The chocolate gianduja praline with a gavotte biscuit crisp is a wonderful dessert. The wine list, unsurprisingly, gives the floor to Sancerre wines, and that is fine by us!

Name: Arraditz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This 19C house located in a small town on the outskirts of Pau is the haunt of a pair of chefs who learnt the ropes in star establishments: chef Olivier Nicolau, from Lescar, and his partner Karine, in charge of the service. Their subtle, well-crafted repertory showcases regional produce: Projan squab, Lucq-de-Béarn mushrooms, Bahus-Soubiran lemon… Intelligent surf and turf combinations and generous helpings, illustrated by beef tartar with smoked samphire and white asparagus; grilled loin of red tuna and a crispy slice of boar’s head. We recommend the fresh tang of confit of strawberries, prepared like an “arrasimat” (stewed or macerated in its juices) for a delicious conclusion to your meal.

Name: L'Amphitryon
Description: Chef Stéphane Goudet has been valiantly regaling his guests in a style worthy of Molière’s Amphitryon since 1997 in this immense vaulted dining room whose stone walls are offset by the odd modern detail and soft lighting. A polished culinary lineup that stars fresh local produce and a reverence for the seasons: truffle in winter, lobster in summer (served on the patio), and whole hare in autumn. Slick, smiling service.

Name: Le Vivier
Address: 9 rue de Beg-Er-Vir, Lomener, Ploemeur, 56270, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In this restaurant facing the open sea, the cuisine showcases fish and seafood (of course!). With the island of Groix as a backdrop, guests could almost dip their toes in the water while the chef serves up extremely fresh fish dishes, from a menu interspersed with a few modern touches.

Name: L'Ami Jean
Description: Passionate about fine seasonal produce, Stéphane Jégo serves cuisine that is bursting with generosity and flavours. Dishes with quite some character! Be sure to book.

Name: Claire et Hugo
Address: 77 avenue du Général-Galliéni, à Sainte-Savine, Troyes, 10300, France
Description: An enthusiastic self-taught young couple runs this restaurant with a subdued decor composed of raw materials. The premises also house a bakery and delicatessen leading onto a lovely terrace and indoor garden (including a citrus tree greenhouse). The ingredients, which are 95% organic, make for healthy, tasty and balanced dishes, organised into a single set menu.

Name: Auberge de Port Vallières
Description: The welcoming establishment of Marie-Hélène and Bruno Leroux offers sustenance to discerning foodies in a chic contemporary setting. Flavoursome cuisine, rich in regional delicacies, awaits you in this stylish, inviting restaurant, whose chef cannot resist prime ingredients: truffle-flavoured homemade white pudding, poultry sauce; seven-hour roasted shoulder of French lamb in thyme… Slick service. The wine cellar is a treasure trove of regional tipples! Good food comes first in this auberge where you are always welcomed with a smile.

Name: Le Mas des Aigras - Table du Verger
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Pleasant stone farmhouse set amid vineyards and fields. The chef rustles up, partly in front of diners, tasty recipes based on organic produce. Tasteful decor and attractive terrace. An ideal spot for stopovers, this hotel’s rooms are enlivened with Provençal colours.

Name: L'Atelier
Description: Cyril Haberland is a chef whose credentials speak for themselves (he worked alongside Thierry Marx, during the Cordeillan-Bages period). He and his wife opened L'Atelier in the centre of Périgueux, creating a modern space with a friendly atmosphere where you feel at ease right off the bat. Through his cooking, the chef fetes the farmers of South-West France and his cherished regional ingredients, such as wild mushrooms sourced by local pickers, Périgord black truffles and local snails. He works with these ingredients, showcasing them in nicely presented modern dishes, for example: pain perdu with pullet and pink garlic, calf sweetbreads with a lemon glaze, butternut confit, pineapple, candied citron and coconut biscuit.

Name: Manger & Dormir sur la Plage
Description: It sounds like the title of a song from the 1980s. This young and relaxed restaurant facing the sea offers marine-inspired cuisine, with a mouthwatering choice of shellfish, fish, and of course oysters: the establishment belongs to the Gillardeau family, the famous oyster farmers. The large terrace offers a lovely view, with the Île d'Oléron on the horizon. As for accommodation, "Dormir sur la Plage" has four large very well-appointed junior suites.

Name: À l’Épi d’Or
Description: This quintessential Parisian bistro of the former Baltard market is the latest acquisition of Elodie and Jean-François Piège. The authentic vintage interior (old tiles and mirrors and stained walls) provides the setting for traditional fare that changes daily during the week. Also available: pork pie, croque madame, foie gras, steak tartare and chips.

Name: Iodé
Description: Sophie Reigner, a self-taught chef from Brittany, has returned to her homeland, after earning her laurels in the kitchen of Alan Geaam in Paris. Her delicate creations and exquisite plating are spot on: abalone cooked in seaweed butter, potatoes smoked in pine needles and a sherry-flavoured poultry reduction; monkfish with Guémené andouille, nori leeks and a light, frothy bergamot-flavoured hollandaise sauce… Attentive service.

Name: L'Altévic
Description: In a contemporary glass and metal setting, Jean-Christophe Perrin serves up-to-date dishes, inspired by the market : poultry and morel mushroom pâté en croute ; stone bass with white beans from Paimpol ; mont-blanc pavlova-style…

Name: Le Jardin
Address: 16 rue de la Redoute, Haguenau, 67500, France
Description: After 38 years of dedicated service, Damien Meyer has passed the torch to his son, Romain, with whom he had worked hand in hand for 8 years. The regulars can rest easy that Romain has remained faithful to the house signature dishes (fish soup, tuna carpaccio, Chateaubriand with Béarnaise sauce), albeit with a hint of modernity. Don’t forget to look up and admire the superb Renaissance ceiling as you dine.

Name: Arcada
Address: 13 rue de la Rousselle, Bordeaux, 33000, France
Description: Tucked away between Place Camille-Jullian and Saint-Michel, a contemporary vibe sets the scene in the vaulted dining room whose bistronomic menu is ingredient-centred: in fact, some 90% of the fruit and veg comes from small, local producers. At lunchtime, you might sample a deliciously priced tataki of marinated watermelon in soy and citrus fruit or confit of loin of hake baked in olive oil. The culinary score becomes more high-flying in the evenings as do the ingredients. The menu changes regularly. Outstanding warm welcome and service.

Name: Les Bords de Mer
Description: Subtle cuisine and a stunning sea view: what more could we ask for? Chef Camille Gandolfo, who hails from Marseille, adds a fresh (occasionally Asian) spin to her original Mediterranean recipes in a bid to showcase seasonal produce. The savvy wine list gives top billing to the organic production of the Domaine de Fontenille wine estate (AOP Luberon), which owns this elegant establishment. An impressive restaurant that takes its food seriously.

Name: Cédrat
Description: A couple, two chefs, two different culinary formulas: at lunchtime, chef Maëlyss Vultaggio chalks up her menu on the blackboard, assisted in the kitchen by Éric Maillet, a young chef who earned his stripes working for the likes of Gérald Passedat. In the evening, the roles are reversed: he takes the lead, creating more of a fine dining menu with his partner supporting him. Dishes such as farmhouse chicken on the barbecue, celeriac confit, sorrel, ginger/lemongrass sauce and XO reduction exemplify this modern Mediterranean-style cuisine. Using organic vegetables, locally caught fish and well-reared meats, the food certainly packs a punch. Contemporary setting.

Name: Epona
Address: InterContinental Lyon - Hotel Dieu, 20 quai Jules-Courmont, Lyon, 69002, France
Description: A hospital for eight centuries, the former Hôtel-Dieu has preserved all the building's historical character. The Epona restaurant serves regional specialities with a modern twist, which you can enjoy in a lovely setting that calls to mind a high-end brasserie. And in fine weather, the team welcomes you in a superb courtyard garden.

Name: La Réserve de Nice
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Elegant, Art Deco cruise liner - inspired decor. Enjoy refined cuisine and superb views of the Bay of Angels and the Estérel mountains.

Name: Relais du Castéra
Description: This traditional inn has been run by the same couple of industry professionals for many years. The mouth-watering dishes give pride of place to the terroir and quality ingredients: lamb shoulder pastilla cooked for seven hours and served with a braising sauce infused with sweet spices; cod piquillos with shellfish bisque; a fine, sautéed pork chop.

Name: Bar des Oiseaux
Description: In this small corner house, Armand Crespo's "Bird Bar" won't fail to have foodies flapping with delight. Fine traditional French dishes (brandade, bourride) feature alongside delicious artisanal pasta: ravioli and stuffed chicken, seafood linguine etc. All at reasonable prices, in a decor inspired by pop art.

Name: Le Bengy
Description: This spot to the north of Nevers, once a roadside café, has been taken over by a pleasant young couple. The chef serves enjoyable traditional cuisine (roast monkfish, curry and lemongrass fumet, courgette and tomato tarte Tatin; chicken supreme, poultry liver and port stuffing), as well as a vegetarian set menu. In fine weather, make a beeline for the quiet terrace to the rear.

Name: Le 27 Gambetta
Description: Cod simmered in olive oil, butternut purée and bacon powder, or young pigeon with creamy sweet potatoes and foamy mashed potatoes: the chef crafts delicate bistro fare to which he adds his own personal signature, two minutes from Place Stanislas.

Name: Pleine Terre
Description: Behind a discreet façade, down the few steps leading to the basement, you will find a chef who is passionate about citrus fruits, spices and pepper: he has developed a cuisine that closely follows the seasons and showcases the work of handpicked small-scale producers. An inventive array of dishes, served by a friendly and enthusiastic front-of-house team: a great find.

Name: Ducasse sur Seine
Description: Well, no one can say that Alain Ducasse lacks for boldness or ideas, as the Ducasse sur Seine once again proves. An electric boat, moored on the quayside of Port Debilly in the swanky 16th arrondissement, offers a gastronomic cruise that is both ecological and silent. At the same time as you discover Parisian monuments, you will taste up - to - the - minute cuisine, masterfully crafted by a kitchen team worthy of the best restaurants. Well done, mon capitaine!

Name: Le Botaniste - La Chenevière
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Wooden panelling, floorboards and 18C furniture make for an elegant and refined setting. The serious-minded chef draws inspiration from the château's vegetable garden and from produce grown by his small-scale suppliers. His delicate cuisine features a variety of appetising takes on Normandy produce and pleasing alliances of flavours, for example: calf sweetbreads sautéed in butter and lime, broad beans and radishes in a lemongrass broth, radish leaf pesto; steamed John Dory, glazed beetroot, chard and shellfish, saffron sauce. The highly attentive service is top-notch.

Name: Le Divil
Description: Between Le Castillet and the prefecture, a specialist of fine matured meats: customers choose their piece (rib steak, entrecote, sirloin), which is then weighed, grilled and accompanied by tasty home - made fries. There are 300 types of wine to wash it down.

Name: Le Café des Artistes
Description: This bistro is the ideal complement to the Michelin-starred restaurant of this oh-so-bucolic establishment on the outskirts of Paris. It serves contemporary, tasty and inspired cuisine made with top-notch produce – delicious cod, Coco de Paimpol beans, chorizo and lobster cream – that you can enjoy on the terrace as you take in the view of the charming garden. Idyllic.

Name: L'Inconnu
Description: The chef, who for a long time was second-in-command at Passage 53, concocts Italian-inspired cuisine with influences from France, as well as his native Japan. He only works with the finest ingredients, using them to produce original and creative dishes, such as Breton langoustine tails topped with a cider and confit lemon emulsion.

Name: Arnaud Nicolas
Address: 46 avenue de la Bourdonnais, Paris, 75007, France
Description: Pork butchers who can cook don't grow on trees, especially not in this residential part of the 7th arrondissement (a stone's throw from the Eiffel Tower, no less). The chef-patron appropriates pâté en croûte and terrine to create his "haute couture charcuterie". The interior is unadorned and elegant. The small shop at the restaurant entrance means you can take a piece of this culinary experience home.

Name: Brasserie Lutetia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Tartare of wild sea bass, sole meunière, Burgundy snails with parsley butter: the famous Brasserie Lutetia proudly serves the classics that have made its reputation, as well as some more contemporary creations. Purists and regulars alike can't get enough of the easy-going refined Art Deco atmosphere. Conservatory, mezzanine or patio: take your pick!

Name: L'Atelier d'Olivier Arlot
Description: Set up by Olivier Arlot on the banks of the Loire, L'Atelier is modern both in terms of the decor and the menu. They serve up tasty and savvy creations, such as oxtail terrine and foie gras – a happy combination that melts in the mouth! This is bistronomy at its best, with intriguing and punchy dishes, plus a menu that is renewed very regularly.

Name: Le Clos de la Fontaine
Description: A welcoming rustic-style interior (tablecloths, English crockery), friendly service and skilfully executed cuisine: Stéphane Ollivier and his wife Corinne certainly know how to receive guests. The generous dishes are made with plenty of good local ingredients (eg scallops, oysters, Breton cheeses) and include tasty local specialties, such as roast duck breast strips with cider and tarragon sauce.

Name: L'Épicurieux
Description: This cosy modern bistro with an immaculate white façade is run by former Top Chef contestant Christophe Pirotais and his partner Julie Dieudonné. Food lovers should take this as an invitation to come and taste delicious dishes made with local produce such as dog cockles, mushrooms, olives and black radish, or pollack, pumpkin, yacón and Jerusalem artichoke.

Name: Bistro Gaby
Description: The restaurant’s name and wholesome French country cooking are a tribute to Gaby, who was the chef’s grandmother. Market- and garden-fresh ingredients take pride of place in this attractive homely interior, adorned in soft provençal colours.

Name: Jardin Tropezina
Description: Idyllically set on the legendary Pampelonne beach, this Mediterranean garden-terrace, dominated by wood and plants, lives up to its promise. An exquisite setting overlooking the sea, a luxury interior with silverware and Vallauris tableware, a large number of attentive staff, valet parking on arrival and even DJ nights. Devised by Jean-François Piège, the menu focuses on summer and Provençal dishes, as well as Italian specialities: local tromboncino with a tonnato and parmesan sauce; barbecued fish fillet with tangy sabayon; garden verbena ice cream.

Name: Hostellerie La Cheneaudière
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The dining rooms of this stylish establishment sport a natural, alpine chic vein. The refined repertory offers a concise range of tempting proposals, some of which are so popular they have become signature dishes. This is the case of pink trout of Alsace, fermented vegetables, cream of cumin and whole lobster roasted in charcoal served with a creamy lobster sauce, both of which have been on the menu since 1982.

Name: Le Relais du Castelet
Address: Mas le Castelet, quartier Montmajour, Fontvieille, 13990, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This former hunting lodge surrounded by hilly olive groves is a genuine haven of tranquillity. You can expect deftly crafted, local Provençal recipes, served generously with a distinct preference for veggies and herbs from the garden, supplemented by ingredients from local producers. Ten out of ten for Jean-Baptiste Bert who has added a contemporary chapter to the family property where he was born.

Name: Les Hortensias du Lac
Description: This local institution boasting an idyllic location on the shore of Lake Hossegor extends a charming welcome to its guests. Chef Philippe Moreno, a protégé of Gérald Passedat, serves carefully prepared, high-quality cuisine, with well-executed dishes organised into a seasonal menu and a tasting menu. Fish from Capbreton's fish market and excellent poultry from the Landes area take pride of place. Enjoy your meal in the bright bistro interior, or on the pleasant terrace, in a chic, laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Emporium
Address: 32 boulevard Napoléon, à San Ciprianu, Lecci, 20137, France
Description: Before setting up shop in San Ciprianu, Italian-born chef Sébastien Salamon clocked up stints in some top establishments (Guy Savoy, Le V). The technical brilliance and precise seasoning on display in his spider crab cappelletti, in particular, are testament to this experience. The grilled escalope of foie gras with flaky brioche and cherry tartare is a real treat. With direct links to the terroir (local fish, Bonifacio market gardens, Corsican veal), the short menu features absolutely top-notch contemporary cuisine – to be savoured in the magnificent setting of a spacious, light-filled veranda.

Name: La Table de Romain
Description: This village restaurant with typical local architecture is located in the heart of this market town. It is the HQ of a chef who proposes a set menu at an unbeatable price during the week, and more elaborate dishes at the weekend, when some premium ingredients are deployed. Menu and produce regularly adapted. To enjoy in a chic and convivial interior.

Name: Cassis
Description: This is a chef who has worked in some prestigious establishments and who serves meticulous, tasty, no-frills cuisine made from quality ingredients (meat from the Haute-Loire area, vegetables from a local market gardener). Be sure to try the memorable pâté en croûte or the Bresse chicken in a cream sauce. The lunch menu is great value; in the evening a mystery menu is served.

Name: La Rotonde
Address: Le Negresco, 37 promenade des Anglais, Nice, 06000, France
Description: The rotunda-shaped brasserie of the legendary luxury hotel has resolutely entered the modern world. In this light-filled space (with a terrace), you choose from a menu (designed by Michelin-starred chef Virginie Basselot) that celebrates a flavoursome and colourful cuisine full of Mediterranean flair, with nods to Nice's traditions.

Name: L'alouette
Description: Nicolas Servant, former chef of the Bon Servant, is at the helm of this friendly eatery acclaimed by good food lovers. Splendid range of aged meat and offal (pig’s ears, calf’s liver and sweetbread), spring veggies from the nearby market (white asparagus and chorizo) and desserts to die for (clafouti of seasonal fruit)! A wholesome, casual vibe is perfectly suited to a drink and meal with the mates…

Name: Chinaski
Description: In a decor fitted out with upcycled materials and untreated wood, the owners propose a short and well-curated menu, rustled up in their large open kitchen. By day, enjoy cake in a coffee shop atmosphere; in the evening, the creative bistro takes over: fillet of pollack cooked to perfection, tres leches (milk cake) soaked in whisky for dessert, and excellent natural wines. Plus pancakes for Sunday brunch.

Name: Sources
Description: The meat, fish and vegetables are all meticulously sourced by Sources. Guillaume and Ingrid, who met at the Ferrandi School (Paris), treat us to fresh, bold cuisine with a vegetarian and seafood slant; a market-based set menu at lunchtime, carte blanche for the chef with the five-course dinner menu. Educational resources service nearby.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Description: Located in a handsome mansion, not far from the Chartreuse cellars, this tastefully redecorated brasserie, which boasts a fine wooden staircase leading up to the guestrooms, offers a patriotic line-up of Gallic fare, in which delicacies from Voiron feature prominently, such as cabbage stuffed with venison, free-range poultry with a Chartreuse-flavoured jus or the iced parfait, also perfumed with Chartreuse. Very pleasant welcome and service.

Name: Bec
Address: 55 avenue de la Vallée-des-Baux, Paradou, 13520, France
Description: Set up in an old Provençal farmhouse standing in the shadow of a small church and boasting a pretty courtyard, this restaurant run by a young couple serves fresh modern cuisine with international influences. Lovers of fine food will appreciate the monkfish marinated in satay served with watercress purée – to be savoured in the inviting rustic-style interior or on the delightful terrace clad in laurel trees and Virginia creeper.

Name: Auberge de Crussol
Description: Perched on the heights of Saint-Péray, a stone’s throw from the ruins of Crussol castle, this former sheepfold is now the venue for regional Ardèche cuisine. The meat, fish and vegetables are baked in a wood-fired oven or roasted on a spit. Burger lovers will be in seventh heaven because one of the staff members was voted Burger champion of France in 2019. Warm, welcoming vibe.

Name: Peixes Opéra
Description: Near the town hall and the opera house is Peixes – pronounced "pesh" (i.e. "fish" in Portuguese). In its small bistro interior with white and blue tiles and a very Mediterranean feel, fish and seafood cuisine is served in the form of tapas-style dishes (ceviche, carpaccio, fried fish, cod accras). This is a popular place, and spots on the terrace are hotly contested (no reservations!).

Name: Le Séjour Café
Description: Shelves filled with books, trinkets and plants, paintings and photos on the walls set the scene for what feels like the inviting sitting room of a lovely private mansion. Now let’s add the appeal of market-fresh cuisine, an abundance of culinary delights and a commitment to respecting the seasons, without forgetting the gracious welcome and service.

Name: Vincent Croizard
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: You will need to ring the bell at this discreet townhouse in a narrow street near the Carré d'Art in order to gain access. The self - taught chef composes lovely creative cuisine, striking out and experimenting with at times surprising combinations. His wife is behind the superb selection of wines, which showcases the Languedoc - Roussillon.

Name: Auberge de la Roussille
Address: 30 impasse de la Roussille, St-Liguaire, Niort, 79000, France
Description: One can't help but fall under the spell of this fine lock - keeper's house, which stands in the bucolic setting on the banks of the Sèvre. An enchanting environment, but that doesn't eclipse the main focus, which is the chef's meticulous and well - calibrated cooking. Ingredients are top notch and enhanced without frills. A real pleasure.

Name: Sellae
Description: On the coattails of Mensae ("table" in Latin) in the 19th arrondissement comes Sellae ("chair"). Another restaurant in the Thibault Sombardier stable, it has a bistro-style interior. The chef cooks up modern, seasonal cuisine, with a penchant for the South of France and above all for indulgence! Fine produce is prepared with real know-how: snail ravioli with herb butter; chanterelle and parmesan risotto; and the chef's signature dessert, warm chocolate mousse, vanilla ice cream and fleur de sel crumble...

Name: Maison Drouot
Description: The chef and his wife wanted to break with classic restaurant codes and welcome people into their home, table d'hôte style. The gamble has paid off, with this wonderful place. In the dishes, the lovely contemporary cuisine blends local ingredients with others from further afield. Solicitous service, discreet and friendly. Two nicely decorated guestrooms on the first floor, for those who do not want to get back on the road immediately – and we can understand why they might be reluctant to leave.

Name: Relais Chantovent
Description: A charming country inn in Cathar, where diners and pilgrims alike arrive on foot, eager to do justice to meat dishes that simmer for hours, illustrated by 24-hour low-temperature roast pork, or 20-hour leg of lamb roasted at 70°C. All the ingredients come solely from the surrounding local markets. The terrace with its view over the Briant valley is sumptuous.

Name: Disini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Established in a hotel surrounded by oak trees, this fine dining venue boasts a bright airy dining room and an alfresco area sheltered by foliage. After a dip in the pool, treat yourself to a meal underscored by Asian influences, crafted by a chef who’s something of a fan of molecular gastronomy.

Name: Marcelle - Domaine de Verchant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few minutes outside Montpellier, amid fields and vineyards, a major surprise awaits. This superb hotel and wine estate boasts enchanting surroundings to be contemplated through the bay windows of the dining area. Favouring seasonal produce from the southernmost reaches of France, the chef composes elegant, meticulous dishes that steer clear of bells and whistles. His creations abound with personality and flavour, eg roast saddle of Lozère lamb with artichoke and Collioure anchovies – best enjoyed with one of the estate's wines.

Name: Au Bon Accueil
Description: There are countless examples of these former inns that have been given a facelift by young business partners. In this case the gamble has paid off! A modern bistro interior is the setting for good homemade fare that showcases ingredients fresh from the market. And at such reasonable prices, who could ask for more?

Name: Magma
Description: This two-storey town house is just outside the centre of Caen, not far from the Abbaye-aux-Hommes. Olivier Barbarin, an experienced chef who is no stranger to fine dining, wanted a location and cuisine that are an extension of himself: confident and delicious food, and decor with a nod to his native Auvergne – the purple walls evoke volcanic rock such as pozzolan. Marengo veal ravioli, hake, Anna apples, pumpkin cream: the formule is a very attractively priced lunch deal, and in the evening a tasting menu is revised depending on the market and the mood.

Name: Au Koning Van Peene
Description: In the centre of an out-of-the-way village in the Flanders region, this place is an unexpected foodie haven: chef Kevin Barata and Lucile Prevost (partners in business and in life) welcome travellers into their inviting restaurant with an interior in which brick and wood predominate. The chef, who knows his stuff, whips up good simple dishes, such as lamb kofta, thyme-lemon hummus, barbecue sauce and kataifi, or farmhouse pork chop, cauliflower, horseradish, asparagus and a reduction of cooking juices. Lunch is excellent value.

Name: Dyades au Domaine des Etangs
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant restaurant serves fine, flavoursome cuisine that highlights herbs, flowers, fruit and vegetables from the kitchen garden. To be savoured in the refined, luxurious setting of the château's former stables.

Name: Maison Kieny
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This inviting coaching inn (from 1850) not far from Mulhouse occupies an imposing traditional Alsatian building in the centre of the village. In an elegant dining room, the chef serves seasonal cuisine with a contemporary bent, such as slow-cooked egg with peas and a creamy sauce made with their pods, or lamb cooked two ways, accompanied by chick peas in a French curry. Simpler bistro fare on weekday lunches.

Name: Michel - Brasserie des Catalans
Description: Soak up the atmosphere of Marseille in this popular restaurant on the Plage des Catalans. Here they take their bouillabaisse very seriously... and it tastes phenomenal! As you would expect, the menu proposes an exceptionally fresh catch of the day: you will see the fish in the tanks as you come in.

Name: Aroma
Address: 7 rue du Brandon, Les Herbiers, 85500, France
Description: This modern and colourful restaurant in the town centre is run by a young couple who have plenty of drive. They have created an evolving menu, never departing from the sacrosanct trio of freshness, tastiness and Vendée ingredients.

Name: TO
Description: Just a stone's throw from Canal Saint-Martin, enter this TO – "door" in Japanese – to discover the French-Japanese fusion cuisine of chef Ryo Miyazaki (who previously worked at Saturne). Inside: a series of three modern spaces, each with a distinct atmosphere. Inspired and meticulously presented dishes, in different "omakase" formats.

Name: Fezi
Description: The epitome of a friendly neighbourhood bistro steeped in an irresistible buzzy vibe. Fezi means "home-made" in Brittany's Gallo language. Cédric Bruneau, the young owner-chef, prepares tasty, straightforward, market-fresh cuisine, favouring regional ingredients. We tasted a carpaccio of wrasses (fish), beetroot, smoked cream and fingered citron; skate wing, mashed squash, cream of mussels; lemon curd, shortbread, steamed meringue and dried lime. Natural and biodynamic wines.

Name: Le 4
Description: The young couple at the head of this dinky establishment in the heart of Mulhouse rustles up a concise menu of enticingly entitled dishes. The food is colourful, inventive and scattered with Mediterranean notes: “our version” of vitello tonnato; gilt-head seabream, spaghetti alle vongole and an emulsion of cockles; tagliata of beef, baby potatoes, rocket salad, Kalamata olives and shavings of parmesan. Enticing wine list.

Name: Le Moulin Babet
Description: "The only neighbours of this old stone - built watermill (19C) are the greenery and the Surmelin, an affluent of the Marne. The interior decor is on the modern, pared - down side, with a light wood ceiling and designer chairs; the traditional cuisine smacks of all things bucolic. And in the guestrooms, you could hear a pin drop. "

Name: La Lanterne
Address: 17 place de la Chambre, Metz, 57000, France
Description: La Lanterne is inspired by "La Lanterne du Bon Dieu", the nickname given to Metz Cathedral, which looms over the restaurant. It is run by a young couple who really give it their all: chef Célia Bertrand, originally from Metz, and Romain Bouchesèche, from the Jura, who takes care of matters in the dining room and in the wine cellar. They propose modern cuisine (pollack, morels, vin jaune) that draws inspiration from the Jura, where they met.

Name: Alleudium
Description: Keiichi Shinohara, a Japanese chef with solid credentials (including a stint at Le Violon d'Ingres during the Christian Constant era), is at the helm of this restaurant with refined contemporary decor. Customer satisfaction is the goal here, in particular when it comes to the food, which is modern and inspired, with the odd nod to Japan.

Name: Au Vieux Pressoir
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the Lac d'Orient road, this half-timbered house, typical of the Champagne Humide region, offers house specialities that juggle with tradition: salad of prawns with fennel and baby spinach, brill and beurre blanc sauce with champagne, chocolate sphere packed with berries. There are also comfortable guestrooms, a pleasant spa area and a bistro in an adjoining building. "Maison Gublin" is doing well.

Name: Le Parc
Description: In the heart of the Parc Micaud, on the banks of the River Doubs, this glass, concrete and steel pavilion is the Modernist work of Besançon architect Michel Demenge. The chic, contemporary interior, with its open-plan kitchen, also offers a view of the river. Dishes are in a contemporary vein, the menu under the supervision of the chef of nearby Château de Germigney.

Name: L'Entre-Roches
Description: In the heart of the self-proclaimed "Republic of Saugeais" on the Swiss border, the proprietors are as meticulous about their spruce and contemporary premises as they are about the food they serve. The chef proposes delicious, indulgent cuisine such as his medley of Haut-Jura trout served with polenta combined with Mont d'Or cheese, or chicken ballotine with Comté and Iberian ham. It is worth mentioning the exceptionally warm and friendly service.

Name: Le Clos des Oliviers
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Taste, simplicity, skilful use of quality ingredients: here, you can enjoy good food without unnecessary complications – and what a real pleasure! The wine list is put together with the neighbouring cellarman. In summer, make the most of the terrace in the shade of the reed screening.

Name: Le Délice des Papilles
Description: In a comfortable, spacious setting that can accommodate groups, chef Florian Bessede has been serving traditional cuisine for the last 15 years: duck foie gras terrine "like grandma used to make it"; loin of wild hake à la plancha; yuzu meringue mandarin tartlet. There are six guestrooms upstairs and a large terrace. Fun fact: some scenes from The Old Gun starring Romy Schneider were shot here.

Name: Le Cèpe
Description: It all starts with fine produce from the local land, mountain porcini or fish from the neighbouring lakes, which the chef comes out and proudly present to diners. He then turns it into delightful, fresh dishes, all the tastier for the unbeatable prices. A place that is quite simply comfortable in its own skin.

Name: L'Escapade Marseillaise
Description: A soft grey colour scheme, light wood, pretty lighting and trendy furniture: the interior invites you to take a break in this neighbourhood restaurant frequented by regulars. Chef Yannick Stein rolls out recipes that capture the zeitgeist, such as royale of mushrooms (think butter, cream and almost mashed mushrooms), velvety parsnips, topped with crunchy cereals... When the weather is fine, make a beeline for the vast upstairs terrace at the rear of the building.

Name: Gusto Caffe
Description: In front of the Canal Baussengue marina, a picturesque trattoria where waiters and clients call to each other in a cheerful and distinctly Italian atmosphere! Homemade fare (spaghetti, gnocchi etc), Parma prosciutto cut with the slicer, and the great Italian classics. The terrace is taken by storm in fine weather, as is the lunchtime chalkboard menu, excellent value for money.

Name: Le Bréard
Description: A contemporary setting and subtle cuisine are on the menu at this restaurant on a narrow cobbled street near the church (Église St Catherine). Tempura oysters, aubergine caviar, a shallot and dill sauce; cod, rainbow carrots, rhubarb beurre blanc sauce; passion fruit soufflé, vanilla ice cream... Offering a choice of three tasting menus, the chef allies fine flavours with creativity and generosity!

Name: La Luciole
Address: 3 place de la République, Luc-sur-Orbieu, 11200, France
Description: The chef fulfilled a childhood dream when he bought this cafe on the small village square. A passionate self-taught chef, he works hand in hand with his daughter, concocting simple, tasty dishes that do justice to fine local produce: rabbit and maki of haddock; plancha-grilled veal steak, chimichurri sauce; rum baba and pina colada sorbet. Served on the terrace, in the shade of a centennial tree.

Name: Chai nous comme Chai vous
Address: 1 rue de la Garde, La Flotte, 17630, France
Description: Friendly and attractive, this pocket handkerchief restaurant instantly makes you feel at home. The concise, appetising menu showcases island produce with a weakness for seafood, illustrated by the flawlessly cooked monkfish, flanked by a chardonnay-flavoured sabayon and white asparagus. Intelligently curated wine list, the occasional inventive note and a scattering of thoughtful attentions.

Name: Le 703
Description: Navigating between France and Japan, chef Naomi Ogaki trained in Alsace and Provence, under the tutelage of Antoine Westermann and Christian Étienne respectively. In his lovely bistro complete with a long counter, he serves high-quality traditional French cuisine that draws on influences of Alsace in autumn and winter, and of the South of France in spring and summer. House classics include pâté en croûte, game, spaetzle, home-made boudin, fish aioli – not to mention some first-rate classic desserts.

Name: Ardent
Address: Loire Valley Lodges, 1 allée de la Duporterie, Esvres-sur-Indre, 37320, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the midst of sprawling private woodland, where lodges on stilts and contemporary art blend in with the trees, a restored farmstead gradually comes into view, appointed in a full-blown arty and sylvan theme. Serenity is the watchword of this establishment, which uses only top-quality ingredients in carefully crafted recipes that scrupulously respect the seasons in a single set menu that can be ordered in a choice of courses. The establishment’s kitchen garden and the harvest of wild plant foraging forays feature prominently in the gastronomic lineup.

Name: Nolinski
Description: On Avenue de l'Opéra, near the Comédie Française, a chic brasserie with a retro setting (incorporating Art Deco and the 1970s, with mirrors, gilding, yellow marble and corduroy). As for the food, chef Philip Chronopoulos, who earned two stars at the Palais Royal Restaurant, creates cuisine with global influences (tacos, ceviche, carpaccio, veal Milanese and fillet of beef flambéed with cognac).

Name: Bistrot du Bac
Address: 19 rue du Bac, à Sainte-Marine, Combrit, 29120, France
Description: This Breton restaurant is located on the quayside of Sainte-Marine's little port, facing Bénodet – to which there is a ferry link in season. The terrace affords picturesque views over the River Odet estuary, the dining area is painted blue and white (as are the guestrooms) and, most importantly, the food celebrates the sea, with fresh and simple dishes (special mention for the sole). A very pleasant port of call.

Name: Osmossi
Description: One of the restaurants of Andreas Mavrommatis, maestro of Mediterranean food in Paris. In a contemporary bistro-style interior, decorated with photos from Nikos Aliagas' collection, diners enjoy meze, pan-fried octopus with fava from Santorini or soudjoukakia (beef meatballs with tomato and cumin). It's fresh and tasty. Delicatessen and wine shop.

Name: Ermitage de Corton
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In this house set in vineyards opposite Corton “mountain”, the chef aims to shine the spotlight on local producers. His modern meticulous cuisine draws upon his classical training and features a traditional Gallic line-up, including snails and œufs en meurette (poached eggs in red wine) crafted with text-book precision. Stylish interior, inviting patio and spacious guestrooms to prolong your stay.

Name: Coretta
Description: In the new Clichy - Batignolles quarter, opposite the Parc Martin Luther King (King's wife was called Coretta), this restaurant aims to be eco - responsible. Designer decor with lots of oak, a view of the treetops from the first floor and fine cuisine made using quality ingredients by an enthusiastic young team. A real taste of nature!

Name: Le Bistrot du Bord de l'Eau
Address: Hostellerie de Levernois, rue du Golf, Levernois, 21200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A delightful rustic dining room with exposed stonework, beams and a fireplace serves as the setting for the traditional, regional cuisine served in this restaurant. Enjoy mouthwatering dishes such as Meurette - style eggs (in a red wine sauce), belly of pork and blanquette of veal.

Name: La Causerie
Description: Two young associates from Le Royal Monceau preside over the destiny of this famous institution in the neighbourhood of La Muette. The chef revisits tradition here, injecting plenty of freshness, through a menu as straightforward as it is tasty; as for the decoration, it has a pleasant retro side: large mirror, ceramic fresco, Sarreguemines pottery etc. Attentive service.

Name: Pouliche
Description: In this friendly neo-bistro, Amandine Chaignot fetes market produce, spontaneity and creativity, without ever betraying the flavours of her carefully selected ingredients. Indeed, that is the approach that has informed her single set menu: only the main course is chosen by the guest – meat, fish or vegetarian – with the rest of the meal left to the chef's discretion. On Wednesdays, the set menu is entirely vegetarian. On Sundays, you can enjoy traditional family-style chicken dishes. Good value for money at lunchtime. Pouliche will steal your heart.

Name: Le Saint-Sébastien
Description: It's an enticing offer in this neighbourhood bar turned into a hub of bistronomie cooking: a short menu that respects the seasons, very vegetable oriented, a judicious choice of seasonings, masterful use of herbs and spices to add character to the dishes… not to mention good natural wines. Spot on.

Name: Siamsa
Address: 13 rue de la Pierre-Levée, Paris, 75011, France
Description: Siamsa, a strange name that conjures up the kingdom of Siam and Thai cooking, but where you will in fact taste good, updated Gallic cuisine, made with fresh, balanced ingredients (ceviche of sea bream with raspberries and crunchy vegetables; smoked pork belly, apricots, chili, etc. ). Siamsa is actually Gaelic and means to “entertain” in a passing nod to one of the partners (Simon Cuddy). A great neighbourhood bistro. The lunch menu is a steal!

Name: La Yole de Chris
Address: Plage de la Concurrence, La Rochelle, 17000, France
Description: This dazzling place by Christopher Coutanceau offers two incomparable pleasures: for the eyes and for the taste buds. A long counter in the shape of a skiff (light, long and narrow boat), houses the open kitchen, where the cooks can be seen in action. Seafood (oysters and shellfish) and fish of the day enjoy pride of place on the menu here... to be enjoyed on the terrace that overlooks the sea, in fine weather. Booking recommended.

Name: Colibri
Address: 14 rue de la Mittrie, Dinan, 22100, France
Description: In the old town of Dinan, a contemporary bistro: pale wood, oak parquet flooring, fireplace and open kitchen visible to diners. The chef, who is originally from Bali and whose travels have taken him all over the world, lets these experiences inform his dishes: chorba, chickpeas, lamb ravioli... His recipes are inspired by cuisines the world over: a perfect antidote to lockdown!

Name: Fleur de Neige
Description: Duck pâté en croûte with foie gras, calf's head with ravigote, pavlova with bilberries: this tasty and hearty traditional cuisine is served in a family atmosphere and – in summer – on the lovely panoramic terrace, with a view of the Chablais mountains.

Name: Brasserie Brunet
Address: 10 rue de la Poste, Annecy, 74000, France
Description: At this restaurant a stone's throw from the train station, you receive a warm welcome in a British-style decor with exposed stonework, wood panelling and moleskin-clad banquettes. "Brunet" pâté en croûte; black pudding with onions, apple and lamb's lettuce salad; calf's liver and spelt risotto – an avalanche of delicious dishes served in a relaxed atmosphere by a smiling team in black attire and leather aprons. A pleasant terrace for sunny days.

Name: Préambule
Description: The chef, a local man, has come back home after clocking up some excellent experiences elsewhere in France. He prepares honest bistronomy dishes: poultry mousseline, herb biscuit and vegetable pickles; veal blanquette, crispy rice and thyme-lemon cream; baked apple douillon, tonka bean ice cream. There are two dining spaces to choose between: the first is a traditional bistro-style setting; the second is contemporary and cosier, with access to the terrace.

Name: Ore
Description: Ore means "mouth" in Latin. A disarmingly simple name for this place that is quite simply exceptional – a 17C pavilion within the Palace of Versailles. Alain Ducasse is the Sun King of the premises, enforcing the culinary law for which he is known. That of naturality and a constantly renewed homage to fine ingredients.

Name: Cap de Castel
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the pleasant terrace, with the Pyrenees in the distance and the Montagne Noire in the foreground, you can sample modern cuisine with traditional touches; the dishes beautifully highlight local produce: plenty to ensure an enjoyable mealtime.

Name: Le Millénaire
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Near Place Royale and the cathedral, this local culinary landmark has been treated to a contemporary makeover. It provides a perfect playground for two veteran fine food lovers: Benjamin Andreux, in the kitchen, and Delphin Cornaille, brilliantly in charge of the front of house. The chef unveils his ambitious vision of fine dining in which seafood features prominently: sautéed girolle mushrooms, apricots and elderflower; monkfish meunière, green peas, cherries and sauce Dugléré; Racan pigeon, a quenelle of puréed onion and a drizzled sauce. The epitome of intelligent creativity. Diners are greeted warmly and seamlessly, in line with the culture of its high-flying, experienced team.

Name: Le Foch
Description: In this restaurant situated on the famous Promenades, chef Jacky Louazé has earned himself a loyal following. Diners come to enjoy a menu showcasing premium ingredients, particularly fish and shellfish: blue lobster, spicy cereals, citrus fruit; whole sea bass cooked in a Vallauris clay crust; turbot in semi-salted butter, Noirmoutier potatoes.

Name: L'Estrade
Description: Located in the centre of the spa town, this restaurant serves delicious cuisine that oscillates between tradition and modernity, while remaining open to creativity. The chef uses local and seasonal ingredients: white asparagus, mimosa condiment and a mousseline sauce with sweet spices; veal with morel mushrooms and grilled shallot confit… Service with a smile.

Name: Le Bœuf en Écailles
Description: Authenticity is a word so often used as to be almost meaningless, but it is nonetheless the right term for the gutsy, flavoursome food of this establishment. The meat and fish recipes are steeped in generous mouth-watering flavours, such as 16-hour roast pork with mashed potato in olive oil. The lovely patio on the banks of the Sèvre Niortaise is also authentic.

Name: Ar Iniz
Description: The restaurant's menu is designed by chef Christian Le Squer. The cooking techniques are spot on, and the top-notch ingredients are expertly prepared, resulting in flavoursome dishes: delicate langoustine ravioli, beurre blanc with chives; Hereford rib steak, home fries; cheesecake-style crème brûlée. The bright, modern setting boasts an exceptional view of the beach, Plage du Sillon. In fine weather, the terrace is a must! A bargain set lunch menu is up for grabs on weekdays.

Name: L'Hippocampe
Description: In his restaurant near the Parc des Sources, chef Gilles Ruyet prepares seafood dishes in a traditional vein: sole meunière, seared halibut with a beurre blanc sauce, not forgetting the crystallised orange soufflé with Grand Marnier – prepared by his daughter Marianne, who is also to be seen on the restaurant floor. Attractive contemporary decor, plus a view of the kitchen and the lobster tank.

Name: La Maison Tourangelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Rustic meets modern in this 18C Touraine building. It boasts a delightful terrace on the Cher and fine cuisine using quality ingredients.

Name: Les Closeaux
Description: Under the Ancien Régime, Les Closeaux – set in a 10ha estate – was used as a hunting lodge by the kings of France. Nowadays, this farmhouse inn remains as secluded as ever in a bucolic setting surrounded by greenery. The chef, who champions local producers and is a proponent of short supply chains, creates delicious market-fresh cuisine at affordable prices: loin of saithe, green beans, black rice, tomato, parsley and shallot; apricot and peach puff pastry, apricot ice cream. Lovely terrace.

Name: Le M - Château de Massillan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This beautiful 16C castle stands in extensive grounds surrounded by vineyards. The food aims to enhance the estate’s organic cottage garden and orchard produce. You can wash down your meal with a biodynamic wine from the Domaine de la Guicharde, which also produces the olive oil used in the kitchen. Slick, smiling service. In summer, take a seat in the courtyard adorned with a fountain, overlooking the garden.

Name: Campagne, Vignes et Gourmandises
Description: With its atmosphere blending rustic charm (exposed stones, painted wooden furniture) and modern touches (contemporary paintings), this restaurant has bags of character.
