From the terrace overlooking the grounds and lavender fields or in the cosy dining room with its vaulted ceiling and a fire crackling in the hearth, get ready to embark on a poetic culinary voyage inspired by regional delicacies. Thanks to chefs Kévin Vaubourg and Lucille Routin, the castle boasts a knockout fine dining option. Each dish is carefully thought out and crafted to allow the ingredients to shout their name, depicted by an incredibly delicate tomato or locally reared lamb prepared in two ways and underscored by a chervil jus and olive seasoning. Delightful welcome. Book one of the lovely rooms and stay longer.

Name: Le Panoramic
Address: Glacier de la Grande-Motte, Tignes, 73320, France
Description: Accessed by a funicular railway, this high-altitude restaurant (elevation: 3 032m!) promises a breath of fresh air as well as fine dining. In an inviting interior that is done out in wood, staff in traditional costume serve up authentic and delicious wood-fired dishes, including choice cuts of meat and fish to share (eg rib steak, pork shoulder and whole turbot). A delightful change of scene.

Name: Les Enfants Rouges
Description: Once upon a time, a Japanese chef, fresh from his apprenticeship with Yves Camdeborde and Stéphane Jégo, opened a characteristic Parisian bistro, serving heart-warming market-fresh Gallic fare. Duck terrine in aspic paired with plum and cucumber pickles; tempura of line-caught croaker with a seaweed dashi stock, cabbage and broad beans; baba with vintage Martinique rum and chantilly cream… And the icing on the cake, it's open at weekends.

Name: Amarante
Description: This bistro wedged between Bastille and Lyon railway station serves a bighearted, no-nonsense score rich in nostalgic flavours. The ingredients, such as ‘triple zero’ jumbo shrimps from Nantes, Kintoa pork or monkfish caught by small fishing boats, are allowed to shout their name. The interior is equally simple and authentic: tiled floor, red imitation leather benches and wooden tables. Bags of substance and atmosphere!

Name: Towa
Description: Japanese chef Shin Okusa is at the helm of the Towa, close to the bustling Aligre market. A champion of old-school French culinary traditions and a true disciple of Escoffier, he not only whisks up the great classics (French lamb stew, breast of duck in flaky pastry), but also sauces, hot terrines and pies, with superlative skill and flair.

Name: Montée
Description: This is what you get when a talented Japanese chef decides to share his love of French cuisine: graphic presentation of the food and solid technical skill. The stripped-back designer decor adds to the experience.

Name: Le Bistro du Clos
Description: Whether outdoors, in the shade of hackberry trees or indoors, in the bistro dotted with old knickknacks, you will inevitably find yourself surrounded by an enthusiastic crowd of faithful regulars. The chef ticks all the boxes in his open kitchen. A talented craftsman, he curates generous, seasonal dishes from fresh, premium ingredients in a Provençal register that hits the spot every time: chuck beef stew, braised vegetables, fresh tomato vinaigrette or red fruit pannacotta. The establishment is located in the left wing of the Maison des Terroirs, aptly devoted to promoting regional produce.

Name: Bistrotters
Description: A lovely place in the southern reaches of the 14th arrondissement near Métro Plaisance. The Spanish chef carefully selects his ingredients, with a preference for small-scale producers in the Paris region, and instils them with various influences (Asian, Mediterranean etc). Laid-back service.

Name: Au Fil des Saisons
Address: 3 rue de la Libération, Étupes, 25460, France
Description: Stéphane and Fabienne Robinne’s establishment is home to a cleverly refurbished interior, depicted by untreated wooden tables and velvet upholstered chairs… A refreshing modern vibe that provides the backdrop to the chef’s signature recipes oozing in traditional accents.

Name: Auberge des Ruines
Address: 17 place de la Mairie, Jumièges, 76480, France
Description: In this pretty half-timbered house just opposite the ruins of the abbey, a friendly green-fingered chef showcases his passion for the riches of Normandy's terroir. Following the seasons, he fêtes ingredients such as trout, beef and lamb, ciders and Calvados, goat's and cow's cheeses. Everything comes from Normandy, not least the fruit and vegetables picked in the restaurant's kitchen garden – the chef does his own planting. With the greens and pastures of Normandy on his doorstep, he composes the magnificent cheese trolley using produce from neighbouring farms. Savour in an inviting and chic contemporary interior, or in the glass-paned extension giving onto the terrace.

Name: L'Arpège
Description: This pair of Japanese chefs cook lovely creative, Japanese - inflected cuisine, in which broths, seaweed and seasonings show off good - quality ingredients. The interior, in keeping with the presentation on the plates, is elegant and contemporary.

Name: L'Agrume
Description: In the open kitchen of this bistro, the chef delicately crafts refreshingly wholesome dishes, such as poultry in vin jaune paired with asparagus or a piece of roast turbot with mashed potatoes and poultry jus. Flawlessly fresh produce is the name of the game (the fish comes from Brittany and the fruit and vegetables from the very best suppliers). Tasting menu in the evening.

Name: Liza
Address: 14 rue de la Banque, Paris, 75002, France
Description: Originally from Beirut, Liza Asseily gives pride of place to her country’s cuisine. In a contemporary interior dotted with Middle Eastern touches, opt for the shish taouk or mechoui kafta (lamb, hummus and tomato preserves). Dishes are meticulously prepared using fresh ingredients. A real treat!

Name: Auberge du Paradis
Description: Two restaurants in one! Dishes to share and a concise menu set the scene at Lucienne (shrimp cooked over hot stones, tataki of tandoori beef, tempura of baby carrots), while Joséphine à Table offers a wine bar with traditional starters and a dish of the day (marbled ham, pork pie, chicken skewers, rice pudding). Brunch on Saturdays. Both establishments boast a pleasant patio and a friendly vibe – all of which washed down with tipples from Mâcon and Beaujolais.

Name: L'Initial
Description: This Japanese chef with a brilliant track record proposes French cuisine that demonstrates remarkable precision and is made with fine produce (sea bass, scallops, langoustine, morel mushrooms) and represents good value for money. The roast rack of Lozère lamb, celeriac purée, lemon condiment and reduced lamb jus was a stand-out dish. Highly attentive service and a refined and light-filled setting.

Name: Le Mazenay
Description: The emphasis here is on good cooking technique, the right jus and fine produce. There is no unnecessary fuss when you feast on wild snails with herbs or a poached farm-reared chicken. But the chef hankers after just one thing – the start of game season! Roasted Scottish grouse, hare à la royale. A place for bon viveurs.

Name: ERH
Description: The initials E, R and H stand for water, rice and men in French (eau, riz, hommes): a mysterious and poetic name for this unusual place that shares its premises with a sake shop and a whisky bar. The Japanese chef delivers lovely French cuisine that is full of flavour and has a distinctly Japanese feel to it; he also takes some rather original detours in his creations. You might like to opt for food and sake pairings. The remarkable contemporary space has a large glass roof and a long counter that stretches out in front of the open kitchen, where, as in Japan, the chef officiates.

Name: Anicia, table nature
Description: Hailing from the Haute-Loire area, François Gagnaire carefully selects small-scale farmers from the vicinity, kitting himself out with excellent raw material for his cooking. Puy lentils, Limousine des Monts-du-Velay beef, Mézenc fin gras beef, Artisous farmhouse cheese, Vellavia beer… His dishes are both delicious and beautifully presented, making a meal here a real treat; the lunch menu is a real bargain in this neighbourhood. Afternoon tea is served, plus a more fine dining menu in the evening.

Name: Étude
Description: Inspired by his encounters with small-scale producers, chef Keisuke Yamagishi, who hails from the rural province of Nagano, Japan, serves surprise menus based on seasonal ingredients. In a minimalist setting (the overhead lighting is by Serge Mouille), the chef treats us to his creative outlook, his refined vision of plating and his passion for Burgundy wines, in particular.

Name: La Laiterie
Address: 138 avenue de l'Hippodrome, à Lambersart, Lille, 59000, France
Description: Grandson of dairy farmers and son of restaurant owners, chef Édouard Chouteau, who trained with the likes of Pierre Gagnaire, Alain Passard and Christophe Pelé, has settled in this historic cottage, a former dairy farm (yes, really!), next-door to Citadelle Park and a stone’s throw from the banks of the Deûle. The tastefully appointed dining rooms open onto a huge garden and a patio. The perfect foil for the chef’s creative score, which delves freely into produce from Northern France with a fondness for surf and turf recipes.

Name: GrandCœur
Description: Take a seat in the warm and welcoming interior (with exposed beams and stonework, marble table tops and velvet banquettes), or on the pleasant terrace in the picturesque cobbled courtyard of the Marais Dance Centre. In the hands of Mauro Colagreco, traditional French cuisine comes with an international twist… We are fans of the Wagyu cecina, which cannot fail to win you over, and the veal cutlet alla milanese with its wonderful Bearnaise sauce.

Name: 24 - Le Restaurant
Description: In a quiet street just a stone's throw from the Champs-Elysées, this establishment offers well-crafted, pedigree Gallic cuisine with an occasional personal spin, such as breast of Dombes duckling, chutney of yellow peaches, pine nuts and duckling jus underscored by mulled wine. Cheerful and professional welcome in a stylish setting.

Name: Méson Chalut
Address: 8 rue de la Corne-de-Cerf, Saint-Malo, 35400, France
Description: In his "méson" (which means "house" in Gallo, the language of Upper Brittany), the chef-owner goes all out Breton, showcasing seafood and other regional ingredients (buckwheat, lait ribot (Breton buttermilk), Coco de Paimpol beans, salted butter) that he sources locally. Freshness, flavour and a respect for nature.

Name: Atelier Maître Albert
Description: An attractive medieval fireplace and roasting spits take pride of place in this handsome interior designed by J.-M. Wilmotte. Guy Savoy signs the menu which boasts a knockout cast of first-class ingredients. T-bone steak, free-range poultry, spit-roasted suckling lamb chops and leg – all that remains is to choose your side dish, for example, gratin dauphinois or purée, both crafted with text-book precision.

Name: Kitchen Ter(re)
Description: In his third establishment devoted to pasta, William Ledeuil crafts a kaleidoscope of pared-back tastes and flavours, starring high-flying creations from spelt, durum wheat, einkorn or tender Roussillon wheat by artisan Roland Feuillas. Chef Julien Jéquier (with stints at Le V and L’Écrin) orchestrates a balanced score in which Asian notes and fresh herbs play major supporting roles. From the exquisitely laid tables to the plating, balance is the key word, as is illustrated by his dish of coquillettes (small pasta shells) made out of fresh milled khorasan wheat flour with chicken wings, Taggiasche olives, spinach and Thai broth! Vibrant, lively and the epitome of charming!

Name: Belle Maison
Description: The three associates of Pantruche and Caillebotte are behind the wheel of this Belle Maison, named after a beach on the Island of Yeu where they used to spend their holidays. The chef rustles up seafood-inspired dishes with disconcerting expertise: crab cannelloni, tom kha gai sauce, black garlic and smoked herring eggs…

Name: Elmer
Description: Close to République, this terribly chic bistro is officiated by a chef with an impressive career (including L'Oustau de Baumanière, Pierre Gagnaire, travels in Asia and Latin America). He composes a flavoursome menu that packs a punch, with fine meats cooked on embers or on the rotisserie.

Name: À La Biche au Bois
Description: In an atmospheric interior reminiscent of historic Parisian bistros and two minutes from Lyon railway station, regulars and travellers rub shoulders as they dig into traditional no-nonsense nosh. Country terrines, Burgundy snails and Royan ravioles star alongside duck breast in honey, fillet of beef served with cèpes and foie gras or coq au vin (the house specialty), without forgetting game in season (venison and even Scottish grouse!). The crème caramel to finish is wickedly addictive…

Name: Mamagoto
Description: Mamagoto is Japanese for tea party. Seasoned chef Koji Tsuchiya serves an appealing selection of dishes you can share (or not!), combining Japanese and Basque influences – for example, sea urchin with parsley sayon or grilled squid with pesto. The wine list includes some unusual natural wines. A simpler set menu at lunchtime.

Name: Semilla
Description: In a street teeming with restaurants and art galleries, Semilla ("seed" in Spanish) is a bistro with an exceptionally friendly atmosphere and trendy, industrial-style decor. In the kitchen, which opens directly onto the restaurant floor, a young and enthusiastic team work exclusively with fresh, selected produce: sea bream ceviche, leche de tigre, quince confit with hibiscus and kohlrabi; roasted cod, Granville cockles, Roscoff onion, Poiré sauce. Delicious and brilliantly done!

Name: Les Toquées by Benoît Bernard
Description: "At the helm of this restaurant on the banks of the Deule, chef Benoît Bernard officiates, back home after six years abroad (including in Madagascar). The short menu comprises cuisine with a solid classical foundation and evocative titles: lobster, vin jaune sauce and morels; sea bass, ginger and samphire. "

Name: Caffè Stern
Description: On Passage des Panoramas, the historical Graveur Stern engraving workshop has been turned into this smart trattoria, while retaining its period cachet (carvings, photos and original wood panelling). The menu features well-crafted and decidedly original Italian cuisine, served in generous portions: seasonal risotto; dill tagliolini with spider crab, clams and black olive sauce; "Stern" pistachio ice cream. Service with a smile.

Name: L'Atelier Bistrot
Description: This adorable stone house, home to an inviting bistro inn, is five minutes from the peaceful Brittany village of Guéméné-sur-Scorff. This rural idyll is in the capable hands of an enthusiastic young couple who expertly rustles up market-fresh menus that shine the spotlight on small local producers and artisans. Simple, down-to-earth lunchtime menu; more elaborate offering in the evening.

Name: Winstub Arnold
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Dive headlong into Alsace traditions at this winstub featuring numerous elsässische Spezialitäten, including kougelhopf, sauerkraut, black pudding, apple purée, baeckeoffe hotpot or specials such as "Marie Leczinsca vol-au-vent"… Choose a wine from the family estate to accompany your food, then sit back and enjoy in a setting that couldn't be more characteristic of the region.

Name: Les Flots
Address: 52 boulevard de la Mer, Châtelaillon-Plage, 17340, France
Description: This picturesque 19C blue and white house stands on the boulevard that skirts the immense beach. Take a seat in a contemporary dining room overlooking the sea and dig into beautifully presented super-fresh fish and shellfish platters, the establishment’s pride and joy. Guaranteed to find favour with seafood lovers!

Name: Les Terrasses de Clairefontaine
Description: In the heart of the Chevreuse Valley and Rambouillet forest, this restaurant on the edge of Clairefontaine pond serves heart - warming, up - to - date food, with a weakness for truffles and game (in season). Fine view of the pond (all year long).

Name: La Tour
Address: Place de la République, Châtillon-sur-Chalaronne, 01400, France
Description: In the centre of this pleasant little town, behind a handsome half-timbered façade, the charming interior of this restaurant lies somewhere between rustic and baroque with its abundance of trinkets. The menu, inspired by the traditions of the Dombes area, is packed with treats, such as creamy pike and crayfish fondant or Dombes poultry with cream. Pleasant guestrooms.

Name: Zorn - La Petite Auberge
Description: Low-temperature poached egg, cream of parsnip, mushrooms and shallots; guinea fowl, cabbage, rosemary jus; jellied strawberries, meringue, strawberry sorbet… The “carte blanche” menu of seasoned chef, Willy-Marc Zorn, at the helm of this eatery near Laon station, highlights market-fresh ingredients. Fine wine list. On the spot every time!

Name: Les Gourmands Disent
Description: In Île St-Laurent's "restaurant street", an enthusiastic double act (Laurent is in charge of savoury dishes, while Nadine handles the desserts) has breathed new life into this engaging eatery. Bare stone walls and high coffered French ceilings set the scene for well-crafted dishes, before perusing the knockout selection of trompe-l’œil desserts, such as the chocolate Montecristo. Do as the regulars do: book well in advance.

Name: Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle
Address: 10 place du Général-de-Gaulle, La Celle, 83170, France
Description: Near Celle Abbey, this remote fine dining inn occupies a stunning 18C edifice. Part of the Ducasse Group, the restaurant boasts all the facilities one would expect of a luxury establishment, including a finely crafted Mediterranean score with a soft spot for veg, illustrated by stuffed Provençal vegetables overflowing with herbs and garlic. Unostentatious tradition.

Name: Auberge du Prunelli
Description: A cosy, inviting atmosphere reigns in this restaurant that first welcomed guests in 1860 in its former life as a coaching inn. It's been a family affair since 1997, when father André Orlandazzi bought the place – today his sons have taken over the reins. Charcuterie, cheeses and honey from the valley, vegetables from the garden, simple dishes simmered for hours on the stove, tarts made with fruit from the orchard, over 200 Corsican wines... Timeless! In fine weather, you might like to take advantage of the large terrace surrounded by greenery overlooking the Prunelli.

Name: La Garenne
Address: Le Dracy, 4 rue du Pressoir, Dracy-le-Fort, 71640, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An appealing place where you can enjoy, for example, melt-in-the-mouth salmon gravelax with a creamy carrot purée and potato espuma, and, for dessert, chou au craquelin, lemon yuzu mousse and citrus fruit flavours. The low-key decor incorporates some pretty prints of artwork by Alain Thomas, and the veranda overlooks the terrace and grounds. The hotel, meanwhile, boasts pleasant guestrooms, a swimming pool and a spa.

Name: Le Quai 21
Address: 15 quai de la Poissonnerie, Colmar, 68000, France
Description: Head down to the docks of Little Venice for a fine dining experience, courtesy of Le Quai 21 and its expertly prepared contemporary cuisine, eg fillet of German sashi beef accompanied by chanterelles, onions, cherry tomatoes and parmesan. The inviting dining area on the first floor is complemented by a pleasant patio terrace. Chic bistro vibe on the ground floor.

Name: Auberge du Pont de Rethondes
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The pretty traditional façade epitomises the charm of this village on the banks of the Aisne. Inside is a modern and refined dining room, perfect for enjoying a meal put together by an imaginative chef with good seasonal ingredients at his disposal. Garden terrace.

Name: La Corniche
Address: 1 chemin di u Fornu (Hameau de Castagneto), San-Martino-di-Lota, 20200, France
Description: A family business clinging to the mountain with a splendid terrace shaded by plane trees overlooking the sea... Exquisite plating, delicious flavours with notes of Corsican saffron and confit of citron, twice-cooked mouth-watering veal or the decadent vacherin dessert perfumed with the one and only Madagascan vanilla, all of which washed down with locally grown vintages.

Name: Les Oliviers
Address: Hôtel Île Rousse, 25 boulevard Louis-Lumière, Bandol, 83150, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In Renécros Bay, this posh, stylish, fashionable restaurant commands a breathtaking view of the Mediterranean. Open for dinner (only!), Martin and Fleur craft colourful, flavoursome Mediterranean and Provençal cuisine, presented in several tasting menus, starring ingredients such as green asparagus from Mallemort, line-caught fish direct from local boats, strawberries from Hyères… As you might expect, the vision of the sun gently setting over the glittering horizon is truly spectacular!

Name: Le Carré des Saveurs
Description: In the charming, peaceful setting of this former silkworm farm, surrounded by vineyards and olive groves, dine in the resolutely contemporary interior or on the pleasant terrace in a pretty courtyard. The cuisine draws inspiration from the terroir and tradition to showcase local ingredients: aubergine caviar with extra virgin olive oil; delicious daube provençale (beef stew); pistachio financier and vanilla mousseline. As an added bonus, you can taste the wines and olive oil produced right here on the estate. Spacious contemporary guestrooms and a sense of serenity.

Name: Smørrebrød
Description: Modernity is the key word, from the Scandinavian decor to the food, which highlights veggies and premium seasonal ingredients (arancini of green peas, creamy green peas in mint; Monts d’Aubrac trout baked at a low temperature, Planèze blond dried peas, miso and beurre blanc…), washed down with a fine selection of wines. Small terrace on the street.

Name: Kapara
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In their new venue, Kapara, whose interior is almost identical to that of the former Balagan, Assaf Granit and his partner Tomer Lanzman have called upon chef Zohar Sasson. In a setting depicted by groovy background music and hoots of laughter from the ebullient kitchen brigade, Ms Sasson cheerfully conjures up dishes loosely inspired by Sephardic culinary traditions. The menu rolls out a colourful culinary anthology, boosted by spices, seasonings and chickpeas. Some of the emblematic dishes of the former Balagan remain on the menu, such as “deconstructed” kebab. Festive, friendly and (very) buzzy vibe.

Name: Les Alisiers
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This lovely panoramic restaurant has a minimalist decor. The food showcases local ingredients but stands out from local dishes by mixing influences and flavours.

Name: Côté Vigne
Description: In this charming village, an imposing 16C half-timbered house. The chef crafts modern dishes, scattered with exotic flavours, such as beef terrine with grated egg and wasabi cream, or grilled squid with leeks, pumpkin gnocchi, mussels and red curry. On the wine side, you will be treated to the organic vintages from the family estate. The terrace is very popular in summertime. Simpler lunch menu.

Name: L'Athome
Description: In this pleasant village bistro complete with wine shop, chef Lionel Cotentin draws on his strong culinary background as well as good local produce – organic market garden vegetables, small-scale fishing – to create a menu that changes with the seasons. The cuisine is modern, meticulous and full of bold flavours, with discernible Asian influences, as seen in the Japanese-style devilled egg with soy sauce mayonnaise, topped with seaweed and roasted sesame seeds. Efficient service – with a smile.

Name: La Vieille Fontaine - Le Club de Cavalière & Spa
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant offers fine seafood, as well as some meat dishes, cooked with great skill. Try ravioli with langoustine and coriander, curry bisque, sea bass roasted in its skin, and crunchy escabeche with condiments. Sea views while you eat!

Name: Auberge de la Vieille Ferme
Address: 58 rue de la République, Le Meux, 60880, France
Description: In this little village not far from Compiègne, a former farmstead is now a very popular hotel and restaurant. The chef signs a culinary score that is both delicate and appetising, dotted with personal touches such as a starter of razor clams, cuttlefish and potatoes, or the peanut, caramel and vanilla millefeuille dessert – to die for! Highly recommended.

Name: Bistro Saint-Jean
Address: 132 boulevard de la Rochelle, Bar-le-Duc, 55000, France
Description: This ex-grocer’s shop is now a contemporary bistro, rich in flavour and colour, that hits the spot every time. The owner, son of a pastry chef, rustles up market-fresh cuisine in tune with the seasons, like this slow-cooked pork belly with baby onions and braising juices. Respect for the ingredients is the motto. Efficient, unobtrusive staff.

Name: Le Pirate
Description: This well-known Cap Corse establishment stands on the pretty port of Erbalunga. Fish soup, tiger veal, suckling pig, barbecued fish: the quintessence of Corsican food, with the odd, unexpected note, such as a new take on vitello tonnato. The setting is idyllic with a few tables on a small balcony and a large waterside terrace.

Name: L'Espérance
Description: If you're lucky enough to be in Bandol, leave the harbour area and make a beeline for the refreshing establishment of Maria and Gilles Pradines, a treasure trove of culinary talent and delight. Born in the Basque country, the chef has retained his love of the south of France, from stuffed piquillo peppers to black cherries and pata negra. Each ingredient is fastidiously sourced and prepared with great care: wild sea bass marinated in fennel seeds, grilled special oyster no. 2, apricots from Provence, olive oil and lemons… The presentation of the dishes is beautiful, and the service is charming!

Name: Le Duguesclin
Description: This intimate restaurant opposite the former Excise and Duty House serves well-prepared seasonal cuisine in its vaulted room. The short menu is available in the form of "land" or "sea" set menus offering very good value for money. During the week, the lunch menu is tailored to the busy business clientele; at dinner, the menu is more ambitious. Summer terrace to the rear to be enjoyed in fine weather.

Name: Le Millésime
Description: In the heart of a winegrowers’ village, this spruce building is home to a contemporary restaurant. The chef cleverly, even daringly, juggles with a range of culinary scores, illustrated by a tartare of whelks flanked by a foie gras emulsion. Examples of the bargain-priced lunchtime menu include a chicken liver cake with a shellfish sauce or a Black Angus steak, pinot noir jus and autumn pickles. The menu slaloms between pure-bred Gallic classics and more elaborate recipes: poached eggs in red wine rub shoulders with Brittany lobster in a chorizo crust flanked by girolle mushrooms and vin jaune sauce. You can taste the wine before purchasing at the Musigny wine shop, abutting the establishment and which also belongs to the owner.

Name: Le Relais du Çatey
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary decor and lighting enhance the authentic character of this regional house from 1774. Arctic char with meadowsweet, roast saddle of venison with juniper and mushrooms or Williams pear on a wafer-thin millefeuille. Pedigree classics and inventive flourishes.

Name: Michel Béjeannin - Auberge de Chavannes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In winter, an open fire burns brightly in this welcoming and contemporary inn. The food sings an ode to the Mediterranean with bouillabaisse (the chef lived in Marseille for some 26 years), and also the local countryside with Bresse hen in vin jaune and morels, a whimsical nod to his Jura roots. Fine wine list with a fondness for organic and biodynamic produce. Spacious rooms for overnight stays.

Name: L'Océanic
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The ocean breeze blows as far inland as Chinon! As its name suggests, this restaurant gives seafood pride of place. The chef prepares very fresh fish, adding a dash of originality, with a pinch of spice here and a hint of sweet and sour there. Good value for money.

Name: Le Matafan
Description: In the legendary Mont Blanc hotel, in an elegant contemporary setting with a central fireplace, the cuisine varies between traditional dishes (Lyon sausage with truffles; barbecued beef chuck) and more modern preparations (pigeon, endives, ginger broth). The health-conscious can also opt for their set menu ("Menu Bien-Être"). Outside tables giving onto the large swimming pool are set up when the weather is fine.

Name: La Botte d'Asperges
Description: With a name that conjures up springtime (it means "bunch of asparagus"), this restaurant delivers delicious cuisine, showcasing local producers and winegrowers as well as herbs from its pretty garden in aesthetically pleasing dishes. At the helm is a professional couple and a chef with a solid track record, Stéphane Bureau – he loves to pop out into the dining area and share his enthusiasm with diners. The comfortable interior is done out in a contemporary bistro style.

Name: L'Instantané
Description: This contemporary bistro located in the art gallery district proposes moments of pure culinary bliss, dreamt up by a seasoned chef (Ritz, Lasserre, Plaza). Veal, poultry and pork “porkpie”, 12-hour melt-in-the-mouth beef, roast loin of hake with hazelnut butter, crème brûlée… Finger licking good from start to finish!

Name: L'Auberge Bressane
Description: A firm favourite: justice is done to regional specialities (Bresse chicken, frogs' legs, crayfish and its legendary pike quenelles) and the wine list is packed with vintage bottles. Terrace with a view onto the church of the Royal Monastery of Brou.

Name: Les Cordois Autrement
Description: This restaurant, run by the same family since 1910, now abuts a 12C church. Take a seat and admire the bright colourful interior or relax on the shaded terrace, as you sample a cleverly updated version of regional country nosh: Burgundy snails, eggs in red wine, veal kidneys in mustard sauce without forgetting the odd intriguing creation such as an escalope of salmon with Morteau sausage and a creamy sauce of runny cheese…

Name: Le Fanal
Description: The lights of Le Fanal (“The Lantern”) will guide you to this idyllic spot overlooking Banyuls marina. Catalan-born Pascal Borrell has decided to drop anchor here after stints in several top Paris restaurants and running the Chapon Fin at Perpignan. The main attraction here is fish: hake, monkfish, sole, turbot, cod and anchovy pickles delicately marinated in Banyuls vinegar.

Name: Le Bistrot du Quai
Address: 1 avenue de la Libération, Charolles, 71120, France
Description: In this new place, standing opposite the parent restaurant on the other side of the road, the chef proposes traditional cuisine and spit - roast meats. Menu du Jour in harmony with the seasons, and Menu Charolais, showcasing produce from Burgundy. Terrace overlooking the river.

Name: Auberge du Bon Laboureur
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant sticks to the proven path of cooking with seasonal ingredients. Chef Antoine Jeudi knows his stuff, and his tasty creations can be paired with a fine choice of wines. A pleasant mealtime, in an equally appealing setting.

Name: La Suite
Description: A fashionably stylish modern interior sets the scene in this warm, friendly eatery. The regularly renewed seasonal menu will make your mouth water... before the flavours and aromas satisfy your tastebuds and obliterate your hunger pangs. Let's not forget the pretty patio terrace or the wine list that leaves nothing to chance – the owner is a trained sommelier, while his brother is in charge of the kitchen.

Name: Les Chênes
Description: This country restaurant right on the main road is surrounded by forests and the Monts du Forez. It is open at lunchtime for traditional, generous and unpretentious cuisine that gives pride of place to local produce (meat, mushrooms, cheeses etc). There is something for every budget in the two set menus ("menu du jour" or "menu gourmand"). A family affair established in 1975 that has put down roots!

Name: La Maison de Petit Pierre
Description: Enthusiastic chef Pierre Augé is at the helm of this restaurant with a personalised decor that is located close to the bullring. He greets each and every customer with an infectious smile because he is there to spread joy with his tasty creative cuisine based on local ingredients! Rather than bask in the media hype, he is clearly driven by a desire to continuously explore new culinary avenues. It's a joy to behold – and tuck into – dishes such as his whisky-marinated pavé de bœuf steak and cauliflower mousseline with vanilla; hake with piperade and green jus; or stracciatella with asparagus and bacon tuile. A buzzy, friendly vibe, enhanced by the personality of the chef, and the warm, cheerful service of his wife, adds the final flourish: recommended!

Name: Le Strasbourg
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Originally a farm mechanic from the former East Germany, Lutz Janisch was trained by chef Jean Albrecht (at the restaurant Au Vieux Couvent in Rhinau). His appetising cuisine is contemporary and generous, and has a variety of inspirations (Italian: home-made strozzapreti to accompany fried squid stuffed with prawns and courgettes; Japanese: quail leg tempura and a roast quail fillet kebab; and French: crêpes Suzette and Grand Marnier ice cream). He often uses local ingredients (trout from Eguelshardt, vegetables from Sturzelbronn etc). There are also guestrooms.

Name: La Tupina
Description: A genuine institution, this country inn champions dishes of yesteryear... Sanguette (blood pudding), macaronade (pasta with beef and tomato sauce), chips fried in duck fat: local produce is promoted with conviction in hearty dishes from South-West France, but also seasonal vegetables and meat roasted in the hearth. The fine produce on the counter certainly whets the appetite.

Name: L'As de Trèfle
Description: Slightly set back from the D - Day landing beaches, this is the restaurant of Anthony Vallette, a chef from Normandy with energy to burn. Over the course of the seasons he draws on the local terroir (fish from the Channel, andouille de Vire, Bayeux pig) and composes meticulous dishes with just the right level of boldness.

Name: Les Impressionnistes - La Ferme Saint-Siméon
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Established in the luxury Ferme Saint Siméon Hotel, a historic hamlet in the upper reaches of Honfleur, this property is the quintessence of stylish. The plush elegant Normandy-style interior, the wooded grounds and the terrace with a superb view of the Seine Estuary may be absolutely enchanting, but not enough to distract us from the matter at hand! The chef creates seasonal contemporary cuisine that draws on top-notch Normandy produce. The estate is also home to the half-timbered, thatched roof La Boucane bistro, which serves equally tasty, but more traditional cuisine.

Name: Lore Ttipia - Auberge Ostape
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A sprawling country estate on the heights of Bidarray and Itxassou is home to this inn that occupies a 17C farmstead. A panoramic terrace commands a jaw-dropping view of the grandiose rolling countryside. Chef John Argaud, who trained with the best of the Basque Country (La Table des Frères Ibarboure, Ithurria) as well as at Le Meurice with Alain Ducasse in Paris, shines the spotlight on outstanding local produce. Some ingredients are cooked over embers or finished on a hot stone for an added distinctive edge. The food is crisp, legible and delicate, like the stuffed courgette flowers with grilled cuttlefish. From Monday to Wednesday, the restaurant only offers a bistronomic menu, which is simpler but just as appetising as that available later in the week.

Name: Le Médicis
Description: "The contemporary - style interior chimes with the up - to - the - minute culinary creations that keep pace with the market and the seasons; the chef also introduces a handful of welcome Asian touches: a pleasant mealtime in store. Friendly service. "

Name: Le Pavé d'Auge
Description: Situated between Caen and Lisieux in the heart of the Pays d’Auge, Beuvron-en-Auge is emblematic of Normandy with its 17C-18C half-timbered houses, manor houses, apple orchards and gardens decked in flowers come summertime. The restaurant, which occupies the village’s former covered market, sports an olde worlde feel inside and out. Chef Adrien Haye, former second here, reverently respects the seasons: oysters from Saint-Vaast, lobster from Carteret, John Dory, as well as foie gras, veal sweetbread, tripe and andouille sausage with baked apples. The quintessence of Normandy!

Name: Le Castel Marie-Louise
Description: A prime example of La Baule’s early-20C seaside architecture, this manor house is home to a hotel and a restaurant appointed in a classical bourgeois style whose windows overlook the grounds and pretty terrace. Local lad Jérémy Coirier draws his inspiration from the region (fish, shellfish, Croisic seaweed, Guérande saffron, Mesquer pigeon) to compose a menu that changes with the seasons.

Name: L'Entre Deux
Description: Young chef Rémy Escale is at the helm of this trendy bistro, which is inviting and tastefully decorated. Food - wise, the objective has been set to stick close to the ingredients and bring out their natural flavour. He weaves flavours together with panache, demonstrating faultless technical know - how: an enjoyable experience.

Name: Gavroche
Description: In a quiet side street in the Krutenau quarter, this restaurant has an intimate feel. Chef Alexy Fuchs serves contemporary cuisine (langoustine, apple salad and mustard ice, or scallops, sweet potato, crispy ravioli and bisque emulsion) with the odd nod to Alsace, as in the foie gras terrine with fruit chutney and dampfnudel. Service is particularly charming.

Name: Au Vieux Moulin
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Take a seat in the luminous dining room overlooking the countryside of this family - run house tucked away in the Graufthal valley and dig into the sparkling cuisine of Guillaum Kessel. The menus are dictated by seasonal availability, a principle adhered to by the entire community. For example, hen’s egg from Moulin farm and Steilberg snails, breast of duckling, fried girolles and cherries. The wine list boasts over 200 references.

Name: Le M
Description: We love this trendy contemporary bistro as much for its charming hospitality as for its tasty, up-to-the-minute cooking, such as a thick loin of cod, fregola sarda and poultry jus. The concise menu-carte, which ensures the freshness and quality of seasonal ingredients, is a steal at lunchtime! Don't miss the excellent cannelé, a nod to the couple's Bordeaux roots. There is a fine selection of wines on the blackboard.

Name: Anthon
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Georges Flaig represents the fourth generation at the helm of this gorgeous half - timbered house, dating from 1860. No nostalgia on his watch. His cooking is modern and tasty, and readily promotes producers from the surrounding area. For instance, Windstein Highland beef and Wingen trout.

Name: Auberge Ramstein
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Tradition takes pride of place here in this establishment surrounded by vineyards, which is run as a family affair. Father and son (Lucas, who has worked in some prestigious restaurants) work together, their cooking underpinned by an ambition to reinterpret the terroir of Alsace. You can enjoy veal filet mignon with morels, and themed menus (mainly in winter). A warm welcome and attentive service, plus guestrooms.

Name: Bürestubel
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This half-timbered farmhouse is brimming with Alsatian charm! Pretty regional decor and (very) local specialities: bibalaskas with smoked ham, bacon, garlic and parsley ; veal fleischnacka with mushrooms and cream ; sourdough tartes flammées…and the unmissable “real crème caramel like my grandmother used to make”.

Name: Ail des Ours
Description: This pleasant, trendy restaurant close to the cathedral is run by young chef Stéphane Bruyer. In a renovated dining space decorated in natural tones (with lots of plants), he serves simple, seasonal cuisine, using market produce to devise a single set menu (with a choice of fish or meat). This is a very popular spot in Amiens... and it's easy to see why.

Name: Akira Back Paris
Address: Prince de Galles, 33 avenue George-V, Paris, 75008, France
Description: In the Prince de Galles hotel, this is the first European restaurant of American-Korean chef Akira Back. After a career as a professional snowboarder (he grew up in Aspen, home to the legendary ski resort), he turned his hand to cooking. He was recruited by Nobuyuki Matsuhisa and later became the executive chef at the renowned chef's restaurant. Diners are given the opportunity to taste this new take on Japanese cuisine, a real melting pot of cultures and flavours, including Back's speciality: AB Tuna Pizza. Meanwhile, feast your eyes on the sumptuous decor of this large modern restaurant with Art Deco light fixtures emitting subdued lighting, while the kitchen team busy themselves at the marble counter.

Name: L'Ambassade
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Fresh ingredients, balanced dishes: chef Patrick Olry, well known in the region, demonstrates his know - how and consistency. In particular, be sure to try the tasting menus based on truffles, scallops or lobster, which are in no small part responsible for the establishment's reputation.

Name: Le Senso
Description: On the market square, this spruce, well-kept restaurant provides the perfect foil for simple, unfussy cuisine in which local produce takes pride of place. Chef Allan Castellote cannot be faulted for his artistic presentations, while his brother Tristan masterfully attends to the wine-food pairing suggestions. The house speciality, kouign amann, is to die for!

Name: Ma Cuisine
Description: Wine takes pride of place in this friendly bistro with an outstanding selection of some 800 different bottles. The chef certainly knows his way around them, and is equally at ease in the kitchen. Diners delight in his homemade jellied ham with parsley, veal chop in jus and crème caramel. The dishes will have you coming back for more.

Name: Sormani
Address: 4 rue du Général Lanrezac, Paris, 75017, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: This Italian restaurant has an opulent feel, with its Murano glass chandeliers, mouldings and mirrors, and is popular with Paris's celebrities. The cooking pays tribute to Italian specialities, with spaghetti alle vongole and Calabrian chilli, for example, or iconic desserts such as the gigantesco – Italian-style vanilla ice cream frozen to order on site, served with meringue, nougatine and liquid caramel.

Name: Le Pergolèse
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: While the decor of Le Pergolèse has been completely redesigned (contemporary paintings, street art, plates by Aurélie Pergay), the food continues to celebrate classicism, in the spirit of a "fine bourgeois house where you receive customers as you would at home".

Name: Racines
Description: Simone Tondo, a chef of Sardinian origin, runs this charming bistro-cum-wine cellar, having made the excellent decision to turn it into a traditionally styled osteria. The chef's cooking is firmly rooted in Italian produce and he gives free rein to his creativity with a carte blanche menu and daily specials. These present a choice of down-to-earth Italian dishes that are rife with distinct flavours and carefully prepared from well-chosen ingredients: vitello tonnato, polpette al sugo, ricotta ravioli, spinach and squid.

Name: Auberge La Cauquière
Address: 7 rue du Chanoine-Bœuf, Le Beausset, 83330, France
Description: The chef-owner of this former inn prepares contemporary dishes that are meticulous and flavoursome: creamy hummus, artichokes and olives in a tomato sauce; fillet of sea bass cooked skin on, minestrone of baby vegetables with pistou sauce and bouillabaisse jus... served in a pretty space with exposed stone walls, or on the terrace in front of the garden. A fresh start!

Name: La Table de Colette
Description: With green electricity, energy-efficient appliances, seed saving and the carbon footprint of the dishes shown on the menu – everything has been thought out with eco-responsibility in mind. Vegetables and pulses, prepared in all manner of ways, take pride of place, eg the medley of lentils – stewed, emulsified and fried. And there is the odd nod to the chef's native Brittany, in the form of the cauliflower surf and turf, Guéméné andouille sausage and abalone.

Name: L'Enoteca
Description: (Temporarily closed) This enoteca is the first restaurant of a young couple overflowing with culinary talent and ambition. In the kitchen, the chef sources premium ingredients to create flavoursome, enticing dishes poised between southwest France and Provence, while his partner warmly and professionally welcomes diners.

Name: Ogata
Description: Ogata, a temple dedicated to Japanese art de vivre, is located in a private mansion in the Marais and masterminded by Shinichiro Ogata, world-famous designer and connoisseur. The (mainly) traditional Japanese food sports an omakase spirit, through a tasting menu comprised of immaculate seasonal produce (first-class sashimi). The best seats are at the counter. Pop into the shop or art gallery on your way out…

Name: Cucina Mutualité
Description: The colourful modern bistro decor and extremely cordial staff make for an appealing atmosphere. As for the food, the wonderful seasonal Italian menu is a pageant of authentic, flavourful and truly generous dishes: you won't be disappointed by the melt-in-the-mouth braised ox cheek paccheri... al dente, obviously! You may even be allowed a second helping.

Name: Terra
Description: At the end of a long corridor, beneath a glass roof in the courtyard of an old Parisian building, this restaurant exudes a vibe that is part winter garden, part neo-industrial atelier. The chef works wholeheartedly and effectively to transform carefully selected ingredients: meagre ceviche with kombu and peach with tarragon; riz au lait with coconut, exotic fruits, Thai basil and buckwheat. The main courses (pluma de bellota pork with chimichurri sauce; Basque veal chop with Choron sauce – tomato-spiked Béarnaise) are designed for sharing. Well-curated and reasonably priced wine list.

Name: Chez Mathilde
Description: Mathilde is the daughter of the famous fisherman of Lake Geneva, Eric Jacquier. She is now established in this cheerful eatery in the heart of the village with a concrete counter, off-kilter lighting and light wood bistro furnishings. Her slate menu resembles her spontaneous, playful and intuitive personality!

Name: L'Œuf de Coq
Description: A fine arts student in a former life, chef Mathieu Lacaze takes great care over the presentation of his dishes. His artistic sensibility shines through in his resolutely modern market-fresh cuisine. In keeping with the seasons, his dishes are prepared using quality local ingredients selected from organic market gardeners and small-scale livestock farmers. The space is contemporary, with exposed tiles and stone walls; in fine weather, make a beeline for the small patio terrace. A surprise set menu is served in the evening, along with a fine selection of independent wines, mainly organic and natural.

Name: Loco by Jem's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A hit with the locals, this buzzy, youthful bolthole is home to Jérémy, nicknamed Jem’s by his mates who think he’s a bit wacky (loco in Spanish). Jem finds inspiration in local ingredients which he crafts into dishes rich in crisp, contrasting flavours. The counter commands a fascinating view of the kitchen team at work. Bargain-priced lunchtime menu and tasting menu in the evening with wine-food pairings; vegetarian menu on request.

Name: La Table de Michèle
Description: Michèle Brouet is a figure on the local gastronomy scene. Her restaurant is the reflection of her generosity and cheer, as is the atmosphere, which is welcoming with its various random objects and bouquets of flowers. Good food and good times are on the menu!

Name: Le Goût du Jour
Description: Good ideas, know - how... Julien Chazal, a young chef from Avignon, shows us how it's done! Furthermore, his seasonal cooking is visually meticulous, with presentations that leave nothing to chance. And let's not forget the down - to - earth, smiling service.

Name: Les Sales Gosses
Description: Les Sales Gosses (naughty kids) chalks up its creative version of heart-warming bistro classics on large blackboards. The food is the work of chef Bruno, who is definitely top of the class! A great meal every time. And if it’s fully booked, there is now a Plan B: Le Bistrot, not far away, on Rue de l'Industrie.

Name: L'Ancolie
Description: Named after a pretty flower, this appealing restaurant successfully blends old stone with contemporary elegance. The fine cuisine errs towards traditional fare, eg crayfish tartare or scallops with vanilla-infused orange.

Name: Bistrot Augustin
Description: Taken over by Guy Martin in 2020, this bistro still lives by the same values: a cosy setting, a small terrace on rue Daguerre, and lovely market-fresh cooking that is all about the ingredients. Rabbit terrine and red onion compote; sautéed farm-reared quasi of veal, seasonal vegetables with country bacon. Table d'hôte to the rear and an appetising menu-carte.

Name: À la Maison
Description: This house rustles up wholesome bistro fare that shines the limelight on regional produce. The chef particularly likes devising dishes around a single ingredient, such as pork or lamb. House specialties include black pudding, a 64° egg and Guéméné andouille. Well worth discovering.

Name: Buerehiesel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This picturesque, half-timbered 17C farmhouse was reconstructed stone by stone in the Orangerie Park, next-door to the Council of Europe. The conservatory dining room and patio command a bucolic view of this leafy haven. The menu features some of the house signature dishes, such as frog’s legs sautéed in chervil or free-range pullet roasted in a casserole dish (backeoffe), together with more contemporary seasonal recipes.

Name: La Ferme de la Fruitière
Address: 337 route de La Plagne, Morzine, 74110, France
Description: In this wood - panelled interior, a lovely fireplace crackles as you choose from the local cheese specialities, such as Berthoud. If you look through the window, you can see the whole cheeses – Abondance, Tomme and Reblochon – in the maturing cellar of the neighbouring cheese dairy.

Name: Le Moulin de Ponceau
Address: 21 rue de la Tannerie, Chartres, 28000, France
Description: This restaurant, well known to the people of Chartres, taken over by hotel industry pros, turns out to be a nice surprise. In an alluring 16C building located in the historic heart of town and on the banks of the Eure, the chef prepares seasonal, deft and colourful cuisine in keeping with a responsible ethos. Attentive service, terrace in a bucolic setting.

Name: Solides
Description: This restaurant opposite the market stands out on account of its fine bistro food, delivered by a chef who is a proponent of short supply chains. It also boasts an excellent (and coherent) natural wine list. In a bohemian atmosphere, sample the house speciality: vol-au-vent with calf sweetbreads, cockerel combs and chicken sauce, as well as terrific cheeses from the region.

Name: Le Bistrot du Port
Description: Opposite the old port, the chef-patron gives free rein to his abundant creativity and his passion for fish and seafood: the tasting menu ("Plongée en plusieurs paliers") is a veritable ode to the sea, with dishes such as sea urchins with grapefruit and spirulina served as a dessert. The produce is remarkably fresh, the cooking is skilful and the risk-taking is constant: this is a restaurant that stands out from the crowd!

Name: Maison Bouquet
Description: Guillaume Assié is living proof that when a chef is happy in their kitchen, the food follows suit. His modern, pared-back score highlights his flawless technique and knowhow, gleaned in the kitchens of great chefs (Oustau de Baumanière, Lameloise, Auberge du Vieux puits). Devoid of frivolous frills, Guillaume’s cuisine is an ode to simplicity. The asparagus, which is green and al dente, is paired with caviar for added saltiness; the fresh gleaming monkfish is enveloped in a velvety grenobloise sauce, while an exquisite concoction of chocolate, peanuts and tobacco adds the final touch to the consummate culinary craftsmanship. Swish seamless service. Established in a mansion dating from 1900, the softly lit interior is cosy and inviting.

Name: L'Empreinte
Description: Solid oak tables, custom-made tableware and a warm welcome… This snug restaurant is the stomping ground of Manuel Godet, who harnesses his impeccable textbook skills to crafting creative recipes that shine the spotlight on local produce, sometimes with surprising twists. Examples include Pyrenean gravlax trout and whipped cream flavoured with locally brewed gin, or a kiwi from Adour with cocoa, buckwheat and truffles. Simple lunchtime menu, more ambitious in the evening.

Name: La Contre Allée
Description: Chef Matthieu Chabroux regales diners in this discreet street parallel to Avenue Denfert-Rochereau. Expect simple, deftly crafted market-fresh fare made using top-notch ingredients, eg Chinese cabbage salad with gambas, crispy dumplings and satay… and the house speciality: rum baba. To be enjoyed in a smart, pared-back interior with an inviting atmosphere. Always a good option.

Name: L'Instant Z
Address: 1 bis rue du Château-de-Cigogne, Le Thou, 17290, France
Description: Z for Zanchetta, the chef's surname. Working with top-notch ingredients fresh from the market and small-scale, local organic farmers, he conjures up dishes with a mixture of influences and a weakness for game in season. Even better, the bread is baked on the premises! The recently revamped interior is casual and friendly with service to match: a real pleasure.

Name: Nous
Description: In this modern bistro overflowing in feel-good vibes, Raphaël and Elise Campas treat the foodies of Montauban to a culinary festival, all made in-house, from the bread to the ice cream. Taking their cue from the seasons, the experienced couple conscientiously selects regional ingredients (vegetables from independent market gardeners and farmstead cheeses), which the chef crafts into colourful, appetising dishes. Élise professionally and seamlessly manages the front of house, while Raphaël pops out from time to time to lend a hand and wax lyrical about his cooking. This excellent establishment, only open for lunch, offers a concise menu that changes monthly, giving you the perfect excuse to return again and again.

Name: Fleurs d'Olargues
Description: It's a real family affair here at this attractive restaurant run by Danish chef Kasper and his wife Fé. The culinary programme comprises local ingredients, vegetables from the garden, foie gras and home-made bread (eg smørrebrød) and a scattering of subtle Nordic touches (salmon marinated in beetroot juice, hasselback potatoes). The bucolic terrace overlooks the 12C Pont du Diable ("Devil's Bridge") and the village, officially designated as one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France.

Name: Les Affranchis
Description: This young duo happily ignore the classics to create tasty cuisine, such as the œuf parfait façon carbonara ("perfect egg" with carbonara) or pollock with cauliflower, orange and botargo. An (excellent) place that is right at home in the bourgeois - bohemian 9th arrondissement.

Name: La Tour des Sens
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the upper reaches of Tencin, this Tower is a treat for the five senses! Run by the same chef since 2016 (2017 Top Chef winner), his creative, natural menus aim to stimulate the taste buds of diners and thus call upon their emotions. When the weather’s fine, why not enjoy the fabulous view of the Chartreuse range from the terrace?

Name: Charbon Kunitoraya
Description: Outside, the attractive timber façade has a Japanese feel. Inside, you'll find an old zinc counter, Paris Métro-style tiling, mirrors, wood panelling and mouldings, and two large bar tables built of solid wood. In this chic setting with a vintage feel, chef Kunitoraya – a pioneer of udon restaurants in France – serves up a range of top-notch yakitori, particularly chicken. Cordial, well-paced service.

Name: La Condesa
Description: La Condesa, an area of Mexico City, has lent its name to this restaurant run by Indra Carrillo. The chef came from Mexico to study at the Institut Paul Bocuse, before going on to work at leading restaurants such as Le Bristol and L'Astrance. Trained by Meilleur Ouvrier de France chefs, notably in fishmongery and bakery, he has also worked in Japan. Although his techniques are French, his culinary inspiration comes from many different cultures, including Mexico. The chic, pared-down interior adds the final flourish.

Name: Thaï Spices
Description: Between the Quai des Célestins and St Paul is the domain of Willy Lieu, who was Jacques Chirac's personal chef. Here, he pays tribute to authentic Thai cuisine, serving all the great classics – pad thai, tom yam –, generously prepared and full of flavour, with the requisite spiciness. Reasonable prices and good service.

Name: Les Résistants
Description: These résistants believe that taste and traceability should be the backbone of all food. Indeed, the credo of owner, Florent Piard, is none other than "good food that respects natural cycles! " and he amply proves his case in this cheerful establishment. The concise menu changes daily in keeping with market availability and the prices are never outlandish. Natural wines bien sûr!

Name: Rouge Barre
Address: 50 rue de la Halle, Lille, 59000, France
Description: In the heart of Vieux Lille, local man Steven Ramon confirms – after his Top Chef adventure in 2014 – that we should be counting on him in the future. A Ch'ti to the core, he concocts inspired and lively dishes that make the most of fine ingredients. The restaurant has a "rouge barre" interior (red brick and white stone). Irresistible!

Name: Drouant
Description: This timeless restaurant is a mythical establishment, where the Goncourt Prize has been awarded since 1914 and the Renaudot Prize since 1926! More recently, still very much alive and kicking, it has found itself with a new decor and a new chef: Romain Van Thienen. With a skillset honed in the kitchens of Cyril Lignac and Yannick Alléno's Allénotheque, he is continuing in the establishment's tradition, preparing the great French classics, from vol-au-vent and sole meunière to the famous "madeleine de Proust".

Name: L'Alexandrin
Description: L'Alexandrin combines originality with generosity, serving dishes made using fine, locally sourced produce. Each menu (vegetarian, revisited Lyon classics or pure creation) proposes a different take on the art of fine dining in an exclusive atmosphere. One novelty is the table d'hôte with four guests seated in the kitchen at the heart of the action!

Name: Loulou
Description: The Musée des Arts Décoratifs promises you an enchanted interlude opposite the gardens of the Louvre. In the kitchen, Benoît Dargère and Zouhair Bouhlal reinvent Mediterranean classics by means of a careful selection of produce. On the terrace or in the elegant interior, the service is just as impeccable as the dishes (risotto of the day; piccata of milk-fed veal al limone, sage; grilled octopus, aioli). It is cosy, refined and delicious.

Name: L'Écume Gourmande
Description: This restaurant is the brainchild of a young chef with an enviable CV. His classical training shines through, albeit with an intelligent inventive twist, illustrated by his organic egg ‘parfait’, French green peas and emulsion of smoked bacon, or a slab of sturgeon served with shimeji mushrooms and basil. The glazed wine cellar is a treasure trove of affordable tipples.

Name: Mon Plaisir
Description: In this inviting country house, chef Christian Pilloud takes the preparation of each and every dish very seriously. As a classically trained chef who is open to new ideas, he selects quality produce from the Burgundy and Franche-Comté regions to create generous dishes: autumn mushrooms and farm-reared snails; crispy knuckle end of veal and sweetbreads with morels, vin jaune jus; pigeon royal in a puff pastry crust.

Name: Éléonore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant restaurant is housed in a pretty little château, which has the art of hospitality down to a T. The globetrotting chef welcomes you with a menu presented in two sections: one “classical” which features a traditional lineup, while the other is more “unusual” with creative twists.

Name: Le Paris
Address: 88 rue de Metz, Le Touquet-Paris-Plage, 62520, France
Description: A few streets away from the seafront, this restaurant is in sync with the markets and seasons and very much appreciated by local gourmets! They know how to pull off happy marriages of flavours, as in the asparagus, egg, morels and pancetta, or the meagre with capers and spinach. Friendly welcome.

Name: Confins des Sens
Description: The house speciality is a delicious muscat-flavoured foie gras soup with a confit of red onions and ‘cromesquis’. The chefs pay tribute to the region whilst respecting the seasons, illustrated by a velvety soup of green peas and an ice cream of fresh cow’s cheese flavoured with wild garlic. Other highlights include pork cheeks braised in a local red wine or free-range chicken wings stuffed with morels and flanked by “pressed” potatoes (finely sliced and stacked before being roasted). The terrace is glorious in the sunshine.

Name: L'Assiette
Description: An honest and generous place where you can see what's going on in the kitchen. Home-made cassoulet (also available in the adjoining shop), pâté en croûte, vegetable pickles; beef chuck braised in red wine and tender carrots; rum baba: Think traditional cuisine with a chic bistro twist.

Name: La Table du Rouan
Address: 2 boulevard de la Jamagne, Gérardmer, 88400, France
Description: "Julien Jeanselme, a committed and welcoming chef, creates fresh and straightforward cuisine, whose regional roots do not preclude nods to other influences, especially Provence (he's a fan of fish soup), or tributes – here, to his great - grandfather, who was awarded a Michelin star... in 1936! – with the ""Ernest Jeanselme"" mountain terrine. A reliably good option. "

Name: Les Pipelettes
Description: Here, the delicious dishes are prepared according to the produce available at the market stalls and the harvests of some 30 farmers based near Pau. The chef does his job well, and that's all that matters: scallops and celeriac purée; wild sea bass from Saint-Jean-de-Luz; pork grenadin, endives and oyster mushrooms. Set menus (without options) at lunch and dinner, but the value for money is excellent.

Name: Passerini
Description: In his convivial restaurant, Giovanni Passerini treats us to tasty, carefully prepared Italian dishes, such as his trippa alla romana, which could hardly be bettered. Here, it's all about the produce and authenticity: sharing plates are a house speciality, as is Black-Headed Manech suckling lamb or whole pigeon in two courses. This place is very popular, so be sure to book!

Name: Kigawa
Description: Kigawa is named after Michihiro Kigawa, the chef at this refreshingly simple restaurant. Buoyed by his experience in a French restaurant in Osaka, he now finds himself in Paris, delighting guests with classic French dishes such as pâté en croûte and roast pigeon.

Name: Le Pavillon Bleu
Address: 315 rue de la Reine-Blanche, Olivet, 45160, France
Description: A "guinguette" atmosphere pervades this 1903 building on the bank of the Loiret, where you can sit on the terrace in the shade of old plane trees, right by the water's edge. Fun fact: the dining area is actually an old boathouse. As for the food, the techniques are deft and the seasonings balanced, making for tasty dishes.

Name: L'Absinthe
Description: A homage to the Green Fairy beloved of many a writer, this bistro has an appealing neo-retro feel, thanks to features such as old tiles and flooring, a zinc-topped counter, exposed brick walls and a monumental clock. In the kitchen, there are plenty of traditional and hearty dishes simmering away for you to choose from. Meat from the wood-fired grill, country terrine, roasted scallops, all at reasonable prices... and an excellent Bourbon vanilla millefeuille.

Name: Ciasa Mia
Description: Originally from northern Italy (the Dolomites, to be precise), Francesca and Samuel Mocci like to highlight their culinary heritage, which proves to be as delicious as it is surprising. The dishes exude authenticity, as does the space, designed in a cosy little chalet spirit. An appealing place.

Name: Aux Lyonnais
Description: This bistro established in 1890 has a delightfully retro decor and serves delicious cuisine that explores Lyon's gastronomy in all its riches. The terrines, pike-perch quenelles with crayfish, and the chicken liver terrine vie with the specials chalked up on the slate, and the desserts are enough to awaken anyone's sweet tooth.

Name: Le Quincy
Description: A cosy ambience prevails in this utterly timeless establishment, which was dominated by its larger-than-life boss, “Bobosse”, for so many years. Even though he doesn’t pop in quite so often anymore, his personality continues to underscore the DNA of this haunt of foodies. For fifty odd years, fine food lovers have been digging into wholehearted, rustic dishes from Berry or Ardèche. The chef scrimps neither on quality nor quantity when it comes to the house terrine of cabbage and garlic, poultry in cream or the rum-flavoured ice cream! An establishment whose existence is almost anachronistic in today’s restaurant universe.

Name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon - St-Germain
Description: Bathed in a studied semi-darkness, two bars face each other around a central kitchen where the dishes are prepared under the gaze of the guests, seated on high stools at the counter. This "chic canteen" is a Western version of Japanese teppanyaki and sushi bars, with a menu that can be “tailored” into small portions and plates that boast superlative ingredients. Caviar on a soft-boiled hen’s egg and smoked salmon in puff pastry; fried whiting "Colbert style" in herb butter…not forgetting the house staples, king crab ravioli, suckling lamb chops and Joël Robuchon's famous mashed potatoes.

Name: Le Domaine de Saint-Géry
Address: Le Domaine de Saint-Géry, Lascabanes, 46800, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Self - proclaimed ‘farmer - chef’, Patrick Duler does not mess around with the origin of his ingredients. Much of what is on your plate – ham from black pigs, truffles, foie gras – comes straight from his own fields! His simple, meticulous dishes reveal the soul of a truly passionate chef.

Name: Clover Grill
Description: Mouthwatering dry - aged meats – Baltic black beef, Bavarian beef, Blonde d'Aquitaine, Black Angus – take pride of place in the window, drawing in diners keen to try them for themselves. From the starters to the desserts, everything is cooked over coals or roasted on a spit, giving the dining experience its own particular flavour. A great success.

Name: Néva Cuisine
Description: The Neva is not only a river in Russia, but also the name of this restaurant, headed by Mexican chef Beatriz González, after completing stints in top establishments including Lucas Carton and La Grande Cascade. In a friendly, modern Parisian bistro setting, she conjures up modern, multi-facetted cuisine, illustrated by blow torch-seared foie gras, smoked eel and dashi stock, or skate meunière with spring vegetables and a gutsy aïoli. Everything tastes of something here.

Name: Le Duc
Description: Despite being in the heart of the Left Bank, you would be forgiven for thinking you were in the cabin of a yacht packed with seafaring acolytes… The chef works with first-rate fish and seafood and is a consummate craftsman: tartare of langoustine with black lemon, sole meunière, lobster sautéed with orange, grilled John Dory… All aboard!

Name: Maison Daniel et Julia
Address: Route de Fabrégas, plage de Fabrégas, La Seyne-sur-Mer, 83500, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Julia is the soul of this hundred-year-old institution nestling in a charming cove. On the patio shaded by tamarisk trees, you can enjoy bouillabaisse and grilled wild fish. On Sundays during the summer, their authentic whole fish barbecues are a hit!

Name: La Grande Ourse
Description: This bistro named after the Ursa Major constellation has a down-to-earth decor done out in a palette of grey, plum and orange. The mouth-watering menu, concocted by a professional and focused chef, gives pride of place to fish, but doesn't exclude other fare; the cooking is technically sound, the flavours distinct, and the ingredients of high quality.

Name: Le Cornichon
Description: Armed with a CV that pulls no punches (Atelier Guy Martin, Lucas Carton, Grand Véfour), Sébastien Dagoneau has been working wonders since taking over Le Cornichon in January 2020. True to his word, he cooks up a fresh and tasty take on ingredient-led cuisine. This is as neo-bistro as it gets, with game in season and a fantastic list of organic and natural wines. Enjoy dishes such as beef chuck lasagne with sauce diable and a crunchy choux bun filled with a Bourbon vanilla cream.

Name: Le Petit Lucas
Address: 9 place de la Madeleine, Paris, 75008, France
Description: The bistro counterpart of Lucas Carton is accommodated on the first floor of the fine dining restaurant, in a space with a more low-key vibe (but with a view of the Église de la Madeleine). Chef Hugo Bourny's cuisine follows in the footsteps of fine French tradition (sole meunière, pâté en croute, chocolate mousse etc), thanks in particular to the quality of the ingredients used. The business menu, albeit without options, is a notable bargain in this upscale neighbourhood.

Name: La Régalade Saint-Honoré
Description: Bruno Doucet regales foodies in the Halles neighbourhood with dishes that sing an ode to fresh market and country produce. After titillating your tastebuds with the chef's delicious terrine, dig into pan-fried snails, mushrooms and chorizo, followed by braised chuck steak with a bourguignon garnish or the “famous” rice pudding with a dairy caramel. Fine wine list.

Name: Les Délices d'Aphrodite
Description: In this charming tavern-style restaurant, you could be forgiven for thinking you are in Greece! Freshly made, sun-drenched dishes such as marinated peppers, spit-roasted leg of lamb on a skewer, etc., all prepared with top-notch ingredients.

Name: Amphitryon
Address: 26 rue de la Boucherie, Limoges, 87000, France
Description: This pretty half - timbered house in the heart of the picturesque "village" around rue de la Boucherie is now the fief of chef Olivier Polla. He proposes modern cuisine that lets the ingredients do the talking, such as langoustine and angel hair pasta, lièvre à la royale, raspberry croquant and milk bastilla. A treat for the taste buds.

Name: Château de Rochecotte
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not far from the Bourgueil vineyards, this elegant château dating back to the Enlightenment is set in sumptuous grounds. In La Verrière with its contemporary decor and huge windows with views onto the greenery, or in the more classical dining area, enjoy fine dining-style cuisine, for instance, a fricassee of smoked eel in a Thai jus with lemongrass and coriander.

Name: Le Petit Saint Thomas
Address: 25 rue de Lattre de Tassigny, La Garnache, 85710, France
Description: This endearing family-run restaurant is popular with a crowd of locals. The chef, at the helm for over twenty years, painstakingly rustles up French staples, albeit with a tasty new twist and the odd hint of exoticism (curry, sobrassada, nori, mafé, coconut).

Name: Atmosphère
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Go up the splendid granite staircase, dripping with flowers and plants, to the entrance of this establishment with atmosphere by the bucketload. The pared-down, alpine interior sports a friendly, casual vibe. Should you be given the choice, ask for a table in the conservatory, which commands a knock-out view of the Arve River and the peaks of Chamonix in the distance! Recipes as Gallic as La Marseillaise, regional specialities and game in season take pride of place on the menu. Splendid wine list.

Name: Au Carillon Gourmand
Description: In this smart, elegant restaurant, dotted with designer touches and a subtle industrial loft vibe, diners can expect finely crafted, exquisitely presented modern dishes (carpaccio of gilthead seabream and medley of carrots). Warm welcome, swish service and fine tableware.

Name: Le Collet
Address: 9937 route de Colmar, Col de la Schlucht, 88400, France
Description: “Instinctive, last-minute” regional dishes, rustled up by a seasoned veteran who has trained many a local chef. In a picture postcard swish Alpine chalet décor, each dish celebrates and pays tribute to authentic regional produce.

Name: L'Atelier des Saveurs by Stéphane Garcia
Description: Fruit and veg from local producers, fish from local fishermen, meat from Southwest France and a knockout selection of Basque cheeses: the “flavour workshop” is fully equal to its name! Examples include a ballotine of Gers poultry stuffed with truffles and hazelnuts with green asparagus from St-Paul-de-Vence… A 100% Basque menu is available to order, in tribute to the youthful chef’s roots.

Name: Le Stofflet - Château Colbert
Description: What style! In the restaurant of this château, high ceilings and Louis XIV crystal chandeliers further enhance the experience of visiting gourmets. The food is contemporary and skilfully done. It is inspired by the terroir and is also made using vegetables from the garden.

Name: L'Astrolabe
Description: An astrolabe is a disc-shaped astronomical instrument that was used to calculate longitudes and latitudes, and this restaurant transports you from one country to another (from Finland to Guatemala) and from one cuisine to another. Each dish is depicted by a fusion of world culinary traditions, as is exemplified by the mohinga of line-caught whiting. A journey to be savoured in a bright, pleasant interior with a buzzy chic bistro vibe.

Name: Le Vioben
Description: Fish from small fishing boats, lobster and seafood, and, more generally, gourmet cuisine which highlights the fine local produce. It is not difficult to see why this establishment is such a hit with the locals, who also appreciate its warm contemporary décor, trendy light fixtures and the friendly, casual vibe.

Name: Maison de Laveline
Description: This rustic Vosges inn, depicted by a spruce yellow facade, is run by a youthful couple. The accent is clearly on wholesome French country fare and theme dinners based on a seasonal ingredient are organised throughout the year. Heart-warming dishes, such as melt-in-the-mouth veal chop and asparagus risotto. Meals are served in the recently refurbished dining room or on the patio in fine weather.

Name: 127 by amphi
Description: Sommelier Anthony Rault and chef Olivier Beurné took over from Jean-Paul Abadie at this local institution. The talented duo are keeping the quality high, while making their own mark. The menu, which is testament to inventive cuisine, features carefully prepared dishes replete with flavours, and top-notch seasonal produce (both meat and fish).

Name: La Table by La Villa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: La Table is part of La Villa, the luxurious decor of which is subjugated by the majesty of the panoramic view – the bay, the citadel, the mountains. It cultivates the beauties of the island, and quality regional produce… to sample on the superb panoramic terrace.

Name: L'Arbre
Description: This red-brick restaurant is located along the route of the legendary Paris-Roubaix cycling race and serves flavoursome food that makes perfect sense. The committed young chef prepares a surprise set menu featuring seasonal and local ingredients in well-crafted dishes, such as line-caught sea bass with broccoli and a creamed fish fumet – delicious and impressive! A pleasant terrace for fine weather.

Name: Etchemaïté
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this mountainous area on the edge of the Basque Country, this traditional establishment is simply charming. It is also the repository of a family history going back four generations.
