Ximun has now taken up the mantle, serving delicious traditional cuisine, characterised by generous portions and tasty well-matured broths and jus. The ingredients are local, and the suppliers are duly listed on the menu. This is comforting fare (think duck raviolo, mix of mushrooms, langoustine bisque; "Axuria" lamb: pressed lamb, macaroni gratin, Xipister, lamb jus), to enjoy in the bright, somewhat rustic-style interior with a superb view of the Pyrenees!

Name: Dupin
Description: Near Le Bon Marché department store, this restaurant champions flavoursome bistronomic cooking, underscored by a steadfast commitment to ecology and local produce. The fruit and vegetables are sourced from the Île-de-France region, organic waste is recycled, water filtered on site, etc. Respect for nature and a passion for "good living" come together in food.

Name: La Fleur de Sel
Description: This modern building en route to the ski resorts serves appetising seasonal cuisine made with quality ingredients comprising regularly changing menus. The interior is modern and cosy, with as a focal point the lovely fireplace crackling in the middle of the room. Delightful.

Name: Le Bistrot
Description: On Île St Laurent, a contemporary restaurant offering a well-crafted lunchtime menu at prices that make sense. For example, warm mushroom mousse with vin jaune and a creamy Mont d’Or cheese topping. The evening menu is more elaborate (foie gras, turbot, lobster). Some of the super fresh vegetables and fruit come from the kitchen garden.

Name: Restaurant du Port
Description: After a walk around the headland, where the pretty beaches are too many to count, head to the little port. At the restaurant, tuck into the catch of the day, turbot fillet, oysters from Sterec, or the lovely sole meunière, which the chef, a pro who has worked under chefs Michel Trama and Stéphane Carrade, complements with a bowl of new potatoes, fine green asparagus, snow peas and confit red pepper. Pleasantly informal atmosphere.

Name: Marnage - Hôtel La Marine
Description: With its panoramic view of the sea and the port, this local institution on the Cotentin peninsula faces the Channel Islands of Jersey and Guernsey. In a pleasant contemporary interior, you will sample modern, elegant cuisine that shines the limelight on Normandy produce, with a weakness for local seafood, illustrated by pollock, fennel (confit and roasted) and a lemon-flavoured butter emulsion.

Name: La Maison
Description: This attractive house in the town centre is built of white stone and has a relaxed atmosphere inside. The cuisine is eclectic, with multiple influences (Asia, the Mediterranean, South America): pan-fried squid with garlic and red chilli; lamb shoulder confit with cumin, tchoutchouka (roasted pepper and tomato salad); beef tenderloin, panko with herbs and chimichurri sauce. Be sure to try the house cocktails featuring cognac.

Name: La Table du Marché
Description: Owner-chef Stéphane Cuzin has been at the helm of this street corner bistro with a distinctive red façade and a snazzy, modish interior for many years now. It faces Bergerac’s covered market, where Stéphane sources the majority of his ingredients. Creative recipes and unusual seasonings set the tone: tonka, nutmeg, cumin and coffee may underscore veal, spinach or asparagus.

Name: La Flèche d'Argent
Address: Hôtel Princesse Flore, 5 place Allard, Royat, 63130, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: La Flèche d'Argent – the name is a nod to the incredible "Silver Arrows" Mercedes-Benz Formula 1 cars of the 1930s – references the nearby Circuit de Charade racetrack. In a plush decor, chef Clément Lorente serves up his contemporary cuisine in a multi-course set menu format. His dishes display excellent technique and incorporate creative touches. The ingredients are of the highest quality: foie gras from the Plaine de Limagne, artichokes from Roussillon, saffron from Mazayes, bluefin tuna from the Mediterranean. For dessert, a tribute to the chef's grandmother's Agen prune flan is a real hit, flambéed tableside. Market-based set menu at lunchtime; brunch on Sundays.

Name: Carré des Sens
Description: In a pretty spot on one of the city's central squares, this building is the stomping ground of a chef who revisits classics from French tradition with passion and precision: boiled egg, fricassee of chanterelles and parsley emulsion; chuck of beef cooked at a low temperature, potato galette and truffle jus; hot soufflé with Grand Marnier – quality ingredients go into these delicious and carefully executed dishes.

Name: Auberge de Cassagne & Spa
Address: 450 allée de Cassagne, Le Pontet, 84130, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This old Provençal bastide on the outskirts of Avignon upholds the traditions of Gallic bourgeois establishments devoted to good food. Noble produce and classical recipes are the name of the game, albeit with the occasional more modern creation, such as tataki of house smoked salmon on a pannacotta of green vegetables. Southern Côte du Rhône wines take pride of place in the cellar. Lovely terrace in fine weather and polished service.

Name: La Bastide
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant has an elegant setting full of character and offers two styles of cuisine. Choose from light, healthy dishes for visitors having treatments at the baths (different choices available every day) or hearty fare that combines regional traditions with fine contemporary cuisine.

Name: Blisss
Description: In the suburbs just outside Bordeaux, this modern restaurant proves to be a wonderful surprise. It has an intimate and immaculate decor featuring made-to-measure furniture and crockery that matches the ethos expressed in the food. Let Anthony Aycaguer transport you with his interactive menus, presented as a series of riddles based on seasonal produce (diners have to guess the ingredients). An unusual experience! Booking is essential.

Name: Le Coq d'Or
Description: ‘The Golden Cockerel’ is aptly named: the interior is full of the birds – brought back by customers from their travels! As for the food, expect an array of fine, well - crafted dishes that offer a creative take on local specialities.

Name: Les Années 30
Description: Trinkets, little paintings and photos from the 1930s contribute to the charm of this restaurant in Chinon's old town. Contemporary cuisine made with fresh ingredients.

Name: Le Vieux Moulin
Description: This restaurant housed in an old mill sports a cheerful interior and a splendid fireplace for cosy winter moments. In summer, the riverside terrace is the perfect spot to dig into appetising, market-fresh food, whose original and well-crafted recipes focus on locally sourced produce.

Name: Le 5ème Péché
Address: 16 rue de la Fraternité, Collioure, 66190, France
Description: This small restaurant in Collioure's old town is run by a chef from Tokyo, who is passionate about French food and wine. Here, Japan meets Catalonia in fusion cuisine that stars ultra-fresh fish. A prime example is the rockfish soup with coconut milk, braised ox cheek with banyuls and prawns. Remember to book well in advance.

Name: A Nepita
Description: English born chef Simon Andrews, a former Michelin star holder, fell head over heels with Corsica. He goes to the market every day to painstakingly select local ingredients, which he then meticulously crafts: red tuna, denti, seabass, brocciu, veal, etc. Some of his signature dishes are always on the menu, such as grilled squid or his medley of local fish, to the delight of regulars and tourists alike. The chef also enjoys scattering his dishes with wild marjoram (“nepita”, after which the restaurant is named). The cheerful front-of-house service is managed by Simon’s wife, Corsican born Roberta.

Name: L'Estellan
Description: Amid vineyards and olive groves, it is difficult not to fall in love with this inviting country house. The staff bends over backwards to make sure your stay is relaxing and that you really take your time. Run by a couple with an extensive catering career already under their belt, they know what they want and how to get there: first-class, regional produce, modern, flavoursome recipes and a concise, mouth-watering slate menu, illustrated by rack of farm-reared pork and butter of cèpe mushrooms.

Name: Le Martin Pêcheur
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Between the Canal des Mines de Fer de la Moselle and the Moselle, this former fisherman's house (1928) exudes the appealing spirit of a country inn and is embellished with a pretty summer garden. Here, tradition mingles with modern trends, and the cellar is well stocked.

This superb medieval château seems bent on upholding the opulent traditions of banquets of yore… Take a seat by the imposing, delicately carved Gothic fireplace and dig into a feast of infinite refinement. The strawberry-rhubarb dessert is to die for: crunchy strawberry topping, savory-flavoured pannacotta and fresh strawberry purée with a rhubarb sorbet. Wickedly tempting!

Name: Le San Felice
Address: 3001 route des Hauts-du-Camp, au Circuit Paul Ricard, Le Castellet, 83330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: San Felice is not only a Dumas novel: at the Hôtel du Castellet, it is also a swish, imaginative bistro! The menu is deliberately concise, with a seasonal line-up and a mouth-watering focus on matured meats and fish cooked over hot embers. The terrace by the swimming pool commands a drop-dead view of the golf course and greenery. Treat yourself to the lunchtime ‘Gourmand’ menu (Mon to Sat).

Name: Au Lavoir
Description: Adjacent to the Canal du Midi, this lovely yellow building seems to shine, especially when the lush green garden (with terrace) is bathed in sunlight. Fully inspired by the Mediterranean, the cooking lets the ingredients enjoy the limelight and exudes the flavours of the South of France. Do not hesitate to book one of the elegant guestrooms upstairs.

Name: Le Lancelot
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the centre of the village, this welcoming flower-decked place with a garden and terrace is a real oasis of calm. Cosy setting and cuisine that navigates between tradition and modernity (notably the melt-in-the-mouth pithivier pie, rum crème brûlée, pistachio ice cream), not forgetting Sologne game in season.

Name: La Réserve
Description: In the 16C former garrison food storeroom, nowadays the Citadelle hotel, Aurélien Person’s cooking demonstrates a gourmet streak paired with a generous nature: stone-bass tartare with fennel, mange-tout and preserved lemon ; seared scallops with chorizo and riso venere, fillet of beef with local bacon and carrots… A storeroom with plenty of surprises in store!

Name: Ko-sometsuke 2K
Address: 156 boulevard de la Plage, Arcachon, 33120, France
Description: Originally from Cambodia, the Khong family settled in Arcachon, and now they are the ones inviting diners on a journey: from China and Japan to Southeast Asia, using regional ingredients. Don't miss the dim sum, the real stars of the show, wrapped in a remarkably fine dough.

Name: La Table du Lavoir - Les Sources de Caudalie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This handsome hall (18C) built entirely out of wood was where the clothes worn during the grape harvest were washed. The menu is traditional: marinade of trout, sea bream a la plancha, rib of beef and béarnaise sauce, Bordeaux canelés. A treat for the eyes and the palate.

Name: L'Aspérule
Description: Sited in an old house in historic Auxerre, the dining room sports a minimalist look with a polished concrete floor and beige walls. The Japanese chef crafts cuisine that pairs local produce with the millimetric accuracy of his homeland, depicted by perfectly rare duckling fillet, duxelles of shiitake mushrooms, balsamic sauce. Sensibly priced lunchtime market menu, more ambitious in the evening.

Name: Loiseau des Vignes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The food here is stamped with the Bernard Loiseau hallmark and served in a "chic bistro" atmosphere (stone, wood and velvet-upholstered banquettes set the tone). The menu includes classics such as eggs in a red wine sauce, pâté en croûte, Charolais ox cheek and Saône catfish, and beautifully fresh Burgundy veal tartare with smoked eel. There is a good wine list with around 50 options.

Name: Le Pérou
Description: Pulpo anticuchero, lomo saltado, tiradito, arroz cremoso, and, of course, the indispensable ceviches: all the classics of Peruvian cooking are on the menu here in the Alps, thanks to a chef and her team, who all hail from Peru. Much of the produce is imported direct from the Andes, via Spain. Anyone who has been lucky enough to taste authentic South American food will be delighted by the incredible range of flavours and tastes of this cuisine rich in seasoning and unexpected ingredients on offer.

Name: Le 180°
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name is an expression used in Belle - Isle - en - Mer to refer to the indefinable colour of the sea... Indeed this would be just the spot to discuss its nuances: the dining area affords breathtaking views over Goulphar cove! At the helm, the chef concocts original recipes using the best ingredients the island has to offer. Enjoy the crossing!

Name: Le Chardenoux
Description: In this Parisian bistro founded by the Chardenoux family and a listed historic monument, the eye wanders from the beautiful painted ceiling to the Art nouveau details, before it is drawn back to the business at hand, the enticing menu in front of us. Fish and seafood are the name of the game here, including Lignac’s iconic signature dishes: lobster roll, salt-crusted sea bass, tuna tartar, avocado, ponzu, wasabi, without forgetting the decadent millefeuille or the rum baba! We fell in love with the crunchy savoury pancake of curry-flavoured crab and avocado: a masterpiece of balanced flavours.

Name: Le Bistrot Flaubert
Description: An inviting space with a delightfully quaint feel, its wooden shelves accommodating bottles of wine and a few old Michelin Guides – this place has all the trappings of an authentic Parisian bistro! Adjoining its parent restaurant, Maison Rostang, Le Bistrot has been an integral part of neighbourhood life for several decades and is popular with MPs and businessmen alike. Serving well-crafted dishes that are rife with flavour, it promises a great experience, right through to the light dessert.

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye
Description: A small medieval village. Tucked away from view, a 12C tower casts a shadow onto a stone wall, and behind this wall you come across this charming inn, which is certainly worth getting to know! Here they serve good traditional food that is at one with the monastic atmosphere of the place, all vaulted ceilings and stone walls.

Name: Le Contemporain
Description: This family home dating back to the 19C was converted into a restaurant in 2008. At the helm, an experienced couple: she works in the kitchen, showcasing the home - grown produce by creating tasty dishes; he is in charge of front of house, as well as upkeep of the vegetable garden. Modern, light - filled conservatory.

Name: La Ferme Saint-Sébastien
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This authentic mid-19C Bourbon farmhouse, next to the fortified city of Charroux, is a pleasant spot to sit down and enjoy the simple dishes concocted by the owner, especially on sunny days on the terrace. Diners appreciate the contemporary cuisine, palpably influenced by the terroir, such as the zucchini fritters with chives sauce. A good place.

Name: L'Îlot Vert
Description: This restaurant, which feels like a smart bistro, ticks all the boxes. Here, Tony Regnier, who trained at some prestigious establishments, conjures up really modern cuisine with creative touches, flawlessly executed and flavoursome, to be savoured in a tastefully decorated room, or on the pretty flower-filled terrace. The guinea fowl and pistachio terrine served with apple chutney left a lasting impression!

Name: Le Voilier
Description: Drop anchor in the marina and climb on board this elegant yacht to sample fresh Mediterranean cuisine (fish soup and carpaccio, ceviche, courgette blossoms) in which the local catch (whole or in portions) takes pride of place. Meat lovers are, however, not forgotten and the menu also offers dishes such as a thick juicy veal cutlet or stuffed saddle of lamb.

Name: Le Cromesquis
Description: After an impressive career working in Michelin - starred restaurants in Switzerland, the chef has returned home, to his wife's region. In an unusual setting – a former forge that has been refurbished with a lot of wood, concrete and picture windows –, he proposes modern and delicious dishes with, of course, a cromesquis (croquette) featuring every day among the starters.

Name: Fouquet's
Description: A restaurant in the Royal Hotel, typical of the large seaside hotels of the early 20C. The cosy wood panelling and the photos of actors by Studio Harcourt recall the atmosphere of the Parisian Fouquet's. The menu is inspired by brasserie fare (seafood, sole meunière, fillet of beef with Béarnaise sauce, andouillette, profiteroles), but there are also light dishes – as you would expect at a seawater therapy resort.

Name: La Source des Sens
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The setting is strikingly contemporary, with black walls and carpeting and atmospheric lighting. The food is equally up-to-date, thanks to the commitment of chef Pierre Weller, who slips in the odd tribute to Japan’s culinary culture, while excelling in the art of precise plating, demonstrated by his arctic char makis with green asparagus, orange foam and pistou. The Source also proposes guestrooms for overnight stays, together with a luxurious spa to pamper your senses.

Name: La Marmite du Pêcheur
Address: Boulevard des Tilleuls, Les Mées, 04190, France
Description: This restaurant is set at the foot of the village’s famous pointed rocks. It serves fish and seafood specialities (bouillabaisse to order) in a modern decor.

Name: Influences
Description: A wind of revival is blowing through this venerable institution, which has changed hands but not name and is still located in a quiet street near Place Gambetta. The handsome sandstone façade now ushers guests into the lair of a youthful couple, cheerful Kéveena, in the front of house and Ismaël who gives free rein to his solid background in the kitchen. Modern, tasty dishes which mainly star ingredients from southwest France, jazzed up with the odd creative twist, like a grilled duck magret, punchy gravy and Japanese-style lacquered aubergine sprinkled in puffed rice. Seamless, smiling service.

Name: La Charrette Bleue
Description: You can't miss this 18C coaching inn with its blue cart on the roof, in a nod to René Barjavel's eponymous book in which he recounts his childhood in this part of the world. The spirit of the region is everywhere, from the terrace shaded by a reed canopy to the generous regional cuisine, examples of which are a terrine of marbled ham, warm potato salad with a spicy ravigote sauce and a decadent île flottante (egg whites in custard) in a culinary lineup as patriotic as the Marseillaise!

Name: Hiély-Lucullus
Address: 5 rue de la République, Avignon, 84000, France
Description: Chef Gérald Azoulay, a native of Avignon, has created an astonishing culinary amalgam of the cuisines of Peru (where his wife Patricia was born) and Provence, dubbing it "Pérouvence". Different Peruvian spices and a commitment to sustainable development guide the chef who takes us on a flavoursome globetrotting journey dominated by acidity, spices and embers: trout in goat’s cheese, aji chaparita and green asparagus; picanha of marinated veal in aji panca spices and Chapa pepper; a Provençal cachaille (cheese) flavoured with a Peruvian species of marigold. The interior is decorated in the Belle Epoque style. The wine list stars tipples from both countries.

Name: Pianovins
Description: Both formerly of the Guy Savoy, Michel Roncière and Éric Mancio have joined forces: the first in the kitchen, the second in the wine cellar. The menu is well designed and prepared according to market availability. Meals are served in a small dining room (20 seats at tightly packed tables) with an open kitchen and counter dining.

Name: L'Assaggio
Address: Castille Paris, 37 rue Cambon, Paris, 75001, France
Description: Assaggio is all about taste! Chef Ugo Alciati (of Guido Ristorante, in Piedmont) devised the menu for this elegant restaurant in the Hôtel Castille. As expected, Northern Italy takes pride of place in the dishes – house-made agnolotti, risotto minute... The pastas are quite something: the spaghettone with lobster, lemon zest, confit tomatoes and trout roe is absolutely delicious. Tables are laid out in the delightful interior patio adorned with a fountain and frescoes.

Name: L'epicurius
Description: In a charming pedestrian street in the old part of Rouen, this trendy bistro serves fine and tasty cuisine, such as bluefin tuna with pea mousseline, cockles and haddock emulsion, or red berry vacherin with a herb sorbet… Carefully selected ingredients, to be enjoyed in a contemporary interior. Charming welcome.

Name: Nestou
Description: Just a few strokes from Catalans beach, this restaurant pays homage to Ernest (Nestou), the young son of Jean-Philippe and Jeanne Garbin, who are the joint chefs of this endearing family establishment. He supervises the hot dishes, while she is in charge of the starters and desserts and together, they devise unusual recipes that surf between Mediterranean influences and more globetrotting inspirations. A great place for a meal with the mates!

Name: Sandikala
Address: 9 rue de la Barsogue, Galan, 65330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Australian-born Luke MacLeod and his wife from Tarbes fell for the charm of this old farmstead and have done it up in a tasteful country chic vein. The chef concocts delicious seasonal cuisine that allies local produce with ingredients from further afield.

Name: Symbiose
Description: Modern and skilfully balanced cuisine, with creative touches and a predilection for spices, not to mention neat presentations: this is what Symbiose has in store for you. The couple who run the show know where they're going and are delighting in the journey.

Name: Juste à Côté
Description: Simplicity is a central tenet of this former roadside eatery transformed into a bistro by chef Olivier Foulon, assisted on the restaurant floor by his wife Amandine and a team of efficient, smiling servers. Though classic, the menu – pâté en croûte, monkfish à l'armoricaine and riz au lait – changes daily to cater to a large clientele of lunchtime regulars.

Name: Oxalis
Description: This ancient edifice, whose oldest stones date back to the 13C, oozes historical cachet (exposed beams and stonework, vaulted cellar that can be rented out for private events), while the open kitchen behind a glass partition and splendid rough-hewn wooden tables add a contemporary touch. The chef-owner, whose CV boasts some top Parisian establishments, conjures up tasty dishes in a bistronomic vein at lunchtime (e.g. burrata with truffle and beetroot seasoning; seabream with aubergine caviar), with a more high-flying score in the evening (white asparagus and scallops; seabass, baby artichoke and cashew nuts).

Name: Opaline
Description: In this modern, spruce little restaurant located next to the Comédie La Rochelle theatre, the cuisine is the handiwork of a motivated young couple who met at Alexandre Mazzia. The pair's trademark is creative, colourful cuisine, each dish coming with three satellite-style variations, such as hake with peas and cabbage, accompanied by lentils with a haddock emulsion and a seaweed blini with home-made taramasalata on the side. Bistronomy-style formule menu at lunchtime; for dinner, their fine dining tasting menus, which change every four months or so, comprise different numbers of "sequences".

Name: Le Doyenné
Description: What are two Australian chefs (with stints at Yard, Spring, Bones and Au Passage) doing in the heart of the grounds of Saint Vrain Castle, more precisely in the tastefully refurbished former stables? Well, they are knocking up spot-on food that is sourced directly from the estate’s huge cottage garden, which actually existed before the restaurant, using fruit and vegetables that are only harvested when perfectly ripe. A fine dining experience that mingles rural charm and gourmet delights, overlooking the surrounding countryside. Booking compulsory.

Name: Jardin Secret
Description: Back from the rock of Monaco, Benoît Witz has hung his hat in a pretty estate in Provence. In the shade of olive groves and released from gastronomic codes, he crafts 100% authentic dishes in a style that he himself joyfully describes as “grandma’s country cooking”! Garden-fresh beefsteak tomatoes, fish of the day with summer veggies, melt-in-the-mouth chocolate cake. Scrumptious and generous – yummy!

Name: L'Hermine
Description: This very pleasant crêperie in a picturesque pedestrian area has wooden beams, polished wooden tables and rustic objects. Choose from some 50 savoury buckwheat and sweet pancakes.

Name: Le Manoir des Impressionnistes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Settle in at your table, in the bright dining room or on sunny days head for the terrace to enjoy the lovely view of the estuary. Savour the modern cuisine, centred on a short and appetising seasonal menu that gives top billing to Normandy's produce from land and sea.

Name: Entre Terre et Mer
Description: On a square near the Vieux Bassin, this restaurant does as its name suggests. This applies to both the decor (photos of cows, sheep and fish) and the cuisine fluctuating between land and sea. Nice oyster bar in the hotel opposite.

Name: Bistrot Instinct
Description: This pocket handkerchief contemporary bistro is in the hands of chef Maximilian Wollek and his enthusiastic youthful team. A market-fresh culinary score and updated classics with bistronomic overtones. Everything is homemade, even the cordials used in the unusual cocktails.

Name: Hôtel du Phare
Description: Belle-Île-en-Mer's emblematic Hôtel du Phare (1880) and its restaurant have been redesigned and revamped by a famous architect. The decor is original, juxtaposing bright colours with the black and white of the Breton flag. The menu focuses on marine flavours, with dishes such as spider crab in its shell, bisque, celeriac ravioli with spider crab; viennoise of sea bass cooked on a stone, artichoke fricassee with clams and black garlic. As much as he can, the chef uses quality ingredients, often from the island (eg lamb reared in Bangor, honey, organic vegetables and fish from a local fisherman). There is a lovely terrace overlooking the harbour, and further dining options at Le Bistrot.

Name: Le Turenne
Description: Modern cuisine is served in this restaurant that combines original stone walls with contemporary design. On fine days the gorgeous terrace adds to the gourmet experience.

Name: L'Écusson
Description: Proudly flying the fine dining flag, the chef, who trained in prestigious establishments (La Côte Saint-Jacques, Lameloise and La Pyramide), crafts a fresh, colourful score that is often jazzed up with citrus fruits. The result is often inspired, illustrated by langoustine and tourteau crab, leeks, buckwheat, watercress and smoked yoghurt or scallops, Belgian endive, salsify and clementines… Meals are served in a bright, contemporary interior.

Name: Jòia par Hélène Darroze
Description: Hélène Darroze's restaurant draws on her memories of her native southwestern corner of France, with nods to the Basque Country, Landes and Béarn. Strong flavours and emblematic dishes (chipirones from Saint-Jean de Luz fried with chorizo, Carnaroli rice with squid ink, parsley and parmesan emulsion), to be enjoyed alone or to share, and desserts that awaken your sweet tooth (chocolate chou with Espelette chilli, peanut praline).

Name: Gaya - Cuisine de Bords de Mer par Pierre Gagnaire
Address: Avenue de la Falaise, Châtelaillon-Plage, 17340, France
Description: Part of La Grande Terrasse hotel, not far from Les Boucholeurs, this restaurant gives seafood pride of place. The menu designed by Pierre Gagnaire comprises generous dishes with finely crafted jus, sauces and creams. The wine list boasts some 700 labels. Tuck into your meal in a cosy interior with a splendid view of the ocean.

Name: Fenêtre sur Cour
Description: Seared scallops, butternut squash and bacon foam; lightly smoked beef fillet, parsnips and candied shallots; sole fillets, white shimeji mushrooms and smoked butter – Jean-Luc Paulhan seamlessly creates meticulous, tasty cuisine, rife with contemporary flavours. The mezzanine room to the rear (with its window overlooking the courtyard) doubles up as a terrace during the summer months.

Name: La Table du Centenaire
Address: 2 avenue du Cingle, Les Eyzies-de-Tayac-Sireuil, 24620, France
Description: Previously an oyster farmer working in the Bassin d'Arcachon, chef Mathieu Métifet draws his inspiration from the Périgord terroir, weaving in fish and seafood elements to create generous, personal cuisine, of which his signature dish is a good example: "Le Centenaire's unmissable razor clams with a morel cream and home-smoked magret de canard". Hand-picked small-scale local producers.

Name: Le Dallaison
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The beautiful exterior of this 18C manor house set in grounds gives little away. Inside, the 21C makes itself felt throughout the various dining nooks: designer furniture, original lights, white walls, wine cabinets. A place like this can only inspire Jérôme Dallet, a chef who has worked with Emmanuel Renaut (Megève) and Anne-Sophie Pic (Valence). Local produce is given pride of place (mogette beans, snails, Confolens lamb…) and the chef uses it to create wonderfully indulgent compositions. In fine weather, you can enjoy the terrace surrounded by greenery.

Name: Dante
Description: After a period of purgatory, this hip establishment in Rue de Paradis is back in favour thanks to an enthusiastic young chef who fell in love with haute cuisine after an internship with Alain Passard. Rébecca Beaufour consummately crafts fiendishly flavoursome bistronomic dishes, such as lobster and king prawn ravioles or crisp sweetbread served with squash and apple caramel. The house also offers a range of dishes to share, like pigeon or whole seabream cooked in salt.

Name: Bord'eau
Address: 17 rue de la Poissonnerie, Colmar, 68000, France
Description: This spinoff by two-star chef Jean-Yves Schillinger is located next to the Lauch River in the heart of Little Venice. The menu allows the chef to express his creativity in recipes that blend Asian traditions with local Alsace produce. Carrots roasted in hay, herby snail fritters and salted kumquats, or pollock with pumpkin purée, maki of vegetables and yuzu gel. Contemporary decor.

Name: Martin Comptoir
Description: A stone’s throw from the market (ideal for fresh produce), the clientele is drawn by the work of youthful chef, Martin Dumas, also a local lad. His culinary score, perfectly in tune with today’s tastes, features a brief seasonal menu, generous hunks of meat to be shared and the house speciality, “thickly sliced calf’s liver”, which he learnt from Jean-Paul Arabian in Paris. Small, quiet terrace.

Name: Jeff envoie du bois !!!
Address: 12 place de la Libération, Auch, 32000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fresh ingredients sourced from the market where chef Thomas Lloret goes twice a week, a spacious terrace on Place de la Libération, a tasteful, elegant exterior, a black and white interior décor and up-to-the-minute market-fresh cuisine. The overwhelming popularity of this canteen-cum-bistro is further reinforced by a fine selection of local vintages.

Name: Les Magnolias
Address: 48 avenue de Bry, Le Perreux-sur-Marne, 94170, France
Description: A young chef is now at the helm of this pleasant restaurant. He pays particular attention to the presentation of his dishes, which are full of flavour and strewn with Asian influences. In the kitchen and the elegant dining room, his young team pulls out all the stops to please.

Name: Auprès du Clocher
Description: Young chef Rémi Genot has come back to his roots in this famous wine-growing village, after a glittering career in the region. He pays homage to local producers and showcases the fine cuts of meat prepared by his father in the neighbouring butchery. As comfortable working with vegetables as with fish and meat, he creates meticulous dishes that are replete with colour and character. He is also skilled at juxtaposing different textures, in dishes such as white asparagus tartlet with mandarin and taggiasca olives; Quercy lamb cooked three ways, black garlic jus and a medley of carrots. Needless to say, the superb wine list revolves around Burgundy.

Name: Monsieur Bleu
Description: For a location in Paris, it would be hard to do better than this address... Nestled in the Palais de Tokyo, it is superb with its Art Deco interior in a palette of grey, green and gold, and its terrace looking out over the Seine and the Eiffel Tower. Not to be outdone by the setting, the food is sophisticated and tasty. A very high - profile place!

Name: La Poule au Pot
Description: The great classics of the French culinary repertoire are given an overhaul here by Jean-François Piège. Service on a silver tray, old-fashioned bistro decor, zinc counter: it has all the trappings. It's Audiard's Paris down to a T... right down to the food: onion gratinée, quenelle of arctic char, beef chuck hash, Colbert fried whiting with tartar sauce.

Name: La Fourchette du Printemps
Description: In this elegant little neighbourhood bistro, the young chef has come through some top establishments. He hones the taste of quality ingredients (the menu evolves according to the market), and takes pleasure in revisiting the classics. A good place.

Name: L'Agapé Bistrot
Description: Just a stone's throw from Guérande's famous fortified wall, this family-run bistro with a sober contemporary decor serves appetising cuisine that combines regional ingredients (catch of the day, seaweed, pork, butter milk, buckwheat) with more exotic touches (spices, ginger, lemongrass, coconut etc). The resulting dishes are hearty, meticulous and balanced: quite a feast!

Name: La Table d'Émilie
Description: At the helm of this friendly restaurant, Émilie and Yoann showcase first-rate produce in the form of a market-fresh set menu that offers excellent value for money at lunchtime and sets its sights higher in the evening. The chef has a sure touch, especially when it comes to desserts. In fine weather, head for the pleasant garden terrace.

Name: Café des Ministères
Description: The name of this bistro that is reminiscent of a neighbourhood café is on the lips of every fan of wonderfully rich sauces and authentic French cuisine (especially South-Western fare). The vol-au-vent with sweetbreads, poultry and truffle jus, as well as the stuffed Pontoise cabbage (French champion in 2022) have put this place on the map: book in advance!

Name: La Table du Caviste Bio
Description: A few well - polished, leather footfalls from Parc Monceau and you are in this stylish restaurant combining a modern dining room and food that is in tune with current tastes, fresh and subtle, concocted by Japanese culinary artist, Junko Kawasaki. The matching wines are naturally organic.

Name: La Passerelle
Description: It was love at first sight when the chef, who hails from Orléans, saw this restaurant located on the edge of Le Havre de la Vanlée, which offers an ideal landscape for walks among the salt meadow sheep. Now well established, it serves contemporary market cuisine that is fresh and tasty, for example the monkfish, chorizo and leek. A pleasant place.

Name: Bouche B
Description: The Bouche B on the "Place Gourmande" of this village near Reims is the HQ of chef Thibault Laplaige (previously Michelin starred in Reims). His modern, well-crafted dishes rely on top-drawer produce such as tartare of scallops and fennel with soy vinaigrette or braised Black Angus in a sort of “applejack” jus with buttered green cabbage. Bouche B for "Bon"!

Name: Blanc
Description: This family inn features two enticing options: an elegant, contemporary restaurant, with a well-designed menu based on fine ingredients, or the chalet-inspired wooden interior of the brasserie, where Savoie cheese specialities take pride of place (alongside frogs' legs and pike). Comfortable guestrooms, for those who wish to stay longer the region.

Name: Auberge du Bois Prin
Description: In a smart, contemporary vibe overlooking the legendary Mont Blanc, Emmanuel Renaut and his team craft an Alpine score with a weakness for produce from the garden and the surrounding meadows. Mouth-watering modern dishes steeped in generous, delicate flavours: tartare of beetroot, celery and horseradish sauce; loin of roast venison, stuffed cabbage, game sauce; citrus fruit soufflé…The view from the terrace is particularly breathtaking.

Name: Amapola Kitchen
Description: The superlative location, at the foot of Pont Vieux overlooking the historic town and its stunning cathedral, is definitely Instagram worthy. This cleverly revamped pocket handkerchief bistro is in the hands of a former art historian, whose healthy, colourful, well-crafted dishes to be shared hit the spot every time. This unorthodox, fine food DJ mixes South American, Italian and Comorian influences, with a generous scattering of lacto fermented ingredients and a definite preference for organic sources, such as the Comorian-style minced beef flanked by red onion and chervil pickles and the delicious house houmous. Fine selection of organic and natural wines.

Name: Olivier Leflaive
Description: A plush house in the centre of the village, a glass-paned wine cellar, a bar with an Art Deco look, a chic and inviting dining room: welcome to Olivier Leflaive's place! The famous Côte de Beaune winegrower has created two eateries. Le Bistro d'Olivier offers a seasonal menu inspired by local produce, and the restaurant Klima has more fine dining ambitions. Great wine list, needless to say, thanks to the estate's 80 appellations.

Name: L'AbSix
Address: 2 rue de la Cerdagne, Saleilles, 66280, France
Description: Do not be misled by the colonial feel of this large building, you can trust the experienced chef to surprise your taste buds. With a single set menu that changes weekly, he cooks up modern and creative dishes that reflect the seasons: croustillant with parmesan, marinated chanterelles and a sweet garlic cream; turbot fillet tempura, coconut, lemongrass and a ginger emulsion.

Name: Dersou
Description: In a pleasant side street near Bastille, Dersou proposes the original experience of pairing food and cocktails in a trendy atmosphere complete with music. A dish of leeks with a coarse grain mustard cream and sorrel vinaigrette is accompanied by a dill, yuzu, gin and Granny Smith apple cocktail; guinea fowl with tangy beetroot puree is paired with a whisky, port and orange cocktail judiciously. The ingredients are top quality and the mixology does not disappoint.

Name: Il Goto
Address: 212 bis rue de Charenton, Paris, 75012, France
Description: This really lovely restaurant is run by Marzia and Simone, an Italian couple who are passionate about what they do. Mozzarella di bufala and sweet and sour vegetables; tagliatelle with veal confit and taggiasche olives; torta with mascarpone cream and lemon – tasty, well-prepared creations, to be washed down with a good Italian red wine!

Name: La Corniche - Sainte-Barbe
Description: Sainte Barbe Hotel offers a choice of Instagrammable views looking out to sea or of the harbour. La Corniche sports and elegant contemporary vibe. Finely crafted cuisine, recipes of bistronomic inspiration with a distinct preference for local fish and seafood. The rooftop bar is heaven for a drink before or after dinner.

Name: La Gare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A very contemporary local institution (since 1874)! It has a perfect combination of elegance, vitality and conviviality, offering a brasserie for those in a hurry or carefully-prepared modern cuisine in a conservatory setting... Goat’s cheese and vegetable terrine, or thick veal chop with morel mushrooms and gnocchi, all accompanied by one of the finest wine lists in the country.

Name: Au Déjeuner de Sousceyrac
Description: A chef dedicated to his craft, Patrick Lagnès draws on solid classical foundations and fine produce to deliver high-quality cuisine. He even tries out a few more contemporary dishes when the inspiration takes him, while desserts are the work of his daughter. Diners are served in the intimate setting of a small dining area done out in traditional style with wainscoting and period furnishings.

Name: Empreinte
Address: 170 avenue de l'Hippodrome, à Lambersart, Lille, 59000, France
Description: Near the old racecourse, tucked away in a residential area, this restaurant with refined decor occupies a 1950s house. Chef Ismail Guerre-Genton crafts creative cuisine, the core ingredients of which are plant-based: vegetable tartlet and watercress; trout, endive and kimchi; dark chocolate, buckwheat and green cardamom – his surprise menus home in on seasonal ingredients.

Name: Umami - La Cinquième Saveur
Description: Not even a stone’s throw from Place de la Canourgue, this small bistro with a minimalist interior invites you to sample the chef’s French-Korean cuisine, dotted with Japanese notes. This talented chef works exclusively with fresh produce, changes the menu every couple of months (except for classics such as the bibimbap) and, of course, shines the spotlight on umami flavours, illustrated by chawanmushi, an egg and shrimp flan with edamame and a dashi stock. Bookings essential.

Name: Le Christine
Description: In a quiet little street, you will spot the inviting façade of this restaurant, where the conviviality and generosity are first apparent on the (short and appetising) menu, then in the nicely crafted dishes, which always include a vegetarian option. Thank you, Christine, and see you soon.

Name: Le Bon Saint-Pourçain
Description: Tucked away behind St Sulpice church in the heart of the high - brow Saint Germain des Prés district, this former 'bougnat' restaurant reopened in the spring of 2015. Bistro traditions with a modern twist depict the delicious food – doubtless due to the high quality fresh produce. Booking advisable!

Name: ASPIC
Description: After ditching the world of finance to enrol in the Ferrandi Culinary School, the chef went on to hone his skills in a variety of establishments (including the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs and L'Épi Dupin). He then went it alone and opened this restaurant. With its vintage vibe and open kitchen, the chef devises a surprise set menu that is unabashedly creative and showcases carefully selected ingredients: free-range meat and poultry, line-caught fish from small boat fishing, citrus fruits, herbs and spices, all sourced as locally as possible.

Name: Garance
Description: This discreet restaurant, which works with carefully selected producers (some of the produce comes from the family farm in Limousin), always hits the mark with diners. Walk past the open kitchens into the intimate dining space where you can tuck into coherent and healthy dishes, such as roasted scallops, Roscoff onions, andouille and buckwheat. The wines showcase small-scale winegrowers.

Name: Shirvan Café Métisse
Description: This restaurant near Pont de l'Alma is the brainchild of Akrame Benallal. Starched white linen has given way to designer cutlery and, first and foremost, a menu inspired by the Silk Road from Morocco to India via Azerbaijan. A delicious melting pot seasoned with a wealth of spices, as in the vegetarian tikki or the confit lamb chops with home-made harissa... Efficient service and you can eat at almost any time of the day.

Name: La Cuisine d'Amélie
Address: Domaine de Fontenille, route de Roquefraiche, Lauris, 84360, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Domaine de Fontenille's restaurant serves pleasant Mediterranean cuisine from a menu that changes with the seasons, as well as an appealing lunch set menu. As you sit on the superb terrace overlooking the grounds, be sure to try the estate's organic wines.

Name: La Cuisine du Cloître
Description: At the foot of the cathedral, this former 17C cloister is the quintessence of characterful! The chef’s market-fresh cuisine varies with his mood (surprise menus) and the season. His consummate technique and the quality of the ingredients hit the spot every time for a fine dining experience.

Name: Odette
Description: Two steps from Les Halles, in the luxurious Albar Hotel, the Rostang family demonstrates that they haven’t lost their touch in this urban inn. Odette regales us with dishes to be shared: sea bass in a pastry crust, one of the house’s signature dishes, veal chops, roast guinea fowl. Each dish showcases the chef’s hallmark talent.

Name: Le Petit Kembs
Description: This pretty half-timbered village house is home to a 5-table only dining room, with colourful walls and an open kitchen. Here, the chef is in charge of everything, from the food (modern, carefully-prepared, tasty) to…the service ! The approach is heartfelt and demands respect. On the plate, seasonal, local, often organic produce, with delicious bread from a local baker.

Name: Au Sourd
Description: A true Toulon institution, created by an artilleryman of Napoleon III, who went deaf while fighting, as referenced in the name. You can't really argue with what the chef offers: his cooking draws whole shoals of fish-lovers (bouillabaisse and bourride made to order, fried red mullet, rainbow wrasse, sole etc, depending on the catch) in a chic and contemporary atmosphere.

Name: La Table d'Angèle
Description: This restaurant flanked by a conservatory proposes appetising bistro food in a contemporary setting. Dishes you may find on the menu include roasted calf sweetbreads, pan-fried chanterelles and lardons, meurette sauce; Angus entrecôte and fresh chips from Savoie... Quiet terrace to the rear.

Name: Les P'tits Fayots
Description: A cosy, stylish restaurant on two levels serving modern and creative dishes, in which organic produce, particularly vegetables, from the Gers takes pride of place. The owner - chef is committed heart and soul to his culinary creations and business.

Name: La Table du Clos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant turns out to be a nice surprise, with its refined and carefully prepared cuisine based on fine – always seasonal – produce: roast Arctic char fillet, chard stems and wild mushrooms; farm-reared guinea fowl with lightly salted butter, spicy sweet potato mash. Pleasant terrace.

Name: La Table d'Emilie
Description: The house where the poet Achille Maffre de Baugé was born is home to this very popular restaurant: the delicious and meticulous cuisine is anchored in French tradition (the pâté en croûte is excellent!). Made using fresh produce, this is particularly artfully plated food. To be enjoyed in a dining space with a vaulted ceiling or out on the pleasant patio.

Name: Le Cotte Rôti
Description: A restaurant made very much in the image of the friendly, exuberant chef , who brings a touch of finesse to bistro tradition: depending on the market and the mood of the day, he composes delicious, indulgent dishes that hit the mark! Memories of the slow-cooked egg with leek, Morteau sausage and hollandaise sauce. And there's nothing like a few Rhône Valley wines to accompany the food.

Name: Richer
Description: This place appeals as much for its arty "canteen" vibe as it does for its dishes, which showcase a fresh and tasty take on market-inspired cuisine, as in the long-braised beef chuck served on a fine broccoli purée. Bear in mind, though, that the only way to reserve is to show up at the restaurant.

Name: Le Petit Gourmand
Description: Near the city centre, this vintage bistro is now the lair of Mathieu Espagnacq, who has taken over from his father, who opened the establishment back in the eighties. Mathieu, a seasoned chef with stints in Paris working with top chefs under his belt, crafts food in the zeitgeist that respects tradition and stars premium country produce (farm-reared pork cheeks braised in red wine, vegetables confit in thyme and gnocchi in a smoky cream sauce). A treat for your tastebuds from start to finish – remember to book!

Name: L'Ardoise
Description: This restaurant, whose walls are covered in slate, wears its name well! It pays a pleasing tribute to bistro heritage by means of its style and also its food – chicken pâté en croûte, foie gras and ceps; fillet of beef with black pepper and pommes Anna; lemon meringue tartlet; crème brûlée – a feast of generous, fresh and tasty dishes!

Name: L'Apibo
Description: In his small bistro in the Montorgueil neighbourhood (hushed atmosphere, oak floorboards, exposed stone), Antony Boucher, a chef with a strong track record, creates beautifully original and delicate cuisine that fêtes ingredients. He is renowned for his two classics: filet of sea bass, black rice and paprika sauce and the eight-hour confit pork with sweet potato mousseline. The laid-back (and very professional) service evokes the rough and ready spirit that used to characterise Les Halles.

Name: Boutary
Description: The ideal place to discover or brush up on your caviar know-how (osetra, sterlet and baeri), as the owners have been raising sturgeon in southern Bulgaria for several generations. The plush smart interior and the chef’s “carte blanche” menus, with a traditional tasting session served on the back of the hand, are very popular.

Name: Sagan
Description: A stone’s throw from the historic Odéon Theatre, this pocket handkerchief restaurant serves inventive, razor-sharp Japanese food: sashimi of semi-cooked salmon and caviar, somen (cold Japanese noodles) and miso soup of clams and sake. The wine list is a treasure trove of Bordeaux and Burgundies. Served with a smile in a hushed, cosy interior.

Name: Bistrot Marloe
Description: In this upscale neighbourhood, on the corner of two pretty streets, Marloe has a chic and cosy bistro vibe and its popularity reaches beyond the neighbourhood. Indeed, the food, made with high-quality ingredients, is deft and unfussy. It is delicious, especially the "black truffle" menu (in season).

Name: Chante Bise
Description: A friendly atmosphere in this family restaurant featuring exposed stone and wood work. Traditional cuisine changing over the seasons. Shaded terrace area.

Name: Tosca
Description: Italy seems to have converged on this small-capacity, smartly furnished restaurant. The food is an ode to Italian gastronomy, showcasing its meat, olive oil, cheese… Classical at lunchtime, more elaborate, and often inspired, at dinner. The Splendide Royal Hotel (formerly Pierre Cardin’s home) offers swish, elegant suites.

Name: Le Quai des Saveurs
Address: 8 place de Strasbourg, Les Sables-d'Olonne, 85100, France
Description: You can expect a warm welcome with the bonus of a sea view at Estelle and Maxime Dourdin’s eatery. The chef, with stints in top restaurants, like the Four Seasons George V in Paris under his belt, signs a single set menu that changes frequently depending on market availability. Unusual, well-crafted dishes in the zeitgeist, such as line-caught meagre à la grenobloise, einkorn risotto and fresh herb coulis.

Name: La Charrue
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of a two-centuries-old edifice, Nicolas Laurent (who trained in places such as Chambard, Auberge de l’Ill and le Vieux Couvent) has now branched out on his own. He has wisely decided to uphold this landmark establishment’s commitment to tradition. However, while classics such as fillet of carp and French fries, flammkuchen and presskopf remain firm favourites with the regulars, he’s more than willing to try his hand at more modern recipes, featuring noble produce such as lobster and langoustine. Rooms for overnight stays.

Name: La Table de Pierre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Le Mas de Pierre has morphed into a sublime, intimate and luxurious resort... and La Table has followed suit. The pair of chefs cooks up modern and locavore Mediterranean cuisine, with subtle international influences. Perfectly cooked and seasoned, there is an overarching harmony to it all: very nicely done.

Name: La Courtille de Solutré
Address: Route de la Roche, Solutré-Pouilly, 71960, France
Description: A pretty country house, its charming terrace in the shade of an old chestnut tree... and a dynamic Basque chef, who puts passion and good - quality ingredients into his cooking, nicely accompanied by a fine selection of Pouilly - Fuissé wines! There is a handful of guestrooms.

Name: La Ponche
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Chef Thomas Danigo (formerly of the Galanga in Paris) signs the menu of this emblematic Saint-Tropez restaurant, located in the eponymous district facing the sea. The cuisine is Mediterranean, giving pride of place to the catch of the day and vegetables from the region, alongside premium joints of meat. The memory of his ceviche of seabream, citrus fruits and coriander-basil sorbet and the dessert of roasted figs with apple and myrtle balsamic, almond crumble and pistachio ice cream lingers with us still.

Name: Toyo
Description: In a former life, Toyomitsu Nakayama was the private chef of fashion designer Kenzo. Nowadays, he excels in the art of fusing flavours and textures. Breaded monkfish, Buddha's hand, seaweed and Mimolette; beef, myoga ginger and red shiso sauce… This is fresh, fragrant cuisine, perfectly washed down with a glass of Burgundy and served up by an attentive but unobtrusive team. Terrific.

Name: Les 110 de Taillevent
Description: Under the aegis of the prestigious Taillevent name, this ultra - chic brasserie puts the onus on food and wine pairings. The concept is a success, with its remarkable choice of 110 wines by the glass, and nicely done traditional food (pâté en croûte, bavette steak with a peppercorn sauce etc). Elegant and inviting decor.

Name: Chez Michel
Description: Since 2015, Japanese chef Masahiro Kawai has been in charge of the kitchens at this restaurant steeped in history. He draws on his experience in Japan, Spain and France (working with Yves Camdeborde and Christian Etchebest) to create traditional yet cheerful bistro cuisine, in which seafood ingredients play a key role. The classics are present and correct – roast foie gras, game in season – the flavours are delicious and the cooking is precise, particularly in the case of the grilled mackerel, ratatouille and pistou.

Name: Court La Vigne
Description: Head for the medieval cloister: this charming 15C sheepfold is just a stone's throw away. The bar and its fireplace, the art gallery and the courtyard are all very pleasant features. Local organic wines are served with the unpretentious local cuisine.

Name: Zen
Description: This enticing restaurant combines a refreshing contemporary interior design and authentic Japanese cooking. The menu is well - rounded and faithful to the classic sushi, grilled dishes and tempura, with house specialities of gyoza and chirashi. Ideal for a quick lunch or a relaxing ‘zen’ dinner.

Name: Le Val d'Auge
Description: It may have an exterior that is typical of northern France, with its white bricks and eaves, small window panes and black surrounds, but this restaurant actually has a smart contemporary interior. Chef Christophe Hagnerelle is a true craftsman, who creates unfussy seasonal cuisine. The menu features excellent fish and shellfish from the North Sea, including turbot, sea bass or John Dory, depending on the catch of the day, but also scallops, as well as grouse and hare à la royale in season, veal sweetbreads and pigeon – from Flanders, of course.

Name: Celest
Address: Radisson Blu Lyon, 129 rue Servient, Lyon, 69003, France
Description: On the 32nd floor of the Part-Dieu Tower (165m in all), which the locals call "The Pencil", you can take in both the magnificent city and the modern cuisine, which gives pride of place to the produce. Variations on mushrooms; fillet of John Dory with parsnips, saffron and white cocoa; pear, sage and pineapple pavlova.

Name: Bloempot
Description: Florent Ladeyn, a great defender of his region's terroir, is at the helm of this self-professed "Flemish canteen". An atypical setting (once a carpentry workshop), good natural ingredients and original recipes – refreshing! There is no telephone here: reservations are made through the website or in person.

Name: Restaurant Le Dalí
Address: Le Meurice, 228 rue de Rivoli, Paris, 75001, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The second restaurant of Le Meurice, located at the centre of the action at the luxury hotel, is a place to meet and to enjoy appealing seasonal cuisine peppered with understated Mediterranean touches, as well as the great classics associated with luxury hotel dining. The beautiful decor – pilasters and mirrors – pays tribute to Dalí, who was a regular patron.

Name: Baffo
Description: Originally from the south of Tuscany, cooking enthusiast Fabien Zannier decided to change careers with a view to paying homage to the flavours that marked his childhood. And so it was that this little Italian restaurant that packs a tasty punch came into being. Fresh organic produce goes into original antipasti, set menus for sharing (based on themes such as seafood or truffles); the cellar is stocked with great Italian wines – buonissimo!

Name: La Ville Blanche
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant in a spruce building typical of Brittany is run by a young couple who have built up a loyal clientele with their modern cuisine and meticulous service. The chef keeps an eye on the seasons, thanks to a trusted network of small-scale producers. He skilfully enhances the top-notch ingredients they supply, often teasing out smoky notes and adding just the right dose of bitterness and acidity: poached langoustines, cabbage with lime; apple, crepe stuffed with apple vanilla compote, fromage blanc sorbet and combawa diplomate.

Name: Au Fil du Zinc
Description: Mathieu Sagardoytho, the new owner-chef of the Zinc, signs a creative menu that pays tribute to painstakingly sourced ingredients (mackerel from Trinité-sur-Mer marinated in mirin, lamb from Clavisy farm, plums from Yonne). Remarkable list of Chablis (and other Burgundies).

Name: Le Petit Henri
Description: The restaurant of the Grand Hôtel Henri is in the extension just off the main hotel building. It has a beautiful decor with a fireplace dating back a century and sparkling chandeliers. There is a terrace shaded by mulberry plane trees with a fountain, as well as lovely seasonal cuisine with a focus on regional flavours. Very good value for money at lunch

Name: Aromatique
Description: A couple works hand in hand in this establishment. Chef Fabien crafts creative and inspired cuisine from fresh premium ingredients, adding the occasional sprinkling of spice. Émilie, in charge of the front of house, ensures diners receive a warm welcome. There is no risk of repetition as the evening menu changes regularly; the lunchtime formula is a genuine bargain. One of our favourite eateries.

Name: Villa Saint-Antoine
Description: In a former textile mill on the banks of the Sèvre Nantaise, diners can enjoy a smart brasserie interior (red velvour banquette seating, bay windows) and the chef's delicious repertoire of dishes, which are full of flavour and lovingly prepared. Last but not least, service courtesy of a young and dynamic team.

Name: Le Gué du Holme
Description: Just opposite the church, in the centre of the village, this house built out of regional stone and its stylish dining room are the picture of hospitality. The seasoned chef showcases the best of seasonal and regional produce: slices of andouille from Vire with apples and camembert; breast of guinea fowl, apple sauce and Crêpes suzette, flambéed in front of you. Pleasant guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Auberge de la Diligence
Address: 4 rue de la Libération, Loiré, 49440, France
Description: This charming place boasts fine old stonework and a garden terrace. Sample the chef's ambitious cooking, which is very personal and varied, and enhanced with herbs from the garden or spices and condiments brought back from his travels (mainly in Asia, his true passion). Good wine menu.

Name: Les Servages
Address: 841 route des Servages, Les Carroz-d'Arâches, 74300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: One thing is sure, the chef loves what he does, and this passion is contagious. He creates food that is contemporary, meticulous and generous with superb quality ingredients such as fresh fish and seafood. His John Dory fillets and squid cooked à la plancha are just one delicious example of his dishes.

Name: L'An Faim
Description: This small restaurant is located at the end of the marina, by the stairs that go up to the citadel. Boasting a terrace, it is a favourite with regulars, attracted by the menu bursting with colourful, flavoursome market-fresh cuisine, including Corsican veal and prawns, pastilla of suckling lamb from Bonifacio, and blanquette-style dentex and vegetables. At lunchtime there is a simpler set menu.

Name: Allard
Description: In the heart of bustling Saint Germain des Près, this authentic Parisian bistro, dripping in charm and now part of the Ducasse empire, has changed very little since it opened in 1932. The culinary score wavers between bistro fare and heroic brasserie staples: snails in parsley, butter and garlic, pâté en croûte, sole meunière, profiteroles. Attractive lunchtime menu.

Name: Tavline
Description: Between Saint-Paul and Hôtel de Ville, a slice of Tel Aviv, a taste of Morocco, a hint of Lebanon – such is the formula of Tavline. Spices supplied by Shuk Ha'Carmel, the largest market in Tel Aviv, adorn the fine cuisine served here, including ksitsot daguim – grilled fish balls with herbs and spices on a bed of lentils with yoghurt and candied lemon, or the memorable memoulam (onions stuffed with lamb), a recipe passed down to the chef from his mother.

Name: La Balade des Saveurs
Description: A pleasant young couple – Benjamin and Sophie Fabre – run this spruce and stylish restaurant, which boasts a terrace running alongside the picturesque River Sorgue. The dishes manage to encapsulate and convey both the character and the sweetness of Provence.

Name: Yen
Description: The highly refined Japanese decor in this restaurant will appeal to fans of the minimalist look. The menu showcases the chef’s speciality, soba – buckwheat noodles served hot or cold and prepared in front of you.

Name: La Table du Mas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Grilled sea bass, artichoke barigoule and summer truffle: the cuisine here puts a clever spin on the classics of Provence. The Mediterranean soul expresses itself as much in the dishes as on the large terrace overlooking the countryside.

Name: Restaurant Bonnet
Description: Beñat Bonnet represents the third generation at the helm of this family-run restaurant, whose reputation is well established in the region. Local ingredients are celebrated in contemporary-style cuisine, with dishes such as Baigorry trout gravlax and braised veal with cep and chorizo viennoise sauce. For dessert, try the coconut finger sorbet, as crisp as it is refreshing!

Name: Chai l'amère Kolette
Address: Parc d'activités de Kernours, Kervignac, 56700, France
Description: Between Hennebont and Port-Louis, this house, set in a small commercial district, is definitely worth a visit. In the kitchen, visible from the airy, tastefully appointed dining room, the chef concocts market-fresh recipes, whilst adding distinctive personal touches.

Name: Le Saint Lazare
Address: 19 route de la Fontaine, L'Abergement-Clémenciat, 01400, France
Description: On the high street of a Dombes village, this establishment has been in the family since 1899! Nowadays, father and son cook together, crafting an inventive "carte blanche" mystery menu of elaborate dishes based on good, fresh ingredients. Meals are served in the low-key, stylish dining room or on the summer patio.

Name: La Grange
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is picture perfect with its exposed beams and open fireplace that call to mind the old farmhouse. Meanwhile, splashes of colour, sleek lines and design make for a modern feel! The chef’s cooking is inspired, well balanced and in harmony with the seasons.

Name: Le Café de la Fontaine
Description: The menu of this Café features a seasonal repertory with Mediterranean influences (Roussillon asparagus, Ventoux pork chop, aïoli of salted whiting) and recipes that are reminiscent of the summer holidays (salade niçoise, club sandwich). Simple, no-nonsense nosh served by a fountain overlooking the swimming pool.

Name: Le Bistrot
Description: On the menu of this bistro near the theatre and the cathedral, you will find hearty Gallic seasonal recipes, starring fine ingredients that shout their name. The Savoie-born chef worked for a long time in Ducasse establishments. In fine weather, meals are served on a shaded terrace, which further increases the pleasure.

Name: ME.
Description: This restaurant is ensconced in the Grand Hôtel Moderne et Pigeon, a former monastery dating back to the early 16C. With a superb 17C stained-glass window, the place has undeniable cachet. With its elegant patio, it has the feel of a bohemian bistro. Chef Stéphane Castaing is as creative as ever: salmon gravlax on tomato panna cotta, fillet of beef with black garlic and vegetable condiment... Laid-back friendly service.

Name: Auberge de la Fontaine du Berger
Description: On a minor road linking Clermont to the motorway, this red-shuttered country inn built out of volcanic stone overlooks the authentic, preserved countryside of the Puy de Dôme and Pariou. Tuck into a tasty, traditional Gallic lineup, assembled with top-drawer ingredients such as seared scallops from Erquy, Belgian endive and pleurote mushrooms in vin jaune, or ham stuffed with free-range chicken. Don’t even try to resist the wickedly tempting home-made Paris-Brest pastry for dessert. A friendly greeting and lovely rustic interior set the scene in this warm, inviting establishment.

Name: L'En-but
Address: 107 avenue de la République, Clermont-Ferrand, 63000, France
Description: The set menus, which are modern and shine the spotlight on local ingredients from the Massif Central, of this restaurant inside the Marcel Michelin rugby stadium, are named after the game's terminology (forward pass, grand slam and backhand spin). Designed in the spirit of a contemporary brasserie, the dining area commands a breathtaking view over the stadium and, from the terrace, over the Puys mountains.

Name: Le Patio
Description: At this town-centre restaurant, discover the cuisine of Gildas Gautier, a chef who is passionate about premium ingredients. Stuffed cabbage with beef shank, porcini, yuzu and oyster mushroom broth; wild sea bass, spinach and cauliflower; crêpe Suzette ravioli with salted butter caramel: tempting traditional recipes prepared in time-honoured tradition, with regularly changing options on the blackboard. In fine weather, dine on the small patio.

Name: I Salti
Address: au golf du Reginu - Moulin de Salti, Speloncato, 20226, France
Description: In the Reginu valley, next to the golf course, this pretty little restaurant housed in a converted mill enjoys a bucolic setting and outdoor café garden vibe. The delicious menu is the culmination of the finest ingredients of the Balagne region (local fish, organic vegetables). The prawn arancini, cold bisque and snow peas is a particularly fond memory. A warm welcome and a really charming setting, far from all the hustle and bustle: a firm favourite.

Name: Le Jardin
Description: In the village, very near St Trophyme Church, this small restaurant initially charms by its rustic appeal and delightful terrace with a fountain and pergola. In the kitchen, a Franco - British couple pay tribute to tradition with a distinctly Mediterranean slant. Everything is homemade and delicious!

Name: Auberge de l'Espérance
Address: 3 avenue des Sycomores, Le Buisson-de-Cadouin, 24480, France
Description: Desperate souls should rush to this restaurant that offers hope! The owner extends a warm and smiling welcome, and there is lots of attention to detail in the food, which combines freshness and taste. A reminder that it can be the simple pleasures that leave the deepest impression.

Name: Le Yachtman
Description: Unsurprisingly, seafood – in particular fish from the local auction – takes pride of place in this pretty restaurant located close to the marina. Simplicity and accuracy reign on the plate, while the dining area has a minimalist and intimate decor.

Name: Da Passano
Description: Overlooking the port, this restaurant and wine bar revisits traditional Corsican fare in a modern, designer interior. Live guitar music on summer evenings on the shaded terrace.

Name: Hōra
Description: At Hōra and its elegant, understated dining room, Gilles Moreau has reinvented his universe, whilst retaining his knack for flavourful cuisine drawing on local produce: Aubrac beef, aligot and a red wine reduction with shallots; organic trout from the Monts d'Aubrac with a bacon foam, risotto with Vieux Rodez cheese; free-range guinea fowl with black trumpet mushrooms and ham-perfumed wheat. In fine weather, the terrace at the rear is blissfully quiet.

Name: La Grange des Agapes
Description: Like every true enthusiast, Thierry Barot is a master of multi - tasking. Not content to offer tasty and appetising theme - based menus (vegetables, Provence, asparagus, truffles etc), he regularly runs cookery classes and is the author of a book of chocolate recipes. What a feast!

Name: L'Aigle d'Or
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few hundred metres from the château you will come across this lovely spot. The restaurant is set in a country house where you can tuck into delicious food at a table near the fireplace or out on the shady terrace. The chef revisits tradition with his tasty fare.

Name: Bistro' 50
Address: 50 avenue de la Plage, Gujan-Mestras, 33470, France
Description: Some 100m from the beach and the La Hume's port, the chef proposes tasty, modern cuisine, which relies on solid technical know - how (cooking techniques, bouillons)… with, as one might imagine, a certain penchant for fish and seafood – even if the crunchy pig's trotter with potatoes remains a classic. A fine discovery!

Name: A Pignata
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This farm-inn, the quintessence of rural charm, specialises in hearty, wholesome dishes that pay tribute to regional traditions through a set menu and top-notch produce. The Corsican cured meats are made from pigs raised on the family farm and the roasted caramelised lamb is exquisite, while the iconic stuffed seabream pays a highly fitting tribute to Corsica’s culinary heritage. Take a seat in the shade of the arbour and admire the knockout view over the mountains and the estate’s vegetable garden.

Name: B2K6
Description: This pleasant bistro was born out of a meeting of minds between two culinary enthusiasts. Jerome Bru, former sous - chef to Anne - Sophie Pic, and Romain Billard, sommelier, also a graduate of some famous establishments. Enjoy the lovely cooking, which is in harmony with the seasons and uses local ingredients, accompanied by just the right wines. A great team.

Name: L'Imparfait
Description: In this medieval edifice in historic Bergerac, the chef has been crafting seasonal cuisine of regional inspiration that packs a punch for over 15 years. In summer on the terrace or in winter by a huge fireplace, you will sample elegant, deftly curated dishes, such as panacotta of white asparagus, crab meat and aïoli or a chou craquelin (half chou – half macaroon) with Timut-flavoured stewed strawberries and basil ganache: the antithesis of imperfect in fact!

Name: Le Clos Monteils
Description: Françoise and Bernard Bordaries turned this 1771 presbytery into an intimate restaurant that feels like a family home. She extends a genial welcome, while he cracks on with the cooking. He builds dishes on simple foundations to highlight seasonal ingredients in well-crafted recipes.

Name: Le Chamagnon
Description: Located in the village where artist Claude Lorrain was born, this snug bistro serves bang-on French country cooking (a juicy fillet of Hereford beef and home-made béarnaise sauce, sweetbread with morels and a crème brûlée worthy of Amélie Poulain), dotted with modern touches (red tuna and seasonings). Top-notch produce and a savvy wine list.

Name: Place Bernard
Description: In the hands of Georges Blanc, this handsome 1900 edifice is home to a splendid brasserie adorned with a fresco of the Blanc clan. The culinary score showcases a regional line-up of classics: Bresse poultry in cream, frog’s legs in garlic and parsley and traditional Nantua-style quenelle of pike. Lovely conservatory-cum-patio.

Name: Restaurant de la Plage
Description: After taking a dip, what could be better than a good meal to recharge your batteries? This restaurant across from the beach is an ode to the sea and its bounty – from perfectly cooked and carefully prepared turbot with beetroot and chorizo, to scallops, in season… And, for dessert, crêpes Suzette flambéed in the dining room in front of the customer. Delicious!

Name: La Matelote
Description: A family-run business that pays tribute to women must be a good sign! A “matelote” is the fisherman’s wife, whose talent cannot be equalled when it comes to preparing fish, just like that of this establishment devoted body and soul to seafood (but not to the exclusion of other ingredients). Fish and shellfish are crafted in keeping with culinary tradition and with the firm intention of encouraging sustainable fishing. Save room for the patriotic line-up of Gallic desserts, such as soufflé, the house signature dish.

Name: La Cabro d'Or
Address: Mas de Baumanière, Les Baux-de-Provence, 13520, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Michel Hulin crafts generous provençal fare using first-rate ingredients from Alpilles and Camargue, illustrated by hot-cold Mediterranean squid cooked like a bouillabaisse or the incredible roast lamb, confit then smoked in AOP Crau hay, courgette flower and parsnips from Moulin de Daudet… The site is jaw-dropping with a terrace shaded by mulberry plane trees and a view over the jagged skyline that has made this enchanting village and its countryside so famous. Thoroughly enchanting.

Name: Saint-Christophe
Address: 1 avenue des Alcyons, La Baule, 44500, France
Description: Established in a genteel early 20C villa, the large windows of this cosy, colourful restaurant overlook a lush green garden. Amidst treelined flowerbeds and shaded by parasols, the spacious alfresco area is bliss in summertime. Appetising traditional cuisine strewn with contemporary touches. Don’t miss their signature dessert: lemon and passion fruit soufflé with a sorbet made out of fermented milk!

Name: Le Jardin Gourmand
Description: This elegant bourgeois ‘garden’ is the lair of chef Pierre Boussereau and his accomplice Olivier Laplaine. They cater to no more than ten diners at a time in a friendly vibe that is half-way between a table d’hôtes and a smart bistro. You will sample delicately crafted food inspired by garden produce and the chef’s globetrotting past, in a seriously plentiful tasting menu.

Name: La Ferme Sainte-Cécile
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Once through the gate, follow the lovely cobbled driveway, at the end of which is this 18C farmhouse that has been turned into a go-to place for foodies! At the kitchen stove, the chef concocts delicate and subtle cuisine that draws on the South of France: royal sea bream, vegetable pistou and roasted garlic ice cream. One of the best restaurants in Moustiers.

Name: Le Clos d'Augusta
Description: With its inviting bottle-green façade and pleasant terrace in the garden to the rear, this restaurant is run by a couple whose genuine dedication inspires confidence. The deft and creative dishes lay the emphasis on local ingredients. One example of their fresh, flavourful and seasonal starters is the generous carpaccio of Zebra tomatoes, smoked scamorza, fresh peas, leeks, basil and a green apple sorbet. Diners can expect a very warm welcome. At lunchtime, the set menu du jour is a bargain.

Name: Villa des Houx
Description: Generous, traditional cuisine that fosters close ties with the terroir: rissole with two types of salmon; Atlantic cod and black lemon… The decor is classic, both inside and on the terrace.

Name: Montcalm
