Description: This is a pleasant neighbourhood bistro, where the tattooed chef sporting a hipster look uses selected market - fresh ingredients. It's well put together, with bold flavours finely teased out. The menu evolves depending on the consignment from Rungis Market.

Name: L'Accolade
Address: 208 rue de la Croix-Nivert, Paris, 75015, France
Description: In a downright convivial atmosphere, the chef – a former sports teacher who has chosen to branch out – prepares tasty cuisine that he changes up every day. He makes ample use of produce from South-West France (pork belly, pointed cabbage and green lentils), but also borrows a smattering of Asian ingredients (carpaccio of Tokyo turnip, crab meat, coriander and black garlic). An appealing place.

Name: Salicorne
Description: Working here is a young chef who majored in science at school and was planning to become a golf teacher when he "stumbled upon" cooking. With some great experience under his belt, he did up an old car garage, retaining its spirit (raw materials, vintage chairs). He offers a short seasonal menu, full of temptations. Mission accomplished.

Name: La Fine Fourchette
Address: 2500 avenue du Bugey, à Virignin, Belley, 01300, France
Description: A jaw-dropping view over the Canal du Rhône and an elegant interior set the scene in this renowned regional temple of good food. Generous portions of Ain produce take the limelight in the chef’s well-crafted score, depicted by fascinating flavour combinations and impeccable plating. Special mention for the strawberry-themed dessert that will knock the tastebuds off fans of fine French fare!

Name: Arraya
Description: An exquisite patio shaded by plane trees in one of the most beautiful villages of the Basque hinterland sets the scene for this former coaching inn on the Camino de Santiago, in the hands of the same family for decades. Locally sourced ingredients are delicately crafted, sometimes with a creative twist. The epitome of a French country inn. Simpler bistro menu at lunchtime.

Name: George's
Description: Boasting an ideal location in the port of Saint-Martin-de-Ré, this chic brasserie has a seaside-inspired interior decor. Featuring alongside the unfussy dishes made with precisely prepared regional produce (freshly caught fish, Challans poultry) are some great French classics (pan-fried foie gras, baked snails). The pleasant terrace lounge and cocktail bar are popular. Attentive service.

Name: Nosso
Description: Brazilian-born chef Alessandra Montagne is delighted to be in her new restaurant, which has an inviting contemporary interior featuring a preponderance of concrete and wood as well as floor-to-ceiling windows. Her recipe for success (and pleasure) comprises meticulous plating, seasonal, locally sourced ingredients, a whirlwind of flavours and a patchwork of influences (from Brazil to Asia). Zero waste and 100% natural. Tasting menus in the evening.

Name: Fleur de Sureau
Description: This elderflower has taken root opposite the train station! Its gardener is a chef who trained under Jean-Georges Klein at the Arnsbourg. The former rustles up food for today’s palate based on top-quality seasonal produce. More sophisticated menu in the evening.

Name: La Table des Délices
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This 1980’s house stands on the road to the grotto where Mme de Sévigné used to seek refuge. The chef concocts hearty regional dishes, such as a terrine of baby rabbit with walnuts and confit of spring onions wrapped in smoked bacon. Fine wine cellar.

Name: Dilia
Description: This small-format restaurant opposite Notre-Dame-de-la-Croix, in the heart of the 20th arrondissement, has buckets of charm and a country house feel. Tuscan chef Michele Farnese has good international credentials, as well as experience in French establishments such as Saturne and Thoumieux. With the name Dilia, he pays tribute to his ancestors, Dino and Illia. With a joyous sense of freedom, the chef cooks up his Italian cuisine. Sage takes pride of place alongside pillowy beetroot gnocchi and raw scallop shavings; the pasta is prepared in time-honoured tradition and marries perfectly with the bottarga and garlic bread. While the lunch menu is a good deal, the multi-course dinner menu ups the ante, and is accompanied by an excellent selection of French and Italian wines. Friendly and smiling service is provided by the manager and sommelier. A well-kept secret to (re)discover as a matter of urgency.

Name: Lune
Description: This restaurant in the small winegrowing town of Vayres is the brainchild of Pierre Rigothier, a chef who learned the trade at some good establishments in Paris. The tempting dishes on the blackboard and in the surprise menu are replete with rigorously selected ingredients: kintoa pig, farmhouse duck breast, sole meunière and tuna (tartar or grilled). A welcoming vibe in a chic country style.

Name: Les Jardins du Moulin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant blends perfectly into the setting of the mill. Through the bay windows, one can admire the garden and magnificent terrace. Diners can look forward to well - crafted creations from the carpaccio of sea bream with citrus olive oil to the fillet of Simmental beef, béarnaise au siphon and buewespaetzle.

Name: L'Artichaut
Address: Hôtel de l'Abbaye, 20 rue de l'Abbaye-d'Ainay, Lyon, 69002, France
Description: Tucked away in a former presbytery transformed into an attractive hotel, this laid-back and stylish restaurant serves tasty contemporary dishes (snails, pumpkin cream, garlic purée and parsley; arctic char, girolles with amaretto, potatoes and coffee powder) in tune with the seasons.

Name: L'Essentiel
Description: Nestled at the foot of the castle, this beautiful tuffeau-stone house sports charming dining rooms (parquet floors, exposed rafters and bare stone walls) and peaceful little patios. Chef Anthony Vaillant crafts food in the zeitgeist, jazzed up by a scattering of deft creative touches: start with a medley of asparagus and green peas, enhanced by a citrus fruit flavoured dressing followed by fabulously fresh cod flanked by a curry sauce and velvety mashed potato. Extremely attentive service. Regional tipples take pride of place on the wine list. An enjoyable culinary experience!

Name: Agastache
Description: A bistronomic establishment opened by the star chef of the Atelier Yssoirien. An extensive menu, updated, seasonal recipes, expertly prepared and artistically presented, in a Scandinavian-style décor.

Name: Le Cairn - Hôtel le Celtique
Description: In the heart of Carnac-Plage, just a pebble stone's throw from the sandy beach and the sea, Hôtel Le Celtique has been treated to a magnificent Art deco-inspired refurbishment. The menu features a happy marriage of traditional foundations and modern trends, with the occasional exotic spice, such as on the lobster with ajo blanco, squash and goji berries.

Name: L & Luy - Château d'Ygrande
Description: Chef Cédric Denaux works his magic in this elegant Directoire château (1835), whose terrace overlooks the Bourbon countryside. His creative and seasonal cooking prominently features plant-based and of course seasonal ingredients. He uses home-grown aromatic herbs, plants and vegetables from the château garden, paired with top-drawer ingredients. The memory of his Roscoff monkfish, dashi stock, marigold petals and purple basil lingers with us still.

Name: Beam !
Description: Beaming and buzzing! The kitchens of the Télégraphe, a high spot of Toulon’s cultural life, are all go! Energetic Arnaud Tabarec, born in Burgundy, honed his skills in prestigious establishments and was the star chef of the Five Hotel’s Roof in Cannes. Today he is acclaimed for his delicate, predominantly vegetarian cuisine, whose ingredients are of course sourced locally and combined boldly.

Name: Yka bar & ceviche
Description: The casual sibling of the Franco-Peruvian star-rated gastronomic Miraflores, Yka is the perfect venue for afterwork socialising in the Brotteaux district. Relax in the warm contemporary vibe (the colourful mural depicts Peruvians from the Cusco region), while sipping a pisco cocktail and nibbling on warm flaky pastry empanadas stuffed with beef and green peas or a ceviche from the wide range on the menu.

Name: La Réserve du Presbytère
Description: Opposite the Romanesque church of a wine-growing village is this eatery serving bistronomy dishes. Diners savour traditional flavours in a decor comprising bistro tables and industrial chairs set up against a backdrop of exposed stone walls. The delicious desserts deserve a special mention: amandine tartlet with figs, raspberry confit and sorbet. Pleasant terrace to the rear.

Name: Chartron
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A local institution in this village famed for its Jean - Sébastien - Bach festival (July). Perhaps it is down to this musical inspiration but the food served by this elegant restaurant is harmonious, refined and full of delicate touches. A lovely place, scored with very great ingredients.

Name: La Casserole
Description: Formerly maître d' at Au Crocodile, the owner of this place officiates in a contemporary and elegant setting that beautifully sets off the refined cuisine made with first-rate ingredients. The surf and turf-inspired "choco-beef" tartare with Kristal caviar and quail egg may be one of his most original dishes, but that's no reason to pass over the crêpes Suzette prepared in time-honoured tradition at your table, accompanied by vanilla ice cream made to order – delicious.

Name: Château Hochberg
Description: Within this majestic 19C residence, chef Arnaud Barberis serves up delicious seasonal cuisine with a few French classics: bouchée à la reine royale, heart sweetbreads with chanterelles. The contemporary decor is dotted with creations by master glassmaker René Lalique, whose work is celebrated in the museum just opposite. Gorgeous terrace to the rear of the château, overlooking the grounds.

Name: Le Maquis
Description: Paul Boudier and Albert Touton, both formerly at Le Chateaubriand, deliver delicious, no-frills cuisine at unbeatable value for money! A menu packed with bistro fare – velouté, pureed sausage, an indulgent crumble – and an old-school setting (with the typical zinc counter and leatherette banquette seating) make for a friendly and lively atmosphere. Irresistible!

Name: Carøe
Description: Scandinavian accents characterise the casual interior of this canteen. The chef, married to a Danish woman, painstakingly sources each ingredient: fish from small boats, organic and local produce. The regularly renewed menu features over a dozen tapas-style dishes. Asian flavours jazz up the Basque produce: for example, mackerel, enhanced by dashi stock and served with vinegar rice and acidic touches of lemon – gutsy and flavoursome! The natural wine list leaves nothing lacking.

Name: Garum
Description: The chef has turned his Jardin des Remparts into a “living table”. This fashionable, classy bistro uses premium ingredients in a menu ranging from pre-dinner snacks to share with friends (Gillardeau oysters, charcuterie and French fries) to a selection of mouth-watering, well-crafted seasonal dishes. The bistro’s namesake (garum) is a fermented sauce, popular with the Romans, that Christophe Bocquillon uses to season beef tartare, in particular.

Name: La Vieille Enseigne
Description: Despite the name, this is a brand new winstub! The magnificent traditional wainscoting is the work of a cabinetmaker, lithographs by Tomi Ungerer adorn the walls, while copious helpings, local ingredients and traditional regional recipes (presskopf, choucroute, game) depict the gourmet tribute to Alsace, down to the splendid selection of mainly organic wines.

Name: Iod'in
Description: On the outskirts of the pretty village of Allauch, this modern and spacious, maritime-inspired brasserie comes highly recommended. Youthful chef Anthony de Filippo (stints with Lionel Levy at Alcyone and Dominique Frérard at Les Trois Forts in Marseilles) takes his crew of foodies on an appetising, no-holds barred voyage, in which fish and shellfish take pride of place. Bouillabaisse on the menu (without prior reservation).

Name: L'Os à Moelle
Description: Thierry Faucher is still in charge of L'Os à Moelle, where, in the early 2000s, he secured his position as one of the forerunners of France's bistronomy movement. Aubergine dip, soft-boiled egg and country ham; leg of lamb and vegetable fricassee; bone marrow; soup of the day… It's simple, delicious and indulgent fare.

Name: Auberge des Matfeux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The highly contemporary and original decor is very elegant. It features abstract patterns on the walls, bright polka dots on the chairs, and crockery made by a local artist. The menu consists of beautiful dishes that reinterpret the classics, and the wine menu features great Bordeaux vintages and Loire wines.

Name: À l'Étoile
Description: Tucked away in a small Alsace village on the Mont Sainte Odile road, this traditional hostelry, opened in 1920, is today run by the fourth generation. A warm welcome and honest, homely recipes, starring market-fresh produce and a slate menu. For example, start with a waffle piled high with smoked salmon and citrus fruit, while offal fans won’t be able to resist the fried kidneys and sweetbread.

Name: Grains de Sel
Description: "Gilles Schnoering, well established in his restaurant near the Halle aux Houblons, treats his guests to a short seasonal menu; his fresh, well - made creations owe much to the quality of the ingredients used. Savvy food and wine pairings. "

Name: Le Baratin
Description: Argentine chef Raquel Carena pretty much invented bistronomy, as many young chefs acknowledge. This stripped-down, retro bistro serves food that is delicate or hearty, but always personal. The blackboard menu makes pleasant reading, the prices are restrained and the wines appealing. Reservations strongly recommended.

Name: Goustut
Address: Quai de la Pêcherie, Capbreton, 40130, France
Description: On the lookout for a friendly restaurant delivering good food with a rich variety of flavours? Sit back in the relaxed atmosphere and enjoy the mezze menus – a host of local dishes served in small portions for sharing. The house specialty, they feature Capbreton fish and vegetables from the Bastelica family market gardeners. Highlights include the excellent cuttlefish and foie gras pâté en croûte, the fried blue whiting ravioli with pil pil sauce and the crispy bonito roll with Asian spinach and courgette purée.

Name: Auberge Sauvage
Description: This former 16C presbytery is now home to a restaurant with a vegetable garden, which provides the chef with plenty of produce as well as inspiration for his surprise menus and modern cuisine occasionally imbued with Japanese touches. His yoghurt and Melonette squash tartlet is a real highlight. Natural wines.

Name: Le Café de Paris
Description: Superlatively located in the heart of town just above the main beach, this restaurant belongs to the iconic Café de Paris Hotel. Everything tastes of something in the intelligently updated brasserie repertory, inspired by local produce with a host of passing nods to nearby Spain. Delightful terrace.

Name: Hito
Address: 26 rue de la Fonderie, Toulouse, 31000, France
Description: Hitoshi Araki's restaurant is near Place des Salins. Working alone in the kitchen, the chef cooks up creative French cuisine enriched with passing references to Japan. His indisputably precise execution, remarkable cooking technique and bold flavours come through in dishes such as melt-in-the-mouth pork belly preserved in its own juices and lightly caramelised on the outside – delicious! The lunch menu is a steal.

Name: L'Hommage
Description: In a neighbourhood swarming with Chinese eateries, this establishment stands out from the crowd by courtesy of a bistronomic purebred Gallic lineup and minimalist Scandinavian-style loft interior. The high-flying culinary score boasts quality ingredients and bang-on cooking and seasoning: ravioles of Ossau-Iraty cheese, smoked pimiento sauce, dusting of chorizo, poached rhubarb and roquette oil, or loin of croaker with asparagus, miso and capers in a gutsy red wine sauce…

Name: Caves Madeleine
Description: A stone's throw from the town centre, this wine bar-restaurant is a little gem. Chef Martial has hooked up with the best local producers, including some top wine growers, to create wholesome, punchy cuisine that is rife with flavour, eg warm potatoes, haddock, and tarragon sabayon. Relaxed, no-fuss service – the focus is firmly on the contents of your glass and your plate. In fine weather, make the most of the pleasant terrace in the shade of a fig tree.

Name: Le Jardin de l'Abbaye
Description: Tucked away in the countryside of Saint-Malo's hinterland, between Mont Saint-Michel, Saint-Malo and Dinan, this hotel was once an abbey (12C). The premises are also home to a quality restaurant serving cuisine inspired by the market and the season, with dishes such as saithe, carrot, potato and gingerbread. Enjoy your meal in the sober interior with views over the countryside and lake, before returning to your nice comfortable guestroom – peace and quiet guaranteed!

Name: Crêperie Grain Noir
Address: 16 rue de la Herse, Saint-Malo, 35400, France
Description: Opposite the Halle au Blé in Saint-Malo, this little crêperie is not to be missed. It serves classic galettes (buckwheat pancakes), as well as more original recipes: the "langouille" galette is with pork tongue; the "Grain Noir" with Breton trout, fresh goat's cheese, crunchy vegetables and lemon; the "Ty Nevez" with andouille from Dinan, egg, Emmental and mustard. They also serve hors d'oeuvre, such as chilli butter and raw cocoa nibs, and salted butter and seaweed tartar. Most of the ingredients are organic; the ciders and wines are natural.

Name: Song Qi
Description: Opposite Grimaldi Forum, this swanky, gourmet Chinese restaurant has opted for premium materials and a serene atmosphere. The appetising menu offers a vast array of Chinese cuisine from Peking soup with smoked chicken to crispy dragon prawns with Chinese mustard or the classic dim sum. Bookings advisable!

Name: L'Auberge d'Anthy
Description: This traditional little hotel - restaurant - café is all about the simple pleasures in life! This is probably one of the best places around Thonon to enjoy the fish of Lake Geneva (true fera and Arctic char), as supplied by local fishermen. The chef also likes to showcase the charcuterie and cheeses of the Chablais area!

Name: La Maréa
Description: Opposite the sea and the ochre-coloured rocks of Esterel and looking down on the beach and port of La Figueirette, this restaurant was founded in the 1950s by a local fisherman. It has been happily taken over by Jérôme Cervera, former fishmonger. The chef whips up à la carte flawlessly fresh seafood and carefully crafted dishes, illustrated by roast loin of gilt-head bream with shrimps, paella-style stock and chorizo. The lunch and evening menus feature à la carte dishes, served alfresco or in the pretty dining room with a sea view.

Name: La Table du Tillau
Address: Le Mont des Verrières, Verrières-de-Joux, 25300, France
Description: A few metres from the Swiss border, this Franche-Comté farmhouse built out of stone and old wood exudes serenity, just like its elegant guestrooms appointed in chalet style. On the menu, modern cuisine that highlights often regional produce, like lemon cream with beetroot-marinated trout gravadlax, or filet of beef, red wine reduction and celeriac puree.

Name: La Table du Monastère de Saint-Mont
Description: To say this place is steeped in history is an understatement: the monastery, rebuilt several times since the Middle Ages, is said to stand on the site of a Roman oppidum. Protected by the Saint-Mont vineyard, it is now home to Jean-Paul Tossens' fine dining restaurant. The chef revisits French cuisine through a seasonal lens, showcasing premium ingredients, and serving up his dishes in an elegant setting. Guestrooms available; hotel facilities include swimming pool and spa.

Name: La Courtille
Description: Trained by Raquel Carena at her Parisian institution, Le Baratin, Natalia Crozon serves deliciously down-to-earth regional cuisine in this restaurant accommodated in a converted silkworm farm built of white stone. Poached calf brains with lemon butter; pan-fried bluefin tuna steak with tomato ragout; apricot cake... plenty to whet the appetite. Take your pick from the appealing wine list that focuses on natural wines and local Tavel and Lirac labels. In summer, tables are laid out on the pretty terrace sheltered by an ancient cedar tree.

Name: Le Berlot
Description: What a pleasure to come across this couple of foodies again! Hervé and Patricia Chardonneau left their Casse-Cailloux in Tours for the heights of this wine-producing village. Hervé proposes "bistronomic" cuisine that draws its inspiration from the seasons and what the markets have to offer. Nice wine list with a focus on organic and natural wines. Separate wine bar.

Chef Michael Durkin is a tattooed Englishman and rugby fan who has worked in some of the best restaurants in the world. He whips up creative modern bistro cuisine, for example seared cod, celeriac and capers – a well-presented and harmonious dish. Not only is the four-course set lunch menu unbeatable value, the small terrace is a real draw in fine weather.

Name: Mokko
Description: Arthur Hantz, a self-taught chef who started out washing the dishes, has adopted a no-holds barred, complex-free approach and his modern bistro at the foot of Montmartre gets right down to brass tacks. The menu (carte or slate only) features a devilishly effective strategy: creative, vivacious, market-fresh cuisine with the odd Asian influence. A few examples: lightly seared cockles and scallops, pho emulsion, pimangue spice; free-range chicken, vitelotte potato crème, violet cauliflower, roast parsley roots, jus of milk-fed veal and toasted sarrazin.

Name: La Table de Léa
Description: In this former farm the female chef creates seasonal dishes with a personal touch. In fine weather take advantage of the attractive terrace beneath the shade of the chestnut trees.

Name: Momento
Address: 5 rue de la Cure, Bué, 18300, France
Description: Here you really are guaranteed a delightful "momento", complete with a view of the vineyards. A very professional couple in their thirties runs the show: Mexican chef Mariana Mateos cooks up seasonal cuisine that demonstrates finesse and generosity, alongside her husband, Thomas Jacquet, a local man (service, sommelier). A real treat.

Name: La Maison Badine
Address: 2 rue du Pont-Prouiller, La Tronche, 38700, France
Description: This welcoming modern establishment, named after one of the chef’s forebears, is depicted by a trendy, casual vibe that mirrors its tattooed maestro. From his open-plan kitchen, Florian Poyet crafts a legible bistronomic score with a strong focus on the seasons: squid in parsley and garlic and white asparagus, Trièves lamb with wild garlic and black limes, slow-baked rhubarb and strawberries in Kampot white pepper…

Name: Les Ombres
Description: On the roof terrace of the Musée Quai Branly – Jacques Chirac, this entirely glass-sided restaurant boasting interior and exterior architecture designed by Jean Nouvel overlooks the nearby Eiffel Tower. The menu, supervised by Alain Ducasse, is skilfully executed by talented chef Alexandre Sempere, a trusted collaborator. The modern seasonal cuisine is made with fine ingredients and smacks of the Mediterranean influences beloved of its mentor. The desserts created by pastry chef Jérémy Schotte, such as the farm-fresh skyr mousse with Buddha's hand and a lemon leaf granita, deserve a special mention.

Name: Café de l'Ardèche
Description: Grey leather banquettes, contemporary furniture, Pop art and a fine collection of works by artist Ricardo Santamaria set the scene in the modern interior. The food is expertly crafted, seasonal and starring local produce, such as farm-range guinea fowl and a gutsy girolles gravy.

Name: AOR La Table, le Goût et Nous
Address: 2 rue de la Piscine, Riquewihr, 68340, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Something of a UFO in the gastronomic universe of Alsace, globetrotting cook, Serge Burckel, is also part poet, part rock star – check out the old LPs and CDs recycled as place mats! He works with his family in a bohemian, laid-back ambience, with a choice of surprise menus.

Name: La Serre
Description: La Serre ("greenhouse") is surrounded by greenery and flooded with light – a wonderful backdrop for the excellent food prepared by chef Anthony Pierson. Devised by chef Arnaud Davin, the menu is replete with well-executed and perfectly cooked dishes, such as roasted John Dory, chard, rhubarb and its flavoursome sauce. There are a few creative touches such as the pomelo jelly on the spider crab. The results are delicious, the flavours shine through and the presentation is meticulous. The tables are set out in a magnificent greenhouse and the terrace is delightful in fine weather.

Name: Le Bistrot du Château - Le Stelsia
Description: This appealing trendy bistro, depicted by a striking décor of black walls, light wooden tables and small colourful armchairs, serves appetising fare with a regional tang: fillet of rockfish seabream, sweet potatoes, salad of squid and samphire; ‘Duroc de Bataillé’ pluma pork, lingot beans, chorizo and tarragon. The leafy sheltered terrace overlooks the grounds of the Stelsia Hotel.

Name: Auberge L'Escale 87
Description: This Auberge alongside the former Route Nationale 6 is really inviting on account of its quaint interior decorated with various agricultural items and its rustic-style furnishings. When it comes to the food, tradition is the name of the game: country-style calf's head; lamb kidney fricassee; tournedos with morels, and, on top of that, service with a smile. An enjoyable mealtime experience. Pleasant terrace to the rear.

Name: Ilura
Address: Pointe Sainte-Barbe, 1 rue Gaëtan-de-Bernoville, Saint-Jean-de-Luz, 64500, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in La Réserve Hotel on the heights of St-Jean-de-Luz, whose superb terrace overlooks the ocean, this exclusive restaurant delivers an enjoyable fine dining experience courtesy of chef Bastien Soumoulou’s creative, modern repertory. His cooking blends turf and surf produce, like foie gras, seaweed and crunchy samphire; veal, walnuts, cockles and mimosa vinegar; pollock, andouille sausage and beetroot; or even beef, gnocchi, spinach and herrings. One dessert showcases hazelnuts in a complex, wickedly irresistible creation that combines coffee and vanilla notes. Swish, seamless, skilful service.

Name: Auberge du Sombral - Les Bonnes Choses
Description: In this house at the foot of the Château des Lapopie, you can be sure that good things – Les Bonnes Choses – are to come! Enjoy the pleasant cuisine du terroir, in which local ingredients are the star (lamb, foie gras, cheese... ). There are a handful of pretty guestrooms, if you wish to stay on in this village overlooking the Lot.

Name: Le Théophile - Château d’Orfeuillette
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The muted, romantic and château-like atmosphere of this restaurant combines the elegance of a historic edifice with a striking modern decor. Drawing upon premium local produce, the chef whisks up modern, delicate dishes. Poised between the Aubrac and Margeride, the 19C hotel surrounded by grounds is theatrically contemporary and glamorous.

Name: Auberge des Grenouillats
Description: This welcoming small bistro sporting a faintly retro aura is run by a friendly couple. The chef works with fresh produce to concoct tasty dishes that pay tribute to the region. The menu includes: charolais beef, frogs’ legs and Burgundy ham with parsley.

Name: Biondi
Description: The talented chef named this restaurant after a famous Argentine clown, Pepe Biondi. Argentina also takes pride of place on the menu, with meat and fish cooked a la parrilla, empanadas and ceviche of the day. Attentively prepared food, served by an efficient team. Good wines and good mood complete the picture.

Name: Saperlipopette !
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This former brewery has had a major facelift, to become an inviting, trendy restaurant, under expert direction. The generous food is in a chic bistro style and neatly presented.

Name: La Passerelle
Description: This restaurant is presided over by a talented and motivated chef who knows how to take you on a culinary journey of taste and flavours! Enjoy rigorously selected ingredients in the fine and colourful cuisine that is peppered with Mediterranean influences. The best restaurant in town.

Name: Prunier par Yannick Alléno
Description: If only to feast your eyes on Prunier's decor, created by the greatest mosaicists, engravers and sculptors of the Art Deco period, it is worth going out of your way to come here. A new era has begun with the arrival of Yannick Alléno, who has created the menu and recruited trusted chef Fabien François to take charge of the kitchen. The menu, of course, gives pride of place to fish, shellfish and Prunier caviar, but not only that (there is some meat). The great classics are also revisited, such as the Christian Dior egg and oysters with almond milk and dill.

Name: La Flamiche
Description: A classical interior lies behind the large windows of La Flamiche. Here, cuisine with robust traditional foundations is enhanced by a touch of modernity: one example would be the duck foie gras and smoked trout in a Granny Smith jelly, cucumber pickles and apple chutney – a beautifully crafted starter. Then there are the medallions of monkfish with lime, carrot and rocket, perfectly cooked in butter, the good old-fashioned way.

Name: Hostellerie Saint-Germain
Description: Opposite the church, this engaging 17C coaching inn has been entirely refurbished in a low-key, contemporary vein. The chef sources fine local produce, often organic, to craft appetising dishes, occasionally peppered with creative touches, such as pink trout and nori seaweed. All of which is washed down with fine Jura wines. The cosy rooms are pleasant, and quieter overlooking the terrace.

Name: L'Essentiel - Domaine de Champlong
Address: 100 chemin de la Chapelle, Villerest, 42300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Enjoy mealtimes as tasty as they are charming in this 18C residence nestled in greenery. Diners are treated to contemporary cuisine in the "salle des peintures", where period paintings hang. Appetising lunchtime set menu and great wine list.

Name: La Ferme de Voisins
Description: You reach this lovely 19C farmhouse via a flower-decked courtyard, which serves as a patio in summertime. The relatively concise menu shines the spotlight on the house classics, which are prawns on sticks, the ‘irreplaceable’ calf’s head and signature desserts such as the rum and orange punch baba, together with a range of tasty and creative dishes. A fine establishment to try out post-haste!

Name: Inima
Description: In her small restaurant with an uncluttered interior (previously home to Cromagnon), young Moldavian-born chef Oxana Cretu (who originally came to Bordeaux as an au pair) gives free rein to her culinary imagination with a surprise menu. A perfectionist with a passion for food, she concocts dishes replete with Japanese influences: dauphine potatoes with buckwheat, black garlic and soy; matured trout with mashed macadamia nuts. Her dessert of meringue with strawberries from the Lot, Namelaka cream, lemon marmalade and jasmine sorbet is an unqualified success.

Name: Une Table à la Campagne - La Fenière
Description: Nadia Sammut crafts seasonal Provençal cuisine that is gluten free and strongly anchored in the region (partnerships with local producers, home-made flours, home-grown vegetables). In fine weather, you can bask on the terrace beneath the reed canopy. A vibrant experience close to nature.

Name: Aho Fina
Description: Right on the beach, looking out to the ocean, the Empire-style Grand Hôtel certainly makes its presence felt! Aho Fina treats diners to cuisine that is inspired by the ocean and the Basque country and aspires to short supply chains: baby squid risotto with squid ink and preserved lemon; duo of slow-cooked veal cuts and creamed red beans; mini patxaran liqueur babas… Bistronomy set menu at lunchtime, more ambitious fare in the evening.

Name: Autour de la Table
Description: This place calls to mind a hotel training school, with its classic menu (paupiette of sole, beef fillet, pancakes with quetsch brandy), serious and applied service – the forgotten art of cutting and preparing in the dining room is still practiced. Here, tradition and classicism are present and correct, both around and especially on the table.

Name: Zest
Address: 32 cours de la Vilaine, Cesson-Sévigné, 35510, France
Description: The secret behind the Zest’s success is market-fresh cooking, original recipes dusted with exotic notes, spices and seasonings, a delightfully friendly vibe and in summertime, a riverside patio on the banks of the Vilaine. Slick service with a smile.

Name: Le Mange-Grenouille
Description: This former coaching inn located in a lane just a stone's throw from the banks of the Cher has a pleasant patio in the courtyard, delightfully rustic dining areas with bare stonework and terracotta tiled floors... but above all ambitious cuisine whose roots are firmly embedded in tradition. At lunchtime, a simpler, great-value set menu is served. Don't miss the house speciality: frog's legs sautéed in parsley!

Name: Le Rocher Blanc
Address: Route du Gévaudan, La Garde, 48200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A country inn with a refreshingly trendy vibe! The chef, a fan of interior design, likes to shake things up, both in the decor – with a blend of styles – and in the food. On the menu: an affinity to the land and innovative touches (snail ravioli with herbs and cream of Pelardon cheese, pike-perch matelote with red wine and candied carrots, exotic baba). A success!

Name: Le Karelian
Description: An understated, stripped-back dining room is the perfect foil for the chef’s modern, creative recipes, illustrated by flawlessly cooked arctic char served with grilled sarrazin wheat and crisp baby leeks in a saté sauce. The chef’s welcoming, professional spouse oversees the front of house. Those with a sweet tooth will be in seventh heaven thanks to the decadent dessert trolley.

Name: Club L'Indochine by The Duc Ngo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A new concept in Asian fusion cuisine by chef Jimmy Coutel in collaboration with renowned Berlin chef The Duc Ngo. The dishes are generous and made using high-quality local produce; the recipes are well executed and carefully adjusted to suit European palates. A good example of this is the sea bass steamed with ginger, shallots, coriander, Chinese soy sauce and hot vegetable oil… The breath-taking view over the Gulf of Saint-Tropez remains unchanged!

Name: La Ferme du Vert
Description: Homemade and regional produce: this farm is still a going concern and the owners – two brothers – divide their time between agriculture and the restaurant. Be sure to try the delicious cheese from their dairy herd!

Name: Le Relais de Sillery
Address: 3 rue de la Gare, Sillery, 51500, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant inn, a post house in a former life, sports a terrace overlooking the River Vesle. The setting is bucolic, the food classical: sea bass meunière, baby artichokes and confit tomatoes, and a Grand Marnier soufflé. The impressive wine cellar is very competitively priced!

Name: Le Crypto
Description: Opposite Reims’ famous crypto portico (an underground gallery dating from Roman times), this bistro is run by chef Frédéric Dupont, whose CV speaks for itself. Generous helpings of wholesome seasonal fare, a judicious wine list, well-stocked in champagnes, and slick service. The establishment’s success is fully deserved.

Name: Le Tastevin
Description: At the edge of the park, this elegantly decorated mansion embodies a distinctly French "art of living"... and gives expression to its love of fine ingredients! Chef Denis Rivoire is of Italian origin and he certainly knows his stuff; he revisits the classics, adding a few Mediterranean touches. Good wine list.

Name: La Croix Blanche
Address: 61 rue de Genève, Cesson, Saint-Brieuc, 22000, France
Description: Two brothers: one in the kitchen, the other serving in the dining room... It is a family affair in this pleasant restaurant overlooking a pretty garden. The cuisine is gourmet and refined, for instance the excellent Dubarry pannacotta with crumbled crab and a shellfish emulsion. You get plenty of enjoyment for the price.

Name: Ô Saveurs
Description: Chances are it won't be the charm of the location near the train station that draws you here, but the restaurant has more than enough of its own merits. Where shall we begin? Scallops from St Brieuc Bay in a Quessoy saffron sauce and seaweed-flavoured conchiglioni or duckling breast roasted in honey and sage with a pear poached in blueberries and shiitakes, and a delicious encounter between cherries and pear with a white chocolate topping to finish…

Name: Bistro'Quai
Description: On the busy docks of the port, this cosy, contemporary restaurant serves seafood that keeps pace with the arrivals at the seafood market of Les Sables, but also with local Vendée produce (Challans poultry, farm - reared pork chops). The most attractive dining room in town.

Name: L'Auberge d'Antan
Address: Avenue de la Résistance, Saint-Girons, 09200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In what used to be the barn belonging to the château, this restaurant boasts an impressively high ceiling. Hams suspended from the ceiling, stonework and beams make for a lovely country atmosphere. No - nonsense cooking at its best, with traditional dishes such as grilled meats and suckling pig prepared right in front of you at the huge fireplace.

Name: Au Fulcosa
Address: 2 rue du Maréchal-Foch, à Fourqueux, Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 78112, France
Description: Fulcosa means "fern" in Latin, a reference to the plant that once carpeted the surrounding forests, suggesting that the young proprietors have a sense of history as well as flavours! In the inviting decor of their "culinary bistro", they treat us to tasty seasonal cuisine in which tradition meets innovation: for example, mushroom ravioli in a chicken broth, with bacon and hazelnut.

Name: Comme Chez Maman
Description: This contemporary bistro near a green square in the heart of the Batignolles neighbourhood is a real home from home. The Belgian chef, Wim Van Gorp, makes lovely contemporary dishes that he peppers with creative touches, and some of which pay delicious tribute to his Flemish roots.

Name: Pierre Sang on Gambey
Description: This is Pierre Sang's second restaurant, the first being in nearby Oberkampf. Both locations are run with the same ethos and have the same concept. The famous chef's commitment to quality ingredients is also present and correct. Care and creativity go into turning produce into innovative, cosmopolitan dishes, with the occasional nod to Korea. The originality does not stop at the food: diners are invited to guess what they have just eaten! An inviting setting in which to indulge in a moment of sharing.

Name: La Table de Reugny
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the road to Montluçon, Arnaud Paulus, a former engineer who learned the trade in the region, crafts modern cuisine with a creative twist and the odd scattering of spices. The menu is concise and seasonal, examples of which are gravlax of trout with a guacamole of broccoli or a ballotine of guinea fowl and langoustines paired with a butternut, feta and walnut maki. Peaceful terrace to the rear.

Name: Mensae
Description: Cuisine of the moment, full of freshness and with spot-on flavours. Among the classics, on the menu all year round, the frogs' legs, garlic and parsley or the mousse au chocolat praliné are good enough to spark a riot. The decor has the good taste to make itself discreet. The small sidewalk terrace is welcome in summer.

Name: Les 3 Cépages
Address: 17 rue de la Gare, Reuilly, 36260, France
Description: In the heart of rural Berry and in the famous wine - growing village of Reuilly, this white - fronted ex - hotel is enjoying a new lease of life in the capable hands of a committed Japanese couple crazy about French food. Fine, flavoursome and flawlessly cooked, with a focus on fine quality produce.

Name: Les Tourelles - Château d'Apigné
Address: Route de Chavagne, Le Rheu, 35650, France
Description: Relax in the blatantly romantic ambiance of this stylish neo-Renaissance castle dating from 1833 set in sprawling grounds. Its exquisite living rooms provide the perfect foil for appetising cuisine made with local produce in tune with modern sensibilities. Rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Etsi
Description: Mikaela, a young chef of Greek origin, has turned her focus to the cuisine of her childhood, after cutting her teeth in some prestigious establishments. Here, she proposes strikingly fresh mezze with bold touches. The feta, olives, capers, charcuterie, cheeses and olive oil have all come straight from Greece. Enjoy in the exceedingly warm and friendly setting.

Name: Le Chiquito
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In a handsome 17C edifice, this restaurant continues to fly the flag of gourmet hospitality and upholds a distinctly bourgeois brand of elegance. Chef Anne-Sophie Godry has remained true to the establishment’s traditional Gallic ethos and its signature dishes, among which calf’s sweetbread with a frothy butter, sole meunière and Paris-Brest praliné à l'ancienne with a chicory custard. The front-of-house team is cheerful, competent and slick. Terrific wine list, with more than 400 references.

Name: Eels
Description: At Eels, the dishes flirt with "bistronomie", and some of them focus on eel (the clue is in the name). The young chef, Adrien Ferrand, already has considerable experience under his belt (six years for William Ledeuil, first at Ze Kitchen Galerie, then KGB). And now he has a place of his own. A success!

Name: Thomas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Owner-chef Thomas Ponson is not one to twiddle his thumbs, to the point that the street could almost be named after him, given the quantity of thriving businesses (bistro, café, bouchon, fish and seafood restaurant) he has opened here. In the parent bistro, he crafts enticing lunchtime menus, while the evening score shines the spotlight on his high-flying technical skills, revolving around ingredients such as scallops, pigeon, lamb sweetbread, etc). A must…

Name: Les Pyrénées
Description: An institution in St Jean Pied de Port, passed down from father to son. Both the decor and the cuisine pay homage to the classicism and taste of the Basque country, all of which with good quality produce.

Name: Sterenn
Address: 432 rue de la Joie, Penmarc'h, 29760, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This pleasant restaurant perched on the Pointe de Penmarch serves cuisine that is rooted in the local area and made using top-notch ingredients. The chef puts a lot of effort into meticulously plating his dishes, particularly when it comes to the fish. For dessert, it's all about tradition and savoir-faire, eg the buttery kouign amann, served warm, is nicely caramelised, and soft and crispy at the same time. Lovely views over the bay and Eckmühl Lighthouse.

Name: Lauryvan
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this verdant setting in a small wood close to the Vienne River, tuck into meticulous cuisine attuned to the seasons. The inspector was a fan of the organic confit egg, creamy parsnip purée, Cantal cheese shavings and ham crisps, as well as the lovely terrace with a view of the lake. Two spaces: restaurant and bistro.

Name: Hostellerie du Prieuré
Description: This 18C sandstone former convent chants a pure-bred Gallic culinary litany based on regional produce (rack of lamb from the Moselle meadows, fillet of Lorraine beef) and seafood (brill, line-caught whiting, scallops). The portions are generous and the desserts by Maeva (the owners’ daughter) are divinely decadent, illustrated by her Grand Marnier-flavoured strawberry soup. Charming welcome.

Name: Au Cœur de la Forêt
Description: A welcoming decor in two rustic rooms, one of which is very spacious with rafters and a fireplace. Shaded summer terrace. Simple, traditional menu in tune with the seasons.

Name: Café Bras
Description: The Café Bras, established in the heart of the Soulages Museum, pays tribute to Averyron produce. Two possibilities: order a snack or picnic basket from the counter or take a seat in the restaurant… The kitchen team crafts crisp, aromatic, light dishes, rich in generosity, colour and scents, like a tartare of tuna marinated in calamansi and Greek-style cucurbits or breast of roast duckling, acidic jus, new potatoes, cone cabbage and tiger courgettes with a sauce vierge. The attention lavished on flavour is second to none, as are the welcome and interior décor. Fully worthy of its ongoing success.

Name: L'Escargot 1903 par Yannick Tranchant
Description: L'Escargot 1903 is enjoying a new lease of life and welcomes a chef with a proven track record (Ritz, L'Abeille). His market - centred cooking sends sparks flying: meticulous presentations, underpinning finesse, harmonious marriages of flavours. The "must" is to get a look in on the terrace, weather permitting. The lunch set menu is a bargain.

Name: Sourire Le Restaurant
Address: 15 rue de la Santé, Paris, 75013, France
Description: Blue velours banquette seating, old-school bistro tables, trusted farmers (Galician pink veal, Clavisy Farm lamb): the tried-and-tested formula hits the spot, a case in point being the Bay of Morlaix scallops, medley of cabbage, candied lemon. The lunchtime set menu provides two options for every course. A second restaurant in the 5th arrondissement serves tapas in the evening and brunch at the weekend.

Name: Lao Lane Xang 2
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Parisian chapter of the history of the Siackhasones, originally from Laos, began in the 1990s with the creation of the Lao Lane Xang 1. In 2007, Do and Ken – worthy heirs of the family know - how – opened this second restaurant. The dishes are Laotian, Thai and Vietnamese specialities. Simplicity and flavour are on the menu!

Name: Le Villaret
Description: Not far from Oberkampf, this bistro serves wholesome, traditional and seasonal cuisine crafted by enthusiastic chef Olivier Gaslain. Oxtail in foie gras, pickles and a salad of garden herbs; calf’s head, tongue and brains in a ravigote sauce and, to finish, a rum-flavoured baba with ginger and clementines flanked by a mascarpone mousse that will leave you speechless! A superb wine list with more than 1 000 labels, some of which are displayed in a splendid glazed wine cabinet.

Name: Caïus
Description: This restaurant is named after the chef's great-grandfather. Indeed, Jean-Marc Notelet keeps one eye on the past, seeking out spices and other ideas with which to reinvent recipes and put together a delightfully creative culinary experience. Quality ingredients are expertly prepared – the starter of pointed cabbage and clams is a masterclass; the snapper fillet, seared with great precision, is accompanied by a good helping of slightly spiced vegetables and a flavourful creamy bisque of green crab; the pear dessert is hearty and delicious. Inside this restaurant with a plain, discreet façade, two areas coexist: metal and leather on one side, velvet and light wood on the other, which has a view of the kitchen. Efficient and precise service.

Name: Vantre
Address: 19 rue de la Fontaine-au-Roi, Paris, 75011, France
Description: In France in the Middle Ages, a vantre was a "place of enjoyment", and indeed that's certainly still the case here today. In a neo-bistro interior, a former sommelier (Le Bristol, Le Taillevent) and his chef serve fine dining cuisine prepared using carefully selected ingredients. Every dish looks and tastes terrific, a case in point being the roast sea bass with marinière sauce and samphire, presented vertically. Over 3 000 wines… and well-deserved success.

Name: L'Institut Restaurant
Address: Le Royal, 20 place Bellecour, Lyon, 69002, France
Description: On Place Bellecour, this training restaurant feels nothing like a school! In a contemporary decor designed by Pierre - Yves Rochon, with open kitchens giving onto the restaurant, the students deliver a high standard of service. The dishes are extremely well made and deserve a high mark.

Name: Osteria Ferrara
Description: Foodies can come here safe in the knowledge that they have found sanctuary in this elegant interior where the culinary magic happens. Sicilian chef Fabrizio Ferrara builds a menu of tasty and well-crafted ingredient-led Italian recipes, such as carpaccio of lean meat, puntarelle and Sicilian citron, or ravioli stuffed with Castelmagno cheese and potatoes. This bistro has soul, and an appealing wine list to boot.

Name: Le Clos du Vigneron
Description: The hillside vineyards of the Coteaux du Giennois lie adjacent to Le Clos du Vigneron. Here you can enjoy hearty, fresh and seasonal cuisine, with an emphasis on fish: the chef works like a true craftsman and is passionate about his profession. Handy guestrooms should you wish to stay overnight.

Name: Les Bas-Rupts
Address: 181 route de la Bresse, les Bas-Rupts, Gérardmer, 88400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the upper reaches of Gérardmer, this imposing chalet has been run by the same family for five generations. The culinary focus is on classical dishes with a regional touch, like duck foie gras with blueberries and Payoux saffran brioche, or boned Vosges quail à la Provençale.. The wine list is out of this world.

Name: Le Suprême
Description: The brainchild of a Franco-Korean couple of chefs who met in New York, the ubiquitous chicken is the star of this vintage bistro oozing with charm. The chef, former right-arm man of Daniel Boulud, consummately signs a gourmet gateau of sautéed chicken livers and a chicken in “half-mourning” that has already become a signature dish. This virtuoso technician has also invented a wafer-thin tart of Nashi pear, scallops and Brussels sprouts. Local game in season. Knockout wine list.

Name: Fuumi
Description: This young Japanese restaurant, located in the centre of Fontainebleau, is none other than the outpost of L'Axel, the Michelin - starred restaurant of chef - patron, Kunihisa Goto, and his wife, Vanessa. In this convivial setting, sample aromatic and generous traditional Japanese dishes, as well as gyoza and ramen. Booking strongly recommended.

Name: Côté Quillier
Description: The sibling of the next-door Relais de la Poste is devoted body and soul to wholesome seasonal cooking. Landes asparagus roasted with parmesan and ham; fillet of hake with celery tagliatelle; roast pineapple, frothy coconut mousse and exotic fruit ice cream. The terrace is a hit in fine weather and, even better, why not linger and enjoy a game of skittles on the lawn afterwards? Friendly vibe.

Name: Chez Flo
Description: Guests are greeted with a smile in this friendly eatery… The same sunny disposition depicts the food, which is in the competent hands of an enthusiastic young chef. Uplifting, modern bistro fare composed with ingredients from carefully selected local producers in a menu that changes monthly. Deliciously eater-friendly priced lunchtime menu. Something of a regional benchmark.

Name: Le Lénigo
Address: 11 quai du Lénigo, Le Croisic, 44490, France
Description: This restaurant located opposite the fish market is run by a very pleasant family. Seaside atmosphere (varnished wood, portholes) and fresh, carefully prepared seafood dishes.

Name: Le Garet
Description: This veritable institution is well known among aficionados of Lyonnais cuisine. Calf’s head, tripe, dumplings and andouillette sausages are served in a convivial atmosphere and in a typical setting.

Name: L'Estérel
Description: Mulhouse's Estérel serves 100% homemade dishes made with market - fresh ingredients that are tasty and very contemporary. The shady terrace is taken by storm in summer.

Name: Au Coin du Bois
Description: A quiet chalet surrounded by fir trees, whose country setting can be enjoyed from the lovely terrace. The chef deftly crafts great French classics whilst respecting the seasons: local frog’s legs; fried trout from Franche Comté; snails in flaky pastry and a Savagnin sauce; game.

Name: Restaurant Fond Rose
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A 1920s mansion transformed into a chic brasserie by the Bocuse group. With its terrace surrounded by 100 year - old trees, it is the epitome of peace and quiet. The food is tasty and generous and squarely in the tradition of the areas around the River Saône, with frogs' legs and quenelles etc.

Name: L'Argot
Description: This restaurant doubles as a butcher’s shop in the Brotteaux district. Customers first choose their cut of meat from the refrigerated display counter: beef from Limousin, Galicia, Aubrac and lamb and veal from Auvergne, served with a tasty side dish of the day. Good, wholesome, no-nonsense food.

Name: Les Remparts
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: If you would like to taste the high-flying cuisine of chef Arnaud Faye, this little sister of the Chèvre d’or is just the ticket. In addition to the jaw-dropping view from the terrace overlooking the Mediterranean, St-Jean-Cap-Ferrat and the Bay of Angels, you will sample consummate, Mediterranean dishes, followed by a trolley of ices and pastries to die for! Heavenly!

Name: Restaurant du Musée
Address: 2 rue de la Rochette, Fréland, 68240, France
Description: In this former mill on the Ure, next to the museum of the Welche country, Alain Schmitt’s cooking finds varied inspiration, close to home in “terroir” dishes (fleischschnaka of local trout) and further afield (line-caught grouper in a yosenabe style dashi broth).

Name: Avelan
Address: Hôtel Coquillade Provence, Hameau Le Perrotet, Gargas, 84400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of a luxury resort in the midst of the sweet-scented Luberon gorse land, this restaurant sports a Provençal-style interior and a patio shaded by a pergola overlooking the surrounding hillsides. Chef Pierre Marty crafts distinctive cuisine, packed with rugged flavours (chilli, ginger, etc.) and strong Mediterranean influences, yet his consummate signature dish is a textbook pithiviers of poultry and foie gras. Vegetarian menu, trolleys brimming with home-made bread and splendid cheeses, plus a remarkable wine list, in which the estate’s wines figure prominently. A bistronomic alternative is available at Les Vignes restaurant.

Name: Ty Mad
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: On the heights of Tréboul in a quiet residential district, sample fresh dishes in which market availability and organic produce are much more than a fashionable concept. Dig into a buckwheat pie of aubergines and sheep’s cheese or black Guengat pork rich in local aromas, before making your way down the coastal path to the beach below for a nap! Vegan menu.

Name: Auberge des Vieilles Pierres
Description: This inn run by a couple of industry professionals is located on the outskirts of Flers. Behind an inviting frontage, it boasts a modern space with contemporary bistro-style furnishings, where you can tuck into the chef's up-to-the-minute dishes. Fast service.

Name: Les Bories
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In Luberon, “bories” are dry-stone huts built by and for shepherds and they inspired the architecture of this farmstead on the road to Sénanque Abbey. Overlooking sweet-scented scrubland, the grounds and gardens provide the foundation of the scrumptious provençal-focused cuisine, which showcases regional produce such as Sisteron lamb and Mediterranean fish without forgetting fruit and veg from Luberon.

Name: Le Moulin des Quatre Saisons
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This delightful 16C building set in the town centre on the banks of the River Loir offers an absolutely enchanting setting whatever the season! The contemporary cuisine follows the seasons and is accompanied by a fine selection of wines (including some from Austria, the proprietor's home country). On sunny days, you can sit out on the terrace and soak up the enchanting setting.

Name: 14 Avenue
Description: Simplicity and quality are the watchwords here. Seafood ingredients are treated with the utmost respect: appetising when presented on the plate, then nicely prepared by chef Antoine Le Moal. The starter of crab, prawn and lobster is fresh and well seasoned, the skate wing carefully cooked, and the rum baba adds the final flourish of deliciousness. The modern interior is elegant, and the friendly service comes with a smile.

Name: Léonie
Description: The name is a tribute to the original founder, who opened this modest eatery back in the 1940’s. It has since morphed into a trendy gourmet bistro in the capable hands of an enthusiastic young couple. Originally from Deux-Sèvres, the chef fell in love with the Basque Country and its produce; he has made game his speciality in season. We sampled leek vinaigrette and hard-boiled mimosa eggs, chuck beef stew, mashed potatoes, finishing with orange mousse and meringue – gutsy, rustic and traditional to the core!

Name: Chez Éric
Description: On the square of a charming village, this dry-stone building has everything you could wish for, from a shaded terrace to a bistro-style interior. To top it all off, the Provençal fare is full of flavour. For instance, the courgette flower stuffed with Brousse cheese and basil, Mediterranean meagre, rockfish stock with saffron and tarte Tatin with apricots from Provence go down a treat!

Name: Les Semailles
Address: 10 rue du Petit-Magmod, La Wantzenau, 67610, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This spruce Alsace house stands in a quiet side street. On the menu: top-notch ingredients, perfectly cooked, intelligently seasoned and paired and a catering tradition that upholds the practice of tableside service (a rack of veal is carved and langoustine is seared on hot stones right in front of the diner). We were particularly taken with the langoustines, asparagus and caviar – a masterpiece of scrumptious delicacy. When the weather is fine, make a beeline for the terrace shaded by a hundred-year-old wisteria.

Name: Hostellerie du Cygne
Description: A classic dining room with plenty of wood panelling on one side, a Renaissance Alsace-style dining area on the other, and in both cases, tasty traditional cuisine such as presskopf of pork cheek with mixed vegetables or lamb chops served with chorizo ratatouille. One thing is for sure, food like this keeps diners coming back for more. There are few comfortable guestrooms, should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Le Table du 6717
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Looking out onto the woods and decorated in harmony with nature, Le Garden serves a buffet lunch during the week and a more ambitious offering in the evenings and at lunchtime on Sundays, in the form of a single set menu. The cuisine is modern and some of the vegetables they cook come straight from the garden. The Herdshire sirloin steak served with crispy chanterelle mushrooms and gravy is nothing short of memorable.

Name: Abacus
Description: This couple from Rouen and Paris were drawn to the South of France, and landed here in the heart of Montpellier's Écusson neighbourhood, in their tiny restaurant with an intimate and warm atmosphere. Meticulous preparations, interplay of textures, seasonal dishes, smiling service and a savvy choice of wines: what more could you ask for?

Name: Côté Jardin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Château de Beaulieu's contemporary brasserie serves cuisine devised by chef Christophe Dufossé that embraces both the traditional and the modern. The setting is superb, and the top-notch dishes are meticulously prepared: tartare of royal sea bream, textures of Granny Smith apple and mascarpone cream; volaille de Licques (free-range poultry) and beetroot; "Signature by CD" choux pastries with dark chocolate, Bourbon vanilla and Arabica coffee... Barbecue on the large terrace in summer, simmered dishes in winter.

Name: La Fourchette
Description: Collections of cutlery, cicadas, photos, greetings cards and knick - knacks: this bistro – with decor that is cluttered yet charming – is often full. Tasty cuisine of southern inspiration.

Name: Les 16 Clochers
Description: The terrace of this restaurant boasts a superb panoramic view over the valley's 16 church towers. The new, young and energetic team swear by local and organic producers (for their mushrooms, eggs and vegetables in particular) to create their well-crafted and market-fresh cuisine. The menu changes regularly and the terrace is popular in summer.

Name: Le K'ozzie
Address: 20 route de Francin, Porte-de-Savoie, Les Marches, 73800, France
Description: This inviting and cosy restaurant is run by Maude and Sébastien, who met in Australia, land of the Aussies or Ozzies (the reference behind the name). The concept is to let yourself be guided by the chef's inspiration; only a (non-exhaustive) list of the ingredients currently in his kitchen will be presented to you. Enigmatic and tasty.

Name: Le Verre à Soie
Description: After a career at Christian Têtedoie’s restaurant (Lyon), Fei - Hsin and Jérôme Lamy decided to take over this place. He still works as a sommelier, offering appetising food and wine pairings that showcase his wife’s lovely cooking, which is inspired by her Taiwanese origins. A wonderful marriage of French and Asian.

Name: C'Yusha
Description: Modern cuisine that makes full use of herbs and spices, created by a chef who works single - handedly in full view of the diners. Minimalist and intimately scaled (numbers are deliberately limited) in a resolutely contemporary setting.

Name: À l'Agneau
Description: In this Alsace inn dating from 1769, catering has been a family affair for seven generations. The two sisters now at the helm serve traditional cuisine that is in lockstep with the seasons and which they vary with the odd modern touch (we recommend the knuckle end of lamb confit for three nights, accompanied by bulgur wheat with sultanas and aromatic coriander).

Name: Le Clos Y
Description: Elegantly arranged next to each other, French cutlery and Japanese chopsticks symbolise the spirit of Le Clos Y. Quality ingredients, attentive execution, pursuit of subtlety: Yoshitaka Ikeda underscores once again all the well - established affinities of French and Japanese food. Simpler fare at lunchtime, "surprise menu" at dinner.

Name: Au Pont M
Address: 3 rue de la République, Wissembourg, 67160, France
Description: In the heart of Little Venice, this former local butcher's now draws crowds of diners keen to tuck into the creations of the chef – truly passionate about ingredients, he pays tribute to his suppliers by displaying their names. Here, the ultimate experience is to dine on the terrace on the banks of the Lauter, or inside with a view of the Église St-Pierre-et-St-Paul.

Name: Au Grès du Marché
Address: 19 rue du Château, La Petite-Pierre, 67290, France
Description: A warm welcome awaits you at this cosy restaurant in the old part of the village! The chef rustles up traditional cuisine made with seasonal ingredients and remarkably fresh meats, such as locally hunted venison, cooked in a stew at a low temperature and accompanied by ceps and spaetzle. He does also cook more contemporary dishes, such as duck tataki served with sauerkraut salad.

Name: À l'Agneau d'Or
Description: Head cheese with vinaigrette sauce, fillet of pikeperch on sauerkraut with Riesling sauce, a different kind of home-made tart every day. These are examples of the delights this Alsace establishment, typical both in appearance and philosophy, has in store for you. The decor is eminently inviting and the dishes exude the great flavour of the region's recipes.

Name: La Maison Despouès
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: The former home of French pop singer, Pierre Vassiliu, who was N°1 in the hit parade in 1973, is now devoted to singing the praises of porkpie with cream of black garlic, line-caught hake, cream of piquillo and a purée of leeks or a creamy delight of rhubarb and hazelnuts. The score is now in the talented hands of chef Julien Razemon, who grew up in les Landes and learned the ropes with the Coussau family. Julien plays a refined, gourmet melody, with the bonus of a view of the Gers hillsides or the Pyrenees (in fine weather) for some tables.

Name: Mademoiselle 10
Description: On the banks of the Ill, this charming restaurant delights its regulars with very reasonable prices, especially at lunchtime. Salmon and leek mosaic wrapped in nori, scallops with sweet potato and coconut cream, or fillet of duck, home-made cep gnocchi and “spicy cocoa” jus...

Name: La Suite
Description: It is well worth hunting out this smart, modern bistro, slightly out of the historic centre, to sample seasonal Gallic fare, entirely made from scratch and reworked to suit today’s tastebuds, with one overriding ambition: searingly good food. Examples include Iberico pork presa coated in soy honey and coulis of courgettes. Consummate technique, gutsy flavours and sweet and sour contrasts depict this culinary score.

Name: Zuem Ysehuet
Description: In a neighbourhood on the bank of the Ill, this inn clad in Virginia creeper also has a quiet picturesque terrace. In the tasty dishes, seasonal ingredients take pride of place: vegetables grown by the chef's father and intelligently cooked by his son. The lamb fillet, osso buco-style vegetables and date condiment is a good example. Terrific wine list, with a particularly good choice of wines by the glass.

Name: L'Instant
Description: Outside the centre, in a residential area near the train station, this lovely 1930s town house welcomes you in an attractive contemporary decor; you are served delicious market cuisine, made with lovely fresh ingredients. Dishes that you wolf down... in an Instant!

Name: Chez Delagare
Description: A delightful surprise awaits you opposite Saint-Roch station, in the Belaroïa complex. Chef is visible in the open kitchen concocting a concise, punchy menu, poised between bistronomy and street food. Appetising, colourful and aromatic: what more can we add?

Name: La Femme du Boucher
Description: Established in a former butcher’s, energetic Laëtitia Visse, who trained at the Paris Ferrandi School before stints in star restaurants and renowned bistros (Guy Savoy, Alain Dutournier, Cyril Lignac, Olivier Nasti at Kaysersberg) has, unsurprisingly given the name, decided to focus on meat: homemade pâté, fried black pudding, sausages, pig’s trotters, etc… Equally in tune with the zeitgeist, her wine list is strongly focused towards natural and biodynamic wines. Casual service and vibe. In the finest traditions of a Gallic bistro!

Name: Les Jardins du Léman
Description: In the heart of the pedestrianised medieval city, this appealing restaurant is laid out over several levels and furnished in a contemporary style. It proposes modern, impeccably crafted and generous dishes, all washed down with the best Savoie wines. Attentive welcome and service. Be sure to book if you wish to enjoy the splendid panoramic terrace overlooking the château and Lake Geneva.

Name: Dorangeville
Description: A picturesque medieval village provides the backdrop for this attractive 14C building, which now houses a restaurant boasting an elegant contemporary interior and a terrace overlooking the garden. Chef Quentin Dorangeville, who hails from France's Sarthe département, cooks up seasonal cuisine that is as meticulous as it is ambitious. Using fine ingredients, he creates striking combinations, such as confit egg, fragola sarda, chanterelles and chorizo. Good food and service with a smile!

Name: Bistro de Montcaud
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Château de Montcaud's chic new bistro serves traditional Southern French cuisine, with priority given by chef Mathieu Hervé to local, often organic ingredients: poultry and foie gras pâté en croûte, vegetable pickles; tomato gazpacho, watermelon granita and shiso leaf; rockfish three ways, bouillabaisse-style fish soup. The shaded terrace looking out onto the grounds is pleasant; plus a warm welcome and cordial service await.

Name: Byblos Beach
Description: On the Plage de Pampelonne, this beachside restaurant was designed with sustainability in mind and; a picture-perfect vision of sanded wood and cotton awnings, it is a must! On the menu: delicious fish, meat from the wood-fired grill and highly popular pasta dishes – to be enjoyed with your toes in the sand and eyes on the waves lapping at the shore.

Name: L'Affranchi
Description: In one of the oldest streets in the city, nestled beneath the arcades, this creative restaurant prides itself on its "no-holds-barred gastronomy". True to their word, the team at the helm whisk up fresh and appetising cuisine, using ingredients sourced via short supply chains. Relaxed service in an inviting space with a nod to street art.

Name: Union
Address: Vieux village de Montalbert, Aime, 73210, France
Description: This is the Union of British chef Phil Howard (The Square then Elystan Street in London) and Martin Cuchet, a French mate, nuts about the mountains. From December to April, they craft simple, heart-warming dishes that reverently respect the seasons, such as “twice cooked” Beaufort soufflé, sautéed leeks and mushrooms, or upside-down tarte tatin with Chantilly cream. Heroically wondrous and uplifting.

Name: À l'Ami Fritz
Description: Mr Fritz is the chef - patron but the restaurant name also refers to the novel by Erckmann and Chatrian (1854), in which the hero sacrifices everything for good food. Quite a patronage for well - made Alsace cuisine, served in an interior that also showcases all the charm of the region.

Name: Côté Lac
Description: This raw concrete and glass parallelepiped looks slightly incongrouous standing on the banks of a small lake in an industrial area in the north of the city. The interior has a distinct modern loft feel with its modern lighting and contemporary paintings. Enjoy the current and carefully prepared dishes from a menu that changes regularly.

Name: Zum Loejelgucker
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a wine-growing village at the foot of the Vosges, this 18C Alsace farmhouse has bags of charm: tasty regional dishes, plus some more modern options, dark wood panelling, frescoes and a flower-decked courtyard in summer. Warm, friendly service and a family vibe.

Name: Partage
Description: Julien Marseault has devised his devilishly well-crafted menu around the “share plate” principle (2 to 4 people). This experienced Breton chef is comfortable whatever the culinary register, from traditional (pig’s trotters and confit of shoulder of veal) to contemporary (tartare of beef and oysters). Delicious and friendly.

Name: Auberge de la Chèvrerie
Description: Tucked away in the countryside, this tastefully appointed contemporary inn draws foodies likes bees to honey. The menu adds a tasty new twist to Alsace classics thanks to meticulously selected seasonal ingredients. For example, the goat’s cheese comes from the next-door cheese dairy run by the chef’s brother. The egg parfait ensconced in a crunchy nest and served with a frothy truffle-flavoured celery sauce is a culinary masterpiece and the nostalgic banana split is to die for!

Name: Maison Colbert
Description: Welcome to this friendly bistro right in the city centre, which fills up quickly with diners keen to sample tasty and aromatic market-fresh cuisine. On our visit, confit beef chuck cooked in Chinon wine and served with crushed potatoes; and vol-au-vent with poulette sauce graced the menu… This is clearly a chef who knows his way around the classics.

Name: Spelt
Description: Here in the historical heart of the fortified town, Raphaël (on savoury dishes) and Marion (desserts) delight diners with full-flavoured and tasty bistronomy creations: cod tempura, broccoli and tartar sauce; lemon, sablé biscuit, meringue and tequila sorbet. In the evening, they serve a tasting menu that includes spelt risotto with lobster, the house's signature dish.

Name: L'Établi
Description: This restaurant run by an alumnus of Christian Têtedoie is a real favourite. The lunch menu is good value for money, the dishes are in keeping with the times and seasonal (hake, asparagus, fennel, smoked raspberry): from start to finish it's a treat. Not to spoil anything, the service is also attentive.

Name: Les Bartavelles
Description: Devoted to pleasure! First-rate, often local produce: smoked trout from the Moulin des Couvent or Touraine asparagus. Ingredients with crisp, legible flavours, such as rack of roast lamb, cocoa flavouring, roast fennel, potatoes and mushrooms. Chef Ghislain Damaye and his sister Véronique, who tends to the wellbeing of the front of house, pay tribute to the memory of French novelist Marcel Pagnol, in their smart, city centre bistro, courtesy of an ethos that seeks to share their love of good food.

Name: La Petite Table
Address: 7 quai de la Pêcherie, Capbreton, 40130, France
Description: Whether seated on the terrace or inside, you are promised an enticing culinary interlude at this really inviting compact restaurant on Capbreton harbour. Generous and colourful dishes enhanced by citrus fruit and spices get to the heart of the matter, showcasing the local catch, lamb from the Pyrenees and vegetables from a market gardener in nearby Tosse. Don't miss the chocolate tart – a proper showstopper!

Name: Le Rouergat
Address: 4 place de la Mairie, Casteculier, 47240, France
Description: This contemporary bistro is bistronomic at lunchtime and gastronomic in the evenings. In the hands of a veteran chef from Aveyron, overflowing with contagious enthusiasm, this friendly, invariably-packed eatery focuses on local, seasonal produce, jazzed up with the occasional globetrotting souvenir. We tasted duck foie gras terrine with pineapple and ginger chutney followed by roast guinea fowl, cream of green peas and a samosa of pleurote mushrooms.

Name: L'Auberge - Les Sources de Cheverny
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in sprawling wooded grounds, the chic bistro of the hotel Les Sources de Cheverny serves fine and meticulous seasonal dishes that constitute something of a whistle-stop tour of the Loire Valley, as well as a tribute to local producers: vegetables from a market gardener in Mont-Près-Chambord, Sologne strawberries, Roi Rose pork loin from Touraine roasted in the fireplace… which takes pride of place in the dining area: here, cooking over a wood fire is a speciality!

Name: La Brasserie des Haras
Description: A buzzing atmosphere at this large-capacity restaurant run by the great chef Marc Haeberlin, set in the former royal stables and stud farm, constructed during the reign of Louis XV. On the menu, modern cuisine, brasserie classics and a handful of local specialities. The superb contemporary décor with the original exposed roof structure is well worth a look !

Name: La Table du Prieuré
Address: 2 rue du Château, Le Louroux, 37240, France
Description: Chef Pierre Drouineau, who hails from Sarthe (near Le Mans), runs this restaurant at the entrance to an attractive fortified priory, the jewel in the crown of this charming country village. Both the setting and the food are a delight, thanks in particular to the wealth of local ingredients: Touraine lentils, spelt from Manthelan, strawberries from Chouzé-sur-Loire. Think modern bistro cuisine, simple and flavoursome, in the form of dishes such as fillet of duck, roasted crisps, new potatoes from Louans and carrot ketchup – a creation that is packed with distinct flavours. Look out for the affordable lunch set menu!

Name: Le Poème de Grignan
Description: This village restaurant is a poem indeed, with its old china, its flowers and flavours of Provence. Everything is carefully prepared, tasty and made on site. An invitation to revel in the best of the region.

Name: Le Piquebaure
Description: At the foot of Roussillon village, this picturesque dry-stone house proposes Provençal-inspired food in an enticing menu in which fresh produce is a major component. The restaurant’s pride and joy is its second terrace overlooking the wonderful Luberon countryside.

Name: L'Éternel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: At the foot of the hill leading to Vézelay basilica, a major pilgrimage site, L'Eternel caters to more earthly needs, in a bright interior.
