Chef Italo Bassi, who presides first and foremost over the kitchens of his MICHELIN-starred restaurant in Sardinia, has devised a menu that allies the cuisines of Italy and Corsica. The mainly local ingredients are handpicked in these masterfully prepared dishes – the double ravioli with two fillings, burrata, guinea fowl casserole and its reduction, light cream of parmesan and fresh thyme is a particularly appetising signature dish!

Name: La Table du Moulin
Description: Green peas and sage-flavoured fresh goat’s cheese gnocchi; lacquered monkfish, curcuma-flavoured carrot juice and aromatic fregola sarda; tarte Tatin and double cream. Behind the titles of the dishes, each more tempting than the last, you get a sense of a confident chef who knows where he’s going. Chef and "Meilleur Ouvrier de France" Jacques Rolancy concocts indulgent bistro fare within the walls of a converted mill (always cool, even in the heat of summer). Bargain-priced lunchtime menu and peaceful terrace.

Name: Acte 2
Address: 3 rue de la Petite-Calade, Avignon, 84000, France
Description: In the city of the famous arts festival, theatre is even part of the restaurant experience. Act I: a young couple of industry professionals set up shop in the historical centre. Act II: dishes that are packed with delicious, fresh local and seasonal ingredients. Act III: excellent value for money, whether you opt for the five-course dinner or the three-course lunch. The scene is set! Tuck into scallop carpaccio and turnip with lemon and juniper, or the veal fillet with truffle and Albufera sauce.

Name: Petit Jacques
Description: As you make your way up through the pretty paved streets of Grimaud to this enchanting leafy patio, you are already bewitched. Spread over two floors, the charm of this house is undeniable (light wooden floors, raftered ceilings, lime plastered walls, well-worn bench seating and soft lighting). The Quebec-born chef and his partner in charge of the front of house regale diners with spot-on market-fresh cuisine and a traditional culinary line-up, featuring family favourites like onion soup or French toast (of brioche) with a scoop of Madagascan vanilla ice cream to die for! Everything is made in house, including the bread!

Name: L'Argousier
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In this pleasant contemporary restaurant, the young chef’s cuisine varies with the seasons. The food is cooked and seasoned to perfection, the presentation flawless, as in this duck fillet with confit vegetables and red wine jus. Friendly and attentive service and a fine selection of vintage rums.

Name: Frédéric Carrion Cuisine Hôtel
Description: The elegant dining room combines the character of this former coaching inn (parquet, fireplace) with more plush and cosy touches. The chef uses fine regional produce to concoct wonderfully creative dishes. Your meal is accompanied by a delightful selection of wines, including a range of Viré - Clessé wines. The pleasant rooms and spa round off your stay in wine - growing country.

Name: L'Orangerie
Address: La Bastide de Gordes, 61 rue de la Combe, Gordes, 84220, France
Description: This famous village is one of the most prized in the Luberon Regional Nature Park. This stately home, which dominates the valley, now houses a luxury hotel – as well as this restaurant and its stunning terrace shaded by chestnut trees. The view is one of the location's greatest assets. In the style of a luxury brasserie, the menu gives some of the classics a Provençal twist: think gambero rosso with grapefruit, sole meunière and dauphinoise potatoes with lemon, or fillet of lamb with white asparagus. Evening tasting menu featuring dishes from the à la carte menu.

Name: La Grange
Description: In this city centre restaurant, old stones blend seamlessly with contemporary decoration. On the menu: market - fresh ingredients and a handful of bistro specialities with Basque overtones. In summer, make the most of the terrace beneath the arcades, on the banks of the Nive.

Name: Le Seize
Description: This small Provençal bistro nestling in the old town of Arles ticks all the boxes, with its decor of burnt sienna and cream tones and wrought-iron tables. Sarah and Julien Richard have hit upon a winning formula right off the bat, serving dishes such as tomato confit with vanilla oil and lime, and courgette and basil velouté; thinly sliced monkfish with seaweed butter, Camargue rice with fennel, and a fish soup jus. The chef uses aromatic herbs and flowers from his kitchen garden to enhance his dishes. The lunch menu is excellent value for money; more extravagant tasting menu on Thursday and Friday evenings; brunch on Sundays. A small selection of regional wines.

Name: Le Bistrot de la Caillère
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ideally located for anyone visiting the châteaux of the Loire, this inn is firmly rooted in its era. It is run by an enterprising couple, who work and live in harmony with the bucolic landscape of forests and meadows. The original 18C farmhouse has been replaced by a modern building – modern like chef Éric Rialland's cuisine. His well-thought-out bistronomy dishes follow the seasons and oscillate between creativity and tradition. Pleasant terrace for fine weather.

Name: Utopie
Description: In the heart of a small wine-growing village, this Utopia is being nurtured by a couple we first met in Strasbourg. Now installed in this handsome old edifice enhanced by contemporary fixtures and fittings, the experienced chef (George V, Pierre Gagnaire, Jean Imbert…) crafts a set menu in several courses in which vegetables take the limelight: green peas, sorrel, hemp oil; romaine lettuce, tarragon, black garlic and meat jus. Insightful wine-food pairings.

Name: L'Escudella
Description: L'Escudella is, aptly enough, "plate" in Occitan! Paul-Arthur Berlan, the young chef, has worked in some prestigious establishments (Michel Sarran, Yannick Alléno). Here, he marries produce from the terroir of the Greater Paris area with the flavours of Languedoc. With fresh, high-quality ingredients and well-crafted dishes, he hits the mark.

Name: Le Lien
Description: The bond here (‘lien’ in French) is that which ties this young couple (he’s in the kitchen, she in the front of house) to the winegrowers and producers whose work is showcased in the plates and glasses of this friendly bistro. Modern food with a creative twist founded on first-class seasonal ingredients that are allowed to shout their name. Two lunchtime menus and a more elaborate offering in the evening. Highly recommended.

Name: Séquence
Description: A mysterious name, no difference between the starters and the mains in the evening, exchanges of ideas with the customers (invited to preview the dishes in the kitchen): chef Antoine Triquet has chosen to break with conventions, true to the path that has led him from insurance to cooking. The culinary fundamentals are present and correct, the portions generous and tasty, nature and the seasons are respected, and the cooking is on point (buttery yet crispy poultry, creamy polenta and ketchup). The space has a poetic interior designed to encourage conversation.

Name: Regain
Description: Near the Saône embankment, a youthful team crafts appetising market-fresh fare (tempura of white tuna, aubergines, blackberries; veal cutlet and sweetbread from Clavisy farm, samphire, potatoes and white butter; figs and goat’s milk). The lunchtime menu offers a concise choice of dishes, while more extensive tasting menus are available in the evening. The interior sports an artfully distressed industrial vibe.

Name: Cascade
Address: 26 cour de la Filature, Salles-la-Source, 12330, France
Description: What a pretty village clinging to a cliff and famous for its cooling waterfall! What a pleasant, convivial place, with its warm, colourful bistro decor, lovely old wooden floorboards, counter and arty posters on the walls (and let's not forget the terrace overlooking the courtyard in front of the town hall). In the kitchen, chef Marine Guichou cooks up a feast, using carefully selected local produce, which she skilfully prepares in a fresh, authentic bistro style. And with her almond pannacotta and chocolate mousse on a cocoa crumble, she has created the quintessential dessert for anyone with a sweet tooth!

Name: Ro'cha
Description: The philosophy of seasoned chef Jean-Luc Rocha (who has captained many Michelin-starred restaurants) is that one experienced chef is worth two – especially one who has been a Meilleur Ouvrier de France since 2007. On every plate, you can sense the work of a wise and accomplished chef who masters all the tricks of his trade without ostentation; this certainly applies to his crispy "croque juste croustillant" with a poultry stuffing and herbs – a masterclass in finesse. From start to finish, the cooking and seasoning are deftly executed, a case in point being the lovely rare-cooked saddle of veal accompanied by seasonal vegetables glazed with butter and a meat jus. Professional service in the refined setting of a townhouse.

Name: Goxoki
Description: Goxoki means warm and cosy in Basque, which is perfectly suited to this restaurant in historic Bayonne, run by the Hourcastagnou family. An elegant, classical setting for food that shines the limelight on local seasonal produce and an attractive game menu. Connoisseurs will be delighted to know that the gravy boats remain on the table – as quintessentially French as La Marseillaise.

Name: Choral
Description: In the Romains district, 10 minutes from the centre, take a seat in this long, Scandinavian-inspired dining room opened by a chef who did a stint at Le Clos des Sens with Laurent Petit, before globe-trotting around the planet. The memory of his line-caught cod, tetragon, lemon and capers à la grenobloise lingers with us still. Alban’s instinctive, fine dining score (free of butter, cream and milk, except for desserts) is, for the most part, dictated by the availability of fresh market produce (such as baked apricots, honey and rhubarb sorbet), which are then given a deft professional spin. Mystery menu in several courses in the evening.

Name: Les Gueules Noires
Address: 66 rue de la Vallée-Coquette, Vouvray, 37210, France
Description: The troglodyte dining room, wood burning fire in winter and the terrace shaded by a wisteria in fine weather are just a few of the discreet appeals of this charming establishment. The cuisine is tasty and wholesome, based on local produce and served with Loire wines. Booking advisable.

Name: Nous Restaurant
Description: With its discreet façade and small glass-paned front door, this restaurant is located in a pedestrianised cobbled street in the city centre. The light-filled interior has bay windows overlooking the street on one side and a pretty courtyard decorated with large window boxes on the other. The chef puts a lot of work into his dishes, which are made using local ingredients. The courgette flower, soufflé with fine pollack stuffing, shellfish sauce vierge, rocket cream and two-lemon fritter is a good illustration of his masterful dishes that are packed with flavour.

Name: Les Toits - Hôtel de Paris Saint-Tropez
Address: 1 traverse de la Gendarmerie, Saint-Tropez, 83990, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Timeless Saint Tropez remains as legendary as ever – this outdoor restaurant perched on the roof terrace of the fabled hotel is further proof of that. Gazing out over the bay and the tiled roofs of the village, you can savour cuisine inspired by the Mediterranean and Provence, with a few Italian touches thrown in for good measure (Sicilian gambas, tiramisu etc) – after all, the new chef, whose CV includes Il Carpaccio, Le Grand Véfour and Pierro TT in Paris, is Italian. A simpler set menu is proposed at lunchtime.

Name: L'EssenCiel
Description: Chef Jean-Marie Baudic (formerly of the Youpala bistro in St Brieuc) chose this modern eatery to craft a bistronomic repertory with his second chef Julien Rouault. Premium seasonal ingredients and intelligently crafted recipes are the focus: seabream and crunchy veggies; melt-in-the-mouth wing of skate with crunchy diced vegetables and a gutsy jus; shoulder of lamb paired with arancini… Different set menus at lunchtime, in the evening and at weekends.

Name: L'ExtrA
Address: 23 ter rue du Temple, Reims, 51100, France
Description: Opposite Boulingrin covered market (a listed monument), this restaurant is housed in an elegant 1920s Art Deco edifice. The majority of the staff from the kitchen to the front house is mentally impaired, in line with the establishment’s founding ethos to operate as an inclusive business. The kitchen team is managed by a seasoned duo made up of chef Philippe Joly (former second of the Foch) and pastry chef Francois-Xavier Cormarie. In a minimalist, contemporary setting, you can dip into a well-crafted modern menu: espuma of asparagus on a tartlet of Reims ham; skate wing, spelt risotto and nettle jus with a beurre noisette; strawberry pavlova and tartare with a red fruit sorbet. Fine selection of champagne wines.

Name: Gric
Description: Marie Gricourt's career has already taken her to the heights of Christophe Hay's La Table d'à Côté, where she was head chef. She has since opened her own restaurant, a convivial place in keeping with her personality. In this restaurant not far from the banks of the River Loire, the chef and her mainly female team (who provide service with a smile) put a new twist on bistro-style cuisine, simply and precisely: a surf and turf starter with scallops cradled in a sweet potato, bacon and prune purée; conchiglioni stuffed with beef chuck and porcini; and for dessert a delicious floating island with citrus fruit, honey and pollen.

Name: Cadet
Description: Between the Villa Majorelle and the Musée de l'École de Nancy, this restaurant is housed in a hundred-year-old former hairdressing salon. In a Scandinavian-style interior, brightened up by crates of vegetables, a few trendy cookery books and a vintage Faema coffee machine behind the counter, chef Theo Mareschal (previously encountered at La Maison dans le Parc in Nancy and Kontrast in Oslo) sticks to the brief and cooks up appealing contemporary cuisine that's simple and accessible, a case in point being the veal, mushrooms and baby potatoes or the surprising dessert of vanilla ice cream with squid ink, as black as a painting by Pierre Soulages!

Name: Agapes
Description: This is a small neighbourhood bistro that hasn't been revamped for the purposes of Instagram. A young couple with impressive interstellar careers give free rein to their (delicious) inspiration: vitello tonnato, rocket, capers and meticulously seasoned parmesan; excellent duck breast, koshihikari rice, Japanese ume plums, and raw and cooked quetsches, with their bittersweet flavours; and for dessert, a deconstructed Bourdaloue tart that leaves no doubt about pastry chef Arnaud Darbas's credentials. Front of house, cordial, competent Virginie Béziaud has up her sleeve well-chosen wines from small winegrowers served by the glass.

Name: Le Bouillon
Address: 9 rue de la Gare, Annecy, 74000, France
Description: In addition to meaning stock, a bouillon also refers to the first restaurants opened in Paris in the 18C. In a recently refurbished modern interior, the chef crafts tasty market-fresh recipes, with the odd Asian twist, such as a splendid loin of croaker in a chorizo crust underscored by a red curry and curcuma stock.

Name: La Table du Château
Description: The lord of the manor, who now owns this beautiful 17C inn, has entrusted the kitchens to chef Élisabeth Passédat. She may have worked abroad for many years, but she hasn't forgotten her French classics – pan-fried foie gras, pâté en croûte with Houdan poultry, veal sweetbreads, tournedos Rossini-style Charolais beef. She puts a modern spin on these dishes, blending them with seasonal ingredients and drawing inspiration from France's terroirs. In this way, she comes up with creations such as monkfish and spaetzle, Normandy cider velouté, or ravioli with mushrooms, Morbier cheese and a vin jaune emulsion.

Name: Ekume
Description: After clocking up some remarkable experiences on his CV, Panamanian chef Edgar Bosquez has dropped anchor in Marseille, not far from the Abbaye St Victor. In a modern and warm decor, he gives a platform to fish, seafood and Provence: fine aubergine tartlet; thinly sliced sea bream, carrot jus, achiote oil, citrus fruit and bottarga… Set menus comprising several courses, including one devoted to bouillabaisse.

Name: L'effet Papilles
Description: In the heart of the town, almost within shouting distance of the castle, this small modern bistro, which sports a workshop vibe of wood and metal, is the brainchild of chef Adrien Barrier, who was born in Le Mans and knows Mayenne inside out. After stints with Yannick Alléno and Philippe Mille, this gifted craftsman curates feel-good, flavoursome food that hits the spot every time, be it his white asparagus with haddock, houmous and hazelnut crumble or the confit of pork belly, pressed aubergine and pork jus.

Name: Lil'Home
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive restaurant on the Quai des Chartrons has a dining area with parquet flooring made up of repurposed wine crates, velvet-upholstered seats, wicker lampshades and hanging plants – think "chic bistro" style. The modern and creative cooking takes the form of multi-course surprise menus. Good selection of organic and biodynamic wines.

Name: Rouge
Description: Behind the port, in the antique dealer neighbourhood, a disciple of Yves Camdeborde is at the helm of this friendly wine bar. The chef prepares lovely Mediterranean sharing plates, concocted with ultra-fresh produce. It is delicious and hearty, and the wallet doesn't take too heavy a hit. A hundred or so lively wines feature on the list, also at reasonable prices. Open all day from noon (no reservations taken).

Name: Le Roc
Address: 13 vieille route des Pensières, Veyrier-du-Lac, 74290, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: "Roc'n Roll" tasting menu and seasonal set menu (smoked whitefish and watercress, Dombe chicken with vin jaune, vanilla millefeuille), comforting terroir-based dishes both local and from further afield, great wine list, contemporary interior with a "mountain chic" feel, and a young team who are on the ball. Chef Yoann Conte has covered all bases in this, his second restaurant, ensconced in the famous blue house. And, as always, the superb view of Lake Annecy.

Name: Braise
Description: The former second of Substance, Sylvain Courivaud, is determined to kindle our appetites in this contemporary venue entirely devoted to wood-fired cooking. Whatever the method from Japanese barbecue or Big Green Egg to a smoker, Sylvain combines consummate technique with a love of high-quality produce. The vibe of this trendy eatery is warm and welcoming.

Name: Auberge des Gorges
Description: With its cosy mountain-style decor, this converted 18C coaching inn on the road to the Gorges de la Diosaz is home to a creative restaurant that piqued our curiosity. Over the course of a single multi-course set menu, the young chef cooks up dishes that draw ingredients both from the lakes and the mountains, such as Arctic char with beurre blanc, cooked to perfection, or crayfish ravioli enhanced by a beautifully emulsified bisque. On top of that, the welcome and service are the epitome of charm. Six guestrooms for an extended stay, and view of the summit of Mont Blanc.

Name: Restaurant du Pont
Description: Next to the small Canal de Goulaine, this white building, once a bar and inn, has a refined contemporary interior and pleasant terrace-garden for fine weather. Having plied his trade abroad, chef Mathieu Corbineau now navigates between rather traditional recipes and more contemporary influences: crispy chicken with tandoori spices, carrot, cumin and kumquat sabayon; herb-crusted catch of the day, cereal risotto, citrus butter; gariguette strawberry, yuzu cream, frosted marshmallow gariguette, Montélimar nougat ice cream. An affordable set menu at lunchtime, and a wine list that gives Muscadet top billing.

Name: Auberge du Cheval Blanc
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: An upscale restaurant, run by the same family since 1785. In the attractive contemporary dining area, meals are paired with fine wines from Alsace, including an interesting selection by the glass. The culinary style is refined, the products of high quality, often locally-sourced, and the presentations elegant. The ambition to treat diners well is clear: you're sure to come out with a spring in your step. Guestrooms.

Name: Maison Renard
Address: 15 place de la République, Béthune, 62400, France
Description: Chef Sébastien Renard (Top Chef semi-finalist in 2022) has taken over the former premises of his mentor, the great chef Marc Meurin. This red-brick mansion oozes style, and its bar and elegant glass roof lend it undeniable flair. The chef, who hails from the region and made his solo debut here, turns out a carte blanche menu inspired by conversations with the growers who supply his kitchen with their produce. Dishes such as green asparagus, sheep's milk fromage frais and tarragon cream, or poached eggs in a red wine sauce with mushroom cream and walnut emulsion showcase all the savoir-faire of this chef with an impressive CV to his name.

Name: Le Bistrot du Brau
Description: A gorgeous country house tucked away in the refreshing shade of a Provençal oak grove, chirping cicadas, the gentle lapping of water in the pool, a menu of traditional cuisine supervised by chef Christopher Hache (whose Michelin-starred Maison Hache is next door) and fresh local ingredients: green asparagus, sabayon, parmesan and hazelnuts; confit shoulder of lamb from Crau; authentic crêpes Suzette. The scene is set for an irresistible interlude on the patio dotted with wrought-iron tables or in the all-white dining area furnished in black.

Name: Delicatessens
Address: Domaine du Berthiol, 725 route de Saint-Chamarand, Gourdon, 46300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the terrace or through the restaurant's large bay windows, the landscape seems to insinuate itself between the tables, as you can drink in a wonderful panoramic view over the grounds and the rooftops of Gourdon's old town in the distance. The menu showcases produce from the region through its own spin on traditional cuisine, which is enhanced by moments of creativity: potato gnocchi with sweet garlic, mushroom consommé and salsify espuma; trout fillet, creamy risotto with wild nettles and green asparagus.

Name: Le 49R
Description: Behind the somewhat terse name (referring to its address at 49 rue Royale), there lies a charming private mansion whose original decor is enhanced by well-placed modern touches. The delightful terrace overlooking the courtyard to the rear of the building is a particular highlight. The dishes are creative and rigorously executed: sea bass ceviche, hazelnuts and seaweed; duck breast, chanterelle mushrooms, red curry sauce. Excellent wine list and selection of spirits.

Name: Isolé
Description: Close to the town hall, this pretty single-storey building stands out from the urban landscape with its terrace and small vegetable garden. Victor Gaillard and Alice di Cagno (previously at Chatomat in Ménilmontant) are at the helm, enthusiastically sharing their love of good food and their commitment to sustainability. The duo propose a superb lunchtime set menu that is reasonably priced and lets the ingredients speak for themselves: watercress, hazelnut and Pecorino Pepato arancini; pulled veal in sauce blanquette, creamy polenta and button mushrooms; rum semolina cake, poached pear with smoked tea. On the last three days of the week, more sophisticated and creative fare can be sampled in the evening. A small selection of natural and organic wines.

Name: Ginko
Description: Near the Grand’Place, this unobtrusive eatery with a glazed facade is the brainchild of two pals, both of whom boast virtuoso CVs: Valentina Giacobbe was born in Italy and grew up in Asia, graduated in political science before she turned to cooking, training at Gaya with Pierre Gagnaire before working at Rozo and then at SOlange; and Julien Ingaud-Jaubert, who trained as a pastry chef and who has also worked in top establishments (Pierre Gagnaire, Meurin, La Laiterie). Their trendy venue is the picture of a sleek contemporary bistro complete with a red-brick wall, a tribute to Lille. Valentina’s creative, delicate recipes are both distinctive and exquisitely balanced. Her seasonal menu features dishes dominated by vegetables (like green peas paired with nettles or the wild garlic-flavoured hollandaise sauce that accompanies the cod), all of which might feature Italian or Asian accents. A fully vegetarian menu is also available.

Name: Maison Zugno
Address: Les Monts de Vaux, Barretaine, 39800, France
Description: Dating back to the late 18C, this former coaching inn has been turned into a charming hotel (nine guestrooms, a swimming pool and spa) and a restaurant with three small dining areas (wooden floors, walnut tables, exposed brick walls, floral wallpaper or a green wall). Chef Quentin Defert makes modern, entirely gluten-free cuisine from seasonal, often local produce (but that's not all). Starters include a pear brunoise paired with blue cheese from the nearby dairy in La Marre, creamed corn combined with hazelnuts, and melt-in-the-mouth Iberian pork belly served with romanesco and elevated by a flavoursome Thai emulsion.

Name: Mr Guss
Description: Augustin Guibert aka Guss, a chef with an impeccable track record, is going solo with this contemporary restaurant set at the foot of a beautiful 19C stone building. This inventive cook impresses with his substantial technical prowess, which allows him to play with flavours and textures, as he does with his violetta aubergine, roasted then glazed with honey and satay, potato fritters, hollandaise sauce with caramelised onions. Without fail, the arrival of the delicious dishes bursting with colour puts a smile on your face. Congratulations, too, for showcasing the finest local produce, most notably the vegetables.

Name: Le Bois Blanc
Address: 11 rue de la Sirène, Romorantin-Lanthenay, 41200, France
Description: Chambord asparagus and Sologne strawberries, freshwater fish like pike, catfish and carp, game in season: chef Maxime Valleye, with stints at Georges Blanc and in his parents’ establishment, sings an ode to his region. Even the restaurant’s name, which is evocative of a birch tree, is in tune with Sologne’s forests. Maxime carefully crafts seasonal dishes steeped in classical overtones: pork, confit of egg yolk, spinach and goat’s cheese crumble. The classy, stylish interior of this contemporary bistro sports varnished wooden tables and vintage incandescent light bulbs. Most of the tipples on the wine list are from the Val-de-Loire.

Name: Emporio Armani Caffè
Description: Just across from the famous Les Deux Magots, this smart contemporary-style brasserie on the ground floor of the Michelin-starred Armani/Ristorante is run at a brisk pace by the same Italian team. From verdure alla griglia drizzled with Apulian olive oil, linguine alle vongole veraci – cooked al dente and served with a delicious helping of bottarga – to classic tiramisu with a light and full-flavoured mascarpone cream, as well as spaghetti al pomodoro, ravioli del plin, risotto, tortellini: all the classics of Italian cuisine are present and correct, executed in time-honoured tradition.

Name: Via del Campo
Description: Authentic Italian cuisine is not as easy to come by in France as one might expect. Thankfully there is this contemporary trattoria, which also boasts a few tables on the verdant pavement terrace in fine weather. Chef Enrico Masia whisks diners off on a culinary voyage that takes in every region of Italy; the traditional fare of Sardinia, his birthplace, inspires the lion's share of dishes. Regulars eagerly consult the daily menu, which is devised in line with the food markets and the chef's inspiration on the day. You can expect dishes such as crunchy puntarella finished with an anchovy sauce, Venetian-style calf liver, and clam paccheri with fresh artichokes and shredded bottarga. Tatiana, the chef's partner, runs the show front of house, providing discreet and efficient service that includes astute recommendations when it comes to their selection of Italian wines.

Name: La Table de Pôl
Description: What luck to have a terrace next to the listed Fontaine de la Noix, with the bonus of a bird’s eye view of the show on market days. Inside, the decor blends exposed rafters, parquet floors, bare stonework and a palette of warm terracotta shades. The young chef, assisted by his Scottish partner for the front of house, whips up mouthwatering dishes: cream of green peas, breaded goat’s cheese with a mint and green pea condiment; grilled haunch of veal, cork-shaped potatoes, baby broad beans and watercress juice; confit kumquat, gingerbread and frothy vanilla mascarpone… Seasonal menus and ingredients.

Name: Les Jardiniers
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Along the old railway line, which is now a greenway, this charming bistro occupies a restored winegrower's house with exposed stonework and beams, an open kitchen and a pewter-topped counter at the entrance. A large kitchen garden and a truffle farm supply the establishment with fruit and vegetables. Formerly sous-chef to Thibaut Ruggeri at Fontevraud le Restaurant, Belgian chef Martin Bolaers makes the most of the vegetable garden to create wholesome and creative cuisine in which plants play the starring role: a starter dubbed "L'Instant T", for example, is improvised using vegetables picked that very morning. Local ingredients – such as poultry and cheese – also feature in the credits.

Name: Monsieur B
Address: 80 rue de la Liberté, Bourgoin-Jallieu, 38300, France
Description: The young chef cooks up fresh, tasty bistronomy cuisine without any showboating. The lunch set menu changes every week, while the evening menu evolves on a monthly basis in line with the market stalls and the seasons. An example might be his simple and tasty starter of peas, red tuna and kiwi. A convivial bistro in the heart of the town-centre pedestrian precinct.

Name: La Table de l'Europe
Description: Opposite the country town’s covered market, this tastefully appointed guesthouse and restaurant invite diners to sit down, relax and enjoy a good meal. You will taste the fine cuisine of a veteran chef who deftly crafts appetising French-accented dishes, depicted by slow-cooked pork belly and fluffy mashed potato. The chef’s desserts (she originally trained as a pastry chef) are wickedly irresistible: a hazelnut extravaganza of praline, hazelnut mousse and butterscotch – to die for!

Name: L'Écrin des Saveurs
Description: A father-and-son team is behind this brasserie-style restaurant with a smart, polished interior and a hint of Scandinavian flair. The father is a seasoned professional who has been cooking since he was 15 (his CV includes the Grand Hôtel du Lion d'Or in Romorantin and the Domaine des Dryades); his son provides enthusiastic service front of house. Farm produce and fish from Brittany are elevated by the sure touch of the chef: pan-fried snails and octopus, root vegetables and black garlic jus; sesame and dried lime biscuit, crumble with toasted sesame oil.

Name: La Table du Connétable - Auberge du Jeu de Paume
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: After visiting the Royal Castle of Chantilly, book a table in this luxurious inn abutting the gardens. In a lavish setting, dripping with fine art, chandeliers and tapestries, diners sample unabashedly creative cuisine with a weakness for vegetables and seafood: gyoza-style veal and eels, tarragon-flavoured labneh; wild turbot, salsify, za’atar and cognac with a peat-flavoured, roast chocolate extravaganza to finish. At Le Jardin d'Hiver bistro, traditional and seasonal dishes are served in the gallery or on the pretty patio.

Name: Au Jardin d'Eden
Description: This corner restaurant with a small teak terrace boasts an array of qualities: a chef - patron with a fine CV – including 15 years at Le Grand Véfour. Having gone back to his roots in Évian, he serves up generous and traditional cuisine that is in harmony with the ingredients and seasons; attentive service.

Name: La Bonne Auberge
Description: Lydia Egloff prepares inventive cuisine with complex flavours, while her sister gracefully welcomes diners. Unusual decor and a winter garden with bay windows. A fine wine list. The name says it all!

Name: La Grillade Gourmande
Description: This restaurant's specialities include boned squab with foie gras in puff pastry or traditional textbook calf sweetbread, all of which are the handiwork of a friendly chef of Lyon origins. The interior is the epitome of friendly and buzzy and the garden is bliss, come summertime!

Name: Cheval Blanc
Description: In this typical Sundgau house, food is a passion that has been handed down from generation to generation. Father and son cook lovely traditional dishes enhanced with a modern edge. Very good choice of wines. This White Horse really is a fine steed!

Name: L'Ô à la Bouche
Description: One site and two moods united by the same desire to make your mouth water! On the ground floor, a contemporary style of decor, and fresh, tasty gourmet cuisine, prepared by a chef with a distinct fondness for fresh produce and fish; in the basement (winter only), raclette, fondue and grilled meat. Try the excellent home-made deli meats, too. Specials announced according to the market. Sit back and drink in the conviviality of the mountains.

Name: J'MCA
Description: In this stone-built restaurant not far from the church and village square, you can look forward to meticulously prepared modern market-based cuisine – tasty and seamless, it lets the quality ingredients shine. Cheerful service and a decor with contemporary paintings and green plants offering charm and comfort.

Name: Château de Courban
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Once a professional cellist, chef Nicolas Thomas (La Promenade in Verfeuil, La Flibuste in Villeneuve-Loubet) now officiates in the kitchens of Château de Courban, a grand 19C building with a burnt sienna-coloured façade. The restaurant is housed in the property's converted barn, which boasts a beamed ceiling in the regional style. A devotee of fine ingredients, he makes good use of the adjoining vegetable garden and draws on the Burgundy terroir to craft a personalised cuisine that is at times innovative and always meticulous, for instance his confit shoulder of lamb, shimeji mushrooms, potato espuma, finished with a delicious mildly spiced sauce.

Name: Le Chou Rouge - Le Petit Chou
Address: 3 place de la République, Entraygues-sur-Truyère, 12140, France
Description: On the town’s main square, the ground floor of a traditional edifice is the HQ of this ‘Parisian - style’ bistro. It is decorated with a jumble of old furniture and knick - knacks picked up by the owners, and it serves market - fresh cuisine, sourced only from local producers. Everything, or almost, is homemade. Four pretty rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Le Castellaras
Description: This family business is established in a refurbished house, whose open kitchen backs onto a splendid terrace, which, in turn, commands a knockout view over the valley and the village of Fayence. The food is steeped in Provençal flavours and aromas and keeps pace with the market and seasons, illustrated by tender roast saddle of rabbit in seasonal herbs and vegetables in a gutsy gravy. A handful of rooms available for overnight stays.

Name: L'Essentiel
Description: At this restaurant just outside the city's touristy centre, a young owner-chef concocts a seasonal menu, underscored by distinctive, harmonious flavours and exquisitely presented. Those pressed for time will opt for the appetising lunch set menu. Best enjoyed on the patio, which is in great demand in fine weather.

Name: La Bartavelle
Description: Located in a picturesque Luberon village, this small but charming family business is run by an experienced couple. In a bid to ensure the dishes attain optimum quality, the chef offers a deliberately limited menu. You certainly can't argue with the results: meticulously prepared and fragrant recipes inspired by Provence and the finest seasonal ingredients. Considered a safe bet in the region, it has its fair share of regulars, which is always a good sign. It is wise to book a table.

Name: Taillard
Address: 3 route de la Corniche, Goumois, 25470, France
Description: The stunning view of the valley is flanked by hearty, country cooking by a chef, who has a knack for flavoursome, delicate recipes. Pedigree French fare, illustrated by a fricassee of morel mushrooms in flaky pastry.

Name: Le Pélican
Description: Olivier Guenoun, chef of this family business since 2010, crafts recipes that appeal to modern tastebuds in a menu dotted with daily specials that vary with market availability. Just like the regulars to the Pelican, open your beak wide to sample a slice of Nantais cake, a ubiquitous regional classic, treated to a new twist with roast pineapple and a mojito sorbet!

Name: Chavant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: It is so nice to come and enjoy summer days in this inn, run by the Chavant family since 1852. The food puts a smile on your face, and other assets include the wine cellar, swimming pool and spacious guestrooms.

Name: La Maison des Cariatides
Description: Located in the antique dealers' quarter, this listed 17C edifice which boats 10 caryatids on the façade, is now in the hands of Vincent and Marie-Cécile Gomis, whose star-studded careers can be tasted in the beautifully presented food. A modern score with intelligent cosmopolitan accents, like gravlax of Crisenon trout, grilled avocado with jerk spices; fricassée of snails and mussels marinière in vadouvan spices. A festival of northern flavours and cooking techniques illustrated by line-caught pollock and squid, courgette flowers and a paella-flavoured stock. Pleasant terrace to the rear.

Name: L'Auberge du Pêcheur
Description: Damien Muller, a fisherman and fishmonger (owner of Poissonnerie Saint-Christophe), runs an open-air restaurant in the courtyard garden of his childhood home. The concept is simple: at lunchtime, a single set menu based on the catch of the day; in the evening, a seafood menu with more elaborate dishes, lobster or sushi. The fish is killed according to the ikejime method, said to bring out its full flavour. The ingredients – needless to say ultra-fresh – and the deft technique underpinning his work promise dining pleasure and conviviality. Save room for the chocolate mousse!

Name: Chez Parenti
Description: Chez Parenti has been around since 1935, its kitchens successively manned by generation after generation of the same family! Those who love seafood are in for a treat – lobster and langoustines sold by weight, fish caught in the bay – but, to cater to all palates, there is also a small selection of Corsican meats, as well as an array of wonderful local cheeses. The cooking is technically on point and the dishes are nicely put together. Enjoy your meal in the comfort of the large shaded terrace that faces the Gulf of Valinco and the boats at anchor.

Name: La Table de Mina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: From your comfortable vantage point beneath a tiled roof by the pool, savour the view of the sweet-scented scrubland and the sea. The repertory, which displays a distinctly modern Mediterranean slant, stars Corsican produce: premium cured meats; local veal in olives with creamy polenta; lemon-flavoured Corsican cheesecake (fiadone). The concise menu is comprised of seasonal ingredients. A single set menu on Tuesdays features island specialties.

Name: Les Maisons  Rabanel
Description: Jean-Luc Rabanel is a colourful character with a lilting accent, who perpetually reinvents his vegetable-based cuisine. Les Maisons Rabanel, a single place but two styles of cooking: Greeniotage, which tends towards bistro food, and Greenstronome for fine dining. Always going out on a limb, this engaging chef shakes things up at every service. A unique personality.

Name: Jiva
Address: Jiva Hill Resort, Route d'Harée, Crozet, 01170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In Sanskrit, jiva means life, giving the visitor a foretaste of what to expect in this luxurious, understated resort. The restaurant specialises in exquisitely balanced French cuisine, using the best, fresh seasonal produce. Diners will enjoy a breathtaking view over Mont Blanc, whenever the weather permits, from the panoramic terrace.

Name: Restaurant de L'Île Benoist
Description: An oyster-farming family is behind this trendy, well-designed restaurant, which gives pride of place to locally fished seafood and, of course, oysters purified just opposite and other fine Normandy produce. The chef places particular importance on the careful presentation of the dishes, which are as attractive as they are flavoursome.

Name: Les Jardins Fleuris
Description: In this well-kept traditional establishment, the chef creates generous and tasty dishes with nods to the local terroir: venison terrine with foie gras, tournedos of rabbit with mushroom duxelle and a beef gravy with morels, frozen soufflé with Marc d'Arbois. Pleasant terrace to the rear and a charming welcome.

Name: Chez Séraphin
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: A characteristic Corsican house in a charming mountainside village sets the splendid scene to sample wholesome country fare, prepared simply from painstakingly selected ingredients, among which Corsica’s famous cured meats and fruit, vegetables and herbs from the garden. Take a seat on the spacious terrace and drink in the jaw-dropping view of the mountains and ancient oak forest. Just a word of warning: bank cards are not accepted, so take cash!

Name: Le Belvédère
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Tuck into ravioli with preserved lemon and a Greek yoghurt cream with coriander, while comfortably seated on the large waterside terrace in the shade of umbrella pines and palm trees overlooking Porto Vecchio's old town... What more could you ask for? Modern cuisine, top-notch ingredients and true technical prowess: the fennel-roasted meagre is precisely cooked and served with a delicious sauce. In the peace and quiet of this enclave, expect a feast for the eyes and a treat for the taste buds.

Name: Don Cesar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of the Don Cesar Hotel is certainly not lacking in charm with its luxurious, refined interior and large bay windows giving onto the terrace. The meticulously prepared and flavoursome food lies at the crossroads of French and Italian cuisine, and gives seafood pride of place, but also serves a wide range of dishes based on pasta made on site!

Name: La Table de la Plage
Address: Domaine de Murtoli, Vallée de l'Ortolo, Sartène, 20100, France
Description: By the prettiest beach in the Domaine de Murtoli, this restaurant with an exceptional decor inspired by fishermen's wooden huts is well worth a visit. Locally caught fish, grilled crayfish, veal, beef or lamb reared on the estate: diners can tuck into dishes such as John Dory à la meunière, courgettes stuffed with caponata and a rock fish jus. The pasta dishes make for a deliciously indulgent option. To access this highly exclusive property, it is necessary to book – you will then also be able to head for the beach with a deckchair and towel after your meal.

Name: Hostellerie de la Mer
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The chef crafts cuisine in tune with the zeitgeist, wonderfully blending fish from the local catch and ingredients from Brittany's terroir, such as house-smoked salmon, tangy herb cream and buckwheat blini, or the blanquette of monkfish and Molène sausage, vegetables and steamed potatoes. The cooking is precise and accentuates the well-chosen ingredients!

Name: La Calypso
Description: This charming maritime inspired bistro has a loyal band of regulars. They come here to savour the freshest fish and seafood prepared with great simplicity.

Name: La Taverne Besson
Description: This is an original Taverne with its contemporary, elegant, light - filled decor – and a terrace giving onto the countryside. Enjoy the enticing food, blending good local ingredients and original touches. You can also stay the night in one of the cleverly designed guestrooms.

Name: Le Vauban
Description: In a bustling street in Antibes' old town, Le Vauban serves up good, contemporary, French cuisine that is in step with the seasons and technically impeccable. The restaurant's reputation is firmly established and the place is often full – be sure to book!

Name: Domaine d'Auriac
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A magnificent 19C property steeped in history sets the elegant scene and provides the perfect foil for classical recipes, enhanced by the odd modern twist. When the weather allows, make a beeline for the terrace overlooking the grounds. The epitome of good taste in a quintessentially French country estate.

Name: Côté Cour
Description: Aix’s exclusive Cours Mirabeau is the place to see and be seen! A pared-back decor of natural materials, (very) soft lighting, a sliding roof, a glamorous edge and lounge music set the distinctive scene created by former Top Chef contestant, Ronan Kernen. The names of the dishes on the menu reflect his unorthodox approach: lamb cooked two ways/‘my version’ of stuffed cabbage, ‘my version’ of Saint-Honoré…

Name: Le Vintrépide
Description: One immediately falls under the charm of this contemporary and cosy decor (designer furniture, light wood and green-blue walls): a pleasant little place run by a pair who are eager to please. The chef prepares delicious seasonal dishes according to his inspiration. Meanwhile, the sommelier always has the right advice to guide you in your wine choice. A winning duo.

Name: Auberge de la Vallée
Description: Locally reared meat (lamb, veal, beef), regional cheeses (mainly goat’s) and veggies from his large market garden… The chef is a fan of the region as you will taste. The delicious food is served in a pleasantly rustic interior. The epitome of a French country inn!

Name: Azimut
Address: 273 rue de la Madelon, immeuble l'Or Blanc, centre station 1300, Le Praz, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: What you get here is cuisine rooted in tradition that is not beholden to the latest culinary fads. Ingredients are carefully chosen and showcased in all their simplicity, in dishes that are cooked to perfection and served with delicious sauces. The food is accompanied by wines from Burgundy or the Jura – the region where the establishment is based during the summer (the village of Bonlieu, to be precise). Reasonable prices (for Courchevel) and friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Le Bistro d'Hervé
Description: In the heart of historic Agde, just off the frenzied tourist path of Cap d’Agde, this bistro sports a colourful, contemporary vibe and serves appetising food in the zeitgeist: hanger steak smoked over vine branches; cod roasted in olive oil with dill-flavoured foamy carrots; French-toast style brioche with dairy butterscotch caramel… Snacks at the tapas bar. The shaded terrace is gloriously refreshing in hot weather.

Name: Fine Gueule
Description: In Nice's old town, opposite the town hall, this restaurant's newly refurbished interior is organised around an open kitchen and a counter where customers can sit to eat. But the real pleasure is to be found in the food, with traditional dishes chalked up on the board each day, including for starters the home-made pissaladière, devilled eggs or calamari a la plancha.

Name: L'Envolée - La Demeure Montaigne
Description: This exclusive venue established in a Haussmannian luxury hotel is a short walk from the Champs-Elysées and Avenue Montaigne. Set in an inner courtyard beneath a glass roof, it is reminiscent of a winter garden conservatory with its cane chairs. Sheltered from prying eyes, you will sample modern seasonal cuisine.

Name: a.lea
Description: a.lea is a play on words, referring to change (‘aléas’) and the name of the talented chef, Léa Lestage, who dabbled in sociology at uni before rolling up her sleeves in the kitchens of the Polisson and the Bristol’s Épicure. Examples of her appetising bistronomic cuisine include creamy soft-boiled egg, cream of green peas, apricots, feta and verbena; duckling, sweet potatoes, blood orange, mild curry seasoning and gravy… Léa’s spot-on recipes feature a market-fresh slant with a bargain-priced lunchtime (including Saturdays) menu. More elaborate and more expensive in the evenings. Also a chef, William Atlan warmly manages the front-of-house experience.

Name: L'Ormeau
Description: Who could turn down a platter of Cancale oysters, scallops and abalone (the restaurant’s namesake)? Even better when served with a splendid view of the fleet of fishing boats that guarantees their freshness! A stylish interior fronted by a pleasant terrace sets the scene for premium seafood dishes, such as razor clams stuffed with parsley, garlic and butter, home-made fish soup or local scallops roasted on the shell, white butter and vegetable risotto. Round off your meal on a sweet note with a pancaked stuffed with warm apples for example.

Name: La Villa Tartary
Description: Fine freestone vaulting, designer furniture, a delightful terrace... This converted water mill – previously used in the silk production process – has bags of charm. Lovely flavours on the menu.

Name: La Barbacane
Description: Set deep in historic Carcassonne, the Hôtel de la Cité is a superb example of neo-Gothic architecture, built in 1909 on the site of the former episcopal palace, whose magnificent gardens abut the ramparts. Inside, stained-glass windows, coats of arms and wainscoting lend it an ambience worthy of 19C French architect Viollet-le-Duc. Based on top quality ingredients, notably Mediterranean fish and seafood, as well as game and mushrooms in autumn, the menu champions the region’s terroir in dishes that add a new spin to classical recipes.

Name: Le Balbec - Grand Hôtel de Cabourg
Address: Grand Hôtel de Cabourg, Les Jardins du Casino, Cabourg, 14390, France
Description: The Grand Hôtel de Cabourg, once frequented by Marcel Proust, is one of the best-preserved seaside hotels from the Belle Époque and a gem of Art Deco architecture. Le Balbec – one of the hotel's restaurants – is located in the gallery, which overlooks the seafront, and where serving precise, refined dishes with an abundance of beautiful flavours is a matter of pride. For food lovers in search of lost time!

Name: Iris Café
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this contemporary building in the heart of the village, Cyril Simon, who has a soft spot for vegetables, fruit and fish, goes to great lengths to source ingredients locally: nothing here is from the agri-food industry, and everything comes from less than 200km away! This eco-responsible approach results in harmonious, carefully prepared dishes, such as Ferme de Ciron fillet of trout, celeriac pulp, lovage emulsion – tuck in on the large terrace overlooking the countryside. Good value for money.

Name: La Maison du Safran à l'Allée des Vignes
Description: The Franco-Mexican chef, Claude-Emmanuel Robin, and his Russian wife, Evgenia, fell in love with this former presbytery in Carjac, an exquisite village in Quercy. They have tastefully turned it into an elegant, charming venue with a restaurant and a shop on the saffron theme. The bistronomic slant shines through in the creative, flavoursome cuisine, served alfresco on the lovely patio in fine weather.

Name: Million
Address: 8 place de la Liberté, Albertville, 73200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family - run establishment that cultivates tradition, both in its restaurant, where the classics are served, and in the nicely old - fashioned guestrooms.

Name: Francis Mallmann au Château La Coste
Address: 2750 route de la Cride, Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade, 13610, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: "The famous Argentine chef's philosophy is adhered to down to the tiniest detail: slowly smoked entrecote, mashed potato and chimichurri; lamb flame - cooked in a dome fire, aubergine, roasted peppers... served in a bright, elegant interior. "

Name: La Table de Beaurecueil
Description: This restaurant is housed in a former sheep barn and features a resolutely contemporary design (only a few of the original rustic features remain). It offers “cuisine du terroir” based on high quality produce. Wine by the glass.

Name: La Bonne Auberge
Description: In this pretty inn, you simply decide how many courses you would like and the chef will do the rest! The young chef is rather bold in his cooking, sometimes dreaming up original combinations of flavours (no bad thing in this region where tradition reigns supreme). Pleasant, efficient service and good value for money. It is worth noting that a new shop adjoining the restaurant has been opened for takeaway dishes, from starter to dessert, concocted by the chef.

Name: Au Fil du Clos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: An old farmhouse in Meursault's vineyards, complete with a garden, terrace and pergola, is the charming setting for the restaurant of chef Jean-Christophe Moutet (previously at Pommard). Tartare of sea bream, royale with fresh herbs; squab, rhubarb, in a sesame crust; a handful of Burgundy classics: the chef's savoir-faire is as appetising as ever.

Name: Auberge de Briant
Description: The spacious and light new dining room gives onto the water and surrounding greenery. Tuck into the delicious dishes made by Filipe, the chef – pressé of Charolais oxtail and crayfish with sauce ravigote, sea bass roasted in olive oil, dill and garlic cromesquis... – and the tasty desserts made by Angélique, his wife!

Name: L'Auberge du Laurier
Description: Comfortably seated in this bright, cheerful Landes inn, you will taste a modern score whose occasional globetrotting influence is paired with local produce: miso soup with duck confit, gnocchis of herbs and sheep milk cheese, pear poached in curcuma. Generous portions of appetising fare and infinite respect for the seasons. When the weather is fine, many patrons make a beeline for the patio abutting the vegetable garden.

Name: Le Quatrième Mur
Address: 2 place de la Comédie, Bordeaux, 33000, France
Description: The quatrième mur (‘fourth wall’) of a theatre is the invisible one that separates the actors from the audience. An apt name for this restaurant set in Bordeaux’ iconic Grand Théâtre. Philippe Etchebest plays a gloriously simple, understated score focusing on first-rate ingredients, high-flying technique, a side dish and a jus. The terrace on one of the opera house’s outdoor side galleries is heavenly. Bookings essential – two sittings at lunchtime and in the evening. The menus change weekly.

Name: La Route d'Argent
Description: On the ground floor of the hotel, this restaurant, which sports a bright, modern interior, has been taken over by a dynamic duo comprised of the former second and his wife. Tuck into heartwarming, bountiful fare made with regional produce: Aubrac beef and trout, persillade of lamb sweetbreads or squab breast. Traditional aligot (mashed potatoes and cheese) is served with the main course.

Name: La Table de Haute-Serre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the wine storehouse of a château in the heart of the vineyards, this restaurant exudes the very particular charm of truly authentic places. Charcuterie rack, butcher's block, ham slicer and cases of wine herald a wonderful moment of gourmet delights, rounded off by wines from the estate. Rotisserie evening every Friday. Just delicious.

Name: JR Bistronomie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a stone's throw from the sea and the Jean Cocteau Museum, in a charming setting that calls to mind a family home (with one corner set up like a kids' playroom), this place serves good seasonal bistronomy food. Under the guidance of an experienced chef (also a member of the Disciples d'Escoffier), the classics are given a tasteful and intelligent modern spin. On this particular occasion, caramelised tomato tarte tatin; confit saddle of lamb; deconstructed lemon pavlova. Lovely fresh ingredients, a sure hand: JR works his magic!

Name: Fleur de Sel
Address: 85 montée de la Bourgade, Cagnes-sur-Mer, 06800, France
Description: In a charming little street in the medieval village, this pretty restaurant with a distinctly Southern French feel serves fresh, colourful bistro cuisine that embraces the seasons.

Name: La Poste et Hôtel La Reconce
Description: The Restaurant de la Poste is now run by a chef who hails from the village, ably assisted by his wife. His ambition is clear: to regale diners with modern dishes that celebrate good local produce – Charolais entrecote with seasonal vegetables is a good example. Stylish, well - kept rooms, should you wish to stay over.

Name: Côté Mer
Description: Inhale the salty sea air of the little port of Cancale, which makes for a picturesque sight with its fishermen's houses. In this restaurant overlooking the bay, you can sample cuisine that showcases first and foremost local coastal produce, but not to the exclusion of other ingredients: scallops, oysters, saltmarsh lamb, lobster, abalones… And all at eater-friendly prices.

Name: Château Le Cagnard
Address: 54 rue Sous-Barri, le Haut-de-Cagnes, Cagnes-sur-Mer, 06800, France
Description: The standout features are the lovely terrace with a view as far as Cap d'Antibes and the flawlessly prepared contemporary cuisine: Vaucluse green asparagus au gratin with aged Parmesan and kumquat; fillet of sea bass with lardo di Colonnata, artichokes from Provence and anchovy condiment; strawberry crisp, elderberry infusion. The detail that seals the deal is the elegant interior with its sliding roof designed to let in the light.

Name: Aux Trois Pastoureaux
Description: Although Jean-François Lucchese started out as a pastry chef, he likes to define himself as a "craftsman of taste", taking care over cooking, seasoning and marriages of ingredients. Here in this old building in the centre of Châteaudun, go back in time courtesy of the "Medieval Menu", which is all about tradition! Delicious bread made in-house.

Name: Les Singuliers
Description: In the heart of Périgord Blanc, this traditional stone-built house has an attractive contemporary restaurant within its walls: a gleaming open kitchen, ochre walls, polished concrete floor and a magnificent oak tree trunk that creates a focal point in the middle of the tables. Louis Festa, a young chef with a great track record, has devised a single surprise set menu (which can be tailored to suit your appetite) out of ambitious and spontaneous dishes inspired by the season: Le Puy green lentils prepared three ways, Blonde d'Aquitaine sirloin steak on the Japanese barbecue.

Name: Le Dauphin
Address: 2 rue de L'Église, Le Breuil-en-Auge, 14130, France
Description: With its half - timbering and charming atmosphere, this former coaching inn represents Normandy at its best, and you will be impatient to come back for more. Mathieu Le Guillois, the new chef, does not skimp on generosity – the portions are gargantuan!

Name: Le Bistro 1911
Description: The chef enthusiastically prepares up - to - date dishes, served in an elegant room adorned with stained glass. Magnificent wine list and a simpler lunchtime menu.

Name: Le Lassey - Château Sainte-Sabine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant restaurant in the historical setting of the Renaissance Château Sainte-Sabine stands out on account of its refined cuisine. Arctic char from the Cévennes accompanied by crayfish and a shellfish sauce; Bresse chicken with green asparagus – these are just two of the wonderful specialities cooked up by chef Benjamin Linard, who has worked at some top restaurants. A simpler set menu is available at lunchtime. The guestrooms invite you to unwind as you take in the lake and bucolic grounds, where deer roam.

Name: Bro's
Address: 36 rue de la Foulerie, Blois, 41000, France
Description: This eatery in the historic town just a stone’s throw from the banks of the Loire, which has quickly been taken by storm by the locals, is the brainchild of two enthusiastic cooks and inseparable pals. The scene upstairs sports a stylish rustic interior with contemporary touches, providing the perfect foil to a bistronomic score that shines the spotlight on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients, naturally washed down with Loire wines. Tapas inspired by the produce of south-west France and Spain are also available (evenings only and without reservations) in the ground-floor room.

Name: Quelque Part
Description: This “somewhere” is the submarine wonderland of former Top Chef contestant Florian Barbarot. Like Captain Nemo, he invites diners to immerse themselves in his subtly creative cuisine in which seafood, seasonal veggies and painstakingly sourced ingredients are inspiringly assembled. While each menu features a different number of courses (3 at lunchtime), the 8-course menu shines the spotlight on one exquisite ingredient crafted in front of diners.

Name: Le Bel Ami
Description: A few hundred metres from the seafront, amid the crêperies and other taverns, don't hesitate to bag a table at this charming, colourful place run by the proprietor of Le Donjon – Domaine Saint-Clair, a Michelin-starred restaurant in the upper town. Here, you can enjoy Mediterranean-inspired cuisine, starting with mezze (hummus/beef tataki, bottarga/kefta, aubergine or even ceviche with citrus fruit and fennel), before tucking into a superb piece of meagre, served with a vegetable tian and rosemary hollandaise. There is also a (small) wine cellar where you can purchase a bottle to enjoy here or take away.

Name: Café Brunet
Address: 18 place Gabriel-Fauré - à Annecy-le-Vieux, Annecy, 74940, France
Description: This café dating back to 1875 is a real haven. It has managed to keep intact its soul of an authentic and convivial bistro (terrace, boules). As time meanders by, enjoy a good hearty meal or tasty little dishes.

Name: Opéra
Description: This Italian chef has set up shop in a chic, refined restaurant slightly outside the town centre. Vasco Baldisserotto has worked in three-star restaurants in Italy, as well as with the Bras family both at the Musée Soulages and at their flagship parent establishment in Laguiole. Now flying solo, he signs a pedigree Gallic score, albeit tinged with Italian influences, particularly from his native Venetian region. Familiar with the finest produce, he painstakingly sources and selects only the best: tajarin pasta with Piedmont hazelnuts, snails and parsley; Aveyron veal with anchovies and parmesan… The menus celebrate the seasons and his suppliers on whom he frequently shines the spotlight.

Name: Loiseau du Temps
Description: Set in a former 18C wheat barn, this handsome dining room, depicted by vaults and contemporary details, is home to the most recent addition to the Loiseau Group. The menu focuses on produce and recipes from Bourgogne-Franche-Comté: gravlax of Jura trout, snails in parsley, poultry reared by Gaston Gérard… Each dish is generously crafted and beautifully presented. Enticing dessert trolley and a fine selection of wines, particularly by the glass.

Name: L'Auberge de Guillaume
Address: 4 place de la Mairie, Vandenesse-en-Auxois, 21320, France
Description: After assisting Christophe Bacquié at Le Castellet, becoming a Meilleur Ouvrier de France in 2015 and then a Michelin-starred chef at La Bussière, local lad, Guillaume Royer, has at last opened his own place in his native village. In this charming inn, half a kilometre from the peaceful Canal de Bourgogne, he rolls out his talent in a contemporary bistronomic vein using knockout regional produce. Pleasant terrace and quiet garden to the rear.

Name: Otto
Description: A welcome addition to the rue Mouffetard: this bistro with a minimalist decor comprising concrete floor and ceiling is modelled on the Japanese izakaya. Under the leadership of chef Eric Trochon, Otto proposes a cuisine for sharing based on a short menu that revolves around the produce, simply accompanied by a condiment or a sauce for that extra kick. Hence chimichurri, sauce vierge or diable, ponzu sauce or lemon condiment are served alongside meat and fish, often cooked over binchotan coals. Please note that they don't take bookings.

Name: Regain
Description: In the trendy Le Camas neighbourhood, this friendly bistro is in the competent hands of experienced chef Sarah Chougnet-Strudel and sommelier Lucien Salomon, who deploys his flair and talent front of house. Whether seated at the traditional chestnut wood and zinc counter or in the leafy courtyard, which is open in fine weather, you'll love the flavoursome market-fresh cuisine, which highlights local produce, particularly vegetables and artisanal fish. Think rack of pork with kale, sorrel cream, lentils and limequat, or a delicious tartlet with maple syrup, coffee mousse and candied celery. To accompany your food, pick a bottle from the enticing selection of around 200 "living" wines. An energising harvest of flavours!

Name: VIVE, Maison Mer
Description: Alsace-born restaurateur Adrien Rech opened this institution dedicated to seafood in 1925. After Ducasse, it is now the turn of David and Stéphanie Le Quellec, whose Breton name alone smacks of the ocean, to celebrate fish and shellfish cuisine. The decor is sumptuous, with its huge bar, dining area on the first floor and long banquette seating. David Le Quellec serves food that is good for sharing and made with excellent, ultra-fresh ingredients from fish markets spanning France, from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. The ceviche of sea bream with coconut milk, lime and coriander is already a house classic – not to mention the dishes prepared from fish matured on site in the maturing cellar.

Name: Resto Dit Vin
Description: In a pedestrian street in the centre of Pau, this inviting and indulgent place is one to keep under your hat, as both the dining area and terrace are invariably packed to the rafters! In his semi-open kitchen, chef Alexis Bourdrel gives pride of place to local ingredients that he knows inside out and sources from farmers with whom he has built up a rapport: the vegetables come from the market-gardener parents of his wife, who works in the dining room; the ale is from Béarn, and the bottles on the menu are for sale at wine merchant prices, to enjoy at home. The short menu changes regularly (seared scallops and Jerusalem artichoke glazed in a meat jus, Pyrenean trout gravlax and, for dessert, Pyrenean flax and pear poached in Jurançon).

Name: Auberge de la Haute-Joux
Description: A former philosopher (and the epitome of courtesy and discernment when it comes to her wine recommendations) plus a globetrotting chef who grew up eating at Michelin-starred restaurants have taken over this family-run inn: just the ticket in the middle of this rural village. This pair promises diners a delightful dining experience that combines rustic surroundings and cuisine that nonchalantly switches between regional and more contemporary dishes, and is littered with nods to the chef's many travels: here you see vin jaune and saffron from Franche-Comté, peanut vinaigrette, seaweed emulsion alongside Thai-style mussels from Bouchot.

Name: Maison Bagarre
Description: This restaurant in the Graslin neighbourhood is often booked up, so it's best to reserve. The chef makes the most of the extensive network of producers (especially market gardeners) operating in Nantes to create an appealing bistronomy menu. The rather original contemporary setting (over two levels) is very attractive, especially the dining area on the large mezzanine overlooking the open kitchen.

Name: Cueillette
Description: A small establishment tucked away in the suburbs of Rennes, an attractive façade, a contemporary interior, a covered terrace overlooking the fields, and a charming welcome. As for the food, the chef has got it spot on: competent, pared-back dishes that are full of finesse, with judicious combinations and precise seasoning. Rich pickings at this lovely place outside of the centre.

Name: Brut maison de cuisine
Description: This tasty bistro with a contemporary feel has an open kitchen, shelves filled with jars of fermented vegetables and books… and just a handful of tables, so it's best to book. The chef, who has a solid track record, devises a short menu that changes regularly. The three pillars of his cooking are seasonality, local ingredients (such as Racan poultry) and modern, often bold cuisine, for example his dessert that combines a naturally sweet Jerusalem artichoke cream and a coffee ice cream with a pronounced flavour. Short list of natural and organic wines.

Name: Deux Restaurant
Address: 58 rue de la Fontaine-au-Roi, Paris, 75011, France
Description: Tiphaine Mollard, from Savoie and Romain Casas, from Béarn, have teamed up, pooling their contagious good humour and respective homelands in this warm, inviting establishment: open kitchen, shelves laden with bottles, knick-knacks, photos and plants. Tomatoes, cream of burrata and vinegar jelly; grilled sardines, green bean salad, pistou and peaches: the food is joyful, tasty, legible and heartily wholesome. Prices that make sense.

Name: Auberge de Monceaux
Description: This handsome country restaurant strikes a tasteful balance between authentic rural charm (terracotta tiles and beams) and modern comfort. Two sisters oversee proceedings front of house while their partners enthusiastically deliver finely crafted, colourful dishes that win diners over with a combination of creativity and tradition: blue lobster and pea tartlet, sabayon bisque; matured squab, barbecued courgettes and pollen vinaigrette; panna cotta and meadowsweet ice cream, strawberry coulis. The menu changes regularly.

Name: Ilô
Description: A marriage between a French gourmet bistro and a Japanese tavern is hidden behind a noren (a vertical fabric divider hung across the doorways of shops in Japan). Ilô is also the lair of a particularly inspired duet, both of whom worked at the star-rated Sola. On one side, Yuki Onuma supervises the service, suggesting perceptive, spot-on wine/saké-food pairings, while on the other, chef Seiya Kumabe conjures up a culinary patchwork of Gallic bistronomy with a smattering of Japanese allusions.

Name: Bulle
Description: Chef Guy Lassausaie masterminded the stylish top to toe refurbishment of this restaurant in a former Jesuit seminary (1853). You enter through a bar which boasts a jaw-dropping panoramic terrace, before heading downstairs into the restaurant, passing by the building’s Gallo-Roman foundations on the way! A swish, historic interior (crystal lighting, parquet floors and a view of the kitchen) sets the scene for colourful seasonal food, such as brook trout, fennel and seasonal mushrooms…

Name: Apicius
Description: This small city-centre establishment with a contemporary minimalist setting is run by a young couple with an impressive track record. Market-fresh cuisine at unbeatable prices at lunchtime, a more elaborate menu on Friday evenings. The chef makes the most of local ingredients as well as wild flowers and plants. In a word: generous!

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye
Description: Treat yourself to a meal in the country, in the professional hands of this couple who have set up shop in a pretty stone house overlooking the abbey and Royal College of Thiron - Gardais. Seasonal dishes and a new subtle version of classical recipes. Flawlessly prepared with distinctive flavours. Lovely!

Name: Miro
Address: Rue de la Nachtweid, Ostwald, 67540, France
Description: This restaurant stands in bucolic grounds on the banks of the River Ill. Familiar with South American, Japanese and French gastronomy, the chef regales diners with tasty and uninhibited cuisine inspired by his many travels, for example Thai-style sea bass ceviche and his superb Argentinian beef entrecote finished over burning embers. The lunch set menu is a steal.

Name: Itsasoa
Description: The Basque overtones of this Brittany eatery are due to Erwann Le Pogam, a Breton who grew up in Southwest France and who worked in the film industry before turning to cooking. A great decision! This unfettered and unblinkered man has a single goal: fine, fresh, wholesome food that respects the produce, the producer and the customer. A few examples from the set menus (which change frequently in line with the seasons): monkfish tail, tempura of courgette flowers and smoked paprika emulsion or farm-reared pork with a mousseline of green peas and xipister Basque sauce.

Name: Les 5 Bouchons
Description: A pleasant restaurant for lunch beneath the arcades of Place Nationale, Montauban's architectural pride and joy. The name refers to the five members of the family of experienced chef David Soulier, who works with his wife Joan front of house. Every fortnight, a new seasonal menu showcases well-sourced local ingredients in straightforward, colourful and tasty dishes, for example roasted hazelnuts grown in Tarn-et-Garonne that accompany the beetroot hummus, or the sticks of celeriac and mustard seed pickles served with the pork loin cooked for five hours. Whether seated on the terrace or in the long room with its vaulted ceiling overlooking the kitchen, you'll have an enjoyable meal without breaking the bank.

Name: Gemellus
Description: This spruce, modern eatery done up in oatmeal shades features a square dining room with painted mouldings, a coffered ceiling, an imposing chandelier and upholstered velvet seats. Chef Maxime Le Meur, who trained with some of the greats, leaves nothing to chance as he crafts cuisine inspired as much by seasonal ingredients as by his Breton (check out the surf ‘n turf dish of Breton squab with lobster) and Grenoble roots (Chartreuse liqueur is never far from the culinary score). A festival of forthright, meticulous flavours overflowing in creative ideas. Affordable lunchtime menu.

Name: Auberge d’Aillon et d’Ailleurs
Address: 795 route de la Correrie, Aillon-le-Jeune, 73340, France
Description: In the Bauges Mountains, an unspoilt natural haven, this contemporary hotel has a lovely restaurant run by a young chef who has both technique and ideas. He throws himself into his work to get the best out of the Val d'Aillon terroir: vegetable garden, cooperative cheese, farm lamb, wild herbs... The menu changes regularly.

Name: La Bòria
Description: The view over the valley and the surrounding Ardèche hills, a lovely timber building, chestnut-wood tables, an indoor aromatic herb garden, the etymology of the name bòria ("small Cévennes farm" in Ardèche dialect): the tone is set! Chef Florian Descours pays tribute to his roots by cooking only fresh and local produce (such as beef from Privas, pork from Beaulieu, snails from the Eyrieux valley and trout from Andaure). A treat from beginning to end, from the beef tongue ravioli and snails with sorrel to the Ardèche lemon, Baix kiwi and Areilladou fromage frais. Hard to beat!

Name: La Récréation Gourmande
Description: In this former schoolhouse, an old stove presides, with a dunce's hat perched on top! Whatever the standard of the class, everyone can tuck into the generous and tasty cooking, which makes the ingredients the star of the class. A Récréation Gourmande indeed!

Name: Chenapan
Description: The pair at the helm of this compact restaurant in Pigalle are chef Bruno Laporte and front-of-house manager and sommelier Florentin Fraillon, who have both graduated with honours from Ze Kitchen Galerie, William Ledeuil's "training ground"! Here, they are going from strength to strength, with dishes such as the plant-based starter (butter beans, fava beans, peas, leaves and fresh herbs) – given a boost by its rhubarb juice sauce spiced up with chilli in the style of a beurre blanc – or the delicious wheat dessert, oozing childhood nostalgia. An intimate, contemporary bistro setting with an open kitchen and pleasant service with a smile.

Name: La Table du Marensin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This former foundry, now a delightful restaurant, is set in a picturesque hamlet on the banks of the lake of Uza. The dining room sports workshop-style windows, rust-coloured tiling and comfy armchairs and leads onto a terrace overlooking the lake. The youthful chef, who honed his consummate technique at Auberge du Prieuré in Moirax, delivers creative cuisine based on a single set surprise menu that can be rolled out in different versions: girolle and brown mushroom ravioli in a frothy hazelnut concoction; veal fillet, raspberry vinegar-flavoured gravy and a harissa of sweet peppers from the Landes.

Name: Em Sherif
Address: Hôtel de Paris, place du Casino, Monaco, 98000, France
Description: A welcome opportunity to celebrate the pleasures of Lebanese cuisine, the Mediterranean and, of course, the philosophy of sharing. In the kitchen, chef Yasmina Hayek (who has worked at the Institut Paul Bocuse and the restaurants of Mathieu Pacaud, Jean-François Piège and Rasmus Kofoed at Geranium in Copenhagen) skilfully juggles the traditional and the modern, in dishes such as her excellent lentil salad (addas) or her delicious aubergine fatteh with yoghurt.
