Description: Jean Cocteau used to eat at this local institution, which has been serving fresh fish and seafood since 1938. It is lovely just to sit on the terrace and gaze out over the harbour!

Name: Boccafine
Description: A small, listed village on the Cap Corse road is home to this demure restaurant, hidden by a curtain of Virginia Creeper and tall plane trees. The chef unveils his know-how as he crafts painstakingly sourced, local and seasonal ingredients, illustrated by ultra-fresh croaker, pancetta and pork jus in a surf and turf recipe of wondrous harmony. Love at first bite.

Name: L'Affable
Description: In the centre of Cannes, this contemporary bistro is always busy and, indeed, it has much to recommend it. First and foremost its menu: courgette flower fritters, cod aioli, rack of lamb roasted with thyme… and the classic Grand Marnier soufflé, the house speciality.

Name: L'Espace PH3
Description: This is the Henriroux family’s second venture, created directly inside La Pyramide. The tasteful interior displays a strong plant focus in line with the menu’s healthy, wellness leaning, without forgetting pedigree classics, like calf’s head and pink praline. Everything is in the energetic hands of a charismatic team. Bags of vitality and flavour!

Name: Asterales
Address: Hôtel du Golf, Les Ritons, 784 route du Clos-de-la-Balme, Corrençon-en-Vercors, 38250, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Poetically named after an order of flowering plants, this tasteful restaurant sports a low-key alpine style. Chef Ludovic Nardozza’s painstakingly crafted cooking showcases his favourite, first-class ingredients: roasted langoustines in marjoram butter, girolles and vin jaune bisque; John Dory lacquered in wild fennel, courgette flowers and grilled cuttlefish; apple like an upside-down pie with local honey and black cardamon… Service with a smile. Pleasant guestrooms make it an ideal basecamp to explore Vercors.

Name: Premnord
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of the Prieuré-Roch estate rises up to greet visitors with its distinctive wood and steel U-shaped architecture, whose centre is graced with a vast patio overlooking the vineyards. Indoors are a parquet-floored lounge, a bar decked in light wood and a spacious contemporary dining room with immense floor-to-ceiling windows. Chef Céline Dedinger (who boasts stints with Thomas Collomb at the Rôtisserie du Chambertin and the Maison des Cariatides) crafts a modern score based on mainly local ingredients (whose exact source is indicated on the menu) in line with the seasons.

Name: Campelli
Description: This diminutive restaurant with a midnight-blue and gold façade boasts a chic yet understated decor (velvet banquettes, wooden chairs upholstered in matching velvet, exposed stone walls) – all the better to showcase the creative cuisine and multicultural culinary experience of chef Vartivar Jarkezian. Firmly rooted in French tradition, his cooking also draws discreetly on the influences and pantry of the Middle East (cumin, pistachio, turmeric, yoghurt sauce).

Name: Godaille
Description: Godaille in French slang means feasting and making merry among good friends. So let's get to it and tuck into this invigorating, flavoursome cuisine! This eatery run by a group of pals gives pride of place to spices and fresh herbs, in dishes such as fried chicken with super-soft meat in a crispy golden crumb, alongside a ginger-lemon sauce; bouchot mussels are served with a coconut-green curry sauce and Thai herbs. The pleasant, slightly retro interior is complemented by a lovely bunch of fresh flowers on each table. A fine selection of natural and organic wines (including some orange wines).

Name: jjii
Description: Exposed stone walls, visible electric cables and streamed music in the long, narrow dining space, and, at work in the open kitchen, Korean chef Jay Wook Hur (encountered at Boutary and Petit Boutary). Going solo in the kitchen, he can be seen cooking up modern, creative French cuisine with a few Asian touches (on this particular evening, they include tempura, sesame, kimchi), as his mystery menu unfolds: a surprising and beautifully fresh starter such as sea bass, kimchi and avocado, accompanied by two raspberries and a quenelle of smoked herring roe; or the oh-so-tender matured Simmental sirloin, fennel, beetroot and its bold jus.

Name: Le Point d'Origine
Description: Situated opposite the Abreuvoir de Marly – the Watering Place – framed by its famous sculpted horses, this former manor house is now home to a delicatessen, wine cellar and restaurant, enthusiastically run by a dynamic team. The restaurant occupies a lovely glass-paned extension with herringbone parquet flooring and an unobstructed view of the Abreuvoir. The chef creates modern, well-polished dishes: fine langoustines as a starter (with courgettes, saffron, snow peas and samphire), pluma of Iberian pig (with potatoes, beans, chanterelles, peaches and satay condiment). And why not enjoy a post-prandial stroll in the grounds?

Name: L'Atelier de Damien
Description: Just 10min from the historic town centre, this restaurant is to be found where you would least expect it: on the first floor of an unremarkable building that, so we're told, was once a fire station. The contemporary setting is definitely appealing, as is the cuisine of the chef, who has an impressive track record (Alain Ducasse in Paris and Py-R in Toulouse). The three set menus, which echo today's culinary standards, certainly whet the appetite: roast onions and grilled mackerel; glazed pork belly, a meat jus, potatoes, leeks and peppers. Cordial service.

Name: Des Terres
Description: The festive casual vibe of this neighbourhood bistro in the 20th arrondissement of Paris is the work of a chef who boasts a solid career in the Pierre Gagnaire empire. In the company of natural wines displayed on bookshelves, you will joyfully do justice to the chef’s meticulously and lovingly crafted dishes: crunchy, fried pleurote mushrooms, confit of egg yolk in soy sauce, herb salad and Iranian black lemon; ikejime pollock and its inimitable pullet sauce, mussels, burnt leeks and spring turnips. Delicious seasonal nosh at eater-friendly prices.

Name: Omma
Address: 38 rue de la Poste, Roussillon, 84220, France
Description: The panoramic view this restaurant affords over the Luberon and the famous ochre cliffs of Roussillon is nothing short of spectacular! As for the food, the short seasonal menu proposes bistronomy-style dishes drawing on Provençal influences: Mediterranean octopus grilled over a wood fire, stuffed peppers and house harissa; Ventoux pork, chanterelles and local blackberries; sponge cake with pistachios, lemon and raspberries. A moment of culinary bliss far from the crowds of tourists.

Name: Nananère
Description: Sometimes it is fun to revisit your childhood! Run by the former owners of Le P'tit Cageot, this restaurant has a playful decor that draws on comic strips and action figures of characters such as Spiderman and Buzz Lightyear. Things get serious, however, when it comes to the delicious food. The menu abounds with French classics (leeks in vinaigrette, saucisson brioché, poire belle Hélène), as well as dishes catering to teenage diners (mac & cheese and burgers) and fresh house-made pasta – everything is professionally prepared using quality ingredients. Large terrace. No reservations for parties of fewer than six people.

Name: Kitchen by Madame Rêve
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Restored from head to toe, the iconic Haussmannian Louvre Post Office building is also home to a luxury hotel and a classy neo-brasserie, nestled under an impressive ceiling. The menu is divided into culinary themes in a tongue-in-cheek poke at your usual restaurant codes: healthy trendy, veg out, flashback, etc. The onus is definitely on unstuffy pleasure!

Name: Dame Augustine
Description: This is the other restaurant of chef Lilian Douchet, who hails from Bordeaux: you can expect a laid-back atmosphere and a veranda-style space with the feel of a small brasserie. He serves several set menus, including a good-value lunch deal. Diners savour dishes such as a selection of heirloom tomatoes, fresh herb pesto, parmesan buttercrumb biscuits and mizuna sorbet, or a fillet of whiting simmered with coco de Paimpol beans and a lemon thyme emulsion. A welcome address in this residential area.

Name: Guefen
Description: At Ohad Amzallag's restaurant a stone's throw from Place de la République, diners sample his cooking in convivial fashion, all seated at a large marble table d'hôte. The Israeli chef serves Middle Eastern-influenced cuisine that gives pride of place to seafood ingredients and fermented vegetables, such as oyster cream with mint granita, chilli and koshu; lobster and agnolotti with ricotta, spinach and sage cream; and a delicious cheesecake with caramelised garum.

Name: Pamparigouste - Le Couvent des Minimes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In addition to his fine dining restaurant, chef Louis Gachet lovingly oversees the mouth-watering cuisine served at this upscale bistro, which is open 7/7. The space is soothing and relaxing, plus there is a dining room-cum-terrace, whose bay windows are opened wide when the weather is fine. Previously sous-chef at La Chèvre d'Or in Èze, the chef devises a menu that skilfully blends traditional favourites (eg farmhouse poultry and pork pâté en croûte; millefeuille) with contemporary dishes punctuated by Provençal touches (eg trout confit, aioli and lemon condiment; einkorn with parmesan and local vegetables; catch of the day with green curry, roast fig and crunchy fennel).

Name: Gaua
Description: Chef Benoit Sarthou (who held a Michelin star at Moulin d'Alotz) has chosen to make his restaurant a celebration of conviviality and the "night" (gaua in Basque). This former garage has been turned into a trendy industrial-style lounge with a central bar-counter and large open kitchen. Share an array of tapas in an ambience fostered by skilfully curated playlists. Think comfort and fusion food, with various ingredients matured or cooked over an open flame.

Name: Colvert
Description: Revealed by the French Top Chef TV show, Arnaud Baptiste and his flamboyant moustache and numerous tattoos, is something of a media darling. He has set up shop in a vintage street corner bistro (banquettes, bistro chairs, tightly packed tables, bare stone walls, cement tiled floor and a counter which now serves standing customers) in the somewhat touristy, but nonetheless picturesque 6th district of Paris. Arnaud happily crafts market-fresh, bistronomic fare. The seasonal menu is suitably concise and hits the spot every time: confit of cod, hollandaise sauce, courgettes and absinthe gel or figs, served roasted, raw and in pickles with a fig sorbet and ice cream.

Name: Mi Kwabo
Description: Chef Elis Bond (a contestant on France's Top Chef in 2022) has moved his restaurant to this cosy and compact place (seating a dozen) with terracotta-coloured walls and pale wood floorboards. His creative cuisine is full of nods to his Caribbean origins and the African roots of his partner Vanessa, who is the sommelier and front-of-house manager: "kankan" spices on the amuse-bouche, garlic, ginger and chilli oil on the starter, good quality ingredients (tender Galician beef, vegetables from market gardener Hélène Reglain etc). The fine selection of wines includes a good range from South Africa.

Name: Le Cercle Guiraud
Description: In the heart of the village, this traditional eatery offers a choice between a dining room whose countrified décor is dotted with the odd contemporary touch, or, in fine weather, a terrace shaded by mulberry plane trees that commands an exquisite view as far as Château Guiraud, which owns the restaurant. Yoann Amado, former chef of Maison Darroze in Langon, and his pastry chef partner, Juliette Bonnard, craft a scrumptious gourmet score that hits the spot every time: truly flavoursome oxheart tomatoes, burrata of goat’s cheese, infusion of tomato water and verbena; trout marinated in miso and confit, baby spinach shoots, beurre blanc of pike roe; vanilla-flavoured crème brûlée, apricots and an exquisite last-minute lemon thyme-flavoured sorbet.

Name: La Table du 5
Description: This contemporary restaurant located within the 5 Terres Hotel looks out over the magnificent Renaissance town hall (1640). In a light-filled space done out in premium materials, you can enjoy contemporary cuisine that brings the best out of carefully sourced local ingredients. The wine list is particularly impressive, featuring hundreds of organic and biodynamic labels.

Name: 19.20 by Norbert Tarayre
Address: Prince de Galles, 33 avenue George-V, Paris, 75008, France
Description: Built in 1928, the Prince de Galles is a legendary jewel of the Parisian Art Deco movement. It has chosen to democratise luxury hotel cuisine by entrusting its kitchens to Norbert Tarayre, the firebrand chef discovered on French TV show Top Chef in 2012. In a cosy setting that pays tribute to artistic life in Paris, the chef serves up traditional cuisine that channels the tasty regional cooking of yesteryear: grated carrot salad, leeks in vinaigrette, celeriac in remoulade dressing, pork shoulder and pommes Anna, salmon tournedos – not to mention the dessert trolley. It's all lovingly prepared and delivered at incredibly reasonable prices.

Name: Achillée
Description: Pieter Riedijk, previously chef at Le Montgomerie (K2 Altitude in Courchevel), has come down into the valley to open this bistro serving "food for sharing". In an inviting and convivial rustic-style decor, he focuses on quality ingredients from the terroir, which he cooks simply: cep and aubergine marmalade, to be spread on toast; roast pork, straw potatoes and a good béarnaise sauce with plenty of vinegar; rhubarb meringue. His goal is to make the most of the treasure trove of seasonal produce the region has to offer in spring and summer. He selects local farm ingredients as well as picking some himself.

Name: Château Fage - La Maison des Vignes
Description: Built in the white stone typical of the region, this 19C château is now a hotel-restaurant standing proud amid the vineyards. Chef Clément Costes (previously at Le Skiff Club) wins diners over with his straightforward and flavourful take on bistronomy cuisine. Ingredients are carefully selected and expertly prepared, a case in point being the fillet of pink sea bream with a shellfish sauce and virgin mussels and samphire, or the appetising pastry trolley. Wines by the glass start at €3; a more elaborate set menu in the evening.

Name: Mansouria
Description: Just a stone's throw from the Bastille, this restaurant has proved popular with fans of Moroccan cuisine for over 40 years. You are instantly transported by the aromas of this venerable institution, which is now run by the daughter of the founder. In a discreetly North African decor, traditional tagines and couscous are served alongside a host of lesser-known dishes, such as pigeon pastilla and traditional spicy lamb mourouzia "Al-Andalus" with sweet notes supplied by honey and sultanas – the house speciality. Top-quality ingredients and attentive service make for a delicious culinary voyage.

Name: Baillotte
Description: Perhaps chef Satoshi Amitsu (previously at Georges Blanc) is just being modest when he uses the term "semi-gourmet" cuisine on his website, because this bistro with an alluring red frontage easily holds its own against other restaurants. Deploying the precision for which the Japanese are renowned, the chef delights diners with French cuisine replete with colours and contrasts, backed up by meticulous jus and sauces: flame-charred mackerel, fregola sarda, beetroot, raspberry, walnut and shiso vinaigrette; veal, mushrooms, chervil root, quince condiment, full-bodied gravy. There's a good selection of wines by the glass, not just the usual favourites, with expert advice from the service team.

Name: Source
Description: This small-capacity restaurant exudes an intimate atmosphere (curtains, felt) in its decor of curved lines (lamps, tables, seats). Fostering this contact with his guests, the chef concentrates on the matter at hand: creative, instinctive cuisine as a single set menu comprising several courses. The inspiration and precision of the execution are plain to see: for instance, glazed duck on the Japanese barbecue, roasted beetroot, ripe condiment and giblets. Pleasant front-of-house team.

Name: Abîme - L'Auberge du Pont
Description: This long-established inn stands by a bridge spanning the gorge – the Chéran River flows a few hundred metres below! A native of the area, the chef likes to work with regional ingredients he sources from local producers. Even amateur mushroom foragers are welcome to offer up their pick of the day. His squash risotto, fricassee of shiitake, polypore and oyster mushrooms is a prime example of his culinary style, which is geared toward plants and vegetables and the interplay of textures. A "discovery menu" made up of several courses is available in the evening and at weekends. Appealing lunchtime set menu.

Name: Le Petit Basson
Address: 4 rue de la Madeleine, Troyes, 10000, France
Description: This is the first restaurant of chef Yann Caputo, who is a big fan of vegetables; not only does he grow them in his kitchen garden, but he also has them tattooed on his arm. No wonder, then, that he refers to his new venture as a "garden bistro", even though he also cooks meat (and wild-caught fish). The reasonably priced lunch menu is a steal: lentils from Champagne, smoked bacon chantilly, watercress from the garden; wild sea bream, turnips from the garden, coconut milk, ginger, lemongrass. The evening menu features more high-end ingredients (eg langoustines, wild sea bass) – these, too, served with vegetables from the chef's garden. Charming natural decor (strings of garlic, wheat and dried flowers adorn the walls) with wooden furnishings.

Name: Twist & Buckle (Tsim Sha Tsui)
Address: 29-31 Chatham Road South, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: Two young South Americans opened this shop specialising in churros. Besides the traditional version with cinnamon sugar, also try them glazed, in dips like dulce de leche and salted caramel, or even in sundaes with ice cream.

Name: Celestial Court
Address: 2F, Sheraton Hotel, 20 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The astute chef has over 25 years of experience and was brought up in a family who owned a dried seafood business. His shrewd insights on sourcing and preparing those gourmet ingredients are reflected in the menu. The speciality roast whole suckling pig with pearl barley and black truffles needs pre-ordering. Scrambled egg with lobster and caviar is another highlight. The windowless dining room is nicely furnished with rich wood accents.

Name: Ippoh
Address: 39 Aberdeen Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Now run by the fifth generation, this family business rooted in Osaka still strictly follows the traditional rules of making tempura. The owner-chef insists on battering and frying every morsel himself without delegating his duty. Seafood is flown in daily from Osaka and Toyosu fish market and they use flavourless safflower oil, so as not to overpower the ingredients’ natural tastes. The sauce is made to a secret recipe. Omakase is the best way to go. Bookings are essential.

Name: Fong Kei
Description: A longstanding shop offering Chinese cakes and biscuits. The almond cakes and egg rolls stand out.

Name: Fat Boy
Address: 3 Hau Fook Street, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: Hong Kong-style snacks including octopus, pork liver & turkey gizzard marinated in soy sauce. Sweet sauce and mustard add to the flavour. The combo set offers great value with three signature items.

Name: Golden Bauhinia Sang Kee
Address: GF, Expo Galleria, Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, 1 Expo Drive, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This space was taken over in 2021 by Sang Kee, a famous Cantonese restaurant with over 40 years of history. In addition to the same specialities from their Wan Chai flagship, the menu here boasts old-time artisan dishes exclusive to this branch. Barbecue chicken liver with pork is hard to find elsewhere; pan-fried deboned fourfinger threadfin with scallion and sea salt entices with its deep umami. The panoramic harbour views are also delightful.

Name: Tsui Hang Village (Tsim Sha Tsui)
Address: Shop 507, 5F, FoodLoft, Mira Place One, 132 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: A staple of the Tsim Sha Tsui restaurant scene since 1970s, this place is famous for its authentic Cantonese and Shun Tak fare, namely its bestselling honey-glazed char siu pork, braised beef ribs and shredded chicken, alongside some original creations by the head chef, such as fried king prawns in mango sauce topped with caviar. The dim sum is also good. Watching the chefs work their magic through the large window is all part of the experience.

Name: Keung Kee
Address: 406 Lockhart Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: After moving to this new spot, this simple shop boasts better comfort and a bigger menu. But signatures like glutinous rice with preserved meat, wok-fried rice rolls, and pork bone congee remain as tasty as ever.

Name: Ngao Kei Ka Lei Chon (Macau)
Address: GF, 1 Rua de Cinco de Outubro, Macau, Macau
Description: Don’t judge a book by its cover because the simple neon signs outside do not reflect the quality of food and service at this friendly, well-run noodle shop. The key draw is the swimmer crab congee – crabs are dressed à la minute and burst with seafood flavours, while the creamy congee imparts a rich aroma of rice. Other recommendations include braised E-fu noodles with crab roe, beef brisket in clear broth, and curry chicken with coconut milk.

Name: Mak Kee (May Ka Mansion)
Address: Shop 1, May Ka Mansion, 21 Fort Street, North Point, Hong Kong
Description: This shop serves Shanghainese delicacies made fresh daily, such as pot-stickers, pan-fried pork buns and sour and hot noodle soup. Scallion pancakes are available from 3pm until they run out.

Name: Lord Stow's Bakery (Rua do Tassara)
Address: 1 Rua do Tassara, Coloane Town Square, Coloane, Macau
Description: For over 30 years, the store has prided itself on its Portuguese egg tarts that have a crisp shell and silky, smooth filling. Tarts are made from scratch, baked throughout the day and sold fresh from the oven. Takeout only.

Name: China Tang
Address: Shop 411-413, 4F, Landmark Atrium, 15 Queen's Road Central, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This handsome restaurant was conceived and designed by the late Sir David Tang as a sister to the London branch, and mixes traditional Chinese art with contemporary Western design. Tables are set closely together and there are several private rooms. Dishes from Beijing, Sichuan and Canton feature and dim sum is popular. The chef has introduced a more modern element to the menu.

Name: Beanmountain
Address: GF, 1 Canal Road East, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
Description: For over 20 years, sugar fiends have been getting their fix of Chinese-style sweets here – from traditional crowd-pleasers such as put chai ko and Hakka tea cake made with stinkvine to novelty treats like mango sticky rice ball.

Name: Plaisance by Mauro Colagreco
Description: Mother of pearl finishes, turquoise accents and a whirlpool of metal fish sculptures introduce the ocean theme. Begin the meal with Chef Mauro's grandma's recipe – house-made bread with his favourite olive oil. The seafood-led menu delivers spellbinding dishes that incorporate the best ingredients from around the world alongside local vegetables, all finessed by solid French skills. Ask the sommelier to pick a wine for you.

Name: Sabah
Address: Shop 1, GF, Pao Woo Mansion, 177-179 Wan Chai Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: Sabah, a staple of Wan Chai’s restaurant scene for 18 years, shuttered its doors in 2019 before reopening here with the same kitchen team. Both the room and the menu are downsized, but signatures like bak kut teh, beef rendang, and seafood laksa remain, tasting just like before. Boneless Hainan chicken rice boasts bouncy skin and velvety juicy flesh. Even the trio of dips and pearl rice are also hard to find fault with.

Name: The Steak House
Address: GF, Regent, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: The iconic Regent Hong Kong has reopened with several new F&B outlets. One of them is The Steak House commanding sweeping harbour views through its tall windows. As its name suggests, the menu revolves around steak – from Italy, Spain, Korea, Japan, Australia, and the U.S. The Moroccan chef ages his own beef - ask the servers. Season your favourite cuts with rock salt, charcoal salt, yuzu salt or the array of sauces and mustards on offer.

Name: Cafe Bau
Address: Shop 8, Podium 1F, J Residence, 60 Johnston Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: Cafe Bau, a new dining concept by the self-proclaimed “Demon Chef” Alvin Leung, is styled like a vintage brasserie dripping in retro glam. Sit at the bar and watch the bartender concoct exquisite beverages. On to the food, order the 3-course menu for traditional European fare, or opt for  the 8-course tasting extravaganza for more innovative, adventurous dishes. Local produce like oysters and fish is used to good effect. Service is off-the-cuff and to-the-point.

Name: Ho Lee Fook
Description: Walls covered in gilded maneki-neko, mahjong tiles, pop art and red Chinese floral motifs make this a bold, unorthodox spot for a fun night out. The 80s Canto-pop soundtrack is also a proud expression of its local DNA. The open kitchen on ground level is a spectacle to behold and its creative Cantonese cooking harnesses bold distinctive flavours and wok hei. Try the crispy three-yellow chicken with sand ginger dip, and other wok-fries. Check ahead for dishes that need pre-ordering.

Name: She Wong Hei
Address: 59 Percival Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
Description: The manager that ran the famous snake soup shop She Wong Yee opened this restaurant on the same street. The classic snake soup is reworked with a slightly altered consistency, alongside fish maw, chicken, hand-sliced pork, dried tangerine peel, wood ear fungus and shiitake mushroom. Of course, you can still order barbecue meats, and glutinous rice to go with the soup. Duck liver sausage with snappy casing is certainly worth trying.

Name: Yuè (Gold Coast)
Address: LG, Gold Coast Hotel, 1 Castle Peak Road, Gold Coast, Tuen Mun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s not often one can enjoy Cantonese food surrounded by verdant scenery but here on the ground floor of the Gold Coast hotel that’s exactly what you get as this comfortable restaurant looks out onto a delightful garden. The menu includes both traditional and more contemporary dishes and it’s worth seeking out the chef’s specialities such as barbecued pork and double boiled pork lung soup with almond milk and fish maw, and deep-fried chicken with shrimp paste.

Name: The Swiss Chalet
Address: GF, 8 Hart Avenue, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Despite moving next door, the room still retains the same quaint Alpine chalet ambiance with wood furniture and beams set nicely against whitewashed walls. The classic Swiss menu covers a variety of cured meats and sausages, over 20 cheeses, and of course the unmissable fondue made with five cheeses and kirsch, to be paired with their extensive selection of Swiss wines. Thinly sliced veal with white mushrooms in a cream sauce is also worth trying.

Name: Ki Tsui
Address: 135 Fa Yuen Street, Mong Kok, Hong Kong
Description: Despite the small size, this shop offers a wide array of Cantonese traditional puddings and pastries like Xiaofeng cake and walnut cookies.

Name: Kika
Address: GF, 11A Travessa da Sé, Macau, Macau
Description: Pop in for an artisan Japanese gelato. Customers are spoiled for exotic choices here – crown melon from Shizuoka, Hokkaido 3.6 milk, Hojicha, and, of course, their famous ultra-strong matcha green tea for die-hard tea lovers.

Name: Terrazza
Address: Shop 201, 2F, Galaxy Hotel, Galaxy, Estrada da Baia de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The menu covers the culinary traditions of every region in Italy and is updated every three months to keep it fresh. Guests get to see how the food is prepared through the glass wall. Pizza dough, tagliatelle, ravioli and tagliolini are made from scratch in-house and the extensive wine list is well worth exploring. Add in exceedingly comfy chairs and warm, welcoming service and you have a great place for a relaxing meal.

Name: Joyful Dessert House
Address: Shop 2-3, GF, Ngai Hing Mansion, 74 Hak Po Street, Mong Kok, Hong Kong
Description: Come for beautifully plated Western desserts, such as waffles, chocolate fondant and velvety shaved ice. Recommendations include mango Napoleon, caramelised pineapple sorbet, and green tea fondant à la mode.

Name: Carbone
Address: 9F, LKF Tower, 33 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A nod to Manhattan’s American-Italian diners circa 1950s, this colourful spot celebrates the era in everything from the floor tiles and chandeliers, to the cutlery and servers’ uniforms. In the same way, the menu embraces classics like pastas and steaks, such as the signature Tasmanian lamb tomahawk. Portion sizes are more American than Italian, enough for a few to share. House-made limoncello makes great apéritifs and digestifs.

Name: Fishball Man (To Kwa Wan)
Address: GF, 50 Tin Kwong Road, To Kwa Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Though local snacks like shaomai and cheong fun are offered, its eponymous speciality remains the most popular. Besides the spicy variety, the springy and flavourful white fish balls drizzled in chilli oil are unmissable.

Name: Cornerstone
Address: 49 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Owner-chef Shane Osborn of Arcane fame calls it an ‘Australian café’ – in fact, it feels more like a hip bistro with its faux-industrial décor. The small menu is a tapestry of global culinary cultures, including Aussie, European and Asian favourites. Though it changes a few times each month to keep things fresh, dishes are always competitively priced and loaded with big flavours and pleasing textures. Online reservations only.

Name: Hung Hom Pancake
Address: Shop 2, Polly Court, Taku Street, Hung Hom, Hong Kong
Description: For over 40 years, this neighbourhood shop has provided the childhood memories of many. Pancakes, waffles and egg waffles are all made to order. Tricolour egg waffles in plain, chocolate and matcha flavours particularly stand out.

Name: Giando
Address: Shop 1, GF, Tower 1, Starcrest, 9 Star Street, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Italian chef Gianni Caprioli owns several restaurants in Hong Kong but this one, tucked away in a quiet corner between Wan Chai and Admiralty, is his jewel. Besides the booths along one side of the smart dining room, outdoor seating is also prized for an al-fresco Italian feast or just a glass of Italian wine pre- or post-dinner. Expect to see dishes from all over Italy, such as hand-rolled strozzapreti pasta, or Milanese-style veal chop.

Name: Owl's
Address: GF, 32 Mody Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: You’ll need to wait as the homemade choux pastries are filled on order with cream and custard of different flavours but, rest assured, the wait is worth it. Check out the occasional limited time offers. Take-out only.

Name: Ving Kei (Macau)
Address: GF, 47 Rua da Tercena, Macau, Macau
Description: Apart from the signature cold or hot tofu pudding and soy milk, it also provides tofu products, squid and noodles.

Name: Hop Yik Tai
Address: 121 Kweilin Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong
Description: The menu at this always busy shop features Hong Kong-style snacks like fish balls, pork skin and braised radish. The hugely popular rice rolls are silky-smooth, with a hint of richness from the lard.

Name: Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira
Address: 3F, The Mira Hotel, 118 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The striking chandelier with hundreds of glowing glass globes is set nicely against the calming green colour scheme and verdant views. Cantonese classics underpinned by solid, traditional techniques are revitalised by creative use of ingredients and modern twists. On top of special dim sum such as crispy frog legs with peppered salt, try also Mrs. Song’s fish soup made with fresh grouper fillet. Wine pairings are thoughtfully matched.

Name: Heimat
Address: 8F, LKF Tower, 33 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Heimat translates as “homeland”. After working in some prestigious kitchens, the German owner-chef Peter Find reinterprets classics from his home country with quality ingredients, dexterous care and much sophistication. The 6-course tasting menu takes diners on a journey across Germany with flavours from his childhood memories. A shorter 3-course menu is available at lunch. And who can resist the gummy bear trolley at the end?

Name: La Brasserie
Address: GF, Lyndhurst Building, 23-29 Lyndhurst Terrace, Central, Hong Kong
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant serves authentic French fare in a convivial atmosphere. Seafood choices abound – from smoked salmon and bouillabaisse to the seafood platter. Meat lovers should check out the pâtés in the charcuterie section. A visit to the pastry counter is a must for classics such as éclairs and opera cake as much as novel creations like genmaicha St Honoré. The wine list boasts a good range of by-the-glass options.

Name: Chiado
Address: Shop 2206, 2F, The Londoner, Estrada do lstmo, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As well as a neighbourhood of Lisbon, Chiado is celebrity chef Henrique Sá Pessoa’s first dining concept outside Portugal. The room is modern and cosy, setting the mood for a feast of Portuguese classics oozing with understated elegance and robust flavours. Choose the 6-course degustation menu to sample all the chef’s signature dishes. Don’t miss the boneless suckling pig that is slow-cooked then grilled, boasting crispy skin and silky meat.

Name: Ho Kee Dessert (To Kwa Wan)
Address: Shop 111 & 122, GF, I-Feng Mansions, 237A To Kwa Wan Road, To Kwa Wan, Hong Kong
Description: The staple in Mong Kok for over 30 years moved to this location in 2020. Rest assured their traditional sweet soups like black sesame paste, and glutinous rice balls in ginger syrup taste as good as ever.

Name: Clarence
Address: 25F, H Code, 45 Pottinger Street, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: After working and living in Asia for over a decade, chef Olivier Elzer founded this restaurant that aims to allow new ways of enjoying French cuisine. He minted an original concept known as “Yakifrenchy” – a menu that serves French classics like duck confit, frogs’ legs and escargots on skewers, like Japanese yakitori. Local family table culture is taken to another level with meat and fish cooked whole on the bone, perfect for sharing.

Name: Testina
Description: Aptly named after its signature pig’s head dish, Testina is the collaboration between the Milanese trattoria Trippa Milano and a local hospitality group. Championing a nose-to-tail philosophy, the kitchen team serves every part of an animal to great effect. Besides pig’s head, expect to see tripe, bone marrow and veal tongue on the menu. For an authentic taste of Trippa Milano’s cooking, try homemade tagliatelle with duck ragù.

Name: Jing Alley
Address: GF, Dawning House, 145 Connaught Road Central, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
Description: The chef’s modern Sichuanese fare is made with ingredients from around the world: duck blood curd from Chengdu, chillies from Yunnan, pork from Japan, chitterlings from Spain… The signature water-boiled black pearl fish uses a green chilli and pork bone stock that doesn’t look red or oily like traditional ones; the freshwater fish with springy flesh also adds to the texture and flavour. The chitterlings with mixed chillies are addictively tasty.

Name: One Harbour Road
Address: 7-8F, Grand Hyatt Hotel, 1 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The split-level room affords sweeping harbour views, while the high ceiling and sound of the fountain exude serenity. Exquisite Cantonese cooking is the name of the game here. Start with the crispy and appetising deep-fried shiitake in osmanthus honey glaze; for mains, opt for Wuxi-style Boston lobster that is spicy, tangy and sustainably sourced. Some dishes are available in smaller portions. Detailed and thoughtful service adds to the experience.

Name: Toritama
Address: GF, Greenville, 2 Glenealy, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Tokyo restaurants keep opening branches in Hong Kong and this time it’s all about yakitori. Seats are limited so it’s worth booking ahead and asking for the counter to watch the expert preparation in the kitchen. 40-day-old chickens are used, and 28 different parts of the birds are offered – rare cuts such as sweetbread may need pre-ordering. Pickles made with different produce according to the season make the perfect side dish for the skewers.

Name: Wing
Address: 29F, The Wellington, 198 Wellington Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The second venture from owner-chef Vicky Cheng who runs the well-acclaimed Vea upstairs, Wing is named after his Chinese name, meaning eternity. The tasting menu features contemporary Chinese courses made with mostly local ingredients but underpinned by European techniques. He reinterprets classic recipes and familiar flavours with creative twists and playful food combinations. Online reservations open at midnight for up to 28 days ahead.

Name: The Ritz-Carlton Café
Address: GF, The Ritz-Carlton, Galaxy, Estrada da Baia de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
Description: Tiles, mirrors and marble are used to great effect in this bright, lively French brasserie with an all-day dining concept. It prides itself not only on its friendly service, but also the array of classic French food on offer. Besides the daily special, steak is big on the menu with many prime cuts to choose from. Seafood lovers should try freshly shucked oysters. Round out your dinner with the spectacular tableside Grand Marnier flambéed crepes.

Name: Ami
Address: Shop 302, 3F, Alexandra House, 18 Chater Road, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ami, decorated on a forest theme, offers a fine dining experience in a casual setting. On top of tasting menus, all-day à la carte choices abound – Gallic classics, plates to share and bar snacks are all up for grabs. The enthusiastic, young chef from Southern France imbues the menu with novel ideas, such as yellow chicken cooked two ways: poached breast and grilled leg with morels and a vin jaune sauce. Made-to-order orange blossom soufflé is fluffy and custardy.

Name: The Kitchen
Address: 3F, Grand Lisboa Hotel, Avenida de Lisboa, Macau, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Beef is the star of the show at this handsome, masculine dining room which also houses a sushi bar, a salad bar and a live fish tank. Choose from prime cuts from the U. S. and Wagyu from Kagoshima and Australia; then have it seared on an open flame to your desired 'doneness' and pair it with one of the 17,000-plus wine labels from around the world. Bread is baked daily and appetisers are made in the open kitchen à la minute.

Name: Imperial Court
Address: GF, MGM Macau, Avenida Dr. Sun Yat Sen, NAPE, Macau, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the same floor as the hotel’s VIP lobby, this sleek, contemporary dining room wows guests with a vividly carved Chinese dragon entwined around a marble pillar. The head chef has over 20 years of experience and updates the menu regularly to star seasonal dishes. Try his crispy-skin fried baby pigeon, and dim sum with a creative twist – order as few or as many pieces as you like. The impressive wine list boasts over 2,000 labels.

Name: Mok Yee Kei
Description: Offering Serradura pudding and ice cream. The signature durian ice cream comes with Musang King, D24 and Mon Tong choices.

Name: A Lorcha
Address: 289 Rua do Almirante Sergio, Macau, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Business is booming at this friendly restaurant near Barra Temple as regulars just can’t get enough of the hearty food from a kitchen helmed by the owner’s mother. Start with the obligatory salted cod fritter. Besides barbecue dishes cooked over a charcoal grill, the extensive menu includes specialities like sautéed pork and clams Alentejo style, mixed seafood rice, and Macanese coconut and turmeric chicken; all great choices to share.

Name: Bâtard
Address: Inside The Fine Wine Experience, Shop E, 165-166 Connaught Road West, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Tucked behind a 7,000 square-foot wine shop, Bâtard is as much about the food as the elixir. The young head chef has worked in some famous kitchens in Singapore and Hong Kong; his classic French techniques are manifested in signatures like roast local three-yellow chicken, and monkfish en croute; pre-order them to avoid disappointment. Wine-wise, over 1,000 labels are offered at retail prices – ask the sommelier to help you navigate the list.

Name: Palace Garden
Address: Shop 306, 3F, Grand Lisboa Palace, Grand Lisboa Palace Resort, Rua do Tiro, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The room is the epitome of lavish maximalism – one wall is covered in a 35-metre-long Suzhou silk embroidery with a chrysanthemum theme. On the menu, ingredients from around the world are used to make refined Cantonese dishes, including labour-intensive items from ancient recipes. Crispy skin squab with lemongrass uses 18-day birds from Shiqi, boasting juicy flesh and mild smokiness. The menu can appear overwhelming, so ask servers for recommendations.

Name: Shum Shum Desserts
Address: Shop C, GF, 46 Kweilin Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong
Description: Classic Hongkongese and Taiwanese sweet soups on offer here include creamy coconut soup – a silky delight on its own but even better with chewy taro or sweet potato balls. Try also purple glutinous rice soup with elastic jelly cubes.

Name: Hyde Park Garden
Address: 44 Hoi Pong Road Central, Lei Yue Mun, Hong Kong
Description: The owner also sells seafood from the opposite stall so diners can pick from a dazzling selection flown in daily. Ask servers for the best way to cook your meal; for instance, razor clams are typically stir-fried in chilli black bean sauce, and abalone with ginger and scallion in a claypot. The signature fish soup is simmered for hours with freshwater fish and tofu. Try also the deep-fried eggplant, and tofu skin sweet soup with pearl barley.

Name: Hing Kee
Address: 1F, Bowa House, 180 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: It started two generations ago in Causeway Bay but the family’s reputation for Boat People style cuisine was made in Tsim Sha Tsui. Elder sister heads the serving team; younger brother runs the kitchen. They are famous for their stir-fried crabs with black beans and chilli, roast duck and rice noodles in soup and congee. You can decide level of spiciness for some dishes. Guests aren’t seated until everyone in the party has arrived.

Name: So Kee
Address: Shop 15, GF, Block A, Ho Shun Yee Building, 9 Fung Yau Street East, Yuen Long, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: There’s just one item on the menu – double-steamed egg white custard with milk, boasting a silky runny centre under a firmer crust. Order the chilled ones if you’re in a rush, or wait patiently as the hot ones are made to order.

Name: Man Kee Cart Noodle
Address: 121 Fuk Wing Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong
Description: The number of topping choices can be overwhelming, but Chinese chive dumplings and Swiss chicken wings are especially good. Fancy a spicy kick? Try the house-made chilli sauce over your noodles.

Name: Yi Shun (Macau)
Address: 381 Avenida de Almeida Ribeiro, Macau, Macau
Description: A longstanding shop offering traditional desserts, such as pineapple with crushed ice and sweet lotus seed soup with egg. Milk custard and ginger milk pudding are house specialties, to which you can add lotus seeds or red beans for extra flavour.

Name: Lei Garden (Wan Chai)
Address: 1F, CNT Tower, 338 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: An inventory of restaurants in Wan Chai wouldn’t be complete without a Lei Garden. This branch is bigger than most and boasts a busy, bustling atmosphere, particularly at lunchtime. It follows the group’s tried-and-tested formula of offering an extensive menu with luxurious dishes alongside less elaborate but classic Cantonese specialities. Seafood enthusiasts should consider pre-ordering the Alaskan king crab or Brittany blue lobster.

Name: Chuen Kee Seafood (Hoi Pong Street)
Address: 53 Hoi Pong Street, Sai Kung, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Two family-run restaurants just a few minutes’ walk from each other have been in business since the 80s; choose the one by the quay for the rooftop terrace and harbour views. A wide array of seafood is available from adjacent fishmongers: cuttlefish, crab, lobster, molluscs, shrimps…Select your meal from the tank and ask the servers the best ways to cook it. Abalone and mantis shrimp in peppered salt are the smash hits not to be missed.

Name: Farm House
Address: 1F, Phase 1, China Taiping Tower, 8 Sunning Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
Description: The aquarium running the entire length of one wall certainly catches the eye. But it’s the traditional dishes painstakingly crafted with quality ingredients and gourmet dried seafood that win the hearts of the regulars. You must try their famous fried chicken wing stuffed with sticky rice. Baked sea whelks stuffed with foie gras, steamed rice with chicken, abalone and dried scallops are also deftly prepared. Friendly, thoughtful service.

Name: Tai Tsai (Tsuen Wan)
Address: GF, 99 Hoi Pa Street, Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: "Tai Tsai" is a homophone of "Taiwanese cuisine" in Chinese. The owner missed his home island's classic braised pork rice so much that he opened his own shop. He cooks the signature rice dish in Taipei style, adding sugar in moderation, and with hand-diced pork belly slow-cooked in aromatics and soy for up to four hours. Top it with onsen tamago or soft-boiled egg. The pepper salt popcorn chicken and boba tea are also well made. Arrive early to beat the crowd.

Name: Lucale
Address: Shop A, GF, 100 Third Street, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong
Description: Named after a portmanteau of the two chefs’ first names, this neighbourhood joint uses fine artisanal ingredients from Italy to craft Italian favourites, ranging from homemade pasta to seafood and meat dishes, best enjoyed with their selection of Italian wines. Black truffle chitarrino with Pienza pecorino is guaranteed to melt your heart with its al dente texture and tantalising aroma. The eater-friendly prices also explain its popularity despite its hidden location down an alley.

Name: Saffron
Address: 31F, Banyan Tree, Galaxy, Estrada da Baia da Nossa Senhora de Esperança, Cotai, Macau
Description: The hotel’s restaurant has been completely revamped and moved to the 31st floor, commanding breathtaking views. Now helmed by a native Thai chef with extensive experience, the kitchen specialises in refined Thai cuisine, such as chargrilled organic pork jowl from the royal farm in Thailand with a tamarind fish sauce that is out of this world. The signature curry king crab is also unmissable with a three-chilli blend adding heat and aroma.

Name: Portugália
Description: After a hiatus, Portugália has reopened in the historic town with the same kitchen and service teams. The blue-and-white interior, dotted in matching azulejo tiles from their previous address, is relaxed and cosy. The menu features authentic Portuguese family favourites in sharing portions, such as gambas a la guillo, and the signature steak ‘a Portugália’ in a secret gravy. Round off the meal with a fluffy, whipped serradura.

Name: The Mews
Address: 1F, The Londoner, Estrada do lstmo, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Diners are bowled over by the high-ceilinged room adorned in colourful lanterns and wood carving, all of which on a mews (stabling for horses in historic London) theme. The native Thai kitchen team reinvents specialities from their homeland with a contemporary spin. Try the mouthwateringly juicy grilled Wagyu beef with red curry and chakram leaves, or the tangy sunflower chicken tom kha soup. Thai-inspired nibbles and cocktails are also highly recommended.

Name: Pin Yue Xuan
Address: Shop 1016, 1F, The Venetian, Estrada de Baia de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: The high-ceilinged room, which sports a smart modern Chinese vibe, is the quintessence of stylish flair. The Hong Kong head chef, who has been honing his skills in Macau for many a year, imbues the mostly Cantonese menu with creative touches and luxe delights, such as crispy quinoa on smoked tofu skin rolls, and steamed savoury custard made with Breton blue lobster and Japanese Ranou eggs. The exquisitely crafted petit fours are not to be missed.

Name: Sếp
Address: 19F, High Block, H Code, 45 Pottinger Street, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The executive chef spent seven years working in Vietnam where he fell in love with wood-fired cooking. He was keen to introduce the concept to Hong Kong audience when he returned home. His project Sếp specialises in modern Indochine Vietnamese fare using a wood-fired grill in the open kitchen. Menus with 8 or 10 courses feature must-tries like Hoi An poulet made with dry-aged local three-yellow chicken, and bún bò Huế with premium black angus beef.

Name: Mosu
Address: 3F, M+ Tower, West Kowloon Cultural District, 38 Museum Drive, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: Nestled in an art museum with commanding panoramic harbour views, the spacious room imparts serenity with its concrete walls and scattered lights that resemble a starry sky. The head chef has years of experience in French cooking, working in some prestigious kitchens in Japan. A single tasting menu is served and it changes from time to time. The courses reflect the chef’s multicultural exposure with its creative combinations of globally sourced ingredients.

Name: Temple Street Beef Offal
Address: 18 Arthur Street, Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This long-standing shop is popular with locals. Tripe, intestine, pancreas or lung can be ordered individually or as an assortment, on a skewer or in a bowl. The offal soaks up the broth nicely, with three sauces on the side.

Name: Jardin de Jade (Wan Chai)
Address: G3-4, GF, Sun Hung Kai Centre, 30 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: The first Hong Kong venture of the renowned Shanghai restaurant group is certainly not lacking in grandeur, with its double-height ceiling and striking chandelier. Shanghainese classics and dim sum are made the traditional way but with updated presentation. The xiao long bao with beautifully pleated paper-thin skin, soupy filling and spot-on seasoning is the jewel in the crown. The seasonal menu covers regional specialities from beyond Shanghai.

Name: SW Steakhouse
Address: GF, North Esplanade, Wynn Palace, Avenida da Nave Desportiva, Cotai, Macau
Description: The room is designed like an auditorium, with all tables providing a decent view of the stage. Multimedia shows are put on every half hour for a total experience of art, sound, technology and gastronomy. On top of classics like oysters on the half shell, crab cake, and beef tartare; beef steak cooked in the 1200°F grill is certainly a highlight. Choose among USDA prime, Aussie Black Angus, pureblood and crossbred Wagyu from Japan, NZ and the U.S.

Name: Yi
Address: 21F, Morpheus, City of Dreams, Estrada do Istmo, Cotai, Macau
Description: Established on the 21st floor of a sky bridge, Yi’s knockout location is matched by stunning views, impressive architecture and an exotic interior. The 9-course seasonal-driven tasting menu refers to the 24 solar terms of the Chinese calendar, incorporating quality produce from around the world. Rare, premium ingredients, such as nodoguro and A4 Wagyu from Miyazaki, Japan, are deftly and creatively crafted with artful plating.

Name: Luk Yu Tea House
Description: Large numbers of both regulars and tourists come to Luk Yu Tea House for the traditionally prepared and flavoursome dim sum, and its three floors fill up quickly. The animated atmosphere and subtle colonial decoration are appealing but no one really stays too long; the serving team in white jackets have seen it all before and go about their work with alacrity. Popular dishes are crispy deep fried chicken and fried noodles with sliced beef.

Name: Leela
Address: Shop 301-310, Lee Garden Three, 1 Sunning Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The room, furnished in a neoteric Indian style, sports a balcony for pre- or post-prandial drinks. The Indian head chef champions a menu starring specialities from all over India, with contemporary, creative twists. Every course tells a story and diners can truly experience India’s food culture from different perspectives. Try the tandoori dishes from the custom-made oven. With firm yet tender flesh, monkfish imported from France works a treat in the curry.

Name: Mrs. Fong Chinese Desserts
Description: This busy family-run shop moved here in 2022. Over 10 Chinese sweets are made from scratch daily, such as red bean cake or put-chai cake. Black sesame roll is especially prized for its soft-springy texture and deep flavour.

Name: Above & Beyond
Address: 28F, Hotel Icon, 17 Science Museum Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The stylish décor, sweeping harbour views and extensive menu make this restaurant a popular choice for Cantonese dining. The chef puts a new spin on the dim sum tradition by melding imported ingredients with authentic local flavours. Signatures such as steamed Alaskan king crab dumplings, and scallop rice flour rolls with cordyceps flowers are nothing short of ingenious. The set lunch can be ordered individually with a vegan option.

Name: Chesa
Address: 1F, The Peninsula Hotel, 22 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Even since opening as a ‘pop-up’ restaurant created by the Swiss-born manager back in 1965, Chesa has been the go-to place in town for those wanting authentic Swiss cuisine. The Alpine chalet-style décor more than compensates for the room’s lack of windows, while the menu covers all bases, offering fondue, raclette and the famous Chemin de Fer wines. You can even specify how strong you want the brandy taste to be in your fondue.

Name: Involtini
Address: 11F, The L. Square, 459-461 Lockhart Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The young chef, an alumnus of Otto e Mezzo, attracts a loyal following with his fresh pasta, handmade in-house daily. Italian eggs and flour are used in the dough which is rested overnight to give it a lovely al dente texture. The signature tagliolini with springy carabineros red prawns boasts a rich sauce loaded with seafood flavours. The pasta menu is updated from time to time to keep it fresh and reflect what’s in season.

Name: Yuè (Causeway Bay)
Address: Shop 1301, Food Forum, Time Square, 1 Matheson Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
Description: Having worked in some prestigious kitchens in Japan and Macau for over 40 years, the chef designed a menu of refined Cantonese dishes using top-notch ingredients from around the world, such as Alaskan king crab, Japanese chillies and Taiwanese bird’s-nest fern. The classic sweet and sour pork is given a new spin with aged vinegar and dried plums, plus an option of plant-based ‘meat’. Private rooms in various sizes are perfect for parties.

Name: Manuel Cozinha Portuguesa
Address: 90 Rua de Femão Mendes Pinto, Taipa, Macau
Description: After a spot of renovation for cosier feel, authenticity and hospitality remain the establishment’s hallmark. The friendly owner-chef has revamped the traditional Portuguese menu, now arranged by key ingredient. Using only top-notch seasonal produce, most dishes are barbecued traditionally. Grilled codfish and fried rice with squid ink are the must-tries. Check out the daily specials on the blackboard before ordering.

Name: The Merchants
Address: Forty-Five, Gloucester Tower, Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Central, Hong Kong
Description: The top three floors of a prestigious office tower in Central have been remodelled into a swanky restaurant with drop-dead harbour views. Green velvet is a prominent feature, with contrasting splashes of orange on the semi-circular banquettes. Well-crafted traditional Shanghainese and Jiangzhe classics like braised wheat gluten, sautéed “dragon beard” shredded mandarin fish, pan-fried eight-treasure rice, and braised Chinese ham in osmanthus honey.

Name: Tuber Umberto Bombana
Address: Shop 113A, 1F, K11 Musea, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This dining concept by the eponymous chef is dedicated to his favourite ingredient – the white and black gold of gastronomy; its name also refers to the genus to which truffles belong. Only one degustation menu is served, combining the best seasonal ingredients from around the world with the prized fungus. Artisanal linguine with jumbo carabinero prawns from Spain stands out in particular, with the tomalley loaded with sweetness and umami.

Name: Hong Kong Cuisine
Address: 1F, Elegance Court, 2-4 Tsoi Tak Street, Happy Valley, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This upstairs restaurant was rebranded and remodelled in 2022. Chef Li started cooking professionally in the UK at the age of 16 and his dishes are rooted in Chinese traditions, but underpinned by modern French techniques and novel food combinations. He has an affinity for perfumed oils and the use of fried tofu and pork rind in caramelised sweet and sour Iberico pork is ingenious. His aromatic smoked soy sauce chicken is also unmissable.

Name: Mâm Amis
Address: Shop A & B, GF, Fu Fai Commercial Centre, 27 Hillier Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The smart wood panelled front contrasts sharply with the distressed walls, vintage lamps and hanging greenery inside. Vietnamese chefs are keen on bringing authentic Vietnamese food to Hong Kong, with chargrilled items and phở among the highlights. Try the chargrilled river prawns that boast bouncy, briny-sweet flesh and exceptional smokiness. Phở comes in generous portions with a flavour-packed soup base.

Name: Auor
Address: 4F, China Underwriters Centre, 88 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Singaporean chef Voon gives familiar Asian flavours a fine dining revamp with great panache and deft use of European techniques. His multi-course dinner menu, which changes every season, celebrates the circle of life; standout dishes include lobster green curry and mud crab. The simple, understated decor puts the creative food centre stage. To watch the alchemy unfold, book the private room with a window onto the kitchen.

Name: Don Alfonso 1890
Address: Shop 307, 3F, Palazzo Versace, Grand Lisboa Palace Resort, Rua do Tiro, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-owned haute cuisine brand from Italy opened this high-end outpost in Macau. Versace may have taken care of the design, but the fashion house's signature glamour doesn't outshine the food. The kitchen excels at delivering vibrant flavours from the Amalfi Coast, using fresh produce from the family's own organic farm – try the handmade tagliolini with scampi and white truffle. Ask the sommelier for help navigating the long wine list.

Name: Tempura Uchitsu
Address: 45F, Four Seasons Hotel, 8 Financial Street, Central, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Traditional Japanese décor, a solid wood counter and the terrarium behind the open kitchen give this place a relaxing vibe. The set menu features more than 10 kinds of seasonal seafood and veggies, such as sea urchin roe and prawn, coated in a thin translucent tempura batter and fried in a blend of cotton seed and sesame oils. Most ingredients are shipped from Japan, except the exclusive item in this branch – deep-fried bird’s nest in rice paper.

Name: Ristorante de LEN
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 66, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the central and very busy Corso Italia, this restaurant has an elegant Alpine feel. Here, subtle lighting, soft background music and larch wood cladding on the walls create an ambience with an attractive blend of the modern and traditional. The cuisine takes inspiration from the local region, with specialities interpreted with a contemporary twist, including a focus on vegetable- and cheese-based dishes such as the excellent “fonduta di Saporito d'alpeggio” (fondue).

Name: Il Rivale in Città
Description: Situated in a beautiful 18C palazzo right in the centre of Brescia, this elegant restaurant consists of several small dining rooms of different colours, fabrics and furnishings yet all with the same historic atmosphere – the room with just one table is truly intimate! The cuisine features substantial recipes with a contemporary Italian flavour including top-quality options such as potato puff pastry, scampi, caviar and hazelnut cream, while one of the highlights of the new formula is the wooden dessert trolley on which a selection of tempting home-made delicacies is presented. The wine list (easily consulted on a tablet) is also impressive, with a particular focus on labels from nearby Franciacorta.

Name: Novo Osteria
Address: piazza De Cristoforis 30, Borgonovo Val Tidone, 29011, Italy
Description: Originally a monastery, this building dating back to the 11C was later transformed into an inn. Having closed at the beginning of this century, the building has now been fully renovated and restored to its original function, while retaining much of its original architecture. In addition to the restaurant, which serves traditional local cuisine with a modern focus and plenty of flavour (we particularly enjoyed the savoury zabaglione gnocchi with porcini mushrooms, Jerusalem artichokes and currants), there are also seven guestrooms available in the adjoining Locanda Borgo Impero.

Name: San Baylon
Description: Not far from Piazza del Popolo and Rome’s most exclusive shopping streets, this restaurant is situated in the Palazzo Ripetta hotel, in what was once the refectory of a 17C convent. Today, the ambience here is more informal, with an almost bistro-like feel, while the cuisine is inspired by classic Italian dishes, including various grilled options among the main courses. Meals are served in the palazzo’s inner courtyard in fine weather.

Name: Osteria La Pimpinella
Description: Situated in the historic centre but near a square with a car park, this modern inn serves Piedmontese cuisine which is contemporary in style yet still firmly anchored in local traditions. The generously portioned, well-presented dishes on the menu include vitello tonnato (excellent – we tried it!), tajarin pasta, Bra sausage and casseroles (the soft suckling pig cheek was delicious), all of which are as much a feast for the eyes as for the palate. The restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, aided by proficient and courteous staff with a feminine touch.

Name: Le Bistrot
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the refined rooms of Grand Hotel Royal e Golf, the dining room with its glass wall looks like a stage overlooking the chain of Monte Bianco and Dente del Gigante. The gastronomic proposal is one of the most appealing in the area: creative rather than local, the dishes are refined and technically elaborate.

Name: Henri Restaurant
Description: The name of this restaurant refers to its owner Henri Prosperi, who returned to his beloved Viareggio in 2021. This accomplished maître d' from another era will introduce you, with both charm and professionalism, to his daughter Serena’s dishes, which are finely balanced between classic and modern flavours, with the occasional French influence. The chef’s menu features meat and fish dishes, with a firm focus on luxury ingredients. The same is true of the wine list, which includes renowned labels such as Petrus and Sassicaia, as well as some of the best French and Italian sparkling wines. Welcome back, Henri!

Name: Hebbo Wine & Deli
Address: Località Lago di Dobbiaco, Toblach, 39034, Italy
Description: Situated on a campsite on the shores of Lake Dobbiaco, this new restaurant demonstrates its owner’s passion for wine and contemporary cuisine. The young Austrian chef here has plenty of experience behind him – in the evening, his dishes are showcased on surprise tasting menus of seven or nine courses, while at lunchtime, there’s also a 5-course option. His recipes feature plenty of vegetables and exciting combinations, such as burnt leek, Romanesco sauce and potato or trout, or alternatively, dried beetroot, reduced cream, thyme and Schüttelbrot. Ingredients are sourced from trusted producers, as well as family members who run a biodynamic farm nearby. The superb wine list demonstrates the friendly, competent owner’s passion for wine.

Name: Gina
Address: via Croce di Città 25, Aosta, 11100, Italy
Description: In the old town, a simple and informal location (but on the floor below there are two rooms between the Roman walls of Aosta!) for a cuisine of remarkable quality: the chef often starts from local traditions to develop them into more creative dishes, whose protagonists are often mountain products.

Name: Maihöfli by UniQuisine
Description: Since its reopening, this lovely restaurant just outside the city centre has acquired a new head chef in Robert Steuri. In the evenings, he and his dedicated team showcase precise craftsmanship and top-notch ingredients in two intriguing and innovative three-, five- or seven-course set menus, one of which is vegan. The dishes are full of finesse and carefully composed, elaborate but not cluttered – a great example is the green asparagus, mushrooms, snow peas and beans. Options are more limited at lunchtime. The attractive setting sees the charming features of this old building, such as high ceilings with decorative mouldings and wood panelling, seamlessly integrated into its sleek and elegant modern design. Professional and well-coordinated service.

Name: Le 1913
Description: This elegant restaurant, whose terrace commands a knockout view of the mountains and the valley, is located in the heart of the recently refurbished Villars Palace. The creative menu subtly mixes regional and Mediterranean accents, illustrated by lightly fried fera (lake fish) with green vegetables and a sweet-sour sauce with caper blossom, or Simmental calf’s sweetbread, summer mushrooms, local cured ham and port sauce. Watching the kitchen team at work is a feast for the eye!

Name: Colani Bistrot
Description: Located just off the reception area of the tasteful and well-appointed Hotel Colani, Colani Bistrot is the alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The food served here – Mediterranean cuisine with a local twist. We can certainly recommend the "Ravioli of the Day". Meat eaters should ask about the main dish centred on venison or veal – showcasing a different cut every day. Friendly service, a laid-back atmosphere and modern interior design featuring light wood and a whole host of decorative details.

Name: Lusi Brasserie
Description: A tip before we get started: In fine weather, be sure to nab a table on the terrace in front of the building, from which you can take in stunning views of the Matterhorn! But the brasserie of the long-established Grand Hotel Zermatterhof also provides a delightful, classically elegant setting with its lovely walnut panelling and partially glass-paned vaulted ceiling. The cuisine is French and draws on international influences. The menu includes "Lusi Classics" such as calf's head, and traditional dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, steak tartare, burgers and flammkuchen – and there is always an evening special.

Name: Langosteria
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This is the new place to see and be seen on the ski slopes overlooking St Moritz. The terrace affords magnificent views, making it a delightful spot in which to savour freshly prepared Italian cuisine. Langoustine, lobster and fish, truffle pizza and pasta are the specialities of this restaurant, which also has locations in Milan, Paris and Paraggi. If you're not skiing, the best way to get here is by taxi.

Name: KCC by Mauro Colagreco
Description: KCC stands for Kulm Country Club. The handsome L-shaped building is located right next to the ice rink and has a garden for summer days. The cuisine is classic and draws on Mediterranean influences. As well as an appealing selection of starters and pasta dishes, the menu includes veal chops and lamb shoulder, which are carved at your table. There are also mouthwatering desserts, such as the pain perdu (French toast). The atmosphere is relaxed and the decor tasteful – the vintage sledges adorning the ceiling are bound to draw the eye! Fabulous terrace.

Name: L'Alkimista
Description: L'Alkimista occupies a two-storey property along a pedestrian street in the centre of town that is impressive for its contemporary decor and relaxed ambience. Here, young owner-chef Pola Hany William creates cuisine that constantly blends influences from other cultures, but with its roots in the Mediterranean and the use of Spanish ingredients (he is a particular fan of Rubia Gallega beef and red tuna). His dishes are full of different textures, aromas and flavours that he combines with great skill, accompanied by a strong focus on presentation. The à la carte is complemented by two tasting menus (Phi and Omega) plus a lunchtime menu (Kappa) that always includes a savoury rice dish.

Name: Regueiro da Cova
Description: This restaurant, located along the well-maintained banks of the Támega, the river that criss-crosses the town of Verín in the province of Ourense, is not be missed, with its focus on traditional Galician cooking and the typical flavours and ingredients (organic veal and chestnuts in season) of the Monterrei area, which the chef combines with a more contemporary approach. A standout dish here is the vanilla panna cotta with homemade caramel, made with almond milk, biscuit crumbs, macerated strawberries and fruits of the forest.

Name: Tramo
Description: One of those restaurants that flies the flag for sustainability, a commitment that is behind its decision to prioritise the recycling of materials and bioconstruction building methods. In this setting occupying one of the legendary concert rooms of the Movida Madrileña movement (the space was previously home to the El Garaje Hermético bar), its natural resources are put to effective commercial use through this socially inclusive project with an honest approach and a desire to help people who have difficulty accessing the jobs market. On the menu here you’ll find contemporary dishes prepared using ingredients from small-scale Spanish producers, farmers and local breeders.

Name: Kamikaze
Description: This unpretentious “taberna”, which takes its name from the Japanese word for “divine wine”, is run by two chefs who formed a close bond while working at Disfrutar (now a three-star Michelin restaurant) and went on to launch of their own joint project. Enric Buendia and Aristide Ribalta apply the techniques they have acquired in their quest for a creative approach that looks at Asian cooking (particularly Japanese) from a strong Mediterranean perspective. The end result is cuisine with surprising presentation and a nod to Catalan gastronomy. Choose between an à la carte that changes with the seasons and the Kamikaze tasting menu, available in two versions (short or long).

Name: Marmurio do Río
Description: A unique restaurant occupying the stone house that was once home to the century-old Casa Fandiño restaurant. Today, the name, which translates as the “murmur of the river” in Galician, pays a discreet tribute to the poem Dark Shadow by the renowned Galician poet Rosalía de Castro. The first thing that strikes you here is the meticulous, rustic-contemporary interior decor, which is almost an extension of the charm found in the streets of Allariz. Madrid-born chef Luis Moreno, who previously enjoyed success alongside fellow chef Daniel Ochoa at the Montia restaurant in San Lorenzo del Escorial, created this project in the town where he always spent his summers. Dining options are based around two tasting menus: one short option entitled “Río” and a second longer one called Marmurio. The chef works with small-scale producers from the locality and the Sierra de Madrid, and even uses lemons from his own lemon tree! Through his menus, he tries to draw comparisons with the tame and at times wilder characteristics of the local River Arnoia.

Name: MAE Barcelona
Address: Carrer de Sant Elíes 22, Barcelona, 08006, Spain
Description: This restaurant occupying the erstwhile Freixa Tradició features a designer-inspired interior and brings together the expertise and dreams of three friends (the name MAE is the Costa Rican Spanish word for “companion” or “colleague”): manager Mariella Rodríguez (from Costa Rica) and chefs Diego Mondragón (from Colombia) and Germán Espinosa (from Spain). The cuisine here is built around the concept of “syncretism” which can be described as the “combination of different theories, attitudes and opinions”. When applied to MAE’s cooking, this translates into a surprising fusion of ingredients from around the world showcased in dishes such as Galician clams or the legendary Tarta de Santiago paired with, for example, chilli peppers or tepache from Latin America. The à la carte is complemented by two impressive tasting menus (MAE and Gran MAE), featuring superb dishes such as “molluscs with dried cherry tomatoes, seaweed and yellow chilli peppers”.

Name: La Taverna del Clínic
Description: A family-run “taverna” featuring a profusion of wood, thoroughly contemporary comfort and two distinct sections: La Taverna and the restaurant itself. Here, the culinary focus is on traditional cooking based around seasonal ingredients, with a particular fondness for stews and great respect shown to time-honoured flavours, albeit from a modern perspective. The extensive à la carte is impressively complemented by various daily specials, with an enticing array of fish sourced from nearby auctions, and “large plate” options perfect for sharing. Several gastronomic menus are also available.

Name: La Oveja Negra
Description: With a name that translates as “the black sheep”, this gastronomic restaurant is gradually winning over a larger flock of clientele! The young couple at the helm, Rafa Bautista in the kitchen and María Vegue overseeing the dining room, put their life and soul into every sitting, serving modern dishes with a traditional flavour that showcase the ingredients and produce of the Somontano de Barbastro area but with a constant nod to the south of the country as a reminder of the chef’s roots. The constantly evolving à la carte, featuring “media ración” options, is complemented by a daily menu. We particularly enjoyed the “leche texturizada de Sieso” dessert, made with milk from the Villa Villera farm.

Name: Coto de Quevedo Origen
Address: Paraje Tejeras Viejas, Torre de Juan Abad, 13344, Spain
Description: Thanks to options such as loaves of candeal wheat flour bread baked in the town’s communal oven, delicious home-produced partridge pâté, comforting soups, and chickpea and bean stews, the dining in this restaurant is very much focused on everyday food, in contrast to its award-winning older sibling (Coto de Quevedo Evolución).
