The chef pays tribute to tradition with a patriotic line-up of no-nonsense Belgian classics, such as shrimp fritters, steak and fries and dame blanche (vanilla ice cream and hot chocolate sauce). The Brasserie de la Gare provides conclusive evidence that some things never change!

Name: Frenchette
Description: A bistro, but not only. Market-fresh, Frenchie fare, but not only! Don’t be misled by appearances. Contemporary textures and trendy ingredients add a modern twist to a line-up of dishes to share. The bar is perfect for a drink and a snack. To sum up, this is the perfect place to finish a day in the likable town of Ostend.

Name: Origine
Description: The whimsical décor of the Origine is depicted by colourful creatures and plants, setting the scene for a modern restaurant run by Xavier Lizen, who demonstrates great maturity despite his youth. The menu is renewed each month and illustrates the chef’s international and original approach, in which each flavour lives up to expectations.

Name: San Daniele
Description: In the Spinelli family since 1982, San Daniele enjoys a stellar reputation. Their unassuming restaurant in the shade of Koekelberg Basilica is the quintessence of Italian charm. Heart-warming dishes such as tagliolini with mushrooms, lamb and Taggiascha olives with a foie gras and lamb jus take pride of place. Chef Franco exalts traditional recipes by his skill and delicacy. The seabass in a salt crust filleted in front of you is guaranteed to lift your spirits. Stefano is near at hand with a wealth of insightful wine pairings.

Name: Cômo
Description: It is no coincidence that charming Renato Favaro named his restaurant after his birthplace. Inspired by his roots and genuine Mediterranean trattoria traditions, his lasagne alla bolognese and fettucine l ragù are to die for! A talented chef who works only with the very best produce.

Name: De Kruier
Description: This picture postcard restaurant stands in the shade of an 1897 windmill in a manicured garden. You can count on the Callant brothers to rustle up a delicious line-up of authentic Belgian dishes, calling on flawlessly fresh, deftly cooked ingredients. The extensive à la carte menu traverses the annals of traditional cuisine to the delight of good food lovers. In summertime, the alfresco terrace is the place to be.

Name: Cinq
Description: Do you want five reasons to book a table here? The pleasant decor, modern combination of ingredients, fresh produce, tasty recipes and extensive beer menu. So what are you waiting for?

Name: Bassud
Description: Bassud is the story of Michèlle and Jan, set in an attractive vintage Scandinavian décor. Chef Jan serves minimalist, no-nonsense dishes, using locally sourced produce and jazzed up by subtle twists, such as fermented ingredients or smoked charcoal oven flavours.

Name: Le Gril aux herbes
Description: Evan Triantopoulos is a champion of produce who avows a weakness for turbot and langoustine. Courtesy of consummate cooking techniques and modern side dishes, he underscores noble ingredients like sweetbread with a velvety creamy concoction of morels. Everything is made in house from scratch, from the freshly made nems to the dame blanche ice cream dessert. A counter seat is the best place to admire the chefs weave their magic in the kitchen. Stop off at the delicatessen, which offers a vast range of ready-cooked meals to take home!

Name: Tablàvins
Description: This wine-decked, book-lined eatery sports a trendy colour scheme that reeks of the Flemish flair for interior decorating. The wine-food pairing suggestions are equally inspired. The food in the zeitgeist sports a subtle blend of tradition and exoticism: you may taste a generous saddle of rabbit or a sole sprinkled in Asian flavours. A deep-rooted respect for heritage paired with a streak of daring.

Name: René
Address: place de la Résistance 14, Anderlecht, 1070, Belgium
Description: René takes us back to a time when life was simple. This former chippy, upgraded into a natty vintage bistro, shines the spotlight on down-to-earth Belgian classics. Mussels stuffed with parsley and garlic butter, rare steak with fresh béarnaise sauce and nourishing stews are all served with heaps of French fries. Huge helpings of searingly good food! What’s not to like?

Name: Colonel Louise
Description: Red meat lovers fall head over heels with this swish brasserie on a street corner near Avenue Louise. As soon as you cross the threshold, you are struck by the array of cured meats on the counter. You must then decide whether you want Aubrac, Wagyu or Holstein beef, before you dig into impeccably cooked steak flanked by fresh sauces and fries cooked in beef tallow as tradition demands. The menu also features a host of other delicacies ranging from bone marrow to vitello tonnato and crispy sweetbread. Perfect for a single dish, lunch or a full-blown dinner – what’s not to like?

Name: Brasserie Fiston
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fiston is a swanky brasserie depicted by a friendly, buzzy vibe. Chef Seynaeve rustles up text-book classics according to best practices. Geert Van Hecke’s pupil sources the best ingredients that he incorporates into home-made recipes. His shrimp fritters, turbot with a signature mousseline sauce and dame blanche dessert hit the spot every time. The suggestions reveal a more modern facet of the chef’s culinary score. Knock-out wine list!

Name: Brasserie Rongese
Description: This characterful eatery is established in a former cafe in Runskt, a district that was once called Rongese. The owner, Peter Merken, is always on hand with excellent wine and beer tips to pair with the wonderful array of wholesome fare chalked up on the slate. Juicy rare entrecote steak with piping hot fries and al dente veggies followed by a Belle Hélène pear with vanilla ice cream and smothered in hot chocolate sauce: you can’t get more traditional than this brasserie score.

Name: Fico
Description: At Fico, Nadia Bruno pays tribute to Sicily and her mamma, Grazziella. The cosy ambience and vibrant, vintage-inspired decor make for the perfect setting in which to savour her sun-drenched cooking. The chalkboard displays a tempting array of authentic dishes. Think al dente fettuccine elevated with sea urchin, an intensely flavoursome semifreddo made with grappa, honey and saffron. Here, bold flavours meet Italian finesse, with no room for pretension. Don't forget to make a reservation!

Name: Brasserie Grand Cru
Description: Chequered tablecloths, a rustic interior and traditional recipes, with a kitchen overlooking the spit roast fire. A heart - warming programme awaits diners, with classical dishes, such as veal kidneys and sole.

Name: Seir
Description: The sunny conservatory of this swish restaurant immediately catches the eye. The leather-seated lounge is ideal to sip a drink while admiring chef Thomas at work. An accomplished artist, he composes his visual masterpieces right on the counter. Intelligent combinations, precise and meticulous cooking. This youthful chef gives a free rein to his creative flair and is clearly determined to go places! A genuine treat for the senses.

Name: iOda
Address: Rue de la Victoire 23, Saint-Gilles, 1060, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: iOda defines itself as a vegetarian rotisserie. Rather than meat, expect vegetables and fruit without forgetting a few delicacies from the North Sea. Chef Hoed unveils his creative talents in dishes such as leek roasted on the rotisserie, shining the spotlight on small local producers whenever possible. Playful, delicate and gutsy – the seasons are reverently respected, allowing the ingredients to shout their name. The trendy, buzzy interior of vintage details and untreated materials is perfectly in tune with the hipster Saint Gilles district.

Name: Philema
Description: A gourmet festival of summertime flavours awaits you at Manos Makrygiannakis. The chef, who hails from Crete, shines the spotlight on ingredients that are steeped in Mediterranean spices and aromas. Authentic food based on top-quality produce (on sale at the shop). A friendly vibe depicts this establishment, ideal to share a delicate spanakopita, grilled cuttlefish and melt-in-the-mouth baklava with friends. A Greek feast!

Name: Leeuw
Description: Marble and black tables set the striking scene inside this splendid townhouse but lift your eyes – the ceiling is covered in mirrors! Chef Snykers, who whisks up dishes ranging from modern (set menu) to classical (à la carte), has a knack for sourcing top produce and a gift for creating punchy sauces. Now, it is up to you to taste the full range and nuances of his culinary flair and talent…

Name: Viticolo
Address: Rue du Bon Voisin 117, Oisquercq, 1480, Belgium
Description: A stopover in this red brick edifice on the outskirts of Oisquercq will whisk you off to Italy. The interior and the peaceful patio are both stylish and comfortably cosy. The produce is local, illustrated by the garden-fresh herbs coating the pluma iberico. Juicy octopus is enhanced and underscored by a sauce featuring the subtle acidity of cime di rapa. The pasta is naturally fresh and home-made in this restaurant, determined to uphold Italian traditions.

Name: Taverne du Passage
Address: Galerie de la Reine 30, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: This emblematic Art deco brasserie, which is housed in the exclusive Galerie du roi, just a stone’s throw from the iconic Grand Place, takes you back in time to the Roaring Twenties. Its vintage charm is enhanced by a host of elegant details like the golden origami birds. The equally nostalgic menu offers a splendid lineup of Belgian family favourites: crunchy shrimp fritters, sole meunière with fresh French fries, warm chocolate mousse with butterscotch ice cream. Living proof that tradition and generosity are timeless values!

Name: Ivresse
Description: The entrance to this trendy eatery is through a small grocery store, which boasts an impressive wine wall. Organic and natural wine fans cannot fail but find something to set their tastebuds tingling! The vibe is unsurprisingly laid-back, and you can eat at the counter. Recipes that hit the spot every time with a focus on sustainable, local and fresh produce. The stars of the show are undoubtedly vegetables and gutsy, full-bodied sauces.

Name: Black Smoke
Description: Black Smoke packs a distinctly American punch. The dimly lit, unpolished, rough and rugged interior is steeped in the smoky aroma of BBQ. The pitmasters have perfected the art of grilled meat in true Texan fashion. Traditional techniques, Latino influences and local produce for meals rich in big-boned, heart-warming flavours. Examples include lamb tacos jazzed up with a spicy za’atar, jalapeno pepper and fresh lemon. Or how about a cut of premium beef from the De Laet & Van Haver butcher’s shop? The drinks menu is practically as long as the food menu, while the ‘Bonanza Experience’ is billed as the ultimate sharing experience! So, let’s crank up the heat!

Name: La Rigue
Description: The legendary La Réserve Hotel boasts an equally swish brasserie within its walls: La Rigue. Lake Zegemeer, which can be seen from the handsome terrace, provides the backdrop for this sharp-edged, cosmopolitan eatery. Peter Goossens works with a team that meticulously adds a new spin to the Franco-Belgian culinary score. A subtle millefeuille and delicately acidic sabayon flank a rich, creamy vol-au-vent, while the crepe suzette is wickedly irresistible… Tailored, hand-crafted, high-flying cuisine for only 120 diners!

Name: Le Roi de Trèfle
Address: Avenue Baron Louis Huart 12, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: On the banks of the Meuse, Brigitte Dekoninck and Patrick Kleeblatt welcome diners to their characterful abode, which sports a lounge vibe oozing in charm. The veteran chef is a champion of classical fare and is all for allowing the diner to choose their own main ingredient and side dishes. His craftsmanship is showcased in melt-in-the-mouth foie gras or in the subtle vin jaune sauce that flanks crunchy sweetbread and cèpe mushrooms. Lovers of nostalgic nosh will fall in love with this King of Clubs.

Name: Atelier Dolce Amaro
Description: The younger sibling of Dolce Amaro is a friendly eatery overflowing in authentic Italian hospitality. The opposite of fussy and pretentious, the food is fresh, hits the spot every time and is served generously. Vitello tonnato de paccheri al ragu to start, followed by a lovingly and patiently simmered ossobuco, finishing with a semifreddo… The pinnacle of Italian simplicity!

Name: Bistro Berto
Description: Zulte-Waregem football club has hired a new striker! In the southern stand, David Bertolozzi hits the bullseye every time with his generous dishes. Start with a range of snacks to share, like generous nuggets of plaice dipped in tartare sauce, before digging into a modern version of classical recipes, such as pheasant with winter side dishes or a heart-warming vol-au-vent. Attractive lunchtime menu.

Name: Gioia
Description: Although the sound of traffic may be somewhat deafening outside, venture into this swish restaurant done up in tasteful light colours, taking a seat on the exquisite rear terrace when the weather is fine. The homemade pasta is out of this world! Rich flavours, fresh ingredients and Italy’s renowned “simplicity” are the hallmarks of this establishment. A new spin on familiar family favourites.

Name: Fortuin
Description: The huge vats of beer and the remarkable tree immediately catch the eye on entering the Staminée. Continue on into the elegant brasserie, where a trendy playlist and hip décor set the cosmopolitan scene. Veteran chef Stijn Rotthier puts his own spin on classical recipes. Examples include tender, juicy veal loaf with a melt-in-the-mouth millefeuille of potatoes and a madeira sauce subtly perfumed with truffle or a rich vol-au-vent in a hollandaise sauce steeped in spicy, fresh and acidic notes. Fortuin’s culinary signature can be summed up as punchy and authentic. Parents may be interested to know that children are welcome (special menu) and that there is a playground almost next-door to the restaurant.

Name: Modest
Description: "Modest" was the nickname Sander Spreeuwers was given at school. His elegant restaurant is intimate and the decor is contemporary in style. To the rear, you can see the vineyard in bloom. He is distinguished as a chef by his subtlety and finesse. A deep respect for classical French culinary tradition, an appreciation for vibrancy and a penchant for incorporating Asian seasonings underpin your dining experience here. For example, he delicately enhances turbot à la meunière and lobster with a light, whipped Béarnaise sauce and potato mousseline infused with green herb oil. This bold, spontaneous cuisine is a reflection of the chef's personality.

Name: Osteria Romana
Description: Don’t even try to resist the appeal of this Osteria Romana - you will be bowled over by the romantic allure of the mansion, the cocktail bar and the flawless tailored service. Roman specialties such as Roman-Jewish deep-fried artichoke and carbonara pasta whose subtlety, generosity and flavour are to die for! Proof that Italians do it better!

Name: Ukiyo
Description: The former presbytery of Stekene is a world in its own right, boasting a sleek, trendy cocktail bar, four luxurious guestrooms and a classy contemporary restaurant. Brothers Timothy and Bodi de Munck bend over backwards to pamper their guests. Their passion for Asia is reflected in both the extensive à la carte menu and in the beverages. Gallic flavours with subtle Japanese nuances. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally and are enhanced by a fascinating range of delicious sauces.

Name: Bink
Description: If you’re looking for good food in a romantic-cum-industrial bistro vibe, make a beeline for the former Brepols printing works, where an open kitchen sets the tone of the establishment. You can choose between a primarily classical menu or a more modern repertory, strewn with Asian influences. The seabass in a salt crust is emblematic of the knowhow of the chef, who enjoys surprising diners with winter side dishes and a tangy sauce jazzed up by Sichuan pepper over a fillet of venison.

Name: Grünewald Chef’s Table
Description: You cannot fail but remark the green marble counter that occupies the heart of this street corner building, appointed elegantly and tastefully. The chairs are positioned around the counter to better admire the chefs at work. Clovis Degrave and his team pour their creative talents into a set menu, rife with international accents, amusing textures and rugged sauces. An example: fillet of zander underscored by a caviar-flavoured beurre blanc and a velvety sauce of samphire and girolle mushrooms. A truly fascinating global experience.

Name: Jaco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: Jaco blends the well-heeled ambiance of Fort Jaco with a vintage interior dripping in contemporary elegance and luxury depicts the tiniest details. From Puglia, Francesco de Vita and Dario Trimigno recreate authentic Italian flavours using outstanding premium ingredients which they craft into unusual, attractive dishes. Don’t miss their version of vitello tonnato or a pistachio soufflé that is daringly paired with a bitter ice cream. Come early and sip a cocktail at the bar, before or after stocking up in the delicatessen store. Jaco is a culinary universe in a class of its own!

Name: Gusto Naturale
Description: Walk through the sleek grocery store (we recommend stopping off to make a few purchases as you leave) to take a seat in Marc Bernardi’s urban eatery. The chef, who hails from Bolzano, Italy, adds his own spin to authentic Italian dishes. For example, he might pair homemade tortellini stuffed with shredded beef and veal with a spot-on veal gravy. He has a knack for mixing powerful, rich flavours and his flair for vegetables and fresh textures is entirely in the zeitgeist.

Name: Bistro J.E.T.T.
Description: “Just enjoying time together” is the philosophy of this small, elegant eatery. Sarah supervises the dining room, while Dries can be seen in the open kitchen rustling up food to be shared with friends and family. Recipes that combine the classicism of Gallic tradition with exotic influences and a scattering of original ideas – convincing!

Name: Colonel Fort Jaco
Description: An offshoot of Colonel, a temple of red meat, this stylish brasserie sports a tasteful colour scheme that is the epitome of suave urbanity. Diners are invited to choose one of the juicy cuts of meat from the butcher’s counter near the open-plan kitchen. The knife-edge precision offered by the Josper charcoal oven, the exquisite flavour of the cured meats, the made-to-order sauces and the crispy fries are indeed admirable, but that is not all. Side by side this traditional Belgian lineup, you will also find dishes like carpaccio or filet américain, and more nostalgic dishes like their excellent vol-au-vent. We recommend a seat at the counter to make the most of the show in the kitchen.

Name: Stable
Description: Enter the stables of Hof Ter Linden and discover a mysterious world of cosy authenticity. The historic character of the edifice provides a perfect foil to the classy designer interior. The food also combines tradition and modernity in dishes that fascinate, strewn with international floral inspirations and creative touches.

Name: Blanco
Description: David and Celine describe Blanco as “highly Instagrammable” and the trendy interior definitely ticks all the boxes: fashionable, spacious and buzzy! After a refreshing cocktail, you will sample dishes of Mexican inspiration: flavoursome tacos, subtly spicy chipotle, home-made ajo blanco (white gazpacho) and fish from the North Sea. A genuine culinary adventure…

Name: le Vugo
Description: An excellent choice for a gourmet dining experience at outstanding value for money. A contemporary, relatively intimist interior provides the setting for up-to-the-minute cuisine. The chef plays with textures, whilst allowing the generous ingredient to shout its name loud and clear.

Name: Nonam
Description: Nestled in the heart of Ghent's Patershol neighbourhood, Nonam has an authentic and cosy ambience with a touch of vintage charm. After stretching out in one of the luxurious guestrooms, pop into the gastrobar, which, in the evening, serves an enticing range of dishes for sharing. In the restaurant, the set menu presents a playful take on fusion cuisine. The chef transforms his grandmother's rice pudding recipe, for instance, with exciting textures of apricot and a koji-based ice cream. Or he boldly combines beetroot, blue cheese and umeboshi. The selection of fine wines, by the bottle and by the glass, has plenty of gems in store.

Name: Markt XI
Description: Benny and Katrijn are full of ambition, which you will appreciate as soon as you step foot in their restaurant. The cheerful lady of the house greets and seats her guests, suggesting food and wine pairings. The chef specialises in modern cuisine, which is best described as fresh and subtle. You won’t be disappointed!

Name: Brabohoeve
Description: Brabohoeve is depicted by a smart, modern interior, ideal to sample a good meal. The classical recipes are crafted by an experienced team. Whether you opt for good quality meat or green eels, their culinary expertise can be tasted in each bite. Very appealing modern suggestions.

Name: Maison D
Description: The customer comes first in the elegant establishment of Delphine and Didier. Delphine’s vivacious personality depicts the front-of-house vibe, while Didier’s enthusiasm is contagious. The chef has a knack for adding a personal spin to fine produce and familiar flavours. He might add a playful edge to consummately crafted turbot, with different textures of parsley, all of which is enhanced by a spicy concoction of clams. The extensive menu embodies the establishment’s desire to pamper. First rate lunchtime menu.

Name: Commotie
Description: Commotie radiates a sense of Zen tranquillity. The verdant surroundings and minimalist Japanese decor create a harmonious whole. The terrace is an oasis of calm. But the arrival of the food interrupts your quiet contemplation. Chef Thomas expresses his originality through fermentation, vegetables, tart flavours, barbecue notes, intense sauces etc. His inventiveness is captivating, and his nose-to-tail vision is an inspiration. He imbues scallops, for instance, with a subtle smoky flavour, injects extra pep with an emulsion of whey and vin jaune, and adds salty nuances. Each plate tells a story, complemented by the wonderful picks of sommelier Lara, who has a penchant for natural wines.

Name: Alexandre
Description: This 18C doctor’s home, set in the picturesque village of Herzele and a well-kept secret among discerning foodies, is depicted by a snug interior, a superb terrace and Tamara’s attentive service. Tim Ritserveldt deploys his virtuoso culinary skills, rustling up set menus overflowing in creativity. Hearty, gutsy flavours are his hallmark, such as feta, watermelon sorbet and guacamole cream which enhance the character and depth of thinly sliced Duroc ham. Full-bodied, spot-on food that enjoys straying from conventional culinary paths.

Name: Huize Alberic
Description: From the ironwork and the restored fireplace to the wooden floors, the former home (1920s) of Alberic Plettinck, ironworker and artist, has been tastefully and respectfully refurbished in a stylish vein. After being welcomed by your gracious hostess, you will sample an updated version of classical recipes in which chef Bram demonstrates his flair for plating. His consummate craftsmanship shines through in the intense creamy gravy that flanks pheasant or in his modern spin on eels in sorrel.

Name: La Strada
Description: Contemporary restaurant faithful to Italy’s culinary heritage. Chef Pierro hails from Umbria and Tuscan cuisine has no secrets from him. His truffle recipes are standout. His son, Valentino, adds his youthful enthusiasm in the kitchen, while Myriame’s gracious welcome completes this family affair.

Name: L'Amandier
Description: Martin Volkaerts and his enthusiastic team have moved to this handsome bourgeois mansion, which sports a modern interior. Virtuoso chef Martin cooks to order and creativity dictates his culinary approach, depicted by exquisite sauces. Inspired by his garden, he crafts dishes that are exquisitely balanced between spicy and acidic notes.

Name: Rizoom
Description: (Temporarily closed) Jars of fermented veggies and the crackle of a charcoal fire – just a quick glance at this sharp-edged designer restaurant gives an idea of what you can expect. Chef Yves Kerckhoffs demonstrates his passion for produce and his weakness for Japanese flavours. For example, he may dry-mature duck or use koji to age it, and his quest for umami flavours is truly fascinating. Sauces and jus take centre stage, illustrated by a torrefied yeast-based sauce and a reduction of langoustine, which flank and embellish grilled gurnard (fish). The fine lineup of natural wines and sakes ensures that you will have no difficulty finding the perfect tipple to pair with your meal.

Name: Les Gribaumonts
Description: The façade of this restaurant is adorned in colourful frescoes, which also set the scene in the contemporary interior. The harmony between Nicolas’ inspired wine pairings and Lisa’s elegant culinary prowess is irresistible. The chef has a fondness for local ingredients, whose rich flavours are further enhanced by delicate touches and a consummate wine list.

Name: Cantine Copine
Description: The bare brick walls of Karen Keygnaert’s friendly restaurant bear witness to their industrial heritage. Diners are welcomed like old friends, invited to share dishes creatively rustled up with fine produce.

Name: Au Vieux Saint Martin
Address: place du Grand Sablon 38, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: The spirit of the arty, well-heeled Sablons neighbourhood is visible in the colourful artwork and even more so on the terrace of this buzzy brasserie. The menu offers a patriotic line-up of heartwarming Belgian specialties such as filet américain (steak tartare), vol-au-vent or brains with a gribiche sauce (boiled egg, mustard, herbs). If you take a peek at the larder, you will see just how fresh everything is in this culinary landmark of Brussels, as popular with the locals as with the tourists.

Name: Du Moulin
Description: The wood-burning fire in the cosy sitting room is the epitome of an Ardennes inn. This nostalgic charm is enhanced by the classical cooking of Jean Goire, who brooks no concessions. He pays tribute to his region, working closely with carefully selected suppliers. His culinary expertise unveils a deep-rooted respect and steadfast commitment to flavours that are gutsy, rustic and traditional to the core.

Name: De Cuylhoeve
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: De Cuylhoeve enjoys a truly magical setting in the heart of the Campine Forest, providing the perfect stage for this romantic restaurant. Start with a glass of bubbly from the impressive list of champagnes, before sampling chef Bart Janssens’ masterful know-how. He finds his inspiration in pedigree French recipes, to which he adds his own more modern spin, sharing his passion for first-class produce along the way.

Name: Les Brigittines Aux marches de la Chapelle
Address: place de la Chapelle 5, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: This Art nouveau brasserie is the epitome of “La Belle Époque” and it is impossible to resist either the décor or the mouth-watering recipes rustled up by chef Myny, a true-blue Brussels lad, whose exuberant personality pervades his knockout traditional nosh. From a vol-au-vent made with melt-in-the-mouth flaky pastry to a tender juicy chicken breast served with piping hot fries or veal cheeks with Cantillon beer, everything is delicious.

Name: Patyntje
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A meal in this elegant colonial-style villa is a must for any self-respecting food aficionado. A superb riverside terrace by the Lys, a bustling vibe and old-fashioned table service set the scene at Patyntje, without forgetting the extensive menu of Belgian brasserie favourites. Timeless classics such as eels in sorrel, vol-au-vent and carbonade flamande (stew) prepared with textbook skill and care. Don’t miss the sweetbread fritters – one of the Michelin inspectors’ favourites since time immemorial…

Name: Caffè Al Dente
Description: The smart, marble - decked interior of the Caffè Al Dente oozes with the warmth and authenticity of Italy. The chef knows his classics and works with top - rate produce. Equally fine wines. Pop next - door to the boutique when you finish your meal.

Name: In de Zon
Description: In de Zon is a haven for foodies and cycling enthusiasts (it is located in the heart of the Heuvelland region). The decor is filled with nostalgic finds from flea markets, which add a touch of charm. On a clear day, you can see all the way to France from the gorgeous terrace. This is a restaurant that is full of character and that showcases Flemish cuisine at its best. Crispy shrimp croquettes, herby paling in 't groen (eel in a green sauce) with fresh fries, succulent pork cheeks cooked in Saint Bernard beer: this heartwarming food leaves a lasting impression.

Name: Spaans Dak
Description: The view from this 16C manor house over Zoet Water is quite simply stunning and the modern wing, done up in designer-inspired vibe, also commands a splendid view. The food is modern and meticulously crafted in a bid to create succulent contrasts with the core ingredient. The three-course menu is one of the highlights of this splendid establishment.

Name: Rooselaer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: (Closed until the end of July 2024 due to renovation works) Lovers of traditional fare have been frequenting this elegant manor with its conservatory and alfresco terrace and garden since 1977. The chef’s generous, traditional fare has attracted a faithful crowd of regulars who appreciate both the set and à la carte menus, in which lobster and grilled meat take pride of place. The second generation is pursuing this classical heritage, albeit with the odd more modern touch, but ever true to its hallmark hearty flavours.

Name: Bistro Cuisine Kwizien
Description: This former village café has lost none of its yesteryear appeal, even though the draught beer taps and bar stools have given way to a warm modern interior, whose open-plan kitchen cannot fail but catch the eye. Steven crafts tasty dishes oozing with flavour, including a patriotic line-up of Belgian classics such as his own take on pear Belle Hélène. His partner Lies elegantly welcomes guests to the establishment.

Name: Numerus Clausus
Description: You don’t get to be a culinary benchmark by accident! Chef Steven and his sommelière Annelies have devoted themselves body and soul to make this restaurant a beacon of French cuisine in Lier. That said, they aren’t afraid of dusting the cobwebs off culinary traditions or adding a personal spin, such as mustard-flavoured ice cream served with steak tartare. The intelligently curated wine list is perfectly paired to the food.

Name: Bonheur Simple
Description: It is the little things that make us happy. Such as an attractive table setting in a contemporary restaurant, a peaceful atmosphere, and authentic Thai flavours in the creative cooking. Simplicity really is good.

Name: La Villa des Bégards
Description: François Piscitello has decorated his handsome villa tastefully and sparingly. The villa also boasts three guestrooms for overnight stays. A seasoned chef, Piscitello works with a set menu in which he crafts a finetuned balance between textbook French technique and Italian flair, together with the odd dash of creativity. For example, he flanks his breast of pigeon with a big-boned gravy, but he can also play with textures in a bid to jazz up a traditional risotto. The 100% Italian wine list further enhances this delicious culinary festival.

Name: Atelier de Bossimé
Description: Ludovic Vanackere’s converted this old farm in line with his sustainable vision. If the produce doesn’t come from his own impressive kitchen garden, which can be admired from the floor-to-ceiling windows, it is sourced locally. The surprise menu showcases the best of Namur and the region. Veggies take the limelight, prompting extra creativity in the winter season, illustrated by the chef’s work with different cabbage textures enhanced by a sauce packed in fermented veg, peanuts and sate-flavoured spices. Regional cooking founded on throbbing recipes and powerful sauces.

Name: La Belle Maraîchère
Description: Depuis 1973, les gourmets apprécient ce restaurant traditionnel où la famille Devreker choie ses hôtes. On y redécouvre le temps où Sainte Catherine était le quartier le plus prisé de Bruxelles pour les restaurants. Croquettes de crevettes, homard, gibier, sauces intenses et bien d’autres plats y sont préparés dans les règles de l’art. Pas de chichis, mais une cuisine chaleureuse et savoureuse.

Name: Le Bouchon et l'Assiette
Description: From the outside it is a small brick farmstead nestling in the green countryside, inside, however, diners are greeted by a surprisingly airy and contemporary décor. A family - run establishment that specialises in generous dishes with a dash of originality prepared on the spot. Fantastic wine list.

Name: Minerva
Description: Minerva was also the name of the legendary Belgian luxury car, the repair workshops of which were located here. The site is now that of a well-oiled restaurant, serving good quality, traditional fare. You might be interested to know that all the meat is sliced in front of you!

Name: Hispania
Description: Hispania is smart and contemporary, but down to earth, like the Spanish cooking it honours. On the menu are tapas and dishes created by a starred Spanish chef. The choice is varied and rich in Hispanic flavours, designed to transport you straight to southern Europe.

Name: La Buvette
Description: We wager that this restaurant will quickly become your favourite watering hole. The vintage interior of this former butcher’s shop oozes character and appeal, further enhanced by reasonably priced bistronomic fare. The single set menu overflows with elegant sauces and creative flair.

Name: 't Truffeltje
Description: ’t Truffeltje has enjoyed a stellar reputation ever since Pol and Greta first opened the restaurant back in 1988. Chef Marien demonstrates his mastery of French culinary technique, deploying his consummate know-how and choosing only the best produce. Subtle exotic influences add an occasional stylish twist.

Name: d'Artagnan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Epicureans will be delighted by the elegant, refined interior and charming rear terrace. Diners can choose between a classical or a more creative menu, both equally precise and flavoursome. Private parking by reservation.

Name: d'Oude Schuur
Description: Wine takes front stage in this pretty farmstead with a courtyard patio and warm lights twinkling indoors. In addition to adorning the walls, it is above all the passion with which the wine is served that sets the scene. Burgundy takes pride of place on the wine list, a genuine bible. The chef adds subtle, modern twists to traditional recipes, underscoring tuna tartare with Asian accents, for example, while the sole meunière is quite simply the summum of textbook perfection.

Name: Siphon
Description: Be it with sorrel, meunière or à la crème, people flock to this characterful restaurant from near and far to enjoy the house speciality, eel. They also offer grilled lobster and steak, as a quick look at their menu, an ode to tradition, will confirm. Siphon has become something of a culinary landmark in the region, further backed up by an intelligent wine list.

Name: De Stadt van Luijck
Description: The deluxe Renaissance interior of De Stadt van Luijck restaurant is a treat for the eyes: frescoes of angels on the ceiling, crystal chandeliers and an abundance of gilded fixtures and fittings, without forgetting the peaceful garden. Chef Pollice gives free rein to his Italian heritage and isn’t afraid to try out creative contrasts. He has a knack for embellishing familiar flavours with a luxurious, polished touch. His highly individual version of the Sicilian cassata tart is to die for!

Name: Laurel & Hardy
Description: In tribute to the legendary comic duo, the chef of this modern restaurant will no doubt bring a smile to your face, thanks to his delicious, well-planned, unfussy cuisine, focused on fresh produce. Fine, reasonably priced wine list.

Name: Pot au Feu
Description: Christine Van Deun has settled down in this lovely Art deco villa. Trendy interior with vintage details, inviting bar and conservatory overlooking the terrace - garden. The chef pampers our taste buds with comforting traditional recipes. The extensive menu makes choosing a conundrum!

Name: Messeyne
Description: The locals adore this cosy restaurant and its terrace in the adjacent gardens. The French cuisine is up - to - the - minute, full of flavour and unfussy.

Name: Njord
Description: Make a beeline for the top floor of the amazing ABC edifice and admire the jaw-dropping view over the port and marina below. Luxurious and trendy, the restaurant specialises in ultra-fresh delicacies straight from the local fish auction. Traditional, authentic flavours that respect the character and freshness of the ingredients. Slick service. The seafood platter is also available in individual portions.

Name: Wine in the City
Description: Walk through the wine shop, continuing on past the shelves of bottles and you will find yourself in the open-plan kitchen-cum-dining room of virtuoso chef Eddy Münster. He is never short of perceptive wine tips to pair with his deftly crafted culinary score. International influences, fresh modern acidity and amusing textures are combined in a menu that will set your tastebuds tingling with delight.

Name: Bar(t)-à-vin
Description: Authentic, polished and vintage – such is the vibe of this delightful bistro, quirkily established in a former butchery, as the colourful wall tiles and meat hooks bear witness. The concise menu is a guarantee of quality. Pedigree Gallic standards like steak tartare or less common dishes like a stew of girolle mushrooms, sea lavender and poached egg are crafted with text-book precision, blessedly free of fripperies and packed in punchy flavour. Ask Bart, a walking wine encyclopaedia, for his insightful tips to help you choose just the right tipple to pair with your meal. At the weekends, Bart Gils and Sally Lauwers run the joint, in line with its founding DNA.

Name: Food Emotions
Description: Food Emotions, whose interior is dominated by black and wood, is the epitome of designer chic with the bonus of a patio to the rear for sunny days. The chef throws his body and soul into his set and à la carte menus. For example, this creative maestro crafts a lamb dish using all the different parts of the animal and his dame blanche dessert is authenticity embodied! The plating is appetising and the sauces throb with flavour… Culinary emotions guaranteed!

Name: Brasserie Boulevard
Description: This swanky, spacious brasserie flooded in light is invariably packed to the seams. Thomas endeavours to ensure that your dining experience is as pleasant as it is flavoursome. Classic brasserie fare enhanced with a few spontaneous personal touches. The inspiring choice ranges from snacks to share, luxury vol-au-vent or trendier recipes….

Name: Les Terrasses de l'Our
Address: rue de la Lesse 1, Our, 6852, Belgium
Description: The opportunity to dine on the riverside terrace of this restaurant is not to be missed. Natural materials adorn the interior of this endearing brasserie, which is emblematic of the Ardennes, as is the food: game, trout, local ham prepared to textbook perfection… A daring new spin jazzes up familiar favourites, always with lashings of fresh flavour.

Name: Nonbe Daigaku
Description: If you like eating Japanese, you shouldn’t miss this modest venue. The very experienced chef has mastered the subtlety and nuances that are typical of the cuisine of his home country. You can see him at work behind the sushi bar, driven and precise, creating a delicious variety of flavours and textures.

Name: Maru
Description: This urban Korean eatery on the doorstep of the Châtelain district never fails to deliver. The locals flock here at lunchtime to polish off a main course or take their time over a more leisurely meal with a glass of wine. Pajeon is one of its star dishes: a crisp pancake filled with meat or fish flanked by a sweet vinaigrette and a spicy chili sauce. This dish symbolises the delicate balance between sweet, sour and spicy notes achieved by the chef, further underscored by a playful melody of varied textures. The epitome of authentic Korean nosh!

Name: Hostellerie De Biek
Description: We wager that before you even set foot in this family-run eatery, you will have fallen in love with the authentic Flemish village. The immense windows of the former brewery overlook the village and a sheltered terrace, while the striking interior sports timber rafters and brick walls. Before relaxing in one of the comfortable guestrooms, treat yourself to something from the extensive menu. Brabançon-style pheasant or bouchot mussels served in a spicy nduja and red curry sauce: the chef adds a kick to Belgian classics thanks to playful, creative inventions. A knockout lineup of regional produce.

Name: De Blauwe Artisjok
Description: Satisfied customers are the raison d’être of this stylish villa, where you are graciously greeted by Nathalie before taking a seat in the elegant dining room. Veteran chef Kurt Verhaege aims to work with fresh, seasonal produce. He boasts a classical training and his textbook perfect champagne sauce is a model of French culinary technique, as are his main courses and side dishes, which also feature a subtle international slant. Delicious eater-friendly prices.

Name: Jacob's
Description: A tasteful colourful scheme creates an elegant setting in this modern restaurant. Excellent choice of red meat, which is cooked to perfection in the wood - burning Josper oven. Heaven for meat lovers!

Name: La Fleur de Thym
Description: David et Olivia vous emportent dans une aventure ardennaise moderne. Les bois de cerf sont bien sûr au rendez-vous, mais dans un décor intime et élégant, aux accents colorés. La cuisine est résolument au goût du jour, surtout dans son exécution. Le chef David respecte les saveurs familières de ses produits, qu’il glorifie avec un grand savoir-faire.

Name: La Croustade
Description: Lovingly tended flowerbeds, a delightful cottage garden and goldfish in the pond - dining on the terrace of this exquisite country house is heavenly in fine weather. Every month, chef Thierry composes a new menu that demonstrates his classical training and know-how. He freely delves into the cottage garden to enhance dishes such as mint-crusted rack of lamb and pan-fried foie gras.

Name: Tanuki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Since 1989 Ivan Verhelle has been treating his diners to a genuine taste of Japan. The table service and interior are larger than life and the open - plan kitchen provides a bird’s eye view of the preparation of fine ingredients, such as fresh wasabi. The chef is a fan of teppanyaki cuisine and can even organise (bookings) a tea ceremony.

Name: Apriori
Description: Kristof Coppens lets his imagination run riot as he endeavours to source and exalt produce from all over the world, combining, enhancing and respecting each ingredient’s intrinsic qualities. For example, classical flavours find their way onto the menu, providing they can be paired with his creative recipes. The wine list is a treasure trove of tipples from Italy, Spain and France. A bijou eatery if ever there was!

Name: Bistro Rombaux
Description: Pieter-Jan Rombaux and his wife, Tineke, do everything themselves and the focus is clearly home-made. She nurtures the cheerful, unstuffy vibe, while he rustles up dishes that seek to enhance the ingredient’s pure flavours with perfect seasonings. Take a seat on the secluded terrace to admire the chef at work in the kitchen. Rather than gimmicky surprises, you can look forward to heart-warming dishes such as foie gras with brioche or hanger steak with a red-wine sauce to die for.

Name: Goesepitte 43
Description: Step into the picturesque Goezeputstraat 43 and be transported to a jungle paradise, complete with a living moss wall and monkeys! Chef Jan Supply likes to come to the table in person to serve his dishes. These are characterised by a deft use of the Mibrasa charcoal oven, rich sauces and intriguing vegetable creations. This is bistronomy with that little bit extra, as evidenced by the hand-whipped lobster béarnaise that elevates smoky filet pur to new heights. Be sure to try the crêpe normande, a house classic.

Name: Maison du Luxembourg
Description: A stone's throw from the EU Parliament, this contemporary establishment champions the bounty of Luxembourg's terroir. The restaurant draws an international crowd, who come to savour an array of culinary treats, frequently sourced from the province of Wallonia, including seasonal specialties such as asparagus and wild game. To suit the palate of the modern urban diner, traditional recipes are reworked with a light touch and a sprinkle of international flair, without sacrificing their core flavours. Smoked eel, for example, forms a winning combination with foie gras, a poached egg and subtly spicy rocket coulis.

Name: Pacht 26
Description: Stefaan, chef and sommelier, is an enthusiastic foodie and wine connoisseur. He regularly scours eastern Europe to enrich his wine list. The many regulars to his friendly, welcoming establishment applaud the wine formula which reveals the full scope of his creativity. Each dish is a consummate blend of character and delicacy with legible ingredients such as duck’s liver and beetroot, depicted in fresh, subtle nuances.

Name: L'Esprit Bouddha
Description: Light years from the clichés traditionally associated with Chinese restaurants, l’Esprit Bouddha is a modern establishment on a permanent quest for subtlety, but that hasn’t forgotten its roots for all that. Start your meal with beef gyoza, before digging into finger-licking tasty little house pancakes stuffed with crisp Peking duck, vegetables and a punchy hoisin sauce. The epitome of Asian generosity with an absolutely knockout wine list.

Name: Brasserie Bijgaarden
Description: This highly popular brasserie with a chic and discreet decor is a real institution. There is a wide variety of specialities on the à la carte menu at reasonable prices (attractive specials). Large terrace surrounded by greenery.

Name: Karel De Stoute
Description: Karel De Stoute is steeped in character, as you will see from the elegant décor of this edifice in the heart of the Patershol district, but also in the plate. Your charming hostess, Lien, is proud to present the menu of creative chef Thomas, who is as attentive to the flavour of his food as to its presentation. Fascinating, cheerful and delicious.

Name: De Mangerie
Description: Kristof Deprez is keen to share his love of Asia. As soon as you venture over the threshold of the Mangerie, it feels like you are on holiday. The chef rustles up local Belgian dishes with oriental influences, creating a finely balanced, tempting menu.

Name: Racines
Description: Leave the noisy Chaussée d'Ixelles and walk past the grocery counter into this delightfully vintage restaurant, which is awash in Mediterranean details and boasts an delightful terrace. Welcome to this authentic Italian establishment, where the chef will take you on a culinary journey from the north to the south of the Boot. Try the house-made tagliolini with parmesan and earthy cavolo nero, or the intensely flavoursome San Marzano tomato flan, drizzled with olive oil. The chef's creative and meticulous take on traditional recipes shines through. Featuring an impressive range of Italian labels, the wine list is well worth exploring.

Name: Lammekeshoeve
Description: The epitome of a swish, luxurious brasserie, this establishment also boasts an exquisite leafy patio for alfresco dining and a conservatory for summer vibes the rest of the year. The chef seamlessly skips from a traditional to a modern repertory, with one guideline: generosity. Whether you sample a fresh Mediterranean medley of haddock or dig into textbook perfect profiteroles, you can depend on each dish being as flavoursome as the next. Quality takes pride of place every time, also in the wine list.

Name: Ricciocapriccio
Description: This bistro is a popular spot for Belgian Italians, as evidenced by the amount of Italian that is spoken here. The chef, a fan of fine produce (sea urchins and squid are his specialties), deftly whisks up enticing dishes featuring carefully considered and, occasionally, unusual combinations. For instance, he prepares risotto with a sea bream tartare and parmesan foam, or puts a new spin on the classic tiramisu, but he always respects the essence of the dishes he prepares. The ample à la carte menu promises a Mediterranean feast!

Name: Amatsu
Description: Amatsu is perhaps the best Japanese eatery in Ghent. Authentic Japanese fare in a characteristic low-key interior. The teriyaki salmon with a subtle soy and sesame sauce unveils and highlights the chef’s skill and talent and for a close-up view of his high-flying dexterity, opt for a table in the first room to see him crafting sushis with less well-known fish. Fine selection of sakés. The lush green patio is heaven for alfresco dining.

Name: Silo's
Description: Silo’s is breathing life into the annex of the former malt house of Boortmeerbeek. The slick, well-oiled operations of this trendy luxury brasserie work like clockwork, seamlessly catering to large numbers of diners. The food is equally spot on, featuring updated versions of brasserie classics such as bouillabaisse and Clamart pigeon steeped in knockout flavours. Generous, voluntarily unfussy recipes that hit the nail on the head every time. The extensive menu and wine list, (including wines by the glass), ensures that there is something to tickle everyone’s fancy!

Name: Assiette Blanche
Description: The locals flock to this bistro, which appeals equally to socialites and a more casual crowd. The jovial mistress of the house and the subtle cooking of chef Timmerman further add to the establishment’s friendly vibe. Gutsy Gallic flavours are combined with vivacious Asian highlights, without forgetting local produce, in particular North Sea fish. Classical fare with a twist in the heart of picturesque Bruges.

Name: La Truffe Noire
Address: boulevard de la Cambre 12, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Black or white (truffle) is a frequent dilemma for diners in this upbeat, refurbished restaurant. Truffles are the pivotal ingredient of cuisine that seeks to showcase classical flavours. Beef carpaccio and raviolis with truffle are a few of the house specialties.

Name: Les Plats Canailles de la Bleue Maison
Address: rue du Pont d'Oye 7, Habay-la-Neuve, 6720, Belgium
Description: The picture postcard scene features a blue-shuttered gingerbread house poised between two rivers. The exquisite neo-rustic interior exudes a romantic vibe. Brice and Martin Thiry have added gusto and verve to this family business. They favour local produce and juggle with modern flavours such as acidity whilst respecting the ethos of traditional recipes. So, fancy sharing a rib of beef, carved in front of you, washed down with a glass of full-bodied wine? Good food and good vibes are the backbone of this endearing eatery.

Name: Boîte
Description: What a pity we don’t live down the road from this amusing "box"! “Taste the world, Share the food” is their baseline! The seasoned chef curates her own version of world cuisine, steeped in variety, harmony and exoticism… For example, deftly crafted spicy Lebanese toast, generous tajine, sweet and sour noodles, etc. Even better, diners can choose their own vegetable side dishes and are invited to share the main course with the rest of the table. Perfect for a casual dining experience!

Name: Cousteau
Description: Guy and Julie’s elegant establishment, flanked by a garden and a leafy alfresco area, is irresistible. Together, they run the show with brio, leaving no detail to chance from the service to the food. Chef Guy’s straightforward approach seeks to craft subtle, flavourful dishes with just a few painstakingly selected ingredients, illustrated by summertime tomatoes and burrata or a generous fillet of fresh fish served with a superlative beurre blanc.

Name: Stirwen
Description: Elegance and comfort depict this restaurant, a long-standing institution in the European district. François-Xavier Lambory takes a new look at textbook Gallic cuisine. He painstakingly sources his ingredients, assembling them into highly inspired, unusual recipes.

Name: Le Flore
Description: Le Flore is magnificently set in a restored farm-castle. The view over the meadows from the terrace is stunning. Chef Verlande rustles up enticing lunchtime fare and a varied menu, where the focus is on fine produce such as turbot, lobster and pigeon. Rich and generous are the hallmarks of his cuisine.

Name: Samouraï
Address: rue du Fossé aux Loups 28, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Samouraï is both minimalist and sleekly contemporary and yet this restaurant, tucked away in a nondescript shopping mall near Rue Neuve, has been a culinary landmark of Brussels since 1974. Razor-sharp precision and rich flavours embody the authentic Japanese cuisine, depicted by a varied menu of sushi and sashimi, together with table preparations like sukiyaki. The chef steams the shiitake with shrimp-flavoured pasta and then flanks it with a ginger and soy stock and with fried ciboule onion and shiso leaves, creating a harmony that is both subtle and distinctive. Popular lunchtime bento boxes; set menus in the evening as well as à la carte.

Name: De Oogappel
Description: This 1760’s edifice, graced in period floors and wardrobes, is now the venue of a friendly bistro serving traditional fare to the joy of discerning gourmets. The appetising menu of starters to share displays a more modern twist with Asian influences. We recommend the crispy sweetbread 'fine champagne' – the house signature dish. Go there your eyes closed.

Name: Wasserette
Description: The washing hanging from the ceiling is a reminder of the former laundromat that has morphed into a hip eatery firmly part of Nieuwpoort’s culinary scene. The menu features mouth-watering dishes served in small and large portions, flanked by a fine wine list. Unfussy recipes, often prepared à la minute, such as grilled brill with Belgian endive, velvety mash potatoes and a flavoursome shrimp sauce.

Name: Butcher's Dining
Description: The cosy restaurant of butcher shop De Laet & Van Haver is a veritable paradise for carnivores. Faced with such an array of delectable options, from Secreto 07 and entrecôtes of aged meat to traditional stews and offal, you'll be spoilt for choice. The carefully considered trimmings are a testament to the butcher's commitment to quality and craftsmanship. Think beautifully marbled cut of Simmental beef, simply seasoned with coarse salt and rosemary, and served with a tomato salad and a lightly whipped béarnaise sauce. What a feast!

Name: Julia
Description: A fishmonger (Mare Nostrum) at the head of a fish bistro, complete with a maritime interior, right down to the fish scales? It sounds so authentic that it just has to be true… Fish and oysters from the “sea to the fork” and the best shrimp fritters of the Belgian coast into the bargain. Julia’s simple, generous cooking is heaven for foodies.

Name: 't Kantientje
Description: Pille Senior and Junior work side by side in the kitchen of this elegant canteen in the picturesque village of Ramskapelle. In summertime, the terrace is very popular. The food is stripped back, handcrafted and traditional with a weakness for fish. Shrimp fritters, lobster belle vue and freshly prepared sabayon: delicate flavours that appeal time and time again. The fine wine list is fully in tune with this high-class establishment.

Name: Storm
Description: Storms do not prevent fishing boats from mooring in front of the door. The experienced chef pays them tribute with a host of delicacies, using modern techniques (including a passing nod to Asia and Scandinavia). However, relax, the cosy interior and cheerful staff will ensure you weather this storm in style.

Name: Mondieu
Description: OMG! Not only is the view over the polders from the terrace jaw-dropping, the bright interior of this former 17C cloister is equally appealing. Seasoned chef Ian Wittevrongel smoothly and seamlessly crafts first-class ingredients such as Steenvoorde pigeon and eel (he avows a weakness for local delicacies). All the no-nonsense dishes are à la carte and unveil his flair for gutsy, full-bodied flavours. The sommelier shares his knowledge and insights, guiding you through the stonking 400-reference wine bin!

Name: La Coupole
Description: La Coupole has been a blue - chip value since 1989. Diners enjoy the low - key, trendy atmosphere. The lobster and fish specialties are served by chef Bonnez’ brother, further proof of the establishment’s quality. Excellent wines.

Name: Saint-Christophe
Description: This handsome town house boasts a classical interior with high ceilings, a pastel brown colour scheme and a delightful terrace. The chef places great importance on the quality of his ingredients, which he incorporates into modern flavoursome recipes that are rich in character. We wholeheartedly recommend the formula and the all-inclusive menus.

Name: Bristol
Description: This bright, spacious brasserie on the seafront has been a landmark of Knokke-Heist for aeons. Expertly prepared Belgian classics are the specialities of the house. Think crispy shrimp croquettes (said to be the best around!) and pan-seared sole with a tartar sauce prepared à la minute. The chef loves working with North Sea fish, but also has a passion for meat dishes and seasonal specialties, such as hop shoots with mousseline sauce. These timeless brasserie classics are simply irresistible!

Name: Flavie's tafel
Description: Valérie's (Flavie) open kitchen takes centre stage in this pleasant restaurant adorned with colourful frescoes. The chef has a preference for fresh, carefully selected fish, as the tempting menu bears witness. A fine feast in store for your taste buds.

Name: Basile
Description: Basile De Wulf’s endearing restaurant is part of La Petite Campagne farm, which boasts both a butcher’s and a dairy. Established in a modern-day wooden chalet, the chef will introduce you to local produce (some from the farm) rich in gutsy, rustic flavours. After stints in a number of top establishments, Basile seeks to showcase fresh ingredients with an international twang. The chef’s surprise menu is tailored to today’s tastebuds and his passion for wine adds the final flourish to a fine meal.

Name: Bistro Le Nord
Description: Pop into this elegant bistro and sip an aperitif with a nibble at Bar 18, before sitting down to a more substantial dish. Dimitris Karagiannis rolls out Franco-Belgian family favourites enriched with subtle international influences such as dashi stock or a buttermilk sauce. Well-crafted, modern, even amusing food that lives up to its promises. Why not stay longer and book a night in the cosy B&B?

Name: Hertebos
Description: In Yasmine and Yoshi's living room-style restaurant, photographs on the walls give a glimpse into their past, and an open fireplace lends the place a cosy feel. In both the set menu and the repertoire of à la carte classics, the freshness of the ingredients stands out. The two chefs are as creative with textures as they are with their intensely flavoursome sauces. For instance, they bring out all the facets of raspberry and yoghurt, combined with a cake soaked in Amaretto, to create a dazzling dessert.

Name: Bistrot L'îlot
Description: A Parisian vibe mixed with industrial and minimalist details sets the welcoming scene. “What you see is what you get” is their motto! The chef intertwines international inspirations and punchy flavours as he orchestrates a mouth-watering score. He gives flawlessly steamed halibut a playful edge by flanking it with a range of mushroom textures and an expressive buttermilk crème. Rather than fussy frills, you can expect dishes in the zeitgeist and a splendid selection of (mainly French) wines.

Name: La Botte
Description: A meal at the establishment of charismatic Peppe and sommelier Gaspare Giacomazza, the second generation of the house, is a genuine feast. This unstuffy eatery, which serves authentic and original Sicilian fare, is depicted by a buzzy, easy-going vibe. The food is fresh, generous and supremely delicate. A fine tribute to Italy’s many delicacies, underscored by a handsome wine cellar, in which the quintessential Piedmontese Nebbiolo grape variety enjoys a star role.

Name: Essenz
Description: Stylish modernity paints the picture in this cosy eatery, both in the setting and the plate. Joris Hoefkens adds fresh, subtle touches to the patriotic Franco-Belgian line-up, with dishes such as marinated hamachi (yellowtail fish) served with an avocado ice cream or scorpion fish with a chlorophyl jus made with mussels. These and other delicacies embody Essenz’ culinary elegance.

Name: Aux Armes de Bruxelles
Description: This institution in the heart of historic Brussels immerses you in the Ilot Sacré district. Its traditional brasserie décor dripping in Art nouveau character and the table service in period costume are a hit every time. The varied menu is a compendium of Belgian favourites: eels in sorrel sauce or veal kidneys in mustard, served with piping hot crunchy fries, and finishing with decadent crêpes Comédie française (Grand Marnier liqueur plus vanilla ice cream) – scrumptious!

Name: Moma
Description: The view of the River Meuse and its lush green banks immediately catches the eye as you enter Moma. Olivier Bruckner reveals his flair for enhancing each dish with subtle details, like a sweet-sour tomato and rich creamy burrata which provide the perfect foil to lacquered calf sweetbread. The menu features classical and gastronomic recipes, all of which are enticingly displayed thanks to inspired plating and at gloriously eater-friendly prices.

Name: Nils
Description: Nils is the epitome of a modern restaurant. Tasteful, low - key interior, delightful staff and a talented chef, whose cooking is both creative and refined. The interplay of textures highlights the subtle varying flavours. A night at Carnac Hotel will round off the experience perfectly.

Name: Meteor
Description: Words such as “organic” and “local” are far more than trendy or faddish for Maarten Van Essche, starting with the lovely natural interior of this former presbytery. His à la carte menu keeps pace with the seasons: when the tomatoes are ripe, he mixes them into a gutsy sauce with nduja and spelt pasta. When it’s mushroom season, he whips up his own version of the nation’s comfort food: mushrooms on toast. In summer, don’t miss the bouchot mussel appetisers. Free of fussy frills, Meteor seeks to showcase pure flavours.

Name: Brasserie Daefnis
Description: It isn’t easy to nab a table in this luxury brasserie, which is always a sign of top-notch quality. Daefnis specialises in first-rate produce: North Sea sole, fillet of venison and premium Holstein beef are just a few of the delicacies that are showcased on the up-to-date brasserie menu. Familiar flavours are nonetheless respected, albeit with judicious nuances.

Name: Atelier Gist
Description: Fire and fermentation are key at Atelier Gist, a converted barn with floor-to-ceiling windows that afford views of the surrounding fields. Seated at a counter overlooking the open kitchen, diners can watch chef Jason work his magic at the barbecue and charcoal-fired oven. He elevates the robust barbecue flavours with bursts of citrus and Japanese seasonings. For instance, he grills venison fillet over the binchotan and then seasons it with koji. A rich beef jus made from the carcass, red cabbage and a delicate beetroot and fig cream bring out the inherent quality of these premium ingredients. The recommended natural wines and house-made kombucha takes this symphony of flavours to new heights.

Name: Plëss
Description: The opulent Plëss brasserie is just as elegant as the swish Place d’Armes Hotel in which it is housed. A quick glance at the menu will reveal that rotisserie and carvery dishes feature prominently in the classic lineup. The veal cutlet is grilled to perfection and flanked by a punchy gravy. You have the choice of side dishes, from Robuchon mashed potato to seasonal veggies, while other delicacies include foie gras in red wine and balsamic vinegar. The meat is carved at the table in traditional brasserie style. A mouth-watering "plëss-ure"!

Name: Domaine la Forêt
Description: This elegant, classical restaurant commands a stunning view over the Luxemburg Moselle valley. Chef, Claude Wallerich, concocts tasty dishes of traditional inspiration that will introduce you to delicious regional produce. The well - stocked wine cellar is an added bonus!

Name: La Rameaudière
Address: 10 rue de la Gare, Ellange, 5690, Luxembourg
Description: Daniel Rameau is a connoisseur of luxury produce, among which foie gras, lobster and pigeon, which he prepares refreshingly simply in dishes that blend generosity and tradition. The equally enticing wine list features a savvy selection of Luxemburg vintages. This former village train station and its flower-decked terrace are steeped in vintage charm.

Name: Bosque FeVi
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If your tastebuds start to tingle at the idea of biting into a “croquetas de jamón” and a “crema catalana” with a hint of citrus fruit, then book a table straight away in this exquisite restaurant, depicted by a striking “undulating” wooden wall-cum-artwork. Fernando Andreu conjures up a Mediterranean score with a dash of modernity by delving into his Spanish roots and the odd international influence like kimchi or tikka masala. If you’re in the mood for tapas, make a beeline for FeVi Gaudium, under the same roof of the Seven Hotel.

Name: Brasserie des Jardins
Description: If only we lived next-door to this modern brasserie… Slick, seamless service, a peaceful patio and a traditional lineup crafted by expert hands. The calf’s liver, cooked to perfection, is paired with a shallot sauce, the salmon, raw, cooked or smoked, glistens in an unusual starter, flanked by, among others, kiwi, mango and a coulis of red beetroot: the chef clearly knows his business. The knockout wine list further confirms the establishment’s commitment to fine produce.

Name: Octo
Description: This updated, new age brasserie is the work of a youthful chef and the trendy vibe and slick service are paired with traditional old-school cooking, albeit tailored to modern tastes. Rossini tournedos with a port-flavoured gravy, eel in sorrel and poached brill in a shrimp sauce. An establishment that never disappoints, all the more so as you can also pop in for just a drink or a snack.

Name: Cécile
Description: A pretty brick edifice in the heart of Pajottenland, wedged in between a church and a beauty parlour. This picture postcard image of Flanders sports a trendy, predominantly black and white interior and natural light. Sisters Judith and Astrid expertly manage the front of house, while chef Tom crafts fine cuisine, such as pheasant cooked whole with a fine champagne sauce. He enjoys jazzing up steak tartare with Asian notes, but is equally at home championing comforting family favourites.

Name: Ciao
Description: The 17C stately house on Poelaert Square belongs to TheMerode, a private club. Have no fear, though, everyone is welcome at Ciao. Our favourite in this edifice, oozing in character and elegance, was the dining room with a pretty bar. Authentic Italian flavours are treated to a sensitive modern makeover, illustrated by homemade tortellini with beef marinated in Chianti and a parmesan sauce subtly underscored by Campari. The chef avows a weakness for Tuscan recipes and delicately crafts succulent comfort food. Making your choice from the menu can be something of a challenge!

Name: Le Bouquet Garni
Description: Thin slices of scallops on a bed of fresh dressed crab followed by a tender fillet of veal admirably flanked by a beurre noisette sauce and a French apple tart that melts in the mouth – what a banquet! This romantic venue steeped in charm owes much of its success to its polished classical repertory. Blessedly free of fads and frills, Johan Félicès and his team pay a savvy tribute to traditional good food.

Name: Um Plateau
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Um Plateau is casual, smart and hip. Start with a glass of wine in the lively bar, before perusing the menu which offers a fine choice of dishes to share. Tataki, ceviche, gnocchi cacio e pepe, crunchy sweetbread… A traditional repertory that whisks you off on a culinary festival spanning the Mediterranean and Asia.

Name: La Maison Lefèvre
Description: L’élégance de la façade de cette maison de maître se confirme à l’intérieur, avec la splendeur de ses grands lustres. Un vaste établissement où l’on trouve pourtant aussi une belle intimité. Les cuissons traditionnelles se parent de touches de modernité riches en contrastes. Le chef aime travailler les légumes avec créativité, ce qui donne à chaque assiette une touche bien personnelle.

Name: Mathes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Today, the third generation of the family captains this lively restaurant, where the artwork adorning the walls cultivates a refined atmosphere. Try your best to snag a table with a view of the Moselle River, or one on the terrace. Foodies have flocked to Mathes for its classic cuisine since 1949, although it has moved with the times beautifully. The undisputed star of the menu is still the pike perch – oven-baked and finished with a delicate Riesling sauce. With an impressive array of Luxembourg wines on offer, this family restaurant cements its place as a highly-regarded establishment.

Name: Bick Stuff
Description: A family-run establishment where you will instantly feel at home. Bick is a local word which literally means ‘beak’ in English but loosely translates as ‘food’. Owners Virginie and Denis Laissy have the same goal: to serve good food in a relaxed atmosphere. Chef Denis rustles up reassuringly classical recipes, adding his own distinctive touch. We recommend the set menu.

Name: De Kwizien
Description: Food loving Hasselt is delighted to have this newcomer. Luc Bellings’ former right hand man creates cuisine with well - balanced flavours and well - prepared ingredients. The dishes are modern but inspired by tradition.

Name: OiO
Description: The pasta is prepared last minute, stuffed with a powerful ossobuco and then coated in a velvety parmesan and gremolata sauce. All the ingredients on the menu are as fresh as the homemade pasta. This fantastic Mediterranean osteria which boasts an exquisite riverside terrace on the banks of the Alzette, invites you to an Italian feast of great delicacy. Don’t miss the Negroni or the dessert trolley!

Name: Un Altro Mondo
Address: Courte Rue du Rivage 1, Wavre, 1300, Belgium
Description: Quirkily tucked away behind shops, this Altro Mondo acquaints you with the highly personal vision of Luca and Caroline. Italian influences dominate the menu, such as Tagliani in truffles in a powerful gutsy sauce. You can also expect a line-up of more modern dishes that reflect the character of the enthusiastic, charismatic sommelier.

Name: Villared
Description: Pink flamingos adorn the wallpaper, green marble abounds and gold and ochre depict the colour scheme. Elegant and fashionable, Villared provides the perfect foil to chef Debal’s eclectic score. Melanzane alla parmigiana, sole meunière, Asian-inspired salmon… The enticing menu by a seasoned craftsman has something for everyone.

Name: Didier Galet
Address: rue du Grand Bru 27, Sprimont, 4140, Belgium
Description: Before you even sit down in this friendly joint done up in an inviting vein, you feel perfectly at home. Christine greets diners with a smile and chef Didier Galet waves a hi from the kitchen. Galet is a champion of his region and committed to working with local ingredients. From wood pigeon to fresh veggies, the chef sources everything locally, crafting each ingredient with infinite respect. His cooking draws on his classical training, jazzed up with expressive sauces. He is equally capable of rolling out a rich mushroom and truffle stock, a light frothy espuma of potatoes or a liberal grating of royal truffle. The alfresco terrace is perfect to sample this ode to Belgian produce and producers.

Name: Delys
Description: Delys is a haven of design in the rural landscape of Verlaine. A black and gold colour scheme provides the backdrop for quick lunches and more leisurely dinners. The modern chef likes pronounced flavours. Legible, familiar food, with the occasional subtle detail, that makes ample use of the excellent local produce.

Name: Bacon
Description: Your host, an enthusiastic disciple of natural and organic wines, used to be a butcher in a former life. In the company of his wife, they have embarked on a new adventure in the shape of a cosy, trendy restaurant. She woos diners with market-fresh cuisine, jazzed up with international seasonings and brimming with flavour in dishes – with or without meat!

Name: Le P'tit Gaby
Address: rue de la Croix Blanche 8a, Thisnes, 4280, Belgium
Description: The bright modern interior of the P’tit Gaby is now located in the heart of the Liege countryside, following a happy change of venue. The hostess’s greeting is as warm as ever, while chef Leruth’s cooking has acquired added creativity. Each dish is faultlessly thought out, meticulously prepared and sometimes inspired by exotic influences.

Name: Un temps pour Soi
Description: The countryside around Villers-le-Bouillet is ideal for a weekend getaway and what could be better than this elegant stone building and its romantic patio? The seasoned chef rustles up appetising food, sprinkled with crunchy, spicy, incisive and acidic notes. In a word: the epitome of market-fresh, wholesome cooking.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: You will instantly feel at home in this minimalist venture, two steps from the French border and founded by self-taught chefs, Slava and Antoine. The irresistible duo bowls us over - his passion and food-wine pairings and her delicate culinary flair and generous helpings. Slava’s meticulous attention to detail results in balanced dishes that combine fresh, acidic, spicy and many other subtle flavours. The ingredient takes pride of place in each carefully thought-out dish, whether it be asparagus that is enhanced in a ceviche, or lamb fillets underscored by an emulsion of beer and meat juices.

Name: Vonk
Description: Stijn and chef Bart are the fifth generation of the Hoonaert family, whose DNA is rooted in culinary excellence! The conservatory of the former café, planted with trees, is now a cosy gastrobar. A charcoal Mibrasa oven adds a distinctive flavour to market-fresh recipes, made with meticulously chosen ingredients (simple lunchtime menu, more varied in the evening).

Name: Cuichine
Description: House-made Peking duck with crispy skin, fresh veggies and pancakes ready to be stuffed, all of which flanked by a gutsy sweet and sour hoisin sauce. This signature dish embodies the philosophy of Cuichine: a modern version of old-school Chinese nosh, starring all our favourite Cantonese recipes. The interior of this eye-catching establishment is ideally suited to the trendy vibe and the restaurant also boasts a pleasant terrace.

Name: VAS
Description: Let’s start with a lesson in the local dialect: “vas” means “fresh”, which encapsulates the ethos of this eatery that shines the spotlight on local produce. Right from the appetisers, the chef deftly adds trendy touches to punchy Franco-Belgian fare. Examples include preserved lime syrup whipped into a beurre blanc which enhances the subtle delicate flavour of turbot. The sommelier’s powerful and mineral wine combinations further underscore the elegant culinary score. Al fresco dining in the covered courtyard with a pretty view – aperitifs are served in the lounge.

Name: L'Atelier Cuisine
Address: voie de l'Air Pur 207, Beaufays, 4052, Belgium
Description: As you set foot in this striking Art deco edifice reminiscent of the 1930s and make your way over a carpet of flowers, you will immediately feel at home. The new venue of L’Atelier Cuisine is a gem! Homemade fare and fresh produce are the name of the game. The patriotic line-up of French and Italian classics has no secrets for the chef who crafts knockout nosh, sprinkled with Mediterranean influences. A bite of the veal escalope alla Milanese will transport you straight to a sunny Northern Italy.

Name: Resto Wald
Description: Lisa and Walter - Wald - are keen to maintain the “Small is beautiful” ethic of their hip eatery, which adds to the home-from-home vibe. Whenever possible, the dedicated chef prepares everything himself using ingredients from the Low Countries. He draws his inspiration from his many overseas trips and enjoys mixing surprising flavours. You can expect a flavourful meal with a modern spin in a cosy setting.

Name: Brasserie Juste
Description: Back-to-basics brasserie cuisine, fresh ingredients and a chef who adds his own personal touch. “Juste” what it takes to satisfy good food lovers. Even better, the chef is a fan of wood fired Josper ovens. Hand chopped beef tartare with crunchy fries, hearty helpings of vol-au-vent and a made-to-order dame blanche with vanilla ice cream and smothered in chocolate sauce: every dish is a model of culinary generosity. A suitably tasteful trendy interior and an alfresco area overlooking the fields and the vegetable garden.

Name: Gus
Description: Pierre Baeyens and Jonathan Delhière acquaint you with the “brassonomy” concept (beer meets gastronomy) in their cosy brasserie.
