They skilfully incorporate the many flavours of artisan beer and hops into a Franco-Belgian line-up, in the glass and also in the subtle food. A foamy beer mousseline nestles up to a soft-poached egg and mushrooms or steak is smoked in hops: the chefs add an individual touch to creative recipes. A bubbling Brussels brasserie-cum-brewery!

Name: Fou du Goût
Description: Fou du Goût manages to be both chic and cosy, with the beautiful glass conservatory being the best spot in the house. Thomas Cocquyt has a penchant for giving familiar flavours an exotic twist – chicken cooked in a spicy masala sauce, or pan-fried plaice with smoked eel and a beurre blanc infused with a yuzu gel for a burst of citrus brightness. This chef is a master of balancing bold flavours with a touch of intrigue. A perennial favourite in the Meetjesland region!

Name: De Mayeur - Patrick Vandecasserie
Description: Fancy a good, traditional meal? Patrick Vandecasserie’s villa is right up your street. The chef has no equal when it comes to finding premium produce that he prepares classically. His game recipes are exquisite! Fine establishment.

Name: San Sablon
Description: San Sablon features a welcoming natural decor in the smart Sablon district, albeit with a trendy, suave twist. Rather than plates, forks and knives, you will eat out of bowls with spoons – all the better to do justice to original recipes that keep pace with the seasons. The main ingredient is enhanced by gutsy vegetable side dishes that illuminate each meal.

Name: Cuisinez-Nous
Address: rue de la Gare 138, Bertrix, 6880, Belgium
Description: In this tasteful townhouse, Alain and Céline further confirm their excellent reputation acquired at the Rosa restaurant. Céline caters to diners’ every whim in the dining room, while Alain deploys his talents in a traditional French repertory.

Name: Tafel 10
Description: A black and white tiled floor and an open fire set the scene in this plush bourgeois 19C home, but the comfort is entirely 21C, as is the splendid terrace to the rear. The à la carte menu offers a choice of beautifully crafted classics made with first-class ingredients and flanked by powerful sauces, while the set menu is more playful and international in spirit.

Name: Roots
Description: A hip bistronomic offering in the heart of the buzzy Patershol district. The establishment’s popularity has nothing to do with luck and everything to do with Kim Devisschere’s uninhibited, no-holds barred cooking, doubled with a commitment to organic, locally sourced ingredients. Be it local meat, North Sea fish or fresh vegetables, each dish fascinates and intrigues. Splendid wine list (excellent natural wines) and pleasant alfresco area in fine weather.

Name: Rascasse
Description: Erwin Denijs is a genuine ambassador of his region, the North Sea and Oosterschelde River. This “North Sea Chef” crafts the best seasonal produce into dishes that combine a tangy freshness with a playful element. For example, beurre blanc flanks a skate wing cooked in butter and paired with mussels and a medley of leeks. Caroline, your cheerful hostess, will ply you with wine, as well as beer tips, all of which in a pared-back setting that provides the perfect foil for striking works of art, starring fish!

Name: Cocotte
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Authentic details, such as stained - glass windows, happily rub shoulders with modern furnishings in this hip, lounge - inspired restaurant. The ambience is warm and welcoming and the chef cooks modern, often creative dishes.

Name: Al Piccolo
Description: Karina et Guiseppe ont plus de trente ans d’expérience, vous ne manquerez pas de le remarquer. Leur sympathique restaurant est connu pour ses saveurs authentiques et généreuses. Le soin qu’ils y apportent transparaît dans les détails. Taglioni à la truffe noire, fazzoletti avec porcini et foie gras… Sans oublier la séduisante carte des vins !

Name: Bachtekerke
Description: Bachtekerke is undeniably smart, but its pride and joy is its fantastic summer terrace on the banks of the Leie, protected by large parasols and enclosed by drift wood fencing – you will almost feel like you are on an island! The chef has no equal for generous cuisine, rich in flavour and variety. A hit with foodies of all sorts.

Name: Maison Belge
Description: A subtle sprinkling of vintage details lends this modern brasserie a pleasant homely feel; the terrace is delightful. The chef specialises in traditional, Belgian in particular, classics, to which she adds her own light, fresh hallmark signature.

Name: Ploegmans
Description: As you enter this former café, you will find yourself immersed in the working class ambience of the Marolles district. Everything from the decor to the menu is steeped in local traditions. Cheese croquettes, steak and chips or vol-au-vent – scrumptious!

Name: Brasserie de l'Expo
Address: avenue Houba de Strooper 188, Brussels, 1020, Belgium
Description: If you’re looking for a characteristic Brussels brasserie, take a seat on the lovely terrace or in the dining room, whose red colour scheme is dotted with Art deco and 1958 Expo details. Slick service by waiters in bow ties. The patriotic line-up of Belgian classics includes cheese fritters, américain (beef tartare in lashings of mayo) and French fries, oysters and mussels in season. The epitome of generosity!

Name: KAN10
Description: “Original”, “captivating”, “adventurous” and “regional” sum up the ethos of this cosy urban eatery. As a result, you can expect to sample a mind-blowing range of flavours and savours. Asian flair depicts the semi-cooked salmon, underscored by excellent homemade sambal and flanked by a traditional beurre noisette… A culinary banquet! Ask the lady of the house to show you the popular menu of shared dishes and get ready to embark on an exciting voyage of international flavours in a casual vibe.

Name: La Bottega
Description: The best Italian restaurant of Eupen is on Gospertstraße. Traditional pizza, succulent lasagne and yummy Gamberoni prawn and pasta. The kitchen team combines generosity and wholehearted authenticity, without forgetting the odd, unorthodox twist. The delicatessen counter is a great success.

Name: Céma Passion
Description: The menu features modern French cuisine, which is rich in enthusiasm and sophistication. Seasonal produce takes pride of place on the inventive menu. A genuine culinary experience.

Name: BÚN
Description: Leave the madding crowd far behind and relax in the hip casual vibe of this trendy Vietnamese eatery. You can expect to sample a fine dining version of characteristic Vietnamese sweet and sour, fermented and spicy flavours. The chef favours local organic produce, an ethos that is reflected in the attractive wine list, rich in natural vintages. The Little Bún noodle shop rustles up gutsy, full-bodied Vietnamese street food.

Name: Convento Wijnbistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Pick out a bottle from the wine shop, take a seat in the pleasant bistro-lounge and get ready to soak up the communicative enthusiasm of Convento. The sommeliers get a real kick out of explaining the wines, hence the low corkage fee. The straightforward, market-fresh menu is perfectly matched to the establishment’s stripped-back concept and stars a fine selection of veggies and authentic flavours.

Name: Het Moment
Description: One invariably succumbs to the appeal of the elegant family home of chef Nicolas. Diners can choose between modern and classical dishes, safe in the knowledge that fine produce takes centre stage.

Name: L'air des Sens
Description: Snug, pared-back and arty – the interior of this historic 1900 edifice is equally as fascinating as David Schulz’ fine cuisine. Veggies, herbs and seasonings form the backbone of his cooking. Almost everything is prepared from scratch and many of the recipes star local meat or North Sea seafood. He works hand in hand with the seasons, adding a creative spin, unexpected twists and exciting new techniques. A keen interest in Dutch wines adds the final flourish to this enticing portrait.

Name: Le Zinc
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Don’t say we didn’t warn you: after a meal or a night in this lovely inn, you will just want to return, again and again. A lush verdant setting steeped in tranquillity sets the scene on the terrace, while regularly changing photo or art exhibitions immediately catch the eye indoors. The chef, a past master of pure-bred classical cuisine, reverently respects the seasons and pays tribute to top local producers. Le Zinc is the quintessence of authentic and friendly.

Name: La Gloriette
Description: This masterfully revamped townhouse enjoys an authentic, contemporary setting. The chef proposes dishes that suit contemporary taste buds, particularly with creative appetisers. His culinary score is personal, varied, often amusing, but always seeks to enhance the intensity of the flavours.

Name: 't Sleutelgat
Description: The daughter Laetitia warmly welcomes guests to this family business, whose terrace overlooks the lush green countryside of the village of Lieferinge. Dad, mijnheer Van Holder, demonstrates his technical precision and eye for detail in dishes served in several plates. From a new spin on traditional flammkuchen to veal jazzed up with a punchy medley of international accents, the food is surprisingly complex and fascinating. Don’t forget to book!

Name: Henri
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This laid-back bistro perfectly embodies the hip, urban vibe of Brussels’ Rue de Flandres and we warrant you will fall in love with its casual ambience, cobbled terrace and splendid choice of wines and Brussels’ beers. The dishes are free of frills, all the better to allow the ingredients to take front stage. Mussels in a pastis-flavoured sauce, beef tartare with a Thai slant or text-book perfect sole meunière: the chef enthusiastically navigates between influences with a fondness for fresh Mediterranean fare. Fine dining with a Brussels’ signature!

Name: Les Caprices d'Harmony
Description: If only there were more little neighbourhood hangouts like this one! The owner chef has voluntarily eschewed modes and trends and his traditional menu is music to our ears (and tastebuds): hanger steak with shallots or dame blanche dessert (vanilla ice cream and hot chocolate). Simple, home cooking, prepared to order – at prices that make sense.

Name: Le Passage
Address: avenue Jean et Pierre Carsoel 17, Uccle, 1180, Belgium
Description: This establishment and its lunchtime set menu are a favourite with the locals, such is chef Rocky Renaud’s reputation for creativity and flair, mingling tradition with modernity. Distinctive food with bold international accents!

Name: Lola
Address: place du Grand Sablon 33, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: The fact that this inviting red and white brasserie has been a firm fixture of the swanky Sablon district since 1994 owes nothing to chance. Whether it’s a quick lunch at the bar or more elaborate fare in the dining room, the service is first class. Classic brasserie fare such as lobster ravioli, an unusual sweetbread vol-au-vent or melt-in-the-mouth Holstein steak and fries, all of which prepared with textbook skill. The chef adds a modern twist, focusing on generosity rather than fussy frills.

Name: L'Écailler du Palais Royal
Description: L'Écailler is a Brussels institution. The turquoise tiles behind the long bar, the wonderful woodwork, the gorgeous carpets and the nostalgic charm of this building make for an irresistibly inviting setting. A champion of classic cuisine, the chef excels in preparing fish and seafood dishes, but during the hunting season, his game specialities are also not to be missed. Briny oysters, the aromatic bouillabaisse, his inimitable sole meunière… Fans of traditional fare will feel right at home.

Name: Ferrier 30
Description: The stylish Ferrier 30 will immerse you in the buzzy, hipster vibe of the Zuid. The terrace opposite the Fine Arts Museum attracts diners like bees to honey in fine weather. The venue is ideally suited to the text-book perfect classical Italian recipes. Truffle-flavoured home-made pasta, slowly braised ossobuco… An explosion of Italian aromas and flavours!

Name: Baarle 90
Description: A meal at Baarle 90, which boasts an idyllic view of the River Leie, is the opportunity for a fine dining experience. The terrace is out of this world and the interior pleasantly trendy. European recipes tinged with Belgian influences, such as shrimp fritters, steak tartare and sole prepared with textbook expertise.

Name: De Fakkels
Description: Seppe Bleus and Liese Bams have taken over the business and welcome you to De Fakkels 2.0. They have kept its soul intact, so the imposing building still exudes warmth and a sense of romance. Goose feather lampshades, designer lighting and wooden ornaments make for a unique setting. In a bid to keep up with the times, the menu features exciting new combinations, such as the bright and zesty interplay of calamansi and orange with ultra-fresh scallops. The depth of his sauces, like the rich game sauce that graces the venison fillet, is testament to the chef's culinary mastery. This long-established haven for foodies is in good hands.

Name: Den Silveren Harynck
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A mother and son team (Els and Sam) welcome guests into the stylishly elegant Van Landeghem family establishment. Floor to ceiling windows lead into the garden which is flanked by a patio. Dad, Luc, can be found rustling up tasty, flavourful delicacies in the kitchen, combining classical training and creative touches, ranging from Rossini tournedos steak to a bouillabaisse jazzed up with subtle, Asian notes.

Name: Royal H.-Bonhomme
Address: rue de la Reffe 26, Remouchamps, 4920, Belgium
Description: This comforting inn is emblematic of the Ardennes countryside and of its history. Eight generations of Daussaint innkeepers have been at its helm since 1768! A wrought-iron pergola provides the romantic setting for a dinner for two featuring classical French fare: fried trout, lobster from the lobster tank, tournedos of venison… Delicious!

Name: Bistro Tribunal
Description: Have you ever heard of a meat sommelier? Well, in this traditional bistro, one such will help you make your choice among the fine cuts of meat supplied by the prestigious Rondou butchers. A refrigerated meat display counter and a lobster tank catch the eye. Rather than prissy, complex preparations, you can expect spot-on cooking, freshly prepared sauces and regular refills of hot, crunchy French fries. The wine list (splendid selection of Bordeaux wines) is at bargain prices.

Name: Zarza
Description: Zarza, an authentic cosy bolthole with a pretty town garden, is the type of place that inspires loyalty. Chef Cordemans pampers his diners with flawlessly sourced ingredients. The patriotic line-up of Belgian fare is jazzed up by the occasional dash of creativity, illustrated by masterfully cooked langoustine, paired with a gutsy shellfish jus and crunchy courgettes. Sophisticated yet full-bodied flavours. The lunchtime menus are always a safe bet!

Name: La Bru'sserie
Address: rue du Comte Théodule d'Ursel 14, Durbuy, 6940, Belgium
Description: In this trendy joint, Wout Bru takes your taste buds on a whirlwind trip around the world. The extensive menu features dishes from Provence, Asia and Latin America without forgetting Belgium. The mouth - watering choice fully lives up to its promise of intense and subtle savours!

Name: Kokovin
Description: Warm and stylish, Kokovin boasts a superb garden patio, but above all, it is the scene of a successful family adventure. The cheerful lady of the house, Peggy, greets guests warmly, plying them with insightful wine tips along the way, while her hubbie, Dominique, and son, Francis, conjure up recipes that range from modern to classical. In addition to textbook prepared sole, you may sample generous shrimp fritters that melt in the mouth and duckling served with piping hot fries, together with a host of more unusual textures. Consider us smitten!

Name: Bistronoom
Description: Bistronoom is an elegant Normandy-inspired villa in the heart of the Flemish Ardennes. The appetising repertory, as authentic and convincing as ever, is in the capable hands of Bernard and his son Henri. The recipes delve into familiar Flemish and French traditions and generously keep pace with the seasons. Choosing is excruciating!

Name: Lesco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The authentic décor of this handsome town house is perfectly paired with modern comforts. Wooden floors, elegant mirrors and a trendy vibe. The lovely terrace in the garden is equally enchanting. The surprise menu reflects the creative talents and playful streak of the chefs.

Name: Wilford T
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The industrial sobriety of Wilford T contrasts with the works of art in the Wilford X exhibition gallery next-door. Meals are served in this arty establishment steeped in serenity, which provides the perfect foil to the exceptionally pure flavours. Chef Vermeiren, who doesn’t hesitate to add the finishing touch right in front of diners, is committed to highlighting the ingredient with unusual combinations. Sometimes complex, always flavoursome.

Name: Auberge de la Roseraie
Address: route de la Marache 4, Ohain, 1380, Belgium
Description: The inhabitants of well-heeled Ohain have adopted this 19C farmstead that is a bastion of French cooking served in a relaxed atmosphere. Rather than surprises, you can expect to sample deftly executed recipes by a chef who combines his deep-seated understanding of ingredients with subtle sauces. An example: juicy quail with a crispy skin, lightly seared veal sweetbread and a honey-flavoured jus. Nostalgic flavours of yesteryear!

Name: Dôme Sur Mer
Description: Oysters, seafood and fish are the hallmarks of this hip maritime bistro. Admire the chefs’ work while seated at the bar. The outstandingly fresh sea produce is underscored by pure, unadorned cooking. Rather than prissy details, the goal is on stripped-back authentic briny flavours.

Name: Bouffard
Description: Bouffard has two different dining spaces to suit different moods: a snug lounge area at the front and a more vibrant room adorned with colourful artworks. Thomas Dockx is very selective when it comes to his ingredients, and he takes a less-is-more approach to preparing them. Eschewing any unnecessary frills, he allows the natural flavours to shine through with the help of robust sauces. In one of his exuberant dishes, he combines golden-brown pan-fried scallops, tender pork cheek and a creamed cheek broth. This chef understands how to create a well-rounded set menu that keeps you engaged from beginning to end!

Name: Chez Duche
Description: You can expect unadorned dishes that throb with flavour in what is the epitome of a neighbourhood eatery: rib of horse meat with house-made fries, lavishly served cassoulet, piled high with duck confit and Toulouse sausage or a waterzooi of seasonal veggies. A patriotic pageant of French and Belgian classics prepared and served with textbook precision and generosity. Chez Duche has been feeding us well since 1993!

Name: Het Nieuwe Palinghuis
Description: There is an authentic feel to the dining area of this charming seafood restaurant. Adorned with various nostalgic photos of maritime scenes, it harks back to its opening year: 1983! Over the years, Het Nieuwe Palinghuis has earned a reputation for its classic fish dishes. The menu features langoustine with an intense nantua sauce, sole Véronique in a full-bodied white wine sauce, as well as a distinctively herby eel in green sauce. The dishes here have always been big on flavour, steering clear of any unnecessary frills. A firm favourite!

Name: Le Mystique
Description: Dinner at the Mystique invariably starts with a wow! as you take in the opulent interior, stylish elegance and historic detail. The cuisine errs towards the creative and the chef has no qualms about using produce from afar. The result is succulent.

Name: Sophie et Nicolas
Description: Sophie Gigot and Nicolas Septon have entirely refurbished their characterful establishment. The infectious friendly vibe is intact, thanks in particular to the lovely patio in the greenhouse. Chef Nicolas crafts dishes in tune with nature that respect both the seasons and his region, through subtle, creative recipes.

Name: Bistro R
Description: Roland Debuyst is inspired by top-quality Belgian produce, but also by his globetrotting background. He focuses on bistro fare with a hint of modernity. Gyosa and ceviche are naturally combined with a dish of game, such as wild boar. This seasoned chef cannot be faulted when it comes to intelligently marrying flavours. The contemporary interior adorned with handsome works of art adds the final flourish to this enticing portrait.

Name: Bütgenbacher Hof
Description: The second generation has further enhanced the already well-established reputation of this family-run establishment. Take your pick from a range of gourmet menus that shine the spotlight on producers from eastern Belgium. The accent is on flavoursome bistro cuisine in tune with the times, washed down with a tipple from the well-stocked wine bin. The guestrooms are equipped with all the mod cons.

Name: Le 1460
Address: rue du Moulin à Vent 10, Virginal-Samme, 1460, Belgium
Description: Just sit back and enjoy the good life in this relaxed eatery! The varied menu overflows in comforting dishes, albeit in the zeitgeist, although the chef is definitely not one for gimmicks. A fine fillet of fish with buttery mashed potatoes or game in a powerful sauce, followed by a light, airy chocolate mousse – feelgood food before all else. This former bank (the wine cellar is in the old vaults) will awaken your tastebuds!

Name: 't Vijfde Seizoen
Description: Broes Tavernier hails his suppliers as “heroes”, which speaks volumes for his commitment to locally sourced produce. From asparagus and fish from the North Sea to partridges, he unfailingly selects the best. His creative, high-flying approach to cooking aims to let the ingredients shout their name. We recommend the insightful wine-food pairing suggestions. After a fine meal in this friendly establishment (great patio), pop into Eetalage and take a few goodies home.

Name: Les Eleveurs
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Les Eleveurs hotel restaurant, a landmark of Halle since 1897, has been run by the De Brouwer family since its foundation. Today, Annelies and Julian are breathing new life into their family heritage. Chef Borsy is in charge of the highly popular culinary score, adding his own personal touch while remaining true to Pajottenland specialties. The extensive menu ranges from family favourites such as chicory au gratin and lamb wellington to more modern fare like a vegetarian risotto of asparagus and celeriac. Go there your eyes closed – you won’t be disappointed.

Name: Calla's
Description: Calla’s immerses you in an enchanting Art deco ambience. In the heart of Aalter, this former solicitor’s home (1930) flanked by a delightful garden, is the epitome of cosy. The dishes to share bear witness to Niels Landtsheer’s creative streak, illustrated by sucrine salad leaf stuffed with subtly spiced North Sea crab and briny seaweed. Niels’ classical background comes to the forefront in recipes such as his rich vol-au-vent. Gutsy, big-boned flavours are the hallmark of this talented craftsman.

Name: Atelier Maple
Description: Authentic details, such as a stunning glazed dome, and a plush, yet cosy ambience depict this stylish Art nouveau edifice. Chef Tynes crafts cosmopolitan fare, adding his own spin to pedigree French dishes, thanks in particular to Asian and Indonesian influences. Splendid terrace.

Name: Amen
Description: Two-star chef Pascal Devalkeneer (Le Chalet de la Forêt) has a knack for picking the best produce. From the contemporary dishes and intense flavours to the range of textures, his dishes are masterpieces of culinary art. Amen!

Name: De Vijf Seizoenen
Description: Vegetables fresh from the fields, herbs picked in the Flemish Ardennes and environmentally sustainable seafood… Authenticity, sustainability and quality are the backbone of this classy, family-run restaurant, depicted by elegant Art deco light fixtures. The creative associations of ingredients and care lavished on the vegetables are truly fascinating. An unconventional new take on asparagus pleasantly surprises, underscored by an incredible concoction of eggs and exciting fermented flavours. A fine tribute to the seasons!

Name: Savoury
Description: This spruce detached house does sport a faintly English hallmark, the menu, however, unveils a patriotic line-up of classical French cuisine. Kick off your meal with an aperitif in the wine cellar before taking a seat in the modern dining room or on the leafy patio. Subtle classicism depicts the textbook precision cooking, albeit with an occasional Mediterranean twang and a refreshing sprinkling of modernity. Pop into the delicatessen before you leave and take a few delicacies home.

Name: Odette en Ville
Description: Odette is a well-known eatery of the trendy Châtelain neighbourhood. The stylish 1920’s townhouse aims to combine British style, Parisian sensuality and New York glamour. The highly varied menu is equally fascinating: both classical and international, with an accent on the ingredient. Crunchy nems in a spicy sauce, al dente taglioni in lemon with pink shrimps, scallops and foie gras in a duck stock: a festival for fine food lovers. And why not treat yourself to one of the swish designer-inspired guestrooms to finish your evening in the lap of luxury?

Name: Le Mucha
Address: avenue Jules Du Jardin 23, Woluwe-Saint-Pierre, 1150, Belgium
Description: The interior and character of Le Mucha are reminiscent of Parisian brasseries in the 1900s, providing the perfect foil to sample traditional French fare. A host of subtle details such as last-minute fresh fries or an unusual béarnaise sauce with steak bears witness to the ethos of this restaurant whose DNA is firmly characterised by lashings of generosity. A must should you get a hankering for nostalgic nosh, such as veal’s brains or an île flottante (meringue floating on velvety egg custard) – even better if you go on one of the jazz nights…

Name: Floris
Description: As pleasing to the eye as to the palate! Wood and iron prevail in the decor, while the regional cuisine displays a blend of talent and creative flair.

Name: Jacqueline
Description: This former butchery is named after the grandmother of Evelien Swiers, who is in charge of the kitchen you can see behind the original counter. Good humoured Raf supervises the dining room, which sports a gentrified workshop vibe. Evelien’s delicious, no-frills cuisine revolves around a menu of four or five dishes. Guinea fowl from Maison Garat is cooked in a frying pan and underscored by a knockout jus enriched in miso, while chicory adds a fresh note with a mandarin sabayon. At Jacqueline, the food is rustic, gutsy and wholesome.

Name: Lijsterbes
Description: Chef Van Der Bruggen combines creativity with classical training, as his spit-roast veal sweetbread or his seabass in a salt crust demonstrate. High precision cooking that allows the top-notch ingredients to shout their name. The set and lunch menus remain a hit with his faithful regulars, who make a beeline for the lovely terrace. A solid bet every time!

Name: Les Caves d'Alex
Description: Alex and Hugues share a passion for first-class produce. The former has a weakness for cured meats, while the enthusiastic sommelier delights in unearthing great wines to pair with your meal. Chef Alex, a fan of textbook French cuisine, pays tribute to tradition through rich recipes and knockout sauces, such as Ostend-style sole or a subtle Nantua sauce that enhances his pike quenelles. Wine vats and paraphernalia set the scene indoors, while the romantic garden provides the perfect foil for a fine dining experience in summertime.

Name: The Thrill
Description: Hunting trophies on the walls, sheepskins on the chairs and a huge fireplace-grill in the centre: the rustic stage is set for the friendly, buzzy Thrill in Genk. The extensive menu will make your tastebuds drool, all the more so as you can be safe in the knowledge that Rik Vandersanden is a high-flying craftsman. His ravioli of woodpigeon or his chuck Black Angus, masterfully grilled to rare on the BBQ, demonstrate his talent and generosity. Heaven for lovers of authentic, down to earth flavours.

Name: Zappaz
Description: Zappaz, noted for its friendly vibe, is living proof that fine dining doesn’t have to be starched and stuffy. The several-course menu is an ode to punchy sauces, featuring a playful approach to vegetables, jazzed up with subtle globetrotting influences. Fascinating flavours add whoomph to each dish – a gourmet pageant of ingredients!

Name: Brugmann
Description: If you fancy a slap-up meal in southwest Brussels, make a beeline for this fancy brasserie adorned with modern art and boasting a lovely alfresco space at the rear. Brugmann offers an extensive choice of pedigree Gallic dishes at lunchtime and in the evening. Traditional recipes are treated to modern, particularly Asian, interpretations, such as langoustine in a tempura of crunchy walnuts with a sweet and sour bisque sauce.

Name: Caillou
Description: Caillou is a hip, modern bistro, strewn with passing nods to ‘pebbles’ (its namesake). The kitchen team prepares the food on a central table that sets the scene for their culinary show. The performance continues in the plate, with an appetising blend of flavours and textures and enticing veggie dishes. The chef doesn’t hesitate to spice up traditional recipes, flanking lobster and turbot, for example, with deftly crafted side dishes such as asparagus flan, a gutsy lobster béarnaise and a poivrade of fried artichokes. The sommelier may suggest an elegant mineral wine, echoing the establishment’s name, to pair with your food.

Name: Le Monde est Petit
Description: This stylish and intimate restaurant enjoys a pleasant location between Montgomery and Cinquantenaire Park. The market determines what's on the menu here. Chef Loïc Villers incorporates delicious produce into well-thought-out dishes that are as international as his diners. Think quail ballotines stuffed with a delicate farce containing pistachio, a parsnip cream, grapes and juices from the meat. This cuisine is all about pleasure and celebrates the genuine flavours of the ingredients.

Name: Plassendale
Description: Royal shrimp fritters with fried parsley and lemon or skate that slips off the bone with a fresh silky butter and caper sauce and creamy mashed potato: such are a few of the patriotic line-up of recipes that have ensured the success of the Plassendale for aeons. Exquisitely located by a lock, it is heaven for fans of traditional nosh in a casual vibe. Unbeatable value for money.

Name: La Brouette
Address: boulevard Prince de Liège 61, Anderlecht, 1070, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Herman Dedapper welcomes you with open arms to his neighbourhood restaurant, decorated in warm colours and adorned with his own photo work. He is an excellent sommelier and loves to share his passion for wine. The chef’s generous, French - inspired dishes are sourced from high - quality produce.

Name: Notarishuys
Description: This former solicitor’s house is ideally located to explore the Westhoek region. You will stay in comfortable rooms, eat in a romantic restaurant and admire the venerable copper beech tree from the pretty patio in the garden. Chef Boussemaere blends tradition and modernity, turning out dishes whose rich familiar flavours are also a masterclass in culinary subtlety.

Name: Kwizien
Description: The ingredient plays the star role in this welcoming farmstead. Thomas Coppejans scours the region for produce such as Malines chicken and asparagus, which are often on the menu. He also crafts a ceviche of seabass that will doubtless find favour with younger foodies. Ellen and her team will ply you with insightful tips to help you make your choice between the à la carte, dishes to share and the set menus. Sit back and soak up the infectiously bubbly vibe.

Name: Vlass
Description: The Lauwereins family bends over backwards to pamper you in its swish, yet cosy restaurant. Chef Stefaan deploys cutting-edge techniques to devise bold creative dishes that suit modern palates and in which every detail is endlessly pondered over. Wine waiter Kenzo’s pairings are surprising and inspired.

Name: De Normandie
Description: It may look like a ship washed up on the dunes, but don’t be mistaken: this 1936 boat-shaped edifice is home to a well-oiled, contemporary brasserie. Super fresh seafood takes pride of place with lobster dishes playing the leading role! Generous, legible fare with a strong French bias, although the chef has no qualms about adding a new spin to classical recipes.

Name: Hostellerie du Grünewald
Description: Fresh, healthy food, but also deliciously generous. This very pleasant bistro with a fine terrace provides an opportunity to sample simple ingredients devoid of unnecessary frills. Save room for the scrumptious desserts. Elegant guestrooms ensure sweet dreams.

Name: L'Horizon
Description: L'Horizon is definitely in tune with the zeitgeist. A fashionable interior and meticulously laid tables set the scene. The chef’s Italian roots, Asian influences and regional produce, such as poultry and herbs, are combined in dishes that cater to modern tastes. Delicate, well-prepared cuisine, fully worthy of a visit.

Name: Lizanna
Description: Their respective grandmothers, Liza and Anna, bequeathed their love of cooking to chef Levy and to the lady of the house, Stéphanie. The couple shares their passion with guests in this elegant restaurant flanked by a delightful terrace. The chef rolls out his consummate craftsmanship in classical dishes: turbot à la meunière, melt-in-the-mouth endives, intelligently seasoned beurre blanc and a subtle Robuchon puree. The pinnacle of fine French dining.

Name: Elders
Description: Urban and exciting, Elders is just the ticket if you fancy sampling modern cuisine in which veggies play the star roles. Tom Pauwelyn reverently respects the seasons, inventing inspired recipes. For example, he exalts cauliflower by preparing it in several ways, including one with an exquisitely subtle Nantua (creamy crayfish) sauce or he celebrates pears with a sabayon of stout beer. Each meal is a treasure trove of discoveries.

Name: L'aperovino
Description: “Wine, dine and unwind” is the motto of this stylish upmarket bistro. Upstairs is the wine bar where sommelière Julie unveils a knockout selection of prestigious tipples and a fine choice of cocktails. Downstairs, you will sample dishes poised between tradition and exotic innovation, ranging from a winter venison stew to Sebastes fish served with a refreshing tom kha kai. “Where wining meets dining” is their other baseline…

Name: Brasserie Nieuwpoort
Description: This is light years from your run-of-the-mill seaside brasserie! The opulent décor will bowl you over, as will the mixologist who rustles up intriguing cocktails behind the bar. Each dish overflows with generosity and is crafted by gifted, veteran chefs who work with the best ingredients. A range of dishes to share and wholesome brasserie fare. Why not start with a fresh, spicy, acidic ceviche of seabass, before pursuing with a royal vol-au-vent served with piping hot crunchy French fries? THE landmark brasserie of Nieuwpoort!

Name: L'adresse
Description: A colourful, designer establishment that serves a single set menu in a bid to guarantee optimum freshness. The focus on quality can be tasted with each bite. Don’t expect fussy frills or superfluous extras – the chef is determined to allow the ingredient to shout its name in each recipe. Immaculately cooked rockfish in a herby chorizo crust and a delicate cream of sea buckthorn berries, paired with a savoury piperade and a velvety fish stock and saffron sauce. A minimalist, stripped-back approach to cooking, particularly in the deftly crafted 100% vegetarian menu.

Name: L'Art de Vivre
Description: Notable's house cultivates the art of living by way of a pleasant setting and a lovely, modern, à la carte menu with a splash of creativity. Set menus described to you; homemade cakes and desserts.

Name: Bachten De Leie
Description: Burnished copper saucepans and a striking colour scheme set the stylish scene in this welcoming restaurant. The youthful chef, Louis Wauters, is a butcher’s son and proud of it. You will sample perfectly cooked rib of beef with a silky béarnaise sauce and French fries, but the chef is also keen to pamper fish and seafood amateurs. Flavour and generosity are the watchwords here.

Name: Bruun
Description: The food of brothers Ruben and Pieter is as elegant as their restaurant and the entirely open-plan kitchen cannot fail but catch the eye. One is inevitably spellbound by the brothers’ seamlessly smooth craftsmanship, as they conjure up dishes free of fussy frills, in keeping with their vision of polished French fare. The focus is on intense gutsy sauces and subtly balanced minimalist flavours.

Name: Vis van A
Description: With love from the North Sea! If you pop in during the morning, you can nibble on a signature smoked salmon sandwich or a few oysters with a glass of champagne at the bar. In fine weather, head for the enchanting patio and do justice to the delicacies of the North Sea. You can even buy some fresh fish to take home from the fish market. Vis van A never disappoints, whatever the time of day! From fried sole and Canadian lobster to sushi and sashimi flanked by a variety of veggies. During the meal, glance up at the ceiling adorned with the skeleton of a whale and cuttlefish.

Name: L'Episode
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Waillimont Estate pays a fitting tribute to the Ardennes countryside and its riverside lodges set an idyllic scene for a getaway destination. The main building is home to a luxurious inn whose snug bar, wood-burning fire, marble floors and timber ceilings would be perfectly at home in an upmarket ski resort. The region takes pride of place in chef Jordan Boreux’ subtle blend of creative and traditional cuisine (knockout sauces!). Some of the textures and personal interpretations may surprise, but familiar Ardennes flavours remain a firm fixture.

Name: Loxalis
Address: 150 Rue de la Libération, Dudelange, 3511, Luxembourg
Description: Immense floor-to-ceiling windows command a splendid view of the surrounding countryside, with the bonus of a peaceful terrace (weather permitting): the scene of Loxalis is set. Diners are greeted by a genuine maitre d’, who carefully takes the time to explain the appetising menu. Chef Boccolini subtly adds a modern spin to characteristic Mediterranean recipes, such as his new take on vitello tonnato flanked by a characterful sauce. Familiar flavours abound but with intriguing new dimensions. The lunchtime menu is a best-seller!

Name: Caudalie
Description: Caudalie, a pared-back fine dining establishment, is perfectly at home in the hip Le Carré neighbourhood of Liège. Chef Simon and Manon, in charge of the front-of-house, share a passion for outstanding ingredients and wine. His technical virtuosity and attention to detail shine through as much in the craftsmanship as in the plating. For example, he might add a characterful Thai stock, sesame oil and a combination of onion and mushroom textures to flawlessly fresh rainbow trout. We recommend the monthly changing menu that hits the spot every time, to the delight of its many regulars.

Name: Parfums de cuisine
Description: The aromas wafting tantalisingly out of Vincenzo Romeo’s open kitchen are quite the opposite of fortuitous. This cosy eatery tucked away in the heart of Namur serves a Gallic line-up of heirloom dishes crafted with virtuoso know-how. Crunchy filo pastry stuffed with frog’s legs is paired with a subtle green vegetable soup, depicted by a distinctive acidic note. The concise but exceedingly well-curated wine list ensures that you will be able to find just the right tipple to pair with this traditional pageant of French classical nosh.

Name: Komaf
Description: This farm has lost none of its 17C character following a top-to-toe refurbishment with a focus on naturality. Julie Van Gool and Anthony Stoop have masterminded an exquisite venue, courtesy of materials such as wood and marble, curtains that offer cosy intimacy and the Antwerp countryside that sprawls as far as the eye can see.Chef Stoop acquired a love of last-minute recipes and raunchy sauces; he also has a knack for exotic aromas and flavours. For example, he sources his pork neck from a local butcher, which he then enhances with spicy peanut flavours. The chef sprinkles his recipes in carefully judged spices like vadouvan and sweet pumpkin and works with vibrant ingredients, thus adding a fresh kick to familiar flavours. His cooking is crisp, legible and surprising thanks to unexpected combinations of ingredients.

Name: La Scarpetta
Description: We warrant that you will fall head over heels when you set foot in this pleasant restaurant. Comfort, a warm welcome and generous portions – what’s not to like? Authentic Italian recipes, mainly from Marche, come to life in familiar dishes oozing with flavour. The chef might enhance fresh al dente calamarata pasta with salsiccia and a parmesan and truffle sauce. A banquet of Italian fare! The restaurant has rapidly become a favourite with the locals – booking highly recommended.

Name: Outro by Vito
Address: 18 Millakbondong-ro 19 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48087, South Korea
Description: With the new name Outro by Vito, the restaurant relocated from a location in the Haeridan-gil area to this spot near Gwangalli Beach. Not only did this fine purveyor of natural wine and cuisine change its name, but it also revamped its exterior and décor with a touch of contemporary elegance. Regardless, its pasta dishes, the quintessential offerings, have remained the same – only with enhanced flavors. The diner’s housemade pasta now features higher flour content and undergoes fermentation. The glutinous texture and impeccable pairing with the sauce make the pasta even more appetizing. In addition to a diverse array of pasta dishes, the menu features salads, meat, and various other scrumptious dishes. Come on down and savor your meal with a chef-recommended natural wine replete with a cultured vibe.

Name: Osteria Aboo
Description: As its sign suggests, Osteria Aboo in Jeonpo-dong oddly labels itself a Western gastropub. Since 2017, this establishment has strived to offer authentic Southern Italian cuisine, a cuisine characterized by ample use of seafood-based ingredients. Among all the exquisite items on the menu, we are partial to the bisque pasta, featuring al dente noodles and a sumptuous amount of fresh and savory red-banded lobster, as well as the newly added Mare (“sea”) course. When paired with a chef-recommended wine, the cuisine will astonish you with the rich flavors of Italy.

Name: Eutteum Iroribata
Address: 20 Suyeong-ro 408 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48308, South Korea
Description: Located near Namcheon station, this Japanese diner specializes in omakase dining prepared using irori (traditional Japanese hearth). Though not as authentic as the ones in old Japanese houses, the irori here is faithful to its role as kitchen equipment. The visual and aromatic appeal of grilling seasonal fish skewers, arranged in a row in front of the irori, adds to the diner’s culinary delight. An embodiment of Chef Jung Eu-tteum’s experience with Japanese cuisine and his personal gastronomic affinities, the eatery is a perfect haven to relish a diverse array of grilled fish. Clay pot rice and other dishes served during the omakase course boast a range of refined flavors that often characterize Japanese cuisine.

Name: Torafuguga
Description: Located on a boulevard near Jungdong Intersection in the Haeundae District, Torafuguga stands out with its quaint wooden exterior and a small aquarium with live torafuku (tiger puffer) at the front. The eatery has no sign except for a small calligraphy of its name penned by the owner-chef Jung Seung-hun himself. Yet, these visual elements are enough to let you know that it’s a specialist puffer fish restaurant. Here, the chef’s precise hand movements bring out the variegated flavors of tiger puffer and deliver them, nonstop, to customers at the tables. Torafuguga’s Japanese-style puffer fish course features a wide array of faithful dishes that are parboiled, served raw in slices, fried, made into a soup, or crafted into a porridge. There are many restaurants that handle puffer fish, but few show commitment to presenting it in authentic Japanese style. In light of this, the chef’s earnestness in preparing and serving puffer fish testifies to his passion for culinary art.

Name: Essence
Description: After a series of twists and turns, Chef Kim Yeong-seon wrapped up his famed career as a classic French chef at Restaurant Soleil and opened Essence to offer his very own version of French cuisine. Here, the chef provides bistro-style French fare that is cozier and lighter, and therefore more accessible, than the fare at his previous restaurant. Although the winds of change are sweeping through the dining industry, he is steadfastly committed to the classic style, delivering deep flavors through precisely baked and cooked ingredients and carefully crafted sauces. In this era of contemporary cuisine that appeals to diners with a wide range of novel culinary styles, Essence’s unpretentious meals highlighting genuine authenticity remind us, once again, of the core of French cuisine.

Name: Iwa
Address: 2F, 13 Haeundaehaebyeon-ro 209 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48093, South Korea
Description: The chef, who holds a patent for the aging of fish, prepares aged ingredients with clear intent. Such meticulous preparation, combined with diverse selections, produces stable flavors and gastronomic delights. Depending on the ingredients available and the chef’s tactics, the proportion of sushi, sashimi, and other Japanese dishes in the omakase can vary. All fish here are aged at least four days, and the chef carefully selects an optimal aging period for each fish based on its type, characteristics, and conditions. At Iwa, customers can enjoy at one sitting a wide variety of Japanese dishes, each prepared with aged ingredients with full-bodied flavors. And reasonable prices make this culinary feast all the more special.

Name: L'OIGNON
Description: Nestled in a quiet alley within the ultra-trendy Garosu-gil district, L'Oignon, which means “the onion” in French, is a French-based pescatarian restaurant that offers dishes made only with vegetables, fish, eggs and dairy products. With a steadfast dedication to the principles of ecological harmony and compassionate treatment of animals, the chef opened this eatery with the intention of imparting to patrons the wholesome sustenance he himself reveres. The kitchen uses vegetable broth with mushrooms as a substitute for rich meat broth and creates the texture of its cakes using cauliflower and pecorino cheese instead of flour. Yet, the umami flavors and textures produced through these novel means are as deep and as luscious as those concocted by conventional recipes. If the allure of a plant-based diet beckons, why not indulge in the captivating flavors of L'Oignon's pescatarian fare?

Name: Le dorer
Address: 2F, 37 Marine city 3-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48118, South Korea
Description: Le Dorer’s Marine City location offers a gorgeous seascape. Dorer is a French word that means “to coat with gold.” The restaurant’s name therefore symbolizes its resolve to provide a swanky and beautiful dining experience. Le Dorer started off as a Korean restaurant, but now serves contemporary fare with a touch of French and Japanese cuisine. It also features a wine cellar that boasts a wide range of vintages and varietals. For those who prefer to focus on the union of food and wine, Le Dorer also offers an a la carte menu and a bar menu with a wine and cocktail list.

Name: Chef Gon
Address: 12 Junggu-ro 23 beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan, 48978, South Korea
Description: Situated in an alley near Jagalchi Market, this joint is run by a former hotel chef with years of experience. Every morning, the chef visits the market to buy fresh ingredients, with which he prepares the day’s seasonal menu. For this reason, the restaurant’s course meal is called “Jagalchi Chef’s Course Special.” Diners sitting near the kitchen can watch the chef in action while listening to his explanations about the ingredients. In addition to seafood offerings, the menu features a wide range of meat and a la carte dishes, as well as a well-balanced wine list, all of which await your indulgence.

Name: Trid
Description: Diversity, deliciousness, and delight are the three D’s that serve as the basis for this restaurant's name. They are also the points of interest to chefs and patrons when it comes to the modern cuisine. Trid is a contemporary haunt that focuses on these elements; in fact, it's here where that perpetual culinary struggle to meet such standards is most strongly felt. The head chef has experienced diverse dining environments in a multitude of cultural milieus, which has allowed him to make bold and interesting choices while pursuing new tastes and combinations of ingredients. The spatial coziness, refined services, and elegantly designed open kitchen blend in with the restaurant’s fare, exemplifying a sense of unity.

Name: Dim Tao
Description: Dim sum, a representative Cantonese dish, literally means “touch the heart,” implying that it’s not intended to fill your stomach, but is supposed to be a simple meal. Dim Tao focuses on the most famous dim sum dishes among its countless varieties, including juicy xiao long bao (soup dumplings); a dumpling filled with plump shrimp and chives; wonton soup; and barbeque pork buns. Traditionally, dim sum is served with tea. We recommend the pu’er and jasmine teas. A long line of customers outside makes this popular establishment in the Haeridan-gil area impossible to miss.

Name: Restaurant OY
Address: B1F, 48-12 Seolleung-ro 148-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06064, South Korea
Description: Nestled in a quiet residential alley, Restaurant OY has a homey façade that befits the ambience of the neighborhood. Run by a chef couple who have spent much of their time in Korea and France dedicated to pursuing their passion for French cuisine, this establishment serves up classy and comforting dishes rather than elaborate arrangements. Blurring the boundaries between the traditional and the modern, the cuisine still remains true to authentic tastes. Their sophisticated understanding of ingredients and precise cooking skills result in dishes with well-defined tastes and depth of flavor. In short, diners can expect culinary gems that consistently satisfy.

Name: Hakusi
Description: Charcoal, fire and paper – these are the three themes Chef Choi Seong-hun seeks to convey in Hakusi’s captivating culinary narrative. The triumphant result is a testament to his masterful storytelling. Beginning at the entrance and extending all the way to the dining area, an arresting visual tableau of black and red imbues the space with personality, punctuated by white elements that exude a sense of harmony and stability. This vivid vitality is also manifest in the establishment’s distinctive cuisine that reflects the chef’s vast culinary experience. In every dish, the allure of seasonal ingredients is brought to life in vivid detail, with distinct flavors and aromas, which transcend the boundaries between modern and classic cuisine, figuring prominently.

Name: Zero Base
Address: 2F, 17 Millak-ro 33 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48285, South Korea
Description: Zero Base is a new Japanese restaurant by Chef Yu Byeong-chan, who previously ran the izakaya Yoo No Woo with a stellar reputation. The chef’s unrelenting thirst for classy Japanese cuisine, which had never been fully quenched at his former spot, drove him to present his newly evolved cuisine at this up-and-coming eatery. His solid culinary skills turn ingredients into sumptuous variations on a classic theme, in a way that accentuates his sensibilities. The eatery pays special attention to selecting the freshest of seasonal ingredients. And it simply makes sense. The delicate juxtaposition between Zero Base’s contemporary décor and classic cuisine conjures up an exclusive vibe.

Name: Chaoran
Address: 5F Signiel, 30 Dalmaji-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of Signiel Busan, Chaoran serves authentic Cantonese cuisine – more precisely its Hong Kong variety, which is based on the former yet characterized by the harmony of new flavors resulting from the city’s culturally diverse geographical contexts. Take, for example, the dim sum: It consists of a gamut of splendid and scrumptious dishes, including har gow (shrimp dumplings), characterized by skin colored with squid ink and topped with gold leaf; a vegetable dumpling filled with truffle, other mushrooms, and asparagus; and a seafood dumpling stuffed with dried scallops in XO sauce and decorated with flying fish roe. Pork Barbeque with Honey Sauce and Crispy Pork Belly, the signature dishes, boast juicy meat and crispy skin accompanied by mild flavors conjured up by seasonings. Its décor, reminiscent of Hong Kong in the 1920s, and its spectacular view of the Haeundae area make this fine diner an optimal location to savor a delectable meal.

Name: Borgo Hannam
Description: “Borgo” in Italian means “village,” helmed by Chef Stefano Di Salvo. Once up the tiny set of stairs, you are greeted with homemade dishes and liqueurs befitting the cozy space. From the bread freshly baked in the morning to pastas and desserts, everything is handmade by the chef himself. The kitchen's signature Caldaro soup was inspired by the fisherman’s soup in Tuscany, which has good rich spicy flavor in it with chef’s own twist. Recreating the ambience of a friendly diner, this is a great spot for heartwarming Italian food from various regions. Don’t miss the diverse range of desserts served on a tiered stand.

Name: Il Vecchio
Address: 332-12 World Cup buk-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul, 03930, South Korea
Description: Il Vecchio is a down-to-earth, homey ristorante run by the chef couple Kim Min-gyun and Kim Bin-na. The eatery’s Italian fare brims with well-defined and focused flavors, and its signature dishes made with fresh local produce and seafood capture perfectly the tastes of the season. With meticulous execution, the chef duo cooks each and every ingredient to a precise degree with optimal juiciness, bringing out a range of nuanced flavors, aromas, and textures. Indeed, its semi-dried fresh pasta sets the standard for such extraordinary attention to culinary detail. At Il Vecchio, unrelenting gastronomic innovation that aims to delight diners with diverse yet consistent epicurean experiences is the norm. Just one caveat: The establishment is nestled in an alley, so parking may prove a challenge.

Name: Kumsu Bokguk
Address: 23 Jungdong 1-ro 43 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48095, South Korea
Description: Kumsu Bokguk in Haeundae District is the head restaurant of a chain that has many outposts in Seoul and Busan. For more than 50 years since 1970, and across multiple generations, this eatery has delighted seafood lovers as a specialized puffer fish restaurant. It offers four types of puffer fish. Brown-backed puffer is chewy and has a nutty flavor. Globe puffer is large and often made into a spicy stew. Yellowfin puffer is sweet, so it is usually steamed or boiled. Ocellate puffer is the largest variety of the fish. Its firm texture makes the fish more suitable to be served raw. Safety is the first priority at this head restaurant as demonstrated by the hiring of dozens of chefs, all licensed to prepare puffer fish. So why not rest assured and visit this time-tested establishment for a gastronomic adventure?

Name: Ryunique
Description: Since its opening in 2011, Ryunique has been constantly reinventing the art of cuisine, driven by Chef Ryu Tae-hwan’s independent research and creative interpretation of ingredients. The chef continually updates the menu to reflect the solar term and season, with an emphasis on fresh ingredients that vary by season and source. His talent for turning his unbounded gastronomic imagination into reality is the secret to Ryunique’s unique fare. Remarkably, this tidy and modern space is home to both the chef’s research center (first floor) and a dining area (second floor). All in all, there is something special about Ryunique’s cuisine that sparks our culinary imagination while never losing its freshness or charm.

Name: Level:0
Description: Level:0 is tucked in the residential area behind Yongsan Station. The name of the joint has a double meaning: the first floor and the pursuit of zero-waste cooking focused on sustainability. Here, diners can enjoy their multi-course meals in a nomadic fashion as they wander from space to space. Committed to sustainable dining, the chef reuses leftover ingredients by drying them into powder or fermenting them. The establishment also sources its beef from organic farms. On the aesthetic side, its tarts in the shape of a finely manicured garden, and a dessert resembling the whole restaurant, are a delicate feast for the eyes as well as the palate. Since Level:0 adjusts reservations to avoid crowding, double-check with the restaurant before visiting.

Name: ELPIC
Description: El Pic, once a famed grill house on Jeju Island, has found its new home in Seoul. Although dry-aged, wet-aged and beeswax-aged beef steaks are signature dishes at this steakhouse, its grilled fresh seasonal squid, caught in the waters off Jeju Island, and ceviche are pleasant surprises as well. The way the steaks are grilled is extraordinary: They are cooked over charcoal at low temperature and cooled, with the process repeating for more than 30 minutes to maximize tenderness and juiciness. The sliced meat looks red, but is indeed cooked to perfection. Pair the meat with wine for additional gastronomic indulgence.

Name: Al'aise
Description: Al’aise is a French restaurant headed by Chef Lee Byeong-gon, who has dedicated extensive efforts to experience and immerse himself in authentic French cuisine. The power of such conscientious dedication is instilled in his dishes that remain faithful to the basics and are brimming with honest passion to convey the innate flavors of the ingredients. The course meals feature an exceptional balance of ingredients and sauces, bringing out the long-standing and dependable flavors expected from fine French cuisine. Another distinct culinary delight is to be found in the kitchen’s classic French sauces adorned with the chef’s singular twists. Treat yourself in this homey and cozy bistro that offers delicately flavored French fare crafted with imaginative seasonal Korean ingredients.

Name: y'east
Description: In a nod to the property’s name, an appellation that invites varied interpretations, Y’east is home to expressions of unlimited culinary possibilities. Chef Cho Young-dong, its chef de cuisine, delights diners with familiar dishes reimagined via his singular aesthetics. The chef channels his passion into creating novel flavors by artfully blending ingredients that are hard to come by in Korea. From the signature amuse bouche inspired by kaya toast to Galbi Stone, braised short ribs that come in several variations, each dish embodies the novel within the familiar, presenting out-of-the-box gastronomic ecstasy that evokes fresh new tastes while still retaining the very essence of the original flavor.

Name: Yulling
Address: 2F, 28 Dalmaji-gil 62 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48098, South Korea
Description: Yulling sits on the second floor of the Mipo Oceanside Hotel at the beginning of Dalmaji-gil Road. The lengthy counter in this vast space commands a panoramic ocean view marked by the spectacular Dongbaekseom Island and Gwangandaegyo Bridge. The restaurant uses a wide array of only the choicest Korean beef cuts graded 1++ No. 9, the highest standard. On top of this, its fresh seafood dishes with an intriguing blend of Japanese and European elements create a menu brimming with impeccably balanced flavors – as suggested by the name Yulling, which denotes “harmony” and “balance.” And one more thing: Don’t miss the well-thought-out wine pairings.

Name: Zhonghuafuchun Salon
Description: To convey its authenticity to diners, a cuisine that transforms and responds to changing times must be founded on a clear and accurate understanding of culinary tradition. At Zhonghuafuchun Salon, Chef Nam Bok-chun’s concern for and dedication to bringing positive change to Chinese cuisine is unmistakable in its culinary creations. The chef pays particular attention to selecting quality ingredients, the basic building blocks of good food, while engaging in active exchanges with chefs in mainland China, to promote a gradual evolution in his native cuisine, one dish at a time. Zhonghuafuchun Salon is a fascinating Chinese establishment, where traditional Chinese recipes combined with local twists translate into a feast of richly flavorful dishes.

Name: Chez Simon
Address: 48 World Cup-ro 10-gil, Mapo-gu, Seoul, 04003, South Korea
Description: Chez Simon, This French bistro has been growing at a steady pace. The couple who runs this eatery closes its doors every year for a certain period, so that they can travel around the world to discover new ingredients. It is this unrelenting dedication to cuisine and humility that has marked the success, even though the chefs have had no professional culinary training. This French kitchen offers only course meals, featuring plain, simple dishes that are the culmination of authentic recipes and fresh, carefully curated ingredients.

Name: Myomi
Address: 5F Arario Space, 83 Yulgok-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul, 03058, South Korea
Description: Myomi is set in a gorgeous space with a spectacular view of Changdeokgung Palace, is an experience that diners eagerly await. Chef Kim Hyo-jung's use of Korean ingredients and cooking techniques remain unchanged, but the chef has added subtle new inflections to his dishes as the venue’s name Myomi (“subtle charm”) fittingly suggests.

Name: Mr. Ahn's Craft Makgeolli
Description: Mr. Ahn's Craft Makgeolli is a most befitting venue for the Korean term banju, or alcohol accompanying a meal. What distinguishes this gastropub is its avoidance of the stereotypical Korean pubs and expression of the direction they should take—in this age of new Korean cuisine that is traditional yet imbued with a modern touch. At this charming spot, patrons can enjoy seasonally changing menus of savory Korean anju (snacks paired with alcohol), main dishes, as well as a wide selection of traditional liquors that simply get better with time. It’s a perfect place for both light meals and friendly social drinking—a versatile venue that appeals to distinct audiences.

Name: Moulin
Description: Located on a quiet alley in Seochon, Moulin is a French establishment whose dark-colored frontage draws attention by forming a stark contrast against its surroundings. Once inside, expect to be visually enticed by an antique-style décor and walls adorned with a collection of moulins, or pepper mills, that the chef has amassed over the years. Chef Yoon Ye-rang’s desire to impart flavors of the season to her French cuisine is expressed in dishes that celebrate the balance of subtle and bold gastronomic elements. The signature pithivier series that continues to be recreated using seasonal ingredients epitomizes the culinary philosophy.

Name: Sandai
Description: Sandai is a kaiseki restaurant helmed by Chef Moon Seung-ju, who appears to be steadily building his own niche in Seoul’s Japanese culinary scene. His approach to and interpretation of the kaiseki tradition are well-attested to in this space reminiscent of the Kansai region, as well as in his classic thematic dishes. The finishing touch of the exquisite course meal is a tea ceremony, featuring the likes of a unique and authentic house matcha. The name Sandai, which means “three generations” in Japanese, embodies Chef Moon’s desire to create a space frequented by multiple generations.

Name: SIIO
Description: At SIIO, the head chef’s experience is seen in imaginative dishes featuring seasonal Korean ingredients, ready to delight diners with sumptuous flavors. SIIO’s fare breaks free from the mold and embraces freedom of expression. At this fine diner, novel dishes represent a melting pot of culinary cultures and techniques. Yet, under the veneer of this freewheeling, fresh take on food lies the careful selection of ingredients that reflect Korea’s four distinct seasons. Meticulous rules dictate the perfect balance of subtle flavors.

Name: Olh Eum
Description: Cooking honest food that respects the integrity of ingredients is the motto of Chef Seo Ho-young, who cooks with the freshest produce sent to him by his farmer parents. Transporting familiar flavors to new territories is his game. Take, for example, his shrimp and sea urchin capellini in a silky smooth bisque-like sauce made with freshwater shrimp heads, fermented fish sauce and doenjang, or his smoked striploin carpaccio served with a mushroom and soy sauce consommé.

Name: Minami
Description: The star of the show at Minami is Japanese-style soba noodles. Trained at the prestigious Tsuji Culinary Institute in Osaka, Japan, Chef Nam Chang-soo is no stranger to the world of Japanese cuisine, but he professes that soba is his one true love. While respecting the time-honored traditions of Japanese-style buckwheat noodles, Nam adds his own spin to the soba dishes he serves. Customer favorites include soba noodle soup topped with soy sauce-braised and grilled conger eel as well as another variety with soy sauce-braised herring imported from Kyoto.

Name: Wooga
Address: B1F, 22 Dosan-daero 49-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06019, South Korea
Description: Wooga was originally born in Hoengseong, the beef capital of Korea. The restaurant is known for preparing the choicest quality local beef in its unique style: dry aged and well done. Chef Heo Se-byeong has been experimenting tirelessly with beef under the slogan meat science to maximize the characteristics of this meat such as tenderness, juiciness and flavor. Don’t miss out on another perennial favorite: a stew made with soybean paste fermented over long stages by the chef’s own mom.

Name: Imun Seolnongtang
Description: Still going strong after more than 100 years of being in business, Imun Seolnongtang was the first eatery in Korea to officially register for a restaurant license when it opened in 1904. To this day, it honors the tradition of boiling ox bones for 17 hours until the broth turns rich and opaque. Other cuts of beef are later added to the intensely flavorful broth, served with a generous portion of sliced beef and soft wheat noodles.

Name: Table for Four
Description: This 'Table' uses a wide range of seasonal ingredients infused with optimal flavors from Taean, South Chungcheong Province—the chef’s hometown. His affection for the region and genuine passion to serve the freshest and healthiest food to patrons are the reasons behind his use of such choice. The chef, sometimes aided by the seasoned master, is able to skillfully transform his hometown ingredients into exciting dishes, and at other times there is minimal culinary intervention. Diners who visit are bound to relish the allure of this European cuisine, imbued with the flair of Taean.

Name: Aelgerizm
Description: Aelgerizm’s Japan-meets-West modern cuisine will delight your palate with delicate seasonable variations on a theme. The food is inspired by Chef Yang Min-woo’s rich culinary and life experience in Japan. He blurs the boundaries of his brand of Japanese cuisine through the inventive use of Western ingredients, always seeking to maintain the right balance to achieve culinary perfection. The menu changes four times a year, reflecting Korea’s four distinct seasons, with each seasonal menu organically related to the preceding one. Each dish brings out the genuine flavors of the ingredients, then delicately balanced with the sauces.

Name: Palais de Chine
Address: 6F L'Escape Hotel, 67 Toegye-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, 04529, South Korea
Description: Located inside the Parisian Belle Époque-inspired L'Escape Hotel, Palais de Chine is the only space within the hotel that offers Eastern tastes and sensibilities. Inspired by designs from Shanghai's own belle époque, the modern space offers both authentic and modern interpretations of Chinese cuisine. There is a good range of dishes on the menu that stay true to their regional eccentricities, including the dim sum selection. Palais de Chine prides itself on its Peking duck, another celebrated Chinese dish with regional distinctiveness.

Name: Continental
Address: 23F The Shilla Hotel, 249 Dongho-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, 04605, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If you are looking for a refined French restaurant with all the elements of classic French luxury, Continental is a solid bet. Perched on the 23rd floor of The Shilla Seoul, the restaurant is decorated in rich colors, with large tables and French empire chairs. What’s more, the bright dining room offers diners a fantastic view of the city. The meticulously prepared food is beautifully plated and served on two different set menus of your choice.

Name: L'Espoir du Hibou
Description: All of the elements at this bistro — from the food to the décor to the outdoor patio — fall into place to create an ambience that is immediately charming and oh so French! Consistency has been key to L’Espoir du Hibou’s longevity, not least when it comes to food. Chef Lim Ki-hak makes traditional French charcuterie like terrines and pâtés from scratch. The onion soup is outstanding, as is the classic duck confit. Terrace dining is a must during the warmer months.

Name: Pyeongyang Myeonok
Description: This establishment has been open for three generations, serving some of the finest bowls of Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles in the city. The long queue outside the entrance constitutes a part of the street’s daily scenery during the sweltering summer months. The clear meat broth is delicately seasoned and the buckwheat noodles have a pleasant texture, firm and not too chewy. Steamed dumplings and boiled pork slices, served warm, are also standout dishes.

Name: Restaurant Jueun
Address: 8F Gyeonghuidang, 36 Gyeonghuigung-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul, 03175, South Korea
Description: Situated behind Gyeonghuigung Palace, Jueun is a Korean restaurant opened by Chef Park Ju-eun, former head chef at Hansikgonggan, and his team. From design elements imbued with Korean aesthetics to elegant artifacts crafted in partnership with artisans to a media art wall occupying the length of the dining hall’s wall, every nook and cranny of the establishment highlights sincere preparation. The menu consists of traditional Korean dishes, ranging from imjasutang, a soup featuring roasted sesame seeds, chicken leg flesh, and Korean mint leaves, to a porridge made with abundant scallops, shellfish, shrimps, and fragrant beach silvertop. The eatery’s solid selection of wine and traditional Korean alcohol adds to its culinary delights.

Name: Vigneto
Address: 55 Suyeong-ro 522 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48299, South Korea
Description: Vigneto is the very first restaurant by an owner-chef couple who settled in Busan after studying Italian cuisine at ALMA, the renowned culinary school in Italy. The building is both their home and restaurant, with the wooden ceiling and furniture in the interior creating a cozy and warm vibe. An Italian wine bar, Vigneto combines authentic Italian cuisine with a rare Italian natural wine pairing. In particular, its pastas and hams, all housemade, boast exceptional textures and flavors. For foodies who seek to revel in food and wine amidst Vigneto’s snug ambiance, we recommend reservations (which are set at 30-minute intervals).

Name: Légume
Address: 2F, Sinsa Square, 652 Gangnam-daero, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06027, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: It’s no easy feat to invent dignified and alluring cuisine that is based only on plant ingredients. Yet, Chef Sung Si-woo at Légume pulls it off with panache. The chef’s fondness for veggies since childhood has led to a deeper understanding of vegetarian diets, which, coupled with his unique perspective, has given birth to his one-of-a-kind delicacies. In pursuit of 100 percent vegan cuisine, this eatery has perfected a refined vegetarian dining style that transcends the provision of mere plant-based meals, thereby highlighting the diversity and direction of Korean vegetarian cuisine. At Légume, sensorial contemporary cuisine meets the chef’s seasoned skills and is transformed into a vegan menu with a distinct identity and imaginative flavors. The evident truth is that the kitchen’s vegan fare not only appeals to vegetarians but also to people with a wide range of palates.

Name: Mater
Address: B1F, 16 Eonju-ro 154-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06021, South Korea
Description: With the focus on fermentation, Chef Kim Yeong-bin brings together the Korean and Asian cuisines he grew up with and the Western and Nordic cuisines he has been exploring as a chef, creating dishes bursting with unbridled imagination. Through the process of fermentation, the chef adds a unique twist to the flavor and texture of his ingredients, which are then exploited, sometimes subtly and at other times vigorously, for resonant and diverse expressions of fermented flavors. Such attempts reveal the kitchen’s intent and efforts to balance sour and umami taste profiles. Since Korea is where fermented foods are regular staples, it is all the more intriguing to witness Mater’s series of gastronomic experiments aimed at balancing the tastes and expressing the varied flavors of fermented dishes.

Name: Haenam Cheonilgwan
Description: Namdo cuisine, the cuisine of South Jeolla Province, occupies an eminent position in the diverse Korean culinary landscape. Haenam Cheonilgwan is a singular undertaking as it has steadfastly safeguarded Namdo cuisine through the generations. It branched out from Cheonil Sikdang, a Haenam-based diner with a proud history, and is headed by CEO Lee Hwa-young, a relative of the original founder. The asset that distinguishes Lee’s establishment from typical diners run by chefs is its tried-and-true flavors and recipes evolved and accumulated through the everyday vignettes she shares with her family. Korean cuisine has modernized to meet changing times, yet this food haven still strives to preserve the menus, recipes, and ingredients used when traditional ingredients were aplenty. Among the mélange of dishes that sumptuously fill your table, standouts bursting with Namdo flavors include banji kimchi (Namdo-style white kimchi), chili pepper kimchi with salted freshwater shrimp, and grilled short rib patties. The dining space consists entirely of private rooms suitable for a diverse range of occasions.

Name: Mustrue
Address: 29 Jwadongsunhwan-ro 433 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48114, South Korea
Description: Mustrue is one of the representative fine dining spots in Busan. Helmed by Chef Jung Jae-yong, a Busan native, it is covertly tucked away in a back alley of Dalmaji-gil Road. Open the golden door, and you’ll be greeted with a bar counter, where the chef masterfully handles everything from cooking to serving. By using unique local ingredients, such as Korean angelica seeds and short-fruit pimpinella, he creates European cuisine with a Korean twist. Chef Jung is passionate about maintaining the harmony between his culinary creations and Korean ingredients. And his passion is uncompromising – just as Mustrue, the eatery’s name, suggests.

Name: Sogonggan
Address: 4F, 47 Haeundaehaebyon-ro 298 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
Description: Sogonggan is a double entendre that can be read as “a small space” or “a space dealing with beef.” Its thoughtfully crafted menu is rooted in Korean cuisine. The chef spent many years perfecting his Western cuisine before making the switch to its Korean counterpart. He says the switching has made cooking more enjoyable and comforting as if he were finally wearing a tailored suit. Indeed, his sense of happiness is genuinely reflected in the fare. With Sogonggan’s elegant plating, original dishes, and refined Korean menu lineup, such as beef bone soup simmered in-house for 48 hours and pot rice, the “small space” moniker is unquestionably a misnomer.

Name: Gucci Osteria da Massimo Bottura
Description: Gucci Osteria was launched in Florence, Italy through a partnership between the chef Massimo Bottura and Gucci. The establishment’s third global branch after ones in Los Angeles and Tokyo has opened in Seoul. Its signature dishes include Seoul Garden Salad, inspired by Korea’s four distinct seasons; tortellini with rich-flavored, 24-month-aged Parmigiano Reggiano cream; and an Emilia Burger served in a petite pink box. The interior spaces colored in Gucci's signature green evoke a splendid verdant garden. Coupled with an assortment of cutlery and furniture that is both unique and classy, this fine diner’s authentic vibes bring out the indelible tastes of its cuisine to the fullest. A visit to the terrace is highly recommended as it offers a gorgeous view of Seoul’s cityscape accompanied by Italian wine.

Name: OPNNG
Address: B1, 22 Dosan-daero 34-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06049, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: At OPNNG, delight your taste buds with hard-to-find rare wines while relishing the overall vibe. The name symbolizes “the opening up of new taste vistas through gastronomy and wine.” Resembling more of a gallery than a wine bar or restaurant, this fine dining venue impresses patrons with an arch-shaped entrance, paintings by renowned artists, and a vast wine cellar that plays host to more than 500 different types of wine. It offers handmade pasta dishes and refined à la carte items.

Name: ON
Address: B1F, 42 Dosan-daero 92-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06070, South Korea
