Address: Clarke House, Farnham Road, Liss, GU33 6JQ, United Kingdom
Description: From the façade, you wouldn’t guess this was once a courthouse, but inside you’ll find a door leading to what was the judge’s bench. It’s a tiny place with exposed beams and a rustic style and is keenly run by a young couple. Cooking sees a little intricacy added to well-presented, country house style dishes.

Address: Elm House, High Street, Pooley Bridge, CA10 2NH, United Kingdom
Description: This immaculately kept bistro is set in the heart of a pretty Lake District village and its name is a reference to the year the property was first built as the local blacksmith’s. Menus showcase seasonal local ingredients in well-executed, modern British dishes. Convivial service and seven comfortable bedrooms further add to the appeal.

Name: Lima
Address: 31 Rathbone Place, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1T 1JH, United Kingdom
Description: Lima is one of those restaurants that just makes you feel good about life – and that’s even without the pisco sours. The Peruvian food at this informal, fun place is the ideal antidote to times of austerity: it’s full of punchy, invigorating flavours and fantastically vivid colours.

Name: Purslane
Address: 16 Rodney Road, Cheltenham, GL50 1JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Located just off the main high street, this modern restaurant has a comforting neighbourhood feel – and the service is equally relaxed. Fresh seafood from Cornwall and Scotland is combined with good quality locally sourced ingredients to produce interesting, original dishes with effective contrasts of flavour and texture. The lunch menu represents great value.

Name: Fuzzy Duck
Address: Ilmington Road, Armscote, CV37 8DD, United Kingdom
Description: Siblings Adrian and Tania – owners of toiletries company Baylis & Harding – took this place from boarded up boozer to welcoming, fashionably attired dining pub. Seasonal modern British dishes use good quality local ingredients; ensure you save room for dessert. Stylish boutique bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Harborne Kitchen
Address: 175-179 High Street, Birmingham, B17 9QE, United Kingdom
Description: Deservedly loved by local diners, this contemporary neighbourhood restaurant is a pleasure to dine in. The attentive team run the place with such passion and the cooking shows the kitchen's ambition across a choice of menus. A tiled bull on the wall is a nod to the building's past as a butcher's shop, with an open kitchen now providing the room's focal point. Desserts are a real highlight, such as a clever, rich creation centred around 20-year-old Pedro Ximénez sherry.

Name: Chiltern Firehouse
Address: 1 Chiltern Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1U 7PA, United Kingdom
Description: It’s easy to be cynical about celebrity-driven restaurants but this one has substance. The atmosphere remains glamorous and contagiously fun and it’s all run with understated efficiency. The menu focuses on North and South American dishes that are strong on flavour, with the grill used to good effect.

Name: Prévost @ the Haycock
Address: London Road, Wansford, PE8 6JA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in the orangery of a lovingly restored former coaching inn, Lee Clarke’s restaurant is bright and colourful, with bird cage chandeliers, pergolas and a faux olive tree. Choose from three set menus of up to 8 courses: imaginative dishes have rich, hearty flavours and are served by an enthusiastic team.

Name: Glebe House
Description: Chef-owner Hugo has returned to his childhood home – a former Georgian vicarage; now a 15-acre smallholding with a kitchen garden. Unfussy, flavoursome, farm-to-fork cooking uses prime ingredients; don’t miss the home-cured meats from their British Lop pigs. Endearing service and a house party atmosphere.

Name: The Brewers
Address: Lower Road, Rattlesden, IP30 0RJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A sympathetic refurbishment has left this village pub with a contemporary look but still plenty of rustic character. It was rescued by the locals and you’ll always find a group of regulars and their dogs by the fire. Pub favourites sit alongside more modern dishes and are cooked with confidence and ambition.

Name: 670 Grams
Address: The Custard Factory, 4 Gibb Street, Birmingham, B9 4AU, United Kingdom
Description: The urban-style monochrome palette and graffiti-covered walls tick all the zeitgeist boxes; ask for a spot on the mezzanine level opposite the open kitchen. The daily tasting menu offers creative, playful dishes with intriguing flavour combinations and contrasts in textures and temperatures.

Name: The Bailiwick
Address: Wick Road, Englefield Green, Egham, TW20 0HN, United Kingdom
Description: This pretty pub sits in a tranquil spot on the edge of Windsor Great Park. The à la carte menu best shows the chef’s experience, with dishes exhibiting attractive flourishes and complementary flavours; at lunchtime, there’s also a lighter bar menu available. Don't miss the Windsor Great Park venison.

Name: MJP@ The Shepherds
Address: 5 High Street, Fen Ditton, CB5 8ST, United Kingdom
Description: MJP refers to Mark Poynton, and The Shepherds is a historic village pub; now a cosy, intimate space. A mix of dish sizes lets you personalise the format of your meal. Flavours are punchy and rich, ingredients are in their prime and there are touches of creativity too. Modern bedrooms are simply furnished.

Name: COOK HOUSE
Address: Foundry Lane Studios, Foundry Lane, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE6 1LH, United Kingdom
Description: After opening a shipping container café, local food blogger Anna Hedworth crowdfunded this stripped-back, industrial-style restaurant with a pleasant terrace and a relaxed feel. Dinner is the main event, with many of the vibrant, fiercely seasonal dishes cooked on the hibachi barbeque.

Name: E. STREET Bar & Grill
Address: New Street, Petworth, GU28 0AS, United Kingdom
Description: Behind a 17C red-brick façade lies a light and airy, contemporary brasserie deluxe. Start with a seasonal cocktail then choose from a range of Mediterranean-influenced dishes and meat or fish from the grill; the grass-fed Hampshire steaks are a hit. The courtyard terrace is a great spot come summer.

Name: Alford Arms
Description: An attractive Victorian pub beside the village green. The menu follows the seasons and offers a broad array of dishes, so alongside British classics you’ll find dishes with more global leanings such as imam bayildi.

Name: Beach House
Address: Turkey Road, Tramore, X91 Y521, Ireland
Description: Close to the beach in a small seaside town is this double-fronted Victorian residence looking out over a lovely garden – and in the basement, its owners lovingly run this sweet bistro. The concise menu of classic, flavour-packed dishes favours seafood and the cellar wine list has some interesting vintages.

Name: Bistro at The Boathouse
Address: Station Road, Henley-on-Thames, RG9 1AZ, United Kingdom
Description: Take in delightful Thames views through the floor-to-ceiling windows or from the lovely decked terrace complete with heated pods. Unfussy dishes are skilfully prepared and see the likes of soft shell crab rubbing shoulders with steak and chips.

Name: Adelina Yard
Address: 3 Queen Quay, Welsh Back, City of Bristol, BS1 4SL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The experienced chef-owners named their first restaurant after their old home. Sit at the chef's table to watch all the action or at the far end of the L-shaped room overlooking the quay. Attractively presented, well-balanced modern dishes are sometimes brought to the tables by the chefs themselves.

Name: Wildebeest
Address: 82 - 86 Norwich Road, Stoke Holy Cross, NR14 8QJ, United Kingdom
Description: Set in the heart of a pretty village and fronted by an attractive terrace, this former pub is now a laid-back restaurant. Modern menus range from a great value daily selection to an ambitious à la carte and an inventive tasting menu, and the refined, colourful dishes blend many ingredients to create pleasing contrasts of flavour.

Name: The Mariners
Description: Part of the Paul Ainsworth stable, this large and popular pub is the ideal spot for some hearty British food while on your seaside holiday. You can arrive in the picturesque village of Rock via the ferry from Padstow, before grabbing a seat on the terrace which boasts stunning views over the Camel Estuary. The extensive menu is chock full of Cornish produce – be it cheddar, monkfish or mussels – with a seasonal menu sitting alongside 'Mariners Classics' such as shepherd's pie and fish & chips. For dessert, you can't go wrong with a crumble.

Name: Rising Sun Inn
Description: This stone-built, 18C moorland pub boasts a cosy, characterful bar and a charming restaurant with exposed stone walls, a semi-open kitchen and local artwork on the walls. The original, highly seasonal British dishes make use of fine local ingredients, and the set lunch is a steal. It’s rurally set, so book a pitch on their campsite opposite and make a night of it.

Name: Y Polyn
Description: This well-regarded country pub sits on an old drovers’ road and is run by an experienced team. Sit downstairs and admire the tin tiles on the ceiling while supping a locally brewed ale, before tucking into unpretentious dishes like fish soup and crispy belly pork. Confidently prepared local ingredients feature heavily, and the cooking is both hearty and wholly satisfying.

Name: Hammer & Pincers
Address: 5 East Road, Wymeswold, LE12 6ST, United Kingdom
Description: The old water pump out the back hints at its days as the village forge but this is now a brightly decorated, intimate restaurant run with natural warmth by its experienced owners. Fixed price menus offer creative modern dishes overflowing with different textures and tastes. Boutique bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Counter 71
Address: 71 Nile Street, Shoreditch, London, N1 7RD, United Kingdom
Description: What was once a well-known local boozer is now a swish dining experience complete with a tasting menu and a Spanish marble counter. Dinner is served to all guests at 7.15pm, so be sure to arrive on time or you’ll miss out on the boldly flavoured, modern British cooking. Cornish seafood and Lancashire Goosnargh duck are among the top quality ingredients on offer, and are brought to life using mostly classic combinations. The bar stays open late, so a post-dinner cocktail is always on the cards.

Name: The Silver Cup
Address: 5 St Albans Road, Harpenden, AL5 2JF, United Kingdom
Description: This Victorian pub, dating from 1838, has been taken on by two Harpenden locals: experienced chef Matthew heads up the kitchen while Michael capably looks after the front of house. British racing green banquettes, leaded windows and a copper-topped bar give the place a comforting, traditional feel and assured modern British dishes deliver bold flavours. Sunday lunch is an event.

Name: Castle Inn
Address: West Street, Castle Combe, SN14 7HN, United Kingdom
Description: This charming inn makes a delightful pitstop, especially for those visiting the nearby motor racing circuit. The menu is just what you want to see in a place like this: a blackboard of daily specials and dishes that are punchy and full of flavour. In season, local game is always worth ordering and the desserts are consistently good too. The building dates back to the 12th century and boasts many original features; comfortable, immaculately appointed bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Fernery
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set inside The Grove, one of the finest country house hotels in Wales, the Fernery is a nature-inspired restaurant that brings the outside in. It’s a proudly Welsh place, with a tasting menu (available in 5 or 8 courses) that showcases the best produce the locale has to offer, including ingredients from their own gardens. Dishes come with incredible levels of detail that belie the understated, somewhat cryptic menu descriptions like “The King’s Estate”. Finesse and originality run throughout, while the superb service ensures your experience unfolds flawlessly.

Name: Kahani
Address: 1 Wilbraham Place, Chelsea, London, SW1X 9AE, United Kingdom
Description: Service is charming at this smart, modern, easy-going basement restaurant. It’s name means ‘Story’ in Hindi; the story in question being that of chef-owner Peter Joseph, whose influences include his Indian heritage, the concept of sharing food picked up on his travels in Spain and the best of British produce.

Name: Bell at Skenfrith
Description: A well-run, restored 17C coaching inn in a verdant valley, offering hearty, classical cooking with the occasional ambitious twist, using ingredients from the organic kitchen garden. There's an impressive choice of vintage Cognacs and service is warm and unobtrusive. Super-comfy bedrooms have an understated elegance.

Name: Halfway at Kineton
Description: In a tranquil Gloucestershire village sits this 17C mellow stone inn, which offers a warm welcome and plenty of rustic charm. The appealing menu of fresh, well-cooked dishes is likely to include steaks, pies, freshly cooked fish and a ham hock to share. It’s also worth exploring the desserts, which include some modernised versions of classic puddings – like the fabulous caramelised hazelnut arctic roll. Cosy bedrooms are also available.

Name: Scorrybreac
Address: 7 Bosville Terrace, Portree, Isle of Skye, IV51 9DG, United Kingdom
Description: Simply furnished restaurant with distant mountain views and just 8 tables; named after the chef’s parents’ house, where he ran his first pop-up. Creative modern cooking uses meats from the hills and seafood from the harbour below.

Name: Parva Farmhouse
Description: This 17C stone farmhouse sits on a bank of the River Wye and is run by a friendly couple. Its simple, rustic interior comprises a spacious lounge and a cosy, welcoming restaurant with an inglenook fireplace. The gutsy, modern British cooking has a classic French backbone and the odd Italian or Asian touch. Booking is essential and the menu is sent a day in advance for pre-ordering. Bedrooms are comfortable and some have river views.

Name: Asador 44
Address: 14 Quay Street, Cardiff, CF10 1EA, United Kingdom
Description: Inside Parador 44, a boutique hotel offering a taste of Iberia in the Welsh capital, sits this dark and moody restaurant. It's divided into lots of different areas; the best spots are overlooking the asador grill, the cheese room or the glass-fronted wine cave. The menu has a focus on cooking over fire, with the likes of squid, cauliflower and rump steak getting the charcoal treatment. The wine list is almost exclusively Spanish.

Name: AO by Daniel Rogan
Address: Sunnyfields Farm Jacobs, Gutter Lane, Marchwood, Southampton, SO40 9FX, United Kingdom
Description: Daniel Rogan – son of L’Enclume’s Simon – is the chef at this relaxed, friendly restaurant named after the initials of his two children. Its location on Sunnyfields Farm is a clue as to the local, sustainable ethos that runs through the cooking; naturally, they grow much of the produce themselves and the seasons guide the menu. Dishes are pleasingly free from gimmicks, with careful preparation and attractive presentation on show throughout the tasting menu.

Name: The Cotley Inn
Description: Despite being just a 10 minute drive from the centre of Chard, there’s a wonderfully rural feeling that accompanies a visit to this former 17C farmhouse. The inn is nestled in a lush green valley overlooking the Blackdown Hills, with its converted outbuildings turned into bedrooms. The cooking offers dashes of creativity while still delivering satisfying pub dishes like slow-roasted pork belly. They take a local, seasonal and nose-to-tail approach to their ingredients, with animals reared on site and produce grown in the kitchen garden.

Name: Paris House
Address: Woburn Park, Woburn, MK17 9QP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A beautiful mock-Tudor house built in Paris and reassembled in an idyllic parkland location; enjoy a drink on the terrace while watching the deer. The seasonal tasting menu offers sophisticated, artfully presented dishes with creative texture and flavour combinations and subtle Asian influences.

Name: Unruly Pig
Address: Orford Road, Bromeswell, IP12 2PU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This modern dining pub is far from unruly; its owner – a former lawyer – sees to that. Wood panelling, interesting art and friendly team add a warm feel – but when the weather’s good, the terrace is the place to be. The Mediterranean-inspired cooking offers plenty of choice. The set menus are good value.

Name: The Hare
Description: Dating back to the 12th century, this Yorkshire stone inn makes for a lovely setting in which to dine. The building has been lovingly restored by owners Paul & Liz Jackson, who run the place with great pride. Paul is in the kitchen crafting a multi-course tasting menu that exhibits Japanese influences across creative and technically accomplished dishes. The intimate, cosy atmosphere – the dining room houses just five tables – and the addition of four splendid bedrooms all help to make The Hare an appealing destination for a weekend getaway.

Name: Crockers Chef's Table
Address: 74 High Street, Tring, HP23 4AF, United Kingdom
Description: Head chef Scott Barnard enjoys interacting with his guests and you’ll always find him centre stage in this striking copper-walled room, where diners sit around a U-shaped counter. Seasonal tasting menus feature creative, eye-catching dishes; arrive early for drinks in the dive bar.

Name: Swan Wine Kitchen
Address: Chapel Down Winery, Small Hythe Road, Tenterden, TN30 7NG, United Kingdom
Description: This rustic, modern restaurant sits above the shop in the Chapel Down vineyard and boasts a cosy lounge and a lovely rooftop terrace with views over the vines. It’s run by a friendly team and, naturally, wines from the vineyard feature – go for the suggested pairings. Ambitious modern dishes have a British heart and have a bias towards local ingredients.

Name: Pheasant
Address: Mill Street, Harome, YO62 5JG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Elegant hotel dining room with both classical and contemporary touches – along with a less formal conservatory and a lovely terrace overlooking the village duck pond. Appealing menus of seasonal dishes with a classical base and a modern touch. Skilful, knowledgeable cooking; smooth, assured service.

Name: Sandpiper Inn
Address: Market Place, Leyburn, DL8 5AT, United Kingdom
Description: You’ll receive a cheery Yorkshire welcome from the friendly owners of this characterful stone pub, set just off the main town square. Menus reflect the location, with the experienced chef carefully preparing tried-and-tested dishes; puddings are a highlight. Two ‘country-chic’ bedrooms offer excellent comforts.

Name: Jöro
Address: 0.2-0.5 Krynkl, 294 Shalesmoor, Sheffield, S3 8US, United Kingdom
Description: Jöro is a simple but stylish place, set within the Krynkl shipping container development and run by a keen husband and wife team. While using British ingredients, the tasting menus have a strong Asian base and feature some unusual combinations. If you really want to feel part of the action, then make sure to book a seat at the Chef’s Bench. The House of Jöro offers four bedrooms just a short walk away.

Name: Salutation Inn
Address: 68 Fore Street, Topsham, EX3 0HL, United Kingdom
Description: This characterful 1720s coaching inn has a surprisingly contemporary interior matched by understated bedrooms. Dinner takes place in the intimate dining room, while lunch and afternoon tea are served in the airy glass-covered historic courtyard – the perfect spot for a sunny afternoon. In the evening, choose between a tasting menu and a seasonally-themed à la carte, where modern dishes are well-judged and nicely balanced. Be sure to pick up some goodies from their deli and wet fish shop on your way out.

Name: Darleys
Address: Darley Abbey Mill, Darley Abbey, DE22 1DZ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Located in the old canteen of a 19C silk mill, Darleys offers a great view out over the river and the weir. It’s a stylish place with eye-catching décor; ask for a table on the narrow terrace or one beside the window on the upper level. Appealing dishes are creative and generously proportioned.

Name: Alice Hawthorn Inn
Address: The Green, Nun Monkton, YO26 8EW, United Kingdom
Description: This smartly modernised dining pub sits on a large village green where, as well as a duck pond, you’ll find the country’s tallest maypole. Hearty, well-presented dishes have classical roots and showcase local and garden produce. Welcoming service and smart bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Ox Club
Address: Bramleys Yard, The Headrow, Leeds, LS1 6PU, United Kingdom
Description: A former mill houses this multi-floor venue comprising a beer hall, cocktail bar, event space and restaurant. The latter boasts a wood-fired grill imported from the USA; rustic, smoky-flavoured dishes showcase Yorkshire ingredients.

Name: Bell
Address: High Street, Ticehurst, TN5 7AS, United Kingdom
Description: With top hats as lampshades and tubas in the loos, quirky is this 16th-century coaching inn’s middle name. Its charm and character is only enhanced by its location within a picture-postcard village that makes you feel like you've stepped back in time. The pub itself offers hearty dishes with a refined edge; look out for the 'All the Chicken' main course to share. The wine list features bottles from some lesser-known countries, while rustic bedrooms and luxurious lodges share the pub’s idiosyncratic charm.

Name: Mark Jordan at the Beach
Address: La Plage, La Route de la Haule, Beaumont, JE3 7YD, United Kingdom
Description: This modern brasserie on Jersey's south coast is split across several areas: there's a small lounge and bar; a paved terrace with bay views; and a dining room with heavy wood tables, modern seashore paintings and animal ornaments. Unsurprisingly, locally caught seafood is a feature of the menu – with produce like wing of Jersey skate on offer – but there are also hearty meat dishes to satisfy.

Name: Zuma
Address: 5 Raphael Street, Hyde Park and Knightsbridge, London, SW7 1DL, United Kingdom
Description: Zuma may now be a global brand, but this long-standing Knightsbridge restaurant was the originator of its informal, izakaya-inspired Japanese cuisine. Managing to still feel fresh over 20 years after opening, its home to a glamorous clientele who fit right in with the striking surroundings and bustling atmosphere. Sharing is a great way to experience as much of the extensive menu as possible – but if you have to prioritise, make sure you try the array of produce cooked on the robata grill, from tofu to chicken wings.

Name: Rubino Kitchen
Address: Kelvedon Road, Inworth, CO5 9SP, United Kingdom
Description: A red-brick former pub provides the new home for this restaurant, which has long been a feature of the local dining scene. A large array of menus is available and the fixed price lunch is a steal. The experienced chef knows how to get the best out of his ingredients and dishes burst with flavour from the effective combinations. They even run regular cookery classes for kids.

Name: Crown
Address: High Street, Bray, SL6 2AH, United Kingdom
Description: Formerly two cottages and a bike shop, this restored, timbered 16th Century building is now home to this dining pub in the gastronomic haven of Bray. Inside, the place has a traditional and cosy feel, accompanied by cooking with a similarly classical outlook. Expect the menu to include robust and flavoursome dishes like grilled pork chop or fish soup with the obligatory rouille, gruyère and croutons.

Name: Bluebells
Address: London Road, Ascot, SL5  0PU, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a degree of opulence to this popular restaurant housed inside a whitewashed building. The striking dark green interior features glitzy rose gold panelling and distinctive tiling, ensuring the dining room feels a little bit special. Modern European dishes make use of effective, well-judged flavour combinations and there’s an assured level of technique in the cooking. Sit in the main room overlooking the fire pit or in the airy conservatory, while the smooth service team look after you with aplomb.

Name: Bass and Lobster
Address: Gorey Coast Road, Gorey, JE3 6EU, United Kingdom
Description: A former pub close to the beach houses this substantial bistro, where you’ll find plenty of regulars drawn in by the great value daily set menu. There’s always plenty to choose from here, including numerous daily specials and a good selection of fresh fish – and the faggots are a must-try. You can watch the island meats, vegetables and seafood being prepared through the kitchen window.

Name: Brassica
Address: 4 The Square, Beaminster, DT8 3AS, United Kingdom
Description: A pretty 16C house on a small town square plays host to this friendly, laid-back restaurant (sister to the homeware shop opposite). Constantly evolving menus list hearty dishes with punchy flavours and a refined edge; produce is from within 15 miles but influences come from the Med.

Name: Thackeray's
Address: 85 London Road, Royal Tunbridge Wells, TN1 1EA, United Kingdom
Description: A softly illuminated clapboard house; the oldest in town and once home to the eponymous author. Classic dishes have modern elements and feature lots of different ingredients. The moody first floor private rooms showcase local art.

Name: Daylesford Organic Farm
Description: There may be Daylesford cafés spread all around London now, but this is the mothership. Found in the heart of the Cotswolds, you enter this stylishly rustic eatery through the farm shop, before dining in a choice of areas: head to the Legbar for charcuterie and nibbles, the Old Spot for pizzas and wood-roasted specials, or the main Trough Café for something a bit more substantial. Everything is organic, with much of the produce coming from the on-site farm and providing a fabulous base for the flavoursome, well-executed dishes.

Name: Paco Tapas
Address: The General, 3a Lower Guinea Street, City of Bristol, BS1 6FU, United Kingdom
Description: Start with either a fine Spanish wine or a chilled sherry straight from the cask while sitting on the terrace of this buzzy tapas bar. Dishes are skilfully prepared, packed with flavour and include all the favourites, from jamón croquetas to tortillas where the rich, golden egg just oozes out. Those unfamiliar with the Spanish way need not fret, as the knowledgeable team will guide you through the menu from start to finish.

Name: Nobu London Old Park Lane
Address: 19 Old Park Lane, Mayfair, London, W1Y 4LB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: There are now Nobu restaurants stretching from Dallas to Dubai and Mexico to Melbourne, but this one was Europe’s first when it opened back in 1997. Like seeing a favourite popstar on stage, you can expect all the greatest hits, from seafood toban yaki to rock shrimp tempura and, of course, the dish that’s been copied a thousand times: black cod miso. There’s a decently priced weekday lunch menu and the service is smooth and confident.

Name: Ocean
Address: Le Mont de la Pulente, La Pulente, JE3 8HE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Perched in a hotel high above St Ouen’s Bay, is this smart, understated restaurant with crisply laid tables; ceiling fans and shuttered windows add a slightly colonial feel. The experienced chef creates modern menus which showcase the best of the island’s produce – seafood is a highlight.

Name: West House
Address: 28 High Street, Biddenden, TN27 8AH, United Kingdom
Description: Set in a picturesque village, West House comprises two 16C cottages. The heavily timbered interior hung with contemporary art is a mirror of the food, where classically based dishes are given a modern twist. Wines are local, service is refreshingly unpretentious, and bedrooms have stylish themes.

Name: Peacock
Address: Bakewell Road, Rowsley, DE4 2EB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: An elegant hotel restaurant where old mullioned stone windows, oak ‘Mousey Thompson’ furnishings and antique oil paintings are juxtaposed with modern lighting and contemporary art. Lunch offers traditional dishes, while dinner is more adventurous. Bedrooms are furnished with antiques.

Name: Soif
Address: 27 Battersea Rise, Wandsworth, London, SW11 1HG, United Kingdom
Description: A classic French bistro and wine shop are rolled into one appealing package at this rustic neighbourhood operation run by a friendly team. The satisfying dishes have a largely French accent, with some Mediterranean influences also coming into play, be it burrata or kalamata olives. The rotisserie chicken to share is something of a speciality, while the thoughtfully compiled wine list includes plenty of natural wines from artisan winemakers.

Name: The Gannet
Address: 1155 Argyle Street, Glasgow City, G3 8TB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: One of the stalwarts of the Finnieston dining scene, The Gannet is a proper neighbourhood restaurant run by a close-knit team. There are playful elements to the ambitious cooking and dishes are visually impressive throughout, available from either an à la carte – supplemented by specials – or a fixed-price 3 course lunch. The passion from both the kitchen and front of house teams is palpable, the latter proving to be both friendly and efficient.

Name: Kitty Fisher's
Address: 10 Shepherd Market, Mayfair, London, W1J 7QF, United Kingdom
Description: Named after an 18C courtesan, Kitty Fisher’s is a cosy, intimate and refreshingly unpretentious bistro; ask for a seat downstairs, in the somewhat Dickensian style room. Fresh, unfussy dishes are all about flavour – those cooked on the wood grill have added depth and character.

Name: Stoke Mill
Address: Mill Road, Stoke Holy Cross, NR14 8PA, United Kingdom
Description: Characterful 700 year old mill spanning the River Tas; the adjoining building is where the Colman family started making mustard in 1814. Confidently prepared, classically based dishes use good ingredients and flavours are distinct.

Name: Dining Room
Address: Pavilion Buildings, Rock Road, Rock, PL27 6JS, United Kingdom
Description: Immaculately kept, understated restaurant with modern seascapes on the walls; run by a friendly, family-led team. Flavoursome, classically based cooking features local seasonal produce. Everything is homemade, including the butter.

Name: Queens Arms
Address: Putt's Lane, Corton Denham, DT9 4LR, United Kingdom
Description: There’s always something going on at this hub-of-the-village pub, which comes with a modern look and immaculately furnished bedrooms. Country cooking evolves with the seasons and focuses on sustainable ingredients: veg is supplied by a villager, pork is reared locally and seafood is from the Jurassic Coast.

Name: Sexy Fish
Address: 4-6 Berkeley Square, Mayfair, London, W1J 6BR, United Kingdom
Description: Everyone will have an opinion about the name but what’s indisputable is that this is a very good looking restaurant, with works by Frank Gehry and Damien Hirst, and a stunning ceiling by Michael Roberts. The fish comes with various Asian influences but don’t ignore the meat dishes like the beef rib skewers.

Name: Benedicts
Address: 9 St Benedicts Street, Norwich, NR2 4PE, United Kingdom
Description: Situated in a bohemian part of the city, the modern bistro vibe perfectly suits this simply decorated restaurant that carries its unfussy ethos through into the cooking. Chef-Owner Richard Bainbridge is proud of his Norfolk roots and an ambassador for the region’s larder, and his understated dishes rely on top quality ingredients to lead the way. They serve a range of set menus, varying in length and with vegetarian and, on request, vegan options available. For those looking for a lighter bite, sit outside and order small plates from the Alfresco menu.

Name: Church Street Tavern
Address: 3 Church Street, Colchester, CO1 1NF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Down a narrow city centre street, you'll find this attractive 18th-century building; a restaurant sits upstairs, while below is a trendy bar serving cocktails and light bites. The extensive menu ranges from bruschetta to quesadillas – plus a roast dinner on Sundays, of course – and the kitchen team ensure the dishes deliver plenty of flavour. The passionately curated wine list isn't the longest, but it's well-priced and comes with helpful descriptions of the wines; bring your own bottle on Wednesdays to take advantage of half-price corkage.

Name: The Wild Rabbit
Address: Church Street, Kingham, OX7 6YA, United Kingdom
Description: Just down the road from the Daylesford Farm Shop is the Bamford family’s stylishly modernised country pub. Accomplished modern dishes have plenty of appeal, with natural flavours of their farm’s superb organic ingredients underpinning the menu. Luxurious bedrooms are delightfully understated.

Name: Gurnard's Head
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Surrounded by nothing but fields and livestock, this dog-friendly pub sports shabby-chic décor, blazing fires and a relaxed, cosy feel. The unfussy, classically based dishes are all the better for their simplicity; if the chefs have got a fresh, sweet fillet of megrim sole, for example, then they wisely don't get in the way of its natural flavours. The wine list is concise yet contains a good selection by the glass and spotlights interesting, lesser-known choices. Compact, antique-furnished bedrooms are available.

Name: Wellington Arms
Address: Baughurst Road, Baughurst, RG26 5LP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: At this smart cream pub they have their own herb and vegetable beds, keep sheep, pigs, chickens and bees, and source the rest of their meats from within 20 miles. Menus feature 6 dishes per course – supplemented by a selection of specials – and cooking is generous and satisfying. Smart, rustic bedrooms come with slate floors, sheepskin rugs and big, comfy beds.

Name: The Antidote
Address: 20 St James Place, Ilfracombe, EX34 9BJ, United Kingdom
Description: Arrive early for a stroll around the harbour before dinner at this sweet, glass-fronted shop conversion where brown paper covered tables contribute to a cool, modish feel. It’s run by a friendly couple with a passion for local produce, so the thoughtfully prepared set menu changes regularly. Well-judged dishes are modern in their make-up and packed with flavour. Bedrooms are contemporary and one even has a small terrace.

Name: Corrigan's
Address: 28 Upper Grosvenor Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 7EH, United Kingdom
Description: This smart spot, with its central Mayfair address and leather banquettes, makes a fitting flagship for the eponymous Chef-Owner. There's a clubby feel to the place, with dimmed lighting adding to the intimacy and Dickies Bar on hand if you're partial to a pre-dinner cocktail. Although there are subtle modern touches, the menu is largely guided by classical French techniques (pommes Anna, vin jaune sauce) and a pleasingly retro approach in dishes like the royal seafood cocktail, filled with sweet and meaty prawns.

Name: Pythouse Kitchen Garden
Address: West Hatch, Tisbury, SP3 6PA, United Kingdom
Description: This red-brick former potting shed sits within a Victorian walled garden. Start with a selection of snacks before choosing a main dish cooked over wood or charcoal. Vegetable dishes are the star of the show and cooking is natural, hearty and generous. You can stay the night in a converted shepherd's hut.

Name: Hakkasan Mayfair
Address: 17 Bruton Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 6QB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This seductive subterranean spot beckons you in through its discreet entrance on Bruton Street, immediately transporting you to somewhere altogether more thrilling. The ground floor is great for lunchtime dim sum, but if you’re here for dinner ask for a table on the lower floor, which has a more energising atmosphere. The extensive menus feature a roll-call of luxury ingredients, from whole native lobster to black truffle roasted duck.

Name: Marksman
Address: 254 Hackney Road, Tower Hamlets, London, E2 7SJ, United Kingdom
Description: With its quirky, brown-tiled façade, this pub has long been a local landmark; the wood-panelled bar retains the feel of a traditional boozer, while the first floor dining room is more modern. Simply cooked, seasonal British dishes are wonderfully fresh, well-balanced and full of flavour.

Name: El Pastor
Address: 7a Stoney St, Borough Market, Southwark, London, SE1 9AA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A lively, informal restaurant under the railway arches at London Bridge; inspired by the taquerias of Mexico City. Flavours are beautifully fresh, fragrant and spicy; don’t miss the Taco Al Pastór after which the restaurant is named.

Name: Sketch, The Gallery
Address: 9 Conduit Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 2XG, United Kingdom
Description: In 2022 artist Yinka Shonibare and designer India Mahdavi joined forces to unveil a striking new look and colour palette for this enduringly fashionable and efficiently run restaurant. The menu is equally original, mixing the classic with the esoteric. Afternoon tea is also a big hit with the bright, young things, who flock here with their cameras at the ready.

Name: Menu Gordon Jones
Description: This tiny, highly likeable restaurant has a relaxed, cheerful feel, which is a reflection of its easy-going Chef-Owner. The room is dominated by an open kitchen, where you can watch Gordon preparing creative, complex dishes. The daily changing surprise menu delivers punchy flavour combinations and several playful elements. He serves many of the dishes himself and chats with guests, adding to the feel that this is a very personal operation.

Name: Read's
Address: Macknade Manor, Canterbury Road, Faversham, ME13 8XE, United Kingdom
Description: An elegant Georgian manor house in landscaped grounds, with traditional country house styling, antique furnishings and lovely oil paintings. Classically based dishes have subtle modern touches and make use of seasonal produce from the walled kitchen garden and the nearby quay. Comfortable bedrooms are full of period charm and thoughtful extras provide a sense of luxury.

Name: The Fox
Address: High Street, Lower Oddington, GL56 0UR, United Kingdom
Description: Sister to The Wild Rabbit in Kingham and the Daylesford Organic Farm, this immaculately refurbished 19C Cotswold inn is bursting with style and character, boasting flagged floors, exposed stone walls and an impressive wood-fired oven. The menu covers all bases – from pizza to Hereford sirloin on the bone – and uses top quality ingredients from their estate in unfussy, generously sized, tasty combinations. Make a night of it with a stay in one of their stylish bedrooms.

Name: The Square at Porthleven
Address: 7 Fore Street, Porthleven, TR13 9HQ, United Kingdom
Description: In summer, bag a table on the terrace of this small harbourside bistro; in winter, cosy up and watch the waves crash on the harbour wall. Coffee and cakes are served late morning, before giving way to more substantial fare. The menu flies the flag for Cornish produce, with local fish like hake and plaice nicely cooked by the kitchen team. They also run the deli and ice cream shop next door.

Name: Howard Arms
Address: Lower Green, Ilmington, CV36 4LT, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Built from golden stone quarried in the village itself, The Howard Arms is very much a part of the local community. They open at 8am for coffee and breakfast, and hearty flavours are the order of the day on the appealing menu, where pub favourites are listed alongside dishes of a more global bent. Bedrooms come in a variety of styles.

Address: Trinity Gardens, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE1 2HH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Start with a gin from the large selection behind the zinc-topped counter then head through to the smart red and black brasserie. Menus offer a comprehensive array of confidently cooked classics; the ‘menu du jour’ is good value.

Name: Greyhound on the Test
Address: 31 High Street, Stockbridge, SO20 6EY, United Kingdom
Description: The picturesque town of Stockbridge plays host to this striking mustard-coloured pub with low beams, elegant décor and a wood-burning stove. The chatty team deliver appealing modern British dishes crafted from local produce. Homely bedrooms and a mile of River Test fishing rights complete the picture.

Name: BiBi
Address: 42 North Audley Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 6ZP, United Kingdom
Description: Chef-Owner Chet Sharma takes inspiration from his grandmothers (bibis) for many of the dishes served at this buzzy Mayfair restaurant. The Indian cooking comes in the form of a tasting menu, with an à la carte available at lunch too. Dishes are carefully prepared and provide a good depth of flavour, with fine British produce running throughout. Sit at the counter to get the full experience.

Name: Maison Bleue
Address: 30-31 Churchgate Street, Bury St Edmunds, IP33 1RG, United Kingdom
Description: A converted 17C house plays host to this passionately run town centre restaurant complete with an open kitchen. Cooking is classically French at heart but has modern and Asian touches. Seafood is a strength and you must try the excellent French cheeses – accompanied by some fine wines by the glass.

Name: Plough at Bolnhurst
Address: Kimbolton Road, Bolnhurst, MK44 2EX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Sit in the rustic bar, modern restaurant or lovely garden of this charming whitewashed pub with Tudor origins. Menus are named after ploughing terms: ‘The Seam’ makes use of offcuts from main menu ‘The Furrow’. British and Mediterranean influences combine and there’s a great cheese selection.

Name: Park Chinois
Address: 17 Berkeley Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8EA, United Kingdom
Description: Old fashioned glamour, strikingly rich surroundings and live music combine to great effect at this sumptuously decorated restaurant. The menu traverses the length of China, with dim sum at lunchtimes and afternoon tea at weekends. The delicious 'Duck de Chine' is roasted to order.

Name: Upstairs at the Grill
Address: 70 Watergate Street, Chester, CH1 2LA, United Kingdom
Description: Inspired by the steakhouses of New York, Upstairs at the Grill has a chic yet cosy atmosphere, courtesy of its mix of modern and retro elements. Prime quality steaks include porterhouse and bone-in fillet or rib-eye; the 5-week dry-aged cuts are from premium Welsh beef, and various rare breeds are sourced from around the world.

Name: Clos Maggiore
Address: 33 King Street, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2E 8JD, United Kingdom
Description: Bright and airy in summer and cosy in winter, Clos Maggiore is one of London’s most romantic restaurants; be sure to ask for a spot in the enchanting conservatory with its retractable roof. Seasonal, French-inspired dishes are joined by a wine list of considerable depth. The lunchtime and pre/post theatre menus are great value and are a hit with one and all.

Name: Barbican Kitchen
Address: Plymouth Gin Distillery, 60 Southside Street, Plymouth, PL1 2LQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An informal eatery in the Plymouth Gin Distillery (where gin was once distilled for the Navy). Brasserie menus offer a good choice of simply cooked dishes, with classic comfort food to the fore; vegetarians are well catered for.

Name: Heritage Dulwich
Address: 101 Rosendale Road, Lambeth, London, SE21 8EZ, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Heritage’ is key to the cooking at this Indian restaurant in a smart suburban shopping parade, where skilfully prepared dishes are knowledgably balanced, well-spiced and packed with authentic flavours. Dayashankar Sharma – who has led many of London’s best Indian kitchens – cooks alongside his son Anmol.

Name: Hoddington Arms
Address: Bidden Road, Upton Grey, RG25 2RL, United Kingdom
Description: ‘The Hodd’ is a characterful pub at the heart of the village, and offers a friendly welcome and charm aplenty with its rustic brickwork, exposed timbers and open fires. Understated menu descriptions belie the skill in the experienced chef’s well-crafted dishes. Be sure to save room for pudding!

Name: Shore
Address: 13-14 Alverton Street, Penzance, TR18 2QP, United Kingdom
Description: The experienced chef delivers an 'omotenashi experience' (Japanese for ‘the spirit of hospitality’) in an intimate venue. He works alone and presents dishes to all his guests at the same time, in a warm, engaging manner. The set pescatarian menu changes daily and showcases the finest Cornish ingredients in original, Japanese-inspired combinations.

Name: Caffè Rojano
Address: 9 Mill Square, Padstow, PL28 8AE, United Kingdom
Description: There’s always a lively buzz at this smart brasserie. The glass-enclosed terrace is a great spot and service is some of the friendliest around. An extensive menu keeps Mediterranean influences to the fore and has some playful touches; the ‘whoopsey splunker’ sharing dessert is a must.

Name: The Woodspeen
Address: Lambourn Road, Bagnor, Newbury, RG20 8BN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It might be set within a restored 19C farmhouse, but The Woodspeen has a contemporary feel, courtesy of an airy, Scandic-style extension with a vaulted larch ceiling. Menus centre on the seasons and bring together ingredients from the kitchen garden and the surrounding area. Arrive early for a drink in the intimate bar; the ‘25 Yards’ gin is crafted using botanicals from their garden.

Name: Buckland Manor
Description: This elegant formal dining room of a quintessentially English country house hotel comes with wood panelling, oil paintings and garden views. Passionately prepared, classically based dishes deliver well-judged flavours and refined modern touches. Begin and end your meal in one of the cosy lounges.

Name: Barshu
Address: 28 Frith Street, Soho, London, W1D 5LF, United Kingdom
Description: The fiery flavours of China's Sichuan province are the draw here, although numerous other regions of China are well catered for too. The menu highlights both new and signature dishes, enlivened by authentic spicing – the legendary chillies and peppers are imported directly from China – and plenty of these generously proportioned dishes are great for sharing. Carved wood and lanterns decorate the room.

Name: Lurra
Address: 9 Seymour Place, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1H 5BA, United Kingdom
Description: Its name means ‘land’ in Basque and reflects their use of the freshest produce, cooked over a charcoal grill. Choose tasty nibbles or sharing plates like 14 year old Galician beef, whole grilled turbot or slow-cooked shoulder of lamb.

Name: Rondo
Address: 199-206 High Holborn, Holborn, London, WC1V 7BD, United Kingdom
Description: Rondo with its open kitchen all down one side occupies a fair chunk of ground floor acreage within the Hoxton hotel and offers a fun night out. The chef is an alumnus of St John so expect cooking that is robust and satisfying, although the menu here is a little more international in its influences.

Name: Food Leigh-On-Sea
Address: 92 Leigh Road, Leigh-on-Sea, SS9 1BU, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away among the shops is this narrow restaurant with a rustic look, given a cosy vibe by the friendly, engaging manner in which it's run. The creative, eye-catching dishes are full of flavour and focus on sustainability and wellbeing. The menu format changes depending on when you visit, with surprise tasting menus for Friday and Saturday evenings, small plates from a specials board at lunch and all-day Thursday, and a roast lunch on Sundays. Vegans are well catered-for too, with plant-based options always available.

Name: Bow Room at Grays Court
Address: Chapter House Street, York, YO1 7JH, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away by the Minster and bordered by the historic city walls, this beautiful Jacobean house with luxurious bedrooms and a peaceful garden is something of a hidden gem. Enjoy an aperitif in the characterful wood-panelled gallery, then head through to the more modern restaurant with its large bow window. Seasonality, purity and freshness underpin the skilful, confidently restrained dishes that often use ingredients from their own garden. The service team have a natural charm and help to make your visit a memorable one.

Name: Red Lion at East Chisenbury
Address: Red Lion Freehouse & Troutbeck Guest House, East Chisenbury, SN9 6AQ, United Kingdom
Description: A pretty thatched pub on the edge of Salisbury Plain, made more characterful by a hotchpotch of decorative touches. The generously flavoured dishes demonstrate that this is a classically trained kitchen; the fixed price menu is great value. Well-equipped bedrooms have private terraces overlooking the river.

Name: Packhorse Inn
Address: Bridge Street, Moulton, CB8 8SP, United Kingdom
Description: Set near the green in a pretty village, is this smart modern pub named after the 15C flint bridge which spans the river. Understated modern dishes have subtle yet effective flavour combinations and use the best local ingredients. Ultra-stylish bedrooms have plush furnishings and roll-top baths.

Name: Orrery
Address: 55 Marylebone High Street, Regent's Park and Marylebone, London, W1U 5RB, United Kingdom
Description: A comfortable and handsome D&D restaurant located in converted stables that date from the 19C; it’s worth having a drink beforehand in the bar or on the terrace. Expect quite elaborate, modern European cooking; strong on presentation and with the occasional twist.

Name: Folium
Address: 8 Caroline Street, Birmingham, B3 1TW, United Kingdom
Description: This smart-looking restaurant in the city’s Jewellery Quarter is run by a two-person team. Ben is in the kitchen and the warm, genial Lucy is out front. The cooking, like the décor, is modern in approach and allows Ben’s personality to shine through in the flavours and presentation. The menu is largely seafood-based, which results in highlight dishes like Cornish turbot with a delicious Arbroath smokie liquor.

Name: Eckington Manor
Address: Manor Farm, Hammock Road, Eckington, WR10 3BJ, United Kingdom
Description: You’ll find this proudly run 13C manor house and its collection of characterfully converted barns located on a 300 acre farm. Attractive modern dishes showcase local ingredients in ambitious combinations – and for those who want to get hands-on there’s a cookery school. Bedrooms are stylish.

Name: Roketsu
Address: 12 New Quebec Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1H 7RW, United Kingdom
Description: Chef-Owner Daisuke Hayashi has created a little slice of Kyoto life here in New Quebec Street. His culinary training and background may have been traditional but he’s not averse to introducing the occasional contemporary touch to some elements of his 10 course kaiseki menu. If you want to make your own choices, there's also an à la carte available, along with a set lunch menu on certain days. The charming welcome, attentive service and the counter fashioned from 100-year old hinoki wood will transport you away from the hurly burly of city life.

Name: Thomas
Address: 3-5 Pontcanna Street, Cardiff, CF11 9HQ, United Kingdom
Description: Having spent time in London, Thomas is back in his homeland, at this elegant bar and restaurant in a leafy suburb. Open with a cocktail on the pavement terrace or in the dark, moody interior. Prime Welsh ingredients are delivered with restraint; the Muscovado tart is a must.

Name: The Pierhouse
Description: As locations go, it’s hard to beat: find a spot on the terrace to watch the ferry chugging across the loch and stay the night to wake up to the fabulous view. Traditional Scottish delicacies and fresh local seafood lead the way – opt for a platter and don’t miss the delicious mussels.

Name: BiBo
Address: 45 Curtain Road, Shoreditch, London, EC2A 3PT, United Kingdom
Description: This no-expense-spared, basement tapas-bar-cum-brasserie is Andalusian chef Dani Garcia's first UK venture; although it’s his 6th BiBo globally. It’s a great place for a fun night out: service is bright and engaging, dishes are designed for sharing and a seat at the counter creates an authentic experience.

Name: The Clarence Tavern
Address: 102 Stoke Newington Church Street, Hackney, London, N16 0LA, United Kingdom
Description: 19C architecture fuses with contemporary details at this lovely pub; head past the bar to the part-panelled, part-brick dining area where the doors open out onto a courtyard terrace. Boldly flavoured dishes arrive in gutsy portions. Try one of the natural wines and be sure to visit the deli before you leave.

Name: Land
Address: 30 Great Western Arcade, Colmore Row, Birmingham, B2 5HU, United Kingdom
Description: The Great Western Arcade in the heart of the city is home to this intimate restaurant, where the chefs harness the power of plants for their creative vegetarian dishes. There's an original streak running through the seasonally evolving set menu – which is largely vegan – alongside a scattering of pan-Asian influences ranging from sake lees to Thai tea. Wine flights are available to enhance the experience and the friendly service team will see to your every need.

Name: Il Borro
Address: 15 Berkeley Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8DY, United Kingdom
Description: From panzanella to cacciucco alla Livornese, pappa al pomodoro to pici all’aglione, it’s all about big Tuscan flavours – and big prices – at this glamorous Mayfair spot. The menu also offers a myriad of other choices, including pizza and crudi to satisfy allcomers. It’s an offshoot of Il Borro estate, owned by the Ferragamo family.

Name: Wild Shropshire
Address: 25-27 Green End, Whitchurch, SY13 1AD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Self-taught chef James Sherwin’s dream came true when he opened this endearing restaurant that’s the epitome of field-to-fork dining. He is alone in the kitchen, cooking for a maximum of 14 guests and working with micro-seasonal produce to craft the daily changing surprise menu. There’s a Japanese influence throughout the flavour-led cooking, including ingredients like furikake, kombu and yuzu, as well as a sake pairing. The passionate, welcoming team offer lovely, personable service.

Name: Watson and Walpole
Address: 3b Church Street, Framlingham, IP13 9BQ, United Kingdom
Description: A contemporary restaurant in the heart of an attractive market town; the appealing Italian menu offers flavour-packed seasonal dishes, with plenty of fresh pasta alongside meat and fish roasted in the wood-fired oven. An all-Italian wine list is well-priced, with most available by the glass. Service is spot-on!

Name: The Greyhound
Address: 33 Windsor End, Beaconsfield, HP9 2JN, United Kingdom
Description: This charming 17C former coaching inn retains many of its original features and owners Daniel and Margriet are natural hosts, providing friendly, attentive service. Eye-catching, modern dishes are refined yet hearty, with carefully crafted, classic combinations which burst with natural flavours.

Name: Sam's Riverside
Address: 1 Crisp Walk, Hammersmith & Fulham, London, W6 9DN, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced restaurateur Sam Harrison returned to the dining scene with this modern riverside brasserie beside Hammersmith Bridge. Daily menus offer an appealing selection of British and Mediterranean classics, including some great raw shellfish. Stock up on provisions at Sam’s Larder before you leave.

Name: Erst
Address: 9 Murray Street, Ancoats, Manchester, M4 6HS, United Kingdom
Description: A modern, industrial-style wine bar run by a group of friends, laid-back Erst offers something refreshingly different in the city. It specialises in natural, low-intervention wines – many of which you can buy to take home – accompanied by a selection of flavoursome small plates.

Name: Lazy Lobster
Address: 5 South Parade, Chew Magna, BS40 8SH, United Kingdom
Description: A charming local couple transformed the old high street hairdressers into this lovely little seafood restaurant complete with a wet fish counter. Choose from shellfish platters or small plates ranging from the classic to the adventurous. The great drinks list includes gin from their son’s onsite distillery.

Name: Larder
Address: 17 Bore Street, Lichfield, WS13 6LZ, United Kingdom
Description: ‘All flavour, no pomp’ is the tagline at this relaxed, warmly run restaurant – and that’s exactly what you’ll get. Sit in the boldly decorated first floor restaurant or book a seat at the chefs table to be close to the action. Attractively presented modern dishes are sure to satisfy.

Name: Next Door
Address: 68 Main Street, Frodsham, WA6 7AU, United Kingdom
Description: A family business has been run on this 17th Century premises for three generations. For many years it was a butcher's shop, the current incarnation of which now sits two doors down, and today Sommelier Vicki has taken on the mantle to run it as this sweet restaurant with her husband Richard. His dishes are founded on excellent quality ingredients, with the meat from the family butcher's unsurprisingly being a stand-out – like the supremely flavoursome Welsh Black beef. Low-ceilinged rooms and exposed beams add to the charm.

Name: Ollerod
Address: 3 Prout Bridge, Beaminster, DT8 3AY, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This attractive stone inn provides a charming setting in which to enjoy the team’s accomplished, classically based cooking. Choose from a seat in the bar, the dining room or the pretty walled garden in the summer months; wherever you sit, you can enjoy an appealing range of dishes that make good use of produce from the South West. Nine individually styled bedrooms are available if you want to stay the night.

Name: Restaurant Meudon
Address: Maenporth Road, Mawnan Smith, TR11 5HT, United Kingdom
Description: Imposing granite pillars and neatly laid tables help to bring an air of classical elegance to this restaurant inside the Hotel Meudon. The dining room overlooks impressive mature sub-tropical gardens, which also contribute to the all-round lovely setting. The concise, daily changing menu is Cornish at heart, especially when it comes to seafood. Dishes like Mylor crab filo tart are understated yet well-executed and wholly enjoyable.

Name: Zafferano
Address: 16-18 Lowndes Street, Belgravia, London, SW1X 9EY, United Kingdom
Description: This long-standing Italian restaurant with a pavement terrace has become something of a Belgravia institution. The reassuringly familiar – if rather steeply priced – dishes take their inspiration from all over Italy, bringing together just a handful of top quality ingredients and allowing them to shine.

Name: Catch at The Old Fishmarket
Address: 1 Custom House Quay, Weymouth, DT4 8BE, United Kingdom
Description: Originally due to open on the first day of the 2020 lockdown, this fish shop and restaurant is a living, breathing testament to the power of determination. Now flourishing in its Portland stone, Grade II listed building, the kitchen's skill is most evident in allowing top-end produce like glistening monkfish tail to thrive unadorned, while employing impressive creativity to elevate less glamorous cuts – as evidenced by the crispy cod's cheek in a tomato and crab sauce. The set menu varies in length depending on the day and time of your visit, but the main course is always the catch of the day.

Name: The Windmill
Address: Chatham Green, Little Waltham, CM3 3LE, United Kingdom
Description: Chef-Owner Tom Clarke built up an impressive resume before returning to his Essex roots to open this lovely village inn with his partner. After a charming welcome from Nancy into the characterful interior, where a small bar still serves some local drinkers, it’s time to enjoy the hearty yet refined cooking. Classical flavour and texture combinations run throughout a menu served well by quality produce, with desserts like dark chocolate crémeux proving a real highlight.

Name: Benoli
Address: 5 Orford Street, Norwich, NR1 3LE, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Benoli’ might have an Italian ring to it but this three-floored restaurant is actually named after chef-owner Oliver and his brother Ben. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming and the appealing menu offers something for everyone – highlights include the homemade pastas and delicious desserts.

Name: The Three Horseshoes
Description: Large fireplaces, stone floors and whitewashed walls feature inside this renovated 17C pub. The pared-back décor is joined by similarly straightforward and equally appealing cooking that includes hearty dishes like rabbit pie and mince on toast. This approach allows the ingredients to speak for themselves, with local Somerset produce a feature. Five bedrooms add to the inn’s appeal, as do an attractive terrace and small walled garden.

Name: The Sparsholt
Address: Watery Lane, Sparsholt, OX12 9PL, United Kingdom
Description: Set in a rural hamlet, this Cotswold stone inn – sister to The Woodspeen near Newbury – has a clean, contemporary style, and is run by a friendly team. In summer, dine al fresco on the lovely rear terrace. Unfussy modern dishes have some Mediterranean influences and complementary textures and flavours. Comfy bedrooms in a converted barn complete the picture.

Name: The Baiting House
Description: In the 19C this was home to a wheelwright; then it was a stop for drovers and waggoners to enjoy a quick snack or ‘bait’; now it’s a friendly country pub welcoming allcomers with its rustic look and friendly atmosphere. The assured yet understated modern British dishes are well priced and nicely balanced and, most importantly, deliver bags of flavour. Make a night of it and book a lodge with a hot tub.

Name: The Angel
Address: 2 South Embankment, Dartmouth, TQ6 9BH, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced chef Elly Wentworth is at the helm of this iconic riverside restaurant; a smart yet informal space set on the ground floor of a historic building looking out onto the harbour. Accomplished, boldly flavoured dishes showcase the best produce from within a 30-mile radius. Service is friendly and efficient. Tasting menu only on Friday and Saturday evenings.

Name: Cora Pearl
Address: 30 Henrietta Street, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2F 8NA, United Kingdom
Description: Sister to Kitty Fisher’s – and similarly named after an infamous courtesan – this elegant restaurant is set in a characterful townhouse just round the corner from what's affectionately known as “The Actors’ Church”. Inside, there’s a buzz to the atmosphere and a rich, cosy bistro feel; the concise menu focuses on seasonal British produce in fresh, unfussy and boldly flavoured dishes. Service is smooth and attentive.

Name: Tyddyn Llan
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A husband and wife team run this attractive, slate-built former shooting lodge in a pretty valley location. Start with a drink in an antique-filled lounge or on the terrace overlooking the lovely gardens, before choosing from wide-ranging menus that mix classic and modern dishes. The cooking is satisfying and wholesome, and the wine list offers a good breadth of options. Service comes from a friendly team and there are elegant bedrooms for those wishing to stay the night and explore the area.

Name: Bob Bob Ricard City
Address: Level 3, 122 Leadenhall Street, City of London, London, EC3V 4AB, United Kingdom
Description: Sister to the iconic Soho original is this impressively ostentatious brasserie deluxe, set on the third level of the Cheesegrater building. Ensconce yourself in a booth, find the button and ‘Press for Champagne’. The classic French dishes are hearty and full of flavour with some luxury touches; for dessert, the tarte Tatin is a must.

Name: Ginger Fox
Address: Muddleswood Road, Albourne, Henfield, BN6 9EA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated on the edge of the woods, this long-standing thatched pub is full of character and you can't help but be carried away by the team's cheerful energy. It's run by the Gingerman Group, primarily based in Brighton, with this acting as their country outpost hidden away in the South Downs. Pubby favourites like Welsh rarebit or prawns with Marie Rose sauce are all present and correct, as are dishes with a little more flair; whatever you choose, the kitchen will lavish the same care upon it. The wine list includes some locally grown options.

Name: The Angel Inn
Address: Polstead Street, Stoke-by-Nayland, CO6 4SA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This red-brick former pub is over 500 years old and is now benefitting from the complete restoration its owners have given it. The stylish restaurant is divided into several rooms – and fans of wooden beams and open fireplaces won’t be disappointed. The Spanish-born chef applies some subtle influences from his homeland in the cooking, lending a boldness of colour and flavour to many a dish. Equal attention to detail has been applied to the decoration of the bedrooms.

Name: Three Chimneys & The House Over-By
Address: Colbost, Dunvegan, Isle of Skye, IV55 8ZT, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Immaculately kept crofter’s cottage in a stunning lochside setting. Contemporary art hangs on exposed stone walls in the characterful low-beamed dining rooms. Modern Scottish menus showcase good regional ingredients and seafood from local waters is a highlight. Spacious, split-level bedrooms are stylishly understated and the residents’ lounge has a great outlook.

Name: Sapori
Address: 40 Stadon Road, Anstey, LE7 7AY, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This sleek, modern, former Victorian Working Men’s Club is proudly run by a passionate Italian family. Sapori means ‘flavour’ and there’s certainly plenty of it in the refined, authentic dishes which centre around their home city of Naples. Service – from the chef’s brother-in-law – is charming.

Name: Samuel's
Address: 10 Swinton Road, Swinton, HG4 4JH, United Kingdom
Description: The magnificent Swinton Estate looks like the platonic ideal of a British country retreat. The commanding country house and surrounding grounds play host to a hotel, a spa, a cookery school and 20,000 acres of farmland – crucially, it also has a restaurant befitting of its grandeur. A gold detailed ceiling and carved wooden fireplace make the dining room an opulent setting for boldly flavoured, generously portioned dishes that still retain a lightness of touch. Sustainability plays a large role, with lots of produce coming from the estate.

Name: Fontana
Address: 61a High Street, Holywood, BT18 9AQ, United Kingdom
Description: A cheery welcome from the chefs in the open kitchen greets all-comers at this long-standing but reenergised first floor restaurant. There’s an appealing flexibility to the menus on offer, with cooking that is crisp, modern and effective – and it’s almost impossible not to find a dessert that will take your fancy. The room is smartly dressed and lightened by contemporary art.

Name: Slice
Address: 73-75 Eversley Road, Sketty, Swansea, SA2 9DE, United Kingdom
Description: A personal welcome from chef-owners Chris and Adam is just one of the charms of this sweet little restaurant hidden away in the Swansea suburbs. The passion and pride of the team comes across not just in the friendly service, but in the carefully prepared dishes centred around seasonally changing ingredients – whether that be fresh crab with watermelon or pan-fried sea bass with butter-poached lobster. Choose from the concise à la carte or opt for the tasting menu for the full experience, accompanied by a well-priced wine pairing.

Name: LeftField
Address: 12 Barclay Terrace, Edinburgh, EH10 4HP, United Kingdom
Description: Honest, intimate and sweet, this is a proper neighbourhood restaurant which focuses on the country's delicious seafood. Straightforward options from Scottish waters kick things off, with fresh mussels and oysters sitting alongside the likes of a zingy crispy squid with gochujang mayo. Comforting and flavoursome main dishes pair well with the homely surroundings, where you can relax with some super views of Bruntsfield Links and The Meadows.

Name: Purple Poppadom
Address: 185a Cowbridge Road East, Upper Floor, Cardiff, CF11 9AJ, United Kingdom
Description: Enter via the glass door between the shop fronts and head up to a smart, sleek room with abstract murals, exposed brick walls and blonde wood chairs. Classic combinations are cooked in a refined modern style and given a personal twist; the seafood dishes are popular.

Name: Felin Fach Griffin
Address: Felin Fach, Brecon, LD3 0UB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Warmth and character abound at this traditional pub. Relax on a sofa beside the fire with a pint of local beer, then head for the Library or Snug to dine. The organic kitchen garden provides herbs, veg and fruit for the simple, unfussy dishes. Cosy bedrooms come with good extras and are dog friendly.

Name: Sun Inn
Address: High Street, Dedham, CO7 6DF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A characterful yellow inn with an appealing shabby-chic style, located in a picturesque spot in the heart of Constable Country. The highly seasonal menu offers generous Mediterranean-inspired dishes and the well-chosen wine list offers plenty by the glass. Bedrooms are cosy – two have a modern New England style.

Name: The Idle Rocks
Address: Harbourside, St Mawes, TR2 5AN, United Kingdom
Description: This stylish, relaxed restaurant – running the entire length of the Idle Rocks hotel – offers superb bay views, and the water laps at its fabulous terrace. Refined, eye-catching dishes feature some fine Cornish ingredients and exhibit a wealth of flavours and textures. For the full experience go for the Signature menu.

Name: Stones
Address: 1c Dale Road, Matlock, DE4 3LT, United Kingdom
Description: Negotiate the steep steps down to this small riverside restaurant and head for the front room with its floor to ceiling windows or the delightful rear terrace which offers wonderful views. Unfussy, modern British dishes are attractively presented and display the odd Mediterranean touch.

Name: Feathers Inn
Address: Hedley on the Hill, NE43 7SW, United Kingdom
Location: Hedley on the Hill, United Kingdom
Description: A good pub can be a hub of the community, and so it is with this warm, welcoming inn set on a steep hill in the centre of a characterful village. The menus incorporate some international touches, but at heart the cooking is traditional, gutsy and proudly local. Ingredients ranging from roe deer to fresh fruit come from the surrounding area; look out for choices like beef flank cooked in ale if you're after something particularly rich and hearty.

Name: Rafters
Address: 220 Oakbrook Road, Nether Green, Sheffield, S11 7ED, United Kingdom
Description: Exposed beams and brick add character to this stylish first floor restaurant, which offers set 4 and 6 course menus of modern, richly flavoured dishes; cooked with enthusiasm and served with pride. Wines are usefully listed by their style and characteristics. For the full experience book the chef’s table.

Name: Old Vicarage
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A delightful former vicarage in a semi-rural spot on the city’s edge. Two fixed price menus offer sophisticated dishes with assured flavours and subtle modern influences; the ‘Prestige’ best showcases the chef’s abilities.

Name: Freemasons
Address: 8 Vicarage Fold, Wiswell, BB7 9DF, United Kingdom
Description: This delightful pub is tucked down a narrow lane in a lovely Ribble Valley village. Downstairs it’s all flagged floors, low beams and open fires, while the antique-furnished upstairs is a little more elegant. Chef-Owner Steven Smith has his own distinct style, often blending numerous flavours, textures and cuisines in one dish – steamed sea bass with Thai mussel curry and tempura tenderstem broccoli, for example. For something a little different, explore the experiences available in "Mr Smith's", like the chef's table and the kitchen bench.

Name: St Kew Inn
Description: A characterful, 15C country pub with flagged floors, wooden beams and an open fire, set in a tranquil, quintessentially English location. Menus offer a wide range of appealing, good value dishes, with an emphasis on local ingredients cooked over a wood fire. Be sure to order a beer from the wooden casks behind the bar.

Name: The Conservatory
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Titchwell Manor’s formal dining room is a bright, airy space looking out over the walled gardens. Cooking champions local ingredients with seafood from Brancaster Staithe and meat and game from local estates. Unfussy modern classics focus on natural flavours, using a less-is-more approach.

Name: HOME
Address: 3 Brewery Place, Leeds, LS10 1NE, United Kingdom
Description: Black is the new black here at HOME, from the flooring to the décor, the furniture to the crockery – and even the staff uniforms. But there’s nothing monochrome about the cooking; the 5 and 8 course tasting menus are made up of creative, ambitious dishes, which are occasionally served by the chefs themselves. The artwork changes along with the menus in order to match the theme and add to the theatre.

Name: Green Island
Address: Saint Clement, Green Island, JE2 6LS, United Kingdom
Description: Friendly, personally run restaurant with a terrace and beachside kiosk; the southernmost restaurant in the British Isles. Mediterranean-influenced dishes and seafood specials showcase island produce. Flavours are bold and perfectly judged.

Name: Gilpin Spice
Address: Crook Road, Bowness-on-Windermere, LA23 3NE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Cumbria was a key player in the spice trade and this slate restaurant in the grounds of Gilpin Hotel is inspired by that history. Enter the colourful rooms via wooden walkways built over stone-filled pools, then follow the Silk Road from Cumbria to Asia on the extensive menu – where many of the vibrant dishes are designed for sharing. A seat on one of the comfortable kitchen counter couches is the best place to feel part of the action.

Name: Samphire
Address: 7-11 Don Street, Saint Helier, JE2 4TQ, United Kingdom
Description: This buzzy all-day brasserie deluxe has a striking colour scheme which takes in blue velour banquettes and yellow leather chairs. Cooking adopts a modern approach and there’s a distinct Mediterranean influence. Island ingredients are to the fore and the oysters are something of a feature.

Name: Lorne
Address: 76 Wilton Road, Victoria, London, SW1V 1DE, United Kingdom
Description: They keep things honest at this narrow little restaurant and you can see the pay-off: a dining room full of happy customers, who are a mix of locals, tourists and business types. Staff are on the ball and well-versed on the menu, while the classically trained kitchen sends forth reliable and consistently good dishes, like Cornish cod with smoked eel, and chocolate delice with cookie crumble. The lunch and early evening menus are very good value.

Name: Grey's
Address: Easton Grey, Malmesbury, SN16 0RB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sitting within the luxurious Whatley Manor Hotel & Spa, but with a feel all of its own, is this elegant grey-hued restaurant. It presents a slightly less formal alternative to The Dining Room, but is run with the smooth efficiency one would expect of this hotel. Salad and vegetables from the kitchen garden feature on modern menus with a British bias. Ask for a booth or dine in the garden in the summer months.

Name: Sun Inn
Address: 6 Market Street, Kirkby Lonsdale, LA6 2AU, United Kingdom
Description: A charming village on the Cumbria and North Yorkshire border plays host to this equally delightful pub; start your evening with a stroll along the river, then enjoy a local beer in the characterful stone-walled bar, before dinner in the smart restaurant. Lunch sees small plates and pub classics, while dinner steps up a gear with refined dishes which let the true flavours of the ingredients shine. Cosy bedrooms blend original features with modern furnishings.

Name: Kilpeck Inn
Description: A popular pub which narrowly escaped being turned into private housing thanks to the villagers’ valiantly fought ‘Save Our Pub’ campaign. Its spacious interior and bedrooms are smart, modern and characterful, with impressive green credentials. Menus offer locally sourced meats and old fashioned puddings.

Name: White Hart
Address: Main Road, Fyfield, OX13 5LW, United Kingdom
