Description: There’s a lot to love about this imposing 15C chantry house. There’s the three-storey, vaulted dining room for starters, joined by a cosy open-fired bar and a minstrels’ gallery, while outside you’ll find a terrace, a vegetable garden and an outdoor kitchen with wood-fired oven. The cooking is guided by their own seasonal produce, with both British and Mediterranean influences on the flavoursome, carefully prepared dishes. The friendly service team run the restaurant well.

Name: Westwood
Address: New Walk, Beverley, HU17 7AE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This smart, modern restaurant occupies one wing of an impressive Grade II listed former courthouse and has a sheltered courtyard terrace for warmer days. It’s run with passion by twins Michele and Matthew, whose menus mix traditional dishes with some more modern, creative choices.

Name: Hawksmoor
Address: 157a Commercial Street, Tower Hamlets, London, E1 6BJ, United Kingdom
Description: It would be easy to pass by this unassuming-looking restaurant but open the door and you’ll be greeted by a friendly team and an appealingly buzzy atmosphere. It’s all about British beef here: hand-butchered, hung for 35 days and cooked to perfection. Flavours are sublime; the tail fillet is worth a try.

Name: Oyster Box
Address: La Route de la Baie, Saint Brelade, JE3 8EF, United Kingdom
Description: The smart tableware gives a clue as to this restaurant’s owners: the famous Jersey Pottery. It’s light and airy and it sits on the promenade, with a terrace affording superb views over St Brelade’s Bay. Fish and shellfish lead the way, with oysters a speciality. The décor is stylish and the service, friendly.

Name: Chadwicks Inn
Address: High Lane, Maltby, TS8 0BG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Well-prepared dishes, a wide-ranging wine list and smartly attired staff add a touch of formality to this village pub – although the locals aren't forgotten and can still come just for a drink in the bar. The modern pub cooking comes in the form of colourful and eye-catching dishes that show a clear understanding of flavours, with steaks a feature. The ‘market menu’ available during certain hours offers great value for money, and their monthly wine tasting evenings sell out in no time.

Name: 63 Degrees
Address: 104 High Street, Manchester, M4 1HQ, United Kingdom
Description: One glance at the menu and you could be convinced you're in Paris, not Manchester's bustling Northern Quarter. Courtesy of a French Chef-Owner, the menu is filled with the likes of escargots, chou farçi and crème brûlée, all of which are delivered with strong classical technique. Interestingly, there's also a burger section to the menu, where the likes of lobster and pigeon join the usual beef option. This is a family affair, with the Chef-Owner's son serving out front, and has the feel of a true neighbourhood restaurant.

Name: Bob Bob Ricard
Address: 1-3 Upper James Street, Soho, London, W1F 9DF, United Kingdom
Description: A small version of a glamorous grand salon; booth seating and tableside ‘Press for Champagne’ buttons add a sense of exclusivity. Menus open with vodka shots at -18° along with caviar – a clue as to the owner’s nationality – then move on to everything from salmon tartare to beef Wellington to share.

Name: Stravaigin
Address: 28 Gibson Street, Glasgow City, G12 8NX, United Kingdom
Description: Their motto here is ‘think global, eat local’ and this clear to see from the menu, where their homemade haggis sits alongside an array of ingredients from multiple Asian cuisines – be it furikake from Japan, tom yum from Thailand or lentil dahl from India. A pleasingly unfussy quality runs throughout these dishes, which are tasty and carefully prepared. The ground floor has a shabby-chic café-bar style, while The Cellar is a more intimate affair.

Name: Roger Hickman's
Address: 79 Upper Saint Giles Street, Norwich, NR2 1AB, United Kingdom
Description: Personally run restaurant in a historic part of the city, with soft hues, modern art and romantic corners. Service is attentive yet unobtrusive. Cooking is modern, intricate and displays respect for ingredients’ natural flavours.

Name: Olive Branch & Beech House
Address: Main Street, Clipsham, LE15 7SH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Characterful village pub made up of a series of small rooms which feature open fires and exposed beams. The selection of refined British dishes changes daily, reflecting the seasons and keeping things fiercely local. These are accompanied by real ales, homemade lemonade and vodka made from hedgerow berries. Bedrooms are cosy and thoughtfully finished.

Name: Brawn
Address: 49 Columbia Road, Tower Hamlets, London, E2 7RG, United Kingdom
Description: Offering a warm welcome and robust, flavour-packed cooking, this is the kind of place everyone needs in their neighbourhood. The passionate team run it with a relaxed, upbeat vibe – sit in the back room to enjoy the buzz from the kitchen – and serve reliably tasty food that evolves with the seasons. The interesting wine list includes a number of organic options, as well as smaller producers and a good choice of orange wines.

Name: Melton's
Address: 7 Scarcroft Road, York, YO23 1ND, United Kingdom
Description: The walls of this cosy suburban restaurant are covered with murals of ingredients and happy diners – a nod to their passion for local produce at this well-regarded neighbourhood spot. Cooking is fresh and flavoursome, with a subtle modern style and well-judged contrasts.

Name: The Star Inn The City
Address: Lendal Engine House, Museum Street, York, YO1 7DR, United Kingdom
Description: This buzzy all-day brasserie sits within an old brick-built engine house and boasts a lovely terrace overlooking the river. Carefully cooked dishes are modern yet gutsy and showcase top Yorkshire produce, with local and seasonal influences leading the way.

Name: Henry's
Address: 4 Saville Row, Bath, BA1 2QP, United Kingdom
Description: The simplicity of the name is reflective of this laid-back bistro as a whole. It sits on a pretty pedestrianised lane and has a simple yet appealing interior, and chef-owner Henry runs it with passion and pride. Dishes are modern and original and include some interesting vegetarian options.

Name: Socius
Address: 11 Foundry Place, Burnham Market, PE31 8LG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: One meaning of the Latin word Socius is ‘sharing’ – and it’s all about sharing at this friendly restaurant. Sit on the steel-framed mezzanine level or the smart ground floor to watch the chefs at work. Unfussy modern small plates feature on a flexible, constantly evolving menu which offers plenty of vegetarian choices.

Name: Potters
Address: 2 Lansdown Road, Bude, EX23 8BH, United Kingdom
Description: Nikki and her team extend a warm welcome to both locals and tourists visiting this striking North Cornish spot. Behind the scenes, Oly is hard at work in the kitchen, crafting attractive, well-balanced modern dishes which showcase the finest Cornish ingredients. Seafood is a particular focus, with the likes of tandoori monkfish and whole Cornish sole sitting alongside a choice of fish to be battered then fried. Be sure to try the cocktails too.

Name: Rules
Address: 35 Maiden Lane, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2E 7LB, United Kingdom
Description: Rules delivers all the charm and character you’d expect of London’s oldest restaurant. Start with a drink upstairs in the glorious cocktail bar, before winding your way down to the ground floor with its assortment of rooms decorated with antique cartoons, drawings and paintings. The menu is unashamedly traditional – game from their own estate is a highlight, along with classics like braised rabbit, steak and kidney pudding, and classic desserts from the nursery end.

Name: Spring
Address: New Wing, Somerset House, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2R 1LA, United Kingdom
Description: Bright, white Spring restaurant occupies the ‘new wing’ of Somerset House that for many years was inhabited by the Inland Revenue. Under the aegis of chef Skye Gyngell, it serves fresh and unfussy Italian-influenced and ingredient-led food that you feel is doing you good as you eat it.

Name: Donostia
Address: 10 Seymour Place, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1H 7ND, United Kingdom
Description: Perch at the counter or sit at one of the tables in this fun, warmly run little spot and enjoy a selection of pintxos and tapas inspired by the food of San Sebastián. House specialities such as gilda, bacalao and txuleta are always worth ordering. Just one dessert is offered, but when it’s Basque cheesecake as wonderfully creamy as this, who would want anything else?

Name: Cartford Inn
Address: Cartford Lane, Little Eccleston, PR3 0YP, United Kingdom
Description: This riverside pub stands beside a small toll bridge and comes with a deli, an art gallery, a farm shop, and 5 greenhouses for all-year dining. Cooking is gutsy and many of the tried-and-tested classics come with a twist. The owner played a big part in the interior design, particularly the boutique bedrooms.

Name: Salty Monk
Address: Church Street, Sidford, EX10 9QP, United Kingdom
Description: Set in an old 16C salt house, this long-standing, proudly run restaurant is a pleasant blend of the old and the new – and is the type of place that’s always evolving. Dine in either the Abbots Den or the Garden Room, and choose 3 small plates for starters, followed by a flavour-packed, classically based main course. Alternatively, come for coffee and cake or afternoon tea. Bedrooms have good extras and there’s a gym and hot tub in the garden.

Name: The Oystermen
Address: 31-32 Henrietta Street, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2E 8NA, United Kingdom
Description: Covent Garden isn’t an area usually associated with independent restaurants but this bustling and modestly decorated little spot is thriving. From its tiny open kitchen come oysters, crabs and expertly cooked fish.

Name: Cambio de Tercio
Address: 163 Old Brompton Road, South Kensington, London, SW5 0LJ, United Kingdom
Description: With three restaurants within a stone’s throw of each other, Spanish-born owner Abel Lusa is well-known for promoting his native cuisine in this smart Kensington neighbourhood, and this is his flagship. The short, well-structured menu features all the favourites, from their house specialty – croquettes – and anchovies in pickled sherry to dishes to share such as Pluma Iberica. The wine list is a voyage around the wine-making regions of Spain, and service is friendly and engaging.

Name: Fischer's at Baslow Hall
Address: Calver Road, Baslow, DE45 1RR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: At the centre of impressive formal grounds sits this fine Edwardian manor house with charming bedrooms and a classic country house feel. Two dining rooms with an elegant, contemporary style are overseen by a formal service team; sit at the ‘Kitchen Tasting Bench’ to really be part of the action. Menus offer original modern dishes with Mediterranean influences.

Name: Cinnamon Bazaar
Address: 28 Maiden Lane, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2E 7JS, United Kingdom
Description: Vivek Singh’s Covent Garden restaurant provides relaxed, all-day Indian dining in a bright, colourful space with a marketplace atmosphere. The extensive menus are influenced by the trade routes of the subcontinent, with twists that encompass Afghanistan, Punjab and the Middle East. Start off with a selection of snacks and chaat, before moving on to larger plates like lamb rogan josh ‘shepherd’s pie’, which has become something of a signature.

Name: Oak
Address: 2 North Parade Passage, Bath, BA1 1NX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: What started out as ‘Acorn’ has matured into ‘Oak’, where a sustainable ethos feeds into the tasty, original vegetarian and vegan dishes served in unpretentious bistro surroundings. When dining in the front part of the restaurant, you'll find shelves adorned with produce from their allotment just outside the city – which provides around 40% of their produce. The well-priced small plates are designed for sharing and a 5 course ‘feasting menu’ is available at dinner.

Name: Dartmoor Inn
Description: You couldn’t meet a friendlier family than the parents, daughter and son-in-law who run this rustic roadside pub. It has spacious bedrooms and a cosy, shabby-chic style. The concise menu of pub favourites utilises the best of local produce and changes regularly to keep things interesting.

Name: Box Tree
Address: 35-37 Church Street, Ilkley, LS29 9DR, United Kingdom
Description: This iconic Yorkshire restaurant was established back in 1962 and continues to draw in diners today. It’s set within two charming, 18th-century sandstone cottages, and has a plush, antique-furnished lounge and two luxurious dining rooms. The cooking these days comes in the form of a modern, creative tasting menu featuring dishes like their take on an 'arroz negro'. Service is formal and professional, while there's a choice between the 'Sommelier's' and 'Premium' wine flights to accompany the food.

Name: Forelles
Address: Fishmore Road, Ludlow, SY8 3DP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An appealing conservatory restaurant offering lovely views over the hotel gardens and named after the pear tree just outside. Attractively presented dishes use local produce and modern techniques, and feature some unusual flavour and texture combinations.

Name: Bistrot Vérité
Address: 7 Liverpool Road, Birkdale, Southport, PR8 4AR, United Kingdom
Description: A friendly, bustling neighbourhood bistro, serving gutsy French dishes with a classic base, punchy flavours and the occasional international touch. It’s a family affair with Mum Michaela, Dad Marc and their sons all involved, either in the kitchen or front of house. Pop into their next-door bar, Petite Vérité, for pre or post-dinner drinks.

Name: Old Butchers
Address: 7 Park Street, Stow-on-the-Wold, GL54 1AQ, United Kingdom
Description: An old butcher’s shop with quirky décor, colourful chairs and ice bucket and colander lampshades. The menu offers plenty of choice, from old favourites to dishes with a Mediterranean slant, and the well-judged cooking comes with bold flavours and appealing textural contrasts. Save room for dessert!

Name: Sir Charles Napier
Address: Sprigs Holly, Sprigg's Alley, OX39 4BX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In summer start with an aperitif in the delightful garden; at other times, sit beside the log fire and get cosy in this quirkily decorated restaurant. The kitchen makes good use of quality ingredients to create dishes whose flavours are punchy and pronounced. The wine list is a labour of love.

Name: The Cadogan Arms
Address: 298 King's Road, Chelsea, London, SW3 5UG, United Kingdom
Description: There’s been a pub of this name here since 1838 and it has now been restored to its Victorian glory. Drinkers mingle with diners creating a real neighbourhood feel. The menu focuses on pubby favourites with a few retro classics thrown in and cooking is unfussy and eminently satisfying.

Name: Delaunay
Address: 55 Aldwych, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2B 4BB, United Kingdom
Description: The Delaunay was inspired by the grand cafés of Europe but, despite sharing the same buzz and celebrity clientele as its sibling The Wolseley, is not just a mere replica. The all-day menu is more mittel-European, with great schnitzels and wieners.

Name: The Parsons Table
Address: 2 & 8 Castle Mews, Tarrant Street, Arundel, BN18 9DG, United Kingdom
Description: This cosy little restaurant is named after its owners – an experienced husband and wife team who run it with passion and pride – and it’s clearly a hit with the locals. Confidently prepared, flavoursome dishes are founded on the classics and have a subtle modern style and an honest feel.

Name: Zoilo
Address: 9 Duke Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1U 3EG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The menus at this lively grill restaurant explore seasonal ingredients and regional specialities from across Argentina. The wood-panelled room is dominated by a U-shaped bar counter and bright red studded banquettes, which provide a striking contrast to the checkerboard floor. Typical dishes include sea bream ceviche, steaks from the grill and slow-cooked shoulder of lamb. The all-Argentinian wine list offers a great range, with many wines available by the glass and carafe.

Name: J.Sheekey
Address: 28-32 St. Martin's Court, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2N 4AL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Festooned with photographs of actors, and linked to the theatrical world since opening in the heart of theatreland in 1896, J.Sheekey's wood panels and alcove tables add to its famed intimacy. Accomplished seafood cooking includes shellfish platters and their legendary fish pie.

Name: Lighthouse
Address: New Road, Boylestone, DE6 5AA, United Kingdom
Description: The Lighthouse continues to shine brightly; this sweet, intimate restaurant is a popular spot so get your reservation in early! The self-taught chef’s seasonal set tasting menu offers ambitious modern dishes and a good selection of keenly priced wines accompanies.

Name: Yorebridge House
Description: This romantic restaurant sits within a stylish former schoolmaster’s house in the heart of the Yorkshire Dales, and offers lovely countryside views. Top quality British ingredients feature in attractively presented dishes with a personal twist. Book a bedroom with a riverside terrace and a hot tub.

Name: Eyas
Address: The Falcon, Castle Ashby, NN7 1LF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Forming part of the sprawling Castle Ashby Estate, this elegant restaurant sits within The Falcon – a Grade II listed former coaching inn that now serves as a 'countryside retreat'. An understated, natural colour scheme is mirrored by subtle flavours in the unfussy, fresh-tasting dishes. The well-pitched service continues the easy-going feel, while garden views enhance the overall experience.

Name: Scott's
Address: 20 Mount Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 2HE, United Kingdom
Description: Scott's is proof that a restaurant can have a long, proud history and still be fashionable, glamorous and relevant. It has a terrific clubby atmosphere and if you’re in a two then the counter is a great spot. The choice of prime quality fish and shellfish is impressive.

Name: The Butchers Arms
Address: Lime Street, Eldersfield, GL19 4NX, United Kingdom
Description: A thick wooden door salvaged from an old ship leads you into this sweet rural inn where hop bines vie for space with the locals’ tankards on low exposed beams. The menu is short but packed full of top quality seasonal ingredients and honest flavours lead the way. The friendly team create a warm, friendly atmosphere, and they serve the ales straight from the keg.

Name: Rocpool
Address: 1 Ness Walk, Inverness, IV3 5NE, United Kingdom
Description: A family owned and run restaurant on the banks of the River Ness; close to town and popular with the locals. Wide-ranging menus offer vibrant, colourful dishes that are full of flavour and have a distinct Mediterranean edge. The room has a modish feel.

Name: Upstairs at the Mill
Address: Tuddenham Mill, High Street, Tuddenham, IP28 6SQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A delightful 18C watermill overlooking a millpond; the old workings are still in situ in the stylish bar, above which sits a beamed restaurant with black furnishings. Good quality seasonal produce is showcased in modern dishes on the tasting menu and more classic dishes on the à la carte. The attractive outbuildings play host to some of the bedrooms.

Name: Café Spice Namasté
Address: 1-2 Lower Dock Walk, Royal Albert Dock, Newham, London, E16 2GT, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Todiwalas have relocated their popular restaurant further east in Docklands: it now occupies the ground floor of a modern apartment building and has a simple style. The menu comprises vibrant, colourful small plates to share, with old favourites like lamb samosas and duck sausage making an appearance.

Name: The Back Garden
Address: Willersey Hill, Broadway, WR12 7LF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The stylish Dormy House hotel hosts this chic and attractive restaurant; its floor-to-ceiling windows bringing the feel of the garden into the light and airy room. The concise menu offers a choice of modern dishes influenced by the Mediterranean. Locally sourced ingredients – including rare breed meats and garden produce – play their part in the flavoursome dishes.

Name: The Wilderness
Address: Unit B, 27 Warstone Lane, Birmingham, B18 6JQ, United Kingdom
Description: Self-proclaimed as ‘rock and roll fine dining’, this dark and moody restaurant brings something a little different to the Birmingham food scene. The all-black colour scheme extends from the décor to the staff uniforms, while punk, metal and everything in between blares out of the speakers. The cooking, for its part, throws together an array of flavours in an imaginative, playful style. A choice of two tasting menus can be accompanied by an interesting wine flight or creative non-alcoholic pairings.

Name: Lovage
Address: Bath Street, Bakewell, DE45 1DS, United Kingdom
Description: The chatty, informative team are sure to put a smile on your face when they enthusiastically explain the modern menu of top quality, seasonal ingredients. The building was once a stable block and the lovely wood-panelled walls of this cosy, laid-back room are now a listed feature.

Name: The Pack Horse
Address: 3-5 Market Street, Hayfield, SK22 2EP, United Kingdom
Description: Real ales and weekly quiz nights help this traditional stone pub to remain a true village local. Hearty pub dishes come with a refined edge and the Manchester (Scotch) Egg has become something of a signature. Characterful open fires mix with warm, contemporary décor, and it’s run by a friendly team.

Name: The Boat
Address: Walsall Road, Lichfield, WS14 0BU, United Kingdom
Description: This smart roadside hostelry continues to evolve with passionate chef-owner Liam Dillon at the helm. He has developed an on-site 'micro farm' where he keeps chickens and pigs, and grows fruit, vegetables and herbs. Outside the restaurant's own land, other local producers are used to power dishes like Staffordshire lamb with BBQ lettuce. Plenty of work goes into the cooking, with desserts such as cherry mousse with white chocolate and smoked hay ice cream standing out.

Name: Bhoomi Kitchen
Address: 52 Suffolk Road, Cheltenham, GL50 2AQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: You’ll receive a warm welcome at this sumptuous restaurant, run by the third generation of a family who settled here from India 50 years ago. The menu is mostly southern Indian with some BBQ dishes from the tandoor representing the north. Save room for the indulgent chocolate samosa.

Name: Brett
Address: 321 Great Western Road, Glasgow City, G4 9HR, United Kingdom
Description: Under the same ownership as Cail Bruich is this small, long-standing restaurant with a compact terrace. The dining room features a large counter wrapped around the kitchen where chefs are busy cooking on the open grills. The menu comprises around 15 simply cooked dishes which showcase the breadth of Scotland’s larder; if you get the chance, the mushroom XO linguini is a must. Natural wines accompany, and there's a relaxed, welcoming feel to the place.

Name: Fletcher's
Address: 27 Princess Street, Plymouth, PL1 2EX, United Kingdom
Description: It may be just around the corner from the Theatre Royal, but this warmly run restaurant is so much more than a convenient spot to eat in before curtain-up. From the good value lunch menu to the à la carte, the eponymous chef-owner, who is a local himself, knows how to cater for all tastes – and it’s clear that plenty of care and attention go into every dish.

Name: Café Bohème
Address: 21-23 Windmill Brae, Aberdeen City, AB11 6HU, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in a city centre side street is a restaurant run by a friendly team with a genuine desire to please. Given the name and the look of the place, you might have expected to find all the time-honoured French bistro classics, but the cooking takes a more creative and contemporary approach. If you want the full experience, go for the tasting menu; they also offer a separate vegan menu.

Name: Savoy Grill
Address: Strand, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2R 0EU, United Kingdom
Description: Entering via the hotel’s beautiful lobby sets the tone for a meal at this iconic restaurant, where chandeliers, mirrors and red lacquered panelling provide a classically elegant environment. The menu follows suit, offering a mix of French and British classics, and is served by a fittingly formal team.

Name: Palmerston
Address: 1 Palmerston Place, Edinburgh, EH12 5AF, United Kingdom
Description: For something a bit different, head to this beautifully converted former bank; now a buzzy café-cum-restaurant-cum-bar. Sit at polished bistro tables and enjoy unfussy dishes with European touches – the pies for 2 are a hit. Local beers, a carefully curated wine list and friendly service complete the picture.

Name: Asha's
Address: 12-22 Newhall Street, Birmingham, B3 3LX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A stylish, passionately run Indian restaurant with exotic décor; owned by renowned artiste/gourmet Asha Bhosle. Extensive menus cover most parts of the Subcontinent, with everything cooked to order. Tandoori kebabs are a speciality.

Name: Fish House Fistral
Address: Unit 5, International Surf Centre, Fistral Beach, Headland Road, Newquay, TR7 1HY, United Kingdom
Description: In amongst the beach shops of the International Surf Centre you’ll find this small bistro looking out over Fistral Beach’s golden sands towards a sea dotted with surfers. Blackboards announce the daily catch, with much coming from Newquay Harbour. Dishes are appealing and full of flavour.

Name: The Pem
Address: 22-28 Broadway, St James’s, London, SW1H 0BH, United Kingdom
Description: Set in the elegant surroundings of the Conrad London St. James Hotel, The Pem is named after suffragette Emily Wilding Davison's nickname. Chef Sally Abé’s experience shines through in cooking that's British in inspiration, using produce like Porthilly oysters and Cotswold venison. Dishes are contemporary in style and accomplished in technique. Ask the personable sommelier for recommendations.

Name: The Wigmore
Address: 15 Langham Place, Upper Regent Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1B 1JA, United Kingdom
Description: The impressively high ceiling can only mean one thing – this was once a bank. Booths, high tables, a sizeable bar and bold emerald green tones lend a clubby feel to this addendum to The Langham. Classic, hearty British dishes are given an update.

Name: Barrafina
Address: 26-27 Dean Street, Soho, London, W1D 3LL, United Kingdom
Description: This is the only Barrafina that doesn’t take bookings – but the one that invariably boasts the best atmosphere – and you can order drinks and snacks while you wait for a seat at the handsome L-shaped counter. The tapas menu is supplemented by an appealing little blackboard of the day’s best produce, which may include mackerel, carabinero or sardines. Sharing a tortilla is always a good start and then, if you look at what your neighbours are having, you’ll find yourself ordering more and more of the colourful dishes.

Name: Karrek
Address: St. Enodoc Hotel, Rock, PL27 6LA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: There are just 10 tables in this small but elegant space within the St Enodoc hotel, whose chicly understated grey décor is dotted with contemporary seascapes. ‘Blas a Karrek’ translates as ‘taste of Rock’ and the two tasting menus certainly showcase the best Cornish ingredients. The kitchen uses plenty of modern techniques in its creative and ambitious dishes.

Name: Claude Bosi's Oyster Bar
Address: Michelin House, 81 Fulham Road, Chelsea, London, SW3 6RD, United Kingdom
Description: What was once the garage forecourt of the stunning Michelin House is home to this reinvigorated neighbourhood restaurant with a bistro-like vibe. The signature oysters and fruits de mer platters are the eye-catching highlights, but the menu offers something for everyone, from salad Niçoise to the 'Bibendum burger'. Kick off your evening in style with an expertly made cocktail from the bar.

Name: The Pony Chew Valley
Address: Knowle Hill, Newtown, Chew Magna, BS40 8TQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Featuring stunning views over the eponymous valley, this aptly named former pub now operates more as a restaurant. The short menu uses the seasons as a guide and showcases produce from the kitchen garden in vibrant, colourful dishes which mix creative and a few traditional elements. Themed menus and evenings are often centred around a particular ingredient or producer, be it a celebration of seafood or a cider pairing dinner. The midweek lunch menu offers great value for money.

Name: Wild Tavern
Address: 2 Elystan Street, Chelsea, London, SW3 3NS, United Kingdom
Description: Set overlooking the tiny Chelsea Green, this homely neighbourhood restaurant has a retro Alpine feel and a feature fire-pit. Ingredient-led cooking takes its influences from Italy. Start with something from the raw bar followed by a tasty pasta or prime quality grilled fish or meat dish.

Name: Amazonico
Address: 10 Berkeley Square, Mayfair, London, W1J 6BR, United Kingdom
Description: There is a tremendous sense of flair to this sexy, stylish restaurant with a party atmosphere. The glowing, flaming grills are an immediate eye-catcher, as is the jungle-inspired décor that combines with live music to make this the perfect place not just for a meal, but for a proper night out. Quality ingredients power the roster of South American dishes from tiraditos to tequeños. There's a small sushi selection available too, from the playfully named 'Japazonico' menu.

Name: MO
Address: Willersey Hill, Broadway, WR12 7LF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Tucked away behind the main restaurant at this stylish country house hotel, this intimate dining room features just 12 seats around a U-shaped kitchen counter. The seasonally changing, 8-course menu is delivered in an interactive and engaging style by the affable chefs, and the colourful, creative dishes showcase top quality ingredients, with some well-chosen wine matches to accompany.

Name: Louie
Address: 13-15 West Street, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2H 9NE, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a decidedly French feel to this smart brasserie spread over two floors. Sit downstairs during the week, where the elegant surroundings include a shellfish counter, banquettes and a lovely old jukebox. The more formal, intimate upstairs dining room opens at the weekend. The menu comprises skilfully cooked French-influenced dishes, including sharing options like sole meunière and côte de boeuf. Desserts are a straightforward, classic affair, with choices like chocolate fondant, tarte Tatin and a cracking pecan pie. Head up to The Alligator Bar for a cocktail after dining.

Name: Townsend
Address: Whitechapel Gallery, 77-82 Whitechapel High Street, Tower Hamlets, London, E1 7QX, United Kingdom
Description: Set within the Whitechapel Gallery, this small, light-filled room has a classic feel and is named in honour of its architect, Charles Harrison Townsend. The menu screams seasonality and flavours burst through – and while it’s evident there’s a confident chef at the helm, no dish is over-engineered.

Name: Cord by Le Cordon Bleu
Address: 85 Fleet Street, City of London, London, EC4Y 1AE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Famous for their cookery schools, Le Cordon Bleu also operate restaurants, including this one in a Grade II listed building originally designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens for the Press Association. The room is stylishly decorated in soothing blues and whites and the impeccably attired chefs are on show in the glass-fronted kitchen. Cooking shows a strong classical bent, and dishes are presented in an eye-catching, modern style.

Name: Prithvi
Address: 37 Bath Road, Cheltenham, GL53 7HG, United Kingdom
Description: A smart, stylish restaurant with smooth service from a welcoming team; start with a drink in the first floor lounge. Dishes are inspired by classic Indian flavours and textures but are presented in a deconstructed, eye-catching modern manner. The charming owner adds to the experience.

Name: No. Fifty Cheyne
Address: 50 Cheyne Walk, Chelsea, London, SW3 5LR, United Kingdom
Description: This brightly painted, flower-festooned former pub looks very much at home in its smart Chelsea location, and the indulgent theme carries on inside with plush dining spaces set over two floors. The menu offers hearty, modern British dishes, with fish and meats cooked over the grill a speciality. In true neighbourhood style, they also offer relaxed Saturday brunches and traditional Sunday lunches.

Name: The Bull's Head
Description: Nestled in a lush valley bordered by the Black Mountains, this drovers' inn retains a homely charm, boasting flagstone floors, slate walls and open fires. Unfussy, ingredient-led cooking is natural, wholesome and full of flavour, with meats from the owners’ farm, homemade charcuterie and a traditional roast on Sundays. Low intervention wines feature alongside a fine selection of beers. Accommodation – in the form of lodges and huts – is planned soon.

Name: Artis by Phelim O'Hagan
Address: 29-31 Craft Village, Shipquay Street, Londonderry, BT48 6AR, United Kingdom
Description: Latin for ‘craft’, Artis sits in the Craft Village area of the city and is, at its core, a celebration of local produce and trusted local suppliers. The two-roomed restaurant is serene in both atmosphere and decoration thanks to the warm service and neutral hues. Dishes are clean, contemporary and technically accomplished, and the desserts are always a highlight.

Name: Petersham Nurseries Café
Address: Church Lane, Richmond-Upon-Thames, London, TW10 7AG, United Kingdom
Description: As you sit in the greenhouse with sand at your feet, surrounded by fresh flowers which even in the winter months perfume the air, it feels as though all is right with the world. A unique spot within the capital's dining scene, this restaurant forms part of the wider Petersham Nurseries complex, where you can buy plants and homeware to spruce up your abode. The cooking is informed by their own fresh produce – try a seasonal vegetable medley to make the most of it – and has a clear Italian accent, from crudo to tortellini.

Name: Six Portland Road
Address: 6 Portland Road, North Kensington, London, W11 4LA, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away off Holland Park Avenue, this intimate neighbourhood bistro is sure to become one of your favourite haunts. The concise European menu changes according to the ingredients available and dishes are robust, skilfully constructed and easy-to-eat.

Name: Kanishka
Address: 17-19 Maddox Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 2QH, United Kingdom
Description: Owner Atul Kochhar’s signature style is writ large across the choice of menus at this smart Mayfair restaurant. Anglo-infused Indian dishes – epitomised by the signature chicken tikka pie – provide plenty of interesting options, with the north-east of India receiving particular attention. There’s a feeling of glamour to the surroundings that would suit a special occasion, and the ground floor is the most fun place to sit.

Name: Olde Glen Bar
Description: This remote inn dates from the 1760s, and its somewhat modest façade gives little indication as to the charm and character that lies within. The bar is always filled with locals, and the large dining room plays host to a set menu which boasts plenty of fish and shellfish from nearby shores, including local oysters and house-smoked salmon; while the fermented potato bread gets things off to a great start. There are cosy bedrooms available too.

Name: Host
Address: 13 Ranelagh, Dublin City, D06 TH72, Ireland
Description: A modern, simply-furnished neighbourhood restaurant with a buzzing atmosphere and a super-friendly team. Ingredient-led, Italian-influenced cooking means an abundance of natural flavours; the concise, daily changing menu features prime meats, homemade pasta and dishes designed for sharing.

Name: Black Bear Inn
Address: Clytha Road, Bettws Newydd, NP15 1JN, United Kingdom
Description: In a rural spot, close to the Victorian market town of Usk, you’ll find the Black Bear Inn; a charming place with a log-burning stove and a rustic feel. The concise, constantly evolving menu is formed around top quality local produce and dishes are full of flavour.

Address: 107 Upper Street, Islington, London, N1 1QN, United Kingdom
Description: A chatty young team serve you at this narrow, pleasantly cluttered bistro, which is decorated with local artists’ work and has a charmingly homespun feel that easily endears you to the place. The well-priced tasting menu – available in long or short form – offers interesting textures and bold flavours, including the occasional hint at the chef’s Scottish-Caribbean heritage. The cooking has a certain delicacy to it, while still leaving you feeling satisfied. Drinks pairings are available, as is a roast on Sundays.

Name: Ox Barn
Address: Southrop Manor Estate, Southrop, GL7 3NX, United Kingdom
Description: This delightful barn conversion sits in an idyllic rural location in the heart of the Cotswolds, surrounded by Provençal-style gardens; it’s part of the Thyme complex and no expense has been spared in its stunning restoration. Beautifully pared-back, flavour-packed dishes follow a nature-to-plate philosophy, showcasing ingredients from their kitchen gardens and farm in Mediterranean-inspired recipes.

Name: Edinbane Lodge
Address: Old Dunvegan Road, Edinbane, Isle of Skye, IV51 9PW, United Kingdom
Description: The characterful Edinbane Lodge dates back to 1543 and is reputedly the oldest inn on Skye. The chef, a native, loves to use the best island and Highland produce – as well as local crockery – and the imaginative multi-course dinner menu showcases bold, natural flavours. Bedrooms have a subtle Scottish theme.

Name: The Hambrough
Address: Hambrough Road, Ventnor, PO38 1SQ, United Kingdom
Description: Set within an intimate hotel, in the heart of historic Ventnor, The Hambrough is a modern, understated restaurant with a formal feel, offering commanding coastal views. Carefully prepared dishes use island grown and reared produce where possible, and natural flavours take the lead. Comfy bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Tutto
Address: 20-22 Marlborough Place, Brighton and Hove, BN1 1UB, United Kingdom
Description: A contemporary transformation of a former bank, with a smart pavement terrace and a large black and gold clock adorning its outside wall. Ingredient-led Italian cooking is packed with flavour and accompanied by an Italian-focused wine list. Start with some snacks before moving on to pasta; or if there’s two or more of you, go for the sharing menu. Friendly, knowledgeable service completes the picture.

Name: Chakana
Address: 140 Alcester Road, Moseley, Birmingham, B13 8HT, United Kingdom
Description: This former bank has all the ingredients for a fun night out with friends: a lively laid-back vibe, great modern Peruvian food and one of the largest ranges of pisco in the UK. Cooking is punchy, vibrant and colourful, and dishes such as ceviches, tiraditos and causas are perfect for sharing.

Name: Rothay Manor
Address: Borrans Road, Ambleside, LA22 0EH, United Kingdom
Description: A Regency-style country house on the edge of town plays host to this elegant restaurant, where original shutters and cornicing sit alongside bold William Morris wallpaper and striking chandeliers. Intricate modern dishes showcase fine ingredients and demonstrate a good understanding of technique.

Name: Angelina
Address: 56 Dalston Lane, Dalston, London, E8 3AH, United Kingdom
Description: Few people would think of combining Italian and Japanese cuisine, but the unusual fusion works a treat at this fun neighbourhood spot owned by two friends. Sit at the marble counter to watch the chefs at work in the open kitchen, as they craft a kaiseki-style tasting menu which could include such creations as rosemary and nori focaccia or chawanmushi flavoured with datterini tomatoes. Keep an eye out for the pasta dishes, as they're a highlight.

Name: Through the Woods
Address: 212 Middle Lane, Haringey, London, N8 7LA, United Kingdom
Description: With seating for just 18 people and a logo rather than a sign outside, it’s clear that understatement and simplicity lie at the core of this cosy and very likeable restaurant. Diners are asked to arrive at 7.30pm as dinner is served to everyone at 8pm; the 4 course, weekly-changing menu offers no choice and you pay when you book. From the tiny open kitchen you can expect nourishing and heartwarming dishes like succulent Blackface lamb with Hasselback potatoes and wonderfully light blood orange & brioche pudding.

Name: Fletchers
Description: Tartan upholstery and woodpanelled walls lend a historic feel to this intimate restaurant inside the luxurious Grantley Hall hotel. The dining room boasts garden views and there’s a lovely terrace on which to enjoy an aperitif in the summer. The large menu is influenced by the local area and ticks all the boxes for unfussy, flavoursome food with dishes like cheese soufflé, beef Wellington for two and a choice of cuts from the Josper grill.

Name: The Ingham Swan
Address: Sea Palling Road, Ingham, NR12 9AB, United Kingdom
Description: This 14C thatched pub now houses a contemporary restaurant, although its low beams and stone walls remain. Service is friendly, and cooking uses the best of the county’s ingredients in a range of dishes, from the classics to those showing more imagination and flair. Smart bedrooms are available in the converted coach house and a nearby cottage.

Name: The Grandtully Hotel by Ballintaggart
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This former railway hotel dates from 1866, but inside it’s been given a super-smart makeover by the owners of nearby Ballintaggart Farm. Pass through the small library-cum-lounge and you’ll find a cosy, homely restaurant where they serve an appealing menu which lists classics alongside a few European choices. Lighter dishes are served in the bar and there’s even a small deli. Eight bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Number 20
Address: 20 Rosedale Lane, Port Mulgrave, TS13 5JZ, United Kingdom
Description: Having previously run the nearby Fox & Hounds, Jason and Sue opened this homely little restaurant in the small coastal village of Port Mulgrave. Concise, daily changing menus have a seafood bias with the occasional Mediterranean element thrown in, and cooking has a fresh, unfussy style.

Name: Sorella
Address: 148 Clapham Manor Street, Lambeth, London, SW4 6BX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: His years spent working on Italy’s Amalfi Coast inspired this operation from experienced London restaurateur Robin Gill. The menu is divided into the classic format of cicchetti, antipasti, primi and secondi, and the selection of dishes includes traditional heavy hitters like aubergine parmigiana, ossobuco and tiramisu. Make sure you kick off with some of the arancini though, as they're certainly a highlight. There's a great buzz to the place and the service is friendly.

Name: Sumi
Address: 157 Westbourne Grove, North Kensington, London, W11 2RS, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a plethora of restaurants on Westbourne Grove but few are ever as busy as Sumi. In 2022 this modern Japanese restaurant from Endo Kazutoshi – which he named after his mother – expanded into next door and the new seating quickly filled up. The atmosphere is always lively thanks to the young crowd and the great cocktail list. The menu is not overly long; the robata dishes are the standouts, but just keep half an eye on the bill as it can quickly expand.

Name: Terrace
Address: Quay Street, Yarmouth, PO41 0PB, United Kingdom
Description: As the name suggests, this harbourside restaurant boasts a wonderful terrace: it's lovely and large – and located right above the Wightlink ticket office. With fish to the fore, the concise menu reflects the seasonality of the island’s ingredients, and the classical dishes are well-executed and very tasty.

Name: Le Pont de la Tour
Address: 36d Shad Thames, Butlers Wharf, Southwark, London, SE1 2YE, United Kingdom
Description: Few restaurants in London can claim to have a better location than this. For over 30 years, Le Pont de la Tour has been wowing diners with its jaw-dropping views of Tower Bridge, best appreciated from the terrace on a warm summer's day. The restaurant itself, as the name suggests, is thoroughly French at heart: expect confidently executed classics from ratatouille Niçoise to gratin Normande. The carefully chosen wine list offers a broad and interesting selection, of both the classic and the esoteric varieties.

Name: Whites
Address: 12a North Bar Without, Beverley, HU17 7AB, United Kingdom
Description: Be sure to arrive early for drinks in the first floor lounge of this small, enthusiastically run restaurant beside the old city walls. Two surprise menus showcase Yorkshire produce in carefully crafted dishes with a modern heart. Eye-catching art punctuates the neutral walls.

Name: Bala Baya
Address: Arch 25, Old Union Yard Arches, 229 Union Street, Southwark, London, SE1 0LR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A friendly, lively restaurant which celebrates the Middle Eastern heritage of its passionate owner. Dishes are fresh, vibrant and designed for sharing and the bright, modern interior is inspired by the Bauhaus architecture of Tel Aviv.

Name: Tehran Berlin
Address: 20 Rosebery Avenue, Finsbury, London, EC1R 4SX, United Kingdom
Description: This is an immeasurably likeable restaurant, where enthusiastic yet softly spoken Chef-Owner Yuma Hashemi – who was born in Tehran and grew up in Berlin – has gradually moved the influences from being French with a hint of Iranian to unashamedly and wholeheartedly celebrating Iranian cuisine. The multi-course surprise menu provides a great opportunity to sample a variety of dishes and this, many of which are inspired by Yuma's family recipes. The cooking, together with the warm service and quirky, characterful interior, ensures everyone has a good night.

Name: Moro
Address: 34-36 Exmouth Market, Finsbury, London, EC1R 4QE, United Kingdom
Description: Full of customers and full of life, with service that is engaging and on-the-ball, Moro remains as popular as ever and is the perfect fit for the increasingly busy Exmouth Market. The Moorish menu is full of interesting, flavour-packed dishes, but the wood-roasted options are the ones to go for. The open kitchen adds to the atmosphere of the animated room, and their next-door tapas bar, Morito, is also worth visiting.

Name: Roux at Skindles
Address: Mill Lane, Taplow, SL6 0AG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You can't keep Alain Roux away from the banks of the Thames. Up the road from his famous Waterside Inn, he owns this contemporary brasserie and cocktail bar in a similarly pleasant riverside setting. The skill and confidence of the chefs is evident across the menu of traditional French and other European dishes, particularly in classical elements like the rich, meaty sauces. Arrive early for drinks on the terrace or in the cocktail bar, where they also serve a 'brioche and bubbles' menu.

Name: Orwells
Address: Shiplake Row, Binfield Heath, RG9 4DP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This 18C building may look like a rural inn but inside it has a modern, formal feel. Creative cooking uses top quality produce and flavours are pronounced. It’s named after George Orwell, who spent his childhood in the area.

Name: Sorting Room
Address: Parkgate Hotel, Westgate Street, Cardiff, CF10 1DA, United Kingdom
Description: Set within an impressive, modish hotel this elegant, brasserie-style spot boasts leather banquettes, attentive staff and a wide-ranging menu of British dishes. Start with Welsh cold cuts or oak-smoked octopus and crispy pork, followed by Brecon lamb or beef Wellington – and don’t miss the Taffy apple cider tatin, which is big enough for two to share.

Name: 33 The Homend
Address: 33 The Homend, Ledbury, HR8 1BP, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a sweet, cosy feel and plenty of homespun charm to this tiny 18C, Grade II listed building in the centre of town. The warm and welcoming Elizabeth performs the service, while her husband James works alone in the kitchen. His menu offers a choice of three dishes per course – often featuring rare breed meats and Cornish fish – and the cooking is classical, comforting and satisfying. It only seats 14, so you do need to book early.

Name: Rebel
Address: 150 Heaton Park Road, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE6 5NR, United Kingdom
Description: Named after chef-owner Lindsay’s boyhood dog, this intimate, personally run restaurant has a quirky narrow shape, art by a member of the family on the walls and rustic wooden tables. The seasonal set menu offers small plates with a light, modern touch. The wine list includes some interesting organic and biodynamic choices, and it’s worth going for the pairings.

Name: Winslade Manor
Address: Winslade Park Avenue, Manor Drive, Clyst St Mary, EX15 1FY, United Kingdom
Description: A beautifully restored, early 19C manor house with 86 acres of grounds provides the lovely setting, while the food is ably taken care of by an experienced and very capable kitchen team. Local ingredients are used extensively in various menus that offer something for everyone and allow for plenty of flexibility. Desserts are a particular highlight. The terrace overlooks the gardens and cricket field.

Name: Barley Sheaf
Description: This attractive 18C pub has a deceptively large interior, with a rustic, pine-furnished dining area, a capacious bar and space to dine upstairs too. The well-priced menu lists pub classics alongside more ambitious dishes and much of the produce comes from in and around the Roseland Peninsula.

Name: Honey & Co
Address: 54 Lamb's Conduit Street, Bloomsbury, London, WC1N 3LW, United Kingdom
Description: Same concept; new, brighter, larger location: Honey & Co has been reborn and fans of the original will be delighted. Vibrant, colourful dishes offer the classic flavours and textures of Middle Eastern cooking and are designed for sharing. If you can’t decide on what to have, go for the tasting option, which offers a small portion of every dish on the menu.

Name: White Hart Inn
Address: 1 High Street, West Mersea, CO5 8QD, United Kingdom
Description: A stone’s throw from the coast, this spacious modernised pub features a parquet floor, a maritime mural and bright blue chairs. The wide-ranging menu offers confidently executed dishes with bold, punchy flavours and the occasional modern twist; don’t miss the Mersea oysters. If the weather is good, head for the sunny courtyard terrace – it’s also well worth staying over in one of the comfy bedrooms.

Name: Zahter
Address: 30-32 Foubert’s Place, Soho, London, W1F 7PS, United Kingdom
Description: Start the day with something new by enjoying a Turkish breakfast at this boldly decorated restaurant. The main menu includes fresh breads, hot and cold mezze, and large platters, with interesting dishes cooked on the chargrill or in the wood-burning oven. Try a Turkish wine to best complement the food.

Name: Note
Address: 26 Fenian Street, Dublin City, D02 FX09, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: There’s a subtle retro touch to this enjoyable wine bar turned bistro. The cooking is modern yet unfussy and unpretentious, so don’t be surprised to find the likes of pork chops or date and toffee pudding on the menu. Bold, distinct flavours abound in dishes where the kitchen’s Irish influences often shine through. A charming team run the restaurant with a relaxed efficiency, and are always happy to recommend wines from their largely natural and organic selection.

Name: Sunday in Brooklyn
Address: 98 Westbourne Grove, North Kensington, London, W2 5RU, United Kingdom
Description: If you’re hankering after a taste of New York City, then this London branch of a Brooklyn-based restaurant can provide it. In this relaxed all-day eatery, it doesn’t have to be Sunday for you to kick off your day with an American brunch favourite. Settle in later on for dinner and be treated to food prepared with care by a kitchen with an excellent understanding of flavour, all served by a lively, caring team. There’s also the option of delighting in one of the many cocktails being whipped up from behind the big, busy bar.

Name: Forde
Address: 7 Town Street, Horsforth, LS18 5LJ, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced chef Matt Healy – a onetime 'MasterChef: The Professionals' contestant – has come home to Horsforth to open this rustic bistro and wine bar. His appealing menu features appetising small plates with Mediterranean influences; two or three per person works well, and there are some well-chosen wines, craft beers and cocktails too.

Name: The Grill
Address: 53 Park Lane, Mayfair, London, W1K 1QA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Grill at The Dorchester Hotel might be carrying a name loaded with history, but that’s no indication of the look or the food. Bright, modern décor and a formal team make you feel cossetted, while the ornate ceiling is something of a talking point. The cooking mixes classical flavours with modern techniques, on a menu that features luxury dishes to share like skate wing, rib-eye steak and 'all the chicken'. The set lunch menu offers value for money and they list some unusual wines by the glass.

Name: Roji
Address: 56B South Molton Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 5SH, United Kingdom
Description: A husband-and-wife chef team are behind this 10-seater Japanese counter restaurant in a side alley just off South Molton Street. There are two sittings at dinner for the set 8 course omakase menu, which includes a nigiri course. Flavours and techniques are kept quite traditional, with much of the fish coming from British waters. As everyone is served together, punctuality is important.

Name: Lisboeta
Address: 30 Charlotte Street, Bloomsbury, London, W1T 2NG, United Kingdom
Description: This Fitzrovian funhouse is Chef Nuno Mendes’ ‘love letter’ to Lisbon and he’s on a mission to showcase its vibrant and varied food and wine cultures, and bring them to the attention of a wider audience. Come with a group of friends to best sample the array of petiscos, plates, pots and platters, all bursting with colour, freshness and flavour. The atmosphere is celebratory, lively and unabashedly noisy.

Name: Launceston Place
Address: 1a Launceston Place, Kensington, London, W8 5RL, United Kingdom
Description: Think South Kensington and you think of Launceston Place. This handsome restaurant has a proud history and a palpable sense of neighbourhood; its nooks and crannies making it ideal for trysts or tête-à-têtes. You choose your dishes from the solitaire-style board presented to you at the table – or you can simply opt for the tasting menu. Expect an ambitious style of cuisine, where dishes are good looking and innovative.

Name: Le Vacherin
Address: 76-77 South Parade, Ealing, London, W4 5LF, United Kingdom
Description: With its part-mirrored walls, belle époque pictures and vintage brasserie styling, Le Vacherin brings a little bit of France to its West London neighbourhood. The menu has the classical French slant you would expect, allowing you to get your fix of 'escargots' or 'longe de lapin' without leaving the country. It's all fresh, flavoursome and prepared with obvious care, while the 'prix fixe' menu offers great value for money. The chateaubriand to share is a popular choice.

Name: Little Fish Market
Address: 10 Upper Market Street, Brighton and Hove, BN3 1AS, United Kingdom
Description: As the name implies, fish is the focus at this unassuming restaurant, which is fittingly located in a converted fishmonger’s opposite the old Victorian fish market. For many years, passionate chef-owner Duncan Ray has been quietly cooking, refining and pushing his restaurant forward – and he is ever-present in the dining room, ensuring his guests are having a good time. The 6 course set menu is packed with skilful seafood cookery which demonstrates great balance and understanding of the ingredients.

Name: Robun
Address: 4 Princes Buildings, George Street, Bath, BA1 2ED, United Kingdom
Description: This skilfully run Japanese restaurant takes its inspiration from 19C author Kanagaki Robun, who is credited with introducing barbecued food to Japan. The cooking reflects his influence, with dishes from the robata grill forming the central part of a menu that is distinguished by fresh produce and an authentic approach. Excellent sushi and a strikingly presented afternoon tea also stand out on the vast menu.

Name: Sheeps and Leeks
Address: 12 East gate Street, Caernarfon, LL55 1AG, United Kingdom
Description: Named after two of the products for which Wales is best known, this unassuming former shop, tucked away in the town centre, features a ground floor kitchen and a basement restaurant with just six tables. Homegrown and local produce form the base of the set menu, where imaginative dishes show classic techniques and subtle global flavours.

Name: Black Salt
Address: 505-507 Upper Richmond Road West, North Sheen, Richmond-Upon-Thames, London, SW14 7DE, United Kingdom
Description: Little sister to Dastaan in Ewell is this modestly decorated neighbourhood restaurant with exposed brick walls, stripped wooden floors and blonde wood tables. Vibrant Indian cooking includes plenty of street food inspired dishes. Curries are highlight and the naan bread and kulfi are must-haves.

Name: Amuse by Kevin Dalgleish
Address: 1 Queen's Terrace, Aberdeen City, AB10 1XL, United Kingdom
Description: Kevin Dalgleish is a well-known chef in Aberdeen and his restaurant occupies the spacious basement of a granite townhouse, in a quiet residential neighbourhood yet just minutes from the city centre. Kick off with a drink in the bar or by the wood burning stove. The kitchen use prime Scottish ingredients blended with French techniques to create good-looking dishes that deliver on flavour.

Name: The Mount
Address: 97 High Street, Henley-in-Arden, B95 5AT, United Kingdom
Description: Glynn Purnell’s characterful beamed pub is set in one of the UK’s prettiest high streets. The modern renovation has been beautifully done and, while the elegant bar offers a great atmosphere and some bar snacks, diners should head to the bistro to enjoy everything from burgers and their signature black pudding scotch egg to Wiltshire pork cutlet with sauce charcutière and some moreish smoked mash. Prices are keen and service, on the ball.

Name: The Suffolk
Address: 152 High Street, Aldeburgh, IP15 5AQ, United Kingdom
Description: With a terrific beachside location, this smart modern brasserie provides just what you want to see on a menu when you're beside the sea – fish and shellfish galore! Time-honoured techniques are used in reliably enjoyable classics like dressed crab and moules marinière, alongside daily fish specials such as pan-friend halibut with beurre blanc. To start, venture onto land with a dozen 'escargots' to share and, if the weather's good enough, make sure you grab a seat on the rooftop terrace that overlooks the beach.

Name: Paradise Café
Address: Daleside Nurseries, Ripon Road, Killinghall, Harrogate, HG3 2AY, United Kingdom
Description: A smart, spacious café behind a garden centre; if it’s sunny, grab a seat on the terrace overlooking the lake. They’re open for breakfast, brunch and lunch, and the frequently changing menu offers seasonal dishes which are fresh, unfussy and full of flavour. Book the chef’s table to watch the kitchen at work.

Name: Ekstedt at The Yard
Address: 3-5 Great Scotland Yard, Victoria, London, SW1A 2HN, United Kingdom
Description: Niklas Ekstedt’s first restaurant outside Sweden is this cosy, designer-rustic spot in the Great Scotland Yard Hotel. The chef has become synonymous with using fire fuelled by wood, so expect dishes cooked over or immersed into the embers – along with plenty of pickling, fermenting and curing. Go for the 7-course menu.

Name: Oar
Address: Toomullin, Roadford, Doolin, V95 KV02, Ireland
Description: A cosy, contemporary, remotely set restaurant with views towards the Cliffs of Moher. The appealing menu offers hearty, well-executed dishes created using good quality Irish ingredients; locally caught fish is a highlight. Stay the night in one of their simply furnished bedrooms.

Name: Cavita
Address: 56-60 Wigmore Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1U 2RZ, United Kingdom
Description: Head to the basement bar for a cocktail before taking a seat in this bright, friendly ground floor restaurant with a view of the chefs at work in the open kitchen. The menu brims with punchy, vibrant Mexican choices, including raw dishes such as hamachi tostadas and street food options like a concise range of tacos. Make sure you bring some friends to make the most of the main course platters to share. There's an enticing brunch offering too, where the mezcal and margaritas are bound to be flowing.

Name: Story Cellar
Address: 17 Neal's Yard, Seven Dials, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2H 9DP, United Kingdom
Description: A lively younger sibling to Story, this bistro de luxe in the heart of Covent Garden offers a relaxed experience with an emphasis on counter dining. There are tables available too, but overlooking the open kitchen is the place to be for a view of the grill-centric cooking. Steaks, fish of the day and rotisserie chicken form the basis of the menu, with bold flavours and generous portions duly delivered. Ensure you leave room for a classic desserts like strawberries and cream trifle.

Name: Smoking Lobster at Foresters Hall
Address: 30 Sun Hill, Cowes, PO31 7HY, United Kingdom
Description: Set inside the Foresters Hall boutique hotel – and not to be confused with the other Smoking Lobster on Cowes High Street – is this simply styled restaurant with a hint of the rustic about it. While not pitched as a seafood restaurant, the dishes showcasing locally caught fish are the way to go, as options like BBQ monkfish with harissa are finely crafted and bursting with both colour and flavour. There is a friendly, informal air to the service, and the courtyard terrace is an ideal spot in the summer.

Name: The Twenty Two
Address: 22 Grosvenor Square, Mayfair, London, W1K 6LF, United Kingdom
Description: There’s an appealingly secretive feel to the restaurant at this converted Edwardian house. Sitting in a prime Mayfair location, it’s also home to a private members’ club. The menu offers something for everyone, with its extensive selection of largely Mediterranean dishes, some of which are designed for sharing. Service is eager and on the ball.

Name: The George
Address: 55 Great Portland Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1W 7LQ, United Kingdom
Description: This handsome, Grade II listed Victorian pub boasts original 18th century features including marble fireplaces and ornate plasterwork, bringing a fair amount of period charm to proceedings. The concise British menu offers dishes like beef & Guinness pie and rice pudding with rum soaked prunes, which are generously sized and eminently satisfying. The English-dominated wine list is another big draw.

Name: Sessions Arts Club
Address: 24 Clerkenwell Green, Clerkenwell, London, EC1R 0NA, United Kingdom
Description: Set on the 4th floor of an old courthouse, the old judges’ dining room is now a characterful restaurant which comprises a rather infectious mix of historical, elegant and shabby-chic. Cooking is vibrant, unfussy and flavour-led, with the mix of small and large plates arriving as they’re ready.

Name: “8” By Andrew Sheridan
Address: 16 Cook Street, Liverpool, L2 9RF, United Kingdom
Description: Chef-owner Andrew Sheridan relocated his immersive restaurant from Birmingham to this city centre Victorian property in his home town of Liverpool. Guests gather in the dimly lit lounge for drinks and precisely made snacks, before heading downstairs to one of the two 8-seater counters, each with its own chef. They cook in front of the guests and talk about the dishes, making for an engaging experience. The cooking takes influences from around the globe and showcases bold, distinct flavours, with quality produce underpinning it all.

Name: Station Road
Address: The Lovat Hotel, Fort Augustus, PH32 4DU, United Kingdom
Description: Their tagline, ‘taste nature’s larder’, says it all at this restaurant housed inside The Lovat Hotel, a lovingly restored country house at the gateway to Loch Ness. From locally foraged ingredients to the best Highland produce, dishes showcase Scottish ingredients in detailed, modern dishes that taste as good as they look. Charming and efficient service adds to the appeal.

Name: Mayha
Address: 43 Chiltern Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1U 6LS, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: There’s a real sense of style to this small Japanese restaurant that relocated from Beirut to London. The chic interior is dominated by a curved wooden counter where the chefs take centre stage, producing a highly seasonal omakase menu. Tree-inspired lights above the counter cast an intimate glow, while a sense of theatre runs throughout the dishes. Luxury ingredients are to the fore and the menu is dominated by a succession of sushi.

Name: The Crown at Burchetts Green
Address: Burchetts Green Lane, Burchetts Green, Maidenhead, SL6 6QZ, United Kingdom
Description: Experienced and capable Chef-Owner Dominic Chapman is at the helm of this charming pub serving food that is befitting of the setting. The rewarding, flavoursome dishes – like the delicious chicken liver and duck parfait with fig chutney – are a perfect match for the warm and comforting surroundings, while the kitchen adopts a seasonal approach to the produce used. For a great value option, go for the fixed-price 'village menu'.

Name: Seacliff
Address: Sandy Cove Hotel, Old Coast Road, Combe Martin, Berrynarbor, EX34 9SR, United Kingdom
Description: This smart, intimate restaurant is set at the front of a long-standing, family-run hotel, which comes with a jewel of a terrace and commanding views of the bay. Colourful, modern dishes make use of seasonal ingredients, with a focus on local seafood. There’s a great 6-course tasting menu – with wine matches available – and service is warm and friendly.

Name: Forest Avenue
Address: 8 Sussex Terrace, Dublin City, D04 C7F4, Ireland
Description: Close to the canal in the Dublin suburbs sits this small, glass-fronted restaurant run by husband-and-wife team John and Sandy Wyer. A tasting menu is available at lunch and dinner, along with a lighter 3 course option at lunch. Across the menus, dishes come with a creative edge and yield punchy flavours; the 'surprises from our kitchen' are a lovely way to kick things off. Service is well-organised from a friendly team and the tables close to the open kitchen are understandably popular.

Name: Silver Birch
Address: 142 Chiswick High Road, Hounslow, London, W4 1PU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Among the numerous eateries on bustling Chiswick High Street, Silver Birch stands out – thanks to its appealing dishes that celebrate the wonderful ingredients we produce in the British Isles, whether that be meaty smoked eel from Devon, sweet scallops from the Isle of Mull, creamy Shetland cod or superb Lancashire fruit. There’s also a good choice of sensibly priced wines by the glass or carafe to accompany these seasonal dishes.

Name: Yaatra
Address: 4 Greycoat Place, Victoria, London, SW1P 1SB, United Kingdom
Description: A Grade II listed former fire station plays host to this smart, warm and colourfully decorated restaurant, which is run with enthusiasm and sincerity. You can choose from an extensive selection of different menus; they all take their influences from across India and her many states, as well as from neighbouring countries. The nicely balanced dishes are prepared with skill, care and understanding.

Name: Tillingham
Address: Dew Farm, Dew Lane, Peasmarsh, TN31 6XD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Nestled deep in the countryside is this 70 acre farm and wine estate with a shop, a tasting room, a restaurant and stylish bedrooms. Flavour-driven cooking focuses on pure, fresh tastes, with some produce coming from the estate. Interesting global wines, including their naturally produced selection, accompany.

Name: eleanore
Address: 30-31 Albert Place, Edinburgh, EH7 5HN, United Kingdom
Description: With its friendly service, high stool seating and bright monochrome décor, there is a pleasantly relaxed feel to this neighbourhood restaurant and wine bar. The kitchen team take plenty of care in preparing a set menu of fresh-tasting dishes, with desserts proving a highlight – if you're lucky, you'll get to try the wonderfully indulgent tirami-choux. Dietary requirements are well catered for, with vegetarian and vegan menus available on request.

Name: MacNean House
Address: Main Street, Blacklion, F91 YK0F, Ireland
Description: It may be found in quite a remote area near the Irish border, but MacNean House is a destination in its own right. Run by celebrity chef Neven Maguire, it houses a cookery school, bedrooms and this perennially busy restaurant. There’s a plushness to the dining room and a degree of formality in the service that make it a popular choice for celebrating a special occasion, while the generous tasting menu offers attractive, detailed cooking. The finest Irish ingredients are used and there’s no shortage of flavour across the dishes.

Name: Gregans Castle
Description: An attractive country house nestled in The Burren, Gregan’s Castle is an enviable location for a restaurant. It’s a luxuriously appointed place, with open fires, cosy sitting rooms and a charming bar. The equally impressive dining room is the stage for a menu based on produce from their own gardens and the surrounding area, such as some of the finest lamb in Ireland. The quality ingredients are expertly cooked and showed off in well-balanced dishes. Ask for a seat by the window to make the most of the fabulous views.

Name: LIGИUM
Address: Slatefort House, Bullaun, H62 H798, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Lignum is Latin for 'wood' and, as such, it’s the ancient method of cooking over an open flame which takes centre stage at this immensely likeable restaurant. It's housed in a modern barn conversion which has a distinctly Scandic vibe, from the large windows and minimalist furnishings to the roaring fire and throws on the chairs. The wood-fired cooking lends a delicious smoky dimension to the creative dishes, which – informed by the chef's heritage – blend ingredients from Ireland (such as sweet lobster tail) and Italy (Amalfi lemon). It all comes in the form of a surprise tasting menu.

Name: Gardener's Cottage
Address: 1 Royal Terrace Gardens, Edinburgh, EH7 5DX, United Kingdom
Description: This quirky eatery was once home to a royal gardener and much of the produce comes from the kitchen garden. It's a tiny place, with two cosy, simply furnished rooms that have long communal tables. A set, seasonally influenced menu is offered at both lunch and dinner, with the lunch version a little shorter. Well-presented modern dishes feature on both, perhaps featuring salmon cured in their on-site smokehouse.

Name: The Little Chartroom
Address: 14 Bonnington Road, Edinburgh, EH6 5JD, United Kingdom
Description: The buzz at this popular restaurant is addictive. Grab a drink in the chilled-out bar before finding a spot in the modern, pared-back dining room; the seats at the counter are the ones to go for. Original dishes have deep, bold, yet delicately balanced flavours, and are inspired by the local larder.

Name: Kinneuchar Inn
Address: 9-11 Main Street, Kilconquhar, KY9 1LF, United Kingdom
Description: The maxim ‘less is more’ is rarely so well applied as it is here. East Neuk’s bounteous local larder is showcased on a menu that changes up to twice a day; fresh fish is a highlight, and the specials are just that. This charming 17C village pub has a modish feel – sit in the cosy bar or vaulted dining room.

Name: Lyon's
Address: 1 Park Road, Haringey, London, N8 8TE, United Kingdom
Description: In many ways the ideal neighbourhood restaurant, this seafood-centric spot comes with sensible pricing, on-the-ball service and a warm welcome from its passionate owner. The cooking takes a sustainable, 'fin-to-scale' approach that's typified by their use of fish collars – an underappreciated ingredient finally allowed its moment in the sun here. While there are a few meat and vegetable options on offer, the focus is largely on eco-friendly fish and shellfish fashioned into understated dishes.

Name: Ananda
Address: Cinema Building, Sandyford Road, Dundrum Town Centre, Dublin City, D16 VK54, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Its name means ‘bliss’ and this smart Indian restaurant certainly feels like a haven from the bustling shopping centre in which it sits. Accessed via a narrow entrance, it's a sizeable place inside with a swish cocktail bar – and is stylishly decorated with attractive fretwork and vibrant art. The combination of accomplished, original cooking and assured, attentive service makes for a great all-round package. The ‘Railway Journey’ tasting menu is encouraged and is certainly the way to go if you want to sample as much of the cooking as possible.

Name: Borough
Address: 50-54 Henderson Street, Leith, EH6 6DE, United Kingdom
Description: An experienced couple run this pleasantly stark, modern restaurant, which sits on a cobbled street in a residential area near the port. Menus take on a tasting format, with a choice of 3 or 5 dishes plus an optional cheese course. Seasonal Scottish produce is to the fore, with just a handful of ingredients on each plate; flavours are distinct, while textures work in harmony. Sweet, endearing service further enhances the enjoyment.

Name: The Peregrine
Address: East Avenue, Killarney, V93 CF30, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: On the ground floor of the privately-owned Killarney Park Hotel is this elegantly dressed restaurant which comes with ornate cornicing and warm lighting. An oval-shaped cocktail bar sits at one end of the room – perfect for a pre dinner drink – while the horseshoe-shaped booths are the best seats in the house. The kitchen focuses its attention on quality produce from the county, with dishes that give the main ingredients the space to shine. If there's a pasta dish on the menu, be sure to order it.

Name: Purslane
Address: 33a St. Stephen Street, Edinburgh, EH3 5AH, United Kingdom
Description: An affluent area of the city plays host to this cosy, atmospheric basement restaurant which comprises just 9 tables. The experienced chef-owner creates ambitious modern dishes which mix tried-and-tested flavours with contemporary techniques. Service is friendly and the set lunch menu is steal.

Name: Hartes of Kildare
Address: Market Square, Kildare, R51 TN60, Ireland
Description: Sample a home-brewed beer in the snug bar before heading to the restaurant for hearty, well-prepared dishes with a modern twist; try the duck croquettes! All ingredients are sustainable and traceable, and they have their own deli selling food from local artisan producers, as well as a cookery school and bedrooms.

Name: Alumni Kitchen Table
Description: There’s something charming about this personally run rural restaurant with a contemporary feel. Stay the night in one of their four rooms to make a proper occasion of your visit and dine either around the eight-seater communal table or at the small open kitchen island. The balanced tasting menu is quite an immersive experience, featuring a range of inventive, adventurous dishes using some prime Irish ingredients. Well-crafted artisan crockery, locally made leather items, fine cutlery and a well-chosen wine pairing all enhance the experience.

Name: Mae
Address: 53 Shelbourne Road, Ballsbridge, Dublin City, D04 XC66, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This cosy first floor restaurant is hidden above the French Paradox wine shop, which not only gives it an appealingly secretive feel but also makes opting for one of the interesting wine pairings a wise move.
