The set priced menu kicks off with an array of snacks to get you in the mood, followed by boldly flavoured dishes that are as comforting as they are satisfying, like lamb shoulder with black garlic or pan-fried cod with mussels. The service team are charming and the atmosphere fun.

Name: The Swan Inn
Address: 1 Lower Street, Islip, OX5 2SB, United Kingdom
Description: Owned by one of the villagers, this traditional-looking pub is not all that it seems; instead of walking through the door and finding yourself at the bar, you’ll now find yourself facing the open kitchen. Sit in the lounge for 'English tapas' or head through to the Cygnet restaurant, where fairy lights hang from the beams and art is for sale on the walls. Modern British dishes feature on two 4 course set menus – one vegetarian – and you can mix and match between them. Colourful dishes have interesting textures, temperatures and tastes.

Name: Sucre
Address: 47B Great Marlborough Street, Soho, London, W1F 7JP, United Kingdom
Description: 20 years after opening in Buenos Aires, Argentinian chef-restaurateur Fernando Trocca opened this buzzy restaurant in an attractive former concert hall in London. Contemporary Latin American inspired dishes are cooked over the open fire of the parrilla. Start with a drink in the moody basement bar.

Name: Yugo
Address: 3 Wellington Street, Belfast, BT1 6HT, United Kingdom
Description: Behind an unassuming façade is this buzzy, industrial-style restaurant, where powerful music plays and a super-friendly team bring the dishes as and when they’re ready. These are good value small plates of Asian fusion cooking; the Iberico pork is a must and there are Asian-influenced cocktails to accompany.

Name: Olde Post Inn
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Start by enjoying a fireside aperitif in the flag-floored bar of this old 1800s post office, then dine either in the atmospheric original building or in the appealing conservatory. The experienced Chef-Owner uses top local ingredients to create flavoursome dishes that are classic in essence; game is a speciality and sauces are a highlight. Stylish bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Vaughan's Anchor Inn
Address: Main Street, Liscannor, V95 FN5R, Ireland
Description: A characterful family-run pub in a small fishing village. Nautical memorabilia lines the walls and along with the impressive fish tank, gives a clue as to the focus of the menu, where locally sourced seafood underpins the cooking. Bright, stylish bedrooms are hung with photos of local sights.

Name: CUT at 45 Park Lane
Address: 45 Park Lane, Mayfair, London, W1K 1PN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This sumptuous restaurant on the ground floor of the 45 Park Lane Hotel comes with moody décor, rich red leather backed seating and Damien Hirst artwork. Some of the best steaks in London – including British, imported USDA prime beef and Japanese Wagyu – are on offer alongside a premium wine list.

Name: Lemon Tree
Address: Unit 32-34, The Courtyard Shopping Centre, Lower Main Street, Letterkenny, F92 EK13, Ireland
Description: It might not be the most glamorous of settings, but you’ll certainly leave this established, family-run restaurant with a smile on your face. A brother, sisters and cousins all work together to deliver surprisingly modern dishes which draw from Donegal’s natural larder. The salted caramel tart is a must.

Name: Noci
Address: 4-6 Islington Green, Islington, London, N1 2XA, United Kingdom
Description: Start with the delicious homemade focaccia and share some starters before ordering the USP: generous pasta dishes which invariably hit the spot, such as veal & pork Genovese ragu or brown butter cacio e pepe. The menus are fairly priced, as are the cocktails, making this a useful pitstop in this busy part of Islington. You’ll leave feeling sated and satisfied.

Name: Maria G's
Address: Coe House, 2-4 Warwick Lane, Kensington, London, W14 8FN, United Kingdom
Description: Memories of living and working on the Amalfi Coast provided the inspiration behind this restaurant from chef Robin Gill. The short seasonal menu certainly follows the Italian culinary philosophy of using prime ingredients paired simply and intelligently to create complementary flavours. The room is stylish and there's also an intimate cocktail bar and a delightful garden terrace.

Name: The Oyster Club by Adam Stokes
Address: 43 Temple Street, Birmingham, B2 5DP, United Kingdom
Description: The name says it all: this is a place that’s passionate about oysters. They arrive here from several sources, provide fresh, pure flavours, and are presented either natural or dressed. There’s a whole host of other top-notch seafood on offer too, in understated, classically based dishes like Dover sole with capers and brown butter. A choice of caviars and a fine selection of champagnes complete the checklist of luxury items, which is matched by the plush dining room with marble-topped tables and counter seating.

Name: Nopi
Address: 21-22 Warwick Street, Soho, London, W1B 5NE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Part of the Yotam Ottolenghi stable, this charmingly run all-day restaurant sports a bright, clean look – and offers food to match. The selection of sharing plates feature some playful elements, along with a fresh acidity running throughout. There’s a great choice of vegetable dishes and influences come from the Middle East, Mediterranean and across Asia – like the char siu cauliflower or the sea bass with saag aloo. The service team work with warmth and pride, which contributes to a wonderfully uplifting atmosphere.

Name: Wild by Tart
Address: 3-4 Eccleston Yards, Belgravia, London, SW1W 9AZ, United Kingdom
Description: This laid-back brasserie is located in a former power station and coal store; the lofty glass roof ensures it’s light and airy, and the open kitchen gives it a real buzz. Rustic, Mediterranean-influenced dishes are tasty and satisfying, with bold flavours and the occasional Asian touch.

Name: The Dipping Lugger
Address: 4 West Shore Street, Ullapool, IV26 2UR, United Kingdom
Description: Named after a sailing vessel, this late 18C former manse sits right on the harbourfront and comes with luxurious bedrooms and a small restaurant with a charming vintage style. The friendly team serve a tasting menu to all tables at the same time and while dishes might appear simple, flavours burst through.

Name: Clarke's
Address: 124 Kensington Church Street, Kensington, London, W8 4BH, United Kingdom
Description: 2024 represents 40 years since Sally Clarke opened her eponymous restaurant, and the loyalty of her many regular diners is testament to the warmth of the place and her kind-hearted hospitality. The seasonal menu is a combination of British and Mediterranean influences, and the kitchen displays a light touch and a healthy respect for the quality ingredients, be it lemon sole or loin of fallow deer. If you want to take something home, check out her shop across the road.

Name: Cin Cin
Address: 21 Foley Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1W 6DS, United Kingdom
Description: Having made their name in Brighton, the owners opened a second branch here in Fitzrovia in 2021. It’s all about big Italian flavours and easy-to-eat dishes to share with family and friends – and it’s also less pasta-centric than many of its competitors. This corner restaurant is bright and welcoming.

Name: Number One
Address: 1 Princes Street, Edinburgh, EH2 2EQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Start your evening with an aperitif in the cosy cocktail bar of this plush restaurant inside the Balmoral Hotel, one of Scotland's most iconic buildings. Red lacquered walls and richly upholstered banquettes lend an air of luxury to the place, as do premium ingredients like N25 caviar and hand-dived Orkney scallops. There is a natural flow to the well-balanced dishes on the 7 course tasting menu, while the professional, well-paced service instantly puts you at ease.

Name: Victoria
Address: 10 West Temple Sheen, Richmond-Upon-Thames, London, SW14 7RT, United Kingdom
Description: With its Sunday lunches, quiz nights and sensible prices, this remains a proper neighbourhood pub – albeit in a very smart neighbourhood. There's a pleasantly lived-in feel to the place; if you're here to eat, head for the conservatory which overlooks the terrace. The appealing menu mixes steaks and pubby favourites like fish & chips with a good range of Mediterranean-influenced dishes such as grilled sardines with caponata. Do try the apple cake for dessert, which is Polish Chef Damian's take on his mother's recipe.

Name: The Glass Curtain
Address: Unit A, Thompson House, McCurtain Street, Cork, T23 DC6C, Ireland
Description: Both the name and the large photo on the back wall pay homage to this building’s former life as the iconic Thompson’s Bakery; now a compact brasserie. Monochrome décor, exposed pipework and a charming team set the scene. Modern dishes have a personal touch and are cooked with grá (Gaelic for ‘love’).

Name: Appleton's
Address: 19 Fore Street, Fowey, PL23 1AH, United Kingdom
Description: Appleton’s is the sort of place we’d all love to have on our doorstep. It’s split over 2 floors and comes with a cocktail bar and a deli. The chatty team deliver Italian dishes which showcase Cornish produce and are cooked with heart and soul. The pastas are homemade and the anchovy fritters are a must.

Name: Collinsons
Address: 122-124 Brown Street, Broughty Ferry, DD5 1EN, United Kingdom
Description: You can’t miss the name etched in large letters across the floor to ceiling windows of this bright modern restaurant. In contrast, cooking is classic to the core, with complementary textures and tastes leading the way. The chef-owner’s experience shines through in every beautifully presented dish.

Name: Yauatcha Soho
Address: 15 Broadwick Street, Soho, London, W1F 0DL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The ground floor of this lively, contemporary Chinese restaurant features cabinets full of pastries and chocolates – but ask to sit in the more atmospheric basement, with its celestial ceiling lights, tropical fish tanks and glimpses into the busy kitchen. The extensive menu offers something for everyone, and over-ordering is easy to do.

Name: The Sea, The Sea
Address: 174 Pavilion Road, Chelsea, London, SW1X 0AW, United Kingdom
Description: This modern fish shop, deli and seafood bar is set in a charming semi-pedestrianised mews off Sloane Square. Dine on the terrace, which opens at lunchtime, or find a spot in the chic interior in the evening. Menus evolve constantly, according to the latest catch, and include raw and cured dishes.

Name: French House
Address: 49 Dean Street, Soho, London, W1D 5BG, United Kingdom
Description: This historic Soho watering hole, once a favourite haunt of writers and artists such as Dylan Thomas, Brendan Behan and Francis Bacon, has only seven tables in its oxblood and wood-panelled upstairs restaurant. It’s run in a bohemian style and offers traditional, honest cooking with integrity and flavour.

Name: Dim Sum Duck
Address: 124 King's Cross Road, King’s Cross St Pancras, London, WC1X 9DS, United Kingdom
Description: An enthusiastic couple run this small, simply furnished restaurant, which is reminiscent of the type of place you’d find on your travels in Asia. The extensive menu sees great tasting, authentic Cantonese dishes cooked carefully using good quality ingredients. You might have to queue to get in, but once inside there’s a lively atmosphere.

Name: Angela's
Address: 21 The Parade, Margate, CT9 1EX, United Kingdom
Description: Set just off the esplanade is this understated little bistro with a fiercely local, eco-friendly ethos – even the tables are made of compressed recycled plastic. With no meat on the menu, dishes are centred around sustainably caught seafood, be it Dover sole with green sauce or turbot with tomatoes and capers. Simplicity is the key to the cooking, with the quality central ingredients allowed to shine thanks to just a few, well-judged accompaniments. The friendly service creates a pleasantly relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Little Hollows Pasta
Address: 26 Chandos Road, City of Bristol, BS6 6PF, United Kingdom
Description: If you’re looking for something a little different, head to Little Hollows Pasta, a rustic bar-cum-bistro where the pasta is freshly made in house each morning and then hung out in the window to dry. The Italian dishes have an honest heart, ingredients are top-notch, and flavours are rich and authentic; be sure to save room for one of the classic Italian desserts. The passion of the knowledgeable team is palpable.

Address: The Globe Inn, 56 High Street, Dumfries, DG1 2JA, United Kingdom
Description: This historic pub – whose name references its origins – is well known as a favourite haunt of legendary Scottish poet, Robert Burns, and with over 300 whiskies available in the snug in which he held court, a drink here is a must. The vintage-style restaurant, with its Tam o’Shanter mural, is an atmospheric place to dine. The menu puts Scottish produce to the fore, and dishes are creative, modern, and full of colour and flavour.

Name: Mercado Central
Address: 24 Green Street, Cambridge, CB2 3JX, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a buzzy vibe to this brightly decorated townhouse with its cheery tiled kitchen and fresh fish display. Sustainable British and Spanish produce features in hearty dishes with leanings to Galicia and the Basque Country. Start with some sharing plates, then move on to grilled meat or fish.

Name: Heathcock
Address: 58 Bridge Street, Cardiff, CF5 2EN, United Kingdom
Description: Sister to the Hare & Hounds in Aberthin, this modest neighbourhood pub shares its passion for sourcing great ingredients and preparing them with care. A nose-to-tail ethos informs the enticing small plates and sharing dishes, homemade breads are a highlight, and two luxurious bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: etch. by Steven Edwards
Address: 216 Church Rd, Hove, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2DJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An attractive former bank plays host to this lively modern restaurant, where an open kitchen and bar take centre stage in the dining room. Tersely described tasting menus deliver ambitious, technique-driven dishes with bold flavours and intriguing textures; Steven's signatures include a marmite brioche and his take on 'dippy egg'. The wine list offers a good selection from Sussex and cocktails are available in the basement Ink Bar, so-called because the premises was once a tattoo parlour.

Name: Cantinetta Antinori
Address: 4 Harriet Street, Belgravia, London, SW1X 9JR, United Kingdom
Description: The Antinori family have owned vineyards in Tuscany since the 12C, producing their own world-renowned red wine, as well as having a hand in numerous other estates. It should come as no surprise, then, that the wine list here is something to behold. It’s joined by classic Italian cooking, pairing a notable simplicity with plenty of Tuscan ingredients and rich, hearty flavours. The delicious torta caprese is a wonderful way to round out your visit.

Name: Plates by Purnell's
Address: 121 Edmund Street, Birmingham, B3 2HJ, United Kingdom
Description: Located just around the corner from Purnell’s, this tapas bar offshoot is a narrow, snaking spot with authentic Spanish cooking. Choose your selection of small plates from a seasonally informed menu filled with tapas favourites like gambas, croquetas and patatas bravas, where adept flavour combinations and seasonings run throughout. The added bonuses of welcoming service and competitive pricing could help to make this your new neighbourhood go-to.

Name: Auldgirth Inn
Description: It’s claimed that Robert Burns was once a regular at this Gothic-style roadside pub. There’s a relaxed, unpretentious air about the place, from the friendly service to the generous cooking. Assured, modern dishes showcase well-balanced flavour combinations and a good level of precision; look out for well-executed desserts like rhubarb custard tart with blood orange and white chocolate. Smart, modern bedrooms make planning an overnight getaway even more appealing.

Name: Dulse
Address: 17 Queensferry Street, Edinburgh, EH2 4QW, United Kingdom
Description: Make it an occasion by starting with a cocktail in the ground floor wine bar before heading upstairs to enjoy terrific Scottish seafood. Traditional flavours, in dishes like Arbroath smokie tart and St Andrews lobster thermidor, sit alongside those boasting more of an Asian accent, such as banana leaf steamed hake with a coconut and coriander sauce; whichever style you prefer, the quality of the fish and shellfish really comes through.

Name: Craig Rogan at The Collective
Address: 33 Boar Lane, Leeds, LS1 5DA, United Kingdom
Description: Housed inside the creative hub that is 'The Collective', in the centre of bustling Leeds, this minimally decorated spot operates as a café by day and a restaurant by night. Thoroughly modern, clever cooking is offered by the eponymous chef, who knows how to put an immense amount of flavour into every dish – the violet potato with ox cheek, bone marrow and lovage is a prime example of the kitchen’s talents. Choose between a 5 or 8 course tasting menu, or from the concise à la carte.

Name: The Butcher's Tap and Grill
Address: 15 Spittal Street, Marlow, SL7 3HJ, United Kingdom
Description: Pick your meat from the butcher’s counter – perhaps prime, 28-day aged grass-fed Aberdeen Angus beef, Bythburgh pork or Suffolk Texel lamb – and it will be cooked to order on the grill in the open kitchen. Tom Kerridge’s team are a laid-back, friendly bunch – and you can even watch the footie as you eat.

Name: Bath Arms
Description: Sample local ales in the open-fired bar or on the delightful terrace of this stylishly updated 18C country inn on the Longleat Estate, then head for one of the numerous cosy, well-appointed dining rooms. The appealing menu mixes classical and modern dishes and keeps local producers to the fore; the delicious pies are a hit. Make a night of it and stay over in one of the modern, country house style bedrooms.

Name: Gauthier - Soho
Address: 21 Romilly Street, Soho, London, W1D 5AF, United Kingdom
Description: Right in the heart of Soho is this charming Regency townhouse, offering intimate, formal dining spread that is rarely found in a fully vegan restaurant – yet it's just what Chef-Owner Alexis Gauthier has set out to achieve. His tasting menu combines original dishes – like kohlrabi with aubergine, kamalata olive, spring greens and confit lemon – with classical French touches such as Landes asparagus with morels and a rich, glossy sauce. The ‘Petit Dîner’ menu, served early evening and Saturday lunchtime, offers a shorter experience and good value.

Name: The Walrus
Address: 2 Lower Claremont Bank, Shrewsbury, SY1 1RT, United Kingdom
Description: Young chef-owners Ben and Carla run this two-floored restaurant in Ben’s hometown; start with a drink in the upstairs bar, then watch them both in action in the open kitchen. Ambitious modern cooking delivers an intriguing blend of pronounced flavours and contrasting textures, and makes great use of Shropshire’s larder.

Name: Zaika
Address: 1 Kensington High Street, Kensington, London, W8 5NP, United Kingdom
Description: There are many original features on display in this wonderfully ornate former banking hall and, while it’s a spacious place, the team look after diners with consummate ease. Authentic cooking methods are used to create dishes from all corners of India; go for the tasting menu to sample the range.

Name: OXA
Address: 11 Rose Mount, Oxton, Birkenhead, CH43 5SG, United Kingdom
Description: The pretty suburb of Oxton is home to this attractive neighbourhood bistro which offers an appealing selection of small plates and sharing dishes, as well as an excellent value lunch menu. Cooking has a British base and the occasional Asian touch, with dishes such as tuna with dashi and onions providing great depth of flavour. There’s a lovely atmosphere about the place and the interesting wine list features almost exclusively British choices.

Name: Akira
Address: Japan House, 101-111 Kensington High Street, Kensington, London, W8 5SA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list
Description: Japan House promotes all things Japanese, so it’s appropriate that upstairs there’s a stylish, buzzing restaurant celebrating the country’s cuisine. The open kitchen is the focal point of the room, which offers both counter and table seating from which to enjoy the extensive selection of Japanese food. There’s a wide range of sushi, but it’s the skewers from the robata charcoal grill that are the highlight – such as asparagus wrapped with bacon or chicken and shiso meatballs.

Name: 45 Jermyn St
Address: 45 Jermyn Street, St James’s, London, SW1 6DN, United Kingdom
Description: Style and comfort go hand in hand at this bright, contemporary brasserie that delivers the classics with aplomb. The menu is a mix of European and British dishes, with the beef Wellington and lobster spaghetti both finished off at your table. Coupes and floats for dessert bring an old-school touch and pay tribute to its past as Fortnum’s Fountain restaurant. Slick service and the undeniably luxurious surroundings make a visit even more appealing.

Name: The Baring
Address: 55 Baring Street, Islington, London, N1 3DS, United Kingdom
Description: It may look like just another renovated pub in a smart residential street, but the food here displays far more imagination and ability that usual gastropub fare. There are influences from across Europe, with dishes that are uncluttered yet full of flavour; the quail shish is already a favourite starter for many. They’ve gone for cool simplicity with the décor; and service that is warm and outgoing.

Name: Cowley Manor
Description: This restaurant inside a glorious Cotswolds country house hotel offers bold, vibrant cooking that’s worthy of the rather lovely setting. Start with a drink in the sleek bar, before settling in the panelled dining room that cleverly fuses its original features with more modern elements. The cooking has Mediterranean influences and uses British ingredients well, in dishes like the house-made taglioni with Cornish lobster and pickled chilli. For dessert, their fresh-out-the-oven madeleines are hard to resist.

Name: 64 Goodge Street
Address: 64 Goodge Street, Bloomsbury, London, W1T 4NF, United Kingdom
Description: Sister restaurant to Portland and Clipstone, this small bistro deluxe delivers intimate and relaxed surroundings in which to enjoy a menu based around classical French cooking. British Racing Green walls blend with simple polished wood, candle-lit tables and wicker chairs, while the semi-open kitchen brings a livelier atmosphere to one end of the room. Fine ingredients are used to good effect in bold, gutsy combinations that deliver on flavour; ensure you save room to finish with the gâteau marjolaine.

Name: Embers
Address: 42 Meeting House Lane, Brighton and Hove, BN1 1HB, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in the heart of Brighton’s famous Lanes, you’ll find this contemporary bistro with a big, wood-fired heart. Their ethos is all about sharing food with friends around a fire, with a menu that combines small plates like charred broccoli with centrepiece dishes for sharing, such as venison rump or whole sea bass. As you would expect, plenty of smoky flavour comes through in the well-executed, accessible dishes.

Name: Locanda on the Weir
Address: Porlock Weir, Exmoor National Park, Porlock, TA24 8PB, United Kingdom
Description: Set overlooking the 15C harbour at Porlock Weir, this relaxed, slightly quirky restaurant with rooms has just five tables. You'll be warmly greeted by manager Cindy, as well as chef Pio, who hails from Naples and brings influences from his upbringing to the daily 5 course tasting menu. Modern Italian dishes champion the produce of Exmoor, with some ingredients either foraged or grown in the garden. Pio’s cooking is creative and full of flavour, but at times takes an unfussy approach to allow the natural ingredients to shine.

Name: Faru
Address: 29 Silver Street, Durham, DH1 3RD, United Kingdom
Description: Its name comes from an old English word for ‘journey’, but there is something decidedly contemporary about this city centre restaurant – from the airy, pared-back interior to the on-trend open kitchen and terse menu descriptions. An antique stained-glass window adds character and makes a fine backdrop for the chefs as they show their immense talent across colourful, precisely executed dishes that utilise punchy flavours like pickled walnut, mushroom ketchup and sweet carrot purée.

Name: MINE
Address: 4 The Old Brewery Yard, Falmouth, TR11 2BY, United Kingdom
Description: Hidden away in an attractive courtyard, this rustic little bistro is well worth the climb up the steep High Street. It’s a cosy, welcoming place, where the informality contributes to a light buzz among the contented diners. An open kitchen allows for a good view of the classic, well-crafted cooking, which takes the form of a concise, regularly changing à la carte which relies on local produce. You'd do well to start with the fabulous crab fritter and end with the honey cake.

Name: Dovetale
Address: 3 Berkeley Street, Mayfair, London, WD1 8DL, United Kingdom
Description: Like the hotel in which it sits – 1 Hotel Mayfair – Dovetale makes good use of natural materials and plenty of plants to create a warm, bright environment. It also has a great terrace and a welcoming atmosphere. The menu looks to Europe for its contemporary dishes; go for one to be shared, like the whole roasted 'Somerset Saxon' chicken. If you’re after a bit of nostalgia, you can design your own Knickerbocker Glory for dessert.

Name: Pignut
Address: 12 Bridge Street, Helmsley, YO62 5DX, United Kingdom
Description: With just six tables, there is a cosy feel to this little restaurant with clean, unfussy décor. Dishes are fed by produce from the surrounding area, including Helmsley Walled Garden and the Castle Howard estate, while the tasting menu – available in 4 or 8 courses – begins with a ‘wastage’ dish which uses up offcuts from the other courses. The cooking showcases a range of textures and flavours, sometimes with an imaginative touch. Foraged cocktails, a short but appealing choice of wines and personable service round out the experience.

Name: Bramley
Address: 10 Main Street, Knockamoe, Abbeyleix, R32 D8C0, Ireland
Description: There’s an endearing quality to this characterful restaurant run by a young, friendly team and set inside a former garage and shop. The cooking champions the County Laois larder and other Irish produce, in satisfying dishes with tried-and-tested flavour combinations. At dinner, choose from the concise à la carte or sample the kitchen’s full range of talents with the 7 course tasting menu. Lunchtime is a slightly simpler affair and features daily specials.

Name: Skua
Address: 49 St Stephen Street,  Stockbridge, Edinburgh, EH3 5AH, United Kingdom
Description: This tiny basement operation in the suburb of Stockbridge comes with dark, moody décor and impressive cooking from the get-go. The menu of rustic sharing plates pushes flavour-packed British ingredients to the fore and the dishes are pleasingly free of superfluous elements, with the signature fried chicken being a particular highlight. A carefully curated list includes a selection of natural wines, with those available by the glass listed on the blackboard. Cheery, well-organised service adds to the experience.

Name: Kebbells
Address: 8 Victoria Parade, Broadstairs, CT10 1QS, United Kingdom
Description: Located right on the coast, in an area known as the jewel in Thanet's crown, this is the perfect spot for a seafood restaurant. The dining room is bedecked with a multitude of mirrors, a large open counter and shelves filled with jars of preserved goods and house-made chilli sauce. As with all good seafood eateries, the menu changes with the daily catch; all the prime ingredients are well-cooked and delivered in carefully balanced combinations. The cheery, relaxed staff run the place wonderfully, giving everything a personal touch.

Name: The Lime Tree Inn
Address: Branton Lane, Great Ouseburn, YO26 9RS, United Kingdom
Description: This North Yorkshire village inn is a 'proper' pub run by a friendly team, so you’ll always find plenty of locals in the bar. The kitchen team work away behind a large glass window on vibrant, flavoursome dishes that marry together complementary local ingredients. Portions are generous and a tasting menu is available too if you want to experience a broader range of dishes. The site also houses seven bedrooms, making it a good base from which to explore York, Harrogate and Castle Howard.

Name: Boys Hall
Address: Boys Hall Road, Willesborough, Ashford, TN24 OLA, United Kingdom
Description: Built in 1616 for the Boys family, this charming old house has been sympathetically converted into a hotel with eye-catching features at every turn, plus 3 acres of gardens and land. The restaurant sits in an extension to the main house and serves local Kent produce, with Romney Marsh lamb a firm favourite. Great wines, also from Kent, are available to pair with your food and, should you wish to grab a drink before dining, the grounds also house a pub with a terrace.

Name: Tendril
Address: 5 Princes Street, Mayfair, London, W1B 2LQ, United Kingdom
Description: There are a range of global influences to be found across the vegetable-led dishes at this ‘mostly vegan’ restaurant, from the massaman sauce with pak choi to the ‘Chinatown’ purple potatoes. There’s technical skill on display too and a strong understanding of textures in particular. It’s a smart place, with the feel of a neighbourhood restaurant; the front room, with plenty of natural light, is best for lunch, while the slightly moodier rear makes for a more intimate dinner.

Name: Archway
Address: Arch 65, Queen's Circus, Wandsworth, London, SW8 4NE, United Kingdom
Description: As the name suggests, this restaurant is nestled underneath the railway arches close to Battersea Park and the chic Battersea Power Station development. You may hear the rumble of trains overhead, but it’s often replaced by the buzz of diners flocking here to try the rustic Italian cooking with an appealing simplicity. Their focaccia is a stand out, while dishes like charred octopus with paprika romesco sauce put quality ingredients front and centre. The personable, engaging service team will make your visit even more enjoyable.

Name: Forge
Address: Middleton Lodge Estate, Kneeton Lane, Middleton Tyas, DL10 6NJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The sprawling Middleton Lodge Estate stretches out over 200 acres and today includes this creative restaurant which sits inside the forge that once served the estate. The tasting menu – which also comes in both vegetarian and vegan forms – features seasonal produce, including some grown on the Estate, where they even harvest their own honey and birch sap. The cooking demonstrates a strong grasp of balance and flavour, with dishes that allow these local ingredients to shine like the picture-perfect Reuben blackberry and pineapple weed tart.

Name: Heaneys
Address: 6-10 Romilly Crescent, Cardiff, CF11 9NR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Arrive early for a cocktail in the bar of well-known Chef Tommy Heaney’s stylishly laid-back suburban restaurant. Dishes are seasonal and modern, with some sophisticated contrasts; the set lunch menu delivers good value while, at dinner, the tasting menu takes centre stage. Next door is Uisce – his no-reservations, small plates restaurant – which showcases herbs and vegetables from the pretty kitchen garden.

Name: Charlie's
Address: 33 Albemarle Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 4BP, United Kingdom
Description: Olga Polizzi’s design provides an elegant, stylish backdrop to this intimate restaurant, which is named after her father, the late Sir Charles Forte, and located in quintessential English hotel, Brown’s. Adam Byatt’s menu offers tasty classic British dishes with a modern twist.

Name: The Hoebridge
Address: Hoebridge Road East, Gattonside, TD6 9LZ, United Kingdom
Description: This welcoming former inn represents a return home for its self-taught Chef-Owner, who grew up in this Scottish Borders village and even worked in this place as a youngster. After a stint in New York City, he and his partner are back to run The Hoebridge as a simple, stylish restaurant serving flavour-packed, internationally influenced dishes. Quality local ingredients form the basis of the dishes, which are carefully prepared with an ambitious touch. Ebullient service adds to the welcoming feel of it all.

Name: North Port
Address: 8 North Port, Perth, PH1 5LU, United Kingdom
Description: Located in an end of terrace cottage dating back to the 18C, this appealing restaurant blends its characterful, dark oak panelled walls and ceiling with a bright, contemporary look. Unfussy, modern cooking proudly name-checks Scottish ingredients and comes with plenty of flavour. Be sure to try their delicious homemade haggis.

Name: The Gaff
Address: 4 The Courtyard, Lion Street, Abergavenny, NP7 5PE, United Kingdom
Description: Three converted sheds hidden away in the heart of town play host to The Gaff: a bright, airy restaurant with a high ceiling and contemporary art hung on white walls. Menus list an appealing selection of well-priced small plates, which range from deep-fried mackerel to local game.

Name: Maiden Arch by Robert Bryant
Address: 14 Maiden Street, Barnstaple, EX31 1HA, United Kingdom
Description: What started as a pop-up at No.16 has now become a permanent restaurant at No.14. Enter into a cosy bar and up the spiral staircase to a dining room with exposed brick walls and a vaulted ceiling. Confident cooking is carefully thought-out and dishes deliver a good balance of flavours and textures.

Name: Peckham Cellars
Address: 125 Queens Road, Southwark, London, SE15 2ND, United Kingdom
Description: This neighbourhood bistro and wine bar is run by three friends, who all hail from this part of South East London. Original small plates have a rustic style; they’re made for sharing, so choose three or four per person – if you’re in a group, consider ordering the whole menu. The wine list features some interesting small producers and they even have some wines on tap.

Name: Henrock
Address: Linthwaite House, Crook Road, Bowness-on-Windermere, LA23 3JA, United Kingdom
Description: Named after a rocky outcrop on Lake Windermere, this elegant restaurant sits inside the charming Linthwaite House hotel and is part of Simon Rogan's ever-evolving empire. The décor is minimal yet cosy, with plain wooden tables and lovely artwork on the walls. Simon's sustainable ethos is evident on the menu, with many ingredients in the colourful dishes coming from his 'Our Farm' estate and other produce – like Cartmel Valley venison – sourced in the local area. Warm, friendly staff enhance the experience.

Name: Osteria Lucio
Address: The Malting Tower, Grand Canal Dock, Clanwilliam Terrace, Dublin City, D02 DW90, Ireland
Description: An elegant restaurant with a lively ambience, set under the railway arches and run by two experienced chefs. Carefully cooked Italian dishes are full of flavour and are accompanied by an all-Italian wine list and a good selection of cocktails. Service is friendly yet professional.

Name: Pompette
Address: 7 South Parade, Summertown, Oxford, OX2 7JL, United Kingdom
Description: Located in a lovely suburb is this neat, attractive modern brasserie run by an experienced chef and his welcoming wife. There are a few Mediterranean and North African influences on the menu, but the French basis is clear – as evidenced by classic dishes like fish soup with rouille, Gruyère and croutons. The cooking is honest, unfussy and full of flavour, and there's a good value ‘prix fixe’ on offer too.

Name: Takahashi
Address: 228 Merton Road, Merton, London, SW19 1EQ, United Kingdom
Description: The eponymous chef-owner of this sweet spot is a Nobu alumnus and his wife runs the service with a personal touch. Prime ingredients might include Wagyu beef and fish landed in Cornwall; dishes offer up pure, delicate flavours – and the sushi and sashimi are a must.

Name: Llewelyn's
Address: 293-295 Railton Road, Lambeth, London, SE24 0JP, United Kingdom
Description: Sitting just outside Herne Hill station, with its large windows letting diners look out and passers-by to look in, Llewellyn’s feels like a proper neighbourhood restaurant at the heart of the local community. The menu offers an appealing mix of dishes with a Mediterranean accent which focus on the freshness of the ingredients, and service is young and endearing.

Name: Colbert
Address: 50-52 Sloane Square, Chelsea, London, SW1W 8AX, United Kingdom
Description: With its posters, chessboard tiles and red leather seats, Colbert bears more than a passing resemblance to a Parisian pavement café. It’s an all-day, every day operation and the menu lists all the French classics, so you can pop in for breakfast or a croque monsieur or linger over a steak Diane.

Name: Leroy
Address: 18 Phipp Street, Shoreditch, London, EC2A 4NU, United Kingdom
Description: As you step through the door of this laid-back restaurant you’ll be greeted by broad smiles and a buzzy atmosphere. The kitchen counter provides the perfect opportunity for chef watching and the friendly team look as though they’re having as much fun as their guests while they serve unpretentious dishes like crispy pigs head with celeriac, date and almond. The interesting wine list, offering a great mix of classics and lesser-known gems, adds to the experience.

Name: Roast
Address: The Floral Hall, Borough Market, Southwark, London, SE1 1TL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Roast is known for its British food and for promoting UK producers – which shouldn’t really come as a surprise considering its location in the heart of Borough Market. Ask for a table looking out over the bustle, and go for the Market Menu with bottomless prosecco.

Name: Trullo
Address: 300-302 St Paul's Road, Canonbury, London, N1 2LH, United Kingdom
Description: A stalwart of the local dining scene, this split-level restaurant is a hit with the locals and has a true neighbourhood feel. An open kitchen contributes to the light, buzzy atmosphere and the casually dressed service team are a perfect fit for the style of the place. The daily changing menu of rustic Italian dishes makes great use of the charcoal grill and the delicious pasta is hand-rolled before each service.

Name: Spry
Address: 1 Haddington Place, Edinburgh, EH7 4AE, United Kingdom
Description: Set on the ground floor of a classic Georgian house by the famous Leith Walk, this wine shop sells a wide selection of naturally produced, organic wines. You can enjoy them in-house alongside some delicious seasonal dishes, where you have the option to choose from the à la carte or go for the 5 course set menu. Owners Matt and Marzena are always on hand to offer advice, and also run a basement coffee shop and in-house bakery selling some delightful sourdough.

Name: Artusi
Address: 161 Bellenden Road, Southwark, London, SE15 4DH, United Kingdom
Description: This enthusiastically run neighbourhood bistro is named after Pellegrino Artusi, who wrote ‘The Science of Cooking and the Art of Fine Dining’ back in 1891. Seasonal ingredients lead the way in honest, largely Italian-influenced dishes – and prices are more than fair.

Name: Cabotte
Address: 48 Gresham Street, City of London, London, EC2V 7AY, United Kingdom
Description: Classic French cooking yields plenty of flavour at this appealing bistro de luxe with distressed décor and plenty of rustic charm. The Gallic influence is clear to see on the menu, with dishes like beef tartare and pâté-en-croûte on offer; quality produce is key to the ingredient-led dishes, to which the chefs bring an assured, accomplished hand. It’s owned by two master sommeliers who share a passion for the wines of Burgundy, so the stunning wine list understandably offers a top-notch selection.

Name: Shikumen
Address: 58 Shepherd's Bush Green, Hammersmith & Fulham, London, W12 8QE, United Kingdom
Description: Set within the Dorset Hotel, Shikumen might not appear to be anything out of the ordinary – that is, until it comes to the food. Care and skill go into preparing a mix of regional Chinese and slightly westernised dishes. The balance of textures and flavours is excellent, and the dim sum are superb.

Name: Scully
Address: 4 St. James's Market, St James’s, London, SW1Y 4AH, United Kingdom
Description: The eponymous chef-owner’s travels and family heritage inform his style of food, so his dishes feature an array of international influences. Punchy, diverse flavours give the cooking an appealing vitality and the kitchen makes good use of the shelves laden with spices, pickles, preserves and oils. The tasting menu leads the way, but there’s also a fixed price 2 or 3 course menu available Tuesday to Saturday.

Name: Pig and Butcher
Address: 80 Liverpool Road, Islington, London, N1 OQD, United Kingdom
Description: In-house butchered meats reign supreme at this rustic, mid-19th Century pub, which is filled with diners and drinkers alike, all contributing to the lively atmosphere. 'Seasonal' and 'British' are the guiding principles behind produce ranging from Aberdeen Angus to Sutton Hoo chicken. The deeply addictive beef dripping served with the bread is one of the highlights of the experience, but it faces stiff competition from the likes of melt-in-the-mouth braised short rib.

Name: Bull & Last
Address: 168 Highgate Road, Dartmouth Park, London, NW5 1QS, United Kingdom
Description: Hearty British dishes which are big on flavour are the order of the day at this sympathetically refurbished Victorian pub. The ground floor bar has a lively buzz and the more sedate first floor dining room opens later in the week. The terrific mushroom tempura is a prime example of what this kitchen does well: straightforward, moreish dishes that come in generous portions. Lovely bedrooms and a friendly, attentive team complete the picture.

Name: Caia
Address: 46 Golborne Road, North Kensington, London, W10 5PR, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Fire, wine, vinyl’ it says outside this cool Notting Hill spot – and that pretty much sums it up. The sharing plates benefit from the kitchen’s skill at cooking over an open fire – don’t miss the black carrot with sea urchin sauce; wines are varied and well chosen; and downstairs a DJ delves deep into a diverse album collection. Come with friends for a fun night out.

Name: Cheal's
Address: 1630 High Street, Knowle, B93 0JU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Behind the half-timbered walls of this stylish building lies a spacious restaurant that pays tribute to British culture, be it the Union Jacks on the curtains or the model Spitfire hanging from the ceiling. In the cooking, Chef Matt Cheal uses prime British produce from Cornish lamb to Orkney scallops for dishes that showcase his adept modern technique. Start your evening in style in the smart Warren’s Bar or, for a lighter meal, stay there all night to enjoy individual dishes from the tasting menu served as small plates.

Name: Langan's Brasserie
Address: Stratton Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8LB, United Kingdom
Description: Few London restaurants can boast quite as colourful a history as this Mayfair institution, which was a veritable trailblazer when it opened back in the 1970s. Now refreshed and relaunched, it retains much of what made it so popular in its heyday, particularly when it comes to its menu; it has something for everyone and every occasion, so you can expect to find all the brasserie classics, from Caesar salad and fish pie, to beef Rossini and rum baba.

Name: Bowleys at The Plough
Address: The  Plough Inn, Taylor's Lane, Trottiscliffe, ME19 5DR, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away down a narrow street, The Plough proudly declares that it is 'community owned, family run'. The community in question is the people of Trottiscliffe, who rallied round to buy and refurbish their local pub when property developers were circling. Among their number was the Yates family, who now look after this small restaurant offering a concise menu of carefully crafted, ambitious and classically based dishes. Local produce, some of it their own, informs the menus – even the butter is homemade.

Name: The Blind Bull
Description: High up in the hills of the Derbyshire Peak District sits this 12C stone-built pub with seating over two floors and a rustic, cosy feel. The concise menu offers refined classics with a focus on flavour and a great selection for vegetarians. Sit in the conservatory overlooking the moors.

Name: Minster Mill
Address: Minster Ridings, Minster Lovell, OX29 0RN, United Kingdom
Description: This characterful, oak-beamed restaurant is set in a charming Cotswold stone building surrounded by beautiful gardens with a river running through them. The modern British dishes come with a creative touch and are prepared with care, letting the natural flavours and textures of the ingredients shine through. Smooth, attentive service adds to the experience.

Name: Chef's Table
Address: 1a Avon Crescent, City of Bristol, BS1 6XQ, United Kingdom
Description: In the old part of the city close to the famous docks you’ll find this intimate, personally run, 2-room restaurant, with a small front terrace, a warm service team and a buzzing atmosphere. The two menus – most diners plump for the tasting menu – offer original, modern and sometimes intricate dishes, which are aesthetically striking and full of flavour.

Name: The Lanesborough Grill
Address: Hyde Park Corner, Belgravia, London, SW1X 7TA, United Kingdom
Description: This ornately decorated restaurant sits at the heart of the Lanesborough Hotel. Its menu moves with the seasons, offering modern British dishes brimming with prime ingredients, and includes lighter options as well as plenty for carnivores. Old school desserts are delivered with a degree of refinement, as befits the surroundings. Weekend dinners come with musical accompaniment.

Name: Bay Horse
Address: 45 The Green, Hurworth on Tees, DL2 2AA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The jewel in the crown of this smart 15C coaching inn is its lovely garden and terrace – closely followed by its caramelised rice pudding! Ambitious modern dishes are made up of many elements and service comes courtesy of a smart, structured team.

Name: Quaglino's
Address: 16 Bury Street, St James’s, London, SW1Y 6AJ, United Kingdom
Description: This colourful, glamorous restaurant manages to be cavernous and cosy at the same time, with live music and a late night bar adding a certain sultriness to proceedings. The kitchen specialises in contemporary brasserie-style food.

Name: Bandol
Address: 6 Hollywood Road, Chelsea, London, SW10 9HY, United Kingdom
Description: A true neighbourhood restaurant, Bandol offers a delightful all-round package to the residents of Chelsea, from the bright, airy décor to the genial, welcoming service. A 100 year old olive tree stands in the middle of the dining room, evoking sunny days spent on the French Riviera. The menu reflects this, with inspiration coming from all over the Mediterranean, including plenty of Provençal and Niçoise influences. Seafood is often a highlight, but if you're visiting on a cold day don't overlook the restorative power of the confit duck with lentil stew.

Name: Hakkasan Hanway Place
Address: 8 Hanway Place, Bloomsbury, London, W1T 1HD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The very first Hakkasan continues to offer a great night out, thanks to its moody, sensual looks and glamorous, energetic atmosphere. It's well-suited to both a romantic date or a group celebration, and it's certainly worth arriving early for a cocktail or two in the bar. Luxury Cantonese specialities are plentiful across the choice of menus, with the set 'Signature' options representing the best value for money.

Name: Quality Chop House
Address: 91-94 Farringdon Road, Finsbury, London, EC1R 3EA, United Kingdom
Description: A landmark London restaurant with a history dating back to 1869, this ‘progressive working class caterer’ champions quality British produce, with the focus on steaks and chops, like Belted Galloway rib-eye, Mangalitsa loin and Barnsley chops; just be sure to also order their deliciously crunchy confit potatoes. The booths are the prized seats and the wine list contains lots of gems, more of which are available at their wine bar just next door.

Name: Café Deco
Address: 43 Store Street, Bloomsbury, London, WC1E 7DB, United Kingdom
Description: The chefs also get involved in the service here at this simply furnished, intimate restaurant. Their dishes are fresh, seasonal, appealingly straightforward and packed with flavour, whether that’s cured ham hock, a lovely smoked eel pie or their delicious chicken. It's one of those relaxed restaurants where you know you’re in the hands of a clued-up and experienced team.

Name: Ochre
Address: The National Gallery, Trafalgar Square, St James’s, London, WC2N 5DN, United Kingdom
Description: Situated on the ground floor of the iconic William Wilkins building, this smart, comfortable bistro deluxe is revolutionising museum dining. All-day menus offer something for everyone, from brunch to dinner, via afternoon tea. Small and large plates have sharing in mind; flavours are vivid and international influences abound.

Name: Chapter One
Address: Farnborough Common, Locksbottom, Bromley, London, BR6 8NF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: They’ve got a loyal following at this long-standing restaurant that offers an extensive and appealing menu of modern European dishes. The cooking has some light, delicate touches and prime British produce cooked on the Josper grill is a feature, like Cornish monkfish or Angus rib-eye. It’s all delivered inside a property that dates back to the 1930s and there are subtle references to this period in the elegant décor. The service team bring an enthusiastic smile and real care to their work.

Name: The Three Fishes
Address: Mitton Road, Mitton, BB7 9PQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Nigel Howarth has always been a strong ambassador for Lancashire produce – particularly from the Ribble Valley – and now has his own vegetable garden and polytunnel at this contemporary dining pub. Set menus change with the seasons, and the cooking lacks pretence, instead allowing the true flavours to shine through. The cheese rolls and mini Eccles cakes look set to become staples.

Name: The Forager
Address: 19-23 Bridge Street, Dollar, FK14 7DE, United Kingdom
Description: A rural village in Clackmannanshire is the setting for this warm, unfussy pub. Set over two floors, The Forager’s place as the local pub has not been forgotten, despite a stylish renovation. A short menu showcases pub classics and a few more creative dishes. At the heart of it all is good produce, which is brought to life with care and attention, in dishes that have plenty of flavour.

Name: Planque
Address: 322-324 Acton Mews, Dalston, London, E8 4EA, United Kingdom
Description: Set under two railway arches, this boldly styled restaurant is centred around a huge communal table. Listed in size order, the modern British dishes are far more complex than they first appear and show tremendous skill from the kitchen. They are often comprised of three main ingredients, all working in perfect harmony to achieve a great balance of flavours: succulent guinea fowl, for example, might be complemented by earthy Jerusalem artichoke and a hint of bitterness from radicchio. The interesting wine list has an emphasis on small-scale and low-intervention producers.

Name: Salt Yard
Address: 54 Goodge Street, Bloomsbury, London, W1T 4NA, United Kingdom
Description: Having opened it 2005, this buzzy basement restaurant was one of the first in the city to offer small plates and promote the sharing philosophy. Spanish and Italian flavours lead the way, with top-notch ingredients showcased in a mix of traditional and more imaginative dishes. Plenty of Spanish wines and sherries are there to accompany, and the serving team are enthusiastic and sincere. The booths at the back are a great spot.

Name: Chatora
Address: 100 Kew Road, Richmond-Upon-Thames, London, TW9 2PQ, United Kingdom
Description: With dining on 3 levels and bifold doors leading onto a small terrace, you can sit somewhere different every time you come. The experienced owner and 3 chefs represent the North, East, South and West of India. Generously proportioned, original dishes are authentically spiced and burst with flavour.

Name: Jolene
Address: 21  Newington Green, Islington, London, N16 9PU, United Kingdom
Description: Jolene is the sort of place that we'd all love to have at the end of our street. It's a bakery first and foremost, selling wonderful pastries, biscuits and cakes – as well as delicious bread from flour they mill themselves. There's also a daily written blackboard menu of confidently executed sharing plates, with their house-made pasta something of a feature. The vibe is relaxed and the friendly service team will ensure you're well looked after. You can find more of the same at their Hornsey Road branch.

Name: Bocca di Lupo
Address: 12 Archer Street, Soho, London, WID 7BB, United Kingdom
Description: Longevity in this part of town is a mighty achievement, but it's easy to see why Bocca di Lupo has remained popular for so long. Besides the switched-on service and buzzing atmosphere, the cooking itself provides the classic Italian techniques that everyone loves. The extensive menu takes you on a journey around Italy, with the region of origin listed beside each dish; share some fritti Romani while you make your decision. The marble counter is the place to sit and, for the sweet-toothed, the team also run an ice cream shop, Gelupo, across the road.

Name: Art Sushi
Address: 42E Poole Road, Bournemouth, BH4 9DW, United Kingdom
Description: You can sit at individual oak-topped tables, but it’s at the counter where you can best appreciate the humble and determined approach of chef-owner Kamil. His dream of opening a bright, busy sushi restaurant became a reality here in the suburbs of Bournemouth. The seafood and vegetarian preparations are undertaken with care, understanding and respect; remove the stress of decision making by going for the omakase menu.

Name: Etto
Address: 18 Merrion Row, Dublin City, D02 A316, Ireland
Description: Etto means ‘little’ and this cosy, rustic restaurant close to the National Gallery certainly fits the bill. Start with a snack and a sherry before enjoying eye-catching, modern dishes which are generously sized and full of flavour. The comprehensive wine list has a focus on the Med.

Name: Pickle
Address: 43 Lower Camden Street, Dublin City, D02 N998, Ireland
Description: The modest exterior of this restaurant belies the buzzing atmosphere within. It’s a busy spot and deservedly so, with fresh, vibrant dishes and a service team that do a great job of handling their huge popularity. With spices lined up on the kitchen counter, the chefs aim to marry Irish produce with Northern Indian techniques and flavours in what they sweetly call ‘pickle country’. There’s a good value midweek lunch menu on offer and a tasting menu at dinner alongside the à la carte.

Name: Apricity
Address: 68 Duke Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 6JU, United Kingdom
Description: Just yards from the bustle of Oxford Street is a veritable sanctuary of calm. Chef-owner Chantelle Nicholson’s bright and welcoming restaurant comes with delightful service and a menu that showcases seasonal British ingredients from small producers with whom she’s built strong relationships. Her green credentials are omnipresent and inform her every decision.

Name: Goldsborough Hall
Address: Church Street, Goldsborough, HG5 8NR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: A pretty village plays host to this grand, 16C country house which is surrounded by delightful grounds. There might be a classically formal feel to the place but not when it comes to the food. Modern, French-based dishes are eye-catching, well-balanced and full of bold flavours, with a good mix of classic and contemporary techniques showcasing the skill of the team. Go for the tasting menu with accompanying wine pairings.

Name: River Restaurant by Gordon Ramsay
Address: Savoy Hotel, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2R 0EU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Gordon Ramsay’s second restaurant within the iconic Savoy Hotel offers a great Thames view and an extensive menu specialising in top quality fish and shellfish from UK waters; sit at the seafood counter if you’re after caviar, oysters or ceviche. The ‘River Trio’ perform as the weekend approaches.

Name: Garden Café
Address: Boath House, Auldearn, Nairn, IV12 5TE, United Kingdom
Description: The Scottish outpost to London’s 'Sessions Arts Club' exudes a charming, bohemian vibe. It is set in a delightful walled garden within the 16-acre grounds of a beautiful Georgian mansion and much of the seating is on a covered terrace. The concise menu delivers a range of unfussy, European-influenced dishes designed for sharing, with some ingredients coming directly from the gardens.

Name: Belzan
Address: 371 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, L15 3JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Its somewhat unassuming location makes this smart, modern bistro stand out even more. The cooking offers well-judged, interesting combinations, with portions that are as generous as they flavoursome, but while sharing is encouraged, dishes work better on their own; the Guinness rarebit potato is a must. They also offer a good value early dinner menu. The narrow room has a cosy feel, and service is confident and clued-up.

Name: The Morrison Room
Address: Carton House, Carton Demesne, Maynooth, W23 TD98, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: We all need a little luxury in our lives and this beautiful restaurant in the heart of Carton House, an impressive Palladian mansion among manicured grounds, ticks all the boxes. The breathtaking room features a high curved ceiling, Greek Corinthian columns, ornate plaster cornicing and sweeping banquettes, while the menu showcases fine Irish produce in well-judged and original combinations with a confident classical base. Dishes like veal sweetbreads with cep vinaigrette and black garlic match their surroundings with a luxurious edge.

Name: Lusin
Address: 16 Hay Hill, Mayfair, London, W1J 8NY, United Kingdom
Description: In the swish streets of Mayfair sits this stylish and moody London incarnation of a restaurant first popularised in Saudi Arabia. If you are unfamiliar with Armenian cuisine then this is an enjoyable place to discover it, whilst relaxing underneath the striking mirrored ceiling. The menu mixes Armenian specialities, such as dolma and manti, with some Levantine dishes, and the kitchen takes great care in what they produce.

Name: Ophelia
Address: 6-10 Bowsden Terrace, South Gosforth, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE3 1RX, United Kingdom
Description: There is a pleasing lack of over-complication to the food at this slick neighbourhood brasserie that wears its French heart on its sleeve. Great care is put into the cooking by an on-view kitchen team and the Gallic influence can be seen across the range of thoroughly enjoyable dishes, which are presented with a friendly smile. The French focus also extends to the low-intervention wine list.

Name: Library Street
Address: 101 Setanta Place, Dublin City, DO2 W3Y7, Ireland
Description: As you open the door to this trendy restaurant, you’re greeted by a lively buzz and smiling faces. Sit at the counter or one of the lovingly restored 100-year-old ash tables, while surrounded by laughter and contented chatter. The cooking comes in the form of a regularly changing menu of sharing plates, including options like roast lamb with kalamata olives and Jerusalem artichoke. Local ingredients are key to the bold, original dishes.

Name: Birchwood
Address: 13 Flimwell Park, Hawkhurst Road, Flimwell, TN5 7FJ, United Kingdom
Description: Set in a sustainable business park in 46 acres of woodland, this bistro features communal tables and a lovely terrace overlooking the trees. The daily changing breakfast and lunch menu is informed by the owners’ sustainable ethos, the seasons and the surroundings, and dishes are fresh and full of flavour.

Name: Homestead Kitchen
Address: Prudom House, Goathland, YO22 5AN, United Kingdom
Description: The North York Moors and their produce are the inspiration behind this charming little restaurant housed inside a rural, stone-built former farmhouse. Local ingredients, be they Moorland roe deer or Whitby crab, are used in hearty dishes that pack a punch when it comes to flavour. Sauces and accompaniments are a particular strength of Chef-Owner Peter Neville, who runs the place with pride alongside his partner Cecily Fearnley.

Name: Maison
Address: Wrecclesham House, Wrecclesham Road, Wrecclesham, GU10 4PS, United Kingdom
Description: In this lovely 15C red-brick house, chef Ben Piette and his wife Lornette found the ideal setting for their dream project. They live upstairs and have converted the downstairs to serve their guests, but view the whole thing as part of their home. The constantly changing surprise tasting menu features plenty of local ingredients in assured dishes which have a French base. Sit at one of just a handful of tables or book “Ben’s Table” in front of the open kitchen; here you can bring in your own ingredient which he will use to create an extra course. Lornette treats guests as if they were old friends, which helps add to the ‘dinner party’ feel.

Name: Cyprus Avenue
Address: 228-230 Upper Newtownards Road, Belfast, BT4 3ET, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You’ll find something for everyone at this appealing, all-day bistro. It’s a big, busy place: head for one of the booths or the lovely covered terrace. There’s an extensive choice at breakfast, while at lunch and dinner, freshly baked breads come with delicious hop butter and are followed by a wide selection of original, modern dishes.

Name: Craig Millar @ 16 West End
Address: 16 West End, St Monans, KY10 2BX, United Kingdom
Description: A former pub with an attractive interior and a small terrace; most of the tables afford superb harbour views and, as one might expect, there’s a seafood bias to the menus. Good quality ingredients underpin refined, attractively presented dishes which are full of flavour. There’s a good value set price lunch menu, and the evening tasting menus come with a choice of main course.

Name: 'Seasgair' by Michel Roux Jr
Address: Inverlochy Castle, Torlundy, Fort William, PH33 6SN, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Seasgair’ means ‘warm and cosy’ in Gaelic, and diners certainly feel cosseted in the impressive Inverlochy Castle. Begin with an aperitif in the Grand Hall, accompanied by a harpist. Once seated in one of the elegant dining rooms, the 5-course set menu is served to everyone at the same time. Dishes are refined and full of flavour, and Michel Roux Jr’s influence sees a few French touches added into the Scottish mix.

Name: Killiecrankie House
Description: A young couple swapped their city lifestyle for this period country house in the Cairngorms National Park, which they lovingly restored to fuse original and modern features. Arrive at 7pm for drinks before dining on a tasting menu of Scottish classics brought playfully up to date. Bedrooms are sumptuous.

Name: Cafe Cecilia
Address: Canal Place, 32 Andrews Road, Dalston, London, E8 4FX, United Kingdom
Description: Don’t be fooled by the name, for this popular local spot is less a café, more a pared-back, industrial-style restaurant with a modern bistro feel. The chef previously worked at St John and the River Café, and now mixes these influences with his Irish heritage. The Guinness Bread ice cream is sublime.

Name: Edie's
Address: 10 Beach Road, Carlyon Bay, St Austell, PL25 3PH, United Kingdom
Description: It's a family affair at this relaxed, friendly restaurant, with Nigel at the stoves, and his wife Kelly out front, aided by their daughter, the eponymous Edie. Inside, brightly coloured chairs stand out against whitewashed brick walls; the shelves are crammed with cookbooks, and there’s a buzz from the open kitchen. Nigel’s experience shows in the unfussy modern British dishes, which deliver appealing and effective flavour combinations with notable clarity.

Name: Lunar
Address: World of Wedgwood, Barlaston, Stoke-on-Trent, ST12 9ER, United Kingdom
Description: Housed in the former staff canteen of the ‘World of Wedgwood’ factory, this vast restaurant is named after The Lunar Society of which Josiah Wedgwood himself was a founding member. Naturally, fine Wedgwood china and tableware is a feature. Dinner is a surprise tasting menu of mostly prime British ingredients but with the occasional Asian influence. The hidden bar is a great place for a drink and the chef’s table looks through a large window into the kitchen. Be sure to take a look round their Lunar Storehouse produce shop as well.

Name: Smoke
Address: Shadowbrook Lane, Hampton in Arden, B92 0EN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: There’s an air of relaxed conviviality at this charmingly rustic restaurant, which sits in the former smokehouse – beside the kitchen garden – in the grounds of Hampton Manor. A seat at the counter means you can join in the buzz of the kitchen, but in summer it's hard to look past the charms of the greenhouse. The food celebrates seasonal produce and, while dishes may appear simple, they have a hidden creativity and harbour some punchy flavours. The small wine list offers interesting natural, biodynamic and orange wines.

Name: Mulcahys
Address: Main Street, Kenmare, V93 W35F, Ireland
Description: Having been a presence in Kenmare since 1995, this smart, intimate restaurant has become a part of the town’s fabric. Come for cocktails and snacks in the bar or settle in for the evening to enjoy a menu underpinned by local beef and seafood. There is a classic edge to the cooking, with options like beef Wellington and fish pie featuring among the flavoursome, carefully cooked dishes.

Name: Mr Fox
Address: 38 Parnell Square West, Dublin City, DO1 X9TO, Ireland
Description: A welcoming restaurant with a charming team and a lovely tiled floor, set in the basement of a striking red-brick Georgian house. The well-priced set menu showcases wonderful Irish produce and the tasty, modern dishes are skilfully enhanced by global flavours.

Name: Volpe Nera
Address: 22 Newtown Park, Blackrock, A94 D780, Ireland
Description: Nestled away in a small parade, the ‘Black Fox’ takes its name from its position midway between the suburbs of Blackrock and Foxrock. Split over two floors, the upstairs has a slightly plusher feel, while the atmosphere is livelier downstairs, in part thanks to the open kitchen. The menu evolves with the seasons, mixing Mediterranean influences like rabbit cavatelli with Asian elements like cep dumplings, across modern, flavoursome dishes. Service comes from a friendly and knowledgeable team, while a carefully curated wine list completes the experience.

Name: Mamó
Address: Harbour House, Harbour Road, Howth, D13 E9H9, Ireland
Description: An experienced couple run this friendly bistro located in a pleasant spot on Howth seafront. Irish ingredients are the bedrock of the menu, including Winetavern Farm pork loin from Wicklow and plenty of seafood from the harbour just over the road. This produce is fashioned into fresh, flavoursome dishes that are carefully cooked and neatly presented. Stick around for dessert, as it’s likely to be a highlight.

Name: Rocket Store
Address: The Harbour, Boscastle, PL35 0HD, United Kingdom
Description: This compact restaurant sits within a 19C store which once housed the coastguard’s horse-drawn rocket firing equipment. The blackboard lists small plates and whole fish dishes; most of the produce is supplied by the owner’s father who, as well as being the harbourmaster, owns a boat and runs a small farm.

Address: 104 Chepstow Road, Bayswater and Maida Vale, London, W2 5QS, United Kingdom
Description: It might only have six tables but the cosy 104 certainly proves that great things can come in small packages. The Chef-Owner works alone preparing a surprise tasting menu of sophisticated dishes with smart flavour combinations and stand-out sauces. Underlining the modernity in the cooking, there is a pleasing simplicity to each dish, allowing superb luxury ingredients like Cornish turbot or Scottish XL langoustine to shine. For dessert, look out for the deliciously rich signature '104 chocolate bar'.

Name: Stove Bistro
Address: 455 Ormeau Road, Belfast, BT7 3GQ, United Kingdom
Description: As you approach the top of the staircase leading to this first floor restaurant, you are hit by the buzz of happy locals, so book well in advance to secure yourself a table. The concise à la carte menu offers flavoursome, modish bistro dishes created using locally sourced produce.

Name: Stage
Address: 31 Magdalen Road, Exeter, EX2 4TA, United Kingdom
Description: A fun, trendy spot set up on a budget by an enthusiastic group of young men known as the ‘Taco Boys’. Foraged ingredients and produce from the kitchen garden inform the daily changing, surprise tasting menus, and the original, modern dishes have bold flavours and contrasting textures.

Name: Tallow
Address: 15a Church Road, Southborough, TN4 0RX, United Kingdom
Description: Rob and Donna – formerly of the Compasses Inn at Crundale – have made this cosy restaurant overlooking the green at Southborough their new home. The concise menu lists well-crafted dishes which display good knowledge of techniques and have bold, hearty flavours. Service is warm and friendly.

Name: Haar
Address: 1 Golf Place, St Andrews, KY16 9JA, United Kingdom
Description: An appealing restaurant with a modern, Nordic edge; ask for a table on the more characterful first floor, with a view of the open kitchen. The tasting menu reflects the owner’s travels, and offers some bold and powerful flavour combinations. Try the signature smoked lobster – and don’t miss Nana's banoffee.

Name: da Mirco
Address: 4 Bridge Street, Cork, T23 H10E, Ireland
Description: Transport yourself to Italy at this authentic osteria in the heart of the city, where light pours over the tightly packed tables and plants line the walls. Both Irish and imported ingredients feature in the rustic, no-frills dishes, with homemade pastas like spinach and ricotta cannelloni a particular highlight. The service is led by eponymous owner Mirco, who brings a chatty approach to this lively little spot.

Name: Kai
Address: 22 Sea Road, Galway, H91 DX47, Ireland
Description: The long-standing, sustainably minded Kai is really two places in one. At lunch, they take walk-ins only and serve one course followed by homemade cakes and pastries (they also have their own bakery). Things ramp up a gear at dinner, with a 3 course à la carte heavily guided by the seasons and the local area. Dishes are often understated in appearance, but just a handful of ingredients are needed for plentiful flavour; keep an eye out for the specials, like a super 'conference pear tarte Tatin'. Excellent wine pairing suggestions will enhance your visit.

Name: Peploe's
Address: 16 St Stephen's Green, Dublin City, D02 KF34, Ireland
Description: An atmospheric cellar restaurant – formerly a bank vault – named after the artist. The comfy room has a warm, clubby feel and a large mural depicts the owner. The well-drilled team present classic Mediterranean dishes and an Old World wine list.

Name: Awabi
Address: 63 Halkett Place, Saint Helier, JE2 4WG, United Kingdom
Description: Owner and self-taught chef, Stephen, takes inspiration from his travels and discoveries across Asia when compiling the immensely appealing menu at this cute neighbourhood spot, which resembles something between a little bistro and an izakaya. There are lots of local ingredients, the bao buns are delicious, and be sure to end with the Japanese French toast.

Name: Neighbourhood
Address: 1 North Main Street, Naas, W91 RH96, Ireland
Description: A pool of young but experienced talent came together to create this contemporary restaurant out of what was formerly Grace’s pub on the main street. The menu is so appealing you’ll have trouble choosing; all the dishes, which rely on superb produce, are comforting and satisfying, with some of the larger dishes designed for sharing. The service team are full of energy and really help bring the room alive.

Name: Gwen
Address: 21 Heol Maengwyn, Machynlleth, SY20 8EB, United Kingdom
Description: This warm and welcoming restaurant from the team behind Ynyshir is more of a cousin than a little sister – thanks to the personality Chef Corrin Harrison brings to both his cooking and the service. After a drink in the wine bar, all eight guests are served together in the intimate dining room. The surprise tasting menu offers bold flavours, a good dose of creativity and no small amount of skill, exemplified by the eel chawanmushi. The chefs chat away with diners as the thoroughly enjoyable evening just flies by.

Name: Olivomare
Address: 10 Lower Belgrave Street, Victoria, London, SW1W 0LJ, United Kingdom
Description: Sardinian cuisine is the order of the day at this bright, well-run Belgravia restaurant. It’s been around for some time, which is a testament to the quality of the seafood-centric cooking. Whether it’s steamed mussels with garlic and parsley or monkfish with courgettes and lemon, the fruits of the sea are celebrated heartily – and the simplest dishes are often the best. Much of the high quality produce in the kitchen is also available to buy at their deli, Olivino, next door.

Name: Oarsman
Address: Bridge Street, Carrick-on-Shannon, N41 AK19, Ireland
Description: This traditional family-run pub sits close to the river and is filled with pottery, bygone artefacts, fishing tackle and, of course, plenty of locals. Service is chatty, there’s a lovely deli, and they even have a lager brewed specifically for them. Flavoursome cooking uses local produce, with the fish dishes being a sure-fire hit, and all of the bread is home baked. The upstairs restaurant opens later in the week.

Name: Delahunt
Address: 39 Camden Street Lower, Dublin City, D02 K277, Ireland
Description: This characterful old Victorian grocer’s shop is mentioned in James Joyce’s ‘Ulysses’ – the clerk’s snug is now a glass-enclosed private dining room. Enjoy an aperitif in the sitting room before dining on flavoursome dishes which take on a modern approach. Service is relaxed yet professional.

Name: Tannery
Address: 10 Quay Street, Dungarvan, X35 XN99, Ireland
Description: Close to the harbour sits this characterful 19C stone tannery that also houses a cookery school. Sit downstairs for small plates at the counter or head upstairs to the bright restaurant. The classically based dishes are generously sized and use good seasonal ingredients – don't overlook the specials either. Stylish bedrooms are spread across two nearby townhouses.

Name: Bay Tree
Address: Newry Street, Carlingford, A91 V054, Ireland
Description: This honest little neighbourhood restaurant sits on the bustling high street of a small town, just a stone’s throw from Carlingford Lough. The carefully prepared dishes are hearty and well-balanced, often featuring vegetables from the garden and seafood from the lough – including its renowned oysters. A range of Asian influences are also on display, be it rogan josh curry or char siu pork belly. Simple, cosy bedrooms are on hand for those staying the night.

Name: The Lookout by Gardener's Cottage
Address: Calton Hill, Edinburgh, EH7 5AA, United Kingdom
Description: Take in some of the best views of the city from the full-length windows of this modern, cantilevered building in a wonderful spot on the top of Calton Hill. The room has a minimalist, design-driven feel – and the contemporary, pared-back dishes allow each ingredient to shine. Tasting menu only in the evenings.

Name: Imperial Treasure
Address: 9 Waterloo Place, St James’s, London, SW1Y 4BE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The first London outpost of this globally renowned group is housed in an imposing former bank, which provides a luxurious backdrop for the traditional, mostly Cantonese cooking. White leather, onyx walls and wood partitions provide some intimacy amongst the opulence, and the extensive selection of dishes offer ample flavour. If you’re after money-no-object luxury, look no further than their signature Peking duck with caviar.

Name: Land to Sea
Address: John Street, Dingle, V92 ET22, Ireland
Description: Proving to be one of the most aptly named restaurants in Ireland, the menu here showcases fine produce from the surrounding fields and nearby waters. The kitchen team take advantage of Kerry meats and wonderfully fresh fish and shellfish with dishes that have a strong classical base and demonstrate a good understanding of flavour. Charming service enhances the overall experience.

Name: Wild Flor
Address: 42 Church Road, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2FN, United Kingdom
Description: A group of lifelong friends own this relaxed neighbourhood restaurant, and they lead the service with obvious pride. The room takes on a modern bistro style and there’s a pleasingly unpretentious feel to the place.
