Well-prepared, seasonally changing dishes – try the goose rillettes with redcurrants in the winter – have a similarly unfussy style and good depth of flavour.

Name: Kildrummy Inn
Description: There is a luxurious feel to this smartly renovated pub, where the cooking mixes the modern with the traditional. Among the well-executed dishes on the menu are some contemporary choices alongside recognisable classics like rib-eye steak, fish & chips and chicken liver parfait. Come at lunchtime to enjoy their classically served haggis, neaps and tatties, which is a real treat. Four bedrooms, cosy sitting rooms and an immaculate terrace complete the very pretty picture.

Address: Church View, Main Street, Adare, V94 R672, Ireland
Description: This pretty little cottage feels right at home in Adare, a picture-postcard village with brightly painted shops and rows of thatched roofs. Inside, there's a cosy, characterful feel to the place, which is run with warmth and confidence by an experienced couple. The interesting, attractively presented dishes proudly spotlight fine Irish produce like Dooncastle oysters and the famous Skeaghanore duck from West Cork; the black sole served on the bone is a real crowd-pleaser. On Sundays, a 'late lunch' menu offers good value for money.

Name: Dean Banks at the Pompadour
Address: 4 Lothian Road, Edinburgh, EH1 2AB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Pompadour is one of the city’s most famous restaurant names and it sits within one of its best-known hotels, The Caledonian – if you’re lucky, you may get one of the tables that look up to the castle. The tasting menu makes creative use of prime Scottish produce but with a noticeable Asian influence; contrasts in flavours, textures and temperatures all feature.

Name: Marle
Address: Heckfield Place, Heckfield, RG27 0LD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Within Heckfield Place – a Georgian country house hotel decorated with the owner’s extensive post-war British art collection – you’ll find this charming, orangery-style dining room looking out over a lake and parkland. Sustainability drives everything they do here, with a great number of ingredients coming from the estate’s own farm; these are fashioned into light, clean dishes that rely on honest, natural flavours. Why not start by ordering the plate of farm vegetables to share, giving you an opportunity to really taste the garden?

Name: The Old Bank
Address: 8 Market Square, Westerham, TN16 1AW, United Kingdom
Description: The contemporary interior of this former high street bank is a perfect match for the beautifully presented modern dishes. Cooking is technically accomplished and flavour combinations display depth and sophistication. You can visit the old vaults to sample wines suggested by the sommelier.

Name: Caractère
Address: 209 Westbourne Park Road, North Kensington, London, W11 1EA, United Kingdom
Description: 'Never judge a book by its cover' certainly rings true here, as within this former pub sits a convivial and really quite stylish restaurant, where sophisticated cooking combines with efficient, unstuffy service. Alongside an à la carte, you have the option to ‘build your own’ 5 course tasting menu by selecting one dish from each of their ‘character’ profiles; these range from 'Subtle' (such as Acquerello risotto) to 'Robust' (roast lamb, perhaps) and finish with 'Greedy' for dessert. Top-notch ingredients and strong classical technique run throughout.

Name: Lucky Cat by Gordon Ramsay
Address: 10 Grosvenor Square, Mayfair, London, W1K 6JP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Gordon Ramsay’s foray into Asian culture is a moody, masculine space in the former Maze, with a chef's table, a striking bar, a banging soundtrack and a fun feel. Accomplished Japanese and Chinese dishes blend British ingredients and are designed for sharing; the bonito fried duck leg bao is a must-try.

Name: Rhosyn
Address: Penally Abbey, Penally, SA70 7PY, United Kingdom
Description: Rhosyn means ‘rose’ in Welsh and there are plenty on display in the gardens of this lovingly restored country house. The gorgeous setting provides a calming atmosphere in which to dine, with a tasting menu or an à la carte to choose from. The modern, flavoursome cooking demonstrates an accomplished touch from the kitchen team in dishes like cod with buttermilk, dill and caviar.

Name: Ugly Butterfly by Adam Handling
Address: Carbis Bay Estate, Carbis Bay, St Ives, TR26 2NP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: From dry ice in the snacks to the original use of beetroot in the desserts, expect creative cooking that is designed to impress at this wonderfully contemporary restaurant. The dishes are often tersely or intriguingly titled – such as ‘All About the Crab’ – and zero waste is also a feature; offcuts are used in bar snacks and also as the basis for drinks, pickles and ferments. The setting, providing uninterrupted coastal views over to Godrevy thanks to floor-to-ceiling windows, is equally impressive.

Name: Pizarro
Address: 194 Bermondsey Street, Southwark, London, SE1 3TQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: José Pizarro has a refreshingly simple way of naming his establishments: after José, his tapas bar, came Pizarro, a larger restaurant a few doors down. A selection of small plates – like croquetas, boquerones and padrón peppers – are joined by larger main courses including presa Ibérica, with dishes proving to be satisfying and cleanly executed. The surroundings are stylish and an all-Spanish wine list boasts some big names.

Name: La Potinière
Address: Main Street, Gullane, EH31 2AA, United Kingdom
Description: An icon in the Scottish restaurant industry, this sweet little restaurant is run in a very personal way by owners Mary and Keith, who share the cooking. They offer a choice of two dishes per course; each prepared with care, pride and an ambitious edge. The wine list focuses on France.

Name: Arros QD
Address: 64 Eastcastle Street, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1W 8NQ, United Kingdom
Description: Rice, and lots of it, is what you can expect to find at this huge, strikingly decorated restaurant from the mind of Spanish Chef Quique Dacosta. Specifically, the menu offers an array of takes on the classic Valencian paella, from pork knuckle to tofu & sea lettuce, but plenty of other dishes are available too, including several cuts of meat and fish cooked over fire. There’s a real theatrical element to the place, so ask for a table on the ground floor where you can watch the action in the open kitchen and see the flames from the wood-fired stoves.

Name: Naïfs
Address: 56 Goldsmith Road, Southwark, London, SE15 5TN, United Kingdom
Description: Owned and run by an alumnus of Vanilla Black, this friendly neighbourhood spot serves solely vegan dishes. The restaurant is simply decorated, with an on-view kitchen, and from here come hearty, original plates full of bold flavours. The set menu makes good use of what's in season and is served all at once, served 'family style' to be shared by the whole table. A few small plates and snacks are available too if you want to enhance the experience.

Name: Little Social
Address: 5 Pollen Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 1NE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Little Social has a clubby, comforting feel and a smart, stylish look, with on-trend copper, dark wood, and duck egg blue upholstery ensuring it fits in perfectly with its Mayfair surroundings. The seasonal British menu offers something for everyone, and its creative modern dishes are full of flavour.

Name: Water House Project
Address: 1 Corbridge Crescent, Cambridge Heath, Tower Hamlets, London, E2 9DT, United Kingdom
Description: As soon as you walk into this calm, Nordic-style restaurant with an open kitchen and smiling team, you just know you’re going to have a good time. Sit back and enjoy the house aperitif and some fabulous snacks before beginning a tasting menu founded on the finest British ingredients. The produce is treated with a deft touch in elegant dishes that offer refined, balanced flavours – such as West Country mussels with native seaweed and koji. The cooking can be accompanied by either a bespoke wine pairing or a homemade non-alcoholic option.

Name: Potager
Address: 7 Church Street, Skerries, K34 V585, Ireland
Description: The old Munster and Leinster Bank is the setting for this formal neighbourhood restaurant, with the original bank vault even acting as the wine cellar. Good quality produce from the north of County Dublin features on a set menu of modern Irish dishes that show off their component parts with wonderful simplicity – the fabulous beetroot with yoghurt and walnut is a prime example.

Name: littlefrench
Address: 2b North View, Westbury Park, City of Bristol, BS6 7QB, United Kingdom
Description: This neighbourhood bistro’s authentic Gallic feel will warm your soul. It’s family owned and run and is certainly a busy place, with visitors being warmly welcomed as if they were regulars. Well-executed dishes are fresh and hearty with a rustic style and bags of flavour; in the evening go for one of their sharing dishes. Service is friendly; ask for a booth beside the semi-open kitchen.

Name: yeni
Address: 55 Beak Street, Soho, London, W1F 9SH, United Kingdom
Description: Anatolian-inspired cooking from experienced chef-owner Civan Er, who made his name at acclaimed sister restaurant Yeni Lokanta in his home city of Istanbul. Daily changing menu of vibrant, gutsy, flavoursome sharing plates; techniques are rooted in tradition, with dishes cooked over oak in the Josper oven.

Name: Exmoor Forest Inn
Description: There’s a rustic charm to this beautifully restored Victorian inn, where they make excellent use of the surrounding estate. The dishes are powered by organic produce from their own farms, which is then turned into a mixture of traditional and modern pub food. Generous and flavourful dishes do these local ingredients proud. A fire-lit lounge and 11 pleasant, relaxing bedrooms complete the package.

Name: Straker's
Address: 91 Golborne Road, North Kensington, London, W10 5NL, United Kingdom
Description: This is a tale of our times: a chef creates a large fanbase by giving cooking demos on TikTok during lockdown and then opens a small restaurant in Notting Hill so that they can come and experience his cooking first-hand. It’s a very likeable place, with no frills, easy-to-eat cooking that’s modern British by way of Italy; always start by ordering one of the flatbreads – and the sweetbreads are always a good bet too. Low intervention wines are a feature.

Name: Penmaenuchaf
Address: Penmaenuchaf Hotel, Penmaenpool, Dolgellau, LL40 1YB, United Kingdom
Description: Set into the hillside, this house was built for a Lancashire industrialist around 1860 and is surrounded by terraced gardens and woodland. Original features include a wood-panelled former billiards room, which now acts as the drawing room; follow this through into the restaurant, where you'll find the best seats are in the conservatory. The cooking has a contemporary look and shows an impressive amount of restraint, which gives the main ingredient of each dish the room to shine.

Name: Furna
Address: 6 New Road, Brighton and Hove, BN1 1UF, United Kingdom
Description: This stylish city centre restaurant is the first solo venture for Chef-Owner Dave Mothersill, who has been a fixture of the Brighton food scene for some time and brings an array of techniques to his precisely crafted dishes. The food is largely served by the proud chefs and focuses on seasonal British produce, with a few international influences and a creative edge. A chic mix of vintage and contemporary décor helps to enhance the experience, with counter seating available to make the most of the fully open kitchen.

Name: Eline
Address: 1C Rosewood Building, Cremer Street, Hoxton, London, E2 8GX, United Kingdom
Description: Named after Chef-Owner Alex Reynolds’ grandmother, this bright, fashionable bistro offers detailed and refined cooking to the Hoxton dining crowd. The menu makes good use of seasonal produce, and beautifully crafted desserts like almond tart prove to be a highlight. Co-owner Maria offers attentive service out front with broad smiles across the team. A wine shop operates here too, and is evidenced in a well-chosen wine list that features skin contact, natural and low-intervention choices.

Name: Bouchon Racine
Address: 66 Cowcross Street, Clerkenwell, London, EC1M 6BP, United Kingdom
Description: Those with fond memories of the original Racine in Knightsbridge rejoiced when chef Henry Harris opened a new version in 2022. Racine Mark II is just a few steps from Farringdon Station, located above the Three Compasses pub. The blackboard menu is a veritable rollcall of classic French bistro dishes, from escargots to rabbit, duck confit to steak tartare. There are so many tempting dishes; just be sure to end with the terrific crème caramel.

Name: Norma
Address: 8 Charlotte Street, Bloomsbury, London, W1T 2LS, United Kingdom
Description: This Fitzrovian townhouse has been transformed into a handsome, intimate restaurant spread over three floors, with Moroccan tiles and cosy booths. The food of Sicily and its Moorish influences inform the menu, with the 'primi' options including the dish that gave the restaurant its name: pasta alla norma. Generous portions add to the appeal, particularly the immensely satisfying fritto misto and the super-sized cannoli for dessert.

Name: The Small Holding
Address: Ranters Lane, Kilndown, TN17 2SG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: There's a rustic, farmhouse-like feel to this former village pub run by two brothers. The team's focus is firmly on self-sufficiency: they grow fruit & veg and raise their own chickens and rare breed pigs. This seasonal produce heavily informs the monthly changing tasting menu, which blends British and Nordic culinary influences in dishes that have bold, well-balanced flavours and lots of personality. In summer, grab a seat on the terrace for an aperitif overlooking the garden.

Name: Aven
Address: 10 Camden Place, Preston, PR1 3JL, United Kingdom
Description: On the ground floor of the Winckley Stays Hotel, you’ll find this sweet restaurant where an open fire greets you on arrival in the colder months. There’s a cosy feel to the room, which is minimally decorated but enlivened by some bright artwork on the walls. The cooking takes the form of a seasonal tasting menu, with dishes like duck leg suet pudding delivering intense flavours. Friendly, efficient service enhances the experience, as does the choice between two wine flights and even a beer pairing.

Name: Orwell Road
Address: 8 Orwell Road, Dublin City, D06 H2Y5, Ireland
Description: Enjoy snacks and cocktails to start at this buzzy neighbourhood restaurant, which showcases ingredients sourced from local producers in its concise selection of modern, skilfully cooked dishes. It’s certainly a cosy space, and its small bar and semi-open kitchen help create a lively ambience. Service is attentive, yet friendly and relaxed.

Name: Cora
Address: 3-7 Duke Street Arcade, Cardiff, CF10 1AZ, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in the Castle Quarter Arcades, this small and personally run operation has just five tables and offers a surprise tasting menu full of fresh, seasonal flavours. Chef Lee Skeet is on his own in the kitchen, with his wife Helen delivering charming service out front. Skilful, pared-back dishes showcase quality ingredients and Lee’s eye for detail; he serves many of them himself, turning down the hip-hop soundtrack to explain his cooking with great pride. Their wine and oyster bar, Jackson’s, is situated on the floor below.

Name: Aquitania
Address: High Street, Seaview, PO34 5EX, United Kingdom
Description: The Aquitania is a delightfully intimate restaurant which upholds the Seaview Hotel’s proud culinary tradition. The team are warm and welcoming and the wide-ranging menu bursts with the island’s artisan ingredients. Dishes are presented in a modern style and fish plays an integral role.

Name: The Red Lion
Address: Church Place, Freshwater, PO40 9BP, United Kingdom
Description: It’s not just the open fires and friendly service that makes this such a warm and welcoming pub – the delicious beef fat crumpet and the sticky toffee pudding also help! The traditional building has origins dating back to 11C and sits next to a church, and it has its own garden which supplies some of the produce. There are 'light' or 'large bites' on offer at lunch, with the kitchen stepping things up a gear in the evenings.

Name: Da Noi
Address: 63 Bridge Street, Chester, CH1 1NG, United Kingdom
Description: To say that your hosts at this little Italian restaurant are passionate would be an understatement. Chef-Owner Valentina Aviotti and her husband Fabrizio bring pride and personality to all that they do, with Valentina's Italian heritage coming across in a tasting menu of freshly made, authentic Italian cooking; the lasagne made using a recipe from Valentina's nonna is a delight. Wine flights are available and, pleasingly, the list is Italian-dominated.

Name: The Farmers Arms
Description: Open fires and exposed timbers set against touches of contemporary design help make this restored Grade II listed pub, set in a delightful hamlet, a charming place for replenishment and recuperation. The frequently changing menu makes good use of ingredients from their own farm; the local hogget makes for a delicious shepherd’s pie and look out for the Forager’s Tart for pud. Wonderful homemade syrups help create some refreshing aperitifs.

Name: Lounge on the Green
Address: 27 The Green, Houghton, CA3 0NF, United Kingdom
Description: Its somewhat unusual name comes from this building's former occupation as a furniture shop, and its location on a street called 'The Green'. A tasting menu (available in long or short form) removes any time-consuming indecision, so you can get on with the important business of eating well-balanced dishes built on the simple principle of top Cumbrian produce handled with skill – full-flavoured fillet of beef is a prime example. The cheery, personable service is befitting of a cosy neighbourhood operation like this.

Name: Levan
Address: 12-16 Blenheim Grove, Southwark, London, SE15 4QL, United Kingdom
Description: You can expect a good soundtrack playing over the speakers at this lively, friendly local restaurant named after DJ Larry Levan. The menu is a sharing plates affair – with dishes of mostly European influence – but there's also a tasting menu option, which allows you to sample more of the carefully prepared, original dishes. Be sure to start with the comté fries, and look out for the range of natural wines from smaller producers. The friendly, attentive service team ensure there's a laid-back vibe to proceedings.

Name: Tytherleigh Arms
Address: Chard Road, Tytherleigh, EX13 7BE, United Kingdom
Description: This sympathetically refurbished 16C coaching inn is an endearing place, with a characterful timbered interior that features a large inglenook fireplace. The cooking is best described as wholesome and boldly flavoured, with a menu that blends more modern dishes with pubby favourites like sirloin steak or haddock & chips. Stylish bedrooms await in the old stables if you fancy staying the night.

Name: Kutir
Address: 10 Lincoln Street, Chelsea, London, SW3 2TS, United Kingdom
Description: A pretty end-of-terrace townhouse in an elegant Chelsea street is the setting for this relaxed, stylish Indian restaurant. There’s a lively buzz throughout the various smart yet cosy rooms, with the more intimate upstairs the best choice if you’re on a date. The interesting style of cooking draws from multiple regions of India and offers a wide choice of dishes, from tandoori broccoli to duck madras. The extensive choice of menus cater for a range of diners, with proper vegan and gluten-free options among them.

Name: Canton Blue
Address: 1 Grosvenor Place, Belgravia, London, SW1X 7HJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed inside the spectacular Peninsula Hotel, this Cantonese restaurant is part of a brand housed inside their hotels around the world. The London version boasts its own entrance at the side of the hotel and a sumptuous cocktail bar, Little Blue, which is the perfect way to kick off a rather glamorous evening. The restaurant itself is equally stylish, and the extensive menu offers a wide selection of authentic, flavoursome dishes, from finely executed dim sum to Peking duck for two. The interesting wine list includes a selection of Chinese rice wines by the glass.

Address: Fairmont Windsor Park, Bishopsgate Road, Englefield Green, Egham, TW20 0YL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Named after the date of the signing of the Magna Carta 'down the road' in Runnymede, this elegant restaurant can be found in the slightly labyrinthine Fairmont Windsor Park Hotel. Choose from two lengths of tasting menu or the à la carte, all of which feature prime British ingredients like Suffolk lamb, Torbay crab and vegetables from their own estate. The chefs treat this produce with an unfussy approach, resulting in enjoyably pared-back dishes. Service is smooth and, if you’re dining as a couple, ask for one of the semi-circular booths.

Name: Pêtchi
Address: Unit 13C, Liberty Wharf, La route de Liberation, St Helier, JE2 3NY, United Kingdom
Description: Overlooking Liberation Square, this buzzing restaurant takes inspiration from the chef’s time working in Spain. Ingredients from Jersey and the surrounding area meet techniques often associated with the Basque region; glowing hot coals and a wood-fired oven are both visible in the open kitchen, with a few counter seats available if you can stand the heat. From chops of turbot and ex-dairy cow to Ibérico ham collar, plenty of quality produce gets the fire-based treatment, in dishes that push natural flavours to the fore.

Name: Giulia
Address: 77 Askew Road, Hammersmith & Fulham, London, W12 9AH, United Kingdom
Description: There’s an authentic, honest feel to this small Italian neighbourhood restaurant. The eponymous owner Giulia can be seen chatting away to guests in her native language and offering great hospitality alongside the cooking. Her partner Endris is in the kitchen following the ethos of pure, ingredient-led cooking with a seasonal focus. Pasta is offered as a separate course, including classic dishes like spaghetti alle vongole. The wine list is sensibly priced and, unsurprisingly, all Italian.

Name: Seasonality
Address: 26 Queen Street, Maidenhead, SL6 1HZ, United Kingdom
Description: What started out as a produce shop – and pivoted into producing dine-at-home boxes during lockdown – has morphed into a bright and airy restaurant, personally run by chef-owner Wesley, who can be seen cooking at the central island. The ingredient-led menu offers confident, colourful dishes with an appealing clarity of flavour. The lunch menu is a steal.

Name: Mazi
Address: 12-14 Hillgate Street, Kensington, London, W8 7SR, United Kingdom
Description: A real neighbourhood restaurant with a pure Greek heart, there is a wonderful buzz to the intimate Mazi. It’s one of those places where you can leave the decision making to the passionate, engaging team, who are ready to recommend their favourite Greek wines and dishes. The menu is designed for sharing and mixes classic choices with more modern creations; for dessert however, it’s hard to look past the loukoumades. A small front terrace and larger rear one add to the appeal – if the weather’s good enough, you can pretend you’re in Athens.

Name: The Dory Bistro & Gallery
Address: 15 East Shore, Pittenweem, KY10 2NH, United Kingdom
Description: Opposite the harbour in this little fishing village, you'll find a thoroughly charming restaurant where East Neuk produce is cooked with the care it deserves. Seafood dominates both the menu and the décor, with the restaurant walls doubling up as gallery space for plenty of aqua-based art. The blackboard is the place to look for fresh daily specials, like plump and juicy langoustines or hake with seaweed butter sauce. If you’re local to the area, this could quickly become a favourite haunt – you may even go home with some new artwork.

Name: The Wolseley
Address: 160 Piccadilly, St James’s, London, W1J 9EB, United Kingdom
Description: Like the other restaurants in this group, The Wolseley serves classic European dishes in an elegant setting with a buzzing atmosphere – well-organised service ensures that everything runs like clockwork even in a packed dining room. The extensive menu features top quality seafood dishes, from clams and oysters to crevettes and caviar. The sweet-toothed among you will not be disappointed by a large dessert menu that includes apple strudel and a choice of coupes.

Name: L'Atelier Robuchon
Address: 6 Clarges Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8AE, United Kingdom
Description: A rebrand in 2023 welcomed what was formerly called 'Le Comptoir' into the international stable of Robuchon Ateliers, yet as the original name implied, the counter still remains the best place to sit if you want a clear view of the chefs at work. The various menus, meanwhile, offer a wide selection of contemporary French dishes, from soufflés to langoustines, sweetbreads to lobster – and, of course, the legendary and gloriously buttery pomme purée.This restaurant is currently closed for refurbishment.

Name: Fallowfields
Address: Housel Bay Road, Lizard, TR12 7PG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Perched on a cliffside and boasting gorgeous bay views, this restaurant really does provide a setting to die for. It’s backed up by generous dishes that emerge from an open kitchen, served as either a short or long tasting menu. The cooking is detailed and creative, as evidenced by dishes like vodka-cured brill with ginger beer granita. Wine pairings are fairly priced and if there’s a chocolate dessert on the menu, you’re in for a treat.

Name: Fish Shop
Address: 3 Netherley Place, Ballater, AB35 5QE, United Kingdom
Description: From the genuine, professional service to the array of quality fish and shellfish, there is a lot to love about this smart restaurant where wicker models of fish hang from the ceiling. Fabulous produce, much of it Scottish, powers a menu that offers a good choice of ways to enjoy your seafood, from a whole undressed crab and natural oysters to fritto misto and lobster taglierini. As always with the best seafood restaurants, keep an eye on the specials board for more fresh delights.

Name: enotèca
Address: Charing Cross, St Aubin, JE3 8AA, United Kingdom
Description: Jersey meets Italy at this wine bar serving hearty, full-flavoured dishes in what was once a delicatessen. The owners run a business called Wild Wine, which imports natural wines from small producers – and a fabulous choice of these bottles is available to enjoy while dining. The pasta and gelato are both made in-house, and all the cooking is executed with such care. Keep an eye out for the blackboard specials.

Name: Kicky's
Address: 9 Castle house, South Great George's Street, Dublin City, D02 WK13, Ireland
Description: A striking, pop art-style mural frames the kitchen pass at this casual, trendy and thoroughly lively restaurant. The airy interior features whitewashed brick walls, some counter seating and loud hip-hop. Start with ‘bites’ and small plates to share, before moving onto the concise selection of main courses cooked over charcoal. Fabulous produce like Wicklow venison and wild brill on the bone yields bold, satisfying flavours. Make sure you finish with the ‘Irish coffee’, their take on a tiramisu.

Name: Hearth
Address: 10.5 King Street, City of Kingston-upon-Hull, HU1 2JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Run by a trio of friends and located among some fine buildings in the old part of town, this buzzy spot operates over two levels. The ground floor houses a bar and bakery, while the upstairs is home to the rustic two-room restaurant. The menu fuses small plates with larger dishes, often coming from the grill – or ‘hearth’ – that takes centre stage in the open kitchen. Start with sourdough from the bakery, then make sure you check the boards for daily specials, as you might get to enjoy delicious seasonal produce like Yorkshire grouse.

Name: Mara
Address: 11 O'Connell Street, Waterford, X91 F304, Ireland
Description: What was formerly known as The Old Couch Café has been reborn as Mara, retaining its predecessor's quirky vibe and bijou space. Chef-Owner Luis Martin has both passion and ambition in abundance, largely working alone in the kitchen and serving his dishes in the cosy, well-lit room to just six tables. His well-balanced cooking incorporates locally foraged produce alongside a few influences from his native Spain, such as ajo blanco or cod buñuelo; the cep tiramisu, meanwhile, has become something of a signature.

Name: ÖRME
Address: 218 Church Road, Urmston, M41 9DX, United Kingdom
Description: You will find a pleasantly welcoming quality at this small restaurant run by three young owners. There’s a distinct Nordic touch to proceedings, yet British produce is at the heart of the appealing tasting menu – which gives you the option to add supplementary courses for a more bespoke experience. Attractively presented dishes offer bold, vibrant flavours with a mix of the classic and the modern in their influences. Wine flights are also available, including a particularly interesting British themed option.

Name: Argile
Address: 21 Argyle Place, Edinburgh, EH9 1JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Inspired by the sticky clay used for making pottery, the naming of this hidden-away neighbourhood restaurant feels rather apt given the wonderful array of china, pottery and earthenware they use. It’s an intimate operation with modern, sometimes technically complex dishes that draw on global influences. Chef-owner Jack Montgomery serves many dishes himself, pouring passion and a personal touch into the experience.

Name: New Coast Kitchen
Address: 1 St Mary's Road, Croyde, EX33 1LF, United Kingdom
Description: With its relaxed vibe and cheerful service, this is just the kind of restaurant you want to know about when on holiday around the North Devon coast. Head for the terrace out front in good weather – a perfect spot for people watching – or sit inside surrounded by the sleek, modern décor. The adventurous cooking is executed with flair and delivers well-judged combinations of bold flavours, as with the contrast between rich butter sauce and citrus marinated fennel in a wild bass dish. Save room for dessert too, as the confit apple terrine is a highlight.

Name: Tamil Prince
Address: 115 Hemingford Road, Islington, London, N1 1BZ, United Kingdom
Description: It’s such an obvious pairing – a revived old neighbourhood pub with sharing plates of Indian food – that you wonder why there aren’t many more. The appealing menu is nominally inspired by Tamil Nadu but is not bound by its borders and does occasionally venture north. Highlights include Chettinad lamb curry and channa bhatura, while nothing goes with a pint quite like onion bhajis.

Name: Dilsk
Address: 44 Marine Parade, Brighton and Hove, BN2 1PE, United Kingdom
Description: Visit this intimate and slightly moody spot inside the Drakes Hotel and you will likely be treated to some of the delicious, red-brown seaweed – more commonly known as dulse – after which the restaurant is named. Both the Short and Full tasting menus on offer include colourful dishes that are the epitome of modern British cuisine, like hogget with wild garlic and purple sprouting broccoli. The roster of well-chosen wines offers less-common choices that complement the food well.

Name: Lilac
Address: Cellar, 57-58 Broad Street, Lyme Regis, DY7 3QF, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a lovely, relaxed feel to this wine bar and restaurant; it’s a place where you can pop in for a couple of small plates, enjoy a glass of wine or two and, if you’re still hungry, order some more. The cellar location has a rustic, cosy yet surprisingly spacious feel and the seasonal dishes make local ingredients a feature. In line with this sustainable outlook, the wine list spotlights natural, bio-dynamic and low-intervention options. Local botanicals and house-made ferments make their way into the creative cocktail selection.

Name: Atrium
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A glass dome at the centre of the room lends its name to this intimate dining space, set in a charming hotel with 17C origins. Dinner is an all-round experience, with a tasting menu showcasing the best of the season’s produce. Classic techniques combine with a modern approach and touches of innovation.

Name: Rathfinny Tasting Room
Address: Rathfinny Wine Estate, Alfriston, BN26 5TU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The upper floor of the Rathfinny Winery houses this smart, well-run restaurant that boasts lovely vineyard views. Modern British cooking is guided by seasonal Sussex produce and the colourful dishes prove fresh and flavoursome. Lunch sees a concise fixed price menu, with a tasting selection at dinner; to drink, look no further than their must-try sparkling wine. They also operate bedrooms in The Flint Barns, a nearby farmhouse.

Name: Temple
Address: 10 Granville Terrace, Bude, EX23 8JZ, United Kingdom
Description: This chic, casually run eatery offers ethically sourced, modern rustic cooking in a lively setting. It’s a place of two halves, with the Temple Up Top bar and roof terrace the ideal spot to get the cocktails flowing. Downstairs is the restaurant, which operates more as a café in the day with a few small plates and cakes from the counter. At dinner, a fixed-price menu is served with a selection of snacks to start, followed by a choice of main and dessert. The provenance of the ingredients is paramount, and dishes are fresh, vibrant and full of flavour.

Name: Margot
Address: 45 Great Queen Street, Holborn, London, WC2 5AA, United Kingdom
Description: The service and the surroundings are equally slick at this plush Italian restaurant on the edge of Covent Garden. The menu offers an appealing choice of dishes, from simply prepared fish of the day to veal-based classics like ossobuco and vitello alla Milanese – and top quality ingredients and bold flavours run throughout. Take time to study the well-chosen wine list, which has a strong focus on the regional wines of Italy.

Name: Vanderlyle
Address: 38 - 40 Mill Road, Cambridge, CB1 2AD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A large, open-plan kitchen takes centre stage at Vanderlyle, which blends shabby chic styling with designer comfort. The well-balanced 10 course vegetarian menu shows imagination and creativity, along with purity and freshness of flavour. Go for the wine or juice pairings to complete your experience.

Name: Twenty Seven
Address: 9 Mill Street, Kingsbridge, TQ7 1ED, United Kingdom
Description: Hidden away in a side street is this small and intimate restaurant which is run with infectious enthusiasm by the chef-owner – it’s obvious why it’s such a hit with the locals. The cooking makes good use of Devon’s seasonal larder, with dishes that are creative yet hearty. Start with a drink in the bar, then head upstairs to a table beneath the beams.

Name: Hannah
Address: County Hall Building, Southbank Riverside, Belvedere Road, Lambeth, London, SE1 7PB, United Kingdom
Description: Never judge a book by its cover – or a restaurant by its entrance! It may be quite quirky in its looks, but this sweetly run Japanese eatery provides an enjoyable and well-rounded omakase experience. It's led by Chef-Owner Daisuke Shimoyama, who shows off his impressive knife skills when preparing a procession of high quality ingredients, be it Wagyu beef, sea bream or lobster. The sake list provides the ideal accompaniment to the cooking.

Name: Heritage by Matt Gillan
Address: The Chequers, Slaugham, RH17 6AQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: You might still be able to get a pint at the bar of this Edwardian country pub but it’s now more of a place for dining. Set price lunches are followed by tasting menus at dinner. Modern British dishes show creativity and depth in their combinations, and careful sourcing and seasonality are key.

Name: Decimo
Address: 10 Argyle Street, King’s Cross St Pancras, London, WC1H 8EG, United Kingdom
Description: Cacti and succulents fill the room and a DJ adds to the buzz at this deliciously different 10th floor restaurant with commanding city views. Peter Sanchez-Iglesias blends the flavours of Spain and Mexico in appealing small plates, by drawing from his father’s Spanish heritage as well as time spent in Mexico.

Name: Bubala
Address: 65 Commercial Street, Tower Hamlets, London, E1 6BD, United Kingdom
Description: Start with a freshly cooked laffa flatbread and one of their delicious dips before feasting on Middle Eastern-inspired vegan and vegetarian sharing plates, which are elevated by their delicate spicing. Wines are mostly unfiltered, natural and orange – and service is charming and attentive.

Name: Number 16
Address: 16 Byres Road, Glasgow City, G11 5JY, United Kingdom
Description: The passionately run Number 16 occupies a narrow former shop and its tables are split between the ground floor and a mezzanine level. Dishes showcase prime Scottish ingredients and many exhibit subtle modern touches. The wine list provides interest and, like the cooking, represents good value.

Name: Adrift
Address: Dunmore House, Dunmore, P85 HC03, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Run by the fourth generation of the owners’ family, this restaurant is set in an enviable position on the ground floor of the Dunmore House Hotel with views out over Clonakilty Bay. Tasty, modern dishes showcase locally sourced produce, including some from their own organic kitchen garden.

Name: OSMA
Address: 132 Bury New Road, Prestwich, Manchester, M25 0AA, United Kingdom
Description: Located in the city’s northern suburbs, this restaurant’s name is a nod to the owners’ birthplaces – OSlo and MAnchester. They offer chatty, genuine service and are keen to recommend dishes from their mightily appealing seasonal menu. Sauces are a highlight, be it their take on ponzu with gordal olive and green tomatoes, or a simply delicious creamy romesco. The set lunch menu offers terrific value, while at dinner small plates take over. The stylish room comes with an open kitchen, a communal island table and smart curved banquettes.

Name: Clockspire
Address: Gainsborough, Milborne Port, DT9 5BA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Clockspire sits within an impressive-looking former school dating from 1854 and its high ceiling with exposed rafters is a striking feature. Attractively presented, modern British cooking uses the local larder to good effect. Service is personalised and it feels as though they really care.

Name: il trillo
Address: 4 Hollywood Road, Chelsea, London, SW10 9HY, United Kingdom
Description: The Bertuccelli family have been making wine and running a restaurant in the Tuscan Hills for over 30 years. Two of the brothers run this smart local which showcases the produce and wine from their region. Cooking is gutsy, with pasta the speciality. Relax in the delightful courtyard.

Name: THOMPSON St Albans
Address: 2 Hatfield Road, St Albans, AL1 3RP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Eponymous Chef-Owner Phil Thompson’s restaurant is split over three contemporary dining rooms, each featuring bold artwork from the local gallery. The dishes are equally good-looking and can be enjoyed from either an à la carte, or a 7 or 9 course tasting menu. The kitchen’s skills are evident across the accomplished cooking, while the friendly and efficient service team run the place well.

Name: Drapers Arms
Address: 44 Barnsbury Street, Islington, London, N1 1ER, United Kingdom
Description: A stalwart of London's pub dining scene, Islington continues to be well-served by this imposing neighbourhood local. Not much has changed over the years and it's all the better for it; rustic décor, eager-to-please staff and a relaxed, unpretentious approach ensure the perfect pub atmosphere. The cooking is as hearty and satisfying as ever, but these days the traditionally British (steak & ale pie) sits alongside French influences (braised rabbit leg), courtesy of a Breton-born Chef. The courtyard garden is a great place to enjoy a glass from the superb wine list.

Name: The Art School
Address: 1 Sugnall Street, Liverpool, L7 7EB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Bright red chairs contrast with crisp white tablecloths at this elegant restaurant which is flooded with light. The experienced local chef carefully prepares a bewildering array of ambitious modern dishes full of colour and contrasts; choose a dessert containing honey from the local hives.

Name: Michael Nadra Primrose Hill
Address: 42 Gloucester Avenue, Primrose Hill, London, NW1 8JD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You'll be spoilt for choice at this neighbourhood restaurant with its extensive, brasserie-style menu. Influences over the cooking come from around the world, so you'll find dishes inspired by everywhere from the Mediterranean (such as a Greek and niçoise salad cross) to Japan (miso black cod). A set lunch menu offers bang for your buck and a roast dinner is available on Sundays – not to mention a wide array of cocktails. The unusual vaulted room adds intimacy, while service is warm and friendly.

Name: Bellanger
Address: 9 Islington Green, Islington, London, N1 2XH, United Kingdom
Description: With awnings stretching over the pavement and walls festooned with classic posters, Bellanger has the feel of a Parisian grand café. The cooking, however, looks more broadly to the Mediterranean for inspiration; the Italian influences are clear, with dishes such as chicken Milanese sitting alongside the ubiquitous French classics like steak frites. The vibe is very much that of a neighbourhood restaurant, despite a well-organised formality to the service, and the large cocktail bar is perfect for an aperitif.

Name: Santo Remedio
Address: 152 Tooley Street, Southwark, London, SE1 2TU, United Kingdom
Description: The cooking inspiration comes from the owner’s time spent in Mexico City, the Yucatan and Oaxaca. Ingredients are a mix of imported – like grasshoppers to liven up the guacamole – and home-grown like Hertfordshire pork. Spread over two floors, the rooms are as colourful as the food.

Name: Noble Rot
Address: 51 Lamb’s Conduit Street, Bloomsbury, London, WC1N 3NB, United Kingdom
Description: With its dark, rough-lacquered wood and tiny candles, there is something pleasingly intimate about this wine bar and restaurant, where the walls are adorned with covers of the owners' Noble Rot magazine. This really is an oenophile's paradise, with the enthusiastic, clued-up team happy to suggest a smart, sometimes surprising, pairing to go with your meal. The cooking itself is decidedly classical, unfussy and more than a little French. The braised turbot with vin jaune sauce epitomises this spirit, which comes in tandem with gutsy, satisfying flavours.

Name: 36 on the Quay
Address: 47 South Street, The Quay, Emsworth, PO10 7EG, United Kingdom
Description: A quayside cottage plays host to this intimate restaurant, which affords lovely harbour views – and the sheltered terrace is a hit come summer. Modern dishes display a wealth of different flavours and textures, with the desserts being particularly playful. Bedrooms are cosy and stylish.

Name: Ginger Pig
Address: 3 Hove Street, Hove, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2TR, United Kingdom
Description: The whole package is here at The Ginger Pig: an early 20C inn near the seafront; a restaurant offering an extensive choice of British favourites and Mediterranean classics; bespoke cocktails; charming staff who are attentive and on the ball; and, finally, comfy bedrooms upstairs for those wishing to make a night of it.

Name: Mount St.
Address: First Floor, 41-43 Mount Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 2RX, United Kingdom
Description: There’s nothing anodyne about the art in this particular restaurant, which is hardly a surprise when you discover that art gallery group Hauser & Wirth are behind it. It’s a striking room with a stunning collection of pieces, from Matisse to Man Ray. The menu offers satisfying, classic British dishes like omelette Arnold Bennett and others inspired by the capital, such as ‘Pigeons in Pimlico’. If you’re early, you can always nip into The Audley pub downstairs.

Name: Elis
Address: Town Hall Hotel, Patriot Square, Tower Hamlets, London, E2 9NF, United Kingdom
Description: Rafael Cagali, chef-owner of Da Terra, named his second restaurant, located in the Town Hall Hotel, after Brazilian jazz singer Elis Regina. The bright and lively 12-tabled room on the first floor reflects Rafael’s Italian and Brazilian heritage, so expect to see sharing dishes like 'bolinhos de bacalhau' vie with panzanella salad, and picanha skewer with crab linguini.

Name: Piazza
Address: 5th Floor, Royal Opera House, Bow Street, Strand and Covent Garden, London, WC2E 9DD, United Kingdom
Description: If you’re coming to see an opera or a ballet at the Royal Opera House, plan ahead and eat here on the 5th floor – either before or after the performance – to really take in its full splendour and magnificence. The room has the feel of a brasserie and its terrific terrace has great views over Covent Garden. The dishes are modern and exactingly prepared; the fish dishes are especially good, as are their sauces.

Name: The Spence
Address: 39 St Andrew Square, Edinburgh, EH2 2AD, United Kingdom
Description: Until 2017 this was the Royal Bank of Scotland, and the restaurant now occupies what was formerly the banking hall. All the grandeur is here, from the granite columns and the exquisite plasterwork to the magnificent cupola which allows natural light to flood in. The Scottish larder is the focus of the accessible menu, with the kitchen showing a keen eye for presentation.

Name: CULTURE
Address: Custom House Quay, 38b Arwenack Street, Falmouth, TR11 3JF, United Kingdom
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at this old quayside warehouse. Each dish on the set menu is named after the inspiration behind it, be it a local farmer or place, and foraged ingredients also play their part. Don’t be surprised to see the occasional South African influence too though, as the chef-owner is from Cape Town. The pared-back room has a natural feel, and it’s worth checking out the glass-walled wine cellar.

Name: Fish & Forest
Description: The name is a clue as to this intimate restaurant’s focus, as well as to its sustainable ethos. Fish comes from small boats, meats are reared putting husbandry first and game is from local shoots. All parts of the ingredients are used too, so that the constantly evolving menu produces little waste. Dishes are ambitious and the self-taught chef shows great skill in cooking fish in particular, while friendly service enhances the all-round experience.

Name: The Yurt at Nicholsons
Address: Nicholson Nurseries, The Park, North Aston, OX25 6HL, United Kingdom
Description: If you’re after something a little different, head to Nicholsons Nursery to dine in this yurt – which is fashioned from upcycled materials – or in one of the themed private huts alongside. Unfussy modern dishes come with bold flavours and Mediterranean influences. Bright and breezy service completes the picture.

Name: The Stile Bridge
Address: Staplehurst Road, Marden, TN12 9BH, United Kingdom
Description: Vintage charm blends with contemporary cool at this roadside pub. The chef’s South American roots are clear to see on the menu, but there are plenty of Mediterranean and Asian flavours too, with much use made of the open fire. If you’ve come in a pair, choose the rib of beef to share.

Name: Ognisko
Address: 55 Prince's Gate, Exhibition Road, South Kensington, London, SW7 2PN, United Kingdom
Description: Ognisko Polskie – The Polish Hearth Club – was founded in 1940 in this magnificent townhouse; its elegant restaurant serves traditional dishes from across Eastern Europe and the cooking is without pretence and truly from the heart.

Name: Brigadiers
Address: 1-5 Bloomberg Arcade, City of London, London, EC4N 8AR, United Kingdom
Description: The army mess clubs of India provide the theme for this large restaurant spread across several rooms on the ground floor of the Bloomberg building. The cooking has a strong live fire element, blending street food dishes and those cooked on the barbecue, like the delicious goat tikki bun kebab. 'Feast' menus are available if you're in a big group and there's a decent selection of beers and whiskies too. It's a perennially busy place and they have several screens for showing sport, so the atmosphere is predictably loud and lively.

Name: Les 110 de Taillevent
Address: 16 Cavendish Square, Regent’s Park and Marylebone, London, W1G 9DD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Ornate high ceilings and deep green banquettes create an elegant look for this formal French restaurant, which is more food orientated than the Paris original. Attractively presented, modern French dishes are accompanied by an exceptional wine list, which includes Château Lafite Rothschild back to 1897 and Château d'Yquem back to 1924. There are also 110 wines available by the glass, with 4 different pairings (covering 4 price brackets and 2 sizes), suggested for each dish.

Name: Noizé
Address: 39 Whitfield Street, Bloomsbury, London, W1T 2SF, United Kingdom
Description: A delightfully relaxed French restaurant, personally run by a warm and welcoming owner. The menu features a mix of classic and more modern French food, prepared with love and care. The wine list – with plenty of depth and fair mark-ups – is a highlight, as are the cheeses and desserts.

Name: Medlar
Address: 438 King's Road, Chelsea, London, SW10 0LJ, United Kingdom
Description: A charming, comfortable and very popular restaurant with a real neighbourhood feel, from two alumni of Chez Bruce. The service is engaging and unobtrusive; the kitchen uses good ingredients in dishes that deliver distinct flavours in classic combinations.

Name: Lovage
Address: 115 St George's Terrace, Jesmond, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE2 2DN, United Kingdom
Description: Head Chef, Kleo, is Albanian by birth and spent time in Italy before making the UK his home, so it’s no surprise to see the flavours and colours of the Mediterranean feature at this charming neighbourhood brasserie. There is a welcome lack of fussiness to the cooking – dishes burst with flavour and are designed for sharing; with sensibly prices wines from across Europe being an added plus. Lisa, his partner, looks after the service and is a natural hostess.

Name: Fell Bistro
Address: 4 Berry Lane, Longridge, PR3 3JA, United Kingdom
Description: This endearing little bistro is is found on the main high street of a busy market town in the Ribble Valley and is named after the nearby Longridge Fell. The ground floor, with its open kitchen and chefs on display, is the engine room, while upstairs it's much quieter. The menu has something for everyone, from mature local steaks to delicious fresh fish, all cooked with care, knowledge and understanding.

Name: Legacy
Address: Station Rise, York, Y01 6GD, United Kingdom
Description: The Grand Hotel – built in 1906 as the HQ of the North-Eastern Railway Company – acknowledged the good and the great from York’s past when naming their formal, ground-floor restaurant ‘Legacy’. Its kitchen is strong on technique and uses Yorkshire ingredients to good effect to provide attractive, modern dishes. A knowledgeable, professional service team add to the sense of occasion.

Name: Gingerman
Address: 21a Norfolk Square, Brighton and Hove, BN1 2PD, United Kingdom
Description: The flagship of the Gingerman Group is a long-standing neighbourhood restaurant a short way from the sea. It has a slight Scandic look and an intimate feel. Understated modern dishes provide plenty of appeal and have an unforced natural style and good clarity of flavour.

Name: The Rectory
Description: All the charm, elegance and character you’d expect from a restored Georgian former rectory are present and correct here, and that includes a lovely garden, dining room and spacious glasshouse. The confident kitchen focuses on seasonality and top British ingredients, and there is never anything extraneous on the plate – just satisfying and complementary flavours.

Name: The Checkers
Address: Broad Street, Montgomery, SY15 6PN, United Kingdom
Description: A low-beamed former village pub, with an unfussy, modern style, run by a husband-and-wife team. The classically trained chef knows how to get the best from the local seasonal ingredients, and his eye-catching dishes come with harmonious flavours. Four cosy bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Where there's Smoke
Address: 7 Silver Street, Masham, HG4 4DX, United Kingdom
Description: Cooking over coals is the USP here – hence the name – and the lovely aroma will hit you the moment you enter this good-looking restaurant. It sits in a delightful market town, and the seasonal set menu is comforting, easy to enjoy and comes from an honest heart. The chef-owner is also a potter, so take time to admire his creations; oh, and the bespoke wooden table-tops, he made those too!

Name: Memsahib's Lounge
Description: There’s a certain style to this two-roomed basement in a smart Georgian terrace: the colonial-themed bar offers a good range of cocktails, as well as gin and vodka infusions, while the adjoining dining room has a clubby feel, with its charcoal portraits and sepia prints. The Indian dishes are for sharing, although the 'Experience' tasting menu is perhaps the best way to go, and there are also vegetarian and pescatarian versions. They even serve an Indian-themed afternoon tea.

Name: Little Seeds
Address: 16-18 Radford Street, Stone, ST15 8DA, United Kingdom
Description: Little Seeds has a bright, fresh, natural look with green walls, foliage and rustic, upcycled furniture. A smattering of cookery books adds to the homely feel – and there’s a walled garden and drinks terrace out the back too. Great quality regional ingredients are used to create eye-catching British dishes with the occasional playful touch. The popular Sunday lunch menu features roast Staffordshire beef.

Name: Another Hand
Address: Unit F, 253 Deansgate, Manchester, M3 4EN, United Kingdom
Description: This 24-seater bistro offers an appealing array of sharing plates which champion produce from local, ethical growers. The eye-catching, vegetarian-led dishes are served one at a time and their flavours are punchy and pronounced. Craft beers and low intervention wines accompany. Service is bubbly and the atmosphere, buzzing.

Name: The Bear Inn
Address: Drayton Road, Hodnet, TF9 3NH, United Kingdom
Description: In the spot where there was once a 16C coaching inn, now sits this smart, modern gastropub hidden away in the Shropshire countryside. A welcoming and homely atmosphere accompanies stylishly presented food that’s full of hearty flavours. The menu is rooted in English classics with occasional international influences, and some of the produce could scarcely be more local, coming from the gardens of nearby Hodnet Hall.

Name: London Stock
Address: 6 Sackville Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 3DD, United Kingdom
Description: Having gained quite a following in Wandsworth, this restaurant relocated to Mayfair in 2023 to a site formerly occupied by the short-lived Amethyst. They've kept the open kitchen, but it’s a little more relaxed all round now. A plethora of set priced menus are on offer, included a vegetarian tasting menu. The kitchen has a delicate touch and the dishes, which feature quality ingredients from around the British Isles, are colourful and good looking.

Name: Blas
Address: Twr y Felin Hotel, St Davids, SA62 6QT, United Kingdom
Description: Originally built in 1806 as a working windmill, the Twr y Felin Hotel features contemporary artwork and is decorated in an understated, modern style. Its restaurant, named after the Welsh word for 'taste’, offers appealing menus which showcase seasonal Pembrokeshire produce from John Dory to lamb in pared-back, modern dishes. The friendly team run the place with pride, enhancing the overall experience.

Name: Arkle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Grade II listed Chester Grosvenor Hotel has stood in the heart of the city since the 19C, and its newly renovated restaurant blends stylish, modern décor with the luxury and elegance for which the hotel is known. The tasting menu highlights the best of British produce, and the modern dishes are tasty and well-presented. Extend your evening in the chic cocktail lounge.

Name: White Bull
Address: 166 New Lane, Oswaldtwistle, BB5 3QW, United Kingdom
Description: This neighbourhood pub’s menus cover everything from bar nibbles to pub classics; they offer lunch, afternoon tea and dinner – and even serve breakfast on Sundays. The endearing team take care in everything they do, portions are generous, and dishes not only look good but taste good too. The traditional Lancashire cheese, onion and ale pie is a must-try.

Name: Kingdom 1795
Address: Main Street, Killorglin, V93 XED7, Ireland
Description: A former town centre pub is the setting for this stylish, relaxed restaurant, whose modern, brasserie-style interior comes as a contrast to its classic whitewashed façade. Experienced chef Damien uses fine local ingredients to create his concise menu of unfussy, well-judged dishes. Service from his partner Suzi is warm and endearing.

Name: Harbour House
Address: Trefusis Rd, Flushing, TR11 5TY, United Kingdom
Description: Local suppliers are at the heart of this attractively refurbished pub on the Cornish coast. Owing to their seasonal and sustainable approach, the daily changing menus are shaped by local producers. The cooking is wholly understated, but impressive all the same, with pared-back dishes like homemade crisps with whipped cod's roe, roast brill from Cadgwith and a marvellous panela Basque cheesecake. The set lunch menu offers super value and drinkers are treated to a selection of local beers, best enjoyed outside overlooking the water with a bar snack in hand.

Name: Nest
Address: 258-260 Chillingham Road, Heaton, Newcastle Upon Tyne, NE6 5LQ, United Kingdom
Description: Set up by a group of friends, the nest theme comes courtesy of tree trunks lining the wall and branches on the ceiling. The interesting set menus offer simple dishes not constricted by culinary boundaries; they are carefully cooked, fresh and well flavoured, and there's a fun element to them that actually works quite well. It’s a relaxed place where you’ll be well looked after.

Name: Pig's Ear
Address: 4 Nassau Street, Dublin City, D02 YX74, Ireland
Description: An experienced team run this long-standing modern bistro, which sits within a three-story Georgian townhouse overlooking the Trinity College Gardens; look out for the bright pink door. The first and second floors have a homely, retro feel while the third floor is for private dining. Menus offer refined yet comforting dishes with plenty of flavour – their signature lamb shepherd’s pie is a must-try.

Name: Kora by Tom Kitchin
Address: 14-17 Bruntsfield Place, Edinburgh, EH10 4HN, United Kingdom
Description: Named after the Greek goddess of Spring, this bright and colourful neighbourhood restaurant is set in the buzzy Bruntsfield area on the south side of Edinburgh. The menu follows a nature-to-plate ethos, offering simply presented, reimagined brassiere classics, which are inspired by the seasons. The well-drilled, friendly team help create an enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Owenmore
Address: Ballynahinch Castle, Recess, Connemara, Ballynahinch, H91 F4A7, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Located inside the grand 18C Ballynahinch Castle Hotel and surrounded by a particularly picturesque part of the Wild Atlantic Way, there are few more impressive locations to dine than here. Spectacular views of the grounds and river accompany well-versed service and modern, precisely executed dishes. The West Coast larder is used to great effect and features the likes of delicious mussels and clams from Killary Fjord. Be sure to fit in a walk around the grounds or spend time on the peaceful terrace before you leave.

Name: Thomas Carr @ The Coast
Address: Lady Edith's Drive, Scarborough, YO12 5TD, United Kingdom
Description: After several ventures in his native Devon, the North Yorkshire coastline has become the home of Thomas Carr and his skilled fish cookery. His restaurant occupies two cosy rooms inside Ox Pasture Hall Hotel, with Thomas' love and understanding of seafood clear to see throughout the well-balanced, classically based dishes. Each individual course on the tasting menu is enjoyable in itself, but the full experience is enhanced when they come together as a whole. The friendly, engaging service perfectly complements this skilful cooking.

Name: Casa
Address: The General, 9 Lower Guinea Street, City of Bristol, BS1 6FU, United Kingdom
Description: The soundtrack is pumping and the open kitchen bustling, at the Sanchez-Iglesias family’s reinvention of what was previously Casamia restaurant. The modern Italian small plates burst with flavour: the fried semolina with parmesan is a great way to start, the pasta dishes are exceptional, and the tiramisu uses a secret family recipe. Service is nicely paced and attentive.

Name: Coarse
Address: Reform Place, North Road, Durham, DH1 4RZ, United Kingdom
Description: Hidden away in a small courtyard in the centre of Durham, this warm, cheerily run restaurant is the realisation of a dream for the three friends who crowdfunded its opening. The simple, rustic décor belies the quality of the cooking found within; the set menu of modern British small plates changes seasonally and the kitchen’s skill is clearly evident in the quality of the sauces.

Name: Seafood Ristorante
Address: Bruce Embankment, The Scores, St Andrews, KY16 9AB, United Kingdom
Description: The simple combination of great quality seafood and commanding bay views is a sure-fire winner at this smart restaurant housed in a striking glass cube. Perched over St Andrews Bay, locally landed seafood is very much at the heart of the menu, which has a subtle Italian slant. The kitchen team know not to mess around with super ingredients like day boat halibut, allowing the natural flavours to come to the fore. The friendly service is of a similarly high standard.

Name: Kudu Grill
Address: 57 Nunhead Lane, Southwark, London, SE15 3TR, United Kingdom
Description: Amy Corbin and her partner have taken Peckham by storm with Kudu’s sister; where the original doors of this old Truman’s pub open into a vibrant yet elegant space. Gutsy, flavour-packed dishes are cooked over the braai in true South African style. Be sure to save room for the delicious melktert.

Name: Engine Social Dining
Address: 72 Wharf Street, Sowerby Bridge, HX6 2AF, United Kingdom
Description: A traditional stone building houses this contrastingly modern restaurant where closely-set, dark wood tables look onto an open-plan kitchen with a wood-burning oven. It’s a friendly place formed around the concept of sharing, and the great value Mediterranean-based small plates burst with colour and flavour.

Name: The Gunroom
Address: Plas Dinas Country House, Bontnewydd, LL54 7YF, United Kingdom
Description: Formerly home to Lord Snowdon, the cosy Plas Dinas Country House dates from the 17C, and was built around the stone fireplace that still stands in The Gunroom today. Come for afternoon tea or for dinner at either 6 or 8pm. Welsh produce takes the lead on the concise, classically based monthly menu.

Name: The Oarsman
Address: 46 Spittal Street, Marlow, SL7 1DB, United Kingdom
Description: Head down the side of this part red brick, part timbered pub and you’ll find first the ‘front’ door, as well as an enclosed terrace hidden to the rear. Sit at chunky wood tables or in a leather-clad booth and enjoy British dishes with big flavours and the occasional Mediterranean or Scottish influence.

Name: James St
Address: 19-21 James Street South, Belfast, BT2 7GA, United Kingdom
Description: A cheery team help add to the vibrant buzz at this long-standing modern bistro. It’s a simple place, with exposed brick walls, a high ceiling and warehouse-style windows – and the classic brasserie menus suit it perfectly. The cooking is unfussy and generous, with the grill dishes always a hit; the succulent steaks are cooked on the Josper, served on boards and come with a choice of sauces – go for the tomahawk or Chateaubriand if you fancy sharing. Keep an eye out for their great value set menu.

Name: Quince
Address: 39 Station Road, Westgate-on-Sea, CT8 8QY, United Kingdom
Description: Two alumni of The Goods Shed in Canterbury are behind this unfussy modern bistro, which is a hit with locals and tourists alike. The simple dish descriptions on the concise seasonal menu belie the depth of the dishes, which are made with high quality ingredients and come with distinct flavours and textures. Smooth service adds to the experience.

Name: Bath Priory
Address: Weston Road, Bath, BA1 2XT, United Kingdom
Description: This elegant restaurant is housed inside a charming country house hotel of the same name, which boasts an immaculately kept rear garden and a delightful terrace that makes the perfect spot for an aperitif. The seasonal à la carte showcases the kitchen’s skills, offering quality British produce – like Wiltshire lamb loin – in carefully executed dishes. Ingredient combinations are well thought-out and dishes are always full of flavour.

Name: argoe
Address: The Strand, Newlyn, TR18 5HW, United Kingdom
Description: Part-owned by a local fishmonger and named after an old fishing boat, this modern, wood-clad 'shack' overlooks Newlyn Harbour, where much of its produce lands. The concise menu offers seafood dishes designed for sharing, varying daily depending on the catch. Whether it's sardines or black bream, the grill-centric cooking remains pleasingly simple, allowing the quality fresh produce to do the work. On-tap natural wines are served by the glass and carafe. Be sure to book a table on the covered waterside terrace when the sun's out.

Name: Manifest
Address: 4a Watkinson Street, Liverpool, L1 0AG, United Kingdom
Description: Set on the ground floor of a converted warehouse; an open plan kitchen dominates the room and there are counter seats for those who wish to be close to the action. Carefully cooked, flavourful modern British dishes are accompanied by a well-presented wine list, with each wine available by the glass.

Name: Maru
Address: 18 Shepherd Market, Mayfair, London, W1J 7QH, United Kingdom
Description: Discreetly tucked away in Shepherd Market, it's easy to miss the entrance to the earnestly run Maru. As with many a good sushi restaurant, the high quality of the produce helps provide plenty of flavour; the ingredients are largely British, including seafood from Cornish waters. The menu takes an omakase approach, made up of around 20 different servings, and the sake pairing makes for a good accompaniment. There are two sittings at dinner, so arrive on time; you pay when you book.

Name: Fallow
Address: 2 St James’s Market, St James’s, London, SW1Y 4RP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A large, open kitchen counter takes centre stage at this lively restaurant in an enviable corner site in St James's. The bold and original cooking is guided by the chefs' nose-to-tail ethos, so don't be surprised to find commonly discarded produce like cod or pig's head on the menu. Their homegrown mushrooms from the basement contribute to a good selection of vegetarian and vegan dishes, such as their signature mushroom parfait.

Name: Fancett's
Address: 96a Mill Road, Cambridge, CB1 2BD, United Kingdom
Description: The former owners of North Street Bistro in Kings Lynn relocated and opened this neighbourhood bistro on the vibrant Mill Road. Cooking is French to the core, with classic techniques and skilful execution resulting is hearty, appetising dishes. Service is friendly and there’s an all-round happy vibe.

Name: Bar des Prés - Mayfair
Address: 16 Albemarle Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 4HW, United Kingdom
Description: From the Mayfair postcode to the impressive marble counter, there is a luxury feel to this first international venture from French celebrity chef Cyril Lignac. Sharing a name with its pre-cursor in Saint-Germain, it also mirrors that restaurant's Japanese-influenced approach – expect maki, sashimi and miso black cod. For the terrific desserts, you travel back to France for classics like mille-feuille, tarte fine and profiteroles.

Name: The Jackdaw
Address: High Street, Conwy, LL32 8DB, United Kingdom
Description: Jackdaw is the name given to a person born within the walls of Conwy, making this an aptly named restaurant in the town centre. It’s a snug, intimate place nestled on the first floor of a characterful building that was once a cinema. The modern tasting menu has a distinct playful edge, backed up by wonderful Welsh produce and complementary flavour combinations. Service is warm and the wines are listed by how far away they were produced from Conwy, as the jackdaw flies.

Name: The Barrington Boar
Address: Main Street, Barrington, TA19 0JB, United Kingdom
Description: Dating back to the 18C, this lovely stone-built inn sits in a picture postcard village and its back garden and terrace is a real jewel. The chef-owner’s personality, his experience in previous kitchens, and his knowledge of the locale, all inform his appealing menu of modern, balanced dishes that are big on flavour and guaranteed to hit the spot. Four bedrooms occupy what was once the skittle alley.

Name: The Victoria
Address: High Street, Oxshott, KT22 0JR, United Kingdom
Description: This red brick, 19C former beer house blends original features like exposed brickwork and fireplaces with tan banquettes, wood panelling and vintage photos. Cooking delivers bold flavours, with dishes to share and salt chamber aged steaks from the charcoal grill. Service comes from a cheery young team.

Name: Holm
Address: 28 St James Street, South Petherton, TA13 5BW, United Kingdom
Description: There’s something special about this former bank, with its impressive architecture and delightful village setting. Seasonal ingredients feature on a range of menus and appealing local drinks accompany. Sit in the spacious dining room with its distressed designer style or bag a spot at the kitchen counter.

Name: One Pico
Address: 5-6 Molesworth Place, Dublin City, D02 YA32, Ireland
Description: A long-standing and much respected restaurant, One Pico is discreetly tucked away in a city centre alley and has long enjoyed a loyal local following. It’s decorated in an appealing, modern style, with the curved banquette tables being the prized seats. The modern French cooking comes with a distinct Irish influence and, while dishes may look quite simple, they do have considerable depth. The sommelier’s recommendations are well worth taking.

Name: Browns Bonds Hill
Address: 1 Bonds Hill, Waterside, Londonderry, BT47 6DW, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The flagship of the Browns group sits on the east bank of the River Foyle and comes with a plush lounge and an intimate, art deco style dining room. The artful modern cooking is elaborate in its techniques and combinations and represents good value for money.

Name: The Broughton
Address: 46-48A Broughton Street, Edinburgh, EH1 3SA, United Kingdom
Description: A warm, genial atmosphere prevails as soon as you enter this smart dining pub, which is located within walking distance of Calton Hill and bustling Princes Street. You can just pop in for a pint if you wish, but you’d be a fool to miss the appealing, good value cooking. Flavoursome dishes like duck confit terrine and vanilla panna cotta hit the mark for elevated pub food, with a strong wine list on hand to accompany.

Name: Max's
Address: 48 Main Street, Kinsale, P17 XY07, Ireland
Description: An efficiently run, two-roomed restaurant on a quaint main street, with a simple yet smart rustic style – a spot well-known by the locals! The unfussy, classical seafood menu offers plenty of choice; try the tasty ‘Fresh Catches’.

Name: Chakra by Jaipur
Address: Meridian Point Centre, Church Road, Greystones, A63 HD43, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An elegant, intimate restaurant with bold décor, unusually set within a shopping centre. Interesting dishes represent the country from north to south. Spicing is delicate, flavours are refined and desserts are a highlight.

Name: The Duck
Address: Marlfield House Hotel, Courtown Road, Gorey, Y25 DK23, Ireland
Description: The Duck is a smart, rustic bistro which sits within the grounds of a grand country house, next to a superb kitchen garden which informs its menu. Sit on the wonderful terrace with a glass of wine and dine on unfussy, global cuisine.

Name: Bon Appetit
Address: 9 St. James's Terrace, Malahide, K36 KR66, Ireland
Description: This smart Georgian terraced house near the harbour is home to a contemporary brasserie with a lively atmosphere. Modern dishes have a classical French base and plenty of Asian influences. The intimate cellar bar offers afternoon tea, with brunch available at weekends.

Name: Black & Green
Address: 49 Hewell Road, Barnt Green, B45 8LT, United Kingdom
Description: A bijou neighbourhood restaurant with stools set at tall tables and a black and green colour scheme. The short, sensibly priced tasting menu moves with the seasons, using prime ingredients to deliver layers of texture and flavour in imaginative dishes. All guests are served at the same time and most go for the wine pairings. Add in the cheese course for a satisfying meal.

Name: MiMi Mei Fair
Address: 55 Curzon Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8PG, United Kingdom
Description: An opulent Georgian Townhouse whose décor takes its inspiration from early 20C Chinese interiors. Sit in one of the ground floor booths or in the brighter first floor 'Parlour'. The wide-ranging menu offers classic Chinese dishes; wood-fire roasted Peking Duck is the specialty and sharing is encouraged.

Name: George V
Address: Ashford Castle, Cong, F31 CA48, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Wood-panelling and Waterford Crystal chandeliers set the tone at this sophisticated dining room within the Ashford Castle hotel. It was built in 1905 to honour the visit of the Prince of Wales, who later became King George V, and retains an impressively grand feel. Classic French flavours are to the fore, but are delivered with a modern flourishes, and warm Irish hospitality completes the picture.

Name: Locks
Address: 1 Windsor Terrace, Dublin City, D08 HT20,, Ireland
Description: Locals love this welcoming fire-lit restaurant, which sits in a glorious spot overlooking the canal – downstairs it’s buzzy, while upstairs is more intimate. Natural flavours are to the fore on the concise seasonal menu and dishes are given subtle modern touches.

Name: Clunie Dining Room
Address: Mar Road, Braemar, AB35 5YN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Queen Victoria made this area fashionable when she bought Balmoral, and this quirky hotel dining room is certainly upholding its reputation, with Murano chandeliers hanging from the ceiling and a huge stag overseeing proceedings. Original, modern dishes use Scottish ingredients from the surrounding estates, and the wood fire adds a gentle, smoky flavour to the dishes.

Name: Grano
Address: 5 Norseman Court, Manor Street, Stoneybatter, Dublin City, D07 XD89, Ireland
Description: To the northwest of the city, you’ll find this lovely little Italian restaurant specialising in homemade pasta. Unfussy dishes like spinach balanzoni or cavatelli with venison ragu are expertly cooked and deliver great flavours thanks to their quality ingredients. It’s a friendly and passionately run place, with an owner and chef who hail from Calabria and regularly import produce from their home town for an authentic touch. The all-Italian wine list features some organic and biodynamic options.

Name: Brown Bear
Address: Two Mile House, Kildare, W91 PWH5, Ireland
Description: The village may seem appealingly sleepy, but this is an area renowned for the breeding and training of some top racehorses. The building sits on what was once part of the owner’s family dairy farm, with a lively locals’ bar on one side and a smart bistro on the other. The menu offers a mix of classical dishes and those displaying subtle international flavours, and there is a reassuring confidence to the service.

Name: aizle
Address: 38 Charlotte Square, Edinburgh, EH2 4HQ, United Kingdom
Description: Aizle sits within the appropriately named Garden Room of the Kimpton Charlotte Square Hotel – a bright, cool setting in the heart of the city. The constantly evolving menu takes on a tasting format, featuring fresh, colourful dishes made up of the latest seasonal harvest and given the occasional creative or Japanese twist.
