Be sure to try their house-made kombucha.

Name: Ondine
Address: 2 George IV Bridge, Edinburgh, EH1 1AD, United Kingdom
Description: Scottish seafood is what they’re all about at this smart, lively restaurant dominated by an impressive horseshoe bar and a crustacean counter. One of the most popular places in Edinburgh for fish and shellfish, the menu is dominated by straightforward, satisfying dishes that let the quality ingredients shine. Sole meunière and fruits de mer platters are just some of the classics you can expect to find on the menu. Desserts are strong too and the warm, genuine service team are always on top of things.

Name: Fhior
Address: 36 Broughton Street, Edinburgh, EH1 3SB, United Kingdom
Description: A husband and wife team run this appealing Scandic-style restaurant whose name means ‘True’. Creative modern cooking showcases local and foraged produce, with their one acre garden the real driving force behind the menus. They preserve their home-grown ingredients so they can use them all year round.

Name: Mister S
Address: 32 Camden Street Lower, Dublin City, D02 P029, Ireland
Description: No one knows who Mister S is  – or if he even exists – but no one really minds either, since they’re all here for the flavour-packed food cooked over charcoal and wood. Go with a group of friends, sit in one of the booths and order several dishes to share. Their specialities include burnt end rendang spring rolls and retired Irish dairy côte de boeuf.

Name: Orā
Address: 12 Great Victoria Street, Belfast, BT2 7BA, United Kingdom
Description: It’s all about sharing at this bright, buzzy tapas-style bar – a fun place which echoes the city’s cosmopolitan vibe. Carefully prepared small plates reflect the owner’s travels and range from arancini to laksa; they’re served as they’re ready, creating anticipation for each one to arrive.

Name: BIGFAN
Address: 16 Aungier Street, Dublin City, D02 X044, Ireland
Description: Colourful décor, bright lights and a loud and lively atmosphere: Big Fan is Big Fun, so start with a cocktail, tick plenty of dishes on the list on your table, tuck in and enjoy. Small plates take their influences from China and Taiwan; expect dumplings, bao buns, Xiao Chi – and some tasty desserts too.

Name: Rasam
Address: 18-19 Glasthule Road, Dun Laoghaire, A96 H2N1, Ireland
Description: The scent of roses greets you as you head up to the surprisingly plush lounge and contemporary restaurant. Fresh, authentic dishes come in original combinations and they dry roast and blend their own spices. You must order the breads; the peshwari naan is delicious!

Name: Dax
Address: 23 Upper Pembroke Street, Dublin City, D02 AK20, Ireland
Description: Dublin’s historic Georgian quarter is home to this well-established restaurant, located in the cellar of an old townhouse near Fitzwilliam Square. The décor has a classical quality to it, with white tablecloths and leather upholstery. There’s a French influence to the menu, which offers simple yet flavourful dishes that make the most of prime Irish produce like Wicklow Gap sika deer and Celtic Sea scallops.

Name: East Room
Address: University of Limerick, Castletroy, Limerick, V94 PX58, Ireland
Description: Start with an aperitif in the drawing room of this whitewashed Palladian-style house, which sits within grounds of The University of Limerick. There's an old-fashioned feel to the place, with the grand dining room boasting ornate plasterwork, Corinthian pillars and an impressive art collection. Beautifully presented dishes have a sophisticated feel, courtesy of quality produce and a deft touch.

Name: Chez Hans
Description: An imposing former Synod Hall built in 1861 houses this long-standing, family-owned restaurant; start with a drink in the bar, surrounded by contemporary Irish art. The classically based dishes are full of flavour and there’s a great value Sunday lunch; the Queen’s egg custard tart is a must-try!

Name: An Port Mór
Address: Brewery Place, Bridge Street, Westport, F28 KP70, Ireland
Description: The friendly chef-owner named this restaurant after his home village. It’s tucked away down a narrow town centre alleyway and its cosy interior has a simple, shabby-chic style. Local produce is showcased in classically based dishes with an Irish heart. The daily specials are more adventurous.

Name: Roots
Address: 141 Belle Vue Road, Southbourne, BH6 3EN, United Kingdom
Description: Just around the corner from the beach, behind frosted glass, is this jovial, laid-back restaurant. The décor is bright and fresh, with pictures of crashing waves on the walls and a large mobile of tiny fish hanging from the ceiling. Chef Jan incorporates influences from his German heritage into the ambitious tasting menu, including in the particularly memorable bread course – a mini picnic that pays homage to Jan's grandparents and time spent on their farm in eastern Germany. Enthusiastic service from Geza illustrates the team's overall passion.

Name: SHUCKS
Address: 168 Hyndland Road, Glasgow City, G12 9HZ, United Kingdom
Description: This smart, nautically themed neighbourhood restaurant is doing a fantastic job of championing the best of Scottish seafood. Start with a glass of champagne from the trolley and snacks such as oysters, prawn tacos or crispy whitebait. As the meal proper begins, keep an eye out for the occasional Asian touch – ranging from tandoori butter to a miso glaze – and their speciality fish cooked on the bone. Across the menu, one thing is clear: this kitchen knows how to cook fish with real skill.

Name: Chutney Mary
Address: 73 St James's Street, St James’s, London, SW1A 1PH, United Kingdom
Description: This long-standing, popular Indian restaurant comes from the same stable as Veeraswamy and Amaya, and its stylish dining room may be the jewel in the group’s crown. A certain luxury is to be expected when Buckingham Palace is just a short walk away, but there’s a relaxed, fashionable feel to the surroundings here too. The appealing menu offers lots of choice and the well-judged, flavourful dishes (mostly from northern India) have been subtly updated, while still respecting the foundations of the cuisine.

Name: CHAPTERS
Address: Lion Street, Hay-on-Wye, HR3 5AA, United Kingdom
Description: A stone-built former meeting room to the adjoining chapel, CHAPTERS exudes an intimate, rustic-cum-vintage style with its parquet flooring, wood panelling and leaded windows. The set menu changes regularly and is dictated by the kitchen's unerring commitment to sustainability. Jars of pickles and preserves line the walls, while locally sourced and hyper-seasonal ingredients of excellent quality deliver fabulous natural flavours. The whole team's passion for their way of working makes the place even more endearing.

Name: Silo
Address: Unit 7, Queens Yard, Hackney Wick, London, E9 5EN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Billed as the world's first zero-waste restaurant, Silo has been a pioneer in the field of sustainable gastronomy for years. It was born out of Chef-Owner Douglas McMaster's challenge to himself to cook 'without a bin', and even the kitchen counter is made from recycled plastic bottles. The tasting menu features many plant-based elements, while the 'siloaf' bread – made using flour milled in-house – typifies the eco-friendly approach, and makes a return for dessert in the form of a 'siloaf ice cream sandwich'.

Name: ANNWN
Address: 1 Market Square, Narberth, SA67 7AU, United Kingdom
Description: Folklore, foraging and flavour guide your visit to this sustainable, proudly Welsh restaurant. Sat inside a lovingly converted former bank, there is a real sense of warmth to the place, with the passionate chef recounting stories while serving and bringing round ‘top ups’ of sauces and ingredients as you dine. From the expertly foraged produce to the Preseli Hills lamb, local ingredients bring with them a great burst of flavour. Extend your experience by joining one of their occasional foraging days.

Name: The Moorings
Address: Gorey Pier, Gorey, JE3 6EW, United Kingdom
Description: The picture postcard location beneath Mont Orgueil Castle is not the only attraction at this good-looking hotel restaurant. Along with a well-stocked bar, is a menu offering the chance to sample the best from Jersey’s waters, including local oysters, scallops and crab. There’s plenty of choice for non-fish eaters too though, with the likes of mature steak or pheasant schnitzel. Save room for dessert, which is a real highlight.

Name: The Wee Restaurant
Address: 17 Main Street, North Queensferry, KY11 1JT, United Kingdom
Description: A likeable modern restaurant in the shadow of the Forth Rail Bridge. Its grey brick walls are hung with bold art and, as its name suggests, it’s small and cosy. Fresh Scottish ingredients are served in neatly presented, classic combinations; be sure to check out the specials board.

Name: Square
Address: 6 Market Square, Dundalk, A91 X9WY, Ireland
Description: Sister restaurant to The Courthouse in Carrickmacross, this cosy, modern bistro offers a concise, balanced menu of seasonal ingredients. The generous dishes are executed with care, full of flavour and won’t break the bank. It’s a keenly run place and the friendly service further adds to the experience.

Name: henne
Address: High Street, Moreton-in-Marsh, GL56 0AT, United Kingdom
Description: ‘henne’ refers to Marsh Henne, the original name of this Cotswold town, and this likeable restaurant – run by two friends – sits proudly at its heart. Local produce is showcased via a surprise tasting menu of modern British dishes which have punchy flavours and an appealing simplicity about them.

Name: Shell Bay
Address: Ferry Road, Studland, BH19 3BA, United Kingdom
Description: Brownsea Island and Poole Harbour can be seen from many of the tables at this superbly located bistro on the water's edge. Unsurprisingly in a place like this, fish and shellfish dominate the menu. Sometimes the produce is treated with international influences, as with the Kerala seafood curry, but the majority of mains involve whole fish cooked over fire, imparting a gentle smokiness while keeping the flesh succulent and adding a crispy skin.

Name: Gordon's
Address: Main Road, Inverkeilor, DD11 5RN, United Kingdom
Description: This long-standing, passionately run restaurant never stands still, always investing and evolving over time. It’s still very much a family concern, with Garry Watson alone in the kitchen and his mother Maria handling the service with aplomb. There’s a modern feel to both the décor and the cooking, with the latter proving colourful and technically accomplished. Dishes really shine in their use of the Scottish larder, like local lamb with seasonal girolles. An interesting wine list and five bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Oren
Address: 89 Shacklewell Lane, Dalston, London, E8 2EB, United Kingdom
Description: Named after Chef-Owner Oded Oren, this small, bustling bistro might not look like much from the outside, but it's clearly a winner with the locals. The menu is made up of appealing Eastern Mediterranean sharing plates; many ingredients are cooked over the chargrill, such as pork chop, chicken thighs or lamb sweetbreads with lemon and za'atar. The wine list is bang on-trend, including lots of low-intervention choices and a decently sized selection of orange wine.

Name: Nest
Address: 374-378 Old Street, Shoreditch, London, EC1V 9LT, United Kingdom
Description: Three friends founded this restaurant and they run the place with obvious pride. A move form Hackney to Shoreditch brought with it a larger premises, lovely vintage décor and the Nest Cellar bar, which also serves a selection of snacks. The set menu is based around British produce and changes regularly, focusing on a season or a particular theme – such as game, beef or seafood – and everything is handled with aplomb by the chefs. Service from the friendly team is smooth and efficient.

Name: Garrison
Address: 99-101 Bermondsey Street, Southwark, London, SE1 3XB, United Kingdom
Description: Something of a Bermondsey institution, this charming pub is known for its vintage look and relaxed, buzzy atmosphere. Get comfy in one of the cosy booths to enjoy contemporary British dishes made from good quality seasonal produce. Roasts are a big hit on Sundays and the daily changing menu includes fresh fish specials, such as fabulous John Dory. The friendly, organised service team have an eye for detail.

Name: The Chandlers Arms
Address: Sibford Road, Epwell, OX15 6LH, United Kingdom
Description: It may sit within a 17C former pub, but there’s now more of a restaurant feel to this intimate family-run operation – where you’re guaranteed a warm welcome. The regularly updated menus showcase cooking that is well-balanced, thoughtfully composed and makes great use of the local larder. Flavour and texture combinations are both original and effective, in dishes largely served by chef Harry Flockhart himself. When the weather allows, head for the terrace.

Name: Pophams
Address: 197 Richmond Road, London Fields, London, E8 3NJ, United Kingdom
Description: Pophams is an artisan bakery during the day but, on four evenings a week, it morphs into an appealingly simple Italian restaurant. Dishes are bright and carefully prepared, with the pasta dishes the stars of the show. A stool at the stone counter looking into the open kitchen is the place to sit, although the pavement terrace is perfect on summer days.

Name: Kintsu
Address: 11a North Hill, Colchester, CO1 1DZ, United Kingdom
Description: Well-crafted and eye-catching modern dishes populate the multi-course tasting menus here, which have a seasonal British element running throughout. The restaurant is tucked away in a courtyard inside a Grade II listed former barn, with stylish contemporary décor. For a special treat book a spot at the two-seater chef's table in front of the kitchen, where the chefs finish off some dishes in front of you. A friendly service team add to the experience.

Name: The Holland
Address: 25 Earls Court Road, Kensington, London, W8 6EB, United Kingdom
Description: It may have been renamed and rebranded, but this is still a proper neighbourhood pub, with local drinkers in with their dogs, families out for dinner and friends catching up. It’s all very comfy and the relaxed air owes much to the warm and caring staff. The seasonal menu is thoughtfully compiled and the cooking hearty and satisfying; the pork collar is good and, if the almond tart is on the menu, don’t hesitate.

Name: Ye Horns Inn
Address: Horns Lane, Goosnargh, PR3 2FJ, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a snug bar, a comfy lounge and a stylish vaulted dining space with an inglenook fireplace at this lovingly restored pub, parts of which date back to the 17C. They keep the menu short and seasonal, offering eye-catching, modern, ingredient-led dishes alongside local ales and an extensive list of sensibly priced wines. Personable service completes the picture.

Name: Bottega Caruso
Address: 2-4 Broad Street, Margate, CT9 1EW, United Kingdom
Description: A fresh-looking former pub plays host to this sweet little deli-cum-osteria offering southern Italian fare. The pastas are made fresh every day and form the core of the menu, with options like Neapolitan lumache with mussels and potatoes. The rest of the simple, rustic cooking consists of small plates and snacks, often using artisanal ingredients from the owner’s family and friends back in her home region of Campania.

Name: Docket N°. 33
Address: 33 High Street, Whitchurch, SY13 1AZ, United Kingdom
Description: Before opening this popular restaurant in an old market town, Stuart and Frances Collins spent many years working overseas, and their tasting menu reflects their travels, offering imaginative dishes underpinned by a strong classical base. Frances is a natural hostess, and the enthusiasm of the service team is palpable. The chickpea chips are a must-order.

Name: The Bell
Address: 1 Church Street, Charlbury, OX7 3PP, United Kingdom
Description: The quaint village of Charlbury is the setting for this 17C pub, which looks gorgeous thanks to a lavish makeover. The bar and dining areas ooze charm and character, with exposed Cotswold stone walls and crackling log fires among the many appealing features. In summer, the garden and orchard come into their own with a covered terrace and even a small stream. Many ingredients come from their sister operation, Daylesford Organic Farm, and are used in comforting, full-flavoured dishes like Cornish fish pie. Tastefully decorated bedrooms complete the picture.

Name: Tom, Dick & Harry's
Address: 153 High Road, Loughton, IG10 4LF, United Kingdom
Description: If you’re after a fun, lively atmosphere, you’re in the right place at this laid-back brasserie with a quirky contemporary style. The experienced chef sources good quality ingredients and the charcoal oven is used to good effect. Global menus include brunch on Saturdays – and it has a playful cocktail list too.

Name: Tamarind
Address: 20 Queen Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 5PR, United Kingdom
Description: Found in the smart streets of Mayfair, this long-standing Indian restaurant is split over two levels; the first floor space is light and airy, while the basement presents the opportunity to watch the chefs working at the tandoor counter. The extensive menu of generous dishes encourages sharing, with a selection of small plates like Rajasthani churi chaat to start, and a good selection of curries and biryanis for the main course.

Name: Covino
Address: 118 Northgate Street, Chester, CH1 2HT, United Kingdom
Description: It might offer over 150 wines – including organic and low-intervention choices – but this sweet, intimate establishment is more than just a wine bar. The daily menu is designed with sharing in mind and features Mediterranean-inspired dishes with some punchy flavours; these include whole fish, meats butchered in-house and creative vegetable options. The friendly team help keep the atmosphere relaxed and have a good knowledge of both the menu and the wine list.

Name: Woodsman
Address: 4 Chapel Street, Stratford-on-Avon, CV37 6HA, United Kingdom
Description: Even in the dead of winter, you’ll likely find a big crowd and a lively buzz at this well-run restaurant. It’s easy to see why it’s such a busy place, as the attentive service is joined by hearty, satisfying cooking. Dishes often revolve around wood-fired produce, be it skate wing or partridge, and there’s a proper roast dinner served on Sundays. Shakespeare fans have an extra reason to visit, as the famed playwright’s childhood classroom is located just up the road and is open to visitors.

Name: Ginza St James's
Address: 15 Bury Street, St James’s, London, SW1Y 6AL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A professionally run restaurant situated in the heart of St James, comprising a stylish, elegant basement space featuring a cocktail bar and three counters for robata, teppanyaki and sushi. Attractive dishes feature excellent ingredients – and are accompanied by one of the best sake lists in London.

Name: The Hut
Address: Colwell Chine Road, Colwell Bay, Freshwater, PO40 9NP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant restaurant is superbly set amongst colourful beach huts and looks out over the sea to Hurst Castle. Sit on one of the terraces or under retractable roofs and enjoy anything from fish tacos to a fruits de mer platter. Most diners arrive by boat (they’ll even collect you from your mooring).

Name: Five Little Pigs
Address: 26 St Mary’s Street, Wallingford, OX10 0ET, United Kingdom
Description: Named after a novel by Agatha Christie, who lived at the nearby Winterbrook House, this neighbourhood restaurant is divided into three areas: the brightly coloured front resembles a modern bistro; a bar fits in the centre; and the rear sports an open kitchen pass and cosy booths. Sharing is encouraged, with larger plates such as roasted halibut and smaller ones like ‘spare bed tempura’ – using vegetables grown in the gardens of neighbours who have some space to spare. The wholesome cooking is joined by a range of local gins to keep enthusiasts happy.

Name: Orasay
Address: 31 Kensington Park Road, North Kensington, London, W11 2EU, United Kingdom
Description: This relaxed, contemporary bistro is named after the Scottish island where chef-owner Jackson Boxer holidayed as a child. Small plates of modern British food rely on excellent seasonal ingredients, which are capably cooked to produce clean, natural flavours. Fish and shellfish forms the heart of the menu and these are the standout dishes. It proves a good fit for this neighbourhood.

Name: Kerridge's Bar & Grill
Address: Whitehall Place, Victoria, London, SW1A 2BD, United Kingdom
Description: The menu bears all the hallmarks of chef Tom Kerridge by focusing on British dishes and the best of British ingredients; good use is made of the rotisserie and maturing meats are on display. When it comes to glamour and grandeur, the huge room offers plenty of bang for your buck.

Name: Tropea
Address: 27 Lordswood Road, Harborne, Birmingham, B17 9RP, United Kingdom
Description: The Italian ethos of uncluttered, straightforwardly delicious cooking is alive and well at this bright neighbourhood restaurant. Let the staff guide you when it comes to ordering the sharing plates, but you could do a lot worse than starting with a gorgonzola-stuffed bombolone, finishing with cannoli and sandwiching a couple of terrific homemade pastas in between. The Italian wine list is as well-priced as the food, and the buzzing atmosphere and friendly service add to the appeal. It's easy to see why the place is so popular.

Name: wilks
Address: 13 Chelsea Road, Bath, BA1 3DU, United Kingdom
Description: Fitting in nicely among a parade of independent shops in the west of the city, this intimate operation holds just three tables. The set menu features plenty of prime seafood like sweet langoustines and meaty wild monkfish, alongside meats such as tender, flavoursome pigeon. This seasonal produce is often accompanied by subtle international flavours, reflecting the chef’s global travels. There’s a French slant to the wine list, with small batch winemakers pushed to the fore.

Name: Barnaby's
Address: Trevibban Mill Vineyard, Dark Lane, Saint Issey, PL27 7SE, United Kingdom
Description: A few miles inland from Padstow and its older sibling Prawn on the Lawn, this lively pop-up-turned-permanent sits within a working vineyard and orchard. Start your visit on the charming terrace with a glass of their own wine or cider, accompanied by oysters either deep-fried or raw. A fixed menu of small plates is joined by larger daily specials from the blackboard, with quality local produce given a kick by hints of Middle Eastern or North African spicing – such as crab toast with muhammara or beetroot with whipped feta and chermoula.

Name: Franco's
Address: 61 Jermyn Street, St James’s, London, SW1Y 6LX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: One of London’s oldest Italian restaurants, this reliably enjoyable spot has benefitted from the years of practice. The kitchen focuses on an extensive menu of classically based dishes like veal and beef lasagne or linguine with lobster, with each one proving to be uncomplicated and well-executed. The many regulars come back time and again for their favourite dishes and the intimate, cosy atmosphere. The wine list is joyfully Italian, with some wonderful barolos among the choices.

Name: Mark Poynton at Caistor Hall
Address: Stoke Road, Caistor St Edmund, NR14 8QN, United Kingdom
Description: The Caistor Hall Hotel is a Georgian country house with a contemporary flourish inside, and a manicured lawn and terrace for those seeking fresh air. Experienced restaurateur Mark Poynton runs the hotel’s flagship restaurant, offering a balanced seasonal set menu in a choice of lengths. The terse menu descriptions belie the complexity of the cooking, evidenced by technically adept elements such as a perfectly seasoned red wine jus with rare aged beef. If there’s a chocolate dessert on the menu, then you’re in for a treat.

Name: LYLA
Address: 3 Royal Terrace, Edinburgh, EH7 5AB, United Kingdom
Description: Edinburgh’s finest row of Georgian townhouses is the setting for this elegant restaurant. Once inside, indulge in an aperitif in the stunning first-floor bar, before enjoying seafood-centric cooking in the understated dining room. A tasting menu format allows for maximum seasonality in the sustainably caught fish and shellfish, be it wild halibut or Scottish langoustines – and the chefs are equally at home chatting with diners as they are producing the attractive dishes, where creativity is only used in service of flavour. If you’re staying the night, luxurious bedrooms are available.

Name: Chef's Table
Address: 46 King Street, West Malling, ME19 6QT, United Kingdom
Description: The chef in question is the passionate Brad Redding, and his ‘table’ is a tiny restaurant in the centre of this pretty market town. It’s a highly personal operation, as Brad cooks his overtly seasonal tasting menu for around a dozen diners. There is technical skill on show across interesting, generous dishes that reflect the locale well – and the friendly service is nicely paced. Both bread and flavoured butters are made in house.

Name: Pearly Queen
Address: 44 Commercial Street, Tower Hamlets, London, E1 6LT, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a terrific buzz about this trendy 21st century take on an oyster bar that feels right at home in the streets of Shoreditch. Contemporary artwork – much of it oyster-based – lines the walls of this well-run restaurant, which is split across two levels. The menu makes great reading for seafood-lovers, mixing small plates with a few larger options like grilled cuttlefish with gooseberry hoisin – alongside a selection of both dressed and natural oysters, of course. Be sure not to leave without trying the sticky toffee madeleines.

Name: Hendersons
Address: 7-13 Barclay Place, Edinburgh, EH10 4HW, United Kingdom
Description: In 1962, Janet Henderson opened one of Scotland's most famous vegetarian restaurants; decades later her grandson Barrie is running the show in a smart new premises by Bruntsfield Links. The appealing, skilfully cooked selection of meat-free dishes are mostly vegan, with options like salt-baked celeriac and their take on classic haggis, neeps and tatties. Friendly service creates a lovely neighbourhood feel, while unfussy plant-based puddings are on hand to satisfy the most sweet-toothed of diners.

Name: Darjeeling Express
Address: 2.1-2.4 Kingly Court, Carnaby Street, Soho, London, W1B 5PW, United Kingdom
Description: The cooking of Kolkata and chef-owner Asma Khan’s Mughal ancestry inform the menu at this bright and breezy restaurant on the top floor of the perennially busy Kingly Court. Asma can be found chatting away with diners while the all-female kitchen team create authentic, vibrant dishes where careful spicing enhances the central ingredient. The menu is presented as an à la carte at lunch and served all together as a thali at dinner.

Name: eòrna
Address: 68 Hamilton Place, Edinburgh, EH3 5AZ, United Kingdom
Description: There's a plush quality to this smart counter restaurant in the suburb of Stockbridge. Small "chef’s table" operations like this allow for a much greater intimacy to your dining experience and, indeed, there are just two people working here: Brian in the kitchen and Glen looking after service and wines. Following a warm welcome, you can enjoy a highly seasonal tasting menu that has a strong Scottish heart, from the Orkney beef to the fantastic Perthshire strawberries.

Name: The Devonshire
Address: 17-19  Denman Street, Soho, London, W1D 7HW, United Kingdom
Description: One of the hottest tickets in town, The Devonshire is a 'proper' London pub that's been restored to its former glory. On the ground floor, and spilling out onto the pavement, you find the drinkers seeing off pints of Guinness, with food served upstairs. Most of the cooking takes place on the first floor, in the aptly named Grill Room, with the top-floor Claret Room providing a little more calm. Dishes are traditional in style and robust in flavour, with the quality of the produce shining through. Highly personable service rounds out the experience.

Name: The Flintlock
Address: 11 Cheadle Road, Cheddleton, ST13 7HN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Set inside a fine stone building overlooking a peaceful canal, this spacious, elegant restaurant is packed with charm. There are period features aplenty across the sitting area and the two dining rooms, where the self-taught chef serves dishes with a modern approach. Hake with fermented lettuce is something of a favourite, as are the fabulous Parker House roles, and puddings are a highlight too. Sweet, engaging service makes a visit all the more enjoyable, as does a stroll along the canal before dining.

Name: Akara
Address: Arch 208, 18 Stoney Street, Borough Market, Southwark, London, SE1 9AD, United Kingdom
Description: The team from Akoko are behind this appealing restaurant tucked underneath the arches in Borough Yards. An akara is a black-eyed pea fritter commonly found in West African and Brazilian cuisine, which gives a clue as to the influences found on the concise menu. Sharp execution and careful balancing of flavours runs throughout, with the signature akara a must to begin with. Some of the friendliest service around adds to the wonderfully warm experience.

Name: Updown Farmhouse
Address: Updown Road, Betteshanger, Deal, CT14 0EF, United Kingdom
Description: Hidden in the heart of the glorious Kent countryside, this delightful 17C farmhouse has been lovingly restored by its owners, and in the garden you'll find a charming, vine-laden conservatory restaurant with rustic décor. There are Italian influences aplenty on the menu, with dishes like ossobuco and crab tagliolini, alongside many cooked over an open fire and steak night on Wednesday. The gardens stretch over 7 acres in total, with individually styled bedrooms spread about the place.

Name: Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO
Address: Whitehall, Victoria, London, SW1A 2BX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: On the ground floor of the mightily impressive Raffles hotel – which opened in 2023 and occupies the former War Office – sits this elegant, comfortable and discreet dining room. Service is formally structured but not without personality, while the cooking is technically elaborate and sophisticated. The accompanying wine list is comprehensive and the wine pairings well considered.

Name: Studio Frantzén
Address: Harrods, 5th floor, 87–135 Brompton Road, Hyde Park and Knightsbridge, London, SW1X 7XL, United Kingdom
Description: A famous chef meets a famous department store, as the world-renowned Björn Frantzén expands his brand to the top floors of Harrods. The restaurant is spread across an elegant dining room and enclosed rooftop terrace, complete with a DJ and a lively atmosphere. The cooking has a mixture of Nordic and Asian influences, typified by ‘Sweden vs Japan’ – a dish which combines Swedish beef brisket and Japanese Wagyu. The turbot with butter sauce, anchovy and caviar is worth looking out for too, and a top-notch wine list makes a welcome addition.

Name: Rambutan
Address: 10 Stoney Street, Southwark, London, SE1 9AD, United Kingdom
Description: When negotiating the plethora of eateries around Borough Market, be sure not to miss this popular spot offering a taste of authentic Sri Lankan cooking. The Tamil region of northern Sri Lanka is the largest inspiration for the menu, with dishes providing satisfying flavours and well-balanced spicing. It’s a busy place, so there’s a suitable buzz in the air – and the knowledgeable service team are on hand with suggestions to suit your palate and appetite.

Name: The Kirkstyle Inn and Sportsman’s Rest.
Description: There’s plenty of rustic character to this appealing pub in a beautiful North Pennine hamlet. A warm welcome gets things off to a great start, before you tuck into dishes founded on produce that all comes from within 50 miles of the kitchen. This is shooting country, so that includes plenty of game – such as roasted grouse or partridge ballotine. Keep an eye out for the raspberry soufflé too, which is a cut above your typical pub pudding. Four bedrooms make this a great base for exploring the gorgeous surrounding countryside.

Name: The Parakeet
Address: 256 Kentish Town Road, Camden, London, NW5 2AA, United Kingdom
Description: Take a 19C pub, add wood-fired grilling, then finish with the buzz of a semi-open kitchen – and you have The Parakeet. It’s still firmly a public house, with drinkers far from neglected thanks to the large bar that dominates the front section; head to the rear to indulge in snacks and sharing plates that have big, gutsy flavours in abundance. A lick of smoke and fire adds to the appeal of many dishes, with grilled mackerel a highlight. A traditional roast is available on Sundays and service is relaxed yet engaging.

Name: Tern
Address: Worthing Pier, Marine Parade, Worthing, BN11 3PX, United Kingdom
Description: Tern sits on the first floor of an art deco building, in a unique location at the end of Worthing Pier – and when the tide draws in, you'll feel like you're on an ocean liner. It has a clean, contemporary feel, with an open kitchen dominating the room. Ingredient-led cooking is the order of the day, using a mixture of modern and classical techniques, while desserts like apple, caramel and buttermilk are a highlight. The short selection of English wines, nearly all available by the glass, cements their credentials in supporting producers along the south coast.

Name: Het Arsenaal 1309
Description: Björn de Waal has a special relationship with fruit and vegetables, which he sources as locally as possible and gives pride of place in his creative cuisine. Think mandarin orange combined with candied kumquat, a light corn foam, crispy potato chips and black truffle. The chef is also fond of cooking with game, but the vegetable accompaniments play a prominent role in those dishes, too. No visit to the picturesque Hanseatic city of Doesburg would be complete without a meal at this former monastery, a stunning blend of old and new.

Name: Savour
Description: Trijntje and Jaap are making waves in this vibrant little town just outside Groningen. They go the extra mile to make their diners feel welcome, and they are always on hand to provide help or advice. Chef Jaap works with a young and enthusiastic kitchen team, and it shows: their culinary creations are well-thought-out, sophisticated and technically accomplished. For instance, they give a perfectly medium-rare venison fillet extra nuances by pairing it with beetroot and elderflower in various guises. There are some great ideas behind the set menus – prepare to be blown away!

Name: De Etalage
Description: What was once a menswear shop is now a cosy bistro with a touch of Parisian charm. The fact that the young chefs have experience at top-flight establishments under their belts is evident in the dishes they create. They put an original spin on the classic combination of veal sweetbreads and onion – the beurre blanc with a hint of caramelised onion is the perfect finishing touch. These chefs have mastered the art of using flavours from around the globe to add nuance to their dishes. So, if you happen to be in Geleen one afternoon, be sure to stop by for a drink and a bite to eat.

Name: Magazzino 52
Description: This restaurant with characteristic brick-vaulted ceilings has retained the feel of its previous role as a warehouse. Despite the limited choice of dishes on the menu here, there is a strong focus on top-quality ingredients with recipes inspired by the Piedmont as well as the sea. The bottles of wine on display on its shelves can be purchased to take away. All-in-all, an excellent address in one of the city’s most elegant districts.

Name: Duo
Address: via Cavour 7, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the charming small village of San Felice del Benaco, Duo is the project of young chefs Daniele Ghedini and Federico Pelizzari (the latter also oversees the front of house). Their personalised, modern cuisine is Mediterranean in style and features meat-based dishes, vegetarian options and fish recipes (salt- and freshwater), with a focus on freshly caught fish which even has its own dedicated tasting menu. This colourful restaurant also boasts an outdoor space shaded by a pergola and surrounded by walnut trees.

Name: Visione Restaurant and Living
Address: Strada Nicolini Basso 34, loc. Tre Stelle, Barbaresco, 12050, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, new, young and enthusiastic managers work alongside a chef with Asian origins (who grew up in Italy) to offer a wide selection of dishes, many with an exotic flavour. Choose from an à la carte or two tasting menus, one of which has its roots in the regional traditions that are always held in high regard in Piedmont. Situated in the Casa Nicolini hotel in a quiet, panoramic location, the restaurant boasts fine views of the hills through its dining room windows and from its terrace, where a bar and bistro with a more concise and reasonably priced menu are set up in the summer months. The bistro also has its own small, dedicated dining room.

Name: Luminist Cafè Bistrot
Description: Situated on the ground floor of the splendid Banco di Napoli building that is also home to the Gallerie d'Italia museum, this restaurant also includes a bar and pasticceria. The varied restaurant menu features international dishes (for a quicker meal), fish based around recipes from around the world, alongside more creative dishes and regional specialities from Campania. The latter, from the aubergine parmigiana to the candele pasta served with a Neapolitan ragu, and the popular babà, are truly delicious and showcase all the colours and flavours of Neapolitan cuisine.

Name: San Tommaso 10
Description: In 1895 Luigi Lavazza opened here a grocery store where he immediately began blending coffee. 129 years later the place hosts a modern restaurant with a superb kitchen run by a chef who, despite hailing from the Marche region, treats guests to one of the most authentic interpretations of Piedmontese cuisine in the city, often with a creative touch. Among the options on offer here, the trolley of antipasti is a must.

Name: Al Gatto Verde
Description: Al Gatto Verde is situated within the walls of the Casa Maria Luigia, the welcoming country house run by Massimo Bottura and his wife Laura Gilmore which is popular with a cosmopolitan clientele. Here, the focus is on wood-fired cuisine – several dishes on the menu are finished over the fire, including tortellini au gratin with 36-month aged Parmesan and Montreal lamb, the latter a recipe from the chef’s native Canada which has been reinterpreted, flavoured with spices, cooked on a spit and served with pear purée. Both the dining room and the verdant outdoor space have a welcoming feel, while the service is friendly and attentive.

Name: Dokjard
Description: Set in a former warehouse by the picturesque Noorderhaven, this relaxed "brew-bistro" offers a delightful blend of pub atmosphere and attentive service. When you first enter, you will be greeted by the aroma of freshly brewed beer and the sight of towering brewing kettles. The kitchen team pushes the boundaries, effortlessly weaving between the classic and creative. From steak tartare with an Asian twist to melt-in-your-mouth pork cheeks with dukkah and sesame seeds, this cuisine is vibrant and imaginative. The house beers perfectly complement the dishes, adding a personal touch. What a place!

Name: LIMES aan den Rijn
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Daan Reijngoudt is a chef who knows the importance of sauces. Think a delicate foie gras cream sauce with a hint of Calvados to add depth to fried duck liver with sweet fruit garnishes and a brioche roll. His cuisine is beautifully in step with the times, without resorting to any unnecessary frills. Inside, you can watch the chef at work in the attractive open plan kitchen. However, a spot on the terrace, nestled right next to a business complex and overlooking the river, might be your best bet.

Name: Zenith
Description: The dishes served at Zenith are a feast for the senses. Chef Joey Stinissen's creations are both visually stunning and bursting with flavour. Prepare to be blown away by the perfectly fried fillet of red mullet with tender octopus, a beurre blanc with lime leaf, and a mild red curry sauce. Beauty and depth go hand in hand. The chef's dedication to his craft is evident in both his meticulous plating and the fact that he goes to the trouble of creating different dishes for the à la carte and the surprise menus. In this elegant, atmospheric restaurant on a corner plot, attention is paid to every last detail – right down to the wine pairings!

Name: Legat 1903
Description: While the chef is a native, the menu at this restaurant in a southern neighbourhood focuses on modern international dishes with an ambitious edge. Ingredients are high-end and they have a live lobster tank; the cuisine changes with the seasons and includes a vegan menu. The wine list features some top growers, service is assured and the room has a sophisticated feel.

Name: Gušti mora
Description: It’s all about fish from the Adriatic Sea at this well-regarded restaurant just outside the city. The waiter presents the daily catch on a platter for you to select, which is then cooked whole, portioned out to your group, and served with salad or vegetables. It’s a comfy place with a rustic look and a long family tradition which started in the bay of Boka Kotorska and arrived in Belgrade in 2003 to share the same passion for good cooking.

Name: The Square
Description: Just behind the busy Knez Mihaliva shopping street, this restaurant takes its name from the Square Nine hotel – one of the most beautiful hotels in the city – in which it is housed. Situated on the ground floor, the elegant dining room has soft lighting in the evening, while a pleasant outdoor space is perfect for alfresco dining. The contemporary-style cuisine features well-balanced French and Italian flavours, although a focus on Serbian specialities is planned for the near future. Superb wine list, plus one of the city’s best choice of cocktails served in The Lobby Bar.

Name: Pinòt
Description: This contemporary-style bistro is situated in Novi Beograd, a modern business and shopping district across the Sava river from Belgrade’s city centre. The menu features seasonal cuisine which changes throughout the year depending on market availability, including a small number of daily specials announced at your table. One of the owners, Vuk Vuletiḉ, is a young, award-winning sommelier, so it’s no surprise that the impressive wine selection is one of the main reasons for making your way here.

Name: Salon 1905
Description: Situated on the first floor of the 19C Geozavod building, this majestic, aristocratic restaurant boasts modern furnishings that provide a pleasing contrast to the marble, stucco, brass and gold-coloured decor which creates a truly spectacular overall effect. This sumptuous setting is the backdrop for cuisine prepared by a new, young chef who offers just one tasting menu (3, 5 or 7 courses) featuring reinterpretations of traditional Serbian dishes such as cheese and tomatoes or Vojvodina sataraš, all carefully cooked, beautifully presented and full of flavour. A restaurant that is definitely on the up!

Name: Langouste
Description: Situated in a typical cobbled street in the old town, this restaurant overlooks the Sava river. Here, the chef uses Serbian ingredients (including some produced in-house) to create dishes that combine the flavours of Serbia with French techniques and inspiration and Italian style. The cockerel cooked in Serbian Pinor Noir and port, served with carrots and various sauces, is completely French in style yet showcases different local ingredients, while the lemon tart bursts with the flavour of Italian lemons. The wine list demonstrates a love of Bordeaux wines, plus there’s a good selection of cocktails. Without a doubt, one of the best restaurants in the Serbian capital.

Name: SkyLounge
Description: As its name suggests, this elegant, modern restaurant with a decidedly international feel boasts stunning views of the city (especially impressive at sunset) thanks to its location on the eighth floor of the Hilton hotel. The chefs here create a varied menu that combines elements of Mediterranean cuisine with Asian influences, with a whole page dedicated to different types of sushi. They have also recently added lobster from the North Sea and king crabs to the menu, which can be chosen directly from the fish tank. In addition to the wine list, you’ll also find a good selection of other drinks on offer.

Name: Homa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: It might be located in the historic Dorćol quarter, but Homa has a thoroughly modern look and feel. Take a sit on the leafy terrace during the day or in the intimately lit restaurant at night to enjoy creative cooking with subtle Italian influences where you can choose from a well-rounded menu with a good selection of meat, fish and vegetarian dishes. The pleasant outdoor space is perfect for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Klub Književnika by Branko Kisic
Description: The young chef at this long-established restaurant popular with locals and tourists alike has been at the helm since 2019. Here, guests can choose to eat in a winter garden or in the dining room, where there’s often live music during the colder months. The menu features classic favourites, such as the Krempita dessert which has been served here since the restaurant opened in 1946, and traditional Serbian specialities (there’s a 25-minute wait for the savoury Gibanica dish), with the occasional interesting, personalised touch and a focus on careful presentation.

Name: Na Ćošku
Description: Situated to the east of the city just outside the historic centre, this restaurant boasts an intimate ambience that comes as a surprise when compared to its exterior. The dining room has the feel of a French bistro, with small tables, background music (often French), and a few cubby-holes that are perfect for couples. The cuisine has solid roots in Balkan tradition, featuring traditional soups and stews, such as lamb in white wine served with mashed potato and seasonal vegetables. More international recipes also feature, such as entrecote steak with a foie gras sauce and various fish dishes.

Name: Mezestoran Dvorište
Description: Both the bright decor and colourful tableware at this restaurant demonstrate the light, happy spirit of the Mediterranean, as does the array of tempting dishes on the menu, including chickpea fritters, tzatziki, different kinds of olives, typical “Dokos” from Crete (imaginatively flavoured croutons), as well as chicken and pork gyros. Enjoy a gastronomic voyage that takes you to Greece (the owner’s native country), including Crete, as well as to Italy.

Name: Magellan
Description: Lots of Italian influence including homemade pastas as well as fresh and contemporary main courses such as turbot with cauliflower and a Tamjanika wine sauce, and pork neck with mushrooms and apple, to be savoured on the à la carte or tasting menu.

Name: L'Adresse
Description: Housed in a boutique hotel not far from the San Sava church in the Vracar district, this contemporary-style restaurant is situated just beyond the modern and welcoming open-plan lounge space. European-influenced cuisine is to the fore here, with a focus on meat (including grilled options), although the menu also features a few fish-based and vegetarian specialities. The comfortable Lounge Bar is the perfect setting for a relaxing aperitif or post-dinner drink.

Name: Ebisu
Description: As soon as you exit the elevator on the seventh floor of the Square Nine hotel, you immediately step into this intimate and elegant restaurant where you can choose to sit on one of the four bar stools or on the terrace boasting fine views of the city centre. The menu features Japanese cuisine, including sushi, sashimi, maki (the tuna maki with jalapeno pepper is particularly delicious), tempura (soft-shell crab served with wasabi mayonnaise and pickled ginger), teppanyaki, at least one ramen, and much more besides. The desserts, on the other hand, are modern European in style.

Name: JaM
Description: This restaurant (JAM is an anacronym for “Just a Maestro”) in a quiet residential district in the city centre boasts a cosy, welcoming atmosphere both in its dining room featuring a white colour scheme and in its plant-filled outdoor space. In the dining room, guests choose their desserts directly from a display cabinet, while the bar offers an impressive selection of home-made cocktails. The cuisine is equally as impressive, with dishes that are generous and yet elegant, skilfully prepared and beautifully presented. If you’re not sure what to choose, we can highly recommend the delicious “Duck Maestro”.

Name: The Twenty Two
Description: Situated on the rooftop of the Metropol Palace hotel, this restaurant offers fine views of the city and St Mark’s church, as well as delicious cocktails, gourmet international cuisine (alongside a few local specialities, which we highly recommend) prepared by a new chef and soft background music. It’s also perfect for an aperitif or a post-dinner drink – in other words, an excellent all-round choice!

Name: Enso
Description: The dishes served at this lively, modern and trendy restaurant are based on solid French culinary traditions, skilfully blended with Serbian flavours (the sea bream with Serbian plum gnocchi is both delicious and original) and Mediterranean influences (the tempting lemon tart is the perfect way to end your meal). The focus here is on seasonal ingredients cooked and presented with real attention to detail.

Name: Metropolitan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Although this restaurant within the Regency Hyatt hotel is situated away from the centre, it boasts a convenient location for anyone visiting the area for business and is the perfect choice for a relaxing meal, offering excellent service. The menu features international cuisine alongside various local specialties. The "Metropolitan Specials" include beef cheek cooked over a low heat for 24 hours, although it's also possible to create your own dish featuring something from the grill, a side dish and a sauce.

Name: Comunale Caffè e Cucina
Description: When the sun shines head for this super riverside spot in the shadow of Belgrade Fortress. It’s one of several whitewashed former customs warehouses with open terraces – but this one is owned by an architect, so inside it’s sleek and stylish. Classic Italian staples include meats cooked in the Josper oven, accompanied by an impressive choice of "liqueurs and spirits", in particular gin, and a good selection of cocktails and mocktails.

Name: Bela Reka
Description: Inspired by traditional Serbian cuisine, this restaurant proudly showcases local and regional ingredients, many of which (such as their goat’s cheese and hams) are produced on their own farm in the Homolje mountains. The tempting menu here is as delicious as it is long, and includes barbecue-grilled meats such as lamb and steak. A professional yet simple outfit that is impressive in the way that it manages to maintain a high quality of cuisine and service despite the large number of covers.

Name: Royd
Address: 95/1 Dibuk Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: There are many courses and many delights to be found on the tasting menu at this cosy little restaurant. Seating is divided between tables and the counter, with room for just 12 guests in total; there is an excellent flow to the parade of innovative Southern Thai dishes like crispy bee hoon topped with morning glory, which are all attractively presented and delivered by a likeable team. Accompany the fabulous cooking with a well-crafted cocktail pairing that uses techniques such as fermentation to make interesting drinks that complement the food well.

Name: Sang Tha Tien
Address: 75 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Formerly an ice factory, this small eatery retains some of the interior structure and incorporates vintage décor in a dining room decorated with basic wooden furniture and collectibles. The chef embraces seasonal Thai ingredients, especially fruit, to produce unique, signature dishes in a home-cooking style, such as strawberry salad with shrimp paste and caramelised pork and spicy plum mango salad. The crab meat with fresh herbs and spicy sauce is unmissable.

Name: Khao Kriab Pak Mor Talat Na San Jao
Address: Na San Jao Market, Tonpo Road, Talat, Muaeng Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: The veteran stall-owner has been making her delicious dumplings for decades in this famous food cart in Na San Jao market. The thin steamed rice dumplings combine a sweet, gooey texture with a savoury filling, made with minced pork, crushed peanuts and herbs in creamy coconut milk.

Name: Day & Night (Surat Thani)
Address: 83/25 Liang Mueang Road, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This enchanting, almost English-looking country pub draws tourists like bees to honey. Boasting a bright, breezy vibe, it serves international favourites, from steak to pizzas and light snacks, with a tempting array of cocktails and craft beers. The fresh watermelon topped with dry salmon and served with a spicy salad dressing is sweet and juicy, while another popular local delicacy, bingsu, salted egg yolk, offers a creamy scent and texture. Smooth live music in the evenings.

Name: The Smokaccia Laboratory
Address: 116/4 Mu 3, Srisoonthorn Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Chef Luca Mascolo has invented a complex crispy sourdough which he has named ‘Smokaccia’, which is served with a variety of inventive fillings. Highlights include slow-cooked Australian Wagyu striploin, Surat Thani oysters and cheese from Nonthaburi. The high-ceilinged dining room features both tables and counter seats overlooking the open kitchen. Things step up a gear at dinner with a creative, 18-course tasting menu showcasing modern techniques. Vegan options are also available.

Name: Pratunam Baan Ko Noodles
Address: Ban Ko, Bang Sai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13190, Thailand
Description: Set beside a peaceful canal, the crowds flock here for their speciality: beef noodles. The noodles come with offal, beef balls, spare ribs and tender beef slices. The soup is also superb, with a meaty aroma. It’s so popular, the chef prepares 25-30 kg of fresh offal every day.

Name: Heng Khao Moo Daeng
Address: 428/1 Namueang Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This simple eatery is always bustling at lunchtime with queues for both dine-in and takeout. The owner's inviting and chatty demeanour sets the scene. His signature barbeque pork comes with crispy pork and sweet sausage inside and a large portion only costs 40 baht.

Name: Lam Phu 2
Address: 23/1 Mu 3, Pak Nam Road, Bang Kung, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Watch the fishing boats on Tapi River while enjoying a bright and airy setting and local seafood cooked southern style. The oyster omelette is gorgeous with a crispy egg base, spot-on seasoning and fresh local oysters; it goes well with steamed rice. The tender stir-fried squid with salted eggs is packed with flavour and flanked by an impressively creamy sauce. With over 100 seats, there is ample room for large groups to enjoy the scenic view.

Name: Saffron
Address: Banyan Tree Samui, 99/9 Mu 4, Maret, Ko Samui, 84310, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Elegantly appointed with floor-to-ceiling windows, contemporary lighting and dark wooden furnishings, Saffron also offers alfresco dining with a fantastic view. You can choose from à la carte and tasting menus. The roast duck red curry is paired with a thick sweet and spicy sauce, a fresh lychee and pineapple compote and roasted skin that excite the tastebuds. The fried softshell crab salad with lychee and passionfruit is also a must.

Name: The Redbox
Address: 6 Soi Jannsaap, Huai Kaeo Road, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: With business acumen and cooking techniques gleaned from their travels, Chef Dan and partner Pimmada offer modern Thai with Malaysian and Brunei influences. They import select ingredients like salted eggs from Chaiya, and Gula Melaka (Malaysian palm sugar) to create treats like Siam Ruby, a signature dessert. We recommend the signature creation cocktail with a complexity of flavours before your unforgettable meal. Seating is limited so bookings are essential.

Name: Saigon Recipe
Address: Piman 49, B3 Building, 46/5 Soi Sukhumvit 49, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: With its canary-yellow walls, vintage posters and Indochinese décor, this place feels like a home in Saigon, if it was staffed by capable Vietnamese chefs. They carefully select ingredients, including rice wrappers and noodles from Vietnam, to create flavourful rice and noodle dishes, salads and rolls the owner might serve family and friends. Weekday lunches offer set menus that please even the time-pressed. Coffee fans should try the authentic Vietnamese brew.

Name: Blackitch
Address: 27/1 Nimmanahaeminda Soi 7 Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Hidden in the city centre in plain sight, this second floor 16-seater is decorated with stone, wood and local blue fabrics in a minimalist style. The creative chef, Phanuphol Bulsuwan, honed his skills under his restaurateur grandmother. He constantly adapts his 10-course meal using Thailand’s seasonal ingredients, uniting Thai, Japanese and Chinese influences. He also ferments kitchen scraps to season his dishes and brews beers and sake for food pairing.

Name: Krua Supanniga by Khunyai Somsie
Address: Supanniga Home, 130/9 Phothisan Road, Phra Lap, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Named after the Supanniga flower, this cute shop offers delightful dishes blending flavours from the eastern seaboard and Isan cuisine. Grandma's recipes inspire the food here. Don't miss the must-order chamuang pork—a juicy stewed pork infused with Chamuang leaf's slightly sour flavour. The restaurant provides indoor and outdoor seating, including shaded tables in the tree house.

Name: Savelberg
Address: 136/1 Soi Yen Akat 2, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Food and mood pair well at Dutch chef-owner Henk Savelberg’s eponymous restaurant, now in a contemporary house in Chong Nonsi. The sparkling dining room features an open kitchen, a refined wine cellar and garden views, with private group dining available. The menu boasts adventurous, modern, colourful French dishes with a classical base, made from fine international ingredients. Rounding out the experience is the professional service. Booking is essential.

Name: Samut
Address: 14/119 Mu 1, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83100, Thailand
Description: Samut (or ocean) is set in a traditional Thai-Chinese building decorated in an Oriental style, with dark teak wood. Previously the lobby of the adjacent hotel, it’s now a gastronomic destination. The set menu, with more than 10 dishes, tours the island’s coastline, offering seafood caught by local fishermen. The chef respects the traditions of the island, selecting flavours and fruits inspired by local creativity, including a reinterpretation of Phuket dim sum.

Name: Rimsaun
Address: U Thong 30 Road, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: The owner hails from Nakhon Sri Thammarat and has been serving quality southern Thai cuisine in the ancient capital for over 25 years. Despite its simple décor, the restaurant with its high vaulted ceilings, shady garden and lack of walls is well worth visiting. The southern Thai sour curry with fish is a family recipe and a must-try, while the fried prawns are glazed in a delectably sticky tamarind sauce. Keep an eye out for the daily specials on the white board.

Name: Embassy Room
Address: 9F, Park Hyatt Hotel, 88 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Authenticity is key with Catalan fare from a Catalonian chef. Chef Ferran Tadeo, formerly of El Bulli and Minibar, showcases his heritage and family recipes using fine local and international ingredients. The private room is perfect for intimate gatherings, while outdoor seating offers views of the sky garden and pool. The signature Lobster Wellington is the pièce de résistance. And there’s a wine list of over 100 labels from seven regions for Spanish wine aficionados.

Name: Khao Horm
Address: 34/36 Mu 4, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
Description: Just 5 minutes from the airport, Khao Horm is a great spot to get your last-minute fill of delicious Southern Thai and local recipes before flying home. The family recipes have been passed down from generation to generation for over a century. We recommend the stir-fried minced pork whose yellow curry paste features a gutsy mix of spices. The main dining room is set in a large open-air pavilion. They also offer AC indoor dining and plenty of parking too.

Name: Aeeen
Address: 4/13 Mu 5, Suthep Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Aeeen goes the sound of Ken’s unique laughter, according to wife Yuki. Under the concept of Neo Shojin Ryori, the Japanese couple craft their plant-based menu using seasonal ingredients. The dining areas span two floors of a cute wooden house that feels like rural Japan. Lines of jars contain the fermented ingredients they use in the food. We recommend the perfectly judged soymilk udon noodles and refreshing mango with ginger and honey drink.

Name: Mana
Address: 420 Mu 21, Sri Chan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: After working for years at Thai-Chinese restaurants in Bangkok, chef-owner Mana returned home to open his own outlet. He’s now been serving flavoursome Thai-Chinese-style seafood dishes that are easy on the pocketbook for over a decade. Inside his restaurant’s one-storey white building are two dining areas, one with AC and another open-air one. The oyster omelette and crispy salad with fish maw, shrimp and cashews are recommended.

Name: Baan Suan Mae Rim
Address: 261 Mu 2, Chiang Mai-Fang Road, San Pong, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Although this restaurant is outside the city centre, it’s worth the drive for its Thai cuisine, and especially its northern dishes, served in a beautiful, natural setting. Open for more than a decade, the place consists of several northern Thai-style pavilions, which all face a pond – and you can also dine in the open air. Either way, there are tranquil views of the trees, pond, and rice fields. Deep-fried snakehead fish with hot and spicy sauce is recommended.

Name: Supanniga Eating Room (Tha Tian)
Address: 392/25-26 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: The homestyle Thai food at this casual restaurant comes with postcard-worthy views of the Chao Phraya River and iconic Wat Arun. Whether you’re sharing lunch with friends after touring the nearby Grand Palace or enjoying a romantic meal at sunset, try a flavoursome signature dish. The recipes come from the owner’s grandmother; standouts include fried Chinese cabbage and braised pork belly with herbs and cowa leaves.

Name: See Na Nuan Café
Address: 64/160 Mu 14, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: This 500-seat crowd pleaser close to Khon Kaen University serves flavoursome central Thai fare and Isan dishes in an industrial-style house with a huge outdoor dining area. Inside is all brick and black steel; outside, the steel continues in a birdcage-like dining area next to more seating centred around a lawn. Seafood tanks attest to the food’s freshness; the grilled snakehead fish served with spicy dip is recommended. Chill live music features nightly.

Name: J'AIME by Jean-Michel Lorain
Address: 2F, U Sathorn Hotel, 105/1 Soi Ngam Du Phli, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: As you enter this restaurant, your world becomes a little topsy-turvy, with a grand piano suspended from the ceiling and upside-down chandeliers. But take one bite of the creative French cuisine and all will be right again. Protégés of the eponymous Jean-Michel Lorain produce the Memoirs and Wonder set menus with one eye on sustainability, using almost entirely Thai ingredients while retaining a French heart.

Name: Gen Japanese Charcoal Grill (Ekkamai)
Address: Vibes Ekkamai (Between Soi Ekkamai 13 and 15), 267/31 Soi Sukhumvit 63, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: This trendy spot for yakitori and drinks has a slight vintage feel not dissimilar to a Japanese whisky bar. Smartly dressed staff offer traditional Japanese service, while the menu includes ingredients flown in from Japan – including the prized Hitachiwagyu beef. A variety of dishes are available, not just yakitori, including sashimi, rice and noodles. If you’re lucky, you’ll get to try one of their multiple Japanese eel dishes.

Name: Methavalai Sorndaeng
Address: 78/2 Ratchadamnoen Klang Road, Bowon Niwet, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: One of the city’s original Thai fine dining restaurants, they’ve maintained a loyal customer base for 60+ years, using the same timeless recipes and cooking techniques. The refined dishes are complex, delivering blasts of flavour. Highlights are crispy rice noodles in sweet and sour sauce, spicy lemongrass salad, and crab meat and acacia red curry. The curry pastes are made from scratch and fishcakes from featherback fish. Small parties should book the private room.

Name: Somtum Der (Si Lom)
Address: 5/5 Sala Daeng Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: While other regional Thai cuisines are represented, intensely flavoured Isan dishes from north-eastern Thailand dominate the menu at this cosy eatery in the busy Si Lom neighbourhood. The big draw is the famous Som Tam (Thai papaya salad), which can be served ‘Isan style’ (with fermented fish) or ‘Thai style’ (without fermented fish) – along with a variety of other topping options. The brand has expanded over the years and now has other branches in New York City, Tokyo and Taipei.

Name: Sornthong
Address: 2829-31 Rama 4 Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: For quality seafood that won’t burn a hole in your pocket, look no further than Sornthong. Easily identified by the crowds dining beneath a large yellow sign in Thai and Chinese, this family-run shop has done a booming trade in prime fresh fish for more than 20 years. Ingredients are taken from tanks outside the restaurant, then cooked under the watchful eye of Mr. Chai – fried oysters with creamy eggs and a sweet-sour-spicy chilli sauce are a must-try. Away from the sea, keep an eye out for the well-marinated grilled pork satay.

Name: Royal Osha
Address: 99 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: A majestic twist on its sister restaurant in San Francisco, Royal Osha aims to engage the senses with enticing flavours, aromas, textures, sights and sounds. The setting is a sleek, modern dining room decorated with Thai art. Start with a cocktail inspired by Ramakien characters, before enjoying dishes like the excellent tom yum kung mae nam (spicy, sour soup with river prawns infused with Thai herbs) and the (seasonal) chilled rice served with accompaniments.

Name: We-La-Dee
Address: 291 Mu 9,  Nong Chom, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
Description: A taste of Bangkok in Chiang Mai, We-La-Dee brings central Thai cuisine north in an airy industrial-style dining room marked by playful accents. The restaurant’s large collection of action figures and a floor-to-ceiling installation of artificial flowers inspire photographs. Its extensive menu, which includes some original recipes from the chef, inspire both relaxed meals with family and friends and afternoons spent sipping coffee or tea and enjoying dessert.

Name: Krua Phech Doi Ngam
Address: 267/1 Mu 2, Mahidol Road, Pa Daet, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: This popular open-air eatery serves well-sized northern Thai favourites at fair prices. Kang Liang, the peppery curry paste in spicy mixed vegetables goes well with the prawns’ natural sweetness; while the local fish marinated in herbs and spices is grilled in a bamboo tube until soft, with a smoky aroma. Do check the blackboard for specials of the day, which often focus on seasonal dishes.

Name: Khrua Ohm
Address: 2/99 Mu 2, Wichit Songkhram Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
Description: After a decade as a musician with a side gig of cooking for bandmates, these days Somphop finds himself enjoying daily walks through the market for fresh catches of the day and hand-cutting them for various southern Thai dishes served at his small, casual restaurant. Braised fish in salted soybean sauce; prawns with salted eggs and acacia; and wok-fried pork featuring the tender, succulent ‘armpit cut’ between the picnic shoulder and belly are not to be missed.

Name: Jay Jia Yentafo
Address: 564 Rama 4 Road, Maha Phruettharam, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: For 30+ years, office workers have been making a beeline to Jay Jia Yentafo for their eponymous pink-noodle soup and legendary homemade shrimp balls. The soup packs a knockout combination of shrimp, fish, fish sticks and fried wontons and explodes in sour and spicy notes.

Name: Vacca
Address: 99 Mu 20, Airport Road, Sila, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Italian chef-owner Fabio Colautti's restaurant near Khon Kaen Airport offers authentic Italian flavours with homemade pasta, wood-fired pizzas, and grilled meats. Opened in 2015, it boasts a classic Italian ambience with a cosy white interior, a large wine cellar, and an open kitchen. Highlights include the Vacca pizza and the grilled Wagyu rib-eye.

Name: Punjab Grill
Address: GF, Radisson Suites Bangkok Sukhumvit, 23/2-3 Soi Sukhumvit 13, Khlong Toei Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Like its sister restaurants in India and across the world, Bangkok’s Punjab Grill serves authentic yet contemporary Northern Indian cuisine. At the helm is Chef Bharath, who jazzes up dishes like chaat; his includes chutney-dressed avocado and puffed rice with yoghurt espuma. Equally flavourful are classics like biryani and tikka. Both come in several variations, including veggie. A glass wall in the elegant dining room provides a view of the tandoor action.

Name: The House by Ginger
Address: 199 Mun Mueang Road, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Open for decades on the edge of the old city, this stylish and quirky spot serves a mixture of Northern Thai classics and those with a more modern twist. Premium ingredients like New Zealand beef are a feature, as are organic vegetables and daily picked herbs from their nearby Ginger Farm. The seasonally changing menu includes the Chiang Mai platter – an ideal way to sample an array of dishes. Pair your food with one of their many lovely cocktails and to extend your evening, continue on to the House Lounge next door.

Name: Reunros (Yan Nawa)
Address: Bangkok Square, 762/2 Rama 3 Road, Bang Phongphang, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: When Ruenros opened 40+ years ago, its owner came from a medical background, hence the focus on herbal and medicinal braised dishes. The 3rd generation heir now runs it and he chooses all the market fresh ingredients himself every day. Specialties include spring rolls using a family recipe, stir-fried goat with celery, fried rice with salted fish and slow-cooked soup, which is packed with flavour. For dessert, try the taro purée with sticky rice.

Name: Celadon
Address: GF, The Sukhothai Hotel, 13/3 Sathon Tai Road, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: There’s more than a hint of romance to dining in these two delightful Salas in the manicured grounds of the Sukhothai Hotel, surrounded by lotus ponds. A wide-ranging menu includes seafood selections and dishes from the charcoal grill; the five- and eight-course set menu delivers smaller tasting dishes. The signature steamed rice dumplings make a delightful starter, while whole seabass baked with Thai herbs impresses. Service is attentive and charming and there are nightly performances of traditional Thai dance.

Name: Yamazato
Address: 24F, The Okura Prestige Bangkok, 57 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Okura Prestige’s Japanese restaurant boasts 3 dining areas: a sushi bar, teppanyaki grills and a stylish dining room. The fish is sourced weekly from Toyosu market in Japan, and they offer a rotating selection of sashimi options, depending on availability. Dressed in traditional kimono, the staff make every effort to ensure that diners have a great experience, while the panoramic high-rise cityscape offers a romantic setting that couples adore.

Name: Ta Khai
Address: Rosewood Hotel, 88/28, 88/30-33 Muen-Ngoen Road, Pa Tong, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Ta Khai means ‘fishing net’, and here diners can choose live seafood from the restaurant’s tank before a chef scoops it up and cooks it. Dishes, including the deep-fried white snapper with fish sauce, are flavoursome, with spicing slightly toned down if you wish, while two set menus offer a variety of items to try. Ask for a table on the lovely terrace for a panoramic view of the bay and cityscape beyond – or for something different, book a BBQ sala.

Name: Sra Bua by Kiin Kiin
Address: GF, Siam Kempinski Hotel, 991/9 Rama 1 Road, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Inspired by its sister restaurant, Copenhagen's Kiin Kiin, Sra Bua is one of Bangkok’s original purveyors of modern, innovative Thai cuisine. À la carte and tasting menus are available, with their dishes – from street food starter to dessert – proving creative and original, yet respectful of traditional Thai flavours. Premium international ingredients are used throughout, while both alcoholic and non-alcoholic pairings are available to complete the experience.

Name: Kinu by Takagi
Address: 2F, Mandarin Oriental Hotel, 48 Soi Charoen Krung 40, Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden behind sliding wooden doors, Kinu's décor combines Japanese and Thai influences, featuring teakwood crosshatch flooring and a mix of Japanese and northern Thai ceramics. Chef Takagi excels in Kyoto-style Kaiseki, highlighting the natural flavours of top Japanese ingredients. The bar offers an excellent sake collection, and a matcha tea ceremony marks the end of your visit. Additionally, welcome drinks are served in a Japanese-style Minka area.

Name: Lenzi Tuscan Kitchen
Address: 69/2 Soi Ruam Ruedi 2, Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: It’s a family affair at this authentic Tuscan restaurant, from the top-notch meats and cheeses sourced from chef Francesco Lenzi’s family farm in Pisa to his mother’s limoncello. The chef uses traditional cooking techniques from back home and often pops out of the open kitchen to greet diners like family. Start with antipasti or an iI primi like Risotto Taleggio e Tartufo and then try the flavoursome Filetto Alla Rossini. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Lumdee Te Khuadang
Address: V Community, 345/9 Mu 3, Wongwaen Rop 2 Road, San Phra Net, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bearing a loose resemblance to San Francisco’s Golden Gate Bridge, the bridge in this restaurant’s name (which translates as 'delicious at the red bridge') forms an iconic landmark while also providing guests with a pleasant spot for dining after dark. The range of healthy Northern Thai dishes provides intense flavours; their biotechnology-derived fermented pork has the highest levels of hygiene and quality, and is used in many of the dishes.

Name: Bang Dean
Address: 16/10 Mu 1, Phet Kasem Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: Nearby the Takua Pa Government Office, this street food place serves Thai-Muslim dishes, including excellent chicken biryani, plus crispy rotis paired with savoury curries or sweet condensed milk and banana. Open for breakfast through late lunch, it closes when the food runs out.

Name: Pa Noi Beef Noodles
Address: 57/8 Sisuttha Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: The aroma of beef noodle soup greets diners at this popular eatery. The distinctive tamarind chilli paste pairs perfectly with deep-fried chicken skin or mixed into the noodles. The boat noodles with rich flavours are also a must-try.

Name: Yangzi Jiang
