Address: Mandarin Oriental Hotel, 48 Soi Charoen Krung 40,  Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Valet parking
Description: The original owner of this 120-year-old heritage house served the government as Phraya, one of the highest ranks of Thai nobility. Previously Mandarin Oriental's cooking school, they switched operations in 2022. Chef Patchara serves traditional Thai dishes inspired by those school recipes. Surrounded by shady greens, the whitewashed house has a terrace with stunning sunset views over the river. The dining room inside fits a capacity of 20 guests a night.

Name: L'Arôme by the Sea
Address: 247/5 Phrabaramee Road, Pa Tong, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Chef Yannick Hollenstein, the skilled Swiss chef, intelligently selects the choicest ingredients for the French set menus – seasonal and vegetarian – and à la carte dishes with a great range of cheese and wines. Start with rooftop drinks and sunset feels before heading downstairs to the nautical-themed restaurant with its views of Kalim beach. The four ways Phuket lobster is a real treat with lobster meat, tail, a poached top and creamy lobster bisque.

Name: Krua Loong Loy Pa Lan
Address: 1010 Phet Kasem Road, Huai Chorakhe, Mueang Nakhon Pathom, Nakhon Pathom, 73000, Thailand
Description: A passion for wild ingredients like wild boar, frogs, seafood, and even greens, and a zeal for local flavours, which tend to be intense, tangy, and spicy, informs everything on the menu here. The stir-fried wild boar with chilies and the grilled, salt-crusted snakehead fish are both recommended, as is the seafood cooked according to local recipes. The atmosphere is relaxed and homely, with air-conditioned dining rooms and outdoor seating available.

Name: Ojo
Address: 76F, The Standard Bangkok Mahanakhon, 114 Narathiwas Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Offering breathtaking views over the Bangkok cityscape, Ojo has the honour of being Thailand’s highest restaurant. Glamorous pink and gold décor adds to the appeal of a truly special location in which to dine, while the authentic Mexican cooking means this restaurant is far more than just its setting. The menu of attractive dishes includes tender cochinillo and a selection of raw seafood. Ask for a table by the window or on the terrace to make the most of the view.

Name: Aim Aot (Udon Thani)
Address: 118/9 Prajaksinlapacom Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: One family has been running this Thai-Vietnamese breakfast spot for over 50 years. In that time, they’ve won many fans, including the local celebs whose photos grace the walls. Especially loved are the homemade ingredients, including pork floss and chilli paste, which are also on sale.

Name: Lab Mu Worachai
Address: 26/3 Posri Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: Pork reigns supreme at this traditional Isan eatery, which may be renowned for its namesake Lab Mu – minced pork, skin and liver – but the flavourful Somtum Lao is another standout. Lunchtime can get hectic, but service is swift. The sharing sets of four to six dishes are perfect for groups.

Name: Nikaku
Address: GF, W Bangkok, 106 North Sathorn Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: This Japanese restaurant originating from Kitakyushu, specialises in authentic Edo-mae sushi. Offering an omakase menu, it serves only 12 diners at a counter, showcasing the chef's skills. Ingredients are sourced daily from Japan, ensuring superb quality fish and shellfish, such as Hokkaido's delicate uni. The chef provides detailed seafood explanations, and diners can opt for special tea pairings.

Name: Krua Samchai
Address: 282/1 Phalochai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Two roosters stand guard at the entrance. Krua Samchai is famous for serving iconic Isan food befitting of the region. Fresh fish from the Mekong and Mun rivers is cooked using the chef's secret mix of herbs and spices that produces a powerful aroma. The grilled chicken has a crispy golden skin from the charcoal flame but retains its juicy meat. The Isan-style spicy fish maw and bamboo shoot soup uses tiliacora juice to perfection.

Name: Kaithong Original (Mueang Thong Thani)
Address: 164/13-15 Soi Chaeng Watthana-Pak Kret 33, Chaeng Watthana Road, Bang Phut, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run establishment is renowned for its traditional recipes, serving fresh meat and seafood flavours in simple yet refined and lightly seasoned dishes. Catering to different tastes, the stir-fried liver with garlic is made with either pork or chicken liver. The inviting, comfortable space can also accommodate larger groups.

Name: Go La
Address: 11 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: In its third generation of family ownership, this is one of Phuket’s best Hokkien-style fried noodle joints. Its charm is conjured up by a concoction of special flavours, the sounds of the wok and charcoal smells. Order the yellow hokkien noodles with an extra egg for a creamier texture.

Name: Baan
Address: 139/5 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: At this sister restaurant to Le Du, comforting family recipes take centre stage. The intimate venue boasts a contemporary look with marble tables and chic lighting. They prioritise high-quality ingredients, including beef from Pak Chong's Islamic farms and responsibly sourced seafood from southern Thailand. Pair dishes with their selection of biodynamic, organic wines and house cocktails.

Name: Beach Grill and Bar
Address: Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas, 79 Mu 3, Khuekkhak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82220, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Offering a relaxing setting with indoor and outdoor seating perfect for enjoying cocktails and a delightful mix of Mediterranean dishes, against the backdrop of the evening sunset. Specialising in fresh seafood grilled over a wood-burning stove, the restaurant's standout dish is a seafood pizza with shrimp, squid, mussels, and mozzarella. Complete your dining experience with a delicious dessert like crispy fried bananas served with coconut milk ice cream.

Name: Khrua Nong
Address: 132/8 Phet Kasem Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: The husband-and-wife team go to market every day to select fresh, local ingredients and seafood and offer a wide selection of Thai dishes. Check the blackboard for the specials which change every day, but the crispy softshell crab with a peppery chilli sauce is unmissable.

Name: Phi Sao
Description: Delicious meals have been enjoyed at P’Saw for more than 40 years. Under a whitewashed pavilion-like structure, diners can enjoy the sea breeze, a view of the beach and southern-style dishes. The recipes, passed from the restaurant’s founder to her younger sister, offer something more personal and familial than their neighbouring restaurants. The baegu leaf salad with crispy shrimp and tom yum clear soup with young coconut deliver a delightful and flavourful experience.

Name: Samchai Coffee (Thepyothi)
Address: 168/4 Thepyothi Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: The menu boasts a tasty dried shredded pork and a range of sausages. A highlight is the Indochina pan-fried egg served with a side sandwich. The eggs are cooked sunny side up with margarine, then topped with sweet and salty Chinese sausage and peppery Vietnamese sausage slices.

Name: Giglio Trattoria Fiorentina
Address: 149 Soi Sathon 12, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: A love of tradition, simplicity and authentic flavours are the guiding principles behind this Tuscan-focused restaurant from the former chefs of Bottega di Luca and Appia. The result is their version of a quintessential trattoria, serving savoury dishes like the recommended home-made pici pasta with fresh black truffle slices and fresh cream and the dry-aged sharing steak. While there’s no on-site parking, valet parking is available; and booking is essential.

Name: Baan Watcharachai
Address: 9 Ban Pom, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This family-owned restaurant offers central Thai cuisine by the side of the Chao Phraya River. Its name joins those of the family’s father, mother and son and means “house of light and victory”. Recipes have come from the owner’s grandmother, with dishes including sweet, salty and spicy fried snakehead fish with prik-king curry paste – a perfect example of the well-balanced cooking on offer. Guests can dine in the vintage house or outside on the deck or docked boat, both with views of Phra Chedi Sri Suriyothai.

Name: Terroir
Address: Acmen Complex, 13-15 Ekkamai Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: Chef Hao believes that the land, climate, and farmers are pivotal in produce quality. This belief echoes in his eatery sourcing 90% of ingredients from Northern Thailand, named meaning 'soil' in French. The restaurant delivers exceptional Franco-Japanese fusion, creatively blending two cuisines. Impressive flavour pairings, notably rich, smoky broths, shine consistently. An outstanding wine selection completes the splendid dining experience.

Name: Jaras
Address: InterContinental Phuket Resort, 333, 333/3 Mu 3, Kamala Beach, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite the luxury setting, Jaras retains honest roots. The intimate design draws influence from the Li Thai, Sukhothai era. The restaurant is named after the owner's grandma whose cooking inspired some of the recipes. Today’s chef embraces sustainability, serving a modern showcase of Thai flavours sourced locally, including microgreens grown on-site. For the full experience, request the Taste of Jaras tasting menu with wine pairing. Book at least 24 hours in advance.

Name: Khanom Jeen Mae Ploy
Address: 7/1 Mu 6, Siriratchathani Road, Muen Wai, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: The secret to Mae Ploy’s bouncy yet gooey noodles is the fermented rice flour from Ban Pra Dok. There’s a creamy, peppery spicy fish curry with coconut cream, a red chicken curry with offal, and a sweet, nutty peanut curry. The spicy fish curry has a lovely, aromatic fermented taste.

Name: Yi-Oui Noodles
Address: Behind Thai Mueang Shrine Chinese theater, Phang-Nga 3025 Rural Road, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82120, Thailand
Description: Aunty Oui has been delighting locals with the intense flavour of her noodle soups since 1971. Each table is laden with a basket of soft-boiled eggs; diners are welcome to finish as many as they can manage. The pork rib soup is a highlight and a Thai dessert rounds off the meal nicely.

Name: Clara
Address: 69 Soi Prasat Suk, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Popular among both Thai and foreign foodies and housed in a Bauhaus-style villa surrounded by sculpture-filled gardens, Clara is an elegant Italian fine-dining restaurant from a seasoned Italian chef and his wife. The villa’s two-floor interior has a warm minimalist vibe. The set menu balances flavours and complex textures which are matched by the fine service. Pair with wine for a complete experience.

Name: Favola
Address: 2F, Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, 108 Chang Khlan Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: With Favola, Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel presents authentic Italian food, including homemade pasta and ravioli from the Italian head chef, in a dining room that adds contemporary stylishness to a classic Italian restaurant ambience. Among the dishes, the Agnolotti Al Brasato and the pizza shine. Feel free to order half or smaller sizes; great for when you’re in the mood to try a few dishes. The excellent wine selection only adds to the experience.

Name: Grand Chaopraya
Address: 42/1 Ban Run, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2009, this riverside restaurant serves Thai cuisine made with local ingredients, including fish sourced from the river. The dining room features high ceilings, spiral staircases and floor-to-ceiling windows, while the terrace offers scenic views and nightly live music. The menu is packed with recipes from the owner’s mother. Her grilled river prawns and grilled fish and shrimp in pineapple curry are a must. Book ahead for an outdoor table at dinner.

Name: Rern
Address: 151/25 Soi Phahon Yothin 34, Sena Nikhom, Chatuchak, Bangkok, 10900, Thailand
Description: You are greeted by an immediate sense of tranquillity when entering this restaurant that brings Southern Thai culture and cuisine to Bangkok. Shaded by verdant trees and sat beside an emerald pool, dining here is a welcome oasis from the hustle and bustle of the city. Traditional recipes are presented with a modern touch, while local ingredients play their role in vibrant dishes that offer strong flavours and intense spicing.

Name: Go Ang Seafood
Address: 226 Mu 2, Phuket Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: From humble origins as a small shop with a zinc roof, it’s now one of the most popular seafood restaurants with a comfortable interior and Chinese décor. Chef-owner Go Ang cooks the entire southern Thai menu. The blue swimming crab, horseshoe crab and mantis shrimp are sourced daily from 5 markets. The steamed crab with tangy seafood dip and fried mantis shrimp with garlic are delightful, while the Southern Thai spicy sour soup with seabass is also a must-try.

Name: Kai Yang Sueb Siri
Address: 49 Sueb Siri Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This 50-year-old family-run business has a large cooking station at the front that radiates a welcoming smell of grilled chicken. Most customers come in big groups to share popular Isan dishes. Three varieties of tender chicken are served; the crowd favourite is their signature barbequed chicken marinated in Thai herbs. The fermented fish sauce, made daily, emits an encapsulating aroma and the papaya salad hits the perfect balance between spicy and sour.

Name: Gu Cherng
Address: 2F, Krungsri River Hotel, 27/2 Mu 11, Rochana Road, Kamang, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Gu cherng refers to the country’s former capital and the dining room, renovated in 2021, mixes elegant modern Chinese style with flashes of the traditional. Popular dishes include a variety of tasty dim-sum. The steamed prawn dumplings with seaweed and steamed rice noodles stuffed with deep-fried prawns use quality ingredients with delicately balanced flavours. The signature Peking duck pancakes use choice cuts of meat, thinly sliced, crispy and with no fat.

Name: Midwinter
Address: 88/88 Mu 10, Thanaratch Road, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30130, Thailand
Description: Sounding like something from Game of Thrones, Midwinter is a mock European castle with white bricks, set among 32 acres of rolling fields with views of Khaoyai mountains. The dining room mixes alpine and vintage designs under high ceilings. The international and Thai dishes boast farm-to-table and homegrown organic ingredients, like asparagus, greens, fruits and herbs. They produce their own dry-aged beef, smoked ham, pork leg, sausages and fresh pastries.

Name: Jay Noi Kratoke
Address: 115 Pibool La-lad Road, Nong Phai Lom, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This three-storey house with simple décor is family run and in its second generation. Jay Noi's house special of hao-dong is a popular local treat using sliced pork and spicy Isan sauce, chilli and roasted rice. The four pad mee Korat is also recommended. Its sticky rice noodles are fresh and go really well with the sweet and sour sauce, fresh bean sprouts and chives. You can order the homemade curry puff for take away, with a variety of optional sides.

Name: Tean
Address: Jumeirah at Saadiyat Island Resort, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: The first thing you’ll be tempted by will be a quick dip as you wander past the pool of the Jumeirah at Saadiyat Island Resort. The smiling service team will make you feel instantly at home, while the open kitchen prepares an assortment of Lebanese, Greek, Turkish and Middle Eastern dishes, all designed for sharing. There are excellent freshly baked breads aplenty; just be sure to order something from the charcoal grill and finish with Umm Ali.

Name: Les Dangereux
Description: One of the big openings of 2023 was this creative partnership between two chefs. There are Arabic and French influences to the food and the dishes are visually striking, sometimes playful and certainly stimulating; to get the full experience, go for the tasting menu of around 15 courses. There’s a subtle ’30s feel to the light, spacious restaurant, located on the promenade of Mamsha Al Saadiyat; it also comes with an elegant bar and a glass wall providing views into the kitchen.

Name: José by Pizarro
Address: Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Corniche Road, Abu Dhabi
Description: A small space on the ground floor of the Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel is the chosen venue for José Pizarro's first venture outside London but, instead of adopting a similarly rustic look for his tapas bar, the designers have used plenty of marble to create a more elegant environment. The small sharing plates include great anchovies, satisfying meatballs in a spicy tomato sauce and the unmissable chocolate pot.

Name: Mijana
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Al Maqta, Abu Dhabi
Description: Classical Lebanese cooking is served here against an elegant and stylish backdrop provided by the luxurious Ritz-Carlton hotel. The menu offers a comprehensive array of traditional dishes from the region, a large selection of hot and cold mezzeh, and plenty of satisfying options from the grill – the mashawee mshakaleh includes four different meats. Finish the night with a shisha pipe on the terrace.

Name: Namak
Address: Dusit Thani Hotel, Sultan Bin Zayed The First Street (Al Muroor Road), Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: A culinary voyage around India drawing on myriad influences is the draw here at this colourful restaurant within the Dusit Thani hotel. The passion of the kitchen team really comes through in the carefully prepared dishes. The lamb specialities are particularly good, whether that’s Kashmiri Rogan Josh or Kakori Reshmi Seekh. There’s plenty for vegetarians too, including sharing platters.

Name: Coya
Address: The Galleria, Four Seasons Al Maryah Island Hotel, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you like your Peruvian flavours complemented with Japanese, Chinese or Spanish influences, you’ll find you have plenty of options. Ceviche is always a great choice to begin, while the ‘Chilean sea bass rice iron pot’ is a popular signature dish. Several elegant dining rooms provide a colourful stage for the vibrant food, while the floor to ceiling windows make the most of the waterfront location. The set lunch menu is always good value.

Name: Yadoo's House
Address: Al Nasr Tower 2, Al Murror Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Sitting beneath an apartment block in the suburb of Rabdan is this likeable spot. The purpose-built white space was always going to be a challenge when it came to giving it personality, but assorted artefacts and articles like spice sacks and a sewing machine go some way towards creating the look of ‘Grandma’s house’. The Emirati cooking is done with care and respect for tradition and the portions are as big as the prices are low. We suggest starting with the katlees, followed by the majbous and save room to finish off with the luqaimat.

Name: Kopitiam by Chandy's
Address: Al Falah Street, Old Pasport Rd, Zone 1, Abu Dhabi
Description: Owner Chandy and his team runs this sweet little Malaysian restaurant with passion, politeness and professionalism - and clearly want everyone to enjoy themselves. That proves easy, thanks to the inexpensive, fresh and flavoursome dishes on the short menu that’s supplemented with a blackboard of specials; roti jala is always well worth ordering. The place is immaculately kept, with views into the equally spotless kitchen.

Name: Ray's Grill
Address: Podium Level 1, Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Thanks to the floor-to-ceiling windows and its perch on the 63rd floor, great views are a given at this smart steakhouse in the Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel. Prime cuts from American grain-fed cattle are offered alongside Australian Wagyu and the steaks are cooked on a chargrill; succulence and great flavours are guaranteed. Tartares are made at the table for a bit of theatre and there’s an assortment of other top produce too, from Atlantic lobster to whole sea bass.

Name: Zuma
Address: Abu Dhabi Global Market,  The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Gliding down the softly lit staircase allows everyone to feel like they’re about to arrive at the best party in town – this really is Fun Central, with the music to prove it. As with all other Zuma branches around the globe, the menu covers a multitude of Japanese bases, with seafood from the robata grill being the standout, although the signature corn-fed baby chicken rightly has many admirers too.

Name: Villa Toscana
Address: St. Regis Hotel, Nation Towers, Corniche, Abu Dhabi
Description: As you’d expect from the name, you can find many a classic Tuscan dish here at Villa Toscana, which sits within the St. Regis hotel on the Corniche waterfront. Familiar favourites like spaghetti alle vongole mix with plenty of pizzas and a wide range of other dishes to form a menu with something for everyone. On weekdays, they serve a good value business lunch comprising an extensive buffet of antipasti and desserts, plus a freshly cooked main course.

Name: Moksh
Address: Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Abu Dhabi
Description: Step into this bright and colourful Indian restaurant and the world will instantly seem a happier place. The menu offers a wide-ranging selection, from popular street snacks to classic favourites originating from various regions across the country. But what makes the food a little different is that the kitchen is unafraid of adding its own contemporary touches, while all the while respecting traditional flavours. We suggest starting off with the colourful chaat served in fine and crisp puris and ensure you finish with the well-presented kulfi.

Name: Li Beirut
Address: Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Abu Dhabi
Description: Its contemporary styling, views of the harbour, well-choregraphed service and good food make this Lebanese restaurant a favourite of many. The core of the menu is classic Lebanese, but the kitchen works hard here to impress, especially when it comes to presentation and the subtle addition of modern touches to some dishes. Whilst the main menu is a little more concise than many places, it is supplemented by a very useful selection of fixed price menus.

Name: Maté
Address: Park Hyatt Hotel, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park
Description: Descend the stairs to the sound of pumping music and you’ll find yourself transported to Buenos Aires at his atmospheric restaurant in the Park Hyatt Hotel. The centrepiece is the open kitchen and the flaming wood-fired grills here. The menu does have some Lebanese influence but it’s really all about Argentinian dishes with great charred flavours and top ingredients, be they prawns or beef. If you really want to feel part of the action, sit at the counter.

Name: Byblos Sur Mer
Address: Intercontinental Hotel, King Abdullah bin Abdul Aziz Al Saud Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Start your visit on the wonderful terrace and spend time admiring, or indeed coveting, the boats bobbing in the marina that it overlooks. Sharing is everything at this two-level restaurant, where the service is affable and organised. The Lebanese menu offers bags of choice – the grilled section is a good place to head to, where lamb-lovers should look no further than machawi mchakaleh. Friday and Saturday evenings see live music and entertainment.

Name: Silk & Spice
Address: Sofitel Hotel, East Corniche Road, Al Danah, Abu Dhabi
Description: In a large, contemporary space within the Sofitel hotel on the Corniche seafront sits this friendly Thai that hits all the right notes. The experienced Thai chef and his team prepare both timeless restaurant classics and dishes displaying subtle modern twists, where flavours are balanced, rewarding and authentic. A variety of à la carte and set menus mean there’s something for everyone.

Name: Café Milano
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Galleria Level 1, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Powerbrokers, movers and shakers in Washington DC will be familiar with the original Café Milano. This elegant sibling is in the Four Seasons – and if you want to be seen enjoying la dolce vita, then start with an aperitivo in the bar. The Italian chef and his team confidently prepare authentic Italian dishes; the homemade pastas are a highlight. There’s also a great terrace.

Name: Oak Room
Address: The Edition Hotel, Al Bateen Marina, Abu Dhabi
Description: Dressed like a smart London club, all wood and leather – but with the music turned up loud – Oak Room is all about meat. Steaks, largely from the USA and Australia, come in various cuts and are accompanied by a large selection of sides; don’t miss the triple cooked chips. Sunday roasts are popular and there’s a wide variety of other dishes on offer too, from fish and chips to burgers.

Name: NIRI
Address: Building 9, Mamsha Al Saadiyat, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Grab a seat at the counter of this contemporary Japanese restaurant to watch the chefs prepare your dishes over the robata grill. The ingredients are top-notch, and the kitchen is clearly motivated. The pared-back interior is very on-trend and comes complete with a sakura tree. People-watchers and anyone who enjoys a good sea view will prefer a seat on the terrace as this spot on Mamsha Al Saadiyat is hard to beat.

Name: Paradiso
Address: Yas Bay Waterfront Pier 71, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: A partnership between celebrated French chef Pierre Gagnaire and Nicole Rubi of La Petite Maison in Cannes resulted in this bright and colourful restaurant. It’s the perfect backdrop to their favoured cuisine – that of the Mediterranean, so expect everything from snails and roast poussin to fritto misto, pizza and assorted pasta dishes. The terrace overlooking the water is nicely decked out and a very pleasant spot.

Name: Cipriani
Address: Building 1, Yas Marina, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Elegance and style are hallmarks of all Cipriani restaurants and Abu Dhabi’s branch of this well-known international group occupies an appropriate glamourous position overlooking Yas Island Marina, with a beautiful terrace to make the most of the great views.  There are Japanese dishes available, but Italian is really the way to go here – and they offer all the classics, from carpaccio to cannoli.

Name: Dai Pai Dong
Address: Rosewood Abu Dhabi Hotel, Zayed the First Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Cantonese is king and sharing the thing at Rosewood’s good-looking Chinese restaurant. Whether you enjoy roasted duck, braised brisket, crispy chicken or double-boiled soups, there’s plenty for you to enjoy here, and if you prefer something a little more fiery there are Sichuan dishes too. ‘All you can eat’ dim sum features on weekday lunches; weekend brunches are hugely popular; while Wednesdays host ‘All You Can Grill’ nights.

Name: Al Farah
Address: Khalidiyah St, Al Khalidiyah, W8, Abu Dhabi
Description: The first thing you’ll notice at this bright, contemporary restaurant is a queue of people picking up their orders of manaqeesh and the fresh breads coming out of the oven. The extensive menu offers a range of flavoursome Middle Eastern dishes and it’s a popular destination for breakfast. The restaurant is right in the heart of Al Khalidiyah and is part of a group of family-owned establishments.

Name: Li Jiang
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Al Maqta, Abu Dhabi
Description: Southeast Asian dishes lead the way at this restaurant within The Ritz-Carlton hotel. All dishes are prepared with equal care – the Szechuan chilli lamb loin will certainly get your taste buds excited – but it’s the wok dishes that are their speciality. Order dishes like wok-fried scallops and butter prawns, then watch the chefs working dexterously and skilfully behind the glass screens. The friendly team run the place well and service is smooth and professional.

Name: Finz
Address: Beach Rotana Hotel, 10th Street, Al Zahiyah, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Eating seafood by the sea – there aren’t many things in life that can beat it. At Finz the fish and shellfish come in a variety of styles to suit all tastes, so if you want to feel you’re holidaying on the Med you can order fruits de mer or moules marinières, while those who prefer a more Asian theme can try the tempura roll or teriyaki salmon. The charming service is another delight here.

Name: LPM
Address: L1, The Galleria, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The history of La Petite Maison began in London in 2007, with further outposts opening around the world in the years since. Here in The Galleria, customers can judge it for themselves, with Mediterranean cuisine prepared with Niçoise touches and served by a well-trained team in elegant surroundings. Dishes like thinly sliced octopus or salt-baked sea bass will put you in a sunny mood; and be sure to leave room for the pistachio cake.

Name: Meylas
Address: Al Raha Beach, Al Muneera, Abu Dhabi
Description: It may be a little hard to find but this all-day eatery hidden away among the apartment blocks of Al Muneera Island is well worth seeking out. It began life as a food truck but now the two sisters behind it have a thriving business where their passion for their country and its food culture are clear for all to see. The chefs in the on-view kitchen prepare a menu of authentic and satisfying Emirati dishes.

Name: Punjab Grill
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Venetian Village, 3rd Street, Al Rawdah, Abu Dhabi
Description: There are Punjab Grills dotted around the world and this outpost, located in the Venetian Village, part of the sprawling acreage of the Ritz-Carlton hotel, is one of the more established branches, having opened in 2015. Ask for one of the booths and sit back and enjoy the Northern Indian specialities and the attentive service. They also have an attractive waterfront location and a terrace from which to enjoy it.

Name: Catch at St. Regis
Address: Nation Riviera Beach Club, Corniche Road, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A lovely spot on the beach provides the ideal setting for this seafood restaurant. Service is warm and quietly confident; the room is bright and spacious; and the menu wide and varied. There’s quite a Japanese influence, with plenty of nigiri and sashimi; there are also plates for sharing, and good use is made of the charcoal grill. The ‘Blow Torch Dynamite Roll’ makes for an explosive start!

Name: Grand Beirut
Address: Unit 12100-1201 (FB), Level 2, The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Adgm Square, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Under the same management as Beirut Sur Mer, this restaurant offers just the thing for refuelling after a gruelling day of shopping around Abu Dhabi. The Lebanese dishes are designed for sharing and generously sized, while proving to be full of flavour and founded upon quality ingredients. Be sure to leave room for their delicious kunafa.

Name: terra
Description: At the quieter end of Al Qana yet still with a view of the boats in the marina, sits terra – relatively new to Abu Dhabi but with a well-established branch in Dubai. Being a Mediterranean restaurant, it’s appropriately relaxed in style and the great music makes it a particularly good choice for dinner. Most of the countries that line the Med get a mention and all the classics are here, including raw dishes and pizza, starters like burrata and croquettes, and plenty of pasta dishes and meats from the Josper oven.

Name: Mazi
Address: St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort, Abu Dhabi
Description: If you have a hankering to holiday in the Greek Islands, then bring some friends here to get yourself in the mood. Mazi began life in London in 2012 and continues here at the impressive St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort, where olive and palm trees decorate the charming terrace. Flavours are traditionally Greek but modernised with smart twists, and the fresh tasting dishes are designed for sharing.

Name: Martabaan by Hemant Oberoi
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In contrast to the huge Emirates Palace hotel in which its located, this Indian restaurant occupies a surprisingly small and intimate space. Its eponymous chef has considerable experience around the world and the menu encompasses all his favourite dishes. The tasting menu is the best form of discovery. The enthusiasm of the service team is thoroughly infectious, and their recommendations are always worth heeding.

Name: Butcher & Still
Address: Four Seasons Al Maryah Island Hotel, 2 Global Market Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Those who like a classic steakhouse will find this one at the luxurious Four Seasons ticks all the boxes. Leather banquettes? Check. Prime American beef? Check. Great cocktails? Check. Start with the generously proportioned crab cake before diving into a steak – there are plenty on offer, from ribeye to porterhouse. To finish, there’s New York cheesecake of course, but the more adventurous should take on the challenge of the Tribune Tower chocolate cake.

Name: Fouquet's
Address: Louvre Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Cultural District 1, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: As befits the remarkable Louvre Abu Dhabi, its restaurant is not only one with a famous name serving classic French cuisine, but is also one decidedly grander than its ‘brasserie’ moniker would suggest. The huge, laminated menu offers something for everyone, from glazed duck breast to chicken supreme; finishing with crêpes Suzette will set you up nicely for more gallery viewings.

Name: PONTE DEL PIATTO
Description: Originality of approach is Hidenori Tadauchi’s strong suit. After being raised by parents who ran a sushi shop, he majored in Japanese cuisine, but his passion for Italian cooking and football persuaded him to travel to Italy, where he honed his modern creativity at restaurants there. Cold pasta with white-flesh fish is braced with kombu kelp, the influence of his father. Risotto of young ayu, served in early summer, imparts a Japanese sense of the seasons.

Name: L'allium
Description: The basement dining room has the air of a concert hall. The conductor, on stage in his brightly lit kitchen, is chef Yoshiaki Shindo. Modern French is the cuisine here, composed of both Japanese and French ingredients. Teppanyaki foie gras is an imaginative variation, while Japanese parsley and Okinawan spinach add a gentle bitterness to fruits and root vegetables, bringing a fresh face to old favourites.

Name: Sushi Marufuku
Description: Aged sushi prepared with originality and passion. Yutaka Isayama ages fish to bring out aroma, tenderness and flavour, favouring dry-ageing to impart a certain wildness of taste. Snacks are interspersed so as not to jade the palate with a succession of intensely flavoured sushi toppings. Aged sushi pairs well with sake, so ask the proprietress, an accomplished sake sommelier, for suggestions.

Name: Kappo Yuichi
Description: This counter-style restaurant hangs out its shingle in a corner of the roundabout in front of the north entrance to Ogikubo Station. Chef Kotaro Tachibana bases the menu around vegetables, showcasing the depth of Japanese cuisine. Takiawase highlight the ever-changing faces of nature, with colourful vegetables that cool you in summer and warm you in winter. Appetiser platters arrayed with salad with mashed tofu dressing, seasoned boiled greens and vegetables dressed with sesame sauce calm the soul still further with their savoury flavours.

Name: Sushidokoro Yamada
Description: Two brothers work in tandem like a well-oiled machine, the elder up front and the younger in the back. The menu contains just 15 items, all nigiri. To maintain complete harmony between topping and vinegared sushi rice, no snacks or ginger are offered. Most fish toppings are aged to maximize their flavour. Other toppings include rare items such as grilled shiitake mushroom and peppered Sakhalin surf clam. The brothers continually switch up the flavours in the flow of sushi.

Name: Sudachi
Description: This Japanese restaurant offers puzzles and coded menus! The puzzles rely on a coded-language tradition called goroawase, so if you know a little Japanese, they are sure to raise anticipation. Counter seating, which affords a view of the food-preparation process, adds a touch of fun as well. The eatery’s name can mean ‘leaving the nest’, and indeed the young cooks create a cheerful atmosphere. Puzzle-solving is for evenings only; lunch is traditional kaiseki, finishing with sea bream rice with green tea poured over it.

Name: Tempura Nakagawa
Description: The chef learned his tempura from a master versed in the old ways. The first tiger prawn is fried at just the right heat to bring out its aroma; the second is served rare to elicit sweetness. Conger eel is fragrantly fried with minimum sesame oil. Nakagawa’s trademark theory is that ‘tempura is a process of drying-out’, by which he means ingredients are steamed and grilled in their batter to remove moisture, bringing their flavour to the fore.

Name: IL GiOTTO
Description: In this white-walled detached house facing Komazawa-Koen Avenue, with its cosy, wood-lined interior, sounds of food preparation from the open kitchen, and the atmosphere of a shop run by a couple, guests feel invited into a home. Chef Naofumi Takahashi specializes in meat dishes, such as bruschetta with home-cured ham and simmered tripe. He takes special pride in his slow-aged, char-grilled meats. Beef, aged to enhance umami, is seasoned with salt and pepper.

Name: Bistro YEBISU
Description: The key to happiness here is the blackboard menu. Sea urchin with new onions, whitebait quiche, veal cutlets and other offerings are chalked simply on the board. The chef is a fount of knowledge; ask about the fare and conversation flows, heightening anticipation of the meal to come. The bistro is run by a couple whose concept is a restaurant that makes people happy. Spend a warm and comfortable time in this casual scene.

Name: PATH
Description: This casual restaurant is the brainchild of a chef and a pâtissier. Dinner is mostly prix fixe, fusing Japanese ingredients with fermented foods as well as spices from various countries. Catering to the local lifestyle, Path offers a selection of organic wines and is open from morning onwards. Music of no particular genre streams through the vintage interior themed on street culture.

Name: Clos Des Gourmets
Description: In his primary school graduation yearbook, the future chef wrote, “I want to be a chef”. He studied gastronomy in Paris, developing his most intimate relationships with a restaurant in the 7th arrondissement. The chef’s culinary philosophy, his restaurant’s name and his signature cuisine are all inherited from his mentor. One representative dish is tête de cochon, grilled cuts from a pig’s head. In this intimate eatery, guests are in close proximity with the chef, as if invited by a friend.

Name: Sushi Rinda
Description: The unconventional restaurant name is in honour of the owner-chef’s daughter; probe further, and you find that Rinda is also the name of a song by the chef’s favourite rock band. With such rock-star inspirations, it’s no wonder that the young cooks are such a blur of motion. The fatty flesh of tuna is sliced thin and piled high before the sushi is moulded so the fat will melt faster. ‘Rindamaki’ is a sumptuous roll sushi of tuna, sea urchin and salmon roe. The lively enthusiasm of the restaurant’s team is sure to lift your spirits.

Name: malca
Description: The painting of a wave and the ornamental terra cotta plates are blue like the sea. Awaji Island, where Chef Tsukasa Kitano grew up, is never far from his mind. He named his restaurant after his grandfather’s old fishmonger’s shop and takes pride in the seafood and Awaji beef that arrives regularly from his home region. All items are served à la carte, as Kitano wants guests to be able to enjoy exactly the food they like. Non-Italian is also available, reinforcing this message of freedom.

Name: TACOS BAR
Description: ‘Tacos that could only be made in Japan’, prepared by a chef born from Mexico. Impressed by the fish he dined on during his studies in Japan, chef Marco Garcia incorporated it into the cuisine of his motherland. Sashimi, shioyaki, fried foods—these and more are reimagined in diverse ways to suit a tortilla. Tortillas are made from Mexican corn to get close as possible to the authentic flavour. Garcia’s idea of Mexican and Japanese seafoods interacting with each other opens a world of interesting possibilities.

Name: Shintomicho Yuasa
Description: The character for ‘food’ (食) is composed of the components for ‘person’ (人) and ‘good’ (良), signifying the power of food to make a person good. Daisuke Yuasa, who puts great store by the principles of a balanced diet and good food for good health, creates dishes he hopes will support his patrons’ health in both body and soul. Another of his wishes is that food should be fun, so he gained a sommelier qualification to help customers expand their enjoyment.

Name: Akasaka Watanabe
Description: Dressed in white and sporting a bow tie, Yujiro Watanabe greets his guests with a smile. His spirit of graceful service is ‘delicious, fun and welcoming’. Sesame ground in a large bowl, karasumi (salted and dried grey mullet roe) shaved before customers’ eyes and the staging of the kitchen are three shared moments. Rice from Niigata, produced by his sister and her husband, is used. Sea bream chazuke (green tea poured over rice) is a legacy from his mentor. The gratitude is palpable, the conversation lively.

Name: unique
Description: Fine dining in a casual setting and price range is the concept. Masaaki Nakai interprets the classics to conjure a cuisine that is unique, hence the restaurant’s name. Stately presentations such as smoked terrine of foie gras and orange-fleshed yam or Asian black bear grilled in pie crust argue the case persuasively. Game such as fowl and rabbit are a seasonal speciality. Enjoy à la carte with a well-aged wine.

Name: Sakuragi
Description: What Izuru Sakuragi prizes is the deliciousness born of freshness. Soup stock is made with dried bonito flakes shaved in front of the guests. Some items are toasted over straw, others grilled over charcoal, at the chef’s discretion. Freshly cooked rice is served steaming, with accompaniments chosen for contrast in flavour. The thoughtful timeliness with which Sakuragi asks if guests would like seconds is a welcome touch. The chef’s character and passion shine in his cuisine.

Name: Hotel's
Description: The concept is the restaurant of an imaginary hotel. The lunch menu is casual, offering a variety of items such as pancakes and salad sets. Dinner, however, presents only the omakase set meal that includes pasta, risotto, and burgers, all crafted with a creative flair transcending traditional genres. The wagyu beef and lamb are grilled over a wood fire, imparting a deliciously savoury flavour. For an immersive experience, sit at the counter where you can watch the flames flicker and enjoy the enticing aroma of the wood-fired grill.

Name: Yakitori Hinata
Description: The owner-chef is passionate about the locally raised chicken of the Tamba-Sasayama region. The concept of yakitori with wine suggests some intriguing pairings; particularly compatible with wine are seared chicken breast dusted with salt from Guérande and liver brushed with balsamic sauce. The appetiser is chicken-liver pâté. The restaurant’s name hearkens back to the names of areas and relatives with whom the couple shares a bond; it connotes a ray of sunshine on a Kurayamizaka, which translates to ‘darkness hill.’

Name: BVLGARI IL RISTORANTE LUCA FANTIN
Description: Luca Fantin is a seeker after Japanese ingredients. He finds ones that bring forth his creativity and interprets them according to his Italian roots. Sea urchin pasta, entwined in a seafood sauce, expresses the bounty of the ocean. The panache of the service staff as they ladle out sauces and soups, desserts arriving on wagons: all are exuberant in presentation. Refined cuisine, gracious service and harmonious interior are all steeped in the elegance of BVLGARI.

Name: Ristorante ACQUA PAZZA
Address: 2F, Passage Aoyama, 2-27-18 Minamiaoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 107-0062, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Yoshimi Hidaka has broadened the horizons of Neapolitan hometown cooking. Acqua pazza, the poached white fish dish that so thrilled him in Naples, is both the restaurant’s name and its signature dish. Prepared by fishermen, it began as fish and tomatoes simmered in seawater but here freshwater is used and Manila clams are added for saltiness. The synergy of umami from inosinic acid in the fish, glutamic acid in the tomato and succinic acid in the Manila clams is classic Yoshimi Hidaka ingenuity.

Name: Tsurutokame
Description: The name means ‘crane and turtle’ and derives from a Japanese folktale in which a crane from the wider world (the guest) befriends a turtle in a pond (the chefs). It reflects the ladies’ desire to spread Japanese culture through Japanese cuisine, so appetiser platters are arranged like the decorations of traditional events. The gracious service puts you immediately at ease. The crane and turtle are a symbol of good fortune. At birthday parties, happiness is sure to descend on your table.

Name: MATSUKI
Description: The husband-and-wife team of chefs make you feel at home. Inspired by life in the south of France, the couple strive to recreate the unpretentious flavours of the countryside. Vegetable soup, fragrant with basil, encapsulates the memories of both chefs. With onion tarts, stewed beef à la Provençal and couscous, visions of everyday life in France float before your eyes. Accompany your meal with one of their select organic wines.

Name: eman
Description: Satoru Kobayashi expresses his connections with the seasons and food producers of Japan through the medium of Spanish hometown cooking. A speciality is rice cuisine. Clams on rice, a Basque dish, is done in a Fukagawa-meshi style (asari clam miso soup over rice). For the squid-ink paella, firefly squid are used. Familiar Japanese rice is harmonized with the styles of each region. The sheer variety of the menu, encompassing tapas, char-grilled dishes and more, testifies to the depth and richness of Spanish cuisine.

Name: Sushi Kanesho
Description: Akira Watanabe inherited old-school sushi traditions but learned from his mentor the spirit of adding his own novel spin. Vinegared sushi rice is regarded as the most important component of great sushi, and Watanabe’s evolved over time through trial and error. The chef displays judgment and skill as he serves gizzard shad first, and his simmered conger eel and kurakake egg (egg straddling the rice like a saddle) reflect his personality. He confides that he tries to ‘investigate the old and understand the new’.

Name: Yakitori Takahashi
Description: A man of few words, the chef fixes his attention on his grill. He focuses on every detail of yakitori—the state of the charcoal, how the skewers are assembled and grilled—pursuing the subtleties of a cuisine. His favoured type of chicken is game fowl, prized for its supple texture and rich flavour. It is seasoned with a salt base and modulated with added chicken fat or vinegar, then wreathed in smoke as it cooks on the grill. Skewers are interspersed with chicken-based snacks such as cold chicken breast and mincemeat potato salad. A procession of dishes of lively originality.

Name: Sushi Ichigo
Description: ‘Ichigo’ means ‘ranking in the top class’, proclaiming the chef’s ambition to stand among the top ranks of chefs. The menu proceeds from drinking snacks to grilled items and steamed dishes, then finally to sushi. Sushi rice is cooked in a broad-brimmed pot at high heat to permeate the rice with the red vinegar; this emphasises the rice grains while drawing out the flavour of the toppings. As he forms his sushi by hand, he engages earnestly with the guests lining the counter.

Name: Oryori Horiuchi
Description: The starting point for Mrs. Sayaka Horiuchi is her early life lived amid natural beauty. Considering that ‘the mountains water the village and feed the ocean,’ the dishes are prepared with a spirit of gratitude for ingredients from land and sea. Horiuchi nurtures relations with food producers nationwide who share her vision. Local vegetables are from farmers in Nerima, clams from fishermen in Kyoto. Her famous chicken offal stew is home cooking from her native Yamanashi Prefecture.

Name: caillou
Description: The carefully selected fare borrows ideas from the local markets of France. The style here is to confer with the chef before you order, perusing the showcase full of ingredients in front of the kitchen. Simple French items dominate, such as smoked salmon, pâté en croûte, fish du jour, pig’s feet, cured beef and vanilla ice cream. Pointing and choosing adds to the fun, and dishes are prepared in the quantity you prefer.

Name: Oryori Ichiho
Description: The name is a play on ‘ho’, which could mean ‘step’, as in ‘stepping forward’ or ‘bounty, prosperity’, reflecting chef Ryusuke Yamazaki’s desire that his restaurant blossom and prosper. The soup stock gets its umami from kombu, with a light flavour reflecting his Kyoto experience. Dishes such as fish steamed with grated turnip on top and dumplings made from bamboo-shoot derive from ages past, recounting the culinary culture of the ancient capital. Pike conger in summer and eddoes in winter are eagerly awaited.

Name: Takumi Sushi Owana
Description: Kenji Oana and his fellow artisans work with practiced synchrony, alternating servings of nigiri and drinking snacks. Rice is seasoned with either red or white vinegar; sushi of tuna and pickled daikon radish is shaped like o-hagi (rice cakes coated with sweet red bean paste), a legacy inherited from his mentor along with the shop’s name. Snacks are delightfully inventive: baked and steeped barracuda and eggplant, for example, or conger eel grilled with Saikyo miso. Never knowing what to expect accentuates the fun.

Name: Maeshiba Ryoriten
Description: The speciality is charcoal-grilled beef and sauce only. On this, the French cuisine of Taira Maeshiba is focused. Ingredients whose producers are listed by name, finely disciplined flame-tending techniques, and traditional yet distinctive sauces combine to form menus only Chef Maeshiba could compose. The fare is simple, the work meticulous.

Name: Uisane
Description: What Kohei Ikeda tries to do is mix freewheeling imagination into traditional fare, an approach taught by the head of Kikunoi during his apprenticeship there. Fine examples include sea urchin wrapped in sea bream and spring rolls of glass shrimp. He focuses on ingredients from his native Ehime, the better to share its wonders with the world. Born and raised in Uwajima, Ikeda dreamed of becoming a chef in his youth. He never forgets to carry out this ‘original intention’, a phrase reflected in the name of the restaurant.

Name: Tinc gana
Description: To convey the gastronomy of contemporary Spain, the chef adopted the concept of Barcelona's local cuisine with a modern sensibility. Pan con tomate is just one Catalan tradition. All ingredients are painstakingly selected to whet the appetite with their lightness. The restaurant’s name means ‘I’m hungry’ in Catalan.

Name: ETHICA
Description: The chef studied in Mexico to learn about a culture that had been evolving for millennia. Based on the natural and spiritual features he sensed there, he created recipes to bring to mind local ingredients and culinary methods. The ‘three jewels’ of Mexican cuisine are maize, beans and chilli peppers. Combining this trio with Japanese ingredients is Ethica’s speciality. Out of concern for the environment and society, the chef aims to minimize food loss at his restaurant.

Name: Ichiu
Description: A door of cedar bark, roof tiles for a nameplate, and a rope curtain with the same diagonals as the ceiling. ‘Ichiu’ means ‘under one roof’, and the ceiling is shaped like a roof to emphasise this point. The menu is faithful to the spirit of Chef Koichi Hamano, a man experienced in Japanese cuisine, particularly sushi. The evening begins with a cup of sake; soup and fried dishes are then served. After the sushi, takikomi gohan - rice with a variety of ingredients concludes the meal.

Name: Nogizaka yui
Description: The chef is passionate about ‘the ties that bind’. He chose the name ‘yui’, meaning ‘ties’ or ‘connections’, to mark his restaurant as a place that links guests with food producers; people with people. The gracious service by the warm-hearted proprietress also conveys that spirit. Cuisine based on Sichuan traditions combines with vegetables delivered directly from farms. Nogizaka yui connects with Japan’s seasons as well, evidenced by sour soup of bamboo shoots and beef in spring and soy-sauce stir fry of organic maitake mushrooms in autumn. Seasoning is restrained to place ingredients centre stage.

Name: D'êtraison
Description: This bistro by Kosuke Mita benefits from the chef’s wealth of experience in gastronomy. He delicately tailors his cuisine, adding unique touches. The sauté of shrimp and scallop is curry-flavoured, for example, and beef cheek is offered as a confit. The risotto of Carnaroli rice from Ishikawa Prefecture is a distinctive detail. Mita and his sommelier focus on pairings. The wordless understanding between Mita and his wife make their marriage, and the restaurant, a success.

Name: songbook
Description: The fire used for cooking is a flickering flame of kindling inside a stove. The chef focuses on the heating power and convection heat of the embers to elicit the desired flavours. Vegetables sent direct from farm and chicken and beef are grilled uncut to cover them with smoky aroma. Western music piped through the chic interior is selected by the chef, a former musician. Artful arrangement of cuisine, interior and music creates a welcoming time and space.

Name: YAUMAY
Address: 2F, Nijubashi Square, 3-2-3 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 100-0005, Japan
Description: A specialist in dim sum, popular in cities around the world. The red exterior belies the classic dining experience within, which is lively on every visit. Enjoy the culture of dim sum with Chinese tea to your heart’s content. The full complement of authentic dishes includes jasmine-smoked pork, steamed scallop siu mai dumplings, steamed shrimp gyoza dumplings and rice-noodle rolls wrapped in fried tofu skin. If the weather’s nice, taking in the local ambience on the terrace is recommended.

Name: Hibinoryori Viola
Description: A mother-daughter team opened this restaurant out of a desire to spread Japanese culinary culture. The chef and author of the menu is the mother, herself the daughter of the head of a tea ceremony school. The guiding principle is to base the fare on daily Japanese home cooking. Soup stock is drawn with painstaking care from select seasonal ingredients. The salad of cooked vegetables in season is generously portioned, while steaming fresh-cooked rice is served with Japanese comfort food. Home-style fare infused with the spirit of kaiseki.

Name: Ishibashi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Shoes must be removed
Description: Ishibashi began as a butcher shop in the early Meiji period. The owners also kept a sukiyaki shop next door, and this restaurant has passed down its original flavours through the generations. The fifth-generation owner-chef chooses wagyu beef by its marbling and the quality of the red meat. Seating is tatami-mat only; cooking is done exclusively by one hostess. In a unique touch, the meal ends with ojiya (flavoured rice gruel) made with fluffy eggs. The old-fashioned atmosphere adds to the flavour.

Name: COMME À LA MAISON
Description: Yuji Wakui faithfully recreates the cuisine of southwestern France, taught to him by a chef from Landes. From pâté de campagne to terrine de foie gras and duck confit, all are prepared with heartfelt affection. But Wakui reserves a special fondness for soupe de garbure, a simmered mélange of ham, duck, white kidney beans and other ingredients that spreads the flavours of Landes to a ready audience in Tokyo. Unwavering faithfulness to tradition wordlessly expresses Wakui’s gratitude to his mentor.

Name: ÉTAPE
Description: A casual French affair near Komagata Bridge over the Sumida River. Keen to develop a rapport with the surrounding old neighbourhoods, Chef Shinji Kawamura installed a counter so that he could converse with his guests. Focus is on à la carte dishes that can be ordered without fuss. The Uni Pain Perdu is sea urchin with French toast. Bouillabaisse is paired with chorizo. On weekends and holidays, lunch is limited to set menus only.

Name: REQUINQUER
Description: Soichi Furuya seeks out the attractions and possibilities of French cuisine while staying in touch with current trends. Terrine de foie gras is a speciality that keeps customers coming back. Soups and crepes made using vegetables that don’t meet JA size regulations support farmers. The various set menus focused on the unique traits of Japanese-French fusion cuisine excite diners. The restaurant’s name means ‘be of good cheer’, and indeed REQUINQUER invigorates diners and food producers alike.

Name: UNE PINCÉE
Description: Gelée of vegetable mousse and consommé is a much-requested dish. The ingredients vary with the season—white asparagus in spring, corn in summer, butternut squash in autumn, Jerusalem artichoke in winter—and are prepared with a light touch. Vegetables arrive from the chef’s parents in Ibaraki Prefecture. For the main course, pastry-wrapped pigeon or quail is a longstanding favourite. The number of dishes, arranged in a modern style, and the portions are adjusted to preference.

Name: Cosi Com'ē
Description: The concept here is ‘a diner where you can enjoy organic wine’. The chef decides what to make based on seasonal ingredients at hand, so the menu changes daily. Something is different each time you visit, which keeps you coming back. Dishes such as Pasta Alla Genovese with celery and basil, or Arrabbiata of beef small intestine and smoked cheese are the works of a chef who creates as he pleases. The relaxed cuisine and organic wine resonate with each other.

Name: Neki
Description: A casual French restaurant with deep roots in Nihombashikabutocho. The interior is festooned with wine bottles and album covers; genre-less music plays in the background. The chef likes a French-based yet free-styled approach to cuisine. Partial to Japanese ingredients and fermented vegetables, he wields Middle Eastern spices with skill. Modern cuisine pairs well with organic wines.

Name: Valinor
Description: The chef aims for nothing less than unforgettable cuisine. His ingredients are the stars of his show, and to place them at centre stage, each dish uses as few as possible. While adding twists to texture and flavour, he leaves a vivid impression of each ingredient. Only those dishes that keep being made, keep being eaten, can be called classics. He puts his stamp on his food through simplifying the complexities of French cuisine.

Name: Tempura Otsuka
Description: The owner-chef, born and raised in Iriya, is an artisan through and through. Proceedings are by the book, starting with milder flavours like tiger prawn, squid and sillago before proceeding to bolder tastes. Edomae toppings are favoured, such as tidepool gunnel and big-eyed flathead. Decorating the walls are senshagaku, wooden tablets typically posted on the pillars of shrines, inscribed with local supporters’ names. The characters suffuse the restaurant with the atmosphere of old neighbourhoods.

Name: Tempura Shimomura
Description: The menu is extensive to cater to diners’ tastes but has strong regional roots. Fish and vegetables are fried in alternation, with the accent on shrimp, sillago and conger eel. Recently, few tempura places offer tendon only, but here, tendon of vegetable tempura and kakiage (all-in-one seafood and vegetable tempura blend) are available at lunchtime. Feel free to add seafood items to the vegetable set menu. Woodblock prints and an icebox vaguely recreate the atmosphere of working-class Edo.

Name: Akebonobashi Kazu
Description: In search of cuisine that only his native country could conceive, the chef devoted himself to the path of Japanese cuisine. The menu observes the basics of kaiseki while imparting creative flourishes. Wanmono include items with fishcake that complements the broth. Fish in season is salted and grilled over charcoal. Takikomi-gohan, served at the end of the meal, is attuned to the seasons as well. He prizes simplicity yet spares neither ingenuity nor attention to detail.

Name: Wakiya Ichiemicharo
Description: The flagship restaurant of Yuji Wakiya, renowned pioneer of nouvelle chinois cuisine. With “tradition and creativity” as his motto, Wakiya professes a new style of Chinese cooking. The starter, ‘Nine Joys Assorted Appetiser’, is so named because nine is a number believed to bring good luck in China. The restaurant name means ‘once a day, let’s relax, laugh and have tea’. Cuisine and hospitality to bring a smile to your face.

Name: Meguro Sushi Taichi
Description: Having hung out his shingle in his hometown, Taichi Tamura runs his sushi restaurant with his wife. This is a place to enjoy sushi prepared by a master in a family-oriented setting. Dishes alternate between snacks and nigiri, as he varies the presentation of items. The sushi rice is prepared with rice vinegar, to bring the sweetness of the seafood. Chub mackerel sushi paired with strips of seasoned and dried shio kombu kelp and rolled eggs matched with sea lettuce are distinctive touches.

Name: LUGDUNUM Bouchon Lyonnais
Description: This ‘Little Lyons’ down a Kagurazaka alley entertains guests with the regional cuisine chef Christophe Paucod remembers from his hometown. The famed quenelle is paired with buttered rice in the style of a doria. Homemade sausages are used in miniature hamburgers. The interior, a faithful recreation of Bouchon, a Lyons restaurant, wraps guests in the warm feeling of travelling in France.

Name: Shokudo Uyuki
Description: The characters for dining hall can be read as ‘jikido’ in Buddhist terminology – a hall where monks take their meals. Yuki Kanazawa chose the name because he aspires to offer respite that soothes people’s souls through cuisine. He eschews luxurious ingredients and sprinkles his menu with simple fare such as o-hitashi (a boiled vegetable side dish) and aemono (a salad of cooked vegetables). Running his restaurant alone, the chef is never far from his customers. Good-humoured service stimulates lively conversation.

Name: KOKYU
Description: A ‘food laboratory’ housed in a small, renovated warehouse. Only creative cuisine, fragrant with spices and suffused with the umami of tea, for pairing with cocktails is offered. Recipes take their inspiration from French cuisine and the restaurant’s name, which means ‘wither and decay’, is from the desire to breathe deeply of love for old cuisine before creating the new. Enjoy the fruits of experimentation in cooking and beverages.

Name: Héritage by Kei Kobayashi
Address: 45F, The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo 9-7-1 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 107-6245, Japan
Description: ‘Héritage by Kei Kobayashi’ is not just a name: The chef has made it his mission to honour and give thanks to the French culinary culture and pass it on to future generations through his eponymous restaurant. Venerable standards such as pâté en croûte, roast dovelet and vacherin are prepared in the traditional way but given a modern arrangement. Homage to the classics and the hospitality of the hotel combine to open new horizons in gastronomy.

Name: MIMOSA
Description: The counter seats are a uniform white, creating a sense of presence, and the sight of cooking right in front of you is reassuring. Amid the sounds and aromas of stir-frying in woks, the chef sometimes makes conversation with guests while plating their meals. Based on Shanghai cuisine, the dishes are set in front of you as soon as they are cooked. The restaurant’s name was chosen for the chef’s grandmother’s favourite flower. This is food created with loving thoughts of Grandma.

Name: Ginza Adachi Naoto
Description: This restaurant values traditional techniques honed at a ryotei. The painstakingly prepared appetisers are a must-try. Seasonal iimushi, mochi rice topped with fish and steamed, is served as an amuse-bouche, paired with seasonal tastes such as sea urchin, salmon roe and chestnut. Instead of rice, the meal closes with konnyaku soba (devil’s-tongue noodles), to relieve uncomfortable fullness after the meal. Meticulous food preparation eloquently conveys the spirit and feeling of the owner-chef.

Name: APICIUS
Description: The name is a tribute to an epicure of ancient Rome. Masterpieces by Maurice Utrillo and Bernard Buffet decorate the art nouveau interior, creating the atmosphere of a salon. A particularly recommended menu item is the mousse of sea urchin, caviar and vegetables, a speciality handed down from the restaurant’s first chef. Interior, cuisine, wine, service: the quintessential elements of a great restaurant are here in abundance.

Name: PRIMO PASSO
Description: The name ‘Primo Passo’ means ‘first step’. The chef was in charge of pasta at the celebrated Quattro Passi restaurant in Naples before taking his first step towards independence in Shintomicho. His aim is to create ‘Italian cuisine with a Japanese twist’. He uses plenty of dashi and Japanese ingredients. Also incorporating Japanese elements are the coffered ceiling, mud walls and vertically written menu. He serves several small dishes featuring his speciality pasta to showcase a variety of flavours.

Name: Toki
Description: The chef works alone in this tiny restaurant. At lunchtime the predominant theme is noodle dishes, such as dandan noodles and hot-and-sour ramen. In the evening, both à la carte and set menu dining are available. Be sure to order the appetiser platter, as it’s packed with variety and the time and effort taken to prepare it are apparent. The spring rolls, a finger food, are also recommended. The ‘Yellow Mapo Tofu with Seafood’ intrigues with its unusual name and distinctive yellow colour.

Name: Tanakada Nishiazabuten
Description: From the Rosanjin crockery to the retro Showa-era coasters, Tadaaki Tanaka’s restaurant is an interplay between authenticity and playfulness. The comments on the menu are easy to understand, enticing with delicious descriptions. When the chef exclaims “Tabetenshai!” meaning “let’s eat” in the Hakata dialect, it makes you want to eat what you like, as much as you like. The courteous staff of this high-grade izakaya, a step above a kappo but not quite a ryotei, ensure you’ll enjoy your visit.

Name: Lyla
Description: Like the restaurant’s name, the cuisine is born of the sensibility of poetry, a work of modern art. Meals begin with contemporary appetisers before proceeding to classic fare. In the presentation, great attention is paid to crockery shapes and colours. Sauces for fish and meat dishes are prepared with wine pairings in mind; flavours are calculated to impart a certain sourness. The infused fruit juice sourced from Oita proclaim the chef’s birthplace.

Name: RISTORANTE Al Porto
Description: Mamoru Kataoka is a pioneer who has broadened the appeal of Italian gastronomy in Japan. His passion for seafood stems was inspired by the seafood restaurants he encountered on a visit to Milan in the 1960s. Al Porto’s famous pasta is a seafood ragù prepared with lashings of clams and shrimp. Kataoka manages the kitchen and restaurant with his son. When time allows, father and son circulate among the tables, ever mindful of the importance of graceful service.

Name: Shunka Nakamura
Description: Relentless curiosity is the driving force of this chef. After going to Hong Kong to study Cantonese cuisine, he then worked at a kappo to learn about Japanese food. He calls the marriage of these two shunka, which roughly translates as ‘Chinese food with a seasonal sensibility’. Spring rolls of pike conger or conger eel are one example. The steamed chicken is a secret recipe passed on from his Hong Kong mentor. He presents the home-cooked flavours that Hongkongers love.

Name: ALADDIN
Description: Inspired by leading figures in the French culinary world, the chef burnished his skills under the supervision of masters. When the restaurant passed into his hands, he preserved the cuisine beloved by ALADDIN diners for many years. Quail stuffed with wild rice is a speciality with a pungent curry aroma. Many guests wait eagerly for the winter game offerings, such as mallard and turtle dove. The chef respects the classics, indulging in rich sauces.

Name: Fugu Club miyawaki Bettei
Description: Takashi Miyawaki is taking fugu (blowfish) cuisine to a new level. Thick-cut sashimi is dressed with caviar and olive oil; skin and milt become spring rolls. While the fare is strictly Japanese, Western ingredients and oils are added to good effect. Even pots of stew are served individually, for a special twist. Prices are set quite reasonably to ensure people see fugu as accessible. Now a much-loved dish especially on celebratory occasions, fugu brings happiness through eating.

Name: Kiyosumi Takahara
Description: Kyoto cuisine has left its mark on chef Shimon Takahara. Like his father before him, he apprenticed as a chef in Kyoto, devoting himself to his gastronomical studies. Guided by the teachings of his mentor, Takahara dedicates his heart and soul to creating dishes that offer a sense of the seasons and reverberate in the senses. Each day’s appetiser, prepared from what is most seasonal, shows this devotion. In spring, expect dishes laden with the colours and aromas of daily variations such as bamboo shoots and asparagus.

Name: Sushi Kobayashi
Description: Guests are greeted in Edo dialect with a hearty “Irasshaimashi”. A short shop curtain hangs under a market-stall roof, lending the shop an Edo-era food-stall ambience. Expect steaming hot towels, piping hot tea and gracious service. Influenced by two mentors, the owner-chef prepares fish patiently in the time-honoured way and uses red vinegar to form rice portions. His aim is to be his patrons’ every-day sushi stop. An old-school, no-nonsense sushi shop in both appearance and demeanour.

Name: Benoit
Address: 10F, La Porte Aoyama, 5-51-8 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 150-0001, Japan
Description: The Tokyo outpost of Benoit, which was founded in Paris in 1912. The cuisine of this bistro that co-stars French and Japanese influences is overseen by Alain Ducasse. The menu is prix fixe, but diners can choose items to their liking. Dishes bequeathed by the Paris flagship, such as oven-baked escargot and terrine, stand alongside regional fare made with ingredients from across Japan. Antique-accented décor and attentive service convey an unmistakeably French esprit.

Name: Arakicho Kintsugi
Description: An intimate Japanese restaurant that fits well among the string of watering holes in the Arakicho area of Shinjuku. The two who run it are experts in cuisine and sake. Set menus are plotted with the tastes of sake drinkers in mind. One piece at a time, in small quantities, is an enjoyable way to dine. As the sake flows, boiled greens, sushi, fried items and other items are served with varying degrees of preparation and temperature. A seasonal selection of steamed items on rice ends the meal.

Name: Arva
Address: 33F, Aman Tokyo, The Otemachi Tower, 1-5-6 Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 100-0004, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Masakazu Hiraki’s aim is to create Italian dishes showcasing the appeal of Japanese ingredients. His work is a cross-fertilization of the knowledge of Japanese farmers with his own experience in Italy, particularly in the Veneto region. Vegetables and fruit bring lively colour to simple, modern fare. His devotion to the good things of the earth manifests in his restaurant’s name, which means ‘harvest’. The stunning view from his dining room atop a 33-floor building adds to the feeling of spaciousness.

Name: LA BONNE TABLE
Address: 1F, Coredo Muromachi2, 2-3-1 Nihombashimuromachi, Chuo-ku, Tokyo, 103-0022, Japan
Description: LA BONNE TABLE lives by the motto ‘farm to table’. Chef Kazunari Nakamura builds strong relationships of trust with food producers, who ship ingredients to him directly from their farms. An amuse-bouche, appropriately named ‘Farm to Table’, is a colourful assortment of vegetables prepared in a variety of ways. Roast shiitake wastes no part of the mushroom, not even the stem. The chef’s ingenuity and creativity bring out the value of his ingredients.

Name: LE BOURGUIGNON
Description: Evoking Burgundy, the name of the restaurant comes from the owner-chef being inspired by the passion of the restauranteur and wine producer where he trained, an influence also evident in the rich selection of wines from Burgundy. His specialities include boudin noir with apple salad and purée, and millefeuille-style horse crab, eggplant and avocado. He also does wild game and offal well.

Name: Tempura Asanuma
Description: Fascination with Edo culinary culture led this chef to open a restaurant in Nihombashi. Knowing that Edokko (natives of Tokyo) would eat thick-battered tempura soaked in sauce, the chef uses the technique completely opposite to the thin coating he learned as an apprentice. But the thicker coating traps air bubbles, imparting a fragrant nose and light texture. In an homage to the port of call where tempura arrived from Portugal, the fried feast begins with shrimp toast, a speciality of Nagasaki.

Name: Tsumakoizaka Keigo
Description: Keigo Abe’s individuality sparkles in this omakase set meal emporium of tempura, soba buckwheat noodles and other dishes. The meal begins with seasonal fare before progressing to tempura fried in Taihaku untoasted sesame oil then to handmade 100% soba noodles and thin noodles, both served chilled. Abe proudly uses noted products of his native Akita. The attentive proprietress supports the shop with graceful service. Tsumakoi means ‘loving couple’: a fitting name.

Name: HYÈNE
Description: Expect creative fare fusing Japanese, Korean and French culinary culture. A perfect reflection of Chef Yoko Kimoto’s life, as she carries both Japanese and Korean DNA and is schooled in French cuisine. Her speciality, potato fondant au chocolat, overlays a French dessert onto a Korean rice-cake snack her mother used to make her when she was little. Imbuing Japanese ingredients with Korean flavours using French techniques, Kimoto conjures a gastronomy that is all her own.

Name: Sushi Taichi
Description: This restaurant loves the chic style of Edo culture and values the human touch. Many sushi shops these days offer two time-limited seatings, serving only omakase set meals. However, Sushi Taichi shows the mettle of an old-fashioned sushi chef. The owner-chef’s agreeable disposition ensures him many regular customers. Above the counter is a shop curtain, while the walls feature woodblock prints depicting street stalls. If you like old-school sushi shops, Sushi Taichi is for you.

Name: Asakusa Nagami
Description: Asakusa is the stage on which chef Takumi Nagami performs. Staying faithful to the native flavours of his ingredients, he brings to bear the seasonal elegance he learned in Kyoto. Soup stock is lightly seasoned so as not to overpower the main ingredients. Two options are available for appetiser platters: drinking snacks adorned with leaves or served in hollowed-out yuzu fruits. The kaminari-okoshi sweet rice puff snack is used as batter for fried items, in a tip of the hat to the chef’s beloved Asakusa.

Name: nerisa
Description: Tonnato of veal, hand-rolled tajarin pasta, agnolotti: Chef's experience with the cuisine of Piedmont is everywhere on display. He stays faithful to the recipes he learned, because he wants guests to know the taste of true Piemontese cuisine, but he links Italy to Japan by incorporating local ingredients. The accent in cooking is on simplicity and his personality shines in his line-up of ingredient-focused fare.

Name: L’éclaireur
Description: Ichiei Taguma was taught that a great chef is one who creates a new culinary culture. He tinkered and tested throughout his apprenticeship, honing his creativity, an experience that led him to where he is today. When he became independent, Taguma decided to focus on wood-fired cooking. Smoking by skilful tending of flame is the key to his presentation of creative French cuisine.

Name: Kappo Ryu
