This busy eatery, occupying an iconic pink building dating back to 1885, is now run by the owner of the Don Julio parrilla, just one block away, and has retained its bygone character (period floors, mirrors, colourful jars of pickles etc) following heavy restoration, while at the same time updating its cuisine with an à la carte that respects the Buenos Aires DNA of this former warehouse. You can’t leave without trying the famous sirloin milanesa, which is striking for the quality of the meat, which is tender and fried almost without any oil, and the sweetness of the accompanying tomato salsa. The menu also features a large selection of artisanal charcuterie: Chacarero salami, spianata, bondiola, pancetta etc. The organic vegetables used are grown by the restaurant itself, and include unique varieties such as heirloom tomatoes.

Name: Riccitelli Bistró
Address: Callejón de La Reta 750, Mendoza, M5509, Argentina
Description: At the Riccitelli Bistró, they have gone one step further to bring together fine cuisine, an appreciation of wine, and sustainability. The Matias Riccitelli Wines bodega in Luján de Cuyo has created this restaurant, built out of remodelled containers and “planted” amid old wines, to enhance its wine experience. Chef Juan Ventureyra’s cuisine, which can be sampled in the informal dining room or on the lower terrace, explores Mendoza’s culinary roots on two menus (one with 6 courses, the other with 7) with a strong focus on native, locally sourced produce and ingredients mainly from its own gardens. Vegetables play a starring role here, hence the vegetarian influence in its “farm to table” concept (in summer, it grows over 80 varieties of tomato from seed), enhanced by adding protein to its dishes. A unique experience and a place that is well worth a visit.

Name: Corte Comedor
Address: Avenida Olazábal 1391, Buenos Aires, C1428DGE, Argentina
Description: Here, in the heart of the Belgrano district, everything revolves around a varied array of top-quality cuts of meat, traceability and the maturing process… which is hardly surprising given the restaurant’s location next door to its own butcher’s shop! The first thing you notice when you walk into the bright and open dining room are the flames and embers from the grill behind the counter. The “asado” croquettes are a good way to start proceedings, along with the Provoleta cheese, although you’ll need someone from your table to help share the huge portion. The sausages here, ranging from merguez to morcilla, are also popular, but the majority of customers come here for one thing: the succulent, tender and delicious cuts of meat. The high ceilings give a sense of space, while the tables and school-like chairs add to the relaxed atmosphere. The restaurant is used to being full, so the team here is fully under control of everything from the word go.

Name: Espacio Trapiche
Description: For those on a quest for a gastronomic experience rather than just a simple meal, this restaurant offering a combination of fine wine and fine dining is the perfect option. Occupying a glass-fronted annexe with views of the vineyards at the entrance to the prestigious Trapiche winery, Espacio Trapiche features an open-view kitchen visible from the entrance hall (part of the floor is covered with glass to enable guests to view the underground wine cellar below) as well as an attractive contemporary-style dining room. Chef Lucas Bustos, whose popularity has skyrocketed since his appearance in a Netflix documentary on Mendoza’s cuisine (Magical Andes), surprises guests with his modern cooking that celebrates ingredients from the surrounding mountains (potatoes, lamb, trout, vegetables from his own garden etc) that are exclusively showcased on his meticulously prepared menus: Premium, Ultra Premium (both with identical dishes, some chosen by guests, but with different wine pairings) and Degustación (Tasting), the latter requiring prior booking.

Name: Renacer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Patricio Reich, founder of the Renacer winery, has revealed the secret to his wines: “A combination of three key factors – our staff, the unique Mendoza terroir, and our passion for excellence”. Alongside these attributes, it was important not to neglect gastronomy when it came to understanding the bodega’s surroundings, hence the idea of offering a complete experience that allows guests to discover more about the region from every angle. The restaurant itself is located in a separate annexe to the winery and features a pleasant lakeside terrace with romantic views of both the Tuscan-inspired stone tower and the imposing Andes cordillera. A visit here usually starts with a short visit to the bodega, with its steel fermentation tanks and barrel storeroom, and a stroll through the vineyards, before continuing to the dining room, where you can choose between three menus (2, 3 or 5 courses). Picnics and more informal dining options are also possible, the latter including a tasting of hams, cheeses and empanadillas.

Name: Crizia
Address: Fitz Roy 1819, Buenos Aires, C1414CIA, Argentina
Description: The veteran Crizia restaurant has been one of the most respected in the city since it opened its doors in 2004 and it’s easy to see why. The contemporary loft-style vibe in the dining room contributes to the sophisticated ambience and makes it the perfect option for a date or to impress friends. The lighting here is intimate and the service professional, with the team attentive to every detail and keen for customers to leave completely satisfied. Owner-chef Gabriel Oggero works with small-scale independent producers, fishermen and farmers in order to source the very best seasonal ingredients. Oysters are a particular speciality and fish-lovers will delight in a menu which is completely focused on seafood and shellfish. The à la carte includes charcoal- and wood-grilled dishes such as the succulent roasted Peking Duck. An expertly curated wine list, featuring a good choice of wines by the glass, provides the perfect accompaniment.

Name: La Carniceria
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a different type of restaurant in which to enjoy Argentinian meat, this restaurant will definitely fit the bill, with a backdrop that re-creates the interior of a butcher’s shop (carnicería) with large photos of cuts of beef hanging from the ceiling to simulate a meat cold store, and a wood-fired grill behind the bar counter with its smoky aromas and glowing embers. In addition to the delicate and impressively updated traditional cuisine (interesting starters, chitterlings, smoked cuts etc), the quality of the meat stands out. This is enhanced by the traceability process from the rearing of 500kg Angus cattle on natural pasture at the “Los Abuelos” de Rivera family farm in the heart of the Humid Pampas region all the way through to the grill. These meat cuts are matured for different periods of time to enhance tenderness and maximise flavour. La Carniceria is full every day and is particularly popular with tourists.

Name: Piedra Pasillo Al Fondo
Address: Campos Salles 2145, Buenos Aires, C1429CFC, Argentina
Description: This restaurant occupies a restored house in the Nuñez district of the city. Boasting tons of charm, it is one of those places with a character that comes as a pleasant surprise due to the charming team at the helm and its somewhat “broken” design, with the kitchen visible through a large hole in the brickwork. It is run by its two owners (Lucas Canga and Tomás Couriel) who focus on modern, creative and complex cooking based around colourful dishes that showcase seasonal ingredients and successful combinations of flavours. One dish that particularly appealed to us was the venison tartare with marinera biscuit and vitello tonnato, which is full of contrasts thanks to the creamy vitello sauce, and a false bun made with biscuits to simulate bread that you need to break into to savour the smooth venison tartare inside. The restaurant also features a spacious patio-terrace and bar (Al Fondo) for a coffee or cocktail.

Name: Duhau Restaurant & Vinoteca
Address: Avenida Alvear 1661, Buenos Aires, C1014AAD, Argentina
Description: The fully laden wine shelves and cheese room with its display cabinets exert a Pavlovian effect as you enter this restaurant in the Park Hyatt hotel. The best Argentinian products – the majority of which are cooked on the parrilla grill – are the main attraction here, accompanied by an impressive wine list featuring the country’s most acclaimed wines. There are lots of dishes for sharing, from the grilled rib chops and Atlantic fish to the slow-grilled shoulder of lamb. Everything is abundant here, both in terms of flavour and portions, but make sure you order a side of the delicious and buttery smoked potato purée! The restaurant is popular with a business clientele, no doubt attracted by the good-value-for-money menu, as well as by the more relaxed ambience in the evening. The dining room is elegantly appointed and the staff highly attentive, while the arched doors lead to a charming terrace with views of the garden. The perfect place if you’re looking for a gastronomic bolthole to escape the hustle and bustle of the city.

Name: Mercado de Liniers
Description: A fine-dining restaurant, the name of which pays homage to the culture of the countryside, the omnipresence of meat and, above all, to the former Liniers livestock market where workers and breeders worked together like a family for generations. It is located in the extensive and lively Palermo Hollywood district and occupies a modern setting that was once a workshop (hence the light industrial vibe) with a kitchen that opens on to the dining room. Chef Dante Liporace, who spent time in Spain working under the legendary Ferran Adrià (at the erstwhile El Bulli) and several years behind the stove at Casa Rosada (under the baton of Mauricio Macri), showcases his cuisine exclusively on menus (Almuerzo (Lunch), Hangar, Highway Star and, lastly, the more gastronomically focused Too Tough To Die), with the leitmotif throughout his dishes the true soul of city of Buenos Aires and its surrounding area.

Name: Buri Omakase
Description: Anyone familiar with Japan and with the challenges faced when setting up a restaurant, will appreciate the complexities posed by Buri Omakase, where you have to ring the bell to property 002 in a small office block, and are then escorted by lift up to the authentically decorated dining room with seating for just 10 guests. There’s just one sitting (which starts at 8.30pm), so make sure you arrive on time to avoid unwelcome glances from other diners! Here, the owner-chef is inspired more by the traditions of Kyoto rather than Edomae, hence the prevalence of dishes prior to the nigiri courses, including an excellent miso soup and a creamy “chawanmushi”. For the nigiri, this chef uses high-quality local fish caught by trusted fishermen, while the rice is the Koshihikari variety from Niigata, famous for its excellent quality. As tradition dictates, the chef starts with fish with a gentle flavour, which then gradually intensifies through the course of the meal. An authentic experience in every sense!

Name: Águila Pabellón
Address: Avenida Sarmiento 2725, Buenos Aires, C1425FGC, Argentina
Description: This white Art Nouveau-style property, which dates from 1905 and has been carefully restored, reopened its doors in 2023 with great fanfare, adding its honourable name to the city’s food scene. The à la carte will appeal to everyone, featuring recognisable dishes and classic flavours which have been brought up to date through the use of contemporary techniques. The ingredients used are high on quality and the chef is conscious of the benefits of allowing space on the plate for natural flavours to fully express themselves, as witnessed by dishes such as chargrilled squid with a sweet red pepper salsa, confit of chicken with a mushroom cream, and pork loin milanesa. Choose from an array of dining spaces in which the traditional decor respects the building’s heritage and style. The large arch-shaped windows provide lots of natural light as well as views of the Ecoparque, the perfect place to spend a family weekend.

Name: CAUCE de los Fuegos
Address: Avenida Alicia Moreau De Justo 440, Buenos Aires, C1107AAJ, Argentina
Description: It’s not easy to be successful in Puerto Madero, so to succeed with a premium steakhouse in a district home to myriad other restaurants specialising in meat is no mean feat! In this modern eatery with a hint of industrial decor that reminds guests of its location in a restored port area (note the iron columns in the dining room and the huge old terrace visible from the terrace), the traditionally inspired à la carte includes an impressive choice of starters, salads, fish such as Patagonian trout, and pasta dishes including Mediterranean-style linguine with prawns, although it also features a particularly varied list of grilled and roast meats. Make sure you choose some of the empanadas (pork loin, pacú fish and lamb), the roasted “Emperador Cauce” short ribs (cooked for 14 hours) and the delicious Shorthorn ribeye from pasture-fed cattle reared at liberty on the restaurant’s Ayacucho estate.

Name: Benedetta
Description: Owner-chef Agustín Brañas brings his international experience to this bright, sun-blessed restaurant named after his oldest daughter. As well as offering an abundance of classic local dishes, the menu also has a decidedly Mediterranean focus in cuisine with a lightness of touch (the type of food that you feel is good for you!). Start by sharing Swiss chard fritters and ossobuco croquettes that will definitely brighten up your day. Follow this, perhaps, with a pasta dish such as the impressively prepared asparagus ravioli, or dishes perfect for sharing, including rice with mushrooms. Laid out on two floors, (the upper one, with its open kitchen, has more character but you’ll need to book a table ahead of time), the restaurant has a distinct Mediterranean feel with a dominant white colour scheme on the walls alongside blue and turquoise azulejo tiling. The young team, dressed in elegant cowboy-style uniforms, adds relaxed and friendly service to proceedings.

Name: Franca - Fuego y Vino
Description: If you’ve heard of or are already familiar with the highly successful Julia restaurant, located just a couple of blocks away, the easiest way to describe this eatery is “Julia’s younger sibling”, with the same independent outlook and principles when it comes to working with organic ingredients but with a strong determination when it comes to the cooking concepts of fire and the parrilla grill, which are its cornerstones. In this modern restaurant with glass-panelled walls that look out on to a colourful street corner, the large work counter, which also doubles as a dining space, is a strong presence, enabling guests to watch dishes being prepared and the constant hustle around the grill, where the colourful embers of white quebracho hardwood burn brightly in the background. Chef Julio Martín Baez’s cuisine includes numerous small plates (raw mullet, tartare, cured prawns with garlic, mushrooms etc) so that guests can try a little of everything, as well as vegetarian starters and aged meats for mains. Impressive choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Sacro
Address: Costa Rica 6038, Buenos Aires, C1414BTN, Argentina
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant focusing on “plant -based” cuisine, this eatery on the ground floor of the CasaSur boutique hotel in the Palermo Hollywood is definitely worth considering, a sensation enhanced by its bright façade in different tones of white, featuring striking circular perforations that create contrast and add light. Its elongated layout boasts a modern design, and includes a pleasant, verdant terrace to the rear. Here, the contemporary à la carte showcases vegetarian dishes made to share and to create an element of surprise, mouthwatering snacks (the unmissable kimchi-based dumplings with ginger foam and coriander), gently flavoured dishes (artichokes with Sicilian caponata, putanesca, corn remolacha and herbs) alongside more hearty options (roasted salsify, kale, edamame cream and hazelnuts), all of which showcase vegetables but from a Far Eastern and Latin American perspective. It’s not a bad idea to pair the dining experience with some of Sacro’s cocktails!

Name: Ruca Malen
Address: Ruta Nacional 7 km. 1059, Bodega Ruca Malen, Mendoza, M5507, Argentina
Description: At the Ruca Malen winery, situated in Agrelo (in the department of Luján de Cuyo) just over half an hour to the south of Mendoza, guests can enjoy a dining experience that will live long in the memory. Its eponymous restaurant (the name comes from a Mapuche legend) takes a fresh, immersive look at the world of wine, with both the chef and the young sommelier wandering around the tables to chat with diners. Here, wine takes on major importance and has always been the key to everything, hence the choice of dishes on the 7-course tasting menu which have been deliberately created with the choice of wine pairings in mind (somewhat unusually, on the menu the wine is listed first in capital letters with the accompanying dish written in lowercase). The dishes themselves are highly contemporary, delicate and influenced by the local terroir, hence the showcasing of seasonal ingredients and produce and the purity of each individual flavour (we particularly enjoyed the spinach, eggs and alubia bean dish).

Name: Abrasado
Address: Lateral Norte Acceso Este 1360, Mendoza, M5519, Argentina
Description: If you rely on a restaurant’s list of awards when it comes to booking a table and if the delicious flavour of aged meats brings tears to your eyes, then the Abrasado restaurant (part of the Los Toneles winery not far from the centre of Mendoza - the recipient of various Best of Wine Tourism awards over the years) is the place for you! The dining room, located next to the spaces reserved for tastings and events, boasts a contemporary design and high ceilings, along with a maturing cabinet at the entrance and a bar to the rear with a resident bartender. Although Abrasado offers an extensive à la carte with an impressive array of fresh and aged meats (dry-aged ribeye, T-bone aged in black garlic, fillet steak aged in kombu) designed for sharing, the vast majority of guests opt for its set menus (Andes, 100 Aniversario and Abrasado) as they all include a wine pairing option.

Name: Narda Comedor
Address: Mariscal Antonio José De Sucre 664, Buenos Aires, C1428DUB, Argentina
Description: The love that locals in Buenos Aires have for meat has been long documented, however Narda Lepes, a woman who is well known thanks to her cookery books and TV appearances, is slowly changing this attitude. She is a champion of healthy ingredients and a vegetarian diet, hence the predominance she gives to vegetables here. Her stuffed onion dish will satisfy even the most die-hard of carnivores, while her silky tofu is a culinary legacy that originates from her travels overseas. Although there’s a plethora of vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, that doesn’t mean that her restaurant is fully vegetarian as evidenced by her ossobuco, a legendary dish in every respect. The bright and roomy white dining space gives the impression of being in a particularly elegant cafeteria, enhanced by the equally spacious open kitchen. Service here begins with breakfast, hence the different dining incarnations through the day, from morning coffee to lunchtime snacks and dinner with friends.

Name: Mishiguene
Description: Situated just a few metres from the stunning Jardín Japonés, a verdant garden that highlights the friendship that exists between Argentina and Japan, you’ll come across Mishiguene (“crazy” in Yiddish), a restaurant that is full every day and that everyone is talking about. In its busy dining room, with its classic English style and a bar counter for customers, discover cuisine that revives the flavours of Jewish cuisine from a contemporary perspective. These revive Jerusalem-trained chef Tomás Kalika’s childhood recollections and his quest for “emotional memories” that demonstrate the imprint of an immigrant population marked by history. On his à la carte, which is complemented by a tasting menu, you’ll find delicious and copious dishes full of personality which usually feature lots of ingredients. One of Mishiguene’s signature dishes is Pastrón, a beef prime rib cured for ten days with salt, herbs and spices, which is then smoked over wood embers for four hours, and steam-cooked for a further fourteen.

Name: Quimera Bistro
Address: Cochabamba S/N, Agrelo (Bodega Quimera), Mendoza, M5509, Argentina
Description: Here, in Achaval Ferrer, 28km from Mendoza, the team at Quimera Bistró consider themselves as the “guardians of a legacy”, a sentiment that goes far beyond the production of wine and is further demonstrated in a restaurant that adds to the wine experience. Once you’ve reached the estate via a dirt track between the vineyards, you come to a landscaped area with a small duck pond, and then the winery with the restaurant on the first floor. The latter features a bright, rustic-cum-contemporary dining room that is particularly striking as a result of the glass floor, through which the wooden wine barrels can be seen on the floor below. The bistro is run by a young, dynamic team who showcase their talents on a single, traditionally inspired 3-course menu featuring highly original seasonal options that champion small-scale producers from the Mendoza region – the kitchen team particularly enjoys working with fruit and vegetables that are home grown and sourced daily, cheeses from La Linqueñita, vinegars from Alquería, Andean oyster mushrooms etc.

Name: Picarón
Address: Avenida Dorrego 866, Buenos Aires, C1414CKQ, Argentina
Description: If you enjoy dishes that come in small portions enabling you to try lots of different options, make a beeline for Picarón, in the Chacarita district, a restaurant with a sign depicting a large bear riding a velocipede, behind which you’ll find a culinary world that is both playful and fun. The colourful façade, complemented by a pavement terrace, leads to a simple bistro-style dining room with an open kitchen behind the bar counter and a glass-fronted wine cellar to one side. The à carte showcased by Maximiliano Rossi, enhanced by an affordable set menu at lunchtime (no bookings so first-come, first served), is centred around contemporary and Argentinian-based small plates which are transformed with touches of fusion, predominantly using recipes from Latin America but also more exotic dishes from Asia. We definitely recommend the popular “picarones” (sweet potato fritters with spiced Mascabo honey), the tatemado avocado, the surprising “tonnato maiale”, and the exquisite smoked prawns – all prepared with the best-possible ingredients.

Name: Ácido
Description: “We don’t take ourselves too seriously” is the claim of the young owner-chef at this modern and lively restaurant in the city’s Chacarita district. The à la carte here features just seven dishes, two of which are desserts, so you only need to order a few to enjoy this family-style dining experience. There’s a contagious exuberance in the kitchen where the bold and honest flavours created emanate from every corner of the globe. As an example, the Korean “tteokbokki” is one of the most popular options here, while another favourite dish, fried chicken, is served with an array of sides. The “Torrija” brioche provides a delicious finale to proceedings. The large open kitchen stands next to the rustic-style dining room which seems to have been decorated and furnished by a grandmother with help from her grandchildren! The atmosphere here is fun and relaxed and you can’t book ahead, so you’ll need to arrive well before 8pm to guarantee a table.

Name: A Fuego Fuerte
Address: Estado De Palestina 1167, Buenos Aires, C1182ADM, Argentina
Description: If you’re keen to enjoy an experience that makes you feel as though you’re eating in someone’s private house, this is the place for you. Ring the bell and you’ll be led into a large room with space for just 16 guests, each of whom is seated at impressively laid out tables adorned with ornamental crystal glassware. Supper starts at 9pm for everyone and lasts for 3 hours, during which the owner-chef, who makes regular forays into the dining room to chat with guests, conjures up a 17-course tasting menu. His culinary influences are mainly from France and Italy, although theatrical presentation and elaborately constructed dishes are also to the fore. Somewhat disguised beneath this culinary spectacle are high-quality ingredients and dishes such as veal with asparagus, smoked trout with almonds, and scallops with a delicious lemon cream. Despite its formality, the service is not lacking in personality, and if you prefer not to have make any decisions whatsoever, the best option is to go for the wine pairing option.

Name: NOÏS
Description: Laura is a warm and welcoming host, and she knows the outstanding wine list like the back of her hand. Her recommendations are absolutely spot on! If you like surprises, chef Vincent is your man. There's no written menu here; your options are presented verbally only, and your trust is rewarded with imaginative, plant-forward cuisine. Whether he's imbuing various textures of celeriac with zingy flavours, or putting pork belly centre stage in an Asian-inspired dish with a bay leaf cream sauce, his elaborate culinary creations are full of flair.

Name: Bisque
Description: Chef Niels Schievink and charming hostess Sabrina Mans's experience shines through in their inviting, intimate restaurant. Their expertise is evident in every aspect of a meal here, from the welcome to the wine pairings to the delicious dishes. The "less-is-more" approach to French cuisine relies on technical skill and a sense of balance. The chocolate and hazelnut soufflé is truly an ode to this classic dessert – not to be missed! This celebration of wonderful produce, underpinned by exquisite sauces, is captivating.

Name: Bistrotel 't Amsterdammertje
Description: Brimming with character, this building by the Vecht River is enchanting, but just wait until you're sitting on the terrace… At Bistrotel, you can truly escape the hustle and bustle for a while! Before you retire to your comfortable guestroom, be sure to pop into the spacious bistro downstairs. André Gerrits has assembled a team here who know their way around bistro classics and flavours from all over the world. With options on the menu such as steak tartare, spicy rendang or farmhouse chicken from the spit; this is the kind of place where anything goes.

Name: Barents Cocktail & Seafood Bar
Description: It’s worth booking in advance for this hidden gem – not only is it compact, but it also acts as the cocktail bar for next door Barents. Seasonal drinks are joined by a concise menu; the seafood platter is a feast for the eyes, but don’t overlook the delicious 'small bites' which change with the seasons. The fish burger is a hit and, if you see the rum soaked baba for dessert, be sure to order it. Naturally, you should start and end with some cocktails from their thoughtfully curated selection.

Name: ZOLTNERS
Description: You'll find the Zoltners Brewery in the heart of the glorious Zemgale countryside, along with this slick, modern restaurant and an attractively restored period house that’s now a small hotel boasting modern bedrooms; make a weekend of it by dining, staying the night and visiting the Tērvete Nature Park. Menus showcase local produce in an appealing mix of flavoursome northern European dishes, and the simple starters go perfectly with their home-brewed beers and local spirits.

Name: Tails
Description: There’s a choice of two bistro-style dining rooms at Tails, but the raw bar counter really is the place to sit to make the most of the experience. The chefs take fish seriously here by adopting a tail to gill approach, and there’s even a drying room on show. They cure their own fish, make their own ceviches, and their shellfish platter is something to linger over. Keep an eye out for the daily specials too, which often feature something a little different. For the ultimate indulgence, order a bottle of champagne to accompany.

Name: Neiburgs
Description: The crowds thin as you wind your way down the cobbled streets of the Old Town and you find yourself in this peaceful spot. Located on the ground floor of a boutique hotel, this restaurant is the place to dine if you’re looking for a smart environment but with a pleasingly unpretentious atmosphere. The menus offer fresh, unfussy dishes with some Mediterranean influences, and the seafood options are particularly appealing.

Name: Kest
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The town’s former fire station is now home to a restaurant which provides an experience of two parts. You start in the bright restaurant, where you dine from a 5 course tasting menu made up of modern dishes which keep local produce to the fore – and this is accompanied by an interesting alcoholic drinks flight which also includes cocktails. After dessert, you head through to the dark, moody lounge for the second part of your night: a coffee and time spent over a relaxing post-meal drink. The team really do run the place with genuine warmth.

Name: Ferma
Description: Sit inside at the chef’s table for a view of the chefs hard at work, or outside on the large terrace to take in views of the city’s oldest park. Chef-Owner Māris’ dishes reflect his love of native produce, with local beef and seafood to the fore, especially herring. The à la carte menu is concise and supplemented by a great value option at lunch, and friendly service completes the picture.

Name: COD
Description: Make for the sultry basement bar for a cocktail or two before heading back up to the atmospheric ground floor restaurant with its dim lighting and on-trend soundtrack. The chefs might be Latvian but the fresh, vibrant cooking respects the fundamentals of Japanese cuisine. Start with a selection of sushi and tempura, then choose something from the robata grill; the black cod with sweet miso is a hit, and the mochi ice cream is the perfect way to finish. In summer, sit outside and fully immerse yourself with the flavours of the season.

Name: 3 Chefs
Address: Torna iela 4, Jekaba Arcade 2b, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: Located in Jacob’s Barracks – a restored 18C building overlooking the Powder Tower and Swedish Gate – this restaurant lives up to exactly what you might expect. It’s run by three chefs – who help serve the dishes and love chatting with their guests – and the menu sticks with the traditional theme by offering classical flavour combinations, albeit updated with touches of creativity and a little refinement. The tasting menu is the best route to having a great all-round experience, and they hold cookery classes for those who like to get hands-on.

Name: Entresol
Description: Set on the ground floor of a grand city centre property, this small restaurant offers two experiences in one. The front area is filled with memorabilia and has more of a vintage lounge feel, while the raised area behind has a less-cluttered look. The good value tasting menu changes twice a year and offers a selection of modern dishes with a pleasingly unfussy approach, allowing the flavours of the excellent quality produce to shine.

Name: Chef's Corner
Description: A friendly team welcome you into this chic city centre brasserie, where you’ll do well to start with a cocktail while choosing from the classic brasserie-style menu. The emphasis is on steaks from the Netherlands, the UK and the USA, with the steaks to share proving a popular choice. Other options include everything from tartares and oysters to burgers and pastas, which are hit with locals and visitors alike.

Name: MO
Description: Beside the promenade in the historical canal area sits Julianna’s Courtyard, where the 19C printing house and later 20C factories have been lovingly restored to create one of Liepāja's go-to areas. Here you’ll find MO, which offers a satisfying meal out at a fair price. Ask for a table either on or overlooking the terrace, then choose from the wide-ranging menu that includes tartares, carpaccios, sharing plates and main dishes such as beef with truffle mash. Locally produced beers and cocktails make the perfect accompaniment.

Name: TAURO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This über-smart steak restaurant is secreted away on the ground floor of the Zunda Towers skyscraper. Forgo starters and enjoy a generous plate of cured meats and salamis from their farm, then move on to a superb steak from Latvia, Spain, California, Japan or Australia. Accompany this with one of their freshly made sauces in myriad flavours, as well as a side – the crispy potatoes with thyme are a must. The 300+ bin wine list is beautifully curated, with some of the North American classics creating the perfect pairing.

Name: Pavāru māja
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A former maternity hospital on the edge of a rural village plays host to this smart, modern restaurant. Here, you are encouraged to relax in their lovely nature observation garden – a place to sit back, listen and watch – before taking time to really savour your meal. Their raised beds and foraging trips provide the kitchen with vegetables and herbs, while the rest of their produce is locally sourced. The 4 course lunch and 8 course dinner are informed by what’s fresh and available each day.

Name: Akustika
Description: In summer, be sure to try for a seat on the popular terrace of this faux-industrial neighbourhood bistro, which sits on the ground floor of the well-known Post and Telegraph building. Tasty, modern dishes are informed by the seasons, with local produce taking the lead, be it pikeperch from nearby Lake Burtnieks or locally reared lamb. The restaurant was created by three friends and designed as a place they themselves would like to dine. Occasional music performances add to the appeal.

Name: Barents
Description: An early 20C art nouveau property on the edge of town plays host to this spacious restaurant with a distinct Nordic style. The seasonally changing menu comprises modern dishes that are made up of numerous elements and combine many flavours and textures in great harmony. Seafood is a strength – with some sourced from the Barents Sea – and the produce is displayed on ice in the middle of the room and explained to diners as they arrive. The champagne selection provides a noteworthy accompaniment.

Name: JOHN
Description: Set within the striking A22 hotel, this chic, stylish restaurant is named after John F Kennedy, who stayed here back in 1939; be sure to keep an eye out for some of the original art nouveau features, which have been carefully restored. An open kitchen counter dominates the small space, with the rest of the tables bordering the room, and there’s a palpable buzz from the chefs being so close. The European-inspired dishes show good attention to detail and are artfully presented.

Name: Whitehouse
Address: Vermane Park, Terbatas iela 2, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: The former Biblioteka – which was something of an institution – reopened in 2020 as Whitehouse, and its dining terrace remains one of the most sought-after in the city thanks to its views over the colourful flower displays of Vērmanes Garden. It’s a sizeable place, with a long, narrow room, stylish décor and even a living wall. The menu blends modern European influences with subtle Asian touches, and there’s a touch of theatre to the presentation. Desserts are a highlight, as are the signature cocktails, and the place really comes into its own in the evening.

Name: Aqua Luna
Description: Since it opening back in 2013, Aqua Luna has maintained its status as one of Riga’s hotspots. Set by the water’s edge and just a short walk from the city centre, this is the place to see and be seen, especially at the weekend when the music is cranked up into the night. Start with cocktails on the terrace, then move on to carefully executed contemporary dishes such as yellow fin tuna with ponzu or a crispy coated schnitzel topped with summer truffle. They open seasonally, so be sure to check your dates before planning a visit.

Name: 36.Line
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beachside locations don’t come much better than this, as you can walk straight in off the sand. Those after some respite from the sun can stay inside, while those wanting to feel the sea breeze should head for the glass-fronted terrace. The accessible menu covers all options, from lighter sushi and tartares to dumplings and hearty grilled fish and meat dishes. The tiramisu laced with the famous Black Balsam – their national drink – is a must-try, and the extensive selection of wines and cocktails is perfect for watching the sun go down.

Name: H.E. Vanadziņš
Description: You’ll find plenty of locals here, from the serving team to the regular guests, which creates a welcoming vibe and a convivial feel. The lengthy menus cover all bases, from flavour-packed soups and salads to delicious flatbreads and hearty mains inspired by northern Latvian cuisine. There’s a lovely terrace hidden to the rear that's worth seeking out, and bedrooms are available should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Le Dome
Description: Tucked away down the cobbled streets of the Old Town is this 400-year-old building which is home to both a boutique hotel and this intimate restaurant. Black and white photos of Riga adorn the walls of the long, narrow dining room, while in summer the operation relocates to the rooftop terrace which overlooks the Daugava River. Seafood is to the fore on the creative, modern menus. Subtle international influences are in evidence, while the prime ingredients originate mostly from the Baltic region.

Name: Riviera
Description: This large restaurant has a warm Mediterranean style and a menu to match, offering an appealing selection of dishes from oysters and tartares to fish and steaks, followed by old favourites like tiramisu. Everything is generously sized, with well-defined flavours and textures, and the sizeable wine list (1,000+) offers some great choices from around the globe. There’s a choice of two rooms in which to dine, but the terrace is the place to be when the weather’s right.

Name: La Vie
Address: Le Dream Boutique Hotel, 139 Jalan Pintal Tali, George Town, 10100, Malaysia
Description: This casual neighbourhood dining spot started out as a steakhouse, but switched to serving European cuisine with Asian influences. Their signature kataifi prawn is tiger prawn wrapped in crispy noodles, fried and served in a prawn bisque sauce. Meat lovers should check out the Australian Wagyu ribeye which is cooked to perfection on a charcoal grill. It comes with a range of condiments but the wasabi works best. Wine is available by the bottle only.

Name: Café Café
Address: 175 Jalan Maharajalela, Kampung Attap, Kuala Lumpur, 50150, Malaysia
Description: Founded by two local chefs who plied their trade in France, Café Café is tucked away in a quiet part of the city. The interior, dripping in contemporary Parisian chic and traditional French grandeur, is ideal for a romantic dinner. The à la carte and set menus include classic dishes such as foie gras, escargots and duck confit. The carefully crafted food is perfectly poised between knockout texture and spot-on seasoning. The leg of duck confit has a crispy, delicious skin and succulent meat.

Name: Teochew Lao Er
Address: 6 Jalan Brunei, Pudu, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
Description: In 1984, Lao Er started out as a street stall. In 2011, the third generation opened a restaurant and established itself as a household name in Pudu district. Teochew classics are given a slight tweak to cater to the local palate. The signature dish, meat marinated in spiced soy, is a great hit – try the assorted platter or the goose alone. Teochew congee with pomfret, mackerel or fish balls, and dim sum like png kueh are also popular.

Name: 888 Hokkien Mee (Lebuh Presgrave)
Description: For 30 years, this small outlet has been serving Hokkien-style noodles in prawn soup. The soup has a beautiful rich red colour and sweet umami flavour. Add a little textural variety to your bowl with tasty options such as braised pork ribs or roasted pork – both highly recommended.

Name: Entier
Address: Level 41, Alila Bangsar, 58 Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur, 50470, Malaysia
Description: The airy, minimalist room atop a sky-scraping hotel tower commands breathtaking cityscapes and is the epitome of casual elegance. The Japanese head chef honed his skills in prestigious European kitchens before taking the helm here. The deftly crafted French menu sports subtle Japanese twists. Order à la carte tapas dishes or go for the 3-course set dinner menu. Though the menu changes quarterly, the must-try beef, dry-aged in house, is a firm fixture.

Name: WhatSaeb Boat Noodles
Description: Come here to get your fix for boat noodles. The owner hires a kitchen team from Thailand to make sure it’s made properly. There are many toppings and noodles to choose from, but pork rice noodle soup with extra pork cracklings will be your best bet. In addition to the noodle soup, the menu also features an array of Thai classics, such as curry, som tum salads and desserts. On weekends, make sure to try their mango sticky rice.

Name: Penang Famous Samosa
Description: This stall in Little India serves a delicious range of samosas, including mutton, chicken, sardine, egg and vegetable. Encased in a crispy shell, the flavoursome fillings are moderately spicy. Prices are fair, too, so no wonder customers are prepared to queue.

Name: Eat and Cook
Address: H6-1, Pusat Perdagangan Bandar Bukit Jalil, Persiaran Jalil 1, Bukit Jalil, Kuala Lumpur, 57000, Malaysia
Description: Tucked in a district, far from the city centre, Eat and Cook is owned by two young, accomplished chefs. The set menu features local ingredients. It changes every three to four months to introduce a new chapter. While the seasonality of Malaysian cuisine may not be obvious, it affects the variety of seafood and vegetables. Each new chapter reveals the characteristics of that season. The counter seats, known as The Stage, have an intimate view of the kitchen team in action.

Name: Il Bacaro
Address: Campbell House, 106 Lebuh Campbell, George Town, 10100, Malaysia
Description: Photos from a by-gone era, retro ceiling fans and patterned tiles exude a nostalgic mood. This restaurant, run by a friendly Italian couple (who also own the hotel), has been serving classics from their home country for more than a decade. You can find most Italian classics on the menu, such as antipasto, pizzas, pastas and mains. Start with bruschetta tradizionale for a refreshing and appetising opener. Save some room for their homemade sweets.

Name: Bao Teck Tea House
Description: This is the place to go for an authentic yum cha experience and tasty Cantonese dim sum. The room has historic appeal, with details worth appreciating such as the patterned tile flooring and the moss garden. But it’s the dim sum that sets it apart – try steamed har gow dumplings made with local shrimp, and the deep-fried yam puffs in airy honeycomb crust. The owner also runs a bakery, and their Chinese baked goods are excellent.

Name: Elegant Inn
Address: 02-01, 2F, Podium Block, Menara Hap Seng, Jalan P. Ramlee, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50250, Malaysia
Description: Since 2008, Elegant Inn has been feeding gourmets with Cantonese classics, especially some Hong Kong-style favourites. The wood-rich interior is traditionally decorated, alongside tables on the balcony for al fresco dining. At lunch, exquisite dim sum takes centre stage, with deep-fried taro pouch being a highlight. Double-boiled soups are not to be missed and need pre-ordering. Sizzling chicken with bitter melon in claypot also stands out.

Name: Bref by Darren Chin
Address: 26, GF, Lorong Datuk Sulaiman 1, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
Description: Another dining concept by the eponymous chef, Bref serves a sensual, modern and progressive menu that appeals to the palate. Cold capellini with cured ama-ebi, ikura, uni and salted kombu in a creamy abalone dressing is the epitome of their cuisine. Despite the minimalist interior, the vibe is lively and bustling. Prized seats are at the marble counter overlooking the open kitchen.

Name: Dominic
Address: 54G, The Row, Jalan Doraisamy, Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, 50300, Malaysia
Description: From the blue façade and a terrace reminiscent of pavement cafes, to the oversized painting celebrating joie de vivre, the restaurant formerly known as 2OX transports diners to a Parisian bistro with its relaxed, convivial vibe. Helmed by Chef Dominic, the kitchen creates modern, sophisticated dishes that are deeply rooted in the French traditions. Most ingredients are imported from Europe; the artisanal cheeses are especially worth trying.

Name: Jawi House
Description: Nestled in a neighbourhood rich in cultural heritage, Jawi House blends in seamlessly. The retro room sets the backdrop for the chef to experiment Indian recipes with Peranakan influences. On the menu, a good selection of biriyani with different ingredients are found alongside jawi laksa lemak (rice noodles with flaked tuna and mackerel in coconut milk broth) and papadum. Fish curry is always good; ask servers about the catch of the day.

Name: Kota Dine & Coffee (Fort Cornwallis)
Address: Fort Cornwallis, Jalan Tun Syed Sheh Barakbah, George Town, 10200, Malaysia
Description: It feels relaxing to sit in the glass-clad room drenched in natural light and furnished in faux-industrial style. In terms of food, they serve a neo-Nyonya menu with a strong East-meets-West concept. On top of Peranakan classics like otak-otak, Western influences are manifested in more adventurous creations such as laksa capellini. Even the desserts take a surprise twist, as in teh-ramisu that uses tea instead of coffee.

Name: Seed
Address: L1-04, Block E, The Five@KPD, 49 Jalan Dungun, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Splashes of earthy colour and cool neutrals adorn the warm dining room, whose seats at the wave-shaped counter ensure a fascinating view of the open kitchen. After a stint at Whitegrass in Singapore, the chef flaunts his consummate grasp of French techniques with two prix-fixe menus that fete Japanese ingredients and cuisine. The umami-loaded amadai with crispy scales in uni sauce is a must, as is the lobster in bouillabaisse sauce with a frothy cognac and gruyere aioli.

Name: Misai Mee Jawa (Butterworth)
Address: 6794 Jalan Raja Uda, Taman Aman Jaya, Butterworth, Seberang Perai, 12300, Malaysia
Description: Popular in the district for more than 20 years, the second generation cooks mee jawa in two ways, either fried or in soup. The soup version features egg noodles in a sweet-spicy pumpkin broth with toppings like tofu and boiled egg.

Name: Air Itam Sister Curry Mee
Address: 612 T, Jalan Air Itam Pekan Ayer Itam, George Town, 11500, Malaysia
Description: This shop in a market serves Penang-style curry mee at friendly prices. The mee is cooked over charcoal, in a well-balanced soup with spices, chilli paste and coconut milk; tofu puffs and spring squid add contrasting textures.

Name: Akâr
Address: 109 Jalan Aminuddin Baki, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
Description: Founded in 2020, this theatre-like dining room with neat designs faces an open kitchen where Chef Low and his energetic team perform. The set menu is mostly informed by European cuisine, using local ingredients like gula apong and engkabang. Creatively refashioned with interesting surprises, the menu changes with the seasons and goes beyond the realms of typical Malaysian cooking. The signature green salad with bagna cauda is packed with flavour.

Name: Goh Thew Chik Hainan Chicken Rice
Description: On top of Hainanese style, chicken is also grilled and served with chicken oil rice here. Silky and succulent bird goes well with chicken liver or gizzards. You may order in halves or single portions.

Name: Limapulo
Address: 50 Jalan Doraisamy, Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, 50300, Malaysia
Description: Opened seven years ago, the restaurant has a rustic edge with vintage canteen-style furniture that evokes waves of nostalgia across a dimly lit venue. Limapulo (which means fifty in Malay), is managed by a team of Malaysian chefs. It’s best to choose plates for sharing and be sure to order the popular Nyonya laksa – a standout dish indeed. The signature sate has a special sauce homemade from star fruits and pineapple. Some menu items are only available on certain days.

Name: Malai
Address: M1 Floor, Menara Ample West, 6 Jalan Puncak, Kuala Lumpur, 50250, Malaysia
Description: Every detail, from the imported tableware to the authentic Thai dining experience, has been pondered and puzzled over. Malai relocated to this venue at the end of 2022 to offer greater comfort and more spacious dining on two floors. It’s regularly packed with office workers, especially at lunchtime. The mostly Thai team of chefs conjures up a traditional Thai menu with modern twists. Don’t miss the tom yum soup or the gaeng keaw waan (green curry).

Name: Flour
Address: 12 & 14 Jalan Kamuning, Off Jalan Imbi, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
Description: The spacious, monochromatic dining room commands views of the kitchen via a glass wall. With the prix-fixe menus that change from time to time, the chef reinvents Indian cooking with modern European techniques, quality ingredients from around the world, and the deepest respect for Mother Earth. He seasons the food sparingly to let its natural flavours sing, and often visits each table to explain his dishes throughout the meal.

Name: Ember
Address: 20 Jalan Wan Kadir 1, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Car park,Counter dining
Description: The dynamic energy of the trendy Ember is fueled by a chef who doesn't like to follow the rules. He boldly infuses Asian ingredients in various contemporary styles in a way that gives customers the experience of familiar flavours but with new and sophisticated recipes. The industrial-style interior presents a modern yet cosy dining area with marble floors, grey walls, an open kitchen and a neat countertop that’s softly lit with warm tones.

Name: Pitt Street Koay Teow Soup
Description: The shop has been selling Penangese’ favourite fish ball soup for over 60 years and has been in this current spot since 2009. Fish balls are made daily in-house using flavoursome sea eel meat that complement their pork broth. Order “extra minced pork and fish ball” – minced pork refers to the flat pork balls – and top it with lots of crispy garlic bits. Homemade cakes and tarts end a meal perfectly, or take them home to enjoy later.

Name: Hide
Address: Concourse, Ritz-Carlton Residences, 105 Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
Description: Like its name, the entrance is tucked away in a secluded corner among some paintings. The room feels trendy, with a U-shaped marble counter overlooking the open kitchen. The young head chef once worked in a renowned restaurant in the U.S. and his seasonally driven 13-course tasting menu is heavy on seafood sourced locally and from Japan. Dishes like lobster mapo with Sichuan pepper oil, and puff pastry with kaya mousse also show Malaysian influences.

Name: Tanglin (Bukit Damansara)
Address: 57G, Jalan Medan Setia 1, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Founded in 1948, the family-owned Tanglin is now run by the second generation and the two-storey establishment is well known for its nasi lemak. This delicious family recipe is paired with either sotong (squid), daging (meat) or ayam goreng (fried chicken). Its fragrant rice has the right mix of coconut milk and its sambal tumis, the right level of spiciness. Whether dining in or taking away, the queues are long. Generous portions and prices that make sense.

Name: Woodlands
Description: This no-frills vegetarian joint in Little India is popular among locals because of their tasty food at friendly prices. The menu could be a bit overwhelming; feel free to ask servers to recommend. Must-tries include dosai – malasa dosai, for instance, is mashed potato wrapped in a thin rice flour crepe with two homemade sauces, presenting a nice contrast between the crispy crepe and creamy potato. Vegetable biriyani is great for a few to share.

Name: Bōl
Address: 15 Jalan Sin Chew Kee, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, 50150, Malaysia
Description: Having cooked together since they were young, Singaporean chef-owner and hotel designer, Kian Liew, and partner, Patrick, opened their brainchild in 2022 and have already earned the support of many regulars. The menu includes à la carte options and two set menus featuring smaller portions of the à la carte dishes. They infuse Nyonya style cuisine with Singaporean and Malaysian flavours, using a healthy mix of herbs and spices to create a succulent range of flavour.

Name: Marini's on 57
Address: 57F, Menara 3 Petronas, Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: At this iconic rooftop venue, diners enjoy superb sunsets and panoramic cityscapes through floor to ceiling windows. Besides the à la carte menu, there are several tasting menus that offer a knockout selection of Italian dishes, featuring innovative elements, choice cuts of imported beef and artisan pasta. The intriguing tiramisu, which comes in a tin of caviar, is made with coffee caviar (rather than fish eggs!).

Name: Sushi Masa
Address: Lot 1-03, 1F, Menara Hap Seng 3, Jalan P. Ramlee, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50250, Malaysia
Description: Following the success of his Edomae-style sushi restaurant in Tokyo, acclaimed chef Masakazu Ishibashi brings his expertise to KL. His unique approach to sushi, founded on a 200-year-old tradition, is presented as a beautiful multi-course meal prepared by his apprentice, Chef Yoshi. The omakase menus showcase creative twists on traditional dishes. The nigiri is made with high quality produce sourced straight from Japan, while the Botan Ebi with egg yolk sauce and caviar is packed with umami.

Name: Shanghai Restaurant
Address: 1F, JW Marriott, 183 Jalan Bukit Bintang, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
Description: In business since 1999, the restaurant was updated in 2021 and now sports a bright, modern interior. The veteran chef traditionally crafts Shanghainese classics, and his xiao long bao is a must-try – soupy pork filling enrobed in paper-thin, meticulously pleated skin. Stir-fried flat glass noodles with shredded pork and preserved vegetable boasts remarkable wok hei, and the salted potherb mustard greens impart briny umami.

Name: Ushi
Address: 3A, The St. Regis, 6 Jalan Stesen Sentral 2, Kuala Lumpur Sentral, Kuala Lumpur, 50470, Malaysia
Description: An elegant, black wave opens up to an intimate room where 12 counter seats face a cooking station. The chef has worked for decades in top-tier restaurants. He crafts an omakase kaiseki-style menu that prominently features Ozaki beef; the epitome of tender, marbled beef. Dishes include beef sashimi with sea urchin, and beef cooked on binchō-tan that accentuates the natural flavour. There’s a good collection of sake served in beautiful glasses. Advanced booking highly recommended.

Name: Curios-City
Description: You need to look hard to find this place – there is no sign and the exterior looks barren. The stunning, moody interior is furnished in wabi-sabi style with lots of greenery, giving it a cosy and stylish ambience. The chef, who used to work in Europe and Hong Kong, creates dishes underpinned by European techniques and punctuated by Malaysian twists. He offers three set menus that change every two months. Try the seven-course set to experience his vision in full glory.

Name: Tamarind Hill
Address: 19 Jalan Sultan Ismail, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, 50250, Malaysia
Description: The glowing stairs lead you to a colonial bungalow amid lush greens with a beautiful terrace. Behind the French doors, the high-ceilinged room feels exotic and resort-like, priming diners for a serene culinary retreat just minutes away from the busy city centre. The menu is dominated by authentic no-frills Thai and Burmese cooking. Though without fancy plating, the food is astutely executed with fresh, quality ingredients.

Name: Nadodi
Address: Level 7A, Four Seasons Hotel, 145 Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
Description: In 2023, Nadodi moved to this stylish venue in an upmarket hotel. The booth seats by the window command sweeping city views and are cosily private. Kick off your meal with one of the magical concoctions created by the professional bartenders. Continue with creative “nomadic” cuisine based on Southern Indian fare. The set dinner menu with 10-plus courses features different taste profiles and traditional snacks, best enjoyed with alcoholic drink pairings.

Name: Qureshi
Address: GF, East Lobby, TPC Kuala Lumpur, 10 Jalan 1/70D, Jalan Bukit Kiara, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
Description: One of the Indian dining concepts owned by the Qureshi family, this prestigious restaurant is nestled within a country club not accessible by public transport, so you’ll need to drive or take a taxi here. The room is furnished in a modern Indian style with a colourful palette, classic motifs and glitzy details. When it comes to the food, a nice variety of exquisite Indian cooking deeply rooted in traditions is served.

Name: Gēn
Address: Unit 6, 8 Gat Lebuh Gereja, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
Description: Gēn is Chinese for root. The owner-chef revisits his culinary roots and childhood memories with nostalgic flavours and a tasting menu driven by local seasonal produce, especially fish, whose courses never fail to surprise. The plating is particularly pleasing, and sometimes playful, such as the silky chicken soup in a glass bottle. The wine list boasts over 30 organic and biodynamic tipples that complement the food perfectly.

Name: Richard Rivalee
Description: Renowned fashion designer Richard Rivalee shares his passion for Nyonya culture and Peranakan food in this smart vintage joint, whose knickknacks and heritage premises are a nod to the Baba-Nyonya culture. Deceptively simple, homespun dishes are finessed with spot-on seasoning and loads of punch. Local spices and produce are aptly used to outstanding effect. Otak-otak, or savoury fish egg custard, combines a velvety texture with just the right amount of heat.

Name: Ling Long
Address: L2-04, Block E, The Five@KPD, 49 Jalan Dungun, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Born into a Chinese family of chefs and formally trained in Gallic cuisine, the head chef strives to add a French spin to Chinese gourmet classics. The tasting menu embodies his culinary vision – crispy duck is aged for seven days making it juicy and tender; the must-try botan ebi dressed in fermented Chinese tofu sauce is marvellously ingenious. The chef occasionally pops out of the kitchen to serve the food himself and chat with diners.

Name: Bee See Heong
Address: 4166 Jalan Kampung Benggali, Butterworth, Seberang Perai, 12200, Malaysia
Description: Since 1966, this simple shop has been welcoming hungry guests who fancy Malaysian home-style cooking. Every dish is made à la minute and you can hear the wok sizzling after placing your order. Specialties include prawn curry – nice and thick with a good kick that goes well with the bouncy prawn. Fried threadfin with sweet black sauce is simply unmissable. The crispy fish fillet in a sticky caramel soy sauce is best enjoyed with steamed rice.

Name: La Suisse
Address: 17, Lorong Rahim Kajai 13, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
Description: Since their opening in 1992, husband-and-wife team Chef Mike Yap and Claudia have maintained alpine levels of excellence. Through their unwavering passion and hard work, they’ve created a restaurant with modern charms and old-fashioned styles that exudes genuine warmth – it’s like being invited into a family home for a meal. The heartwarming menu includes cheesy favourites like raclette and malakow, classic beef dishes and a veal that evokes waves of nostalgia.

Name: Feringgi Grill
Address: Mezzanine Level, Rasa Wing Lobby, Shangri-La's Rasa Sayang Resort and Spa, Batu Feringgi Beach, George Town, 11100, Malaysia
Description: Sweeping ocean views are nicely framed by brick-red curtains, walls and upholstery. Since 1973, Feringgi Grill has attracted a discerning following and the room retains its old-world romantic charm. On the menu, seafood and Aussie Wagyu beef are popular choices, and nothing starts a meal more theatrically than the tomato soup – prepared tableside and, flambéed with a splash of gin for extra fragrance. The private room seats 20, making it perfect for banquets.

Name: Sushi Ori
Address: Unit PG-01, GF, Podium Block, Menara Keck Seng, 203 Jalan Bukit Bintang, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
Description: Tucked away from the main street, Sushi Ori is famous locally for its sushi sets and omakase. The eponymous Japanese chef has lived in Malaysia for over 10 years and opened this traditional restaurant in 2019. Seasonal ingredients are delivered from Japan three times a week. The sushi rice comes from Akita and contains a secret mix of vinegar. With only eight seats at the counter, book well in advance for the personalised omakase experience. Private rooms are also available.

Name: Gai by Darren Chin
Address: 26A Lorong Datuk Sulaiman 1, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, 60000, Malaysia
Description: Gai (Thai for chicken) delivers tasty northern Thai food to the people of KL. The restaurant embodies the spirit of family and dishes are best shared for a group. Don’t miss Papa Suwit's tom saeb oxtail stew; a spicy-sour broth that boasts intense flavour from a mix of vegetables and herbs. The signature free-range chicken is grilled with a secret family recipe that emits a pleasant, chargrilled aroma. There are several seafood options too, including the flower crab.

Name: Li Yen
Address: 2F, The Ritz-Carlton, 168 Jalan Imbi, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
Description: Embroidered wall panelling, a semi-circular velvet banquette, and mirrors in bronze frames prime diners for a luxury dining experience. On the menu, classic Cantonese takes centre stage – think dim sum, honey-glazed BBQ Iberico pork, and roast goose. Also check out the chef’s recommendations on the first page, often featuring one hero ingredient prepared in a myriad of ways. Most items are available in different portion sizes.

Name: Vantador
Address: 38 Jalan 25/70A, Desa Sri Hartamas, Kuala Lumpur, 50480, Malaysia
Description: Vantador’s vintage yet modern interiors are drenched in soft lighting. Aussie and Spanish beef is either dry-aged for up to 35 days in salted butter, or vacuum-sealed and wet-aged in its own juices for 14 days. Steaks are precisely grilled over charcoal and wood to desired doneness, striking a fine balance between smoky and full-bodied, meaty flavours. Non-steak dishes are also available, together with meticulously prepared desserts.

Name: Marble 8
Address: 56F, Menara 3 Petronas, Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
Description: It takes a few lift rides to get to Marble 8, but as soon as you set foot in the dining room, you know it’s all worthwhile. The stunning skyline with the Twin Towers in the foreground is the perfect backdrop for a sumptuous meal featuring top-quality halal-certified Wagyu and Angus beef straight from Australia. Premium cuts are dry- or wet-aged for at least 21 days for deep flavours and tender texture, and then grilled to perfection.

Name: Air Itam Duck Rice
Address: Air Itam Wet Market, Jalan Pasar, George Town, 11500, Malaysia
Description: There are many shops in Penang selling roasted duck, but this stall's tender braised duck is packed with flavour, including soy sauce, anise and cinnamon. They also serve braised pork belly, pork intestines, egg and bean curd.

Name: Jit Seng Hong Kong Roasted Duck Rice
Description: The chef-owner started his own business after years as a chef in a larger restaurant. Open for three hours a day, the shop is famous for his roasted duck with deep-red skin and juicy meat, for which customers are prepared to queue. The roasted pork belly and char siew are tasty extras.

Name: Sambal
Description: Located on a buzzy, vibrant street, Sambal serves a tantalising mix of Asian and European flavours. There’s a unique twist to the beloved Lap Mei Fun, with fragrant rice, Chinese sausage, char siew (honey BBQ pork) and crispy pork lard. The Udang Entangled claypot boasts a rich, creamy broth infused with Chinese wine, served with glass noodles and succulent prawns. The standout dessert is taro purée, a modern adaption of creamy Teochew yam.

Name: Wagyu Kappo Yoshida
Address: Unit 3-48, 48F, Naza Tower, Platinum Park, 10 Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
Description: Based on Kappo cuisine, chef Yoshida's philosophy aims to establish a bond between the diner and the chef. Veteran chef Hattori dons the role of culinary host by tailoring this omakase beef experience at the counter for 12 guests in an intimate setting. This satisfying feast for beef lovers uses different parts of premium Wagyu from Japan in each dish. The chef also makes his own soba, onsen tamago and truffle ice cream.

Name: Chao Xuan
Description: The shophouse has a Chinese-style façade: a wooden plaque bearing the shop’s name, wood carvings and red lanterns. Young diners flock here in droves at lunch. Arrive early to beat the crowd. Kuih, or Teochew dumplings, are the must-try items seen on every table – try steamed or fried mangkuang kuih with yam bean filling. Yam cake; and char siew dry noodles are also delicious. Besides Teochew food, they also serve Taiwanese braised pork rice.

Name: Bali Hai Seafood Market
Description: Bali Hai has been feeding seafood lovers with the freshest critters and best quality fish for over ten years. Pick your own catch at the live fish tank by the entrance. Specify the way you want them cooked – in Teochew, Nyonya or even Thai style. The must-try “cereal prawns” are tossed in butter and milky oat powder that forms a crispy crust. Stir-fried crab with salted egg yolks that strikes a balance between umami and saltiness is not to be missed.

Name: Fook Cheow Cafe
Description: Located on a street corner, the signage is inconspicuous, but its popularity with locals mean that it can’t be missed. This simple eatery has been open for some 30 years, but only in the mornings, which makes it just the ticket to sample the local breakfast. The signature dish, koay teow th'ng, is rice noodle soup with fish balls, deep-fried garlic, shredded chicken and lettuce. The tasty soup broth is made from hen and pork bones.

Name: Ceki
Address: 11-A Jalan Sri Bahari, George Town, 10050, Malaysia
Description: Ceki is decorated in a traditional vibe with antique clothing and knick-knacks that tell a story from the past. The extensive menu is chiefly composed of home-cooked style Peranakan cuisine and features interesting dishes that can be hard to find, such as too kwa kean. The high-quality seafood menu features signature dishes such as assam pedas fish and sambal goreng prawns paired with a knockout herbal sauce. With only a few large tables, booking is advisable.

Name: Flower Mulan
Description: The café sits atop the florist of the same name and serves a small menu of Paranakan food. Sambal tumis ikan pari, or sambal fish curry, is rich and aromatic, whereas assam prawn strikes the perfect balance between sweet and sour. Dimly-lit rooms are decorated in maximalist style with a Chinese theme – red lanterns, flowers, art, sculptures and patterns cover every surface. Intimate service from the friendly owner makes diners feel right at home.

Name: Skillet
Address: Lot 1-01, Level 1, Menara Hap Seng 3, Jalan P. Ramlee, Kuala Lumpur, 50250, Malaysia
Description: (The restaurant is relocated to Jalan P. Ramlee.) The classy room boasts a black colour scheme punctuated by brass trims and details, befitting the exquisite European fare it serves. Though the menu often changes, try the duck breast if it’s available. Cherry Valley duck is aged for at least three days before it’s seared on the grill for crispy skin and juicy pink flesh. The tangy cherry jus aptly cuts through the richness. The chef’s chocolate dessert is the perfect way to end a meal. The lunch set menu offers great value.

Name: Sushi Taka
Address: 3A, The St. Regis, 6 Jalan Stesen Sentral 2, Kuala Lumpur Sentral, Kuala Lumpur, 50470, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: Since 2016, this upmarket sushi-ya in a prestigious hotel has been prized for their authentic sushi made with the freshest and most seasonal fish flown in from Japan. The Japanese chef is specific about every detail, including the sushi rice from a town in Niigata. To experience his culinary vision in full glory, opt for the omakase menu with 10 nigiri sushi, appetisers and sashimi. Oenophiles should check out the well-curated sake list.

Name: Passage Thru India
Address: 4 Jalan Delima, Off Jalan Bukit Bintang, Imbi, Kuala Lumpur, 50400, Malaysia
Description: Established in 1993, Passage Thru India catches the eye with its artistic interior as much as its cooking. The owner-artist painted the murals on the walls and ceilings to create a technicoloured yet intimate cottage feel. The sizeable menu offers a good variety of traditional Indian favourites, including tandoori, naan and roti from the coal-fired oven. The aromatic biriyani rice puts you right at home and goes well with any of the tapas-sized plates.

Name: Tenmasa
Address: Unit 3.3 (annexe), 2F, Tower 1, Platinum Park, 11 Persiaran KLCC, Kuala Lumpur, 50088, Malaysia
Description: Watch the chefs weave their culinary magic from the 10-seater counter, but book in advance. The omakase menus showcase classic signature dishes and seasonal specials made with fresh local produce and high-quality Japanese imports. The seafood and vegetable tempura are lightly battered and deep fried for a light crisp coating. The signature uni with shiso leaf comprises fresh, sweet uni from Hokkaido, served on a tempura shiso leaf.

Name: Yun House
Address: 5B, Four Seasons Hotel, 145 Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur, 50450, Malaysia
Description: Set under high ceilings, this remarkable dining room with nice views is a great choice for both casual and formal gatherings. A specialist in Cantonese cuisine, the chef has lived in Southeast Asia for many years. His concise menu is pork free with a quality selection of seafood and dim sum. Don’t miss the daily Inspirational Soup or fresh prawns simmered with glass noodles. Wrap up your meal with a crispy red bean pancake. The signature duck must be ordered in advance.

Name: The Brasserie
Address: 2F, The St. Regis, 6 Jalan Stesen Sentral 2, Kuala Lumpur Sentral, Kuala Lumpur, 50470, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The chef draws from experience working with some of the biggest names in London and in fine dining restaurants across Europe and Asia to create a French contemporary menu with Mediterranean influences and a touch of Asian. They serve a five to seven-course tasting menu, à la carte and plenty of vegetarian options. The beverage list is outstanding, with a good selection of wine and spirits to be paired with the food. The Sunday brunch offers a huge range of fresh seafood.

Name: Ali Nasi Lemak Daun Pisang
Address: Sri Weld Food Court, 19 Lebuh Pantai, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
Description: This halal stall only sells nasi lemak: the national dish of coconut milk rice wrapped in banana leaf, topped with sambal and one of the six toppings. Try anchovies with a hard-boiled egg. And go easy on the fiery sambal.

Name: The Pinn
Description: The Pinn moved to this spot opposite Lee Jetty in 2023. Like the room, the menu is small but powerful, offering Malaysian-Chinese dishes, dumplings and even some Taiwanese and Indonesian titbits. Homemade mackerel fish balls are their speciality and you can order noodles on top to make it a complete meal. The food tends to be slightly on the sweet side to suit local tastebuds.

Name: Lao San Tong Bah Kut Teh
Address: 1 Lorong Perniagaan Melur, Jalan Raja Uda, Butterworth, Seberang Perai, 12300, Malaysia
Description: The heady scent of bak kut teh will draw you into this friendly neighbourhood joint. Since 2005, they have been serving their own secret recipe in sizzling hot claypot – the pork falls off the bone; the broth strikes a balance between meaty umami and herbal depth. If you can’t get enough, ask them to refill the broth for free. Order it with pork offal if you like organ meats. On top of that, spicy food lovers shouldn’t miss their spicy pork stir-fry.

Name: Soleil
Address: Lot-13A & 15, 2F, Damansara City Mall, 6 Jalan Damanlela, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: The European-trained chef has no hesitation in mixing trans-continental influences. His thoughtful use of Asian ingredients delivers a good variety of contemporary European cuisine with local characteristics. Dishes like the Hokkaido scallops with tagliatelle and cod roe butter are good examples of the chef’s deft harmonisation of East and West. From classic dishes to modern cuisine, there’s something for everyone. Take your pick from a broad selection of wines.

Name: Frangipaani
Address: The Republik, Lot No.M.03, Mezzanine Floor, Jalan Medan Setia 1, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: The softly lit interior, outfitted in warm wood and tan leather, sets a rustic mood, while the terrace is relaxing and cosy. Since 2019, the kitchen team has been delivering tasty traditional cuisine, tweaked to suit local tastebuds. Go for the vegetarian samosa chaat and the tandoori specialities. The raan dum biriyani, or whole lamb leg cooked in basmati rice, is great for sharing.

Name: Jwala
Address: E-02-01, Block E, The Five@KPD, 49 Jalan Dungun, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, 50490, Malaysia
Description: Named after the Sanskrit word for fire, Jwala is famous for chargrilled dishes cooked in its custom-built tandoori oven. Familiar ingredients like chicken and lamb chop are presented alongside less common offerings such as croissant, cottage cheese and hamachi collar. Tandoori tiger prawns marinated in mustard oil, yoghurt and spices, in particular, boast deep, rich flavours. The knockout curries are seasoned with local fruits and herbs.

Name: Bite N Eat Dindigul Biriyani
Description: Since 2014, this simple shop in Little India has been serving authentic dishes from all over India. The namesake signature biriyani is a rice dish with Indian spices and a must-try for all. Pair it with kongu nadu kozhi fry, or spicy dry-fried chicken with grated coconut, a speciality from Tamil Nadu in southern India that imparts tangy flavours. Portion sizes are not huge; perfect for solo diners and small groups. They are closed on Tuesdays randomly.

Name: BM Yam Rice
Address: 7 Jalan Murthy, Bukit Mertajam, Seberang Perai, 14000, Malaysia
Description: Since opening its doors in 2006, this shop has been serving the owner’s family recipe. There is only one thing on the menu: yam rice with pork soup – you can choose to have pork offal in the soup or not. The yam rice is nicely cooked, with strong shrimp flavour. The pork broth is briny-sweet and the pickled cabbage gives it a tangy depth. The offal is cooked to the perfect texture while the pork balls are peppery and flavoursome.

Name: Kayra
Address: F-8, 1F, Bangsar Village 1, Jalan Telawi 1, Bangsar, Kuala Lumpur, 59100, Malaysia
Description: As the culinary heart of southwest India, and productive capital of peppers and spices since ancient times, Kerala has had a profound influence on the dishes here. Kayra builds on Kerala’s venerable traditions, serving contemporary recipes with a rich mix of spices – central to the cuisine's identity – and modern aesthetics. Beef features prominently here. Prices are reasonable and the industrial interior with brick design gives a modern and simple impression.

Name: Kebaya Dining Room
Description: The restored heritage building is home to a lavish restaurant with a high-ceilinged room, crystal chandeliers and scarlet velvet drapes. The concise menu showcases a good selection of Peranakan cooking alongside some vegetarian offerings. Meat lovers may try tamarind glazed grass-fed beef from down under, or the prawn geng curry that can be made vegetarian. Round it out with Markisa semifreddo. Also check out the competitively priced wine list.

Name: Cilantro
Address: MiCasa All Suite Hotel, 368B Jalan Tun Razak, Taman U Thant, Kuala Lumpur, 50400, Malaysia
Description: At lunch, it serves unfussy French bistro fare. The tables and chairs are covered in a cheerful yellow fabric, emblematic of the friendly vibe. It sports a 100% Gallic ambiance with L’atelier by Cilantro. By night, it morphs into a fine dining venue whose tasting menu boasts eight Japanese-French fusion courses. Quality produce is meticulously crafted into spot-on dishes like its signature capellini or Japanese Wagyu.

Name: Fatty Loh Chicken Rice
Address: 21 Jalan Fettes, Tanjung Bungah, George Town, 11200, Malaysia
Description: Into the third generation, this shop famous for Hainanese chicken rice also serves other Southeast Asian favourites. Chicken that boasts springy skin and velvety flesh can be ordered in halves or standard portions.

Name: Tok Tok Mee Bamboo Noodle
Description: “Tok Tok” is an onomatopoeia of the sound made by a chef when kneading noodle dough with a bamboo pole, a tradition still practised at the entrance of this shop. Cantonese wonton noodle soup is a must-try for its bouncy noodles and flavoursome shrimp filling. Blanched noodles tossed with dried shrimp roe, and Cantonese barbecue meats are also popular. Also try their Chinese pastry – both BBQ pork pie and pandan kaya dumplings are terrific.

Name: Nuits
Address: 68 Tongren Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The bistro may not have a big shopfront, but its bright orange sign and full-height windows more than compensate in terms of impact. Named after Côte de Nuits in Burgundy, it serves a nice selection from that wine region. Head to the cellar to talk to the sommelier. The menu is mostly classic French and the signature beef tartare is laced with lightly cooked geoduck and oyster liquor, reflecting the bounty of sea and land.

Name: Chaimen Hui
