Address: Shop S-L4-04, Stone Zone, Taikoo Li Qiantan, Lane 500, Dongyu Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This outpost of its famed namesake in Chengdu operates in a sleekly furnished space – the centrepiece is no doubt the oversized starburst sculpture over the circular counter. The kitchen is run by a team from the parent restaurant, and their Sichuan menu showcases creative fare and the best produce from around the world. Try the wild-caught yellow croaker braised with pickled chillies, and preserved spare ribs and sausage with Sichuan peppercorns.

Name: Jardin de Jade (West Nanjing Road)
Address: 3F, Chong Hing Finance Center, 288 West Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: It’s located in a shiny office block overlooking People’s Park, so it’s not altogether surprising to find the local business community flocking here at lunchtime – although this can lead to the service team becoming a little stretched. On offer at this big, stylish restaurant is a menu of Shanghainese dishes and, in particular, Jiangnan cuisine. Dishes are presented in a modern style and menus are supplemented by seasonal specials.

Name: Stonesal
Address: 1M, 9 Donghu Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The owner-chef is a culinary veteran with 20 years of experience. He opened Stonesal in 2017 specialising in quality U.S. and Australian steaks house-aged in the Himalayan salt chamber next to the kitchen. Top picks include USDA prime T-bone from Creekstone Farm and M9+ Wagyu from Mayura Station Farm on the Limestone Coast in South Australia. On top of that, their spicy beef soup is simmered for hours to build layers of flavours.

Name: The Meat
Address: 2F, Kerry Hotel Pudong, 1388 Huamu Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The gloriously blunt name chosen by this hotel restaurant says it all. The beef – mostly Australian, is served in a characteristic steakhouse vibe, sporting antlers and booth seating. On your way in, you will see the room where the beef is aged for 25 to 31 days. The signature dish is New York pressed steak: Aussie Tajima Wagyu sirloin smothered in melted Raclette cheese, served with bourbon whisky sauce.

Name: Sui Tang Li
Address: 2F, The Middle House Residences, 366 Shimen Yi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This modern, sun-drenched hotel restaurant is known for its host of regional dim sum with a creative twist, such as xiao long bao with marbled skin, and novelty bites made with Iberico ham and beetroot juice. The Yunnan duck tagine with Sichuan pepper boasts delicate flesh and a garlicky kick; the accompanying house-made duck dumplings are simply divine. Wine and literature lovers should check out the poetic wine list with rhyming verses.

Name: Dining Room
Address: 87F, Park Hyatt, 100 Century Avenue, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This high-ceilinged room with full-length windows affords panoramic river views, while the home-style furniture, warm lighting and booth seating make for a cosy feel. On the menu, Jiangzhe classics meet creative recipes that are rarely found elsewhere, such as steamed belt fish with fermented grains. Nicely pleated xiao long bao with umami-loaded soupy filling are simply unmissable – as are the appetisers.

Name: Wan Yan (Changning)
Address: Inside Jin Jiang Cypress Hotel, Block 8, 2419 Hungqiao Road, Changning, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Brace yourself for nostalgia aplenty: velvet tufted chairs, walls covered in vintage blue bricks, art pieces from around the world…Most ingredients are shipped from Anhui, including mouldy tofu – a speciality you can’t miss. Wine-scented fermented mandarin fish is another classic slightly adapted to suit the local palate. On top of the à la carte menu that covers most bases of Huizhou cuisine, you can also have one tailored in advanced.

Name: Char
Address: 29-31F, Indigo Hotel, 585 Zhongshan Dong Er Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Great views are a given as this large steakhouse is located on the top floor of the Indigo hotel. It’s also a warm and intimate space, thanks to the rustic wooden ceiling and the big, comfortable armchairs. The menu offers a large choice of meats, with the highlight being the Blackmore Wagyu from Australia. The Char Bar is an equally pleasant spot for a drink before or after dinner.

Name: Mercado 505
Address: 505 North Wulumuqi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Judging by its name, this restaurant on a corner strives to create the buzzing vibe of a market; judging by the blue and white stripes on its sign, it has a nautical theme. Yes and yes. Imported seafood such as live oysters, scampi, carabinero shrimp and baby eel are deftly prepared in myriad ways. The signature Spanish seafood stew loaded with umami has to be pre-ordered. You can enjoy alfresco dining on a sunny day or reserve a private room for groups.

Name: Lao Xing Xian
Address: 5F, Parkson, 918 Middle Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Xian, or umami, is the fifth core flavour of food; it also means “fresh” in Chinese. At Lao Xing Xian, the owner aims to serve the freshest seafood, caught by his own fleet in the East China Sea that is deftly crafted with a knockout umami kick. The fish is neatly displayed for diners to choose – beltfish and yellow croaker taste best when steamed plain. Braised wild rice paddy eel is lightly seasoned to accentuate its natural flavour.

Name: Kanpai Classic (Huangpu)
Address: 5F, Bund 5, 20 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If anything demonstrates the international nature of restaurants it’s this: a Shanghai restaurant from a Taiwanese group, specialising in Australian Wagyu beef that also serves Japanese dishes. There are 14 cuts of premium Australian Wagyu, along with other meats and seafood, and each table has its own charcoal stove. The inexperienced shouldn’t be afraid of asking the staff for assistance. The house-brand sake makes a great accompaniment.

Name: Min He Nan Huan Xi
Address: 2F, MIXC East Alley, 111 North Shanxi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The F&B group has been active in Fujian Province for over 30 years and its Shanghai outpost sports a classy décor. The menu features a line-up of lavish recipes, but even simple dishes like radish rice can be a highlight – long-grain rice is cooked with dried seafood, pork meat and bones for impressive sweetness and depth. Another iconic dish is layered chitterlings that delivers a gutsy mix of texture and flavour. The tea menu is worth exploring.

Name: Cellar to Table
Address: 20 Donghu Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: With wine glass racks hanging above the communal tables, it’s clear that wine is at the core of this industrial-style bistro. The food was also created with wine in mind. Small bites, like drunken pigeon basted in sherry sauce, and grilled piquillo stuffed with crabmeat mousse, are best enjoyed with the French and Italian wines on the extensive list. There are also dishes for sharing, like koshihikari rice in cast iron pot with foie gras and garlic bits.

Name: Frasca
Address: 1F, The Middle House Residences, 366 Shimen Yi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This fashionable restaurant is part of the stylish hotel next to the HKRI Taikoo Hui shopping mall. The chef team deliver authentic Italian classics with home-style flavours. The pasta menu is especially worth exploring, with the al dente handcrafted ravioli standing out. Try also their home baked breads, Pinsa Romana and meats roasted on the Josper grill. Check out the wine list for its lovely selection of Italian vintages.

Name: 1515 West Chophouse
Address: 4F, Jing An Shangri-La Hotel, 1218 Middle Yan'an Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: They’ve certainly nailed the classic American look at this nicely styled chophouse. Start with a cocktail in the masculine, wood panelled bar before passing by the inviting bakery into the restaurant. All the favourite steakhouse dishes are here, from Caesar salad mixed at the table to steak tartare and cheesecake. However, it’s the grill that takes centre stage – the various cuts of dry-aged Australian beef are chargrilled to perfection.

Name: Hai Wei Guan (Jingan)
Address: 18 Kangding Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: It may have been around since 2004 but this restaurant feels modern and cosy after a makeover in 2017. The owner believes in the motto ‘innovation while respecting tradition’ and champions a new spin on Shanghainese classics using ingenious creativity. His signature crispy roast chicken with Périgord truffle that imitates Nakhi cooking needs pre-ordering. Steamed hairy crabs marinated in Maotai liquor and herbs for 48 hours exude intoxicating aromas.

Name: Shanghai Club
Address: L-418, 4F, North Building, HKRI Taikoo Hui, 789 West Nanjing Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A premium brand from the Jardin de Jade Group, the restaurant serves old Shanghai classics with an emphasis on finesse and attention to detail. Walnut-crusted duck fillet square in bean paste is a rare gem that is painstaking to make. Live seafood is another highlight on the menu, while some Cantonese dim sum are served at lunch. Ask the servers about the seasonal offerings which truly embodying the essence of Shanghainese cooking.

Name: Arva
Address: 6161 Yuanjiang Road, Minhang, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The passionate chef advocates a farm-to-table philosophy and cooks quality ingredients à la minute. Try his ravioli from among the dazzling array of homemade pasta on offer. While the airy dining room is cosy and elegant, the al fresco barbecue lunch at weekends exudes a backyard party vibe. It’s nestled in a remote luxury resort, so driving here is the best option. Reservations are mandatory and a security check is undertaken at the hotel entrance.

Name: Charbon
Address: Shop 606, 6F, iapm, 999 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Celebrity chef Paul Pairet's latest venture in Shanghai is housed in a wood-rich space with brass finishes. Chargrilled kebabs are seasoned with Middle Eastern or Southeast Asian spices, and served with a dip made to complement the ingredients. Try frogs' legs with peanut satay sauce that marry springy texture and rich nutty depth. Pair this with Indonesian oxtail soup and citrus smoky rice. Finish off with ice cream in an array of flavours.

Name: De Xing Guan (Guangdong Road)
Address: 471 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Founded in 1878, this two-storey noodle shop is something of a local landmark thanks to its gilded sign and elaborate façade. Chefs start work at 4am, making noodles and dim sum from scratch. The ground floor serves 20 different noodle and rice dishes, including the famous three-treasure soup noodles (fried eel, fried fish and pork hock). The dining room upstairs offers more comfort and a bigger Shanghainese menu, from soups to hot dishes and dim sum.

Name: Villa Le Bec - Bistro 321
Address: 321 Xinhua Road, Changning, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A lovely renovated villa, dating from 1924, is home to this French bistro. It’s divided into several rooms, all decorated differently: a simple bistro occupies the former garage; one cosy dining room has a charming beamed ceiling, another has a fireplace, and the garden terrace is a delightful spot on warm days. The classic bistro dishes include an excellent pâté en croute and côte de boeuf prepared barbecue style.

Name: Épices & Foie Gras
Address: A1-05, 309 Hankou Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: It’s no great surprise that foie gras is the speciality here. It comes in different preparations, so try the ‘Trilogy’ if you want to sample various types. This ‘modern French bistrot’ is run by a young French couple and they wisely also serve other classic Gallic dishes, like roasted lamb rack with crispy pistachio and a light garlic infused cream sauce. Lunch sets offer exceptional value. The main dining room is somewhat diminutive but it is pleasantly decorated.

Name: Les Nuages
Address: 57F, East Tower, Raffles City The Bund, 999 Dongdaming Road, Hongkou, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Sitting atop a skyscraper, this aptly named restaurant boasts high ceiling and commands breathtaking river views. Open for afternoon tea and dinner only, it serves Western classics like beef steaks dry-aged in-house. But it’s the chef’s menu melding Chinese ingredients with European techniques that truly surprises. Try deep-fried seaweed meatballs with runny crab roe and vinegar centres, and Chocolate Trio styled after Shanghainese retro snacks.

Name: Hong Yu Fang
Address: B1-06, Mix 6, 686 South Xizang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A household name in Huangpu district, this place has been around for 10-plus years. Regulars keep flocking to its new shop since it moved into a shopping mall. Open in the morning only, it always attracts a queue of customers coming for a hearty meal. With their juicy, generous pork filling, Shanghai classic potstickers are a must-try. Cabbage rice with sausage and salted pork is another hit, each grain of rice enrobed in creamy lard.

Name: Shi He Yuan (Pudong)
Address: L4-02 & 03, IFC Mall, 8 Century Avenue, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This sleek restaurant is the brainchild of a celebrity chef and the founder of the upmarket F&B group Yong Fu. The menu is partly Shandongese and partly Beijingese, reinvented with modern techniques and novel presentations. The signature dish, Mr Duan’s delicious fish head, boasts silky flesh in a mildly spicy sauce, best eaten with deep-fried dough sticks. There are also five private rooms perfect for business entertainment.

Name: Nan Xing Yuan
Address: Building 12, 1728 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Helmed by a team of Sichuan chefs, this restaurant takes a deposit upon reservation and serves only tailored menus that need to be pre-ordered. A typical menu includes classics such as fuqi feipian, and pork belly layered with red bean paste over glutinous rice, alongside dishes that feature premium ingredients like fish maw, sea cucumber and scallops. The dining room is spacious and private rooms are available on the upper floors.

Name: Shanghai Tavern
Address: 1F, Shanghai Edition, 199 East Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It may be located within the contemporary backdrop of the Edition Hotel but the Shanghai Tavern celebrates a bygone era; the elegant space shows off its original 20C heritage and there are potted palms, waiters in white jackets, a champagne chariot and even a dessert trolley. The menu covers all bases from clam Rockefeller to steak from the Josper grill and even mac & cheese. Keen service and a soundtrack all add to its appeal.

Name: Jade on 36
Address: 36F, Grand Tower, Pudong Shangri-La Hotel, 33 Fucheng Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Even when this longstanding restaurant gets a makeover, nothing is really able to compete with the stunning views of Huangpu and the river. With an experienced French chef at the helm, the menu ushers in some sophisticated creations; they may be deeply rooted in traditions, but they are also jazzed up by modern touches and subtle Mediterranean influences. Blue lobster can be ordered in three servings and the lunch menu offers good value.

Name: Summer Palace
Address: 3F, Jing An Shangri-La Hotel, 1218 Middle Yan'an Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This smart and sumptuously decorated Cantonese restaurant is divided into three distinct areas, each serving a different speciality. You'll find dim sum in the Pantry, claypot dishes in the Lantern and sophisticated Cantonese classics in the Imperial. Every facet of Cantonese cuisine is covered, alongside seasonal offerings such as hairy crabmeat and roe for a Shanghai twist. The private rooms are impressive, as is the wine list.

Name: Lin Jiang Yan
Address: 216 Fucheng Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Remodelled from a heritage building circa 1902, this restaurant is perfect for banquets and entertainment. Along with the main room, there are also private rooms with river views. The executive chef, who used to work for a famous hotel in Shanghai, takes care of the Jiangzhe cooking, while dishes made with luxury ingredients and dried seafood are the strong suits of the Cantonese chef. Try braised three treasures with black truffle.

Name: Xin Yuan Lou
Address: Building No.4, InterContinental Ruijin Hotel, 118 Ruijin Er Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A 1920s villa plays host to this Cantonese restaurant boasting plenty of old-world charm thanks to its period furniture, fireplace and Chinese artwork. It’s spread over two floors and includes a bar, a lounge, a tea room and several private rooms. The menu is mostly Cantonese with some Shanghainese dishes. Try marinated meats, roast goose, salt-baked chicken or char siu pork. Seasonal offerings, like the mushroom menu in autumn, need pre-ordering.

Name: Yong Feng Mian Guan
Address: 320 Hankou Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Now run by the second generation, this family-run halal noodle shop has been around since 1962. Forced to close due to urban renewal, many regretted the demise of the original venue. Recently re-opened in a new spot, the original kitchen team proudly delivers its distinctive culinary score. The signature red-braised lamb noodles are served in curry beef stock or tossed in scallion oil. Either way, order an over-easy egg so the yolk spills over the noodles.

Name: Sir Elly's
Address: 13F, The Peninsula Hotel, Bund 32, 32 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Named after the hotel's founder, the opulent space punctuated by red accents commands gorgeous river views. The upscale ambiance makes this a perfect venue for a date. The kitchen turns local ingredients into original creations with bold flavours, dramatic plating and modern Asian twists. The substantial wine list will keep any oenophile happy. If you're not quite ready to call it a night, consider heading to the rooftop bar for digestifs.

Name: Yè Shanghai
Address: 3F, Infinitus Mall, 168 Hubin Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Though moved into a shopping mall, the grey-brick façade is reminiscent of Shikumen architecture style. In stark contrast, the interior sports velvet sofas in gold and modern art for a touch of glamour. Start your night with creative cocktails from the bar. Then sample their Shanghainese classics like braised pork belly, sautéed shrimps with wild garlic, or xiao long bao. Try also hairy crab dishes such as stuffed crab shell when available.

Name: Pop
Address: 7F, Bund 3, 3 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Blue and white sofas work well with the wood and marble décor to exude a casual, yet elegant vibe, but it’s the breathtaking river views from the terrace that leave everyone in awe. Classic European choices abound on the menu, especially grilled meats and seafood. Try the house-made foie gras pâté, or pasta with black truffle. Pop also serves brunch every morning – so you can start your day with bacon and eggs with gorgeous vistas in the gentle morning sun.

Name: The Pine
Address: 333 Changle Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Both the manicured garden and exquisite interior of this historical British-style mansion are charming, with many classical and modern art pieces on display. The young chef shows solid skills in traditional European cooking and gives it a new spin, with Chinese seasoning and produce. Chargrilled Australian Wagyu steak is served with braised beef sinew and a mildly spicy sauce; the soupy rice with pickles features coral grouper fillet.

Name: Scarpetta
Address: 33 Mengzi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This two-storey restaurant takes its name from the act of using bread to mop up the last bit of sauce left on the plate. Homemade pizza and pasta, such as pizza vongole, and other specialities like Wagyu carpaccio topped with shaved black truffle slices, mean you’ll certainly not want to waste anything. The last facelift in 2018 left the dining room with a warm and romantic ambiance, making it an ideal choice for a date.

Name: River Drunk
Address: 5F, Wanda Reign Hotel, 538 Zhongshan Dong Er Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A recurring motif of white Yulan, the city flower of Shanghai, is part of the lavish decoration here, along with opulent materials such as glass and jade. The menu, as its name suggests, is geared slightly towards river fish lovers, with dishes such as steamed dried river fish Ningbo-style, puffed rice in seafood soup with leafy greens, and Xihu pastry with Zha Cai filling. Each private room is named after a flower, with matching themed cutlery.

Name: Xuji Seafood (Xuhui)
Address: 500 Zhaojiabang Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Since 1999, the Hunan brand has been expanding its footprint across the nation, and this multi-storey branch is its Shanghai flagship. Thanks to close ties with fishermen and farms, locally and globally, it secures sources for the best-quality and freshest seafood. Try the live scallops from the East China Sea blanched at your table in a boiling, milky sea perch stock. Xuji glass noodles in a casserole are the Hunan speciality you can't miss.

Name: Jamoteca
Address: S-L3-03, Stone Zone, Taikoo Li Qiantan, Lane 500, Dongyu Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The wood-rich room benefits from full-length windows and is furnished with style and finesse. The Barcelonian chef excels in authentic Spanish cooking, ranging from tapas in small-plate portions to the must-try seafood paella meant for sharing. The deconstructed gazpacho is disguised as a garden salad; Iberico pork cap seared to rare doneness boasts a juicy centre and milky aromas. On a nice day, ask for a table on the expansive terrace.

Name: Mr & Mrs Bund
Address: 6F, Bund 18, 18 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A key player in the city’s dining scene for over a decade, Chef Paul Pairet’s brasserie never gets old. Lovely service, great music, a terrific wine list and bags of French joie de vivre make dining here quite an experience. The clean, modern room in a former bank circa 1922 is dotted with 18C French-inspired furniture. The menu offers a vast choice of French classics, some displaying a subtle Asian twist, some in sizes meant for sharing.

Name: Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan
Address: No 22, Lane 494, Middle Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: To the passer-by, this simple shop hidden in an alley on Huaihai Road looks pretty much like any other. What sets it apart, however, are the authentic noodles it serves. It is particularly famous for its shredded pork noodles with scallions, its yellow croaker noodles with pickled vegetables, and its deep-fried pork chops. You can also enjoy congee, rice and snacks – and it stays open 24 hours a day.

Name: Le Patio & La Famille (Huangpu)
Address: 216 Middle Sichuan Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The first time you come to this restaurant you may find yourself walking past a couple of times as its non-descript façade makes it easy to miss. The decorative style inside is influenced by the look of Shanghai’s coffee shops in the 1930s – but, somewhat surprisingly, this is actually a Hangzhou restaurant. The dishes to try are steamed grass carp in vinegar sauce; pork trotter and duck casserole; and braised pork belly in soy sauce.

Name: Shaughnessy
Address: No.2201-2202, 22F, East Huaihai International Mansion, 45-49 East Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Sitting atop a skyscraper, this American-style steakhouse commands vistas of the Bund and the Huangpu skyline. The menu stars premium cuts of suitably marbled Black Angus beef, all dry-aged in-house for 28 to 180 days. The steaks are artfully carved tableside and served with pan jus. If you’re not a red meat fan, you could opt for the aged squab which is something of a rarity. For more privacy, consider booking your own room.

Name: Royal China Club
Address: 3F, Bund 5, 20 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Operated by London’s Royal China Group, this Cantonese restaurant specialises in dried seafood like abalone and fish, along with other assorted seafood dishes. The quality of the seafood is good, with some of the ingredients imported from the UK, such as lobsters from Scotland. Dim sum is popular at lunch and, during Chinese festivals, handmade products like glutinous rice dumplings and mooncakes are provided.

Name: Wang Lu
Address: 01-02, 3F, New Bund 31 Mall, No.15, Lane 666, West Haiyang Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The room sports a modern Chinese vibe, dotted with framed orange scarves and table mats in matching equestrian motifs. To suit the local palate, the kitchen dials down the heat slightly, but the food still packs an authentic Jiangxi kick. Rich, flavoursome double-steamed soft-shelled tortoise with fish maw is served according to a ritual that symbolises good fortune. Jiangxi-style three-cup chicken boasts firm flesh and perfect caramelisation.

Name: Zhou She (Minhang)
Address: Shop 116, Hongqiao Lihpao Plaza, No.16-101, Lane 318, Suhong Road, Minhang, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: In Hongqiao district close to a train station and airport sits this restaurant, a popular choice among travellers. The head chef is a Shanghai native who respects traditions but is still willing to explore other Chinese regional flavours. His menu is heavily based on Shanghainese, with occasional Cantonese and Huaiyang offerings. Try his marinated pigeon with green Sichuan peppercorns, and Yanduxian soup with braised pork balls.

Name: Canton Disco
Address: 2F, The Shanghai Edition, 199 East Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: A fully-fledged homage to Hong Kong’s discotheque era, neon signs included, may not be to everyone’s taste, but Canton Disco somehow manages to pull it off with sophistication and little cheese factor. In addition to Cantonese menu staples such as dim sum, double-boiled soups, and sweet and sour pork, the experienced chef also puts on his creative hat for some novel items. The various set menus are great for larger parties.

Name: Yong Xing
Address: No. 1, Lane 626, Middle Fuxing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This cozy little gem is hidden in a tiny alley and its non-descript façade makes it even harder to find. An archway, fireplace and red-brick wallpaper - reminiscent of someone’s home from a by-gone era - set the tone for the warm welcoming service. Yong Xing serves delicious home-style Chinese food at wallet-friendly prices and is hugely popular among locals. Try steamed perch with shredded ginger in Jiangdong style.

Name: Mercato
Address: 6F, Bund 3, 3 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: From Jean-Georges Vongerichten comes this lively Italian restaurant with Mediterranean twists. The interior sees an eclectic mix of natural materials matched with urban savviness. On the menu, family-style dishes come in sizes large enough for sharing. Signatures such as wood oven-roasted whole Icelandic halibut, and porcini-crusted salmon with warm leek vinaigrette and herbs, are well worth trying. Also ask about the chef’s specials.

Name: Hokkien Huay Kuan
Address: 5F, Xintiandi Style I, 177 Madang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The interior is inspired by Fujian-style ink paintings, with water features dividing the room into zones. On the menu, premium produce from the province is deftly prepared by Fujian natives for the most authentic experience possible. Try the signature Shuizhu seafood trio – live prawns, razor clams and giant red squid are blanched in a mild mala broth over a bed of pickled broccoli stems, cucumber and bean sprouts for crunch and tartness.

Name: Narisawa
Address: L7-05, 1000Trees, 600 Moganshan Road, Putuo, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Narisawa brings Japan’s sustainable, naturalistic satoyama dining experience to Shanghai. The head chef has worked with chef Narisawa for 17 years and crafts the same menu as the Tokyo sister establishment, but with Chinese twists. Its iconic “Bread of the forest” is fermented and baked in a stone pot tableside and infused with white tea from Fujian. Chinese ham jazzes up the umami of the chicken and shellfish consommé.

Name: Shi Chuan Fei Chuan (Xuhui)
Address: Shop 603, 6F, iapm, 999 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The kitchen reimagines Sichuan cooking using top-notch produce from around the world, finessed by exquisite plating. Duck and pork tripe soup with pickled radish delivers unsurpassed umami alongside tang and tartness. Fluffy hand-made pork buns burst with the addictive aromas of spiced chilli oil. Cool down your palate with house-made bingfen: transparent jelly noodles made from shoofly seeds in brown sugar syrup. Booking recommended.

Name: Stiller
Address: No.22-23, Lane 181, Taicang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This establishment, which chef Stiller launched before the gourmet Taian Table, is less formal and starched than its high-flying sibling. Splashes of orange lend the space youthful energy and the dishes, made with seasonal quality produce, are to share. The aptly entitled “German inspired” section features dishes inspired by the chef’s culinary roots. Smoked eel on toast with silky scrambled egg on crisp sourdough is deeply satisfying.

Name: Dong Ping Chao
Address: 1 Dongping Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This restaurant in a century-old heritage building reinterprets Chaozhou fare with refined touches and local twists. Quality ingredients, especially seafood, are shipped from Chaoshan region twice a day to ensure freshness. Menus are tailor-made at least one day ahead and there is no à la carte ordering. The speciality crispy-skin braised sea cucumber provides a nice contrast of texture, with a subtle hint of peanut butter in the abalone sauce.

Name: Madam Zhu's Kitchen (Wanhangdu Road)
Address: L3-20, Yueda 889 Plaza, 889 Wanhangdu Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Although it’s located in a shopping mall, the exposed brick, tiles, bookcases and stained glass window add genuine warmth and colour to this large room. Sichuan and Shanghainese dishes are the mainstay of the menu and dishes are simply prepared, full of flavour and affordably priced. Look out for Madam Zhu’s specialty roast duck; steamed chicken in scallion oil sauce; and fried smoked pomfret in soy sauce.

Name: Hang Yuen Hin (Xuhui)
Address: Xujiahui Park, 290 Wanping Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant opened in the lungs of the city and the lush greenery outside the windows works magic with the décor to make a relaxing ambiance. The chef has worked in both Guangzhou and Hong Kong, putting his know-how to good use in the authentic Cantonese dishes that are also low in salt and oil. Signature dishes include almond-crusted fried shrimp rolls, and crispy pigeon. Dim sum with family and friends is also a delight here.

Name: Beef & Liberty (Jingan)
Address: Shop 111, Shanghai Centre, 1376 West Nanjing Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: For those times when only a burger will do, there is Beef & Liberty. New Zealand grass-fed beef is ground in-house twice a day, in time for lunch and dinner, and then served in homemade buns. The ribeye burger boasts a juicy, 220g patty cooked medium or medium-well, alongside caramelised onions, mustard mayo and cheese. Their super-rich milkshake, made with just ice cream and whipping cream, is also well worth a try.

Name: Shanghai
Address: 2F, Central Hotel, 555 Jiujiang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Perched on the second floor of the Central Hotel is this sister restaurant to the famed hairy crab restaurant, Wang Bao He. You’ll find this speciality here in season but it’s equally known for its authentic Shanghainese cooking. Their classic dishes use quality ingredients and are prepared with care. One highlight is the house-manufactured yellow rice wine, which you can buy to take home with you, along with various other ingredients.

Name: Lin Family of One - The Bund
Address: 4F, The Central, 123 East Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This upmarket dining concept nests in a shopping mall where century-old buildings are connected by a glass dome. The owner Mr Lin, a Taizhou native, has been cooking since the age of 19 and he ensures dishes are as authentic as they can be. Homestyle braised pomfret boasts a velvety texture and deep flavours, served with hand-made glutinous rice cake. Marinated tofu, and sweet potato noodles with sea anemone are also worth trying.

Name: Cuivre
Address: 1502 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Echoing its name, this welcoming bistro in the French Concession amusingly features copper trimming on its walls and dinnerware. The kitchen excels in reinventing bistro classics with modern techniques and subtle Asian twists. L’agneau, or rack of lamb, is nicely charred on the outside and juicy on the inside. Round off with baba Zacapa. The wine list offers vintages from French small-batch wineries, alongside affordable new world choices.

Name: The Commune Social
Address: 511 Jiangning Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A former police station circa 1910 is home to this tapas bar exuding minimalist chic that also comes with a terrace. The chef reinvents classics with modern techniques and exotic flavours, such as the use of African spices in grilled pumpkin with cheese and nuts. Ibérico pork and foie gras burger also evokes much love. Daily specials are offered at dinner. Reservations are not accepted at weekends; additional service charges apply for private rooms.

Name: Wei Xiang Zhai (Yandang Road)
Address: 14 Yandang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: For over 80 years customers have been flocking here for its noodles. No one seems to mind the congested, somewhat tired room – just as long as the flavour in the bowl remains unchanged. The menu is set in two frames: noodles on one side, toppings on the other. Those in the know order a bowl of noodles dressed in sesame sauce, alongside spicy chopped pork topping and beef clear broth. Chilled noodles also hit the spot in summer.

Name: Hakkasan
Address: 5F, Bund 18, 18 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Though its name means Hakka people, this chic restaurant on the Bund serves modern Cantonese fare with Western influences, but not necessarily of Hakka origin. The must-try Peking duck with caviar boasts interesting layers of flavours. Top-notch ingredients are used for the hand-made dim sum; and the dim sum set lunch offers great value. Don’t miss the cocktails featuring local liquors. The sweeping river views are a beauty to behold.

Name: Yunhe · Jinting
Address: 111 Surpass Court, 570 Yongjia Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Amid historic mansions, where celebrities once lived, sits this serene restaurant with a patio dotted with lush greens. The head chef, with over 40 years of experience, excels in labour-intensive dishes no longer made elsewhere. Sautéed mackerel liver that is creamy and velvety is the must-try in winter. On the menu you can also find pork kidney dressed in sesame sauce, and dishes painstakingly made with finely shredded quail, pigeon or mandarin fish.

Name: Coquille
Address: 29 Mengzi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Next to the Italian trattoria Scarpetta you’ll find its younger sibling Coquille, a charming French restaurant with brass and mosaics. It’s spread over two floors, with the upstairs room providing a little more intimacy. The French classics come with subtle Southeast Asian influences. Signature dishes include foie gras crème brûlée and oven-roasted Dungeness crab. Pre-ordering beef Wellington is a must.

Name: Legend Taste (Jingan)
Address: 1025 Kangding Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: For those craving something a little more adventurous, this Yunnan restaurant may well hit the spot. The simple room is dotted by photos of Yunnan and tie-dyed blue tablecloths; the style of service is equally simple. The team uses mushrooms and herbs extensively in their cooking à la Dai ethnics. Try his chicken soup with Chinese quince and ham that exhibits a fruity tanginess.

Name: Ling's Ravioleria Migrante
Description: A young couple (she was born in China; he’s half-French, half-Italian) have settled in this quiet residential district where they now run a tiny yet successful restaurant with around 20 seats in the dining room and a few small tables outdoors in summer – booking is essential! The menu includes various types of Chinese ravioli as well as dishes described by the couple as “migrant”, in other words “which draw inspiration from different cuisines from around the world, not only Asia but also the Mediterranean, France and Italy, with Emilia Romagna at its heart”. Examples include Peking-styleMora Romagnola coppa ham and pink Adriatic prawns marinated in mirin and soy sauce. The menu changes daily in line with market availability and the inspiration of the chef. Drinks include tea, beer and a small selection of wine.

Name: Osteria Grande
Description: This restaurant overlooking the magnificent Piazza Grande and the Loggia Vasariana that takes up one whole side of the square was opened in the summer of 2022 by the enthusiastic Fatjon and Lorenzo (if you ask, they’ll happily share their knowledge of Arezzo’s history with you). The former is at the helm in the kitchen where he expresses his passion for cuisine in seasonal, contemporary-style dishes such as pigeon breast, leg and fillet (each cut is prepared in the appropriate way) served with sweet onion and cocoa nibs, while the latter oversees the wine selection and recommends suitable pairings to guests. For the chef’s pigeon speciality, he may, for example, suggest an original Maturato Tiberini 2018 (a white wine made from grapes that are left to ripen on the vine). Cocktail staff are also hand for guests keen to choose an aperitif or an after-dinner drink from the extensive cocktail list.

Name: Carusu
Description: Situated on the road that crosses the archaeological park, this smart and elegant restaurant boasts two dining rooms arranged on two floors. In the kitchen, a young chef with plenty of previous experience working in renowned restaurants creates reinterpreted Sicilian dishes of the highest quality.

Name: Kohaku
Description: As if by magic, once you step over the threshold at this restaurant you feel as though you are in Japan, thanks to the soft music, elegant ambience and stylish decor. Japanese Kaiseki dishes take pride of place here, all made from seasonal ingredients with a real respect for integrity. We particularly enjoyed the duck with miso cooked at low heat for eight hours. An interesting sake selection and a lighter menu at lunchtime add to the appeal.

Name: Ladinia
Address: strada Pedercorvara 10, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Both the Berghotel Ladinia and its restaurant of the same name boast a warm, vintage Alpine-style ambience, with wood decor that tells the story of this business which opened as a simple inn back in 1930. Little has changed since then and guests return here time after time thanks to the warm welcome and attention to detail offered by the Costa family. The traditional cuisine has the occasional modern twist, while the few Ladin-style guestrooms are decorated with a profusion of wood.

Name: Al Malò - Cucina e Miscelazione
Description: Under the porticoes of the evocative Piazza Cavour you can see the double entrance: the door for the evening cocktail bar on the ground level, while–hidden on the left–there is a lift to the first level where there is the restaurant: the contemporary dining room is animated by bright wallpaper that seems almost to reveal in advance the imaginative cuisine of the chef-patron. Colorful, contemporary, with neat creative presentations he skilfully alternates meat (their signature is tongue mille-feuille, on the menu since the opening in 2019) and fish, but there is no lack of vegetarian dishes. Half portions are available. The fun grows with the mixology option of the cocktail list–in the evening–as well as the good wine list that, ça va sans dire, has great consideration for Franciacorta.

Name: Casu Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Situated on Giarre’s main street, this small, simple restaurant has just a few tables and an informal atmosphere. The menu offers a small selection of reasonably priced dishes with a focus on Sicilian cuisine made from top-quality ingredients that guarantee delicious flavours.

Name: Le Vie del Borgo
Description: Le Vie del Borgo is situated in a restored rustic building situated in the historic centre of the picturesque village of Toceno in the Val Vigezzo. Here, a young couple with a real passion for cuisine serve recipes from the region and elsewhere, as well as dishes that demonstrate remarkable modern techniques, all made from top-quality seasonal ingredients and accompanied by an interesting selection of wines. The restaurant consists of several intimate dining rooms decorated in Alpine style, with an elegant feel and carefully chosen furnishings. The attractive outdoor space with just a few tables is popular in summer, so advance booking is recommended!

Name: La Posta
Description: This traditional restaurant boasts small dining rooms adorned with wooden ceilings, which were redecorated a few years ago with evocative photos and documents depicting its history. The restaurant’s interesting cuisine is also traditional in style, featuring home-made pastas, a typical boiled meat trolley (“carrello dei bolliti”), and an excellent rabbit stew served with a generous portion of peppers. The selection of delicious home-produced fare includes vegetables, preserves and pastries.

Name: aldìVino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Shelves stacked with wine bottles line the walls at this smart bistro-style restaurant, which also boasts a quiet outdoor space for summer dining. The cuisine is contemporary and creative, and is showcased on three tasting menus from which dishes can also be ordered à la carte. We particularly enjoyed and can highly recommend the chef’s two signature dishes (“piatti firma dello chef”), squid “dripping” and spaghetti with smoked butter, oysters and raspberries. Courses here are divided into meat, fish and vegetable sections (Terra, Acqua and Vegetale).

Name: InAlto Alfio Ghezzi Dolomites
Address: via San Pellegrino 32, stazione a monte della funivia Col Margherita, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: Situated on Col Margherita at an altitude of 2 550m and accessible in winter via a cable car (from the San Pellegrino pass in Moena), this new ski bar bears the name of Alfio Ghezzi, the Michelin-starred chef at the Mart museum in Rovereto. Options include burgers and a children’s menu as well as a more elaborate and creative selection of some of the chef’s best-loved dishes. In summer the bar can also be reached on foot or by bike (for the truly athletic!) with recharging stations available for e-bikes.

Name: Savô
Description: The reopening in 2022 of the Hotel Windsor with its romantic vintage decor, is a real bonus for Laigueglia, especially the hotel’s new gourmet restaurant Savô (which translates as “flavour” in Ligurian dialect). Here, a contemporary dining room and an outdoor space with views of the beach and the sea provide the setting for modern cuisine prepared from regional, seasonal ingredients with a focus on fish (there is also a meat option for each course). The impressive selection of wine and choice of cocktails from the elegant Windsor Bar adds to its appeal.

Name: Il Grottino
Address: piazza Beato Ugolino 5, Gualdo Cattaneo, 06035, Italy
Description: Situated in the old medieval village of Gualdo Cattaneo, amid the gentle valleys not far from Foligno, Il Grottino is the perfect choice for anyone keen to sample the authentic flavours of Umbrian cuisine. Here, truffles and zero-km produce take pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on meat which is carefully cooked on the open-view barbecue grill. Alongside locally sourced produce, you’ll also find a choice of carefully selected Prussian beef. Comfortable and welcoming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: CRUdoRE
Description: A restaurant/lounge with a very contemporary and elegant atmosphere. The cuisine is appealing with variations of raw fish, which are sometimes creative and elaborated, but can also be requested au naturel. This is followed by dishes chiefly of the classic seafood tradition and something more imaginative, which go along with the fish catches on view in the kitchen.

Name: Hostaria di Bricai
Description: Situated in the gardens next to the Sacro Monte funicular, this beautiful and bucolic residence overlooks the village. In this relaxing setting, Giorgio serves traditional local cuisine: the rabbit leg in porchetta with mountain-style purée is one of the highlights.

Name: Osteria dello Strecciolo
Description: Situated in the centre of the village, this popular and professionally run restaurant has an informal atmosphere. The cuisine is inspired by Mediterranean recipes and more regional traditions, with great care taken in the choice of ingredients and beautifully presented dishes. A business lunch menu is also available.

Name: Palazzo Branciforte
Description: A relaxing oasis in the city centre which offers friendly service from staff who obviously want to ensure that your experience here is memorable. The dishes served are carefully prepared and full of flavour, boasting the occasional modern touch yet also inspired by local traditions. Try the "Capricciosa vista mare": toasted black bread with capers and oregano served with red prawn, dried tomato, artichokes, basil and buffalo mozzarella mousse.

Name: Hosteria del Platano
Description: Situated on the main road overlooking the lake, this pleasant family-run restaurant serves excellent traditional cuisine with a focus on local fish. Atmospheric dining room with stone walls and vaulted ceilings, plus an attractive outdoor space, and friendly, attentive owners.

Name: Locanda 53 Supper Club
Description: Partners in life and business, Evelyn and Carlo are a young couple who have settled in Arco’s old town where they have restored this old inn, embellishing it with three modern and comfortable guestrooms. The restaurant offers two tasting menus featuring meat or fish – guests are asked to make their choice when booking. Once that’s done, all you have to do is sit back and enjoy the intimate atmosphere of the couple’s small “supper club” and leave everything to the talented Evelyn in the kitchen and skilful Carlo front of house. The recipes here are modern yet unfussy, with a focus on carefully selected ingredients that are prepared with respect and real attention to detail. Fine cuisine and an exquisite welcome combine to offer a truly memorable dining experience.

Name: Il Circolino
Description: At Il Circolino, enjoy interesting cuisine designed by Claudio Sadler and prepared by skilful resident chef Lorenzo Sacchi. There’s a café-cum-bistro at the entrance, with its own kitchen and an attractive garden for summer dining, while the elegant, contemporary-style restaurant is hidden behind a folding door. The gourmet meat and fish dishes served here are showcased on various menus from which guests can also choose courses à la carte style. On the “C’era una volta” menu, we particularly enjoyed the spaghetti with missoltino fish and carp butter, which is decorated with colourful flowers and has decisive flavours, while the mullet served with a Spanish-style “suquet” made from carefully chosen ingredients stood out on the “Viaje” menu. Among the desserts, the black lemon, shiso and kombu seaweed has a fresh and exotic flavour. If you enjoy watching the chefs at work, make sure you book the table in front of the kitchen.

Name: Il Grifone
Address: via Ca' Masino 611/a - loc. Varignana, Castel San Pietro Terme, 40024, Italy
Description: This fine-dining restaurant housed in the 18C Palazzo Bentivoglio Bargellini is part of the luxurious Palazzo di Varignana resort (with which it shares the Il Grifone symbol), the latter also home to a farm producing olive oil, wine and fruit. In the evening, choose between two tasting menus and an à la carte offering a selection of meat and fish dishes on which the modern recipes feature a careful balance of colours and flavours.

Name: SaQua by Il Frantoio
Description: This restaurant, previously known simply as “Il Frantoio”, now has new out-of-town premises but any regret you may have at leaving the town centre will soon disappear, thanks to the wide range of modern Tuscan dishes prepared by the chefs in the new, larger kitchen. A further attraction is the outdoor space which boasts beautiful sunset views in summer.

Name: Porcino
Description: After gaining experience in top-quality restaurants, chef Marco Verginer has embarked on a new adventure running his own brand-new restaurant in the equally new Badia Hill hotel. In an elegant and spacious setting, enjoy modern, occasionally creative cuisine which skilfully blends Alpine flavours and ingredients with delicious Mediterranean influences.

Name: Stefano Mocellin al Padovanino
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Padova, this restaurant is home to owner-chef Stefano Mocellin, whose colourful, creative and personalised cuisine is influenced by his past culinary experience in cities such as Milan and Venice. From Milan, for example, he has taken the legendary “cassoeula”, to which he gives a lighter touch thanks to his use of more than one type of meat (pork and duck), while his “saor” and the sardines that he uses to stuff his plin pasta are inspired by Venice. Underlying all of this is his passion for cooking over the barbecue grill, the main focus of almost all the dishes on the menu.

Name: Al Baccanale
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre just a stone’s throw from Piombino’s former Medici fortress, this quiet restaurant boasts a backdrop of exposed stonework and vaulted ceilings and just a few tables, so booking ahead is recommended. Here, the enthusiastic and talented owner-chef serves traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern and highly individual twist.

Name: Dallo Zio
Description: A beautifully kept restaurant just a stone’s throw from the Arch of Augustus. Warm and welcoming, the restaurant’s vintage style echoes the 19C origins of the building as well as the 1970s, the decade when it first opened. Divided into two floors with small tables set close together, the menu features meat dishes and, more especially, “fresh fish from Rimini’s fishing boats” prepared in delicious, classic recipes that often have their roots in local traditions.

Name: Rinaldi al Quirinale
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant that eschews modern trends, where you can enjoy Italian cuisine made from quality ingredients with a focus (although not exclusive) on fish and seafood, and where dishes are simple, reassuringly familiar and prepared according to traditional culinary techniques, then this restaurant behind the Quirinale is definitely for you! There’s also an excellent wine list which includes a combination of rare and well-known labels.

Name: Da Luciano
Address: via Nazionale 11, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description: Enjoy beautiful views of Lake Trasimeno from the outdoor terrace of this restaurant, where the menu focuses mainly on fish, alongside original ingredients such as beans and Umbrian truffles which are used in typical specialities such as tegamaccio (fish stew).

Name: La Risacca Blu
Address: via Tunisia, angolo via Tadino, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description: The first thing you see when you enter this restaurant near the central railway station is its large display of fresh fish, all delivered daily. The menu features a selection of classic and authentic fish and seafood options, with pride of place given to its raw fish dishes.

Name: Locanda Martinelli
Description: It’s well worth leaving the coast and climbing into the foothills to get to this small restaurant serving excellent cuisine. Housed in a rustic-style house with individual furnishings, in what could be the sitting room of a private house, the restaurant serves meat and fish specialities prepared with imagination from local produce and ingredients from further afield. As well as being a wine expert, the female owner gathers herbs, flowers and berries to flavour her recipes.

Name: Il Frantoio
Address: via del Castello 40, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: The 19C millstone, press and cisterns can still be seen in the dining room at this restaurant, bearing witness to its past as an olive oil mill. Situated in spectacular Colle di Val d’Elsa, Il Frantoio boasts old stone and brick walls and vaulted ceilings, as well as tables set out in the piazza for summer dining. Although the setting suggests simple and rustic cuisine, the chef surprises guests with top-quality dishes which are technical and often highly creative, such as liver with sour cherries and pistachios, and smoked spaghetti with an anchovy sauce, capers and black garlic cream.

Name: Il Piraña
Description: A classic fish restaurant that opts for simply prepared dishes rather than fussy, inventive avant - garde cuisine. The perfect address for those in search of traditional fare.

Name: La Barca
Description: Run by the Virgilio family since 1967, this popular restaurant pays tribute to historic Bari with its delicious fish dishes and specialities from Puglia. Don’t miss the grilled fish and the reinterpreted cannolo dessert made with sheep’s milk ricotta, pear sauce and pistachio waffles.

Name: El Brite di Larieto
Address: Località Larieto, strada per Passo Tre Croci, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: If SanBrite boasts a collection of Michelin stars (a classic star for its cuisine and a green star for its sustainable approach), it’s also thanks to this agriturismo’s location in a small larch wood, where it is surrounded by the spectacular Dolomites. Opened 20 years ago and renovated over the years, this smart agriturismo is also home to a stable annexe, where its restaurant celebrates the flavours of Alpine culinary traditions in its meat and charcuterie, cheeses, creamy butter and ice cream, as well as herbs, berries and other local ingredients.

Name: Benso
Description: Situated in a small garden in the historic centre, this modern bistro has a light, airy feel thanks to its large windows and its outdoor tables perfect for alfresco dining in summer. The young kitchen staff, supervised by a talented chef and with plenty of experience behind them, serve contemporary cuisine with an individual flavour. Simple aperitif-style options are available between 6 and 8pm.

Name: Bar à Fromage
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: A cosy, elegant Stube-style restaurant where the staff wear typical Aosta Valley costume and the menu features dishes with a particular focus on cheese (including an excellent fondue!) alongside traditional regional fare. Typical decor with refined, personalised furnishings and a profusion of wood.

Name: Chicco di Grano
Address: viale dei Caduti del Lavoro 5, Castel Mella, 25030, Italy
Description: Solid, professionally prepared regional cuisine, with its roots in classic recipes which are full of flavour and demonstrate real culinary skill and expertise.

Name: Le Tre Colombe
Description: This intimate and romantic restaurant occupies an old 18C rural house which is situated in a small hamlet in the Cembra valley. In two small dining rooms with a vaguely modern feel, the husband serves just one tasting menu, from which guests can choose two menus of different lengths, featuring delicious, well-presented, contemporary Italian cuisine prepared by his wife.

Name: La Terrazza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the top floor of the exclusive and luxurious Eden hotel, this famous restaurant boasts an elegant, hushed ambience in its softly lit dining room, as well as stunning views of Rome. Originally from Campania, chef Fabio Ciervo has been at the helm here for over 10 years (a fact that is celebrated on his classic X Yearsmenu), serving spectacular creative cuisine that aims to appeal to the eyes and the palate alike.

Name: Farmacia dei Sani
Description: Occupying a corner of the central Piazza del Popolo in the delightful historic centre of Ruffano, this family restaurant (also a liqueur-maker) is surrounded by old palazzi which add to the charm of its setting. The Puglian cuisine served here has a modern twist while remaining unfussy in style and firmly anchored in the region. The service is quick, and each guest is greeted with a smile by the Rizzo family.

Name: Terrazza Costantino
Description: In just a few years, young owner-chef Giuseppe Costantino has turned what was once the family trattoria into an elegant restaurant serving delicious reinterpretations of local specialities. There is just one tasting menu which features either meat or fish (although this can be discussed when you make your booking, which is essential). Given the excellent quality of the food here, this menu offers exceptional value for money.

Name: I Savi
Address: via Spangaro 6, località Peseggia di Scorzè, Scorzè, 30037, Italy
Description: Situated in a small rural hamlet, this restaurant is one of the best in the Venetian hinterland for top-quality fish. Served in welcoming dining rooms, the fish and seafood dishes here are traditional and unfussy in style, and full of natural flavour.

Name: Lo Stornello
Description: Offering quality and professionalism in a tourist setting, this small restaurant is popular with locals as well as visitors. The menu focuses on imaginatively presented Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: Parma Rotta
Description: Here, where the Parma river once broke its banks, you’ll find an attractive trattoria with pleasant dining rooms and excellent cuisine cooked over a wood and herb fire, one of the oldest culinary techniques in the world. The main courses feature meat only, with an extensive number of dishes on the menu. Among the home-made desserts, we recommend the fior di latte ice-cream, which is served with a choice of delicious sauces.

Name: Marcandole
Description: This restaurant managed with passion has become a cornerstone of Treviso restaurants thanks to a fish cuisine contaminated by contemporary inspirations. Do not miss the raw specialties!

Name: La Martinatica
Description: This renowned restaurant occupying an old mill with rustic yet elegant decor has recently been taken over by new chefs who have come here from elsewhere in Versilia. The menu offers a selection of fish and meat dishes, all of which are prepared in the same modern and unfussy style.

Name: Bistrot de Venise
Address: calle dei Fabbri 4685, sestiere San Marco, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: Diners will enjoy the lengthy wine list (available by the glass) and "historical" cuisine at this restaurant in a location known for its atmosphere.

Name: Corte Sconta
Address: calle del Pestrin, sestiere Castello 3886, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: From its flooring to its tables, this restaurant has the charming, nostalgic feel of a typical trattoria in its simple dining room, while the outdoor space in an inner courtyard under a vine-shaded arbour is a charming place to eat in fine weather – a real gem right in the centre of Venice. The cuisine is as simple in style as the decor, with traditional Venetian fish and seafood dishes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: Risorgimento
Description: This restaurant situated in the centre of Sirmione just a stone’s throw from the lake is striking for its elegant outdoor terrace. This refined setting provides the backdrop for creative meat and fish dishes full of individual character. A fine display of wines adorns the shelves in the lounge-cum-wine bar on the first floor.

Name: Corte Visconti
Description: A classical, rustic style environment with walls in stone and brick vaulted or wood and stone ceilings. The cuisine is authentically local but with a pleasant touch of creativity.

Name: La Cantinella
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A little country restaurant with pleasantly distinctive interiors and summer service al fresco on the terrace. Traditional Tuscan cuisine on the menu, with a modern touch.

Name: Il Giardino del Gusto
Description: Although not on the seafront, this restaurant is well worth a visit thanks to its excellent owner - chef, who has had years of experience to perfect his French culinary techniques. Exciting tasting menus with dishes which can also be ordered à la carte.

Name: Forte del 48
Address: via Vizzotto 1, San Donà di Piave, 30027, Italy
Description: This pleasant restaurant started life in 1848 as a bastion used by the Habsburg army and was later transformed into an inn. Recognised as a “Locale Storico Veneto”, it’s now run by the third generation of the De Faveri family who serve traditional meat and fish dishes here. Comfortable guestrooms are also available for guests wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Da Cesare
Description: As the Florentine lily on the glass at the entrance implies, the specialities of this place are Tuscan in origin as well as seafood. Friendly atmosphere, ample wine list.

Name: Lazaroun
Address: via Del Platano 21, Santarcangelo di Romagna, 47822, Italy
Description: The prototype of a typical Romagna restaurant, run by an efficient and friendly family team. Excellent choice of high - quality first and second courses, including fresh pasta, hams and salamis, meat options and grilled dishes. An interesting feature of the restaurant is the presence of ancient tufa caves in the basement. Created around 400 AD and part of an intricate network of underground passages, they were later used by the Malatesta family as an escape route and are now open to the public.

Name: Vitello d'Oro
Description: This restaurant boasts a new, even more beautiful look following its complete restoration in early 2019. However, one thing that has not changed is the excellent fish cuisine which has given the restaurant its fine reputation and drawn guests here since the mid 19C!

Name: La Valle
Address: via Umberto I 25, località Valle Sauglio, Trofarello, 10028, Italy
Description: A well - run restaurant in a quiet area just outside the village, where the owner - chef serves modern cuisine with the occasional regional influence. Careful attention is given to the use of seasonal produce and natural herbs, and there is a small selection of fish - based dishes.

Name: La Chiocciola
Address: via Runco 94/f, Quartiere di Portomaggiore, 44015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant and an inn in a small country village, it’s the right place if you’re looking for hospitality and you appreciate the regional cuisine, made of snails and frogs, but also fish from the nearby sea. Something for every palate.

Name: Le Jardin de Russie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite the French name, Le Jardin de Russie serves creative and contemporary Italian cuisine in sublime surrounds and its colourful dishes have been inspired by the Mediterranean ingredients of the region. Nestled at the foot of the hotel’s Secret Garden, the Stravinskij Bar is a green oasis offering contemporary and classic cocktails. Brunch is available on Saturdays and Sundays.

Name: Lapprodo
Address: via Roma 22, Vibo Valentia Marina, 89900, Italy
Description: Definitely one of the most reliable restaurants in this area, Vibo Valentia Marina overlooks Vibo Marina port and is the perfect choice for anyone keen on classic Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on fish (most of which is caught locally), although meat dishes also feature on the menu. The restaurant also offers guestrooms in its Cala del Porto hotel.

Name: Trattoria alla Pergola
Description: An old-fashioned trattoria with a simple, homely atmosphere which attracts guests from all over the province who are drawn here by the classic, unfussy regional cuisine. Although the menu is concise, it includes specialities such as tortelli, tortellini, the region’s famous risottos (this is rice-growing country) and renowned boiled meats. Make sure you leave room for the tempting dessert trolley.

Name: Bacco e Arianna
Address: via Circonvallazione 1, Trezzano sul Naviglio, 20090, Italy
Description: Enjoy attentive service from the female owner in this small modern restaurant, where the cuisine will definitely make an impression. Focused mainly on fish, the dishes served here are striking for their quality and variety (try the “metro di mare”, a tasting dish of raw fish for two people).

Name: Osteria Manzoni
Description: This restaurant housed within a colourful, skilfully restored historic building with exposed stonework has a young friendly couple at the helm. The menu features delicious, refined and traditional Italian cuisine.

Name: I Tigli
Description: An iconic pizzeria which has brought Italy’s favourite street-food snack right up to date! With almost 30 years’ experience behind him, Simone Padoan knows how to make difficult things easy: he uses a mix of wholemeal flours and pays meticulous attention to natural leavening processes to create a dough which has a crispy crust yet soft interior. He also focuses on different types of toppings, including fish, meat and vegetables – whether your preference is for traditional or more imaginative pizzas, every option is of the highest quality. A choice of excellent desserts provides the perfect conclusion to your meal!

Name: Villa Arcadio
Address: via Palazzina 2, località Villa di Salò, Salò, 25087, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant prioritises beautiful presentation in his modern interpretations of Italian dishes, which are even more enjoyable in summer when meals are served outdoors, surrounded by greenery and with fine views of the southern part of Lake Garda and its shoreline.

Name: Agli Amici Dopolavoro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You cross a small garden-cum-olive grove to get to this romantic and elegant restaurant situated on the enchanting Isola dell Rose, a private island accessible only by boat. Here, the chef delights guests with local and seasonal ingredients (often from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden), which he transforms into dishes with a modern twist. In the evening, tempting aperitif snacks based on reinterpretations of typical Venetian “cicchetti” are also available.

Name: Arva
Address: calle Tiepolo, sestiere San Polo 1364, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: Dine surrounded by a decor of stucco and paintings or alfresco overlooking the Grand Canal in this highly luxurious restaurant. Arva, from the Latin "cultivated land", pays homage to the sea, the land and its best seasonal ingredients purchased from the Rialto market and the islands of the Venetian lagoon. Chef Matteo Panfilio, who has an international experience in good restaurants, pays great attention to local vegetables.

Name: San Lorenzo
Description: Situated within the Clitunno hotel, this well-managed family-run restaurant serves classic, seasonal meat and fish dishes, including generous portions of black truffles in some dishes. Recently refurbished, the intimate, elegant dining room also occasionally features live music at weekends, while the outdoor terrace on the small square offers pleasant alfresco dining. Guests are advised to park outside the ZTL (restricted traffic zone) and make their way on foot, via a short walk through the beautiful historic centre.

Name: Mater Terrae
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated on the top floor of the Raphaël hotel just behind Piazza Navona, this restaurant serves some of the best vegetarian cuisine in Rome. Each of the elaborate dishes boasts numerous ingredients and every single course is a delightful surprise. Equally stunning is the panoramic terrace overlooking the city’s rooftops, where meals are served in fine weather.

Name: Vini da Gigio
Address: calle Stua Cannaregio, sestiere Cannaregio 3628, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: In the district of Cannaregio, a rustic environment and informal service in an inn where you can see into the kitchen, and which offers both fish and meat dishes; a good choice of wines.

Name: Trattoria Glisenti
Description: Situated on the lakefront with beautiful views from its terrace, this restaurant focuses on freshwater fish, while also serving a selection of classic regional specialities. Careful attention is paid to natural ingredients, with vegetarian options also available. An elegant restaurant which belies its description as a “trattoria”.

Name: Boccon DiVino
Address: via Traversa dei Monti 201, località Colombaio Tozzi, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description: In a farmhouse on the edges of town, this restaurant has a rustic dining area with modern tables and chairs and a beautiful summer terrace with a view. Authentic local dishes.

Name: Ansitz Romani
Address: via Andreas Hofer 23, Termeno sulla Strada del Vino, 39040, Italy
Location: Termeno sulla Strada del Vino, Italy
Description: An attractive, well-kept restaurant in a historic building with a romantic, rural feel, especially in the beautiful garden. Although the menu is not that extensive, the chef is highly skilled, and it doesn’t feel as though anything is missing here. The dishes reflect the flavours of the region, making use of local ingredients such as venison and asparagus from Termeno accompanied by home-produced speck ham. The menu also features a couple of fish-based recipes and all dishes are modern and imaginative in style. Beautiful guestrooms are also available.

Name: Giorgio e Flora
Address: via Baldonò 1, lago di Velo d'Astico, Velo, 36010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This small chalet - style villa overlooks the valley. It has an attractive, elegant and quiet dining room decorated with a feminine touch and a panoramic outdoor terrace. Modern cuisine from the Veneto takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: Braunwirt
Description: A modern and welcoming restaurant in the heart of the town, where the modern design is echoed by the contemporary cuisine which combines regional dishes with influences from elsewhere in Italy. Food-lovers will enjoy creating their own tasting menu by choosing dishes from the à la carte. Friendly service and a cosmopolitan clientele.

Name: Da Nicolo
Description: Located in an advantageous spot along the promenade, where there is a summer dining area, this restaurant is really patronized for the quality of its food. Serving seafood and Carlofortinian specialties.

Name: Meltemi
Description: A maritime focused oasis in a city where the traditional specialities revolve around meat, this restaurant serves fish dishes with various options ranging from raw fish to antipasti. Pleasant ambience with an attractive modern decor.

Name: Enotavola
Description: The entrance to this restaurant through a wine-bar can be misleading, as you are eventually led to simpler – yet still attractive – dining rooms. In this wine-themed setting, enjoy delicious fish and seafood dishes with the occasional creative twist, accompanied by a particularly extensive selection of wines by the glass. A highly recommended address for fish lovers, situated right in the historic centre of Padova.

Name: Viva il Bistrot
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the cathedral, this restaurant has tables set out on Noto’s attractive pedestrianised street in fine weather, although if these are all taken the contemporary-style dining rooms are just as appealing. Viviana Varese, a Michelin-starred chef from Milano, oversees the interesting menu which showcases Sicilian cuisine prepared from local ingredients alongside more exotic fare.

Name: Scatto
Description: From Turin’s beautiful Piazza San Carlo, you head through an inner courtyard to this restaurant’s modern dining room with its open-view kitchen. Whether you opt for the à la carte or tasting menu, you’ll find a balance of traditional Piedmontese and more creative dishes, all of remarkable quality, in keeping with the superb wine list.

Name: Concezione Restaurant
Description: This minimalist-style restaurant is home to one of the most interesting young chefs in Catania. In this historic building with beautiful ceilings, enjoy top-quality Sicilian cuisine created by Manuel Tropea, who focuses in particular on specialities from Catania which he interprets in a highly personalised way with a real focus on tradition. Dishes such as “L’Asina e la lattuga” and “Good morning in Catania” are good examples. The chef’s surprise menu takes guests on a culinary journey full of contrasts which is inspired by his own memories and experiences.

Name: Futura
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre overlooking the monumental Piazza San Giustino, this restaurant has a traditional feel in keeping with its location, enhanced by typical brick walls in dining rooms arranged on two floors. In contrast, the predominantly meat-based cuisine is contemporary in style, with some interesting technical and creative twists.

Name: Li Somari
Description: Transferred to piazza Rivarola 21, Tivoli.Adriano Baldassarre’s small, intimate restaurant is situated in historic Tivoli, which is renowned for its fascinating history and Hadrian’s Villa. Popular with food-lovers, the restaurant serves delicacies such as oxtail ravioli and tripe, with a whole page of the menu dedicated to offal dishes, as well as panzanella and char by Alessandro Narducci, the latter paying tribute to a chef friend of Baldassare’s. A few tables set out on the promenade provide outdoor dining options, while the restaurant’s sustainable approach to dining is explained at the top of the menu.

Name: Delicato
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval hill-top village in the province of Rieti on the border with Umbria, this restaurant serves cuisine that is influenced by different regions and traditions. Choose between the minimalist-style dining rooms with exposed stone walls and, in fine weather, a charming outdoor space at the foot of Contigliano’s church. Here, chef Carlotta Delicato brings out the best of local ingredients in dishes that are kept deliberately simple and unfussy yet are full of flavour.

Name: Nugolo
Description: A restaurant with a friendly ambience and a chic, colourful decor and design that includes an open-view kitchen. In the latter, the young, talented chef uses seasonal ingredients to create contemporary-style dishes with an imaginative twist. The enthusiastic front-of-house team provides friendly and attentive service.

Name: Belé
Description: The name says it all – in Milanese dialect, “belé” means beautiful and the word is an apt description of this restaurant. Belé is charmingly lit by an old-fashioned chandelier on which the pieces of crystal create a play of light resembling an intricate and shifting lace-like pattern. The dining rooms are decorated in attractive contemporary colours, with comfortable armchairs and acoustics perfect for conversation, while the cuisine is Italian with a modern twist.

Name: Essentia
Address: piazza San Nicolò 2, Castrocaro Terme, 47011, Italy
Description: Situated at the foot of the fortress in the historic centre of Castrocaro, this restaurant has an interesting young chef at the helm, Andrea Giacchini. The cuisine often (but not always) has a local influence and demonstrates remarkable technical expertise that is neither overly ostentatious nor an end in itself, but rather a way of skilfully showcasing the top-quality ingredients used.

Name: Kosmo Taste the Mountain
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the centre and also accessible from the ski slopes, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant boasts a spacious dining room and large picture windows.
