Traditional regional and mountain cuisine with a modern twist and a wine cellar focusing on mountain wines from producers working  sustainably.

Name: Gennaro Di Pace
Address: vicolo della Chiesa 8, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: The owner-chef’s Calabrian origins are evident on a menu that combines Mediterranean cuisine (including fish and seafood) with Piedmontese specialities and showcases beautifully presented dishes prepared using contemporary techniques. This small modern restaurant situated near Perno castle is also open at lunchtime (by prior reservation only).

Name: Ai Porteghi Bistrot
Description: Situated under the picturesque arcades on Via Cesare Battisti, this restaurant is home to a young chef whose cuisine is inspired by traditional and well-known recipes which he reinterprets with his own personal touch to create highly interesting dishes. Simpler and more reasonably priced options are also available at lunchtime.

Name: Café Quinson
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The Café Quinson has reopened! In this rustic yet elegant “mountain restaurant”, the whole family makes guests feel welcome, serving a selection of regional dishes with an imaginative and contemporary touch. Excellent choice of wines, almost all of which are available by the glass.

Name: Chalet Gerard
Address: via Plan de Gralba 37, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a breathtakingly beautiful natural setting between the Sassolungo peak and the majestic Sella mountains, this restaurant serves simple mountain fare alongside a few more modern dishes, all of which are prepared from typical ingredients from the Alto Adige. Although you can’t book at lunchtime, bookings are required in the evening. Beautiful guestrooms are also available.

Name: Acciuga
Description: This restaurant with a simple dining room and open-view kitchen serves some of the most interesting fish cuisine in the Della Vittoria district. Chef Federico Delmonte skilfully searches out “poor” varieties of fish which are nonetheless full of flavour on an open menu that is adjusted according to the catch of the day. The chef’s native Fano makes an appearance in a few recipes from the Marche, including the famous brodetto (a typical fish soup).

Name: Cortile Arabo
Description: In one of Sicily’s most iconic fortified villages which once prospered as a tuna fishery and is now a popular tourist attraction, Cortile Arabo serves carefully prepared and occasionally elaborate dishes of the highest quality, with a focus on fish (the menu also features a few meat dishes). The terrace on the rocks overlooking the sea, where the sound of the waves provides a soothing backdrop, is one of the highlights here.

Name: Giannino dal 1899
Description: A renowned name in Milan, this restaurant is the setting for a Mediterranean cuisine  with an international twist. Although recently renovated, the dining room has an attractive old-fashioned feel with old photographs of celebrities who have eaten here since it opened more than 120 years ago.

Name: Maragoncello
Address: via San Giovanni 1, località Vighizzolo, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: Situated in a small village in the Bassa Bresciana region, this restaurant comes as something of a surprise due to its focus on fish, with the selection of raw seafood options and the good-value-for-money tasting menu particular highlights. Personalised cuisine which is full of flavour, served in modern, convivial dining rooms.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci Pizzeria
Address: piazza San Domenico Maggiore 5-7, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Situated right in the city centre, this pizzeria with the same name and owners as the gourmet restaurant has a contemporary, minimalist feel, plus an attractive outdoor space on the piazza. Among the excellent pizzas made from top-quality ingredients, you’ll find a few created by the young, skilful pizza chef, as well as one by chef Scarallo. Don’t miss the desserts!

Name: Trattoria I Masenini
Description: Situated in an attractive part of Verona right opposite the famous Castelvecchio, this restaurant boasts a relaxing ambience with wood ceilings, classic yet informal furnishings, subtle lighting and soft background music. The menu features regional dishes alongside typical Italian fare, as well as the house speciality – meat kebabs cooked on a skewer. There’s also an outdoor space for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Al Capitan della Cittadella
Description: Situated just outside the town walls, Al Capitan has been one of the most renowned fish restaurants in Verona for over fifteen years. Classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist added by the owner-chef take pride of place here, with an emphasis on top-quality ingredients. The wine list includes a good selection of French wines, with a particular focus on champagnes.

Name: Profumi di Cous Cous
Address: via Regina Margherita 80, San Vito lo Capo, 91010, Italy
Description: As the name of this restaurant suggests, couscous takes pride of place on the menu, although other Sicilian specialities can also be sampled here. Delightful atmosphere, especially in summer when meals are served in the internal courtyard among the citrus trees.

Name: Taverna Kus
Address: contrada Castello 14, San Zeno di Montagna, 37010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: An attractive restaurant situated on the western slopes of Monte Baldo overlooking Lake Garda, with a number of rustic yet elegant and welcoming dining rooms, including a bright veranda with partial views of the lake (enjoy the full vista from the outdoor terrace). Various culinary options feature on the menu, including meat, fish and vegetarian dishes, all colourful, full of flavour and beautifully cooked and prepared using mainly local and seasonal ingredients. The well-stocked and carefully chosen wine list deserves a special mention: among the 1 000 or more bottles stored in the old giasàra (underground cellar), you’re sure to find something you’ll enjoy.

Name: Le Lampare al Fortino
Address: via Tiepolo, molo Sant'Antonio, Trani, 76125, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Built over a medieval church, this old fort that once guarded the port has become the enviable location of a restaurant. It serves delicious fish and seafood specialities with the distinct flavour of Puglia.

Name: Salamensa
Address: via Monsignor Oscar Romero 29, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: A multi-function open space, with a bar for breakfasts and a classic restaurant serving pizzas made from naturally fermented dough. Although the ambience is modern, friendly and minimalist, the attention paid to the choice of ingredients and preparation of dishes is of the highest quality.

Name: Colonne
Address: via Fincarà 37, Santa Maria del Monte, 21100, Italy
Description: Beautiful views of Lake Varese and its surrounding countryside, especially from the attractive summer terrace. At lunchtime, the upper section of the restaurant houses the bistro, while the elegant dining room provides the backdrop for more creative cuisine in the evening. Chef Silvio Battistoni is very well known in the region.

Name: Darmagi
Description: Small villa in secluded position with warm, homely atmosphere, especially in the nice room with fireplace. The range of cuisine is rich in tradition.

Name: Macallè
Description: Elegant historical restaurant with several inviting rooms and a large, bright modern dining hall. Serving excellent traditional cuisine.

Name: Battipalo
Description: A young couple opened this attractive restaurant next to the ferry dock some years ago. The large windows offer romantic views of the lake, while the distinctly modern cuisine focuses on meat and fish alike. Excellent care has been taken in selecting the wine list. There is also a pleasant outdoor area for alfresco dining.

Name: La Fugascina Ristorante
Description: Situated on a small square with an attractive outdoor space, this restaurant offers a menu which features fish from the lake and other seasonal produce prepared with both modern and traditional techniques, but always with a contemporary flair. The focus is on locally sourced (zero-mile, wherever possible) produce.

Name: Cavallino
Description: Three talented young entrepreneurs who are passionate about good food have taken over this historic restaurant and have given it a new lease of life. The cuisine is contemporary and imaginative, with a firm focus on the region. Local cuisine is also to the fore in the simpler and more informal Trattoria da Ciccio.

Name: Osteria del 36
Description: The oldest osteria in the town centre, this restaurant has delighted locals and visitors in two simple yet convivial dining rooms since 1880. The cuisine here is regional, with many dishes freshly prepared, from the excellent pasta to the delicious ice cream. Specialities include duck breast in a raspberry sauce with parmesan cheese flan.

Name: La Coccinella
Description: Three brothers, all of them experts, are the enthusiastic managers of this very fine restaurant. Recent renovation has increased the comfort and popularity of the place. The cuisine is Piedmontese.

Name: Abraxas Osteria
Address: via Scalandrone 15, località Lucrino, Pozzuoli, 80078, Italy
Description: Situated inland at a slightly higher altitude than the coast, this restaurant on two floors focuses all its attention on its regional cuisine and its wine list. Very good value for money, although you will spend a bit more (and it’s worth it! ) if you choose one of the grilled meat options.

Name: Mangiare Bere Uomo Donna
Description: She’s from Hong Kong, while he’s from Suzzara – together this couple run this welcoming restaurant where their international focus extends from the dishes which feature on the menu to the wine selection and the couple’s love for applied arts. Once seated, you can either choose traditional fare, including a few delicious fish dishes, or you can be tempted by the decidedly Asian options. Whatever you decide, one thing’s for sure – authenticity and seasonal, locally sourced ingredients are guaranteed.

Name: Ristorante Alpes & La FuGa
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant, choose between three tables in the elegant, contemporary-style purple Stube, and another three in the more rustic, historic and romantic Stube. Wherever you choose to sit, you’ll enjoy creative, sophisticated dishes that will particularly appeal to anyone keen on innovative and imaginative cuisine. At the helm, chef Mattia Baroni has an unusual background, having moved from computer studies to working in renowned restaurants around the world.

Name: Ponte Pietra
Description: An old building next to the Roman bridge Ponte Pietra, with a couple of romantic small balconies overlooking the river. Charming dining rooms provide the backdrop for regional cuisine with creative touches and a carefully selected wine list. An attractive apartment is also available for anyone wish to extend their stay here.

Name: Il Favri
Address: via Borgo Meduna 12, San Giorgio della Richinvelda, 33095, Italy
Description: This inn, which has been serving food since the early 19C, boasts a warm atmosphere with a rustic feel. The beautiful garden makes a delightful setting in fine weather, while the cuisine focuses on traditional dishes from Friuli, such as “frico” (potato, onion and cheese fritter) and cured ham.

Name: Da Annetta
Description: In an 18th Century building, a rustic yet elegant atmosphere with a particular attentiveness at the tables and in the cuisine, which has a traditional base, but also knows how to add imaginative variations.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this restaurant occupies an old spinning mill ("filanda")  that has been completely restored without losing any of its original charm. Here, self-taught chef Barbara serves traditional dishes reinterpreted with real flair, such as the involtino di ciaffagnone filled with Maremma beef on a bed of melted pecorino cheese and crispy leek. The chef’s husband oversees the wine list, which includes a selection of Tuscan labels.

Name: Controcorrente
Address: via XXV Luglio 23, Morciano di Romagna, 47833, Italy
Description: A welcoming restaurant with a rustic - style dining room, a young, lively atmosphere and beautifully prepared dishes with an emphasis on fish – it is difficult not to be impressed!

Name: Al Covo
Address: campiello della Pescaria, sestiere Castello 3968, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Authentic family hospitality for this renowned restaurant, which makes niche products - mainly seafood - its flagship, even if some land specialties are always present on the menu. Almost all of the vegetables come from the Osti in Orto property garden on the island of Sant'Erasmo.

Name: Quellenhof Gourmetstube 1897
Address: via Passiria 47, Saint Martin in Passeier, 39010, Italy
Description: Situated in a refined and elegant setting (also home to an intimate private dining area separated from the main room by a few steps), this new gourmet restaurant offers various tasting menus with a distinctly creative flavour.

Name: Osteria Fernanda
Address: via Crescenzo Del Monte 18/24, Rome, 00153, Italy
Description: In the district famous for its Porta Portese market, this restaurant run by two talented business partners is definitely worth a visit. Andrea oversees the minimalist-style dining room, while Luca demonstrates real passion in his creative cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients, as well as produce from further afield. Among the desserts, we highly recommended the Porter beer ice-cream with black garlic mousse, chocolate and tuber peelings.

Name: Gna' Sara
Address: via Duca degli Abruzzi 8, San Vito lo Capo, 91010, Italy
Description: Situated on a road running parallel to the main street, this simple and busy restaurant with an attractive outdoor eating area serves traditional local cuisine such as fish couscous, hand - made busiate pasta and the ever - popular pizza. Always busy, the restaurant doesn’t take bookings in the evenings – it’s a simple case of first come, first served.

Name: Mondschein
Description: You’ll feel immediately at home in this gourmet restaurant in Sappada, where Paolo Kratter and his family offer a warm welcome to guests. In the romantic setting of an elegant mountain hut on the edge of the village, skiers can enjoy simple, informal dishes at lunchtime (the ski slopes are just behind the restaurant), while in the evening the cuisine is more elaborate and of the highest quality. A true taste of the Dolomites!

Name: Muraglia - Conchiglia d'Oro
Description: Here, choose between the simply furnished, bright dining room with a proudly vintage feel that dates back to its opening in the 1970s and a tiny yet attractive terrace with sea views (there are just a few tables, so it’s best to book in advance). Fish has always been – and still is – the house speciality, with fresh, top-quality dishes simply prepared according to classic methods such as the barbecue grill visible in the dining room. The fish is so fresh that the handwritten menu changes daily.

Name: Baracca - Storica Hostaria
Description: A classic, attractively elegant restaurant which boasts an extensive choice of dishes on its menu. The varied options here range from meat to fish dishes, often prepared in regional recipes such as tagliatelle with duck ragù and toasted hazelnuts, chicken liver risotto, Vicenza-style baccalà and meat casserole.

Name: Rezzano Cucina e Vino
Address: via Asilo Maria Teresa 34, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
Description: This restaurant was opened in 2003, completely renovated in a significantly simple style. The tables are wooden; the cuisine is enjoyable, tried and true.

Name: Il Melograno
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In the village centre and therefore not right by the sea, this successful, well - established restaurant is decorated in elegant contemporary style. The menu focuses on fish dishes reinterpreted with a touch of imagination.

Name: Enoteca Del Duca
Description: Despite the change of ownership at this centrally located restaurant right behind the castle and the main square, there’s a certain continuity to the cuisine which remains focused on classic dishes with a regional flavour (with the option of steak on the menu). The dining room features old stone walls, plus there’s also an attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Menegaldo
Address: via Pralongo 216, Monastier di Treviso, 31050, Italy
Description: This restaurant, once referred to as “l’osteria dei cava’i” in reference to the cart drivers and their horses who used to stop here after the First World War, has a history dating back 100 years. Now specialising in fish and shellfish from the Adriatic, Menegaldo has become one of the area’s most popular restaurants.

Name: Spin Ristorante-Enoteca
Address: via Carlo Barabino 120 r, Genoa, 16129, Italy
Description: Originally a wine shop, it was then converted into a restaurant that also opens for happy hour: the interiors closely resemble those of a bistro and bottles of wine, especially Italian ones, and of spirits are spread about, while the cuisine focuses on mostly Ligurian flavors (brandacujun, Genoese stuffed pumpkin flowers, trofie al pesto,...) and Italian ones, with fish and meat. Quality regional and national food and wine products are also for sale.

Name: Trattoria di Coronate
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Warm, welcoming, intimate and friendly – it’s easy to get carried away with the adjectives when describing this restaurant housed in a 16C farmhouse! This is the perfect choice for anyone looking for excellent and typical regional cuisine, accompanied by an equally good choice of wines. A visit to the wine cellar is highly recommended.

Name: Alla Corte Lombarda
Description: Housed in a restored hay barn on the edge of the village, this charming rustic restaurant offers traditional cuisine with a modern twist, a good selection of wine and an excellent choice of beer. Every week, the menu features five records which played a major role in the history of music or which represent an important moment in time for the restaurant owner.

Name: Villa Giulia - Al Terrazzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Housed within an elegant late-19C hotel overlooking the lake, this romantic restaurant offers stunning views from its outdoor terrace. The cuisine is mainly Italian, with the occasional modern and imaginative twist. Add in a charming stone wine cellar stocked with top-quality labels, plus modern guestrooms for anyone wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Il Chiosco di Bacco
Description: This restaurant boasts a rural location in the Montefeltro region, to which half the menu is dedicated (fresh home-made pastas, salumi, porchetta-style rabbit etc). The other half focuses on meat dishes, with an interesting selection of steaks and ribs from Italian and Scottish breeds (including more expensive beef that has been left to age for a month). You’ll find the perfect wine pairing on the excellent wine list.

Name: Pomiroeu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant, one of the finest in the region, is run by its owner Giancarlo Morelli and celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2023. Situated in the centre of Seregno, the restaurant is intimate and welcoming with walls adorned with beautiful works of contemporary art thanks to the restaurant’s partnership with a local art gallery. The cuisine here is modern yet unfussy and the chef is equally at ease with meat, fish and vegetable dishes. One of the few restaurants around Monza to still offer a cheese course!

Name: Osteria La Sangiovesa
Address: piazza Simone Balacchi 14, Santarcangelo di Romagna, 47822, Italy
Description: This simple and informal inn is the perfect setting in which to get together with friends, sitting around small tables laden with piadine flatbreads and slices of ham and salami. There’s also a restaurant here – a network of small rooms laid out in the cellars of an old palazzo – where portraits of local historical characters can be made out in the subtle lighting. Here too, the cuisine is inspired by the region and its traditions, with top-quality ingredients (cured hams, meat, oil, wine, vermouth etc) all coming from the restaurant’s own farm and estate.

Name: Perbacco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A rustic restaurant offering an authentic taste of the Cilento area, both in its setting amid lush Mediterranean vegetation and in its regional cuisine. Fish and seafood dominate the antipasti selection, while the main courses focus more on meat and vegetable dishes. Good choice of regional wines, plus the option of a few pleasant guestrooms.

Name: Hanswirt
Description: Situated in an old farmstead, this elegant and pleasant establishment has a warm and typically Tyrolese atmosphere.

Name: La Passion
Address: via San Nicolò 5/b, Vandoies di Sopra, Vintl, 39030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A small, cosy, completely wood - panelled stube has been set up in this residential building. The menus are traditional but inventive.

Name: Del Fagioli
Description: This historic Florentine trattoria now has a slightly new look, with the open-view kitchen visible as soon as you enter the restaurant. The friendly and welcoming ambience here makes it a popular choice, so booking ahead is highly recommended. Delicious, authentic cuisine is to the fore, including delicious Florentine steaks and other classic favourites.

Name: Casa D'Angelo
Address: via San Nicola 5, Fara Filiorum Petri, 66010, Italy
Description: Housed in what was once an old family home, this elegant restaurant serves delicious regional cuisine. The menu includes dishes that have been skilfully and imaginatively enhanced by the chef, such as warm pheasant terrine with apple, alongside more traditional fare, from cured ham to charcoal-grilled local lamb and potato gnocchi with a duck sauce. The restaurant’s own extra-virgin olive oil often adds further flavour to the dishes. The 4-course tasting menu deserves a special mention for its excellent value for money.

Name: Kleine Flamme
Description: In his small open-view kitchen situated in the centre of this restaurant, chef Bacher Burkhard develops his vision of fusion cuisine with energy and precision, combining flavours from Italy and the Alto Adige with Asian spices and techniques to create delicious and imaginative dishes. His tuna tataki is superb, seasoned with salty lemon oil and accompanied by intriguing bitter herbs that (as Professor Montanari has noted in a recent book) are particularly popular with Italians. The chef’s wife Annelies works front of house, where she looks after guests in a friendly and professional manner.

Name: Panevin
Description: In a district surrounded by greenery just outside Feltre, Gianluca Campigotto’s cuisine becomes more and more interesting with each passing year. The small menu focuses on fish and seafood, although meat dishes also make an appearance.

Name: Derby Grill
Description: Situated opposite the Villa Reale, this restaurant has the same classic, vaguely British ambience as the Hotel de la Ville in which it is situated, with tables also laid out on its elegant adjoining veranda. The menu features carefully prepared creative meat and fish dishes as well as traditional specialities from Lombardy, including risotto with Monza luganega sausage, ossobuco with gremolata parsley sauce and saffron rice, and an excellent costoletta alla Milanese (breaded veal).

Name: Fattoria delle Torri
Description: A small slice of paradise in the historic centre of Modica, where the daughters of owner-chef Peppe Barone continue the family culinary tradition while adding their youthful influence to the innovative and yet traditional cuisine served here. In fine weather, dine among lemon trees on the attractive outdoor terrace.

Name: Voltalacarta
Description: A tiny doorway leads to this simple, friendly and intimate restaurant with just a few tables, where booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s excellent reputation in the city. Its renown stems from the owner-chef’s cuisine, which focuses mainly on top-quality fish prepared in imaginative and personalised recipes using classic techniques. If it’s on the menu, make sure you try the “cappon magro” (a type of seafood salad), which is so good that it even has its own identity card!

Name: Da Vincenzo
Description: It's never easy to find the right balance between quality and quantity, especially in a town that is very much on the tourist trail. However, Da Vincenzo has succeeded in doing just this for years, ever since it was first opened by the family’s grandfather Vincenzo in 1958. Today, the founder’s grandson (who shares his grandfather’s name) is at the helm here, creating dishes which focus mainly on fish. Pleasant atmosphere, with a few small tables on the pavement of the street that runs through the centre of Positano. A choice of cocktails supplements the wine selection from lunchtime onwards.

Name: Acaja
Description: Central, elegant and modern, the cuisine of Acaja winds along two lines: the traditional regional one, with ravioli del plin, cardi gobbi, Piedmont veal and hazelnuts to mention just a few that cannot be missed, but also various fish dishes that are truly remarkable, with a touch of contemporaneity, starting with excellent raw materials.

Name: Dimora Ulmo
Description: The three tasting menus (Contaminazioni, Dimora Ulmo and A mano libera) served at this restaurant housed in an old restored palazzo with a splendid summer terrace overlooking the Sassi feature a balance of modern cuisine and traditional local dishes. The dining room is equally attractive, while the interesting wine list includes labels from the region alongside a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Osaka
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Tucked away in a short arcade on the old road from Milan to Como, this restaurant has a simple, minimalist style with a bar where diners can watch the skilful chefs slicing and preparing the fish. Set menus dominate at lunchtime, while in the evening the à la carte options include sukiyaki, a celebratory dish in Japan.

Name: La Cantina di Manuela
Description: The dining room in this young, dynamic restaurant is surrounded by bottles of wine. Elaborate dishes feature on the menu, with antipasti available in the evening. At lunchtime these are replaced by various salads aimed at a business clientele in a hurry. Milanese-style cutlets are the house speciality.

Name: Stefano Paganini alla Corte degli Alfieri
Description: Occupying a superb 17C castle, this restaurant has two dining rooms: one is decorated with works by local artists which change throughout the year, while the other, more romantic in feel, is adorned with roses and boasts splendid frescoed ceilings. There’s no choice here, just a tasting menu (although guests can select just a few courses if they wish), but the cuisine is of excellent quality and offers good value for money.

Name: Da Miky
Address: via Fegina 104, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Situated right on the seafront, Miky is one of the best restaurants for fish (including the famous Monterosso anchovies) in the region, serving cuisine which is more and more exciting and individual every year. There’s also a small shop selling local produce.

Name: La Corte
Address: via San Pancrazio 41, Palazzolo sull'Oglio, 25036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Mediterranean-style dishes take pride of place in this attractive restaurant which serves meat and fish dishes and prioritises seasonal ingredients. A visit to the well-stocked wine cellar is highly recommended!

Name: Buca di Bacco
Description: The seafood specialities, the care in the choice of rare produce and the originality of the Proprietor characterise this establishment, situated as it is in the basement of a building.

Name: Da Bibe
Description: Immortalised by the Italian writer Montale in his poetry, this trattoria has been run by the same family for almost two centuries. The menu features traditional Tuscan dishes, such as pici pasta with wild boar sauce. Alfresco dining in summer. There are also apartments with kitchens for guests that wish to extend their stay.

Name: Il Trillo
Description: Situated in the hills overlooking the town, this restaurant occupies an old house that is also home to the estate’s wine cellars. Charming setting and cuisine full of flavour, with the option of alfresco dining on the panoramic terrace in summer.

Name: La Gallina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This attractive restaurant offers three tasting menus featuring traditional and more creative dishes, in which influences from Piedmont, Liguria and Campania (the chef’s native region) combine, with truffles taking centre stage in autumn and home-grown vegetables in spring. Culinary highlights include Piedmontese-style Fassona beef tartare (the beef is sourced from the La Granda consortium) and cream ice-cream whipped in a 1982 Carpigiani machine served with a selection of sweet delicacies. The decision to offer wine uniquely from Champagne and Piedmont is somewhat unusual but works well – we recommend the house Barbera del Monferrato, preferably one that has been laid down for a few years.

Name: Locanda del Falco
Address: Castello di Rivalta 4, Rivalta Trebbia, 29010, Italy
Description: Housed in a medieval hamlet, this traditional restaurant serves typical specialities from Piacenza, as well as other dishes full of creativity and imagination. All are accompanied by wines from the region (the wine list seems to have them all! ) and elsewhere in Italy. Winter evenings are brightened by the large indoor fireplaces, while a 100 year - old wisteria provides shade in the welcoming inner courtyard in summer.

Name: Pacifico
Description: Although its dining rooms are fairly small, this restaurant, which acts as an ambassador for Peruvian cuisine with the occasional Asian influence, has an attractive, trendy ambience and a theatrical feel. Excellent choice of ceviche – raw fish or seafood dishes marinated in lemon and flavoured with spices such as chilli pepper and coriander – which are a typical speciality of Latin American countries along the Pacific coast.

Name: Il Liberty
Description: Occupying an Art Nouveau-style palazzo, this small restaurant with two rooms and a loft area has a friendly, welcoming atmosphere. The menu includes a selection of fish and meat dishes.

Name: Il 25
Description: Housed in a late-19C palazzo, this restaurant serves a good selection of meat and fish dishes with both traditional and creative cuisine on the menu. Delicious flavours typical of the Emilia region.

Name: Opera|02
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A farm with rooms, a spa, a bistro and a gourmet restaurant! At the latter, enjoy regional cuisine with a creative twist added by the chef, on two tasting menus that can be modified as required. Don’t miss the chocolate soufflé served with hazelnut ice cream and caramel sauce. The farm’s own produce can also be purchased here.

Name: Tosca
Description: This restaurant has a charming decor that combines classic elegance and typical Tuscan features such as stone arches and walls, as well as stylish sofas and comfortable armchairs. The cuisine is heavily influenced by local traditions, albeit with a fresh and innovative twist.

Name: Tola Rasa
Description: Having mastered his culinary repertoire working in other restaurants, the chef at the elegant and minimalist Tola Rasa creates successful reinterpretations of classic Italian dishes by adding exotic spices and other ingredients (often from Asia) to his dishes. The gourmet dining room on the ground floor is supplemented by a wine bar in the annexe which serves a selection of snacks. Book a table facing the kitchen to watch the chef at work!

Name: La Leggenda dei Frati
Description: After an uphill approach if you’re arriving here on foot, you come into the Villa Bardini museum complex and from there into this elegant and welcoming restaurant which provides the setting for delicious, creative and modern cuisine. Here, chef Filippo Saporito, never one to rest on his laurels, continues to experiment and perfect his cuisine, which focuses mainly on Italian culinary traditions and a scrupulous selection of top-quality ingredients, preferably from sustainable supply chains (various types of meat, bread and pasta), all showcased on different menus, including a vegetarian option. In summer, enjoy your meal on the romantic terrace surrounded by greenery and the scents of herbs, with a glimpse of Santa Croce church as a backdrop. Although the centre of Florence is not far away, it seems as though you’re already in the Tuscan hills, even with the occasional sound of cicadas in the background.

Name: Cascina Vittoria
Description: Situated in a rural setting surrounded by rice fields outside Milan, this restaurant specialises in home-made pasta and breads, vegetables grown in its own garden, and Piedmontese meat cooked in traditional fashion over a barbecue grill. Takeaway produce is also available for purchase.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Housed on the first floor of an old silkworm factory, with a contemporary-style dining room that opens out on to a beautiful terrace in fine weather, this restaurant is one of the few in the province to serve top-quality fish and seafood, including a good selection of raw options. The cooked dishes on offer demonstrate a light modern touch and are prepared whenever possible using vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Umberto a Mare
Description: Situated in a breathtaking location below the Chiesa del Soccorso, this restaurant boasts views of the sea and sunset that are hard to beat, while its fine, elegant cuisine, based on updated Campanian recipes, is more than a match for the spectacular setting. Featuring delicious dishes such as tagliatelle with squid, lemon and soya milk, a reinterpreted version of parmigiana, “mescafrancesca” (mixed pasta) with prawns and Controne beans, and a mouthwatering dessert trolley, Umberto is one of the island’s unmissable restaurants. The impressive wine cellar (which can be visited) is home to more than 1 000 labels, including a fine selection of champagnes.

Name: Lillotatini
Description: Situated in the heart of a small medieval castle-hamlet, this traditional-style restaurant with an attractive terrace on the historic square provides the setting for local specialities such as freshwater fish and truffles in season. There’s also a wine boutique on the same piazza (reached as soon as you come into the historic centre), which sells typical local produce and a good selection of wine. The latter also features on the restaurant’s wine list, with the family on hand to offer recommendations.

Name: Imperialino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Treat yourself to dinner in this elegant restaurant right on the lakefront, dining in summer in the beautiful garden within a stone’s throw of the lake. The menu features imaginative Mediterranean specialities (meat as well as fresh- and saltwater fish) on two tasting menus and an extensive à la carte.

Name: Da Gigi
Address: piazza IV Novembre 4, Crandola Valsassina, 23832, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Enjoy specialities from Valsassina in this friendly restaurant in a panoramic location. There is a rustic ambience in the dining room with cuisine focusing on local ingredients (many of which are organic), and produce from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Hidalgo
Description: Although fish dishes also feature on the menu, Hidalgo has long enjoyed a reputation for its excellent meat options thanks to its different cuts of steak and beef sourced from all around the world and cooked mainly (but not exclusively) on the barbecue grill. In a separate room(Aomi, a kind of restaurant within the restaurant), guests can choose from a menu dedicated uniquely (from antipasti to main courses) to Japanese Wagyubeef.

Name: Ai Cadelach
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Enjoy local cuisine in a rustic - style dining room or alongside the swimming pool in summer. The menu focuses on meat dishes (especially grilled meat), such as traditional Fiorentina steak and Alpago lamb. Wine lovers will appreciate the excellent wine cellar kept by Ezio, one of the restaurant owners.

Name: Antica Moka
Description: Situated on the Via Emilia, this elegant, owner-run restaurant has for decades been renowned for its top-quality regional cuisine with an updated twist, as well as its reinterpreted fish specialities. Our inspector very much enjoyed the cuisine here, with a particular mention for the home-made pastas and excellent wine selection.

Name: Forentum
Description: This rustic, family restaurant in the historic centre serves local specialities, some of which are made using produce grown in the family vegetable garden. The inner dining room has a charming ambience, thanks to a natural cave which is hundreds of years old. Simple yet well - equipped guestrooms are also available.

Name: Le Vele
Address: via Litoranea Sud 71, Bagni 70, Misano Adriatico, 47843, Italy
Description: This modern, minimalist - style restaurant is practically on the beach and almost within touching distance of the sea. It specialises in fish dishes with a contemporary flavour.

Name: Al Fogher
Address: strada statale 117 bis, Piazza Armerina, 94015, Italy
Description: This small, rustic-style restaurant just outside the centre of Piazza Armerina serves personalised cuisine in which local ingredients take pride of place. Influences from elsewhere in Italy are also evident, with dishes such as artichoke pansotti (stuffed pasta) with local tuma cheese and black truffles on the menu.

Name: Antica Locanda dell'Orco
Description: Fans of Piedmontese cuisine will find one of its best exponents in this restaurant located at the end of a beautiful porticoed street in the historic centre. Savour some of Italy’s most exciting regional cooking, such as snails, bagna caoda, agnolotti pasta, a few (mainly freshwater) fish dishes, braised and boiled meats, “finanziera” stew and some extraordinary desserts – all prepared in magnificent style.

Name: La Refezione
Description: An imaginative cuisine for the elegant "club - house" located inside a sports centre; managed by two great enthusiasts of the culinary art. You will receive a hearty welcome.

Name: Io Osteria Personale
Description: The young owner of this restaurant has an interesting background – a former vet with a passion for food. He has opened one of the most fascinating restaurants in Florence, serving original dishes to diners looking for a change from more traditional fare.

Name: La Lumira
Description: Situated in a village famous for its “tortellino in brodo” dish, Lumira serves Emilian cuisine with a modern twist. Highlights on the menu include fresh home-made pasta such as traditional tortellini and modern tagliatelle verdi with a beef and pea ragù, as well as the highly recommended veal fillet in a traditional balsamic vinegar sauce, which is full of intense flavours. Contemporary decor and welcoming service add to the relaxing dining experience. Among the Sangiovesi wines from Romagna on the wine list, we recommend Lillybet, a well-structured red with superb floral notes.

Name: Due Pini
Address: via Spinale 37/bis, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Although recently restored, this restaurant has retained its strong Alpine character. The cuisine is regional in style and reinterpreted with an imaginative and contemporary twist.

Name: Il Barolino
Description: The friendliness and Emilian genuineness of the Barolo brothers and of the whole team cheers a break here where you can enjoy the authentic regional cuisine. Parmesan cream tortellini are a must: large portions and top quality of these little pasta bundles still strictly made by hand! The room is simple and suitable above all for informal meetings among friends and colleagues.

Name: Giardinetto
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated on the lakeshore in the elegant Hotel Giardinetto (now approaching its centenary), this restaurant boasts stunning views of the lake and San Giulio island. The focus here is on Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist, while the hotel’s Roof Top Bar is the perfect place for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Locanda del Feudo
Address: via Trasversale 2, Castelvetro di Modena, 41014, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic upper section of this picturesque village, this romantic restaurant serves imaginative and colourful cuisine including some excellent local cured hams. There are also six elegant, recently renovated suites with a historic feel, plus a small, charming outdoor space overlooking the main street.

Name: La Sponda
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: An elegant restaurant within Le Sirenuse, one of the most prestigious and glamorous hotels on the Amalfi coast, with an attractive outdoor terrace for summer dining with views of Positano’s colourful houses clinging to the cliff face. Whether you choose to eat inside or out, a romantic atmosphere is guaranteed thanks to the hundreds of candles lit every evening. At the helm, Neapolitan chef Gennaro Russo maintains the restaurant’s high standards with his Mediterranean dishes, often influenced by Campania and inspired by classic favourites. The flavours of southern Italy are showcased in delicious dishes such as lemon risotto with capers.

Name: Riso Amaro
Description: This elegant, contemporary-style restaurant is situated right in the historic centre. The menu features a host of gourmet dishes as well as more modern fish and meat options, all created by the talented owner-chef.

Name: Bistrot 64
Description: The classic-style dining room in this restaurant situated in the Flaminio district belies the gourmet discoveries that await here, with echoes of traditions from Lazio that act as inspiration for creative, top-quality dishes with the occasional Asian twist.

Name: L'A Gourmet L'Accademia
Address: via Largo C. Colombo 6, Reggio Calabria, 89125, Italy
Description: From the classic restaurant on the first floor (no lift) of this early 20C palazzo, you’ll enjoy fine views of the sea and the Strait of Messina. Here, skilled chef Filippo Cogliardo prepares fish-based dishes which include classic recipes (raw seafood and amberjack with rapini) as well as more modern options (cuttlefish tagliatelle with avocado cream, cucumber and salted lemon). A few meat dishes also feature on the menu. Definitely the best restaurant in town!

Name: Bistrot
Description: Overlooking a delightful, quiet little square, this romantic, welcoming restaurant serves traditional local specialities, often with an individual flavour. The menu includes some fish dishes, although the house speciality is the maltagliati pasta served with ‘Bistrot’ sauce.

Name: Il Merlo
Address: via Bernardini 660, Lido di Camaiore, 55041, Italy
Description: With a new location right on the beach, Il Merlo boasts a welcoming dining room decorated in elegant, contemporary style. Fish dishes take pride of place on the menu, although meat options are also available.

Name: Osteria Numero Sette
Description: There’s been a recent change in management at this informal, friendly restaurant which serves generously portioned, carefully prepared dishes from the region and elsewhere in Italy, all at highly competitive prices. Although the cuisine might not be particularly modern, this is good solid cuisine served in a welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Boccadoro
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Padova, this classically elegant restaurant is very popular with locals – and for good reason! The menu includes skilfully prepared dishes influenced by the traditions of the Veneto (from bigoli pasta to dried cod and liver Venetian-style) as well as a selection of grilled options.

Name: LeoneFelice Vista Lago
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant has an all-encompassing approach that includes fish, meat and vegetables on a classically influenced menu featuring dishes such as snails in butter and “liquid buttons” with Parmesan cheese and cinnamon. The “field and garden” vegetarian dishes include interesting recipes such as roasted broccoli with toasted cashews. The wine list focuses on the estate’s own labels and the Franciacorta region in general.

Name: Al Vigneto
Address: via Don Pietro Belotti 1, Grumello del Monte, 24064, Italy
Description: An elegant restaurant occupying a restored hay barn surrounded by its own vineyards and fruit trees. The menu here focuses on modern cuisine, including marinated raw fish and seafood (especially from Sicily), although meat dishes also feature. We highly recommend the restaurant’s own wine – you’ll definitely want to buy a few bottles to take home with you!

Name: Essenziale
Address: piazza di Cestello 3 r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant (once a garage) on Piazza di Cestello has a young, minimalist ambience. The welcome and service here are friendly, while the cuisine is never ordinary, offering combinations that are pleasantly contrasting without being too bold. The chef, who is originally from Livorno, is particularly adept at creating fish and seafood dishes. You’ll find your cutlery in a drawer in your table, in an interesting nod to household traditions of bygone days.

Name: Trattoria del Vicolo
Description: Overlooking the piazza for almost 50 years, this restaurant has been modernised but has nonetheless managed to retain its friendly, no - frills appeal. The walls are decorated with paintings by the chef, who serves up regional gastronomic creations reinterpreted with a contemporary twist.

Name: Punta Lena
Address: via Monsignor Di Mattina 8, località Ficogrande, Stromboli, 98055, Italy
Description: Service is under a pergola with an exceptional view over the sea and Strombolicchio, it is perfect for any type of occasion. Fish based cuisine.

Name: Da Giovanni
Description: An excellent wine list and Piacenza dishes to taste at tables which are well spaced out in the large dining room with an elegant - rustic character, furnished in a pleasant fashion.

Name: Hosteria Giusti
Description: Situated in an attractive retro-style room to the rear of an elegant delicatessen, this restaurant offers just four tables and a restricted menu of top-quality, traditional Emilian dishes. In the evening, the restaurant is open by reservation only for groups of at least 12 people with a pre-arranged menu.

Name: Oberwirt
Description: The various Stube-style dining rooms in the Oberwirt hotel restaurant have a typical Tyrolean ambience, while the cuisine is decidedly traditional with its focus on seasonal and regional ingredients, although a few fish options also always feature on the menu. Wine-enthusiasts will be delighted with the excellent wine selection.

Name: Il Capestrano
Address: via Gian Francesco Pizzi 14, Milan, 20141, Italy
Description: This restaurant takes its name from the warrior statue dating back to the 6C BC which was discovered in Capestrano (Aquila province) in 1934. The statue, carved from a single block of local stone, is one of the most mysterious finds in history. No such mystery surrounds the dishes served in this restaurant, which focuses on cuisine from the Abruzzo, including top-quality hams and cheeses produced by small-scale producers, as well as mutton, lamb, beef, barbecued lamb kebabs and other culinary delights.

Name: Locanda dei Salinari
Description: In the old village of Salinari, a young enterprising chef runs this simple restaurant. His creative cuisine is prepared with the best regional produce of Romagna.

Name: Il Gallo della Checca
Description: This restaurant wine - bar proposes some interesting culinary specialities based on local recipes. The dining hall features a fine display of bottles and, needless to say, the wine list is all that one could wish.

Name: Cucina Cereda
Address: via Piazzini 33, Ponte San Pietro, 24036, Italy
Description: A typical entrance leads into the courtyard of what was a monastery in the late 16C at this restaurant, where the dining room has a classic atmosphere. However, it is the cuisine that steals the show – it is creative, yet down-to-earth with no unnecessary frills, full of flavour, and features meat and fish dishes inspired by Italian traditions with the occasional local twist. There’s a simpler, business-style menu at lunchtime, while among the à la carte options we particularly enjoyed the snails served with morel mushrooms and a careful seasoning of parsley and coriander, and the paccheri pasta with fish soup in which the bouillabaisse-style sauce added a real Mediterranean flavour.

Name: Il Rivale al Lago
Address: via Marconi 93, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant serving Mediterranean cuisine, where the emphasis is more on meat in winter and fish in summer. Welcoming ambience, with a number of different dining spaces, including a small room in the wine cellar where numerous bottles act as a backdrop (including a good selection of champagnes) and a spacious outdoor area with views of the lake and well-tended garden.

Name: Cielo
Description: Cielo is the gourmet restaurant at the splendid and aptly named La Sommità hotel, which is housed in a typical old mansion right at the top of this whitewashed town with its limestone steps. The restaurant offers the perfect setting for a romantic summer dinner, either among the citrus trees in the small inner courtyard or in the dining room crowned with a vaulted ceiling. Boasting a highly respectable CV, the chef from Martina Franca serves modern reinterpretations of Puglian cuisine, while the delightful terrace is perfect for an aperitif at sunset. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime.

Name: L'Archivolto - Osteria Nostrale
Description: This restaurant in set in a typical country inn. It has heavy hams, which jealously guards a small niche, and chequered tablecloths. Sample the Piedmontese cuisine with a Ligurian influence, abundant portions and quality ingredients. You will find a good dose of friendliness and charm.

Name: Locanda Perbellini
Description: Highly renowned in his native Verona, Michelin - starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini has now opened a restaurant in Milan, where he continues to offer traditional Italian cuisine from the north and south of the country, with a nod to new techniques and contemporary trends. Situated in the central Brera district, his warm and welcoming restaurant is small, discreet and, of course, highly elegant.

Name: Sapereta
Address: via Provinciale Ovest 73, località Mola, Porto Azzurro, 57036, Italy
Description: Housed in a historic winery, this simple, rustic - style restaurant is surrounded by a well - kept garden where farmyard animals roam freely. Don’t be fooled by appearances, however – the cuisine here is modern, with meat dishes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: Ora d'Aria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Situated behind the Uffizi, this restaurant boasts a large open-view kitchen and an original approach that focuses on creating meaningful dialogue between guests and the chefs in the kitchen. The restaurant owes its name to the old Florentine Le Murate prison nearby, as well as to its stated aim of providing guests with time to breathe and relax. The dishes here are influenced by Tuscan traditions and Italian cuisine alike yet reinterpreted with a creative touch and a greater emphasis on vegetables. The tasting menus include the Menu Bendato, which features specialities chosen by the chef, and the La Bistecca alla fiorentinaoption (available by prior booking only), on which the famous Florentine steak is presented in different guises. An impressive wine list completes the picture.

Name: Kro
Address: via Tollarini 70/c, località Pontagna di Temù, Ponte di Legno, 25050, Italy
Description: The courteous service, stylish mountain decor of wood and stone, and regional cuisine with a modern twist are just some of the attractions of this restaurant, whose name loosely translates as “inn”. A real treat for the eyes and the tastebuds!

Name: Aimo e Nadia BistRo
Description: This bistro with a small yet charming and original dining room is a simpler and more informal version of the famous starred restaurant. The focus is the same, with an emphasis on Italian ingredients used in dishes which bring out their full flavour and integrity.

Name: Truth Restaurant
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant, with an open-view kitchen, where two different styles of cuisine can be enjoyed: creative tapas influenced by different traditions, or more classic, local dishes.

Name: Gino Sorbillo
Description: Situated along the "via della pizza", this historic restaurant boasts a simple yet lively ambience with a local and international feel. Excellent pizzas made from quality - label produce. You’ll need plenty of patience if you’re here at busy times and if you choose to share a table, you’ll really enjoy the convivial atmosphere!

Name: La Kuccagna
Address: via Milano 14, località Barbuzzera, Dovera, 26010, Italy
Description: Boasting a fresh, top-quality feel, La Kuccagna is run by a young and energetic management team. The menu features meat and fish dishes alike, including cuts of meat cooked over the ever-present barbecue grill. An excellent wine list including labels from outside Italy, an exquisite rural location and a modern, comfortable decor complete the picture.

Name: Marina del Nettuno
Address: viale della Libertà-Batteria Masotto, Messina, 98121, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant and lounge bar is situated right on the jetty of the Yachting Club Messina. Elegant and minimalist - style decor, as well as creative cuisine with a focus on fish dishes.

Name: Alla Laguna - Vedova Raddi
Description: Situated in a charming small town criss-crossed by canals, this restaurant serves traditionally inspired fish-based dishes. The restaurant stands on the port facing the fish market, so it’s no surprise that the fish served here is of the freshest quality.

Name: Chalet Piereni
Address: località Piereni 8, Val Canali, Tonadico, 38054, Italy
Description: The delicious cuisine served at this restaurant is the only thing that could possibly distract from the beauty of its delightful natural setting. Typical local produce takes pride of place in the regional fare served here, which includes special dishes for younger diners.

Name: Gratschwirt
Description: Housed in a building which dates back to the 16C and is part of the hotel of the same name, this Stube-style restaurant at the foot of the Tre Cime is typical of the Alto Adige, as is the simple, abundant regional cuisine served here. Highlights on the menu include dumplings in broth, herb-crusted lamb, apple strudel and the less traditional but excellent beef tartare which is seasoned at your table.

Name: Rio Bistrot
Description: Situated on the street that heads down to the port in charming Riomaggiore, this lovely, well-kept restaurant offers a small selection of dishes split between Ligurian specialities and more creative options. Dine in the rustic, elegant dining room or on the outdoor terrace.

Name: I Sette Consoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In this simple restaurant boasting an attractive outdoor summer garden and splendid views of the Duomo, chef Anna Rita focuses on carefully selected ingredients from the region and beyond. Highlights include soft egg, pan-fried courgettes and spring onions, and pecorino crumble, as well as soft veal rump, Jerusalem artichoke sauce and home-made pickled vegetables. The wine and spirits selection is particularly appealing – as an example, the Orvieto Classico Superiore Doc “Vendemmia Tardiva” is the perfect pairing for your dessert.

Name: Belvedere
Address: Forte Village - SS 195, km 39,600, Santa Margherita, 09050, Italy
Description: Il Belvedere is the gourmet restaurant at Forte Village. Enjoy modern, distinctly Mediterranean cuisine either in the dining room or on the terrace overlooking a delightful garden. Although you pay for a fixed menu, in practice you can choose à la carte; in summer the hotel hosts cooking shows and themed dinners with famous chefs.

Name: Il Giardino "Da Felicin"
Description: A bastion of classic Piedmontese cuisine, this restaurant housed in a beautiful period palazzo boasts a panoramic terrace and a romantic garden for alfresco dining. The dining rooms echo the palazzo’s sumptuous and traditional feel, as does the timeless, regional cuisine which is carefully prepared and full of delicious flavours. The building is also home to an “albergo diffuso” hotel, with some guestrooms in the building itself and others dotted around the village, including in Palazzo Boeri which also has a small spa (reservation required). The owners are happy to share their knowledge of the Langhe, either on their own guided tours or visits led by another local expert.

Name: Trita Pepe
Address: via Gabriele D'Annunzio 4, Manoppello Scalo, 65024, Italy
Description: Situated on the road that passes through Manoppello Scalo, this restaurant with a car park right in front of the building boasts a spacious, simple dining room and is our recommended choice in the region for anyone keen to try typical Abruzzo cuisine. Meat takes pride of place among the main courses (with an exception for salted cod), while menu highlights include excellent fried gnocchi with local salumi and cheese.

Name: Casa della Rocca
Description: Situated in picturesque Dolcedo, this restaurant occupies an early 20C mill complete with millstone and press. The cuisine focuses on an interesting selection of traditional Ligurian dishes with a satisfying balance of meat and fish (occasionally on the same plate), plus creative touches and hints of the Piedmont, all of which combine to make a trip to this inland restaurant well worth while!

Name: Dina
Description: Housed in what appears to be a simple village house on a street corner, this restaurant boasts four original and comfortable dining rooms, including the romantic rustic ambience of the former wine cellar, with its mix of modern, designer-style furnishings. Sitting at pleasantly large and elegant tables, guests have a choice of tasting menus from which individual dishes can also be ordered. Alberto Gipponi’s cuisine is a fine balance of tradition and creativity, served in one of the region’s most interesting restaurants.

Name: Koinè
Description: Whether you dine in the modern dining room at this centrally located palazzo or in the small courtyard in fine weather, Alberto Buratti offers a choice of tasting menus (including the vegetarian “1MQ d’orto”), alongside a concise à la carte. His cuisine includes a combination of local dishes (from classic risottos to breaded veal) and more creative fare.

Name: L'Uva e il Malto
Description: A talented couple run this modern, intimate restaurant with a wine-bar right in the town centre. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with the catch of the day announced at your table, including delicious shellfish. The female owner oversees the extensive wine list, which features reasonably priced and mostly Tuscan labels.

Name: Maso Burba
Address: via Bernardelli 32, località Piano, Commezzadura, 38020, Italy
Description: Having spent time working in top-quality restaurants, Gianpaolo Burba – alongside his partner Paola who works front of house – has returned home to the family restaurant in a small village in the Val di Sole region. Here, he makes the most of his experience and skills acquired elsewhere to showcase the best of the region’s ingredients in his beautifully presented dishes (although fish does make a rare appearance on the menu). The dining rooms, including a covered veranda, are bright, elegant and typically regional in style.

Name: Il Fico trentacareghe
Description: Situated on one of the region’s most beautiful coast roads, this restaurant with a charming garden of olive trees boasts stunning views of the sea which can be admired either from the dining room or, even better, from the summer terrace. The cuisine is equal to the setting, with a focus on fish and seafood dishes influenced by Ligurian traditions.

Name: 20Tre
Address: via David Chiossone 20 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of Genoa’s historic centre, this contemporary-style restaurant focuses on just a few dishes, almost all fish-based, presented in a very modern style and in generous portions. Seasonal ingredients and market-fresh produce are the guiding philosophy here.

Name: Valli di Lanzo
Description: The sign outside this restaurant in the centre of the typical village of Céres bears the words “Ristourànt Valàdess at Lanss con Oubèrgi”. Enjoy regional cuisine with a personalised twist, with local products from the valley featuring in many of the specialities served here, all accompanied by a good selection of regional, Italian and international wines. Outdoor dining area available in summer.

Name: Blaue Traube
Description: This extremely old restaurant (its name is said to have existed as early as the mid 17C) has been given a new lease of life in 2019 by its young chef Christoph Huber, who puts to good use the many experiences gained over the years in different restaurants, including Michelin-starred addresses. His dishes pay tribute to Southern Tyrolean recipes and ingredients with an added contemporary twist.

Name: Cuoco di Bordo
Description: An attractively furnished restaurant on the seafront with a small dining room and a veranda offering partial views of the sea. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, which focuses on raw fish dishes and classic recipes. The wine list is excellent, especially the whites (although the reds also include some impressive options) with many different vintages of the same wine available.

Name: QB DuePuntoZero
Address: via Pietro da Salò 23, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description: On the lakefront facing the small port, this modern, simply styled restaurant has a pleasant area for summer dining. Contemporary cuisine made from carefully selected produce.

Name: Nives
Address: via Nives 4, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
Description: Housed within the Boutique Hotel Nives, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant focuses on specialities from the Alto Adige (with the addition of a couple of fish dishes that nearly always feature on the menu), as well as large cuts of meat for sharing, served on a hot stone. An interesting wine list completes the picture.

Name: Le Colonne
Address: via Benefattori 7, Santa Maria Maggiore, 28857, Italy
Description: In the small historic center of town, a couple with comprehensive management experience operates this well maintained, modest restaurant offering eclectic cuisine.

Name: Piazza dei Mestieri
Description: Situated on a redeveloped industrial site and part of a training school, this restaurant offers a more concise menu at lunchtime with lower prices than the evening, but with the same high-quality cuisine. Our inspector recommends the spaghetti with spring onion and bottarga, accompanied by one of the craft beers produced on site. There’s also an attractive terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: Al Dragone
Description: Occupying a natural cave, this typical restaurant serves traditional regional dishes prepared with care and imagination. House specialities include scampi in an almond crust.

Name: Antinoo's Lounge
Address: calle del Bastion, sestiere Dorsoduro 173, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: Situated in the luxurious Centurian Palace hotel, this restaurant with large windows overlooking the Grand Canal boasts a decidedly designer - style decor. Colourful, modern and imaginative cuisine created by a young chef takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: LPV Ristorante & Bistrot
Address: riva degli Schiavoni, sestiere Castello 4171, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Following the hotel’s rebranding, this restaurant has also recently changed name and chef and now offers bistro-style dishes at lunchtime and more elaborate, refined cuisine in the evening. Choose from three tasting menus: Acqua (an equal balance of fish and seafood); Terra(meat dishes) and Aria (vegetarian options).

Name: Osteria Vecchia Noce
Description: This former 18C mill, located in the centre of a tiny medieval district on the outskirts of Uliveto Terme, boasts a warm, elegant ambience full of character. Expertly run by the same family for the past 35 years, it serves honest, traditional cuisine with a focus on regional recipes and an equal balance of meat and fish.

Name: Filippo
Description: In this modern and elegant restaurant, Filippo chooses three products every day and creates a surprise meal for guests with these ingredients. An original idea which is certainly worth a try, but for less adventurous diners there is also a small menu.

Name: La Colombina
Address: campiello del Pegoloto, sestiere Cannaregio 1828, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: If you find yourself on the road leading to Rialto from the railway station, then you can’t miss this small trattoria - cum - chichetteria serving traditional cuisine with a slightly inventive twist. With the mother working front - of - house and the son in the kitchen, you really can’t go wrong!

Name: Il Molo
Address: via Falcone Borsellino 2, San Leone, 92100, Italy
Description: Situated on the seafront facing the small tourist harbour of San Leone, this elegant restaurant boasts an attractive summer terrace with a relaxed ambience. Here you can savour a selection of regional fish and meat dishes prepared by the owner-chef with ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Osteria alle Testiere
Address: calle del Mondo Novo, sestiere  Castello 5801, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: This restaurant, now one of the most popular bistros in Venice, started out as a typical Venetian “bacaro”. The cuisine focuses on traditional Mediterranean and Venetian dishes, including vegetables, many of which are grown in a kitchen garden on Sant'Erasmo island (Osti in Orto) – an initiative which sees a number of small restaurants coming together to grow and share produce. The menu changes in line with market availability. With just a few tables, booking well in advance is highly recommended.

Name: Alpenrose
Address: via delle Sette Chiese 1, loc. Pinzago, Brixen, 39042, Italy
Description: Situated in a panoramic location a few kilometres outside Bressanone, this simple yet modern restaurant serves regional, classically prepared cuisine with an equally simple, contemporary feel plus a few dishes with the occasional Mediterranean influence. There are also elegant apartments available, plus a wellness space, for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Antico Ristorante Forassiepi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is renowned in the province of Lucca, thanks to the reliable owners who have been at the helm here (the restaurant’s history goes back to the early 20C) since 2004. With its elegant decor and courteous and attentive service, the restaurant has a charming ambience in summer when meals are served alfresco with stunning views of the typical Tuscan hills, valleys and villages all around. The restaurant also owes its success to its cuisine, which focuses on regional specialities (both meat and fish) reinterpreted with a modern twist.

Name: Menarosti
Description: Dating back to 1903, this historic restaurant has a warm, welcoming feel. Excellent fish and seafood prepared using top - quality ingredients, where simple preparation allows the flavours to shine through.

Name: L'Accanto
Address: via Santa Maria Vecchia 2, loc. Seiano, Vico Equense, 80066, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Having left the busy coastal road behind you, you come into the peaceful and luxurious enclave of the Angiolieri hotel and its classically elegant L’Accanto restaurant. As soon as the weather allows, dinner is served outdoors on one of the most spectacular terraces in the area, overlooking the Bay of Naples and its breathtaking sunsets. The top-quality cuisine focuses mainly on the abundant recipes and ingredients of Campania.

Name: Ai Gondolieri
Address: fondamenta de l'Ospedaleto, sestiere Dorsoduro 366, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Situated behind the Guggenheim museum, this rustic restaurant with wood panelling on the walls offers a meat-based menu that focuses on traditional, regional cuisine (the braised rack of lamb with spinach tortino with butter and parmesan cheese is superb). The well-stocked wine cellar is home to a huge selection of white, red and sparkling wines, plus there’s an extensive choice of cocktails. At Ai Gondolieri, enjoy a good glass of wine accompanied by typical Venetian fare such as cured hams and sweet-and-sour vegetables.

Name: Tancredi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Having trained with Antonino Cannavacciuolo, young chef Vincenzo Manicone has, with his wife Sara, embarked on a new venture in this elegant restaurant with a glass-fronted dining room and a terrace suspended between the lake and the sky. Showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte, the chef’s cuisine demonstrates a maturity that pays close attention to colour and flavour, with beautifully presented dishes prepared from top-quality, well-balanced ingredients. Also evident is the aim, currently in vogue, of reducing food waste by using every single part of the animal (as in the case of the excellent amberjack, curly salad and sea urchin dish that we very much enjoyed). In summer, we recommend requesting a table at the front of the terrace, right over the lake.

Name: Sogno
Address: via Porto San Felice 41, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This aptly named restaurant (“sogno” is the Italian for dream) really is a dream come true, especially in summer when you can dine on the romantic lakeside terrace. The delicious Mediterranean-style cuisine will more than satisfy your tastebuds, while there’s also the option of staying in the hotel of the same name. Private mooring available.

Name: Locanda Perbellini - Ai Beati
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated amid the foothills around Garda, this restaurant boasts fine views from its verdant terrace which take in much of the southern part of the lake, while its dining rooms occupy the interior of an old olive mill. The menu features freshwater fish such as pike and whitefish as well as seafood and meat dishes.

Name: Beccaccino
Description: Situated within a nature reserve, this recently renovated restaurant makes the most of its natural materials and bright, airy feel. The menu focuses on fish dishes made from freshwater and saltwater fish alike.

Name: Piccolo Lord
Address: corso San Maurizio 69 bis/g, Turin, 10124, Italy
Description: Professional service in a welcoming, modern restaurant run by a young couple. He works in the kitchen while she (having also worked as a chef in the past) runs the front of house. Delicious Mediterranean cuisine with a seasonal focus.

Name: Vairo del Volturno
Address: via IV Novembre 58, Vairano Patenora, 81058, Italy
Description: Showcasing regional produce, from vegetables to meat and mozzarella to fish from the nearby Tyrrhenian sea, is a real mission for the owner-chef of this elegant restaurant, who makes the most of these ingredients in his contemporary-style cuisine.

Name: Hostaria alla Tavernetta
Address: via Artico di Prampero 2, Udine, 33100, Italy
Description: This fine restaurant immediately puts you at your ease thanks to a very jovial and friendly atmosphere. The lit fireplace, wood furniture with stylish linen runners and background music make for an excellent break. In addition to traditional courses such as cjarsons or the typical frico, there are more seasonal and Mediterranean fish dishes. Vegan menu available.

Name: Terrazza Danieli
Address: riva degli Schiavoni, sestiere Castello 4196, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Mirrors and fabrics add to the luxurious atmosphere in the dining room at this restaurant, but it is the outdoor terrace (open between May and October) with its 180° views of the lagoon and islands that is its crowning glory. The menu changes regularly in line with the seasons, and features fresh, local ingredients with the occasional hint of exotic spices as is only fitting for Venice!

Name: Le Grenier
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Modern Cuisine
Description: In the heart of Saint Vincent, this restaurant has a hint of an old granary (grenier in French) with tumbling grain, a fireplace and period tools on the walls. But the surprise doesn’t end there: the kitchen seduces its guests with unexpectedly modern dishes, some reminiscent of the Val d’Aosta tradition.

Name: Il Calandrino
Address: via Liguria 1, loc. Sarmeola, Rubano, 35030, Italy
Description: Situated next to the three-Michelin-starred Le Calandre (and run by the same family), Il Calandrino is an elegant and eclectic restaurant which includes a bar-cum-pasticceria that is well worth visiting at any time of day. The cuisine here ranges from creative dishes such as hare cappuccino in red wine to classic house favourites such as Erminio’s legendary tartare and the pazientina cake with zabaione.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: A small indoor dining room and a veranda with a lake view and sliding windows which open completely in summer provide the setting for regionally inspired dishes and lake specialities at this restaurant.

Name: Antico Morer
Description: Not far from the Duomo, this historic restaurant takes its name from the mulberry tree (morer in local dialect) that once stood in front of the building. Elegant, simple decor in the dining room, which is adorned with a wooden - beamed ceiling. The menu features fish and seafood, including a good choice of raw dishes.

Name: Scrigno del Duomo
Description: This restaurant boasts a stunning setting that includes Roman foundations, 15C frescoes and 19C furnishings. Choose between two types of cuisine: traditional ham, salami and regional dishes in the Wine Bar, or more sophisticated, inventive fare in the old cellar.

Name: Il Convito della Venaria
Address: via Andrea Mensa 37/g, Venaria Reale, 10078, Italy
Description: This restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, with Lucia front of house in the classic and welcoming dining room and Christian at the helm in the kitchen. The menu is lighter (and less expensive) at lunchtime with a wider choice of regional and Italian fare in the evening, plus a few more creative options, including fish dishes. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, two of which have views of the royal palace.

Name: Svevia
Description: Housed in the wine cellars of a historic palazzo, this restaurant is a successful combination of the traditional and the modern. The cuisine focuses on the fish and seafood specialities of the Molise region, with only a few meat dishes on the menu.

Name: La Taverna di San Giuseppe
Description: This building evokes the origins of Siena, from the wine cellar (open to visitors) occupying an Etruscan house from the 3C BC, to the dining room itself, with its Roman brick walls. Courteous staff and authentic Tuscan cuisine, including ribollita soup and galletto al mattone con aromi (brick - baked chicken).

Name: Don Camillo
Description: Miteco, Artemide, Archestrato, and La Nostra Storia are the names of the menus at this restaurant, all of which showcase the ambitious Sicilian cuisine created by chef Guarneri, a lover of beauty and fine wine. The dining room is traditional in style, with tufa walls dating from the 15C, period wood furnishings and wrought-iron chandeliers. The delicious cuisine is expertly prepared, while the service is attentive and professional.

Name: L'Aia dei Cappellani
Description: In the dining room there are old photos and equipment from country life, from the terrace the entire valley. Among widespread grasslands and olive trees enjoy fresh produce and home - cooked local dishes. In the dining room there are old photos and equipment from country life, from the terrace the entire valley. Among widespread grasslands and olive trees enjoy fresh produce and home - cooked local dishes.

Name: Riva
Description: In a small village with a fascinating crenellated castle, this restaurant is run by a husband and wife team. They offer a refined cuisine that is a balanced blend of local recipes and creativity.

Name: Antica Pesa
Description: Typical Roman dishes made from carefully selected ingredients grace the menu of this restaurant, which is housed in a grain storehouse that once belonged to the neighbouring Papal State. Large paintings by contemporary artists hang on the walls and there is a small lounge with a fireplace near the entrance.

Name: Osteria del Mirasole
Address: via Matteotti 17/a, San Giovanni in Persiceto, 40017, Italy
Description: A delightful restaurant overflowing with memories of the past, where the top-quality cuisine has strong roots in the gastronomic traditions of this region, including a selection of meats cooked over the charcoal grill. Fans of Emilian cuisine will be happy to return to this restaurant time and time again, never tiring of its delicious regional fare.

Name: Caffè Dante Bistrot
Description: This restaurant boasts an outdoor terrace overlooking one of the most beautiful squares in Verona, plus an equally attractive 19C-style room for indoor dining.
