It serves a selection of typical local and Italian dishes, with an emphasis on grilled main courses and a careful selection of high-quality meat.

Name: Malga Ces
Address: località Ces, San Martino di Castrozza, 38054, Italy
Description: Located at an altitude of 1 600m, this property close to the ski slopes has a chalet feel. Regional cuisine, plenty of character, plus spacious Alpine-style guestrooms perfect for anyone looking for peace and tranquillity.

Name: Osteria la Fontanina
Address: portichetti Fontanelle Santo Stefano 3, Verona, 37129, Italy
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Roman Theatre and Ponte Pietra, Osteria La Fontanina is one of Verona’s oldest restaurants with a history that dates back over 200 years. The restaurant has a “bohemian” feel, with old mirrors, prints, silverware and plants that combine well with the subdued lighting (even at lunchtime) and just about enough space for the small tables. The cuisine showcases Italian and regional flavours, while the impressive wine list focuses on red wine vintages from the Verona region.

Name: Al Grop
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A long - established, rustic - style restaurant with an impressive open fireplace in the middle of the dining room. The cuisine is seasonal, with grilled meats and white asparagus on the menu at certain times of year. Comfortable apartments with a kitchen area, as well as a delightful courtyard.

Name: La Maison Delfino
Address: via Lagrange 4, borgo Mercato, Moncalieri, 10024, Italy
Description: This small, elegant restaurant outside the centre is enthusiastically run by two brothers: round tables and well - kept dining room for savoring seafood specialities.

Name: Le Rune
Description: Various small dining rooms, including one directly above the kitchen (very popular despite the heat). The food is regional with an emphasis on fish and seafood, and the menu includes some reasonably priced options, as well as individual dishes.

Name: Fana Ladina
Address: via Plan de Corones 10, San Vigilio di Marebbe, 39030, Italy
Description: This restaurant occupies one of the oldest houses in San Vigilio. It serves typical Ladin specialities in wood - clad dining rooms and has a delightful Stube. Among the various specialities on the menu, the crafun (savoury krapfe stuffed with a ragú sauce) are particularly worth sampling.

Name: Trattoria del Pesce
Description: A good selection of fresh and raw fish dishes served in a welcoming, vaguely bistro-style restaurant with young and competent staff. Parking can be difficult, but your patience is definitely rewarded!

Name: Federico II
Description: A quiet restaurant right in the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the cathedral. The young owner prepares creative dishes from the fresh fish and seafood that he purchases on a daily basis.

Name: I Due Cippi dal 1976
Description: The first sight to greet you when you enter this restaurant is a barbecue grill for cooking meat; the meat itself can be seen ageing nearby, with numerous cuts and meats to choose from and the famous Chianina beef taking centre stage. The small yet elegant dining rooms, welcoming ambience and friendly service all add to the appeal, as does the excellent section of wines. Meals are served outdoors in summer.

Name: Patauner
Description: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant on the side of the road dates from the 17C and has been run by the same family for the past century. Today, the third and fourth generations work side by side in the kitchen, preparing dishes with a strong regional flavour. Highlights include the white Terlano asparagus in season and offal dishes throughout the year.

Name: Il Ridotto
Address: campo S.S. Filippo e Giacomo, sestiere Castello 4509, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Both father and son are in the kitchen at this simple yet elegant small restaurant, serving up imaginative dishes that focus not only on local recipes and ingredients but also on gastronomic influences from the whole of Italy.

Name: Villa De Winckels
Address: via Sorio 30, località Marcemigo, Tregnago, 37039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This 16C villa, a period residence with many intimate dining rooms, boasts a picture-postcard setting. The cuisine is typical of the Veneto region, with dishes such as home-made pasta (with or without stuffing) and home-produced charcuterie on the menu. Named after General De Winckels who once lived here, the Cantina del Generale offers a wide selection of the best vintages which include local wines and labels from further field, with a focus on Amarone wines.

Name: Trattoria al Pompiere
Description: This trattoria opposite Juliet’s house (open to the public; admission fee payable) in Verona’s historic centre boasts wood panelling, period photos and tables set close together and adorned with checked tablecloths. The menu features mainly regional cuisine, with plenty of pasta and meat dishes, plus an excellent selection of Italian salumi and cheeses, all accompanied by a good selection of wines.

Name: Osteria del Borro
Address: località Borro 52, San Giustino Valdarno, 52024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Decorated in soft colours, the elegant gourmet restaurant on the first floor (lift available) serves classic regional dishes reinterpreted with a contemporary flavour and hint of modernity. At the Tuscan Bistro on the ground floor, the menu is simpler in style but just as delicious and firmly rooted in the traditions of the local area.

Name: La Perla del Mare
Address: via della Meloria 9, San Vincenzo, 57027, Italy
Description: The occasional creative touch is evident in the fish and seafood dishes served in this welcoming Mediterranean - style restaurant with an attractive outdoor terrace. The restaurant stands right on the beach!

Name: Le Logge del Vignola
Description: This small establishment is a good spot in the old town centre. Its tables are a bit cramped but they have smart table settings and well - prepared, regional ingredients are served.

Name: Ristorante Da Anita - Chalet Prà delle Nasse
Address: via Cavallazza 24, località Prà delle Nasse, San Martino di Castrozza, 38054, Italy
Description: This family-run restaurant is surrounded by views of the Dolomites that are particularly impressive from the outdoor terrace in summer. A historic culinary stalwart among San Martino di Castrozza restaurants, Prà delle Nasse focuses on regional mountain cuisine, although a few more personalised dishes also feature on the menu. The desserts include the grandmother’s traditional tarts alongside more contemporary options.

Name: Baia del Silenzio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In a beautiful position inside the bay, the restaurant serves dishes with a contemporary twist that enhance the local products and the good ingredients. The offer is divided between the bistrot for lunch, the gourmet dinner and the wine bar. In summer you can dine alfresco on the outdoor terrace or directly on the beach.

Name: Osteria Frangipane
Address: via Maraldo da Trani 5, Trani, 76125, Italy
Description: This osteria on the edge of the historic centre is run by two young brothers who have one clear aim – to serve local fish dishes which are both delicious and imaginative. Pleasantly informal atmosphere.

Name: Da Politano
Description: At the kitchen in this restaurant, father-and-son team Claudio and Luca (the latter with experience in numerous renowned restaurants) reinterpret local traditions in their enticing, generous and contemporary-style dishes (fish also features on the menu). The result is top-quality cuisine, which is served by Luca’s friendly and enthusiastic mother Ivana.

Name: Quartopiano Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Perhaps because of its out - of - the - way location in a business district where you would never normally expect to find a restaurant, this restaurant has made every effort to become one of the best in the region, aided by its skilful and gifted chef. Creative cuisine accompanied by an excellent wine list, with a panoramic roof garden for summer dining.

Name: Osteria la Lanterna
Address: via Finali 1, frazione Cressogno, Valsolda, 22010, Italy
Description: Situated on the road leading to Lugano in Switzerland, this charming restaurant with elegant furnishings and a rustic decor boasts bright dining rooms and a pleasant terrace for summer dining. The dishes are prepared with a focus on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients and are inspired by traditional recipes reinterpreted in contemporary style.

Name: i-Fame
Description: Enjoy creative cuisine made from excellent, locally sourced produce in this attractive restaurant. It is decorated in the same white colours and modern style as the hotel.

Name: Antico Albergo
Description: With its exposed bricks and beams, this restaurant housed in an 18C building has a historic feel. Delightful wisteria-shaded summer terrace, plus a menu featuring fish dishes and more creative options alongside traditional specialities from Lombardy.

Name: Al Vecchio Convento
Description: Ask for a table in the main dining room, with a classic atmosphere and elegant furnishings, to taste the dishes of a cuisine, which is seasonal and mainly Tuscan.

Name: Da Orlando
Description: Simply arriving in Cusago near Milan, where the imposing castle dominates the attractive centre, puts you in a good mood. At Da Orlando, the menu is equally balanced between top-quality fish dishes such as the “bollita di mare” and meat-based dishes that will delight food-lovers, such as snails with trumpet mushrooms and duck breast with ginger. Two elegant dining rooms are the perfect setting for a romantic evening, while the attractive outdoor space comes into its own in summer. A good restaurant with over 40 years of history.

Name: Tana de 'l Ors
Address: via Roma 28, Forno di Zoldo, 32012, Italy
Description: A favourite with food-lovers, this restaurant serves lighter meals at lunchtime which are nonetheless carefully and imaginatively prepared (don’t miss the orsoburger!). In the evening, the best daily ingredients are prepared with a lightly modern touch – meat is the undisputed start of the show, although a few fish dishes also feature. One-room and two-room apartments are also available.

Name: Trattoria 'petito
Description: Located on the outskirts of Forlì’s charming historic centre, this simple, modern yet attractive restaurant serves eclectic and varied cuisine. More traditional fare on offer includes an excellent selection of hams and grilled meats, as well as delicious tagliatelle al ragù, while the menu also features a few more creative options including a few fish dishes.

Name: Locanda Mammi
Description: Situated amid beautiful countryside with views of the tranquil hills and rustic farmhouses that surround it, this restaurant is home to young and talented chef Stefania Di Pasquo who creates dishes using regional ingredients to which she adds her own personalised and modern touch. The wine list also includes a few champagnes, while the dining room with its stone walls, wood ceiling, elegant furnishings and bright colours is in complete harmony with its surroundings. Guestrooms are also available.

Name: L'Oste Scuro
Description: Nice family trattoria atmosphere in a popular, central fashionable location that stresses the freshness of the proprietor's dishes: fish.

Name: Il Sale
Address: via San Bartolo 100, frazione San Carlo, San Vincenzo, 57027, Italy
Description: Il Sale stands in a region where the typical hills, cypresses and olive trees of Tuscany meet the sea. The connection between the land and the quality of the cuisine served here is reinforced by the amount of produce grown by the restaurant itself.

Name: San Basilio alla Pergola
Description: Enjoy simple, carefully prepared dishes that are both typical and modern, either outdoors under the attractive arbour or in one of the two dining rooms with wooden floors and rustic furniture. For dessert, the apple tart with red wine caramel is highly recommended.

Name: Soho
Address: via al Ponte Calvi 20 r, Genoa, 16124, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre just a stone’s throw from the aquarium, this designer-style restaurant has retained some of the palazzo’s historic features. Specialities here range from raw fish dishes to classic favourites such as a reinterpreted version of “cappon magro” (seafood salad). The surprise tasting menus are particularly popular.

Name: La Quartina
Description: Outdoor service in the summer on the terrace with an exceptional view of the lake. Original furnishings and extremely well kept rooms. Menu including lake specialities. The rooms are simple, comfortable and always neat and tidy.

Name: Durnwald
Address: via Nikolaus Amhof 6, località Durna in Selva, Gsies, 39030, Italy
Description: A delicious plate of Schlutzkrapfen (ravioli stuffed with spinach and ricotta) is just what’s needed after a good day’s skiing or a hike through the woods. And that’s not all – Durnwald is an excellent place to appreciate the Alto Adige, both in terms of its landscapes, which can be admired from the dining room windows, and its cuisine, which keeps alive the genuine traditions of the region. Specialities include Valle Aurina cheese with pumpkin seed oil, and sfoglie di patate (potato fritters) with sauerkraut, sausage and mustard sauce.

Name: Bove's
Description: The grandson of Martini, one of the most famous butchers in Italy, focuses almost entirely on meat dishes in this restaurant in Cuneo, as well as a few first courses, salads and gourmet hamburgers. The two nostalgic dining rooms have a typical 1940s bistro ambience.

Name: Brindo
Description: The service is characterized by a cohesive and friendly team in welcoming guests to their small home. Brindo is an informal reality, where the cuisine is fun, engaging and more than simply territorial: raw foods, tartar and fish of the day are at the top!

Name: Santa Teresa
Address: via di Porta Soprana 55 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Located just a stone’s throw from the house thought to have belonged to Christopher Columbus, this restaurant boasts welcoming dining rooms where the experienced Scala family serve seasonal, regional cuisine with a focus on fish and seafood dishes (often including the famous Genovese “cappon magro”, a type of seafood salad). The menu also features a few meat dishes, beautifully presented and with a light contemporary touch. The good wine list means that you’ll have no problem finding a suitable pairing for your meal.

Name: All'Olivo
Description: Situated in one of the typical squares of Lucca’s beautiful historic centre, this restaurant boasts four dining rooms – the central room is adorned with shelves of wine bottles, while the others are decorated with drawings by authors who have visited the legendary Lucca Comics festival. The cuisine is regional, with fish and meat dishes featuring on the menu, plus there’s an attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Sora Maria e Arcangelo
Description: Those who judge only by appearance will walk on, those who do not will cross the threshold of this small restaurant to savour the delight of local recipes reinterpreted in modern form.

Name: Le Cicale in Città
Description: A classic-style dining room adorned with mirrors and silverware acts as the backdrop for fish and seafood dishes at this restaurant. The raw fish is particularly excellent, as are the mupa (a little-known fish that lives in the deep waters of the Mediterranean), prawns (in season) and home-made primi served with delicious sauces, such as the chicken plin with brown gravy. For special occasions, we recommend the table to the rear of the room near the arte povera-style dresser. Cheerful, friendly service adds to the appeal.

Name: La Stella
Description: One of the best addresses in the province, this charming country trattoria offering excellent value for money is superbly run by a friendly family. The dishes, which focus on traditional recipes and seasonal, regional ingredients, are announced at your table, as are the wine selections.

Name: Da Ercole
Description: Situated on Crotone’s seafront, Da Ercole is a culinary institution for anyone who loves fish, with the benefit of 40 years in the business behind it! The salty tang of the Ionian sea is celebrated on an extensive menu, although if you really want to enjoy yourself to the full, let owner-chef and old-school host Ercole guide you in your choice (including some excellent raw fish dishes).

Name: Bacucco d'Oro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: From the coast, you take a winding road uphill to this family-run trattoria which boasts sea views from its terrace. Apart from the salted cod, the menu only features meat dishes, with a focus on traditional Abruzzo specialities such as arrosticini (skewered grilled meat) and mazzarelle teramane (lamb offal wrapped in chicory and lettuce).

Name: Sichelburg
Description: Treat yourself to a great meal in an idyllic setting in this village restaurant occupying the first floor of a castle dating back to the 13C. The romantic dining rooms are furnished with wood, while the creative cuisine focuses on typical mountain produce.

Name: Da Nilo
Description: Overlooking the picturesque main square of Cetona, which can be admired from the outdoor tables, this restaurant has a classic ambience. Typical Tuscan cuisine with an emphasis on meat dishes.

Name: Manuelina
Description: Very few restaurants in Liguria can compete with the long gastronomic tradition of this restaurant, which was named after its original owner back in 1885! It was Manuelina herself who made the typical focaccia of Recco famous, offering it as a dish in her tavern. The fourth generation of the family now runs the business with the same passion and enthusiasm – part of the building houses the typical Focacceria, where family traditions are kept alive, while the other is home to the restaurant itself (even here the legendary and highly recommended focaccia is on the menu) with its round tables. The cuisine is traditional yet with modern touches and based on Ligurian ingredients with a focus on fish (although meat also features).

Name: La Conchiglia d'Oro
Address: via Nazionale Adriatica nord, Pineto, 64025, Italy
Description: The rather anonymous location does not in any way detract from the quality of this historic restaurant, which is renowned for its excellent fish and seafood. The menu showcases fish from the Adriatic cooked using classical techniques with the occasional modern twist, such as in the tuna tartare seasoned with caramelised onions and citrus powder-flavoured mayonnaise. Considering the quality of the fish here, the prices are very reasonable. The beautifully presented desserts are an added bonus.

Name: L'Ancora della Tortuga
Address: salita Cappuccini 4, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Decorated in maritime - style, this restaurant is literally perched on the cliff (one of its walls is actually rock). The views from its upper terrace are breathtaking. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, which also features a few meat dishes.

Name: Capo Santa Chiara
Address: via al Capo di Santa Chiara 69, Boccadasse, Genoa, 16124, Italy
Description: The chef at this modern, renovated restaurant at the end of the romantic Boccadasse beach serves creative cuisine that is the result of years of experimentation. Charming terrace overlooking the sea for summer dining.

Name: Il Monticello
Address: via Romoli 27, Monte Porzio Catone, 00078, Italy
Description: Not far from the centre, an attractive restaurant with a warm rustic - style ambience. The cuisine from Rome and the Lazio is full of flavour and the vegetables are grown in the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Le Bubbole
Description: In a refined restaurant within the walls of Palazzo Gattini, a historic residence in the heart of Matera, a local cuisine that is also open to some external contamination. Dinner on the terrace overlooking the Sassi will be unforgettable.

Name: Acanto
Description: Large elegant spaces full of light characterise this modern restaurant which pampers its guests with attentive service and classic cuisine with a contemporary twist.

Name: Ego
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the Sassi historic quarter, this modern, contemporary - style restaurant serves creative cuisine prepared by a young chef who already has plenty of experience under his belt.

Name: Villa Fiordaliso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Fiordaliso is one of the beautiful early 20C villas that line the lake front. Surrounded by verdant grounds and extending out into the lake on a pontoon, the restaurant serves creative, modern cuisine. The chef is equally at ease with fish and meat dishes, while the extensive wine list suggests that you’ll have no problem finding your favourite wine here.

Name: Osteria Antico Brolo
Description: Situated in the upper part of the town near the Vittoriale estate, this rustic 18C building is the setting for regional cuisine prepared using seasonal ingredients. The charming small courtyard offers shade for summer dining, while the interior dining room also includes a single table on a small balcony which needs to be booked well in advance.

Name: Cibrèo
Address: via A. Del Verrocchio 8 r, Florence, 50122, Italy
Description: This restaurant has an informal, fashionable atmosphere, with young, confident staff and fine, inventive cuisine inspired by traditional dishes.

Name: Kirchsteiger
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant has long been one of the most interesting in the area. It has a pleasing combination of traditional and modern cuisine created by the expert chef. The dining rooms have the same blend of old and new with an elegant use of local materials in the decor. Ask for one of the newer guestrooms.

Name: Taverna dello Spuntino
Description: This Roman trattoria has a particularly striking interior. From its old tufa passageways converted into a wine cellar in the basement, to its charming dining rooms with brick - vaulted arches where hams, flasks of wine, fruit and antipasti all form an attractive display.

Name: La Corniola
Address: via dei Mastri Lombardi 24, Pescocostanzo, 67033, Italy
Description: Known throughout Italy for its pillow lace, the small town of Pescocostanzo is home to this charming restaurant that specialises in cuisine from the Abruzzo region. Ingredients on the menu include grilled polenta, mountain bacon, smoked ricotta cheese with juniper and the famous local saffron – all served in elegant and creative cuisine.

Name: La Braja
Address: via San Giovanni Bosco 11, Montemagno, 14030, Italy
Description: A traditional Piedmontese restaurant, where owner Giuseppe Palermino welcomes guests to his elegant dining room with his consummate style. The specialities here have a regional focus with the occasional influence from further afield. The “tajarin al ristretto di coniglio” (shredded rabbit pasta) and the superb cheese trolley are particularly recommended.

Name: Miranda
Address: via Cornello 8, Riva di Solto, 24060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Enjoy year - round dining on the glass - fronted terrace, which overlooks the garden and the beautiful lake. The cuisine here encompasses the whole of Italy, occasionally using ingredients from other countries and continents which combine well in its recipes. Attractive guestrooms, plus a refreshing swimming pool which is available for residents only.

Name: InGalera
Description: Thanks to its location inside Bollate prison, InGalera offers a unique dining experience. Here, guests eat in a room within the prison itself, while dishes – of equal quality to other restaurants in the area – are prepared with the contribution of prison inmates. In this subdued ambience, choose from meat and fish dishes, with a restricted choice at lunchtime and the option of ordering a single dish.

Name: Scaraboci
Address: via XX Settembre 27, Marciana Marina, 57033, Italy
Description: Located just a few metres from the enchanting seafront at Marciana, this restaurant is one of the island’s gastronomic gems, offering a menu that features interesting combinations of beautifully presented meat and especially fish dishes There’s also a private terrace for romantic dining in summer (book well in advance) and although wines are not available by the glass, choosing a top-quality half-bottle is always an option.

Name: Bislakko
Address: via Thaon de Revel 87, Vercelli, 13100, Italy
Description: This unusually named restaurant (bislacco is the Italian for eccentric) delights guests with its fine cuisine, especially its delicious chocolate desserts. There is even a chocolate fountain for guests.

Name: La Capuccina
Address: via Novara 19/b, località Capuccina, Cureggio, 28060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A 16C farmhouse right out in the countryside, with its own working farm complete with livestock, vegetable gardens and vineyards. The enthusiastic family at the helm serve dishes made from their own produce alongside other top-quality, locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Vecchia Sorni
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the northern wine-producing area of Trento, this trattoria is a real highlight, thanks to its delicious, beautifully presented cuisine which is always full of flavour. The menu includes regional dishes as well as more modern specialities (plus a few fish-based options) which can be enjoyed either in the typical dining room or out on the veranda (also open in winter) with its stunning views of the Adige valley.

Name: Idea Verde
Address: via San Francesco 17/19, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled in a tranquil garden, this cheerful restaurant with large windows continues to focus on fish and seafood.

Name: Bel Ami
Description: A 19C palazzo renovated in modern style in its guestrooms and restaurant alike. The menu features fish and seafood, including raw dishes, and champagnes.

Name: Il Michelaccio
Description: A veritable bistro in a modern style and in a central position, a short distance from the famous Via XX Settembre, where the chef patron turns his hand to a fragrant cuisine, from the market, often dedicated to the Ligurian tradition (cream of potato with Genoese sea snails), but opening up to Italian flavors (pappa al pomodoro and burratina). He sometimes allows himself an imaginative touch, as in the risotto with anchovies and raspberries. Only natural wines.

Name: Da ö Vittorio
Description: Formerly a post house, today this is a characteristic restaurant with bedrooms available; the dining room is developed along the two wings with a veranda. Cuisine consists of many Ligurian specialities. Overnight section with classic cut rooms in the main body, stylish and modern in the annexe.

Name: La Corte
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Housed within the luxurious Hotel Villa Abbazia, this restaurant boasts a sumptuous dining room adorned with a fireplace, frescoes and period decorations, alongside an equally elegant outdoor space for summer dining. The young chef, who was practically brought up here, offers tasting menus from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte, with a focus on fresh and colourful dishes featuring herbs and vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden, alongside ingredients sourced from trusted suppliers, most of whom are local. The result is an enjoyable all-round dining experience, with the adjacent bistro offering more informal options, particularly at lunchtime.

Name: Trattoria Leoni
Description: Situated amid gently rolling hills, this restaurant with large picture windows boasts fine views of the surrounding countryside, which can be enjoyed even more from its summer terrace. For many years, the Leoni family have served Parma specialities here, including excellent salumi and recipes handed down by their grandmother, as well as typical mountain ingredients such as mushrooms and game.

Name: Kandoo Nippon Restaurant
Description: Dark colours and a modern decor are the main features of this excellent restaurant which occupies two floors and is highly recommended for its gourmet Japanese specialities. Cooked and raw dishes feature on the menu, plus there’s a quicker “combo formula” available at lunchtime.

Name: Tanzer
Description: Situated right under the bell tower in a small hamlet, this restaurant has two romantic Stube - style dining rooms. One is decorated in elegant 19C - style, while the other is simpler and more rustic in feel, dating from the 17C. Local cuisine with the occasional modern twist.

Name: Al Vedel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A temple for the production of culatello ham, which feature in the dishes served, and is also matured on the premises (the maturing rooms are well worth a visit). Al Vedel also serves other regional specialities such as typical stuffed pasta dishes, as well as more imaginative fare. An elegant, long - established restaurant now run by the sixth generation of the same family.

Name: Hostaria Uva Rara
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An ancient farmhouse dating back to the 15th century; the characteristic vaulting of the ceilings is in stone; furnishings are in excellent taste and professional management guarantees full enjoyment of some fine local recipes.

Name: Li Jalantuùmene
Address: piazza de Galganis 9, Monte Sant'Angelo, 71037, Italy
Description: This rustic restaurant is faithful to the culinary traditions of the area, with an added spirit of discovery. It is located in a charming square. Pleasant outdoor area for summertime.

Name: Osteria da Pietro
Address: via Chiassi 19, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: Housed in an elegant period building in the historic centre, this restaurant is run by a friendly couple, with the wife at the helm in the kitchen and the husband keeping a skilful eye on the front-of-house staff. Highlights on the menu include pumpkin tortelli and rose tart with Muscat zabaglione.

Name: L'Osteria dell'Orologio
Address: via di Torre Clementina 114, Fiumicino, 00054, Italy
Description: Chef Marco Claroni brings style and finesse to this excellent restaurant which offers a good selection of fish dishes with an emphasis on carefully chosen local fish, including the occasional rare variety. The menu features raw dishes, classic marinated options (some with an Asian influence), cured fish and seafood and the restaurant’s own home-made bottarga (cured fish roe).

Name: Sa Musciara
Description: A modern, fresh restaurant situated next to the town hall, with views of the sea from the dining room. Fish and seafood carefully prepared by the owner - chef (also a sailing enthusiast) take pride of place on the menu.

Name: Ratanà
Address: via G. de Castillia 28, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description: This lively, dynamic restaurant is in a converted building that once housed a cinema and later belonged to the railways. Top quality ingredients take pride of place here, while the pleasant outdoor area overlooking a small park is an added attraction.

Name: Le Cedrare
Description: This restaurant is housed in the 18C Villa Perez - Pompei - Sagramoso, in a room once used as a conservatory for orange and lemon trees. It serves excellent, inventive and regional cuisine in a charming location.

Name: Il Cigno Trattoria dei Martini
Description: This elegant, delightfully old-fashioned restaurant has been run by the Martini family since the late 1960s and is a temple to Mantuan cuisine. The setting is an attractive 16C building in the historic centre (yet slightly off the beaten track), which has developed around a 15C well, providing a magical ambience for alfresco dining in summer. With so many tempting options on the menu, it’s difficult to make a choice. Specialities include the region’s legendary pumpkin tortelli, delicious veal tripe cooked Mantuan style in a vegetable broth, traditional warm capon breast in a sweet and sour sauce, and a mouthwatering dark chocolate pudding served with a smooth zabaglione.

Name: Coltivare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This small restaurant next to the Brandini winery has chef Luca Zecchin at its helm, a true connoisseur of Langhe culinary traditions and one of the more recent disciples of Lidia Alciati (known as the “queen” of Piedmontese cuisine). Nearly all the ingredients used here are sourced locally, some even from the property itself, such as eggs and vegetables from the kitchen garden. The dishes are divided between those which pay tribute to the traditions of the region (don’t miss the “plin”) and others which showcase the chef’s personal style, including a menu dedicated to the barbecue grill. The latter is even used in some of the sweets, such as the smoky-flavoured bread and chocolate dessert. The wine list demonstrates the same affection for Piedmont, as well as featuring a selection of champagnes. During the day, enjoy the splendid view through the picture windows that surround the dining room, which also boasts a large fireplace.

Name: Feria
Description: Feria has two different spaces – a bistro-bar serving cocktails and street food, and a gourmet restaurant where chef Feltrin and his team showcase the full range of their culinary skills. The dishes here are colourful, full of flavour and carefully thought out, demonstrating Indonesian influences that recall the chef’s personal and professional experiences in this Asian country. Options include two tasting menus (a good starting point that allow you to appreciate the chef’s creativity to the full) and an à la carte. The excellent wine list is overseen by sommelier Régis Ramos who skilfully assists guests with their choices.

Name: Canova by Sadler
Description: The partnership between chef Sadler and the Baglioni chain can now be experienced in Venice, at this restaurant occupying a quiet, intimate dining room with an open-view kitchen in an elegant hotel literally a stone’s throw from St Mark’s Square. Here, the gourmet cuisine is prepared by a trusted resident chef from Puglia who creates visually impressive dishes from carefully chosen ingredients, with a choice of à la carte and two tasting menus (one creative Venetian, the other vegetarian). Simpler fare is available in the bistro next door or at tables on the outdoor terrace in fine weather.

Name: Osteria Origano
Address: via Giuseppina Scarciglia 18, Minervino di Lecce, 73020, Italy
Description: A small wine boutique at the entrance to this osteria in the village centre, displays the restaurant’s own wines, which are the perfect complement to your meal, as well as being available to purchase and take home with you. To the rear, an attractive closed veranda and an outdoor space are the perfect settings for hearty, traditional cuisine which ranges from spit-roasted meats to local salumi and home-made pastas. A few fish options are also available.

Name: Equilibrio
Description: Consumed by a passion for cooking, young Jacopo Chieppa began his career working with sweet and savoury leavened products and gaining experience in renowned restaurants such as the Mirazur in Menton and Antica Corona Reale in Cervere. He has now opened his own restaurant in an old restored mill, where he serves exciting, delicious cuisine that is contemporary in style yet traditional in its ingredients, some of which are grown in the property’s own kitchen garden next door. We particularly enjoyed the playful (and tasty) opening “picnic”, as well as the mupa (a type of fish) served with asparagus and a clam and parmesan emulsion. Front of house, the chef’s wife Melania displays an equal passion for her work, while in summer there’s an attractive outdoor space for alfresco dining.

Name: La Corte Gourmet
Description: An interesting choice of wine with plenty of options by the glass, attentive service in a classic yet contemporary-style dining room, and good, honest cuisine prepared by owner-chef Paolo. The seasonal menu features classic favourites such as Fassona beef tartare and breaded veal cutlets cooked in butter alongside imaginative pasta dishes and truffles (in season). Guests have the option of dining in the attractive “champagneria”, surrounded by exposed brickwork and bottles that have been carefully selected by Antonella, the life and soul of the restaurant.

Name: Osteria de' Mercati
Description: Slightly set back from the bustling streets of the historic centre yet still in the heart of the town, this delightful small restaurant is a recent addition to Sassari. It boasts a modern, elegant decor, friendly staff and a menu featuring carefully prepared fresh, seasonal dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the seafood risotto. A choice of regional wines completes the picture.

Name: Alajmo Cortina
Description: Situated in the restored premises of the historic El Toulà restaurant, Alajmo Cortina is home to a bar on the ground floor, with the restaurant occupying the two upper floors (no lift). Although traditional in feel with a profusion of wood, the restaurant is run by a young and enthusiastic team. The cuisine focuses mainly on the region, although the menu also features fish and other imaginative options on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: San Domenico
Description: Perched high on the tufa cliffs overlooking the Costa degli Dei, this contemporary-style restaurant boasts superb views from its dining room and especially from its panoramic summer terrace. The cuisine served by the young owner-chef is as modern as the setting – dishes are light and almost exclusively focused on local fish.

Name: Soprattutto
Address: via Noalese 124, Santa Maria di Sala, 30036, Italy
Description: This tiny, welcoming restaurant with a bright, simple decor has long since come of age, having been opened and run by the same family for years. The wife supervises the front of house, while the husband (whose past experience includes working as a metalworker as well as a chef) is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates classic fish dishes which are full of flavour and simply prepared from top-quality ingredients. As the restaurant is very popular with its regular clientele, booking in advance is essential – you won’t be disappointed!

Name: Musciora
Description: Located not far from the town centre, this restaurant offers friendly, professional service and three tasting menus including the particularly appealing 8-course “La vera esperienza Musciora”. The dishes here pay tribute to Sardinia’s culinary traditions, while the ingredients are all sourced from the region, as are most of the wines. Highlights include the cuttlefish, potato and pea, and the Su Filindeu pasta (served in a seafood broth).

Name: Emozioni
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this quiet restaurant with attractive stone walls and wooden ceilings boasts a pleasantly elegant and relaxed atmosphere. The chef pays particular attention to local ingredients which he reinterprets with modern and highly personal touches.

Name: Angiò-Macelleria di Mare
Description: The phrase “macellaria di mare” translates as “fish and seafood butcher’s”, a reference to the cured and seasoned fish that features on the menu here. The restaurant offers an original formula in which guests chat to the chef and choose their dish at the counter where ingredients are displayed, before taking a seat in the simple yet attractive dining room with its open-view kitchen. Our advice is to give young chef Alberto Angiolucci free reign – the result is a new take on fish and seafood cuisine.

Name: Alla Locanda
Description: A colourful, contemporary-style restaurant within the Locanda degli Artisti Art Hotel, a new address that is striking for its large art collection displayed throughout its various rooms. The cuisine here focuses on seasonal ingredients which are used to create personalised and imaginative dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte. Interesting wine list, with a special emphasis on labels from the Trentino-Alto Adige region.

Name: Veranda
Description: Alberto Faccani, the two-Michelin starred chef at the Magnolia restaurant in the hills inland from Cesenatico, oversees the cuisine at this restaurant. Fish takes centre stage here, in unfussy dishes that faithfully reflect the maritime traditions of the Adriatic. Primi courses include raw dishes, gratins, seafood salads, pasta and risotto, while secondi feature a selection of grilled, baked and fried fish (depending on the day’s catch).

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Boasting a sumptuous Art Deco setting that contrasts pleasingly with the traditional cuisine served here, this restaurant is the Milanese sibling of Il Marchese in Rome which pays tribute to the famous Italian film “Il Marchese del Grillo” starring Alberto Sordi (it is also the first bar in Europe to offer more than 600 “amaro” liqueurs). The culinary philosophy here is based on traditional Roman cuisine with a contemporary flavour, including delicious specialities such as pasta with carbonara, matriciana and gricia sauces, veal saltimbocca, pork belly and much more besides!

Name: GioEle
Description: Situated in the town centre, this colourful and discreetly elegant restaurant offers friendly and professional service. The classic cuisine served here is modern in style, offering a choice of meat and fish dishes as well as a convenient business lunch menu. In summer, tables are arranged outdoors on the terrace and in the small courtyard.

Name: Da Lorenzo
Address: via Fra' Gerardo Sasso 10, Scala, 84010, Italy
Description: Slightly off the beaten track in the lesser-known village of Scala opposite Ravello, this authentic family trattoria offers an informal change from the many Michelin-starred luxury restaurants dotted along the Amalfi Coast. Da Lorenzo has been serving simple yet excellent fish and seafood cuisine for decades, with a wonderful and highly recommended array of fresh fish on display. A popular panoramic terrace adds to its appeal.

Name: MaMe Restaurant
Description: Situated in central Viareggio near the town’s shipyards, MaMe occupies a long, narrow space that is reminiscent of Oriental restaurants with its long bench running alongside one wall and small bistro-style tables. This informal yet beautifully kept dining room is the backdrop for cuisine with interesting technical details such as the home-made mayonnaise served with the highly recommended steamed fish dish, and the delicious sourdough loaf which is freshly baked and served warm.

Name: ConTatto
Description: Situated in a small town just a few kilometres from the capital, this restaurant run by two young food enthusiasts serves regional dishes with a modern touch, such as cuttlefish with asparagus and a Bernese sauce. Guests can visit the interesting tufa-rock cellar, where the chef experiments with old preserving techniques and special flavourings. In addition, the cellar is used as a venue for exhibitions by different art galleries every season.

Name: La Pista
Address: Centro Commerciale Lingotto - via Nizza 262, Turin, 10126, Italy
Description: This restaurant is situated on the top floor of Turin’s iconic Lingotto building, the former Fiat factory, where the famous test track for cars has been transformed into a botanic garden – an interesting place to visit before your meal. Once at your table, choose from Alessandro Scardina’s three tasting menus: “Radici, gli essenziali” (traditional Piedmontese cuisine); “Botanic World” (vegetarian dishes); and “Trust” (a surprise menu where you leave all the choices to the chef). Whatever you choose, you’ll enjoy remarkable dishes that are balanced and full of substance and intense flavours. To avoid getting lost in the Lingotto shopping centre, make sure you follow the instructions you receive and take the lift to the restaurant.

Name: Antica Osteria del Mare
Description: Situated on the Naviglio away from Milan’s bustling nightlife, this rustic-style restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. As the name suggests, fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a good choice of antipasti to whet the appetite, as well as inviting trays of raw fish dishes (shared by the whole table), followed by delicious traditional pasta and grilled options.

Name: Cestello Firenze
Description: Situated in the beautiful piazza overlooked by the old church of San Frediano in Cestello, this restaurant serves fish specialities in atmospheric rooms decorated in a range of styles. Cestello Ristoclub’s exacting guests can choose from the creative dishes on the menu or, if they prefer, head to the fish counter to make their selection, which is then prepared in more a traditional way by the chefs.

Name: Roscioli
Description: This restaurant is part of one of the best food outlets in Rome, which offers delicacies such as typical Roman pastas, cooked and raw fish, meat, an impressive selection of cured hams and cheeses, as well as top-quality ingredients such as anchovies and mozzarella. Excellent home-baked bread and a varied wine list complete the picture. Make sure you book ahead, as it’s hard to get a table here without a reservation.

Name: Bàcaro Il Gusto
Description: A simple, modern restaurant where all the attention is focused on the extraordinary skills of the chef. The name is a nod to the typical Venetian bars known as bacari, and, in keeping with them, the restaurant serves a range of snacks, both traditional and creative in style, which allow the chef to demonstrate his culinary skills to the full. Other classic and more imaginative dishes also feature on the menu, alongside a choice of excellent desserts.

Name: Locanda delle Tre Chiavi
Description: This restaurant housed in an 18C building is run by its talented and enthusiastic owners Sergio (front of house) and Annarita (in the kitchen), who do their utmost to provide guests with the best seasonal, regional ingredients prepared in classic dishes full of flavour. The wine list focuses on good-quality labels from the region.

Name: Alle Ciaspole
Address: località Plazze 4, frazione Tret, Fondo, 38013, Italy
Description: The name of this excellent hotel-restaurant on the border with the Alto Adige region is a clear reference to the snowshoes used in winter excursions in Tret, as well as to the local traditions which inspire the cuisine created here by the owner-chef. Precise, classic cooking methods plus the use of locally sourced produce (with the exception of the fish dishes which also feature on the menu) are showcased in the cuisine, with dishes announced by the chef’s wife at your table in the unexpectedly elegant Alpine-style dining room.

Name: Hosteria La Cave Cantù
Description: Situated within the 18C Cantù monastery, now also home to a museum and library, this modern restaurant with a friendly ambience in its dining rooms and wine cellar also boasts an attractive outdoor space and a convenient car park. The menu features personalised cuisine with the occasional exotic influence prepared by the owner-chef (his wife, who works front of house and oversees the excellent wine list, is from Ecuador). The result is colourful, generous and beautifully presented cuisine which is full of flavour.

Name: Lucia
Description: Having just celebrated their 50th anniversary (they opened in 1971), this restaurant and hotel of the same name remain a solid culinary reference on the Abruzzi coast. The menu here is dedicated solely to fish and, as a result and is often the case, the wine list focuses almost exclusively on white wines. The fish (almost all of which comes from the Adriatic) is carefully sourced, while in the kitchen the chefs prepare classic dishes (such as enormous local langoustines cooked – and served – in a pan with oil, wine, garlic and rosemary) and a few more modern recipes (crispy mullet served with the award-winning spicy Ventricina salami).

Name: Wine & Dine
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Popular with locals, this restaurant has the typical atmosphere of a traditional Alpine hut with its old wood furnishings and romantic corners. Surrounded by high mountain peaks, the restaurant focuses on creative cuisine, including a few fish specialities.

Name: W Villadorata Country Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Part of the Country House Villadorata resort in the hills outside Noto, this restaurant boasts a delightful setting with the sea as a backdrop, surrounded by gardens which provide many of the vegetables used in the cuisine. Viviana Varese, a Michelin-starred chef from Milan, is in partnership here with Matteo Carnaghi, who is at the helm in the kitchen, with excellent results. The cooking is rooted in Sicilian ingredients, with one weekday evening in summer dedicated entirely to barbecue-grilled dishes.

Name: Bramea
Address: viale Villa d'Errico 10, Palazzo San Gervasio, 85026, Italy
Description: This gourmet restaurant with just a few tables is run by two young friends, now business partners at Bramea, with one at the helm in the kitchen, the other front of house. Extensive tasting menus are the focus here, featuring creative and original dishes often made from local ingredients. The end result is fascinating and of the highest quality.

Name: Foresta
Address: via Litoranea 2, Marina di Pisa, 56128, Italy
Description: Overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, all the tables at this restaurant offer sea views, whether you’re sitting in the winter dining room or on the outdoor summer terrace. The menu here focuses on top-quality fish dishes, which are classic in style, as is the background music and wine list, although the desserts have a more imaginative flavour.

Name: Taverna Rovita
Description: This restaurant in the historic centre of Maratea has been run with passion and enthusiasm by the same family since 1981. The emphasis is on a careful selection of top quality ingredients. For small groups (maximum 6 people) it is possible to dine in the room/cellar surrounded by old and precious bottles.

Name: Ba Restaurant
Description: Two huge red lamps welcome guests to this minimalist-style restaurant decorated in dark, typically Asian colours. The carefully prepared cuisine focuses on modern, reinterpreted Chinese dishes, while the wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: via Privata Fratelli Gabba 7/b, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: Housed within the Bulgari hotel right in the heart of Milan and opposite an exclusive garden, this restaurant is run by three-Michelin-starred chef Niko Romito from the Abruzzi, who creates light Italian dishes with a contemporary feel. Trendy atmosphere and bar.

Name: La Locanda del Notaio
Address: Via Piano delle Noci 42, Pellio Intelvi, 22024, Italy
Description: An elegant restaurant with a warm atmosphere embellished by a central fireplace. Chef Marco Moretto creates modern dishes which are elegant and balanced, with a focus on seasonal produce from the region and elsewhere – in this region of lakes, just a stone’s throw from Switzerland, you’ll be surprised by the fragrant seafood specialities which feature on the menu alongside freshwater fish dishes.

Name: Da Guido
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The story of this restaurant began in 1967, when Guido and Giovanna Fasan, both of whom still work front of house, met in Germany. They then moved back to Italy, where they opened Da Guido in the early 1990s. White dominates in the elegant, contemporary-style dining room, while the cuisine features delicious seafood dishes with a focus on grilled specialities. In summer, there’s a welcoming bar in the garden, which boasts a romantic atmosphere. Together with other restaurant-owners from Venice, the Fasan family also have a kitchen garden on the Venetian island of Sant’Erasmo, where they focus on sustainable growing methods.

Name: Bon Wei
Description: China on a plate! This attractive restaurant with an intriguing decor combining elegance, modern style and Asian influences serves a wide selection of Chinese specialities. Dishes include appetisers, dumplings, noodles and meat options, as well as a huge array of specialities from eight different regions, from the spicy dishes of Szechuan to the delicate flavours of Zhejiang.

Name: MikEle
Description: Located in a residential district on the edge of town, this unexpected, elegant fish restaurant offers a refreshing change from the typical boiled meat dishes of Modena. Guests can choose their fish from the display cabinet, with classic Italian seafood recipes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: La Taverna di Fra' Fiusch
Description: Nestling in a charming hill town, this restaurant will delight visitors looking for traditional cuisine with an updated, contemporary flavour. Specialities include agnolotti (a type of ravioli) and Piedmontese fritto misto (fried seafood and vegetables).

Name: De Gustibus
Address: via Martiri della Libertà 9, Chieri, 10023, Italy
Description: Enjoy modern, Mediterranean-influenced cuisine in an elegant restaurant with an attractive vintage-style ambience, where the excellent menu is announced at your table and varies according to daily availability. Very friendly and attentive service.

Name: Osteria Il Maialetto
Address: via Della Repubblica 348, Monsummano Terme, 51015, Italy
Description: This lively restaurant with a young, vibrant atmosphere stands next to the butcher’s shop run by the same family. The menu features delicious Tuscan cuisine, including dishes such as pappa al pomodoro and Florentine steak, which you choose from the display counter. Good wines and friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Rovello 18
Description: This lively and welcoming bistro furnished with smart wooden furniture is the setting for cuisine which focuses on carefully chosen ingredients presented with the minimum of fuss. Although the menu features a few specialities from Milan, most of the dishes here are Mediterranean in style. Interesting wine selection, including by the glass.

Name: Zero Milano
Description: There’s absolutely zero compromise on attention and quality in this restaurant, where the cuisine is made from top-quality ingredients using all the technical expertise typical of Japanese cooking. Chef Hide is now assisted by two of his compatriots who are real sushi experts, emphasising Zero Milano’s ambition to be one of the best Japanese restaurants in Milan, with its menu featuring Japanese specialities alongside dishes with a more contemporary Western flavour.

Name: La Notizia
Description: Although situated away from the tourist centre, Enzo Coccia’s pizzeria continues to be considered one of the best places for pizza in Campania. Featuring classic Neapolitan pizzas with soft, stringy dough, the menu offers traditional and creative toppings alike. The “'mpustarella”, a five-grain and wholemeal flour roll with different fillings, more than compensates for the lack of “fritti” on the menu. The first historic restaurant at number 53 has now been joined by a second address at number 94/a nearby.

Name: Da Noemi
Description: The mother of the current owner opened this busy restaurant in a medieval alleyway in the historic centre, giving it her own name. The historic dishes here reflect the culinary traditions of Ferrara, with specialities such as salama da sugo (pork sausage) and pasticcio di maccheroni (a baked pasta dish) on the menu. A must for anyone looking to sample local dishes already famous during the time of the Este family.

Name: Trattoria Al Passo
Description: Successive generations of the same family have run this pleasant restaurant just outside the city for over 70 years. Enjoy a selection of fish and seafood dishes (raw, grilled or fried with numerous condiments to accompany your starters) in a maritime themed dining room or on the light and airy veranda. There is a good selection of desserts to round off your meal.

Name: Al Segnavento
Address: via Gatta 76/c, località Santa Lucia di Tarù, Zelarino, 30174, Italy
Description: An elegant restaurant run by an entire family, whose philosophy could be summed up in the phrase “from farm to fork”. Fruit, vegetables, mutton, lamb, pork, plus a delicious breed of duck are all showcased in this zero-kilometre restaurant. If you’re looking for simpler fare and wine by the carafe, the restaurant also has a more informal bistro nearby. Charming guestrooms also available for visitors wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Posillipo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a superb location above Gabicce Monte, this excellent restaurant run by the third generation of the same family offers breathtaking views of the Romagna coast. Posillipo’s superb fish dishes have made the restaurant a must in the region, with options ranging from raw fish to traditional pasta specialities and delicious main courses (fish fillets, catch of the day, fried options etc). There’s also a tempting dessert trolley and an excellent wine list.

Name: La Mugnaia
Description: Tucked away in a narrow street in the centre, this pleasant restaurant has retained its historic brick-vaulted ceiling and is decorated in contemporary style. Here, a professional, enthusiastic chef serves modern, carefully presented cuisine with a blend of regional and Mediterranean flavours. The menu also features fish and home-grown vegetables.

Name: La Palomba
Description: Boasting the attractive ambience of a typical Italian trattoria, La Palomba has been run by the Cinti family since 1965 and is now in the hands of the third generation. The menu features Umbrian specialities including delicious home-made umbrichelli pasta served with various sauces.

Name: Incàlmo
Description: “Clean”, almost naive dishes full of clear and defined flavours take centre-stage at Incàlmo, where the cuisine is distinctly unfussy with no unnecessary frills. As a result, ingredients are clearly recognisable (as is the way they are prepared), allowing guests to focus on their contrasting textures and flavours. In the chef’s view, “if one element does stand out, it’s probably the bitter flavours that we enjoy playing with,” says the chef, “while at the same time balancing this with other elements. We also prioritise the use of vegetables.”

Name: La Pineta
Address: via Gualco 82, località Struppa, Genoa, 16165, Italy
Description: Now a gastronomic institution in the city, in a secluded setting immersed in nature, La Pineta occupies the ground floor of a nondescript building in which the simple, “dated” yet comfortable decor provides the backdrop. Although there is a menu (but no wine list), the dishes are usually announced in person at your table by the owners. Simple, traditional and abundant cuisine which is mainly cooked on the open grill in the centre of the room, including meat (its signature speciality) and fish.

Name: Osteria Boccolicchio
Description: Having gained experience in various restaurants throughout Europe, Tespi has now returned home to open this delightful small osteria in the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the sea. His huge passion for fish is evident from the menu, where fish dishes feature in numerous regionally influenced recipes. The excellent wine cellar includes a good choice of sparkling wines.

Name: Toe Drûe
Address: via Corsi 44 r, Sestri Ponente, 16154, Italy
Description: Soak up the ambience of historic Genova in this restaurant which serves specialities such as panissa rice, seafood salad and Ligurian fish dishes in its informal and comfortable dining room. The building dates back to the early 19C: fans of naval history may be interested to know that the REX transatlantic liner was built right opposite. There’s also a small lounge space where you can savour a glass of wine and a selection of cheeses.

Name: La Limonaia
Description: This restaurant occupies a large veranda decorated with an original array of tastefully arranged objects and furnishings. The cuisine is both contemporary and exciting, featuring dishes such as spelt pappardelle pasta, chicken giblet ragù and savoury zabaglione.

Name: La Ciambella
Address: via dell'Arco della Ciambella 20, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: A small restaurant with a friendly ambience run by an all-female team. Regional home-style food is to the fore here, with an emphasis on pasta, offal and other meat dishes. The tasting menu is highly recommended, enabling you to enjoy a selection of chef Francesca Ciucci’s varied dishes to the full.

Name: Osteria da Fiore
Address: calle del Scaleter, sestiere San Polo  2202/a, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: An osteria in name only, this restaurant has an elegant ambience, with two romantic tables overlooking the canal. If you enjoy Venetian cuisine you will be in your element here, as Signora Mara skilfully combines traditional local dishes with her own personal touch.

Name: Connubio
Address: corso Carlo e Nello Rosselli 54, Turin, 10129, Italy
Description: A restaurant with just a few tables amid a beautiful wood decor, where the young owner-chef creates dishes from bold and yet not overly excessive combinations of ingredients. A typical example is the blend of sweet, acid and bitter flavours in his swordfish carpaccio with avocado and burnt chicory.

Name: Antica Trattoria al Gallo 1909
Description: It is an unavoidable reference point in the gastronomic panorama of Ravenna and, as a matter of fact, it is almost always full! An "Historical Establishment of Italy", and rightly so considering that it has been run by the same family for over 100 years, this restaurant is a trattoria only in its name, given the blaze of art nouveau decorations inside. As regards the cuisine, you can expect regional dishes: truffles, succulent meats and local fish. In the dining room everyone is involved, while the young owner will illustrate the wine selection with the typically delightful congeniality of Romagna.

Name: Trattoria dall'Antonia
Description: Housed in a delightful 19C house facing the Naviglio del Brenta, this restaurant has been fully renovated to offer a welcoming space in which fish and seafood reign supreme. Prepared wherever possible from local fish, the dishes served here are simple, traditional and either from the Veneto or elsewhere in Italy.

Name: Gnocchetto
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant (opened in 1926) with an updated contemporary decor continues to serve cuisine that is classic and generous in style yet adapted to modern tastes. Individual dishes take pride of place on the menu at lunchtime, although you can also order from the À la carte if you wish. There’s also an outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Suscettibile Salerno
Description: Separated from a street in the centre of Salerno by an inner courtyard, this restaurant is a peaceful oasis with comfortable chairs arranged on a modern and stylish veranda (which opens almost completely in summer) and in an equally elegant dining room. Young chef Mario Quarta (born in Battipaglia) combines influences from his native region with techniques learned in renowned restaurants elsewhere in Italy and abroad, including Michelin-starred addresses. The French influence evident in his cooking techniques makes his Campania-focused cuisine even more exciting and contemporary. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the “Rombo R-otto” – four mouthwatering textures of meaty turbot served in a beautifully presented dish. Elegant, professional service overseen by manager Marco Sesso completes the picture.

Name: Mima
Description: You’ll be won over by the seasonal Mediterranean cuisine created by the young yet experienced chef at this restaurant. Accommodation is also available in modern guestrooms, plus there’s an enchanting roof garden in which to sip an aperitif while the sun goes down.

Name: Locanda Altobelli
Description: A pleasant little restaurant that differs from the many fish options in town with its traditional regional meat-based cuisine. There’s a real alchemy here between the young owner who is passionate about wine and the talented chef who boasts an impressive CV. Carefully chosen ingredients sourced directly from small local producers are the basis for its exciting, delicious dishes, while the wine list features some interesting organic wines. Small outdoor space for alfresco dining.

Name: Osteria Mood
Address: via Cesare Battisti 58, San Bartolomeo al Mare, 18016, Italy
Description: Situated just a few minutes from the seafront promenade in a quiet, residential district, this restaurant with a relaxing ambience serves delicious Ligurian cuisine with a focus on organic vegetables, fish and seafood (local whenever possible), and home-made bread, desserts and fresh pasta. In summer, meals are served by the swimming pool in the garden, while in winter, the welcoming covered veranda boasts extensive sea views.

Name: MU Dimsum
Description: This Chinese restaurant run by owner Suili Zhou has a beautiful and elegant ambience in which the chef is keen to introduce guests to the authentic culinary traditions of his homeland via a selection of refined dishes. You’ll also find an interesting choice of teas – served in traditional style at your table – plus a selection of champagnes and Italian sparkling wines.

Name: Peperosa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite its idyllic location facing the picturesque Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, this restaurant has avoided becoming a tourist trap, evolving instead into one of the most interesting restaurants in Lucca. The menu is finely balanced between meat and fish dishes with more than just a hint of added creativity, plus there’s now a new chef at the helm.

Name: Bentōteca
Description: Top-quality Japanese cuisine with heavy Mediterranean influences takes pride of place at this restaurant, where talented chef Toku Yoji Tokuyoshi creates dishes such as horsemeat tataki with a pizzaiola sauce, and barbecued fish neck with friggitello pepper. If you opt for a seat on the large bench facing the kitchen, you’ll be able to watch the chefs at work and admire the precision required to prepare different types of sushi. Modern, understated decor.

Name: L'Atelier 26
Description: Situated in a secluded location, this small gem of a restaurant boasts a skilfully restored stone dining room with a welcoming feel. The menu here has a clear French influence evident in both the style of its dishes and ingredients used. Our inspectors particularly recommend the young chef’s iconic snails and duck breast dishes.

Name: Il Poggio
Description: This simple yet welcoming family-run restaurant is situated on the wine route that wends its way through the hills behind Sondrio, less than 5km away. The dining room boasts a cheerful open fireplace (also used as a grill), while an attractive outdoor terrace offers fine views of the valley. In the kitchen, the family’s second generation combine traditional recipes and ingredients with the occasional modern twist.

Name: /gu.stà.re/ oltrecucina
Description: An attractive contemporary-style restaurant right in the town centre, with a striking colour scheme and minimalist decor. The cuisine is inspired by traditional Piedmontese recipes which are reinterpreted with an imaginative touch by young, talented chef Valentina Maioni who selects top-quality ingredients and cooks with real passion.

Name: Signore te ne ringrazi
Description: At this restaurant in the charming historic centre of Macerata, chef Michele Biagiola serves dishes inspired by rural culinary traditions, with herbs gathered in the fields nearby featuring in some of his recipes. Elaborate, gourmet cuisine is served at lunchtime, while the evening menu focuses on simpler, less expensive fare.

Name: Menabò Vino e Cucina
Address: via delle Palme 44 d/e, Rome, 00171, Italy
Description: Two brothers have brought fresh life to this exciting bistro in the heart of the Prenestino-Centocelle district, where the delicious cuisine is prepared by Paolo and the wine selection overseen by Daniele. The menu features a good balance of meat, fish and vegetarian dishes with a focus on seasonal ingredients and the best market produce. Very popular, so booking is recommended!

Name: Mater
Description: Nature plays a starring role here, both in terms of the restaurant’s location at the foot of the Camaldoli monastery and in the seasonal cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients. Choose 3 courses from à la carte or opt for the tasting menu Deeper.

Name: Claudio Ristorante
Description: An unexpected surprise in the heart of the lowlands. In this charming farmhouse situated in open countryside, Claudio prepares top-quality, almost exclusively fish and seafood cuisine with a southern Italian influence (especially from his native Puglia). There’s also a simpler, cheaper menu on weekday lunchtimes.

Name: Bino
Description: Situated in the historic centre near the ceramic museum (some of its pieces are also on display in the restaurant), Bino Ricchebuono boasts an attractive outdoor space in a charming small square. Michelin-starred chef Ricchebuono from Noli is the brains behind this restaurant, which serves fish and meat dishes prepared with a touch of creativity.

Name: IO Luigi Taglienti
Description: In this charming restaurant in Piacenza, where tables are arranged in the courtyard of the deconsecrated church that is also home to the Galleria Volumnia, Luigi Taglienti delights guests with his elegant and refined cuisine. The chef’s personal and decidedly contemporary reinterpretations of classic Italian and international favourites will linger long in the memory, while the interesting menu "Riscoperta" features  local dishes at an attractive price.

Name: Osteria a "Le Due Spade"
Address: via Don Arcangelo Rizzi 11, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: This beautiful Stube-style restaurant in the city centre has existed since the Council of Trent, with a succession of chefs and owners serving food here ever since the 16C. Still run with skill and expertise today, the restaurant boasts a small, intimate Alpine-style dining room where Trento specialities (char, apple strudel with vanilla ice cream) are served alongside typical Italian fare (risotto with mussel power and parsley pesto). All the dishes are cooked with an imaginative touch, resulting in a perfect balance of tradition and modernity!

Name: Trattoria Da Lucio
Description: The focus at this restaurant, named after the son of one of the partners, is on fish, fish and more fish! Lucio serves the best-quality fish, which is dry aged and then cooked (often over the charcoal grill) or served raw. The wine list pays particular attention to “natural” wines. The word "Trattoria" in the restaurant name is intended to convey a sense of the friendly, welcoming ambience and informal service here.

Name: Flurin
Description: Flurin occupies an old medieval tower in Glorenza, a small hamlet in the Val Venosta which is surrounded by walls that also date back to the Middle Ages. Furnished in a modern style that contrasts with its old vaulted ceiling, the restaurant serves contemporary cuisine that the enthusiastic owner-chef prepares from carefully selected seasonal ingredients from the region. His creative and imaginative recipes include dishes such as Alpine char ceviche with grapefruit, cucumber and sesame seeds. A bar and guest suites complete the picture.

Name: Ventuno Bistrot
Description: Some distance from the historic centre, in the neighborhood where Amerigo Vespucci was born, this restaurant takes its name from the number of the house in which it is located. The young chef works hard both in the kitchen and front of house, bringing his delicious, seasonal Italian dishes to the table himself.

Name: Grow Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Technique, creativity and a focus on and respect for the past are just some of the criteria that guide chef Matteo Vergine. His modern dishes aim to reflect the ancestral flavours of Brianza and Lombardy in bygone days when hunting, freshwater fishing, growing vegetables and gathering wild herbs were all part of everyday life. In the evening, choose between three tasting menus – in an effort to minimise food waste, guests are required to make their choice at the time of booking. We particularly enjoyed the quail served with its own broth and a brioche, and the gnocchi with stracchino cheese, caramel and venison bottarga. Lighter and less expensive options are available at lunchtime, as well as a convivial table for eight which can be shared with “strangers”. This love for the region extends to the whole of Italy when it comes to the wine list, which is concise yet personal and exclusively features natural Italian wines, all of which are served skilfully and with a wealth of information by sommelier Riccardo.

Name: Orto
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Orto is the restaurant of the delightful Nina Trulli resort. In its beautiful Mediterranean courtyard, enjoy personalised, well-presented dishes where meat and fish are balanced by the use of fruit and vegetables, many of which come from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden and orchard. Reservation strongly recommended.

Name: Il Melograno
Address: via delle Fornaci 1, località Marginone, Altopascio, 55011, Italy
Description: Along a road outside the fine town of Altpascio, the restaurant’s menu is equally split between meat and fish, but for a long time they have built their reputation on seafood products, served in classic, Italian and Mediterranean dishes. The restaurant’s other passion is the truffle, which whether black or white embellishes the dishes throughout all the seasons.

Name: Locanda Toscano
Description: This attractive restaurant with delightful views seems to be perched on the cliff, whereas in fact it’s situated just a stone’s throw from the town’s main piazza and Murat castle. Although inspired by Calabria’s maritime traditions, the contemporary-style cuisine also includes a few meat dishes.

Name: L'Imbuto
Description: One of the most talked about and controversial chefs in Italy, thanks to his creative dishes and original combinations, Tomei has made his home in the former stables of the 17C Pfanner palazzo-museum. Here, guests choose the number of courses they want, let the chef know if they have any allergies and then sit back and enjoy whatever surprising dishes he creates for them.

Name: Il Bikini
Address: SS 145 Sorrentina km 13,900, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This Mediterranean - style restaurant surrounded by a small outdoor terrace stands slightly above the beach club of the same name. Its elevated position gives it stunning views, which guests can enjoy as they savour the top - quality meat and fish dishes on the menu.

Name: Carter Oblio
Address: via Giuseppe Gioachino Belli 21, Rome, 00193, Italy
Description: Following years of experience in renowned restaurants, owner-chef Ciro Alberto has achieved his dream of opening his own place. With its clean lines and natural colour scheme, his restaurant has a slightly Nordic feel, while the reasonably priced cuisine demonstrates the imagination and creativity of a chef who is keen to stand out. Expertly prepared and attractively presented contemporary dishes are to the fore here.

Name: Frades Porto Cervo
Description: This new Milan venture is the brainchild of three brothers who already run a restaurant and delicatessen in Porto Cervo. Elegant and extremely contemporary in style, the restaurant serves modern Sardinian cuisine, while a corner reminiscent of their delicatessen allows guests to taste the island’s hams and cheeses by the slice.

Name: Josef Stube
Address: Località Certosa 29, Madonna di Senales, 39020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Run with passion by the two owners who continue the long family tradition in this hotel-restaurant is one of the most picturesque sights in the Val Senales. Its beautifully kept dining room is romantic and typical of the region, providing a backdrop for just a few dishes which are prepared by the chef with a focus on local ingredients. A hint of Mediterranean influence adds to the appeal.

Name: Razzo
Description: A quiet restaurant with a relaxed, young and modern feel serving contemporary cuisine prepared from seasonal, regional products. Charming romantic outdoor area with soft lighting.

Name: 3.0 Ciro Cascella
Description: Fans of Neapolitan pizza will be in their element at this restaurant, where the pizzas are light, with a larger and softer crust, thanks to the long fermentation and leavening process – some people come here simply to eat the crust, it’s so good. There’s also a wide choice of excellent toppings, including top-quality ingredients from Campania. Gluten-free options and dough made from different flours are also available.

Name: Adelaide
Description: Although it’s not obvious from the exterior, once you’ve crossed the threshold of the Vilòn hotel you step into a succession of highly decorated rooms that are full of charm. The cuisine is of the highest quality, showcasing dishes from chef Gabriele Muro’s native Campania alongside the famous pasta specialities of his adopted city (amatriciana, carbonara, cacio e pepe etc), and finishing with the superb “l’oro di Procida” dessert.

Name: Almatò
Description: Situated in the elegant, residential streets of the Prati district, this modern, minimalist-style restaurant is the setting for top-quality creative cuisine. For the most part, the menu eschews traditional Lazio dishes making this a good choice for anyone looking for something a little different.

Name: Stefenelli Desk
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Creative
Description: This restaurant is situated in an alleyway in the historic centre of Aoste. Full of character and accessed via a staircase from the entrance hall, the dining room is housed in what were probably the palazzo’s 18C stables.
