Under a brick-vaulted ceiling and arches, enjoy cuisine from the Aosta valley with a creative twist.

Name: Teresita by Giardino di Mari
Description: Housed in the private beach club of the same name, this elegant restaurant serves fish and seafood dishes made from carefully selected and top-quality ingredients. A whole page of the menu is dedicated to oysters and raw fish options. An attractive outdoor dining space completes the picture.

Name: Dolia Gaeta
Description: This brand-new restaurant boasts an elegant, chic decor and a relaxed and informal ambience. The very young team here is overseen by a talented chef who prepares modern and creative dishes with a focus on fish from the local gulf, as well as elsewhere. The wine list is also particularly interesting, featuring a remarkable choice of champagnes and a special emphasis on labels from Lazio.

Name: Il Portolano
Address: via Molara 11, Porto San Paolo, 07020, Italy
Description: This simple restaurant right on the seafront facing the island of Tavolara is run by a highly experienced couple working alongside an excellent chef who creates modern cuisine from the best fish in the region, as well as offering a few local meat dishes. Reservations are highly recommended in summer when the large outdoor panoramic terrace is always teeming with customers.

Name: De' Minimi
Description: Situated within the beautiful Villa Paola hotel just outside Tropea, this gourmet restaurant is named after the Frati Minimi (Order of Minims) who once occupied this old monastery. The cuisine here is modern and occasionally creative, especially the à la carte dishes (meat and fish), all of which are prepared from the best Calabrian ingredients including many vegetables and citrus fruit grown on the property. The small wine list also has a regional focus and is complemented by a choice of cocktails served at the bar.

Name: Selvatico
Address: via Silvio Pellico 19, Rivanazzano Terme, 27055, Italy
Description: Opened in 1912 and now run by the fourth generation of the same family, this is one of the best restaurants in the Oltrepò Pavese area. If you’re looking to sample the gastronomic delights of this region, you’ll find a whole host of delicious specialities on offer, from charcuterie and stews to boiled meats and excellent fresh pasta. Attractively furnished guestrooms with the same nostalgic feel as the restaurant are also available.

Name: Makorè
Description: Makorè’s new gourmet venture offers guests a delightful dining experience where the focus is on vegetables, as well as fish from the adjacent fishmongers. The chef demonstrates his culinary skills and techniques on three surprise tasting menus (of different lengths) and an à la carte, featuring dishes such as the familiar yet far from ordinary grilled squid (with a fragrant tuna and stracciatella stuffing) and a selection of boiled fish including cod tongue, ventresca tuna, tuna and cuttlefish sausage, gurnard, giardiniera vegetables and potatoes. We asked the excellent sommelier for recommendations and enjoyed a deep-gold Abate wine made from red Fortana grapes in line with local tradition. An elegant restaurant that has really made its mark in Ferrara.

Name: Locanda Belvedere
Address: via San Giuseppe 736, frazione San Rocco, Saludecio, 47835, Italy
Description: Using local ingredients, this restaurant offers regional cuisine with some creative touches. Pretty and inviting rooms, tastefully decorated and with period furniture. All overlooking the valley.

Name: Il Narciso
Description: Housed in the Polda baths near the marina, this recently opened small restaurant on the beach serves cuisine with a contemporary yet classic flavour. The restaurant boasts excellent bread, home-made pasta, traditionally cooked dishes such as chicken casserole and creative desserts. Highly recommended, especially the terrace with its fine sea views.

Name: Enoteca di Buttrio
Description: Housed in a beautiful historic building, this business, originally a wine bar (hence the name “enoteca”), gradually developed into a restaurant over the years. The menu focuses uniquely on fish, almost all of which comes from the Adriatic, showcased in traditional dishes enhanced with a creative twist.

Name: Osteria 1861
Address: via Valentino Izzo 1, Santa Maria di Castellabate, 84048, Italy
Description: Accessed via a narrow alleyway behind the beach, this restaurant housed in an old warehouse once used for smoking cured meats and drying Cilento figs boasts stone-vaulted ceilings, a romantic ambience and a small terrace embellished by beautiful plants. Chef Antoni Tafuri’s cuisine features on various tasting menus (including vegetarian and vegan) and an à la carte and demonstrates careful combinations that aim to showcase his regional ingredients to the full.

Name: Al Baliaggio
Address: via Vittorio Emanuele II 136, Venosa, 85029, Italy
Description: Housed in a 15C building in the centre of town, this restaurant boasts beautiful vaulted ceilings and a smart, elegant ambience. The young owner-chef serves cuisine with a traditional focus which is reinterpreted in modern style and made from excellent regional ingredients, as well as a few fish options. Efficient, punctual service.

Name: La Musa Restaurant & Rooftop Terrace
Description: Just six intimate tables in a modern restaurant with fine views of the lake through its large windows – the view is even more delightful from the summer terrace. The chef blends the flavors of his Sardinia with alpine ingredients, creating tasting itineraries that enhance the territory and the season.

Name: La Piemontese
Address: via San Martino 48, Mariano Comense, 22066, Italy
Description: The focus at La Piemontese, a simple yet modern restaurant with a convenient car park, is mainly on meat dishes, although game and fresh truffles also feature in season, plus there’s a generous business menu at lunchtime. An enjoyable dining experience that offers good value for money.

Name: Prato Gaio
Address: Località Versa, bivio per Volpara, Montecalvo Versiggia, 27047, Italy
Description: The restaurant trade is in the family genes: already an inn in the 19C, the Prato Gaio takes inspiration from the cuisine of the Oltrepò region. A selection of traditional specialities alongside dishes reinterpreted with flair and imagination are served. An essential stop for anyone looking for local flavour.

Name: Acqua
Address: via Filippo Corridoni 1, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
Description: The Possoni continue with their family tradition in this contemporary-style restaurant situated opposite the long-established Ma.Ri.Na. Here, their emphasis is on the quality of their ingredients, namely fresh fish and seafood that they use to prepare a broad range of dishes, some simple and traditional in style, while others are more complex and creative.

Name: Shiroya
Description: One of the most popular restaurants in the historic centre of Rome, Shiroya has just a few tables, so booking ahead is recommended. Served with courtesy and professionalism, dishes include well-known Japanese specialities such as home-made gyoza (dumplings) with various fillings, tempura and other fried options, the inevitable raw fish in all the classic combinations, ramen, different rice dishes and much more besides.

Name: Locanda della Luna
Address: via delle Oche 7, San Giorgio del Sannio, 82018, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In a remote location in the Sannio, this authentic inn offers fine views from its well-kept dining room-cum-veranda and outdoor terrace. The owner-chef creates dishes with a regional flavour using produce from his own garden, without straying too far from local traditions.

Name: Sottovoce
Description: One of the first rooftop restaurants in Como, Sottovoce boasts an elegant, contemporary feel. Stefano Mattara’s gourmet cuisine makes full use of Italy’s wealth of ingredients, with a particular focus on local produce such as fish from the lake which is served in creative and imaginative dishes. There’s a quiet, intimate dining room, a private balcony for groups (a maximum of eight people) and a spectacular outdoor Infinity Bar in which to enjoy an aperitif in the afternoon while admiring the beautiful views of the lake.

Name: Santamonica
Description: Head down to the beach along a narrow street parallel to Corso Italia in the Albaro district of the city to reach this restaurant, where the views from both the dining room and summer terrace embrace the sea to the full. And it is, of course, from the latter that most of its ingredients are sourced (it’s not a coincidence that half a page on the menu is dedicated to raw fish dishes), with Santamonica’s chefs creating modern dishes with a strong emphasis on beautiful presentation. As an example, the traditional, fresh and crispy marinated anchovies are plated with geometric precision and attractively embellished with pine nuts and confit cherry tomatoes.

Name: Essenza Bistrot
Description: A welcoming and original bistro-restaurant in the historic centre, where the stone walls are typical of the region’s architecture and an attractive outdoor area offers a few tables just in front of the entrance. The experienced owner-chef is at the helm in the kitchen, preparing beautifully presented, contemporary-style dishes which are full of flavour. The menu also features a selection of raw fish and seafood options.

Name: Il Molo
Address: via Aganor Pompili 9, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Passignano, where the village seems to jut out into the Lake Trasimeno (some tables in the main dining room boast views of the lake – make sure you book in advance), Il Molo has become a popular choice for guests keen to try top-quality fish from the lake as well as excellent poultry dishes. We highly recommend the delicious stuffed quail served with mushrooms and liver and accompanied by an excellent glass of local biodynamic red wine. There’s also a good choice of sparkling wines and champagnes.

Name: Borgia Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Interesting wine list
Description: This Milanese restaurant with a young talented chef at the helm boasts a breakfast area, as well as a lunchtime bistro and evening wine bar. The atmosphere in the dining room is lively and modern, allowing plenty of privacy, while the service is highly attentive to guests’ needs. This is especially true on the flagship “Psyche” menu, on which the chef creates special dishes in accordance with the guest’s personal preferences. The cuisine is creative, contemporary and technically adept as demonstrated in the carefully prepared pigeon served with hibiscus, blackberry and juniper cream. The interesting wine list includes bottles from across the globe, including some rare labels.

Name: Chat Qui Rit
Address: calle Tron, sestiere San Marco 1131, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: The generous, colourful and carefully prepared dishes served at this Italian bistro just a stone’s throw from St Mark’s Square could be described as “lagoon fusion” cuisine, thanks to one of the two chefs who demonstrates his love of Japanese flavours in some of his creative recipes.

Name: Crub
Address: corso Umberto I 125, Cava de' Tirreni, 84013, Italy
Description: A modern restaurant with an elegant, contemporary decor situated on the main pedestrian street in the town centre. The menu features an excellent selection of raw dishes, as well as a good choice of oysters and caviar, plus an excellent buffet of more elaborate contemporary-style fresh fish options. Sparkling wines are to the fore on the wine list.

Name: Terrazza Bartolini
Address: via A. Boito 30, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: Following its reopening in 2020, this seafront restaurant overlooking the beach and small harbour now offers its guests a choice between its indoor dining room or the panoramic terrace in fine weather (if you prefer the latter, it’s best to book ahead due to its popularity). The cuisine here focuses entirely on simple, unfussy fish dishes, with raw options and cooked dishes which make much use of the local Cervia salt. Daily, market-fresh specials are announced at your table.

Name: Osteria Europa
Description: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant housed in the hotel of the same name serves interesting, traditional cuisine which is well prepared and full of flavour.

Name: Cetaria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This beautiful restaurant inland from Salerno is run by an enthusiastic couple, with Salvatore at the helm in the kitchen and Federica front of house. The dining room has an intimate ambience and just a few glass tables arranged under a high ceiling which evokes the palazzo’s historic character. Federica’s service is attentive and courteous (she won Michelin’s 2024 Service Award), offering recommendations from the excellent wine list which also features a good selection of wines by the glass – she also painted two of the works of art exhibited in the dining room. In the kitchen, Salvatore uses recipes and ingredients from the region to create mainly fish-based dishes which he reinterprets in a decidedly contemporary and imaginative style, using skilful techniques and extravagant and stunning presentation. The top-quality ingredients are sourced from a local kitchen garden, as well as from a small family farm in Federica’s native Calabria. On the “Amore per il mare” (Love for the Sea) tasting menu, we particularly enjoyed the fragrant, generous flavours of the different small bites served at the beginning and end of the meal, as well as the exquisite bluefin tuna, mushrooms and miso, and the risotto with yellow plum tomatoes, raw red prawns, fingerlime and aromatic herbs.

Name: Eggentaler
Description: Renowned for being one of the best places in the region for steak cooked over a barbecue grill, this excellent restaurant has a varied menu which also includes a few fish dishes. There’s also a very good wine list, plus the restaurant also offers comfortable guest accommodation.

Name: La Cucina de' Mibabbo
Description: The name (“My grandfather’s cooking”) says it all: this restaurant serves cuisine from the owner’s native Tuscany, with a focus on Tuscan ingredients prepared with an updated and modern twist. Good selection of Tuscan specialities such as grilled meats and dishes cooked in a wood-fired oven in the evening, while the lunchtime menu is more restricted and Italian in feel.

Name: L'Osteria di Santa Marina
Address: campo Santa Marina, sestiere di Castello 5911, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: This classy inn is managed by young professionals who serve seafood and traditional dishes, but they also offer some interesting culinary innovations.

Name: [bu:r]
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Eugenio Boer offers a 100% Italian menu which focuses on local ingredients, with the aim of showcasing some of Italy’s favourite traditional dishes while at the same time supporting small-scale producers. However, this Italian focus in no way restricts the imaginative talents of the chef, who offers four tasting menus here: I Classici (meat-based dishes); Lo Stagionale (fish); L’Italia Vegetale (vegetables); and Per mano (which changes depending on the chef’s creative inspiration). There’s a 1960s and 70s feel to the decor.

Name: Mirabelle
Address: via di Porta Pinciana 14, Rome, 00187, Italy
Description: Without a shadow of a doubt, the view of Rome from this restaurant situated on the penultimate floor of the Splendide Royalhotel has few equals: from Villa Medici to Trinità dei Monti, and St Peter’s to the Gianicolo, the only way to enjoy a better view is to head up a floor to the hotel’s new Adèle lounge bar for an aperitif or after-dinner drink. Excellent service (especially in the evening) and modern yet traditionally influenced cuisine make this one of Rome’s best fine-dining restaurants.

Name: Tenne Lodges
Address: strada Racines di Dentro 51, Colle, 39040, Italy
Description: Situated near the ski slopes in the Gourmethotel Tenne Lodges, this restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. The large dining room is the backdrop for delicious modern cuisine which is regional in focus yet also influenced by the chef’s professional experience around the world. Excellent wine list offering plenty of choice, plus a stone wine cellar which makes a charming setting for a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Bianca sul Lago
Description: Housed in a smart hotel, this modern and minimalist-style restaurant boasts large picture windows which allow guests to enjoy some of the most beautiful sunsets in the region, either from the dining room or perhaps while sipping an aperitif in the lounge bar. The new chef serves contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional international influence, in which his creative flair is enhanced by expertly applied modern techniques. Good wine selection.

Name: Cortile Pepe
Description: Situated among the narrow streets of the historic centre just a stone’s throw from both the cathedral and the sea, this restaurant boasts a dining room with an old, vaulted ceiling and an attractive outdoor space. Here, the chef (who has plenty of experience working in Michelin-starred restaurants) serves regional cuisine reinterpreted with elegant and modern touches that result in precise, colourful and beautifully presented dishes. Attentive, friendly and welcoming service.

Name: Osteria Il Cappello
Description: The outdoor terrace at this restaurant overlooks a pleasant pedestrian piazza in the historic centre, while the welcoming dining rooms are decorated in a style typical of the Trentino. The cuisine – reliable, seasonal and full of flavour – is traditionally Italian, yet with a contemporary touch. The menu also features a few regional options as well as the occasional fish dish. The quail stuffed with acacia honey, pumpkin purée and stewed radicchio is superb.

Name: Finger's Porto Cervo
Address: via Porto Vecchio 1, Promenade du Port, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: A culinary name that is particularly well known in Milanese circles, Finger's is now attracting a following on the Costa Smeralda thanks to its renowned cuisine which combines Japanese styles and flavours with Brazilian and Italian touches. To this is added a good dose of creativity, all accompanied by a selection of superb cocktails.

Name: Adele Restaurant
Address: lungomare Colombo, località Marina di Pisciotta, Pisciotta, 84066, Italy
Description: Situated at the foot of a picturesque village perched on a hill, from where you head down to the marina to get to the restaurant, Adele showcases the culinary traditions of the Cilento region. Simply prepared cuisine which is full of flavour, with a focus on locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Café Cracco
Address: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: The bar-pasticceria in Milan par excellence, this café run by the famous Michelin-starred chef (his gourmet restaurant is on the first floor of the same building) also makes a pleasant choice for food, with a menu which moves easily from Milanese specialities to international dishes, including pizza. The display of sweet options at the dessert counter is a feast for the eyes and the palate. This extraordinary corner of Milan’s famous Galleria also offers outdoor tables.

Name: Luciano Cucina Italiana
Address: piazza del Teatro di Pompeo 18, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: It is widely accepted that the best carbonara in Rome is served in this restaurant. We have to agree – and this is no mean feat, given that this is one of the capital’s iconic dishes. However, Luciano Monosilio’s culinary experience also extends to other equally delicious dishes, some inspired by the traditions of Lazio, others more creative in style, but all full of intense flavours.

Name: Oishi Teramo
Description: East meets West in this attractive restaurant situated in the centre of Teramo. Tribute is paid to Japan in the intimate dining room, where photos of the country adorn the walls and Japanese influences are evident in the fusion cuisine which is prepared using a blend of ingredients from Italy and further afield (raw and marinated dishes, sashimi and nigiri, sushi rolls, tempura etc). The new section entitled “temporary food” has a more seasonal feel.

Name: Grantosco
Description: This elegant yet informal bistro - style restaurant is in the town centre. It is the ideal place to sample excellent cuisine made largely from local produce from the Maremma. You are sure to receive a warm welcome from the owner, who is the life and soul of the restaurant.

Name: La Taverna del Leone
Description: Situated three kilometres east of Positano, this family-run restaurant has been in business for almost 60 years and is one of the most popular in the region – and for good reason. The classic-style dining room with a striking open-view kitchen adorned with local blue-and-white ceramics provides the setting for meat and fish dishes (mainly local) prepared from top-quality ingredients with the occasional personal touch.

Name: Da Fausto
Description: Situated in these premises since 2015, Fausto has become a local favourite thanks to the quality and style of its cuisine which combines classic flavours and regional influences. Two of the chef’s great passions (chocolate and ice cream) always feature on the dessert menu, while the cool outdoor space near the entrance adds to the appeal.

Name: Ippogrifo
Description: This elegant restaurant with a smart, classic feel is situated in the Expo Fiera area not far from the city centre. Ever since it opened in 1982, this restaurant has been a reliable choice for top-quality fish (although meat also features on the menu), which is prepared using classic techniques and recipes. Highlights include dishes such as tuna and amberjack carpaccio, warm seafood salad, grilled fish, fish cooked in typical Ligurian style with potatoes and Taggiasche olives, and fish soup with croutons.

Name: Antica Macelleria Cecchini - Solociccia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: One of the most famous butchers in Italy has now turned his hand to cooking. At two locations, Solociccia or Officina della Bistecca, the menu is unique and served at a specific time with a meat proposal or a vegetarian option. Solociccia is only open for lunch.

Name: Dim Sum
Description: This restaurant with a partially open kitchen introduces its guests to the delicious specialities of Guangzhou and Southern China in rooms full of decorative details. The small dishes which characterise the culinary traditions of these regions have been refined with just a hint of contemporary flavour. A truly authentic Chinese dining experience.

Name: La Voglia Matta
Description: In the courtyard of the classic Ca' Ruffo hotel, Carlo's cuisine is based on the fish of the nearby Adriatic Sea, and more besides! Moeche crabs (when in season!) and a tasting of fagottini di magro with mantis shrimp are proverbial. In the wine cellar, the varied choice also includes an excellent local organic wine, Scambio bianco, made just a stone’s throw away and ideal for the most delicate dishes. For lunch, an appealing business proposal to be enjoyed in one of the two bright rooms.

Name: San Michele
Address: via Castello di Fagagna 33, Fagagna, 33034, Italy
Description: Situated next to the ruins of the old castle and the small church of San Michele, this 13C building, thought to have once housed a guardroom, is now home to a small restaurant serving regional, seasonal cuisine with a modern twist. During the week, the restaurant offers a lunchtime menu of top-quality snacks (the Venetian “cicchetti”), as well as a few “primi” and desserts.

Name: Osteria dei Vespri
Address: piazza Croce dei Vespri 6, Palermo, 90133, Italy
Description: Situated in the palazzo where the famous ball scene in the “The Leopard” by Luchino Visconti was filmed, this restaurant serves cuisine that moves with the times, featuring modern dishes made from local ingredients, while a friendly welcome from the long-established owners adds to the appeal. Cocktails, tapas and simpler yet equally delicious cuisine is served in the Occhiovivo! Bistrot next door, the name of which refers to a Sicilian saying which means “Be careful!”.

Name: Pierre Alexis 1877
Description: Situated in a house dating from 1877 (as the name suggests) in the pedestrian heart of old Courmayeur, this restaurant serves traditional cuisine with an imaginative twist. In spring, wild herbs picked in the surrounding valleys are added to the dishes.

Name: Il Funghetto
Address: strada Litoranea 11412, località Borgo Grappa, Latina, 04010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu at this restaurant just a few minutes’ drive from the beach. The owner-chef (the second generation since 1973) is happy to advise guests on food and wine choices alike, offering a wide choice of wines from all over Italy and around the world. Welcoming dining room and shady arbour. Gluten-free options available.

Name: Ceresio 7
Description: This designer-style restaurant is housed on the fourth floor of the historic ENEL palazzo, remodelled and converted into the Dsquared2 building. It combines the use of brass, marble and wood to create a successful blend of attractive colours and vintage decor. The view of Milan (even better from the long outdoor terrace with its two swimming pools) completes the picture, while the cuisine reinterprets Italian classics with a contemporary twist.

Name: Osteria della Corte
Description: This small restaurant with 17C stone walls and exposed stone arches also boasts a courtyard for summer dining, while the delicious yet simple cuisine focuses on fish and seafood. Rich flavours are a must for chef Silvia Cardelli, whose classic dishes include spaghetti with seafood and Tournedos Rossini. There’s also an excellent selection of wines (700 labels), with interesting recommendations provided by the sommelier.

Name: Doppio Gusto
Description: Fish specialities take pride of place on the menu of this elegant, contemporary - style restaurant with friendly, informal service. Good selection of wines, also available by the glass.

Name: Le Baccanti
Description: Simple premises with two large windows overlooking its kitchens. It serves imaginative dishes where tradition and creativity become one. Informal service.

Name: Canapone
Description: In elegant settings or, in the summer, overlooking the splendid Piazza Dante, you will find a fragrant Maremma cuisine based on excellent ingredients. The solid family management makes it a valid point of reference. Next door, Osteria Canapino offers more traditional and informal cuisine.

Name: L'Angolino da Filippo
Address: via Sangritana 1, Marina di San Vito, 66038, Italy
Description: A red door just a few metres from the sea marks the entrance to this long-established restaurant (a family-run business for over a century), which boasts two small dining rooms with brick-vaulted ceilings and a lively atmosphere. Unsurprisingly, the menu focuses on fish and seafood specialities, which showcase a combination of delicious modern and traditional flavours.

Name: Aquariva
Address: via Marconi 57, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Renowned for its fish, this restaurant offers a good choice of raw fish and a delicious plateau royale. The elegant, spacious dining room boasts a restful colour scheme and views of the lake through its picture windows.

Name: Trattoria del Nuovo Macello
Description: Named after the slaughterhouse opened opposite the premises in 1927, this restaurant was taken over 30 years later by the grandfather of one of the current partners, as he was convinced that the restaurant’s busy location would contribute to its success – and he wasn’t wrong! The traditional, regional cuisine served here is reinterpreted with a contemporary flavour and includes delicious specialities such as cotoletta alla milanese made from meat matured for 40 days.

Name: L'antica Pizzeria da Michele
Description: You can really sense the history of Naples in this pizzeria, which was founded in 1870 and boasts a lively, convivial atmosphere – if you sit alone, you’re sure to find yourself sharing travellers’ tales with fellow diners by the end of your meal! Note that the restaurant only serves two types of pizza – Margherita (tomato and mozzarella) and Marinara (tomato, oregano and garlic). Numbered tickets are issued to diners, who then take a seat and are called in turn (open all day). A second restaurant has recently been opened nearby.

Name: I Banchi
Description: Housed in a palazzo full of history – the building was a synagogue before the 1693 earthquake and has retained its ritual bath in its charming room of mirrors – this restaurant bears the imprint of renowned chef Ciccio Sultano, holder of two Michelin stars at the nearby Duomo restaurant. The cuisine is eclectic yet with a Sicilian focus, plus the wine list is complemented by a choice of interesting cocktails.

Name: Johnson & Dipoli
Description: This intimate bistro with tables laid out under picturesque arcades in the centre of Egna is run with professionalism and enthusiasm by its owner Vincenzo. The delicious Italian cuisine is prepared using the best fresh ingredients, while the wine list boasts a careful selection of labels including a good choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Chichibio
Description: Despite its lack of awards, this restaurant stands out for the quality of its cuisine. Situated in the town centre, it has a small intimate dining room with just a few tables (it’s best to book ahead) that acts as a backdrop for good-quality dishes made from local, seasonal ingredients, as well as a few modern and imaginative fish options. Highly recommended!

Name: Antica Trattoria del Gallo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A splendid example of a country trattoria, which has been delighting its guests with typical dishes from Lombardy for over a century. Meals are served either in the attractive vintage-style dining room or, in fine weather, outdoors under the Virginia creeper and mature wisteria. Truly enchanting!

Name: Le Tamerici
Description: Located just a few metres from the Trevi Fountain, this top-quality restaurant stands out among the many ordinary tourist-style options available in this district. In a quiet ambience, with an outdoor dining area in the alleyway, enjoy excellent modern Mediterranean cuisine created by the chef and owner.

Name: Bistrot Donatella
Description: This restaurant in a small village dominated by a bell tower boasts a charming inner courtyard which provides a romantic setting for a meal in fine weather. The Piedmontese cuisine served here is prepared using top-quality ingredients. A friendly welcome completes the picture, making this an enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Locanda '800
Description: Whether you dine indoors, on the bright veranda or in the wine cellar with its barrels and wines produced by the estate, you’ll enjoy cuisine at this family-run restaurant which has gained a reputation in the region for its balance of meat and fish dishes. Excellent service and a pleasant setting in a rustic building surrounded by greenery.

Name: Il Cipresso - Da Cioni
Address: via Alcide De Gasperi 28, Loro Ciuffenna, 52024, Italy
Description: Standing on a round terrace, this restaurant with a fairly plain interior serves dishes made from some of the best produce of the region – cured hams, bread, pasta and famous Tuscan meats. The restaurant also offers simple, rustic - style guestrooms.

Name: Albergaccio di Castellina
Address: via Fiorentina 63, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
Description: This rustic but stylish establishment is in wood and stone. Find Tuscan cuisine that leans towards imaginative dishes, without betraying regional flavours and produce.

Name: La Ferrata
Description: Copper pots and lids and photos of locomotives adorn the walls of this friendly and welcoming trattoria. Enjoy generous portions of local specialities, including delicious snails cooked in butter.

Name: Wicky's Innovative Japanese Cuisine
Description: Although the contemporary, minimalist-style decor is typical of Japanese restaurants, the cuisine will come as more of a surprise, with its magical blend of classic Japanese dishes made from Mediterranean ingredients, beautifully presented and full of flavour. There are two dining rooms: one overlooking the road, and the other with an open-view kitchen and sushi bar, where the chef serves an evening tasting menu for guests happy to put their faith in his imaginative improvisational skills.

Name: Innocenti Evasioni
Description: Chef Tommaso Arrigoni’s restaurant has a wonderful new location, where floor-to-ceiling windows in the spacious modern dining room overlook a large Mediterranean garden that is just as appealing as the Zen-inspired outdoor space at his previous venue. The chef’s colourful cuisine is showcased on three tasting menus, from which dishes can also be selected à la carte. The interesting “Delle Mezze” menu allows guests to sample several small portions of different dishes.

Name: Alessandro Mecca al Castello di Grinzane Cavour
Description: There’s no shortage of classic Piedmontese ingredients (such as anchovies, peppers and veal) on the menu at this restaurant, where traditional recipes are reinterpreted with a personalised and contemporary touch. Dishes from outside the region, including various fish-based options, also feature, while the restaurant aims to avoid food waste by using every single part of its ingredients where possible. The location in a splendid castle with 11C origins, once the home of Camillo Benso, count of Cavour, adds to the appeal.

Name: Cala Luna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The elegant fine-dining restaurant at Le Calette boutique hotel, Cala Luna boasts an attractive dining room (Rizz'i Mari) where meals are served in low season, as well as an open-air garden on Via Presidiana for summer dining where, just like the dining room, the views take in the Caldura rocks and the La Rocca outcrop, albeit from a slightly different perspective. Chef Dario Pandolfo uses creative techniques acquired during his time working at renowned restaurants, which he applies to Sicilian ingredients and traditions. The result is exciting and colourful cuisine which is creative and full of Mediterranean flavours.

Name: Restaurant 700
Address: largo Michele Ayroldi Carissimo 14, Ostuni, 72017, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated at the entrance to Ostuni’s historic centre, this restaurant is part of the luxury Paragon 700 hotel. The charming dining room combines historic features with a more modern decor, while the exclusive garden is perfect for dining alfresco in fine weather. The menu offers a concise selection of classic Italian dishes at lunchtime, while in the evening the chef conjures up more high-level and elaborate dishes showcasing strong technique.

Name: Rosita
Description: Decorated in the same simple and rustic style as the Hotel Rosita in which it is housed, this restaurant boasts an attractive terrace overlooking the sea and the coast (call in advance to book one of the tables with the best view), which more than compensates for the narrow, winding road that you have to follow to get here. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, including seafood options such as the excellent stuffed baby squid in a sauce served with mashed potatoes, and meat dishes that include a tasty rabbit casserole.

Name: La Péniche
Address: via Lungo Brugiano 3, Marina di Massa, 54100, Italy
Description: This little corner of France right on the Brugiano canal occupies a house-on-stilts and has a unique, warm and romantic ambience thanks to its combination of colonial style and Parisian decor. Specialities include raw fish and seafood, including oysters, although you’ll also find meat-based dishes on the menu. The tables on the deck – which brings to mind a barge on the Seine – are very popular in summer.

Name: Winter Garden Florence
Description: Horse-drawn carriages once entered the old courtyard of the St Regis hotel, now converted into an elegant winter garden which also includes a cocktail bar with sofas and armchairs. Seasonality and local gems are fundamental pillars of the modern Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: Di Martino Sea Front Pasta Bar
Description: Situated opposite the Maschio Angioino (Castel Nuovo) in Naples, this restaurant was opened by a pasta producer from nearby Gragnano, making it the perfect choice for pasta-lovers. Sit at a sushi-style counter watching the chefs at work and choose from a menu that is dedicated almost entirely to pasta dishes (as well as desserts), most of which are based on traditional recipes. When ordered individually, the dishes are generously portioned; however, for a more complete overview, opt for the tasting menu which includes more courses but smaller quantities.

Name: Carlo e Camillo
Description: This quiet and elegant bistro, the Grand Hotel Sitea’s second restaurant, offers a charming setting in which to enjoy skilfully prepared Piedmontese-influenced cuisine. The venue is also perfect for an aperitif, with excellent wines and cocktails.

Name: Il Tufo Allegro
Description: In the heart of the Etruscan resort, close to the synagogue: Tuscan dishes, a small restaurant with a well stocked wine cellar and two dining rooms hewn out of the rock.

Name: La Ruota
Description: The chandeliers in this restaurant hang low over the tables, contributing to the attractive ambience, while the lighting is subtle, with several lights echoing the lamps reflected in the sea along Moneglia’s seafront. The life and soul of this restaurant is Edoardo, the attentive chef and host who explains his cuisine and wines with real passion, accompanying guests throughout his surprise tasting menu which is based on fresh fish. Simple, imaginative cuisine that pays little heed to passing trends.

Name: La Masseria
Address: via Chiesa 61, località Marzaglia, Modena, 41123, Italy
Description: What used to be an old watermill is now a welcoming restaurant with a rustic feel and a beautiful garden for summer dining. Home-made bread and pasta, typical specialities from Puglia, savoury pies and grilled meats all feature on the menu.

Name: Remo Villa Cariolato
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Long recommended by the Michelin Guide, the historic Remo moved a few years ago from its old premises to this beautiful villa typical of the Veneto region, once the home of an Italian hero, one of Garibaldi’s famous “Thousand”. Large and small dining rooms, perfect for special events, act as the backdrop for good regional and Italian cuisine, with a menu divided between meat and fish options. The latter comes almost exclusively from Chioggia market.

Name: Ca' del Profeta
Description: Situated in a tranquil location overlooking the vineyards, this winery and elegant restaurant is owned by the “Prophet” Hernanes, a Brazilian footballer who played for many years in the Italian championship. The menu here features regional dishes alongside a few more creative options, while five modern guestrooms (some with a view) and a panoramic swimming pool complete the picture.

Name: Da Oscar
Description: Standing on the hills overlooking Lake Garda, this attractive, spacious restaurant has an elegant atmosphere. There is a delightful terrace for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Oberlechner
Description: From Merano you climb to an altitude of 1 000m to this restaurant, which boasts breathtaking views of the town and surrounding mountains. The menu here focuses mainly on local ingredients which are carefully prepared without too many creative twists, resulting in delicious and generous dishes such as braised beef with a Lagrein sauce (accompanied by rice and vegetables). All the attractive guestrooms have a balcony and the same stunning view.

Name: ZELO
Description: The elegant ZELO restaurant enjoys a beautiful setting in the garden of a 15C inner courtyard, which also boasts an attractive summer terrace. The cuisine is modern in style, created by a chef who uses the best Italian ingredients to prepare creative and contemporary dishes, as well as a few Italian classic favourites such as vitello tonnato and breaded veal. Some dishes are not available at lunchtime, when they are replaced by salads, while in the evening raw fish and seafood options take centre stage.

Name: Osteria Veglio
Description: With its own convenient car park and a large terrace boasting views of the Langhe, this minimalist-style restaurant built in the 1920s serves excellent food. As fans of offal dishes, we were delighted to see lamb kidneys in a Marsala sauce on the menu – a dish which certainly did not disappoint! Guests are required to choose a minimum of two dishes from the à la carte, excluding dessert.

Name: Da Andrea
Address: viale della Vittoria 68, Marina di Cecina, 57023, Italy
Description: This white, modern and minimalist - style restaurant has lovely views of the Tyrrhenian sea from its dining room and summer terrace. Not surprisingly, fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with daily specials based on the catch of the day announced at your table.

Name: Il Sanlorenzo
Description: A historic palazzo built over the foundations of the Teatro Pompeo is home to this atmospheric restaurant, which brings together history and contemporary art. However, the real star is the fish on the menu, most of which comes from the island of Ponza, and is served either raw or cooked very simply in a modern style.

Name: Enoteca San Nicola
Address: contrada di San Nicola 11/a, Bobbio, 29022, Italy
Description: This fascinating little restaurant set in the maze of narrow streets around the abbey of San Colombano invites you to its succession of small dining rooms decorated with pictures and wine bottles. Atmospheric rooms, each with an open fire.

Name: Alex
Address: via Versilia 157/159, Marina di Pietrasanta, 55045, Italy
Description: Modern, personalised dishes with something for everyone and a careful balance between meat and fish options. The three tasting menus showcase the chef’s culinary philosophy, all served in a trendy atmosphere with an ethnic touch. The wine list is one of the restaurant’s highlights, featuring an excellent selection of international labels, all of which can be purchased at the wine bar.

Name: Antica Locanda di Sesto
Address: via Ludovica 1660, loc. Sesto di Moriano, Ponte a Moriano, 55100, Italy
Description: The origins of this inn date back to the late 14C, making this one of the Italy’s recognised “Historic Restaurants” – and one that is still flourishing today! The dishes served here are often inspired by Tuscan peasant traditions, while the owner also runs an organic farm which produces wine, vinegar and extra-virgin olive oil. Highlights on the menu include soup with cavolo nero, spaghetti with guanciale (cured pork cheek) served on pecorino cheese, and an array of main courses barbecued on the grill.

Name: Da Gigetto
Description: A long-established restaurant with a renowned reputation thanks to the enthusiasm of the family at the helm and the excellent cuisine on offer. The carefully designed menu focuses mainly on classic regional dishes, yet also includes more contemporary options and even a few fish-based specialities, while the impressive wine list features more than 1 000 different labels, including some surprising names and various vertical wine-tasting options.

Name: Serendepico
Address: via della Chiesa di Gragnano 36, Capannori, 55012, Italy
Description: The Japanese chef at this restaurant adds his own personal interpretation to Italian dishes. There is a focus on regions such as Marche, Piedmont and Tuscany, where he gained most of his culinary experience. He creates dishes with a delicate feel that is typical of Japan. Traditional cuisine with a unique and exciting twist.

Name: Tavola di Guido
Address: Località Le Piazze 41, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is as comfortable as the rest of the hotel, while its outdoor dining area allows guests to enjoy the peace and tranquillity of the beautiful garden. Chef Guido creates dishes with a regional influence, some of which are more modern in flavour.

Name: Osteria Numero 2
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A beautiful farmhouse not far from the town, with a friendly, welcoming and colourful feel. Here, the menu features Italian dishes alongside a few local specialities, such as agnoli pasta in broth (also available as an antipasto in a “sorbir” wine broth). Special mention goes to the superb selection of beers chosen by owner Moreno, which ranges from local craft beers to labels from across the globe – there’s even a beer-themed dessert, the Birramisù. Excellent value for money and highly popular, so booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Materia Prima
Address: Località Piana Santa Liberata, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant boasts a pleasant terrace overlooking a small man-made lake used for water sports, as well as a simple, modern dining room with picture windows offering the same view. The minimalist style of the decor is echoed in the cuisine, which is creative with occasionally more technical twists. The desserts offer a fitting end to your meal – the interesting selection includes one striking dish featuring the unusual combination of chocolate and saffron.

Name: Rueda Gaucha
Description: This restaurant is justifiably renowned for two specialities – firstly, its wide selection of cured hams including the famous Friuli prosciuttos as well as hams from further afield; and secondly, dishes (mainly meat sourced from Italy and further afield, although fish also features) cooked on the barbecue grill.

Name: Il Cascinalenuovo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Having been in business for over 50 years and with a newly expanded team, Il Cascinalenuovo continues to serve its classic favourites (such as veal’s tongue millefeuille and foie gras with port jelly, and Piedmontese tonnato) while also extending its repertoire to include new options, including fish. The Ferretto brothers are still at the helm here, one front of house, the other in the kitchen. If the weather allows, book a table in the attractive outdoor space overlooking the garden and swimming pool.

Name: Le Cementine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This rustic, vintage-style country restaurant run by the Alajmo brothers stands on the banks of the Sile river, just a few minutes from the Venetian lagoon, and overlooks a vegetable garden, vineyard and beautiful green meadows. The cuisine demonstrates a strong focus on seasonal, regional ingredients, featuring meat and fish alike, with vegetables taking centre stage in many of the dishes.

Name: El Primero
Description: Situated in a building with a striking appearance (the Uruguay Pavilion in Expo 2015), this restaurant boasts stunning views of the mountains in the distance. Inside, the large dining room acts as a backdrop for South American cuisine with a focus on grilled specialities. A simple atmosphere and friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Zàghara Restaurant
Description: Housed in the elegant Relais Villa Flora, this restaurant occupies a natural terrace with breathtaking views of the Nissene hills. The dishes are predominantly regional in style yet reinterpreted with a modern twist. There’s also a good wine selection with a focus on Sicilian and Italian labels.

Name: Mogano
Address: via del Praticello Alto 7, Formello, 00060, Italy
Description: Aiming to promote craft beers as a worthy pairing for gourmet cuisine, the Faenza family opened Mogano – a modern, elegant restaurant with a wood-inspired decor, soft lighting and just five tables, right next to their Ritual Lab brewery. One of the sons (Matteo, the chef here) greets guests before dinner with an aperitif served in the kitchen. With plenty of international culinary experience behind him, he combines Italian flavours with influences from all around the world. Despite the focus on beer, a wine list is also available.

Name: Casa Vicina
Description: Renowned over the years for its traditional Piedmontese cuisine, Casa Vicina is situated near the Lingotto factory (easily accessible by metro if you don’t have a car) on the top floor of the “Green Pea”, a building that showcases sustainable and environmentally friendly products. Meat dishes (including specialities such as Fassone steak in a tuna sauce, rabbit and ossobuco-filled agnolotti pasta) dominate the main courses although fish options are also available. Make sure you leave room for desserts such as ice cream, zabaglione and Ivrea tart.

Name: La Rosa dei Venti
Address: via Piero della Francesca 34, Milan, 20154, Italy
Description: This small restaurant is perfect for anyone keen on fish prepared simply with a personal touch – and with the added bonus of providing good value for money. The restaurant belongs to the AIC network (Italian Association for Coeliacs) and therefore offers a good selection of gluten - free dishes, including bread and pasta.

Name: Terre Alte
Address: via Olmadella 11, località Balignano, Longiano, 47020, Italy
Description: One of the best-known addresses in this region for fish enthusiasts, this restaurant serves freshly caught fish prepared in simple, traditional dishes that allow the quality of the flavour to shine through. A good wine list (particularly champagnes) and a panoramic terrace add to the appeal.

Name: Quel Fantastico Giovedì
Description: Two small modern dining rooms with contemporary paintings on the walls provide the backdrop for classic specialities from Ferrara, as well as the chef’s renowned fish dishes at this restaurant, where booking is highly recommended, even at lunchtime!

Name: Camana Veglia
Description: Typical wood interiors and attention to detail, in a typical establishment with recently renovated "themed" bedrooms; Valtellino cuisine.

Name: The Cesar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This restaurant offers Mediterranean dishes prepared mostly with organic produce from the restaurant’s own garden. Dine in a romantic setting overlooking the blue expanse of the Mediterranean sea.

Name: Cacciani
Description: One of the most famous restaurants in the Castelli Romani region in 2022 celebrated 100 years of life under the management of the same family: the Cacciani. Authentic and excellent regional cuisine, served in a welcoming dining room, with the open - view kitchen on one side and a panoramic terrace on the other.

Name: Bagatto
Description: Hidden down an alleyway in the town centre, this friendly trattoria boasts an attractive ceiling with exposed brickwork. An excellent address for fans of Ligurian cuisine, fish and seafood. House desserts include sour orange semifreddo.

Name: 28 Posti
Description: The main focus of 28 Posti is its ethical stance, with seasonal ingredients sourced from small producers and an emphasis on making the most of each and every ingredient in order to keep food waste to a minimum – a philosophy that has been important to the restaurant for many years now. New chefs Franco Salvatore and Andrea Zazzara, both from the Abruzzi, have brought their own personal touches to cuisine which has its roots in the rich gastronomic traditions of central Italy and their native region.

Name: Dodici Fontane
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The scenery that you drive through to get to this restaurant on the slopes of Mt Etna is as breathtaking and impressive as the charming luxury Villa Neri hotel in which it is housed. In the modern dining room, the chef serves cuisine with a focus on Sicilian recipes and ingredients to which he adds a personalised and creative twist, resulting in occasionally complex dishes which are always of the highest quality. The wine list includes an excellent and highly recommended selection of local Etna labels.

Name: Da Manuela
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Specialities from Lower Piedmont and the Lomellina region are accompanied by a few freshwater fish dishes and traditional frogs’ legs on the menu at this restaurant, which also offers a fine array of delicious cheeses. The wine selection is also excellent.

Name: Oscar
Description: Situated off the tourist trail in a charming residential district, this restaurant is popular with locals from Livorno who come here to enjoy the fresh fish on offer – the vast selection on the buffet makes dining here a real treat. In summer, choose a table on the delightful outdoor veranda.

Name: Il Verso del Ghiottone
Description: This restaurant in the heart of the historic centre has been set up in an 18C hamlet. The cuisine is strictly traditional but skilfully reinterpreted to take advantage of contemporary tastes.

Name: Piacentino
Description: Restaurant with pension near the old town, where you can enjoy Piacentine dishes served outdoors in nice weather and in the airy indoors dining hall during the colder months. The rooms are in two styles, one with wrought iron beds and Arte Povera furniture, the other being more modern.

Name: La Cucina di Donna Carmela
Address: contrada Grotte 7, località Carruba di Riposto, Riposto, 95018, Italy
Description: Enjoy Sicilian specialities and the best produce from the hotel’s orchards and vegetable garden. Dine in a welcoming dining room or on the attractive outdoor terrace in the shade of the palm trees. All dishes are presented with contemporary - style.

Name: Tubladel
Description: Although this restaurant with wood-adorned dining rooms has the rustic and romantic ambience of an old Alpine hut (the name “tubladel” is the Ladin for hay barn), it is actually situated just a stone’s throw from the centre of Ortisei. The cuisine focuses on local ingredients such as meat and game, with dishes such as venison pappardelle and roast pork shank on the menu, and very few fish options. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Coppola Rossa
Description: Situated in the historic centre not far from the sea, this typical family - run restaurant specialises in fish and seafood. There is an antipasto buffet and a good choice of fish, as well as an open - view grill used in winter for cooking meat dishes.

Name: Trattoria della Posta
Description: Standing in open countryside, this country restaurant is decorated with elegant and romantic touches, such as silverware and candles. The menu features regional cuisine, including an excellent selection of the best local cheeses. Friendly welcome and experienced service.

Name: Cosmo Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Although the cuisine at Cosmo is influenced by the ingredients and culinary traditions of Campania, this restaurant is also an excellent choice for those in search of more elaborate and creative fare. Top-quality, complex dishes prepared by two young chefs.

Name: Bottega Lucia
Description: Bottega Lucia serves a cuisine which is mainly Italian in style, with the addition of a few specialities from the Iberian Peninsula and other countries. Home-made pasta, meat and fish can be enjoyed in an attractive New York-style bistro, while the American bar serves drinks and a selection of delicious, tempting snacks in the evening.

Name: Cavallino
Description: Il Cavallino, a long-established restaurant which pays tribute to Ferrari – a symbol of Maranello and Italy across the globe – now has the added attraction of Massimo Bottura’s creative cuisine. Traditional regional dishes, such as the delicious tortellini del Tortellante, are given interesting, personalised twists, as evidenced by the crème caramel made with 36-month-aged Parmesan cheese, chives and 12-year-old balsamic vinegar. Trendy decor, plus a flower-decked garden.

Name: Locanda Viola
Description: In this elegant restaurant with chairs and tables of different designs and original workmanship, it is skilful chef Filippo Moriggi’s cuisine that really captures your attention. The interesting appetisers take guests on an exotic journey, featuring options such as empanadas, fish bao (steamed buns, also available with a barbecue sauce) and Chinese dumplings. Other dishes are more typically Italian in style, with pastas, risottos and Bergamo-style mutton all on the menu. Desserts include a selection of ice-cream and affogato.

Name: AlpiNN
Address: Plan de Corones, alt. 2235, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description: Situated at an altitude of 2 000m in the Plan de Corones ski area, this restaurant stands next to Lumen, a museum dedicated to mountain photography. To get here, you take the cable-car from Riscone and then, in winter, walk for around 150m through the snow. This impressive project by Norbert Niederkofler, holder of three Michelin stars, showcases the chef’s “Cook the Mountain” philosophy, where a modern approach and Alpine traditions combine to create perfect dishes full of flavour and historic appeal. The memory lingers long after your return back down the mountain (NB: the last cable-car leaves at 5pm!).

Name: Senso Alfio Ghezzi Lake Garda
Address: via IV Novembre 86, Limone sul Garda, 25010, Italy
Description: Eala is a new luxury, designer-style hotel jutting into the lake, where top chef Alfio Ghezzi from Trento is at the helm in the restaurant. The gourmet formula on offer here, already successfully tried and tested at the Mart in Rovereto, consists of just one single tasting menu (guests choose the number of courses and some of the dishes), with precise, well-balanced cuisine made from carefully selected seasonal ingredients, including plenty of vegetables.

Name: PS Ristorante
Address: via di Petriolo 7, Cerreto Guidi, 50050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the beautiful countryside outside Cerreto Guidi, PS Ristorante is housed in the magnificent Medici Villa Petriolo which is also home to 36 luxurious guestrooms. The restaurant’s appeal is enhanced not only by the charm of the villa and its delightful garden (overlooked by the restaurant terrace), but also by the property’s delicious home-produced ingredients, such as extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pork, meat and chicken, produce from the kitchen garden, traditional cereals and other zero-mile ingredients, all reinterpreted in a creative, modern style by the chef (as in the egg and artichoke dish). The estate’s wine is also highly recommended – we particularly enjoyed the organic red Golpaia, a medium-structured blend of Merlot and Sangiovese with characteristic soft aromas.

Name: Anastasia
Description: This cocktail bar on the seafront is also a restaurant specialising in fresh fish served in a selection of classic dishes (such as tartare) and more elaborate recipes. The dining room is modern and spacious, plus there’s an outdoor terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. Guestrooms and luxury apartments are also available (swimming pool on the roof).

Name: Campo Cedro
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the centre yet away from the tourist crowds, this restaurant is well worth the effort needed to find it! Here, Japanese chef Sugihara, who has more than 20 years’ experience working in Italy, creates modern and skilfully prepared Italian meat and fish dishes which are fresh and elaborate. You’ll nearly always find seafood risotto on the menu, which is made with fish, mussels and finely chopped shrimps all cooked together with rice and then sprinkled with crumbled seaweed and dotted with tomato paste. Excellent value for money!

Name: Enoteca Meucci
Description: Comprising a wine boutique and a wine bar in its rustic-style room on the ground floor, Enoteca Meucci is also home to a restaurant in the more elegant, classic-style rooms on the first floor. The expertly prepared cuisine is colourful and contemporary in style, with a focus on regional ingredients. Beautiful outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Al Moro
Address: via Pietri 1277, Marina Di Campo, 57034, Italy
Description: Situated away from the main tourist area, in a rustic building that is striking for its attractive outdoor space shaded by a wooden gazebo, this restaurant boasts an informal and relaxing atmosphere. The Mediterranean cuisine is full of character and prepared with top-quality ingredients, including a small selection of oysters.

Name: Portanova
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Italian Contemporary
Description: A new restaurant in Urbino’s beautiful old town, where the designer-style decor blends harmoniously with the historic architecture. The modern, contemporary-style cuisine finds inspiration in ingredients from the Marche, as well as featuring flavours and traditions from other regions of Italy such as Sardinia, Campania and Lazio.

Name: Trattoria da Me
Description: This lively and very busy trattoria run by the energetic Elisa owes its success to a winning combination of traditional dishes (the fresh hand-made pasta, also sold in the shop next door, is a particular highlight) and specialities reinterpreted with a touch of imagination by the female chef, such as the ossobuco cut lengthways. You may like to try both by choosing a typical Bolognese dish as a starter followed by one of the chef’s more original options for your main course.

Name: Terrazza Tiberio
Description: Housed within the Tiberio hotel not far from the famous piazzetta, this elegant restaurant boasts a charming terrace with spectacular views of the rooftops of Capri. The skilful chef prepares creative dishes with a focus on ingredients from Campania, as well as delicious bread including a tempting “casatiello” (a savoury bread from Naples). Lighter options are available at lunchtime.

Name: Mugolone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from Piazza del Campo, this elegant restaurant serves excellent traditional Tuscan cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist. Professional yet friendly service, plus a separate dining room which can be booked for private dinners.

Name: Gennaro Amitrano
Description: Owner-chef Amitrano has moved from the centre of Capri to Marina Piccola, where his welcoming restaurant boasts beautiful sea views. Here he delights his guests with imaginative dishes full of flavour.

Name: Vitique
Address: via Citille 43/b, Greve in Chianti, 50022, Italy
Description: Providing a splash of modernity in the Florentine Chianti region, this restaurant is highly contemporary both in its decor and its cuisine, the latter available in the form of tasting menus only (guests can choose the number of courses they want). Meat and fish are cooked with expert precision and prepared with real creative flair.

Name: Locanda Perbellini al Mare
Description: Enjoy imaginative Sicilian dishes created by multi-starred Michelin chef Perbellini in this beach restaurant that was once a family-run trattoria. The delightful natural setting acts as the perfect backdrop for Giancarlo’s original and exciting cuisine.

Name: 85 Bistrot
Address: piazza Martiri di Via Fani 85, Sesto San Giovanni, 20099, Italy
Description: This simple, modern, family-run trattoria with a welcoming ambience is the kind of restaurant that everyone would love to have as their local. The owner-chef, who has plenty of experience working in Milanese restaurants, is a real culinary expert who creates traditional dishes from Milan but also from further afield. Here, the popular breaded cutlet is served thick so that the delicate flavour of the veal can be enjoyed to the full.

Name: Le Macine
Address: via Lino Carlo del Favero 11, Vittorio Veneto, 31029, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a recently renovated 18C mill on the banks of the Meschio river, this restaurant is run by brothers Giuseppe (front of house) and Adriano (in the kitchen), who serve top-quality cuisine with its roots in local traditions and the occasional imaginative twist with warmth and professionalism. It is even more appealing in summer, when meals are served on the beautiful outdoor terrace.

Name: La RiMa
Description: This restaurant in the heart of the city provides an elegant setting in which to enjoy excellent contemporary Mediterranean cuisine, all with a personalised twist added by the talented chef. Female staff provide the service and the friendly welcome.

Name: Sücar Brüsc
Description: The name of this interesting new restaurant in the historic heart of Mantova is a phrase in local dialect which translates as “sour” sugar. The cuisine here is regional yet modern, served in an informal dining room where traditional Mantuan sayings are written on the ceilings. The wine list features a selection of both well-known and less familiar wines.

Name: La Botte
Description: A modern and welcoming contemporary bistro situated in the heart of Stresa’s historic centre. Run by an entire family, the restaurant serves modern and imaginative fish and meat dishes where the focus is always on seasonal ingredients. The interesting wine list also includes a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Pellico 3
Description: Situated in the luxury Park Hyatt hotel just a few metres from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, this restaurant is home to a young chef who serves elegant and occasionally complex cuisine. His dishes include sauces and traditions learned from his time working in France, as well as plenty of vegetables and Mediterranean influences.

Name: Gunè San Frediano
Address: via del Drago d'Oro 1r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: The chef at this small gastronomic restaurant serves cuisine which acts as a bridge between Basilicata and Tuscany, the two most significant regions in his life, resulting in creative, delicate and beautifully presented dishes.

Name: I 5 Sensi
Description: The whole family (mother and four children) is involved in the running of this restaurant, both front of house and in the kitchen. If you’re looking for top-quality cuisine which focuses on local ingredients yet is also creative and innovative, then this is the place for you! Classic-style dining room with the occasional modern decorative touch, plus a well-stocked wine cellar offering a selection of 700 labels.

Name: Dulchemente
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant which serves modern dishes alongside simpler, more classic options, with a notable focus on fish. A splendid outdoor terrace for alfresco dining and friendly, professional staff complete the picture.

Name: Mesadoria
Description: Enjoy excellent fish and seafood cuisine in this modern restaurant with three floors, including a beautiful terrace for cocktails and an outdoor area on the top floor for aperitifs. The small wine list has a regional focus, and we recommend leaving space for dessert – you won’t regret it!

Name: L'Ostreria Fratelli Pavesi
Description: Overlooking a 20C courtyard typical of the Bassa Padana area, this restaurant’s name (a play on the word “osteria”) refers to the three (“tre”) brothers who share the work in the kitchen and front of house. It’s clear that the saying “many hands make light work” holds true here: the many dishes served in this simple, friendly dining room include local specialities such as cured hams, salumi, anolini pasta, ricotta and spinach tortelli and “bomba di riso” (a moulded rice dish), as well as main courses of venison and sturgeon and a delicious “zuppa inglese” (trifle) for dessert. Booking ahead is recommended, even for a weekday lunch, as it gets very busy.

Name: Frades La Terrazza
Address: SP94 - Località Abbiadori, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Situated in a panoramic location on Cala di Volpe bay, this trendy restaurant serves excellent cuisine with a focus on Sardinian specialities and other Mediterranean dishes. There’s a beautiful terrace for an aperitif, plus tapas options to share and a good selection of sparkling wines. Young and enthusiastic staff.

Name: Radici Gourmet
Description: Housed in a charming small villa dating from the early 20C, this multifunctional space combines an informal bar-cum-bistro with a gourmet restaurant where the chef delights guests with his interpretation of local cuisine, as implied by the name of the restaurant (“radici” is the Italian for roots). Two tasting menus, plus an extensive à la carte which offers something for all tastes. Professional service and personalised wine recommendations complete the picture.

Name: Calvi Ristorante
Description: This welcoming, contemporary-style restaurant with a large open-view kitchen serves two different types of cuisine – one regional and Mediterranean in style, the other more creative allowing the chef’s culinary skills to take centre stage. The black rice tacos with roasted eel, green beans, soya bean sprouts and spicy hummus mayo are truly delicious – definitely to be eaten with the hands!

Name: Oltremare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Due Torri hotel, the restaurant has recently been refurbished, giving it an even more charming and atmospheric feel than before. The cuisine is creative in style, almost always using ingredients and recipes from Campania as its inspiration – a good example is the many different ways tomato is used, including tomato water distilled in an alembic still. Chef Alfonso Crisci’s recipes are complex and always full of different ingredients and colours, with a selection of delicious and generous desserts to finish your meal.

Name: Urubamba
Description: Situated amid luxury boutiques and historic palazzi in one of Naples’ most exclusive districts, this restaurant boasts a chic and romantic dining room with soft lighting on the first floor, as well as an exclusive outdoor terrace for fine weather. The cuisine is totally in keeping with the trendy setting, featuring a successful combination of two different gastronomic cultures (namely Peruvian and Japanese) that blend together perfectly.

Name: L'Agave
Description: Perched on the cliff overlooking the small port of Framura, the terraces at this restaurant boast one of the most stunning views in the area. The dishes served up by the young chef are a declaration of his love for Liguria (as is the wine list), featuring a remarkable selection of top-quality regional ingredients such as artichokes and asparagus from Albenga, beans from Pigna, pine nuts, prebugiun (a mixture of wild plants), Taggiasca olives and of course local fish and seafood.

Name: Marotta
Description: Nestled amid the verdant hills of the Upper Caserta region, this delightful restaurant is a real gem. Young chef Domenico Marotta serves surprisingly high-quality cuisine with a focus on local ingredients and vegetables (some from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden) which he transforms into modern, minimalist yet generous dishes which are anything but predictable, and are showcased on three tasting menus and a short à la carte. We particularly enjoyed the Leccarda-style pigeon, a reinterpretation of a traditionally Umbrian dish, in which every part of the bird is used. The sommelier/head waiter is as impressive as the talented chef, as he guides guests on their culinary journey with his detailed and enthusiastic explanations.

Name: Altatto Bistrot
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the edge of old Milan, this former bakery has been converted into a tiny restaurant serving vegetarian cuisine in a contemporary-style setting. The two tasting menus include delicious, colourful and beautifully presented dishes which can also be ordered à la carte. Booking is essential.

Name: I Due Buoi
Description: This restaurant offers three tasting menus: Stile Libero, Tradizione e Territorio, and Quinto Quarto , the latter featuring various types of offal which the chef transforms into creative dishes, plus an à la carte that includes local specialities and a good choice of bread. Top-quality wines with a focus on Asti and its surrounding area, as well as on the Langhe region.

Name: Indiniò
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant (the name Indiniò means “nowhere” in old Carnian dialect) is run by an enthusiastic female owner-chef who left her former job to realise her dream: namely, to create personalised cuisine of the highest quality with ingredients from her local region and elsewhere, while her partner takes charge of the dining room. Indiniò is both welcoming and elegant, with just a few tables, an intimate ambience and a small space for more private dining.

Name: Cocun Cellar Restaurant
Address: strada Prè de Vì 31, San Cassiano, 39036, Italy
Description: At this restaurant within the elegant Ciasa Salares hotel, guests dine in a wine cellar with a pleasantly informal and friendly atmosphere. In addition to the excellent cuisine, the fine cheese selection comes highly recommended, as does a visit to the room dedicated entirely to chocolate.

Name: Principe di Belludia
Description: The Principe di Belludia is the gourmet restaurant at the Il San Corrado di Noto hotel, a luxurious resort in a secluded rural location with two enormous swimming pools. The new executive chef Martin Lazarov showcases his love for Sicily, with a particular attention to vegetables dishes.

Name: Cuculia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This beautiful restaurant with a smart and elegant decor has the feel of a stylish French bistro with a small library-style dining room displaying books on cookery and other subjects. Chef Oliver Betancourt left his home country of Venezuela to train in well-known restaurants in France, Spain and Italy, experiences which have resulted in multi-faceted cuisine influenced by different traditions and prepared using seasonal Italian produce as well as more exotic ingredients such as kombu, soy sauce and koji. The menu offers a good selection of vegetarian dishes, as well as a few vegan options. The wine list includes extensive information on the different labels featured, including an excellent red from Bolgheri Acciderba.

Name: Diana's Place
Description: Facing the square in front of Termini station, this wine bar-cum-restaurant is striking for its fresh and creative approach to cuisine. Nearly all the top-quality ingredients are local and can be purchased from the food counter. The excellent staff are happy to help with your choice of wine, which is also available by the glass.

Name: Impronta
Description: Occupying the site of a restaurant that was highly successful in the 1980s and 90s, Impronta is home to a young local chef who showcases skills acquired in a leading Michelin-starred restaurant in Sicily. As a result of this experience, his enticing dishes have a light Mediterranean feel, embellished with the occasional personal twist.

Name: Maso Runch-Hof
Description: Surrounded by woods, a trip to this restaurant housed in an 18C farmhouse is like taking a journey back in time. Take a seat in one of the wood-adorned Stube-style rooms and enjoy generous portions of delicious home-cooked Ladin specialities featured on a single tasting menu, including cajinci t’ega (spinach-filled ravioli), excellent pork ribs with polenta, and apple strudel. The small wine list has the same local focus, featuring labels from the Alto Adige region. A recent addition, the restaurant also now has a few spacious, welcoming chalets available for guests.

Name: John Restaurant-Casamadre
Address: via Santa Maria la Nova 35, Afragola, 80021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a district of large shopping malls on the outskirts of town, Casamadre is a specialist food shop, while John is the restaurant next door. The latter has just a few tables and an open-view kitchen, and while you certainly don’t come here for the scenic views, you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the modern and imaginative reinterpretations of Campanian dishes created by the remarkably talented chef.

Name: Essencia Restaurant
Address: piazza Santa Maria la Nova 9, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Having spent many years living in Spain, the young chef at this quiet, elegant restaurant offers an appealing combination of Spanish and Italian dishes, resulting in his own interesting interpretations of Mediterranean cuisine. Situated in the heart of the historic centre, the restaurant has an open-view kitchen and chef’s table for four guests near the entrance, while the main dining room is on the first floor.

Name: Il Tempo Nuovo
Description: Now occupied by a charming boutique hotel, the Castello di Ugento is also home to this restaurant where the Puglian chef reinterprets the traditions of Salento in contemporary dishes that feature an array of meat, fish and vegetables. The staff will be more than happy to recommend the best accompaniment to your meal, whether this is a good wine from the plentiful wine list or a delicious cocktail.

Name: Bites
Description: The cuisine at this tiny, simply furnished restaurant includes barbecued dishes and fermented ingredients, all of which feature on a tasting menu. Guests can also choose à la carte: the small portions (as the restaurant name suggests) make it possible to taste several dishes at a reasonable cost. Booking is essential in the evening and also advisable at lunchtime.

Name: Vivace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated right in the heart of Brescia, this new 4.0 restaurant with geothermic heating and technologically controlled energy serves contemporary-style cuisine in a modern bistro with a “wine theatre” in the middle of the dining room.
