There’s also an attractive space with a brick vaulted ceiling in the basement.

Name: Al Bagatto
Description: A small, elegant restaurant in the city centre decorated in warm colours. Two private rooms (one very intimate, just for two people, the other slightly larger) are also available. Fish - based cuisine with a modern touch.

Name: Bacchus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ideal for visitors to Olbia, this modern, fresh and young restaurant serves typical regional specialities alongside more imaginative fish dishes. In fine weather, ask for a table on the lovely terrace overlooking the swimming pool.

Name: uovodiseppia Milano
Description: This completely renovated restaurant is situated in a pedestrianised area near Piazza Gae Aulenti, a new elegant restaurant district in Milan. Here, a wood-fired stove, attractive bar counter and small bistro-style tables provide the setting for carefully prepared Sicilian cuisine. Octopus, grouper and Mazara red prawns are just some of the top-quality Sicilian ingredients on the menu here, which includes reinterpreted recipes such as the “fuori Norma”, where the pasta is wrapped around the stuffed aubergine to create a dish full of Mediterranean flavours and aromas. The outdoor dining space in the pedestrianised street is perfect for early summer evenings, with its almost bohemian feel.

Name: Alto
Address: via Circondariale San Francesco 2, Fiorano Modenese, 41042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The top floor of the renovated Executive Spa Hotel now houses chef Mattia Trabetti’s fine-dining restaurant, where the rooftop dining room boasts relaxing views of the surrounding hills and the Santuario della Beata Vergine del Castello through its floor-to-ceiling windows. The young, innovative cuisine is showcased on a “green” tasting menu (Emilia Vegetale) with a seasonal and regional focus, as well as on a menu dedicated to local traditions (Modena Safari). Original options that will appeal to curious palates include trout with alchermes, cat fish and hops; green tagliatelle with chicory, black garlic and roe (with grated egg adding an interesting twist); and Montese-style duck. The wine list offers plenty of choice, starting with a regional focus but also extending to the rest of Italy and then to France. We particularly recommend the Giorgio Melandri Sangiovese di Romagna "Acereta" with its balanced aromas, which offers excellent value for money.

Name: Antico Arco
Description: At Porta San Pancrazio, a stone’s throw from Gianicolo where you can enjoy a breathtaking panorama of Rome, here instead the kitchen plays the lead: some echoes of Lazio, but mostly creative, both meat and fish.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: piazza della Vittoria 14, Marciana Marina, 57033, Italy
Description: Situated in a corner of the charming little square in Marciana Marina, just a few minutes from Cotone, one of the oldest and most beautiful parts of the town. The restaurant serves Mediterranean dishes and specialities from Elba, all reinterpreted with an individual twist. Raw fish is one of the house specialities.

Name: Degusteria del Gigante
Address: via degli Anelli 19, San Benedetto del Tronto, 63074, Italy
Cuisine: Country cooking, Cuisine from the Marches
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre of the upper part of the town, right behind the Torre dei Gualtieri, this restaurant occupies a 19C building with 15C foundations. Regional cuisine skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist takes pride of place on the menu, where the focus is on flavour and seasonal ingredients rather than a vast selection of dishes. House specialities include options such as boned caramelised rabbit served with its own jus (inspired by the better-known traditional Marche dish), while daily visits to the market usually result in one or two fish-based recipes.

Name: Alla Vedova
Description: Although now surrounded by the suburbs of Udine, this restaurant is proud to boast two centuries of history. Its current owners have been at the helm in the kitchen here for five generations, creating authentic traditional Friulian specialities such as cjalçons (ravioli) – both the sweet and savoury versions of the dish – as well as a whole host of dishes cooked over the charcoal grill which dominates one of the dining rooms.

Name: Pierino Penati
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Surrounded by the greenery of the Brianza hills, this villa on the outskirts of the village boasts a delightful garden and an elegant dining room with a veranda. Although the cuisine here is traditional in style, it showcases the best of the Mediterranean in dishes that often feature modern preparation and combinations. Special attention is paid to the desserts, many of which are highly innovative, including one that pays homage to the Rubik’s cube. The impressive, well-structured wine list includes a selection of renowned labels from Italy and further afield alongside some younger, lesser-known options.

Name: Mamma Rosa
Address: via XXIV Maggio 1, San Polo d'Enza, 42020, Italy
Description: Although from the outside this restaurant looks to be no more than a group of houses on the outskirts of the village, all the effort here focuses on creating fish and seafood dishes made from the best quality fish. Prepared in Mediterranean - style.

Name: A Spurcacciun-a
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Always a good choice for gourmet cuisine, this lovely restaurant within the Hotel Mare boasts a fine location with a garden for summer dining overlooking the beach and the sea. Whether you’re soaking up the views outside or sitting comfortably in the attractive contemporary-style dining room, it’s Simone Perata’s cuisine that will convince you that you’ve chosen the best place in town. The menu is teeming with delicious dishes made from top-quality ingredients (especially fish, such as the delicious whitebait with grilled artichokes and green curry sauce), all prepared with a modern twist and beautifully presented. The excellent wine list (including a few vintage labels) provides the perfect accompaniment to your dining experience.

Name: Sibilla
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant occupies a stunning location at the foot of the Temple of Vesta, which can be admired from the attractive outdoor terrace. The classic cuisine served here is prepared mainly with local ingredients, although a few fish dishes also feature. Grilled dishes are among the house specialities.

Name: Cavallini
Address: viale Bigioli 47, San Severino Marche, 62027, Italy
Description: A restaurant with light and relaxing tones, run by two brothers, one in the kitchen and the other in charge of the front of house, who continue the family tradition in these new premises. Mostly fish, the chef's true passion, but the menu also offers valid meat alternatives.

Name: La Pecora Nera
Address: via San Martino 18, Montecatini Terme, 51016, Italy
Description: Murano glass chandeliers and elegant period flooring provide a contrast to the fresh, contemporary - style decor of this restaurant. Imaginative cuisine with a focus on fish dishes.

Name: Il Capriccio
Description: An unmissable stop for anyone looking to try the best restaurants in the Gargano, Il Capriccio overlooks the marina, with tables laid out on the jetty in summer. The delicious cuisine combines creative fish options with the traditional vegetable dishes which are so popular in Puglia. The rice, potato and mussel dish is highly recommended, while food - lovers might like to try the unusual menu based on recipes from bygone days.

Name: Apollinare
Description: Surrounded by walls dating back to the 13C, this intimate and romantic setting is typical of old Spoleto. With their exposed beams and stonework, the elegant dining rooms are the perfect backdrop for superb, traditional Umbrian cuisine, to which the chef adds a few fish dishes.

Name: Tre Noci
Description: Situated in the centre of a village in the Bassa Bergamasca area, this long-established, family-run restaurant has a rustic decor softened by the owners’ female touch. The overall feel is that of an elegant trattoria, which provides a pleasant backdrop for delicious specialities from this lowland region, including meat cooked over the large grill in the dining room. There’s also a gazebo for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Cip's Club
Description: Elegant atmosphere, but informal in an establishment which offers a service overlooking the Giudecca canal in the summer; traditional meat and fish cuisine, with Venetian specialities.

Name: Le Viole
Address: strada nuova di Castelnuovo 60/a, Castelnovo di Baganzola, 43126, Italy
Description: Regionally based cuisine with the occasional hint of creativity and a good choice of à la carte dishes are the highlights at this friendly restaurant on the outskirts of Parma. An authentic, genuine welcome, with an attractive lounge near the entrance and the warm ambience of a private home.

Name: Soltojo
Description: Housed in an old wood- and stone-built mill, this restaurant boasts an elegant, romantic and stylish dining room with large windows offering views of a stream surrounded by greenery. Here, the talented chef creates personalised cuisine with a focus on modern fish and meat dishes that include the occasional hint of Asian influence.

Name: Cocchi
Description: This restaurant adjoining the Daniel hotel is the town’s pride and joy. Here, two quiet, rustic-style dining rooms provide the backdrop for typical Parma specialities that change with the passing seasons – the “tortelli alle erbette” (tortelli pasta with herbs) with parmesan and melted butter is particularly delicious – all accompanied by an excellent choice of wines. Booking in advance is highly recommended as the restaurant is extremely popular with visitors and locals alike.

Name: Il Basilisco
Description: Situated in a residential district on the outskirts of town, this simple restaurant with a colourful decor serves excellent cuisine. Although many of the dishes are typical Italian favourites, it is the local specialities, such as the sopa coada di piccione (a type of warm pigeon soup), that particularly won us over. The menu also features a few fish options.

Name: Trippi
Address: via Stelvio 297, loc. Montagna in Valtellina, Sondrio, 23020, Italy
Description: This long-established restaurant just outside Sondrio has been run for the past decade by Gianluca, whose experience injects new life into traditional dishes from the local region, as well as introducing the occasional Mediterranean twist. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, plus a good selection of local wines and cheeses on sale at takeaway prices near the restaurant entrance.

Name: Osteria Mercato
Description: The anonymous location of this restaurant in a car park just a stone’s throw from the historic centre is more than compensated by its lively and welcoming atmosphere. Attractive outdoor area, plus Italian cuisine reinterpreted with a creative twist.

Name: L'Arcangelo
Address: via Giuseppe Gioacchino Belli 59, Rome, 00193, Italy
Description: Simple and austere: the rightfully earned fame of this restaurant is due to the search for the best regional (but not only) products. A real passion of the owner who, like an archangel, will guide you to the paradise of the palate and gastronomic niches.

Name: Casa Rispoli
Address: piazza san Francesco 7, Cava de' Tirreni, 84013, Italy
Description: Overlooking a piazza surrounded by picturesque arcades in the historic centre (a walk around this district is highly recommended), this restaurant run by the Rispoli family continues to uphold its fine-dining traditions. Although a few meat dishes feature on the menu, it is its fish options (mainly traditional, such as tuna with mussels and escabeche-style aubergine) and occasionally imaginative desserts, such as the cheesecake with toffee and raspberry, that are the main attraction here.

Name: Osteria Perbacco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This delightful restaurant has a romantic terrace overlooking the river. The many specialities include fish from the lagoon, the inevitable dried cod, spiced pork sausage served with mashed potatoes, and veal cheeks.

Name: La Brughiera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This old farmhouse in the Groane Regional Park has never lost its warm family atmosphere. The interior is spacious and attractive and the menus are based on traditional and national specialities.

Name: L'Altro Eden
Address: via Calata Porto 11, Santa Margherita Ligure, 16038, Italy
Description: Located on the quayside, this restaurant boasts a pleasant view of the port from its attractive outdoor space. The menu showcases fish specialities prepared in classic style, with the best fish from the daily catch announced at your table.

Name: Urbino dei Laghi
Address: via San Giacomo in Foglia 15, Pantiera, 61029, Italy
Description: This harmonious building featuring carefully chosen, unusual furnishings boasts a superb setting. Delicious regional cuisine with many ingredients from the restaurant’s own farm.

Name: Taverna dell'Oca
Description: Occupying what were once old stables and a coach house, this traditional restaurant is directly run by its owner, who is also at the helm in the kitchen. His recipes range from regional specialities to fish, complemented by a more extensive evening menu which also includes tasting options (one of which is entirely dedicated to goose dishes). Although there’s a more limited choice at lunchtime, the high quality of the cuisine is unchanged. A small outdoor space overlooks the quiet street, offering views of the beautiful garden nearby.

Name: Al Gatto Nero
Description: Family - run, informal service, care in the choice of raw materials in a typical welcoming trattoria with Venetian and seafood cuisine; delightful outside area in the summer.

Name: Tre Galline
Description: A bastion of traditional Piedmontese cuisine, the main dining room at this restaurant boasts a profusion of wood from its parquet flooring to the wood panelling and exposed roofbeams. The warm, hearty cuisine features local specialities such as vitello tonnato, agnolotti pasta with roast meat sauce and a selection of mixed boiled meats, as well as a cheese trolley.

Name: Osteria da Afro
Description: An expertly run family restaurant not far from the historic centre. Warm atmosphere in the two dining rooms (especially the one with the fireplace), where the daily specials are marked on a blackboard. A real gem of restaurant, which also has a few charming guestrooms furnished in fir and cherry wood.

Name: Alle Corone
Address: campo della Fava, sestiere Castello 5527, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Modern Mediterranean and Venetian cuisine served in three elegant dining rooms or – on request – in the wine bar surrounded by bottles of wine. Through the windows, enjoy the spectacle of gondolas passing by along the small canal outside.

Name: Fiorentino e Locanda del Giglio
Description: Just like the beautiful centre of Sansepolcro in which it is situated, this restaurant has much to boast about, with a history dating back over 200 years. The beautifully decorated dining rooms on the first floor of the palazzo are a picture of elegance, while the service is friendly and more informal. Traditional cuisine from inland Tuscany, plus welcoming guestrooms which add to its appeal.

Name: Estro Vino e Cucina
Address: calle Crosera, sestiere Dorsoduro 3778, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Situated slightly off the beaten track, this modern wine bar is also a restaurant serving Mediterranean cuisine accompanied by a selection of 700 organic wines. Snacks are available at aperitif hour.

Name: Fiorfiore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant occupying an elegant villa in a panoramic location with views of Todi and the surrounding countryside serves modern cuisine with its roots in Umbrian tradition. The extra-virgin olive oil comes from directly from the estate, as does some of the wine; there’s also an interesting selection of champagnes. Our inspector recommends the roast suckling pig accompanied by rosemary-flavoured potatoes, as well as the hazelnut cream, yoghurt sorbet and warm chocolate foam dessert. Quiet, comfortable guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Osteria da Mualdo
Address: via Privata Crespi 6, Capriate San Gervasio, 24042, Italy
Description: In this “company village” (now a UNESCO World Heritage site) with its textile factory, workers’ houses and castle belonging to the Crespi cotton manufacturers, an attractive farmhouse has been converted into an elegant restaurant. You’re greeted by tempting displays of cured hams and cheeses on Mualdo’s bar as soon as you enter the restaurant, but the delicacies don’t stop here. The menu features meat and fish dishes which are contemporary yet unfussy and full of flavour. So much more than a farmhouse!

Name: Papaveri e Papere
Description: The cuisine at this restaurant focuses on local recipes and ingredients yet also has a light, modern flavour and beautiful contemporary presentation, as seen in the pici pasta with roast peppers, sweetbreads and pecorino cheese. The chef here is equally at ease with meat and fish, and particularly keen on vegetables, with white truffles from San Miniato featuring on the menu in the autumn.

Name: Regina Lucia
Description: Overlooking a square of monumental beauty where tables are laid out for alfresco dining in summer, Regina Lucia is well worth a visit even when it’s not fine enough to sit outside. In a dining room with plenty of historic character, enjoy classic Sicilian cuisine reinterpreted with a creative twist – and make sure you don’t miss the delicious desserts!

Name: Onda Blu
Address: via Orsa Minore 1, San Mauro a Mare, 47030, Italy
Description: Almost appearing to rise up directly out of the sand, this unexpectedly elegant restaurant is home to a simple yet stylish dining room with large windows overlooking the sea. Fresh fish of the highest quality takes pride of place on the menu, served in classic, traditional dishes from the Adriatic. Daily specials are available alongside the à la carte, while the excellent wine list includes labels from outside Italy, with a particular focus on French wines.

Name: Amo
Address: calle del Fontego dei Tedeschi, Ponte di Rialto, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: Situated within the Fondaco dei Tedeschi, once a type of stock exchange where merchants from northern Europe traded with their Venetian counterparts and now a luxury shopping centre for those in search of high-end brands, Amo is the trendiest of the Alajmo group’s restaurants. Gourmet yet casual in style, the restaurant boasts an internal courtyard setting and lounge-style decor by Philippe Starck. The view of the Grand Canal and the rooftops of Venice from the top-floor terrace is stunning (booking is recommended although you may be lucky enough to get a table here when you arrive).

Name: Corte Matilde
Address: via Pelate 38, Pieve di Coriano, 46036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The owners' professionalism and passion go hand in hand with a cuisine made with first - class products. The dishes are simply prepared but tasty, exalting the flavour of the ingredients. It is located in a pretty, refurbished farmhouse on the road that Matilda of Canossa once travelled on.

Name: Castello
Address: via Cagna 4, Santa Vittoria d'Alba, 12069, Italy
Description: This restaurant offers several different options in which to enjoy its delicious meat and fish dishes with a modern twist. In summer, the beautiful veranda with views of the hills and surrounding countryside offers alfresco dining, while in winter the bright, modern dining room is a perfect setting for your meal.

Name: S'Andira
Address: via Orsa Minore 1, Santa Reparata, 07028, Italy
Description: In Italian this translates into "he who goes", but you will never feel like leaving this place. Located amidst granite boulders sculpted by the wind, juniper trees and the sea that will tantalize your vision and your palate.

Name: Moscatello Muliner
Description: Situated in a rural setting on a huge agricultural property, this attractive restaurant is dominated by an early 20C millstone. The menu combines traditional Italian fare with regional specialities, all at reasonable prices.

Name: Al Cavallino Bianco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Situated near the banks of the River Po, this century - old, family - run restaurant serves regional specialities, such as the famous culatello ham. You will find reasonably priced local dishes at the ‘Tipico di Casa Spigaroli’ at lunchtime during the week, and themed menus at the weekend.

Name: La Locanda dei Narcisi
Description: Visitors come here for the fresh fish caught in the nearby Ligurian Sea, such as prawns in hazelnut tempura with grapefruit granita and raw fish dishes served with delicious risotto from the Upper Langhe region, as well as meat dishes that include Fassona beef and agnolotti pasta. The cakes and pastries are also well worth a mention, as is the bread which is also available for purchase. In summer, the dining room is supplemented by outdoor tables which offer a pleasant alfresco dining experience.

Name: Da Severino il Vecchio - Di Luciano
Address: largo Abruzzi 2, ang. via Piemonte 23, Senorbì, 09040, Italy
Description: This historic restaurant now has new premises with a classic yet modern feel. Mediterranean cuisine with a traditional and regional influence.

Name: Posta
Address: viale Vittorio Veneto 169, Sant'Omobono Terme, 24038, Italy
Description: Situated in the Imagna valley, this welcoming, family-run restaurant serves delicious regional specialities alongside traditional Italian favourites, including a few fish options. Highlights include the dried-cod cannelloni, soft braised “guancialino” and the unmissable zabaglione mousse with sbrisolona-cake crumbs and marzipan ice-cream.

Name: Ai Mercanti
Address: corte Coppo, sestiere San Marco 4346/a, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: A family-run “gastrosteria” hidden in a small Venetian courtyard, with a modern and elegant decor dominated by beige and black tones. Full of exciting and imaginative flavours, the modern meat and fish dishes prepared by promising young chef Nadia Locatello make a change from the typical specialities of the region.

Name: Al Tonno di Corsa
Description: Not only the restaurant, but a large part of the tantalising menu as well is based on the tuna caught in the nets. Open kitchen; two small dining rooms and two pleasant little terraces.

Name: Rifugio Fuciade
Address: località Fuciada - Soraga di Fassa, San Pellegrino, 38035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: At 1980 meters, a mountain lodge where guests enjoy a panoramic view of the Dolomites; outdoor dining in summer, with an enchanting view.

Name: Antica Osteria La Rampina
Address: via Emilia fraz. Rampina 3 ang. via Rocca Brivio, San Giuliano Milanese, 20098, Italy
Description: It is said that General Radetzky, fleeing from the city during the Five Days of Milan rebellion, camped his troops right in front of La Rampina’s courtyard. Surrounded by nature and full of fascinating history, the restaurant now makes an ideal spot in which to enjoy the various culinary options served by Lino and his young son Luca, which offer a careful balance of local traditional flavour and skilful innovation.

Name: Il Capriolino
Address: via Nazionale 108, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description: This elegant restaurant has been run by the same family for years and has a history dating back over two centuries. It serves regional yet creative cuisine and has a distinctly Middle European ambience with its hunting trophies, clocks and frescoes.

Name: Gatto Rosso
Description: This small, long - established restaurant has been run by the same family for three generations, as depicted by the black - and - white photos on the walls. Simple and well - maintained dining room, plus a menu which focuses uniquely on fish dishes.

Name: Locanda 4 Cuochi
Description: Situated behind the amphitheatre right in the historic centre, this attractive restaurant serves simple yet top-quality cuisine and is run by two former pupils of chef Giancarlo Perbellini. The menu features contemporary Italian cuisine, including dishes such as creamy risotto with saffron, prawns and lemon curd, and lamb kebabs with aromatic herbs, corn salad, mint yoghurt and black sesame seeds.

Name: Casa Format
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A sustainable complex, the vegetable garden and a lot of passion are the elements that distinguish this high-quality restaurant. The modern building is characterized by very large windows that make the most of solar energy. The cuisine is authentic, tasty and with original ideas: the ice cream whipped with a Carpigiani machine before service is a delicious example.

Name: Casa del Nonno 13
Address: via Caracciolo 13, loc. Sant'Eustachio, Mercato San Severino, 84085, Italy
Description: Recently re-opened under new management, this charming restaurant winds its way from room to room until you finally arrive at the palazzo’s old cellars, the jewel in its crown. The cuisine here has quickly made a name for itself, focusing on strong links with regional traditions and showcasing local favourites on a menu full of tempting options, including salumi, local vegetables, pasta dishes, grilled meat options and typical local ingredients such as San Marzano tomatoes. The delicious cuisine pays tribute to the fine culinary traditions of Campania.

Name: l' Ciocio - Osteria di Suvereto
Description: Although this restaurant in the historic centre of Suvereto has the welcoming ambience of a traditional trattoria, its cuisine is more creative and elaborate in style (while still offering a few Tuscan classics). One of the house favourites is the “reale familiare”: a delicious cut of beef served with capers and anchovies.

Name: Osteria 1126
Description: The 1126 in the name of this restaurant refers to the year in which the hilltop hamlet in which it is situated was founded. Today the hamlet is home to apartments with their own kitchen, as well as the main villa. In the restaurant, a young enthusiastic couple serves contemporary - style cuisine made from local ingredients.

Name: Baia Marinella
Description: Fish and seafood are to the fore in this restaurant with a stunning location jutting out over the sea. It has breathtaking views of the bay, as well as a sun terrace and access down to the water.

Name: Osteria Borgo Ronche
Description: Just a few tables and an elegantly contemporary decor provide the setting for cuisine with a focus on the sea, with simpler dishes available at lunchtime and more creative fare served in the evening. There’s just one thing left to do and that’s book a table!

Name: 4 Ciance
Description: This restaurant in Cuneo’s historic centre boasts two bright dining rooms, as well as friendly and professional female staff and dishes prepared by two chefs that are a feast for the eyes and the palate! The cuisine here is rooted in tradition, and is prepared with skill, enthusiasm and the occasional contemporary touch. There are two tasting menus from which individual dishes can be chosen, plus a daily special (that varies according to market availability) announced at your table. Meat takes pride of place, as is typical in Piedmont, although a few fish and seafood options also feature.

Name: Cavour
Description: Cavour serves top-quality cuisine rooted in regional traditions, making it the type of restaurant that everyone would like as their local. Daily specials with a seasonal focus, such as the ultra-fresh puntarelle chicory salad with anchovies and Parmesan cheese, are also available.

Name: Osteria Vecchio Borgo
Description: Described as a “meeting point between Piedmont and Liguria”, this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the historic centre of Cuneo focuses on ingredients and recipes from these two regions – the family, all of whom are involved in the restaurant (the women in the kitchen and the men front of house), are from Liguria. The generous, top-quality cuisine is prepared using seasonal produce with a personalised touch and is accompanied by a good selection of wine, also available by the glass.

Name: Christian & Manuel
Description: This restaurant features sophisticated, creative cooking and top quality ingredients, without forgetting the culinary traditions of the area and region. Therefore, don't be surprised by the special attention reserved for rice: the menu offers a selection of twenty risottos, but also a lot of delicious land and sea specialities.

Name: Osteria del Trentino - Da Marco
Description: A typical neighbourhood restaurant with a characteristic feel and lovely al fresco summer service. Inviting local cuisine, and a fish menu too.

Name: Campiello
Address: via Nazionale 46, San Giovanni al Natisone, 33048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Although the homemade breadsticks and preserves (available for purchase) at this long-established restaurant should not be missed, Campiello’s highlights are its fish and wine – the fish served here is among the best in the region. We highly recommend the fish soup served with shellfish and a Buzara sauce, while the wine cellar is home to a selection of 25 000 bottles, with wines from the nearby Collio and Colli Orientali vineyards taking centre stage. A selection of renowned labels from Italy and abroad also features, offering an incredible choice of the highest quality for wine connoisseurs. There’s also the option of dining at the informal osteria next door.

Name: La Saletta
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the seafront promenade in the historic centre of Alghero, this small gem run by Gian Luca Chessa offers the best of Sardinia. The cuisine is showcased on different tasting menus, including Rivoluzione (creative yet with a regional focus); Radici (vegetables take centre stage); Riviera (local fish); and Cortile (traditionally inspired dishes). We particularly enjoyed the gnocchi stuffed with sheep’s ricotta cheese, beetroot sauce and Sardinian scorzone truffle – a real treat! All the wines are available by the glass, so don’t hesitate to ask the sommelier for recommendations.

Name: La Perla
Description: Housed in a historic palazzo on the charming Piazza della Motta in the town centre, this restaurant is one you will immediately want to share with family and friends thanks to its delicious cuisine. The menu focuses mainly on fish and seafood (including impressive raw fish dishes) although a few meat options are also available. Good choice of wines and spirits.

Name: Balin Sestri Levante
Description: An intimate restaurant on the seafront with a tiny dining room and small veranda, and a young, contemporary ambience. The Mediterranean-style cuisine is modern and creative with a focus on Ligurian ingredients to which the chef adds the occasional Asian twist, often in the sauces. Booking ahead is recommended given the limited number of tables here!

Name: Sabir
Address: via delle Ginestre 1, Zafferana Etnea, 95019, Italy
Description: Colourful Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional creative twist, yet always based on local specialities. This attractive restaurant takes its name from an old dialect once in use in the ports of the Mediterranean – a sort of Esperanto for sea merchants. In summer, ask for one of the tables in the cool and romantic garden.

Name: Lucenti
Description: This small, family - run restaurant furnished in warm, pastel shades offers a traditional setting in which to enjoy local cuisine. The dishes served in the younger, more informal Enoteca are even simpler and more traditional in style.

Name: Il Cortiletto
Description: Standing on the Lake Garda road, this small, simple, yet far from ordinary restaurant serves Mediterranean dishes with the occasional inventive twist. Two words of advice – opt for alfresco dining in fine weather, and don’t miss the maccheroncini served with perch and lemon pesto sauce.

Name: Vineria Derthona
Description: Situated in the heart of town, this secluded, busy and welcoming wine bar serves delicious Piedmontese dishes and a good selection of wines by the glass, chosen from the well-stocked wine cellar on a daily basis. House specialities include braised beef in a Barbera Colli Tortonesi sauce and gianduia chocolate semifreddo with mascarpone cream.

Name: Kisté - Easy Gourmet
Address: via Santa Maria de' Greci 2, Taormina, 98039, Italy
Description: Housed in the 15C Casa Cipolla, with a romantic terrace for summer dining, Kistè is a treasure trove of gourmet Sicilian cuisine prepared in contemporary style.

Name: La Fiaschetteria
Description: Enjoy excellent reinterpretations of Emilian classics in this large 18C farmhouse. It is lit with modern designer - style chandeliers and warmed by a large fireplace. The three splendid guestrooms combine elegance with typical regional decor.

Name: Alla Lanterna
Description: Despite its not particularly romantic location alongside the road, this restaurant attracts a loyal following who come here for the excellent fish cuisine. Guestrooms are also available for those wishing to prolong their stay.

Name: Ansitz Steinbock
Description: Following recent renovation work, this beautiful castle has an even more romantic atmosphere than ever. The restaurant is typical of the Alto Adige, boasting traditional Stube-style rooms that are furnished with a profusion of wood, from the floors to the walls and ceilings. The menu is more varied than previously, with a classic à la carte available for lunch and dinner, while fine-dining options are only available in the evening. The latter are presented on two tasting menus – “Roots” (dedicated to the local region) and “Creativo” (which includes ingredients from elsewhere) – both of which are striking for their imaginative approach.

Name: Walser Schtuba
Description: This delightful Alpine - style restaurant stands in the picturesque upper section of the Val Formazza. The menu features local specialities reinterpreted with a light, modern twist. Outdoor dining in summer.

Name: Antica Osteria Il Monte Rosso
Description: Situated on the lakeside in the residential district of Verbania, this small, Old England - style restaurant serves a selection of freshwater and saltwater fish specialities. If the weather allows, ask for one of the few tables on the panoramic terrace.

Name: Un Posto a Milano
Description: Un Posto a Milan is a farmhouse in the city: an ideal place to spend a few hours outdoors, but also an agricultural market, a kitchen serving food, a carpentry workshop and a venue offering a host of other activities. The menu features traditional Italian dishes (sometimes given a modern twist), made with top-quality fresh, seasonal and – as far as possible – organic ingredients.

Name: Ma.Ri.Na.
Address: piazza San Gregorio 11, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
Description: The classic and timelessly elegant Ma.Ri.Na restaurant has been a bastion for fish and seafood enthusiasts for decades. The menu features classic Italian specialities alongside more creative options, including a good selection of raw dishes as well as delicious seafood pastas and risottos. The wine list is also impressive and includes an array of wines by the glass.

Name: La Veranda
Description: Situated a few metres from the lake in the centre of the village, this welcoming and long-established family restaurant boasts a dining room that transforms into a veranda with outdoor dining in summer. The cuisine here is traditional, with generous portions of fish from the lake and sea.

Name: Quattro Gigli
Address: piazza Michele da Montopoli 2, Montopoli in Val d'Arno, 56020, Italy
Description: This restaurant occupying a 15C palazzo in the centre of a charming village has a warm and welcoming feel. Here, the chef delights his guests with regional meat and fish specialities, which are served in original ceramic dishes. The restaurant also offers a few guestrooms, the best of which boast panoramic views, as does the outdoor terrace used for summer dining.

Name: Locanda Radici
Address: SP 21, contrada San Vincenzo, Melizzano, 82030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A rustic restaurant with contemporary Mediterranean-style decor surrounded by the greenery of the Sannio region, which can be admired through the large windows. Modern cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients by the owner-chef, who has vast experience working in top restaurants, both in Italy and abroad.

Name: Malga Roncac
Description: An Alpine farmhouse built from wood and stone with a superb panoramic location on the edge of the woods. Traditional Ladin cuisine served in a typical local ambience.

Name: Gong
Description: East meets West in a harmonious fusion of flavours at this restaurant, which takes its name from the imposing gongs dotted around the modern, elegant dining room. The attentive and thoughtful staff are always on hand to explain the different dishes, which are influenced by Chinese traditions yet often have an innovative feel. Beautiful presentation and carefully chosen ingredients typify the contemporary international flavour of this type of cuisine, with an extensive and varied selection of dishes on the à la carte and various tasting menus. One of the latter is dedicated to Peking duck, the restaurant’s signature dish.

Name: Crotto Valtellina
Address: via Fiume 11, località Valle, Malnate, 21046, Italy
Description: With a bar or wine cellar located just inside the entrance, followed by a rustic dining hall, this restaurant serves strictly Valtellinese cuisine. Outdoor service in the summer, in the area below the cliff.

Name: Nicolin
Address: via Paisiello 4, località Maggianico, Lecco, 23900, Italy
Description: Run by the same family for over 30 years, this restaurant has recently been fully renovated. It serves traditional cuisine, as well as some imaginative dishes and a good choice of wine. Alfresco dining on the terrace in summer.

Name: Duo Ristorante
Description: This elegant, intimate restaurant with subdued lighting is the perfect choice for a romantic gourmet dinner. The chef offers several different menus, allowing guests to choose their main course from any of these. Creative cuisine, with a strong focus on ingredients from Puglia.

Name: Menzaghi
Address: via San Giovanni 74, Fagnano Olona, 21054, Italy
Description: Once you’ve found the car park, make your way to this restaurant’s small, traditional dining room where you will be warmly welcomed by the owner (a real wine enthusiast) and well looked after by his friendly yet efficient staff. Generous cuisine with plenty of attention paid to local, seasonal ingredients and daily specials that come highly recommended.

Name: Osteria Il Principe e Il Pirata
Description: This restaurant is housed in a typical island house with rustic furniture and a large terrace with sea views. Here, the Casano family look after guests, are responsible for the impressive wine list and, of course, prepare the cuisine that focuses on top-quality ingredients and Sicilian recipes. Specialities include couscous with fresh fish and vegetables, cuttlefish “alla fiamma” and courgettes marinated in mint, as well as typical desserts such as the “bacio pantesco”.

Name: Antica Trattoria dei Leoni
Description: Despite this restaurant’s contemporary feel, it nonetheless offers traditional cuisine from Lazio including grilled dishes (and spit - roasted specialities at weekends or by advance booking). The guestrooms occupy an old monastery, with those overlooking the square the most spacious.

Name: Buca di Sant'Antonio
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Piazza San Michele, in the heart of the beautiful historic centre of Lucca, the Buca di Sant'Antonio is one of the city’s oldest restaurants. Specialising in traditional Tuscan cuisine, the main courses here focus almost entirely on meat dishes. The old copper pots and pans that hang from the ceiling add to the homely atmosphere.

Name: Buriani dal 1967
Address: via Matteotti 66, Pieve di Cento, 40066, Italy
Description: A family-run restaurant in the province of Bologna with an excellent reputation for good food. Whether you choose one of the fish-based recipes or meat dishes, you’ll enjoy cuisine with a balance of classic flavours and modern influences, including a few regional specialities.

Name: Da Nonna Sceppa
Description: Founded in the 1960s by Grandma Giuseppa, the inn has today become a restaurant. The management has stayed within the hands of the same family: nephews and great - nephews are spread over dining room and kitchen. Local recipes on the menu, which changes daily.

Name: Le Due Lanterne
Description: Situated in the town centre, this typical family-run trattoria is highly popular with locals and offers excellent value for money. Iconic dishes on the menu include rabbit all'Arneis and Piedmontese battuta (a type of beef tartare), while the extensive wine list features a good selection of labels. We recommend booking a table in the first, more comfortable dining room.

Name: 50 Kalò
Description: In the Neapolitan tradition of interpreting dreams, 50 means bread (dough), while the word “kalò” has Greek origins and means good – the name “good dough” explains the secret behind the pizzas made by Ciro Salvo, one of the most famous pizza masters in Naples. This chef makes traditional Neapolitan pizzas, which are large in size and have a soft dough. The restaurant doesn’t take reservations – if it’s busy you just leave your name and wait to be called. However, if you prefer not to wait, there’s a second restaurant at 2, Piazza della Repubblica where you can book ahead of time.

Name: La Rosina
Description: With over 100 years of history behind it, La Rosina is still looking good, thanks to renovation work carried out a few years ago which has given the restaurant a new look. Situated in an attractive location in the hills around Marostica, this excellent restaurant is a sound choice for good food in the province of Vicenza, serving modern regional and Italian dishes which are full of flavour. Enjoy beautiful views of the surrounding hills from the guestrooms.

Name: Osteria Bellavista
Address: via Piovega 30, località Farra, Paderno del Grappa, 31017, Italy
Description: An excellent modern inn offering a warm, family welcome. Imaginative yet traditional dishes made from market-fresh ingredients, with a balance of fish and meat dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: Cavalluccio Marino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Imaginative cuisine in a long - established family restaurant, which is constantly updated by each generation. Situated away from the town centre, yet easily accessible, the restaurant boasts an enviable seafront location. Excellent selection of local and international wines.

Name: La Cascina 1899
Description: Situated on the main road running alongside the sea, this pleasant restaurant with a large car park occupies a late-19C building that has been transformed into an attractive, rustic-style eatery with plenty of outdoor areas and air-conditioned rooms with exposed-stone walls and wooden ceilings that provide welcome respite from the heat of summer. It’s no surprise that fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, although meat dishes also feature. The shop next door sells regional specialities, some produced by the restaurant itself, including the famous local bergamot citrus fruit.

Name: Antica Osteria Magenes
Description: This fascinating restaurant occupying an old house renovated in modern style comes as a surprise given its location in a small village deep in the countryside. Enjoy traditional cuisine reinterpreted in a playful and original way in the well-tended garden, where six exclusive tables provide the perfect setting for an intimate and romantic alfresco dinner.

Name: Villetta Annessa
Address: via Monte Oro 9, Riva del Garda, 38066, Italy
Description: A charming annexe to the Villa Miravalle hotel on the edge of Riva’s historic centre, this restaurant boasts a warm atmosphere and a pleasant outdoor space for summer dining. The regional, seasonal dishes served here are listed on a blackboard brought to your table, while the house speciality is undoubtedly the meat cooked over the sizzling grill – the first sight to greet you as you enter the dining room.

Name: Eea
Description: Named after the Ancient Greek name for the island, Eea is a long-established restaurant situated in an elevated position with panoramic views of the sea and the port. Enjoy delicious local cuisine with a modern twist, either on the outdoor terrace or in the dining room embellished with an attractive Sienese marble floor. Most of the fish on the menu is caught locally.

Name: Il Sole di Ranco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: An elegant residence with gardens sloping down to the lake. The charming terrace, where meals are served in summer, offers superb views of the lake, while the cuisine combines the traditional and the modern, including imaginative flavours with a focus on locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Emilio
Address: via Girardi 1, loc. Casabianca, Fermo, 63900, Italy
Description: With 60 years of history behind it, Emilio can definitely be described as a leading light on the region’s restaurant scene. The restaurant is renowned for its excellent fish, which is usually cooked in classic style (fish stew and mixed steamed fish served on steamed vegetables are prime examples) and often announced at your table, although a concise menu is also available. The elegant dining room is enhanced by a collection of striking works of art.

Name: Osteria dalla Peppa
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Traditional Cuisine
Description: Already popular in the late 19C, this inn in the town’s historic centre has retained its vintage atmosphere, period furnishings and decor. The cuisine focuses on local produce, with fresh pasta a house speciality.

Name: De Gustibus - Maurizio
Description: Simple, modern fish dishes full of flavour take centre stage at this family-run restaurant in the charming historic centre of Palmi. The raw fish dishes served here include a delicious carpaccio made with the catch of the day and seasoned with a delicate home-made vinaigrette and cherry tomatoes, while the “Intrusi” menu offers three or four meat options for non-fish eaters. Desserts are announced at your table and always include a delicious cannolo. The wine list features mainly Italian labels, as well as a choice of champagnes. An intimate and warmly recommended restaurant.

Name: Il Pozzo
Description: This restaurant is housed in a historic palazzo. It has a traditional dining room, as well as an area that was once home to a wine bar (vaulted ceilings and more convivial atmosphere). A full range of Italian specialities are served.

Name: La Nicchia
Address: salita San Gaetano 11, località Scauri Basso, Pantelleria, 91017, Italy
Description: A simple but well - tended restaurant offering traditional fish specialities. You can eat inside, in the essentially - furnished dining room, or outside beneath a delightful bower.

Name: Mildas
Address: via Rosmini 7, località Vadaione, Giustino, 38086, Italy
Description: Housed in what was once the chapel of a medieval monastery, Mildas serves classic specialities from Trento alongside a selection of dishes created by Mirko, the late founder of the restaurant, which is now run by his son. The wine list features illustrations and descriptions.

Name: Botero
Description: Close to the town centre and within walking distance of the Duomo, this restaurant is housed in a beautiful historic palazzo. The cuisine is delicious, with a menu featuring fish dishes (depending on market availability) and a few more traditional recipes such as sweet tortelli and the excellent nettle and angler fish gnudi. The friendly welcome and streamlined service explain the restaurant’s popularity at both lunch and dinner, so booking is recommended!

Name: Next2
Description: This restaurant is renowned for its excellent, modern and inviting cuisine. The menu showcases mostly regional ingredients (including meat) that are transformed into delicious recipes – the spinach ravioli with braised beef and blue bufala cheese, and the raw and cooked tuna with burrata, cherry tomatoes and basil are highly recommended. The impressive wine list and selection of cocktails can also be enjoyed as an aperitif or post-dinner drink at the wine bar.

Name: Osteria dai Mazzeri
Description: Once the town hall of Follina, this building dating from 1704 is now home to a restaurant run by two brothers who serve delicious regional and seasonal cuisine here (in winter, don’t miss the spit-roasted chicken, veal or pork cooked according to local tradition). A beautiful mulberry tree, the old symbol of the village that was once involved in the silk industry, graces the outdoor dining space.

Name: La Pergola
Address: via Flaminia km 63,900, Magliano Sabina, 02046, Italy
Description: La Pergola has just celebrated its 50th anniversary, marking more than half a century of delicious regional cuisine, including grilled meats, served in pleasantly rustic yet classic-style dining rooms with brick-vaulted ceilings and accompanied by a choice of wines from a well-stocked cellar. Conveniently situated near the motorway, the restaurant also offers guestrooms plus a few electric charging points in the car park.

Name: 3 Archi
Description: Well over 50 years of life for this Abruzzo cuisine classic, on the menu you’ll find lots of meat, especially grilled meats, traditional pasta dishes such as chitarra alla teramana con polpettine, Italian desserts with some local references (sweet Teramo pizza above all), so a plain and simple cuisine served in generous portions.

Name: Degli Angeli
Address: località Madonna degli Angeli, Magliano Sabina, 02046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The family that runs this excellent restaurant with views of the surrounding countryside has been doing so with passion and experience for over a century. The menu here focuses on the culinary traditions of Lazio, while the wine and extra-virgin olive oil are also sourced locally. The restaurant is part of a hotel and includes a shop (La Bottega delle Delizie) selling home-made produce.

Name: La Gritta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Two of your senses will experience powerful marine sensations in this place. Your sight will be delighted with the enchanting view, especially from the terrace, and your taste will be tantalised by the imaginative, top - quality cuisine.

Name: L'Ottava Nota
Description: This is one of those bright, pretty and modern restaurants that are very much in fashion nowadays. The cuisine is strongly linked to the region with fish dishes to the fore presented in an attractive and contemporary style.

Name: Li Lioni
Address: SS 131 km 244,400 - regione Li Lioni, Porto Torres, 07046, Italy
Description: The highlights of this restaurant just outside the tourist centre of Porto Torres are its informal atmosphere, spacious garden and traditional cuisine. The frattaubread is well worth sampling (also available in a vegan version), as is the legendary porceddu(suckling pig), which must be ordered when you book. When choosing wine, we recommend the well-structured and intense house red.

Name: Lipadusa
Description: In the centre of the village, a classic very simple atmosphere for this family run establishment with typical gastronomic dishes.

Name: Ristorante 1500
Address: via Pavicolo 43, funivia per raggiungere il ristorante in via Villa 3, San Vigilio, 39011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re not a guest at the Vigilius Mountain Resort hotel where this restaurant is situated, leave your car in Lana and take the short cable-car ride to Monte San Vigilio where you’ll find the hotel at an altitude of 1 500m (remember to check the time of the last cable-car back down the mountain!). Decorated with a profusion of wood, the dining room has the same modern feel as the creative mountain cuisine prepared by the new chef who started here in 2023.

Name: Vino Buono
Address: via Castello 20, Grumello del Monte, 24064, Italy
Description: Housed in an old 17C hay barn near the Duomo belltower, this interesting wine bar offers around 400 different labels to accompany an array of simple yet well-prepared traditional dishes (including a few fish options). Highlights include the cured hams, cheeses and the excellent starters.

Name: Finger's Garden
Description: Firmly aimed at a trendier crowd, this restaurant has soft lighting and an Oriental feel. The chef here skilfully creates a range of dishes, including raw fish options and original fusion cuisine with a hint of Brazilian flavour. Gourmet diners will be happy to give full rein to the chef on his surprise menu.

Name: Trattoria al Ponte
Address: via Bertolda 27, località Bornio, Lusia, 45020, Italy
Description: Meat and freshwater fish feature on the menu at this restaurant, where the chef creates traditional dishes with an imaginative twist, such as his legendary risotto (made from seasonal ingredients) and breast of guinea fowl with mustard. An oasis surrounded by greenery, situated right by a bridge, and embellished by a small illuminated pool.

Name: Baccanti
Description: Facing Matera’s picturesque cave churches in one of the most charming parts of the old town, this restaurant is housed in a complex of old caves. Despite being inspired by local traditions, the cuisine is modern and creative in style and always of the highest quality.

Name: L'Oste della Bon'Ora
Description: One of the best restaurants in the area, where the friendly, exuberant owner, Massimo, is a real gourmet enthusiast who enjoys helping his guests choose from the reinterpreted Lazian specialities on the menu. Excellent wines and produce, including dishes such as carcotto (veal) with wild herbs, capers and tuna mayonnaise, liver with onions and bay leaves, and creamy tiramisù.

Name: Extra
Description: Situated slightly inland behind Marina di Carrara, Extra (the name refers to the quality of the region’s world-famous marble) is a bright, modern restaurant with a menu inspired by the area’s fish and seafood culinary traditions. The menu is slightly more elaborate and the ambience more elegant in the evening and on Saturday lunchtimes.

Name: L'Anfora
Description: Typical Lipari cuisine created with passion and enthusiasm. The colourful presentation offers a feast for the eyes as well as the taste buds. Generous portions.

Name: Controcorrente
Description: In this minimalist restaurant, situated below the medieval San Giovanni tower in the picturesque pedestrianised historic centre of Noli, the owner-chef serves contemporary cuisine that echoes the dining room’s modern decor. The menu features meat and fish dishes alike, all prepared from almost exclusively Ligurian ingredients, including delicious purple Sanremo prawn tartare with celery mayonnaise, lemon cream and plankton chips, as well as lamb cooked in its own juices with Albenga artichokes.

Name: Al Palazzo
Description: Al Palazzo is the renowned restaurant at the Palazzo Murat hotel which is run by the Attanasio family. Dine alfresco in the restaurant’s beautiful botanical garden with its tiny vegetable patch, apart from on rare days of bad weather, when guests are served indoors in its small, elegant dining rooms. The Mediterranean cuisine includes meat and fish dishes alike, with slightly different menus at lunchtime (simpler options) and in the evening. Le Petit Murat bar is still open, offering an interesting selection of cocktails to supplement its excellent wine list.

Name: Il Galeone
Description: Housed on the ground floor of the Elisabeth Due hotel, this restaurant enjoys a fine reputation in the area around Fano. In recent years, the owner-chef has intensified his efforts to source seasonal fish and other ingredients from the region, which he uses to prepare dishes that showcase a perfect balance of classic and modern influences.

Name: El Filò
Address: strada Dolomites 103, Pozza di Fassa, 38036, Italy
Description: Following recent refurbishment, El Filò is now even more comfortable than ever, boasting an Alpine-influenced decor that is striking for its contemporary style. The Dolomites and Ladin culinary traditions are still very much to the fore in the cuisine, which is prepared by the excellent owner-chef, although modern touches and influences from outside the region also feature. The wine list offers a fine selection of options from the region.

Name: Casa Perrotta Restaurant
Description: This small, welcoming restaurant with a hint of minimalism and just a few tables serves personalised meat and fish dishes which aim to offer something a little different, with a choice of three tasting menus and an à la carte. Having previously gained experience outside the area, the young family team from Campania runs the restaurant with enthusiasm and a real love for the region’s cuisine.

Name: Impronta
Address: via Angarano 7, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
Description: Located right next to the Ponte Vecchio, the symbol of Bassano del Grappa, this restaurant boasts an elegant, almost Alpine decor with soft lighting and a minimalist feel. In summer, our advice is to book one of the few tables on the outdoor terrace with its views of the famous bridge and the River Brenta (book well in advance!). Modern cuisine with a regional influence, as well as the occasional fish and seafood option.

Name: Il Principe
Address: via Colle San Bartolomeo 4, Pompei, 80045, Italy
Description: This restaurant focuses on a skilful and creative reinterpretation of Campanian specialities, serving the type of cuisine that you’d be happy to eat every day. Although the dishes are inspired by the chef’s childhood memories and his grandmother’s cooking, he adds his own contemporary touch and careful presentation. Both meat and fish feature, showcasing all the colour and imagination of the best regional cuisine.

Name: Faletta 1881
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid the wine estates and rolling hills of Monferrato, this historic farmhouse has been carefully restored its enthusiastic owners. The restaurant here serves contemporary dishes inspired by regional and Italian recipes, as well as offering welcoming guestrooms (one or two with their own kitchen), a saltwater swimming pool and the relaxing ambience that comes with this rural setting.

Name: Da Attilio
Description: Situated in one of the liveliest working-class neighbourhoods of Naples, this restaurant serves traditional Neapolitan pizzas, including a few unusual innovations such as pizzas in the shape of an 8-pointed star. In business since 1938 and now run by the third generation of the same family, Da Attilio has just a few tables arranged in two small dining rooms and doesn’t take reservations. Although you may have to wait at the busiest times of day, you’ll find the wait well worthwhile!

Name: Il Cavallo Scosso
Description: A young and modern restaurant situated in a residential area about 2km from the centre, where the owner-chef offers three tasting menus: Territorio e Tradizione, Il Cavallo Scosso and the more creative Fuori Gara.

Name: Da Miro alla Lanterna
Description: It would be difficult for the menu at this restaurant to convey the beauty and quality of the fresh fish on display near the kitchen, where guests can make their own selection. Here, all sorts of shellfish and different fish of all shapes and sizes are transformed into delicious dishes full of flavour. Classic decor, professional service, an excellent wine selection and good value for money all add to the appeal. An address which has been delighting guests ever since 1954!

Name: Il Frantoio
Description: This restaurant has undergone a skilful refurbishment with a focus on colour, light and furnishings which combine harmoniously with the valley below, as well as with the dishes in which extra-virgin olive oil takes a starring role (not just as a condiment but as an ingredient in its own right). The view through the floor-to-ceiling windows, which extends along the valley as far as San Pietro abbey in Assisi, is as enticing as the cuisine.

Name: Salsedine367
Address: via Marradi 11, Lido di Savio, 48125, Italy
Description: Meals are served outdoors at this beach restaurant, which is also a private beach club. Here, the cuisine focuses on imaginative and personalised dishes that stand out for their excellent ingredients, among other things! The “blind” tasting menu is based around the chef’s inspiration, while the varied à la carte offers dishes with generous portions.

Name: All'Angelo
Description: Just outside the town of Quistello, the restaurant is in a nineteenth century villa enclosed by its own garden. The interior decoration and atmosphere have a classic style, while the kitchen draws fully from the local tradition: agnoli in brodo, tortelli di zucca, lonza di maiale con mostarda di mele, sbrisolona... white truffle when in season! Five rooms available if you want to prolong your stay.

Name: Casa Leali
Address: via Valle 1, Puegnago sul Garda, 25080, Italy
Description: Year after year, the young, enthusiastic Leali brothers demonstrate their ability to run a top-quality restaurant: their Casa, elegantly housed in a restored 15C farmhouse, has become a renowned name in the region. In the kitchen, Andrea is precise and attentive in his selection of seasonal produce, preferring to concentrate on just a few ingredients in each dish, which he transforms with technical expertise and imagination. One example is the oysters cooked over the barbecue grill, served with olive pesto and shallots – a truly interesting antipasto, in which the sinuous flavour of the oyster is retained while combining it with other more elegant and subtle bitter tastes. The bread is also delicious. Marco is at the helm front of house, where he also oversees the wine list, demonstrating a real love for champagne and other sparkling wines.

Name: Evo Ristorante
Description: This restaurant at the entrance to the historic centre boasts a delightful garden which leads to a porch where tables are set out in summer – an enchanting setting that feels as though you’re eating in the countryside despite the village location. The chefs’ imagination knows no bounds in complex and elaborate dishes that focus on ingredients from Puglia and are grouped into themed tasting menus.

Name: Deste
Description: Set back slightly from the port, this restaurant boasts stunning views from its terrace which is highly recommended in fine weather. The culinary focus here is on modern dishes with an interesting choice of meat and fish options. Tea and kombucha offer an alternative to wine, while the home-produced gin is definitely worth sampling.

Name: Meta Ristorante
Address: via Generale Pescetto 5, Celle Ligure, 17015, Italy
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Celle, this old boathouse with a typical brick ceiling is now home to an excellent gourmet restaurant, where a young chef creates some of the most interesting dishes in the region.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: This genuinely Roman restaurant which takes its name from the Marchese del Grillo, a film which symbolises the spirit of Rome, is elegant and noble in style yet with a hint of irony. Although the focus is on traditional cuisine, the stylish decor, beautiful furnishings and dishes full of delicious flavours will instantly appeal to visitors from other cultures as well as locals. There are no fixed times for eating and drinking here: you can enjoy the fried meatballs, amatriciana pasta, stuffed chicken or a quick spaghetti with a tomato sauce at any time of day.

Name: Voce Aimo e Nadia
Description: Situated in the heart of Milan, this restaurant owned by the historic Aimo e Nadia in Via Montecuccoli is accessed via its bar-cum-pastry shop which includes a bistro serving a selection of simpler dishes. From here, you enter the main dining room with an open-view kitchen serving excellent Italian dishes reinterpreted in contemporary style. Voce in Giardino, the restaurant’s outdoor summer dining space adorned with interesting sculptures, is a green oasis in the heart of the city.

Name: Villa Pizzini
Description: From Lake Maggiore you climb up Mottarone mountain to an altitude of around 1 400m to reach this 19C hunting lodge, where a young couple of self-taught chefs provide a warm and friendly welcome. The cuisine here speaks for itself – delicious meat dishes, plus a few specialities from the lake which are also served outdoors to a backdrop of stunning views. This couple are passionate about using seasonal ingredients and learning about every different stage in their supply chain. Local game dishes are highly recommended.

Name: Nascostoposto
Description: Easily found despite its name (nascosto posto means “hidden place”), this restaurant lies in the alleyways of Terni’s old town. In its modern, minimalist-style dining room, an enthusiastic couple (she runs the front of house, while he’s in the kitchen) delight their guests with delicious and imaginative cuisine with regional, Italian and unexpectedly exotic influences.

Name: Salvo Cacciatori
Description: This restaurant has come a long way since 1906, when the owner’s ancestors opened a modern inn and wine tavern, evolving into an inviting restaurant with an elegant, contemporary-style decor. The cuisine focuses on traditional fish and seafood recipes reinterpreted with a personalised twist, while the impressive wine list features labels from Liguria and beyond. If you want to eat on the pleasant outdoor terrace overlooking the pedestrianised street it’s best to book ahead.

Name: Franceschetta 58
Description: This lively, welcoming restaurant serves simple and traditional regional cuisine, especially from Emilia Romagna, alongside more creative fare. The “Tradizione in evoluzione” menu features classic favourites such as gramigna pasta with cream and sausage, while the “I love Modena” menu showcases more imaginative recipes, including a sweet cacio e pepe dish as a dessert. The menu also includes tortellini made by the Il Tortellante association founded by Massimo Bottura, a rehabilitation centre where young people and adults on the autistic spectrum learn to make fresh pasta by hand. The wine list has just a few carefully chosen wines, with a whole page dedicated to Lambrusco.

Name: Olona - "Da Venanzio" dal 1922
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A bastion of regional cuisine housed in an attractive group of buildings with a large outdoor summer dining area shaded by a pergola and a charming dining room with a retro feel. Traditional recipes with interesting and personalised twists.

Name: Da Nadia
Description: Occupying new premises in the Relais Mirabella in Clusane d’Iseo, this restaurant now boasts a beautiful panoramic location. Fish specialities take pride of place on the menu here, including an excellent fish soup which is a real favourite with guests!

Name: Nni Lausta
Address: Via Risorgimento 188, Santa Marina Salina, 98050, Italy
Description: Fish plays the starring role here, where the genuine traditional taste of Eolian cuisine is capably interpreted with a bit of fantasy and innovation. Dynamic management.

Name: Il Santo Bevitore
Address: via Santo Spirito 64/66 r, Florence, 50125, Italy
Description: Both the simple, friendly atmosphere and the cuisine served at this restaurant are typical of a Tuscan trattoria. The menu features classic favourites from Tuscany (highlights include pappa al pomodoro and cured hams), which are full of the strong traditional flavours that you would expect to find in Florence and are occasionally reinterpreted in more contemporary dishes. For guests keen to take a culinary souvenir home with them, the Santino delicatessen is just next door.

Name: Regio Patio
Address: via San Francesco d'Assisi 23, Garda, 37016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lakefront, this elegant restaurant boasts an attractive English-style garden, as well as a beautiful outdoor patio and a stylish dining room. Here, talented chef Andrea Costantini has very precise ideas about cuisine, in which he showcases the traditions of Lake Garda and its surrounding region with a creative twist using vegetables from his own kitchen garden and a focus on seasonal ingredients. The two menus (“Tradizione” and “Orto”) can be chosen with either four or eight courses.

Name: Acqua
Description: Situated slightly above the marina, this elegant restaurant has a young chef at the helm who has cemented his reputation via contemporary, occasionally creative dishes which showcase the best local ingredients, including fish and seafood. The fact that the latter come directly from the family’s own fishmongers adds to the appeal.

Name: Osteria il Moro
Description: Boasting an attractive outdoor space on Trapani’s main street, Osteria il Moro focuses on dishes that are deeply rooted in Sicilian tradition yet enhanced by original and creative touches, resulting in cuisine that is full of flavour and personality thanks to owner-chef Nicola Bandi. The menu features plenty of fish dishes as well as meat, including beef fillet in a red sauce with spices and wild herbs, and Trapani-style mullet. The impressive wine list includes a good selection of regional labels.

Name: Hostaria da Franz
Address: salizada Sant'Antonin, sestiere Castello 3499, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Founded in a different venue by an Austrian soldier in the late 19C, this historic Venetian restaurant is now run by owner Maurizio, who oversees the front of house in a courteous yet friendly manner. He introduces guests to its variety of dishes, which aim to please rather than surprise. Fish specialities are to the fore here.

Name: Miseria e Nobiltà
Description: The name of this restaurant occupying a late-18C palazzo with attractive flooring and Murano glass chandeliers alludes to the peasant traditions that influence its cuisine (miseria) and the creative, elegant dishes served here (nobiltà). The menu features excellent home-made pastas, vegetables and meat dishes, including boned rabbit with leeks and Annurca apples and white and black truffles from the Molise in season.

Name: U' Vulesce
Description: First opened over 60 years ago, this restaurant has been built up into a successful business over the years by the Di Donna family, who serve top - quality produce from this fertile region, including meat and fish dishes, cured hams and cheeses, all accompanied by a selection of good wines.

Name: Caffè Meletti
Address: via del Trivio 56 (piazza del Popolo), Ascoli Piceno, 63100, Italy
Description: Housed on the first floor of the historic café where the aniseed liqueur of the same name was created, this restaurant serves simple yet creative, regional and maritime - inspired cuisine. Don’t miss the terrace with views of Piazza del Popolo. Faster options available at lunchtime.

Name: Feva
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Castelfranco Veneto, this restaurant has an intimate, elegant and contemporary-cum-minimalist feel despite its period courtyard setting and original wooden beams in the first-floor dining room. Nicola Dinato’s cuisine is showcased on two tasting menus, namely Anima and Corpo. The former offers a selection of new dishes created by the chef, who is constantly updating his cuisine, while the latter features his historic signature specialities (don’t miss the artichoke, crab, fig and leek dish). A lighter, less expensive menu is also available at lunchtime. The impressive wine list includes many French labels – unsurprisingly, perhaps, as the sommelier (and chef’s wife) is from France!

Name: Collina
Address: via Ca' Paler 5, Almenno San Bartolomeo, 24030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family style trattoria has now been converted into these modern premises that, while jealously upholding their homely origin, offer dishes of contemporary inspiration. One small dining hall has an open fireplace and the other gives a panoramic view.

Name: Residenza del Lago
Description: Boasting a tranquil, homely atmosphere typical of the region and with a name that pays homage to Lake Candia, this restaurant occupies a mid-18C farmhouse that is now located within the town. Its traditional cuisine includes popular dishes such as potato cake with seared shrimp and artichokes, “tajarin vecchio Piemonte” (pasta with a meat sauce), and beef cheeks cooked in Erbaluce di Caluso wine.

Name: Antico Ristorante Pagnanelli
Description: In business since 1882, yet constantly evolving, this restaurant boasts a superb location overlooking the lake. The menu features meat and fish dishes, enhanced by wild herbs. The extensive wine selection is presented on two wine lists. Don’t miss the famous wine cellars built into the rock, plus the small wine museum.

Name: La Sosta
Address: via San Martino della Battaglia 20, Brescia, 25121, Italy
Description: Housed in a 17C palazzo, this charming restaurant is very popular with locals. Alfresco dining in summer (just a few tables, so it is best to book), as well as efficient and attentive service.

Name: Alla Fassa
Address: via Nascimbeni 11, Castelletto di Brenzone, 37010, Italy
Description: Although the beautiful views of the lake (with only a cycle path between the restaurant and the water) and mountains on the opposite shore can be admired from the dining room, in fine weather it’s a race for the outdoor tables just a few metres from the water. The cuisine is as impressive as the setting, with a fine balance of classic and modern dishes featuring fish from the lake (such as the “il lago in un piatto” – the lake in a dish – starter) and the sea. A few guestrooms with views of the lake are also available.

Name: La Locanda di Pietracupa
Address: via Madonna di Pietracupa 31, San Donato in Poggio, 50028, Italy
Description: Housed in a beautiful early-20C residence with a panoramic terrace overlooking the hamlet of San Donato in Poggio, this restaurant comprises a dining room and a winter garden to the rear of the building. Tuscan classics take pride of place on the menu, which features a selection of familiar and popular dishes. Four guestrooms are available for anyone looking to extend their stay.

Name: Le Cicale
Description: The owners of this pleasant restaurant, once owned by their grandparents, have given it a light, modern feel. A married couple welcome guests front of house, while the wife’s brother creates delicious Italian and regional dishes in the kitchen. Delightful outdoor area to the rear surrounded by greenery.

Name: Antica Locanda
Address: piazza della Seta, località San Leucio, Caserta, 81100, Italy
Description: This establishment is practically a trattoria; one can dine in either of two characteristic rooms separated by a brick archway. The cuisine is typical of the Naples area and rice dishes are the specialty.

Name: Pinocchio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This glorious, elegant restaurant is surrounded by a delightful garden where guests can dine à la carte or order copious appetisers in the summer months. The recipes focus on the gastronomic traditions of the Piedmont reinterpreted with a modern flavour, as well as more contemporary dishes with original combinations. Meat and fish dishes (including fish from the lake) always feature, alongside some of the restaurant’s classic house specialities.

Name: Romolo Mare
Description: Situated in a private beach club facing the sea, this restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere with an elegant feel thanks to its professional owners who have worked as restaurateurs for many years. Here, they serve excellent fish and seafood cuisine with a focus on raw dishes, plus a choice of daily fish specials. A selection of interesting local wines completes the picture.

Name: Mistral
Description: Situated at the tip of Bellagio’s promontory where the two branches of the lake meet, this villa occupies a superb panoramic location, with its restaurant housed in a covered veranda boasting delightful views of the opposite shore, its little villages and exclusive residences. The atmosphere here is reminiscent of a grand hotel, with background piano music in the evening and guests from all around the world. The moderately creative cuisine offers a choice of Italian dishes alongside more international options.

Name: Pernambucco
Description: This restaurant boasts a garden setting with a pleasant outdoor dining space, plus a long, narrow interior decorated in decidedly classic style. Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a focus on local fish, including excellent tartare (usually either seabream or tuna, depending on the catch of the day) and shellfish (cooked in salt, baked or grilled). The vegetables are sourced from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: El Gato
Description: Chioggia is famous as one of the more active fishing ports in the region and this restaurant takes full of advantage of the local catch. Situated on the central promenade of this picturesque town, the restaurant serves fish of truly exceptional quality served in traditional recipes from the Adriatic.

Name: Saporium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Saporium is the new fine-dining restaurant at the superb Relais Borgo Santo Pietro, an old property where the internal decor demonstrates a rare elegance, especially in the evening when hundreds of candles provide soft lighting and a romantic ambience in the dining room. In fine weather, meals are served under an elegant 13C portico overlooking the garden, with the property’s 100ha grounds and the Valle Serena as a backdrop.
