Much of the produce used in the cuisine designed by executive chef Hagen and transformed by resident chef Luca Ottogalli into modern, delicate dishes comes from the hotel’s own olive groves, vineyards, orchards and vegetable gardens. The focus here is on seasonal ingredients from this extraordinary region, such as the Borgo’s walnuts which are used in some of the delicious desserts. A whole host of wine-pairing options are possible thanks to the 1 000 different labels on the wine list.

Name: Rifugio Col Alt
Address: strada Col Alt, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: During the day this restaurant can be reached in just a few minutes by cable car, providing you with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, while in the evening (when the service is more attentive – things are faster paced at lunchtime) you have to arrange transport via snowcat. The name “refuge” refers only to the location as the cuisine is definitely that of a restaurant: although the menu features hearty mountain fare, it also includes modern options and a few fish-based recipes, including oysters. Last but not least, there’s a good selection of wines.

Name: Castello Malvezzi
Address: via Colle San Giuseppe 1, Brescia, 25133, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This elegant 16C hunting lodge offers a modern menu of fish dishes and regional specialities. Particular attention is paid to the excellent Calvisano caviar, with a dedicated menu. There’s an attractive outdoor dining area facing the gardens with views of the city of Brescia.

Name: Baretto di San Vigilio
Address: via al Castello 1, San Vigilio, Bergamo, 24129, Italy
Description: Situated in the small square in front of the cable-car entrance, this typical bar-cum-restaurant with a retro, vaguely English feel serves generous traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist, including home-made bread and desserts. In summer, meals are served on the terrace with enchanting views of the town, while the two winter dining rooms have a rustic yet elegant feel.

Name: Tenuta Casa Virginia
Address: via Cascina Violo 1, Villa d'Almè, 24018, Italy
Description: Surrounded by the property’s own vineyards, this restaurant nestlings at the bottom of a gentle hill features an elegant dining room and a beautiful terrace for outdoor dining in fine weather. The cuisine is contemporary (yet not excessively so), with a few freshwater fish also featuring on the menu, while the wine list showcases a good selection of wines. The property’s own wines are available for purchase in the shop.

Name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
Description: Situated in a hidden corner of the historic centre, this small bistro-style restaurant has a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with photos alternating with books, wine bottles and glasses on the walls (the wine list includes a few labels from elsewhere in Europe). Small tables set close together, warm, subtle lighting and an almost Parisian ambience make this a perfect choice for a romantic dinner or a meal with friends. There’s also a small outdoor space for fine weather but seats are limited, so it’s best to book ahead!

Name: Fiamma Cremisi
Address: via De Gasperi 37, località Viadana, Calvisano, 25012, Italy
Description: This country restaurant serves regional cuisine with an innovative twist. Dine either in the main dining room warmed by an open fireplace or outdoors under a gazebo in summer. Lunchtime options are restricted to a business menu or a shorter and more reasonably priced menu.

Name: Le Chiavi d'Oro
Description: Situated in Arezzo’s historic centre, this restaurant boasts an original, minimalist ambience with an elegant wood decor. The main focus here is on the cuisine, which is among the best not only in the city but also in the region. Skilful interpretations of traditional dishes, with a focus on Tuscany, where the gastronomic pleasure increases with each course.

Name: Lio Pellegrini
Description: Despite its location in the town centre, the attractive outdoor terrace of this restaurant offers a peaceful atmosphere with its decor of light drapes. The red - coloured dining room makes a pleasant backdrop for the modern, Mediterranean cuisine served here. Elegant ambience.

Name: Laurin
Description: In the magnificent setting of the exclusive Parkhotel Laurin, this restaurant is one of the best in Bolzano, boasting a Liberty-style dining room and tree-shaded tables in the garden for summer dining. The traditional cuisine also includes a few modern touches with ingredients and techniques from all over Italy and beyond, such as the grilled trout and leek terrine wrapped in nori algae in the shape of a flower. The menu features meat and fish dishes, with a small section dedicated to traditional local specialities.

Name: Ca' 7
Address: via Cunizza da Romano 4, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The highlight of this luxurious 18C villa, which also comprises a hotel and banqueting facilities, is its renowned restaurant. Served in a setting of columns and period features which provide a striking contrast to the contemporary paintings and lighting, the cuisine focuses on simple, modern fish and seafood dishes.

Name: Zafferano
Address: viale Vanni 1, Città della Pieve, 06062, Italy
Description: Famous for its saffron, Città della Pieve is also well worth a visit to admire the Baciadonne alley (“one of the narrowest streets in Italy”) in its beautiful historic centre. This welcoming restaurant in a quiet and elegant hotel boasts an attractive veranda for summer dining that provides the perfect backdrop for delicious cuisine that is influenced by Umbria and Tuscany alike.

Name: Particolare di Siena
Description: A fine-dining restaurant which changed tack in 2020, reducing its number of tables to just ten and embracing a sustainable approach to its cuisine. It now prioritises local suppliers and certified organic and environmentally friendly ingredients, while the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, featuring produce grown in line with biodynamic techniques, provides some of the best seasonal ingredients used in the dishes here.

Name: Locanda Solagna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Although this restaurant has been in business since the 1950s, it feels much more modern thanks to its updated appearance. Renowned for its excellent regional cuisine served in the evening, the restaurant pays careful attention to seasonal ingredients. At lunchtime, the ”osteria”-style menu is much simpler. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Duomo
Description: This small restaurant with a bright and welcoming dining room stands out for its contemporary-style cuisine (based around seasonal ingredients) and many home-cooked dishes. The two brothers at the helm create interesting, often regionally inspired recipes with clever personalised twists. On the autumn menu, we particularly recommend the venison with cauliflower, almonds and Barbera wine sauce. Those with a sweet tooth will enjoy the panna cotta with a persimmon coulis (delicious but not too sweet!), while wine-enthusiasts will find plenty to interest them on the extensive wine list. The restaurant also boasts a superb location, nestled in the narrow streets of the centre just a stone’s throw from the Duomo.

Name: Evan's
Description: This restaurant is run with great enthusiasm by the Evangelista family (hence the abbreviation Evan’s). It specialises in delicious fish and seafood prepared mainly in a classic style, although local dishes also feature on the menu.

Name: Scola
Description: Instead of the simple, rustic-style dishes you might expect at this restaurant, the cuisine is actually elaborate and of the highest quality – an excellent reason for venturing out here!

Name: Cravero - Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Warm colours such as teal and ochre give this restaurant a cosy and welcoming ambience. The cuisine here is authentic and traditional in style, with dishes based on top-quality local ingredients accompanied by a choice of regional wines. There’s also an outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Malenco
Address: via Funivia 22, Chiesa in Valmalenco, 23023, Italy
Description: Modern furnishings in the dining room, with panoramic windows looking out over the valley, typical local menu: traditional dishes at reasonable prices.

Name: Baita Piè Tofana
Description: On the slopes of the Tofana and directly overlooking the ski slopes, a characteristic and romantic mountain lodge with a contemporary touch, whose design manages to combine tradition and modernity, is also a source of inspiration for the cuisine. Dishes with a contemporary taste–Rossini al mare (beef, foie gras, cuttlefish and Teriyaki sauce) is excellent–made with considerable use of charcoal grilling, in both summer and winter, and ample use of local raw materials. With friends, experience the convivial Larin table, with a central built-in fireplace around which the seats are arranged. The wine list is worthy of note with a large choice of Champagnes and Italian bubbly.

Name: San Quintino Resort
Description: Once you have crossed the plain and climbed up into the San Quintino hills, you come to this restored farmhouse surrounded by an attractive garden. The restaurant is divided into a brick - walled dining room and a winter garden, while the charming guestrooms make this a romantic place to stay. Creative dishes with a focus on local ingredients and a few fish specialities feature on the menu.

Name: Antica Cucina 1983
Description: An excellent establishment in the town centre, with a dining room that is an old oil - mill. Traditional Puglia dishes tastefully personalised; the service is fast and attentive.

Name: Castel Toblino
Address: località Castel Toblino 1, Castel Toblino, 38076, Italy
Description: Situated in a bucolic location in the Trentino where the excellent Vino Santo is produced (we recommend rounding off your meal with a glass of the equally superb grappa), this restaurant and adjacent bar occupy a fascinating medieval castle (tours of which can be arranged) jutting out into the lake of the same name. The generous, modern meat and fish dishes are featured on various tasting menus, along with an extensive à la carte. In summer, make sure you book a table on the charming terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: Osteria Casale Ferrovia
Address: via Stazione 1, sulla SP 34, Carovigno, 72012, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in what was once the 20C dwelling of an old olive mill, this restaurant boasts elegant decor, including a few antique family pieces and Art Deco - style tables. The female owner - chef prepares light and modern dishes with a regional flavour, while the wine list also showcases the best of Puglia. As the name suggests, the railway lies to the rear of the property, although there’s very little noise and no disturbance at all.

Name: Luigi Pomata
Description: This famous classic restaurant in Cagliari serves top-quality cuisine in its modern dining rooms and on an outdoor terrace. The menu features interesting reinterpretations of Sardinian dishes among other options, including their own tuna (the house speciality), which is also available in tins to take away.

Name: Al Camin
Description: On the road to Misurina lake, this friendly restaurant with a modern Alpine style offers dishes of the regional tradition with imaginative touches and modern technique. So a great deal of practicality, then, as in the beef tenderloin wrapped in speck dry-cured pork with cep mushrooms and Ampezzo-style potatoes. The chef and sommelier Fabio Pompanin manages a wine list with approximately 200 labels. In the warmer season, take advantage of the open-air service.

Name: 12 Ristorante
Description: An original ambience with real character, as well as top quality fish and seafood. There is also a charming outdoor area overlooking the canal where old boats from the Museo della Marineria are moored.

Name: Ginevra
Address: Rupi di via XXIX Settembre 12, Ancona, 60122, Italy
Description: Situated on the fourth floor of the Seeport hotel, this restaurant boasts a summer roof garden offering stunning sea views. The chef, a native of Ancona who trained with Gualtiero Marchesi, serves traditional local dishes prepared using ingredients from the region, as well as remaining open to the rest of the world (just like his town and its port). Lighter fare is available at the Seeport Bistrò.

Name: Da Tonino
Description: Allow a good half-hour to get to this small restaurant with a simple ambience and an airy terrace which is perfect in the heat of summer. The cuisine has its roots in local traditions – its first courses are particularly good. There’s also an excellent wine selection.

Name: Trattoria di Campagna
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Modern Cuisine
Description: This famous trattoria, now run by the third generation of the same family, serves traditional, seasonal cuisine from the Aosta valley, enhanced by the occasional imaginative and personalised touch. The new well-stocked wine cellar includes a table for a dozen guests, while sommelier Beatrice is on hand to assist guests with their choice of bottle. Excellent array of delicacies from the dessert trolley.

Name: Vite
Address: via Montepirolo 7, località San Patrignano, Coriano, 47853, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the San Patrignano community, which grows its own crops, raises its own livestock and makes its own cheeses, Vite is now the setting for new, talented chef Giuseppe Biuso’s cuisine, which is made from top-quality ingredients using modern, creative techniques. His Mediterranean dishes are also inspired by his native Sicily, and include several vegetarian specialities. In summer, don’t miss the outdoor dining space which offers fine views of the surrounding countryside.

Name: Armando al Pantheon
Description: This small restaurant just a few metres from the Pantheon has been run by the Gargioli family since 1961, with the third generation now at the helm. Popular with locals and visitors alike for its traditional cuisine, which includes Roman and Lazian dishes, meat and fish options, and specialities such as offal, veal intestines, spring lamb, fresh anchovies, and sour-cherry tart.

Name: Da Poli alla Stazione
Address: viale della Repubblica 10, Castelnovo di Sotto, 42024, Italy
Description: Once you have passed a promising display of products, sit down in one of the two light and airy elegant dining rooms or on the pleasant summer terrace; cuisine from land and sea.

Name: Osteria Il Granaio
Address: via dei Monaci, Rapolano Terme, 53040, Italy
Description: Although it calls itself an osteria, Il Granaio is really a restaurant. It has elegant brick - arched dining rooms occupying a 17C palazzo in the historic centre of Rapolano. On the menu you will find Tuscan specialities such as pici pasta cooked with various sauces, peppery Tuscan beef stew and a selection of fish dishes.

Name: Livello 1
Address: via Duccio di Buoninsegna 25, Rome, 00142, Italy
Description: Situated in the suburbs off the main tourist trail, this fish restaurant also has a fishmonger’s next door. The fish and seafood cuisine served here is highly interesting, featuring modern recipes made from top-quality ingredients. There’s also a small lounge in which to enjoy a cocktail, plus a selection of good wines. The open-view kitchen allows guests to observe the skilful chef at work.

Name: Nido del Picchio
Description: This restaurant with a low-key, hushed atmosphere has the feel of a tastefully furnished private home, with an open fire lit in winter and a cool, welcoming outdoor dining space for the warmer months. The restaurant has built up a well-deserved reputation for its fish dishes, although the menu here is equally divided between fish and meat. Options such as anolini in brodo (filled pasta in broth) pay tribute to the region’s traditions, while most of the dishes served here are highly creative. Originally English, the owner’s wife runs the front of house with skill and a warm, friendly manner. The wine cellar is home to more than 700 of the best Italian and international wines, with a curious emphasis on labels from cooler climes.

Name: I Pifferi
Description: This restaurant occupying an old post house that dates back to the time of Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma, lies amid the verdant landscapes of the Parco Regionale dei Boschi di Carrega, just a kilometre outside the village of Sala Baganza. This stunning setting is the backdrop for typical dishes from Parma, such as Nonna Lina’s herb tortelli served with melted butter and parmesan cheese. In summer, dine alfresco in the cool, shady garden.

Name: Molin Vecio
Description: In a 16C working mill, rooms full of atmosphere (one with a fireplace) and service in summer on the lakeside; typical Vicenza cuisine with vegetarian dishes.

Name: Lamberti
Description: This restaurant is situated just a stone’s throw from the sea in a building dating from the 1930s. It serves traditional, regional dishes made from carefully selected ingredients. Don’t miss the fish and the pesto sauce.

Name: Posta
Description: A corner of Tuscany in Bologna, where famous soups such as ribollita and pappa col pomodoro are followed by pappardelle pasta with wild boar, tripe, beef pepper stew and, of course, Fiorentina steak, although there’s also room on the menu for local specialities such as tagliatelle and tortellini. Many of the wines served also come from Tuscany.

Name: I 5 Campanili
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Contemporary cooking with an emphasis on Mediterranean fare in tune with the seasons is to the fore in this elegant restaurant occupying a 20C building with an attractive veranda to the rear. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on raw dishes and shellfish, but the splendid desserts are also worthy of note, such as cherries in sour cherry juice with fior di latte ice cream.

Name: Osteria da Nando
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Traditional Cuisine
Description: Opened in 1957, this osteria in the heart of the historic centre is one of the town’s leading restaurants for anyone wanting to sample the cuisine of the Aosta valley. Delicious regional specialities such as cured meats, polenta and fondue are prepared with the best ingredients and served in a simple dining room with plenty of character. Wide choice of excellent wines by the glass.

Name: Sotto l'Arco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Villa Aretusi is a pleasant 17C villa surrounded by its own garden on the outskirts of Bologna. At the hotel’s gourmet restaurant, Sotto l’Arco, on the first floor (lift available), the skilful chef creates modern, interesting Italian dishes, while at the Trattoria on the ground floor the focus is more on traditional Emilian cuisine.

Name: Il Credenziere
Address: via Quattro Strade 12, Annone Veneto, 30020, Italy
Description: Situated in a small country hamlet, this restaurant is run by a chef from Puglia, whose origins can be glimpsed here and there in his dishes. The influence of the Veneto, where the chef has been working for some time, is also evident in the local dishes which appear alongside more creative options on the menu.

Name: Il Tesoro Living Resort
Address: via Settefrati 96, Rivalta sul Mincio, 46040, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There actually is a “treasure” and it is precisely the location, definitely a contemporary structure yet enclosed in a rustic setting, enclosed by a broad green area (moreover they also have a wellness center and fine suites). The cuisine is of Mediterranean inspiration, half of the menu is dedicated to fish, while among the meat dishes there are also some references to the local territory.

Name: Sa Cardiga e Su Schironi
Address: strada statale 195 rotonda per Capoterra, Capoterra, 09012, Italy
Description: Since 1967, this small restaurant has been delighting locals and visitors alike with its vast array of fish and seafood dishes, including grilled and skewered specialities. The fresh fish display cabinet at the restaurant entrance is one of the highlights here, as is the extensive selection of antipasti which includes tuna and mullet bottarga, “agliata alla bosana” (blue shark with tomatoes in a light sweet and sour sauce) and “burrida alla cagliaritana” (with dogfish). Other dishes include fresh and pasta with various seafood sauces, fried fish, soup, lobster, barbecued fish and even eel.

Name: Baita Fraina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Warm little bar rooms, reminiscent of the German wine bars or "Stube", a summer terrace and well - prepared regional dishes: for those who want to escape the mundane life of Cortina for the silence of an isolated "baita" [mountain hut]. Delightful rooms, colourfully furnished in warm tones so you can better enjoy the silence and scents of the mountains.

Name: Quintilio
Description: For over a century, and from generation to generation, Quintilio has acted as a junction between two beautiful regions, Liguria and Piedmont – and not just in a geographical sense. These regions take pride of place on the wine list (overseen by the friendly and talented owner Lorena) as well as on the menu, which is created daily with dishes made from top-quality local ingredients full of flavour. Regional specialities such as plin, Ligurian-style rabbit tortelli, risottos, vitello tonnato (veal) and brain are all skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist by owner-chef Luca Bazzano.

Name: Regallo
Description: Situated slightly on the outskirts, this contemporary-style restaurant occupies the unusual setting of an old factory. Here, picture windows in the dining room overlook the stream below, with the sound of the water adding an almost musical note to the ambience. In the open-view kitchen, skilful chef Claudio Ravinetto prepares dishes with an exclusive focus on fish, including delicious house specialities such as scallops with anchovy cream, tomatoes and basil, and the “Sicilia” dessert which pays tribute to the island with its ricotta cream topped with chocolate shavings, orange jelly and dried capers.

Name: Marsupino 1901
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Marsupino family has been running this trattoria enthusiastically and warmly since 1901. The chef's suggestion pays homage to the territory in accordance with tradition and the wine cellar, managed by the friendly expert Luca, is immense, with an excellent choice by the glass. Five rooms and two suites in the adjacent late nineteenth-century palazzo.

Name: Il Tartufo
Description: Housed in a small villa in the residential area of the village, this intimate and secluded restaurant serves delicious cuisine with distinctly regional roots. In season, locally sourced truffles take centre stage, while fish and seafood dominate the menu at other times of year.

Name: Agorà
Description: Michele Rizzo is the owner-chef of this interesting restaurant situated in a modern part of Rende. His menu focuses mainly on fish (although a few meat dishes are also available) which he prepares in light, modern dishes with an emphasis on local ingredients. There’s also an interesting wine list.

Name: Dispensa Franciacorta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An informal restaurant with bottles of wine from the enoteca on the walls adding a charming touch. The menu features delicious traditional dishes made from top-quality Franciacorta ingredients, including vegetables grown in a large organic garden supported by the restaurant. Many of the ingredients used by the chef (pasta, cheese, ham and salami etc) are served as snacks at the lively bar throughout the day.

Name: Dama Restaurant
Description: The cuisine served at this restaurant comes from a deep knowledge of the region, is inspired by tradition and yet constantly evolving. At Dama , guests will find creative cuisine with an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Housed within Ca’ Bonfadini, the restaurant boasts an outstanding location overlooking Cannaregio canal, while the attractive dining room has just three elegant wooden tables that encourage sharing and can accommodate up to 10 guests.

Name: aede dining & wines
Description: A small gem of a restaurant with a contemporary minimalist-style decor. The highly creative and technically modern cuisine has the same Nordic style as the dining room, influenced by the chef’s experience working in a number of Michelin-starred restaurants in Scandinavia. The menu changes every month and consists of twelve different dishes, with a minimum of four in the evening. Organic wines and a small outdoor dining space complete the picture.

Name: A' Paranza
Description: For more than 30 years, this restaurant run by the Proto brothers has been a popular choice for visitors to the beautiful Atrani valley. Simple cuisine served in a simple and informal setting (dishes are nearly always announced at your table rather than listed on a menu), with a focus on Mediterranean and Campanian dishes.

Name: Poldo e Gianna Osteria
Description: This cheerful and attractive contemporary restaurant near the Parliament building serves traditional Roman cuisine made from interesting seasonal ingredients. There’s a pleasant outdoor space (book well in advance), plus an unexpected wine cellar which is extremely well stocked and includes some top-quality wines.

Name: Vitis
Description: A modern wine bar in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen), situated in the same building as the delightful family restaurant, the Oste Scuro. Here, small armchairs, benches and stools are dotted among low square tables and higher tables, all surrounded by walls completely lined with wine bottles. The contemporary cuisine features tempting, generous dishes such as cod with cauliflower, cavolo nero and beurre blanc. Accommodation is available just two minutes’ away in the historic Adler Historic Guesthouse run by the same owners.

Name: Il Riccio
Description: Situated just a few metres from the Blue Grotto and perched right above the water, Il Riccio is the quintessential Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant thanks to its tasteful and elegant decor. Undoubtedly one of Capri’s iconic addresses, it focuses uniquely on fish and seafood dishes. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, a visit to the tempting dessert buffet to admire its array of delicacies is a must!

Name: Rosso di Sera
Address: via Pietro Nenni 2, Castelletto sopra Ticino, 28053, Italy
Description: Situated closed to the motorway exit, this restaurant’s rustic exterior belies its young, colourful and contemporary interior. The dishes are as modern as the decor, yet they have their roots in strong local traditions. The owner has a real passion for French and sparkling wines, including around 160 different champagnes and a wide selection of Burgundies, plus a good choice of wines by the glass, craft beers and cocktails.

Name: Elephant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the famous Elephant hotel (with which it shares a name), this restaurant has a unique, historic ambience thanks to its decor of antique wood panelling. The cuisine here is regional with a modern twist, featuring dishes such as char with cream of celery and green apple on a bed of fragrant elderflowers. The interesting wine list boasts a selection of almost a thousand different labels.

Name: Burjè 1968
Address: str. Burje 11, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Ambitious Italian cuisine including some dishes inspired by French traditions, all creatively prepared with the occasional use of more exotic ingredients. If you’re having problems choosing from the à la carte, why not opt for the 5- or 7- course tasting menu?

Name: Casa Federici
Description: The area around Montoro, famous for its cipolla ramata (copper onion), is now also home to a gourmet restaurant thanks to young chef Francesco Cerrato, whose cuisine is inspired by locally sourced ingredients from this inland region as well as fish and seafood from the coast. The menu also features creative, carefully prepared dishes served by the attentive young staff. Minimalist-style ambience.

Name: Erbaluigia
Description: This attractive restaurant with a simple, minimalist decor stands almost opposite the thousand-year-old church of San Frediano. The inviting menu here focuses on regional dishes with a successful combination of traditional and modern styles, including a section dedicated to barbecue options. Meat takes pride of place, although offal, cheese and a few vegetarian options also feature.

Name: Il Colmetto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A genuinely gourmet agriturismo offering a menu that changes almost weekly in line with the seasons. The superb ingredients (many home-grown and others sourced locally) are cooked with precision, avoiding unnecessary technical frills and preferring instead to focus on a practical, traditional approach that aims to satisfy and delight the tastebuds. Barbecued dishes, such as the sweetbreads and the excellent Jerusalem artichoke, are truly superb, while the light and fluffy goats’ milk butter served with bread and focaccia is also delicious, but a word of warning – you may find yourself addicted to this soft and delicious delicacy!

Name: Trattoria la Rosa 1908
Address: via del Bosco 2, ang. via Facchini, Sant'Agostino, 44047, Italy
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Ferrara, this reliable, classic-style restaurant now run by the fifth generation of the same family serves carefully prepared cuisine based around local ingredients. Highlights include truffles, sometimes served with fettuccine, butter and parmesan cheese, and the “sformato dell’Artusi” (a type of flan), served with a classic and intensely flavoured velouté.

Name: Trattoria Rigoletto
Description: A simple environment, manages to create an interesting cuisine. The menu is quite extensive, the dishes are authentic and the atmosphere is welcoming.

Name: Scuderie Sabaude
Address: via Amedeo di Savoia 5, Pollenzo, 12042, Italy
Description: This restaurant just a stone’s throw from the Università del Gusto di Pollenzo is accessed via an old courtyard with a beautifully tended garden. Housed in the rustic setting of the former royal stables, the restaurant serves a delicious Piedmontese cuisine, light and impeccably presented. The “Tistot”, a delicious panna cotta, is a must!

Name: Miil
Description: Housed in a converted 15C mill on the Kränzelhof wine estate, this smart, elegant restaurant provides the backdrop for excellent, contemporary-style cuisine prepared wherever possible using locally sourced (and always top-quality) ingredients.

Name: Sostansa
Description: The philosophy of this restaurant of the town centre, situated just outside the traffic-restricted zone, talks about “stories from the kitchen” and “urban” dishes: in other words, it chooses the best market ingredients with an emphasis on (but not exclusive use of) seasonal produce, from which generous, delicious and attractive dishes are created. At lunchtime, there’s a choice of à la carte dishes or a business lunch announced at your table; in the evening, two surprise tasting menus are also available.

Name: Locanda Alpina
Description: Situated in the enchanting Val di Non with its castles and apple orchards, this restaurant housed in a 19C building has been run by the same family since 1933. It serves excellent cuisine that makes good use of regional produce alongside occasional ingredients from further afield, such as the delicious pistachio ice cream.

Name: Enoteca di Canelli - Casa Crippa
Description: Occupying a late-19C palazzo, in what was a historic wine cellar right up to the late 1960s, this well-run family restaurant serves regional cuisine with a contemporary twist. The basement dining room is accessible by stairs only.

Name: Il Giurista
Description: This restaurant is named after Bartolo da Sassoferrato (as is the street on which it stands), a distinguished 14C jurist. From the street, you head down a few steps to the welcoming dining rooms with their historic ambience and brick-vaulted ceilings that keep the temperature pleasantly cool. The cuisine, which focuses exclusively on meat, is traditional and regional in flavour – an entire section of the menu is dedicated to black truffles in season. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Stube Gourmet
Description: Situated in a pedestrianised area in the centre of Asiago, this small restaurant on the first floor of the Hotel Europa has just five tables and is certain to attract food-lovers thanks to its exquisite cuisine. Now with a new chef at the helm, Stube Gourmet continues to delight guests who are lucky enough to dine here. Classic traditional cuisine based on carefully selected local ingredients with a keen eye for what’s in season provides the foundation for this chef’s dishes. There’s also an excellent wine list that continues to expand, plus a wine shop on the street outside.

Name: Degusteria Italiana
Description: This small, welcoming restaurant in the heart of the city, not far from the Uffizi Gallery, specialises in three typical Italian ingredients, namely cheese, truffles and game, from which it creates intriguing and delicious dishes.

Name: Locanda San Martino
Address: via Don Ermolao Barattin 23, Chies d'Alpago, 32010, Italy
Description: Founded in 1952, this inn has been run by the same family – and especially its female members – ever since. It now boasts the presence of a chef whose many years of experience are evident in his dishes. Much of the meat (especially lamb) is raised in the restaurant’s own farm nearby, while the dishes on the menu are seasonal and classic in style yet with a hint of modern flavour. When the weather allows, make the most of the large terrace boasting fine views of the sunset over the surrounding Alpago region.

Name: Terrazza Gallia
Description: Situated on the seventh floor with panoramic views of the city, this restaurant is an excellent choice for a light lunch, a cocktail or an informal dinner. Two young brothers from Naples are at the helm here, creating traditional Italian and Lombardian dishes with a creative and contemporary touch.

Name: I Rodella
Address: strada esterna vicinale della Rocca 2, Deruta, 06053, Italy
Description: This complex, which also includes two junior suites and seven guestrooms, dates back to the early 17C and was commissioned by the Church as a stopping off point for travellers on their way to Rome. For many years now, the restaurant has been run by a Venetian family with twin brothers (both highly experienced) working in the kitchen and a third brother, a sommelier, at the helm in the dining room. The cuisine is inspired by local and Venetian traditions, with a modern approach to the combinations of flavours (including home-grown herbs) and to the presentation of its delicious, generous dishes. We recommend that you do as we did and follow Samuele’s advice when making your choice from the dishes prepared by Stefano and Andrea with great skill and passion.

Name: Felter alle Rose
Address: via Gasparo Da Salò 33, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description: This historic trattoria has been brought back to life by a local family with years of experience in the hospitality industry and a real commitment to quality. Convenient private parking, an indoor dining room, a closed veranda and a few tables set out in the wine cellar for tastings and aperitifs are just some of the attractions here. The short menu features simple yet carefully made dishes prepared from seasonal ingredients.

Name: Locanda Baggio
Address: via Bassane 1, località Casonetto, Asolo, 31011, Italy
Description: Standing in a quiet location behind Asolo, this restaurant with an attractive summer garden serves authentic cuisine with an emphasis on top quality ingredients. Wine lovers will appreciate the good selection of international wines on offer here.

Name: Osteria L'Abbiccì
Address: via Medici da Seregno 29, Seregno, 20831, Italy
Description: Situated in the centre of Seregno, this modern inn boasts a bright, spacious dining room with an ambience which is both friendly and yet respectful of guests’ privacy. The cuisine is overseen by Davide, who trained with Mauro Elli, the owner-chef of Il Cantuccio in Albavilla. Here, he creates dishes full of character, with a focus on top-quality ingredients and skilful presentation techniques. For a memorable dining experience, the chef’s surprise menu makes an excellent choice. Impressive wine selection and professional service overseen by Gabriele add to the appeal. The business lunch offers excellent value for money.

Name: Osteria Bertaina
Description: Overlooking the picturesque square in the town’s oldest medieval district and accessed through its arcaded portico, this restaurant boasts two dining rooms with an attractive nostalgic feel and ceilings decorated with early 20C frescoes. The excellent cuisine focuses on local dishes, accompanied by occasionally more creative options.

Name: Locanda Lo Scopiccio
Description: Run by the owner-chef and her husband, Locanda Lo Scopiccio is a charming restaurant where careful attention is paid to every detail so that guests feel totally pampered. The cuisine is regional with the occasional hint of creativity, with a choice of two surprise menus or à la carte dining. There’s also a winter garden with a bright yet romantic feel.

Name: Materia | Spazio Cucina
Description: The entrance to this restaurant is typical of an old residential-style building, giving the impression that you are stepping into the chef’s own home. Here, the beautiful dining room boasts shared tables and an entire wall covered with shelves of jars containing dried fruit, pumpkin seeds and red lentils. The classic-style cuisine focuses on grilled dishes and modern cooking methods to create typical Sicilian meat and fish dishes that pay careful attention to the seasons. The first courses are excellent, including the spaghetti with butter and anchovies, which is served with Favignana tuna bottarga and muddica atturrata(spiced breadcrumbs) made from Perciasacchi flour.

Name: Vescovo Moro
Description: Situated 50 metres from the basilica of San Zeno (the patron saint of Verona), this restaurant housed in a renovated workshop boasts plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. Here, enjoy eclectic cuisine with an equal balance of Mediterranean and traditional flavours, including an excellent array of raw fish dishes and a small selection of Italian caviar.

Name: AB Osteria Contemporanea
Description: A small village just a few kilometres from Udine provides the backdrop for modern, regionally influenced cuisine with plenty of character. The renovated dining rooms have two distinct styles: the one near the entrance is friendly and relaxed; the other has a much more formal ambience. The large outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: Exé Restaurant
Address: via Circondariale San Francesco 2, Fiorano Modenese, 41042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This pleasant, elegant and contemporary-style restaurant on the ground floor of the Executive Spa Hotel boasts spacious dining rooms and an extensive menu ranging from traditional dishes to raw fish options, grilled meats (aged by the restaurant itself) and gourmet pizzas. The wine list features an impressive selection of labels, including by the glass, while the talented sommelier will delight wine-enthusiasts with his willingness to open almost any of the bottles in his cellar.

Name: Blum
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Although there is an extensive à la carte at this restaurant, it is on the tasting menus that the chef showcases his creative cuisine to the full. His Suggestioni menu features dishes such as scampi carpaccio with green apple and caviar, while the vegetarian Naturalmente option includes a robustly structured black garlic and almond noodle dish full of decisive flavours, which is well worth trying. The romantic, modern platform where tables are set out is practically on the beach, which means that the restaurant is closed in bad weather.

Name: Ruris Waves
Description: A twin of the similarly named Ruris di Isola in Capo Rizzuto, Ruris Waves opened in summer 2023, setting up home in the small Palazzo Foti hotel on Crotone’s seafront where guests dine either on the small outdoor terrace with its sea views or in the classic-style dining room. The owner-chef takes his culinary inspiration from the sea, creating classic dishes alongside more imaginative options such as octopus parmigiana.

Name: La Chandelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Decorated in the same classic, elegant style as the famous Hermitage hotel in which it is located, this spacious restaurant offers an impressive menu of modern yet unfussy dishes alongside a selection of more traditional options. Grilled meats are cooked over the imposing charcoal grill in the evenings, while the fine views of the surrounding mountains and an excellent wine list add to the enjoyment of your dining experience.

Name: Casa Rapisarda
Description: This small welcoming restaurant on the famous Scalinata della Costarella in Numana, with a tiny terrace for summer dining and just a few tables, serves delicious cuisine with an imaginative twist. Originally from Sicily, the highly talented owner-chef has spent much of his life in the Marche and has plenty of experience in leading restaurants. Given the limited capacity here, booking is essential, especially in summer.

Name: La Locanda dei Beccaria
Description: Housed in the village’s historic wine cellar, this well - kept, rustic - style restaurant with typical wooden ceilings serves traditional, regional cuisine.

Name: Tano Passami l'Olio
Description: Tano Simonato, chef-patron of this stylish modern restaurant located in a fine residential district, offers his creative cuisine that reinterprets Italian flavors in a modern key: food for him is not just nourishment, but also fun. He will then come to your table to advise you and tell you about his dishes, suggesting the best wine pairing, also thanks to a well-stocked cellar. The inspector recommends: Tiramisù of cuttlefish and potatoes, as well as Almond Cannoli stuffed with mousse of ricotta with almonds, candied lemon and chocolate drops, with citrus fruit cream and almond jam.

Name: L'Ostì
Address: strada Sassongher 2, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: A minimalist-style restaurant featuring a wood decor, an extensive display of bottles, and some windows boasting partial yet splendid views of the Dolomites. The chef here prepares creative cuisine using local ingredients alongside produce sourced from other regions. The wine list includes a wide selection of natural wines.

Name: Osteria alla Chiesa
Description: A young couple has brought life back to this old country inn, retaining its rustic ambience while introducing a menu which focuses on creativity and innovation. Claudio creates a host of meat, fish and vegetable dishes with imagination and originality, while one of the highlights remains the menu dedicated to donkey meat.

Name: Balìce
Description: The chef patron Giacomo Caravello in the short span of a few years has created his “space” in the area, definitely becoming one of the best places in Milazzo: the contemporary interiors are truly refined and airy, while the cuisine–which grows year after year–is assured thanks to modern techniques and Sicilian and Mediterranean references. The wine selection is accompanied by an intriguing range of cocktails.

Name: Ensama Pesce
Address: via Aristide Dondarini 4, Sala Bolognese, 40010, Italy
Description: A menu which focuses only on fish (from the daily market) which is prepared with a hint of Puglia, the chef’s native region. As soon as guests are seated at their table, they are brought a selection of homemade breads, including taralli bread rings and focaccia. Owner-chef Sabino is the heart and soul of this restaurant, where guests can be sure of a memorable culinary experience!

Name: Cracco Portofino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Famous chef Carlo Cracco has opened a restaurant in what was once Il Pitosforo, right opposite the small harbour in Portofino, so that his lucky guests enjoy fine views of the water, the small square and the enchanting bay. Here, skilful and competent executive chef Mattia Pecis serves lightly modern cuisine with occasional references to Ligurian recipes (such as cappon magro salad) and ingredients (many of the vegetables are sourced from Iva’s kitchen garden on the hills nearby), with a new cooling cabinet in which fish are “aged”. The delightful terrace, open in summer from 6.30pm onwards, is the perfect setting for alfresco aperitifs and dinners.

Name: Le Cupole
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This delightful restaurant on the 10th floor of the Grand Hotel Bristol occupies a roof garden with breathtaking views of the promontory of Portofino. Dishes from all over Italy feature on the menu, with a particular emphasis given to regional specialities. Make sure you try the tortelli di Preboggion (pasta with local herbs) served with a Vaise cheese and walnut sauce.

Name: Guallina
Address: via Molino Faenza 19, località Guallina, Mortara, 27036, Italy
Description: Situated in a small house in an outlying village in the countryside, this is a simple, inviting restaurant where you can enjoy seasonal local cuisine. Excellent wines.

Name: Locale
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Situated within a palazzo full of history, from the medieval basement to the Renaissance-style architecture of the restaurant itself, Locale is also home to an old courtyard with a lounge bar and large cocktail counter, as well as some beautiful rooms to the rear of the building. Enjoy creative, innovative cuisine with personalised touches influenced by the chef’s professional experience around the world (Australia, Japan, France). Our inspector particularly enjoyed the Risoni pasta with cuttlefish liver and cherry tomatoes.

Name: Repubblica di Perno
Address: vicolo Cavour 5, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of the gastronomic Langa region, this small, renovated restaurant in the centre of town (reservations required) is imbued with the passion of the couple at the helm (he’s in the kitchen, while she’s front of house). In keeping with Piedmontese tradition, you catch a glimpse of the open-view kitchen as you make your way to the first floor, which is laid out with just five tables. Enjoy traditional cuisine in a rustic, bistro-style setting where the daily menu showcases dishes with a strictly regional focus. Three guestrooms are also available.

Name: Fàula
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fàula is the restaurant at the Casa Langa hotel, a large property which opens out like an amphitheatre to offer panoramic views of the valley. Here, the young chef skilfully creates cuisine which blends the culinary traditions of the Piedmont with more modern dishes. A good selection of wines from the region, plus a biodynamic kitchen garden add to the appeal.

Name: Lofficina
Description: This building with a minimalist, contemporary design is situated on the edge of the historic centre at the Sant'Erasmo belvedere from where, in summer, panoramic views extend over Monte Conero and the sea (booking ahead is recommended). In the kitchen, owner-chef Davide Breccia conjures up creative dishes featuring original combinations and mainly inspired by the sea. Our inspector’s favourite dish was the marinated amberjack with passion fruit, black pepper and vanilla. The freshness of the fish is enhanced by the chef’s balanced and individual approach.

Name: Villa Lattanzi
Address: contrada Cugnolo 19, Torre di Palme, 63900, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gourmet restaurant housed in a restored period residence that once belonged to the counts of Adami is surrounded by the green maquis and hills of the Marche, with the sea visible in the distance just a few miles away. Here, the young Neapolitan chef creates cuisine that is surprising for its attractive, clean lines, providing a real explosion of flavours and a tribute to the region and the Mediterranean in general. The restaurant also owns a nearby agricultural estate which provides many of the wines and olive oils served during tastings.

Name: Retrobottega
Description: Minimalist decor and clean lines characterise this restaurant decorated in dark tones, where the two owner-chefs have both worked in various Michelin-starred restaurants (and others) over the years. Modern cuisine which showcases seasonal ingredients in regional yet refined dishes.

Name: Al Persef
Description: A small yet very comfortable dining room with large windows and just a few tables provides the setting for modern, creative cuisine prepared by a young and ambitious chef. Locally sourced ingredients are prioritised here, plus there’s an excellent wine list.

Name: Asina Luna
Address: via della Resistenza 23, Peschiera Borromeo, 20068, Italy
Description: A restaurant with an attractive atmosphere, thanks to its profusion of wood, soft lighting and contemporary colour scheme. Meat aged for different periods takes pride of place on the menu. Sourced from different countries, it includes sweet Piedmontese Vicciola beef fed on hazelnuts and tender and delicately marbled Australian Scottona beef. Good selection of strongly flavoured and aged meat options.

Name: Gainn
Description: Since 2007, Gainn has showcased the fascinating and delicious flavours of colourful Korean cuisine, with its rice-based dishes, soups, meat, fish, plenty of vegetables and soya. The best way to experience the food here is to order a selection of different dishes to be shared with your dining companions. Those with a sweet tooth, be warned – there are no desserts on the menu.

Name: Osteria del Tasso
Address: via Bolgherese km 3,9, località San Walfredo, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the famous Viale dei Cipressi avenue in one of Italy’s best-known wine-producing areas, this restaurant occupies one of the region’s most famous wineries, namely Guado al Tasso, renowned for its excellent wines. In fine weather, guests can dine in the shade of plane trees looking out over the vineyards. Simple, delicious and well-prepared cuisine, mostly traditional in style, plus specialities such as cured hams and grilled dishes.

Name: MARdiVINO
Description: Francesco is in the kitchen and his partner is front of house in this bright, modern and elegant restaurant serving beautifully prepared dishes in which fish takes pride of place. Contemporary cuisine with the occasional Puglian influence in a nod to the chef’s native origins.

Name: Comi 107
Description: Situated near the lake at the entrance to a narrow street dotted with various shops, this small contemporary-style restaurant boasts an equally tiny outdoor space for summer dining and is run with skill and professionalism by a young couple. The friendly, welcoming wife oversees the front of house, while her husband creates dishes full of character in the kitchen.

Name: Il Fenicottero Rosa Gourmet
Description: Situated within the Villa Abbondanzi luxury hotel, this restaurant is surrounded by a large park home to a flock of flamingos (fenicottero is the Italian for flamingo). Stylish and elegant dining rooms provide the backdrop for equally impressive cuisine, which is elaborate and full of imaginative touches. The same attention to detail is evident in the wine list, which includes several natural wines and from which the talented sommelier will find the perfect choice for you. We particularly enjoyed the Alto Adige Sauvignon Weingut In Der Eben: a rich and complex 2019 wine which was the perfect pairing for the entire meal, including dishes with real character.

Name: Moebius Sperimentale
Description: Occupying an old textile workshop, this restaurant is one of the most attractive in Milan with its modern, chic-industrial setting divided into three separate spaces: a cocktail bar with an impressive selection of gins, a bistro serving tapas, and an experimental restaurant. The restaurant is housed in a glass-enclosed room with space for 30 guests, built on a suspended platform in the centre of the building. Creative and exciting cuisine.

Name: La Canonica
Description: A small, minimalist restaurant in the town centre, where both the ambience and the cuisine are contemporary in style with a hint of Sardinian influence (the chef is originally from the island). Some of the dishes features fermented ingredients prepared on site.

Name: Cucina Rambaldi
Description: Regional dishes with the occasional subtle contemporary twist are to the fore here. The chef’s culinary techniques bring out all the flavour of the carefully selected and preserved ingredients, with a focus on cooking temperatures and the cut of the meat, resulting in excellent cuisine. The menu also features a few specialities from Ferrara, the chef’s native city.

Name: Madama Piola
Description: The aptly named Madama Piola (in Piedmontese dialect, “piola” is a village inn) has a simple yet attractive and friendly ambience that serves as a backdrop for typical Piedmontese dishes. Highlights include the memorable stuffed onion, as well as tonnato, braised cheeks and hot zabaglione. Regional wines take pride of place on the wine list, which includes a good selection by the glass.

Name: Altriménti
Description: An informal and contemporary restaurant which is elegant and yet retains a bistro feel. The cuisine is modern with meat and fish dishes featured on the menu, as well as a good number of vegetarian options. Good wine list.

Name: Gaudenzio
Description: Just a short walk from the Mole, a small, original and informal establishment, where the cuisine is characterized by a limited selection of dishes, a good option if you want to leave the better known tradition. There are indeed references to the local gastronomy, often however imaginatively revisited sometimes also with exotic ingredients.

Name: Osteria del Posto
Address: via Calderini 15, loc. Chiugiana, Corciano, 06073, Italy
Description: It's well worth the climb up to this restaurant, where you can be sure of a friendly welcome and professional service. With advice on hand from courteous female staff, choose from a selection of imaginative, locally influenced dishes that are full of flavour. We particularly recommend the pigeon (piccione di tutto un po’), accompanied by a glass of the potent Gamay del Trasimeno Opra red wine with an alcohol content of 14.5°!

Name: Ciblèo
Address: via Andrea del Verrocchio 2r, Florence, 50122, Italy
Description: Although the cuisine at this restaurant is influenced by Asian concepts, the young Korean female chef uses many Tuscan ingredients in her skilfully prepared dishes which have a real individual flavour and are often inspired by Japanese cuisine (such as the gyoza noodles). The extensive menu features numerous small plates, while the prints on the wall and the wooden trays lined up on the counter give the intimate dining room an Asian feel. Guests are required to book in advance.

Name: Quattro Sensi
Description: After working in top-level restaurants both in Italy and abroad, the young chef at this restaurant in the Borgobrufa hotel offers a host of interesting dishes featuring excellent Umbrian ingredients, often sourced from local growers and farmers. Meat dishes dominate the menu, alongside a good selection of vegetables.

Name: Cinque Archi
Description: Overlooking one of the most famous squares in Taormina with its breathtaking views of the sea and Mt Etna, Cinque Archi serves classic cuisine with a focus on fish and seafood and a large selection of raw fish dishes. If you’re looking for a romantic setting overlooking the promenade, ask for one of the tables on the small balcony.

Name: Fè Ristorante
Description: Situated near the centre, this restaurant occupies a small group of eight carefully restored trulli which provide an elegant and charming setting, with just 20 seats arranged throughout its small buildings. Traditional, regional cuisine reinterpreted with a skilful modern twist.

Name: Radici
Description: Situated beneath the walls of Castello Oldofredi in the centre of this delightful lakeside village, not far from the lake itself, this restaurant with a young team at the helm has a light contemporary feel, both in its decor and cuisine. The modern design contrasts with the restaurant’s setting in a historic building, while the dishes are inspired by the recipes and ingredients of the region. Influences from elsewhere in Italy as well as further afield are also in evidence on the menu.

Name: Ichikawa
Description: Ichikawa is one of the culinary masters who played a part in introducing Japanese cuisine to Italy. After decades in the country working in various restaurants, this chef has finally opened his own eatery, where he serves top-quality Japanese cuisine ranging from familiar favourites such as sushi and sashimi to other less-known family dishes and street food from the land of the Rising Sun. A good place to discover the joys of Japanese cuisine!

Name: Lupaia
Address: Località Lupaia 74, Torrita di Siena, 53049, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming Tuscan hamlet nestled in the hills between Montepulciano and Montefollonico, this restaurant boasts stunning sunset views from its garden in the summer months, while guests in the dining room can enjoy views of the open kitchen in winter. The cuisine changes daily, with the chef offering a tasting menu based largely around produce from his own farm.

Name: La Società Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated near Porta Venezia and its lush gardens, Giulia and Andrea’s restaurant boasts a warm and original ambience. Three dining rooms adorned with tapestries and an entrance with a fine white marble fireplace act as the setting for Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional exotic twist. Don’t miss the amberjack caponata in which the ceviche flavours contrast with the sweetness of the fried breaded aubergine.

Name: Antica Osteria il Ronchettino
Description: The name seems to originate from the broken horseshoe (ronchetto) of Napoleon, who in 1800 appears to have stayed the night here, where there was indeed a post house where horses were shoed. Later converted into a bakery, butcher’s shop, but also a trattoria with an annexed bowling alley, today it is a restaurant of rustic elegance; the regional cuisine expresses itself in specialties such as fried brains and the ever-present Milanese-style cutlet that here becomes even “imperial”, definitely to be shared.

Name: Saur
Description: In a tiny rural village, this contemporary, almost minimalist-style restaurant serves modern cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal, regional produce.

Name: Antica Osteria Moirago
Description: This old monastery in Moirago, overlooking the Naviglio Pavese canal, was founded in 1250 and converted into an inn as early as 1478. Centuries may have passed, but the tradition of hospitality continues in the building’s enclosed painted portico, as well as in its two warm and atmospheric dining rooms. The chef’s Puglian origins explain the abundant use of vegetables and raw fish dishes, while in winter the cuisine takes on a more northern Italian flavour. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This historic restaurant, run by the same family for many years, is situated right on the lake (with its own private mooring), which can be best appreciated from the charming veranda. The current owner-chef has retained the cuisine’s classic style, while adding his own contemporary touch to top-quality meat and fish dishes (including freshwater fish).

Name: Antiche Carampane
Address: rio Terà delle Carampane, sestiere San Polo 1911, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: From the typical flooring to the decoration on the walls, the warm and appealing decor in this restaurant highlights its historic feel, providing a setting to which guests happily return time after time. The local fish and seafood specialities served here include sarde in saor (sardines), salted cod, fried soft-shell crab and cuttlefish in black ink – skilfully prepared dishes which remain faithful to traditional recipes.

Name: Phi Restaurant - Giancarlo Morelli
Address: località Forte Cappellini, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Glamour and fashion are the hallmarks of this restaurant in Phi Beach, one of the most attractive nightclub-cum-lounge bars on the Costa Smeralda. Take a seat on the terrace right by the water and soak up the romantic sunsets and sea views as you enjoy Italian and Mediterranean dishes created by a famous chef from Lombardy who adds just the right touch of contemporary flavour. Also open for lunch, with some of the evening menu dishes available alongside an array of simpler options.

Name: Le Petit Bellevue
Cuisine: Italian Contemporary, Cuisine from the Aosta Valley
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in one of the region’s most famous and romantic hotels, this small gem of a restaurant offers just a few seats at period-style tables in a small dining room, in addition to two tables with scenic views of the valley and Gran Paradiso. Here, the Tuscan chef focuses on specialities from the Aosta Valley, including popular dishes such as Lillaz char with roe and a butter sauce, and “zuppa del bosco” (stewed seasonal mushrooms served with Aosta blue cheese and a pinch of fresh marjoram), followed by an extraordinary cheese trolley that focuses on regional specialities. Last but not least, talented sommelier Rino Billia (a previous winner of the “passion for wine” award) demonstrates skilful understanding of guests’ requirements as he chooses the most suitable wine for them out of the more than 1 600 labels on the wine list.

Name: Locanda del Marinaio
Description: Delicious cuisine full of the flavours of the Mediterranean (prepared by the German owner - chef! ) in a delightful little restaurant in the bustling centre of Cefalù. Simple surroundings but excellent food!

Name: Il Doretto
Description: Restaurant within a refined farmstead. The ancient structure has maintained the rustic style in spite of several hints of elegance in the furnishings. On the menu: interesting offer of meat and seafood (with a slightly more limited wine cellar at lunch). Pleasant exterior for summer service.

Name: Zanze XVI
Address: fondamenta dei Tolentini, sestiere Santa Croce 231, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description: Although the setting and convivial atmosphere in this restaurant recall that of a typical Venetian bàcaro , the cuisine is completely different in feel. The ingredients are sourced from the best markets and local producers, resulting in unique dishes that reflect the culinary traditions of the lagoon and its surrounding area. The few tables arranged outdoors with views of the tranquil canal add to the appeal, while the professional yet friendly service helps to put guests completely at ease.

Name: Roof Garden
Description: Make sure you ask for one of the tables next to the glass wall in this restaurant, which boasts romantic views of Bergamo’s Città Alta. The innovative, inventive cuisine is tempting and full of flavour.

Name: Osteria Ardenga
Description: An authentic trattoria which is a joy to visit, where time seems to have stood still for decades. Situated on the border between two provinces, the restaurant focuses on specialities from Parma, many of which are made from home - grown produce. Homemade pickles and chutneys are also sold here.

Name: Antica Osteria da Penacio
Description: A family - run restaurant in a villa on the edge of a wood: inside two refined dining rooms and a small, but well stocked, wine bar; traditional cuisine.

Name: Il Pavone
Description: Situated in the heart of Alghero and with a beautiful veranda overlooking the sea, this restaurant serves delicious fish and seafood made from top-quality ingredients. Highlights include the “Alessandrina” fried fish and the octopus salad. If available, make sure you try the goats’ cheese made by the owner himself, although be warned – the flavour is quite strong!

Name: Doc
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 1, Borgio Verezzi, 17022, Italy
Description: Quiet, well - kept restaurant located in an aristocratic, early twentieth - century villa surrounded by a pretty garden.

Name: Stube Ladina
Description: The hotel owner is also the chef, serving carefully prepared and well - presented dishes made from regional produce in a quiet Stube - style dining room. An interesting wine list provides the icing on the cake.

Name: Osteria de l'Umbreleèr
Description: Situated in Cicognolo in the Lower Po valley, where early morning mists create an evocative atmosphere in autumn, this traditional restaurant with a rustic feel serves specialities from Lombardy with a focus on delicious starters and top-quality meat. Our inspector particularly recommends the white onion gratin soup and the Burgundy-style snails. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime and there’s a small garden for alfresco dining on summer evenings.

Name: Osteria le Logge
Description: Having retained its old shop counter and glass - fronted display cabinets, this former grocer’s shop is perfect for anyone in search of old - world charm. However, the cuisine is the real draw with its focus on quality of the highest level. Wine buffs can ask to visit the wine cellar nearby, housed in a tunnel of Etruscan origin. Simpler dining room on the first floor.

Name: Feel Como
Description: Wild regional produce, game and freshwater fish take pride of place on the menu at this elegant restaurant which celebrates nature in all its glory, despite its town-centre location. The dishes prepared by chef Federico Beretta have a contemporary feel, while the tasting menu is dedicated to wild ingredients foraged from the woods.

Name: Osteria dell'Oca Bianca
Description: In the heart of a small town, right opposite the church, this typical village osteria run by a friendly family serves traditional cuisine from the Piedmont, including goose dishes. Highlights here include the rustic, welcoming ambience, an excellent wine list, a wine cellar that can be visited, and a charming glass-fronted veranda that is used throughout the year. There are also three beautiful guestrooms reserved exclusively for guests dining at the restaurant.

Name: Cascina Lautier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated outside the town on top of a small hill, this elegant restaurant serves modern country cuisine, with some personal interpretations.

Name: Walter Redaelli
Description: This old 18C farmhouse has exposed brick, ceiling beams and an impressive fireplace. It makes a feast of tasty, Tuscan cuisine elaborated from local ingredients, especially meat. Settle into the comfortable chairs and indulge in the pleasure of dining snugly.

Name: Il Labirinto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Brescia, this long-established restaurant has an elegant retro atmosphere. The cuisine is varied with a balance of fish and meat dishes, as well as some excellent home-made salumi.

Name: Lou Ressignon
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: A pleasant family trattoria which has been in business since 1966, this restaurant serves simple and authentic cuisine which showcases the products of the Aosta Valley, as well as excellent meat, most of which comes from outside Italy. In addition to the first-floor dining room, there’s also a historic taverna, while four welcoming guestrooms are available for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: La Fermata
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the countryside around Alessandria, this 18C farmhouse has a modern, minimalist decor which serves as a backdrop for traditional Piedmontese cuisine with a clever modern twist. The chef offers just the right amount of creativity, with a focus on meat dishes and satisfying, memorable flavours that appeal to the emotions as well as the palate. Adding to the appeal, the elegant and exclusive ambience is the result of careful refurbishment, which has transformed the dining room into a triumph of art and design.

Name: Badessa
Description: This restaurant has a surprising location in a 19C cheese factory which once produced parmesan cheese. Although the purpose of the building has changed, the love of the region remains the same: the chef goes out of his way to source local ingredients and serve traditional Emilian dishes, often with a modern twist. One of the best restaurants in rural Reggio Emilia.

Name: Trippini
Address: via Italia 14, Civitella del Lago, 05023, Italy
Description: Just a few tables and spectacular views of Lake Corbara characterise this restaurant, which has been run by the same family since 1964. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, showcasing home-cooked recipes and typical Sunday favourites yet with a contemporary twist that incorporates plenty of intense flavours.

Name: Saffron
Description: If you like fish and you find yourself in Arezzo, then this is the place for you. Saffron serves a range of traditional and imaginative raw fish dishes inspired by different traditions, from the Mediterranean to Japan, alongside a few cooked fish options and the occasional Japanese speciality such as tempura and Japanese spaghetti and ravioli.

Name: La Galleria di Sopra
Address: via Leonardo Murialdo 9, Albano Laziale, 00041, Italy
Description: The modern, minimalist - style dining room in this restaurant is a far cry from the stereotypical image of the Castelli Romani region. The menu features local produce, albeit served in creative, carefully prepared and original dishes.

Name: Daniela
Address: piazza Matteotti 7, San Casciano dei Bagni, 53040, Italy
Description: Just a little under 100m from the Sette Querce hotel and situated opposite a lovely viewpoint, this restaurant is housed in the castle’s old stables. The vaulted ceilings and old stone create a charming ambience, while the excellent local cuisine will definitely appeal to the palate.

Name: L'Osteria del Castellazzo
Address: via Borgo Castellazzo 40, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description: The determined and enthusiastic young owner of this restaurant graduated with a literature degree before giving in to her passion for food. She swapped her pen for a ladle and now creates delicious local specialities such as braised veal cheeks, alongside dishes from Pïacenza and Mantua, such as pisarei (a type of gnocchi) and sbrisolona cake.

Name: DaMà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The gourmet restaurant at the Villa d’Amelia hotel serves creative, innovative cuisine with Asian influences (especially from Japan and India) and strong traditional roots. These traditions are carefully explored through the use of old recipes, some of which were only ever printed in the Piedmontese language! The wine list is excellent, especially in its choice of Barolo and Barbaresco labels.

Name: La Conchiglia
Description: This small restaurant with a vaulted ceiling provides the setting for dishes that have by now become classics thanks to their focus on top-quality ingredients. The cuisine is light and simple rather than bold and elaborate, with a focus on bringing out the full flavour of the fish (a few meat dishes are also available). If you’re keen to learn more about Ligurian gastronomic specialities, take time between courses to chat with the friendly owner, who has an impressive knowledge of the region.

Name: L'Argaj
Description: In the Piedmontese dialect, “Argaj” translates as “satisfaction” and never has a restaurant name seemed more appropriate! In a simple, colourful and welcoming dining room with windows looking out at the hills, all the attention is on cuisine which is skilfully balanced between classic local dishes and more creative options. Choose between the à la carte and tasting menus, all accompanied by an excellent array of wines.

Name: I Salotti
Address: Località Querce al Pino, SS 146, Chiusi, 53043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In summer, the outdoor spaces at this restaurant, such as the garden gazebo, are the perfect setting for a candlelit dinner in total harmony with nature, while in winter, the elegant dining room with just a few tables (book well in advance) really comes into its own. Creative cuisine prepared using produce from the restaurant’s own farm, plus a long-established wine cellar that has been extended over the years so that it now boasts over two thousand different labels from the region and elsewhere in Italy, many of them of the highest quality.

Name: Il Portico
Description: Chef Lopriore returns to his native region with this new restaurant which offers an original format – the lunchtime menu focuses on single course options, while in the evening the tasting menus comprise an interesting combination of imaginative fish, meat and vegetable dishes which can be combined as you wish. Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal market ingredients where locally sourced produce takes pride of place.

Name: Kürbishof
Description: This romantic inn with guestrooms occupies an old farm with a hay barn. In two typical Stube-style rooms, one of which offers views of the Cembra valley, enjoy cuisine prepared by a mother-and-son team. They work side by side, preparing dishes from mainly regional ingredients (the menu often includes the names of producers) each in their own individual way, which is highlighted on the menu: to the left, you’ll find the traditional dishes made by the mother, Sara, while on the right you can choose from a selection of modern, creative options prepared by young chef Mathias. Our inspectors were delighted with their combination of choices from both lists!

Name: All'Osteria Bottega
Description: Enjoy top-quality Emilian cuisine at this restaurant, which focuses on the region’s most traditional, best-known and authentic recipes. Featuring a superb selection of hams and salamis, fresh pastas, meat and desserts, the menu offers a real feast for the tastebuds that will linger long in the memory.

Name: CiPASSO
Description: This contemporary bistro with a hint of vintage style in its decor now has a new location. The menu is inspired by Roman traditions, with the occasional imaginative twist and other more Mediterranean-inspired dishes, all showing a strong focus on seasonal ingredients. The excellent wine list includes a whole page dedicated to wines by the glass. Friendly yet professional service from the young team completes the picture.

Name: La Tavernetta al Castello
Address: via Spessa 7, Capriva del Friuli, 34070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The greenery of the vineyards and nearby golf course (with a clubhouse and restaurant) provide a pleasant setting for this rustic yet elegant inn with a welcoming fireplace. Regional, seasonal cuisine, plus comfortable guestrooms for a tranquil stay.

Name: Clandestino Susci Bar
Description: Built on stilts, the Clandestino is a unique restaurant with a simple yet trendy ambience, which overlooks a beautiful unspoilt beach with views of the sea from all the windows and a distinctly romantic feel at night. Here, Moreno Cedroni focuses on gourmet cuisine at lunchtime as well as in the evening. In addition to two tasting menus (Eros & Susci and Susci Memories), for lunch there’s a small à la carte.

Name: Faraglioni Restaurant
Address: lungomare dei Ciclopi 115, loc. Aci Trezza, Aci Castello, 95021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated next to the hotel of the same name (a reference to the Faraglioni islands just off the coast here) but with its own entrance, this restaurant overlooks the beautiful Riviera dei Ciclopi. Sicilian ingredients take pride of place here in traditional and creative dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (vegetarian options are also available).

Name: Enoclub
Description: Under the arcades of a piazza named after Michele Ferrero, this restaurant has a simple, modern ambience with walls covered with wine bottles, as well as friendly, efficient female staff. The beautifully prepared Piedmontese cuisine is showcased on an à la carte and a tasting menu, accompanied by an impressive selection of quality wine.

Name: SOMS
Description: Situated in a pedestrianised area of the old town, the historic “società operaia di mutuo soccorso” (SOMS – a workers’ mutual aid association) has been transformed into a bright, welcoming restaurant where the chef creates dishes influenced by the traditions of the Abruzzi yet decidedly original in style (barbecued dishes are one of the specialities). Classic decor, plus a pleasant outdoor space for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: La Veranda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: As its name suggests, the dining room at this restaurant is a splendid and elegant veranda, which transfers out onto the terrace overlooking the lake in fine weather. A perfect setting for the modern, international and Italian influenced cuisine served here.

Name: Trattoria del Bivio
