Description: Situated in the Alta Langa region, this old restored farmhouse is now home to an elegant restaurant with a contemporary rural feel. The cuisine has strong regional roots, although the menu also offers a few fishes dishes. Excellent food, as well as attractive guestrooms and a warm, family welcome.

Name: La Casa degli Spiriti
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant celebrates its 25th birthday in 2021, with owner Federico Chignola returning to the kitchen, ably assisted by his son Filippo. The cuisine has changed too and now focuses on local products and simple regional dishes made from carefully chosen top-quality ingredients – the style is innovative, balanced and always with a keen eye on beautiful presentation. A luxurious gem boasting breathtaking views of the lake.

Name: Lanzani Bottega & Bistrot
Address: via Albertano da Brescia 41, Brescia, 25127, Italy
Description: This modern restaurant (open from 7am to 11pm), once the family butcher’s, also acts as a delicatessen and wine boutique. Full restaurant service in the evening with simpler dishes and a more restricted choice at lunchtime. Situated some distance from the centre.

Name: Oste Scuro - Finsterwirt
Description: Run by the capable Mayr family, this long-established restaurant has occupied a narrow alleyway in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen) since the late 19C. The dining rooms are decorated in historic style, plus there’s a charming terrace for alfresco dining in summer. Dishes are presented on different tasting menus with the option of choosing traditional or Mediterranean dishes à la carte style – we highly recommend the soup made with Sylvaner wine from the Isarco valley, as well as the Tirtl (fried pie) stuffed with ricotta, spinach and cinnamon. Guestrooms are available in the nearby and recently renovated Adler Historic Guesthouse, which is run by the same owners.

Name: La Foresteria
Address: Contrada Passo di Gurra  SP 79 km 91, Menfi, 92013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A luxurious guesthouse belonging to the famous Sicilian winery Planeta and surrounded by beautiful vineyards is the setting for this restaurant serving top-quality Sicilian cuisine. Home-grown ingredients make an appearance in some dishes, while the extensive wine list obviously features a good selection of Planeta’s own labels.

Name: Ristorante del Lago
Address: via Acquapartita 147, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
Description: Once off the main road, follow a series of twists and turns uphill to reach the village of Acquapartita, at an altitude of almost 800m, where you’ll find one of the best restaurants in the region. Here, the Bravaccini brothers are at the helm, with chef Simone creating dishes that are proudly focused on local ingredients such as mushrooms, trout and game. His signature dish of wild boar is delicious and full of flavour – the meat is sliced tartare-style so that it cooks quickly and is then served covered with soft mashed potatoes sprinkled with juniper. Front of house, his friendly and skilful brother Andrea oversees an encyclopaedic wine list – two volumes featuring almost 1 600 labels, with a focus on Italy and France (almost 40% of the wines are French). The choice of wines is as impressive as the quantity and the service. All in all, an excellent choice!

Name: Sale Grosso
Address: viale II Giugno 15, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: One of the town’s authentic favourites, this fish restaurant has a pleasant, light - coloured decor inspired by the sea. The eclectic cuisine includes tapas and raw fish dishes.

Name: Satricvm
Description: Their experience in London, as well as in restaurants around the world, is evident in the pleasant yet somewhat unexpected international atmosphere created by this husband-and-wife team. Using modern techniques and locally sourced produce, the chef succeeds in showcasing the Agro Pontino area in his cuisine which is contemporary while still respecting the traditions of the region.

Name: DanielCanzian
Description: Situated in the heart of Brera and refurbished in the autumn of 2019, this restaurant showcases Italian artisanal skills through its bespoke furnishings, creating a fine setting for Canzian’s superb cuisine. A great choice for anyone looking for classic Italian dishes plus a few more inventive options, all of which are prepared using the very best ingredients. Simpler fare available at lunchtime.

Name: Antica Locanda del Villoresi
Description: What was once a post station is now a renowned restaurant overlooking the Villoresi canal. Although the attractive dining room has retained some of its historical features, the decor here is more contemporary in feel. The Mediterranean-style cuisine focuses mainly on fish and is beautifully presented, with dishes such as fried artichokes with red prawns and bottarga on the menu in season. Raw fish dishes are also occasionally available.

Name: Filippino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: An historic establishment for the archipelago and for all of Sicily, it allows you to taste a large selection of local fish; typical preparations, served in an informal atmosphere.

Name: Il Convito di Curina
Address: SP 62 24, località Curina, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Tuscan cuisine, accompanied by a wide selection of wines (including regional labels and champagnes made by small producers) is served in the rustic yet elegant ambience of this restaurant. In fine weather, enjoy alfresco dining on the panoramic terrace.

Name: Entrà
Address: via Salde Entrà 60, località Entrà, Finale Emilia, 41034, Italy
Description: Make sure you use your sat-nav to get to this restaurant as finding the right road through the countryside can be a challenge, although once you’re here you’ll be glad you made the effort. The trattoria occupies a wine shop dating from 1919, from which it has retained a few attractive and nostalgic touches despite its renovation. The cuisine focuses on a few regional dishes which are announced at your table by the owner himself.

Name: Lo Scudiero
Description: Young, enthusiastic chef Daniele Patti is at the helm at this restaurant housed in the delightful stables of a restored 16C palazzo. Here, he serves a selection of creative dishes, including two tasting menus – the intriguing Vieni in Sicilia con me (inspired by his native Sicily) and the Adriatico  - and an à la carte which focuses on the local region’s abundance of fine ingredients. Wine-enthusiasts can ask to visit the impressive cellar, which also offers a good choice of wines by the glass.

Name: Retrogusto
Description: Although this restaurant is slightly set back from the seafront, the high quality cuisine focusing on the flavours of the Salento makes the short walk well worthwhile. A classic ambience with simple yet tasteful furniture, soft background music and an informal atmosphere.

Name: Alla Coà
Description: Situated alongside a fairly busy road, this old house has been furnished in typical country style with a hint of romanticism. The menu focuses almost exclusively on meat dishes, with salted cod and shrimp among the few fish and seafood specialities available.

Name: La Locanda di Piero
Address: via Roma 34, strada per Dueville, Montecchio Precalcino, 36030, Italy
Description: Despite the name of this restaurant, its owners are actually called Renato and Sergio! Housed in a small country villa with the ambience of an elegant private residence, the restaurant boasts a dining room with a welcoming fireplace and a veranda full of natural light. The cuisine is modern yet decidedly Italian in influence.

Name: Ilario Vinciguerra
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This beautiful Art Nouveau-style villa is a restaurant, bistro and lounge-bar in one – the ideal setting for a meal, whether you’re planning a business lunch or a romantic dinner. Guests will feel immediately at ease both with Ilario’s modern, Mediterranean cuisine and the vaguely private feel of the small dining rooms. There’s also an original collection of Romano Levi grappas, plus several rare labels on the wine list that will definitely appeal to wine buffs.

Name: Osteria del Borgo
Description: Situated in the heart of the old town, this restaurant is run by friendly and welcoming staff. The menu features a mix of meat and fish dishes that are prepared in traditional style with the occasional personalised touch.

Name: Al Volt
Address: via Fiume 73, Riva del Garda, 38066, Italy
Description: As you explore the narrow streets which lead from the commercial port to the centre, you’ll come across this restaurant comprising several inter - connected dining rooms with low ceilings and antique furniture. The menu focuses on regional cuisine, albeit with the occasional creative twist.

Name: Gibas
Description: This modern restaurant stands on the road that heads north from the town. It boasts panoramic views of the sea that can be enjoyed from the deck in summer. Contemporary - style fish dishes dominate the menu.

Name: L'Officina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Tradition and a cosmopolitan spirit combine in this highly original and exciting restaurant which has stepped off the usual gastronomic bandwagon in spectacular fashion! It’s not by chance that L’Officina describes itself as a “cultural restaurant”.

Name: Taverna La Cialoma
Description: This restaurant housed in Marzamemi’s old tuna fishery boasts an outdoor terrace with tables overlooking one of the most picturesque squares in Sicily, as well as an indoor dining room and another terrace to the rear facing the sea. Wherever you choose to sit, you’ll find authentic Sicilian cuisine on the menu, with just a few simply prepared dishes in which the full flavours of fresh fish shine through.

Name: Belle Parti
Description: Occupying the ground floor of the historic Palazzo Prosdocimi in a delightful arcaded alleyway in Padova’s pedestrianised centre, this charming restaurant has a warm and romantic atmosphere thanks to its decor of paintings, mirrors and wood panelling, plus a beautiful ceiling with exposed wooden beams. The menu follows the changing seasons, offering a selection of delicious, classic dishes, with meat and – especially – fish (mostly from the Veneto) featuring on the menu.

Name: L'Antico Giardino
Description: Choose from an interesting, traditional à la carte and two tasting menus (one autumn-based, the other traditional, both excellent value for money) at this comfortable restaurant, where guests are welcomed by the friendly owner who is on hand to offer wine pairing recommendations. The menu features meat tartares and flans, agnolotti and ravioli pasta, and superbly cooked, top-quality cuts of meat, with truffles often making an appearance in season. We visited in autumn and particularly enjoyed the pumpkin cappellaccio with butter, sage and almonds – a dish that stood out for its delicious, creamy flavours.

Name: Antiche Mura
Address: via Bastione 19, Riva del Garda, 38066, Italy
Description: At Antiche Mura, savour contemporary cuisine that takes its inspiration and ingredients from both the land and sea, as well as the passing seasons. Situated behind the historic centre, the restaurant also offers an outdoor space for the summer months and ten simple yet comfortable guestrooms.

Name: L'Acchiatura
Description: Delicious cuisine from Puglia, including excellent orecchiette pasta with clams and chickpeas, served in a delightful ambience with a number of different rooms and internal patios. The same traditional atmosphere is evident in the attractive, well - equipped guestrooms, as well as in the picturesque swimming pool housed in a grotto.

Name: Osteria del Guà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Guà was the name in local dialect of the River Novo, alongside which the property is situated. Dine under the arcades of the barchessa in fine weather, soaking up the tranquil atmosphere of the park, and in the intimate, romantic dining room in winter, which boasts the same elegant style as the rest of the hotel. Enjoy refined reinterpretations of local specialities in the evening, and simpler fare at lunchtime.

Name: Colline Emiliane
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Piazza Barberini, this simple, friendly, family-run restaurant has just a few tables arranged close together. It serves typical dishes from the Emilia region, including fresh pasta stretched by hand in the traditional way.

Name: Trattoria Paola
Address: via Porta Lago 23, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: A very simple little restaurant, its sign is barely visible at the entrance. While at lunchtime the formula is easier, typically Italian, geared to fast working lunches (but an à la carte menu is available on asking in advance), in the evening the cuisine is inspired by the region and the season, presented with little personal touches.

Name: Il Faggio
Description: An elegant dining room with large windows and classic decor provides the setting for modern Mediterranean meat and fish dishes. The wine list features a good selection of labels from the region and further afield.

Name: Da Odino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant has stood on this square for many years, having been built as a “casone” and previously used as a dance hall. Despite its large size, the atmosphere is pleasant and convivial, helped by the staff here who are friendly yet professional. Situated just a stone’s throw from the Park Hotel Junior, a modern hotel under the same ownership, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood, although you’ll also find meat and vegetarian options on the menu.

Name: Stella d'Italia
Description: Regional specialities, including snails and pike, in a historical establishment, once an inn now an elegant establishment under the management of Signor Umberto.

Name: La Braseria
Description: This restaurant is a paradise for meat-eaters – its signature dishes are prime cuts of meat (mostly beef) from different breeds, which are displayed in the refrigerated cabinet at the entrance. There’s an extensive à la carte, with various appetiser options and a small choice of “primi”, but all the attention here is on the main course. The meat is either smoked and grilled over beech wood or roasted in the wood-fired oven – there’s something here for every taste! A cheese selection and delicious desserts complete the picture.

Name: Marcelin
Address: piazzetta della Vecchia Segheria 1, Montà, 12046, Italy
Description: If you are in search of creative and innovative cuisine in this region renowned for its great gastronomic tradition, then Marcelin is the place for you. This is thanks to its occasionally complex and always beautifully presented dishes (including a few fish options). Housed on the first floor of an old sawmill, the restaurant boasts a restrained yet elegant decor.

Name: Ai Torchi
Description: Occupying a 17C olive oil press in the heart of a charming medieval village, this restaurant has retained its old stone mill and wooden press in its vaulted dining room, which provides the backdrop for imaginative fish and seafood dishes prepared using top-quality local ingredients. The delicious Italian-style ceviche is made from the catch of the day, while the Mare Mare mixed fish dish is baked in a casserole with cherry tomatoes, courgettes and bay leaves. If you’re looking for a simpler option, try the I Torchiettibistro on the corner of the same street.

Name: La Torre
Description: Overlooked by a medieval tower in the main town square, this restaurant is perfect for anyone keen on classic, traditional cuisine. House specialities include dishes cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: Trattoria Via Vai
Description: Although the original chef has now left, the cuisine remains unchanged with a concise menu of regional specialities and a focus on meat dishes. Poultry takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: Locanda Nelli
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 15, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: A friendly and welcoming little restaurant in the heart of the town’s historic centre. It’s no surprise that the specialities here focus mainly on fish and seafood, with an emphasis on Mediterranean cuisine, homemade pasta and the use of extremely fresh ingredients – the menu changes daily depending on market availability. The charming outdoor space boasts tables set out along the small pedestrianised street.

Name: Al Paradiso
Address: via Sant'Ermacora 1, Paradiso di Pocenia, 33050, Italy
Description: A small gem of a restaurant housed in an old farmhouse adorned with beautiful drapes and decorations. Although there’s a new chef here, the long family tradition of regional cuisine (mainly meat dishes and game) remains unchanged, with a large spit for roasting meat in the fireplace in the main dining room.

Name: I Giardini dei Rodo
Address: via Bonomo Alto - Scauri, Pantelleria, 91017, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant’s guests can enjoy their meal surrounded by verdant gardens, which are planted with palms, flowers and citrus trees. Regional flavours take centre-stage in the modern dishes in this romantic and original setting.

Name: Osteria del Benedet
Description: Once an old inn, this family-run restaurant now occupies two floors with the wine bar on the ground floor and the dining rooms above. Inspired by traditional cuisine the dishes here are reinterpreted in modern style with plenty of character. The excellent wine list makes this a good choice for wine aficionados.

Name: Langosteria
Description: If you are looking for fish specialities, you will find this restaurant a real revelation. Raw dishes, oysters and seafood take pride of place on the menu, alongside freshly caught fish. An excellent wine selection and a glamorous ambience complete the picture.

Name: La Sosta di Ottone III
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Ask for directions to this restaurant when you make your booking, as you’ll need to leave your vehicle in a private car park at the entrance to the village and then make your way uphill on foot. Situated in one of Liguria’s most typical and picturesque inland villages with views of the sea in the distance, the restaurant offers outdoor dining under a wisteria in fine weather. The menu features a small choice of regional dishes, with the same focus on Liguria evident on the wine list.

Name: da Omar
Address: via Dante Alighieri 21, Lido di Jesolo, 30016, Italy
Description: Passion and enthusiasm overcome all obstacles and lead to the best results: this summarises the professional journey of the chef at this restaurant. He prepares fish dishes inspired by classic Italian cuisine, sometimes with a modern twist, but always using the best quality produce.

Name: La Maison de Filip
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated at the entrance to the pedestrian section of the beautiful city of Trento, this intimate restaurant has a modern, minimalist and vaguely Nordic style, with just a few solid wood tables and stools of different sizes. The menu features a concise selection of carefully thought-out dishes, with starters, first and main courses (meat, fish or vegetarian) that are elegant, well prepared and contemporary in style. Beautiful presentation completes the picture.

Name: Osteria L'Orciaia
Description: A small rustic - style hostelry set inside a 16C building, with a cosy summer terrace. Typical Tuscan fare based on excellent produce and with some personal touches.

Name: Trequarti
Address: piazza del Donatore 3/4, Val Liona, 36044, Italy
Description: This modern and minimalist-style restaurant with three small dining rooms full of character provides the backdrop for contemporary-style cuisine which is constantly evolving. The menu includes a few snack options for those in a hurry or looking to sample a variety of dishes in smaller portions. Open at lunchtime by prior reservation.

Name: Morelli
Description: The new Milan restaurant of renowned chef Giancarlo Morelli, housed in the fascinating, new Hotel Viu. The creative gourmet dinner menu served in the stylish and discreetly lit dining room is complemented by the Bulk mixology and food bar, which serves simpler dishes throughout the day.

Name: Osteria Arborina
Description: Housed within the elegant Arborina Relais hotel, this restaurant boasts modern, bright and stylish rooms, although the main attraction here is the exciting cuisine in which different culinary styles and techniques are showcased in every dish. The new Neapolitan chef Fernando Tommaso Forino takes inspiration not only from Piedmont but also from elsewhere in Italy, occasionally including playful influences from his native region. Examples include scapece-style beetroot served on beetroot-marinated venison, accompanied by a savoury maritozzo bun filled with venison civet and caramelised onion cream. The whole menu has a no-waste focus, with all parts of the ingredients used, even the fish bones. Meanwhile, the bistro-style “The Lab” (also open at lunchtime) serves slightly more traditional cuisine.

Name: Da Concettina ai Tre Santi
Address: via Arena alla Sanità 7 bis, Naples, 80137, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of the ancient, lively and often chaotic working class district of Sanità, this excellent pizzeria has been run by the Oliva family for over 60 years. It has succeeded in reinventing itself with each generation while retaining its traditional roots. Modern and imaginative pizzas feature on the menu alongside various fried specialities.

Name: Casa Coppelle
Description: Situated in the heart of the city, this delightfully intimate restaurant offers a number of different dining rooms, from a ‘gallery of portraits’ to the British-style library rooms and the ‘herbier’ with prints on the walls. There is something for everyone here, although every guest will enjoy the same modern reinterpretations of Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: L'Osteria di Chichibio
Address: largo Gelso 6, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Combining simplicity, a cheerful decor and a touch of elegance, this restaurant serves fish specialities and vegetables cooked in many different ways. It’s also renowned for its raw shellfish (opened in front of guests), tartare dishes and sashimi from locally caught fish.

Name: Hostaria Baccofurore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Patience is needed to get to this restaurant from the coast, as a result of the winding road which makes its way through small villages, but once here the view of the sea is breathtaking. The village of Furore is built alongside the road and is famous for the Marisa Cuomo winery situated opposite the restaurant. The cuisine is as impressive as the vista, with its focus on different local ingredients cooked with a mix of traditional influence and imagination. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, almost all of which have been recently renovated and boast impressive views.

Name: J Contemporary Japanese Restaurant
Description: Arranged over several floors and in different dining rooms, this smart, elegant restaurant offers excellent service. In this modern setting with subtle lighting, enjoy typical Japanese specialities (almost exclusively fish dishes) which are showcased on an extensive menu.

Name: Il Mecenate
Description: Occupying the premises of a historic local laundry along the city “moat”, this authentic trattoria has a friendly, convivial ambience. The menu showcases local dishes to the full, including specialities such as “tordelli lucchesi” (ravioli stuffed with different meats, thyme and nutmeg and always served with a meat ragù), tripe and bread pudding, the original recipe of which dates back to the 18C. A picturesque outdoor terrace facing San Francesco church and an excellent wine selection complete the picture.

Name: Da Giacomo
Description: This is a small restaurant in the historic centre of a picturesque walled town; the environment is one of rusticity and modernity. Interestingly reinterpreted local cuisine.

Name: Radici
Description: Accursio Craparo from the nearby Michelin-starred Accursio restaurant is the chef at the helm at Radici. In two simple yet elegant dining rooms, he serves more traditional and authentically Sicilian cuisine than at Accursio, offering guests the opportunity to sample dishes created by a great chef at a reasonable price.

Name: La Pajara Gourmet
Address: via Venezia 28, Fiera di Primiero, 38054, Italy
Description: Situated within the Castel Pietra hotel, this pleasant restaurant with a combination of traditional and modern decor serves contemporary-style meat (often with a regional focus) and fish dishes which represent the different origins of the restaurant owners: the husband comes from Salento, while the wife is from the mountains.

Name: ME Restaurant
Address: SP per Vibo Marina, località Ponte di Ferro, Pizzo, 89812, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying an old restored farmhouse, this large, spacious and attractive restaurant is run by a couple who offer their guests Mediterranean cuisine which is full of flavour. The focus here is on the traditions of Calabria, but the chef’s native region of Campania is also evident in many of the dishes.

Name: Teresa
Address: piazza Lido di Pegli 5 r, Pegli, 16156, Italy
Description: Over half a century has passed since this restaurant was opened in 1968 by “mamma” Teresa and “papa” Giuseppe – and it’s still going strong! And although the staff here are proud of the restaurant’s long history and sense of tradition, they are not bound by it, as demonstrated by dishes that have successfully moved with the times, incorporating modern touches to the classic recipes, while always retaining a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients (especially when it comes to choosing fish).

Name: Parizzi
Description: Based around carefully chosen ingredients sourced from the best local producers, the cuisine served at this restaurant is light and yet tasty. You’ll find typical Parma dishes on the menu here alongside more creative fare, with a slight emphasis on fish and seafood although meat and game (one of the chef’s passions!) also make an appearance. Together with his wife Cristina who oversees the front of house, chef Marco Parizzi continues his family’s tradition of providing a warm welcome and excellent cuisine. Guestrooms (this is a convenient central location) are also available.

Name: L'Oste e il Sacrestano
Description: A small welcoming restaurant full of Sicilian charm. Chiara welcomes guests front of house, and Peppe works in the kitchen creating fine, traditional cuisine reinterpreted with his own personal touch.

Name: Jamantè
Address: via San Vito 97, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Located not far from the historic centre and the picturesque Lama Monachile beach, Jamantè is an elegant restaurant with well-spaced-out tables perfect for a stylish night out. With a focus on fish and seafood, the dishes have their roots in Puglian traditions yet have been successfully reinterpreted with personalised touches by the chef.

Name: Nidaba
Description: Andrea and Daniela, the young and enthusiastic team at Nidaba, have created a modern restaurant with a cosmopolitan feel despite its location in the provinces. It offers contemporary cuisine, as well as French fries, sandwiches and gourmet hamburgers. There is also a new cocktail bar and a good choice of beers, with around 200 different varieties available on tap every year. An excellent address, which is justly rewarded by its popularity.

Name: Corsaro Nero
Address: Località Portu Maga, Marina di Arbus, 09031, Italy
Description: A wide choice of fresh fish and a menu with a firm focus on fish and seafood served in a large dining room offering views of the spectacular sunsets.

Name: Armani/Ristorante
Description: Elegant and carefully prepared contemporary cuisine served on the seventh floor of a palazzo which is totally dedicated to the world of Armani. Superb views of Milan combine with a decor of black marble and backlit onyx to create an exclusive and fashionable ambience.

Name: Cucina Bacilieri
Description: There are just a few tables in this excellent restaurant, which takes its name from its owner - chef. It serves modern and occasionally creative cuisine with strong links to typical regional specialities, such as eel and pasticcio ferrarese (a baked pasta dish).

Name: Hostaria del Teatro
Address: via Ordanino 5b, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: This welcoming restaurant with an open-view kitchen serves cuisine influenced by the traditions of Mantova and the Veneto, alongside more creative dishes inspired by the chef’s imagination. The chef’s wife provides a friendly welcome front of house, plus there’s a delightful garden for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: La Meridiana
Description: In business for over 50 years, this long-established, centrally located restaurant has changed its look over the years and is now a modern bistro with an attractive outdoor summer space overlooking the magical town centre. Here, the owner-chef serves fish prepared in two different ways, either in typical Italian tradition or in a style inspired by his native Spain – his paella is definitely worth sampling! The front of house is overseen by the owner’s friendly wife, who is also at hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: Achilli al Parlamento
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Parliament building, this elegant restaurant’s origins as a wine bar are visible in the many wine bottles that line the walls of the dining room. Various tasting menus feature creative dishes with the occasional influence from Campania in top-quality cuisine that is rooted in traditional flavours. There’s a huge choice of wines by the glass, while bottles can be chosen directly from the wine boutique. In the room nearest the entrance, you’ll find the bistro which serves simpler fare and is also open at lunchtime.

Name: Osteria Il Bagatto
Address: via XX Settembre 16, Limone Piemonte, 12015, Italy
Description: In a typical mountain - style ambience, enjoy carefully prepared cuisine made by a skilful chef using the best ingredients. The menu includes a good choice of regional specialities, as well as fish dishes and imaginative contemporary fare.

Name: Da Gerry
Description: At this centrally located, contemporary - style trattoria sample local dishes, and much more besides. It also offers excellent accommodation. The Da Gerry’s bedrooms are both comfortable and spacious.

Name: Ruris
Address: Via Spiaggie Rosse, località Mazzotta, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
Description: Despite its rural setting inland, this restaurant is still situated within the Capo Rizzuto e Mar Ionio protected marine reserve, which helps to explain the focus on fish and seafood dishes demonstrated by owner-chef Natale Pallone on the menu. The wine cellar boasts over 200 different wines and more than 60 internationally renowned spirits.

Name: Ai Campi di Marcello
Description: Not far from the shipyards, simple but pleasant atmosphere in a family-run restaurant with good seafood options. Among the many specialties, we recommend the cold soup with raw and cooked fish. Curious note: the owner's passion for rum translates into an intriguing and unexpected selection of this liqueur.

Name: Da Nando
Description: The whole family is involved in running this typical trattoria, which has become one of the standard - bearers of the region. The decor is classic and elegant, while the menu focuses on local specialities such as excellent hams, good fish and, in season, superb truffles. The huge wine cellar is home to 120 000 bottles, so you are bound to find a wine that suits!

Name: Le Case della Saracca
Description: Situated in the delightful Saracca district (Monforte’s old historic centre), this restaurant occupies an old, restored house with a glass and steel decor that provides a harmonious contrast with the building’s original features. Tables are arranged on different levels connected by a series of vertiginous staircases. Quiet and intimate, the restaurant serves a dual purpose: there’s a wine bar for aperitifs, while the dining room provides the backdrop for dishes from the region and further afield. Superb wine list with various labels available by the glass, plus guestrooms that offer the chance to spend the night in this unique setting.

Name: Gasthofstube Stafler
Description: This restaurant situated in the splendid Stafler hotel on the road to Austria is perfect for a romantic dinner, with a comfortable Stube-style dining room and an internal garden for fine weather. Friendly and welcoming staff and traditional Tyrolean cuisine with a focus on ingredients from the Isarco valley, plus interesting personal twists added by the chef.

Name: La Caprese
Address: via Garibaldi 7, località Borghetto, Mozzo, 24030, Italy
Description: Since 1975 one of the local points of reference for seafood enthusiasts. The name alludes to the owners’ origins in Campania, which takes shape in some recipes with markedly Mediterranean and especially Campania flavors and colors.

Name: L'Osteria H20
Address: via Pergola 10, Moniga del Garda, 25080, Italy
Description: This bright, minimalist - style restaurant is situated on the road but its dining room faces the lake. It serves imaginative and personalised cuisine with both fish and meat dishes on the menu.

Name: Cantine Cattaneo
Address: strada Vicinale della Madonetta 1, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Not far from the town centre yet in a surprisingly bucolic setting, this restaurant preceded by its own vegetable garden occupies the premises of an old olive oil cellar dating from 1590. In a pleasantly rustic and romantic dining room adorned with decorations, enjoy skilful reinterpretations of traditional Ligurian cuisine, with the occasional exotic dish also making an appearance on the menu. Dishes include “prebugiun” (wild plants) and specialities grilled over an olive-wood fire.

Name: Osteria Billis
Description: The former bar of the railway station (situated in the park next to the station) has been transformed into this glass-fronted restaurant with a terrace for summer dining. Exciting, personalised dishes based around regional traditions and seasonal ingredients feature on the menu here.

Name: DaV  Mare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The classic, wrought-iron outdoor dining space at this restaurant overlooks one of the most romantic little squares in Italy, while the view takes in the promontory dominated by its castle – a picture-postcard view that is famous around the world. The experienced Cerea family from the famous three-starred Michelin Da Vittoria restaurant in Bergamo are at the helm, serving consistently top-quality cuisine whether you’re here for a quick lunch or a gourmet dinner. It’s best to book ahead as the few tables are much in demand!

Name: Duo
Description: In this restaurant housed in a historic palazzo in the centre of Chiavari, the owners have used the structural beauty of the building to showcase the skills of local artisans, resulting in a very attractive ambience. The modern cuisine is simple in style, allowing all the flavour of the ingredients to shine through.

Name: Hazama
Description: Japanese cuisine served in a small restaurant where both the cuisine and decor are minimalist in style. Here, young chef Satoshi Hazama creates light dishes full of Japanese flavour, all made from top-quality ingredients. The kaiseki menu served in the evening consists of seven or nine different courses.

Name: Michelasso
Description: Situated in the city centre, this refined restaurant with an elegantly classic decor is perfect for a romantic, intimate dinner. The menu features meat and fish, with traditional dishes reinterpreted thanks to the chef’s expertise and proven experience. In summer, choose a table on the pleasant outdoor space overlooking the lively Via Santa Brigida.

Name: Aquadulcis
Address: contrada Tenda, Vallo della Lucania, 84078, Italy
Description: Following careful restoration, this old mill has been transformed into a gourmet restaurant with just a few tables. Here, skilful young chef Vincenzo Cucolo delights guests with his cuisine – a combination of creative dishes and old recipes focusing on traditional Cilento ingredients.

Name: Agriturismo Il Cavallino
Address: SP 55 Saturnia-Semproniano, località Fibbianello, Semproniano, 58055, Italy
Description: Situated in a very quiet and secluded location, this restaurant is run by an enthusiastic young couple: he has inherited the family business and, having gained experience in other restaurants in the region, is now at the helm in the kitchen, while his partner oversees the front of house. The options on the à la carte and wine list, the latter featuring a small yet impressive choice of wines, have a strong regional focus.

Name: Hosteria Toblino
Address: via Garda 3, Sarche di Madruzzo, 38070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The most welcoming section of the extensive Cantina Toblino complex is home to the large, contemporary and minimalist-style Hosteria. Here, a young chef serves simple reinterpretations of regional dishes with a focus on zero-mile produce with the occasional yet astute use of ingredients from further afield.

Name: 20 Posti
Description: A small bistro-style restaurant with an evening lounge bar, situated in a narrow alleyway in the town centre. The young team here serve imaginative Mediterranean meat and fish dishes prepared from an array of carefully chosen ingredients.

Name: La Maison du Gourmet
Description: Housed in a fully renovated old farm in the countryside outside Parma, this gourmet restaurant serves top-quality meat and fish dishes with a focus on creativity rather than local traditions. The starters are particularly delicious!

Name: La Ciotola
Description: Situated along the SS13 which leads to nearby Pordenone, this restaurant has a fresh, busy feel. At lunchtime, the service is quicker, the menu smaller and the prices lower, while in the evening guests can choose from a full menu. Whether you’re here for lunch or dinner, you’ll enjoy meat and fish dishes made by the Cover brothers from top-quality ingredients and prepared simply yet with an imaginative touch.

Name: Motelombroso
Description: An old, carefully restored road worker’s house on the Alzaia Naviglio Pavese canal is the setting for this modern, stylish restaurant where Alessandra and Matteo welcome guests in a graceful, elegant and yet informal manner. The menu features contemporary meat and fish dishes accompanied by a good choice of wines. If you’re curious about the restaurant’s name, ask the owners for an explanation: could it be something to do with the private dining room perhaps?

Name: La Taverna di Bacco
Description: A small restaurant just a stone’s throw from the sea which is memorable for its chic decor and intimate ambience. The cuisine combines traditional influences with an innovative approach resulting in ambitious, creative and modern dishes. The wine list is particularly worthy of note.

Name: Casa Coloni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated opposite the archaeological site, this restaurant occupies an old farmhouse which is part of a splendid 19C residence converted into an elegant hotel following a long and meticulous restoration. In fine weather, tables are set out under a cane pergola in a charming setting in the romantic garden. Here, the chef from Paestum serves his own reinterpretations of regional dishes with superb results. Impeccable service.

Name: Ad Astra
Address: via Cavour 11/13, Santa Maria della Versa, 27047, Italy
Description: This small yet smart restaurant in the Oltrepò Pavese region is a dream come true for owner-chef Alessandro Folli, whose cuisine shows the influence of his experience working in different restaurants around Europe. Ad Astra delights guests with dishes which demonstrate a perfect balance between modern and classic culinary styles. Bravo!

Name: Marechiaro
Description: This smart, elegant restaurant, which has a particularly romantic ambience in the evening, has been serving top-quality fish in Bolzano for over 20 years. Prepared in traditional Italian style, the dishes here focus on the flavour and quality of the fish and seafood on offer, most of which comes from the Mediterranean. The two friendly brothers who run the restaurant are originally from Naples, which explains the specialities from Campania and the excellent pizza which also features on the menu. A simpler selection of dishes is available at lunchtime.

Name: L'Armadillo
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Modern Cuisine
Description: Situated in the district of Palaud at the foot of Mont Blanc, this small wine bar with a tranquil ambience serves interesting cuisine prepared by a talented Japanese chef who adds his own personal twist to the valley’s top-quality ingredients. Dishes include a delicate tempura served with tongue or beef, plus some exquisite desserts, while wine is chosen directly from the shelves in the dining room. Booking is recommended in high season.

Name: Antica Trattoria Centro
Description: Situated in the heart of Levanto just a stone’s throw from the sea, this trattoria serving traditional fish and seafood (as well as a few meat options) has been run by the same owners for almost 20 years. Friendly ambience, good service, plus a few tables in a small outdoor space which need to be booked well in advance.

Name: MoS
Address: via Porto Vecchio 28, Desenzano del Garda, 25015, Italy
Description: The young Stefano Zanini, with plenty of experience in Italy and further afield, has injected new life into this old trattoria situated right in front of the marina in the historic heart of Desenzano. The personalised cuisine focuses on seasonal ingredients, including meat and fish from the lake and sea; one of the restaurant’s key tenets is recycling waste as much as possible. In summer, dine at one of the outdoor tables with views of the boats in the marina.

Name: Mater Bistrot
Description: An informal bistro where the imaginative cuisine prepared by the owner-chef showcases the best Italian recipes while remaining open to influences from other parts of the world, resulting in strong, unique and captivating flavours. Guests also have the option of smaller dishes to share, but if you really want to get to know the essence of this restaurant, it’s best to go for the guided menu.

Name: Augurio
Address: via Dietro le Mura B 16, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: Opened by three brothers (Augurio is the family name), this restaurant in the city centre successfully combines the traditional and the modern in both its cuisine and its decor. The dining room, with an open-view kitchen on the ground floor, boasts an old, vaulted ceiling, while its wood furniture adds a contemporary look. The menu features local and Italian dishes reinterpreted with flavour and style. Lighter options are available at lunchtime; the grande carte needs to be ordered ahead of time.

Name: Osteria della Foce
Description: This simple restaurant stands out for its delicious, authentic cuisine which is influenced by Ligurian and Italian traditions alike. The culinary techniques used are classic, both in its meat dishes (the roast veal is excellent) and fish options (raw fish dishes often feature on the menu). First courses include a home-made bronze-cut pasta (“trafilata al bronzo”) which is served with sauces inspired by whatever is in season or available in the market.

Name: Bottega Culinaria
Address: contrada Pontoni 72, San Vito Chietino, 66038, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid a charming landscape of olive groves, this restaurant is not particularly easy to find, so make sure that you use a satnav or ask for directions when booking. A simple, minimalist-style dining room provides the backdrop for imaginative cuisine which includes plenty of vegetables and is full of contrasting flavours and reinterpreted regional influences.

Name: All’Ombra del Gabbiano
Description: This friendly Mediterranean-style bistro started out 20 years ago as an inn-cum- -cicchetteria (a type of Venetian tapas bar). It now offers 100% gluten-free recipes, including a few vegan options, without compromising in any way on the quality or beautiful presentation of the dishes featured on its well-constructed menu. Friendly, attentive service and summer outdoor dining in the pedestrianised area add to the appeal.

Name: Osteria degli Angeli
Description: An attractive restaurant which offers a friendly and informal welcome and service, alongside an elegant, personalised yet classic decor. The cuisine is mainly Mediterranean in flavour, emphasised by the use of local and seasonal ingredients. The self-taught chef here is passionate about his cuisine.

Name: Antica Farmacia
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant was used as a pharmacy until the late 1970s. In 2010, it was taken over by owner-chef Juri who now runs his own restaurant here, serving Tuscan-inspired cuisine made using local ingredients and recipes which he reinterprets with a light touch. Full of flavour, dishes include highlights such as baked marrow and Tuscan Chianti beef stew.

Name: Locanda Marchesani
Description: In addition to specialities such as oysters and caviar, this restaurant serves sophisticated classic, traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist. Choose between à la carte options or tasting menus prepared with refined ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Casa Fantini/Lake Time
Description: Situated on the lakefront in the attractive town of Pella, this modern and welcoming restaurant occupies an old building which has been restored and furnished with a stylish and harmonious decor. Offering simpler options at lunchtime, the restaurant serves traditional cuisine reinterpreted and presented with a contemporary flavour. A lounge, garden, swimming pool and 11 guestrooms add to the exclusive appeal.

Name: Pepenero
Address: piazza del Duomo 4, San Miniato, 56028, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: In its new home in Piazza del Duomo, in beautiful San Miniato, in the hands of chef Gilberto Rossi Pepenero continues to serve cuisine that showcases the best ingredients (both meat and fish) from this bountiful region, with delicacies such as excellent truffles featuring on the menu throughout the year. Prepared with a light and modern touch, meals are served in a spacious dining room where the many windows offer glimpses of the town centre.

Name: Terrazza Fiorella
Address: via Vincenzo Maggio 5, Massa Lubrense, 80061, Italy
Description: Housed in the Villa Fiorella Art Hotel, this restaurant boasts a stunningly located terrace with spectacular views of the Bay of Naples and its islands. The cuisine pays tribute to Campania and its top-quality ingredients which the chef uses to create imaginative dishes reinterpreted with his own personal twist.

Name: Al Cjasal
Address: via Nazionale 30, località San Giorgio al Tagliamento, San Michele al Tagliamento, 30028, Italy
Description: A new generation is now at the helm in this warm and elegant restaurant decorated with a profusion of wood, adding a more modern touch to the cuisine while maintaining its regional character and excellent local ingredients. The menu has its own unique flavour thanks to the option of numerous cicchetti (tapas-style snacks) options available, either in half- or full portions, enabling guests to create their own menu.

Name: Lineadombra
Address: Ponte dell'Umiltà, sestiere Dorsoduro 19, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Boasting a splendid location with an outdoor dining space on a kind of raft-cum-platform, this restaurant boasts one of the most delightful views in Venice, with the Giudecca on the opposite side of the canal. Contemporary cuisine with a focus on fish and the occasional creative twist.

Name: Mirepuà Food Lab
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval village with a castle in the Monferrato hills, this restaurant serves classic Piedmontese cuisine with plenty of meat options, alongside a few specialities from the chef’s native Liguria. Raw fish, Piedmontese-style fritto misto and grilled meat and vegetables are available by prior reservation.

Name: Filo
Description: This restaurant boasts a superb lakeside location, offering views of the opposite shore, Comacina island and Villa Balbianello. The experience is enhanced by the modern cuisine, in which dishes from all over Italy are created by the young chef from Campania, from the opening appetisers to the coffee-paired desserts at the end of the meal. The recipes are sophisticated without being overly complicated, offering a choice of tasting menus or à la carte options. The full flavours of Italian cuisine delight the palate, while the beautiful presentation provides a feast for the eyes.

Name: Podere Belvedere Tuscany
Address: via San Piero a Strada 23, Pontassieve, 50065, Italy
Description: Occupying a tower house dating from 1700, this restaurant is surrounded by typical Tuscan scenery of olive groves and vineyards, as well as vegetable gardens and farms which produce many of the ingredients featuring in the dishes here. The friendly self-taught chef celebrates the best of Tuscan country cuisine, with a focus on meat, including grilled dishes and top-quality vegetables, as well as the occasional more creative dish – the result is cuisine of a very high standard. The restaurant also has a few guestrooms – a convenient option given the property’s attractive secluded location.

Name: Gimmi Restaurant
Address: via San Pietro in Lama 23, Lecce, 73100, Italy
Description: Despite its location in a Dominican monastery dating from 1442 (also home to a boutique hotel), this restaurant is decidedly modern and minimalist in style, with a light-coloured floor, imposing stone columns, a cross-vaulted ceiling, and a dining room with a view of the glass-fronted wine display. The service here is friendly, attentive and highly efficient, while the top-quality cuisine includes highly recommended specialities such as Capelli d’angelo Benedetto Cavalieri, angel-hair pasta with mantis shrimp, seaweed spaghetti, Galateo saffron, celery and sweet pepper.

Name: Locanda La Raia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The magnificent biodynamic La Raia farm, an enchanting 180-hectare oasis between Novi Ligure and Gavi, is home to a contemporary art foundation, the Rossi Cairo family winery, a Steiner school for employees’ children, guest accommodation, and this restaurant which benefits from a fertile ecosystem that provides much of its zero-mile produce. The cuisine is rooted in local traditions which have been reinterpreted in contemporary style. In the evening (and at lunchtime at weekends), choose between an à la carte, a tasting menu inspired by wines from the property’s estates between Gavi and Langhe, and a delicious “Sei mezze” menu featuring small samples of the restaurant’s most iconic dishes.

Name: Innocenti Wine Experiences
Description: As you enter this restaurant, you’re struck by the sight of hundreds of bottles of wine lining the walls. First and foremost a wine bar, Innocenti Wine Experiences is transformed into a restaurant for lunch and dinner, serving creative cuisine which focuses mainly on meat dishes with the occasional elaborate and original twist. There’s obviously no problem choosing your wine – just look around you!

Name: Caffè delle Rose Bistrot
Description: Occupying an early 20C building in the heart of Pallanza’s picturesque historic centre, this authentic bistro now has a young and contemporary feel. Run by Massimiliano Celeste, a talented chef who is very well known in the region, the restaurant specialises in Mediterranean cuisine prepared with a touch of imagination. There’s a small chef’s table in front of the kitchen, plus an old ice-house (now a small wine cellar housing some excellent wines) which is well worth visiting.

Name: L'Insolita Trattoria Tre Soldi
Description: A long-established trattoria opened by a married couple in the 1950s and now run by their son Lorenzo who serves highly personalised cuisine with a focus on local ingredients. The dishes have amusing and entertaining names such as “Amici per la pelle” (“Friends for life”), “Non è un pomodoro” (“This isn’t a tomato”), and “Solo un chicco di caffè” (“Just one coffee bean”). In addition to a classic menu, an intriguing "Unconventional Experience" is offered, in which guests have to guess the ingredients of the dishes by following some clues.

Name: Cucine Nervi
Description: Housed within the Cantine Nervi in the town centre, this contemporary restaurant with a completely open kitchen offers guests the choice of eating at the large counter facing the kitchen or at one of the more traditional tables. Very chic ambience, with a focus on imaginative and creative cuisine.

Name: Giano
Description: Conveniently situated in a quiet setting just behind Via Vittorio Veneto, Giano is housed within the modern Hotel W with which it shares a comfortable cocktail bar and attractive garden. The atmosphere here is modern and informal, with simple fare served at lunchtime and more gourmet dining options in the evening. The resident chef is supported by skilful and experienced Ciccio Sultano who provides valuable input on menus and ingredients. Iconic dishes such as the spaghetto taratatà (with a tuna and bottarga sauce), the em>caponada, and the carpacci are highly recommended, as are desserts such as the reinterpreted millefoglie . Sicilian cuisine takes pride of place here and the service is excellent.

Name: L'Ambasciata
Address: piazzetta Ambasciatori del Gusto 1, Quistello, 46026, Italy
Description: This has long been one of those restaurants in Italy where the opulent interior decor has no equal – at Christmas, the mirrors, rugs, silverware, chandeliers and piles of books are joined by the largest and most ornate Christmas tree that you’ll ever see in a restaurant. The cuisine created by owner-chef Matteo Ugolotti is inspired by Mantuan traditions and the restaurant’s previous famous owners, occasionally going all the way back to the Renaissance. Special mention should be made of the extraordinary chocolate salami – a dessert coated with a delicious, frothy, warm zabaglione poured from a copper pan at your table. The menu also features more modern recipes and tasting menus.

Name: Maxi
Address: via Luigi Serio 8, SS 145 Sorrentina km 14,500, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: From the entrance to the Capo la Gala hotel, you head down to the seafront to this restaurant, where a long terrace overlooks the rocks – if you’re looking for a romantic place to eat, this is one of the best options on this coastline (there’s also an indoor dining room for inclement weather). The cuisine is equal to the setting, thanks to the chef from Ischia who skilfully creates imaginative dishes using ingredients from Campania.

Name: Tuorlo
Description: Decorated in elegant bistro style and skilfully renovated with contemporary furnishings, Tuorlo serves dishes based on traditional Piedmontese recipes reinterpreted with modern techniques and personal touches. Good choice of wines, plus an attractive little courtyard to the rear for relaxed summer dining.

Name: Alessandro Feo
Address: via Angelo Lista 24, Marina di Casal Velino, 84040, Italy
Description: In a beautiful stone-vaulted building (an old 17C monastery) on the town’s seafront promenade, young owner-chef Alessandro Feo has made his mark in this region that perhaps has fewer gourmet restaurants than many places elsewhere. Here, he creates dishes that combine traditional influences and classic favourites from Campania with his own individual flair and creativity. His focus is on local, seasonal ingredients, including produce from his two kitchen gardens and fish sourced from local fishermen as well as from his own ventures out to sea.

Name: La Tavola Rossa di Vincenzo Guarino
Description: With just ten seats and an open-view kitchen, this restaurant literally reduces the space between chef Vincenzo Guarino and his guests in order to guarantee an interactive dining experience. There’s just one tasting menu with a strict focus on home-made ingredients, including delicious bread and rolls.

Name: iPalici
Address: via Antonello da Messina 3, Viagrande, 95029, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated behind Acireale at the foot of Mount Etna National Park, this restaurant is located within the Relais San Giuliano. Deceptively uninteresting from the outside, this historic building and its inner courtyards boast a charm and grandeur that will take your breath away. A huge 16C wine press provides the backdrop for fine cuisine that is more than equal to its impressive setting. Here, the menu makes full use of vegetables and other Sicilian ingredients in dishes that are influenced by the island’s culinary traditions yet reinterpreted with a skilful contemporary twist by the chef.

Name: Da Carla
Address: via Necchi 3/5, fraz. Molino Isella, Gambolò, 27025, Italy
Description: Once a mill, this restaurant still stands next to its old canal which lends the setting a delightful bucolic ambience echoed in the warm, welcoming dining room. Highlights on the menu include risottos, frog’s legs, snails and goose - based dishes, as well as cured meats. Inviting guestrooms complete this delightfully rustic picture.

Name: Rada Rooftop
Description: Right at the end of Positano beach, and above the ground-floor night club, this restaurant on the first floor of an old fishermen’s warehouse offers breathtaking views of the village and the sea. Creative cuisine inspired by Mediterranean traditions.

Name: Sa Corte
Description: Local gastronomic traditions are demonstrated at their best in this rustic restaurant, which serves delicious pasta, excellent meat and fragrant Sardinian wines. Our favourite dishes include the goat kid with artichokes and the almond and flower petal desserts.

Name: Opera
Address: via Sant'Antonio da Padova 3, Turin, 10121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The former nineteenth century refectory of the nearby church has become the laboratory of a chef who is as skillful as he is creative: wrapped in the warm atmosphere of the brickwork of the evocative dining room, all the dishes have fruit as a recurring ingredient, which adds a touch of acidity and flavor to dishes of creative cuisine, whether of meat or fish, further enhanced by the work of an excellent sommelier.

Name: Grual
Address: via Alpe di Grual 16, Pinzolo, 38086, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed within the Lefay Resort & Spa Dolomiti, an elegant hotel that dominates Pinzolo and is one of the best hotels in the Trentino region, this gourmet restaurant takes its name from the mountain behind the hotel (the Grual). Here, in the evening, chef Matteo Maezza serves his own reinterpretations of typical mountain cuisine inspired by the three different altitudes from which he sources his ingredients. For example, the bottom of the valley (“fondovalle”) is the inspiration for his marinated whitefish from Lake Garda, served with different types of turnip and Mugo pine milk; the Alpine pasture region (“alpeggio”) has inspired the delicious rib of beef with mustard and carrots; while the high mountain area (“alta montagna”) is behind the elaborate saddle of venison with cardoon gratin with a beef marrow and creamed rye crust. There’s also an impressive wine list featuring an impressive selection of champagnes.

Name: Radici Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Having moved to the pedestrianised section of historic Gallarate, Radici Osteria Contemporanea has also adopted a new look, with a lounge-bar ambience that is young and trendy, making it the perfect setting for its aperitifs and superb cocktails. The restaurant’s excellent, modern and personalised cuisine remains unchanged, however.

Name: Langosteria Paraggi
Address: via Paraggi a Mare 1, Paraggi, 16038, Italy
Description: The elegant Milanese style of the famous Langosteria restaurant has been given a maritime and holiday feel in its seasonal sibling which is housed within the Bagni Fiore overlooking the small yet stunning Paraggi bay. Langosteria Paraggi boasts a vintage decor which is at the same time glamorous and up-to-date, views of the beach and the sea, and a menu focusing on delicious fresh fish and seafood such as oysters and shellfish.

Name: Aprudia
Description: At this restaurant in the historic centre, where the vaulted brick ceiling provides a striking contrast with the modern furnishings, the chef celebrates the seasons through a whole range of ingredients to create truly delicious cuisine. Interesting tasting menus add to its appeal.

Name: Bros' Trattoria
Description: Eat amid the verdant surroundings of a large, beautifully kept garden planted with olive trees and embellished with subtle lighting, wooden tables and straw-seated chairs. The highlight here is the wood-fired oven in which nearly all the specialities (available on a single daily menu) are cooked. The strictly traditional dishes include options such as the region’s classic “pucia” bread.

Name: Mammaròssa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant, owner-chef Franco Franciosi focuses on the Abruzzo in dishes which are both traditional and modern. The cuisine showcases the best ingredients from the region, including home-grown vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden and excellent bread made with solina wheat (typical of the Apennines), amid a decor that focuses on sustainability. Daniela looks after guests front of house, offering recommendations from the short yet carefully chosen wine list.

Name: Marelet
Description: The name of this restaurant discreetly hidden away in an alleyway on the edge of the town centre is a dialect word meaning “old bachelor”. Small tables set close together give the ambience of a French brasserie and provide the setting for modern, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, including salads, tapas and sandwiches, while more choice is available in the evening. Lively atmosphere.

Name: Hostaria del Vicolo
Description: Situated in a central yet secluded location, this intimate and elegant restaurant serves typical Sicilian cuisine with a focus on fish, vegetables from the kitchen garden and delicious cheeses. A good wine selection completes the picture.

Name: Antinè
Description: Manuel Bouchard’s cuisine impressed our inspectors thanks to striking features such as his minimalist approach and the use of just a few well-chosen ingredients. Traditional recipes, such as plin pasta and Fassona beef, feature on the menu alongside more alternative, imaginative dishes (including fresh- and saltwater fish). This elegant restaurant is located on the first floor of a building in the old town, just a stone’s throw from the medieval tower. A warm welcome and an excellent wine list complete the picture.

Name: Il Giardino delle Esperidi
Description: The ideal starting point for an exploration of the area. In summer one dines on the terrace located in the heart of the historic centre while drinks and cigars may be enjoyed in the lounge bar.

Name: Sarti del Gusto
Address: via Vico II Vincenzo Sulis 1/a, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description: A small, beautifully maintained restaurant offering a concise selection of carefully prepared and attractively presented dishes. The cuisine here is often creative yet inspired by Sardinian traditions, with an equal focus on meat and fish.

Name: Maré
Address: via Molo di Levante 74, Cesenatico, 47042, Italy
Description: An unexpected gourmet restaurant in a typical private beach club on the Romagna coast, with a dining room that opens on to the beach with its long line of beach umbrellas. The dishes here are carefully prepared and occasionally creative, and all of good quality. We particularly recommend the monfettini (fresh egg pasta) mantecati with cuttlefish, clams, mantis shrimp and ink, which looks like a risotto and is absolutely delicious. The restaurant also boasts a good wine list with an excellent choice of champagnes.

Name: Marina Grande
Description: Establishment on the beach: wooden floors and white chairs in the linear room, where you can sample the traditional country cuisine; pleasant terrace for service in summer.

Name: Villa Baroni
Description: This romantic restaurant on the lakeshore has a welcoming, elegant ambience and a delightful terrace for summer dining. The cuisine pays particular attention to top-quality, seasonal ingredients prepared in traditional recipes with a focus on fish. Cosy, Provençal-style guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Loewengrube
Description: This building has been home to a restaurant since the 16C, making it one of the oldest in Bolzano. Today it houses an elegant restaurant that serves a balanced combination of traditional local dishes and Mediterranean options, the latter including a few fish-based recipes such as the octopus and fish soup. The attractive wine cellar boasts a selection of approximately 1 000 wines from the region and elsewhere in Italy, as well as a choice of labels from further afield.

Name: La Porta Restaurant
Address: piazza Vieira de Mello 4, Bologna, 40128, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a futuristic building, La Porta Restaurant is a multi - purpose establishment which offers a bar for aperitifs and a highly modern cigar room, as well as a well - stocked wine cellar offering the best wines from Italy and elsewhere. The cuisine is creative with a particular focus on fish recipes, while lighter options are available in the Café from 7. 30am to 7pm.

Name: La Veranda del Color
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This aptly named restaurant in the Color Hotel just a short distance from Lake Garda boasts a modern, colourful decor and cuisine worthy of its name. Dishes are inspired by Mediterranean traditions and are showcased on a number of different tasting menus.

Name: Gimmy's
Description: Traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist, with a whole page of the menu dedicated to meat dishes. Meals are served in an attractive Stube-style room with a warm mountain ambience.

Name: Il Caminetto
Description: Situated just 100m from the Albergo Villa Canu in the typical small town of Cabras, this restaurant serves traditional fish and seafood dishes from the island, as well as meat options (first and second courses), delicious antipasti and Sardinian desserts.

Name: Il Focarile
Address: via Pontina al km 46,5, Aprilia, 04011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The sumptuous entrance gives an elegant tone to a large bright dining room with well spaced out tables; a touch of Tuscany with a cuisine rich in tradition and also imagination. Now offers new, elegant rooms.

Name: San Martino 26
Address: via San Martino 26, San Gimignano, 53037, Italy
Description: Occupying the wine cellars of an old palazzo in the historic centre, this restaurant has a fashionable feel with just a few tables and a selection of contemporary - style dishes inspired by classic recipes (from Tuscany and elsewhere) on the menu.

Name: La Stella Marina di Montecristo
Description: A simple seafood osteria in both appearance and style, run by friendly and welcoming staff. Guests can rely on the owner’s recommendations when choosing from the fish and seafood dishes, which are simple but generously portioned and reasonably priced.

Name: Al Caminetto
Description: A village trattoria with a vocation for the simplest and rustic Abruzzo cuisine; local dishes, then, drawing on farming and shepherding with charcoal grilling that naturally appears in all the meat-based dishes, sausages, steaks, lamb, mutton, arrosticini, chicken and so on... Ingredients and recipes of the backcountry, which–however–start feeling the effect of some flavors of the nearby Lazio region.

Name: Pescarino-Sapori di Terra e di Mare
Description: This warm, welcoming restaurant with a wooden ceiling and walls serves simple dishes as well as more creative, elaborate fare. The focus here is on showcasing the top-quality ingredients used (especially fish and seafood) in dishes which are influenced by Liguria, as well as elsewhere in Italy. Given the secluded location, the guestrooms on offer here are a good option.

Name: Osteria Taviani
Address: piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 28, Bientina, 56031, Italy
Description: This pleasant, warmly decorated restaurant is run with passion and enthusiasm by Elena and Alessandro, the former supervising the front of house, the latter at the helm in the kitchen. The cuisine here is modern and full of flavour, with a focus on meat dishes (although a few fish options also feature) with their roots firmly anchored in Tuscan traditions (such as the fried steak). During the hunting season, the contemporary-style game dishes are particularly delicious. The wine list includes a few French labels.

Name: Pescheria
Description: The name of this restaurant between the historic centre and the seafront refers to the main item on its menu, which is dedicated almost exclusively to fish (fresh and not farmed). Fish and shellfish are displayed in a glass cabinet and aquarium respectively, both of which are situated to the rear of the long, narrow dining room near the open-view kitchen. Classic fish dishes full of flavour (served raw, baked, cooked in salt, in water or grilled) are to the fore here.

Name: Ca' Mia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This welcoming restaurant in the hills surrounding Lake Alserio makes guests feel completely at home. The two young chefs with plenty of experience behind them create modern dishes with a preference for quick cooking methods and a focus on a wood-fired oven and barbecue, as well as fermented ingredients.

Name: La Locanda del Cardinale
Description: A medieval house with stone arches, built over the remains of mosaics from a Roman villa – the location alone makes this restaurant truly memorable. Add to this modern, beautifully prepared cuisine with a focus on regional ingredients, and all that’s left to do is book your table!

Name: Da Cecco
Address: piazza Belvedere Puccini 10/12, Torre del Lago Puccini, 55049, Italy
Description: A cosylittle restaurant at the beginning of the lakefront. Mainly seafood dishes, though in the winter there is also game. Rustic atmosphere.

Name: Meraviglioso Osteria Moderna
Address: largo Gelso 16, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This attractive, welcoming modern restaurant stands in Polignano’s main street, scene of the town’s evening “passeggiata”, not far from the statue of the great Domenico Modugno, a native of this beautiful town. Although the lunch menu is simple in style, it is still inspired by fresh fish and seafood, while in the evening the young yet experienced chef creates more imaginative and inventive fare. There’s a convenient private car park nearby: if you want to take advantage of this, make sure you advise the restaurant of your arrival time.

Name: Il Giardinetto
Address: piazza Garibaldi 10, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Looking out over the calm blue water, this classic restaurant serves traditional cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist. Fish from the lake feature on the menu, as do meat and seafood options with something for everyone. There’s also a small outdoor terrace where guests can enjoy a pre- or post-dinner drink.

Name: KELINA Fine Dine
Address: Strada Lech de Boà s.n., Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: From Corvara, take the ultra-modern Boè cable-car to this restaurant (accessible also on skis or by foot) which is one of the dining options at the Piz Boè Alpine Lounge (for access, turn right as you exit the cable car). Open at lunchtime only, KELINA serves unexpectedly gourmet cuisine in a minimalist-style dining room which allows the stunning views of Sassongher, Santa Croce and La Varella to take centre-stage through the restaurant’s large floor-to-ceiling windows. There’s a restricted choice of dishes, all of which are creative and based on Alpine ingredients, with a new, highly experienced chef at the helm since early 2024. An excellent wine list completes the picture.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: The aptly named Terrazza is a delightful open - air restaurant overlooking Asolo’s historic centre. In an elegant, fashionable ambience enjoy innovative delicacies that nonetheless make full use of the best local traditions and produce. Ideal for a romantic dinner.

Name: Da Peppe
Description: Situated in the historic centre of a small village in the Parco del Pollino, this long - established restaurant has one culinary aim – to keep alive traditional local dishes such as ravioli with nettle tips, lamb with potatoes and lampascioni onions, and ricotta and Stigliano pistachio mousse. Four modern and comfortable guestrooms are also available a few hundred metres away.

Name: Ventuno.1
Description: Closed for renovations until April 2024.Two natives of Campania who have settled in the Langhe run this centrally located restaurant, where the black and white decor has a modern feel. The menu focuses on fish and seafood, in addition to meat dishes and truffles in season.

Name: Da Marino al St Remy
Address: via San Salvatore da Horta 7, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description: Situated on the edge of the pedestrianised area near the Bastione di Saint Remy, this restaurant is named after its charismatic owner Marino, who helps guests with their choice of menu and is happy to tell them all about the history of the restaurant (the street in front of the restaurant, for example, has not always been there). At the helm in the kitchen, his wife Silvana prepares Mediterranean dishes with a Sardinian flavour – the fish and seafood options are particularly delicious.

Name: Filia Ristorante
Description: An intimate and modern restaurant with just five tables and a minimalist design (with the exception of the “hip-hop” bathroom). Filia expresses the full character of its owner Michael Silhavì who has chosen Borgo Trento, a residential district not far from the city centre, in which to fulfil his dream of opening his own restaurant. He serves two tasting menus here (although he also sensibly also offers à la carte options), which are creative in style and occasionally play with traditional recipes such as the “Polpo alla Luciana” octopus dish. Simpler, faster options available at lunchtime. A colourful restaurant in every respect!

Name: Casamare
Description: Elegant and refined, this top-quality restaurant is the perfect choice for special occasions. Vietri ceramics, an open-view kitchen, fish on display and a successful mix of traditional and modern decor all combine to create an atmospheric setting in the dining room. As the restaurant’s name suggests, this is a good option for anyone who enjoys delicious classic fish and seafood dishes (mostly from Campania).

Name: Capriccio
Description: Young chef Graziano Accolla has returned to his native city where he serves creative cuisine of the highest quality, while at the same time raising Augusta’s gastronomic profile. Thanks to his experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, he offers highly interesting dishes which focus on the use of top-quality ingredients.

Name: Soul Kitchen
Address: località Caldè di Castelveccana, Caldè, 21010, Italy
Description: Enjoying an excellent location on a small, picturesque square overlooking the lake, this restaurant boasts a relaxing and beautifully kept outdoor terrace with fine views of the small port. The menu features fish from the lake, as well as meat and seafood dishes – the owner here is a true professional!

Name: La Loggia Bistrò
Description: Slightly off the beaten track yet still in the town centre, this restaurant boasts a courtyard setting for summer dining plus an intimate interior room with just a few small square tables, subtle lighting and an attractive decor featuring old wine bottles. A far cry from the classic tourist fare often available elsewhere, the cuisine served here is imaginatively presented with a focus on the use of seasonal ingredients.

Name: Pietramare Natural Food
Address: SS 106, loc. Praialonga,, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In an elegant setting of dry-stone walls and Mediterranean vegetation, this stylish restaurant boasts personalised decor right down to the smallest detail. The new chef prepares modern dishes inspired by the region and more generally by southern Italy, with a menu that focuses on fish rather than meat, as well as a vegetarian menu. There’s also a charming cigar room with small lounge areas and a fireplace.

Name: Tamo
Description: This new restaurant occupies  a historic palazzo in this small town. Served by the owner (outdoors in summer with views of Città Sant’Angelo in the distance), the cuisine is authentic, unfussy and prepared using top-quality ingredients with a focus on vegetables from a nearby farm.

Name: Remulass
