Description: “Cooking with roots” is the mantra at Remulass, a phrase that has inspired the restaurant’s name (“wild radish” in the local Milanese dialect). This small, lively restaurant gets very busy in the evenings when booking is highly recommended. The attractively modern and colourful dishes here always feature plenty of root vegetables and aromatic herbs. We recommend the fermented vegetables with baked ricotta and a gin dressing.

Name: Osteria del Teatro
Description: Enjoy traditional cuisine served in an elegant 16C dining room with a fireplace or in more informal trattoria-style rooms, all of which are decorated with the same theatrical theme. The recipes here focus on local traditions and seasonal ingredients, resulting in colourful, well-balanced and beautifully presented dishes that are full of flavour. There are just a few tables on the small terrace near the entrance overlooking the pedestrianised street, so if you want to sit outdoors make sure you book well in advance.

Name: Locanda del Molino
Description: This rustic yet charming restaurant occupies an old family mill. It has attractive guestrooms that reflect the elegant simplicity of the Tuscan countryside. In the kitchen, the female chef creates traditional specialities such as fried rabbit and nettle with ricotta cheese gnudi (ravioli filling without the pasta) in a fresh tomato sauce.

Name: Stilla
Address: Località Casette 1, Colognola ai Colli, 37030, Italy
Description: Run by an enthusiastic and committed young couple who left the big city to restore the family home and transform it into an elegant, welcoming restaurant, Stilla stands in a tranquil location surrounded by vineyards. Here, Silvia creates original, generous and colourful cuisine which is showcased on an à la carte with just a few dishes which change regularly. We particularly enjoyed the freshly seared bonito served with wild spinach, sour cherries and a cherry barbecue sauce. Meals are served on the outdoor terrace in summer. Accommodation is also available in five beautiful yet functional guestrooms. Well worth a visit.

Name: Locanda Sensi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: We highly recommend this pleasant country restaurant run by friendly and enthusiastic staff, where the owner appears frequently in the dining room. The ambience is modern and comfortable, the outdoor dining area boasts typical views of the Piacenza hills, and – last but not least – the food is excellent! The options on the fine-dining menu range from regional specialities to fish-based dishes, as well as various delicacies cooked on the barbecue grill, such as pigeon breast (served with pigeon leg, marinated breast, offal and rice timbale). The wine selection is also excellent.

Name: RistoFante
Description: The motto of this restaurant is “In step with the times yet inspired by tradition”. The cuisine here is made from fresh, seasonal ingredients (with a particular focus on fish) prepared using modern techniques. Elegant dining room, plus a shaded outdoor space for the summer months.

Name: Molteni
Description: Hospitality abounds in this establishment where the cuisine is inspired by local traditions, especially fish, in a favourably located restaurant in the historical centre on the banks of the Bianco canal.

Name: La Torre
Description: Housed in the picturesque medieval castle of Spilimbergo, this restaurant boasts a splendid façade adorned with 14C frescoes, plus two rustic yet elegant dining rooms. If you’re looking for somewhere for a romantic dinner and modern cuisine, then this is the place for you!

Name: Taverna del Castello
Description: Occupying a 15C castle in a medieval village, this restaurant offers fine views of the majestic hills all around. The chef here uses top - quality regional ingredients with a focus on seasonal produce to create tasting menus full of imagination and artistic flair. Excellent meat and fish dishes inspired by Italian traditions.

Name: Vecio Macello
Description: Although Vecio Macello has retained a few unusual features on the ceiling from its former life as a meat-processing plant (such as the old pipes used to provide steam for the plant’s pasteurisation and meat preparation processes), this restaurant now has a strong focus on fish. The menu offers a selection of raw dishes and classic seafood recipes alongside a few regionally influenced meat options.

Name: Campocori
Address: via di Santa Maria de' Calderari 49, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: This gourmet fine-dining restaurant, the brainchild of the South African designer Tristan Du Plessis, has arrived in the Italian capital where it’s overseen by chef Alessandro Pietropaoli. Here, choose from the à la carte or opt for one of the tasting menus (5 or 7 courses). Elegant, contemporary and cosmopolitan cuisine.

Name: Belvedere
Description: Over the years, this family restaurant has become one of the most popular along this coastline. An informal dining room provides the backdrop for the decidedly Mediterranean cuisine served here, where the focus is the fish display cabinet that changes daily and from which guests can make their choice. The friendly and professional approach of the two brothers that run the restaurant has contributed to its success, while the brand-new terrace-lounge, with its stunning view, is the perfect spot for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Millo Ristorante
Address: via Garibaldi 4, Santa Teresa Gallura, 07028, Italy
Description: An attractive restaurant serving reasonably priced fish and seafood (try the delicious squid with an orange and chicory sauce). There’s also a charming summer terrace from which to watch the town’s bustling nightlife.

Name: Anticofurlo
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Country cooking
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the Gola del Furlo nature reserve, this restaurant is run by the talented and enthusiastic Alberto and Roberta, whose focus is on typical Marche specialities such as fresh pasta, cured hams, fine cheese and regional dishes full of intense flavours. The picturesque grotto carved into the rock is perfect for an aperitif, while the inn also offers charming guestrooms.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Description: This traditional family restaurant has been recently renovated to include an attractive veranda - style dining room overlooking the valley. Typical dishes from Calabria, fish specialities by prior arrangement, and a good wine list all add to the appeal.

Name: TerraMadre
Description: This small, modern and minimalist restaurant is tucked away among the alleyways of the historic centre. The predominance of black combined with a dark colour scheme gives the dining room an elegant feel, while the cuisine, prepared using regional ingredients, is contemporary and creative in style.

Name: Osteria della Tana
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Occupying the same red house as chef Alessandro Dal Degan’s gourmet restaurant, the Osteria is where this chef turns his attention to more traditional dishes (meat and fish alike), which are often typical of the Veneto. There’s one highly recommended exception, however, namely the carbonara dell’Osteria, prepared with top-quality ingredients from the region. Also popular are the baccalà alla vicentina (dried cod) and the tripe, both of which feature on a menu with a wide selection, including renowned dishes from the chef’s Michelin-starred restaurant. Full-bodied flavours that will delight the palate.

Name: Cut
Description: Situated right in the heart of the Bergamo plain in the small town of Caravaggio, famous for the painter of the same name and for a much-visited pilgrim shrine, this welcoming restaurant boasts a modern decor and vintage furnishings. At lunchtime, it serves a good, competitively priced business menu, while in the evening the more elaborate à la carte features contemporary-style meat and fish dishes (mostly the latter).

Name: Qualia
Description: Situated in a side street in the centre of this charming small town, this restaurant boasts a dining room with exposed brickwork and glimpses of the kitchen, plus a small outdoor space with a few tables for alfresco dining. The dishes here are full of flavour and focus on regional ingredients and fresh fish.

Name: Seta Sushi Restaurant
Description: It was friendship and passion for Japanese cuisine that prompted two young business partners to open this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the heart of Bologna. Situated in a courtyard with medieval origins, Seta Sushi Restaurant has a modern bistro-style dining room, as well as plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. The menu features an impressive selection of traditional Japanese dishes with the occasional personalised touch, all made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t worry if you’re new to Japanese cuisine – Maurilio is front of house to offer guests friendly, expert advice on both food and beverage. The latter includes a choice of sake for those wishing to immerse themselves fully in the Japanese dining experience.

Name: Locanda de Banchieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: After spending time working in the Aosta Valley, chef Giacomo Devoto from Sarzana has returned to his native region, where he has converted an old 17C country farmhouse nestled amid tranquil verdant landscapes into an intimate inn with guestrooms and its own farm. Sitting on the panoramic veranda with its views of the sea and the coast, guests are served creative cuisine full of the delicious flavours of the Lunigiana. Devoto’s imaginative recipes are inspired by seasonal ingredients, with many of the vegetables (and the extra-virgin olive oil) grown on the farm itself, while the meat and fish are sourced either from inland or the nearby sea.

Name: Andree
Address: via San Martino della Battaglia 16, La Spezia, 19121, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the centre of Spezia boasts a striking open-view kitchen in its small brick-vaulted dining room. Modern cuisine with a focus on superb fish dishes, accompanied by professional service and a wine list full of character.

Name: Tre Scalini
Description: The menu at this restaurant features meat and seasonal ingredients served in personalised recipes and contemporary-style dishes. There are also three tasting menus: the main one consists of eight courses prepared by the talented chef. The restaurant brings to mind a modern bistro with its warm ambience and attentive service.

Name: Konnubio
Address: via dei Conti 8 r, Florence, 50123, Italy
Description: Different options under one roof: a bar open from morning to evening, a wine bar in the cellar serving cold dishes and offering wine tastings, and a restaurant serving light, quick options at lunchtime and more elaborate, original fare in the evening. There are also seven new guestrooms for visitors wanting to stay in the heart of Florence.

Name: Sine by Di Pinto
Description: Sine serves contemporary cuisine influenced by the chef’s native Naples, as well as the local region of Lombardy. The dishes are occasionally playful in style, as demonstrated by the shrimp ravioli served in various ways, including with an intensely flavoured fish stew. The chef’s speciality is his fried pizzetta with palamita fish and courgettes, while his new dishes are showcased on the exciting and creative “Sine Confini” menu, on which he demonstrates his culinary skills to the full. Attentive, courteous service and a constantly evolving wine list which includes some lesser-known labels complete the picture.

Name: Verbano
Address: via Ugo Ara 2, Isola dei Pescatori, Stresa, 28838, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Within the confines of the small, charming Verbano hotel on the beautiful island of Pescatori, chef Marco Sacco serves top-quality cuisine in what can only be described as a stunning setting. The contemporary-style dining room boasts panoramic windows, while the outdoor terrace with its views of Palazzo Borromeo and Isola Bella is the perfect setting for dinner in fine weather.

Name: Radici
Address: Località Borgo La Chiaracia, Castel Giorgio, 05013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Served in an elegant dining room or on the delightful outdoor terrace in fine weather, the highly creative cuisine at this restaurant has its roots in regional traditions and excellent local producers, while its stunning location within the luxurious Hotel Borgo La Chiaracia among the region’s verdant winding valleys makes it difficult to leave. With a choice of à la carte and tasting menus, our inspectors were particularly impressed by the Origini 20menu, on which all the ingredients are sourced within a 20km radius of the restaurant.

Name: La Fortuna
Address: via Ponte Rino 6, Campagnola Cremasca, 26010, Italy
Description: This restaurant is constantly reinventing itself, offering a fresh ambience with a minimalist yet welcoming decor. The menu changes in accordance with what’s available at the weekly market – as a result, there are always new, carefully prepared dishes to try. The wine list boasts a selection of more than 200 labels!

Name: San Giorgio
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Umbertide, beneath two arches in the main square where a monastery once stood, this restaurant serves personalised and modern cuisine in its three dining rooms and a small courtyard near the entrance. Presented on various tasting menus and an à la carte, the generously portioned dishes focus exclusively on meat (white and red) and offer excellent value for money. We particularly enjoyed the hearty and original “Pensando a un vitello tonnato” (literally “Thinking of a veal tonnato”). The friendly and knowledgeable sommelier is on hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: Secondo Tempo
Address: via Vittorio Amedeo 55, Termini Imerese, 90018, Italy
Description: Situated on the first floor of a building (formerly home to an apartment owned by chef Salvatore Campagna’s family), this intimate restaurant dates back to the 1920s, as do the frescoes on the ceiling and the Art Nouveau-style flooring. In contrast, the cuisine is modern Italian with obvious Sicilian influences, including a focus on seasonal vegetables (there’s even a tasting menu that is completely vegan). All the extra-virgin olive oil used for cooking and as a condiment is home produced.

Name: L˜ARIA
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying a modern lakeside building nestling in botanic gardens, this restaurant has an elegant and contemporary feel. Although the dishes served by new chef Massimiliano Blasone have a cosmopolitan flavour with the occasional hint of Asia, the selection of delicious desserts that follow are prepared with a combination of regional and exotic ingredients.

Name: [àbitat]
Address: via Henry Dunant 1, San Fermo della Battaglia, 22020, Italy
Description: A young, enthusiastic and professional couple has taken over the reins at this modern and welcoming restaurant, serving cuisine that is inspired by a sustainable and seasonal approach. Ingredients include herbs harvested from their own garden, as well as typical produce from the mountains and the sea, all sourced from trusted suppliers who demonstrate full respect for nature and animals. Food waste is kept to a minimum to ensure a circular-based cuisine.

Name: Pierre - Trattoria Sartoriale
Description: Situated on the edge of the historic centre, this simple restaurant with just a few tables serves beautifully presented dishes. The menu features a limited number of options, all made with the best of whatever the market has available, and creatively prepared with little fuss and a focus on bringing out the ingredients’ full flavour.

Name: Modì
Description: This restaurant has moved from its previous location in central Torregrotta to a more secluded setting slightly above the town centre, where it aims to offer its guests an even better dining experience. The owner-chef has more than achieved this, serving excellent Sicilian dishes reinterpreted with careful precision and a contemporary twist. A good wine list completes the picture.

Name: Bebop
Description: Having studied classics, this young self-taught chef decided to follow his true passion, namely cooking. He prepares dishes inspired by Sicilian traditions yet reinterpreted with a personal twist, using the best regional products. The restaurant, situated in the heart of Palermo, is quiet and elegant yet also pleasantly informal in its service.

Name: Corbezzoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the Relais Bellaria hotel on the outskirts of the city, this contemporary-style restaurant serves equally modern cuisine which ranges from vegetarian dishes to meat and fish options, all of which are featured on three tasting menus and an à la carte. In the kitchen, the chef from Campania skilfully combines the flavours of his native region with those of his adopted Emilia in dishes which are both copious and colourful.

Name: Le Beccherie
Description: Situated in the heart of Treviso, this restaurant – once a stronghold of traditional cuisine – is now a splendid designer-style bistro. The most atmospheric tables are those by the canal, while the dishes themselves combine regional influence with a touch of fantasy. In addition to the à la carte, guests can choose from two tasting menus: the more creative Ti P'Orto al Mareand the Essenziale, perfect for anyone tasting this style of cuisine for the first time. Traditionalists will be pleased to hear that the famous tiramisù is still on the menu!

Name: Punto G
Address: via Gian Francesco Parravicini 34, Monza, 20900, Italy
Description: Situated not far from the town centre, this restaurant has two different spaces – a ground-floor bistro, plus a gourmet dining room on the first floor, both beautifully maintained and decorated with simple elegance. Here, a young chef from Campania who has experience working both in Italy and abroad creates modern, elegant and contemporary cuisine. In the bistro, the choice of gourmet pizzas is a reminder of the chef’s origins.

Name: Bistrot La Perla
Address: strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Take a culinary journey from the north of Italy to the south from the comfort of your table at the Bistrot La Perla, where guests are enthusiastically introduced to the many delightful flavours and ingredients this beautiful country has to offer. Excellent fish specialities also available.

Name: Osteria Cascina dei Fiori
Description: This restaurant’s warm, elegant and rustic atmosphere with wooden furniture and exposed beams provides the setting for its seasonally inspired, regional cuisine. The experienced owners are welcoming and attentive, while the menu features specialities such as frogs’ leg and courgette flower risotto.

Name: La Nicchia
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This tastefully decorated restaurant is housed in a late - 18C building, which is marked on an old map from the Napoleonic era. Here the best local ingredients are selected to create regional dishes with the occasional contemporary twist.

Name: Lu Pisantinu
Address: viale Giovanni Maria Orecchioni snc, loc. Liscia di Vacca, Arzachena, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A terrace framed by granite columns overlooks the coast and Porto Cervo at this restaurant, which is decorated in light shades and pastel tones echoing the colours of the sea. Imaginative fish cuisine.

Name: Frosio
Description: Housed in a 18C villa which was once a family inn, this restaurant is run by the dynamic and professional Frosio family who have over 30 years’ experience in the restaurant business. There’s nothing improvised about Frosio, where Camillo guarantees impeccable service front of house and Paolo is at the helm in the kitchen, creating carefully prepared dishes with a classic-modern feel and an equal emphasis on meat and fish, often made from traditionally “gourmet” ingredients such as scampi, lobster, foie gras, pigeon and caviar. The wine list continues to offer an excellent selection, with one section dedicated to Italy and another to the rest of the world. Decorated with austere elegance, the wine cellar in the 13C tower is home to more than 1,000 different labels. Attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Villa Tiboldi
Address: via Case Sparse 127, località Tiboldi, Canale, 12043, Italy
Description: A delightful combination of good food and a romantic ambience in this old restored farmhouse surrounded by hills. Top - quality cuisine and a wine cellar that is well worth a visit.

Name: Ristorante Mas-cì
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre, this hotel and restaurant are now run by the third generation of the same family. Welcoming dining rooms with a fireplace provide the setting for cuisine which makes the most of local produce while also including dishes from elsewhere in Italy. Don’t miss the black truffle specialities!

Name: Mirko's
Address: discesa Annunziata 1, Castellammare del Golfo, 91014, Italy
Description: This small restaurant, located near the steps to Cala Piccola, is run by an entire family and is beginning to earn an excellent local reputation. The son is at the helm in the kitchen. Having gained experience elsewhere for many years, he decided to start his own venture, which shows every sign of having paid off. Enjoy excellent fish and seafood specialities cooked in Mediterranean and Sicilian style in a quiet, beautifully kept dining room.

Name: Alle Codole
Address: via XX Agosto 27, Canale d'Agordo, 32020, Italy
Description: ‘Codole’ is the nickname of the family that runs this restaurant and whose ancestors once worked in the copper mines in the area. Today, the family has exchanged mining for cooking, offering guests specialities such as ricotta and black truffle ravioli with a lamb ragù, and loin of venison in a porcini mushroom crust.

Name: Al Carroponte
Description: This restaurant is renowned in Bergamo for its good choice of varied cuisine, as well as its lively, buzzing atmosphere. The excellent, tasty cuisine is typically Italian and contemporary in style, and includes luxury ingredients such as lobster and caviar, while the “classic” à la carte is enhanced by a selection of cured hams, cheeses and finger food. But the Carroponte’s beating heart is owner Oscar Mazzoleni’s passion for the world of wine, with an incredible selection of over 2 000 labels that puts many more famous Michelin-starred restaurants in the shade.

Name: Carlo Magno
Description: This restaurant housed in a country house dating from the 19C offers elegant period dining rooms and a menu featuring Mediterranean-style meat and fish dishes.

Name: med
Address: piazza del Quartiere Latino 13, Treviso, 31100, Italy
Description: In the pedestrian area of the town, with views of the Sile river from the ground floor, this attractive restaurant serves regional cuisine with a focus on local ingredients, prepared in a classic style attentive to modern tastes. There’s an excellent wine list, plus live music and a pleasant outdoor space for fine weather dining.

Name: La Tavernetta
Address: contrada campo San Lorenzo 14, Camigliatello Silano, 87052, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Firmly focused on the cuisine of Calabria, this restaurant serves dishes full of the mountain flavours of the Sila region, including Podolica beef, mushrooms, potatoes and hams. “We have excellent ingredients in this region” says the chef, “All we have to do is prepare them properly” – something which he manages very successfully!

Name: Macelleria Motta
Address: strada Padana Superiore 90, Bellinzago Lombardo, 20060, Italy
Description: Motta has established a reputation for quality, especially for its meat which is carefully sourced from farms in the Piedmont region. Some of the excellent options on the menu are aged in a large fridge near the entrance, along with different types of delicious salumi which are produced and cured by the restaurant. Various types of meat feature here, cured or cooked using classic methods with the occasional modern touch. Piedmontese beef is one of the highlights, with different cuts grilled on the barbecue or served boiled. Enjoy alfresco dining in a typical Lombardy courtyard in summer.

Name: Da Felice
Description: This welcoming restaurant, in business for many years now, boasts an open-view kitchen to the rear of the dining room. The menu here focuses on fish from the daily market which is prepared in different traditional ways, including carpaccio, fried and oven-baked dishes. Prices are reasonable on the whole, while the short tasting menu offers excellent value for money. A fresh, cool outdoor space adds to the appeal.

Name: Locanda Gulfi
Description: Situated in a secluded area of olive groves and vineyards, Locanda Gulfi also produces its own oil and wine, as confirmed by the view of the wine cellar from the dining room. The cuisine features an attractive selection of classic Sicilian dishes, while guestrooms are available for anyone keen to extend their stay.

Name: Galileo
Address: via IV Novembre conc. 25, Civitanova Marche, 62012, Italy
Description: Boasting a dining room overlooking the beach, Galileo is a typical Adriatic restaurant serving fish and seafood dishes that are popular with many Italians. Options include seafood salad, a selection of antipasti, fish and seafood pastas, assorted small fried fish, and grilled recipes. In other words, delicious, traditional and unfussy cuisine in which fish takes centre stage.

Name: Lord Nelson
Description: Situated right on the seafront, this restaurant plunges its guests back in time with its polished wood, mirrors and classic decor giving it the feel of an English galleon. Mediterranean cuisine made from top-quality ingredients takes centre stage here, while the extensive wine list features some vintage labels. The American bar offering a good selection of cocktails is perfect for the winter months.

Name: Aqua
Description: The most attractive space in this restaurant is its contemporary, almost Milanese-style veranda-dining room which boasts relaxing views of Lake Garda, with sailboats bobbing on the water ruffled by the famous Ora wind, and the peaks of Trentino in the distance. The Italian cuisine served here is prepared simply, allowing the quality of the ingredients (many of which are sourced locally) to shine through. Fish from the lake takes pride of place, although saltwater fish also features. There’s also a good selection of wine.

Name: Osteria Al GiGianca
Description: Although the out - of - town location is a slight drawback, this restaurant passionately run has a welcoming atmosphere. Seasonal, regional cuisine, plus a good choice of wine and beers.

Name: San Marco
Description: A long-established restaurant in the Asti region renowned for its regional cuisine, impeccable service and warm welcome. In the classic-style dining room the open fire is always lit, creating a cosy atmosphere.

Name: Zunica 1880
Address: piazza Filippi Pepe 14, Civitella del Tronto, 64010, Italy
Description: The pleasant outdoor space and some of the hotel rooms at Zunica overlook Civitella del Tronto’s central square on which this restaurant stands. For more than 100 years, Zunica 1880 has been a proud standard-bearer for typical Abruzzi cuisine, as well as dishes influenced by the nearby Marche region. Seasonal vegetables take pride of place on the menu, served with carefully selected meat (make sure you try the lamb and pigeon!), all prepared with a fine balance of traditional and contemporary styles.

Name: Aubergine
Description: Situated in a town famous for its thermal baths, this classically elegant restaurant serves meat and fish cuisine including specialities from the Veneto such as Berico ham, bigoli pasta with sardines, and veal liver with onions.

Name: L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
Description: For almost 40 years, the Angolo d’Abruzzo restaurant has been home to the Centofanti family, who act as excellent ambassadors for the region by offering the best local, seasonal ingredients (for this reason, there’s no fish on the menu) in a host of traditional, regional recipes. Specialities such as cured meats, local ham, bruschetta and fresh home-made pasta (including “chitarra” spaghetti) take centre stage, while main courses include grilled dishes (porcini mushrooms in season, cuts of beef and veal at any time of year) and stews (mutton etc). When it comes to dessert, make sure you try the crème caramel with Navelli saffron. A misleading sign saying “sagrestia” (sacristy) actually indicates the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Le Colonne
Description: You’d recognise this cuisine as southern Italian even if you were blindfolded, thanks to its strong and intense flavours. Imaginatively prepared and presented dishes, many of which showcase the region’s mozzarella cheese, plus a delicious selection of desserts and pastries. All in all, an excellent choice!

Name: Cacciatori
Description: You pass through beautiful hilly scenery to get to Cartosio, where you’ll find this typical country house (part of which has been recently renovated) specialising in local cuisine. Although it’s been in business for five generations, the formula has hardly changed, with a focus on Piedmontese dishes made as much as possible from locally sourced produce, cooked in the wood-fired stove and announced at your table. Simple but pleasant guestrooms are also available.

Name: SottoSopra
Description: A pleasant and colourful restaurant in the village centre, divided into several dining rooms. The owner-chef prepares a range of eclectic dishes with passion and enthusiasm, offering a menu which includes meat dishes alongside fish options (salt- and freshwater), as well as a few regional specialities.

Name: Lalibera
Description: A modern, designer-style restaurant staffed by a young and efficient front-of-house team. The cuisine showcases traditional Piedmontese recipes created with respect and enthusiasm, resulting in top-quality dishes, generous portions and an attention to detail in the presentation.

Name: Arca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In business for over 20 years, Arca is definitely one of the best restaurants in this area. Elegantly modern in style, with part of the kitchen open to the dining room, the restaurant owes its success to its enthusiastic and imaginative owner-chef Massimiliano, who, assisted by his sister, reinterprets meat and fish specialities from the Abruzzo. All the ingredients are certified organic – so much so that the restaurant describes its style as “organic Mediterranean cuisine”.

Name: Locanda Stella d'Oro
Description: The original flavour and magic of a trattoria can still be found in this establishment. The cuisine is traditional with a personal touch.

Name: Coeur de Bois
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: The name of this elegant restaurant was inspired by its wooden ceiling. Surrounded by spruce decor dating from the 18C, antique furniture and paintings, enjoy interesting traditional cuisine in this excellent gourmet restaurant, which is all the more attractive thanks to its location in the Gran Paradiso national park.

Name: Taverna da Ciacco
Address: via Dante Alighieri 30/a, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: A welcoming restaurant with a rustic feel. The owner - chef delights guests with his traditional yet imaginative delicacies, such as pici pasta with Pachino cherry tomatoes, garlic and chilli peppers and the renowned Chianina steak. Fish occasionally features on the menu.

Name: Il Baretto
Description: Il Baretto on the outskirts of Padova is a must for anyone who loves classic, traditional fish and seafood, thanks to its menu which includes a number of typical Venetian dishes. The top-quality fish is skilfully prepared to bring out its full flavour and distinctive characteristics, providing a real treat for the tastebuds in this inland temple to the sea.

Name: Pascalucci
Address: via Appia 1, San Nicola Manfredi, 82010, Italy
Description: A traditional restaurant serving regional cuisine, as well as skilfully prepared fish dishes made from fresh produce. Specialities include Beneventano beef fillet and octopus in aspic jelly.

Name: Crotasc
Address: via Don Primo Lucchinetti 63, Mese, 23020, Italy
Description: Here one can choose between a smaller, typically mountain style dining room with stone paving and open fireplace and a larger room in contemporary rustic style. In summer one can dine on the terrace.

Name: Ai Do Campanili
Description: Both the building in which it is housed and the dining room of this restaurant are on the small side, but the quality of the food more than compensates for the lack of space. Run by young and enthusiastic staff, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood with raw options and modern dishes featuring on the menu. Excellent selection of wine, also available to take away.

Name: Unterwirt
Description: Occupying a private house, this restaurant boasts a couple of old Stube-style dining rooms, one of which is highly romantic and dates back to the 13C – although it looks as though the vintage wood may have come from elsewhere, it has in fact all been here for centuries. The owner-chef creates carefully thought-out dishes which combine precision and classic comfort with the occasional modern touch, harmoniously combining the flavours of the Alto Adige with Mediterranean influences, with a particular focus on fish. A welcoming outdoor terrace for summer dining completes the picture.

Name: Locanda dell'Arcimboldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the town gates, a friendly inn with a family atmosphere in a fine building, with a pleasant veranda. Fish dishes prevail on the menu, featuring an interesting selection of oysters. At midday there is also an easier set menu.

Name: Zur Kaiserkron
Description: Now under new management, this historic restaurant in the centre of Bolzano occupies the ground floor of the attractive Palazzo Pock overlooking the square. Here, elegant, contemporary-style dining rooms with charming vaulted ceilings provide the setting for Mediterranean-influenced cuisine with a distinctly contemporary flavour.

Name: Paolo Teverini
Address: via del Popolo 2, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the charming village of Bagno di Romagna and surrounded by beautiful rolling hills, Teverini is a culinary name full of history in this area. The cuisine here demonstrates different traditions – the local region is an obvious influence (especially its mushrooms), but fish and seafood also feature along with plenty of vegetables.

Name: Babette
Description: Situated just beyond the centre of Albenga in a beautiful location right on the beach (with only a small private beach club separating it from the sea), this restaurant has been in business for over 20 years (10 years on this site, and 10 in the town centre before that). It is renowned for its excellent, modern cuisine that focuses on top-quality, fresh and seasonal fish. A lighter (yet equally excellent) menu is also available at lunchtime.

Name: Osteria del Mare già il "Votapentole"
Address: via IV Novembre 15, Castiglione della Pescaia, 58043, Italy
Description: This charming restaurant right in the town centre boasts colourful decor and a lively, relaxed atmosphere. Fish and seafood from the nearby Mediterranean are served in imaginative dishes full of character, including highly recommended raw dishes and the popular “caciucco” (Tuscan fish stew).

Name: Parco Gambrinus
Address: via Capitello 18, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A rustic and romantic setting provides the backdrop for the traditional and creative cuisine served here. It is made from typical local produce with an emphasis on ethical and sustainably produced ingredients (vegan and gluten - free options are also available). Exotic animals inhabit the park, where a stream is home to the house specialities of crayfish, eels and sturgeon. The restaurant also offers a few comfortable guestrooms nearby.

Name: Antica Osteria dei Camelì
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying an attractive farmhouse dating back to the 16C, this restaurant boasts an interesting combination of antique elegance and modern style. The cuisine is equally impressive, offering a selection of traditional and innovative dishes that pay close attention to nutritional balance and the healthiness of the combinations of ingredients.

Name: Tenuta del Gallo
Description: Whether you dine indoors in the charming, romantic dining room or outdoors with views of the surrounding countryside, you’ll enjoy traditional local cuisine and classic Italian favourites at this restaurant. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the excellent beef carpaccio with truffles and the local guinea fowl with chickpeas. Comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Bottega Aleotti
Description: Situated in a secluded street in the town centre, this restaurant run by a couple boasts an elegant dining room with an attractive dark parquet floor. The cuisine is a good example of how to add a light modern touch to local specialities as well as typical Italian dishes, while the menu also includes a few fish-based options. Don’t miss the home-made pasta!

Name: Il Pescatore
Address: via Acqua Dolce 7, Cala Gonone, 08022, Italy
Description: This Mediterranean-style restaurant has the evocative feel of a seaside village with its beautiful photos of the coast on the walls. It’s best to book ahead if you want one of the tables on the small terrace overlooking the sea. To avoid confusion, note that the Il Pescatore that we recommend is situated at 7, via Acqua Dolce.

Name: La Luge
Address: Perreres, loc. Varvoyes, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Italian
Description: This attractive, rustic - style restaurant is situated just a few kilometres from the centre of Cervinia. It stands in a tranquil, panoramic basin where the only neighbours are the marmots in the hills around. Popular with passing tourists, as well as locals who feel the journey out here is well worth the effort. The restaurant offers a good range of choices for all palates. This includes soups, different cuts of meat, typical specialities from the Aosta valley and even a few fish dishes. This address is also worth a mention for the attractive guestrooms available.

Name: La Kucina
Address: via Giulio De Petra 67, Foggia, 71121, Italy
Description: This modern, welcoming restaurant on the outskirts of town serves contemporary cuisine on a varied menu which also includes simpler options to suit all budgets, especially at lunchtime. In the dining room, a cabinet for ageing meat houses some excellent Iberian hams.

Name: La Bul
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Here, in one of Bari’s most interesting restaurants, chef Antonio Scalera serves top-quality cuisine accompanied by intelligently chosen wines with fascinating stories behind them. The dishes often feature traditional recipes and ingredients from Puglia yet are creative and of the highest quality.

Name: I Carracci
Description: The ceiling at this restaurant is adorned with superb frescoes thought to be by the school of the Carracci brothers, whose painters were definitely responsible for decorating other rooms in this palazzo. This is one good reason for choosing this restaurant, and the cuisine is another – the new chef here creates dishes which are appealingly creative without being overly fussy or excessive.

Name: Trattoria la Colonna
Address: Via Emilia Est 6, località San Nicolò, Rottofreno, 29010, Italy
Description: This classic-style restaurant with a recently renovated dining room is situated on the street that runs through the village of San Nicolò. Although the menu features some meat dishes (on Sundays in winter, this includes specialities such as boiled meats, anolini pasta in broth, and typical desserts such as ciambella cake with zabaglione), it is particularly renowned for its wide selection of fish options. At lunchtime during the week, there’s a choice of simpler recipes, but if you ask, staff will be happy to offer you the longer evening menu.

Name: Acqua Pazza
Description: Although this restaurant is not in the centre, if you’re looking for excellent fish (mostly from the Mediterranean) personally selected by the owner - chef, then it’s well worth the few minutes it takes to find a parking space here. Beautifully cooked food, which is simply prepared using top - quality produce.

Name: Sale Grosso
Description: A simple, bistro - style restaurant serving well - prepared, mainly Mediterranean - style cuisine. Although fish and seafood dominate the menu, there are also a few vegetarian dishes and vegan specialities available.

Name: Trattoria Battibecco
Description: Situated in a narrow street in the city centre, this stylish, elegant restaurant is renowned for its traditional dishes and seafood specialities. Simpler fare at more moderate prices available at lunchtime.

Name: Bacco
Description: The focus at this restaurant is on a variety of local ingredients and specialities that even a novice food-lover would recognise as typical of this region. The owner-chef at this intimate and elegant gem of a restaurant is Ruggiero Doronzo, whose mantra is “simplicity and seasonality”.

Name: Il Ristorantino - Da Dino
Address: via XXV Aprile 11, Anzola dell'Emilia, 40011, Italy
Description: Tucked away in an unexpected location in a residential district, this restaurant is nonetheless popular with its loyal and regular clientele. And the reason is obvious – the high quality of the cuisine served here. Bologna’s traditional specialities and other Italian dishes are joined on the menu by a few fish options on Thursdays and Fridays.

Name: Mirò il Ristorante
Description: Notwithstanding its central location, this restaurant's surroundings offer a number of parking places (on payment. Menus are imaginative with a wealth of creativity served in two small dining rooms and outside in summer.

Name: Vicolo Colombina
Description: Situated right in the heart of the historic centre among the narrow alleyways near the market and Piazza Maggiore, this restaurant serves traditional cuisine (no fish) with a subtle contemporary twist. Two modern dining rooms with modern decor, plus a wine list with a focus on regional labels.

Name: Oltre.
Description: This restaurant in the lively Mercato delle Erbe district has an entrance adorned with hundreds of stickers, giving it the appearance of a record shop rather than a contemporary-style eatery with a bar counter and a highly original surfboard table near the entrance. The modern cuisine has its roots in the region yet also includes skilfully prepared dishes from around the world. There’s also a choice of cocktails to start or round off your meal. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Madama Vigna
Description: This restuarant has a good wine list with a focus on local labels, as well as an excellent selection of regional specialities on the menu. Dishes include agnolotti (a type of stuffed pasta) with fondue, Piedmontese beef, Villanova chicken and the inevitable bunet dessert.

Name: Osteria dell'Arco
Description: Enjoy a warm family welcome at this centrally located restaurant with an internal courtyard, where the menu features a good choice of traditional and authentic dishes full of flavour. The restaurant is run by the same friendly managers as the renowned and popular Boccondivino in Bra, where the Slow Food concept was born. Booking ahead is always a good option.

Name: Locanda dei Cantù
Description: At the bottom of a steep valley, a rustic restaurant that offers fine cuisine, much appreciated in the area, with a great preference for local products. Old traditional recipes are revisited with a personal touch.

Name: Taverna Kerkira
Address: corso Vittorio Emanuele 217, Bagnara Calabra, 89011, Italy
Description: Kerkira (Corfu in Greek) owes its existence to the chef’s Greek mother, who passed on the culinary traditions of her native island to her son. These traditions are alive and well in this taverna, which also features Calabrese and Mediterranean dishes on the menu. Simple dining room with a friendly ambience, not far from the centre and seafront in the village where singer Mia Martini was born.

Name: Serpillo
Address: via di Mezzo 1, località Torre del Colle, Bevagna, 06031, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming medieval village which is also home to a couple of small hotels, this attractive, rustic restaurant in an old olive mill acts as the backdrop for regional and Italian cuisine. Dishes with a touch of modern flavour are presented on a menu which, although not extensive, offers good value for money.

Name: Carne & Spirito
Description: The environment here is elegantly rustic thanks to fine furnishings and colourful décor – an attractive background to the variety of creative and imaginative specialties on offer. Rooms are neat and simple. Charming rooms, furnished in different styles with elegant simplicity.

Name: Hostaria Ducale
Address: Salita di San Matteo 29 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Situated just behind the beautiful Piazza De Ferrari, this restaurant with a quiet ambience and elegant decor provides the backdrop for young chef Daniele Rebosio’s superb, ever-evolving cuisine, which is modern, creative and imaginative and yet inspired by regional traditions. Equally at ease with meat and fish, Rebosio occasionally combines the two in one dish, as evidenced by his veal tongue served with langoustine (carpaccio marinated in passion fruit and salted biscuit stuffed with tartare) or with ravioli with rabbit and mussels dedicated to Fabrizio De André’s song Crêuza de mä .

Name: Benedikto
Address: via Eremo delle Carceri 1/a, Assisi, 06081, Italy
Description: Situated in the elegant setting of the Nun hotel on the edge of Assisi’s historic centre, Benedikto serves typical Umbrian ingredients which are transformed into creative and imaginative dishes by talented chef Enea Barbanera. In fine weather, dinner is served on the romantic outdoor terrace with views of Assisi’s castle.

Name: Cappuccini Cucina San Francesco
Description: Housed in the resort of the same name, this elegant restaurant is full of historic charm, enhanced by its white damask linen and beautiful candlesticks. The wine list pays obvious tribute to the famous Franciacorta region and also includes an excellent choice of champagnes, while the modern cuisine shows touches of traditional influence alongside more creative twists. Seasonal ingredients are to the fore here.

Name: Barbieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Enjoy your meal in the classic - style dining room or on the outdoor terrace in fine weather. The menu here is seasonal, with a focus on delicious Calabrian cuisine, while the wine list also features exclusively local options.

Name: Il Grano di Pepe
Description: While you’re trying to decide between the tasting menu and the à la carte at this restaurant, you can tuck into its excellent bread, including the “sfincione” – a type of tomato-flavoured focaccia from Palermo which makes the journey here worthwhile on its own! If fish is your preference, we recommend the “Palermo and Marseille” fish stew, an intense dish full of bold and delicious flavours. Minimalist decor and a friendly welcome from chef Rino Duca complete the picture.

Name: Trattoria del Cimino da Colombo dal 1895
Description: Situated on the hill leading to Palazzo Farnese, this restaurant occupies the oldest building in the village, which dates back to 1370. Since 1940, the Calistri family have been delighting their guests with delicious specialities from Lazio, including excellent cured hams, fresh pasta (the amatriciana is particularly renowned), grilled meats and an impressive selection of cheeses and desserts. Excellent wines and spirits complete the picture.

Name: Campamac
Description: A real gourmet inn which serves traditional Piedmontese dishes made from excellent ingredients alongside top-quality meats cooked on the barbecue grill. An elegant ambience with a deliberately retro feel, which is beautifully maintained and has plenty of charm.

Name: Villa Pignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A veritable Garden of Eden just 15km from Volterra, this 300ha estate is home to a restaurant with a strong zero-mile philosophy. This is backed up by its careful use of ingredients grown or produced on the estate itself, such as vegetables, olives and grains, as well as chicken, pork and honey – a sustainable approach that results in delicious, contemporary cuisine. The dishes here are fresh and full of flavour yet elaborate and modern in style (note the simpler menu at lunchtime). The interesting wine list explores Tuscany through its choice of top-quality organic labels as well as including wines produced from the estate’s own vines.

Name: Casa Bertini
Description: This unexpected gourmet restaurant is housed in a sports centre just outside the historic centre of Recanati, birthplace of famous Italian poet Giacomo Leopardi. At the helm in the kitchen, young, talented chef Andrea Bertini has returned to his native region where he reinterprets the traditions of the Marche (especially meat) to create light, simple and unfussy dishes. The same simple style is echoed in the decor, which is elegant and very understated.

Name: Osteria Contemporanea
Description: This modern osteria serves Piedmontese cuisine with the occasional influence from Trentino (the young chef’s native region), as well as an unusual menu dedicated to offal. Minimalist-style decor, with romantic lighting that creates a pleasant and intimate ambience.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Bulgari with views of the Mausoleum of Augustus, Il Ristorante - Niko Romito boasts a spacious terrace and an elegant, welcoming dining room with mahogany walls adorned with works of art. The menu features traditional Italian cuisine reinterpreted with a light and imaginative touch as demonstrated by memorable dishes such as the chef’s own take on classic spaghetti in a tomato sauce.

Name: Quintogusto
Address: piazza Sandro Pertini 54 r, Savona, 17100, Italy
Description: Recently opened in the renovated section of Corso Italia in central Savona, Quintogusto is a small, contemporary and minimalist-style restaurant occupying one side of the former hospital. Here, the owner-chef (once sous-chef at the excellent Michelin-starred Il Vescovado in Noli) cements his reputation with Ligurian-influenced cuisine to which he adds his own modern and imaginative touches.

Name: Matteo Ristorante
Description: The soft-toned decor is modern and intimate, while the cuisine also has a contemporary feel. Dishes include meat and fish options, plus numerous types of risottos, many of which feature distinctly modern ingredients. Coffee service and aperitifs in the near Laboratory, at n 10.

Name: Pantagruele
Description: Situated in the town centre just a stone’s throw from the port, this small, typical trattoria is renowned for its delicious fish and seafood, including an excellent antipasto buffet and fresh fish cooked mainly on the grill. The large outdoor area is perfect for summer dining. Informal service.

Name: Trattoria Toscana al Vecchio Forno
Address: via Poliziano 18, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: If you are looking for a place to eat that is centrally located and has good prices, you have found it. Captivating trattoria atmosphere. Pretty summer garden.

Name: La Madia
Description: This authentic rural trattoria overlooking the valley and Franciacorta specialises in regional produce and typical Italian cuisine. Each dish on the menu lists the origin of the ingredients used, plus the name and address of the producer. Specialities include tagliolini pasta sautéed in a walnut sauce with tuna. Top quality cuisine offering excellent value for money.

Name: La Porta Antica
Address: via Quarto dei Mille 16, Brescia, 25128, Italy
Description: Having gained experience elsewhere in Italy, especially in Liguria where he gained confidence preparing the best-quality fish and seafood, Augusto Valzelli has returned home to demonstrate his own modern approach to fish cuisine. Fish-lovers will delight in his “gran crudo di mare” (raw fish selection) which allows the quality of the fish – the restaurant’s main attraction – to shine through. If you want to order this particular dish, it’s best to mention it when booking.

Name: La Bottega del 30
Address: via Santa Caterina 2, località Villa a Sesta, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
Description: There’s a story behind the name of this restaurant: on the 30th day of every month a travelling salesman used to stop in this small, delightful village. In the meantime, a young French chef, Hélène, arrived here and fell in love with Chianti and its cuisine. She named her restaurant after the travelling salesman and the name has been kept in his memory. In a typical setting of stone walls and old rural objects from bygone days, Hélène is now front-of-house taking care of guests, while Nadia Mongiat has replaced her in the kitchen, where she continues with the restaurant’s tradition of creating simple Tuscan cuisine. The focus here is on preparing ingredients in traditional ways, such as pork liver (the thinnest part of the liver is used) cooked at a low temperature and then stored in lard with fennel for a few days before being re-heated sous-vide in a bain-marie. As a result, the liver (served lukewarm on a bed of Tuscan green beans) is soft and delicious.

Name: Il Mirto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: When you arrive at the luxury Botania hotel, you’ll be accompanied through 3ha grounds of lush Mediterranean vegetation to the restaurant. You couldn’t have a better introduction to the cuisine that awaits at Il Mirto, where you can choose between two long tasting menus or a shorter four-course option featuring dishes from these menus. One of the menus is vegetarian, the other vegan and almost all the vegetables are sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden or from other local growers from Ischia. A delightful experience in a beautiful natural setting, with excellent service provided by young, friendly staff.

Name: Hydra
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Salerno, this is one of the city’s best restaurants. The dining room here is almost minimalist in style, yet thanks to the soft lighting and beautiful background music it has a pleasing atmosphere; in fine weather, tables are set out in a charming inner courtyard. The cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary, with a selection of light and creative meat, fish and vegetable dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: Dry Aged
Address: via Cesare Da Sesto 1, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: Two partners with significant experience opened this lively venue: the rooms combine modern and classic styles in an industrial-New York style decorated with works by major street artists. At the entrance, the glass counter shows off meats of different breeds to be enjoyed even charcoal grilled, but there are also other specialties: appealing dishes with a modern preparation and homemade pastas.

Name: Antica Trattoria Giovanelli
Description: Situated in a charming rural setting at the foot of the surrounding hills, this trattoria has been run by the same family (now on the third generation) since 1939. Regional cuisine is to the fore here, with cured hams and roast and boiled meats all featuring on the menu, as well as its highly recommended homemade pastas and the almond tart with zabaione.

Name: Volta del Fuenti by Michele De Blasio
Address: SS 163 Amalfitana km 47,300, Vietri sul Mare, 84019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Once you’ve passed through Vietri heading towards the Amalfi Coast, you come to the Giardini del Fuenti perched on a cliff sloping towards the sea. This hotel complex boasts a beach, terraced garden and the Riva Restaurant, which is open at lunchtime only and which also hosts various food and wine events. In a spacious dining room with large windows overlooking the beautiful bay, chef Michele De Blasio serves modern, elaborate and minimalist-style dishes based on reinterpretations of classic specialities from Campania, all showcased on two tasting menus and an à la carte. We particularly enjoyed the excellent and copious welcome snacks, with a special mention for the local speciality, Vietrese donkey meat, and the veal sweetbreads with citrus fruit, walnuts and rocket.

Name: Sushisen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Two smart dining rooms offer two different dining experiences at this restaurant: one with chairs at the bar and a conveyer belt of traditional Japanese dishes; the other serving contemporary Japanese cuisine, including the intriguing Omakase tasting menu. Nearly all the wines and sakes on the wine list are also available by the glass.

Name: Vineria Modì
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Taormina, this restaurant started out as a wine-bar which explains its name as well as the extensive wine list featuring over 1 000 different labels. Today, the wine accompanies fine cuisine prepared by a skilful female chef, whose brother oversees the front of house. Creative and elaborate dishes with a Sicilian flavour (as well as influences from elsewhere) are served in an elegant dining room and in an attractive outdoor space on the pedestrianised street.

Name: 177 toledo
Description: On the fifth floor of 177, via Toledo this restaurant exhibits works of art by contemporary artists in its elegant dining room. Delightful artisanal skills from Campania are also featured on the menu, which is made from handmade paper from Amalfi; the manner in which the menu is written recalls the game of Tombola (which originated in Naples), in original and creative reinterpretations of classic regional dishes.

Name: Autem*
Description: A modern direction with the kitchen well in view, even from the outside, just a short walk from Porta Romana, in a district buzzing with pubs and restaurants. The engaging initiative of bringing the menus written in the chef’s hand enhances the artisanal work and allows explaining the various dishes in person. This is the cuisine of Luca Natalini, a real Tuscan who loves illustrating his region and the produce he knows best: charcoal-grilled whole pigeon served with an offal tartlet is an excellent example of his culinary skill. A bright room at the entrance and a more private space at the back.

Name: Azotea
Description: Situated in a central location with a small outdoor space, this restaurant boasts a striking interior with old walls, a verdant decor and climbing plants that add a South American feel. The cuisine shines the spotlight on the chef’s native Peru, with appetisers such as potted umbrine tacos and delicious yet atypical antipasti such as raw squid with saltwort and peas. Soy sauce, umeboshi, and yuyo seaweed sauce provide added exotic flavour. We highly recommend one of the excellent cocktails, such as the slightly sour Americano with yuzu.

Name: Seraf Mahmutbey
Address: Mahmutbey Mahallesi, Peyami Safa Caddesi No:38/D, Bağcılar, Istanbul, 34200, Türkiye
Description: Sinem Özler sets great store by goods from local producers. You can taste and see this for yourself, because they are also for sale in the shop of this spacious, modern restaurant, just outside the city centre. For example, she works with Trakya Kivircik lamb in a bid to keep traditional recipes alive. The İçli Köfte with the same lamb is an absolute must. To bring those ancient Anatolian flavours to the table, this chef likes to use a wood-fired oven, and she never loses sight of the changing seasons and her surroundings.

Name: Orfoz Restaurant
Address: Kumbahçe Mahallesi, Zeki Müren Caddesi No:13/1, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The beautiful bay this restaurant overlooks is the pride of the Bozçağa brothers – not only for the azure waters, but also the bountiful fish and seafood they have to offer. The chefs' love for the sea is palpable in every dish, from the tuna sashimi with a light Asian touch to the oysters topped with a parmesan foam, and the perfectly grilled squid. The wine list is worth a look, as it is clearly a passion of the owners.

Name: Vogue Restaurant
Address: Süleyman Seba Caddesi No:92, BJK Plaza, A Blok Kat: 13, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34353, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Iconic photographs from the archives of the illustrious Vogue magazine lend the bright interior a fashion-forward touch, but it is the views of Dolmabahçe Palace and the Bosphorus that really steal the show. The extensive menu includes everything from Turkish classics and pasta to sushi and sashimi. So, you can look forward to both a knife-cut tuna tartare with fresh spring vegetables and a beautifully risen chestnut souffle with caramel and tahini. And why not round off your evening with a refreshing cocktail and a dance?

Name: Ristorante Pizzeria Venedik
Description: Venedik has been a popular spot in Izmir for over 40 years. Diners are drawn by the cosy Venetian decor and Italian classics prepared in time-honoured tradition. The tempting menu has something for everyone, from al dente hand-made ravioli with a delicate shrimp filling to crispy pizza alla turca, not to mention the deliciously creamy tiramisu. This is a perennial favourite in every sense of the word.

Name: Seraf Vadi
Address: Ayazağa, Kemerburgaz Caddesi No:7G, İç Kapı No:7, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34396, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Start your meal with the içli köfte, a house speciality combining a creamy yoghurt sauce with a steamed bun stuffed with highly aromatic lamb. And be sure to sample the other mezze, such as the imam bayildi: stuffed aubergine with a subtle smoky flavour, caramelised onion and candied red pepper. The main courses featuring various cuts of lamb are to die for. This contemporary restaurant not far from Vadistanbul Shopping Mall is a celebration of Anatolian culinary heritage.

Name: Lokanta 1741
Address: Alemdar Mahallesi, Profesör Kazım İsmail Gürkan Caddesi No:34, Cağaloğlu Hamamı, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This beautiful contemporary restaurant with a romantic roof terrace is right next to Cağaloğlu Hamam, through the door on the right. It serves Turkish culinary classics, some dating back to 1741, with a modern twist. The chef sometimes introduces surprising textures and flavours but never loses sight of tradition.

Name: Eleos Yeşilköy
Address: Ümraniye Mahallesi, Yeşilbahçe Sokak No.9, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34149, Türkiye
Description: Yeşilköy is a residential area outside the centre of Istanbul with airs of a seaside resort. A couple of streets away from the marina, you will find this exciting restaurant reminiscent of a Greek tavern. Delicious seafood is the speciality of the house. Think various mezze bursting with Mediterranean freshness. The sea bass is grilled to perfection and served simply, allowing the natural flavours of the fish to shine through. This is a great place to enjoy good no-nonsense food made from fresh, simple ingredients.

Name: Bağarası
Address: Bitez, Pınarlı Caddesi No:59, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: Authentic and welcoming are two words that sum up what Bağarası is all about. Simply to enjoy delicious food in a relaxed environment, this is the place to come. You can choose from a variety of mezze displayed in the refrigerated counter, including marinated cauliflower in red wine with caramelised onions. At the same time, you can order popular classics, such as grilled kofta or sea bass, for your main course. But do leave room for dessert, because you absolutely must try the sweet artichoke confit with ice cream – a house speciality!

Name: Tuğra Restaurant
Address: Çırağan Caddesi No:32, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
Description: At Tuğra you'll feel like royalty. Here you can bask in the historical splendour of the magnificent Çırağan Palace – the luxuriousness never fails to impress. Look beyond the marble pillars and admire the sparkling Bosphorus. Ottoman culinary tradition goes hand in hand with the customs of haute cuisine. Chef Emre Inanir puts his own spin on classic flavours. For instance, grilled beef liver is paired with crispy börek, deliciously unctuous on the inside, and an onion compote seasoned with sumac. What a combination!

Name: Rumelihisarı İskele
Address: Yahya Kemal Caddesi No:1, Rumeli Hisarı/Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34470, Türkiye
Description: A waterside pavilion on the impressive Bosphorus, which can be admired from any table. In this beautiful setting, the best the sea has to offer is what's on the menu. After some spicy mezze, choose from a wide range of fish and decide if you want it steamed, grilled or fried. There’s no pomp and ceremony here, just the enjoyment of the finest produce.

Name: Sunset Grill & Bar
Address: Kuruçeşme Mahallesi, Yol Sokak No:2, Ulus/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34345, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sunset Grill & Bar could be in a Hollywood film. This spacious, upscale restaurant is located in the heights of Ulus Park, providing a magnificent view of the city and the Bosphorus. It draws a well-heeled crowd, who come to enjoy classic French cuisine, Asian-inspired dishes and sushi, as well as an impressive wine list. This is the place to be!

Name: Mürver
Address: Novotel İstanbul Bosphorus, Kemankeş Caddesi No:57-59, Karaköy/Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The open fire is the heart of the open kitchen at Mürver. Smoked and grilled ingredients form the basis of the creations in which regional produce and innovative combinations make for a culinary adventure. Butter-soft grilled octopus with caramelised onion and a zingy vinaigrette is a signature dish for good reason. This trendy rooftop restaurant also boasts a fabulous cocktail bar where you can soak up the vibe and let Istanbul reveal all its charms on the sublime terrace.

Name: AŞEKA
Address: Müeyyedzade Mahallesi, Arap Oğlan Sokak No:6, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
Description: Within the walls of this rather unremarkable historical building tucked away on a side street in the Karaköy district, this restaurant with intimate lighting is done out in a tasteful palette of dark brown hues, and displays regularly changing artwork. To showcase his creativity, Ömer Akosman focuses exclusively on an à la carte approach. His dishes are not unnecessarily complicated, but bursting with flavour – spiciness and robust sauces make the difference here. An intense gravy and garnishes such as marinated tomatoes, kalamata olives and crispy polenta are the perfect accompaniment to the patiently braised beef.

Name: Zuma İstanbul
Address: İstinye Park No:461, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34460, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Istanbul branch of this chic Japanese restaurant is on a par with those in London and Dubai, among other places. That means top-notch ingredients showcased by a contemporary approach to authentic Japanese cuisine. On the menu: sushi, tempura dishes, fish from the robata grill, vegetarian options... High-quality produce and subtle influences from the East always hit the mark. Rest assured, the cosmopolitan Zuma feels right at home amid the most exclusive fashion boutiques.

Name: Beyti
Address: Şenlikköy Mahallesi, Orman Sokak No:8, Florya/Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34153, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beyti Güler is a living legend in Istanbul. Since the 1980s, Istanbulites have been coming to dine here in this stylish building, which is a fine example of nostalgic Turkish charm. The charcoal grill is at the centre of the kitchen, where the experienced chefs cook to perfection all kinds of meat. Traditional kebab fare as it should be.

Name: Borsa Restaurant
Address: Vaniköy Caddesi, Liseli Sokak, Adile Sultan Sarayı, Üsküdar, Istanbul, 34684, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The Adile Sultan Palace is an events venue that is as spectacular as its name suggests. A stroll through the building will give you a sense of its grandeur and splendour – characteristics that Borsa is fortunate to share. To dine against a breathtaking backdrop of the Bosporus, head to the terrace. This is an upmarket restaurant showcasing traditional Turkish cuisine on an à la carte basis. Think medium-rare roasted lamb served with a refreshing salad and grilled aubergine. Less is more at Borsa. Make sure you leave room for dessert – the classic katmer (crispy filo pastry filled with pistachio) is very tempting!

Name: Aila
Address: Büyükdere Caddesi No:76/B, Mecidiyeköy/Şişli, Istanbul, 34394, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Aila radiates luxury and grandeur. Smooth marble, high ceilings, dark wood: the decor is a feast for the eyes. Turkey's rich cuisine is given a contemporary twist, with the focus on spices – they even have a spice library – and getting the most out of top-notch produce. This modern take on tradition should definitely be combined with a glass of raki – what a selection!

Name: Akira Back İstanbul
Address: Ataköy 2-5-6. Kısım Mahallesi, Rauf Orbay Caddesi No:2/1 LB, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34158, Türkiye
Description: The view of the Sea of Marmara is the highlight of this modern and inviting restaurant located in the JW Marriott hotel. Be sure to go for a spot on the terrace! Akira Back has restaurants all over the world and has appointed one of his right-hand men as head chef in Istanbul. The dishes embody a distinctive fusion of predominantly Japanese and other Asian cuisines. Fine sushi, tasty gyoza, beef tataki that melts in the mouth, perfectly robata-grilled prawns… You will definitely want to come back for this contemporary whirlwind of Eastern flavours.

Name: The GALLIARD Vadistanbul
Address: Ayazağa Mahallesi, Cendere Caddesi No:109C, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34396, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: The upscale Vadistanbul shopping mall is home to The Galliard, a restaurant that exudes contemporary elegance and boasts a spacious waterfront terrace. The extensive menu comprises international favourites including a unique take on sea bass ceviche, creamy risotto-style creations, generous pizzas, stews quietly simmering in the background… and even soufflés for dessert! Don't be put off by the sheer number of options – these chefs work to the highest standards and their skills are second to none. Those who stay later in the evening can look forward to an electrifying DJ set.

Name: Tatbak
Address: Valikonağı Caddesi, Akkavak Sokak No:38/B, Nişantaşı/Şişli, Istanbul, 34365, Türkiye
Description: Tatbak has been the go-to kebab place for many an Istanbulite since 1960. They come for the retro setting, with its beautiful stained-glass windows and marble, but mostly for the local vibe and great value for money. The spicy lahmacun (Turkish pizza), and the kebab with lamb and minced beef are just two examples of their top sellers.

Name: 1924 İstanbul
Address: Istiklal Caddesi, Olivya Geçidi No:7, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34435, Türkiye
Description: The original incarnation of this restaurant was opened by Russian refugees in 1924. Today diners can relive those glory days in a beautifully restored and opulent setting that exudes historical grandeur and features eye-catching panelling and mirrors. Live music makes for a buzzing atmosphere. Here they put a modern spin on Russian specialities. Think generous portions of stuffed pirozhki and beef Stroganoff, juicy meat and amazing flavour. And to drink? A glass of vodka from their impressive selection, of course!

Name: Deraliye
Address: Divanyolu Caddesi, Alemdar Mahallesi, Ticarethane Sokak No:10, Sultan Ahmet, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: Deraliye is a landmark of the historic Sultanahmet neighbourhood. The colourful, opulent decor immediately catches the eye and, like the cuisine, is a tribute to the Ottoman Empire. Do you have a hankering for goose, lamb or duck kebab with spicy rice baked in a traditional tandoori oven? This is the place to discover the rich flavours of Ottoman cuisine.

Name: OCAK
Address: Hobyar Mahallesi, Mimar Vedat Sokak No:5, Fatih, Istanbul, 34112, Türkiye
Description: Exposed brick walls, soft lighting, marble details: OCAK is an appealing restaurant located in the Old Town area. The chef puts his own spin on Turkish tradition – thinkwonderfully creamy hummus with strawberries, sorrel and a pomegranate vinaigrette. He always manages to strike the right balance of traditional and contemporary in his combinations of bold flavours. Here, your curiosity will be piqued with every dish.

Name: Levan
Address: Kuşçular, Kuşcular Caddesi No:3, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Dining with a view of the vineyards, or surrounded by the grapevines on the terrace, is an experience that will leave a lasting impression. Levan offers a convivial atmosphere in a charming and intimate setting. On the chalkboard, you will find a dozen dishes, from mezze to share to main courses to savour on your own. The traditional cuisine of the Aegean coast is given a subtle new twist here. Rice-filled vine leaves served with a yoghurt cream and tomato sauce, and rich lamb stew cooked in white wine: get ready for a Mediterranean feast!

Name: Malva
Address: Torba, Kaynar Caddesi No:15, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Housed in luxury hotel Susona, this restaurant feels both elegant and hip – the adjacent bar regularly hosts DJs. But the most stunning feature of all is the breathtaking view of the coastline. The chef and his team will be happy to tell you about their commitment to sustainability, including a zero-waste approach and close collaboration with their suppliers. Their creative cuisine draws on traditional and modern influences, celebrating the authentic flavours of the ingredients. For instance, the courgette flowers stuffed with rice, minced beef and chopped mussels are seasoned with a classic blend of herbs and a judicious twist of lemon. The charcoal-grilled mussels add delightful smoky nuances. A compelling dining experience guaranteed!

Name: Amavi
Address: Alaçatı Mahallesi, 13003. Sokak No:1, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: Alaçati is a picturesque town with a lot to offer, but Amavi is the place to be for foodies. Walk through the cocktail bar, where DJs play in the evening, and take a seat in the trendy restaurant, which exudes its own unique elegance. The chef loves working with fish, and there is even a dedicated maturation cabinet in the open kitchen. His cuisine is a vibrant expression of his personality, as seen in his innovative take on ceviche of sea bream with samphire, fried quinoa and a pomegranate jus. Or you might prefer the barbecued dry-aged sea bass with its bold accoutrements. The chef will be more than happy to talk you through his captivating dishes.

Name: Orkide Balık
Description: At Orkide Balik, you can almost feel the sand between your toes as you enjoy your meal. The chef takes advantage of the restaurant's location to bring fresh fish straight from the sea to your plate. But before you order your main course, be sure to check out the mezze in the refrigerated counter. The dishes are prepared without any fuss, and with that traditional sense of generosity. Think marinated squid or deep-fried sea bass with aubergine and a bechamel sauce seasoned with mustard. Sometimes the best things in life are the simplest.

Name: İsabey Bağevi
Address: Gölcükler Mahallesi, 901. Sokak İstasyon Mevkii No:38, Menderes, Izmir, 35470, Türkiye
Description: The Isabey wine estate grows mostly Sauvignon Blanc, but you will find more than impressive rows of vines on its land. Indeed, there is a magnificent terrace on which to dine in the shade of a majestic poplar tree that is over 350 years old. This restaurant is committed to serving food and wine of the highest quality. The buttery lamb stock with medium-rare lamb chops and the squid stuffed with minced lamb and accompanied by a fine white wine sauce are testament to the depth and flavour of this classic cuisine.

Name: Lokanta Göktürk
Address: Göktürk Merkez, İstanbul Caddesi No:16/E, Eyüpsultan, Istanbul, 34077, Türkiye
Description: Leave the centre of Istanbul, head to Eyüpsultan district and sit down on the terrace or in front of the open kitchen. That's it, your work is done. Now all you have to do is enjoy! Muhsin Ertürk draws inspiration from, and puts a new spin on, recipes from Anatolian tradition, and has a penchant for regional produce. For instance, you can enjoy wonderfully creamy hummus, as well as prawns marinated in ginger then fried in garlic butter and served with creamy risotto, strands of soft cuttlefish and an aromatic clam broth. A creative blend of old and new!

Name: Sia Eli
Address: Gümüşlük Mahallesi, 1120. Sokak No:108, Gümüşlük, Bodrum, 48970, Türkiye
