It makes a big impression, and not just because of its expansive space. Snuggle up by the two-sided fireplace, nab a seat by the stage, where nightly live music is performed, or pull up a chair at the marble bar—it's all on offer. The best part? It's not just about good looks and sensational sips. Snack on a variety of sushi, including salmon motoyaki, a signature roll with chopped wild sockeye, steelhead trout, avocado, cucumber and warm motoyaki sauce. Miso soup is a good bet for a cold night, and braised local octopus is a simple delight. Local salmon and steelhead figure largely on the menu.

Name: Elephant
Description: Elephant is proof that tiny is often mighty. The space is decidedly diminutive but big-deal Chef Justin Ell (Lee) runs the show here, and diners may just feel as if they're dining in the chef's apartment. It's a wonder how he does all of this in this space but he makes the most of it, delivering a parade of plates in an "omakase" style. A tiny sachet of charred cabbage filled with roasted, Xian-spiced lamb, kale and black vinegar kicks things off. Creamy beef tartare with smoked oysters and bonito-flavored horseradish is rich and luxurious, then a dish of winter lettuce tossed in a potent fermented chili sauce with deep fried panko on top may seem simple but reflects this chef's vision for complementary, yet contrasting, cuisine.

Name: Tetsu Sushi Bar
Description: Omakase is typically an intimate affair, but at Testu Sushi Bar, only three lucky diners are served at once by two young and talented chefs. This isn't a hipster hangout—there's nothing flashy or trendy about this simple yet tasteful spot. While you won't find gold flakes or caviar gilding the lily, you will discover exceptional quality. The meal begins with a quartet of cool openers including poached Spanish mackerel with mountain potato and seawood sauce; coins of tender octopus in soy-dashi; Japanese cherry trout with battera kelp; and firefly squid with creamy miso-vinaigrette. Nigiri is crafted with care, with standouts including aged-smoked goldeneye snapper, bigfin reef squid with yuzu, and creamy cutlass fish.

Name: New Mandarin Seafood Restaurant
Description: This boisterous dining hall draws crowds for its highly enjoyable Cantonese fare, while dim sum rules the day and dinner service offers a wide range of specialties. The interior leans elegant with a curved wall of floor-to-ceiling windows, glittering crystal beaded chandeliers and a photo-realistic mural of cherry trees in blossom. However, families and groups looking for good eats and good times keep things grounded.Diners check off their dim sum choices from a printed menu bearing helpful photos for novices, and selections emerge from the kitchen freshly prepared and steaming hot. Some of the hits include black pepper pork biscuits; supple wasabi shrimp dumplings; and steamed hot/sour pork soup dumplings.

Name: Ophelía
Description: Stunning murals, colorful carvings...Ophelía is quite literally a bright spot in Vancouver's Olympic Village. It's always packed, so make a reservation. Of course, if you didn't plan ahead, a bevy of special margaritas will help you pass the time. Chef/co-owner Francisco Higareda prepares traditional pan-regional Mexican fare just as his mother, Ophelia, did. Corn-crusted octopus sided by cilantro rice, braised kale and zucchini is bested with a Oaxacan mole blanco that's rich and creamy. A trio of tacos rewards diners with delectable ingredients piled high atop locally made tortillas. End things with that ultimate classic—tres leches cake.Weather permitting, the outdoor patio is the spot to while away the night.

Name: Hawksworth Restaurant
Address: 801 W. Georgia St., Vancouver, V6C 1P7, Canada
Description: Respected native son Chef David Hawksworth helms this eponymous restaurant nestled inside the posh Rosewood Hotel Georgia. Enter through the lobby or directly from Georgia Street into an elegant bar where guests who look as if they just stepped off a fashion shoot sip well-crafted drinks. In the dining room, a shimmering chandelier and an eye-catching wall of wine set an elegant tone.Simple luxuries never disappoint, as in the caviar and oysters. Then, savor the light and elegant mushroom consommé stocked with meaty matsutake and foie gras. Agnolotti with hazelnut & celery foam is almost too pretty to eat, but then you'd miss the earthy umami of the roasted king oyster mushrooms. Finally, it's difficult to pick just one, so order the macaron sampling.

Name: PiDGiN
Description: There are many reasons why Vancouver is considered a culinary destination, and PiDGin certainly has something to do with that. Inside, stirring artwork from local artists, soft industrial lighting and wood banquettes set a city-chic tone. Chef Wesley Young has been running the show here for a handful of years, and his menu is distinctive. Playful, even irreverent, he is clearly having fun surprising diners with unusual combinations that not only work, but they wow. Signature dishes, like the Korean rice cakes cooked in an umami-rich gochujang "bolognese" with crunchy, spiced hazelnuts, make a nightly appearance. Other dishes include refreshing tuna tartare with nori puree and salty ikura, accompanied by taro root crisps.

Name: Sushi Bar Maumi
Description: Sushi omakases can be serious affairs that cost as much as a ticket to Tokyo, but this counter by Chef Maumi Ozaki is a refreshingly affordable alternative. Once seated at the counter with room for just under 20 guests, Ozaki gets right to business. His movements are practiced and confident and the quality ingredients are fresh and enticing. Expect around a dozen or more nigiri, with several standouts, including the botan ebi draped over rice and seasoned with a shake of salt. Sweet and creamy, it's a definite highlight. Gently smoked skipjack topped with grated ginger and green onion is a good bet, and Murasaki uni delivers on texture and taste. A wide variety of sake, champagne, shochu, and Japanese whisky serves as a nice accompaniment to the meal.

Name: L'Abattoir
Description: When a restaurant called L’Abattoir is found next to Blood Alley and Gaoler’s Mews, you do begin to wonder if Sweeney Todd ever visited Gastown. But as soon as you step inside this quasi-industrial setting you'll find yourself instantly relaxing, thanks to the warmth and enthusiasm of the team. Dining happens on the mezzanine level, where the lighting is flattering and the atmosphere fun; if you haven’t booked, then try for a seat at the bar downstairs which affords views of the kitchen. The chefs add a French accent to quality local ingredients; the baked oysters are a firm favorite, and the Fraser Valley duck with golden turnip will satisfy the hungriest of souls. Torn layers of buttery mille-feuille tucked with a salted honey cream with buckwheat and bourbon is a triumph.

Name: Delara
Description: Chef Bardia Ilbeiggi helms this restaurant where natural lights pours in, bursts of blue calm and lattice screens and paintings by local Iranian artist Golnaz Kianipour mesmerize.Complex and elegant, Delara's dishes deliver the essence of fresh, flavorful Persian cooking—tartness from dried limes, yogurt and berries; freshness from herbs; richness from nuts and seeds; and aromas from spices. Served in a deep bowl, hearty aush bobs with barley and legumes. Served with bread, it could be a meal alone, but don't stop there. Beef short rib with tangy gheymeh fills the room with a heady scent. Finally, turmeric and orange cake is a burst of sunshine with strong citrus notes.

Name: Bar Susu
Description: Note: This restaurant is temporarily closed.Bar Susu offers a concise range of well-prepared, creative dishes served in a laid-back setting that fashions itself as a wine bar focused on natural pours. The room sports a comfortable, vintage vibe with dark wood plank flooring, forest green walls and a touch of exposed red brick.Natural wines star, while clever cocktails feature fortified/aromatised wines, like the amaro with house-made kola syrup. The bold cooking here stands up to the beverage selection in compositions like fillets of torched mackerel resting in gem lettuce dabbed with emulsified bagna cauda; and smoked lamb belly slicked with warmly spiced jus and plated with minted grains and labneh. Pavlova in a pool of chicory-root crème anglaise is a delightful dessert.

Name: Riley's Fish & Steak
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the heart of downtown's waterfront, Riley's Fish & Steak lures guests with stunning views and a polished nautically informed interior that pours on the glamour. Don't let the high rollers and spendy tourists turn you off; the staff's warmth and the kitchen's precise techniques will charm you in no time. Dishes that may seem tried-and-true are far from ho-hum. Take the Louie salad, for instance, with Baby Gem lettuce bested with beautiful lump crab, crunchy onion rings, creamy avocado and Thousand Island dressing—it's refreshing and satisfying. Then, fish and chips is surprisingly light yet savory, thanks to the ultra-crisp batter. Charred broccolini with an herbaceous and citrus-forward gremolata is a virtuous side dish.

Name: Arike
Description: Though located in a dimly lit space below street level, you’d be well advised to keep your expectations elevated. Since opening, Arike has evolved and now offers a singular tasting menu. Named after Chef Sam Olayinka's Nigerian grandmother, this cooking displays depth, managing to feel both personal and inventive. The chef weaves together local ingredients with a broad range of global flavors, as in grilled leeks with a crayfish ginger chili sauce or grilled pineapple carpaccio tucked with mint and herbs. Exquisite boar is seared perfectly and accompanied by grilled plantain and sweet onion, but dessert may be the most impressive of all with a kicky chocolate cake set over a crème anglaise that teems with fragrant Thai basil oil, vanilla and citrus.

Name: Neptune Palace Seafood Restaurant
Address: 470 S.W. Marine Dr., Vancouver, V5X 0C7, Canada
Description: Ensconced on the second floor of the Marine Gate shopping mall, this expansive banquet hall-cum-restaurant is no secret to locals in search of excellent dim sum and Cantonese specialties. The spacious room readily accommodates large groups, the better to sample a wide range of mouthwatering options—though at peak hours, you may face wait times. During the day, the menu offers the traditional array of carefully prepared dumplings, many featuring exceptionally plump, juicy shrimp, as well as warming bowls of congee. At dinner, expect a broader variety of seafood, including pricier delicacies like lobster, abalone and sea cucumber, as well as a wide selection of meaty options, from crisp-skinned roasted duck to sweet and sour pork with pineapple.

Name: Bar Gobo
Description: Scrunched into a bare-bones space scarcely more ostentatious than the humble root vegetable whose name it bears, the appeal here is more than skin-deep. At first glance, an air of insouciance seems only fitting for a wine bar with pours exclusively from hip natural producers, but the friendly service will quickly allay any fear of snobbery. The best surprise is the cooking, emerging from a tiny corner kitchenette tucked behind the bar and offering an impressive degree of polish in a slim three-course prix fixe—utilizing local, seasonal ingredients, of course. Whether wild nettle tortelli or roasted halibut with fiddlehead ferns, expect clear, hearty flavors; add-ons like rosemary focaccia with burrata and a lightly smoky apple onion butter are similarly pleasing.

Name: Folke
Description: Friends Colin Uyeda and Pricilla Deo have brought bright, delicious plant-based fare to Kitsilano with Folke. A wall of wine greets guests at the entrance to this small-but-sophisticated spot where deep blue walls are adorned with original seaweed pressings and dried grasses complement the tranquil, coastal ambience. The fully open kitchen turns out impressive items. Don't skip the irresistible bread served with kale "butter" sprinkled with sesame seeds. A main dish of tender yet crunchy cabbage resting in a silky mole made from potatoes has terrifically tangy and smoky notes. In addition to the selection on display, the Folke team features a small selection of natural wine and locally produced ciders, as well as non-alcoholic libations to pair with your meal.

Name: Archer
Description: Nestled alongside high-end retailers in the posh shopping district, Archer fits right in. It's sexy and sultry here, where natural materials are abundant, white-washed walls are adorned with contemporary art, and dark wood tables are set with leather-covered chairs. Dining solo? The bar in back is the perfect perch.The kitchen gives local and seasonal ingredients the royal treatment in classic preparations like seared sablefish served with snow crab yuzu butter and crab chowder. In addition to offering a prix fixe, à la carte offerings include lush items such as creamy uni and ribbons of lardo atop toasted brioche, and a tenderloin cooked to perfection accompanied by pomme paillasson. Go for broke and add Hokkaido scallop for a luxe touch. Chocolate semifreddo makes a nice ending.

Name: Bonjour Vietnam Bistro
Description: With looks somewhere between a tropical greenhouse and a nightclub, plus a cool, clubby atmosphere, this lively, colorful boîte could just as well be in West Hollywood as Vancouver. Some of the plant life is artificial, but rest assured the homey Vietnamese fare is the real deal. A hip, fashion-forward clientele is drawn in by the cooking, but the energetic vibe and disarmingly sweet service can’t hurt. You might start with grilled skewers, like a pork sausage shaped around a lemongrass stalk, or a pepper-crusted beef carpaccio topped with fragrant herbs, crispy garlic and shallot—but save room for the soul-warming bowls of pho (a short rib version is noteworthy) and bun bo hue. Each item has a vegetarian counterpart, so there’s no shortage of options.

Name: Yuwa
Description: Yuwa's chic interior may lean European, but just one bite of Chef Masahiro Omori's creations and you'll be firmly planted in Japan. This is not fusion cuisine; instead, the chef adheres to the classics. External influences may not come into play, but freshness does—the menu shifts daily to take advantage of the best products available. His nigiri selection features a masterful presentation with a nest of radish threads, fragrant shiso leaf and crushed ice. Buttery chutoro melts in your mouth, and the other offerings might include  snappy, clean-tasting nodoguro, premium kinmedai, delicious sayori and local bluefin tuna, but it's the sockeye salmon that will be etched in your memory forever.

Name: Ask for Luigi
Description: There are myriad reasons why we all eat out – to meet up with friends, to be seen, to celebrate special events – but at the most basic level it’s about getting fed, and no one feeds you quite like Ask for Luigi. Pasta is the order of the day, whether that’s pappardelle with rich duck ragu or bigoli with an abundance of shellfish; dishes that are as generous in size as they are in flavor—many plates are large enough for two. If you can take on Luigi’s meatballs and still finish your pasta dish, then take a bow.It’s a cute little corner spot, more cabin than restaurant, with just 32 seats, and everything has been cleverly thought through. So, start with an aperitivo, be prepared to share and do explore the exclusively Italian wine list.

Name: Bao Bei
Description: Bao Bei may mean "precious," but there's nothing twee about this brasserie located at the edge of Vancouver's old Chinatown. Instead, Chef Joël Watanabe shows off his playful, creative cooking style, delivering food that's inventive and fun. Far from traditional, these unique takes on classic Chinese cuisine are crafted from top-notch ingredients. Take the "kick ass fried rice," their savory and a tad sweet version of the ubiquitous standard. This dish punches above its weight with an ingenious blend of prawns, bitter melon, masala-preserved mushrooms and papadam. Mantou buns filled with braised pork, hoisin, pickled ginger and miso-serrano aioli are positively irresistible, and even seemingly simple plates, like braised pea shoots with garlic, bring the flavor.

Name: Wildlight Kitchen + Bar
Address: 5380 University Blvd., Ste. 107, Vancouver, V6T 0C9, Canada
Description: Wildlight Kitchen + Bar is at the center of the quickly growing community of leləm̓ Village. This light-filled space is enhanced with natural and organic decorative elements, but the relaxed sophistication belies the serious nature of Chef Warren Chow's kitchen, where sourcing is paramount. Begin with a stunning charcuterie board that substitutes seafood for the ubiquitous meat to snack on everything from house-made salmon pastrami, marinated Salt Spring Island mussels, and pickled sea asparagus to tataki of smoked albacore tuna and cod rillette topped with cured ikura. A thick fillet of Gindara sablefish rests over soba noodles with baby bok choy for a main dish that is deeply satisfying. Finally, go for broke and order both the caramelized honey cheesecake with cardamom granola crust and the lemon tart.

Name: Botanist
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Glide through the elegant lobby and up the sweeping staircase of the Fairmont Pacific Rim to arrive at Botanist, where dressing up is de rigueur. Headed by the passionate Chef Hector Laguna, the kitchen takes great pride in sourcing the best local product, whether it's wild, locally caught seafood or produce from the Fraser Valley. Every dish on this modern Canadian menu is delightful, but some of the standouts include hand-cut tagliatelle bathed in a mushroom sauce and crowned with wild mushroom ragout. Pan-seared striploin is perfectly cooked, resting alongside a tender cabbage roulade stuffed with lush beef tongue, Chinese broccoli and spicy XO sauce. To finish, desserts are impressive; especially when faced with the refreshing lemon syrup-soaked cake dressed with Meyer lemon curd and bay leaf ice cream.

Name: Bacchus
Description: Bacchus is very special indeed. Cocooned inside the Wedgewood Hotel & Spa, this elegant restaurant is the kind of place where quotidian concerns immediately disappear. Just off the intimate lobby, where stunning flower arrangements, a glittering chandelier and marble reception area exude tasteful luxury, Bacchus transports guests to a more refined era. There's even a grand piano to boot. Of course, it's not all style and no substance; Chef Montgomery Lau turns out classic but  memorable dishes. Humble tomato soup is elevated; halibut from Haida Gwaii delivers a clean, sweet flavor complemented by a cool "chopped salad" of shaved apples, anise-sweet roasted fennel, beets and cucumber. Desserts by Kraków-born Chef Chris Janik will surprise and delight.

Name: ¿CóMO? Taperia
Description: Prepare for a trip to Spain sans passport when pulling up a seat at ¿CóMO? Taperia—that is if you can score one at this perpetually packed spot. Equal parts tapas bar and despensa/bodega, it boasts all the warmth, authenticity and conviviality of similar spots in Spain.From the fritos and the raciones to a whole world of spectacular conservas, there's plenty to whet your appetite. Start with the tart and fleshy boquerones accompanied by a side of pan con tomate. If the silky berenjenas con miel are on the menu, go for it—you won't be disappointed. Daily specials show the kitchen's flair for bridging classic Spanish fare with local product.Rare Spanish wines are a special treat here, so have the server guide you through a wine pairing.

Name: Chang'An
Description: Diners flock here to indulge in the waterfront views and the sometimes-fiery culinary specialties from Shaanxi, but the signature theatricality is what gilds the lily. Peking duck is given a prima donna treatment: it must be ordered beforehand on the phone, later to appear tableside with a fanfare of flambéed rum. After the choice morsels of crisp golden skin and tender meat have been artfully carved and served, you’ll even get an encore, where the last bits of the duck are transformed into a soup or a rustic peppery stir-fry. Those unwilling to make an advance commitment will find no shortage of other diversions, from pricy seafood delicacies to hearty dishes of roast lamb, not to mention satisfyingly chewy hand-pulled biang biang noodles.

Name: Sushi Jin
Description: A nondescript facade and a location tucked amidst forgettable neighbors mean you could miss Sushi Jin, but don't. This place is tiny but mighty, with room for just six at the bar, plus two additional tables. It is something of a local secret, but those in the know come here for traditional Japanese served with a distinctive voice. Begin with otsumami like live lobster sashimi topped with osetra caviar in an olive oil and thick, savory soy sauce finished with fresh satsuma rind.Ankimo in a ponzu bath is brilliantly simple yet luxurious, followed up by miso soup in lobster broth that is far from humdrum. Nigiri, from hirame to anago, balance sweet and salty, but the otoro with Hokkaido uni and white baby prawn is as pretty as it is pleasing.

Name: Café Medina
Description: The clink of glasses, the hissing steam of the cappuccino maker, even the shuffling back and forth to the counter by loyal patrons...Café Medina hums with activity all day long. This casual spot attracts locals who flock here for hearty Mediterranean-style fare. Mornings are especially great here—it's when egg dishes take center stage. The heady smell of freshly made Belgian waffles may have you trying to jump the (long) line outside, but ask nicely and they'll share a few of the hand-sized waffles while you wait. Once seated, don't waste any time deciding, as the paella is a must order. Inspired by the Spanish classic, their version is made with orzo flecked with cubes of smoky, spicy chorizo, roasted vegetables, avocado and a textbook-perfect fried egg.

Name: Elisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the heart of Yaletown, this stunning steakhouse is an inviting space where contemporary style blends with serious chops—quite literally. The butcher shop next door isn't just for show; it's a defining principle of this kitchen that sources only the best. Bite into the thoroughly enjoyable Dungeness crab spring roll before considering something from their tartare menu, which runs the gamut from traditional and vegetable-focused to gamey smoked bison from Turtle Valley. Steaks are sourced locally in British Columbia and from the U.S., and there is a selection of Japanese wagyu for deep-pocketed diners. The Vancouver cut, bone-in tenderloin is just perfect, though beef Wellington or Nonna's coniglio brasato are also good choices.

Name: Suyo
Description: The façade may be simple (think white-washed cement with a black framed door) but inside, this place is one-of-a-kind. Filled with greenery and stunning tall plants, plush seating and elegant lighting, Suyo is sophisticated without a trace of fuss. Word is out, so make a reservation, unless you care to take the chance of finding a seat at the always bustling bar. Hamachi tiradito, with its supple slices and bright yellow sauce, impresses at the first bite. White asparagus is grilled, then topped with a vibrant huancaína and tart salsa verde atop a purple potato puree. Arroz con pato delivers that beloved, rustic taste while riffing with the addition of duck confit. Conclude with the chocolate tres leches cake with berries and whipped toasted honey.

Name: Torafuku
Description: The main influences on the cooking at Torafuku come from countries like Korea, Japan and Taiwan, so it seems entirely apt that this restaurant is located close to, but not in Chinatown. Lunch is quick and easy and all about rice bowls featuring kakuni-style braised meats, but at dinner the kitchen’s more adventurous side comes out to play. This is when you’ll discover more European elements to the dishes, like tuna tataki with Niçoise salad or Brome Lake duck rillette; and if there’s a dish you simply must order it’s their wonderful Basque cheesecake. The open kitchen is the focus of the understated room, which makes use of plenty of concrete for that ersatz-industrial look. Those of a more sociable bent will enjoy the communal table.

Name: Osteria Savio Volpe
Description: Clean and contemporary, with white marble and modern light fixtures, Osteria Savio Volpe could easily fit right in on a street in Milan, Naples or Rome. Simple materials, including red-and-brown tiles and a muted palette, set a modern tone for cuisine that takes inspiration from the regions of Italy while balancing authenticity and expectations. Dig in to warm and tender garlic knots studded with black pepper and a thatch of grated pecorino. Sop up every last dot of the piquant marinara—it's worth the additional charge. Thinly sliced beef carpaccio is plated in traditional fashion, then topped with a flavorful leek-accented aioli, and creste di gallo is an ideal pasta for the richly flavored lamb ragu with zippy sage and pecorino.

Name: Fanny Bay Oyster Bar
Description: It doesn't get much more tide to table than Fanny Bay Oyster Bar. Tucked on a quiet street within walking distance from the city's stadiums, this hot spot gets crowded, especially on game days, and for good reason. This menu features some of the best shellfish and seafood-driven entrees around. Should your shucking skills be slightly rusty, they'll gladly offer a primer. Whether perched at the bar or settled in at a table, raw bar items should be top of mind. Prefer cooked items? The grilled oysters, served hot and bubbly, shellacked with Creole butter and a fresh herb-flavored gremolata, will float your boat. Then, tuck in to intensely rich sablefish collar, served crisped alongside with hot-sweet peppadew puree and grilled shishito peppers.

Name: Bacaro
Address: 1029 W. Cordova St., Vancouver, V6C 0B9, Canada
Description: From its marble-clad entrance to its modern furnishings and bright colors, bacaro bridges cool elegance and simplicity, and blends right in with the upscale lobby of the Fairmont Pacific Rim. The address may be Vancouver, but this spot is decidedly Venetian with its menu leaning toward the art of cicchetti, or small bites enjoyed on the go while quaffing a glass of wine. Some of the best  include sardines in saor, and fusilloni, enrobed in a veal and pork ragu with chanterelles and red wine-braised snails, is nothing short of divine. Capesante, or seared scallops in a cannellini bean stew crowned by fish-stuffed cabbage and a baci-baci sauce, is a Venetian kiss.

Name: Chef's Choice Chinese Cuisine
Description: Copper and wood panels lend a handsome appeal to the dining room, but make no mistake: Chef's Choice Chinese Cuisine deals in spectacular food. The kitchen offers dishes that are unique and classic, including many not often seen on other menus. Peruse the "kitchen specialties" to discover dishes like Chinese wine-marinated crispy duck tongues and kidneys. Few things beat a warm bowl of congee with dried oyster, salty pork and preserved egg. Minced pork and seafood soup dumplings are steamed pockets of soul-soothing and savory broth, but it's the signature marinated chicken with thick and fragrant black truffle sauce that lives up to the hype.

Name: Homer St. Cafe
Description: Nestled within a hip neighborhood, Homer St. Cafe entices with its inviting patio, but step inside and and you'll quickly see that this contemporary bistro is no slouch indoors, either. Equal parts trendy and quirky, with chairs doubling as wall hangings, Homer St. Cafe delivers on its promise of comfort food done really well. The rotisserie chicken is the draw, brined in their signature sauce overnight to render tender, flavorful meat. Order it half or whole and then tuck in to the crispy skin doused in gravy or buttermilk ranch. Sided by fluffy, buttery biscuits, it's a stick-to-your-ribs satisfying meal. If you have room, order the cheesecake with white chocolate-almond crumble resting over quince preserve.

Name: Cioppino's
Description: When there’s a business deal to close or in-laws to impress, look no further than Cioppino’s. This big, bold restaurant has been part of the city’s restaurant landscape for over 20 years and was an early pioneer in this part of town. It’s run with smooth, confident efficiency, so you can relax and just get on with the job in hand. The menu offers a roll call of classic Italian and Mediterranean dishes, from calamari and cannoli to prosciutto and pappardelle; all executed with care and craftmanship using locally sourced and seasonal ingredients. One taste of the deliciously silky and expertly rendered gnocchi cacio e pepe will result in your abandoning any attempts at mastering this Roman classic at home and vowing instead to simply always come to Cioppino’s whenever you fancy it.

Name: Carlino
Description: It’s only fitting that this verdant sanctuary should be tucked away on a terrace of the Shangri-La Hotel, offering a sense of placid elegance. The cuisine is inspired by Friuli, in Northern Italy (as well as neighboring Trentino-Alto Adige and Veneto) and reflects the area’s Slavic and Germanic influences—think braised cabbage agrodolce with pork cutlet Milanese. The menu displays a typically Italian devotion to simplicity, celebrating seasonal produce from local farms. Freshly made pastas are a feature, in particular regional specialties like cjarsons, a half-moon shape that might be filled with creamy beet puree and gilded with poppy seed butter. At dinner, a family-style tasting option (dubbed “fai tu” or “you pick”) puts the kitchen in charge.

Name: per se Social Corner
Description: They may occupy a corner location, but this well-run establishment deserves center stage. It's the sort of place where you might pop in for a tapa or two one night, then return a few nights later to tuck into a heartier pasta. Service is accommodating and friendly, and the menu is loaded with items that will please many diners.Nestle in to one of the side booths for an enjoyable meal. Hummus is sized generously and served with warm, freshly made flatbread. Salads, such as the heritage greens with crispy goat cheese and candied walnuts, are lovingly made. Lobster & crab ravioli in a chipotle coconut milk reduction is a top pick, while come dessert, you'll be debating between the tiramisu or pizza di Nutella.

Name: noumi
Description: The restaurant in the basement of the venerable grand hotel Bellevue Palace (Switzerland's official accommodation for foreign dignitaries) used to be Bern's mint – the name is a derivation of "numismatics". The atmosphere is cosmopolitan, chic and relaxed (the resident DJ plays in the evening). In the open kitchen, the chefs prepare "world food" incorporating influences from Asia, Peru and the Mediterranean. The dishes are made with excellent ingredients and are also suitable for sharing. Competent and laid back in their approach, the waitstaff provide recommendations from the selection of fine wines and interesting cocktails.

Name: Ilge
Description: This restaurant is housed in an old half-timbered building in the heart of this idyllic little town. The interior design is chic and tasteful, and in fine weather there is a lovely terrace overlooking the pedestrian zone. Serbian-born Zoran Baratovic presides in the kitchen, turning out dishes that draw on classical and Mediterranean influences. We highly recommend the mouthwatering veal shank ravioli. And to accompany your meal, the attentive maitre d', who is always on hand, will provide you with a well-curated wine list that includes one or two interesting magnums.

Name: Auberge de la Couronne
Description: Housed in a tastefully renovated traditional edifice, the Auberge de la Couronne morphs from a simple bistro at lunchtime into a fine dining gourmet establishment in the evenings. Generosity and indulgence are the order of the day in dishes such as crisp golden roasted sweetbread served with fresh crayfish and crunchy glazed mini vegetables. The front-of-house team is on hand to help you find the perfect food-wine pairing as you take a seat in the handsome vaulted dining room.

Name: La Fontana
Address: Via ai Monti della Trinità 44, Locarno, 6600, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Splendidly located inside the Hotel Belvedere, at an altitude of approximately 240m, this elegant south-facing restaurant boasts a splendid terrace and a lounge space. Depending on where you sit, watch the chef at work in the kitchen or enjoy the impressive views through La Fontana’s ground floor picture windows overlooking its verdant surroundings. The culinary focus here is on modern and seasonal Mediterranean cuisine without neglecting the region’s gastronomic roots. In addition to the classic menu, you can also choose the 4- or 5-course tasting option as well as the restaurant’s signature dishes such as the La Fontana tartare, the Chateaubriand, and the Raviolini del Plin. The extensive glass-fronted wine cabinets at the entrance provide an impressive backdrop.

Name: Au Vieux Manoir
Description: This spot is truly the stuff of dreams! Built in 1882 by renowned physician Dr Victor Guénebaud, the property boasts historical charm and a magnificent location, complemented by what is probably one of the finest terraces in the Valais canton! Inside, aesthetically pleasing details such as a wonderful old parquet floor, a beautifully crafted wooden ceiling and striking fabric wallpaper make for a stylish setting. The chef-patron's French-based cuisine alone merits a visit – the dishes are expertly prepared with top-notch, super-fresh ingredients. Should you wish to spend the night in this wonderful place, book one of the five comfortable guestrooms done out in a tasteful, classical style.

Name: Restaurant LA
Description: If you're not careful, you might end up walking right past the narrow façade of this mid-terrace restaurant. Here, an intriguing modern dining experience is proposed – and that goes for both the minimalist interior and the seasonal cuisine. Available as a set menu or à la carte, the dishes are well-thought-out, with harmoniously balanced flavours. From some tables it is possible to see into the kitchen. In summer, there is terrace seating on the pavement overlooking the tram line.

Name: GLACIER
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a great location right in front of the Eiger North Face! The fine dining restaurant of the chic boutique hotel (also called GLACIER) makes the most of its surroundings with a floor-to-ceiling window front – and a wonderful terrace for a magical view! The cuisine is ambitious, modern, creative and seasonal. In the evening, a set menu is available in three formats: "Découverte" with three courses, "Promenade" with five courses and "Excursion" with seven courses (the last two courses are surprise dishes). There are vegetarian versions of all three. Great emphasis is placed on selecting high-quality ingredients, with a preference for supplies from local producers. The 320-year-old wine cellar is home to around 500 labels, 160 of which are also available by the glass. An enthusiastic sommelier provides astute recommendations.

Name: Gasthof zum Rössli by Vittorio Conte
Description: This traditional restaurant is run by Vittorio Conte, who previously served up MICHELIN-starred star cuisine at Osteria TRE in Bubendorf. He has also made a name for himself outside Switzerland. With the motto "a few products – different textures", his dishes draw on Italian and Swiss influences. Everything is pared down to the essentials, and the produce takes centre stage. In the evening, an ambitious set menu is served – this must be pre-ordered. The terrace in the garden is delightful in summer.

Name: Gandria
Description: Chef-patron Adriano Peroncini is originally from Puglia, but his years of travelling took him through Italy and far beyond. Since 2016 he has had his own restaurant, here in Zurich's Seefeld district. In this nice, cosy space, where an inviting atmosphere reigns, he introduces diners to his fresh southern Italian-inspired cuisine – good choices from the menu include the octopus or Piedmontese Fassona beef and, of course, the delicious pasta dishes! In addition, there is an exclusively Italian wine list that covers most of the wine-growing regions, as well as "servizio alla maniera italiana" – authentic service that will make you feel at home!

Name: La Terrasse Brasserie
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Befitting the elegance that characterises the Victoria Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa, which is steeped in tradition, a classically refined atmosphere awaits you here. The location against the impressive backdrop of the mountains is a real draw in itself. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace on the promenade! The menu includes a broad assortment of Arab, Asian, Mediterranean and Swiss dishes – flavoursome food made from high-quality ingredients.

Name: Millennium - La Brasserie
Description: Set in the prestigious Millenium complex, a state-of-the-art business and conference centre, the elegant La Brasserie is under the expert supervision of Fabien Foare. This is the go-to place for a business lunch. A pared-down, less expensive lunchtime menu gives way to more ambitious fare in the evening, with a choice between "Les Inspirations", dishes created to reflect the seasons (cooked and raw Puits d'Amour melon), and "Les Incontournables" such as free-range guinea fowl supreme or fillets of perch from Lake Geneva). Not to mention the trolleys laden with charcuterie and pastries, which will have your mouth watering from the aperitif right through to dessert! The gourmet grocery shop is open in the afternoons.

Name: Trübli
Description: There are plenty of reasons to stop off at this historical inn (1785) located in the heart of the old town – the cosy and relaxed atmosphere, the friendly and experienced service team, the wonderful food. In the evening, the concept is a surprise set menu comprising three courses (a vegetarian version is also available), to which you can add an extra dish and/or a dessert. The extremely dedicated chef brings a personal touch to the service, and his passion for wine is palpable, not least in his excellent recommendations drawn from the nicely curated wine list with a focus on German estates. There is a pretty terrace in front of the house. Tip for motorists: the public car park 200m away.

Name: Esprit par Guy Ravet
Description: The setting by Lake Geneva is genuinely remarkable – during the summer, the terrace becomes a standout feature, offering a magnificent view! This restaurant is housed in the luxurious Grand Hôtel du Lac, which dates back to 1868. Its elegant interior, complete with a bright and airy conservatory, does full justice to the location, as does the food. Under the guidance of executive chef Guy Ravet, the menu is seasonal and based on French cuisine; tradition and modernity come together harmoniously. Dishes such as grilled Grisons salmon or Swiss Grand Cru entrecôte exemplify this fusion. You can order à la carte, but the proposed set menu is equally recommendable.

Name: PURO
Description: The restaurant on the first floor of the Mövenpick Hotel serves interesting and ambitious cuisine. This comes in the form of a very appealing fusion concept of Asian and Latin American-inspired dishes made with plenty of regional produce, but also ingredients from around the globe. The food is down to earth, flavoursome and fresh! This is complemented by an international wine list, extremely friendly service and a stylish interior.

Name: Le 42
Description: This stylish restaurant, part of the comfortable and tastefully designed Hotel Le White, is located right at the entrance of the village, facing the Dents du Midi mountain range. The decor here is a draw in itself; the seating is spread over two levels, with sleek modern furnishings complemented by warm reclaimed wood and quarry stone, creating a pleasing Alpine feel. The proprietor personally attends to the diners, while his partner manages the kitchen. Her French heritage is reflected in her dishes (be sure to leave room for dessert and try the classic rum baba), but she also incorporates international – especially Asian – influences, such as in her unique take on gyoza.

Name: Equo 1706
Description: Records of this building go back to 1706, at which time it was a tavern. Today, the restaurant of the Rössli hotel, which is not far from Vierwaldstätter See, has a nicely pared-back interior and a pleasant terrace. It serves ambitious modern cuisine with seasonal and international influences – you can order à la carte or opt for the surprise menu. Hotel patrons get to relax in well-kept guestrooms and the spa facilities.

Name: Le Partage
Description: Located in the luxury Aïda Hotel and Spa, this restaurant’s concept is downright intriguing. The set menu is served in courses, each of which is comprised of several small dishes and diners choose either 10 or 15 "tasting portions" to be shared. The ambitious cuisine rolls out a regional score courtesy of a wide range of local ingredients. Established on two floors, the Alpine-inspired interior is both welcoming and stylish thanks to a profusion of reclaimed wood and dressed stone, elegant herringbone parquet flooring and an open fireplace, complemented by high-quality fabrics and splendid solid wood tables, without forgetting the knockout view from the terrace. The front-of-house staff is friendly, attentive and polished. Teatime in the lounge and brunch on Sundays.

Name: Au Mai
Description: A dapper restaurant with a smart, minimalist interior and large windows that let in plenty of light. In one of the dining spaces, a glass partition offers views into the kitchen, where the seasonal dishes, mainly of Italian and Mediterranean inspiration, are prepared. Pasta is also on the menu. The quality, craftsmanship and seasoning are all on point. The food finds its perfect partner in the Swiss and Italian wines. Also a pastry chef, the owner ensures that the dessert menu includes an excellent choice of ice creams and tarts. In summer, diners can make the most of the covered terrace – despite its roadside location, you have a view of meadows, villages and mountains. There is also the option of staying overnight.

Name: Sonne Seuzach
Description: Located in the town centre, Sonne is an inviting restaurant. The interior is tastefully sleek, the atmosphere warm and welcoming, and there is a gorgeous terrace out in front of the glass-paned façade. The cuisine is seasonal, and showcases a range of regional produce. Reduced menu at lunchtime. Friendly and professional front-of-house team. There is also a bar. Modern guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Badalucci
Description: A historic restaurant with its roots in Italian cuisine. Originally from the island of Procida in southern Italy, the chef here focuses mainly on fish-based dishes, although the menu also features delicious meat options and vegetarian recipes for each course – whatever you order, seasonal ingredients are to the fore in this urban-style eatery situated slightly away from the centre. The wine list highlights the owners’ passion for champagne via highly respected labels from interesting small-scale producers.

Name: Le Restaurant
Description: The stylish restaurant of the tasteful and historical La Couronne hotel not only has a unique atmosphere but also promises exquisite French and Swiss-inspired cuisine served by a friendly and attentive front-of-house team. The location in the old town, nestled beside Kathedrale St Ursen, is a draw in itself; the terrace in front of the hotel makes for a delightful spot in which to "see and be seen" – especially during a romantic sunset. The wine list comprises some 150 moderately priced labels and includes a decent selection of half bottles. The fantastic wine bar is ideal for a nightcap. Smaller lunchtime menu. Tip: Complement your culinary adventure with a leisurely stroll between Baseltor and Bieltor.

Name: La Padella
Description: Cornelia and René A Donatz run their business with great dedication. In an elegant rustic-style decor, they serve good fresh cuisine, including classic veal dishes, Angus beef "bestsellers", vegetarian fare and fish such as Graubünden salmon from Lostallo. They stock some 550 wines (20 available by the glass) – a passion of the owner. Donatz Wine Bar proposes a smaller menu. Hotel Donatz has appealingly modern and comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Wirtschaft zur Rosenburg
Description: Wherever you look, there's history – the old fortified tower is magnificent! As well as international cuisine, the owner has been serving up local specialities such as whitefish fillet and dishes with pork from whey-fed pigs for more than 25 years. The courtyard terrace is especially pleasant. Tip: This pretty restaurant also makes an ideal venue for weddings and other celebrations.

Name: La Table du Palafitte
Description: The “Menu Découverte” carries guests away on a journey inspired by the time-honoured culinary traditions of the Mediterranean coast. Choose between the dining room or the large waterfront terrace.

Name: ROSI
Description: With its vibrant atmosphere and unique charm, this inviting self-proclaimed "neo-Bavarian" restaurant stands out from the crowd. It embodies a fusion of trendy, urban-casual vibes and cuisine inspired by the owner's Allgäu roots. In the four-course "Schmankerl Menu", the 12-course "Wirtshaus Maximus Menu" and the small à la carte selection, Markus Stöckle transforms traditional dishes into original creations packed with flavour. A prime example is the "Radi Wickerl" (braised leaves, sansho, pickled kombu and radish). The wine list, which includes a selection of natural wines, is also impressive. The service is pleasingly down-to-earth and friendly – the charismatic proprietor is also on hand, making sure each guest feels well looked after.

Name: parkhuus
Description: The restaurant of the luxurious Park Hyatt international business hotel is spacious and high-ceilinged . It has an open kitchen, upscale furnishings and sophisticated modern lighting; the glassed-in wine library, with its outstanding exclusive wine selection, is well worth seeing! Chef Tarik Lange and his team prepare modern dishes that are available as a set menu or à la carte.

Name: Spices Kitchen & Terrace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The aromas that waft out of the large show kitchen here are sure to get your taste buds tingling with their promise of pan-Asian delights from Japanese to Chinese, Thai and Indian dishes, all authentic and made using the very best ingredients. There’s also a stunning view!

Name: L'Etoile
Description: Whether you are seated in the chic bistro, in the winter garden or in the attractive shaded garden, this family-run establishment offers a warm welcome and a friendly atmosphere. The seasonal menu, with dishes prepared to order, features local producers. The thick and creamy crème brûlée, delicately flavoured with orange, is unforgettable. The set lunch menu is a must!

Name: Windows
Description: This restaurant of Hôtel D'Angleterre commands a panoramic view of Lake Geneva and its emblematic Jet d'Eau, with the mountains and Mont Blanc in the distance. Fresh, seasonal produce takes the limelight in well-crafted French cuisine that mixes classical and traditional influences and which is quite the equal of its splendid setting! Pop into the Leopard Bar for evening cocktails in a buzzy, jazzy vibe, (there is a cigar lounge in the basement). Afternoon tea is very popular, as are Sunday brunches.

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye de Montheron
Description: Located in a former Cistercian monastery that dates back to 1442, this restaurant proposes food that is very much of the moment. The original and exciting dishes draw heavily on local organic produce and heritage vegetables. Diners are won over by thoroughly modern fare that has been devised with a genuine concern for sustainability, such as suckling lamb served with pak choi and rhubarb. Appealing terrace on the edge of the forest, and a young and trendy atmosphere. A winning formula.

Name: Chez Be
Description: Following on from their successful restaurant, Amrein's, the amiable couple at the helm has embarked on a new culinary adventure. Romy takes good care of customers, while Beat cooks up fresh Mediterranean dishes. Shorter menu at lunchtime. The charming modern bistro-style interior with its open kitchen and the terrace giving onto the little square (Mühleplatz) are both lovely places to sit and eat.

Name: Sablier
Description: Definitely one of the coolest restaurants in town, this is the sort of place you might expect to find in London or New York. On the eighth floor of a newly built section of the airport, the high ceilings, exclusive interior, two large glass-fronted wine cabinets and stylish bar are impressive. The rooftop terrace has to be the highlight! French-inspired cuisine; Sunday brunch. Use car park 4, south exit.

Name: Silex
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is located in a lively residential area. Plenty of Swiss produce goes into the modern seasonal dishes, which are created in the partially visible kitchen. The restaurant is just as committed to sustainability as it is to wine – selected by connoisseurs, the distinctive wine list is testament to a true passion for the grape. British-born chef George Tomlin, previously sous-chef at London's The Clove Club, expresses his creative streak in dishes such as grilled slices of elm mushroom with roasted black onions and a creamy buttermilk and roasted yeast espuma. You can opt to go à la carte or take the five-course tasting menu (also vegetarian). The vibe is deliberately kept simple, with a decor boasting clean lines, and there is a nice terrace outside, in front of this corner plot. The service is friendly and laid back. Just the sort of restaurant you would want in your neighbourhood!

Name: Potato-FINE FOOD RESTAURANT
Description: This pleasant little restaurant in a lively street (Bahnhofstrasse) has a down-to-earth and friendly atmosphere, where the cordial service is in invitation to sit back and enjoy your evening, while. Tasty modern dishes are served in the form of a set menu made from top-notch regional ingredients sourced from within a 50km radius whenever possible.

Name: Lumières
Description: The location is simply divine! The restaurant at the Château Gütsch hotel affords a magnificent view over the city and the lake surrounded by mountains, especially from the large terrace – it is the perfect place for a romantic dinner! In keeping with the hotel's 140-year history, the restaurant draws on Belle Époque design elements but also incorporates nods to the natural surroundings. Well-placed fresh, modern accents successfully bridge the gap to the present day. They serve Mediterranean cuisine with a strong Italian influence, made using first-class Swiss and international products. There is a four-course tasting menu alongside à la carte dishes. The "Time for Lunch" set menu comprises three courses.

Name: Restaurant Burgstrasse9
Description: Dating back over 300 years, this establishment, once a smithy and locksmith's shop, has a rustic-meets-historical charm that beautifully incorporates more modern features. French-born chef-patron Stephan Koltes uses exclusively regional produce to create modern cuisine that is full of contrasts. The individual courses of his set menu are each available in the form of two small dishes made from the same ingredients – an enticing option. Tip for motorists: Use the Schlossberg multi-storey car park.

Name: Franz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Here in the elegant restaurant of the Grand Hotel National, you could almost be in Vienna: marble columns and high ceilings, waltz music (as well as more modern tunes) playing quietly in the background, and classic Austrian dishes, from Tafelspitz and Wiener schnitzel to apple strudel. Choose from a list of good Austrian wines. Great view of the lake, especially from the terrace. Smaller menu in the afternoon. Tip: Breakfast is served on weekends. Cakes are available every day.

Name: Ochsen
Description: Located just metres from the monastery, the venerable Ochsen dates back to 1596. In its current iteration with an avant-garde look, it is part of the three-building Hotel Caspar, which has stylishly designed guestrooms. In the open kitchen, regional ingredients go into modern and creative cooking – interesting cuisine that is "close to nature", with fire, aromatic woods, smoked and grilled dishes play a central role.

Name: Gasthof Kreuz
Description: This family-run hotel and restaurant steeped in tradition offers a cosy atmosphere indoors and an attractive outdoor terrace. Classic and traditional dishes on the menu, such as beef fillet in Pommery mustard sauce, plus comfortable country-style guestrooms also available. The open-air swimming pool at the rear can be used free of charge.

Name: Osteria del Centenario
Description: A restaurant that has been renovated in contemporary style, in complete harmony with its attractive setting overlooking the scenic lakeside promenade. Talented chef Egon Bajardi conjures up interesting Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on creative technique and the occasional exotic touch. Don’t miss his selection of desserts, including Crema Catalana with pumpkin, orange and bay leaf gelato.

Name: Kreuz
Description: Take a seat in one of the gorgeous dining spaces, or on the lovely, pleasantly peaceful garden terrace, to enjoy traditional and regional fare. The menu features, for instance, local lake fish; European perch from the Lötschberg mountains is also popular. The good food is complemented by a really friendly family atmosphere, which comes courtesy of the attentive service team. In the simpler Gaststube, you can order the dish of the day.

Name: Käserei
Description: Whether you are seated at a bare or beautifully set table, in this listed former cheese dairy, the dedicated hosts serve high-quality international and regional cuisine that is not only a hit with the locals. Tip: From Tuesdays to Fridays, an inexpensive lunch is served. Incidentally, the building is located in the heart of the pretty old town – perfect for a stroll!

Name: dr Egge - das restaurant
Description: Located in Muttenz's old town, this compact restaurant delights diners with its stylish and charming decor, warm hospitality and Italian-inspired cuisine. They propose a seasonal set menu made using regional produce wherever possible; the "Piedmontese Autumn Menu", featuring Alba white truffles, is also a popular choice. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d'.

Name: Didi's Frieden
Description: A fun place to eat. In this friendly restaurant with an attractive ambience (note the unique wine-glass chandeliers), guests can choose their own menu from the à la carte, while a set menu is offered at lunchtime. The wine list includes some good, carefully selected wines. Charming terrace.

Name: Kronenhalle
Description: This building, constructed in 1862, is a Zurich institution, and is located on Bellevue Square. Be sure to take a look at the art collection put together over a period of decades. The atmosphere is traditional, as is the cooking.

Name: Sonnenhof
Description: Set above the valley, this cosy, rustic restaurant boasts a wonderfully sunny terrace and fabulous views of the mountains.

Name: Auberge Les Platanes
Address: Rue du Vieux Collège 2, Chéserex, 1275, Switzerland
Description: An elegant 17C patrician manor house with smart dining rooms furnished in Regency-style. The fine, classic cuisine is in keeping with its surroundings and changes with the seasons, ensuring that only the freshest ingredients are served.

Name: Brasserie 1809
Description: The restaurant is done out in a modern Alpine style, with an interior that is upscale, sleek and at the same time inviting. As for the food great store is set by regional produce and sustainable farming. Select ingredients go into creating tasty seasonal dishes. It is pleasant to eat on the lovely terrace, and not only in summer! The Capra hotel has wonderful inviting guestrooms.

Name: Les Jardins de la Tour
Address: Rue de la Placette 16, Rossinière, 1658, Switzerland
Description: Guests are made to feel very much at home in this comfortable and cheerfully decorated house dating back to the mid-19C! French chef Patrick Gazeau is a true culinary artisan who does everything himself. His cuisine is classic, colourful and tasty (eg fillet of pike-perch from the Alps, saffron emulsion with candied Sicilian lemon). He draws heavily on local produce (in particular the cheeses made by his son, a breeder and producer) and gives pride of place to the flowers and herbs of the Vaud mountain pastures. In the dining room, his wife provides the perfect foil for her talented husband.

Name: La Maison du Village
Address: Rue de la Fontanette 41, Sauges, 2024, Switzerland
Description: With its resolutely relaxed ambience, this auberge is far from the traditional image of a high temple of gastronomy. Here, Marc Strebel, a young chef from the Valais, conjures up dishes very much inspired by a return to nature. Superb view of the lake from the terrace.

Name: Vecchia Osteria Seseglio
Description: Traditional local dishes, excellent regional produce, plus a few fish and seafood options, all served in warm dining rooms with low wooden ceilings and exposed brick vaults or outdoors in the garden in summer. Friendly service and a good selection of wines accompany the delicious cuisine.

Name: MEGU
Description: At this chic offshoot of the New York flagship restaurant, diners can enjoy a highly successful combination of traditional Japanese cuisine and modern influences. The menu ranges from tuna tataki served with Kanzuri radish, ponzu and nori vinaigrette to seared scallops with truffle miso to fermented lemon with Szechuan pepper and Sablé Breton. Fittingly, star designer Noé Duchafour-Lawrence drew inspiration from the Far East to create the sophisticated and distinctive interior. Incidentally, there is also a sushi counter where – as you might expect in an establishment of this calibre – sushi master Tsutomu Kugota works his magic. Note: closed Tue to Thu in summer.

Name: Oliveiras
Description: The friendly Oliveira family runs this establishment, making sure guests feel at home in the harmonious and deliberately informal atmosphere. They are attentively looked after as they tuck into Mediterranean cuisine made from excellent produce. All of this is accompanied by a fantastic selection of wines from the owner's Portuguese homeland.

Name: Auberge aux 3 Tilleuls
Description: If you're passing through Genolier, be sure to stop off at this charming Auberge! Filipe, the young chef here, serves fresh, tasty cuisine infused with contemporary flair: think fillet of turbot grilled skin on, with pesto and crunchy vegetables. An enjoyable mealtime.

Name: L'Auberge
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Opt for a table in either the modern, minimalist dining area or the more elegant dining space; in summer, there is also a delightful garden terrace. Made with top-quality ingredients, the modern French cuisine is infused with a Mediterranean character. Competent sommelier service comes courtesy of the manageress, who will advise you on the appealing wine list. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime. Tip: Book a stay at the tasteful hotel of the same name.

Name: Zum See
Description: A pleasant walk in the mountains leads to this charming restaurant with a romantic terrace. Simple, good cuisine is served.

Name: Wirtschaft zum Frieden
Description: This centuries-old inn enjoys a prime location right on Marktplatz, and its charming ambiance, redolent of a bygone era, will have you yearning to return. The dedication of your hosts is also infectious. While maître d' Heidi Bischoff graciously attends to diners in the cosy wood-panelled dining areas, chef-patron Fabrice Bischoff cooks up classic, home-style fare using fresh, high-quality ingredients. Some dishes also incorporate a Mediterranean twist. On the menu you will find beef fillet Stroganoff, as well as Swiss salmon steak with accras. A simpler set menu of the day is also available at lunchtime. The verdant terrace is a delightful spot in the summertime!

Name: Sala of Tokyo
Description: Classic Japanese cuisine made from top-notch ingredients is the name of the game here. The sushi and sashimi, tempura, and robata grill specialities, as well as the sukiyaki and shabu shabu stews all come highly recommended. Another draw of this place is its inviting interior, which is sleek and simple, yet cosy at the same time. You can watch the sushi master at work at a small counter.

Name: Accademia del Gusto
Description: This restaurant is a smash hit with its many regulars, which is hardly surprising considering the terrific food and lively and buzzing atmosphere. Over time, various dishes have achieved classic status. While Stefano Piscopo conjures up delectable creations such as home-made pasta (eg veal ravioli with sage butter) or marinated tuna tartare, his charming wife presides front-of-house. The handful of tables on the pavement tend to get snapped up quickly.

Name: Lindenhofkeller
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This place takes home-style cuisine up a notch with its "feinbürgerliche Küche". But soul food is also a very apt description of what is served in this gorgeous traditional restaurant in a desirable old town location, as Sebastian Rösch delivers truly feel-good cuisine. He preserves, for example, the familiar traditional character of a classic beef roulade with potato purée, preparing it without unnecessary frills, but bringing into play a precise craftsmanship and a degree of sophistication, as well as premium-quality produce. The modern decor and relaxed ambience are reminiscent of a chic, trendy gastro pub; the courtyard terrace is also pretty. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Real passion has gone into curating the wine list – a fine selection of well-established names but also lesser-known or smaller winegrowers. Or perhaps you prefer a fresh draught beer? Tip for motorists: Parkhaus Urania is just a short (if steep) walk away.

Name: Chasellas
Description: This charming restaurant in the Suvretta House hotel at the entrance to the skiing and hiking area has found a winning formula, offering rustic specialities for lunch and more sophisticated dishes in the evening, such as herb-crusted rack of lamb, mashed potatoes, chanterelle-asparagus ragout and baby carrots.

Name: Landgasthof Wartegg
Description: In this historical inn – run by the Frei family since 1982 – they serve fresh, flavoursome seasonal cuisine with classical foundations, made using excellent produce. The lunch menu is also popular. The ambience ranges from rustic to elegant, with a beautiful outdoor terrace shaded by trees. There are comfortable guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Centovalli
Address: Via Alla Stazione 5, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This attractive restaurant boasting rustic yet modern dining rooms and a beautiful terrace shaded by a pergola has offered the same format for over 20 years – a single risotto-based dish (the house speciality) served with a delicious meat option, nearly always lamb fillet, and very few fish dishes. Reasonably priced, with everything of an excellent quality.

Name: Le 1424, La Fabrique Cornu
Description: "La Fabrique" has many strings to its bow: it is a biscuit-maker, an interactive museum and, on the third floor, it houses this chic, contemporary restaurant with a panoramic view of the Vaud Alps. The ambitious and tasty dishes are made with a wide range of regional and national ingredients and given an international spin. Good value for money.

Name: Hide & Seek
Description: If you like to dine in a lively, modern atmosphere, the restaurant of Hotel Giardino Mountain is for you. The decor features a combination of trendy, chic features and rustic wood. Attentive front-of-house team and Mediterranean and Swiss dishes that are aromatic and flavoursome, made with fresh, often regional produce. Lunch is served in the bar-lounge.

Name: t3e terre
Address: via Vecchia Stazione 2, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: Owned by the Meneganti family, this beautiful house is home to a restaurant with an attractive dining room and stunning terrace that provide the backdrop for delicious Mediterranean cuisine. A charming hotel with welcoming guestrooms (additional rooms are under construction) adds to the appeal.

Name: Löwen - Gaststube
Description: Run by Rita and Domenico Miggiano-Köferli, Gasthof Löwen's second eatery is a delightful and more down-to-earth alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The atmosphere is inviting, not least because of the warm hospitality provided by the waitstaff. The freshly prepared, flavoursome dishes include pan-fried Lötschberg perch fillet with lemon thyme and almond butter, and Zurich veal ragout with glazed vegetables and butter rösti. Vegetarian options available. Popular lunch deal.

Name: Villa Honegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Set 914m above the ground, Villa Honegg offers a truly grandiose view from its terrace. Inside, enjoy the classic, regional cuisine with a modern twist, which includes the Honegg meatloaf and a six-course set menu.

Name: Restaurant Olivo
Description: Its Belle Epoque style lends this restaurant on the first floor of the Grand Casino a distinct elegance and charm that hark back to a bygone era. Under a high ceiling with moulding and chandeliers, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is served in the form of a set menu or à la carte. The "Dinner & Casino" packages are also worth mentioning. Fabulous balcony terrace with lake and mountain views. Tip: Park in the casino garage.

Name: De la Cigogne
Description: Trained in some of the world’s leading restaurants, the chef at De la Cigogne creates fine French cuisine which is full of flavour and always beautifully presented. Choose between the “old school” interior decor of mahogany panelling and padded chairs or the pleasant terrace in fine weather.

Name: Auberge d'Onex
Description: Since 1977, this inn has been nestled in verdant surroundings in the former clubhouse of Geneva's first golf course. It serves traditional Italian cuisine, including the chef's specialities of penne with vodka and penne alla Norma (a Sicilian dish that pays tribute to the composer Vincenzo Bellini, who was from the island), but also classics such as vitello tonnato. The dessert trolley features Italian specialities and a choice of fresh fruit.

Name: Thai Garden
Description: You could almost fancy you are in Thailand: with dim lighting, Far Eastern background music, Thai decoration, large ceiling fans and a babbling fountain, the setting alone transports you to an exotic world. Complementing this is exceptionally friendly service and authentic Thai cuisine – the spiciness can be adjusted to suit diners' individual preferences. Tip: The appealing lunch deal is available in two variations: the "Thai Box" and the "Vegi Box".

Name: Des Balances
Description: This place boasts an enviable location in the historic old town, with a magnificent terrace right alongside the River Reuss. Diners can enjoy the chic space of the restaurant, bar and lounge. On the menu: grilled specialities and French-Mediterranean dishes based on regional and seasonal produce; none of the meat comes from factory farms. The restaurant is ensconced within the stunning Hotel Des Balances.

Name: Stiefels Hopfenkranz
Description: This attractive, personally managed restaurant boasts beautiful pictures on the walls, a relaxed atmosphere, and warm, friendly service from the female owner, who also offers good wine recommendations. In the partly open kitchen, guests can watch the chefs at work. Seasonal produce takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: Landhaus Liebefeld
Description: Diners at this restaurant in a converted bailiwick (1671) choose between the Gaststube and the more elegant – but no less cosy – Rôtisserie. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, eg beef entrecôte with a herb butter foam. In summer, you can tuck into barbecue dishes in the small garden. On Thursday, Friday and Saturday evenings, le caveau serves a vegan set menu. For guests wishing to stay overnight, there are also tasteful guestrooms.

Name: Osteria Cyrano Cibo e Vino
Description: Enjoy personalised cuisine full of flavour and prepared with excellent ingredients at this restaurant, which offers a simple menu at lunchtime and a wider choice of dishes in the evening. Delicious recipes and a good balance of meat and fish options.

Name: Scalottas - Terroir
Description: At this trendy Alpine-style restaurant, the kitchen works exclusively with regional produce, much of it their own. Seasonality and sustainability are a central tenet – the staff will be happy to tell you more about their concept. To order, simply mix and match the dishes on the menu that pique your interest. The wines are also sourced from the region and surrounding areas – astute recommendations come courtesy of the friendly service team.

Name: Ahaan Thai
Description: A slice of Thailand in Graubünden! As well as dim sum and the usual range of curries, the menu features specialities such as Goong Hom Pha (shrimp in a blanket) – deep-fried king prawns with a sweet chilli sauce. Diners can also look forward to friendly service in a comfortable setting with elegant Thai-inspired decor. The restaurant is housed in the attractive Arosa Kulm Hotel, which dates back to 1882.

Name: Le Guillaume Tell
Address: Route de la Petite Corniche 5, Aran, 1091, Switzerland
Description: A charming pink house in the heart of this wine-producing village overlooking Lake Geneva. In this traditional setting, chef Denis Velen conjures up creative gastronomic cuisine that combines originality with delicious flavours as witnessed in dishes such as crispy spiced sea bass with choucroute.

Name: Hide & Seek
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ayurvedic philosophy inspires part of the menu at this restaurant, where Mediterranean culinary techniques and ingredients result in colourful, playful dishes. In fine weather, don’t miss the magnificent terrace overlooking the garden with its small lake and abundance of flowers.

Name: Belle Vue
Description: To make the most of the simply stunning mountain views, opt for a table near the large glass-planed front – or on the delightful terrace! Complementing the wonderful scenery, the interior of the Bellevue Parkhotel & Spa restaurant boasts a sleek design that provides the backdrop for the fine dining menu: classic dishes such as roast duck breast with potato galettes are served in the evening, and a simpler à la carte selection is available at lunchtime. Choose an accompaniment from the exquisite wine list.

Name: Roter Bären
Description: This pretty restaurant in the red-light district has a rather original concept that is popular with diners: in an open kitchen, the chefs conjure up ambitious appetiser-sized dishes that draw inspiration from modern culinary trends – three are recommended, then maybe a dessert to round things off. Great bar.

Name: Rössli
Description: Since 1995, Susy and Markus Sager-Meyerhans have been the friendly faces behind this long-established restaurant with its roots in the 18C, when it was a tavern. In addition to cordial service, you can expect a hybrid of traditional and modern-meets-classic cuisine; at lunchtime there is a somewhat reduced menu. Outside you will find the Rosenterrasse and Rössligarten. Charming guestrooms are also available.

Name: Le Café Suisse
Description: This former village café has been transformed into a vibrant, convivial restaurant. Young chef Marie Robert is passionate about what she does, delighting diners with creative dishes that are in tune with the seasons and washed down with excellent local wines. She has a flair for spontaneously showcasing seasonal ingredients. At the head of a mostly female kitchen team, she whips up trout-filled ravioli with lemon or an excellent veal filet mignon with pearls of vin cuit and polenta chips. Be bold and opt for her surprise menu – a hit with regulars, it is as playful as it is indulgent.

Name: OX'n
Description: Where the old Ochsen inn once stood, the new OX'n stands today with its eye-catching modern design – all the glass gives the place an airy feel and a pleasing sense of transparency. The overall atmosphere is trendy yet inviting. In good weather, the terrace beckons. Friendly service. A surprise menu is served on Fri and Sat evenings, and on Wed and Thu, you can dine à la carte. At lunchtime, a simplified version of the evening surprise menu is available. Alternatively, there is a set menu that changes every week, as well as an à la carte selection. Featuring ingredients sourced from local producers, the seasonal cuisine is both flavoursome. A must-try is the Entlebuch trout with asparagus and beurre blanc. Tip: If you fancy an after-work beer or a cocktail, pop into the bar for a quick drink, or feel free to stay a while longer.

Name: Waldheim
Description: This pretty restaurant is panelled in light wood and located in a quiet residential area. It boasts a healthy number of regulars thanks to the fresh Swiss cuisine (try the marinated leg of lamb, spit-roasted to a perfect pink) and the friendly service.

Name: mille sens - les goûts du monde
Description: At this pleasantly lively, modern restaurant in the Schweizerhof Passage near the train station, chef Domingo S. Domingo takes you on a culinary journey around the world, also drawing on his Australian and Filipino roots. At lunchtime, options include a small set menu ("Business Lunch") and the "Quicktray" comprising four dishes on one plate. In the evening, guests can choose from the "Domingo Pur Menu Surprise" and "Tavolata" – also available in a large portion to share. The small selection of bowls is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Carlton
Description: This tasteful, elegant restaurant is located in a historical building that was erected in 1913 to house a department store and later converted into the Carlton Elite hotel. They serve classic, top-notch cuisine; in the evening a more modern five-course menu with beef Wellington, tartar and crêpes Suzette is also available. Great wine list, including an impressive selection of 40 or so types from the Domaine Romanée-Conti.

Name: Sauvage
Description: This place has been dedicated to hospitality for over 500 years. Not only does the long-standing Hotel Wilden Mann have charming, individually styled guestrooms, it is also a bastion of fine dining. Sascha Behrendt has been the head chef at the upscale and elegant fine dining restaurant since April 2022. He incorporates Japanese elements into his classic cuisine, as well as nods to the region and the season. The four- to six-course set menu is available in both an omnivore and a vegetarian version. There are à la carte options too. In addition, the tempting caviar menu showcases different varieties – quail egg, blini, toast and butter are excellent accompaniments. Tip for motorists: the Kesselturm multi-storey car park is just a short walk away. Alternatively, you can park on the other side of the river, stroll through the beautiful old town and then cross the bridge (Reussbrücke).

Name: Les Touristes
Description: This restaurant has been a culinary landmark for decades, thanks to well-crafted cuisine and inspired recipes. Two young local lads are now at the helm. Their culinary creations, which exhibit a particularly minimalist approach and are refreshingly succinct, star carefully selected ingredients, often sourced locally. There are three set menus to choose from, one of which is vegetarian. In addition to outstanding food, there is a strong emphasis on creating an enjoyable dining experience. The buzzy vibe, stylish interior and attentive and friendly service all play their part, including excellent wine tips (the white Metphusus goes down a treat with the poultry breast stuffed in morels). In summer, the terrace is heavenly.

Name: Corso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This modern, urban restaurant on the edge of the old town is dedicated to the Alpine region, serving good, seasonal produce and game dishes in the autumn. The ambience here is minimalist, with an open kitchen which allows guests to watch chef Franz Ackermann creating his culinary works of art. Simpler lunch menu. The bistro “Unikatessen am Corso” next door also sells regional produce.

Name: Le Rossignol
Description: The Mediterranean cuisine served in this restaurant is as enchanting as the song of the nightingale (rossignol is not only the French word for nightingale but also happens to be the chef’s name!). Willy Rossignol creates classic dishes full of colour and flavour, all prepared from fresh ingredients, while his wife Mara takes excellent care of guests front of house in the simple yet elegant dining room. There’s also a small terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: Le Deck Restaurant
Address: Route de la Corniche 4, Chexbres, 1070, Switzerland
Description: The restaurant is part of Le Baron Tavernier, the chic little spa hotel opposite, and boasts a magnificent location with panoramic views. In addition to a fabulous vista over Lake Geneva, this place promises ambitious and tasteful French cuisine, prepared with top-notch produce, as well as friendly and attentive service. In summer, the open-air bar is the perfect spot for a drink.

Name: Auberge de la Veveyse - Salle grise
Description: In this small space of the Auberge de la Veveyse dedicated to fine dining, owner David Tarnowski offers the best of the market and local produce in the form of several surprise set menus that are not short on finesse: tarragon jelly with lake fish; whitefish from the nearby lakes with tomato; loin of Swiss veal, courgette and a thyme jus…

Name: Alter Torkel - Huus vum Bündner Wii
Description: Even from the outside, Alte Torkel, which is located right on the road through the vineyards, is liable to turn heads!
