The old stone house at a remove from even its closest neighbours has maintained its regional charm while incorporating modern touches; the wine theme is omnipresent. In keeping with its "Fine Wineing" motto, the menu is characterised by a regularly changing selection of wines by the glass. A contemporary influence makes itself felt in the seasonal, regional cuisine. The hosts are cordial and dedicated. In summer, the terrace with a view of the valley is a real boon!

Name: Baur's
Description: The chic, rather imposing deluxe brasserie of the famous Baur au Lac hotel does full justice to the top-notch spirit of gastronomy with which the grand hotel is synonymous. It serves international cuisine firmly rooted in the classics and made with excellent ingredients. The wine list is compiled by one of the best sommeliers in the world.

Name: Le Vingt Deux - Table d'hôtes
Description: It is well worth venturing into this discreet and exclusive fine dining table d'hôte concealed by a secret door behind the bar. A handpicked group of 15 or so guests are welcomed by the owner himself, who is then on hand throughout the meal to ensure that everything runs smoothly. The kitchen sends out elegant and carefully crafted classic dishes based on excellent regional ingredients – some with subtle Mediterranean touches. An intimate and hospitable atmosphere reigns here, with the same relaxed style as in the lively, bustling bar. You'll need to book well in advance.

Name: Bocuci
Description: Here you get an authentic slice of Italy – thanks both to the pleasant and cosy atmosphere and the tasty dishes cooked up in the open kitchen behind the counter. The latter are a combination of traditional and modern cuisine, and the reasonably priced lunch offering is also popular. Plus, you can buy the decoratively presented Italian specialities and wines in the restaurant's own bottega.

Name: Schmitte
Description: This is the fine dining restaurant of the comfortable Hotel Schweizerhof. The small space is inviting, with an elegant and cosy feel, and the service team is friendly and attentive. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian. The dishes are rooted in classic cuisine but prepared with modern techniques and a personal touch.

Name: PRISMA Expérience
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The modern Asian cuisine served at the elegant yet casual restaurant of the exclusive Park Hotel Vitznau is distinctive in that it is completely gluten- and lactose-free, and the use of white sugar is kept to an absolute minimum. The wine list leaves nothing to be desired. The location overlooking the lake is a draw in itself, and it goes without saying that tables on the terrace are highly coveted.

Name: Bären
Description: In this old 17C inn, a passion for gastronomy is shared with diners! Owner Christian Mutschler is always on hand, recommending and serving, but also sharing stories about the eventful history of the place. The no-frills food is tasty, and most of the ingredients come from the region. The game dishes are definitely worth trying – made with game hunted by the owner, they could hardly be fresher or more seasonal. At lunchtime, meanwhile, the menu is significantly pared down. The wine list is also dominated by Swiss labels, and there are plenty of good bottles to choose from. Be sure to make the most of the terrace and the great view it offers!

Name: SACHI
Description: The luxurious Mandarin Oriental hotel complex houses this restaurant presided over by chef Mitsu – a former disciple of master chef Nobu Matsuhisa, who has earned his spurs in the world of Japanese fine dining. In a resolutely contemporary setting, he serves set menus rife with delicious modern marriages of flavours, plus a fine selection of sushi. You might like to sample these at the counter of Omakase Bar, as you watch the master at work. Alternatively, head for the terrace alongside the Rhône.

Name: Monsieur 14
Description: Opposite the park and the villa of the same name, Monsieur 14 (located at no 14 of the avenue) serves enticing, meticulous dishes, such as veal chop, vegetable medley with citrus fruit and sauce mousseline, or fillet of sea bass cooked skin on, served with carrot and fennel. The covered terrace is a big plus!

Name: Montalbano by Mirko Rainer
Address: via Montalbano 48, San Pietro di Stabio, 6854, Switzerland
Description: Situated on the hill of the same name, this charming, recently renovated restaurant with an attractive veranda and terrace for summer dining has reopened under a new owner who is already well known in the region. The excellent, reasonably priced set menu is announced at your table at lunchtime; in the evening, choose from a selection of exciting dishes from a personalised à la carte.

Name: Eden - Belle Époque
Description: The food here has a strong regional flavour but is also open to more cosmopolitan influences. Try the tasty duo of Rhine valley corn-fed chicken or the home-made tagliatelle with black tiger prawns, either in the stylishly elegant restaurant or on the covered terrace – both are equally attractive. Reduced lunchtime menu.

Name: La Muña
Description: In this elegant and contemporary-style setting, the friendly waitstaff serve food that is an interesting fusion of Peruvian and Asian cuisine. The restaurant of Hotel Schweizerhof offers a choice between raw (crudo) and hot (caliente) dishes – the ceviche comes highly recommended. Don't miss out on the desserts either! Incidentally, la muña is the name of a medicinal plant in the Andes.

Name: Principe Leopoldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Situated in a panoramic and picturesque location outside the town centre, Principe Leopoldo is the gourmet restaurant of a classic-style hotel with an intimate ambience. Take a seat on the veranda with its stunning views of the lake and mountains or make yourself comfortable in the elegant dining room in winter. The cuisine here is based on solid traditional technique and is prepared from local and (especially) Mediterranean ingredients which are enhanced by delicious sauces. The wine list has something for all tastes, including a selection of memorable vintages.

Name: Groven
Description: A small restaurant with a focus on simple local dishes. If you stop here for lunch on the terrace, you’ll find a different menu every day inspired by whatever ingredients are in season. There’s also a tempting selection of cheeses and game such as venison and wild boar during the hunting season, plus an interesting wine list.

Name: Repas
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fancy a delicious meal above the rooftops of Biel? On the sixth floor of the Hotel Elite, in this central location near the railway station, you get a great view of the city and the Jura. The atmosphere is unpretentious, the service is friendly and the cuisine is contemporary, with regional and Mediterranean influences. If you're coming as a group, order a few of the finger food dishes ("Amuse") to share.

Name: Osteria San Gallo
Description: This pleasingly animated little osteria is located at the start of the pedestrian precinct, with the terrace area laid out in front of the entrance. The attractive interior is comfortable, with simple bistro chairs, wooden tables and the activity in the kitchen visible to diners. Authentic Italian dishes are served by an ambitious team – try, for example, the agnolotti piemontesi (handmade dumplings filled with veal).

Name: Taverne zur Krone
Description: This stately, beautifully restored historical building proposes two dining options: an elegant wood-panelled restaurant as well as a modern-style brasserie. In summer the terrace is particularly delightful. You'll find a great selection of traditional and classic dishes on the menu.

Name: Helvetia
Description: In Svenja and Adrian Nessensohn (both recent graduates of fine dining restaurant Lampart's in Hägendorf), Helvetia has dedicated and friendly hosts, who make a point of using regional produce. Get comfortable in the pretty restaurant, where a relaxed atmosphere reigns, and enjoy an appealing set menu with dishes designed to be shared. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace.

Name: Da Adriano
Description: As a true Italian, maître d' Adriano Feraco, after whom this ristorante in a side wing of the Grand Hotel des Bains Kempinski is named, treats diners to an authentic experience. In an attractive setting (here, elaborate moulding, herringbone parquet flooring and pretty details such as wine racks and the unique-looking service station are sure to draw the eye), dedicated and charming waitstaff serve typically Italian cuisine including mouth-watering options such as spaghetti with clams or "duo of lamb".

Name: Bodega Noi
Description: A really attractive restaurant: sleek, modern, spacious and – thanks to the large glass frontage – pleasingly bright, not to mention the view of the beautiful countryside. The leafy terrace with its shady chestnut tree is also very inviting. On the menu: flavourful cuisine prepared using excellent ingredients and drawing on Mediterranean and regional influences. Lunchtime options are more limited and more moderately priced.

Name: Stiva Veglia
Description: Situated in an idyllic little village, this lovingly restored Graubünden house dating back to 1761 is replete with Alpine charm. The interior is exceptionally pretty with its wood-panelled rooms that are welcoming and stylish in equal measure. Make a beeline for the terrace in summer. Tino Zimmermann delivers modern regional cuisine. There is a set menu of up to nine courses. A classic of the house is the "Schmauser 45-minute egg". A vegetarian menu is also available upon request. Fantastic produce such as Val Lumnezia Arctic char demonstrates a clear connection to the region. Diners are waited on by a dedicated and friendly front-of-house team, with the chefs themselves making an appearance from time to time in order to talk diners through their dishes. Tip: house-made specialities such as liqueurs, grape jelly, herb salt and lemon salt are also available to buy.

Name: La Bagatelle
Description: Here you can look forward to classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients, including an appealing selection of dishes for two. The cosy ambience created by warm wood, soft lighting and a touch of elegance is inviting. Plus they have a terrace with a stunning view. The service is charming, and there is a terrific wine list – half bottles are available, too. For an overnight stay: Hotel Le Grand Chalet has cosy rustic-style guestrooms.

Name: Da Valentino
Description: Although it is the beautiful terrace that first catches the eye at this restaurant, the friendly welcome and attentive service offered by Valentino in the kitchen and Sabine front of house add to the appeal. Mediterranean specialities and traditional classic dishes feature on the menu, while an open fireplace creates a warm ambience in winter.

Name: Taverna Romana im Sternen
Description: Sternen is the name of the lovely 19C timber-framed house in the centre of the village of Hessigkofen to which the Meofa family have moved their taverna. The restaurant serves fresh Italian cuisine, including sea bass with clams and mussels, as well as two interesting taster menus – Pesce and Carne. Good wine selection.

Name: Eder's Eichmühle
Description: A terrific place that is understandably popular! The picturesque location on a hill with a wonderful garden and view of the lake is its calling card – needless to say, the terrace is a big hit in summer! Dining inside the Eder family's traditional inn is also an excellent option, whether in the more cosy dining area or in the airy, modern extension. The service is friendly and professional with a personal touch. As for the sophisticated dishes, choose à la carte or opt for one of three set menus – omnivore, vegetarian or fish and shellfish. Another stand-out feature is the extensive, top-notch wine list. Their lunch menu is also an appealing option.

Name: Haus zum Rüden
Description: This beautiful guild house on the Münsterbrücke bridge, only a stone’s throw from the town hall, dates back to 1348, as does the unique 11m-wide wooden barrel-vaulted ceiling in the Gothic Room. Dishes are based on seasonal ingredients and include classics such as Zurich-style veal and mushroom ragout in a cream sauce. Less expensive menu at lunchtime, plus a selection of dishes available in the modern bar with a terrace.

Name: Porto Pojana Ristorante Terminus
Address: Via Poiana 53, Riva San Vitale, 6826, Switzerland
Description: A modern, elegant restaurant with an open-view kitchen, a wine cellar built into the rock, a cigar room, a winter garden and – the highlight – a beautiful terrace overlooking the lake with private mooring. The chef creates excellent Mediterranean-inspired cuisine and fish dishes, including recipes that make full use of fish from the lake.

Name: Relais du Mont d'Orge
Description: Originally from Auvergne, chef Bernard Ricou was a pupil of Paul Bocuse. He extends a warm welcome at this charming, friendly place with a timeless atmosphere and a terrace commanding one of the best views of Sion. Three different classic and seasonal set menus are served. Lobster playing an important role year round and is almost always to be found on the menu.

Name: La Parenthèse
Address: Rue de l'Hôtel-de-Ville 114, La Chaux-de-Fonds, 2300, Switzerland
Description: On the road into town, enjoy a gourmet interlude in this spruce, yet unpretentious restaurant depicted by a cosy, contemporary interior and a warm welcome. The culinary score is the work of chef Gennaro Rotella, hence the Italian twang of dishes such as cappellacci stuffed with greater amberjack (fish), confit of yellow tomatoes and smoked provola. Delicately crafted, the chef’s cuisine stars regional produce like raw and cooked Seeland vegetables and beef from the Franches Montagnes district. Head to the cellar to choose your cheese, which you can wash down with a 10- or 20-year-old Tawny port. A most charming front-of-house team.

Name: Du Théâtre
Description: Established in 1890, this fashionable restaurant full of historic charm is located close to the Zurich Opera. It offers traditional and Southeast Asian cuisine ranging from beef tartare to chicken teriyaki with poached egg and mushrooms, as well as ‘Sashimi Du Théâtre’. There's a smaller lunchtime menu.

Name: La Sitterie
Description: Here you can tuck into appealing French-Mediterranean cuisine with plenty of creative touches, spices and aromatic herbs. There are several risottos, but also a tomato tartlet with serac ice cream; crumbled Appenzell duck leg confit with savory; iced vacherin with red berries. Quality ingredients, good workmanship and a delightful landscaped garden terrace.

Name: Sternen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In this gorgeous inn, a winning father-and-daughter team conjures up modern takes on classic dishes. They propose a surprise menu – slightly cheaper at lunchtime than in the evening. Incidentally, they smoke the salmon themselves. If you would like a vegetarian menu, please indicate this when making your reservation. Well-stocked wine list. Tip: Across the road, there is a terrace shaded by plane trees, right by Lake Zug and with a view of the Rigi – in fine weather the sunsets are magical!

Name: Bianchi
Description: This bright, modern restaurant is located in a quiet spot on the banks of the River Limmat. It serves Mediterranean cuisine and diners are invited to take their pick from the fish and shellfish on offer at the generous buffet.

Name: Balm - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The charming and laid-back second restaurant at Hotel Balm also serves ambitious cuisine. This can be enjoyed in the form of a set menu of three or four courses which you can mix and match as you see fit. Options include dishes such as Lake Lucerne whitefish fillet with a champagne sauce, morels, leaf spinach and new potatoes. It is also possible to dine à la carte. At lunchtime on Wednesday to Friday, the moderately priced two-course set menu draws a crowd. The terrace is a delightful spot.

Name: Adler
Description: A little off the beaten track, this inn is delightfully cosy with its wood-panelled interior. The chef, who hails from South Tyrol, serves up classic cuisine with a modern twist, making a point of working with regional produce. The attentive front-of-house team includes his partner, a trained sommelier – the wine cellar boasts over 600 labels. There are a few attractive guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Auberge de la Gare
Address: Rue de la Gare 1, Grandvaux, 1091, Switzerland
Description: The first thing that impresses guests here is the stunning panoramic view of Lake Geneva. The dishes are simple and fresh – house classics include tartare and fillets of perch from the lake served with fries. Family atmosphere and a lovely terrace. Comfortable guestrooms are available for guests wishing to stay the night.

Name: Balm - La Pistache
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The elegant restaurant of Hotel Balm has a classical feel when it comes to both the service and Beat Stofer's cuisine – this is unpretentious fare made with excellent ingredients. Diners can opt for a tasting menu with four to five courses or order à la carte. There is also a well-curated wine list. In good weather, the terrace is a fabulous spot from which to enjoy the mountain views. This place is always busy, so be sure to book well in advance! Cheerful guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Tout un Monde
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated in the heart of the village, this restaurant occupies an old 13C church that enjoys a stunning location overlooking the lake and the vineyards. Regional produce such as locally sourced meat and fish from the lake are transformed into elegant dishes, which are accompanied by equally impressive wines from the region.

Name: Le Vallon
Description: With its pink façade and green shutters, this elegant and classically styled inn is an inviting proposition. The tastefully luxurious interior is adorned with bouquets of fresh flowers and floral wallpaper. In his open kitchen, Julien Poulain concocts classic dishes with a sprinkling of extremely subtle modern touches (roasted langoustine, celeriac risotto, bisque emulsion, tarragon, chopped hazelnuts). Friendly, attentive service and a very appealing wine list (a noteworthy selection of red wines, also available in magnums). In fine weather, make the most of the terrace and the verdant garden.

Name: Krone
Description: This restaurant in the hotel of the same name is located in a medieval castle complex on top of the mountain – the view couldn't be more beautiful! The stylish decor is a winning combination of modern design and historical charm. Drawing on contemporary influences, the cuisine takes its cue from the changing seasons and is made with produce sourced from Switzerland and the region. There is a gourmet menu on Fri. and Sat. NB: Due to the location, in a reduced-traffic zone, parking is available a few minutes' walk away – the hotel also provides a shuttle service (to be booked in advance).

Name: Landgasthof Bären
Description: The inviting exterior of this 17C half-timbered house gives a taste of the traditional dining rooms inside, which are lovingly decorated with high-quality furnishings. It is the garden terrace, however, that is the real highlight! In the evening, you can order an ambitious set menu, the appealing vegan alternative, or regional classics and modern dishes à la carte. More limited options at lunchtime. Decent wine list. Contemporary-style guestrooms.

Name: Gasthof zum goldenen Kreuz
Description: This restaurant is steeped in tradition, and much sought after for its excellent seasonal cuisine. Goethe himself was a guest here – the pretty Goethe-Stübli is named after him – and the well-preserved, painted panelling from the 17C adds rustic charm. Modern, functional guestrooms are available for overnight stays. Tip for drivers: public car park behind the building.

Name: Tenne
Description: Your welcoming hosts run this long-standing family business with great dedication. Done out in a contemporary take on Alpine style, the cosy interior is very pleasing. The wide-ranging menu includes some exquisite game dishes – the chef himself being a hunter! For overnight stays, there are well-kept, modern guestrooms.

Name: L'Accadémia
Description: This ‘academy’ offers a good lesson in taste and delicious flavours. As such, it is the ideal place to discover top quality Italian cuisine that is fresh and tasty. This is enhanced by an ambience that is relaxed and friendly. In summer, make sure you sit out on the terrace to enjoy the view of the lake.

Name: La Cène
Description: This establishment draws the eye with its refined decor as much as it appeals with its two mouth-watering set menus: the weekly lunch menu ("Inspiration de la Semaine" – three to five courses) and the evening menu ("Éclosion des Sens" – three to seven courses), which is changed every month. Diners enjoy modern seasonal cuisine with a dash of creative flair, which keeps them coming back for more. A food and wine pairing event is also organised one evening a month.

Name: Gasthaus am Brunnen
Description: The picturesque Gasthaus am Brunnen sits in the centre of this Graubünden mountain village. Locals meeting for lunch or a drink favour the rustic dining room, while the smart, minimalist-style restaurant is more elegant. The food is modern and uses exclusively local produce. Try the veal tenderloin cooked on a rock salt slab and served with herb caviar, mustard and garlic risotto and vegetables. The female chef's desserts are delicious.

Name: Heugümper
Description: This venerable townhouse in the heart of Zurich has an elegant, contemporary ambience and a delightful female host. The freshly prepared cuisine includes classics such as Zurich ragout of veal with a creamy mushroom sauce and potato rösti, alongside more modern dishes. At lunchtime a smaller menu is available.

Name: Marée
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Park Hotel Sonnenhof's wonderful location and comfortable accommodation options are not its only trump cards. The restaurant, run by chef Hubertus Real, is also in high demand. In a tastefully elegant setting, at attractively laid tables, diners are served classic cuisine made with first-rate ingredients. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team also provide expert advice on their very extensive selection of wines. The magnificent terrace also has a viewpoint – the "Adlernest" (eagle's nest) – from which you can take in the stunning view.

Name: The Omnia
Description: A lift whisks you up here from the pedestrian area – to some breath-taking views! In the restaurant of the eponymous hotel, the focus lies squarely on vegetarian cuisine. You can nonetheless round out the dishes with "supplements" – these include fish and meat options in addition to plant-based extras. The chic interior is sophisticated, sleek and modern with its large granite-topped tables. Our tip: Enjoy an aperitif by the fireplace.

Name: Tao's
Description: Tao's has you covered if you are in the mood for Euro-Asian cuisine. The wide-ranging menu includes sushi and sashimi, steak tartare, poke bowls and dim sum, plus "Signature Grill" dishes such as Thai-style fillet of sea bass, lime, herbs, ginger, soy. The dishes are accompanied by a fantastic and extensive international wine list. A pleasantly relaxed yet stylishly elegant atmosphere prevails. In summer the cosy terrace is a huge draw, and there is also a bar.

Name: AURA
Description: A stylishly urban restaurant, a top-flight events venue, a lounge or a club? AURA is a little bit of each, but above all the place to be for lovers of modern crossover cuisine with a weakness for grilled food – just watch the chefs at work! Located near Paradeplatz in the old stock exchange building.

Name: Kakinuma
Description: This small restaurant in the lively Eaux-Vives district is definitely worthy of its current success. The couple that run it create fresh and elegant dishes that include the most exquisitely sliced fish, tempuras that are as light as a feather, and silky chawanmushi (an egg flan). A feast for the senses!

Name: Chez Meyer's
Description: This elegant little restaurant charms its guests with piano music and a lovely mountain view. The classic fare comes in the form of a surprise menu that is accompanied by a reasonably priced wine list.

Name: CLOUDS Kitchen
Description: One of Zurich’s culinary hotspots, CLOUDS boasts spectacular views of the city from the top of the Prime Tower! While you enjoy the fantastic views of the city and the region, you can choose from a selection of international dishes. Simpler fare is served in the Bistro.

Name: Casa Tödi
Description: Manuel Reichenbach represents the third generation of his family to run the kitchen here. The cuisine showcases regional and seasonal ingredients of the finest quality. Sustainability is also a core value at this restaurant. Take a punt on the surprise menu, which comprises four to seven courses, or go à la carte. The friendly and adept front-of-house team is managed by the proprietress.

Name: Kronenstübli
Description: Premium materials, tasteful fabrics and attractive pinewood panelling make for a cosy yet elegant atmosphere – just the right backdrop for the sophisticated cuisine served here, which is classic French with Italian influences. Tip: Try the canard à la presse – pressed duck – (available if ordered by at least two of your party). The restaurant is housed in the traditional and stylishly luxurious Grand Hotel Kronenhof.

Name: Bistrot du Boeuf Rouge
Description: This restaurant is well known in the local area for its simple yet gourmet Lyonnaise specialities: rosette sausage, hot saucisson, pike quenelles, etc. The Farina family's culinary skill is demonstrated on a daily basis, to a backdrop of attractive old-fashioned decor.

Name: Seven Lugano - the restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the rooftop of the casino and accessible via a glass-sided lift, this restaurant boasts fine views of the lake. In summer, the popular seats on the terrace need to be booked well in advance, while the lounge bar on the ground floor is perfect for a post-dinner cocktail. The cuisine here is varied and wide-ranging, both on the set menus and the à la carte, plus there’s an excellent choice of wines featuring labels from around the world.

Name: Nagomi
Description: Two distinct restaurants in Les Pâquis district, run by a Japanese family: one dedicated to sushi, prepared by the father (who you can admire at work if you are seated at the counter); the other to tempura dishes cooked by the son. Both places have an authentic atmosphere, straightforward service, and top-notch ingredients: you're in for a simple treat.

Name: Le Patio
Description: Philippe Chevrier (chef at the Domaine de Châteauvieux in Satigny) has opted for an original twin-pronged culinary concept here based around beef and lobster, alongside a selection of traditional French bistro dishes, such as pan-fried frogs’ legs with sweet garlic, and crispy snails with mushrooms. A highly enjoyable dining experience!

Name: Seegarten
Description: For over 30 years, this elegant restaurant with a pleasant terrace has been making the most of its wonderful location on the marina. The menu is inspired by the seasons; there is also an appetising set menu, which changes on a monthly basis, but the classics are just as much in demand. Book your spot at the traditional seafood festival – Festival de Fruits de Mer – from late November to late January. Other highlights are the extensive wine list, and friendly, professional service.

Name: Salmen
Description: A delightful place with a lively atmosphere! This elegant 19C townhouse opposite the Church of St Martin houses a charming brasserie with decorative details such as old photos, a striking chandelier and attractive parquet flooring. There is also a heritage-protected dining room with stuccoed ceilings. Chef-patron Daniel Bitterli cooks classic, traditional dishes that take their cue from the seasons and draw on Mediterranean influences. Dishes such as the sole fillets with two kinds of asparagus and hollandaise sauce exemplify the restaurant's commitment to fresh, high-quality ingredients and flavoursome cuisine. The waitstaff are very attentive, friendly and adept.

Name: La Cantine des Commerçants
Description: A neo-bistro in the old abattoir district of the city, characterised by white and bright green walls, retro decor and a large counter where you can sit and eat. The varied menu is very much in keeping with the times: risotto with prawns and wild herbs, grilled fish and pan-fried fillet of beef.

Name: Römerhof
Description: This beautiful building, the origins of which date back to the 16C, is run with dedication by Dominique and Gerald Bergue-Hunziker. Classic and international dishes are served in an elegant setting – the coffered ceiling is striking. In the evening, there is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising three to six courses, and an à la carte menu. At lunchtime there is a shorter menu including a reasonably priced set menu. You can also relax in the cigar lounge or the pretty salons. Cosy and charming guestrooms are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Brasserie Les Trois Rois
Description: This attractive brasserie with its classic, elegant design and a fantastic view of the Rhine is located in the left wing of the hotel Les Trois Rois. The French-Swiss cuisine also has international influences: The menu includes a good selection of classic and seasonal dishes, which are presented at your table by the attentive waitstaff. Brunch is served on Sundays. Tip: You can look into the kitchen through a window in the passageway leading to reception.

Name: Sternen - Gartenzimmer
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in a converted 18C farmhouse, this family-run business is now in its third generation. The Gartenzimmer is a stylish restaurant with a pretty terrace. On the evening menu, you'll find sophisticated classic dishes. At lunchtime, the cuisine is somewhat simpler. The wine list is beautifully put together. Alternatively, head to the Dorfbeizli for burgers and schnitzel. Modern, comfortable guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Namun
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: For fans of Thai food, this restaurant in the luxurious Grand Resort Bad Ragaz is the place to be! The focus is on Thai cuisine, but there are also Chinese dishes. Elegant and minimalist, the Far Eastern-style decor makes for the perfect setting. Tip: Ask about the Thai curry – even if it's not on the menu. In case you were wondering, the name Namuntranslates as "lukewarm water" and is a reference to the local thermal spring.

Name: Brasserie du Poisson
Description: This contemporary brasserie close to the lake offers unpretentious cuisine. Fish has the starring role (tuna tartare, perch fillets), as well as hearty traditional recipes such as croûte aux morilles (with morel mushrooms) and veal cutlets. A real treat for the taste buds, particularly as everything (including the bread and ice cream) is homemade.

Name: Zwyssighaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This charming 18C restaurant named after the composer of the Swiss national anthem enjoys a fine location and a view of Lake Lucerne. Wood sets the tone inside, while outside you'll find two wonderful terraces – one on the balcony. A modern take on classic cuisine is served in the form of a three- to six-course menu, accompanied by a decent wine list. For overnight stays there are four simple yet cosy guestrooms.

Name: Panorama
Description: The name says it all! The location at an altitude of over 1 000m makes for a fantastic panoramic view of the surrounding mountains – it would be a crime not to enjoy it from the terrace in summer. The Rindisbachers have been running their establishment for well over 30 years, serving food influenced by tradition, made with quality ingredients and paired with good wines. The pasta is manufactured in their own workshop. Panoteca sells delicatessen wares.

Name: L'Artichaut
Description: Only the street separates this appealing restaurant from the River Arve. You will feel completely at home here, thanks to both the pleasant bistro atmosphere, including decorative paintings and posters of vintage advertisements, and the French cuisine reinterpreted with seasonal influences. The owner and sommelier is committed to providing his customers with a great experience. Excellent wine list.

Name: Buffet de la Gare
Description: An old-fashioned restaurant of the type that is quite hard to find these days. It has Art Deco-style wood panelling, enamel plaques and coloured windows, as well as a terrace overlooking the surrounding greenery. There is also a traditional feel to the menu, which includes perch from Lake Geneva.

Name: Schloss Binningen
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This stylishly furnished restaurant housed in an attractive 13C castle serves contemporary international cuisine with Mediterranean and Asian influences. At lunchtime choose between the "Business Lunch" deal and the four-course "Sorpresa" set menu; in the evening, they serve a four- to six-course "Emozione" tasting menu – or you can dine à la carte, which includes a vegetarian alternative. Under the direction of the dedicated sommelier, the service is friendly and proficient. In summer, the terrace is inviting. The hotel area beautifully combines modern and historical features. Tip: There is covered parking next door; if you prefer to get here by tram, line 10 stops right by the castle grounds. The narrow River Birsig also flows past here.

Name: Loy Fah
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This chic restaurant on the fourth floor of the tasteful Panorama Resort & Spa boasts a stunning panoramic view over Lake Zurich. Inside, you are served by an extremely friendly and attentive team. The food is a modern take on authentic Thai cuisine, which is also adapted to European palates in terms of spiciness. You can put together your own menu.

Name: Casa Novo
Description: This place is now under new management, although the name has not changed. Since chef-patron Dirk Wagner took over the restaurant, the cooking has a more international flavour, but has retained a Mediterranean side – for example, beef tongue carpaccio or French guinea fowl in a wild garlic sauce. In addition, tapas are served from 5-7pm, and the "Casa Novo beef tenderloin tartare" is a house classic. At lunchtime, the menu is significantly slimmed down. The location on the River Aare is as idyllic as ever, and the terrace is wonderful! La Vinoteca also remains in operation. The Klösterlistutz car park on the other side of the river is conveniently close.

Name: moment
Description: Set in the historical heart of Bern, this trendy, modern restaurant spread over two floors serves creative cuisine with a focus on regional and seasonal produce. The "Carte Blanche" menu offers a choice of two four- to five course set menus, – one completely plant based. A laid-back front-of-house team takes care of the service. There are entrances on both Postgasse and Gerechtigkeitsgasse.

Name: Stazione Da Agnese & Adriana
Description: There’s a change of guard at this Ticino dining institution where young couple Eloa Geiser and Yanick Walker have taken over the running of both the kitchen and front of house service. Eloa, the charming female half of the partnership, is also a qualified sommelier and takes very good care of her guests, while Yanick, adds his classic-French culinary stamp without neglecting his Valois roots, although he is not averse to adding some Mediterranean flair to his cuisine. In addition to its usual menu, on Tuesdays guests can order the “Adriana” veal liver, and on Saturdays the special braised beef with Merlot. The gracious building housing the restaurant with its beautiful views remains unchanged, as do the comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Ustria Miracla
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: The ambience here is a successful mix of traditional Alpine decor and contemporary design. The restaurant offers sophisticated Mediterranean and traditional dishes, as well as an excellent selection of wine. More limited menu at lunchtime.

Name: Weisses Rössli
Description: At the Weisses Rössli, good-quality ingredients are used to create dishes inspired by French cuisine with Mediterranean and seasonal influences, including options such as monkfish with gnocchi, beetroot, radicchio and cassis. In the rear courtyard away from the street, there is a quiet terrace that can be covered by an awning. We recommend parking in the nearby car park on the Hürlimann site.

Name: Le Soleil de Dugny
Description: In this restaurant standing at an altitude of 1 000m, the friendly and dedicated family at the helm offers guests a seasonal menu that can also be ordered as a half-portion, on which numerous local products are used to create tasty classic dishes such as the speciality “local veal with Valais gnocchi”. Spectacular views of the valley and mountains, plus a stunning terrace in summer!

Name: La Muña
Description: Do you fancy Peruvian-Japanese cuisine? This restaurant on the sixth floor of hotel La Réserve Eden au Lac, on the shores of Lake Zurich, serves interesting and unfussy dishes made from top-notch ingredients. Up here you can dine in a cosy atmosphere beneath the exposed roof beams or out on the fantastic rooftop terrace – the view over the lake and the old town is magnificent! Exclusive wine list.

Name: Mapo
Description: Mapo is run by Emmanuelle and Paul, a talented couple who have opened this refreshing restaurant that breaks with the city’s more traditional dining options. A concise yet mouth-watering menu, meticulously prepared dishes teeming with energy and freshness, and all at a moderate price. A favourite haunt where a delightful experience is guaranteed.

Name: Nouvo Bourg
Description: In the heart of the historical village of Saillon, this laid-back little restaurant oozes modern bistro charm. It also boasts a very pleasant terrace. They serve three ambitious set menus (including a vegetarian one) based on the French classics and accented with modern and creative details. At lunchtime they also serve a short "business menu".

Name: National da Sergio
Description: A pleasant and down-to-earth restaurant in the historic old town, right next to Klosterplatz square. The former “Felsenburg” team offers classic Italian cuisine made from top-quality ingredients, including dishes such as Spaghetti Scampi and the classic Piccata Milanese. As you’d expect, Italian wines feature on the wine list.

Name: Beaufort
Description: This small restaurant is located in the Marina Fallenbach clubhouse, on the outskirts of Brunnen. The place has a lovely friendly atmosphere, refined decor and beautiful views of the marina, lake and mountains, not to mention a wonderful terrace! Their modern and cosmopolitan cuisine is made with good, fresh seasonal produce. In addition to à la carte dishes, there is also a three- to five-course seasonal set menu. Inexpensive lunch menu.

Name: Wave
Description: This chic restaurant is part of the Bad Horn Hotel & Spa and as such is located right by Lake Constance. The divine views over the water certainly add an air of romance to proceedings; the terrace is also gorgeous. The food is modern with classical foundations and international influences ranging from the Middle East to Asia. Committed and very friendly service. Good wine list.

Name: Les Montagnards - Brasserie
Description: Fine dining is not the only option! Hotel Les Montagnards offers a culinary experience that goes beyond its renowned restaurant Le Sommet. The Brasserie can hold its own! The attractive modern interior featuring warm wood and sleek design is as much of a draw as the friendly service and, last but not least, the good cuisine. Here, the focus is on the region and the changing seasons. One of the house specialities, for example, is stuffed morels with a cream sauce. The pike-perch, fished from local lakes, is another popular choice. Tip: Try to get a window seat, then you can take in the view of Gruyères Castle and the surrounding area while you eat!

Name: Le Jardinier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant on the first floor of The Woodward hotel is a magical place, boasting an unobstructed view of the lake from its terrace, and promising attentive service and fresh, harmonious dishes. At the helm is Alain Verzeroli, who, along with chef Olivier Jean, has created a delicious culinary offering that espouses nature, the seasons and the ingredients. And, true to the name (meaning "gardener"), they give plants pride of place. Tasting menu or à la carte choice, plus a wide selection of vegetarian and/or gluten-free dishes. The restaurant also serves an exceptional breakfast and afternoon tea.

Name: Zum Löwen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This picture-perfect establishment has been run by the same family for seven generations. At the entrance is a bar with bottles from the wine list on display (ideal for an aperitif or digestif) and, just next to it, the open kitchen. In a gorgeous setting, diners are offered a choice of two set menus (one vegetarian), as well as a small à la carte selection and daily specials at lunchtime. Much of the produce used comes from the region. Service with a personal touch – the chefs get involved in serving and talk you through the dishes. The family also runs a winery.

Name: Tredecim by Monika Jans und Thomas Huber
Description: Thomas Huber (the 13th generation) and Monika Jans are dedicated to their work in the Krone, an establishment steeped in history. While she is responsible for the cordial and professional service, he takes care of things in the kitchen, preparing seasonal, traditional dishes. They will also prepare a creatively inspired set menu if you order in advance. The cheese trolley selection is fantastic! The wood-panelled interior exudes charm and contributes to the delightful atmosphere. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are attractive individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: Izumi
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: The atmosphere is truly international: top-notch ingredients go into a fusion cuisine of Japanese and other Asian influences. Perhaps you will be tempted by the Wagyu beef gyoza with a spicy ponzu sauce, or the izumi rolls? The lively atmosphere and chic, modern look of this restaurant on the seventh floor of the Four Seasons Hotel are just as much of a draw as the food. Don't miss the rooftop terrace, one floor up, with its breath-taking view over Geneva, the mountains and the lake. Make a reservation without delay!

Name: La Croix d'Or
Description: In the centre of the peaceful village of Ballaigues, not far from the French border, this restaurant is housed in a magnificent historical building. Two French chefs, David Sauvignet and Damien Lanza, run the show with professionalism and a passion for good food. Their ambitious take on seasonal French cuisine is full of finesse and infused with subtle Mediterranean influences. Pretty terrace.

Name: Afghan Anar
Description: Take advantage of the rather rare opportunity to discover Afghan cuisine! Here you can sample some of the country's most popular dishes, such as bolani, kabuli pulao or baklava. The atmosphere is laid back and down to earth, which is in part down to the open kitchen and authentic decor. As an alternative to the conventional tables and chairs, you have the option to dine on traditional mats.

Name: L'instinct
Description: Chic and relaxed, this restaurant delights the taste buds with its French-Mediterranean dishes and grilled meats (matured in the display case that was hewn directly out of the stone between the bar and the kitchen). They also like to perpetuate the tradition of serving flambé dishes, lit in the dining area, as well as classic dishes (still recommended!). In keeping with the terrace surrounded by vines, the wine list has a thousand references. Insider tip: come with at least two people and opt for the set menu.

Name: Madre Nostra
Description: Classic Italian cooking is served in the charming restaurant of the modern hotel CERVO Mountain Resort, which is located a little above the village and right next to the slopes. The produce and flavour are the main focus here. At lunchtime, they offer a limited selection from the evening menu, as well as highlights from the establishment's other restaurants. The terrace is impressive!

Name: Bergwelt - BG's Grill Restaurant
Description: Modern chic with an Alpine touch: Done out in warm tones, with lovely parquet flooring, striking designer lamps and an open kitchen complete with an impressive barbecue, this restaurant – part of the equally attractive Bergwelt Grindelwald hotel – has a truly unique atmosphere. The cuisine has a Mediterranean feel but also draws inspiration from the region. The menu is full of tempting dishes, such as the butter-soft octopus starter. For meat lovers, the fragrant, golden-brown Wiener schnitzel is sure to whet the appetite, and the same goes for the top-quality signature cuts from the barbecue. There are plenty of options for vegetarians, too. The well-curated wine list predominantly features Swiss and French labels.

Name: il tiramisù
Description: This restaurant is near the centre but slightly tucked away – it goes without saying that it is a joy to sit on the terrace overlooking the River Murg. The atmosphere is friendly, the service attentive. In the open kitchen, the team meticulously prepares seasonal Italian dishes that are flavoursome and fun! It is definitely worth trying the pasta dishes, smaller portions of which are also available as a starter. Of course, the dessert after which the restaurant is named features on the menu. In the evening, order à la carte or opt for a surprise menu comprising three to four courses. Tip: moderately priced set menu at lunchtime.

Name: Zum Zähringer
Description: In the Matten neighbourhood, just a block away from the River Aare, this restaurant is run by Gaston Zeiter. He is originally from the Valais canton, but settled here in the lower part of Bern's old town some time ago. In the stately old building that is the Zähringerhaus, he cooks up classic French cuisine, but also dishes with Swiss influences – for example, there is fried sea bass with risotto, as well as a terrific cordon bleu. Top tip: the bargain-price menu of the day! In addition to the charming restaurant, there is a wonderful garden terrace with venerable old trees and a covered outdoor area. The wine list is also well stocked, including with numerous Valais wines.

Name: Weinlaube
Description: Countrified and charming, congenial and friendly! This former farmhouse in a quiet little hamlet not far from the border with the Vorarlberg region offers cosy Stube-style dining rooms and a beautiful outdoor terrace. The menu here features unfussy cuisine with a focus on classic, regional, seasonal and international dishes and the occasional use of the smoker.

Name: Les Ateliers
Description: After having been deserted for some 25 years, this former stainless-steel workshop just behind the railway station has been revived by Jean-Sébastien Ribette and Sahondra Verdan (formerly of Auberge de la Veveyse). An off-kilter, smart industrial vibe sets the scene for a choice of culinary options: brasserie fare to the fore, or more ambitious (and surprise) set menus in the gourmet section. Market availability dictates the menu, hence the freshness of the ingredients. For example, scallops, roasted and tartare, with pumpkin and cloves, roast monkfish in cider butter with textured vegetables, perfectly roasted Bresse pigeon with apple molasses.

Name: La Soupière
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This sophisticated restaurant on the first floor boasts a stylish interior and professional service. As for the menu, it offers modern variations on classic French cuisine.

Name: Jack's Brasserie
Description: The second Meyer's restaurant is just as appealing a place to eat as the first. Its beautiful high ceiling complete with mouldings and striking chandeliers, plus a classic decor, make for a distinct atmosphere. The food, too, is in a classic, traditional vein, and it is as enticing as the setting – eg "Sushi from the valley to the mountain pasture". Guestrooms are available at the venerable Hotel Regina.

Name: Löwen
Description: In this cosy little restaurant in the vaulted cellar, you can look forward to the "Gourmet Menu", which is served at lunch and dinner, with the option of up to seven courses. At lunchtime, Beiz serves a set menu, as well as a choice of à la carte dishes. There is also a decent wine selection, and the front-of-house team is friendly and competent.

Name: Schotte-Sepp-Stube / Flickflauder
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you choose to dine in the cosy Schotte-Sepp-Stube, the bright Veranda or the contemporary, minimalist-style Flickflauder, you’re guaranteed good-quality, seasonally inspired cuisine and friendly service at this restaurant, which hosts an “Appenzell evening” with a buffet every Wednesday. The à la carte is available to non-resident guests from 8pm onwards.

Name: Arté al Lago
Description: Modern, impeccably presented cuisine with a Mediterranean influence and an equal emphasis on meat and fish in a restaurant whose name lives up to its promise. Interesting wine selection, including a choice of international labels.

Name: L'Arabesque
Description: The attractive decor featuring gold mosaics, white leather and black lacquerware, evoking the magic of the Orient, in particular the Lebanon, provides the backdrop for classic dishes including hot and cold mezzes and chiche taouk – chargrilled chicken with a white wine, garlic and citrus marinade.

Name: Restaurant Pony
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family-run restaurant, now in the third generation. In the elegant Pavillion dining room, friendly staff serve classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences, while the cosy Beizli is an inn-style room offering more everyday cooking. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Gildo's Ristorante
Description: If you’re in the mood for some authentic, upmarket Italian food, you should try the line-caught sea bass, cime di rapa, garlic, pine nuts and peperoncino at this restaurant. Expect excellent service, plus a stylish Alpine ambience.

Name: Le Grill
Description: The knockout view of Lake Geneva and its iconic Jet d’Eau is unquestionably one of the highlights of this fine establishment. However, that afforded by the kitchens, the rotisserie and the cold room where the superb cuts of meat are stored is equally uplifting. Unsurprisingly, specialities include grilled fish and meat but there is also tofu. The set menu known as "Le Grill Experience" is an excellent option for those with a healthy appetite, as is the Grill Burger! Impeccable service.

Name: Locanda Locarnese
Description: Hidden in an alleyway, this pleasant, modern restaurant serves Mediterranean cuisine made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t miss the “Terreni alla Maggia” risotto and the chocolate dessert with a passion fruit sauce. A large fireplace adds to the cosy ambience, making diners feel as though they are guests in a private house. Friendly service.

Name: Spettacolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the Lenkerhof spa resort's elegant restaurant, hotel guests can look forward to a great half-board set menu, while à la carte diners are treated to a high-quality and modern take on classic cuisine that also draws on international influences. You can put together a menu of variable length from a selection of 15 dishes. The attractive wine list includes small bottles, as well as magnums. Friendly and proficient service.

Name: Restaurant de l'Hôtel DuPeyrou
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This exquisite 18C palace ticks all the boxes: elegant yet unconventional, classical yet quirky and even better, it is located right in the heart of town! You will taste the cuisine of Edmond Bavois who works with premium produce, adding an Asian spin to a classical repertory.

Name: Hôtel de Ville
Description: This restaurant with a vibrant and upbeat atmosphere is run by a chef who is brimming with energy. He regales diners with delicious and indulgent cuisine that draws on local produce. Daily lunchtime menu inspired by local market fare; fine dining tasting menu in the evening. The opulent interior (a former apartment) is decorated with numerous works of art: paintings, photos, sculptures etc.

Name: Auberge du Prévoux
Description: This inn on the edge of a forest in the heart of the Neuchâtel mountains is well known to food-lovers, who head here to enjoy French cuisine with a focus on the very best products selected by a chef who enjoys working with lake fish and different types of game, in particular. Good value for money in the brasserie at lunchtime, with more ambitious cuisine on offer in the evening.

Name: Le Jardin des Alpes
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There’s a new chef and a new concept at this gastronomic restaurant within the walls of the Chalet RoyAlp luxury hotel & spa. In this elegant yet welcoming setting, savour dishes such as snails with herbs and a potato mousse, and fettuccine with parmesan and Alba white truffle sauce, complemented by highly professional service and an impressive wine selection. The terrace is a must in fine weather!

Name: White Elephant
Description: This restaurant in the Marriott Hotel is a must for fans of authentic Thai cuisine. Made with market fresh produce, the food is authentic and authentically spicy! Whatever you do, don’t miss the curries.

Name: Le Bocca - Restaurant
Description: This restaurant serving mouth-watering cuisine has been taken over by Alexandre Luquet and Ana Ronc! Whether seated in the bright, elegant dining space or out on the pretty, leafy terrace, you can enjoy ambitious, contemporary French cuisine, such as the "langoustine and fresh peas" starter or the sole meunière made with fish from small-boat fishing, black garlic and braised endives, which is as tender and juicy as can be! They have a good wine cellar (including Swiss wines) that is open to visitors.

Name: Restaurant Chastè
Description: In their delightful little hotel, the Pazeller family offers not only attractive, comfortable guestrooms but also sophisticated cuisine. The restaurant combines two concepts: "Ustaria Chastè" with an upscale evening menu and a simpler lunchtime menu, and "Bocca Fina Chastè" with an evening fine dining set menu. The interior is tasteful and cosy, the service friendly and attentive.

Name: Stapferstube da Rizzo
Description: Here at Stapferstube, a well-known Zurich eatery, Italian dishes such as tris di pasta della casa, gamberoni aglio olio peperoncino, and brasato di manzo al Barolo are a hit with diners. In this vibrant and welcoming restaurant, regulars and first-time guests alike are treated to Mediterranean hospitality and a cosy atmosphere. Their quick lunch at a reasonable price is also popular.

Name: Ornellaia
Description: Modern-inspired Italian dishes, such as carne cruda, filetto di vitello Rossini and ravioli carbonara, are prepared in kitchens that are visible from the dining area. The appealing wine list includes a selection from the famous Tuscan wine-growing estate, Ornellaia – from which the restaurant takes its name. You are waited on by a friendly team assembled around host Antonio Bordone, who puts his heart and soul into serving you. This gem of a restaurant is located in a beautifully refurbished building that was once a bank – the door even opens automatically. Sleek design meets historical-looking sandstone walls and decorative art, lending the distinctive high-ceilinged space a modern and elegant Tuscan ambience. At lunchtime there is a small selection of additional dishes.

Name: Cavigilli
Description: Combining modern features with the original wood and stone, plus cordial service and a pleasingly down-to-earth atmosphere, this charming 15C Grisons building provides a wonderful setting in which to enjoy seasonal ingredient-led cuisine. The focus is on the essentials, so the flavoursome dishes are served in pared-down combinations. Tip: Make the most of the quiet terrace in summer! There is a small and simple lunch deal.

Name: Le Bistrot des Ours
Address: Route du Pas de l'Ours 41, Crans-Montana, 3963, Switzerland
Description: It's easy to feel at home in this bistro with its rustic, mountain-inspired atmosphere, complete with terrace commanding a magnificent view of the valley and the surrounding mountains. Here they serve ambitious French-Mediterranean cuisine that caters to all food lovers, courtesy of chef Franck Reynaud, who also cooks at the Michelin-starred restaurant, L'Ours. You'll want to come back for more of this delicious fare that will have your taste buds tingling!

Name: Landhaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: This 16C farmhouse is now a really charming restaurant boasting a splendid view of Lake Constance. Featuring warm wood finishings and sleek design, the decor embodies a winning combination of the old and the new. Regional cuisine is served in the cosy parlour. Reduced menu at lunchtime. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace. There is a hall for events in the modern converted barn.

Name: Mulania Brasserie
Description: With its combination of sleek, contemporary style and rustic ceiling beams, this old Graubünden building provides an attractive setting. Host couple Yvonne Marx and Sascha Meyer have reimagined their place as a brasserie, serving tried-and-tested regional specialities such as capuns (chard rolls) or quark pizokels (buckwheat spaetzle), plus brasserie classics like moules frites or beef bourguignon. Last but not least, there are some delicious seafood options – the chef's first love. Delightful terrace. Open from 3pm.

Name: La Tavola Pronta
Description: Run with great dedication and a personal touch, this little restaurant has bags of charm and specialises in Piedmontese cuisine served in the form of two set menus – a vegetarian alternative is also available. The lunch menu is less expensive. Thanks to the location in a reduced-traffic zone, it is pleasant to sit on the pretty terrace overlooking the little piazza.

Name: La Croix d'Ouchy
Description: This restaurant boasts a loyal following of regulars in Lausanne, attracted here by cuisine that features superb traditional flavours alongside a few pasta dishes with an Italian touch, in a classic setting with plenty of character. Prior booking essential.

Name: Au Chat Noir
Description: In this lively, welcoming restaurant close to the theatre, guests will be tempted by delicious dishes (such as oxtail parmentier – something of a speciality here), a menu of market-inspired specials (on this particular day, a delicious cep fondant as a starter), classic and rather fine flavours. In short, Au Chat Noir is the type of bistro you'd be happy to come across more often. Be sure to book!

Name: La Grappe d'Or
Description: A restaurant where superb flavours and a friendly atmosphere go hand in hand. Chef Theotim Bioret is strongly inspired by northern Italy, from Venice to Ventimiglia: Piedmont-style agnolotti del plin, sage and a parmesan jus; calf's liver saltimbocca, spinach and polenta. In addition to the à la carte menu, the chef serves a more affordable weekly dish. Meticulous plating, precise cooking and delicious sauces combine to create a faultless dining experience.

Name: La Brasserie du Royal
Description: The Royal Savoy hotel was one of the favoured haunts of the Spanish court. The brasserie’s culinary focus is highly enticing menu that features dishes such as pâté royal en croûte, goose foie gras, and a mousseline of crayfish from Lake Geneva, as well as seasonal recipes such as hare à la Royale. A truly chic experience!

Name: Rössli
Description: The first-floor dining area of this 16C half-timbered house is a really pleasant setting in which to dine: the space has a cosy, rustic atmosphere, plus a small conservatory overlooking the lake. Seasonal influences can be detected in the traditional cuisine, while the menu also features classics such as Wiener schnitzel with warm potato salad.

Name: Chez Vrony
Description: All the wood and pleasant decor make for a cosy, rustic atmosphere indoors, but with the spectacular view you have at 2 100m above sea level, the terrace is unsurprisingly popular too! Traditional regional cuisine is served by the charming waitstaff. Incidentally, they produce their own dried meat and sausages here.

Name: Castelgrande
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Housed in the charming castle overlooking Bellinzona, this restaurant serves Mediterranean cuisine with the chef’s own personal touch, served by friendly and professional staff. Simpler regional cuisine is available throughout the day in the Grotto below.

Name: Marktküche
Description: One tip at the outset: be sure to reserve in good time – this restaurant always gets booked up, so it's hard to get a table! The clue is in the name: the cuisine takes its cue from what the market has to offer, dispensing with meat and fish. Diners can look forward to a vegetarian surprise menu made up of four to eight courses. There is also a lunch menu available on the penultimate Friday of every month.

Name: Paradiso
Description: In good weather, you can take in breathtaking views up here at 2 181m above sea level. This down-to-earth Mountain Club restaurant appeals to diners of all ages. You can look forward to good food and a great wine selection, as well as a relaxed atmosphere, partly thanks to the music and DJs. Note: there is an entry fee for non-members. Accessible by chairlift and a short walk (10min).

Name: Motto del Gallo
Description: A historic gem of a restaurant, part of a tiny hamlet of 15C houses, featuring a cool, shaded outdoor space for summer dining. Elegance and refinement are to the fore inside, enhanced by antique furniture and works of art, while the menu takes its inspiration from the local region and the Mediterranean. The Chateaubriand is an absolute must!

Name: Da Enzo
Address: Via Ai Grotti, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This Ticino-style stone house boasts a sun-blessed, verdant setting and a beautiful garden-terrace. Take a seat at one of its typical granite tables, either crowned by stone vaulting or shaded by trees, where you can savour exquisite Mediterranean on several tasting menus (including vegetarian) and an à la carte that includes daily specials. Other features include a well-stocked wine cellar and two romantic rustic-style guestrooms. Open for over three decades, Dan Enzo is now run by the second generation of the family.

Name: Casa Alva
Description: This former parsonage has been refurbished to give an attractive mix of old, rustic features combined with a high-quality modern interior. The host’s dedication and warm welcome add to the cosy ambience, ensuring that you’ll feel completely at home here. Choose between “From the coast” and “From the mountains” menu options. Attractive guestrooms are also available.

Name: La Coupole - Matsuhisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: "Irasshaimase" – this is the exclamation with which diners are greeted here. Housed in the building that was once home to Europe's first indoor tennis courts, Nobuyuki Matsuhisa's restaurant buzzes with infectious vibrancy. The wide-ranging menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines – everything is prepared in the open kitchen (there is also a sushi bar). The black cod miso is definitely worth trying.

Name: Kindli
Description: A place steeped in history and full of charm – from the hotel's pretty, individually designed guestrooms to the restaurant, in which old wood panelling exudes cosiness. In a pleasant and lively atmosphere, they serve good classic cuisine in the form of dishes such as sea bass with a lemon and caper butter, or Geschnetzeltes Kalbsfilet Zürcher Art (veal strips in a mushroom and cream sauce). At lunchtime, check out the additional daily specials for a quick meal. Tip: Don't forget to make a reservation, as they always get booked up!

Name: Elisa - Bistro & Terrasse
Description: It might have been more accurate to call this restaurant "Le Tapis Vert", given the green philosophy that underpins its sustainable culinary offering. Located in the time-honoured Grandhotel Giessbach (built in 1875) – right at the foot of the waterfalls of the same name, it boasts a wonderful view of Lake Brienz. Soak up the atmosphere as you enjoy refined modern cuisine that is created primarily using ingredients from the establishment's 2ha vegetable garden. Produce that is not immediately used is pickled, fermented or marinated. The restaurant's own home-grown ingredients are supplemented by local farms and small-scale producers. A vegetable-focused set menu and a completely vegetarian set menu are served. Dishes such as ancient spelt risotto with wonderfully aromatic and fresh vegetables and Tschingelfeld Alpine cheese hide behind names such as "Our Garden Vegetables".

Name: Zum Goldenen Schäfli
Description: Located in the last surviving guild house in the town (1484), this restaurant is full of charm and atmosphere with an all-wooden interior that is especially pleasing. One quirk of the Zunftstube (guild room) is its sloping floor – you might find yourself walking uphill! The cuisine is classic and seasonal, with a Mediterranean touch. Attentive service.

Name: Du Cheval Blanc
Description: The former chef at L'Écu, in Bulle, has turned Du Cheval Blanc into a veritable haven for foodies. In this convivial light-filled restaurant, he delights diners with his well-crafted, unfussy and straightforward take on traditional cuisine, prepared with care and served by a professional team. The real deal.

Name: 4 Saisons
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Attractive picture windows, elegant pale wood, and a menu that takes the four seasons as its starting point, as reflected in the market-fresh ingredients. Locally grown vegetables, fish from the nearby lakes and Swiss meats are accompanied by an appealing wine list that focuses on local producers. Delight in dishes such as morel stuffed with Agria potatoes and Vully asparagus tips. Friendly service and attractive guestrooms at Hotel Cailler.

Name: La Place
Description: Cristina and Vincenzo De Rosa run this restaurant with passion and enthusiasm. Throughout the year they delight guests with their modern and colourful cuisine, with dishes such as lobster ravioli in a Thai red curry sauce featuring on the menu.

Name: First
Description: Somewhat tucked away, this delightful restaurant in the Zurich Oberland has plenty of regulars. One of its draws is the wonderful view; in good weather you can see Mount Säntis. The interior is very pleasing – some aspects are cosy and traditional, others rather more modern. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in front of the building. The menu changes with the seasons. Friendly and dedicated front-of-house team.

Name: Old Swiss House
Description: If ever you eat in this friendly 19C half-timbered house, don’t miss the Wiener schnitzel prepared at your table. The classic, traditional menu also includes home-made terrines and turbot in champagne sauce. The cellar holds some 30 000 bottles including a complete collection of Château Mouton Rothschilds dating back to 1911!

Name: Gasthaus Höhwald
Description: In this gorgeous restaurant boasting a stunning view, the atmosphere could hardly be more welcoming. Since December 2023, a dedicated couple have been at the helm, bringing their superlative fine dining experience to the table: Mara Graef cheerily oversees the team front of house, while Thomas Graef prepares tasty seasonal dishes. His is regional cuisine for the most part, but some dishes are clearly influenced by the owners' Austrian homeland: for instance, their classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef), available as a Monday special. Hot meals are served throughout the day. Wonderful terrace. Tip for motorists: You can reserve a parking space in the garage.

Name: Le Maguet
Description: The Le Maguet brothers, Jonathan (serving) and Benjamin (cooking), are carrying the culinary torch of their father Olivier with their sustainable and 100% local concept! They use organic and/or wild ingredients that are of excellent quality, and draw on both traditional know-how and the most modern techniques, resulting in simple and tasty cuisine. For example, pata negra pork shoulder and salsify, slowly and perfectly cooked. Thirty years on, the dessert trolley is still the domain of their mother, Pierrette: don't leave the table without trying her tartlets!

Name: Verena
Description: This charming historical customs house dating back to 1786 has undergone a transformation under Dave Wälti, who previously worked in the kitchens at Eisblume in Worb and Casino Bern. The cuisine is contemporary, with vegetarian components playing a major role – but not to the complete exclusion of fish and meat. Warm wood tones and clean lines make for a lovely atmosphere, and the service comes courtesy of a friendly, laid-back and professional team.

Name: Oberer Mönchhof
Description: The dining rooms in this lovely, centuries-old half-timbered building are tastefully and comfortably furnished. Outside a fabulous terrace is laid out under chestnut trees overlooking the lake. The cuisine is seasonal, traditional and international with an additional tasting menu on offer at lunchtime and in the evenings.

Name: Drei Könige
Description: In this restaurant with a friendly bistro atmosphere, the emphasis is on high-quality regional produce. The dishes are fresh, pleasingly pared down and unpretentious. In the evenings, they propose, among other things, "La Grande Bouffe": a surprise menu for two. At midday, they only offer a small lunch set menu, which changes daily.

Name: Sapori
Description: Worth a visit for its stylish historic interior alone, Sapori promises a wonderful parquet floor and an impressively high painted ceiling complete with stucco work. The Italian menu includes tasty stone-baked pizzas

Name: Hirschen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Classic, seasonal and regional food is the name of the game here. Guests can enjoy fine dining and vegetarian options in the Zeitgeist restaurant, as well as house classics, including the signature dish: chateaubriand. Tip: The chocolate cake with coffee is sensational! Alternatively, you can order burgers, pasta etc in the cosy Hirschenstube. Popular terrace for summer meals, plus comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Chrüz
Description: This centrally located inn has tables in the stylish conservatory or a simpler dining room where you can tuck into traditional fare that often draws on international influences. The wide-ranging menu includes spaetzle with Sbrinz (hard cheese) and truffle, cordon bleu with Alpine cheese, "Vorässä 2.0" (beef stew with a twist) and salmon green curry. The service is friendly and attentive. Lunchtime options are more limited and moderately priced.

Name: Vieux-Bois
Address: Avenue de la Paix 12, Geneva, 1202, Switzerland
Description: Just behind the United Nations, this 18C building houses Geneva's hotel management school (EHG) and its restaurant, where tradition reigns supreme. Under the expert supervision of their teachers, students prepare the meals and wait tables. The terrace is also very pleasant.

Name: Rössli
Description: Rössli is a pleasant restaurant decorated along clean, modern lines in warm colours. Enjoy the smart place settings and friendly service led by the lady of the house and Ueli Kellenberger’s flavoursome, contemporary cuisine. The mouthwatering offerings include open ravioli with spinach, egg, parmesan and beurre noisette.

Name: Seven
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The views extend from the lake to the mountains in this informal restaurant, where windows into the kitchen allow guests to watch the chefs busy at work. The menu features creatively reinterpreted, classic-style dishes, with the option of choosing between meat and fish, while the delicious bread comes from the Bottega del Gusto in Porto Ronco. At lunchtime, there’s a bistro-style menu with lighter but equally delicious options such as salads, antipasti and primi, hamburgers, club sandwiches, baked seabass and grilled Tomahawk steak. There’s also a lounge bar plus a wine bar of the same name, the latter offering an interesting array of labels (also available by the glass), as well as cocktails which are a perfect pairing for the dishes on offer. Given the restaurant’s superb location, the tables on the terrace are much sought after in summer, so it’s best to book ahead! Three luxury apartments are also available if you’d like to extend your stay here.

Name: Pinte
Description: Set in a 19C building, Pinte offers something for everyone in its cosy dining room and comfortable restaurant. Menu offerings include ravioli with pear, Jersey Blue and walnuts and pot roast with Ticino polenta and purple carrots. Delightful terrace.

Name: Auberge de la Veveyse - Brasserie
Description: A worthy heir to this renowned restaurant, David Tarnowski serves ambitious, refined cuisine that showcases beautifully plated classics and his own personal creations. The creamy risotto with chanterelles and Vaudois sausage deserves a special mention. The pared-back setting is filled with light. Fair prices at lunchtime; bistro vibes in the second space.

Name: Pfändler's Gasthof zum Bären
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Steeped in over 200 years of history, this building makes for a really delightful setting: Bärenstube and Orangerie are full of charm and attention to detail. The garden is also attractive – a truly idyllic spot! The seasonal food has regional and Mediterranean influences. You will feel right at home in the pretty guestrooms, some of which are in Casa Beatrice.

Name: Perroquet Vert
Description: This intimate, lively restaurant on the Place de la Fontaine exudes the Belle Epoque charm of the Parisian brasseries of old. A feel that chimes perfectly with the traditional, French dishes chalked up on the blackboard. Favourites include scallop risotto, entrecôte and tarte tatin.

Name: Al Braciere
Address: Via Livurcio 50, Ronco sopra Ascona, 6622, Switzerland
Description: Situated just above Ascona, about 1km from the town centre, this friendly hotel boasts panoramic views of Lake Maggiore, the surrounding mountains and the island of Brissago. Enjoy modern, carefully prepared cuisine in the comfortable dining room or on the idyllic outdoor terrace in summer.

Name: Wildenmann
Description: Set in a lovely Zug house built in 1708, Wildenmann serves classic fare with menu favourites including local Zugersee Arctic char and perch. It also offers charming service, welcoming dining rooms and a lovely terrace.

Name: Essort
Description: This modern restaurant housed in the former US embassy is decorated with photographs taken by the well-travelled owners. In their open kitchen, and in keeping with their cosmopolitan outlook, they cook up contemporary yet pleasantly down-to-earth cuisine. You are free to mix and match dishes from their two set menus ("Essort" and "Essort Vegi"). Lunchtime options are more limited but include an appealing "Business Lunch" set menu. Lovely terrace to the rear.

Name: Les Ateliers Brasserie
Address: Rue des Deux Gares 6a, Vevey, 1800, Switzerland
Description: If you're a fan of traditional dishes with a modern twist, then this brasserie under the same roof as Les Ateliers, run by the talented pairing of Jean-Sébastien Ribette and Sahondra Verdan, is just the place for you! Market salad with orange and turmeric vinaigrette; duck confit with shredded green beans in vinaigrette; Madagascar vanilla crème brûlée… Savour cuisine that revolves around freshness and simplicity in a chic industrial-style setting. Dish of the day served at lunchtime.

Name: Fiskebar
Description: A Nordic enclave at the Ritz Carlton in Geneva, Fiskebar has made a name for itself thanks to its delightful fish- and seafood-based cuisine. The finest ingredients are sourced via short supply chains and skilfully prepared by an expert kitchen team. Diners are treated to fresh and healthy Scandinavian cuisine, enhanced with subtle Mediterranean touches – smoking and fermentation techniques are also put to good use. In a setting that tastefully combines rustic materials with more modern touches, diners take their seats at tables that look onto the open kitchen or afford a view of the lake. On top of that, the wine list abounds with pleasing discoveries, including a range of biodynamic wines.

Name: Le Flacon
Description: This appealing restaurant is located in the old town of Carouge, not far from the Place du Marché. With its high ceilings, bare stone walls and warm red tones, the very tastefully decorated interior is somewhat reminiscent of a loft.
