Description: Verso exudes Italian charm. The interior is truly stylish, with varying shades of gold, while the back terrace offers welcome peace and quiet beneath the vines. Here, diners can enjoy authentic Italian dishes that are delicious and perfectly seasoned.

Name: Kale & de Bril
Description: It would be a shame to pass up a visit to this discreet property where chefs Marc (the bald one or “Kale” in Dutch!) and Niek (the one with glasses – “de Bril” in Dutch!) certainly know how to please their guests. In their pleasant restaurant, savour Zeeland products (in particular from the “homarium”), generous flavours and subtle culinary creations that are always fascinating.

Name: Old Skool
Description: Druten's old school has been converted into a restaurant with a charming retro-modern location and a menu offering a choice of modern, traditional and vegetarian dishes. Although the chef will readily produce a game dish based on pheasant, he tends towards the contemporary end of the spectrum. This manifests itself in his use of seasonings from around the globe and the presentation of the dishes. A delicious lesson for any foodie!

Name: De Houtloods
Description: This old woodshed (1867) has retained its industrial character while combining it with modern comforts. The menu is clear and straightforward, offering guests a choice of fresh, spicy, rich or sweet dishes. The surprise lies in the intense flavours of each dish, with the occasional Asian twist, and the way the ingredients are prepared. The restaurant’s food bar, De Wagon, has the same creative feel.

Name: Infini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The interplay of modern art and rustic features make this elegant villa a lovely setting for a fine dining experience, the terrace is the prettiest of South Limburg! The ambitious chef strongly favours modern cuisine, resulting in elaborate dishes. House specialities include the highly recommended soufflé.

Name: Kasteel Ter Worm
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This 14C castle is brimming with character, and a meal here promises an experience beyond compare. With its wooden floors, medieval paintings and old stone walls, the setting couldn't be more enchanting. The waterside terrace overlooking the verdant surroundings is an absolute delight! Dave Beckers's approach is refreshingly modern and his sophisticated creations frequently feature flavour profiles based on koji, yuzu and koshi. For instance, he adds extra depth to his lamb fillet and crispy braised lamb neck by incorporating powdered seaweed into the potato mousseline and kombu into the rich lamb jus. This is easy-to-enjoy cuisine that also pushes boundaries. An overnight stay in the castle makes for the ultimate grand finale.

Name: The Bishop
Description: The Bishop is where the bustling centre of Leiden truly comes alive. The wooden beams and supporting columns are a reminder of the building's past, yet the trendy decor and lively atmosphere give it a contemporary feel. Take a punt on the surprise menu or order from the small à la carte selection – the chef's creations include subtle nods to his Indonesian heritage. He draws inspiration from all over the world, dabbling in international flavours to create exciting dishes: serundeng and Asian spices are added to the rendang, kimchi and gochujang to the veal tartare, hot and spicy aji amarillo to the kingfish. This place is a surefire hit, especially because of the terrific wine list. Be sure to make a reservation!

Name: de Molenaar
Description: The charm of the converted Hunsingo windmill (1855) is as captivating as this picturesque village, and it houses a really special restaurant. Chef Kooijker works only with a surprise menu in which he brings to bear all his creativity, paying special attention to the presentation, creating elaborate garnishes and giving a new perspective on familiar flavours. Rest assured, you are in good hands here. And why not treat yourself to an overnight stay in the mill or granary?

Name: DeliCees
Description: You could certainly call Cees Timmerman's cuisine delicate and delectable. He scours his region for the finest produce, and likes to incorporate Mediterranean influences. For instance, he has no qualms about combining beetroot with burrata and anchovies. He proposes only a surprise menu that lives up to its name, with combinations such as pluma iberico and corn. At this elegant establishment, whose decor incorporates vintage and modern design, you are in for a full evening's entertainment.

Name: Bosq
Description: Bosq is a cosy establishment on the outskirts of the National Park, overlooking beautiful surroundings – the sunny terrace is particularly attractive – and offering the many delicacies that Texel has to offer. The chef here cooks with real Mediterranean finesse, serving a selection of smaller-sized portions. An appealing concept for a restaurant with real character.

Name: Bøg
Description: Slick Scandinavian design is beautifully executed at Bøg. You have the choice between a vegetarian menu and a meat/fish menu, both as creative as they are appealing. The pure flavours drawn from local ingredients are truly delicious.

Name: Oogst
Description: With its warm and welcoming atmosphere, Oogst is right at home in the cosy Buurtschap Centrum 2005 neighbourhood. There is something of the lively Parisian bistro about this place, which makes it all the more enjoyable to dine here. The set menus are always determined by what the Laantje Voorham vegetable garden has to offer. The versatility of vegetables and herbs provides subtle nuances. By incorporating herbs into ice cream and broths, chef Van Bommel gives dishes a new twist. His modern and always generous creations are fragrant with punchy flavours.

Name: Elea
Description: Located in a grand building in the heart of The Hague, Elea is a modern restaurant with a Greek soul. This idea finds expression in a fabulous Mediterranean-style setting that incorporates natural materials. Takis Panagakis is an inventive chef who draws on Greek tradition, using ingredients such as smoked yoghurt, caper leaf and fava beans to lend his original creations an individual touch. Vegetables play an important role here, with top-notch vegetarian options, such as a celeriac Wellington. The charming Bibi is on hand to suggest some excellent wine pairings.

Name: Oxalis
Description: Prepare yourself to be blown away as you drive past fields full of red and white cabbages en route to this cosy little establishment housed in a former post office. Geoffrey van Melick cut his teeth at top-flight restaurants such as The Fat Duck and 't Nonnetje, and it shows in his selection of quality ingredients, the depth of his sauces and his meticulous garnishes. Take, for example, the perfectly pitched and beautifully reduced veal jus that accompanies the rich fillet of veal Rossini, with fine vegetable accompaniments that add their distinctive nuances. This chef proves that creativity need not be at odds with respect for tradition!

Name: Citrus
Description: Paul Hermes and Jill van Orsouw treat their guests like friends in their intimate, convivial restaurant. The chef, who can be seen at work on his “podium” to the rear of the dining room, likes to bring his carefully prepared dishes to the table himself. He prepares dishes which are full of different textures and flavours, showcasing exciting ideas and delighting guests with his rich cuisine.

Name: 't Havenmantsje
Description: A spot in the conservatory is an absolute must when you come to this restaurant in a converted courthouse – the view of the water and the passing boats is magnificent! The restaurant is open throughout the day, so you can come for lunch, high tea or dinner. The chef skilfully navigates his way between classic and modern culinary traditions. For instance, he won't do too much to a steak tartare, but then he will conjure up a vegetarian dish based on roasted fennel and an apple jus. Be sure to check out the Asian-inspired appetisers.

Name: Kruiden & Jasmijn
Description: Located just inside the historical city walls, this is an elegantly appointed restaurant featuring modern art and imposing chandeliers. The terrace exudes tranquillity, and the attentive service creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere. A passionate advocate for local produce, chef Patrick de Rade especially loves Eastern Scheldt lobster when it is in season. He also regularly harvests fruit and vegetables from his garden. Sourced from a friendly local farmer, red cabbage adds a touch of sweetness to his venison fillet, perfectly complementing the sweet-and-sour pickled red beets. His rich sauces are testament to his culinary expertise and generosity.

Name: DIELS
Description: Dietmar and Elsko's restobar is a friendly, relaxed spot where diners can come for a full dinner or a pleasant drink. The chef draws inspiration from across the borders and serves modern dishes prepared with an eye for detail.

Name: La Mère Anne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: La Mère Anne is a huge business encompassing a range of activities. You can hire the venue for parties, spend the night in modern guestrooms, but above all, enjoy good food! The chef favours regional produce, which he showcases in contemporary dishes. These steer clear of frills, focusing instead on straightforward, delicious flavours.

Name: Landgoed de Wilmersberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At Landgoed de Wilmersberg nature takes centre stage, beginning with a wonderful view of the landscape of Twente, both on the terrace and in the charming dining room. The chef makes vegetables the focus in his modern dishes. He is bold enough to present the occasional challenging combination, always applying the correct techniques.

Name: Noble
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Noble pays tribute to the rich history of this building, which once housed Chalet Royal. Having undergone a drastic makeover, the decor features a blend of sleek design and warm materials. Wine is a serious business here, which becomes clear when you see the imposing cabinet. Thanks to the small portions, you can explore how global influences and attention to freshness create tantalising flavours. We were delighted by the chocolate mousse with peanuts, unctuous ice cream with bay leaf, crunchy caramel and a citrus cream. The bold combinations on the extensive menu never fail to impress!

Name: Aan Sjuuteeänjd
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sustainability takes centre stage at this cosy farmhouse restaurant with its eye-catching designer lighting. Even before it was trendy, chef Thoma was working with organic produce, mostly from his own vegetable garden. He has now even planted a food forest for the future. This ambassador of local Limburg produce proposes only a surprise menu, demonstrating his close ties with small-scale suppliers. Think rosefish from the North Sea, a beautifully grainy spelt risotto and a spicy/tangy beurre blanc sauce with nettles.

Name: Lokaal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nowadays, Villa Ruimzicht is both a hotel and home to this elegant and chic yet warm and welcoming restaurant. The name Lokaal can be translated as "classroom" and is a nod to the building's past as a school. But it is also much more than that: it reflects the commitment of Bjorn Massop and his team to sustainability. They source everything from vegetables to meat and fish from local small-scale suppliers who share their values. This dining experience is a real education. For instance, you will learn that coffee grounds are used to lend earthy notes to a medlar and sherry dessert. Embracing a zero-waste philosophy fuels the chef's innovation. For example, by fermenting spruce in a vegetable broth, he creates a harmonious accompaniment to trout from De Smallert fish farm. The set menu is a celebration of the riches of the Achterhoek terroir.

Name: Japans restaurant Shiro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Shiro has been famed for serving traditional Japanese cuisine since 1989. In this intimate restaurant you will discover all the delights of kaiseki-ryori cuisine – a traditional interplay of intense flavours and subtle textures. Sushi made with the finest rice and ultra-fresh fish (it's best to order sushi when you make your reservation), beautifully crispy shrimp tempura, a deeply aromatic teriyaki sauce... Accompanied by exciting sake recommendations courtesy of your hostess.

Name: Het Roode Koper
Address: Jhr. Dr. C.J. Sandbergweg 82, Leuvenum, 3852 PV, Netherlands
Description: At Het Roode Koper, diners are immersed in the fairytale setting of a romantic decor that exudes luxury and sophistication, set against fabulous English gardens and the forests of the Veluwe all around. Dennis van den Beld's cuisine is rather classical but in keeping with the times. This translates into fabulous sauces, an emphasis on the produce and creative garnishes. The excellent wine list offers both prestigious bottles and finds from small wineries.

Name: Stiel Oriental
Description: Stiel exudes an Oriental vibe – with bright Eastern motifs, warm tones and wicker furnishings, this is as cosy as it gets and you immediately feel at home. The front-of-house team is beautifully in sync with the enthusiastic kitchen brigade, who you can see at work in the open kitchen. Often inspired by Indonesia, their wide range of dishes to share (a regular menu is also available) pack the spicy punch you would expect. House-made dim sum with veal and five spices, a rich curry with prawns, juicy satay kambing – this is a veritable feast for the taste buds!

Name: C.E.O baas van het vlees
Description: Top-quality meat cooked on the American grill is the secret to the success of this lively, urban bistro. The result is meat that melts in the mouth, accompanied by sophisticated garnishes which add both freshness and texture. If you’re part of a larger table, make sure you order the charcuterie platter and the bigger steaks on the menu.

Name: 't Golfje
Description: Housed in a quintessential Terschelling farmhouse just outside Midsland, this is a charming restaurant where diners are made to feel right at home. The gorgeous natural surroundings not only foster a mood of tranquillity, but they also determine what ends up on your plate. Many of the ingredients are picked by the staff themselves or sourced from the restaurant's own vegetable garden. These then feature in modern dishes which also draw on Mediterranean and Asian influences. This is no-nonsense cuisine. Think a perfectly fried quail fillet, a robust chicken stock and Jerusalem artichoke in cream and deep-fried. Divine!

Name: 't Pestengasthuys
Description: The red-brick façade, mezzanine floor and modern dining area with a high ceiling and timber beams lend this location (1450) plenty of character. A spot under the tree is perfect for a romantic dinner of a summer's evening. The hostess wins diners over with her jovial manner, as does her husband with his generous contemporary cuisine with a preference for local, organic ingredients. He does not shy away from more down-to-earth produce such as rabbit, and he respects traditions.

Name: Faulk
Description: Menno and Monique ensure that everything is to your liking in their cosy neighbourhood bistro. The ambitious, contemporary-style dishes are presented in a thoughtful, balanced way. The friendly enthusiastic service is also an indicator that this couple have a bright future ahead of them.

Name: Wox
Address: Lange Voorhout 51, The Hague, 2514 EC, Netherlands
Description: The name gives you an inkling of the ambience here and the interior confirms it: this flashy brasserie is an ultra trendy venue. Fashionable Franco-Asian dishes feature on the menu, as well as phenomenal wines with a good selection available by the glass.

Name: De Havixhorst
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Local produce from Drenthe including herbs from the castle gardens and game from the region take pride of place in the modern creations served here at De Havixhorst. You can savour these in a grand dining room with fine views of the French gardens. Classic and contemporary guestrooms in an 18C castle, where storks nest on the roof every year.

Name: Vive La Vie
Description: This retro-style building with a warm ambience is the perfect place for a special meal. Chef Jeroen Sportel prepares complex and creative dishes, regularly taking inspiration from Asian cuisine and offering just one surprise menu which is highly influenced by the passing seasons.

Name: Vanille
Description: The locals (Belgian and Dutch) flock to this snug restaurant, whose vintage floor tiles immediately catch the eye. The menu is carefully crafted, subtle and deliciously in tune with the zeitgeist. The inspired chef bends over backwards to rustle up fine fare to the delight of his patrons.

Name: Catch by Simonis
Address: Dr. Lelykade 43, The Hague, 2583 CL, Netherlands
Description: No, you are not in New York, although this impressive restaurant in the Scheveningen marina would not look out of place there with its highly fashionable decor, prestigious bottles adorning the wine walls, and luxury terrace on which to soak up the trendy atmosphere… Talk about a hip hangout! Fish and seafood steal the show in traditional dishes, seafood specialities, sushi etc. Whether classically prepared by frying in butter or drawn into original creations, the flavours of the sea take pride of place here.

Name: Amused Food & Wine
Description: On one side is Next wine bar, which is a stylish and trendy spot in which to sample vinologist Corine Vink's latest finds, served with freshly prepared bar snacks. Then there is the elegant restaurant with its chic decor, where Chiel de Groot incorporates his creative ideas into a surprise menu and beautifully presented plates of food. He likes to use produce from his own vegetable garden to bring his creations to life. Intensity is his guiding principle: a grilled sandwich filled with game stew, for instance, makes for an original accompaniment to a medium-rare roe fillet, an exquisite game jus and a cream sauce with chanterelles. Prepare to be surprised with every bite!

Name: In den Doofpot
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Enjoy an aperitif on the restaurant’s boat or on the terrace overlooking the water before sampling cuisine which pays real tribute to the history of Leiden. In this trendy restaurant, a highly imaginative chef serves subtle and precise reinterpretations of classic dishes, while the extensive wine list is a veritable Bible!

Name: Pomerol
Description: As warm and classic in character as a fine glass of Pomerol, this restaurant makes its guests feel immediately at home. Chef Rico continues to reinvent his cuisine, while still paying tribute to the traditions which are so popular with his guests. Top-quality ingredients, sauces full of flavour and an excellent wine list complete the picture.

Name: Fris
Description: Meticulously prepared sea bass terrine, perfectly fried veal sweetbreads, koji butter (fermented on site) and a penchant for exotic flavours such as coconut milk and kombu – the culinary worlds of France and Asia meet at Fris. Classic techniques, top-of-the-range ingredients and playful originality bring the dishes to life. The non-alcoholic beverage accompaniments include delicious kombuchas made using kitchen scraps, among other things.

Name: Meijers 2.0
Description: 2. 0 version of Meijers is modern and simple, while the kitchen has grown more refined. The restaurant still offers the Meijers’ Ten, a selection of small portions including a couple of classics. Be sure to opt for the four- or five-course set menu to make the most of the high-quality creations, which are packed with flavour.

Name: Rikus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Surrounded by tranquil landscapes, Rikus offers guestrooms in a natural setting and serves cuisine prepared largely from produce grown in its own vegetable garden. Authentic, modern cuisine made from top-quality ingredients, including locally sourced meat and fish. In the room to the rear, the panoramic view and moss wall bring nature inside, while the front room is more authentic in feel.

Name: Landgoed Groenendaal
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a magnificent location! Set in the beautiful Groenendaal forest, this former coach house exudes luxury and boasts a terrace that is among the loveliest in the region. The chef likes to draw on the finest ingredients when devising his set menus (one of which is vegetarian). Diners can therefore indulge in a rich terrine of foie gras as well as a carrot dish prepared with miso, pumpkin and yellow curry. This fresh and unfussy take on authentic flavours never disappoints.

Name: 't Pakhuus
Description: This restaurant's designer decor is delightful, with a moss-clad wall that brings a touch of nature into the dining room. However, the ultimate appeal of this historical warehouse is its view of the harbour and the shrimp boats. Fish and seafood are the speciality of the house – the centrepiece is the fish tank, which is replenished daily. Think fresh Wadden oysters or scallops, enhanced by Asian flavours such as ponzu, ginger and pimento. Of course, the menu also features other local delicacies, such as Texel lamb. To cap it all off, why not spend the night in one of the designer suites?

Name: Kaagman & Kortekaas
Description: Giel Kaagman and Bram Kortekaas have clearly chosen to focus on quality in their lively bistro, where the chef enjoys working with vegetables, wild game and fish, transforming these ingredients into exciting dishes which are striking for their contrasting flavours. Both the menu, which changes regularly, and the wine list are full of surprises!

Name: Red Chilli
Description: Asia is a world away from the peaceful polders but this intimate restaurant creates a real Eastern ambience. Its fusion Asian cuisine is authentic yet modern in style. Red Chilli will definitely spice up your evening!

Name: Oostergoo
Description: Oostergoo is an ideal base from which to explore the picturesque town of Grou and, for that matter, the lovely province of Friesland – starting with a visit to this beautiful marina terrace. It's quite an experience! The old Dutch interior, with its Delftware and lovely parquet flooring, is no less enchanting. They serve up an authentic brand of traditional cuisine. The locally caught smoked eel is a real treat!

Name: Dell'arte
Description: Robbert Dellaert has transformed his childhood home, dating from 1878, into a restaurant with a romantic feel. This is an intimate space with a beautiful garden. Thanks to Julie's excellent service, you can just relax and delight in the love that the chef expresses for his terroir – Zeelandic Flanders. He treats local produce with reverence, and his well-thought-out combinations create a sense of depth. For instance, he enhances ultra-fresh soused herring with avocado ice cream, yuzu gel and sweet and sour daikon. A unique culinary adventure!

Name: Dorset
Description: Dorset is intimate and trendy, with a pleasant lounge atmosphere. Chef Davy Roord will delight you with his modern fusion of local ingredients and Asian flavours. This enthusiastic cuisine is occasionally innovative and always fresh. Guest satisfaction is the priority here, both on the plate and in the wine glass!

Name: De Herberg van Smallingerland
Description: Dating back to 1791, this charming inn is full of character and extremely popular. Tables in the gorgeous courtyard garden are in high demand, as are the guestrooms. With a special emphasis on vegetables, Chef Freddy and son Jurmen showcase Frisian cuisine at its best. For instance, they will draw on the distinct flavours of beetroot, cherries and capers to give a fillet of red mullet a special twist. The menu at de Herberg is full of surprises!

Name: TOV
Description: TOV stands for Team Onvergetelijk Verrassend (literally, an unforgettably surprising team), giving an indication of what is in store at this trendy restaurant. The young staff are full of enthusiasm and everything is organised just as it should be. Resolutely contemporary-style cuisine created by an imaginative chef.

Name: Wilhelminapark
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Utrecht's city park is an ideal spot to unwind, and where better to do that than in this stylish restaurant with its authentic thatched roof and idyllic terrace overlooking the magnificent lake? Wilhelminapark has been a fixture since 1926, and you'll notice that right away. The chef wins diners over with both a rather classic fish dish accompanied by a rich beurre blanc and a steak tartare with an Asian twist. The wine pairings are equally impressive. Or just drop in to enjoy a drink and some delicious oysters.

Name: Tante Blanche
Description: In this contemporary restaurant Charles Ek honours the memory of his aunt’s fine cooking. Enjoy delicious, fresh dishes that are simple, copious, full of flavour and exciting without being overstated.

Name: De Kleine Toren van Baarland
Description: There is something impressive about eating in a church that has been converted into an elegant restaurant. The combination of original features and modern decor really works here. The chef will have guests' mouths watering with local delicacies, such as Eastern Scheldt lobster, prepared with a tasty modern twist.

Name: De Kluizenaer
Description: This former savings bank has been converted into a restaurant with a touch of industrial decor, with large drawings providing a bit of fun. The internationally seasoned chef brings punchy flavours to the plate to present his own vision of gastronomy. His cuisine is resolutely contemporary, involving robust taste combinations.

Name: Ron Gastrobar Oriental Downtown
Description: Subdued lighting, Asian decor and natural materials set the mood inside, while a celebrity bartender mixes cocktails behind the extensive bar. This place has a lovely bustling atmosphere! The ducks you can see dry-ageing come into their own in fabulous Chinese/Indonesian dishes. Authenticity and a modern playfulness are combined here with a sure touch. Whether you choose the dim sum, the Peking duck or the rijsttafel (a medley of dishes with rice), this is a real culinary adventure.

Name: Bij Brons
Description: At John and Yvonne Brons’ restaurant you can enjoy good food in a cosy pavilion, right in the harbour area of Almere-Haven, where fresh fish is served in season (outside the spawning period) straight from the sea onto your plate. The meat dishes are also a fine example of chef Brons’ focus on quality. Generous classic cuisine offering a delightful dining experience.

Name: De Goede Gooier
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The thatched roof and trendy yet welcoming interior are a draw in their own right. However, it's the pergola and the gorgeous terrace overlooking the heathland that steals the show. The kitchen is run by a highly skilled chef who produces French cuisine with the utmost respect. The sole meunière and pan-fried foie gras do not disappoint with their robust flavours, but the chef also has some surprises up his sleeve, such as a swordfish carpaccio finished with a spicy harissa vinaigrette. There is an appealing lunch menu, an extensive dinner menu, and they are open every day for both lunch and dinner: a firm favourite!

Name: John Dory
Description: A romantic ambience pervades this old warehouse dating back to 1680, in which the well-drilled team shares its love of fish and seafood with its guests. Whether you’re ordering crab, tuna or everything in between, quality and freshness are always to the fore, with creative side dishes adding extra intensity. You won't resist the enticing menu!

Name: Trattoria Da Giulio
Description: Giulio keeps the traditions of his native Sardinia alive in this cheerful trattoria. He makes his own pasta and bread every day, and the orata (gilt-head bream) in a salt crust is even filleted at the table. Here the Italian art of simplicity is at its most exuberant. House-made pappardelle with a creamy duck sauce, an aromatic panna cotta topped with a subtly flavoured juniper jam... Da Giulio is undeniably the best Italian in Arnhem!

Name: De Steenen Tafel
Address: Weg achter het Bos 1, Arnhem, 6822 LV, Netherlands
Description: Fans of fine food put on their Sunday best to dine at this elegant conservatory restaurant on the edge of the pretty Klarenbeek park (what a view!). They come here for the traditionally prepared lobster or the wild game from the Veluwe region, although the chef also prepares more original fare such as the occasional oriental dish with foie gras. Rich, authentic cuisine is to the fore here.

Name: Bistro Bord'o
Description: European wines take centre stage in this casual establishment – hence the name (a pun on Bordeaux)! Start with an aperitif before digging into fine French classical fare. Rather than prissy frills, the focus is on quality ingredients, spot-on cooking and wholesome flavours! In summertime, you can even hire a rowing boat!

Name: Auberge de Veste
Description: Dating from 1849, this restaurant right by the river is the perfect setting in which to enjoy complex and beautifully presented cuisine. The chef prepares contemporary influenced dishes with bold flavour combinations. The owner’s passion for wine is a bonus, as are the extra dishes which can be added to the interesting set menu.

Name: Zuid by Adrian Zarzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Adrian Zarzo brings the world to your plate in this trendy, chic establishment. For example, you start with dim sum, then move on to an intense bouillabaisse and continue your journey with a Mediterranean take on sea bass. Zuid advocates a relaxed approach to gastronomy and is run by a chef who knows how to win over the modern diner. Be sure to drop by the bodega next door for some delicious snacks and a good glass of wine.

Name: DYLANS
Address: Oude Zeeweg 63, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CJ, Netherlands
Description: The founder of Alexander Hotel was born a butcher's son and can be proud of this restaurant for meat lovers. The trendy intimacy of the decor, the gold elements, the hip lounge and cocktail bar all make for a magnificent venue. Many of the modern dishes are prepared on the Josper charcoal oven, resulting in robust, pure flavours. A fine côte de boeuf, a salt-crusted tenderloin to share, a choice cut of Japanese Wagyu beef: a feast for carnivores!

Name: Woods
Description: From the magnificent sawmill next door to the wonderful waterside summer terrace to the rear, this modern restaurant enjoys a fantastic location. The chef reveals his fresh, tasty cooking style in a selection of small dishes.

Name: Mezger
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Mezger is the dream of Jeroen and Sanne Tanis who found the perfect setting in this orangerie which they have redecorated with wood and trendy furniture. His cuisine highlights his own experience, which respects the seasons and products from the Zeeland region. He adds to this mix perfect cooking techniques and ingredients that work together to create a dream that is now a pleasurable reality!

Name: 't Arsenaal
Description: This traditional building next to the Lebuïnus church is now a modern, bright, no-frills restaurant. Attractive bar, patio garden with terrace amongst the church buttresses, tempting menus and attentive service.

Name: Carelshaven
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Carelshaven has been providing comfortable overnight accommodation since 1772, in a stunning location near Twickel Castle. Here, the chef prepares fine French cuisine using produce from his own vegetable garden, giving classic flavours a fresh twist without the need for excessive flourish.

Name: De Ertepeller
Description: The steady stream of boats passing by provides a captivating backdrop for this bright and airy restaurant located at a point where three rivers meet. Large windows afford uninterrupted views. During the week, Arjan Kuipers serves up an appealing selection of simple dishes, including crispy battered fish and freshly cut chips. Alternatively, you can opt for a more ambitious and adventurous set menu. A variety of textures and international flavours are expertly combined, and the dishes are beautifully presented. With an accomplished chef at the helm, De Ertepeller offers the best of both worlds, and the quality is second to none.

Name: Sillyfox
Description: Located at the top of a converted grain-processing plant, this delightful space combines a raw, industrial aesthetic with modern design elements. It also boasts a roof terrace affording panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. With years of experience, Joppe Sprinkhuizen meticulously crafts each dish, blending timeless French cooking techniques with international influences. For example, the entrecôte, cooked rare, is served with a bitterbal (Dutch meatball) filled with rendang, alongside beans cooked in red curry and lemongrass, plus a peanut cream and a red berry cream providing sweet and fruity nuances. The set menus are fantastic, although an appealing à la carte selection is also available in the evening.

Name: Scherp
Description: Mart Scherp's restaurant, which also offers accommodation, merges the historical charm of Middelburg's town centre with a trendy vibe. The talented chef likes to work with Zeeland's local produce and Asian seasonings. Enticing flavours and subtle spiciness are common features, so it's no surprise that he has gathered a loyal following.

Name: Hanasato
Description: In this atmospheric restaurant diners will discover authentic Japanese cuisine in all its glory. The chef cooks with respect for tradition and unites subtlety of flavour with precise preparation methods. The smoked sashimi and the Shabu Shabu menu are particularly popular.

Name: De Hinde
Description: Harmen Ligthart has converted his grandfather's café into a cosy restaurant with an endearing and authentic soul. The view over the IJsselmeer (also from the two luxury guestrooms) is truly stunning! A stroll through the village and down by the boats is a must. Whether you opt for fish or game, you can rest assured that the ingredients are locally sourced and that the classic sense of generosity is adhered to. The pâté and fine Riesling wines are firm favourites here.

Name: Dudockx Bar & Kitchen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Architect Dudok is the designer behind this trendy 1930s pavilion. Each table overlooks the Hilversumse kanaal, which really is something to behold as you sit on the gorgeous terrace. The resolutely modern cuisine shows a preference for organic and local produce, yet remains down to earth. This is the place to come if you want an original take on wonton or a perfectly cooked cut of meat with an elegant sauce. The restaurant also rents out boats!

Name: Restaurant Eindeloos
Description: The biggest draws of this warm and welcoming restaurant are Willem Schaafsma's culinary prowess and the exquisite pairings dreamt up by his sommelier. Here, you can savour dishes made with top-quality ingredients that are sourced as locally and sustainably as possible – and all at excellent value for money. A firm favourite!

Name: Breakers Beach House
Address: Koningin Astrid Boulevard 5, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 BK, Netherlands
Description: Welcome to the "Dutch Riviera", where dining with your toes in the sand is sure to give you that holiday feeling. The relaxed terrace affords a wonderful view of the sea, or you can enjoy the trendy brasserie ambience inside. This is the place to come for a plate of ultra-fresh oysters and seafood, followed by classically prepared dishes in which the produce (mainly fish, of course) steals the show. Simple and delicious!

Name: Villa la Ruche
Description: This 19C villa is alluring, chic and inviting. The classic cuisine is the real standout feature here. The chef has a good command of his techniques and cooks with wonderful subtlety. He also regularly ventures into more modern dishes to treat his guests to a whirlwind of flavours.

Name: Le Moulin
Description: At the warm and cosy Le Moulin, they have been paying their respects to classic French-Flemish cuisine for more than 35 years. Frans Glas knows the importance of a sauce, like the amazing beurre blanc that he serves with the flawless sole meunière. They steer clear of unnecessary frills and everything revolves around flavour. Salmon is still smoked according to an old family recipe. His sister Yvonne provides charming service and astute wine recommendations.

Name: Bistro Madeleine
Description: As typical as the name sounds, this place is far from being your average bistro. Rather than a stuffy decor, you can expect a 21C take on the standard bistro setting. The chef conjures up the same impression on the plate. Upon entering, you are greeted by the delicious aroma of fresh bread. Here, simplicity is synonymous with robust flavours. The modern touches he brings to the dishes add a surprising twist. Think ray wing with a roasted pepper sauce vierge, creamed celeriac and a frothy tarragon sauce. The carefully curated wine list is second to none. An atypical bistro!

Name: Bistro Sophie
Description: Don't let the name fool you; this is an upscale restaurant with a stylish interior that features vintage decor and natural materials. Working in an open kitchen, Dejan Gavric is clearly keeping up with the times. He is a chef who likes to incorporate Mediterranean influences and techniques. This is evident in the dish comprising pan-fried sea bass fillet with mussels and sea lavender and featuring a variety of garnishes. The wine list, while not too extensive, is international, well curated and great value for money.

Name: Oesterbeurs
Description: Lobster, oysters, sea lavender and mussels are just some of the Zeeland delicacies served in this restaurant which is decorated in warmly gilded tones. More than 80% of the dishes served here are fish based, with a richly flavoured classic bouillabaisse featuring on the menu alongside more creative fare. A true ode to Zeeland.

Name: Hendrik van Maurick
Description: A visit to this medieval castle (1257) is an experience in itself. The wooded surroundings, the drawbridge, the courtyard... What a magnificent place this is! Inside, all that historical character meets with modern comfort. The portrait of the knight Van Maurick holding a smartphone is certainly a talking point. The menu may seem classical at first glance, but it features inventive dishes in which Dutch produce is given a French twist. This cuisine is sophisticated, vibrant and ambitious!

Name: Restaurant MANNA
Description: Fashionable restaurant in a beautiful old building, which acts as a backdrop for cosmopolitan, modern cuisine with a focus on fish. Attractively priced 4-course menu.

Name: Wolf Atelier
Description: Michael Wolf likes to experiment with sophisticated flavours and surprising ideas, giving diners the opportunity to test them out and then refining them to retain their best features. He is just as happy to cook up a turnip-based vegetarian take on Beef Wellington as he is to concoct surf and turf combinations that put a new spin on familiar flavours. The name Atelier is therefore particularly appropriate in this trendy, industrial-style restaurant, which is located on an old railway bridge with a beautiful view of the IJ.

Name: Etablissement 1880
Description: Etablissement 1880 is much more nuanced than the black and white that dominate its colour scheme. The charm of the decor and the location on Groede's historic market square make for a cosy setting. For her surprise menu, chef Mariëlla draws on flavours from around the globe and Zeeland produce. With an eye for detail, the creative chef focuses on subtle touches such as zesty garnishes and rich sauces that bind her dishes together. If you wish to extend your stay, book one of the two guestrooms upstairs.

Name: Het Binnenhof
Address: Bocht van Guinea 6, Goes, 4461 BC, Netherlands
Description: Het Binnenhof exudes all the charm of Goes's historic centre. A narrow alleyway leads you to this stylishly refurbished restaurant, which is tucked away in a courtyard and boasts an inviting terrace. The seafood comes directly from the Vismijn Colijnsplaat fish auction; the vegetables and meat are also locally sourced. Chef Arjen spoils you for choice with his à la carte and set menus, and it doesn't stop there! Generous and highly accomplished, he whips up the most fabulous sauces.

Name: Restaurant Kasteel Engelenburg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this restaurant, occupying a 19C conservatory, the cooking style is modern and the wines South African. Lounge featuring an impressive whisky collection to round off the evening.

Name: Het Bosch
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: From this contemporary restaurant diners enjoy a breathtaking view of the Nieuwe Meer marina. In this dream location the chef entertains diners with lavish, up-to-date dishes prepared with real know-how.

Name: Maris Piper
Description: Done out in green and gold, this handsome luxury brasserie has a chic, London-style atmosphere. For the ultimate experience, be sure to secure a seat at the Chef's Table (only available on Fridays and Saturdays). In keeping with the location, the menu presents an original take on brasserie dishes. For example, you could start with a crispy brioche bun with smoked eel and foie royale; then you might move on to the barbecued turbot served with a beurre blanc that possesses a delicate acidity. The chefs here work with the finest – often Dutch – produce, and it pays dividends.

Name: Restaurant De Lage Vuursche
Description: This restaurant was opened by Willem van Oosterom in 1865 and is now run by the fifth generation of his family. Authentic details, such as a fireplace and wooden tables, add to the charm of this quintessential Dutch café and restaurant, which also boasts a delightful terrace. The kitchen team takes pride in serving up traditional French cuisine. Perfectly pan-seared scallops with blood sausage and a rich bisque, crispy sweetbreads and succulent veal tongue with a Bordelaise sauce, and a delectable Eton Mess to finish: a symphony of flavours awaits! The nearby woods are ideal for a tranquil post-prandial stroll.

Name: Inter Scaldes
Description: To say that Sanne and Jeroen Achtien have breathed new life into this institution would be an understatement. The beautiful manor has undergone a drastic makeover, creating a luxurious and trendy space with a lounge feel. The light and airy extension looks out onto the magnificent garden. After the appetisers, you can take a walk past the kitchen to see the impressive team in action and enjoy an additional dish. Chef Achtien draws on his Frisian heritage, his Zeeland surroundings and the experience he gained in Switzerland. His cooking is creative and grounded in expertise, occasionally complex, and highly exuberant. Think lobster and beetroot given extra depth by a fabulous lobster jus with magnolia petals. Sommelier Tessa van de Wouw adds the finishing touch with her intriguing pairings.

Name: Villa de Duinen
Address: Oude Zeeweg 74, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CE, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Arriving at this Anglo-Norman-style villa (1902) feels like coming home. The cosy interior, reminiscent of a cottage, and the endearing personality of the hostess are irresistible. The youthful kitchen team favours a resolutely modern approach to cooking. They play with textures, allow the main ingredient to shine and sometimes come up with surprisingly imaginative ideas. Hand them a butternut squash, and they will turn it into something amazing, with great technical skill and subtle influences from around the globe.

Name: Pirandello
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A trendy restaurant with charming views of vines and a stork’s nest, as well as one of the most attractive outdoor terraces in the Netherlands! Both the cuisine and the wine list have a strong Italian focus, the former offering authentic flavours with the occasional daring twist. The option of overnight accommodation completes the picture.

Name: Allemansgeest
Description: The Vliet canal provides the stunning backdrop to this former farmhouse with an elegant decor. The waterfront terrace (with mooring facilities) will take your breath away. This is the perfect setting in which to savour a modern approach to French cuisine that is replete with subtle exotic nuances. How about tuna with foie gras, foie gras ice cream and a spicy vinaigrette? A surprising culinary delight!

Name: De Gaffel
Description: De Gaffel creates a wonderful dining experience under the old Saxon farm's thatched roof and around the open hearth, which fills the rustic interior with a homely feel. Outside, the chef grows his own vegetables, working with top-quality ingredients, accentuated with contemporary techniques.

Name: In Den Rustwat
Description: In den Rustwat adds an exotic touch to metropolitan Rotterdam with its thatched roof, history dating back to the 16C and an idyllic setting close to an arboretum. The food here is anything but traditional, offering contemporary-style dishes with an abundance of ingredients and cooking methods.

Name: Brasserie Goeie Louisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This brasserie shares the medieval charm of the upscale hotel, Karel V, to which it belongs. Once a monastery, the property has been elegantly decorated but has retained its original character. The chefs here like to put their own unique spin on classic recipes. They understand the value of a decent béarnaise sauce with a succulent cut of meat, but they also enjoy playing with the tartness of orange to elevate a dish based on lobster and fennel. This cuisine presents familiar flavours with an exciting twist.

Name: Bistro de Holterberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Experience the charms of each season in this cosy bistro, whether it's winter by the large open fireplace or summer on the stunning terrace, offering an awe-inspiring vista of the Salland Ridge National Park. The extensive set menu features authentic French dishes that each showcase one or two bold flavours. Crispy fried sea bass fillet, langoustine sauce and boiled fresh vegetables: unadulterated flavours at their best.

Name: La nouvelle Auberge
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Ask for a table in the elegant glass conservatory at this intimate restaurant with its modern auberge feel and enjoy the view of the greenery outdoors. The chef here delights fans of rich cuisine with dishes which are influenced by French and international culinary traditions and made from locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Merlot
Description: It will come as no surprise that wine plays a special role in this atmospheric, trendy restaurant. The fabulous selection, also available by the glass, will lend extra verve to your meal. A great deal of care goes into the chef's modern dishes; he works meticulously to revamp predominantly French flavours.

Name: Valuas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The stunning view of the Maas River from the terrace here is something you won't soon forget. The same goes for the warm welcome you will receive and the genuine hospitality that is so characteristic of the Limburg region. At this restaurant, they aim to please, as you will see from Eric Swaghoven's extensive menu. The range of delectable options includes a rich North Sea crab remoulade with textures of potato and an exquisite shrimp bisque, a guinea fowl and rabbit paté en croûte, mackerel sashimi, as well as a Mediterranean-style risotto. The experienced chef's versatility shines through, and the value for money is exceptional. Oenophiles will delight in the extraordinarily extensive wine list.

Name: De Silveren Spiegel
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: These two step-gabled houses from 1614 take you back in time . From the open fireplace with matching tiles to the romantic candlelit setting, silver cutlery and beautiful porcelain plates, everything here exudes Dutch charm at its best. The menu features exquisite, intricate dishes that showcase Dutch produce. The young chef has a keen eye for freshness, as demonstrated by the foamy mussel sauce he uses to elevate the salty symphony of mussels and seaweed. With its good selection of natural wines and a penchant for French labels, the wine list is definitely worth a look.

Name: Senses
Description: Indulge your palate at Senses, where the cuisine brims with vibrant Asian flavours, invigorating acidity, and showcases a mastery of both classic and new techniques. Prepare to be captivated by the imaginative and daring flavours. The enthusiastic team behind this graceful restaurant leaves nothing to chance. The sophisticated atmosphere and fine wines are the icing on the cake.

Name: MEI
Description: Marco Blok is an enthusiastic champion of sustainable development. His menu and restaurant have been treated to a makeover, in particular the splendid counter. This seasoned chef crafts subtle dishes in which the wide diversity offered by vegetables is exploited to its full. He plays with fermentation, acidity, fruity flavours and slow cooking… Subtly balanced guest star appearances of local meat and fish.

Name: Fermin
Description: Fermin has a natural feel that permeates every aspect of this operation. Fruit and vegetables are sourced as locally as possible; foraging and fermentation are standard practices. When it comes to meat, only wild game is used. As for seafood, the selection is limited to shellfish. This unconventional approach to nature is captivating. Opt for a spot at the bar if you want to watch the chef work his magic with the wood-fired oven and yakitori grill. Our inspectors were blown away by his parsley root ice cream, Douglas fir granita, redcurrant caramel and a tangy redcurrant garnish. A perfect match for the suggested natural wines.

Name: Céline
Description: The austere appearance of Fort Jutphaas is in marked contrast to the restaurant it houses, which boasts an intimate atmosphere with subdued lighting and cosy terrace. Chef Rick works principally with Dutch produce, such as Dutch yellowtail, which he likes to season with subtle Asian flavours. This is original and modern cuisine, in which vegetables take pride of place. In fact, why not opt for the appealing vegetarian set menu?

Name: Plantage 87
Cuisine: Modern Cuisine, Cuisine from the Marches
Description: The first thing that strikes you at Plantage 87 is the phenomenal view of the surrounding marina. Stephan Möllers's biggest source of inspiration, however, lies a little further away, in his generously sized vegetable garden. He likes to express his creativity by working with vegetables so that they yield the right acidity or spiciness to bring out the best of the main ingredient – letting it speak for itself.

Name: Sequenza
Description: The intimate Sequenza has conquered a place in the hearts of its many regulars, who keep coming back for the French-influenced market menu, offering a selection from a limited number of dishes. The choice is small and the flavours are big. The high quality produced by the chef bears witness to real knowledge of his craft.

Name: Pollevie
Description: Martin Berkelmans has a passion for vegetables. He sources them from a food forest and a local farm and likes to experiment with them in his fermentation lab. The versatility of vegetables makes his dishes both playful and intriguing – they dictate the culinary direction, although meat and fish are also incorporated into his cooking. The succulent partridge breast and the rich stew are elevated to new heights with parsley root, a vegetable and walnut purée and a robust sauce featuring cassis for a sweet-and-sour note. The slightly industrial feel and organic vibe lend this inviting restaurant a unique character.

Name: Lyf's
Description: One of this neighbourhood restaurant's main assets is its convivial atmosphere. The commitment to quality is palpable on every plate that is brought to your table. Martijn Stroosma serves up beautifully presented dishes that showcase his creativity. This astute chef never goes over the top. For instance, he will mellow the combination of langoustine tail tempura and confit bacon with touches of mango and celeriac. He always strikes the right balance, including in the mouth-watering à la carte and lunch options.

Name: Gebr. Hartering
Description: Niek and Paul Hartering share a love of ingredients. This cheerful venue proposes a short menu, which changes regularly, as the fusion cuisine depends on the ingredients at their best on the day. Flavours don't lie.

Name: LIZ Restobar
Description: The wooden horse heads on the walls, the impressive chandeliers that call to mind the wheels of a horse-drawn carriage, the partitions between the tables: you can't help but notice that you're dining in the former stables of Amerongen Castle. The terrace overlooking the castle and gardens is breathtaking! The cuisine is characterised by its use of locally sourced ingredients, French cooking techniques and a global outlook. The duck gyoza in a rich game broth with marinated mushrooms and crispy scallions says it all!

Name: Vermeer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This relaxed restaurant is the culinary playground of Chris Naylor, a highly creative chef who makes maximum use of fresh ingredients from local producers to enable nature to express itself to the full. His love of contrasts sees him bring together eclectic flavours to create unique combinations. The surprise menu here (there’s no à la carte) certainly lives up to its name!

Name: MARIO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A former inn on a dyke across from a canal. Italian cuisine featured on the single menu. Elaborate Italian wine list and excellent advice from the sommelier-owner. A handful of well-kept rooms with good bedding.

Name: Soigné
Description: At Soigné, which might be described as cosy and charming, you are in the right place to discover the contemporary culinary aspirations of Dennis Jong. He makes an impression by complementing familiar flavours with exotic ingredients and rich sauces. The adjoining room can be booked for private dinners.

Name: Breda
Description: Breda is a lively brown café with a difference. Here, traditional Dutch pub charm is elevated by elegant touches and a retro-luxe aesthetic. Opt for the appealing lunch or surprise set menus and experience how the chef creatively spices up his dishes with delicate acidic flavours. For example, vibrant yoghurt cream gives a fresh twist to sweet peas, watercress oil and a vinaigrette with chopped shallots. This chef knows how to make a dish sing with just a few ingredients. The wine list, which mostly features European labels, is sure to please even the most discerning palate.

Name: Marque
Description: The open kitchen and spacious bar (which you can eat at) will grab your attention as soon as you walk into this former cheese warehouse (1618). The character of this property is enhanced by the elegant decor. Marque is proud of its Mediterranean soul, and the experienced head chef wins diners over with modern textures, delicate acidic touches, and all the panache and exuberance of the South.

Name: Buitenplaats Slangevegt
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The River Vecht is the star of the show at this warm and welcoming restaurant – the riverside terrace alone is reason enough to book a table! Another draw of this place is the extremely attentive service. The cuisine here is playful and creative. Classic combinations are elevated with original ideas and exquisite textures. The chef also enjoys adding a touch of spice to his sauces for that extra kick.

Name: Zheng
FacilitiesAndServices: Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Zheng takes you back to the banquets of Imperial China. Through a parade of small dishes, often served on three plates, you will discover the traditions of the four main branches of Chinese cuisine. The succulent Peking duck, with its crispy skin, is deservedly a signature dish – it is heavenly when paired with hoisin sauce and the house-made sambal! The typical tableware and objets d'art (also for sale) add to this unique dining experience. Subtle cuisine which nonetheless offers a wealth of flavours.

Name: Beulings
Description: Beulings is a little gem full of atmosphere. Lisja offers guests a warm welcome, and is also in charge of the excellent wines, while Bas and his team create delicious meals in the open kitchen. They put a lot of effort into the preparation of their dishes, which are full of versatile textures and carefully thought-out flavours. A delightful experience!

Name: Ledeboer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Until 1994 this stately building housed a bank. Today retro and industrial features complement one another beautifully at this trendy restaurant offering quick snacks as well as larger meals, with the top choices on the set menu. The chef produces modern combinations with a sophisticated twist. At Ledeboer, taste reigns supreme.

Name: De Jonge Dikkert
Description: The Jonge Dikkert has given a new lease of life to this windmill dating from 1672, with its chic decor, intimate atmosphere and attractive dining room with wooden beams. The chef here focuses on predominantly Dutch ingredients to create carefully prepared dishes with Asian flavours, with a nod to classic cuisine which will surprise and delight guests in equal measure.

Name: Tollius
Description: With its sleek decor done out in burgundy and white and contemporary artwork on the walls, Tollius has an inviting feel. This is also down to chef Barry's expertise in producing hearty classics such as his wonderfully crispy pithivier filled with a rich combination of quail, foie gras and morels. But he is just as adept at whipping up a surprisingly zesty modern dessert involving wasabi and a lemon gel. If the extensive wine list is anything to go by, this place is certainly run by people with excellent taste.

Name: Brasserie van Baerle
Description: There is no getting around it: wine is part of the core business of this elegant, ever-inviting luxury brasserie. The impressive selection of wines by the glass and extensive drinks menu will impress even the most seasoned connoisseur. Classics from the brasserie repertoire are served up here with great attention to detail and a sense of generosity. The steak tartare is a real crowd pleaser.

Name: EN
Description: Whether you opt for one of the seven seats up at the counter or for a regular table, there is no escaping EN's vibrancy. This energy is also reflected in the food. The set menus introduce you to creative Japanese dishes including an original take on tuna sashimi. The à la carte options, on the other hand, are more traditional. Whatever you choose, you can count on the characteristic finesse and richness for which this cuisine is world-renowned. The extensive sake selection is terrific.

Name: Choux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Giving prominence to vegetables may not always be the obvious choice, but at this trendy restaurant it works beautifully. The continually surprising ingredients, creative preparations and intense flavours ensure complete fulfilment, taking diners on a wonderful voyage of discovery.

Name: Triptyque
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Chef Niven Kunz and Virginie van Bronckhorst-Kunz have created a natural, relaxing ambience in this restaurant, where the decor is simple yet also elegant and luxurious, with details such as dried flowers adding an attractive touch. Kunz favours local and regional ingredients, using his creative skills to prepare dishes with a particular emphasis on vegetables. Surprising yet authentic cuisine, accompanied by a choice of excellent wines.

Name: Oud-Zuid
Description: Oud-Zuid is a restaurant that is full of character. Take a seat inside to admire the trendy brasserie-style decor or sit out on the pleasant pavement terrace where you can enjoy the vibe of this neighbourhood. The chef puts a modern spin on tradition in his tempting and no-nonsense menu that has a focus on fish, seafood and organic produce. There is something for everyone in the impressive wine selection. Less than 10 minutes' walk from the renowned Concertgebouw.

Name: Les Salons
Address: Joseph Corneli Allée 1, Valkenburg, 6301 KK, Netherlands
Description: The Belle-Époque elegance of Les Salons is a sight to behold. The character of this historical chÂteau, the art and murals, the modern furnishings and the terrace set in the meticulously tended gardens give it that "wow" factor. The chefs put a contemporary twist on French tradition and understand the importance of precise cooking and rich sauces. Playful garnishes and fresh nuances bring their dishes to life.

Name: IJssel Restobar
Description: Part of the Pillows hotel, this stylish restaurant encapsulates the best of Deventer. Seating options include a lovely conservatory and a terrace overlooking the River IJssel – the perfect place from which to take in the city's skyline. Wouter van Leeuwen creates a menu that's simply irresistible. Timeless classics such as steak tartare are accompanied by contemporary creations that draw on international influences and feature playful textures. For instance, he serves a combination of North Sea crab, leek and carrot with an espuma and powdered tomato. Foodies are sure to be delighted by the wide range of options.

Name: De Boet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying a beautifully renovated traditional carpentry house, De Boet blends in perfectly with the picturesque harbour of Urk. Here, chef Cees Kramer demonstrates his clear appreciation of top-quality ingredients through his beautifully prepared modern dishes with the occasional Oriental twist. Reasonably priced wines add to the appeal.

Name: Hofstede Meerzigt
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Zoetermeer harbours a secret oasis that is waiting to be discovered. This enchanting estate boasts a chef’s table in a wine barn, a wedding venue in a converted stable, a terrace overlooking a lush garden, not to mention a stylish restaurant in a converted 17C farmhouse. The hospitality here is genuine, as is the kitchen team's appreciation of their ingredients. Alain Adriaanse shares his passion by delivering dishes that give familiar flavours the odd twist. With an Asian touch and fresh flavours, he elevates the sea bass tartare to new heights. He also puts a unique spin on steak tartare by adding playful textures. The extensive wine list is the icing on the cake.

Name: Den Burgh
Description: This impressive farmhouse dating from 1859 has retained its original charm and gained in elegance since its refurbishment. Inlaid with golden coins, the main bar is sure to draw the eye, as is the terrace. This bustling establishment is popular with business people, not only due to its proximity to a business park and the airport. The extensive menu includes appetisers, salads, steak tartare and bouillabaisse. The succulent pan-fried halibut accompanied by an exquisite fish sauce shows that, although the dishes may have a modern look, they are rooted in beautiful classic flavours.

Name: Bridges
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Fish reigns supreme at this sleek restaurant, which also offers a beautiful view of the canals. Salted delicacies take centre stage in dishes that are distinctly contemporary in style. The chef combines classic sauces with the occasional Asian twist to showcase the fresh flavours of his ingredients.

Name: De Koetsier
Description: A romantic atmosphere reigns supreme at De Koetsier. Shades of blue and pink provide the colourful modernised decor at this auberge without taking anything away from its authenticity. An old wardrobe has even been converted into a cheese store! Martijn will be delighted to share his passion for wine, while Ayesta brings elegance and a subtle modernity to the kitchen.

Name: De Saffraan
Description: This old clipper moored in the canal has been converted into an elegant and intimate restaurant with a terrace on the deck where you can while away the hours. De Saffraan really is an exceptional restaurant with great service provided by charming waitstaff. Chef van Wechem has a penchant for punchy flavours and innovative techniques, handling top-notch ingredients with finesse. For instance, he elevates fried turbot with a wonderfully robust beach crab jus and adds coconut for depth. This place has real personality!

Name: Teppanyaki Restaurant Sazanka
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: After being greeted by ladies dressed in kimonos, you sit down around the teppenyaki grill and the show begins. Seven to ten people can be accommodated here to watch the teppan-chef juggle with all kinds of produce. It is an entertaining spectacle that results in delicious Japanese dishes.

Name: Restaurant Crijns
Description: Crijns creates comfort with its elegant restyling of a beautiful villa, working in old features. The perfect menu to fit the setting presents classic flavours and more modern combinations, avoiding overly complicated techniques and prioritising flavour.

Name: Graham's Kitchen
Description: The highly creative and eye-catching mural, a mix of Amsterdam and Liverpool, adds life to this pleasant restaurant. Graham Mee’s English roots are also subtly distilled in his cooking, which has a penchant for strong flavours. A single menu gives full rein to his huge creativity.

Name: Cristó
Description: A stroll along the Oude Haven (old harbour) of Zierikzee, with its characteristic boats and drawbridge, is sure to capture your imagination. This picturesque setting adds to the appeal of the romantic Hotel Mondragon, whose elegant restaurant, Cristó, will take you on a gastronomic adventure. The Anjou pigeon, cooked to perfection, demonstrates the classic culinary know-how of a chef who also puts a contemporary spin on his dishes. Occasional Basque influences lend his creations extra flair.

Name: Lagrange
Description: Picture the scene: You are in the lovely town of Buren, and step into an elegantly converted barn in anticipation of an intimate dinner. The dishes served embody a modern take on French cuisine. The chef knows how to cook a fillet of wild duck to perfection, for example, but also makes his mark by seasoning leg rillettes with hoisin. At Lagrange, flavours from the local area and around the globe go hand in hand.

Name: Restaurant 1857
Description: Restaurant 1857 achieves its goal of being chic but by no means stuffy. A narrow street leads to this former coach house – an elegant combination of authenticity and contemporary class. Joke, the charismatic maître d', presides front of house; chef Joey conjures up creative and at times complex cuisine that is technically and visually impressive. A game sauce enhanced with hints of coffee, or dairy cow beef given depth of flavour by a meat jus seasoned with koji and fermented ingredients – diners will be swept along by this modern fusion of vegetables and global influences.

Name: Sizzles at the Park
Description: The monumental building that provides the setting for Sizzles is truly impressive – the contemporary elegance, trendy ambience and terrace almost whisk you away to Ibiza! You can eat here morning, noon and night, enjoying Leon Habers’ family-inspired and highly original dishes that include a dynamic twist, a hint of Asia and an acidic touch. Fascinating!

Name: Rue de la Plume
Description: Everything about this inviting restaurant makes it clear that Luella and Madelene are passionate about what they do. Luella likes nothing better than to amaze her guests with her contemporary surprise menu. Her dishes revolve around a main ingredient of the finest quality, elaborate garnishes and velvety sauces that bring it all together. The wines recommended by Madelene complement the intense flavours beautifully. This duo's enthusiasm is infectious!

Name: Nassau
Description: A centuries-old beamed ceiling, glossy parquet flooring, sleek furniture design and views of the beautiful Prinsentuin walled garden – you really dine in style at Groningen's Nassau. The chef knows the importance of an intense sauce and loves working with top-notch produce such as langoustine and Anjou pigeon, which he showcases in elaborate dishes. For instance, he elevates hamachi, along with a medley of vegetables and seasonings, with a Thai-style sauce made with miso, coconut and lemongrass. His plant-based creations are equally remarkable. A beautifully curated wine list featuring an interesting range of German wines has the perfect accompaniment in store. Sophistication is in Nassau's very DNA.

Name: De Hemel
Address: Moeregrebstraat 35, Bergen op Zoom, 4611 JB, Netherlands
Description: Enjoy an intimate dinner in a romantic dining room, or on the rear terrace in fine weather, and choose from a selection of tasty dishes prepared in French style, with a nod to modern cuisine. A delightful dining experience.

Name: Elkaar
Description: This pleasant restaurant with its lovely summer terrace is highly recommended for a relaxing meal out. The finesse of the dishes reveals the chef's French soul. Flavours from around the globe, meticulously prepared vegetables and a masterful use of spices and acidity guarantee that seductive touch.

Name: Oan Tafel
Description: 80% homegrown produce and vegetables, the remaining meat and fish comes from further afield. Such is the concept of this natural restaurant, whose interior sports raw materials, a handsome counter and a casual vibe. Eastern exuberance meets Frisian temperance. Fermentations, sweet and sour touches, surprising flavours… Intriguing!

Name: Ni Hao
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant with an intimate Eastern feel introduces its guests to “chistro” dishes, a combination of bistro and Chinese cuisine. Chef Chen creates delicious contemporary dishes, which are made to share and which include specialities from Sichuan, Guangdong, Beijing and Wenzhou. An innovative approach to authentic Chinese cuisine.

Name: Bar BAUT
Description: With its Banksy-style frescoes, trendy, intimate interior and delightfully relaxed ambience, Bar BAUT is a must in Amsterdam, where guests can choose from the enticing à la carte featuring international ingredients cooked in contemporary style. Enjoy intense flavours, well-prepared produce and original ideas – plus excellent value for money!

Name: Ron Gastrobar Indonesia
Description: Top chef Ron Blaauw has a nose for a winning concept, as proven by this typical Indonesian restaurant with its bustling terrace by the River Amstel. The flavours are distinctively Asian, but he and his colleague Agus Hermawan also add their own twists for that extra fragrance and depth. The rijsttafel options "Agus" (15 dishes) and "Tim" (12 dishes) provide the perfect opportunity to share all kinds of delicious treats, such as satay kambing and udang peteh.

Name: Restaurant Bakboord
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The view you have here of Almere's marina as the boats sail away is quite something to behold. The lounge terrace is a great place to sit, but equally charming is the contemporary decor indoors. The dishes, which showcase vegetables, are brimming with creative enthusiasm. They are elaborate, even daring at times, and always display technical mastery. There are plenty of delicious vegetarian options on the à la carte menu should you wish to avoid meat and fish.

Name: Hemel & Aarde
Description: Rene van der Weijden and his team move heaven and earth (Hemel & Aarde) to showcase the seasons in their cuisine. It's hard to miss the majestic building on a corner plot that houses both this restaurant and the Nox Hotel. Done out in blue, gold and white, the stylish interior makes for an opulent setting. Rich flavours derived from garums and time-honoured techniques, such as fermentation, are incorporated into modern, sophisticated creations. This dynamic chef takes a bold and creative approach to highlighting the wealth of delicious produce the earth has to offer.

Name: Oesterput 14
Description: The oyster tanks and the Eastern Scheldt reveal all their secrets in this sparkling establishment, which is the height of contemporary cuisine. Fish-lovers are well placed here for mouthwatering sea delicacies delivered fresh and unadulterated to the plate. Those who opt for a delicious piece of meat will also find tailored dishes on offer.

Name: Visaandeschelde
Description: Fish and seafood enthusiasts will be in their element here! Since 1999, this nautically inspired brasserie has been serving salty oysters and lavish fish and seafood of an unsurpassed quality. The chef adopts a relatively classic approach to the cooking, allowing his creativity to be expressed in his side dishes. The lunchtime menu comes highly recommended!

Name: Kook Atelier op Oost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Nature takes centre stage at this tastefully converted farmhouse, which also has splendid guestrooms. The restaurant's Nordic-inspired design and large windows that make you feel connected to the outdoors reflect the house's commitment to sustainability. The menu is centred on ingredients from the Wadden Sea and Texel, which they have either grown themselves or sourced from friendly local purveyors. Produce such as peas, algae and lamb are showcased in vibrant creations, in which techniques such as fermentation and koji add intensity and depth. This exploration of Texel's ecosystems is truly fascinating.

Name: Broederenklooster
Description: The authenticity of this former monastery (1293) has been preserved in every detail. Where once the friars used to take their meals, you can now enjoy a luxurious dining experience in a historical setting. The ultra-modern open kitchen immediately catches the eye. Niels van Dooijeweert prepares French dishes using contemporary techniques. Turbot fried À la minute, a robust jus enriched with butter and juicy veal cheeks. For fans of such delicacies, this is the place to be. Top-notch produce takes pride of place at Broederenklooster. The beautiful guestrooms are perfect for a good night's rest.

Name: Prix de Rome
Description: As far as Maastricht foodies are concerned, all roads lead to Prix de Rome. Inside this impressive building just outside the city centre a cosy interior awaits, in which exposed beams work well as part of the otherwise modern design of the place. The open kitchen at the back is a nice added touch. Here, chef Wouter alternates sophisticated, original creations with dishes that focus mainly on the produce. Among the favourites on the menu are the salmon ceviche and house special crispy fried veal sweetbreads. A winning combination!

Name: Porta Sud
Description: This pleasant restaurant with its charming Art Nouveau style is located along the Passage Zuidpoort. Don’t expect a traditional Italian dining experience, however; instead, you’ll be treated to contemporary Southern European flavours with a local and Nordic influence and a different take on time-honoured combinations that will definitely tempt your tastebuds.

Name: The Green Rose
Description: Vegetables, fish or meat – the wonderful produce that the Netherlands has to offer is the biggest source of inspiration for Jin Hu and his team of artisans. He takes his cue from the micro seasons and lets nature dictate what goes into his French-Asian fusion dishes. Sustainability is at the heart of this cuisine, which is characterised by the intense authentic flavours of ultra fresh ingredients, as well as an element of surprise. Be sure to sample the extraordinary range of natural wines and special beers.

Name: Bij Hammingh
Description: It is impossible to resist the authentic charm of this former ferry house, from the terrace of which you can fully appreciate the lovely views across the canal and drawbridge. Inside, you can sense the building’s rich heritage, where the chef focuses on regional delicacies that showcase modern techniques and natural finesse.

Name: Old Dutch
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Old Dutch exudes charm and nostalgia. The serving staff are dressed in suits, the vintage dining room has a distinguished air and the spacious terrace is a must. Here, you can savour classic French cuisine prepared with fitting generosity and finesse. If you enjoy a culinary spectacle, make sure you order the lobster bisque prepared at your table.

Name: Wijnhuis De Blauwe Camer
