Description: The medieval site of St Catherine's Valley convent is an oasis of charm. The coach house has been turned into a modern restaurant, bathed in natural light and with a rustic vibe. There is also a kitchen garden and several hectares of vineyards (hence the wine barrels at the entrance). The food has just as much character as the site. Home-grown vegetables, influences from around the globe and spicy/subtly acidic details skilfully combined to create expressive dishes. Highly impressive.

Name: Foer
Description: Foer certainly has character both in terms of the stylish decor – nab a place at the dining counter if you can – and the food. The focus here is on vegetables and herbs, perhaps complemented by a fish or meat dish. Using inventive preparation techniques, Steven Broere succeeds in elevating vegetables in original combinations. For instance, he marries intense beetroot cooked in a salt crust and an emulsion of egg yolk with subtle acidity to create a remarkable flavour sensation. The select wines add to this unique sense of harmony.

Name: Tres
Description: Walking down the steps to Michael and Emy's intriguing basement restaurant is akin to embarking on an extraordinary adventure. At Tres, the vintage-style decor is pared down and somewhat rugged yet inviting. The best of what local producers have to offer is showcased here. At the expansive dining counter, you will discover the fascinating work of the inventive self-taught chef: his tangy fermentations, rich garums, complex ageing processes, state-of-the-art preparation techniques. Every season brings with it a new set menu, and it is always full of surprises.

Name: Puur Zee
Address: Van Ogtropweg 2, Wijk aan Zee, 1949 BA, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Master chef Imko Binnerts knows how to bring out pure seafood flavours, and how to combine them into a delicious meal. His interesting cuisine is cleverly presented, while the modern combination of flavours is as elegant as the decor.

Name: De Harmonie 23
Description: Whether you opt for the 23-course tasting menu or something from the enticing à la carte selection, creativity is the hallmark of this restaurant. Marco Sommer uses his own house-made ingredients as much as possible in his ambitious cuisine. His dishes are finely balanced and unpretentious. For example, he brings together juicy chicken with a crispy crust, fried morels, Cévennes onion with a surprising pine nut stuffing, as well as a rich poulette sauce, creating a glorious ensemble. This stylish establishment, with its tranquil terrace at the back, pushes boundaries while maintaining a sense of harmony.

Name: Flores
Description: Flores is a champion of bistronomy. The chef harnesses his culinary flair and subtlety to underscore the umami flavours of vegetables, without however forgetting meat and fish, even if they don’t play the leading roles in this production. Nature is the watchword of the cuisine. The terrace overlooking the wine cellar is heavenly.

Name: Bistrobar Beaune
Description: The magnificent Rosendael Castle houses this fashionable upscale bistro that affords views over the delightful surrounding grounds. This is a seriously cool bistro bar! The wide-ranging menu proposes a range of appealing entrées served in modest portions that diners will find hard to resist. Vegetarian options, a classic cod dish, meat specialities, the house version of an eclair for dessert… You'll be spoilt for choice!

Name: Savage
Description: Two friends who are passionate about what they do are the driving force behind this modern, casual gastrobar. Drop by for some delicious oysters and a glass of good wine or for a creative set menu. The talented chefs show their wild side by elaborately working their ingredients, taking care not to obscure their natural flavours. A vibrant and playful place!

Name: Joann
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Contemporary elegance and the original stylistic features of this impressive building come together in perfect harmony. It won't escape your attention that every detail here is on point, from the attentive service to the selection of wines and exuberant dishes. As Emiel Kwekkeboom's creations are brought out, you can sense the anticipation. The creative and playful combination of colours, techniques and flavours is a wonder to behold. They harvest ingredients from their own herb and vegetable garden to create depth with subtly spicy, zingy, sophisticated flavours.

Name: Hof aan Zee
Description: Only 500m from the North Sea, this historic Scandinavian farmstead stands in the heart of the countryside. The stripped-back interior weaves a rustic spell, while the menu shines the spotlight on the rich produce of Zeeland. Seaweed, fish from the Oosterschelde, fermented vegetables, smoky flavours – superlative purity!

Name: Karel V
Description: Oozing with character, this 1555 historic edifice on the embankment of the port of Goes leaves no one indifferent. An open fire, harbour terrace and artwork set the inviting scene in the Karel V. The youthful chef blends the intensity of classical recipes with refreshing modernity. Flavoursome, authentic food stamped with the chef’s signature.

Name: Restaurant Calva
Description: This intimate restaurant is a love story in itself, where chef Tom enjoys explaining his dishes at the table and is always happy to recommend the best wine to accompany his well-constructed culinary creations. As an example, his traditional savoir-faire shines through in the way he cooks pigeon to perfection as well as his intensely flavoured sauces. His exquisite and more modern side dishes provide the perfect harmony.

Name: De Keuken van Arragon
Description: Herco van Arragon’s unashamedly contemporary cuisine is based around modern techniques, a variety of menu options and home-grown vegetables. He has a good eye for quality, which he uses in his subtle garnishes to emphasise the main ingredient of a dish. The hospitality of friendly sommelier Cynthia accentuates the warmth of this rural property.

Name: Mei Wah
Description: Mei Wah has been a household name since 1965. The third generation now at the helm has returned to authentic Chinese cuisine with a focus on finesse and purity, not adapting to Western taste. The result is a contemporary look with flavours from overseas, accompanied by a choice of wine or sake.

Name: Ambrozijn
Description: Previously a church, Irenekerk (1891) is now a restaurant where design reigns supreme. The organ has been converted into a bar, dark brick walls surround you, and the new roof truss is magnificent. You can also see the impressive Sven Nijenhuis in action in the completely open kitchen. This place is all the more exceptional because of the way the talented chef draws on French cooking styles and innovative techniques. He really makes his mark with his exquisite sauces and meticulous seasonings.

Name: Sukerieje
Description: Sukerieje has now relocated to Hopmanshuis, a tastefully converted warehouse brimming with character. The menu has also been revamped. Chef Yannick Roodhof likes to focus on vegetables and enjoys expressing his creative side – his creamy cashew nut 'pâté with melon and chilli causes quite a stir. Through his expertise in using exotic ingredients and his patience in imbuing his sauces with depth, he creates an exceptional intensity of flavours. This restaurant is going places!

Name: In de Oude Stempel
Description: In this former post office, stamps and letters have made way for the on-trend cuisine of Mark van Loon. This is a chef who doesn't hesitate to play with textures or bring bold combinations to the table. His creativity is complemented by his prowess in the art of making sauces – think a rich game jus to accompany the venison fillet. For something more low key, head to Puur, the brasserie next door.

Name: NY Basement
Description: A jazzy vibe reigns supreme in the cellar of the New York hotel, which is reminiscent of the Big Apple of the 1920s and 1930s. After a delicious cocktail at the 11m-long bar, guests can enjoy the modern cuisine on offer here. Choose from a delicious fish or meat dish, vegetables prepared on the charcoal grill and an array of trendy suggestions.

Name: Amber Garden
Address: Van Heuven Goedhartlaan 15, Amstelveen, 1181 LE, Netherlands
Description: Amber Garden is a lavish, swanky Chinese restaurant, whose guiding line is authenticity, as the house specialty, roast duck, demonstrates. The chef enjoys adding the occasional western touch and cannot be rivalled for his ability to subtly blend texture, taste and fresh produce. A tantalising insight into Chinese cooking.

Name: Pichlmaiers zum Herkner
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Well worth a trip to the outskirts of the city. The inn formerly run by famous Viennese chef Heinz Herkner has been given a successful makeover that combines modernity and tradition – this applies to the warm and charming setting as well as the food. The Austrian and classic French dishes are peppered with modern touches. The pretty terrace extends over two floors.

Name: Meissl & Schadn
Description: "Schnitzel love" is the name of the game at this restaurant in the heart of the old town. Even from the outside you can peer into the open kitchen and see the house speciality, Wiener schnitzel, being prepared. The menu also includes Austrian classics such as Tafelspitz, Esterházy lentils or goose (when in season), as well as desserts such as Salzburger Nockerln. Reasonably priced lunch. Tip: Leave your car in the multi-storey car park Altstadtgarage A.

Name: Kommod
Description: This popular restaurant proposes predominantly plant-based cuisine, with little meat and fish featuring on the menu. They are careful to select top-quality produce; the vegetables are locally grown. The chef serves guests himself and talks them through the dishes. Wine pairings are available to accompany the set menu. The changing temporary art exhibitions make for an extra point of interest.

Name: Trattoria Martinelli
Description: This restaurant run by the Barbaro family is in the courtyard of the fine Baroque Palais Harrach. They offer a fresh, authentic take on Mediterranean cuisine, made with fish and other produce that the owners themselves have been importing from Italy for around 30 years. There are also a few seasonal dishes that do not feature on the menu – the friendly waitstaff will be happy to fill you in.

Name: Meissl & Schadn
Description: Here, the Wiener schnitzel is the obvious choice – it's best to order it "mit allen Schikanen" (with all the trimmings)! At this attractive restaurant on the Ring that encircles Vienna's old town, good food is accompanied by classical music, Viennese service culture and an elegant yet pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere. In the open kitchen (which is also visible from outside), you can see the schnitzels being pounded. Why not take part in the weekly schnitzel course. There is even a book for sale: The Wiener Schnitzel Love Book.

Name: LABSTELLE
Description: An appealingly upmarket bistro setting with a relaxed bar area. Labstelle serves ambitious seasonal and regional fare such as Styrian black-feathered chicken served with carrot and house-made dumplings. The chef makes a point of working with high-quality produce from Austria. Reduced menu at lunchtime. Gorgeous courtyard.

Name: Goldener Hirsch
Description: This restaurant in the eponymous hotel in the old town serves modern dishes that draw on international influences as well as Austrian classics. You can dine à la carte or opt for a set menu (vegetarian option). Be sure to peruse the decent wine list with an emphasis on Austrian labels. A striking white vaulted ceiling, lovely parquet flooring and delightful nods to tradition in the decor contribute to the atmosphere. Parking at Altstadtgarage A.

Name: Esszimmer - Everybody's Darling
Description: An intriguing, innovative concept combining Tagesbar ("daytime bar", serving great cocktails) and Esszimmer (meaning "dining room"). Hidden behind a curtain, and with only a handful of covers, the stylish restaurant has a pleasantly private feel. They serve a modern set menu (a vegetarian version is available if pre-ordered), in which chef Alexander Kumptner incorporates the occasional and subtle Italian or Asian accent into his own style – "vongole, 'nduja, orzo, basil" is a good example. The focus is on the high quality of the ingredients. The professional and charming service runs like clockwork.

Name: SHIKI Brasserie & Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This minimalist-style brasserie with its large terrace is SHIKI’s less formal eatery. It offers a wider range of dishes from miso soup to tempura and sushi – the latter prepared before you as you sit at the sushi bar.

Name: Goldgasse
Description: The speciality here is new interpretations of old Salzburg recipes taken from a cookbook published in 1719! The food is a perfect match for the period setting with modern touches and the lively atmosphere – the charming service is the icing on the cake! Try the fried breaded chicken with potato and cucumber salad and cranberries and the apple strudel with vanilla sauce.

Name: Kussmaul
Description: Where a slaughterhouse once stood, a long time ago, today you can dine on one of the two levels in a stylish interior and enjoy modern international, Mediterranean-influenced cuisine, e. g. confit sea bass with tomato coriander sauce, orange and potato cream. Lovely historical setting with cross vault, and a pleasant, casual atmosphere.

Name: Eckel
Description: This family-run restaurant in Vienna's beautiful 19th district has its fair share of regulars who come to sample its range of classic, flavoursome Austrian specialities. On the menu, you will find familiar favourites such as Wiener schnitzel, seasonal dishes with game, but also seafood including lobster. The attentive waitstaff and cultivated atmosphere add to the appeal of this place, not to mention the splendid garden terrace!

Name: Kutschker 44
Description: This relaxed and friendly, modern restaurant is very popular with locals, and no wonder given the delicious fare on offer. Menu options include chanterelle terrine with walnuts, lamb’s lettuce and bresaola as well as Viennese specialities such as veal lights and Black Angus rib-eye steak. The terrace looks onto the pedestrian zone.

Name: Herzig
Description: In the 15th district, Sören Herzig's restaurant is on the ground floor of the former Dorotheum Fünfhaus (auction house and pawn office). In this listed building dating back to the 1920s, the dining space was once an auction hall and has a minimalist, industrial-style atmosphere that is reminiscent of a New York gallery – casual and original. Beautiful parquet flooring, comfortable designer chairs and artwork by the likes of Peter Jellitsch and Clemens Wolf underscore the tastefully stylish interior. The spectacular rooftop terrace has a fantastic view, making it a great spot for an aperitif or nightcap. As for the food, the modern dishes are made from the best ingredients and without excessive gimmickry, eg trout, almond, koji, sea buckthorn. There is a set menu in a large or smaller format, which can also be made vegetarian by prior arrangement.

Name: Ludwig van
Description: This place is steeped in history! The ground floor of this listed building where Beethoven once lived now houses an inviting restaurant that exudes traditional charm. Diners come here to enjoy a contemporary take on regional fare, served by a friendly and attentive front-of-house team. Chef Andreas Spindler sets great store by the quality and freshness of the produce he uses in his dishes. Two set menus are proposed, and you also pick and mix their courses as you see fit. Tip: Don't miss out on the Austrian wines, which are also available by the glass.

Name: Buxbaum
Description: Somewhat tucked away, this restaurant is run with great dedication and has a pleasingly friendly and welcoming atmosphere. The charming front-of-house team serves up appealing dishes such as pike-perch with crayfish, garlic and citrus stock. Tip: wines from selected Austrian vintners.

Name: Umar Fisch Bar.
Description: At the second Umar restaurant, located next to Umar Fisch, casual fine dining is the name of the game. Here, in a laid-back atmosphere, you sit at one of a handful of high tables to savour creative fresh fish and seafood dishes. You can order the "Chefs Menu" or choose à la carte.

Name: Servitenwirt
Description: An appealing restaurant with a cosy atmosphere in a quiet spot near the church – in summer, places on the terrace are highly coveted! The menu comprises an appetising selection of international dishes and traditional Viennese specialities. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced daily specials go down a treat.

Name: DiningRuhm
Description: Housed in a corner plot building in an inconspicuous location in the 4th district, this restaurant serves an interesting mix of Nippon and Nikkei cuisine – ie Japanese- and Peruvian-inspired dishes are in the spotlight. This unpretentious cuisine also goes wonderfully well with the interior, which is decked out in warm colours and characterised by modern lines. The sushi bar is located in one of the three rooms. Try the delicious finger food, sushi (including lobster nigiri with a creamy spicy sauce) or main courses such as black cod yuzu miso. Attentive service from staff who also provide good wine recommendations from a selection that highlights Austrian labels. Unless you would prefer a sake…

Name: Skopik & Lohn
Description: The first thing you’ll notice here is the wonderful painted ceiling, the work of artist Otto Zitko. The service is friendly and attentive, the food flavoursome and the Austrian classics on the menu include Wiener schnitzel with cucumber, potato and sour cream salad and, for dessert, perhaps an île flottante?

Name: Freyenstein
Description: This place calls itself a "gourmet inn", which hits the nail on the head! The pleasingly laid-back atmosphere you would expect of an inn is complemented by flavourful, sophisticated cuisine that nevertheless has a rustic feel to it. The chef proposes an appealing set menu with each course usually comprising two small dishes. Tip: the medley of desserts!

Name: Edlingers Tempel
Description: This restaurant is somewhat tucked away, but it's well worth seeking out. The atmosphere is cosy, the service is friendly and the regional cuisine tastes fantastic. Staff may also recommend specials that do not appear on the menu. Be sure to look out for the special set menus that reflect the different seasons. In fine weather, the secluded outdoor area beckons. This place is also a good option for a relaxed lunch.

Name: Huber's im Fischerwirt
Description: At Andrea and Harald Huber's, hospitality par excellence is the name of the game: a charming, elegant space with various dining areas, exceptionally friendly service, plus tasty dishes that straddle classic and traditional cuisine and draw on regional influences and seasonal ingredients. Tip: Don't miss out on the delicious curd dumplings! There is also a delicatessen selling products such as chocolates, jam and spices.

Name: Duchardt
Description: Now with a new name and under new management, this listed building in the centre of the old town has plenty of Viennese charm, as well as a wonderful vaulted ceiling in the restaurant. Having taken over from Walter Bauer, chef-patron Marcus Duchardt proposes his own take on classic cuisine imbued with Austrian and French influences – available à la carte or as a set menu.

Name: Le Salzgries Paris
Description: A slice of Paris in Vienna? Mais, oui! This lively brasserie with a distinctly chic feel has become an institution in the city and – in no small part thanks to patron and chef Denis König – brings to life the concepts of "bistronomie" and savoir-vivre. If you are a fan of fresh seafood, then you've come to the right place: just order the plateau de fruits de mer! The beef tartare is another fine example of the French classics served here. In the evening, you can also choose an even more refined and creative five-course set menu. An exclusively French wine selection and charming service contribute to that Parisian feeling.

Name: Zum weissen Rauchfangkehrer
Description: This cosy restaurant is divided into four traditionally decorated rooms – in one of them, gentle piano music provides the soundtrack to your evening meal. Delicious Austrian cuisine is the order of the day, including house specialities such as "Rauchfangkehrers Wiener Schnitzel". The wine list is exclusively Austrian and organised according to grape variety.

Name: LOLA
Description: A word to the wise: You should definitely make a reservation because this Spanish restaurant is extremely popular. On the one hand, this is down to its convivial atmosphere and charming interior – the high ceilings and striking bar are bound to catch the eye. On the other, there are the flavoursome tapas from various regions of the Iberian Peninsula – these are perfect for sharing! When it comes to wine, the focus is also on Spanish labels.

Name: Gasthof Schloss Aigen
Description: The history of this place dates all the way back to 1402! The kitchen team puts a modern spin on traditional Austrian cuisine, and diners can opt for a set menu or order dishes à la carte. Our tip: Try the boiled beef, which is prepared in a range of different ways. The charming interior is tastefully decorated and exudes an appealing family atmosphere. In summer, don't miss the gorgeous terrace laid out in the courtyard beneath the boughs of the chestnut trees.

Name: Unkai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasantly light and modern restaurant where you can eat either at authentic teppanyaki grill tables or more conventionally. You will also find the Unkai sushi bar on the ground floor serving a sushi brunch on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

Name: Umar Fisch
Description: Here at the famous Naschmarkt, the name "Umar" is synonymous with the freshest fish. The establishment has housed a fish shop since the mid-90s and this simple restaurant since 2003. It owes its success to the quality of the fish, which is served in the form of classic dishes.

Name: Wirtshaus Hoheneck
Description: A charming, rustic restaurant, equally cosy upstairs and down, with a terrace offering magnificent mountain views on both levels. The food is regional and seasonal, including Hirschegg beef goulash with bread dumplings, accompanied by some good Austrian wines. The afternoon brings coffee and homemade cakes.

Name: Sonnenstüble
Description: Here in the restaurant of the peacefully situated Hotel Birkenhöhe, the next generation is bringing a breath of fresh air to this place in the form of Felix Bantel. Diners can look forward to cuisine that incorporates modern trends while remaining true to its regional roots. Great selection of wines including rarities from Italy and France. Warm wood panelling and a tiled stove make for a cosy atmosphere.

Name: Riedenburg
Description: In a beautiful building just outside Salzburg's historical heart, the pleasant classical setting of this stylish restaurant has been infused with traditional charm. On the menu are tasty dishes with a regional bent, which also reveal the personal touch of the chef. To accompany your food, choose from the very decent wine list.

Name: Brandstätter
Description: A real Salzburg institution! The atmosphere in the various dining areas is perfect for a cosy dinner, but in the summer, you might prefer to sit out on the gorgeous terrace. Traditional Austrian fare dominates the menu, but you will also find dishes that take their cue from the seasons or from global culinary trends. The service comes courtesy of an attentive and well-drilled front-of-house team. Good to know: You can buy house-made jams to take home.

Name: Léontine
Description: An authentic little corner of France, tucked away in a quiet yet central location near the Stadtpark. The bistro atmosphere is charming, the service provided by the owner is cordial and professional, and the modern French cuisine is delicious. The dishes revolve around the seasons and are made with select ingredients. The pair serve a five-course tasting menu and an à la carte selection; at lunchtime there is the more affordable "Menu du Midi" – a three-course set menu. The wine list takes you through the regions of France.

Name: Fuhrmann
Description: An exceptionally friendly restaurant that feels almost neighbourly with its inviting, cosy atmosphere and friendly service. As for Mike Feierabend's truly tasty Austrian cuisine, choose à la carte or go for the five-course set menu that changes every month. At lunchtime there is a cheaper three-course menu. Your hosts will be more than happy to recommend a local wine, but big names from Europe are also served, including some spanning numerous vintages. On that note, it would be remiss not to mention owner and sommelier Herman Botolen, whose genuine passion for wine is plain to see. Tip: be sure to book, as places are limited! In summer, make a beeline for the pleasant terrace in the courtyard.

Name: Rote Bar
Description: This restaurant in the famous Hotel Sacher, a piece of the city's history, epitomises the charm of this great Viennese establishment with its striking red interior, elegant oil paintings and crystal chandeliers. The menu features dishes that draw inspiration from modern culinary trends as well as Viennese and Austrian traditional specialities, including Tafelspitz and Sachertorte. Gorgeous little veranda.

Name: O boufés
Description: This bistro serves fish and seafood in a pleasantly informal, modern interior. Vegetarian options are also available. This trendy restaurant is right next to its fine dining counterpart and also has a nice garden.

Name: Weibel's Wirtshaus
Description: Just a few minutes’ walk from St Stephen’s Cathedral, Weibel’s Wirtshaus is the archetypal Viennese restaurant – warm and friendly, rustic and snug! It also has a charming garden in the small alleyway. The food is traditional and Viennese.

Name: Pastamara - Bar con Cucina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In the luxurious Ritz-Carlton Hotel you will find this modern restaurant with its large bar. A pleasantly relaxed and elegant atmosphere reigns, and the experienced staff are very friendly. Traditional Sicilian cuisine with a modern touch, including an interesting "Street Food Siciliano" aperitif.

Name: SHIKI Japanese Fine Dining
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Shiki translates as "four seasons", and , indeed, this tastefully elegant fine dining restaurant takes its cue from the seasons, serving up both traditional and a modern take on Japanese cuisine – fascinating, expressive and made with top-notch ingredients. There are two set menus in the evening, which are supplemented by the brasserie selection at lunchtime.

Name: Das Loft
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The location on the 18th floor of lifestyle hotel SO/Vienna is undeniably spectacular – the view of Vienna is phenomenal! Add to that the attentive, laid-back service and cuisine that draws on modern influences. Great wine selection. There is also a popular cocktail bar.

Name: Zum Buberl Gut
Description: More than just a pretty face, the gorgeous 17C country estate is also a delightful setting for a delicious meal. As you soak up the pleasant atmosphere in the series of appealing, elegant dining rooms, savour this tasty cuisine – a blend of Austrian and Mediterranean classics. The wine list, too, is definitely worth a look. In summer, grab a table in the garden. Tip: The set menu at lunchtime.

Name: Veranda
Description: The restaurant in the Hotel Sans Souci is smart and fashionable. It proposes modern Austrian cuisine, which can be ordered à la carte or as a set menu in the form of a "culinary voyage through Austria". Wine list with a focus on Austria and a wide selection of champagnes.

Name: Heunisch und Erben
Description: Due to its being an interesting mix of wine bar and restaurant, this place has a remarkable wine list and around 120 open wines to accompany the ambitious modern cuisine. Diners put together their own four- to nine-course menu from a lovely selection of dishes. The service is relaxed, attentive and experienced. The terrace is a popular spot on warm summer evenings.

Name: Fabios
Description: The clientele of this fashionable urban restaurant is a veritable Who's Who of Vienna! The Italian cuisine served is modern and pared back, in keeping with the minimalist interior design – two good reasons to come here for a meal! Plump for one of the house classics such as fried calamari or vitello tonnato. Or perhaps you would prefer saffron risotto with Norway lobster? Friendly and attentive service, a large terrace in summer, and a bar that is ideal for a light bite or a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Paradoxon
Description: The atmosphere here is pleasantly down-to-earth, and the waitstaff laid-back and friendly. The cuisine is modern and seasonal. Along with à la carte options such as char ceviche or local ribeye steak, there is a set menu comprising four or six courses. Tip: Brunch is also served on Sat and Sun (10am-2pm). N.B. cash payments only. The restaurant also has an online shop selling home-made goods (sauces, pesto, jam etc), as well as beer and wine.

Name: Do & Co Restaurant am Stephansplatz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Up on the seventh floor, this is one of the city's hotspots: a modern, elegant restaurant with a great terrace and a view of St Stephen's Cathedral. In the open kitchen the team cooks up international cuisine. Alongside the many Asian-influenced dishes, including sushi, the menu also features Austrian classics.

Name: OPUS
Description: Done out in the style of the Viennese workshops of the 1930s, this restaurant is located in the prestigious historical building of the Hotel Imperial, which has been an integral part of life in Vienna since it opened in 1873. Against this elegant backdrop, classic French-influenced cuisine made with select ingredients is served. There are two set menus (one with meat, one vegetarian) with a variable number of courses; if you wish, you can pick and choose from both set menus. The bread course gets the meal off to a great start! Friendly and skilful front-of-house team.

Name: Hong 0871
Address: 5F, Shanghai Chengtou Holding, 130 Wusong Road, Hongkou, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: In Chinese, ‘Hong’ means vast and deep, aptly describing the menu and the Yunnanese food culture that the owner from Kunming wants to popularise. Over 90% of the ingredients ship from Yunnan and the mushroom feast in summer is especially spectacular. Start with Nuodeng ham cured for 3 years alongside paper-thin dry cheese called rushan. Try also lard-layered buns, either steamed or deep-fried, with ‘winter melon’ pork and bean sauce filling.

Name: Café des Banques
Description: In the banking district, this chic and contemporary bistro is the latest venture for Yoann Caloué. Here, the MICHELIN-starred chef serves confident modern cuisine, made with high-quality fresh ingredients to exacting standards. The desserts are also meticulously prepared, cf. his lemon tart, basil sorbet and limoncello sabayon. Those curious to see the chefs at work can sit at the counter facing the kitchen. Business lunch menu (without options). A very appealing restaurant.

Name: Samwon Garden
Description: In the cultural landscape of Korean barbeque, Samwon Garden has long enjoyed fame based on its intricate balance between comfort and haute cuisine. It is where diverse cuts of prime Korean beef meet the seasoned grilling skills of its staff, a synergy that creates a delightful and comfortable gastronomic experience. What’s more, a gorgeously landscaped outdoor garden, coupled with high ceilings and glass walls infused with the Korean aesthetics of empty space, adds a sense of openness to this gracious dining. Its various private dining rooms cater to a variety of communal dining needs. For several decades, Samwon Garden has transformed Korean barbeque culture while carrying on the country’s culinary tradition. Visit this culinary landmark and enjoy a meal loaded with great traditional flavors.

Name: De Tempore
Description: As the name suggests, De Tempore is a modern French restaurant that focuses on seasonal ingredient-driven dishes. Within the culinary grammar of traditional French cuisine, the menu finely reflects the chef’s desire to impart a sense of sustainability and balance to his food. A wide selection of French-style sauces, such as the signature vin jaune drizzled over grilled monkfish, adds to the eatery’s culinary appeal.

Name: Casa De Carli
Description: A modern, family-run restaurant with a beautiful straightforward interior, open show kitchen and a walk-in wine fridge worth seeing as well as a wine fridge wall. Flavoursome cooking has a subtle North Italian bias, and the breads, pastas and ice creams are homemade. In front of the house there are tables on the cobbled street. Tip: private chef's table in the kitchen for up to 12 persons.

Name: Portfolio
Address: Lannův Palác, Havlíčkova 1030/1, Prague, 110 00, Czech Republic
Description: A keenly run restaurant with an appealingly relaxed atmosphere, set over two floors and decorated in a contemporary style. The cooking has its roots in French and Italian cuisine and the ambitious dishes are elaborate in their construction.

Name: Výčep
Description: Jars of preserved fruit and veg fill the walls, delicious pork matures in small fridges, and you can watch the chefs in the kitchen via the TVs at this rustic, modern pub. Czech recipes from yesteryear are brought up-to-date in generous, flavoursome dishes – and there are some great beers to accompany.

Name: Café Imperial
Description: The Imperial hotel’s restaurant is an impressive room, with a high ceiling and colourful mosaic-tiled walls and pillars. Menus list robust Czech dishes. It was the place to be seen in the 1920s and, as they say, Kafka's spirit lives on...

Name: Benjamin
Description: Ten seats are set around a horseshoe counter; come for the full tasting experience up to 10 courses. Chefs interact with guests, presenting carefully executed, boldly flavoured dishes, which are inspired by the history of Czech cuisine using only local products. Wine pairings are offered to match.

Name: QQ Asian Kitchen
Description: The Mosaic Hotel plays host to this pleasant restaurant with a sunny terrace and photos of Asia decorating the room. The cheery team serve well-priced dishes which are superbly spiced. The beef rendang curry will soon become a favourite and don't miss the delicious changing desserts.

Name: Salabka
Description: Set in a boutique winery on the outskirts of the city; vines have been grown on the hillside here since the 13C. Imaginative modern cooking focuses on local ingredients, with each plate containing many textures and flavours. A degustation menu is served, also vegetarian. The best tables are on the first floor overlooking the vines. Six spacious and stylish apartments.

Name: Grand Cru
Description: Across a cobbled courtyard is this sophisticated orangery-style restaurant where an experienced chef takes classic Czech and French recipes and delivers them in a balanced modern style. The charming wine bar offers simpler fare.

Name: Monarch
Description: With its comprehensive range of aged Czech and American USDA steaks and a blackboard filled with numerous special cuts, Monarch is a carnivore’s delight. The shelves are packed with wines and they offer some superb choices by the glass. The semolina mousse with cinnamon and gingerbread ice cream is a must.

Name: CottoCrudo
Description: Refined Italian cuisine based on seasonal ingredients awaits you in this restaurant of the elegant "Four Seasons Hotel". You can dine à la carte or in menu form. You will be looked after attentively in a lively atmosphere, and in summer you can enjoy the terrace with a view of the Vltava. Don't miss the cosy, modern bar with its Czech-inspired cocktail menu.

Name: V Zátiši
Address: Liliová 1, Betlémské Nám., Prague, 110 00, Czech Republic
Description: This modern city centre restaurant is a popular spot. Its name means ‘timeless’ and with its clever blend of modern Czech and international dishes, it looks set to stand up to its name. In the kitchen, local products are used that are bought daily at the farmers' market.

Name: Pot au Feu
Description: The chef-owner’s cooking is inspired by the French classics but also by his travels. The intimate interior comes with striking artwork and shelves packed with directly sourced French wines. Service is relaxed yet clued-up.

Name: Yamato
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Booking essential - dinner,Notable sake list
Description: The chef is a local but he trained in Japan, so alongside an array of authentic dishes you’ll find some original creations. A selection of Japanese beers and whiskies complement the cooking, and the place is run with real passion.

Name: La Finestra in Cucina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Booking essential - dinner,Interesting wine list
Description: You’d never guess but from 1918-1945, this lovely restaurant with its red-brick vaulted ceiling was an Alfa Romeo showroom! Expect rustic Italian dishes, an extensive selection of daily specials and fine Italian wines – and be sure to stop off for some treats from their neighbouring shop.

Name: Kampa Park
Address: Na Kampe 8b, Malá Strana, Prague, 118 00, Czech Republic
Description: Kampa Park is stunningly located by the water’s edge, next to Charles Bridge. Choose from several dining areas: the best spots are the Winter Garden and the riverside terrace. The décor is contemporary, as is the interesting menu.

Name: La Veranda
Description: Sit surrounded by books in the colourfully decorated main room or head down to the intimate basement. Cooking takes its inspiration from the Med, with Italy playing a big part. Staff are friendly and welcoming.

Name: Taro
Description: Close to the famous Staropramen Brewery is this counter restaurant centred around Asian cuisine. A 4 course tasting menu for lunch is followed by an 8 course set menu in the evening. A nice example of a dish is summer roll, chicken, tamarind sauce . A vegetarian menu is also available upon reservation.

Name: Bockem
Description: There’s something very endearing about this warmly run restaurant which occupies a house dating from 1905 in a quiet part of town. During the day it’s all about breakfast, but at dinner a 5-course set menu is offered where traditional Czech flavours are given a contemporary uplift; expect flashes of originality.

Name: Aromi
Description: A friendly team welcomes you to this bright, contemporary restaurant. Simply prepared, classically based Italian dishes are given modern touches; the fresh fish display demonstrates the owners’ commitment to sourcing good quality produce.
